## [Regulatory mechanism of M2d tumor\-associated macrophage\-derived exosomal apolipoprotein E on platinum resistance in ovarian cancer](../publications/c1ef5afb7e27993fe083.md)

Chunmei Wang; Ranjun Wu; Genhai Zhu

Background Platinum\-based chemotherapy plus cytoreductive surgery represents the standard first\-line therapy for ovarian cancer \(OC\), which yields robust early therapeutic responses in most patients\. However, platinum resistance is a formidable clinical hurdle, and how macrophages mediate drug resistance within the OC tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood\. Methods We cultured SKOV3 OC cells and THP\-1 monocytes, induced THP\-1 differentiation into M2d tumor\-associated macrophages\. Stable apolipoprotein E \(ApoE\) \-overexpressing SKOV3 cell lines were constructed via lentiviral transfection and puromycin screening\. We established nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models with mixed tumor cells and M2d macrophages, administered cisplatin treatment and collected tumor tissues after sacrifice by cervical dislocation\. RNA was extracted from tumor samples to conduct RT\-qPCR for gene expression detection\. Tumor tissue sections were prepared for HE staining, TUNEL apoptosis staining, and Western blot analysis to detect ApoE and phosphatidylinositol 3\-kinase \(PI3K\)/AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin \(mTOR\) pathway protein expression\. Results Using nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models, we demonstrated that M2d\-type tumor\-associated macrophages \(M2d TAMs\) promote platinum resistance and elevate tumoral ApoE levels\. In OC xenografts with stable ApoE overexpression, cisplatin\-induced apoptosis was profoundly repressed, resulting in reduced cisplatin sensitivity, while this inhibitory effect was not observed in the empty vector control group\. Mechanistically, ApoE activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade to counteract cisplatin cytotoxicity by suppressing cell death and sustaining pro\-survival signals\. Conclusions Overall, this study reveals that M2d TAMs induce platinum resistance in OC cells via exosomes carrying ApoE\.

## [Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery](../publications/c1f76c76d2376926a983.md)

Pingchuan Ma; Rui Ding; Shuai Wang

LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out\. Whether they do more than that, such as noticing where an algorithm went wrong and fixing it with further tests, is hard to tell from current benchmarks\. Most of them give the variables meaningful names, and an LLM shown only the names of the Tübingen cause\-effect pairs already gets 99% of the directions right\. With the names removed, the data are usually clean enough that picking a better algorithm than PC closes most of the gap\. We introduce Heuresis, a benchmark of anonymous simulated datasets whose mechanisms range from linear Gaussian to heavy\-tailed\. For each family of datasets it separates what a better existing algorithm can gain from what only a closer look at the data can gain, and it traces every edge an agent changes\. Every family leaves a gap that none of the algorithms, the router and the two causal\-discovery foundation models we ran can close, so a score above the best chosen algorithm has to come from using the data\. We instantiate the benchmark with an agent harness and three LLMs, GPT\-6\.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5\.5 and Qwen 3\.8 Flash\. GPT\-6\.1 Sol surpasses the best chosen algorithm on all six families, by 14% adjacency F1 on the most difficult one, and Claude Opus 5\.5 does so by 7\.4% there\. A third of the true edges the two agents restore on the two hardest families appear in no algorithm&\#x27;s output\. The code and data will be publicly released to facilitate future work\.

## [Evaluating the performance of the surface water and ocean topography \(SWOT\) mission for monitoring reservoirs across the conterminous United States](../publications/c20581feb3097fe0e57c.md)

Justin Tyler Huber; Peyman Abbaszadeh; Heejun Chang

Remote sensing provides critical insights into reservoir operations at sites with minimal in\-situ data\. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography \(SWOT\) mission improves upon previous satellite altimetry missions with two\-dimensional water surface representations, enhanced discharge estimates, and simultaneous water surface elevation \(WSE\) and surface area/width data\. We found median agreement \(Spearman rho\) greater than 0\.9 between SWOT and 773 United States Geological Survey \(USGS; ρ = 0\.96\) and US Army Corps of Engineers \(USACE; ρ = 0\.94\) WSE time series at Conterminous US reservoirs\. At USGS sites, 68% of observations had relative errors compared to in\-situ observations \(after adjusting for bias using time series average WSE\) with an absolute value under 10 cm, versus 22 cm at USACE sites\. However, low agreement clusters appeared in the Pacific Northwest and Southeastern US\. For SWOT\-derived downstream discharge, agreement \(ρ\) with in\-situ data was lower \(USACE: 0\.57, USGS: 0\.39\) with a low performance cluster in the Pacific Northwest and a high performance cluster in the central US\. At USGS sites, 68% of observations had relative errors with an absolute value under 108 cubic meters per second \(m 3 /s\), compared to 133 m 3 /s at USACE sites\. This research supports the ability of SWOT to accurately represent reservoir water levels at ungauged sites while recognizing potential for improvement on downstream discharge estimates\.

## [From Chaos to Peace\. Let Me Let Go\.](../publications/c207ec1a50bdfb1ccb31.md)

Charlene Poranganel

First responders and 911 professionals operate in environments where chaos is not the exception — it is the norm\. The psychological and physiological toll of managing not only the demands of emergency calls, but also the unrelenting human impulse to control outcomes, colleagues, and circumstances, contributes significantly to chronic stress, compassion fatigue, and emotional depletion in this workforce\. This article applies Mel Robbins&\#x27; Let Them, Let Me Theory \(2024\) to the unique occupational context of the 911 professional, exploring how the release of control and expectation can serve as a transformational pathway to personal peace, emotional resilience, and authentic presence\. Drawing on neuroscience, mindfulness research, somatic awareness, and behavioral psychology, the author presents a practical framework — the 3 P&\#x27;s for Release: Pause, Perspective, and Peace — alongside evidence\-informed mindfulness practices specifically adapted for the dispatch environment\. The article argues that letting go is not passivity, but rather an act of profound self\-empowerment that redirects energy from what cannot be controlled toward what can: the self\. By anchoring in present\-moment awareness and releasing the residue of past experiences and future anxieties, 911 professionals can replace chaos with clarity, and suffering with fulfillment\.

Annelise Yost; John McCarthy

This study explored the outcomes of an Interprofessional Education \(IPE\) event between preprofessional speech\-language pathologists \(SLPs\) and special educators aimed at identifying the outcomes of IPE on preprofessional teachers’ and SLPs’ knowledge of co\-teaching and classroom\-based models to support students who use AAC\. A focus group with preprofessional SLPs and special educators was run to identify perceptions and practicality of classroom\-based models to support AAC users\. Results demonstrated the ability for a short, focused IPE session to increase knowledge of classroom\-based service delivery for both preprofessional SLPs and special educators in the context of supporting AAC users\. Thematic analysis of the focus group interview identified five themes, views of co\-teaching, necessary supports, IPE session improvements, willingness to collaborate, and current practices\. The results of this study indicate the power of short IPE sessions to improve knowledge of co\-teaching and classroom\-based service delivery to support students who use AAC\. Responses highlight preprofessional educators’ positive perceptions toward co\-teaching\. However, challenges like time restraints and support may impact the perceived feasibility of classroom\-based models in practice\.

## [Coverage Cliffs in Off\-Policy Quantile Certification](../publications/c2271c0acfc40e1181e6.md)

Pauline Bourigault; Emmanuelle Bourigault

We study when logged contextual\-bandit data can certify an upper tail quantile for a policy selected from the same sample\. We construct a PAC\-Bayes Bernstein lower\-confidence envelope for the target cumulative distribution function \(CDF\), simultaneous over a predeclared threshold grid and all data\-dependent posteriors\. The resulting procedure, TailCert, uses the envelope&\#x27;s first crossing of level p to return an atom\-safe upper confidence bound on the selected posterior&\#x27;s pooled p\-quantile \(or inconclusive\)\. It can also be used to select a policy under a certified tail constraint\. The concentration ingredients are standard; the main theoretical contribution is a matched finite\-class certification boundary comparing full logs with their joint weighted CDF indicators at a fixed threshold\. On an explicit rare\-action class, the required sample size grows linearly with the overlap factor W, logarithmically with policy\-search and confidence complexity, and quadratically with the inverse CDF safety margin; the upper and lower bounds agree up to constants in the stated regime\. On this class, the CDF reduction hides which actions exceeded the budget; retaining action counts restores the full\-log rate\. Simulations verify the predicted search\-complexity shift, winner&\#x27;s\-curse failure of naive reuse, and the power cost of splitting\.

## [LAPLACE: una plataforma de IA para usarse con múltiples repositorios de código de proyectos de software](../publications/c227b4dd9b27a6a2b5ac.md)

Nicolás Crespo; Alejandra Lliteras; Patricia Bazán; Joaquín Bogado

The emergence of large language models \(LLMs\) can be applied to the optimization and improvement of source code within software project development environments, providing automatic feedback and contextual suggestions, and leveraging the project repository itself as a source of knowledge to support the programming process\. LAPLACE proposes the design and implementation of a unified platform for integrating large language models focused on software development\. The proposed solution avoids the fragmentation resulting from the use of multiple independent environments\. A key feature of LAPLACE is its high versatility regarding the large language models involved: it allows interaction with both global APIs \(OpenAI, Anthropic, Google\) and the deployment and use of local models \(such as Ollama\) by default\. This flexibility ensures proper management of sensitive information, reducing or eliminating the exposure of source code to third\-party services\. To optimize workflows, LAPLACE implements an architecture based on Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) and AI Agents\. This approach uses code repositories as a contextual knowledge base, enabling the model to provide assistance, analysis, and precise feedback tailored to the project’s codebase\. This promotes change traceability, data security, and efficient collaboration among development teams\.

## [Inaccurate Wind Power Forecasting During Extreme Weather Events Using Normalized Machine Learning](../publications/c23ea0aa01be05e196cb.md)

Dr\. Manoj Singh Amisha Nandansingh Negi

Wind\-power prediction is reasonably accurate in normal weather but degrades during high winds, gusts and rapid changing conditions, and a model fitted to one turbine does not directly transfer to turbines of other capacities\. This paper presents an extreme\-weather\-aware, capacity\-normalized framework that converts 10\-minute SCADA and meteorological data into turbine power with Random Forest regressor\. The model predicts power as a fraction of rated capacity, uses features such as air density, density\-corrected wind speed, gust factor, rapid wind changes and one\-hour variability, labels statistically extreme conditions with thresholds learned from training data, and gives extreme observations five times the training weight\. The framework is demonstrated on a dataset of 11,520 records from site \(coastal, flat inland, hilly and plateau\) with 2\.0–5\.0 MW turbines, using a per\-site chronological 80/20 split\. On the unseen test period the model reached an NMAE of 2\.01%, an NRMSE of 2\.55% and an R² of 0\.992, with an aggregate energy error of −0\.06% \(414\.42 MWh predicted versus 414\.68 MWh actual\)\. Errors rose under extreme conditions \(NMAE 2\.25% versus 1\.97% in normal conditions\), confirming that extreme periods should be reported separately\. Sensitivity test showed that the extreme weighting did not reduce extreme\-condition error on this dataset\.

## [A growing challenge: stakeholder perceptions of AI and ML applications in U\.S\. agriculture](../publications/c248ad693dcbcc9577e6.md)

Jennifer Koch; Andrew Fox; Richa Bhattarai; Hank C\. Jenkins‐Smith; Jonathan McFadden; Audrey Reinert; Juan Sesmero; M\. Z\. Walkup; Wolfgang Jentner; David S\. Ebert

Abstract Context The global population is expected to exceed ten billion by 2050 and food demand is projected to increase by up to 100% in the same timeframe\. Agricultural management must adapt to meet the increasing global demands\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) technologies can help the agricultural community respond to these needs\. Aims An online survey and follow\-up interviews were conducted to examine patterns of use, perceptions, and barriers among early adopting stakeholders regarding AI and ML\. Methods The online survey with agricultural stakeholders \(n=129\) included questions regarding the participants’ views on incorporating AI and ML techniques into farming practices and individual follow\-up interviews with agricultural stakeholders \(n=10\) were conducted to better understand their concerns toward technology use and adoption of AI\-enabled tools and technologies\. Key results Using a mixed\-methods approach, four challenges to establishing AI\-/ML\-enabled technology in agriculture were identified\. Namely, challenges related to \(1\) systems of systems \(SoS\), \(2\) sub\-seasonal to seasonal weather \(S2S\) forecasts, \(3\) precision soil management, and \(4\) policy and economics\. Each challenge was discussed in the context of recent literature\. Conclusion Concerns were voiced clustered around four broad research themes\. This brief communication brings the perspective of agricultural stakeholders to the discussion of the potential of AI/ML\-enabled technology and the direction of their development in the agricultural sector\. Implications Data collected in 2021, establish an important baseline for the early phase of AI/ML use in U\.S\. agriculture, enabling comparison of future perceptions and developments in the sector\. Impact This brief communication describes a survey and follow\-up interviews conducted with agricultural stakeholders on factors influencing their willingness and reluctance to incorporate AI and ML techniques into farming practices\. The findings, summarized and discussed as four key challenges for AI and ML in the agricultural sector, have the potential to streamline research activities\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management: Examining Employee Acceptance, Perceptions, and Workplace Outcomes in Indian IT Firms](../publications/c24fc0f8fc22eb2ede12.md)

Dr\. Neeraj Gupta Richa Sharma

This study considers the implementation of Artificial Intelligence in the area of Human Resource Management at Indian Information Technology firms\. This paper considers the acceptance, perceptions, and work outcomes due to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the process of Human Resource Management\. It covers the impact of AI on recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance evaluation, engagement and administration\. The research design used is quantitative\. The Research Onion model served as guidance in selecting the methodology\. The positivism philosophy helped to ensure objective research\. The deductive paradigm was applied to test the relationship between Artificial Intelligence adoption and reactions of employees\. The primary data were obtained via a Google Forms survey\. The total sample size was 200 respondents, who were HR professionals from Indian IT firms\. The data analysis was carried out with the help of SPSS and Microsoft Excel\. The descriptive statistics, t\-test, ANOVA, chi\-square, correlation and regression analysis were applied to analyse the data\. The AI technologies helped in achieving personal learning, engaging employees, and improving HRM services\. However, the employees had concerns over issues such as privacy of data, surveillance in the work environment, algorithmic biases, and lack of human interaction\. These aspects affected the employees&\#x27; trust and satisfaction in the use of AI technology\. The results of this study show that there are numerous advantages of using AI in Human Resource Management for Indian IT companies\. For the successful application of AI in HRM, ethical HR policies, employee training, transparency in AI, monitoring, and human decision\-making are essential\.

## [Study Habits and Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Tools Among Anesthesia Trainees in Türkiye: A Descriptive Survey: Study Habits of Anesthesia Trainees](../publications/c2626c96d5b6812ffbfd.md)

Çağrı Özdemir; Beyza Mehri Büyükgebiz Yeşil; Miray Gözde Özdemir

Objective: To describe the study habits and attitudes toward the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools for studying among anesthesia trainees in Türkiye, and to explore the associations between these factors and performance in national in\-training examinations\.Methods: A cross\-sectional online survey was administered to anesthesia trainees in Türkiye between April and June 2025\. The questionnaire addressed study frequency and duration, preferred resources, AI use patterns, and 5\-point Likert ratings for reliability and usefulness\. Performance in the national online trainee assessment examination \(ÇADS\) was analyzed using Kruskal\-Wallis tests and Spearman correlation, with ÇADS scores encoded as ordinal ranks \(1\-4\)\.Results: A total of 148 responses were analyzed\. Study sessions were reported as “occasional” by 60\.1%, with typical sessions lasting 1\-2 hours \(48\.6%\)\. Although 96\.6% of the respondents perceived a need to study more, the main barriers were fatigue and burnout \(46\.9%\) and time constraints due to clinical duties \(29\.4%\)\. The most commonly used resources were textbooks \(92\.6%\), spaced repetition \(60\.8%\), and online journals \(52\.7%\)\. AI tools were rated as useful \(mean 3\.89 ± 0\.99\) but only moderately reliable \(3\.22 ± 0\.97\)\. Two\-thirds of the respondents participated regularly in ÇADS \(66\.2%\)\. Among the 130 participants who had completed at least one ÇADS examination, the most frequently reported score category was 60\-79 \(73\.1%\)\. Frequent AI use was significantly associated with higher ÇADS performance \(p = 0\.003\)\. No associations were found between ÇADS performance and study frequency or specific study techniques\.Conclusion: Anesthesia trainees in Türkiye display irregular, brief study patterns, with fatigue and burnout as the main problems\. AI tool adoption remains low, likely due to moderate trust and a lack of guidance\. Frequent AI use and higher self\-confidence were associated with better examination performance in exploratory univariable analyses\. Educational programs may benefit from addressing workload and burnout while providing structured guidance for the appropriate integration of AI tools\.

## [CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell‐Type‐Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts](../publications/c265cb53d4ccdfa90747.md)

Liangying Yin; Yujia Shi; Ruoyu Zhang; Yong Xiang; Jinghong Qiu; Pak\-Chung Sham; Hon‐Cheong So

Integrating single\-cell RNA sequencing\(scRNA\-seq\) with the phenotypic depth of population\-scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases\. However, this is hindered by limited scRNA\-seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks\. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype\-imputed transcriptomes\. CausalCellInfer employs an invariant causal prediction\-inspired method\(scRNA\-seq\-based invariant generalized covariance measure, scI\-GCM\) to select environment\-stable marker genes, a parsimonious deep neural network for cell\-fraction deconvolution, and regularized matrix completion to reconstruct cell\-type\-specific \(CTS\) expression profiles\. This design is optimized for biobank\-scale data with technical heterogeneity and limited gene overlap\. Validated across simulated data, pseudo\-bulk and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell \(PBMC\) datasets, CausalCellInfer demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency over existing methods\. Applied to ∼500 000 UK Biobank \(UKBB\) participants across 29 traits, it captured known pathological shifts, such as reduced pancreatic β\-cell proportions in type 2 diabetes, and identified novel biological signals, including disrupted excitatory neuron\-oligodendrocyte interactions in depression\. Inferred CTS differential expression patterns showed significant concordance with independent single\-cell studies and were enriched for Open Targets disease genes\. Overall, CausalCellInfer bridges single\-cell insights and population\-scale genomics, enabling systematic discovery of putative disease mechanisms at cellular resolution\.

## [Global Research Trends in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Drug Delivery Technology: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis \(2015–2026\)](../publications/c26a191f6b9315675b1f.md)

evolution, collaborative networks, and emerging research themes remains limited\.The present study aims to systematically map the global research landscape of AI and ML applications in drug delivery technology through a bibliometric analysis of publications published between 2015 and 2026\.Bibliographic records will be retrieved from the Scopus database using a predefined search strategy, screened according to established inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using Bibliometrix \(R\-package\) and VOSviewer\.The study will evaluate annual publication trends, citation performance, influential authors, institutions, countries, journals, collaborative networks, keyword co\-occurrence, thematic evolution, and emerging research hotspots\.The findings are expected to provide a comprehensive overview of the intellectual structure and development of AI\-driven drug delivery research, identify influential contributors and collaborative patterns, and highlight promising directions for future investigations\.The study also seeks to offer practical insights for researchers, pharmaceutical scientists, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and industry stakeholders by identifying technological innovations that can enhance drug development processes and improve patient\-centric therapeutic outcomes\.By integrating bibliometric techniques with science mapping, this study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI\-enabled pharmaceutical technologies and provides a strategic research agenda for advancing intelligent drug delivery systems\.

## [Experiences of moderate\-to\-severe demoralization syndrome among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a qualitative study](../publications/c28338c003e5aa05e64d.md)

Jianfang Bao; Yijia Yin; Xuan Cheng; Jiang XiaoXue; Binhong Luo; Suping Guo; Jun Xu; Min Qian

Background Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis \(MHD\) are at high risk of demoralization syndrome \(DS\), which may adversely affect psychological wellbeing, quality of life, and treatment\-related self\-management\. However, limited qualitative evidence exists regarding their experiences\. Aim To explore the experiences of moderate\-to\-severe DS among patients receiving MHD, focusing on stressors, psychological and behavioral experiences, coping strategies, and stress\-buffering resources\. Methods A descriptive qualitative design guided by the Stress Process Model \(SPM\) was adopted\. Purposive maximum\-variation sampling was used to recruit 15 patients receiving MHD with moderate\-to\-severe DS \(DS\-II score &gt;9\) from a tertiary hospital in China between January and March 2026\. Data were collected through semistructured, face\-to\-face, in\-depth interviews\. All interviews were audio\-recorded and transcribed verbatim, and the transcripts were verified by participants\. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s six\-phase framework\. Results Four framework\-informed themes and 14 subthemes were identified, corresponding to the major SPM domains of sources of DS, impacts of DS, coping strategies, and stress\-buffering resources\. Two important distinctions were identified: reduced social participation primarily reflected illness\- and treatment\-related restrictions, whereas social withdrawal represented a more intentional behavioral response associated with greater demoralization; and apparent acceptance of dialysis sometimes reflected helpless resignation and passive compromise rather than adaptive acceptance\. Conclusion DS among patients receiving MHD reflects a complex process shaped by interacting treatment\-related stressors, coping responses, and social support resources\. Interventions should aim to reduce modifiable stressors, strengthen adaptive coping and perceived control, and support psychological adaptation, functioning, and meaningful engagement during long\-term dialysis\.

## [Deep learning\-assisted sustainable design of a multi\-substrate 2\.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna](../publications/c29ad28712b658df24d9.md)

Ameni Mersani; Kawther Mekki; Omrane Necibi; Mohamed O\. Altaieb; Alameen Eltoum Mohamed Abdalrahman; Omer Hamid; Hassen Chouaib; Kais Khaldi; Ali Gharsallah

Wearable antennas are essential components of modern Internet of Things \(IoT\) systems, enabling wireless communication for body\-centric, healthcare, environmental\-monitoring, and smart\-textile applications\. Deep learning provides an effective means of accelerating antenna design and optimization under complex material and operating conditions\. This paper presents a deep learning\-assisted and sustainability\-oriented framework for designing a compact 2\.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna implemented on three representative substrates: FR4, Rogers laminate, and felt\-based textile\. A unified slotted microstrip patch topology is adopted to enable a consistent comparison between rigid and flexible antenna realizations while highlighting trade\-offs among impedance matching, bandwidth, mechanical flexibility, and material characteristics\. A multi\-substrate full\-wave electromagnetic dataset containing approximately $$1\.09\\times \{10\}^\{5\}$$ samples is generated in CST Microwave Studio by varying the principal geometrical parameters, substrate descriptors, and operating frequency over the 2\.0–3\.0 GHz range\. A fully connected deep neural network surrogate is trained to predict the reflection coefficient from antenna geometry, substrate properties, and operating frequency, achieving an RMSE of 0\.8500 dB and $$\{R\}^\{2\}=0\.9553$$ on the held\-out sample\-level test partition\. A separate geometry\-level holdout evaluation is also conducted using six antenna configurations whose complete frequency responses are excluded from training and validation\. The optimized antenna designs are fabricated on the three substrates and experimentally evaluated through calibrated reflection\-coefficient measurements\. For the felt\-based textile prototype, additional measured reflection\-coefficient responses under on\-arm bending and progressive surface\-wetting conditions demonstrate stable impedance matching around the 2\.4 GHz ISM band\. Radiation patterns, realized gain, radiation efficiency, on\-body behavior, and specific absorption rate are evaluated using full\-wave simulations only; no experimental over\-the\-air radiation validation is claimed\. The simulations predict broadside radiation behavior and simulated SAR values below the applicable international safety limits\. An equivalent parallel RLC model is also introduced to support the physical interpretation of substrate\-dependent impedance behavior\. The results indicate that the proposed surrogate\-assisted framework enables rapid, substrate\-aware antenna design and reduces dependence on repeated full\-wave simulations\. The felt\-based implementation provides a practical compromise among simulated electromagnetic performance, flexibility, reduced substrate mass, and wearable suitability\.

## [Decline of the Degree](../publications/c2b13eecd310224ba16f.md)

Levente Horváth; Ákos Simon

Micro\-credentials have become one of the most exciting products in higher education, adult education and the labour market in recent years\. This paper argues that micro\-credentials are not just a complement to university courses but can be one of the most important tools for competence development in a rapidly changing world\. We seek an answer to the question of why the university degree may lose its relative importance as the primary measure of knowledge and why skills, competencies, adaptability and job\-specific skills are coming to the fore\. We also present two short examples: the Irish practice and the example of University at Buffalo, how micro\-credentials can become one of the strongest elements of the connection between the labour market and higher education\. Our main assumption is that the degree will not disappear, but its value may slowly fade into the background, and in the future, micro\-credentials that demonstrate verifiable, performance\-based competence, immediately applicable skills and the ability to continuously learn will become a competitive advantage\. Micro\-credentials offer flexible, labour\-market\-relevant skills but lack the trust, recognition, and quality assurance of degrees, with employers citing consistency concerns more often than skill\-fit benefits\. Uneven recognition, oversupply, and barriers like cost, language, and digital access further weaken trust and risk excluding vulnerable learners, potentially deepening inequality in adult education\.

## [Terminal\-RSI: Recursive Self\-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self\-Rewrite and Policy\-Refine](../publications/c2b3a93a626a737f87eb.md)

Junyao Yang; Zongxia Li; Yucheng Shi; Zhongzhi Li; Ruhan Wang; Ruiwen Zhou; Haitao Mi; Shuicheng Yan; Leowei Liang

Converting verifier outcomes into useful policy updates and partial progress into complete task resolution is crucial for terminal agents\. We present Terminal\-RSI, which alternates Recursive Self\-Rewrite \(RSR\) of verified trajectories with critic\-inheriting Recursive Policy\-Refine \(RPR\)\. We formulate Turn\-Boundary Skip\-Observation GAE \(TB\-GAE\) to retain token\-specific baselines while applying decay across interaction turns\. Family Dense Reward \(FDR\) calibrates semantic progress across task families; Success\-Prioritized Reward \(SPR\) separates strict success from bounded partial credit\. A Warm\-up Critic Model, recursive critic handoff, and stage\-specific learning rates coordinate the two refinement phases\. The five\-stage sequence from Qwen3\.8\-27B base model through RSR\-1, RPR\-1, RSR\-2, and RPR\-2 yields Terminal\-RSI\-27B: 19\.84% on Terminal\-Bench 4\.0, 86\.52% on Terminal\-Bench 2\.1, 16\.95% on Terminal\-Bench 3\.0, and 79\.00% on Terminal\-Bench Hard\. On LHTB, process reward rises from 0\.21 to 0\.37 and strict completion from 0/46 to 5/46; SWR100 success doubles from 3\.00% to 6\.00%\. By recursively coupling verified trajectory rewriting with critic\-inheriting policy refinement, each retained stage consolidates discovered behaviors and progressively advances the agent from partial local repairs to strict terminal verification\.

## [Coupler Modification for Periodic Preventive Maintenance on Sakai SV526D and SV700TF Compactor Units to Improve The Efficiency and Reliability of Hydraulic System Inspection](../publications/c2c12f97b2da92f0b87a.md)

Roni Supriyadi

Hydraulic pressure inspection is essential for the preventive maintenance of heavy equipment; however, incompatible diagnostic connections can prevent mechanics from completing scheduled inspections\. At PT Antareja Mahada Makmur, Mifa Jobsite, the hydraulic test ports on Sakai SV526D and SV700TF compactors were incompatible with the available Komatsu pressure gauge equipment, while the procurement of dedicated Sakai diagnostic tools was constrained by uncertain availability\. This study aimed to identify the hydraulic pressure inspection constraint, implement a hydraulic test coupler modification, and evaluate its implications for preventive maintenance activities\. A descriptive qualitative case study was conducted using the Suggestion System framework, encompassing problem identification, improvement planning, technical implementation, and field evaluation\. Data were obtained from maintenance documentation, component damage records, dealer quotations, and field observations conducted before and after the modification\. The intervention involved replacing the original hydraulic test couplers with Genuine Komatsu couplers, thereby enabling the existing pressure gauges to be connected to the compactors\. Field observations indicated that the modification restored hydraulic pressure inspection capability, improved test\-port cleanliness, reduced the observed risk of hydraulic oil spillage, and facilitated easier connection and disconnection of the pressure gauge equipment\. These findings suggest that adapting diagnostic interfaces can address equipment compatibility constraints while supporting scheduled hydraulic system inspections\. However, reductions in breakdown frequency, improvements in equipment reliability, and financial savings were not quantitatively established\. The study concludes that hydraulic test coupler modification represents a practical improvement for preventive maintenance activities; however, further quantitative evaluation is required to determine its effects on maintenance efficiency, operational performance, cost savings, and equipment reliability\.

## [أنماط الأسئلة العلمية لدى طلبة الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى في محافظة المفرق](../publications/c2c25e720ed5ca40d7a4.md)

الزعبي ، عبد الله

هدفت الدراسة إلى تقصي أهتمامات وأنماط الأسئلة العلمية لدى طلبة الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، ومعرفة إذا ما اختلفت تلك الأنماط باختلاف متغيري الصف الدراسي، وجنس الطالب، ولتحقيق ذلك استُخدم المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، وطورت بطاقة تحليل لأسئلة الطلاب وفق اهتمامات الأسئلة وأنماطها، وجرى التأكد من صدقها وثباتها، وتكونت عينة الدراسة من \(164\) طالبًا وطالبة من طلبة الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى في مدينة السلط\. وأظهرت النتائج أن الأسئلة الأكثر شيوعًا لدى عينة الدراسة تمثلت بموضوعات الحيوانات، والنباتات، والفضاء، كما بينت النتائج أن أكثر الأنماط شيوعًا في أسئلة الطلبة هي الأسئلة السطحية، والأسئلة التفسيرية، وأقلها الأسئلة الاستكشافية، والأسئلة الفرضية، وأظهرت النتائج وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في انماط أسئلة عينة الدراسة وفقًا لمتغير الصف الدراسي، ولصالح طلبة الصف الثالث الأساسي، وكذلك عدم وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في تلك الأنماط تعزى لمتغير جنس الطالب\. وبناءً على نتائج الدراسة يوصى بتضمين مهارات التساؤل العلمي كجزء أساسي من مناهج العلوم الدراسية، وتطوير دليل إرشادي للمعلمين يتضمن أمثلة عملية لإثارة الفضول العلمي لدى الطلبة، لطرح الأسئلة الاستكشافية والفرضية\.

## [Artificial Neural Network Estimation of Sea Surface Temperature from Oceanographic Variables](../publications/c2ca604042afb66dbb30.md)

Mfon David Umoh; Felix Evans Udoh; Esin John

Sea surface temperature \(SST\) sits at the centre of the climate system, but estimating it accurately is hard because the oceanographic processes that drive it interact in complex, non\-linear ways\. In this study we build and test a feedforward artificial neural network \(ANN\) that estimates SST from three physically meaningful inputs, sea surface salinity and the eastward and northward components of ocean current velocity, using monthly reanalysis fields from the Copernicus Marine Service \(January 2024 to October 2025, 22 months\)\. The predictors and the target are contemporaneous monthly means, so the model estimates the SST field rather than forecasting it at a lead time\. We varied the number of hidden neurons from 10 to 100 in steps of ten, trained each configuration from 30 random initializations with the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, and evaluated it on a temporally held\-out test period \(the final six months\) using four metrics computed on the unscaled values in degrees Celsius: mean squared error \(MSE\), root mean squared error \(RMSE\), mean absolute error \(MAE\), and mean absolute percentage error \(MAPE\)\. In\-sample, every network of 30 neurons or more interpolated the training months almost perfectly, so in\-sample accuracy carried no information about generalization\. On the held\-out months, test RMSE fell from 1\.467 °C at 10 neurons to 1\.162 °C at 100 neurons, but all configurations beyond 30 neurons performed within one standard deviation of one another: extra width bought fit to the training data, not generalization\. The network clearly beat the training\-mean climatology \(test RMSE 1\.892 °C\) and a linear regression on the same predictors \(1\.811 °C\), confirming that salinity and velocity fields carry genuine SST information, although persistence from the previous month \(0\.869 °C\) remained stronger on this seasonal series\. The study&\#x27;s contribution is a protocol\-correct architecture evaluation, held\-out testing, repeated initializations, and baseline comparison, and its clearest lesson is that single\-run in\-sample sweeps can suggest a capacity–performance story that does not survive validation\.

## [The First\-Offender Paradox in Indonesian Plea Bargaining: Lessons from Italy and Implications for Corruption Cases](../publications/c2ce892dc39fea6ca62f.md)

Erwin Susilo; Dharma Setiawan Negara; Ong Argo Victoria; Joel Niyobuhungiro

This study analyzes the regulation of plea bargaining \(PB\) under Indonesia’s Criminal Procedure Code \(KUHAP\), examines the inconsistency in the first\-offender requirement under Article 234, and proposes a regulatory model informed by comparison with Italy’s patteggiamento\. The study addresses the discrepancy between Articles 78 and 205, which require defendants to be first\-time offenders, and Article 234, which does not explicitly impose this requirement\. This inconsistency creates legal uncertainty regarding repeat offenders’ eligibility for PB and may result in inconsistent application\. The study employs a normative juridical method using statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches\. The findings reveal that Indonesia’s PB framework lacks consistency, whereas Italy’s patteggiamento restricts eligibility according to specific offender categories and legal conditions without universally requiring first\-offender status\. The Italian model serves as a comparative reference rather than a framework for direct adoption, highlighting the importance of clear and coherent eligibility criteria\. In Indonesia, adding a first\-offender requirement to Article 234 would align it with Articles 78 and 205 and strengthen the internal consistency of PB regulation\. The ambiguity surrounding Article 234 also raises concerns about corruption cases, which Article 205 excludes from PB but Article 234 does not expressly address\. Accordingly, Article 234 should be revised to specify the first\-offender requirement and clarify which offenses are excluded from PB\. These amendments should reflect Indonesia’s legal context rather than replicate the Italian model, promoting legal certainty, reducing interpretive differences, and ensuring consistent application of PB within the Indonesian criminal justice system\.

## [Predicted visual attention and cognitive demand in luxury beauty retail: an exploratory AI\-based neuromarketing study](../publications/c2cfaca5e7eb491c9015.md)

Hedda Martina Šola; Jasenka Gajdoš Kljusurić; Aljoša Šestanović

Introduction This exploratory study examines how AI\-supported neuromarketing tools can be used to predict visual attention and cognitive demand in a luxury beauty retail environment\. Methods The research was conducted in a high\-end cosmetics store in Zagreb, where 11 static images, selected from 21 photographs of the store, and a 9\-minute in\-store video recording, edited into an 85\-second simulation of the consumer journey, were analyzed using a predictive platform informed by large\-scale eye tracking and EEG datasets \(eye\-tracking data from approximately 180,000 participants and EEG data from 27,000 participants; more than 100 billion data points in total\)\. No shoppers were tested; all reported values are model predictions\. The analysis focused on how store layout, product positioning, visual hierarchy, and branded communication elements influence predicted focus, attentional efficiency, and cognitive effort\. Results The results reveal several consistent patterns\. Brand areas that were visually separated from competing stimuli attracted stronger, more sustained predicted attention, whereas visually crowded or externally exposed zones reduced attentional efficiency\. Central product placement proved particularly effective when surrounded by fewer distracting elements, suggesting that spatial clarity can support more efficient visual processing of branded and product\-related stimuli\. At the AOI level, Engagement and Cognitive Demand rose together \( r = 0\.90\)\. In the video simulation, Cognitive Demand remained uniformly high while Focus varied with the field of view, and the two were not related\. Discussion These findings highlight the interaction between attention allocation, cognitive load, visibility conditions, and spatial organization in luxury retail communication\. Overall, the study demonstrates the value of AI\-supported neuromarketing for understanding how consumers process visually complex retail spaces\. It contributes to communication and consumer research by clarifying how visual structure and cognitive demand shape brand visibility and decision\-related processing in luxury beauty retail\. The findings also offer practical guidance for improving store design, in\-store communication, and experiential branding strategies by applying state\-of\-the\-art technology for predicting consumer behavior in visually complex retail environments\.

## [Improving the Forecasting of Budget Revenues by Tax Type](../publications/c2df350f8b45fdb197b7.md)

Uzmanov Ikhtiyor Ibragim ugli

This article examines how budget revenue forecasting can be improved by modeling individual tax categories rather than relying primarily on aggregate revenue projections\. Using official budget execution data for Uzbekistan for 2020–2025, the study analyzes corporate income tax, personal income tax, turnover tax, value added tax, excise tax, customs duty, property tax, land tax, subsoil use tax, and water use tax\. Three transparent benchmark methods—linear trend extrapolation, compound annual growth, and median year\-on\-year growth—are assessed through rolling\-origin validation\. The exercise shows that forecast performance differs materially across taxes because tax bases, payment schedules, administrative changes, commodity exposure, and policy adjustments are heterogeneous\. The paper therefore proposes a tax\-specific forecasting architecture in which statistical models are selected by out\-of\-sample error, then supplemented by explicit tax\-base assumptions, policy\-costing adjustments, scenario ranges, and continuous forecast\-error monitoring\. The proposed framework is designed to improve both technical accuracy and the transparency of fiscal planning\.

## [Factors influencing the professional identity of medical care assistants: a qualitative study](../publications/c2e1b2e70de6ec6f64ec.md)

Jing Zhao; Dongping Xu; Ying Hong; CHANG Hongjuan; Yicheng Xiong

Objective This study aimed to explore the factors influencing the professional identity of medical care assistants \(MCAs\) and to interpret relevant findings through the lens of social identity theory, thereby informing strategies to support professional identity and workforce stability\. Methods A qualitative descriptive research design was adopted\. Using purposive sampling, 15 MCAs from a tertiary grade A hospital in Wuhan, Hubei province, China, were recruited for one\-to\-one semistructured interviews\. Data were analyzed via inductive thematic analysis, and this report was prepared according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research \(COREQ\)\. Results Four themes and eight subthemes were identified: social evaluation influencing experiences of professional value and dignity, including recognition of professional value and challenges to professional dignity; role positioning and practical needs constructing professional meaning, including professional role positioning and practical needs as a driving factor; care interactions and self\-adjustment shaping professional experiences, including communication and trust building and professional competence and emotional adjustment; and team and organizational support strengthening professional identity, including acceptance by the healthcare team and professional training and institutional support\. Participants described social evaluation, professional role positioning, recognition or devaluation experienced during care interactions, team acceptance, and organizational support as factors influencing their professional identity\. Practical needs primarily shaped occupational choice and intentions to remain, whereas self\-adjustment functioned as a coping process within emotionally demanding care experiences\. Conclusion Accounts from participants suggest that the professional identity of MCAs is shaped by social evaluation, role positioning, care interactions, and team and organizational support within the context of their workplace\. Healthcare institutions and relevant employers should enhance social and team recognition, clarify responsibilities of the role and collaboration boundaries, improve training and supportive employment arrangements, and consider performance\-based incentives to support professional identity and workforce stability of MCAs\.

## [From Bare to Informed Looking: An Art\-Historical Proposition on Mindful Art Engagement, Emotion Regulation, and Cognitive Enrichment in the Age of AI](../publications/c2e5476b188115939250.md)

Ewelina Chwiejda

The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence has unsettled more than the labour market\. It has given rise to two related anxieties: an existential unease about human meaning, agency, and uniqueness—“AI anxiety”—and a quieter abdication of critical effort to machines, which recent works call “cognitive surrender\.” The remedies most often proposed for these conditions, among them psychoeducation, regulation, engineering ethics, and therapy, leave a conspicuous gap, since none of them draws on aesthetic experience or on the making of meaning\. This article, written from an engaged, applied art\-history position, proceeds as a conceptual analysis rather than an empirical study\. It defines “mindful art engagement” as a receptive, two\-phase practice that moves from bare to informed looking, an open and contemplative looking followed by art\-historically informed interpretation, sets out its boundaries, distinguishes the three constructs on which it bears \(felt meaningfulness, art\-historical understanding, and cognitive enrichment\), and maps the existing evidence onto its components\. On this basis, it advances a hypothesis that such a practice could contribute to emotion regulation and to cognitive enrichment in the age of AI, and that meaning is the point at which the two pathways meet\.

## [Beyond the Algorithmic Scriptor: Generative AI, Reader Interpretation, and the Limits of Barthes’s &quot;Death of the Author&quot;](../publications/c2f07e3c979f80694c50.md)

Kunal UpadhyayG\.; Dr\. Nisha Khan

Roland Barthes argued that author’s identity and intentions are less important in any text, suggesting that the actual literary meaning is created by the reader of the text\. Generative Artificial intelligence \(AI\) makes Barthes’s concept of &quot;Death of the Author&quot; a reality, by producing brilliant as well as complex prose without biological subjectivity, or human creative intent\. However, contemporary literary studies have mainly focused on computational mechanics, disputes regarding copyrights, and stylistic mimicry\. This creates a crucial research gap in understanding that how human mind or reader hermeneutics work when the author of the text is a non\- human element and is algorithmic\. This study addresses this critical theoretical omission\. Main objectives of the research include examining how algorithmic generation challenges traditional human written texts, evaluation of the reader’s reaction to authorial absence, and finally, exploration of the fact that why readers are used to ask who or what controls the discourse\. Grounded in in post\-structuralist critique, this paper focuses on re\-evaluation of Barthesian reader\-response theory with computational textuality\. The findings indicates that readers find it difficult to interpret the text completely due to absence of actual human author or the intention behind it\. They naturally look for meanings, purpose, or intention to guide their interpretation\. AI shows that readers still expect a human intention behind every text they read, suggesting that meaningful literary interpretation depends upon the connection between reader and the author\. People still lack empathy, sympathy and connection towards AI generated works\.

## [BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING REENGINEERING: ESSENCE AND IMPLEMENTATION FEATURES](../publications/c3034dcad6bb4882cfa5.md)

Oksana Onyshchenko; Володимир Ковальов

The purpose of the paper is to explore theoretical and applied aspects of outsourcing business process reengineering\. The essence of reengineering is substantiated in the context of transferring non\-core functions to external contractors, and key stages of process redesign, selection criteria for outsourcing partners, and integration mechanisms are defined\. Methodology\. The study employs methods of scientific generalization, structural\-functional analysis, and process modeling to investigate the transformation of management systems\. The research identifies core process stages, evaluation metrics \(KPIs\), stakeholder roles, potential risks, and control mechanisms through a systematic approach to business process optimization\. Results of the study\. The findings demonstrate that combining reengineering with outsourcing allows enterprises to optimize operating costs, accelerate operational cycles, improve service quality, and form an integrated business ecosystem capable of rapid adaptation to market changes\. An integrated management model for outsourcing reengineering was developed, outlining six sequential stages from process diagnostics to continuous monitoring\. Practical implications\. The proposed reengineering program model and functional\-process management mechanism can be utilized by enterprises across various industries seeking to enhance their competitiveness, reduce operational expenses, and streamline non\-core functions during digital transformation and market instability\. Value / originality\. The paper provides a comprehensive theoretical and methodological framework for integrating business process reengineering and outsourcing, establishing a structured management model that bridges the gap between internal process optimization and external partnership coordination\.

## [Ageism toward older adults during COVID\-19: associations with emotional coping and intergenerational contact](../publications/c303af373282e7b43733.md)

Theresa Scott; Melissa Kugelman; Amanda Jane Salmon

Introduction The COVID\-19 pandemic brought substantial social and emotional stressors, alongside widespread messaging that framed older adults as particularly vulnerable\. It remains unclear whether these conditions were associated with hostile and benevolent ageist perspectives of older people\. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the factors associated with ageism, perceived changes in emotional coping, and the attitudes and experiences of Australian residents toward older adults\. Methods Ageism, aging expectations, and contact quality with older adults in the context of COVID\-19 were explored using an online, cross\-sectional correlational study design, participants responded to both established and novel measures for these factors\. Results A total of 273 Australian residents completed the online study \(aged 19–82 years, M = 40\.73, SD = 14\.74\)\. There was no association between emotional coping and ageist beliefs\. More positive aging expectations were related to lower hostile ageism, but not benevolent ageism\. Positive contact with older adults was linked with lower hostile ageism and higher benevolent ageism, while negative contact showed the reverse pattern\. Conclusion The current study suggests that ageist messages portraying ‘vulnerability’ reflected commonly held attitudes toward older Australians during the pandemic and highlights the importance of considering both the quality and nature of intergenerational contact when developing ageism\-reduction strategies\. Potential explanations, limitations and directions for future research are discussed\.

## [Ajeesh, A\. K\. &amp; Rukmini, S\.: Posthuman perception of artificial intelligence in science fiction: an exploration of Kazuo Ishiguro’s Klara and the Sun](../publications/c3139cdffa1bac529a5e.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 38 \(2\):853\-860\. 2023Our fascination with artificial intelligence \(AI\), robots and sentient machines has a long history, and references to such humanoids are present even in ancient myths and folklore\. The advancements in digital and computational technology have turned this fascination into apprehension, with the machines often being depicted as a binary to the human\. However, the recent domains of academic enquiry such as transhumanism and posthumanism have produced many a literature in the genre of science fiction \(SF\) that endeavours to alter this antagonistic notion of AI\. In his novel Klara and the Sun, Kazuo Ishiguro explores this notion of AI as a caring machine capable of nursing an ailing young girl back to health\. Through this portrayal of AI as a sentient being capable of empathy and cognition, Ishiguro is attempting to usher in a new perception of AI: a posthuman perception that challenges the conventional notions of AI as a machine devoid of emotions\. The novel further expands on the idea of self, soul and human consciousness and ponders on the question, what makes humans human, and if it is possible to imbibe these qualities onto an AI\. Owing to the novelty of this notion, an unexplored avenue that deserves further exploration, this paper examines the plausibility of this new notion of AI through a careful exegesis of the novel\. The paper also attempts to chart the impact of SF in society and culture\. The study reveals a positive shift in perception towards AI, and there seems to be much scope for interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research\. \(direct link \)

## [Feasibility, acceptability and usability of InControl web\-platform intervention for older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain: A mixed\-methods pilot study protocol](../publications/c3151561d78750a96bfd.md)

David Oliveira; Nelson Pacheco Rocha; Anabela G\. Silva

BACKGROUND: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is highly prevalent among older adults and is associated with disability, reduced physical activity, and decreased quality of life\. Digital health interventions can improve access to care and support pain self\-management\. InControl is a user\-centered web\-based platform that combines exercise and pain science education\. The aim of this pilot study is to assess the usability and acceptability of the InControl platform and the feasibility of the research methods\. This will help inform methodological improvements in the design of a future randomized controlled trial\. METHODS: A randomized, parallel\-group, mixed\-methods pilot study will be conducted with two groups: usual care group and the InControl intervention\. Thirty\-four participants aged 60 years or older with chronic musculoskeletal pain will be recruited at the Local Health Unit of Aveiro Region\. The InControl intervention will last 8 weeks and will combine in\-person sessions with remote interventions\. Feasibility will be assessed using indicators of recruitment, retention, adherence, refusal, and dropout rates\. Usability will be measured using the System Usability Scale, while acceptability and appropriateness will be assessed through a questionnaire and semi\-structured interviews\. Secondary outcomes will include pain, physical function, psychological factors, quality of life, and cognitive function\. Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative thematic analysis\. DISCUSSION: The findings will inform the design of a future large\-scale randomized controlled trial and contribute to the development of more effective digital interventions tailored to the needs of older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain\. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is registered on clinicaltrials\.gov, NCT07774416 \(https://clinicaltrials\.gov/study/NCT07774416?tab=study\), August 18, 2026\.

## [Multiagent Assortment Optimization in Sequential Matching Markets](../publications/c329af619e47796fe4bc.md)

Alfredo Torrico; Margarida Carvalho; Andrea Lodi

Motivated by the challenges faced by choice\-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two\-sided assortment optimization model\. Specifically, this model consists of two sides \(e\.g\., customers and suppliers\) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models\. A matching is realized through a two\-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side\. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching\. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant\-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences\. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one\-sided choice\-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly\. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two\-sided choice\-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a \[Formula: see text\]\-approximation factor, which is the best possible\. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well\-known multinomial logit \(MNL\) choice model under the small probability regime\. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a \[Formula: see text\]\-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models\. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions\. Funding: M\. Carvalho thanks the support of the Institut de valorisation des données \(IVADO\) and Fonds de recherche du Québec \(FRQ\) through the FRQ\-IVADO Research Chair and of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada \(NSERC\) \[Grant 2019\-04557\]\. ## [Ibogaine for Substance Use Disorders](../publications/c33859baf9353930b34a.md)

Ahmed I Anwar; Abdul\-rahman A\. Hegazi; M\. Farris Sawaya; Joshua R\. Nelson; Audrey E\. Lashley; Jillian M\. Gatti; Kristy M Pham; Ibraheem A\. Hachem; Molly E\. McNulty; Destiny S\. Lewis; Kevin Sean Murnane; Alan D\. Kaye

Substance use disorders \(SUDs\) are a major global health burden, and psychedelic\-assisted therapies are now gaining scientific interest, with ibogaine being considered as a candidate for anti\-addictive effects across multiple substance classes\. Ibogaine is a multi\-target indole alkaloid acting on opioid, glutamatergic, serotonergic, and sigma systems with potential to rapidly reduce withdrawal and cravings after a single administration\. Ibogaine is metabolized into noribogaine, which has a longer half\-life and contributes to sustained pharmacological effects\. These compounds act on multiple neurotransmitter systems including NMDA receptors, serotonin receptors, and opioid receptors, which allow it to have a broad neurobiological effect\. It also has anti\-addictive properties linked to neuroplasticity, dopamine modulation, and opioid receptor activity\. Additionally, iboga has use in African rituals, with modern interest increasing in the twentieth century\. Ibogaine now is an unregulated or semi\-regulated substance with increased interest in controlled clinical development as well\. Clinical evidence for ibogaine comes from observational studies and case reports, e\.g\., particularly in opioid use disorder\. Ibogaine carries significant risks, particularly cardiotoxicity, neurological adverse effects including hallucinations, and reported fatalities\. Safer derivates such as noribogaine and tabernanthalog \(TBG\) are being developed to retain anti\-addictive efficacy and reduce toxicity\. Ibogaine induces prolonged oneirogenic states involved in autobiographical memory processing, and outcomes are influenced by setting, integration therapy, and psychotherapy\. Current research is largely observational, and studies are small, which highlights the need for standardized protocols and clinical trials\. Overall, ibogaine represents a therapeutic candidate for SUDs, with broad anti\-addictive potential\. In this review, we provide an overview of ibogaine&\#x27;s history and pharmacology, critically examine its therapeutic potential in multiple SUDs, and discuss current limitations, emerging alternatives, and future directions\.

## [Solvation‐Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide‐Temperature Operation of High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries](../publications/c33d43e77065c5a8b201.md)

Qingyu Dong; Nan Chen; Yang Li; Li Li; X\.J\. Liu; Feng Wu; Renjie Chen

ABSTRACT High‐energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep‐sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature‐sensitive ion transport, Li \+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry\. A solvation‐equilibrium‐locked electrolyte \(SELE\) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite \(DMS\), a low‐freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr 13 DFOB \(1‐methyl‐1‐propylpyrrolidinium difluoro\(oxalato\)borate\) as an ionic‐liquid co‐solvent\. Cooperative ion–dipole and weak C–H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr 13 \+ regulate the free‐solvent reservoir, while TFSI − \(bis\(trifluoromethanesulfonyl\)imide\) and DFOB − enrich the primary Li \+ coordination shell\. Variable‐temperature 7 Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent‐separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature‐responsive Pyr 13 DFOB‐free electrolyte\. This locked anion‐rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li \+ , mitigates solvent‐derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF‐ and borate‐rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811\. Consequently, Li\|\|NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at −85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to −122\.9°C\. A 6\.6 Ah Li\|\|Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg −1 under lean‐electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation‐equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range\.

## [Fundamental data regarding the emergency management of infectious diseases in higher education institutions: HIV knowledge and stigma among college students in Southwest China](../publications/c33e6727e427d9639f34.md)

Fang Pei; Xin Li; Hao Yao; Rong Pei

This study aimed to assess the knowledge on human immunodeficiency virus \(HIV\) and factors related to HIV stigma among college students to enlighten them on the development of HIV prevention strategies and better understand the additional benefit of HIV risk reduction, supplied fundamental data for the emergency management of infectious diseases in higher educational institutions\. This cross\-sectional study enrolled students from 10 universities in southwest China \( n = 4,133\)\. Survey questions included demographic information, HIV knowledge, HIV stigma, and self\-esteem\. Descriptive and inferential statistics were applied to summarize the data\. Logistic regression was used to analyze factors related to HIV knowledge and stigma\. The knowledge level of respondents on HIV was 74\.2%\. Stigma was highly prevalent in the form of fear of casual transmission \(79\.8%\), moral judgment \(71\.1%\), personal stigma \(72\.2%\), and perceived community stigma \(71\.8%\)\. The findings demonstrated that a high level of relevant knowledge regarding HIV was consistently associated with lower stigma levels in four dimensions, and that seven variables—, namely, gender, ethnicity, grade, only\-child or not, sexual orientation, awareness of the HIV/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome epidemic, and self\-esteem—, played different roles in affecting various dimensions of HIV stigma\. The level of HIV knowledge was low whereas HIV\-associated stigma was high among college students in southwest China\. Addressing HIV in colleges should incorporate efforts for reducing stigma associated with HIV\. For effective infectious disease emergency management in academic settings, this study underscores the necessity of integrating stigma\-reduction strategies into institutional preparedness plans\. Addressing these barriers is essential for optimizing risk communication, intervention uptake, and response efficacy during public health emergencies\.

## [O&\#x27;ZBEK TILI MORFOANALIZATORIDA FE&\#x27;L BO&\#x27;LMAGAN SO&\#x27;ZLAR\+FE&\#x27;L TARKIBLI QO&\#x27;SHMA FE&\#x27;LLAR VA SO&\#x27;Z BIRIKMALARINI FARQLASH MODELI](../publications/c350099258b5ca2061d3.md)

Nurova Feruza Kamolovna

Annotatsiya\. Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tili morfoanalizatorida fe’l bo‘lmagan so‘z \+ fe’l tarkibli qo‘shma fe’llar hamda erkin so‘z birikmalarini avtomatik farqlash masalasi tadqiq etilgan\. Qo‘shma fe’l va so‘z birikmalarini farqlash uchun leksik, morfologik, sintaktik va semantik mezonlarga asoslangan lingvistik\-kompyuter modeli taklif etilgan\. Model leksik tekshiruv, qoidaviy filtrlar hamda statistik/mashinali o‘qitish modulini o‘z ichiga oladi\. Tadqiqotda COMPOUND\_VERB, NOUN\+VERB\_PHRASE va UNSURE teglari asosida annotatsiya va avtomatik tasniflash mexanizmi ishlab chiqilgan\. Mazkur modelni o‘zbek tili morfoanalizatoriga integratsiya qilish orqali qo‘shma fe’llar va erkin so‘z birikmalarini aniqroq ajratish hamda morfologik tahlil sifatini oshirish imkoniyati ko‘rsatilgan\. Kalit so‘zlar: o‘zbek tili, morfoanalizator, qo‘shma fe’l, so‘z birikmasi, fe’l, morfologik tahlil, tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, mashinali o‘qitish, lingvistik model, avtomatik tasniflash, teg, COMPOUND\_VERB\. Аннотация\. В статье исследуется проблема автоматического различения сложных глаголов, образованных по модели «не\-глагольное слово \+ глагол», и свободных словосочетаний в морфологическом анализаторе узбекского языка\. Обосновывается, что формальное сходство данных конструкций создает определенные трудности при морфологическом анализе и обработке естественного языка\. Для их дифференциации предлагается лингвистико\-компьютерная модель, основанная на лексических, морфологических, синтаксических и семантических признаках\. Модель включает лексическую проверку, систему правил и статистический/машинно\-обучаемый модуль\. Разработан механизм аннотирования и автоматической классификации на основе тегов COMPOUND\_VERB, NOUN\+VERB\_PHRASE и UNSURE\. Показана возможность интеграции предложенной модели в морфологический анализатор узбекского языка для более точного различения сложных глаголов и свободных словосочетаний, а также повышения качества морфологического анализа\. Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, морфологический анализатор, сложный глагол, словосочетание, глагол, морфологический анализ, обработка естественного языка, машинное обучение, лингвистическая модель, автоматическая классификация, тегирование, COMPOUND\_VERB\. Abstract\. This article examines the problem of automatically distinguishing compound verbs formed according to the “non\-verb word \+ verb” pattern from free word combinations in an Uzbek morphological analyzer\. It is shown that the formal similarity of these constructions creates difficulties in morphological analysis and natural language processing\. A linguistic\-computational model based on lexical, morphological, syntactic, and semantic features is proposed to differentiate the two types of constructions\. The model incorporates lexical verification, rule\-based filters, and a statistical/machine\-learning module\. An annotation and automatic classification mechanism based on the tags COMPOUND\_VERB, NOUN\+VERB\_PHRASE, and UNSURE is developed\. The study demonstrates that integrating the proposed model into an Uzbek morphological analyzer can improve the automatic distinction between compound verbs and free word combinations and enhance the accuracy of morphological analysis\. Keywords: Uzbek language, morphological analyzer, compound verb, word combination, verb, morphological analysis, natural language processing, machine learning, linguistic model, automatic classification, tagging, COMPOUND\_VERB\.

## [A Web Engineering Approach to AI\-Enabled Japanese Tutoring via Instructional Design Pattern Mining](../publications/c361649fddf88fa1222b.md)

Xiaomei Gai; Yanjia Tian

Despite the proliferation of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-enabled web applications for Japanese language learning, existing platforms suffer from three critical challenges: insufficient integration of AI capabilities with pedagogical design, limited scenario adaptability across proficiency levels, and suboptimal lightweight deployment on the browser side\. To address these gaps and explore instructional design patterns tailored to diverse Japanese learning needs, this study focuses on web application technology implementation and interaction design as the core analytical dimensions\. Three typical AI\-enabled Japanese tutoring web applications were selected as research objects, and 192 Japanese learners participated in the empirical research\. Quantitative data were obtained through technical disassembly, questionnaire surveys, and web\-based behavior tracking; learning effects were verified by comparative experiments, and the weight of instructional design elements was determined via the analytic hierarchy process, finally extracting core instructional design modes suitable for the mainstream Japanese learning stages from beginner to upper\-intermediate \(Japanese\-Language Proficiency Test \[JLPT\] N5–N2\), with preliminary applicability discussion for the advanced stage \(N1 and above\)\. The results show that web\-based lightweight AI technology deployment and real\-time AI interactive feedback design are the core elements, with a combined weight of over 40%\. There is a significant positive correlation between web\-based AI technology implementation and user satisfaction, with the highest implementation effect and user acceptance in listening, speaking, and grammar modules\. Compared with traditional Japanese web learning platforms, AI\-enabled instructional design can improve learners’ listening and speaking abilities by 58\.0%\(M=58\.0,SD=4\.2,95% CI \[56\.4, 59\.6\], Cohen’s d=1\.82, large effect\), grammar analysis abilities by 46\.5% \(M=46\.5,SD=5\.1,95%CI \[44\.8, 48\.2\], Cohen’s d=1\.45, large effect\), and enhance learning sustainability by 85\.7% \(M=85\.7,SD=6\.3,95%CI\[83\.5,87\.9\], Cohen’s d=2\.01, large effect\), based on N5–N2 learner data with robust statistical power\. Three core instructional design modes were identified, adapted to zero\-based\-N4 fragmented learning, N3–N2 systematic learning, and N1\+ immersive learning, respectively\. This study clarifies the core elements and optimization direction of such applications, providing standardized and practical theoretical references and paths for their design, development, and teaching practice\.

## [From smart sensing to adaptive remediation: artificial intelligence and Internet of Things for persistent organic pollutants](../publications/c36454d93b97471881d6.md)

Khaled Chawraba; Abrar Hussain; Obaid A\. Alharbi; Amal Abdelhaleem

Persistent organic pollutants \(POPs\) remain a major environmental challenge because of their persistence, long\-range transport, bioaccumulation, and resistance to degradation\. Conventional monitoring and remediation systems provide reliable analytical performance but are largely fragmented, laboratory dependent, and unable to deliver the continuous, predictive, and adaptive management required for complex, dynamic contamination scenarios\. Recent literature reports substantial advances in biosensors, Internet of Things \(IoT\)\-enabled sensing, machine learning \(ML\), and artificial intelligence \(AI\) for pollutant detection, forecasting, source identification, and remediation optimization\. However, these developments often operate separately, with limited coordination between environmental sensing, data analytics, treatment processes, and decision\-making\. The literature further highlights persistent barriers to field deployment, including limited and geographically heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent sensor performance and calibration, restricted model transferability, insufficient independent validation, uncertainty in AI predictions, and the lack of mature regulatory frameworks for AI\-assisted environmental assessment\. From our perspective, the next advance in POP management should move beyond isolated AI applications toward integrated, closed\-loop AI\-IoT architectures that continuously connect sensing, prediction, remediation, and feedback control\. Such systems could transform POP management from reactive assessment to proactive and adaptive environmental governance\. Future progress will depend on standardized, Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable \(FAIR\) environmental datasets, explainable and uncertainty\-aware AI, robust field validation, and interoperable sensing infrastructures\.

## [A Dataset for AI Literacy in Secondary Schools in Tanzania:](../publications/c36ebf9d8515e2a12a6b.md)

This dataset contains survey responses collected from 273 teachers in public secondary schools across Tanzania to assess different dimensions of teachers’ AI literacy and preparedness for the use of Artificial Intelligence in education\. The dataset captures teachers’ demographic characteristics, including gender, age, teaching experience, school location, familiarity with AI concepts, and frequency of digital technology use in teaching\. It also includes structured Likert\-scale responses measuring three key constructs: AI Knowledge \(KN\), AI Awareness \(AW\), and AI Tool Proficiency \(AI\)\. Each construct was measured using multiple reflective items on a five\-point scale ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree\. The dataset therefore provides a valuable empirical resource for examining teachers’ AI literacy and their capacity to engage with AI technologies in secondary education\.

## [Development and Evaluation of Herbal Cosmeceutical Face Mask Containing Extracts of Amla, Neem and Turmeric](../publications/c37118187351272cfb65.md)

Shreyash Salpure; Mansi Nikam; Suresh Waghamare

Background\- There is growing demand for safe, effective cosmeceutical products that combine cosmetic and therapeutic benefits while minimizing the risks associated with synthetic ingredients\. This study aimed to formulate and evaluate a semisolid polyherbal face mask containing extracts of neem \(Azadirachta indica\), amla \(Phyllanthus emblica\), and turmeric \(Curcuma longa\), together with natural additives \(multani mitti, rice powder, and chandan powder\), for potential anti\-acne, antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory, cleansing, and skin\-rejuvenating effects\. Methods:\-Neem leaves, amla fruits, and turmeric rhizomes were extracted by maceration \(hydro\-alcoholic or PEG systems\) and concentrated under controlled temperature\. A gel base was prepared with polyvinyl alcohol; the herbal extracts were incorporated along with glycerin, polyethylene glycol, rose water, benzoic acid, and the powdered natural ingredients\. The final formulation \(100 g\) was evaluated for organoleptic properties, pH, viscosity \(Brookfield viscometer\), spreadability \(glass\-slide method\), washability, homogeneity, consistency, irritancy \(preliminary skin test\), and short\-term physical stability \(room temperature and 40 ± 2 °C for 1 month\)\. Results:\-The mask was a homogeneous, pale yellowish\-brown semisolid with a pleasant herbal odour, smooth texture, and no grittiness or phase separation\. Mean pH was 6\.1 \(near the skin\-compatible range\), viscosity approximately 28 867 cP, and average spreadability 8\.87 g·cm/s\. It was easily washable, left no sticky residue, and produced no visible irritation \(redness, itching, or swelling\)\. Physical parameters remained stable over one month with only a minor pH shift \(6\.1 → 6\.0\)\. Conclusion:\-The developed polyherbal face mask demonstrated acceptable physicochemical, organoleptic, and preliminary safety characteristics, supporting its potential as a stable, skin\-compatible herbal cosmeceutical for cleansing, oil control, and supportive anti\-acne use\. Keywords: Polyherbal face mask, cosmeceuticals, Neem extract, Amla extract, Turmeric extract, Multani mitti, Antioxidant activity\.

## [The Effect of GeoGebra Supported Teaching of Fractions on Success, Permanence and Students’ Views](../publications/c3727d8afe14c36554d7.md)

Murat Fidan; Ruhşen ALDEMİR ENGİN

The study was designed to examine the effect of using GeoGebra on student success and permanence in fractions and to evaluate students&\#x27; views about teaching methods\.
