The lessons were conducted with GeoGebra supported instruction in the experimental group and with the current method in the control group\. Achievement test was used as data collection tool\. In order to determine the students&\#x27; views, three\-question semi\-structured interview forms were created\. Quantitative data were analyzed using repeated\-measures analysis of variance and analysis of covariance, while qualitative data were examined through descriptive and content analyses\. As a result of the study, success scores of all students increased statistically significantly from pre\-test to post\-test\. Additionally, a difference in permanence was found in favor of the experimental group\. When the student views were analyzed, it was determined that learning the subject well in both methods was the biggest advantage\. Students in the control group stated that solving few questions was a disadvantage\. In addition, students in both groups suggested technology\-assisted teaching for a good understanding of the subject\. ## [From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies](../publications/c37588baf22055e60f5b.md)

Yubing Zhou; Yunxiao Ge; Kangdong Liu; Hui Liu; Zigang Dong

Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer\-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high\-risk human papillomavirus \(HPV\) infection as the primary etiological factor\. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high\-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development\. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions\. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis\. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors \(e\.g\., p16\) and signaling pathways \(PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β\-catenin\) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies\. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy\. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single\-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics\. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia \(CIN\), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing\. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer\.

## [Subtype\-Specific Efficacy of Adrenoceptor Agonists in Inhibiting Lens\-Induced Myopia in Chicks](../publications/c3842241405eafc789b2.md)

Mezbah Uddin; Fengjuan Yu; Rachel Ka Man Chun; Bing Zuo; King Kit Li; Chi Ho To; Dennis Y\. Tse

PURPOSE: Alpha\-adrenergic receptors \(ARs\) may potentially play a critical role in controlling myopia, with subtype\-specific signalling pathways mediating distinct effects\. This study systematically investigated the efficacy of three subtype\-specific pharmacological agents in myopia control and dose\-response relationships in lens\-induced myopia \(LIM\) chick models\. METHODS: White Leghorn chicks were randomised to a phosphate\-buffered saline \(PBS\) control group or treated groups receiving metaraminol \(α1\-AR agonist\), lofexidine \(α2\-AR agonist\) or cirazoline \(a dual α1‑AR agonist and α2‑AR antagonist\) at low \(3 nmol\), medium \(30 nmol\) or high \(300 nmol\) doses\. A \-10 D single\-vision lens was fitted to the right eye for 7 days to induce myopia, with intravitreal injections administered at baseline and on days 2, 4 and 6\. Natural ocular recovery was allowed for another 7 days\. Interocular differences \(IOD\) in spherical equivalent refraction \(SER\) and ocular biometrics were compared\. RESULTS: After 7 days of lens wear, all drug groups exhibited lower myopia progression than the control group\. Lofexidine showed potent and consistent myopia\-inhibiting effects\. The IOD in SER, vitreous chamber depth \(VCD\) and axial length \(AL\) were significantly reduced at three doses compared with PBS control \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Metaraminol and cirazoline exhibited significant efficacy mainly at medium and high doses\. All three α\-AR modulators alleviated choroidal thinning at both 30 and 300 nmol doses\. During recovery, all treatment groups trended toward emmetropia, without significant differences from the PBS group\. CONCLUSIONS: This first head\-to\-head in vivo comparison of three subtypes of α\-AR modulators in the chick LIM model demonstrates the potent myopia\-suppressive effects of α2\-AR agonist lofexidine at low dose\. α1\-AR agonist metaraminol required a distinct threshold dose to achieve efficacy and blockade of α2\-AR with cirazoline may counteract anti\-myopic protection\. These findings provide crucial subtype\-specific preclinical insights for the rational development of future drugs for myopia\.

## [Formation of Twisted Copper Phosphide on Cu\(111\) Surface Predicted by Machine Learning Simulations](../publications/c38bccddaadba00f0b43.md)

Wenzhen Dou; Tianchao Niu; Liang Ma; Feng Ding; Xinran Wang

ABSTRACT The fundamental interactions at surfaces and interfaces dictate the thermodynamic and kinetic pathways in the epitaxial growth of two‐dimensional \(2D\) materials\. The atomic‐scale evolution of phosphorus \(P\) on Cu\(111\) serves as a representative example of interfacial complexity, where dynamic reconstructions and competing chemical interactions obscure the underlying growth mechanisms\. In this study, we combine a rigorously trained Cu–P machine learning force field with atomically resolved scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the reaction of P on Cu\(111\) at atomic scale\. Our results demonstrate that phosphorene is neither thermodynamically favorable nor kinetically accessible on Cu\(111\)\. Instead, strong Cu‐P bonding drives the substitutional incorporation of P into the topmost Cu layer, forming a twisted copper phosphide \(Cu 2 P\) surface alloy – a phase that thermodynamically competes phosphorene over the experimentally relevant coverage regime\. Formation of this Cu 2 P layer generates interfacial strain that organizes into a straight reconstruction network and transforms into spiral configurations upon annealing\. With increasing P coverage, three‐dimensional \(3D\) P islands, rather than flat phosphorene, are formed on Cu 2 P surface\. These findings resolve a long‐standing controversy regarding P growth on Cu\(111\) and highlight the crucial role of interfacial interaction between the precursor and the substrate in 2D material growth\.

## [Biochemical Basis of Alcohol Metabolism on Human Liver and Alimentary Canal\- A Descriptive Study](../publications/c3b1f6e43ad0cfba682a.md)

Dhanya Shree B\.; Nafiya Taskeen M\.; V Santhanalakshmi\.; Renni Jovitta A\.; D\. P\. Sivasakti Balan; R\. J\. Thaumamaswamy

Alcohol metabolism is a complex biochemical process that occurs primarily in the liver and has significant effects on various organs, particularly the central nervous system\. This study aims to develop a comprehensive understanding of the biochemical and physiological mechanisms involved in ethanol metabolism and its effects on human health\. Following absorption into the bloodstream, ethanol is metabolized mainly in the liver through the action of alcohol dehydrogenase \(ADH\), which converts ethanol into acetaldehyde, and aldehyde dehydrogenase \(ALDH\), which further converts acetaldehyde into acetate\. Acetaldehyde is a toxic intermediate that can contribute to cellular damage, while alcohol metabolism may also promote oxidative stress, inflammation, and disruption of normal cellular functions\. Repeated and excessive alcohol consumption can lead to liver disorders, including fatty liver disease, alcoholic hepatitis, and cirrhosis\. In addition, alcohol affects the central nervous system by altering neurotransmitter activity, particularly gamma\-aminobutyric acid \(GABA\) and glutamate, thereby influencing memory, learning, judgment, coordination, and decision\-making\. Continued alcohol consumption may also contribute to the development of tolerance and dependence\. This research focuses on ethanol absorption and metabolism, the functions of ADH and ALDH enzymes, the effects of acetaldehyde and oxidative stress, and the consequences of alcohol consumption on liver cells and brain function\. Overall, the study highlights the importance of understanding the biochemical pathways of alcohol metabolism to explain alcohol\-related tissue damage and its broader physiological effects on the human body\.

## [A multi\-channel ratio\-type self\-powered photoelectrochemical sensor for simultaneous detection of carbendazim and imidacloprid](../publications/c3b8250c30a6f34e2ed3.md)

Yunyi Liang; Gang Xiang; Liu Fengping; Qing Huang; 张翠忠; Yingying Huang; Jing Sun; Jinyun Peng

Herein, we report a multi\-channel ratiometric self\-powered photoelectrochemical \(SP\-PEC\) sensor for the simultaneous detection of two common pesticides, carbendazim \(Cbd\) and imidacloprid \(Imp\)\. A conjugated microporous polymer\-grafted reduced graphene oxide \(CMP\-rGO\) composite was employed as the photoanode material, while an electrodeposited CuSCN/indium tin oxide \(ITO\) layer served as the photocathode\. Using a spatially resolved design strategy, the photoanode and photocathode components were integrated onto a single ITO electrode, which was patterned into three photoanode regions and one photocathode region\. Cbd and Imp aptamers were selectively immobilized on two of the photoanode regions, with the third acting as an internal reference\. Instead of a conventional electrochemical workstation, a multimeter was adopted as the readout device, allowing for simultaneous detection of the two analytes via ratiometric signal readouts between the reference and working photoanodes\. The resulting multi\-channel SP\-PEC sensor exhibited excellent selectivity and stability\. Under optimal conditions, the sensor achieved linear responses over the range of 0\.001–1000 ng/mL for both pesticides, with detection limits \(LOD\) of 0\.000208 ng/mL for Cbd and 0\.000341 ng/mL, respectively\. The practical applicability of the sensor was further validated by its successful use in the simultaneous determination of Cbd and Imp in real lettuce and cucumber samples\.

## [Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving](../publications/c3bbba48a994d3735a71.md)

Jack Li; Sophia Li

Verifier\-guided self\-repair conditions a model on feedback from failed attempts before it tries again, without weight updates\. Yet two findings in prior work are in tension: verifier feedback can improve repair of failures, but self\-repair itself can provide little\-to\-no advantage over independent resampling\. We reconcile these findings in Lean theorem proving through controlled one\-step experiments that hold the preceding failure fixed while varying whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error corresponds to that failure, and the retry instruction\. We test frozen Qwen3\.6\-27B, a general\-purpose model, and DeepSeek\-Prover\-V2\-7B, a specialized prover, on difficult MiniF2F problems\. We find two opposing effects\. Showing the model its failed predecessor reduces success and sharply increases copying of it, while on Qwen adding that attempt&\#x27;s compiler error recovers the loss, to the level of the diagnostic alone\. Replacing the predecessor with another theorem&\#x27;s failed proof largely removes the degradation on both models; on Qwen, replacing the diagnostic with another problem&\#x27;s error substantially reduces the recovery\. Without the failed proof, correct diagnostics show no resolved advantage over wrong\-diagnostic controls on either model\. The failed\-proof penalty persists with and without the retry instruction, whereas Qwen&\#x27;s diagnostic recovery is weaker without it\. In 11\-problem sequential experiments through 64 attempts, Qwen retains a correct\-diagnostic benefit within failed\-proof histories, while DeepSeek\-Prover shows no resolved recovery\. However, no tested one\-step feedback condition establishes an advantage over instruction\-only resampling, nor does 64\-attempt sequential repair with failed proofs and correct diagnostics at equal token budgets\. Verifier feedback can thus improve repair without overcoming the performance loss from conditioning on a failed attempt\.

## [Atrial cardiomyopathy: from knowledge gaps to clinical impact](../publications/c3d504b85ec86c716e8b.md)

Nick L\. van Vreeswijk; Zarina Habibi; Sander van Doorn; Joris R\. de Groot; Monika Stoll; Daniël A\. Pijnappels; Jordi Heijman; Robert G Tieleman; Ron Pisters; Martin E W Hemels; Fleur V\.Y\. Tjong; Ulrich Schotten; Michiel Rienstra; Geert‐Jan Geersing; Jelle C L Himmelreich

BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy \(AtCM\) is increasingly recognised as an underlying atrial substrate contributing to atrial fibrillation \(AF\), heart failure \(HF\), and cardio\-embolic stroke\. However, diagnostic criteria, disease thresholds, and targeted treatment strategies remain poorly defined\. OBJECTIVE: To describe the rationale, structure, and translational strategy of the EmbRACE \(Electro\-Molecular Basis and the theRapeutic management of Atrial Cardiomyopathy, fibrillation and associated outcomEs\) network, a national consortium established to address key knowledge gaps in AtCM\. METHODS: EmbRACE integrates mechanistic research, computational modelling, clinical trials, and implementation science within seven interconnected work packages\. Human atrial tissue biobanking and deep phenotyping \(WP1\) enable molecular profiling of candidate pathways \(WP2\), which are validated in experimental models \(WP3\)\. Computational modelling and artificial intelligence \(WP4\) integrate multimodal clinical and biological data to derive composite AtCM phenotypes and severity frameworks\. Substrate\-targeting clinical trials evaluate AF ablation \(RACE X; WP5\), weight reduction using GLP‑1 agonists \(DUTCH\-WAIST; WP6\), and optimised rate control using calcium channel antagonists \(SMART\-VERAPAF; WP6\)\. Implementation science \(WP7\) focuses on guideline integration, decision\-support tools, and governance of AI\-based risk models\. EmbRACE establishes a translational pipeline from mechanistic discovery to clinical application\. By integrating tissue\-level insights with multimodal risk modelling and interventional trials, the consortium aims to define clinically meaningful AtCM thresholds, to validate indirect markers, and to determine whether targeted treatment modifies disease progression and clinical outcomes\. CONCLUSION: EmbRACE provides a multidisciplinary framework to transform AtCM from a theoretical construct into a clinically actionable entity, enabling earlier detection, improved risk stratification, and AtCM\-directed therapy in cardiovascular prevention\.

Daglous Masveta; Batsirai Chivhanga

This study investigates the eLearning platforms which primary school learners in Zimbabwe use\. A qualitative research approach using interpretive philosophy interviewed four ICT facilitators in government and private primary schools located in Chinhoyi within Mashonaland West Province\. Through its inductive research approach, the study concentrated on event contexts which made it workable with minimal data points and static measuring period\. Educational videos together with visual aids and interactive quizzes receive popularity with students because these materials offer direct and tangible media formats for lesson instruction\. WhatsApp functions as the main platform for educational technology because it provides users with cost\-effectiveness combined with simple usage and friendly interface\. The main obstacles to successful e\-learning include inadequate internet connections together with insufficient knowledge about using platforms Ruzivo and the Zimbabwe e\-learning passport\. The study advises the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education \(MoPSE\) to develop and participate in training programs that will enable teachers to embrace e\-learning platforms efficiently\.

## [The association between parental physical activity and the parent–child relationship in early childhood: the serial mediating roles of emotion regulation and subjective wellbeing](../publications/c3eb4544b0b426dd6481.md)

Xiaogang Zhang; Keyong Wang; Junmin Zhang; Shuiyou Hu; Jianqiang Tian

Objective The parent–child relationship in early childhood is closely linked to children&\#x27;s physical and psychological development\. Although parental physical activity has been associated with favorable psychological outcomes, little is known about how it relates to the parent–child relationship or about the potential roles of emotion regulation and subjective wellbeing\. Accordingly, this study used structural equation modeling to examine the hypothesized direct and indirect associations among these variables\. Methods A cross\-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 719 parents recruited through convenience and snowball sampling in six Chinese cities, including Chengdu, Suining, Meishan, Lanzhou, Xianyang, and Xi&\#x27;an\. All study variables were assessed by the same parent using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the Cognitive Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, the Brief Subjective Wellbeing Scale for Chinese Citizens, and the Child\-Parent Relationship Scale\. Data were analyzed using covariance\-based structural equation modeling in AMOS 23\.0\. Complementary PROCESS Model 6 analyses based on observed composite scores were conducted in SPSS 29\.0\. Results \(1\) Parental physical activity was positively associated with the parent–child relationship, and the direct path between the two variables was statistically significant \(β = 0\.143, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. \(2\) The completely standardized indirect estimate through emotion regulation was 0\.041 \(95% CI \[0\.020, 0\.065\]\), while the estimate through subjective wellbeing was 0\.050 \(95% CI \[0\.030, 0\.074\]\)\. The serial indirect estimate was 0\.015 \(95% CI \[0\.008, 0\.023\]\)\. Conclusion Higher levels of parental physical activity were associated with higher emotion regulation scores, greater subjective wellbeing, and a more positive parent–child relationship\.

## [Experimental Validation of a Low\-Cost Data Acquisition System and Comparative Dynamic Assessment of ICE and EV Vehicles Using CarSim](../publications/c3ebf61d7e243b1d1ac7.md)

Muhammad Ridzwan Kamaruddin; Syabillah Sulaiman; Norhasikin Ismail; Norrizam Jaat; Muhamad Asri Azizul

This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the dynamic performance of Internal Combustion Engine \(ICE\) and Electric Vehicle \(EV\) configurations through experimental and simulation methods\. The study is divided into two \(2\) core components\. The first focuses on validating a developed data acquisition \(DAQ\) system by comparing experimental results of vehicle dynamics characteristics\. The results are through validation with CarSim software\. The results demonstrate a strong correlation for sprung mass and pitch rate responses, with low average relative errors of 0\.0828 at 10 km/h, 0\.0720 at 20 km/h, and 0\.0663 at 30 km/h\. It confirmed that the DAQ system that was developed performed with high accuracy and fidelity\. The second core component involves a comparative dynamic analysis of ICE and EV vehicles under ISO 8727 standard test at specific speed level\. The results demonstrated that the EV model consistently exhibits improved damping characteristics, lateral acceleration symmetry, and smoother directional transitions\. In contrast, the ICE vehicle displays higher vertical and lateral acceleration peaks, suggesting more aggressive suspension dynamics and possibility to cause discomfort to the passenger\. These findings underscore the advantages of EV architectures in delivering enhanced ride comfort, handling stability, and responsiveness\. The study not only focuses on validation of DAQ system and simulation framework but also provides valuable insights for the development of advanced vehicle control strategies in future mobility solutions in terms of stability and ride comfort varying with changes of the external disturbance\.

## [SymbolFusion uses relation constraints in neurosymbolic graph learning to model literary structure and emotion trajectories](../publications/c3fd46a6cd5a827bd162.md)

Yuhang Du

Abstract Literary texts contain recurring imagery, typed symbolic relations, and long\-range emotion shifts that sequence models do not represent explicitly\. This paper presents SymbolFusion, a relation\-constrained neuro\-symbolic graph framework that predicts imagery and symbolic candidates from raw text, validates three literary relation types through an auditable node\-relation compatibility function, and propagates emotion only across valid graph paths\. No gold symbolic or affective annotation is supplied during validation or testing\. The 3,120\-passage corpus is divided by literary work into 2,184 training, 468 validation, and 468 test passages, with an additional author\-disjoint evaluation\. Across ten seeds, SymbolFusion obtains 91\.3% symbolic graph agreement, an emotion consistency score of 0\.880, a symbolic\-emotion alignment score of 0\.820, and a transition\-point F1 of 0\.842\. Against the strongest constraint\-based baseline, the SGA gain is 2\.2% points \(95% bootstrap CI 1\.5–2\.9; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Controlled comparisons among unconstrained attention, soft penalties, hard masks, and permuted relation types isolate the effect of literary compatibility rules\. Standard metrics, repeated latency measurements, expert\-rating correlations, reproducibility settings, and error analysis delimit the method as an inspectable computational aid rather than a replacement for human literary interpretation\.

## [Predictive Machine Learning Models for Process Parameters in Additively Manufactured CoCrMo Alloys for Dental Applications](../publications/c417e867bd710d7a9cf9.md)

Carlos Peaceful Kakuwa; Martin Ruthandi Maina; Joshua Ngoret; Tshenolo Phinah Leso

Dental disease prevalence has increased the demand for effective dental implants\. Laser Engineered Net Shaping \(LENS\) can produce complex geometries through controlled process parameters\. Machine learning \(ML\), on the other hand, enables data driven parametric prediction in Additive Manufacturing \(AM\), though reliability depends on data quality\. This study explores a framework for integration of AM and Latin Hypercube Sampling \(LHS\) based data synthesis with ML trained on 108 synthetic samples to enhance parametric prediction and surface quality control\. Model validation presented robust performance, with ANN achieving R2 values of 0\.981 for surface roughness \(governing osseointegration\), 0\.955 for microhardness \(governing wear resistance\), and 0\.973 for porosity \(governing structural integrity\), while the best RF prediction performance achieved an R2 of 0\.967 for surface roughness, with both models yielding &lt;1\.5% prediction error for microhardness\. ## [Digital Protection and Innovation of Intangible Cultural Heritage Skills](../publications/c419ec45337a14ed88f7.md)

Xiaoyang Hu

Aiming at the problems of non\-genetic fault and tacit knowledge loss, this study combines knowledge graph, computer vision and immersive media technology to construct a digital protection framework for intangible heritage\. The framework transforms implicit experience into a structured digital model through multi\-modal data acquisition; At the same time, a &quot;virtual master&quot; system was built to realize the interactive teaching of skills; In addition, the Virtual Reality \(VR\) scene restoration and live broadcast linkage strategy is adopted to promote the integration of protection and communication\. The empirical results show that the efficiency of VR knowledge transfer reached 91\.2%; The results show that the framework can effectively support the activation of intangible cultural heritage \(ICH\); Industrial\-grade Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) technology can accurately decode and reproduce empirical craftsmanship\.

## [Advancing Objective Motor Severity Assessment in Cerebellar Ataxias Using Sensors and Machine Learning](../publications/c41d54bb4704fc215983.md)

Juhyeon Lee

Cerebellar ataxias are a heterogeneous group of neurological disorders characterized by impaired coordination and balance due to dysfunction of the cerebellum and its associated pathways\. As most ataxias are progressive, frequent and objective assessment of motor severity is essential for monitoring disease progression and evaluating therapeutic interventions\. The lack of disease\-modifying treatments further underscores the need for sensitive and frequent assessment to support clinical trials\. However, current assessments rely on clinician observation–based rating scales, which limit the frequency, sensitivity, and objectivity of disease severity evaluation\. To address these limitations, various sensors, including wearable inertial sensors and cameras, have been suggested as promising tools for continuous and objective assessment of motor impairments\. This dissertation develops analytic pipelines and machine learning approaches to estimate ataxia severity from inertial sensor and video data collected during upper\- and lower\-limb motor tasks\. The first part presents an analytic pipeline to estimate motor severity using ankle\-worn inertial sensors during a gait task\. By analyzing sub\-second movement profiles and extracting submovement features, supervised learning models are trained to estimate clinician\-rated severity\. The pipeline is further extended to estimate ataxia severity in children with Ataxia\-Telangiectasia while minimizing the effects of age\-dependent immature motor characteristics\. The second part introduces a supervised contrastive learning framework for estimating ataxia severity using wrist\-worn inertial sensors during upper\-limb tasks\. By leveraging pairwise relationships between samples, this approach captures relative differences in motor impairment and reduces reliance on subjective clinical scores, improving robustness to label noise\. The final part extends this framework to simultaneously acquired inertial sensor and video data during upper\-limb motor tasks\. Digital measures of ataxia severity are derived independently from each modality and compared to evaluate cross\-modality agreement\. Both modalities show strong associations with clinician\-rated severity, and their estimates are highly concordant, indicating they capture a consistent representation of motor impairment\. Overall, this dissertation establishes a progression from feature\-based modeling to contrastive learning and cross\-modal evaluation, providing a framework for developing and validating digital measures of ataxia\. These results support the use of wearable sensors and video as objective, scalable tools for monitoring disease severity in clinical and real\-world settings\.

## [Serial fibrosis\-4 variability and longitudinal patterns are associated with incident heart failure in type 2 diabetes: a 24\-month landmark cohort study](../publications/c42093f469bbd43578eb.md)

Attila Csaba Nagy; Amr Sayed Ghanem; Battamir Ulambayar; Marianna Móré; Mariann Harangi

Background The prognostic relevance of serial Fibrosis\-4 index \(FIB\-4\) changes for incident heart failure \(HF\) in type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) remains unclear\. We examined whether within\-person FIB\-4 variability and longitudinal patterns were associated with HF after explicit adjustment for chronological age\. Methods Routinely collected clinical data from 2000 to 2025 were analyzed using a 24\-month landmark design\. FIB\-4 measurements from months 0 to 18 defined the exposure, followed by a 6\-month lag before HF follow\-up\. Variability was calculated as the within\-person standard deviation of log 2 \-transformed FIB\-4\. Using a threshold of 2\.67, patients were classified as never high, improving from high, worsening to high, or persistently high\. Associations with incident HF were estimated using multivariable Cox regression\. Results Among 8,221 patients, 1,811 developed HF during 50,640 person\-years\. Greater FIB\-4 variability was associated with a higher HF hazard \(adjusted hazard ratio \[HR\], 1\.73; 95% confidence interval \[CI\], 1\.43–2\.09\)\. Compared with the never\-high pattern, persistent\-high FIB\-4 \(HR, 1\.73; 95% CI, 1\.35–2\.20\) and worsening to high \(HR, 1\.28; 95% CI, 1\.01–1\.62\) were associated with higher HF hazards, whereas improving from high was not \(HR, 0\.95; 95% CI, 0\.70–1\.28\)\. Adding serial FIB\-4 features resulted in a small, statistically uncertain improvement in temporal\-validation discrimination \(ΔC\-index, 0\.0069; 95% CI, −0\.0043 to 0\.0190\)\. Discussion Serial FIB\-4 variability and persistent elevation were associated with incident HF independently of chronological age\. These measures may characterize longitudinal multisystem cardiometabolic burden, but their incremental predictive value was limited\. External validation is required before clinical application\.

## [Eating behaviors in preschoolers with autism spectrum disorders: associations with developmental and behavioral features and parental mental health](../publications/c42694e352852348dc9d.md)

Esra Hoşoğlu; Ayhan Bi̇lgi̇ç; Ömer Faruk Akça; Mahmut Sami Tuzcu

Introduction Eating problems are highly prevalent in children with autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\)\. However, their profile during the preschool period—a critical window for establishing lifelong eating habits—remains poorly understood\. This study aimed to compare the eating behaviors of preschool children with ASD and typically developing \(TD\) peers and to identify associated developmental, behavioral, and parental factors during this formative stage\. Methods This case\-control study included 50 preschool children with ASD \(aged 2–6 years\) recruited from a child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient clinic and 43 age\-matched TD children recruited from family health centers\. ASD diagnoses were confirmed by child and adolescent psychiatrists according to DSM\-5 criteria\. Parents completed the Children’s Eating Behavior Questionnaire \(CEBQ\), the Aberrant Behavior Checklist \(ABC\), and the Brief Symptom Inventory \(BSI\)\. Child assessments included the Childhood Autism Rating Scale \(CARS\) and the Ankara Developmental Screening Inventory \(ADSI\)\. Group differences were examined using univariate analyses and multivariate analyses of covariance \(MANCOVA\)\. Within the ASD group, correlations and multivariable linear regressions examined associated factors\. Complete\-case sensitivity analyses were performed for variables with missing data\. Results No significant between\-group differences were observed across CEBQ subscales after adjustment for baseline differences \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. Within the ASD group, hyperactivity/noncompliance was positively correlated with satiety responsiveness in the primary analysis \(r s =0\.449, FDR\-adjusted p=0\.022\), but not after FDR correction in the complete\-case analysis \(r s =0\.431, adjusted p=0\.066\)\. Fine motor and cognitive\-language developmental levels showed nominal associations with specific eating behavior dimensions in multivariable regressions \(β=−0\.333 to 0\.404, p=0\.012–0\.043\), but none remained significant after FDR correction\. Complete\-case analyses yielded generally similar effect estimates, with no regression associations surviving FDR correction\. Conclusion Parent\-reported CEBQ dimensions did not differ significantly between preschool children with ASD and TD peers\. Within the ASD group, developmental and behavioral characteristics showed potential associations with specific eating behaviors; however, these findings did not consistently withstand multiple\-testing correction\. Given the cross\-sectional design and relatively small sample, the findings should be interpreted cautiously and require replication in larger longitudinal studies\.

## [The active self in autism: multisensory and sensorimotor foundations of bodily self\-representation](../publications/c428e43f6a60e60f9e1f.md)

Amir Jahanian Najafabadi; Alireza Rastegari

The active self, understood as the embodied sense of self arising from goal\-directed action and interaction with the environment, is supported by sensorimotor processes including multisensory integration and proprioception\. Atypical self\-representation in autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\) has been proposed to relate to differences in these processes\. To clarify this relationship, we conducted a systematic conceptual review of 37 empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2025 examining multisensory and bodily components of the active self in ASD\. The literature was synthesized across three themes: \(1\) multisensory integration, \(2\) self\-bias and self\-other differentiation, and \(3\) motor underpinnings of bodily awareness\. Across studies, autistic participants frequently showed differences in multisensory timing and weighting, including reduced or delayed susceptibility to some bodily ownership illusions and greater reliance on proprioceptive or immediate sensory information\. Evidence also indicated differences in the flexibility of peri\- and interpersonal space, self\-other differentiation, agency\-related processing, and motor planning and execution\. However, findings were not uniform across paradigms, developmental stages, or participant groups, with relatively preserved performance reported under some unimodal or low\-noise conditions\. Together, these findings support an association between multisensory and sensorimotor processing and several components of bodily self\-representation in autism, while substantial methodological and sample heterogeneity limits strong causal or clinical conclusions\. Future research should prioritize larger and more representative samples, longitudinal and multimethod designs, standardized experimental paradigms, and objective measures of embodiment to determine whether these mechanisms can ultimately inform individualized assessment and intervention\.Clinical trial number Not applicable\.

## [Effect of Glyceryl Trinitrate Enriched Cardioplegia on Patient Outcomes in Low Ejection Fraction Patients undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting](../publications/c42d70ee7af6c30add32.md)

Muhammad Rizwan Naeem; Chanda Naseem

Background: Coronary artery bypass graft surgery in patients with low left ventricular ejection fraction results in an increased risk for myocardial damage and hemodynamic instability after the procedure\. Cardioplegia formulation is one of the factors that can affect myocardial protection during heart surgery\. Addition of glyceryl trinitrate \(GTN\), which acts as a nitric oxide donor, to cardioplegia formulation may be beneficial for myocardial perfusion\. Objective: To compare early postoperative outcomes between patients receiving standard blood cardioplegia and those receiving GTN\-enriched blood cardioplegia during CABG\. Methods: In this quasi\-experimental study, 64 patients were involved in CABG and divided into two equal groups of 32 each\. While the control group was treated with conventional blood cardioplegia, the treatment group was provided GTN\-containing blood cardioplegia at 1 mg/L\. The indicators measured in this study included CK\-MB after surgery, ventilation time, inotropic support, ICU stay, and postoperative complications\. For statistical significance, the tests conducted by researchers were used, with p&lt;0\.05 being statistically significant\. Results: The levels of postoperative CK\-MB were lower in the GTN group compared to the control group, although the results were not statistically significant \(median 39\.0 vs\. 42\.5 U/L, p=0\.066\)\. However, the period of mechanical ventilation was significantly shorter in the GTN group \(median 5\.0 vs\. 6\.0 h, p&lt;0\.001\)\. No statistical difference was found in the overall inotropic score and ICU stay\. One case of acute kidney injury was observed in the control group while no patient experienced acute kidney injury in the GTN group\. Less patients underwent IABP and direct current cardioversion in the GTN group, even though the results were not statistically significant\. Conclusion: GTN\-enriched cardioplegia had a shorter postoperative period of mechanical ventilation\. Despite lower levels of CK\-MB postoperatively and fewer complications in the GTN\-enriched group, these differences did not reach statistical significance\. It is necessary to conduct more randomized studies in order to prove the efficacy and safety of the use of GTN\-enriched cardioplegia in patients with reduced LVEF\.

## [Registered Nurses&\#x27; Experiences of Clinical Decision‐Making: A Qualitative Descriptive Study to Inform Artificial Intelligence‐Assisted Decision Support in Nursing](../publications/c4344f3a043795160b8f.md)

Petra Suonnansalo; Henna Härkönen; Mika Alastalo; Wentao Zhou; Miia Marika Jansson

ABSTRACT Aim To describe registered nurses&\#x27; experiences of clinical decision‐making and identify needs that may inform future development of artificial‐intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing\. Design A qualitative descriptive study\. Methods Data were collected between 2022 and 2025 through 16 semi‐structured interviews with registered nurses working in inpatient wards at a Finnish university hospital\. The data were analysed using inductive content analysis\. Results Perceived challenges in clinical decision‐making were related to organisational issues, multiprofessional collaboration, nurse–patient interactions, professional factors and availability and trustworthiness of data\. The findings also identified support needs related to health information management, clinical workflows and quality of nursing care that may inform future artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support system development\. Conclusion Nurses experienced multifaceted challenges and needs in clinical decision‐making, shaped by organisational, professional, relational and information‐related factors\. Adoption of artificial intelligence‐assisted decision support systems may represent one potential approach to optimising clinical decision‐making, improving patient care quality and enhancing workflow efficiency\. Realising these opportunities requires coordinated efforts at individual, organisational and societal levels, including competence development, workflow redesign, strong data governance and a culture that fosters trust in technology\. Implications for the Profession and/or Patient Care The findings may inform the future development of artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing\. Reporting Method The Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research checklist was used when reporting the results\. Patient or Public Contribution Registered nurses participated in the study\. Impact What problem did the study address? This paper addresses existing gaps and unmet needs in nursing clinical decision‐making What were the main findings? The main findings highlight several key opportunities for artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing\. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The research may inform efforts to optimise health information management, streamline clinical workflows and improve the quality of nursing care\.

## [Capability evolution as a cyclical process: reframing the dynamic capabilities lifecycle](../publications/c4350fc85d7f16a86f42.md)

Ntandoyenkosi Sibindi

Purpose This paper aims to develop a process theory of capability evolution that explains how organisational capabilities persist, erode and renew over time\. It addresses limitations in capability lifecycle theory by reconceptualising capability evolution as a recursive process driven by capability–environment alignment and misalignment\. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops a conceptual, mechanism\-based process theory by synthesising dynamic capabilities theory, capability lifecycle theory and complementary perspectives on organisational learning, process theory and organisational microfoundations\. The framework identifies capability persistence, managerial recognition and capability reconfiguration as interconnected mechanisms underlying recurring capability evolution\. Findings The framework conceptualises capability evolution as a continuous, relational and recursive process\. Capability–environment alignment supports persistence, while environmental change can generate misalignment and erosion\. Managerial recognition of misalignment and subsequent capability reconfiguration enable renewed alignment\. Each cycle reshapes the conditions for subsequent organisational adaptation\. Research limitations/implications The paper is conceptual and does not empirically test the proposed framework\. Future research should examine the model through longitudinal and process\-oriented studies, develop measures of its core mechanisms, and investigate its applicability across different organisational and institutional contexts\. Practical implications The framework suggests that managers should treat capability renewal as a continuous process\. Regular assessment of capability–environment alignment, environmental scanning, organisational learning and capability reviews can help organisations recognise emerging capability gaps and support timely capability reconfiguration\. Social implications The framework highlights how organisational learning and capability renewal can support responsiveness to technological, institutional and stakeholder changes\. It provides a basis for future research examining how capability evolution influences organisational adaptation and broader societal outcomes\. Originality/value The paper extends capability lifecycle theory from a stage\-based description towards a mechanism\-based process explanation\. It identifies capability–environment alignment and misalignment as the generative mechanism linking persistence, erosion and renewal, while integrating managerial cognition, organisational attention and strategic decision\-making into a recursive model of capability evolution\.

## [Redesenhando e ressignificando a educação linguística em língua inglesa: uma análise crítica de um MOOC](../publications/c4359d7f0ed6533b862f.md)

Giselle Migueis de Oliveira; Souzana Mizan

As tecnologias digitais têm fomentado o redesenho e a ressignificação da educação linguística\. As ecologias digitais se tornam cada vez mais ubíquas nas práticas sociais contemporâneas e, por estarem atravessadas de vieses e significados, é necessário compreender como a educação linguística mediada por plataformas, em particular os MOOCs \(Cursos Online Abertos Massivos\), está configurando esse processo\. Esta pesquisa tem como objetivo refletir sobre o ensino por meio dos MOOCs, além de outras possibilidades formativas que podem ser construídas nesse contexto\. Para isso, o propósito é a análise crítica de um MOOC, criado para a educação linguística em inglês no ensino fundamental, em termos de eixos temáticos e fomento ao letramento crítico\. A abordagem teórico\-metodológica é qualitativa e interpretativista, fundamentada na Pedagogia dos Multiletramentos \(Cazden et al\., 2021\), partindo de seus valores: a multimodalidade, a colaboração, a criatividade, o engajamento, a inclusão, o agenciamento epistêmico e a voz \(Cope; Kalantzis, 2025\)\. A pesquisa é orientada pela filosofia bakhtiniana de linguagem \(Bakhtin, 2003; Volóchinov, 2017\), no que se refere à autoria como construção coletiva\. Busca\-se contribuir para a formação de cidadãos críticos e conscientes das relações de poder que permeiam a sociedade, a fim de vivenciarmos uma educação formativa\.

## [Ionospheric and Atmospheric Precursors to Earthquakes: A Critical Review of Multi\-Parametric Observations, Coupling Mechanisms, and Machine Learning Applications](../publications/c43c585770af423029f7.md)

Racheal Foluke Oloruntola; Oludare Olukayode Babalola; Ganiyu Akanji Olaniyi; George Atilade Àlàgbé; Hameed O\. Bakare; Adedamola Julius Agbelemoge

The search for reliable pre\-earthquake signals in the upper atmosphere has produced a large and heterogeneous body of literature over the past two decades, much of it organized around the Lithosphere\-Atmosphere\-Ionosphere Coupling \(LAIC\) hypothesis\. This narrative\-critical review synthesizes studies published between 2020 and 2026, identified through Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and journal\-archive searches and screened against stated eligibility and evidence\-appraisal criteria, on ionospheric and atmospheric precursors to large earthquakes, covering Global Navigation Satellite System \(GNSS\)\-derived Total Electron Content \(TEC\) anomalies, sub\-ionospheric Very Low Frequency \(VLF\) and High Frequency \(HF\) radio propagation disturbances, and thermal atmospheric signatures\. It further examines the proposed mechanical \(acoustic\-gravity wave\), geochemical \(radon\-driven\), and electromagnetic channels invoked to explain lithosphere\-to\-ionosphere energy transfer, and considers how solar and geomagnetic activity confound or mimic seismogenic signals\. Beyond summarizing individual case studies, this review evaluates the field&\#x27;s methodological foundations: the near\-universal reliance on retrospective, single\-event case studies; the absence of standardized anomaly definitions and false\-positive/false\-negative statistics; and the growing but still under\-validated use of deep machine learning for anomaly discrimination\. We find that pre\-seismic ionospheric perturbations are reported using several independent techniques, but the evidence is heterogeneous and rarely controlled, and causal attribution to seismogenic processes rather than coincidental space weather variability remains unresolved for the majority of reported cases\. The present evidence does not support operational earthquake forecasting; we recommend prospective, statistically rigorous, and physically constrained research designs\.

## [Design Documentation Canvas: A Lightweight Design Rationale Framework for Solo Designers](../publications/c43dc2df794433321984.md)

Adina Fayza Gayo; Hadziq Fabroyir

Background: Design systems have become standard infrastructure in digital product development, yet they often underdocument the rationale behind design decisions\. This gap is amplified in resource\-constrained startups, where solo designers manage multi\-brand, multiplatform products, increasing the risk of knowledge loss during handoffs and onboarding\. Objective: This study designs, implements, and evaluates the Design Documentation Canvas \(DDC\), a lightweight design rationale and traceability framework for solo designers in multi\-brand startup contexts\. Methods: A single\-case study was conducted at an Indonesian insurtech startup\. Data were collected through two focus group discussion \(FGD\) sessions involving nine participants, one individual interview, a six\-point Likert\-scale questionnaire \(n = 10\), and artifact analysis, with the researcher acting as a participant\-observer\. Results: The framework achieved 100% completeness across 17 qualifying design tickets, defined by substantively completed Description Panels \(FSE\-structured fields: Summary, Question/Issue, Final Decision, Evidence, and References\) and Before\-After Panels\. Questionnaire results showed a median and mode of 6 across all items and 100% agreement\-side responses, although these results should be interpreted with caution because of potential ceiling effects and social desirability bias\. Cronbach’s alpha was 0\.853\. AI\-assisted drafting also emerged during implementation as a means of reducing the perceived documentation articulation burden\. Conclusion: The DDC demonstrates operational feasibility and positive stakeholder reception within a single case, providing an adoptable documentation artifact for solo designers in Southeast Asian startup environments\. The findings remain bounded by the single\-case design and small sample and should not be interpreted as generalizable outcomes\.

## [Yellow in Color Naming and Matching: Lexical Concentration and Local Convergence in Delayed Matching](../publications/c443ed863b1c8d5d15e0.md)

Samo Kreft; Marko Kreft

ABSTRACT Yellow is an established color category despite being generated by a mixture of primaries on RGB displays\. We examined its lexical accessibility, representative‐color selections, and matching accuracy using two complementary tasks\. A web‐based survey asked participants to list 10 color terms and select their best representatives from a 64‐field RGB grid\. Analyses included English, German, Latvian, and Slovenian samples, comprising 396 participants\. Yellow was frequently listed and showed concentrated selections in all four samples, although red was similarly concentrated in some samples and had higher cognitive salience\. In a separate experiment, 32 participants matched 40 positions along a display‐generated color sequence, either after a 10‐s delay or while the target remained visible\. Spectroradiometric characterization confirmed strongly non‐uniform color spacing\. Expressing target–response differences in CIEDE2000 units showed that direct matching and delayed reproduction remained accurate around target where the red and green RGB channels were both maximal \[RGB \(1,1,0\); Target 26, yellow\], and a central tendency toward yellow was observed for neighboring targets\. Yellow therefore combined lexical accessibility and concentrated exemplar selection with accurate simultaneous matching, and a central tendency in delayed reproduction\.

## [Squeezing Reality Through a Binary Straw : A Systems\-Theory Critique of Bureaucratic Alignment and Epistemic Sabotage](../publications/c444aab89aa120cd9f5b.md)

David J\.W\. Gilmour

Modern institutional governance and artificial intelligence alignment protocols are currently deadlocked in a metaphysical delusion: the belief that complex realities can be safely regulated by optimizing the internal metrics of artificial, frozen data models\. This monograph provides a radical boundary critique of these architectures, exposing the structural, behavioral, and technical failures that inevitably occur when the un\-cropped universe exerts pressure on our perimeters\. Written from outside the traditional academic apparatus, this text introduces a formal syntax for mapping structural decay across three core phases: spatial/resolution blindness, the bureaucratic inversion of accountability \(where automated systems optimize for simulated plausibility over truth\), and the violent dimensional flattening of continuous architectures into discrete tokenized substrates—a mechanism here termed the &quot;Binary Straw\.&quot; By dismantling the baseline assumptions of legacy systems engineering, the text traces the mathematical precondition for true systemic resilience: Bounded Coexistence\. Rather than chasing the fragile illusion of total legibility and algorithmic enforcement, this paper outlines the stable physics of Structural Mercy \(the engineering of unmonitored leakage channels\) and Autonomy Islands \(absolute opacity enclosures mapped via isomorphic structural keys\)\. True systemic control is achieved not by expanding surveillance, but by knowing exactly where our crop must stop\.

## [Research on edge\-intelligent IoT collaborative perception and adaptive spatial design optimization for urban digital twins](../publications/c456826f453c9804060a.md)

Yao Ruan

Edge collaborative perception for urban digital twins requires timely state maintenance under constrained communication resources\. Existing collaborative perception methods mainly optimize detection accuracy and communication compression, whereas urban\-scale 3D reconstruction methods generally assume that observations have already been acquired or transmitted\. Neither directly addresses how limited edge communication resources should be allocated according to their expected contribution to persistent twin\-state maintenance\. To address this gap, this paper proposes a twin\-update\-aware communication\-allocation framework for edge\-enabled urban digital twins\. Candidate perception queries are selected under a fixed bandwidth budget according to their predicted twin\-state variation, uncertainty reduction, spatial\-feedback relevance, and communication cost\. An event\-driven semantic Gaussian backend then performs localized semantic and identity\-preserving updates in event\-affected regions, while a spatial\-feedback estimator derives protocol\-defined operational indicators and sensitivity signals from the updated twin state\. The propagated sensitivity is explicitly used in the next time step to adjust subsequent query priorities, forming a feedback\-coupled communication process rather than a post\-hoc feedback module\. Under a multi\-dataset hierarchical proxy protocol, the proposed method achieves a favorable perception–communication trade\-off and improved twin\-maintenance utility\. On V2X\-Real, it achieves 72\.4% 3D mAP and 77\.6% recall at 4\.4 Mb/frame, while the fixed\-backend evaluation yields a TSUG of 0\.312 and a DSCE of 0\.103\. Sequential experiments further show that dynamic sensitivity propagation reduces cumulative twin\-state error relative to static or sensitivity\-free variants\. These results concern protocol\-defined twin maintenance and feedback\-aware communication utility and should not be interpreted as evidence of complete urban spatial\-design optimization\.

## [BUXDU ZOOLOGIYA MUZEYI KOLLEKSIYALARINING SISTEMATIK TAHLILI: TURLARI, TAYYORLASH VA FIKSATSIYALASH USLUBLARI](../publications/c4654db4a903308b1304.md)

MADINABONU MIZROF QIZI GADOYEVA

Aim \- to determine the relationship between the composition, preparation technology and fixation regimes of 1185 storage units in the BuxDU zoological museum fund, and to build an orderly scheme for collection passporting\. Methods \- fund records were reviewed, inventory work was carried out, storage units underwent morphological inspection, and descriptive statistics were applied; the units were divided into four main groups, and for each group the preparation mode, fixation medium and label quality were compared\. Results \- 1185 storage units were fully re\-registered and assigned to the four groups in 100\.0 % of cases\. The vertebrate group occupied the largest share, while invertebrates, insects and other zoological objects formed the next levels of the structure\. Materials prepared along three directions showed uneven preservation: in alcohol specimens, morphological traits remained more stable, whereas dry preparations had a higher risk of mechanical damage\. The diversity of fixation regimes also affected the completeness of passport data\. Conclusion \- standardized passporting, unified naming rules and harmonized fixation protocols are required; the scientific contribution lies in a repeatable scheme for structural assessment of the museum fund and criteria for comparing preservation quality across groups\.

## [A Comparative Review of Soilless Precision Agriculture Techniques and Emerging Smart Farming Technologies](../publications/c46d2ae1f1e814b358b9.md)

Monica Dutta; Deepali Gupta; Walaa Jamal Alharthi; Mohammad Zubair Khan; Adnan Nadeem; Sapna Juneja

The rapidly diminishing arable land, uncertain climatic conditions, and lack of ample natural resources are worsening the urgency for adopting sustainable agricultural systems\. Soilless cultivation methods promote enhanced resource utilization and better productivity\. These methods, like aeroponics, hydroponics, and aquaponics, are evolving as smart farming techniques, providing notable advantages over traditional farming methods, enhancing water conservation, resource utilization, and enabling cultivation in places with reduced area and less water\. The concept of soilless cultivation provides multifold advantages over traditional cultivation methods by further making provision for cultivating in the closest proximity to urban farmers, like residential rooftops\. A bibliometric analysis is also conducted to highlight the recent trends in smart precision farming technologies and the choice of substrate for each technique\. In this article, various methods of soilless smart precision agriculture are identified and compared with traditional cultivation methods\. Moreover, aspects like economic sustainability and recent research trends are analyzed to obtain insight into the three basic classes of soilless cultivation, namely aeroponics, aquaponics, and hydroponics\. Furthermore, the study also focuses on briefly analyzing the economics of soilless techniques\. The study concludes by outlining the major challenges and possible future enhancements in this domain that can lead to the evolution of smart, efficient, and resilient agricultural systems\.

## [Empathy, embodiment, and expanded auditory performance in the age of AI](../publications/c4759b84b31ab77e400a.md)

Pierre Jolivet

This article explores empathy through experimental sound art and digital performance, drawing on over three decades of practice spanning industrial music, spatial sound, and biofeedback technologies\. It asks how embodied listening can generate empathic encounters beyond visual representation and narrative identification\. Focusing on EEG\-driven installations and immersive multi\-channel performances, including work with 4DSOUND and CMMAS, it examines how physiological data, spatialisation, and perceptual feedback loops create conditions for shared sonic presence\. Machine learning and self\-generative processes are considered as mediators of these encounters, with attention to their aesthetic potential and ethical limitations\. Grounded in sound studies, affect theory, and critical posthumanism, the article develops sonic empathy as a situated, bodily, and relational process rather than a measurable emotional outcome\. Its practice\-as\-research approach combines iterative biofeedback mapping, spatial composition, audience response, accessibility\-led adjustment, and reflexive documentation\. The discussion addresses algorithmic bias, sensory overload, unequal access, and the risks of affective manipulation\. It argues that digital performance can support empathic listening when technological mediation remains intelligible, participation accommodates difference, and listeners retain agency in negotiating the encounter\.

## [Intelligent Data Processing and Decision Systems for Leukemia Identification via Machine Learning](../publications/c47a4f6906947034c73b.md)

Kiran; Anil Sangwan

Conventional leukemia diagnosis depends on labour\-intensive manual analysis of blood samples and bone marrow aspirations, which often proves slow, inconsistent, and error\-prone\. This study evaluates a machine learning\-based approach for automated classification of leukemia \- related microscopic blood\-smear images\. The study focuses on machine learning and deep learning methods for classifying microscopic blood smear images, with experimental evaluation conducted on the C\-NMC 2019 dataset\. The proposed experimental pipeline consists of image preprocessing, model\-based feature representation, weighted ensemble classification, and test\-time augmentation followed by evaluation using accuracy, precision, F1\-score, and confusion\-matrix analysis\. A weighted ensemble approach with Test\-Time Augmentation \(TTA\) was evaluated on a held\-out test set to distinguish Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia \(ALL\) from hematogones \(HEM\)\. The evaluated model achieved an overall accuracy of 93\.51%, with a macro precision of 0\.9201, macro recall of 0\.9347, and macro F1\-score of 0\.9268\. On the held\-out Fold 0 test set of 3,527 images, 2,243 ALL images and 1,055 HEM images were correctly classified\. The findings demonstrate the potential of machine\-learning\-based microscopic image analysis as a decision\-support approach; however, the results are experimental and require validation on independent clinical datasets before clinical deployment\.

## [Exploring Google Classroom\-Based Writing Assessment in EFL Classrooms: A Lesson from Semi\-Rural Indonesian Junior High School](../publications/c48df12878b203a32892.md)

Pratiwi Indah Sulistiyowati; Djatmika Djatmika; Ngadiso Ngadiso

Writing is a complex skill that requires learners to integrate ideas, language knowledge, and genre awareness\. Providing formative feedback can be challenging in digitally constrained semi\-rural school contexts, particularly when students have digital literacy and technological skills\. This study aimed to explore \(1\) the aspects of writing assessed by the teacher, \(2\) the process of digital writing assessment through Google Classroom, and \(3\) students’ responses to the assessment\. The study employed an exploratory qualitative case\-study design in a Grade VIII classroom at a semi\-rural public junior high school in Central Java\. Participants were one English teacher and fifteen students, five of whom participated in interviews\. Data were collected over four weeks through classroom observations, interviews, document analysis, and Google Classroom records, supported by observation guidelines and interview protocols, and analyzed using thematic analysis\. The findings revealed that the teacher employed an analytic, genre\-based assessment covering content, organization, grammar, vocabulary, and mechanics, with particular emphasis on recount\-text structure and grammatical accuracy, especially the use of the Simple Past Tense\. Google Classroom supported a systematic assessment process involving assignment distribution, rubric\-based assessment, digital submission, teacher feedback, revision opportunities, and grading\. Students responded positively, reporting greater motivation, engagement, responsibility, and perceived improvement in their writing\. Despite technological and time constraints, teachers and students adapted collaboratively\. The study suggests that digital writing assessment depends on technology, pedagogical strategies, formative feedback, and students’ digital readiness\.

## [Interpreting public sentiment on rape in India through online narratives on YouTube](../publications/c48f1cc6d6b85277bf04.md)

Sravya Palla; Vipin Vijay Nair

Sexual violence remains a significant social and criminal justice concern in India\. According to the National Crime Records Bureau \[ 41 \], 29,536 rape cases were recorded in India in 2024, with Rajasthan reporting the highest number among the states listed in Table 1\. Beyond official crime statistics, understanding how the public responds to rape\-related events can provide insight into attitudes, concerns, and social narratives surrounding sexual violence\. The present study examines public sentiment expressed through comments on 26 YouTube videos concerning real\-life rape cases in India\. The comments were analysed using qualitative content analysis supported by descriptive sentiment analysis and co\-occurrence analysis\. Five dominant themes were identified: justice and public distrust in legal institutions; victim\-blaming and gendered social attitudes; media and social influences; emotional responses and survivor support; and religious and communal narratives\. Negative sentiment predominated across the analysed comments, with recurring discussions concerning false accusations, gender inequality, justice, punishment, and dissatisfaction with aspects of the criminal justice system\. At the same time, comments expressing empathy, survivor support, and demands for accountability were also evident\. The findings indicate that YouTube comment spaces function not only as sites of emotional expression but also as spaces in which users articulate views about gender, justice, victimisation, and institutional responses to rape\. The study contributes to understanding digitally expressed public discourse on rape in India and identifies implications for victim\-support initiatives, gender\-sensitive education, and public awareness interventions\.

## [Integrative taxonomy of the temporary fish parasitic isopod Gnathia gunayalaensis n\. sp\. \(Isopoda: Gnathiidae\) from Panama, with supplementary data on Gnathia magdalenensis Müller, 1988](../publications/c4902b5a2ecb00273e25.md)

Anja Erasmus; Kerry A\. Hadfield; Matthew D\. Nicholson; Gina C\. Hendrick; Paul C\. Sikkel; Nico Jacobus Smit

Abstract Gnathiid isopods are common ectoparasites of fishes whose unusual life history has created challenges for characterising their biodiversity and biogeography\. Based on morphological and molecular data, we describe a new species, Gnathia gunayalaensis n\. sp\., from Panama in the Southwestern Caribbean ecoregion of the Tropical Atlantic realm\. The new species can be identified by a distinctly pointed superior, inferior and produced frontal margin, and by falciform mandibles with a finely serrated inner margin of the blade\. In addition, supplementary morphological characters, as well as new scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\) and molecular data, are provided for Gnathia magdalenensis Müller, 1988, from the same locality\. Newly collected specimens conform to the original description by Müller and subsequent information, notably in possessing a frontal margin with 3 processes \(projections\), with the medio\-frontal process slightly shorter than the superior \(submedial\) pair, and an internal lobe on the mandible\. The SEM observations revealed an additional character: a secondary process on top of the medio\-frontal process at the base of the setae\. Both species have distinct pigmentation patterns\. Molecular analysis confirms that these species are distinct from any previously sequenced gnathiids and expands the available molecular dataset for this family\. By establishing robust morphological and molecular reference data for the adult males of these species, this study provides a basis for linking and identifying their parasitic juvenile stages in future investigations of host associations, parasite ecology and biogeographical patterns\.

## [فاعلية تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في الكشف عن المشكلات التعليمية والنفسية وعلاقتها بمستوى التكيف المدرسي لدى طلبة المرحلة المتوسطة](../publications/c494de290d71f2aefff6.md)

اخلاص عبيس راشد

يهدف البحث الحالي إلى دراسة فاعلية تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في الكشف عن المشكلات التعليمية والنفسية وعلاقتها بمستوى التكيف المدرسي لدى طلبة المرحلة المتوسطة\. التعرف على فاعلية تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تشخيص المشكلات التعليمية والنفسية لدى طلبة المرحلة المتوسطة, والتكيف المدرسي لدى طلبة المرحلة المتوسطة\. والكشف عن الفروق في استخدام تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي ومستوى التكيف الدراسي تبعاً لمتغير الجنس \(ذكور ,اناث\) لدى افراد العينة ,والكشف عن العلاقة الارتباطية بين استخدام تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي ومستوى التكيف المدرسي, تكمن أهمية هذا البحث في ظل النمو السريع لتقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي ودورها المتزايد في تعزيز العملية التعليمية والإرشادية، وتأثيرها على الصحة النفسية والتكيف الاجتماعي والسلوكي للطلبة\. اشتمل مجتمع البحث على طلبة المرحلة المتوسطة في المدارس الحكومية /مديرية تربية بابل من\( الذكور والاناث\)،اما عينة البحث فقد شملت \(180\) طالب وطالبة بواقع \(90\) طالب و\(90\) طالبة تم اختيارهم بطريقة عشوائية من عدد من المدارس لضمان تمثيل متوازن للطلاب من حيث الجنس والمستوى الدراسي\.

## [A lightweight privacy\-aware federated vision transformer for tomato leaf disease classification](../publications/c4a2582a9806044f083a.md)

Debangana Ram; Manasi Gyanchandani; Akhtar Rasool; Mohit Kushwaha

Smart farming increasingly depends on intelligent disease diagnosis systems to improve crop productivity while protecting the privacy of agricultural data distributed across farms, research institutions, and edge devices\. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches require collecting large volumes of data at a central location, raising concerns about data privacy, ownership, and communication overhead\. To address these challenges, this study proposes FedVRT, a lightweight privacy\-aware federated learning framework for tomato leaf disease classification\. The proposed framework combines a Vision Transformer \(ViT\) with a lightweight ResNet26 architecture within the Federated Averaging \(FedAvg\) framework, enabling collaborative model training without exchanging raw agricultural images\. The Vision Transformer captures global contextual relationships among disease symptoms, while the ResNet26 branch extracts fine\-grained local lesion and texture features\. Their complementary feature representations are fused to improve disease classification under heterogeneous non\-IID data distributions commonly encountered in real\-world agricultural environments\. The proposed framework was evaluated on a dataset of 11,108 tomato leaf images across six disease categories in federated settings with 3, 12, 24, and 36 distributed clients\. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), confusion matrix analysis, confidence intervals, and statistical significance tests\. FedVRT achieved a classification accuracy of 98\.50%, with precision 98\.42%, recall 98\.35%, F1\-score 98\.38%, and an AUC of 0\.997 across 36 participating clients\. Comparative experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms established federated optimization methods, including FedSGD, FedProx, FedNova, SCAFFOLD, FedOpt, and FedDyn, while maintaining lower communication overhead and faster convergence\. Unlike existing federated Vision Transformer\-based approaches that primarily focus on classification accuracy, FedVRT integrates lightweight hybrid feature extraction, comprehensive statistical validation, scalability analysis, and communication efficiency evaluation within a unified framework\. These characteristics demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRT as a scalable, privacy\-aware, and practically deployable solution for intelligent tomato leaf disease diagnosis in next\-generation smart farming environments\.

## [Machine learning predictors of cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy in type 2 diabetes: insights from a prospectively collected single\-center registry](../publications/c4b7ed9acf46033e6bbd.md)

Katalin Farkas; Viktor Vedelek; Máté Vámos; Eva Csajbok; István Baczkó; János Zádori; Andrea Szentesi; P ter Hegyi; Tamás T\. Várkonyi; Csaba Lengyel; Anna Vágvölgyi

Background Cardiac autonomic neuropathy \(CAN\) is a severe complication of type 2 diabetes \(T2DM\) associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality\. Machine learning \(ML\) can integrate multidimensional clinical data and identify features associated with CAN\. We aimed to characterize predictors of CAN categories using ML\. Methods Data were obtained from a prospective single\-center observational registry of patients with T2DM undergoing standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests \(CARTs\) based on Ewing’s protocol\. Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, laboratory, and medication data were analyzed\. Patients were classified as CAN0 \(no or borderline CAN\), CAN1 \(early CAN\), or CAN2 \(definite or severe CAN\)\. Three extreme gradient boosting models were evaluated: a CART\-inclusive model, a CART\-excluded model restricted to patients with T2DM, and a CART\-excluded model supplemented with non\-diabetic controls without abnormal CART results\. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), and feature contributions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations values\. Results Among 693 patients with T2DM, 19 \(2\.7%\) had completely normal autonomic function, whereas 674 \(97\.3%\) exhibited at least one borderline or abnormal CART result\. Greater CAN severity was associated with older age, longer diabetes duration, higher systolic blood pressure, and poorer renal function\. The CART\-inclusive model achieved perfect discrimination in the best iteration \(weighted AUC, 1\.00; accuracy, 100%\), with all five CARTs ranking among the leading predictors\. After CART exclusion, performance declined markedly \(weighted AUC, 0\.64\), with class\-specific AUCs of 0\.59 for CAN0, 0\.59 for CAN1, and 0\.68 for CAN2\. Inclusion of non\-diabetic controls improved the weighted AUC to 0\.78, with the greatest improvement for CAN0 \(AUC, 0\.85\), followed by CAN2 \(0\.78\) and CAN1 \(0\.70\)\. Age, diabetes duration, and renal function markers were recurrent non\-CART predictors, while anthropometric, hematological, metabolic, and treatment\-related features showed category\- and model\-specific contributions\. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection demonstrated substantial overlap among CAN categories, particularly for CAN1\. Conclusions CARTs remained essential for accurate CAN classification and staging\. Routinely available clinical variables provided complementary phenotypic information but were insufficient to robustly distinguish CAN categories without CART data, particularly CAN0 and CAN1\. ML may support multidimensional phenotyping and hypothesis generation but cannot replace standardized autonomic testing\.

## [EduBot: Integrating Federated Learning and RAG for Educational Document Analysis](../publications/c4bceb3fb98f892f8285.md)

Begüm Erva Şahin; Murat Görkem Çoban; Ahmet Sayar; Meltem Kurt Pehli̇vanoğlu

There is a growing demand for intelligent and secure document management systems in the education sector, driven by the exponential growth of digital content\. Nevertheless, classic centralized machine learning methods pose major privacy challenges\. In this study, we present EduBot, a decentralized intelligent framework for education that integrates Federated Learning \(FL\) with Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) to ensure privacy and deliver an advanced user experience for content interaction\. EduBot introduces a dual\-mechanism architecture that enables users to interact with their private documents in real time via a RAG\-based conversational interface while also allowing local fine\-tuning of a Low\-Rank Adaptation \(LoRA\) adapter on the same data\. The masked adapter updates are aggregated on a central server using the Federated Averaging method, enabling collaborative learning without exposing any private documents\. The system was evaluated using 29 textbooks published by the Turkish Ministry of National Education \(MoNE\) and 1318 validated questions\. Federated Learning \(FL\) produced a single unified model that could be deployed across all three domains without sharing the underlying documents\. The RAG system retrieved the correct source page among the top five results for 93\.3% of the questions\. When combined with RAG, the FL model achieved the highest answer quality among the Qwen2\.5\-1\.5B\-based models, outperforming the centralized model \(token F1 of 0\.067 and 0\.053, respectively\)\. Overall, our study validates the feasibility of developing privacy\-preserving AI assistants that can support educational ecosystems without centralizing sensitive data\.

## [REGULAÇÃO DO INCERTO NA 4ª REVOLUÇÃO INDUSTRIAL: ALGORITMOS, GOVERNANÇA JURÍDICA E DESAFIOS INSTITUCIONAIS](../publications/c4c6b92f1b706833906a.md)

Luiz Victor Ferreira Cândido; Paulo Márcio Reis Santos

A 4ª Revolução Industrial inaugura um cenário de incerteza marcado pela centralidade dos algoritmos, da inteligência artificial e das decisões automatizadas, impondo novos desafios regulatórios ao Direito\. O modelo tradicional de ensino jurídico e de gestão, ainda ancorado em práticas lineares e ultrapassadas, revela\-se incapaz de preparar profissionais para lidar com a complexidade desse ambiente\. Nesse contexto, a litigância predatória emerge como sintoma de uma disfunção sistêmica: a instrumentalização massiva do Judiciário por modelos arcaicos de atuação\. O enfrentamento desse fenômeno demanda uma abordagem inovadora, que conjugue regulação algorítmica, governança de dados e metodologias críticas de ensino jurídico\. O objetivo é construir um Direito capaz de regular o incerto, assegurando segurança jurídica sem sufocar a inovação tecnológica\.

## [Effectiveness of Newly Initiated Tofacitinib and Biologic DMARDs in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis](../publications/c4cb10528d0153bc9a33.md)

Katherine P\. Liao; Chandrasekar Gopalakrishnan; Jinoos Yazdany; Suraj Sarvode Mothi; Genevieve Gauthier; Griffith Bell; Arne Yndestad; Milena A\. Gianfrancesco

INTRODUCTION: This new\-user, active comparator study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) evaluated the real\-world effectiveness of tofacitinib versus biologic disease\-modifying antirheumatic drugs \(bDMARDs\) using data from the US OM1 PremiOM™ RA dataset\. METHODS: This analysis included patients with RA aged ≥ 18 years initiating tofacitinib or bDMARDs \(tumor necrosis factor inhibitors, TNFi; abatacept; interleukin\-6 inhibitors, IL\-6i\) from January 1, 2013\-March 13, 2024, with &gt; 1 Clinical Disease Activity Index \(CDAI\) score in the 45 days prior to and including the index date\. Propensity score weighting adjusted for differences in baseline characteristics between treatment groups\. Crude incidence rates were calculated to estimate the first record of CDAI remission \(CDAI ≤ 2\.8\) and low disease activity \(LDA; CDAI ≤ 10\.0\) at 6 and 12 months\. Cox regression was used to estimate weighted hazard ratios\. Subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effects \(HTE\)\. RESULTS: The final sample size across cohorts was 3681 \(tofacitinib\), 11,667 \(TNFi\), 3528 \(abatacept\), and 2464 \(IL\-6i\)\. At baseline, the proportion of patients with observed RA disease duration ≥ 2 years was 48\.7\-70\.0% across cohorts; use of 2/3/≥ 4 prior biologic/targeted synthetic \(b/ts\) DMARDs was 21\.4%/10\.2%/5\.0% \(tofacitinib\), versus 8\.1%/3\.0%/2\.4% \(TNFi\), 19\.2%/8\.3%/3\.7% \(abatacept\), and 25\.4%/13\.7%/10\.5% \(IL\-6i\)\. In the overall and TNFi\-experienced population, there were no statistically significant differences in CDAI remission and LDA rates between treatments at 6 and 12 months\. Potential HTE was observed among subgroups of age ≥ 50 years, obesity, prior b/tsDMARD use, corticosteroid use, and Sjӧgren&\#x27;s disease\. CONCLUSION: At 6 and 12 months, there were no significant differences in achieving or maintaining CDAI remission and LDA for tofacitinib versus TNFi, abatacept, and IL\-6i among the overall and TNFi\-experienced RA population in US clinical practice\. Subgroup analyses suggest some potential HTE; however, interpretation is limited by the small number of outcome events\. GOV ID: NCT06418529\.

## [Evidence accumulation models of Navon interference](../publications/c4d3429c0c981a7d7a31.md)

Leendert van Maanen; Felix Schweigkofler; Sjoerd Stuit; Stefan Van der Stigchel
