The Navon task is a classic paradigm to study selective attention, in which participants identify target letters presented at either a local or global level within compound figures\. Traditionally, differences in reaction time \(RT\) between local and global trials – precedence effects – are used to quantify individual biases towards local or global processing\. However, such RT\-based measures conflate attentional bias with general differences in speed\-accuracy trade\-offs\. Here, we applied evidence accumulation models to dissociate these mechanisms and evaluate whether Navon interference reflects conflict resolution processes similar to those in tasks such as the Flanker and Simon paradigms\. Participants performed a letter\-Navon task with congruent and incongruent trials with local or global focus\. We fitted four models – the Diffusion Decision Model, Dual\-Stage Two\-Phase model, Shrinking\-Spotlight model, and Diffusion Model of Conflict\. All models captured the overall RT distributions and conditional accuracy functions, but evaluation of model complexity and parameter estimates favoured the Dual\-Stage Two\-Phase and Diffusion Decision models as the principal accounts of Navon interference\. The findings support an interpretation of the Navon task as a conflict\-resolution paradigm and demonstrate that evidence accumulation modelling provides a principled framework for disentangling attentional and strategic contributions to selective attention performance\.

## [Perceived Challenges and Strategies for Digital Preservation at the National Space Research and Development Agency \(NASRDA\), Nigeria](../publications/c4e24f853d67dbe0429f.md)

Hussaini Idris Danjuma; Joyce Aisha Egbunu

This study examined the perceived challenges hindering digital preservation and the strategies for enhancing digital preservation at the National Space Research and Development Agency \(NASRDA\), Nigeria\. A descriptive survey design was adopted\. The population comprised 183 staff members drawn from the library, media, ICT, and registry units of NASRDA headquarters and two activity centres\. The entire population was studied because it was small enough to manage without sampling\. A structured questionnaire was used to collect data\. The instrument produced an overall Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha coefficient of 0\.99 across the 16 items\. This high coefficient is interpreted cautiously because it may indicate substantial overlap among items rather than exceptionally high measurement quality\. Data were analysed using frequency counts, percentages, mean scores, and standard deviation\. All eleven challenge items were above the 2\.50 cut\-off, with mean scores ranging from 3\.37 for inadequate funding to 2\.89 for technophobia\. The five proposed strategies were also above the cut\-off, with training and development recording the highest mean \(3\.38\) and policy and procedure development the lowest \(3\.19\)\. The findings indicate that NASRDA staff perceive digital preservation as being affected by financial, institutional, technological, and human\-capacity factors\. The study concludes that improvement at NASRDA requires coordinated attention to funding, policy, infrastructure, staff competence, collaboration, and monitoring\. The study recommends that NASRDA strengthen its digital preservation policy, provide sustained funding, upgrade preservation infrastructure, and organise regular staff training\.

## [Longitudinal physical\-mental multimorbidity trajectories by sociodemographic factors: a cohort study using electronic health records in Scotland \(2000–2021\)](../publications/c4ee8f0fe38b54ea1a1d.md)

Thu Nguyen; Katherine Lisa Keenan; Colin McCowan; Michail Papathomas; Areti Manataki

Multimorbidity, the co\-occurrence of two or more chronic conditions, is a pressing global health challenge\. However, research capturing the dynamic, longitudinal nature of health trajectories, particularly the intersection of physical and mental domains, remains scarce compared to traditional cross\-sectional &quot;snapshots\.&quot; Leveraging up to 21 years of electronic health records data from 858,789 Scottish patients in the University of Dundee Health Informatics Centre, we used multistate modelling to explore how individuals transition from a disease\-free baseline into multimorbidity, evaluating how age, sex, and socioeconomic status shape these pathways\. Overall transition estimates were driven by the younger demographic of our baseline disease\-free cohort\. The findings highlight the critical role of severe, hospital\-contacting mental health conditions in driving early\-onset multimorbidity, particularly in young men and socioeconomically disadvantaged groups\. These findings underscore the urgent need to prioritise integrated physical\-mental care and address upstream structural determinants of health\. This temporal approach identifies high\-risk populations for targeted early interventions and informs policy initiatives aimed at reducing health disparities\.

## [İnci Aral’ın Yeni Yalan Zamanlar Romanında Postmodernizm Eleştirisi](../publications/c4ef1597cf7dc21a9c99.md)

Ebru Değe Güven

20\. yüzyılın ikinci yarısında modernizme karşı gelişen postmodernizm; yıkıcılığı, öznelliği, parçalı yapısı, çoğulculuğu, oyunsallığı ve fantastik özellikleriyle ön plana çıkar\. Mimariden sinemaya, felsefeden müziğe kadar pek çok alanda etkisini gösteren postmodernizm, edebiyat sahasında da özellikle roman türünde belirgin bir yer edinmiştir\. Klasik roman anlayışından farklı olarak kişi, zaman, mekân ve olay örgüsü gibi unsurları belirsiz ve parçalanmış biçimde kurgulayan postmodern roman, içerikten çok biçim ve dil üzerine yoğunlaşır\. Türk edebiyatında 1970’lerden itibaren modern romanla birlikte gelişim gösteren postmodern roman, 1990’lı yıllarda ayrı bir estetik yönelim olarak belirginleşmiştir\. Bu süreçte kurmaca yazarlar, önceki örneklerden farklı olarak postmodern özellikleri daha yoğun biçimde barındıran romanlar kaleme almıştır\. Kendisini postmodern bir yazar olarak tanımlamamasına rağmen eserlerinde postmodern unsurlara yer veren İnci Aral, Yeni Yalan Zamanlar \(1994\) adlı romanında dikkat çekici bir postmodernizm eleştirisi ortaya koyar\. Bu çalışmada öncelikle postmodernizm ve postmodern roman kavramları ele alınmış; ardından Yeni Yalan Zamanlar romanı, içeriksizlik, üstkurmaca, parçalanma ve belirsizlik, çoğulculuk, ironi ve fantastik ile metinlerarasılık başlıkları altında incelenmiştir\.

## [DIGITAL LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL AGILITY: DRIVING GOVERNMENT PERFORMANCE THROUGH INNOVATION CAPABILITY](../publications/c4faf4428b9b0d295d63.md)

Adnan; Rahmaniar; Hamilur Rahmah; Ahmad Yani; Aiyub Yahya

This study investigates how Digital Leadership, Organizational Agility, and Technological Innovation shape Government Performance, while considering Leadership Enhancement and Digital Innovation as intervening mechanisms\. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory, the study argues that organizational capabilities generate performance improvements primarily through processes of capability transformation, rather than solely through direct relationships between organizational capabilities and performance\. A quantitative explanatory research design was adopted, based on survey responses from 300 civil servants holding managerial positions within local government institutions in North Aceh Regency, Bireuen Regency, and Lhokseumawe City, Indonesia\. The hypothesized relationships were empirically assessed using Structural Equation Modelling–Partial Least Squares \(SEM\-PLS\)\. The empirical results indicate that Digital Innovation constitutes the strongest determinant of Government Performance, as reflected in both its largest direct effect and highest effect size\. Technological Innovation likewise exerts a statistically significant direct influence on Government Performance\. However, neither Digital Leadership nor Organizational Agility demonstrates a direct effect on Government Performance; instead, both significantly contribute to Digital Innovation and Leadership Enhancement\. The mediation results further establish Digital Innovation as the principal pathway through which Digital Leadership, Organizational Agility, and Technological Innovation translate into improved Government Performance\. Leadership Enhancement also mediates these relationships, although its mediating contribution is comparatively weaker\. Taken together, the findings provide support for fourteen of the seventeen hypothesized relationships, whereas three hypotheses are not supported\. The study advances the literature on digital government and strategic management by broadening the application of Dynamic Capability Theory to the public\-sector context\. The findings indicate that organizational capabilities contribute to superior government performance mainly when they are converted into innovation\-driven transformation processes\. From a practical perspective, policymakers should place greater emphasis on developing digital innovation, strengthening digital leadership capabilities, fostering organizational agility, and maximizing the potential of technological innovation as complementary pathways for improving government performance and creating greater public value\.

## [AI\-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality\-Emotional Attachment\-Loyalty Pathway in 2025\-2026](../publications/c500e1f1d6ded424ab97.md)

Heyam Almousa

Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies\. Official Saudi digital\-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although the retailer\-specific investment figures cited in an earlier draft have not been independently substantiated\. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026\. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling \(PLS\-SEM\) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty \(β = 0\.421, p &lt; 0\.001\), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment \(reported indirect effect = 0\.238, 95% CI \[0\.187, 0\.289\]\)\. We discuss a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment\. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human\-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient \(β = 0\.187\) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment\. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents \(β = 0\.289, p = 0\.001\) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents \(β = −0\.023, p = 0\.811\)\. Age\-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output\. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51\.2% of the variance in loyalty \(R2 = 0\.512\) and has positive predictive relevance \(Q2 = 0\.289\)\. Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance\-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication\. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions\. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship\-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty\.

## [Rethinking selection criteria for liver transplantation in hepatocellular carcinoma: from morphology to artificial intelligence](../publications/c50fadb27b8b9606e02a.md)

Quirino Lai; Silvia Quaresima; Chiara Matrascia; Fabio Melandro

INTRODUCTION: Liver transplantation \(LT\) is a uniquely curative treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\), as it removes both the tumor and the underlying cirrhotic liver\. However, organ scarcity makes candidate selection a central clinical and ethical issue\. Over the past three decades, selection has evolved from simple morphologic thresholds toward increasingly multidimensional models of oncologic risk\. AREAS COVERED: This review examines the evolution of selection criteria for LT in HCC, from the Milan criteria and subsequent morphology\-based expansions to models incorporating tumor biology, serum biomarkers, treatment response, waiting\-list dynamics, and artificial intelligence\. The literature discussed includes landmark morphologic criteria, AFP\-based models, PIVKA\-II and AFP\-L3 integration, downstaging strategies, dynamic scores such as TRAIN and NYCA, and machine\-learning models including MoRAL\-AI, TRIUMPH, and TRAIN\-AI\. EXPERT OPINION: The field is moving from categorical eligibility rules toward individualized, continuous risk estimation\. Future selection should not aim merely to expand transplant access, but to identify patients most likely to achieve durable oncologic benefit\. Artificial intelligence, radiomics, liquid biopsy, and multi\-omic profiling may refine risk prediction, but their clinical adoption will require prospective validation, transparency, calibration, transportability, and integration into allocation systems\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL E ACESSO À JUSTIÇA EM DEMANDAS DE POLÍTICAS PÚBLICAS: EFICIÊNCIA JUDICIAL, DESIGUALDADES E SUPERVISÃO HUMANA](../publications/c51bdb09995302ed03fd.md)

Daniele Alves Moraes; Kauany Aparecida Martins Ferreira

O presente artigo analisa as condições de legitimidade e os desafios decorrentes do uso da inteligência artificial \(IA\) pelo Poder Judiciário brasileiro no âmbito do gerenciamento e julgamento de demandas ligadas à judicialização de políticas públicas\. Partindo de uma abordagem qualitativa, bibliográfica e documental, examina\-se em que medida as ferramentas de automação e algoritmos de triagem podem ampliar o acesso substancial à justiça sem reiteração de disparidades socioeconômicas ou mitigação do devido processo legal\. Consideram\-se os parâmetros regulatórios vigentes, notadamente as Resoluções do Conselho Nacional de Justiça \(CNJ nº 332/2020 e nº 615/2025, alterada pela nº 674/2026\)\. Conclui\-se que a inteligência artificial constitui instrumento legítimo de otimização e eficiência jurisdicional quando restrita à função de apoio e mapeamento informacional, sob estrita supervisão humana, transparência algorítmica e garantias de contestabilidade e inclusão digital\.

## [Machine learning based prediction of activation energy of pure lithium titanate pebbles fabricated by sol\-gel technique](../publications/c522dd2d8e67028be7f8.md)

Sujit Kumar Chatterjee; Subhash C\. Pandey; Sanjay Kumar Sinha; Gyanendra Tiwary; Gaurav Vishnu Londhe

Lithium titanate \(Li₂TiO₃\) is considered as one of the most promising ceramic breeder materials for fusion reactor blankets because of its favorable tritium release characteristics and low activation energy requirements\. In this study, pure Li₂TiO₃ pebbles were fabricated using Sol\-Gel technique followed by urea\-acetone\-assisted spherodization\. The thermal and structural characterization was performed using DTA/TG and XRD analyses\. Activation energy \(Ea\) characterizes the temperature dependence of tritium diffusion and release in Li₂TiO₃ breeder materials and is a key kinetic parameter governing tritium extraction efficiency in fusion reactor blankets\. Accurate \\\(\\:\{E\}\_\{a\}\\\) determination is essential for designing tritium extraction systems\. Therefore, a machine\-learning model based on a feed\-forward Neural Network \( NN \) was developed to estimate activation energy of Lithium titanate \(Li₂TiO₃\) for tritium release\. Unlike conventional Arrhenius fitting approaches that are sensitive to experimental variability, the proposed framework incorporates multiple process variables simultaneously and captures nonlinear relationships\. The dataset consisted of 10,000 synthetically generated samples derived from consistency verification of Arrhenius relationships and literature\-reported parameter ranges for Li₂TiO₃ breeder materials\. The neural network demonstrated high predictive capability \(R²=0\.94\) and estimated activation energy of 1\.12 eV, closely matching the Arrhenius\-derived value of 1\.15 eV\. The results demonstrate the potential of machine learning as an efficient tool for kinetic analysis and tritium extraction optimization in fusion energy systems\. The present work should be regarded as a methodological demonstration of machine\-learning\-assisted kinetic analysis using a physically motivated synthetic dataset derived from consistency verified Arrhenius relationships and literature\-reported parameter ranges\. Independent consistency verification using newly acquired tritium release datasets remains a subject of future investigation\.

## [Consumer trust in ai\-generated advertisement content](../publications/c5581d8051d039199dfb.md)

Barbara Krajnc

Diplomsko delo obravnava področje sodobnega oglaševanja s poudarkom na vplivu generativne umetne inteligence na zaupanje potrošnikov\. Problem izhaja iz hitrega napredka tehnologij UI, ki podjetjem omogočajo avtomatizirano ustvarjanje naprednih oglasnih besedil, slik in videoposnetkov, medtem ko se pri potrošnikih pojavljajo skepticizem in etični pomisleki\. Delo temelji na teoretični opredelitvi koncepta zaupanja in k temu sodečih pojmov, empirično pa analiziramo odziv slovenskih potrošnikov na konkretni UI\-generiran video oglas z uporabo prilagojene merske lestvice ADTRUST\. V raziskavi ugotavljamo zadržano in nevtralno splošno zaupanje potrošnikov v UI\-generirane oglasne vsebine\. Potrošniki najvišje ocenjujejo čustvene, estetske in tehnične vidike oglasov, bistveno nižje pa resničnost in pripravljenost za sprejemanje nakupnih odločitev na njihovi podlagi\. Nadaljnji rezultati potrjujejo, da splošni pozitiven odnos do UI vpliva na višjo stopnjo zaupanja v UI\-oglase, medtem ko demografske značilnosti, kot so spol, starost in izobrazba, ne pokažejo statistično pomembnih razlik v stopnji zaupanja\.

## [Cascaded deep learning for synthesis of 18F\-FDG PET from 18F\-octreotide: model parameter optimization and performance evaluation](../publications/c55ec88d8b55ff00d5d5.md)

Ruxi Chang; Liping Yang; Jungang Gao; Xiang Liu; Bo Wang; Yan Li; Xiaoyi Duan

Objective To investigate a cascaded conditional generative adversarial network \(cGAN\)–based method for synthesizing 18 F\-FDG PET images from 18 F\-octreotide, optimize model parameter configurations, and evaluate the quality of the synthesized images\. Methods Imaging data from 71 tumor patients who underwent dual\-tracer PET/CT examinations with 18 F\-FDG and 18 F\-octreotide between May 2022 and November 2025 were retrospectively collected\. A cascaded deep learning architecture \(first stage: 3D U\-Net; second stage: self\-attention 3D V\-Net\) was employed to evaluate the effects of image preprocessing, resampling size, and patch size on synthesis quality\. Three preprocessing strategies \(log transformation, normalization, and a combined approach\) were compared\. Image quality was assessed using five objective metrics \(SSIM, PSNR, MSE, MAE, and NMI\) and Likert 5\-point ratings from three nuclear medicine physicians; liver and lesion\-level SUV agreement were further evaluated\. Results In the held\-out test cohort \( n = 14\), the combined preprocessing method \(log transformation \+ normalization\) significantly outperformed the individual methods \(SSIM: 0\.8454 ± 0\.0328 vs\. 0\.7831 ± 0\.0337 vs\. 0\.7438 ± 0\.0362, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. On the identical held\-out test cohort \( n = 14\), the Group 2 parameter configuration \(resampling size: 256 × 256 × 512; patch size: 128 × 128 × 128\) outperformed Group 1, with an SSIM of 0\.8854 ± 0\.0455 and a PSNR of 28\.15 ± 3\.35 dB, representing relative improvements of 19\.1% and 83\.5%, respectively, over Group 1 \(paired\-samples t\-test, both P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The mean Likert score was 4\.53 ± 0\.19\. Quantitative analysis of liver SUVmean showed no significant difference between synthesized and real images \( P = 0\.967, paired t\-test\)\. Lesion\-level quantitative analysis demonstrated high agreement between synthetic and real 18 F\-FDG images, with Pearson correlation coefficients of 1\.0000, 0\.9995, and 0\.9991 for SUVmax and SUVmean \( n = 14\) and SUVpeak \( n = 13\), respectively \(all P &lt; 0\.001\), no significant differences on paired t\-tests \(all P &gt; 0\.05\), and all Bland–Altman differences within the 95% limits of agreement\. Conclusion The cascaded deep learning model enabled cross\-tracer synthesis from 18 F\-octreotide to 18 F\-FDG PET images\. In this exploratory, single\-center pilot cohort, the optimized configuration demonstrated promising quantitative and visual performance, supporting image\-synthesis feasibility and potential clinical utility of a single\-injection, dual\-parameter molecular imaging approach for neuroendocrine tumors\. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before any clinical application\.

## [BEYOND CRIMINALISATION: DIGITAL VICTIMISATION AND VICTIM PROTECTION AGAINST AI DEEPFAKES IN INDONESIA](../publications/c564b4f7d9bd85b70041.md)

Kus Rizkianto, Siswanto, Estiana Nabila

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) deepfakes enable the convincing imitation of an individual’s image or voice, creating risks that extend beyond the identification and punishment of offenders\. This article examines how Indonesian law responds to digital victimisation and whether its remedies address reputational, psychological and social harm\. Using normative legal research and a focused interdisciplinary literature review, it analyses the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, Personal Data Protection Law, Sexual Violence Crimes Law, the Criminal Code and criminal procedure reforms, including the 2026 Witness and Victim Protection Law\. The analysis identifies three interconnected problems: harm may arise before distribution; protection depends on fitting conduct within fragmented offences; and criminal proceedings alone do not ensure rapid content containment or sustained recovery\. It proposes a victim\-centred response linking accessible reporting, lawful evidence preservation, timely platform action, risk\-sensitive support and restitution where legal conditions are met\. Rather than claiming an absence of relevant laws, the article argues that coordination and remedies should reflect the continuous nature of technology\-facilitated harm\. This framework offers a policy\-oriented contribution to debates on digital victimology and access to justice in Indonesia\.

## [Low‐Frequency Vibration Damping Polyurethane Elastomers with High Mechanical Robustness via Constrained Pendant Chains](../publications/c5764c529f77c95f6079.md)

Xiang Han; Tianyu Wang; Chenxi Huyan; Zhiyuan Ma; Haoxiang Li; Dong Liu; Fei Chen; Liqun Zhang

ABSTRACT Low‐frequency vibration damping in polyurethane elastomers remains difficult to reconcile with mechanical robustness\. Effective dissipation of low‐frequency vibration requires the characteristic relaxation time of polymer chains to match the timescale of slow external oscillations\. However, such long‐timescale chain relaxation is typically associated with stress relaxation, creep and irreversible deformation, compromising mechanical robustness\. Here, we report a polyurethane elastomer that addresses this trade‐off through a constrained pendant‐chain architecture, in which grafted pendant chains are locally constrained at their roots while retaining flexible terminal alkyl segments\. This architecture is created by placing urea and urethane motifs at the pendant‐chain roots, where neighboring pendant‐chain units assemble into a reversible hydrogen‐bonded association network\. This reversible network kinetically constrains pendant chain relaxation, shifts the characteristic relaxation toward longer timescales and thereby enhances low‐frequency damping\. Meanwhile, the association network provides dynamic physical crosslinks that restrict backbone slippage and preserve structural integrity\. The optimized polyurethane elastomer exhibits a loss factor of 0\.98 at 1 Hz while maintaining a tensile strength of 60\.2 MPa\. These results establish constrained pendant chain engineering as a molecular design strategy for polyurethane elastomers that combine low‐frequency vibration attenuation with high mechanical performance\.

## [Pulmonary hypertension in a patient with HHV\-8–negative multicentric castleman disease and epstein\-barr virus co\-infection: a case report](../publications/c57d256962b9f10969cc.md)

颜晰; Lipin Xie; Hongrui Li; Jiao Tang; 王茂筠; Lan Wang

Pulmonary hypertension \(PH\) seems to be a rare but severe complication of Castleman disease \(CD\), especially the multicentric type \(MCD\)\. We report a case of recurrent fever, anemia and progressive dyspnea\. She was finally diagnosed with pre\-capillary PH in the setting of MCD and Epstein–Barr virus \(EBV\) co\-infection after right heart catheterization and lymph node biopsy\. After receiving siltuximab, an anti\-interleukin\-6 monoclonal antibody along with diuretic agent, the symptoms were relieved\. However, the patient died 8 months after diagnosis due to a pulmonary hypertensive crisis secondary to clinically diagnosed bacterial pneumonia presenting with severe dyspnea, refractory hypoxemia, and acute right ventricular failure\. This rare case improves recognition of this infrequent etiology of PH\.

## [O EFEITO ÓPTICO MACH BAND E SUA INFLUÊNCIA NA IDENTIFICAÇÃO DE CÁRIES INTERPROXIMAIS](../publications/c58251d2ee60ef152e5a.md)

Luiz André Dias Telles

A cárie dentária é uma doença crônica que afeta os dentes, sendo as faces proximais mais suscetíveis, devido à retenção de alimentos e dificuldade de higienização\. A interpretação radiográfica pode ser comprometida por erros associados à percepção do profissional e os efeitos ópticos, podem influenciar na análise correta das radiografias\. Este estudo teve como objetivo, avaliar a capacidade de identificação de cáries proximais em estágio inicial nas radiografias periapicais e interproximais, tanto convencionais digitalizadas quanto digitais, e a interferência do efeito Mach band na interpretação destas imagens\. Um questionário contendo imagens de cárie ou efeito Mach band, foi preenchido por 84 acadêmicos de Odontologia e 79 profissionais graduados\. Em todos os grupos, as marcações com a identificação correta proposta nas questões apresentaram as maiores frequências de acerto\. As marcações incorretas foram mais comuns nas relacionadas às radiografias interproximais, enquanto a opção “Não identificada” foi mais prevalente nas radiografias periapicais\. Conclui\-se que é imprescindível aprofundar o conhecimento sobre os efeitos ópticos, especialmente o Mach band, devido à sua relevância na interpretação de radiografias convencionais e digitais\. Isso visa garantir maior segurança na implementação de um tratamento precoce e eficaz para os pacientes\.

## [AI\-driven whole\-life costing for decision\-ready UK public building retrofits](../publications/c590bc02b32609c1c989.md)

Ziru Tao; Paul Baguley; Rashid; id\_orcid 0000\-0001\-9983\-5929 Maqbool; Obuks Ejohwomu

Abstract Public\-sector building retrofits in the United Kingdom require decisions that balance whole\-life cost, carbon reduction, service continuity and auditability under limited data and constrained capital budgets\. This paper develops a decision\-ready whole\-life costing \(WLC\) workflow that integrates environmental, social and governance \(ESG\) priorities with uncertainty\-aware artificial intelligence \(AI\) for public\-building retrofit appraisal\. The workflow combines national non\-domestic Energy Performance Certificate \(EPC\) and Display Energy Certificate \(DEC\) data, Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme \(PSDS\) delivery evidence and stakeholder inputs to construct a scenario library of public\-building archetypes, retrofit actions and appraisal constraints\. Stakeholder priorities from interviews, a questionnaire and a co\-design workshop are translated into transparent weights using fuzzy analytic hierarchy process \(F\-AHP\)\. These weights parameterise a reinforcement learning \(RL\) planner, while a Bayesian convolutional neural network–long short\-term memory \(BCNN–LSTM\) surrogate provides uncertainty\-bounded energy, carbon and cost trajectories for repeated policy evaluation\. Results show that the workflow supports auditable retrofit sequencing across archetype and budget conditions and improves composite ESG performance relative to conventional WLC\-only, £/tCO 2 e and static multi\-criteria decision analysis \(MCDA\) baselines\. For 1000 matched archetype–budget cases, the trained deep Q\-network \(DQN\) decision\-search stage achieves a 30\.03\-fold speedup over traditional scalar feasible\-sequence enumeration\. The contribution is an integrated and explainable WLC–ESG–AI workflow for early\-stage public retrofit decision support\. The current validation remains based on public datasets and scenario\-level evidence so future work should extend the framework using project\-specific metered data, digital twins and live portfolio deployment\.

## [Bipartición balanceada en grupos homogéneos con correspondencia posicional](../publications/c595019911d74742b972.md)

Margarita Ruiz\-Olazar; Diego Ihara; Benjamín Barán; Miguel Méndez‐Garabetti

In many applications requiring fair comparisons \(e\.g\., control vs\. treatment or equitable resource allocation\), forming “internally compact” groups is not sufficient: it is necessary to partition a dataset into two balanced subsets that are as similar as possible to each other, and additionally, with an explicit one\-to\-one correspondence between elements\. This work studies the case of two groups \(c = 2\) as a combinatorial optimization problem, minimizing a cost function based on the sum of squared distances between pairs matched at equivalent positions \(positional matching\)\. As the main contribution, a hybrid heuristic is proposed that constructs an initial solution via nearest neighbors supported by spatial indexing \(KD\-Tree\) and refines it with local search through swaps accepted by pure descent, exploiting the additive nature of the cost to evaluate improvements efficiently\. The experimental evaluation on synthetic and real datasets shows that the method attains consistently low objective values, practical execution times, and stable behavior across runs\. Finally, future directions are discussed to extend the approach to the general case c &gt; 2 and study scalability strategies \(e\.g\., parallelization and ANN structures\), maintaining positional correspondence as the central constraint\.

## [LITERATURE AND THE ECOLOGICAL CRISIS: AN ECOCRITICAL STUDY OF THE NOVEL GEMURUH IN THE CONTEXT OF THE SINABUNG ERUPTION](../publications/c59a64151c233351a419.md)

Sumiati Sumiati; Zul Fitrah Ramadhan

This study applies Greg Garrard&\#x27;s ecocritical framework to analyze Gemuruh, a novel by Hilmi Faiq that explores the complex relationship between humans and the environment in the context of the eruption of Mount Sinabung\. Using six main aspects of ecocriticism, this study identifies how natural disasters are represented not only as destructive events, but also as triggers for personal transformation, community resilience, and ecological awareness\. The analysis shows that volcanic ash and environmental degradation \(pollution\) are depicted alongside the cultural and emotional attachment of the Karo people to their land \(settlements and wilderness\)\. Apocalyptic imagery affirms the destructive power of nature as well as the ethical urgency of disaster preparedness, while representations of animals and the earth highlight interconnectedness within the ecological system\. Through a combination of documentary\-style narrative and lyrical prose, Gemuruh builds a layered reflection on the struggle for survival, loss, and coexistence with an unpredictable environment\. This research contributes to the international ecocritical discourse by highlighting the Indonesian literary perspective on the environmental crisis and offering insights into the role of literature in fostering ecological empathy and disaster literacy\.

## [A quantum\-resilient, blockchain\-enabled SDN framework for securing IoMT systems](../publications/c5af2857606c5874c85d.md)

Sajan Shrestha; Kumar Sekhar Roy

Abstract The Internet of Medical Things \(IoMT\) is revolutionizing the healthcare industry through connected medical devices and real\-time data exchange\. However, the sensitive nature of this data requires a security infrastructure capable of resisting both current and future threats, including those posed by quantum computing\. This paper presents a unified framework that combines Software\-Defined Networking \(SDN\), Blockchain, and Quantum Cryptography to secure IoMT systems\. The SDN architecture is enhanced with a Quantum Key Distribution \(QKD\) plane for quantum\-safe session key generation and a Blockchain plane for decentralized identity verification\. To improve efficiency, we introduce a self\-mutable blockchain, blocks are automatically deleted after expiration to reduce storage and maintain scalability, while remaining tamper\-resistant to attackers\. The system utilizes Kyber, a lattice\-based quantum\-resistant algorithm, to mitigate future quantum threats\. The proposed protocol was evaluated through mainnet simulation, BAN logic, and AVISPA formal verification, confirming strong security against classical and quantum attack vectors\. This framework delivers a scalable, efficient, and future\-ready solution for secure IoMT networks\.

## [Multi\-class Alzheimer’s disease classification using VGG19 transfer learning with hybrid Harris Hawks Optimization and random forest](../publications/c5af8007f37f8e9dea4d.md)

G\. Anbu Selvi; T\. Karthick

Abstract Accurate cognition\-state classification of Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\), Mild Cognitive Impairment \(MCI\), and Cognitively Normal \(CN\) is essential for early evaluation of the disease\. Existing deep\-learning approaches often retain redundant features, depend on dataset\-specific configurations, and provide limited methodological optimization\. This study proposes a transfer\-learning\-based MRI classification framework integrating spatial and intensity normalization, histogram equalization, double bilateral filtering, VGG19\-based deep feature extraction, Harris Hawks Optimization with Simulated Annealing \(HHO\-SA\) for feature selection, and Random Forest \(RF\) classification\. The framework was implemented using Python and PyTorch and evaluated on the ADNI1 Complete 1Yr 1\.5T dataset, containing 2,294 MRI observations from 639 subjects\. Subject\-level partitioning was employed to minimize data leakage\. The proposed framework achieved 98\.70% accuracy, 98\.55% macro\-precision, 98\.93% macro\-recall, 99\.28% macro\-specificity, 98\.73% macro\-F1, and 99\.40% macro\-ROC\-AUC\. Compared with the strongest reported benchmark accuracy of 98\.20%, this study developed into 0\.50%\. The findings demonstrate effective retrospective three\-class MRI classification and provide a reproducible computational framework for AD research\.

## [GPU\-Accelerated Robust MA\-\-RIS Pre\-Optimization for Communication and Target Illumination](../publications/c5b6fbe691d797a88297.md)

Tran Le Dung; Ho Viet Duc Luong

Movable antennas \(MAs\) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces \(RISs\) offer strong spatial control for integrated sensing and communication \(ISAC\), but repeatedly adapting MA positions and RIS phases to each channel realization can be impractical\. This letter develops a GPU\-accelerated robust pre\-optimization framework that jointly selects slow\-timescale MA geometry and RIS phases and returns a reusable Pareto set balancing expected worst\-user rate and transmit\-side worst\-target illumination\. The illumination objective measures directional transmitted power rather than complete echo\-detection or parameter\-estimation performance\. The proposed Regime\-Aware Multiobjective Pre\-optimization \(RAMP\) preserves regime\-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross\-regime mating using Pareto\-survival feedback, and constructs a worst\-regime robust archive\. Numerical results demonstrate competitive robust Pareto quality against the considered evolutionary baselines while avoiding online physical re\-optimization\.

## [AI literacy of library and information science students in Africa: insights from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Uganda](../publications/c5c9feb5a795442715c3.md)

Zakir Hossain; Md\. Sakib Biswas; Sophia Vivian Adeyeye; Monica Mensah Danquah; Margaret Sraku\-Lartey; Berthilde Uwamwezi; Corinne Hertel

Introduction\. As artificial intelligence \(AI\) reshapes global education and information systems, Africa’s readiness remains uneven\. This study examines AI\-literacy among Library and Information Science \(LIS\) students—future librarians—across five African countries: Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Uganda\. It assesses their technical proficiency, tool usage and ethical awareness in an AI\-driven era\. Method and Analysis\. A quantitative survey was conducted with 437 LIS students from five African countries\. The Games\-Howell Post Hoc Test was used to compare AI literacy across countries\. ANOVA and Multinomial Logistic Regression \(MLR\) were applied to analyse variations in AI literacy levels based on country, study level, gender and English proficiency\. Results\. The findings reveal significant disparities in AI literacy between the five African nations\. The results of the Games\-Howell post hoc test show that both Rwanda and Uganda have significantly higher mean AI literacy scores compared to Ghana and Nigeria\. In contrast, South Africa&\#x27;s scores did not show a statistically significant difference from the other countries, highlighting the varied readiness levels\. The study found that ChatGPT dominates usage at 71\.9%, while specialised tools such as Elicit remain significantly underutilised at just 4\.6%\. Ethical concerns among students are also notable, with 39\.6% citing worries about privacy risks and 33\.2% being troubled about algorithmic bias, highlighting AI anxieties and its societal impact\. Conclusion\. This study calls for integrating AI literacy into LIS curricula and advocating for multilingual AI tools\. Where new modules are not feasible, institutions can leverage existing courses such as Information Retrieval, Digital Libraries and Research Methods to embed AI content\. The results emphasise that context\-driven interventions are essential to ensure AI enhances equitable knowledge access rather than deepening existing disparities\.

## [ANALYSIS OF FACTORS HINDERING LOGISTICS LEARNING DURING CLASSES: A THEORETICAL\-EMPIRICAL STUDY](../publications/c5d86c70e4de162aae7c.md)

Mateus Amaral Pereira; Giovanna da Silva Meireles; Daniel Nascimento\-e\-Silva

This study aimed to analyze the factors hindering learning among students in the Higher Education Technology Program in Logistics during classes, addressing three guiding questions: which factors impede learning, how these factors interfere with the process, and why they produce such effects\. This qualitative, exploratory, descriptive study involved students in a class in the Logistics Technology Program at the Federal Institute of Education, Science and Technology of Amazonas \(IFAM\), Manaus Industrial District Campus\. Data were collected through an online semi\-structured instrument and analyzed using a similarity technique, followed by grouping responses into analytical categories\. The results revealed five dimensions of factors interfering with learning: pedagogical, technological, individual, behavioral/social, and structural\-organizational\. Pedagogical factors stood out, mainly related to a lack of practical application, an excess of theoretical classes, poor teaching methods, a lack of focus/conciseness, and issues with teaching approaches and instructor performance\. The analysis showed that these factors primarily interfere with attention, concentration, focus, comprehension, interest, content retention, and the integration of theory and practice\. Students cited attention deficits, comprehension difficulties, monotony, excessive complexity, lack of focus, absence of practical contextualization, insufficient resources, and low engagement\. The study concludes that learning difficulties are a multidimensional, process\-oriented phenomenon in which various factors can combine to compromise the conditions necessary for learning\. The results suggest, therefore, that understanding learning in Logistics requires an integrated approach covering pedagogical, individual, technological, behavioral, social, and structural dimensions\.

## [Missed Detections and False Alarms in a CNN Technosignature Detector on Breakthrough Listen Data](../publications/c5d8fde41448744aafe0.md)

Omer Imran

Radio technosignature searches rely on machine learning detectors to shrink the candidate pool before a human looks at it\. They are validated on held\-out data from the training distribution, which excludes the cases where they are most likely to fail: a technosignature has unknown morphology, and terrestrial interference is unbounded in variety\. I trained a standard competition detector once, froze it, and probed it with 15,000 injections across ten morphologies and five amplitudes, placed into real Green Bank backgrounds\. Two directions were tested: genuine signals with morphologies other than a straight narrowband line, and interference resembling the training data\. Recall did not follow the predicted ordering, and it fell as signals brightened, even for a needle of the kind the detector was trained on \(from 0\.590 to 0\.090\)\. One interference morphology reached a false positive rate of 0\.627, comparable to the detector&\#x27;s own baseline recall of 0\.5525 on genuine signals\. Gradient\-weighted Class Activation Mapping \(Grad\-CAM\) showed attention along the injected path in one missed family by a pre\-specified test, and visually in a second\. A pre\-specified, time\-averaged ON\-OFF filter removed false alarms and genuine detections at the same rate\. The detector reads only the ON panels\. Since the only evidence distinguishing a genuine candidate from terrestrial interference lies in the discarded OFF panels, it cannot tell if a signal originates from the target star; it can only tell if it resembles the training data\. This explains the false alarm directly; the missed signals reflect what the detector learned to recognise, which reading the OFF panels would not by itself change\.

## [A sequential multi\-model machine learning framework integrating environmental and management factors for mapping exchangeable potassium in rice soils](../publications/c5d9a85b13da557abdb0.md)

Aditya Nugraha Putra; Teguh Dharmawan; Novandi Rizky Prasetya; Luqman Sholahudin Ridwan; Yosi Andhika; Novalia Kusumarini; Rizki Pambudi; Gatot Haryo Pramono; Mochtar Lutfi Rayes; Sammi Ullah

Exchangeable potassium is a key determinant of rice productivity, yet its spatial distribution is difficult to predict because it is influenced by both pedogenic factors and intensive agricultural management\. This study developed a staged multi\-model machine learning framework to map exchangeable potassium in rice systems by progressively integrating terrain, spectral, geological, soil, climate, and management predictors\. A total of 318 soil samples were collected across irrigated and rainfed rice fields, and exchangeable potassium was measured using ammonium acetate extraction\. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated across five feature\-integration stages\. Model performance improved consistently as predictors were added, with R2 increasing from 0\.38 to 0\.68 under random validation \(0\.16–0\.41 under spatial block cross\-validation\)\. Variable importance and SHAP analyses showed a progressive shift in the most influential predictor groups, from terrain and hydrological factors to geological and soil properties, and finally to management variables\. Irrigation, cropping intensity, and planting schedule were the most influential predictors in the final model\. Spectral indices showed weaker relationships than soil and management variables\. These findings demonstrate that integrating environmental and management predictors is essential for accurate potassium mapping and provide a framework whose transferability to other regions and periods remains to be tested\.

## [Global Phylogenetic Insights into the Moth Orchid \(Phalaenopsis amabilis\) Population from the Meratus Mountains of South Kalimantan, Indonesia](../publications/c5f531a6e4604033ddc1.md)

Dindin Hidayatul Mursyidin; Tanto Susilo; Yudhi Ahmad Nazari; Nove Arisandi

Phalaenopsis amabilis constitutes one of the most valuable and economically significant orchids \(ornamental plants\) worldwide\. The present study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and phylogenetic relationships of the moth orchid \(Phalaenopsis amabilis\) population native to the Meratus Mountains of South Kalimantan, Indonesia, using the matK marker\. Sixty\-one samples of Phalaenopsis, comprising six of Phalaenopsis amabilis from the Meratus Mountains of South Kalimantan, Indonesia, and 55 of another Phalaenopsis species from GenBank, were molecularly characterized using the matK marker to assess genetic diversity and phylogenetic relationships\. Genetic diversity was determined using the Maximum Composite Likelihood method, and phylogenetic relationships were estimated using the Kimura 2\-Parameter Maximum Likelihood method\. In this study, moth orchid populations had lower levels of matK polymorphism at the intraspecific than at the interspecific level, with values of 10\.07% and 47\.91%, respectively\. Similarly, this is directly proportional to the genetic diversity at both levels, which is lower \(0\.016\) at the intraspecific level than at the interspecific level \(0\.062\)\. However, this marker reveals unique phylogenetic relationships in Phalaenopsis, both locally and globally, with P\. amabilis ‘Halong 2’ closely related to three similar species from Singapore, Japan, and the USA\. At the same time, all samples of P\. amabilis are closely related to two other Phalaenopsis species, i\.e\., P\. sanderiana and P\. aphrodite\. The findings are expected to provide critical insights to guide future conservation strategies and targeted breeding programs for these native orchids\.

## [HUMAN TRANSLATION AND AI IN MODERN EDUCATION: WHY WE NEED BOTH](../publications/c6053191db80e6855331.md)

Sitora Yarasheva

This thesis examines the intersection of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and human expertise in modern higher education&\#x27;s translation processes\. While neural machine translation offers unprecedented speed and cost\-efficiency, it frequently compromises conceptual depth, cultural nuances, and factual accuracy\. This study argues against a binary substitution model, advocating instead for a hybrid paradigm\. By integrating the scalability of AI with the critical evaluation of human translators, global universities can optimize educational content delivery without sacrificing academic rigor\.

## [Citrus leaf pathology multi\-class image dataset and a hybrid multi\-branch attention fusion network for lemon leaf disease classification](../publications/c60fa9126f6ee904b35c.md)

Chayan Mondal Abir; Subir Biswas; Prabodh Kumar Sahoo; Aswini Kumar Samantaray

Abstract The productivity of lemon \(Citrus lemon\) crops is severely undermined by foliar diseases, which constitute the leading cause of global harvest degradation\. The conventional reliance on manual identification by experienced specialists poses a significant bottleneck, as these methods are both time\-consuming and prone to human error under field conditions\. Recently, deep learning techniques have been employed to identify and diagnose citrus foliar diseases from digital images, automating the classification process and providing non\-experts with accessible diagnostic tools\. While several deep learning applications have been used to classify lemon diseases with the aim of improving classification accuracy, most of these studies fail to achieve high accuracy and rely on datasets with an insufficient number of disease classes\. In this paper, we introduced a dataset named “Citrus Leaf Pathology Multi\-Class Image Dataset” with 14 different classes, and we proposed a Hybrid Multi\-Branch Attention Fusion Network \(HMAF\-Net\)\. The architecture consists of four parallel feature extraction branches, each incorporating branch attention and channel attention, followed by classification using a Neural Network \(NN\)\. A DenseNet121 backbone is combined with lightweight convolutional branches, refined through squeeze\-and\-excitation channel attention and a learnable branch\-weighting fusion mechanism to adaptively integrate complementary feature representations\. The model attains 96\.63% precision and 95\.59% accuracy on the proposed dataset\. The model further demonstrates strong generalization, achieving 97\.48%, 95\.89%, and 98\.23% accuracy on three independent external lemon and citrus leaf datasets, with statistical significance confirmed through paired t\-tests across five independent runs\. Explainable AI visualizations further confirm that the model’s predictions are grounded in disease\-relevant leaf regions, supporting its potential for reliable deployment in real\-world agricultural diagnostic systems\.

## [The need for supportive policies: connecting individual placement and support to the domains of employment and mental health care](../publications/c61c5cf5608d75cd251f.md)

Jaap van Weeghel; Angelo Fioritti; Dorothea Jaeckel; Gary Johnston; Greta Mazzetti; Minna Ahola; Ulrika Bejerholm; Cris Bergmans; Fréderic Debroas; Lars de Winter; Soffia Erla Einarsdottir; Dina Guglielmi; Hlynur Jònasson; Anna Kárníková; Débora Koatz; Julia Kropeit; Anne Lise Lunder Arvesen; Denise Manchisi; Jan Markerink; Kine Nan Lium; Noora Sipilä; Una Twomey; Chantal Van Audenhove

Background Individual placement and support \(IPS\) is an effective vocational rehabilitation programme for people with mental illness\. This article analyses national policies that directly promote IPS and broader employment\-related policies on mental health in 13 European countries\. Analysis IPS alone cannot address the broader workplace and policy conditions that influence sustainable employment\. Therefore, creating mentally healthy working conditions also requires action by employers, healthcare systems, and policymakers\. Policy options Recurring barriers and facilitators were identified across countries, alongside variation in governance and implementation contexts\. IPS services often operate in isolation, with limited access to consistent training, data, and cross\-sector coordination\. A national infrastructure for IPS is therefore needed to offer implementation support, intersectoral collaboration should be strengthened and employers need to be supported to advance equity, diversity and inclusion\. IPS practice will benefit from policies addressing poor mental health conditions in the workplace, and policies endorsing a recovery\-oriented mental healthcare system\. Conclusion IPS can build a solid bridge between mental healthcare and employment when integrated into recovery\-oriented services and supported by policies that promote inclusive, mentally healthy workplaces\.

## [Oxygen Saturation Index as a Predictor of Surfactant Requirement in Neonates with Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Prospective Observational Study](../publications/c621c95a9bee6bffa13f.md)

Mukund Kantilal Vaja; Garvit Godawat; Bhavika Gaurav Datta; Kavya Rupesh Shah; Shraddha Awadesh Mishra; Adish Gandhi

Objectives The study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of the oxygen saturation index \(OSI\) for surfactant requirement in neonates with respiratory distress syndrome \(RDS\) and to determine optimal cutoff values for guiding surfactant therapy\. Material and Methods This prospective observational study was conducted at the neonatal intensive care unit \(NICU\) of a tertiary care teaching hospital in Gujarat, India, over 18 months \(IEC Approval No: SVIEC/ON/Medi/BNPG/22/DEC/23/II2\)\. A total of 104 neonates with RDS requiring respiratory support within 6 h of birth were enrolled\. Surfactant \(beractant 100 mg/kg\) was administered based on clinical deterioration, radiological evidence of RDS, and FiO₂ requirement, following European Consensus Guidelines on RDS management \(2022 update\)\. OSI was calculated using the formula: \[mean airway pressure \(cmH₂O\) × FiO₂ \(%\)\]/SpO₂ \(%\)\. For neonates on nasal continuous positive airway pressure \(nCPAP\), mean airway pressure was estimated as set CPAP pressure plus a correction factor\. Measurements were recorded at admission \(0 h\) and at 2, 4, and 6 h\. Receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis determined optimal cutoff values\. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26\.0\. Results Of 104 neonates, 42 \(40\.4%\) required surfactant therapy\. Of the total cohort, 84 \(80\.8%\) were initially placed on nCPAP and 20 \(19\.2%\) on mechanical ventilation; 22 \(21\.2%\) required escalation from nCPAP to mechanical ventilation\. The median time to surfactant administration was 3\.2 h \(IQR: 2\.1–4\.8\)\. The surfactant group had significantly higher mean OSI at admission \(3\.58 ± 0\.89 vs\. 2\.04 ± 0\.62, p &lt;0\.001\)\. ROC analysis revealed an optimal OSI cutoff of 2\.6 at admission with 85\.7% sensitivity, 77\.4% specificity, and an AUC of 0\.913 \(95% CI: 0\.857–0\.969\)\. A critical OSI cutoff of 2\.2 provided 95\.2% sensitivity with 56\.5% specificity\. Multivariate analysis identified gestational age &lt;30 weeks \(OR 7\.85, 95% CI: 2\.89–21\.32\), OSI ≥2\.6 \(OR 6\.78, 95% CI: 2\.45–18\.76\), and FiO₂ ≥0\.4 \(OR 5\.13, 95% CI: 1\.98–13\.29\) as independent predictors\. On separate multivariate logistic regression analysis for mortality, OSI &gt;3\.5 at admission \(OR 22\.74, 95% CI: 4\.12–125\.63, p &lt;0\.001\) and gestational age &lt;28 weeks \(OR 14\.12, 95% CI: 2\.56–77\.89, p = 0\.002\) were significant independent predictors of mortality\. Conclusion OSI at admission is a reliable, non\-invasive predictor of surfactant requirement in neonates with RDS\. An OSI cutoff of 2\.6 provides optimal predictive accuracy, while 2\.2 serves as a critical threshold for high\-sensitivity screening\. OSI &gt;3\.5 is an independent predictor of mortality on multivariate regression analysis\. Serial OSI monitoring can guide timely surfactant administration, particularly in settings where arterial blood gas analysis is unavailable\.

## [A brief history of horticultural applied research capability in the UK](../publications/c625570da6d256b33a48.md)

William E\. Parker; ROSEMARY H\. COLLIER

Commercial horticultural production in the UK is worth c\. £4\.22 billion annually, making a vital contribution to food security and to wellbeing through ornamental plants\. Research and knowledge exchange have been an integral part of the support network for the industry\. This paper considers the history of public research institutions/organisations which were specifically tasked with addressing the applied research needs of the UK’s horticultural industry\. It covers England, Wales and Scotland\. While the university sector still has the capacity to undertake innovative academic research relevant to commercial horticulture, the UK now has diminished capacity to conduct applied horticultural research compared to the situation even 20 years ago\. Decisions taken over time in the context of the politics and economics of the day have had far\-reaching and long\-term consequences for the UK’s ability to support its commercial horticultural industry with relevant and high\-impact research covering the spectrum from discovery to application\.

## [The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Administrative Decision\-Making in Iraq: Digital Transformation as a Model](../publications/c63aaca63e2a69cc1db0.md)

Zahraa Alhalfi

This research aims to examine the role of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in enhancing the quality and efficiency of administrative decision\-making in Iraq, adopting digital transformation as both an analytical model and an integrated practical framework\. The study focuses on the readiness of Iraqi government institutions to adopt intelligent systems and the impact of these technologies on improving decision\-making speed and transparency, reducing human error, and fostering a work environment grounded in data and intelligent analysis\. The research employs a descriptive\-analytical approach to review concepts related to AI and digital transformation, an inductive approach to infer relationships between variables, and a field\-based approach involving the analysis of government documents and reports\. Content analysis tools were also utilized to assess the extent to which AI applications—such as predictive systems, decision\-support algorithms, chatbots, and big data analytics tools—are being employed\. The findings indicate that the implementation of AI within Iraqi public administration remains in its early stages, despite official moves toward digitalization\. Key opportunities identified include faster decision\-making, increased transparency, reduced human intervention in routine tasks, and the creation of reliable databases to support planning and policymaking\. Challenges include weak digital infrastructure, limited technical skills among staff, the absence of a legal framework regulating artificial intelligence applications, and poor integration between government systems\. The research recommends formulating a comprehensive national strategy for artificial intelligence, developing digital infrastructure, upskilling government personnel, strengthening partnerships with the private sector and academic institutions, and updating legislation to align with digital governance and privacy protection standards, thereby ensuring a secure and effective environment for the adoption of smart technologies\.

## [Barroso Fontanals, Miguel Enrique ; Pacios Dorado, Juan Leonardo ; Fabars Bueno, Yudel Tomas ; Pompa Castillo, Michel &amp; Traba Vázquez, Marco Alejandro: Characterization of the Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools among Students at the University of Medical Sciences of Santiago de Cuba](../publications/c6465665a5579a2d48df.md)

A medium level of knowledge about the definition of artificial intelligence predominated \(51,14 %\), and the most commonly used AI tool was OpenAI ChatGPT \(100 %\)\.
