## [The Concept of Teacher Personality in Islamic Education: Exploring Qur’anic Principles and Prophetic Guidance](../publications/c654d6b5ab4af82a1354.md)

Muhamad Rizza; Siti Nuranisa Azahra; Dhea Shania Harvia; Ayunda Sahila Fathin

Teacher personality influences students’ character, moral values, and spiritual development, extending educators’ responsibilities beyond knowledge transmission\. In Islamic education, these responsibilities require the integration of professional competence with ethical and religious commitments\. This study examines teacher personality from an Islamic perspective grounded in Qur’anic values and Hadith teachings, focusing on Islamic personality concepts, teacher roles, and moral characteristics\. A qualitative library research approach was employed, using content analysis of primary sources comprising Qur’anic verses and Hadith and secondary sources comprising Islamic educational literature and relevant academic studies\. The findings indicate that Islamic teacher personality integrates intellectual understanding, spiritual awareness, and moral conduct\. The concepts of ‘aqliyah and nafsiyah represent Islamic thinking and behavioral orientations, respectively\. Teachers’ responsibilities are articulated through their roles as murabbi \(nurturer\), mu‘allim \(knowledge provider\), and mu’addib \(character builder\)\. Essential characteristics include sincerity \(ikhlas\), trustworthiness \(amanah\), patience \(sabr\), compassion \(rahmah\), and exemplary conduct \(uswah hasanah\)\. Together, these findings position moral integrity and spiritual responsibility as integral dimensions of teacher professionalism alongside teaching competence\. The study provides a conceptual basis for developing teacher personality through Qur’anic and Prophetic guidance, highlighting its relevance to meaningful and holistic educational practice\.

## [Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Customer Satisfaction in the Banking Sector](../publications/c65bb0cde99dd4bffec3.md)

Ajay Kumar Varshney; Bonthu Sai Pujitha

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is transforming the way banks provide services, but there is not much evidence on the impact AI\-enabled services have on customer satisfaction\. This study investigates the effect of AI based banking service on customer satisfaction and evaluates the mediating role of AI service quality, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, AI reliability and accuracy, customer trust and perceived security and privacy as well as difference in terms of age, bank type, income and digital literacy\. The study was conducted using non\-probability sampling of the bank customers in Andhra Pradesh and a structured 5\-point Likert type scale was administered online\. Duplicate records and one incomplete response were excluded leaving 44 valid responses which were analysed using chi\-square tests, one\-way ANOVA and simple, multiple and hierarchical linear regression with ancillary bootstrapping mediation and interaction analysis\. The overall satisfaction of the customers was at a moderate level \(M = 3\.53, SD = 0\.68\)\. The satisfaction was greatly predicted by AI\-enabled banking services \(β = \.66, R² = \.435, p &lt; \.001\) and each perception construct had a positive association with satisfaction\. This effect was partially mediated by customer trust and perceived security and privacy \(indirect effects = 0\.27 and 0\.19; both bootstrap 95% confidence intervals \(BCIs\) were non\-zero\)\. Satisfaction level was associated with digital literacy, χ²\(4\) = 14\.21, p = \.007, and mean satisfaction differed by age group, F\(3, 40\) = 4\.29, p = \.010, and by digital\-literacy level, F\(2, 41\) = 4\.76, p = \.014, but not by gender, income or bank type\. There was no moderation effect by digital literacy on the relationship between AI and satisfaction\. Results are only indicative due to the small non\-probability sample\. Trust building, clear communication of security and privacy protection, reliable AI results, and digital\-literacy support for customers should be the main areas of focus for banks\.

## [Land Cover Change, Ecosystem Service Implications, and Economy–Land Use Decoupling:](../publications/c6606b4f9ac47f317be3.md)

Safril Kasim; Hasddin Hasddin; La Fariki; Abhishek Agarwal

Land cover change plays a critical role in shaping watershed ecological conditions and supporting regional economic activities\. This study analyzes land cover dynamics in the Tiworo Watershed, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, for 2014, 2019, and 2024, and examines their relationship with sectoral economic growth\. Remote sensing and GIS were used to map and quantify land cover changes, while sectoral Gross Regional Domestic Product \(GRDP\) data for agriculture, forestry, and fisheries represented economic performance\. Economy–land use interactions were assessed using the Tapio decoupling elasticity index\. Economy–land use interactions were assessed using the Tapio decoupling elasticity index as a retrospective empirical measure based on observed changes in land cover and sectoral GRDP over the study periods\. The results show increasing sectoral GRDP accompanied by relatively limited changes in dominant land cover classes\. Absolute decoupling was observed during 2014–2019, relative decoupling during 2019–2024, and overall absolute decoupling for 2014–2024, indicating that economic growth was not proportionally associated with large\-scale land conversion\. Spatial analysis reveals localized landscape transformations, including mangrove degradation, settlement expansion, and plantation growth, which signal emerging pressures on environmentally sensitive areas\. Although ecosystem services are not directly valued, land cover change is interpreted as an indicator of ecological pressure with implications for provisioning ecosystem services\. These findings highlight the importance of integrating land\-use monitoring and economic indicators to support adaptive watershed management, spatial planning, and sustainable development\.

## [A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle \(Popillia japonica\)](../publications/c6730878202b47bd3a6e.md)

Davide Martinetti; Laura Erbetta; Danièle Bevacqua; Olivier Bonnefon; Marino Gatto; Lorenzo Mari; Renato Casagrandi

Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities\. Here we develop a process\-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P\. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies\. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short\-distance human\-mediated transport, and ovo\-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions\. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival\. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023\. Results reveal that the ongoing outbreak is occurring in one of the most favorable areas for the beetle, the Po Valley, which favors rapid spread and can sustain high population densities\. Mountain regions emerge as obstacles to the progression of the invasion, with the Alps, excluding the valleys, being an almost insurmountable defense, whereas the Apennines only slow down the southward advancement without stopping it altogether\. The projected speed of invasion, within and outside the outbreak area, ranges between 0 and almost 20 km/year and it is modulated by environmental conditions\. The predicted speed of invasion at continental level constitutes an actionable tool for invasion management, since it provides phytosanitary services with a critical evidence base for optimizing the geometry and extent of delimitation and containment areas\.

## [Reconceptualizing Teacher–AI Partnership in Inclusive Education: A Multi\-Level Socio\-Educational Psychology Framework](../publications/c674da7ea87223018c57.md)

Chohra Faycal

The integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) into inclusive classrooms presents opportunities for personalised support alongside risks of deepening educational inequities, particularly for students with disabilities\. Existing frameworks address AI in education and inclusive pedagogy largely in isolation, lacking theoretical integration that explicates psychological mechanisms through which AI systems may support or undermine belonging, participation and wellbeing of learners with diverse needs\. This conceptual article addresses this gap by developing a multi\-level socio\-educational psychology model of teacher–AI partnership, synthesising theoretical and empirical work across disability studies, inclusive education, teacher professional agency and technology\-acceptance literatures\. The proposed framework connects three interdependent levels: \(a\) school\-level conditions, including climate, governance and resources; \(b\) teacher\-level processes, encompassing beliefs, emotions and instructional practices and \(c\) student\-level outcomes, comprising learning, participation and wellbeing\. The model positions AI as a socio\-technical mediator that can function as either protective or risk factor for inclusion, contingent upon implementation conditions and disability\-responsive governance structures\. The article derives testable propositions and offers evidence\-informed guidance for special education practice, teacher education, school leadership and participatory AI governance that safeguards children’s rights and promotes educational justice\.

## [Liability at the Authority Boundary: A Framework for Allocating Responsibility Across Distributed and Agentic AI Systems](../publications/c682a879ff0b68f30ec4.md)

Deusdedit Ruhangariyo

Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed through systems in which authority, execution, oversight, and consequence no longer belong to the same actor\. A model may be developed by one organization, integrated by another, configured by an enterprise, instructed by a human, executed through an AI agent, routed through external tools, and experienced by a person who had no role in any of those decisions\. The resulting liability problem is not adequately described by asking whether a human remained &quot;in the loop&quot; or whether an audit trail exists\. This working paper develops the GAILC Authority Boundary framework\. It defines the Authority Boundary as the point at which consequential decision rights, discretion, intervention responsibility, or consequence\-bearing responsibility passes from one actor, system, organization, or layer to another, and analyses each boundary through five elements: Authority, Transfer, Reliance, Intervention, and Consequence\. The framework identifies two difficult liability cases that conventional control models often leave unresolved\. Intended\-Execution Liability concerns harm produced when a system remains within its authority, follows policy, uses permitted tools, and operates substantially as designed\. No\-Action Liability concerns harm produced or worsened where an actor bears an identifiable duty or assigned responsibility to act, possesses the authority, information, timing, and practical capacity to do so, yet no consequential intervention occurs\. The paper introduces the Authority Envelope, the distinction between authorization and judgment, the Silence\-as\-Authority Problem, the GAILC Allocation Test, Consequence Ownership, Allocation Completeness and Allocation Adequacy, Residual Consequence, and Orphaned Harm\. It proposes a standardized Authority Boundary Record \(ABR\) designed to support verification, contestability, and independent adjudication, together with a boundary failure taxonomy, an irreversibility threshold, an inter\-organizational allocation procedure, and a pre\-deployment test\. Its central proposition is that traceability is evidence, not allocation: an authority and execution chain may be fully reconstructable while accountability and consequence allocation remain incomplete\. The framework is analytical and does not determine legal liability\. It is positioned in relation to agency law, duties concerning failures to act, design\-defect analysis, and scholarship on the problem of many hands, responsibility gaps, and moral crumple zones\. This paper is the third in the GAILC Working Paper series, following WP001 \(The Human Presence Economy\) and WP002 \(The Intervention Test\)\.

## [Touch Localization with a Resistive Position Sensor\-Gated Oxide Neuromorphic Transistor](../publications/c685423831339c2b1e67.md)

Bo Li; Si yuan Zhou; Wei  Sheng Wang; Lin Feng Wu; Wan Lin Zhang; Yu Fan Hu; Ya Rong Yuan; Chen Rui Zhai; Li Qiang Zhu

Abstract The ability to localize external mechanical stimuli is fundamental to human tactile perception, making its hardware implementation of significant interest for advanced human–machine interaction\. Here, a resistive position sensor \(RPS\) is proposed for touch location recognition, exhibiting a high sensitivity of ∼55 kΩ/cm and excellent stability\. A tactile perceptual system \(TPS\) is proposed by integrating the RPS with a chitosan\-gated oxide ionotronic neuromorphic transistor\. Benefiting from the strong proton relaxation effects of the chitosan\-based electrolyte, the neuromorphic transistor can effectively process electrical signals generated from the RPS\. The TPS can emulate various synaptic behaviors under mechanical stimuli\. As a proof of concept, it demonstrates Braille code recognition\. Furthermore, the TPS enables touch intention recognition through machine learning, demonstrating a high recognition accuracy of ∼99\.2%\. The results demonstrate great promise in human−machine interaction\.

## [Arabica Coffee Seedling Growth under Drought with Potassium, Boron, and Trichoderma spp\.](../publications/c6876b2f1257cf9edebd.md)

Selly Gunawan; Mochamad Arief Soleh; Intan Ratna Dewi Anjarsari

Drought stress during the seedling stage can restrict vegetative growth and compromise the successful establishment of Arabica coffee \(Coffea arabica L\.\) under field conditions\. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of potassium \(K\), boron \(B\), and Trichoderma spp\. on the morphological growth responses of LS 795 Arabica coffee seedlings under drought stress and during subsequent recovery\. The experiment was conducted at the Bale Tatanen Experimental Garden, Faculty of Agriculture, Universitas Padjadjaran, Jatinangor, Indonesia, from February to May 2026\. A randomized complete block design \(RCBD\) was employed, comprising eight treatments with four replications\. The treatments included an untreated control, potassium \(1\.38 g/L\), boron \(384 mg/L\), Trichoderma spp\. \(20 g/plant\), and their respective combinations\. Plant height, leaf area, and leaf number were measured throughout an 18\-day drought stress period and the subsequent recovery phase following rewatering\. Analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) revealed no statistically significant treatment effects on plant height, leaf area, or leaf number during the drought stress period\. However, significant differences in plant height emerged during the recovery phase, particularly at 15 days after rewatering, when seedlings treated with K \+ Trichoderma spp\. and K \+ B \+ Trichoderma spp\. exhibited the greatest plant heights, significantly exceeding those of the untreated control\. In contrast, leaf area and leaf number did not differ significantly among treatments during recovery\. These findings indicated that the tested treatments did not significantly alleviate drought\-induced growth suppression during the stress period\. Nevertheless, potassium application combined with Trichoderma spp\., either with or without boron supplementation, was associated with improved plant height during post\-drought recovery\. The results suggest that these treatment combinations may support the recovery of vegetative growth in Arabica coffee seedlings following drought stress, although further investigation is required to determine their effects on physiological drought tolerance and long\-term field establishment\.

## [Translation, contextual adaptation, and preliminary evaluation of INCRESE\-Norwegian Young](../publications/c6a736196ff6814351d5.md)

Anna Leiler; Kristin Øksendal Børresen; Malle Vogelsang; Jone Trovåg; Ingunn Anita Kulstad; Cathrine Fredriksen Moe; Helga Dis\-Isfold Sigurdardottir; Victor Manuel Pèrez Colado; Teddy Nambazira; Fiona Ng; Stefan Rennick‐Egglestone; Mike Slade; Paul William Craig Botnvik; Siv Anita Aasum; Unn Kristin Vedal; Kristin Berre Ørjasæter

Background The mental health of young people is a global concern\. Norway has seen a rise in mental health challenges among young individuals in recent decades, including both Sámi and non\-Sámi youth\. Culturally responsive and accessible mental health interventions are needed\. The NEON Young Norway Study investigates the use of mental health recovery narratives as a low threshold intervention\. To engage in recovery narratives mostly have beneficial impact, however, there is also a risk of triggering harmful behavior, which is why safe use of narratives requires careful analysis\. For this reason, the Inventory of the Characteristics of REcovery StoriEs \(INCRESE\) has been developed in English\. Our aim was to translate, contextually adapt, and to preliminary evaluate INCRESE for use among young people in Norway\. Methods INCRESE was translated into Norwegian using the UPSIDES proportionate translation methodology\. Contextual adaptation was carried out in collaboration with cultural experts and young individuals with lived experience\. For reliability assessment, five coders independently coded 32 narratives \(whereof 6 Sámi\) twice, with a two\-week interval between assessments\. Test\-retest reliability was assessed with Cohen’s kappa and interrater reliability with Gwet’s AC1, with scores above 0\.40 considered acceptable\. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed qualitatively\. Results Multiple adaptations were required to ensure contextual fit for both general Norwegian and Sámi youth\. Test–retest reliability \(Cohen’s K\) was moderate, with a mean κ = 0\.59 \(SD = 0\.27; range –0\.02 to 1\.00\)\. Mean percentage agreement between the two rating rounds was 90\.7% \(SD = 10\.03\)\. Interrater reliability \(Gwet’s AC1\) ranged from 0\.36 \(fair\) to 1\.00 \(perfect\) per item, mean AC1 0\.86 \(SD = 0\.14\), and with a mean percentual agreement of 72\.8% \(SD = 26\.64\)\. Reliability varied considerably between items\. Coders generally found INCRESE\-NY feasible and acceptable and provided suggestions for further refinement\. Conclusions INCRESE\-NY showed overall acceptable reliability for characterizing recovery narratives produced by young Norwegians, including Sámi youth\. The adapted inventory appears promising as a tool that can support the safe and systematic use of recovery narratives in youth mental health contexts\. However, further refinement is needed to examine its conceptual, cultural and practical applicability\.

## [Forecasting South Africa’s Consumer Price Index Using Seasonal ARIMA, LSTM, Support Vector Regression, and Gradient Boosting Models](../publications/c6aae032f5ec4b084fa8.md)

Naledi Blessing Mokoena; Johannes Tshepiso Tsoku; Martin M\. Chanza

Accurate forecasting of the Consumer Price Index \(CPI\) is essential for effective monetary policy, inflation targeting, and macroeconomic planning\. This study evaluates the forecasting performance of a traditional statistical model, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with exogenous variables \(SARIMAX\), alongside three machine learning \(ML\) models: Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), Support Vector Regression \(SVR\), and Gradient Boosting Trees \(GBT\) for forecasting South Africa’s CPI\. Monthly data spanning February 2012 to January 2026 are used, incorporating CPI and key macroeconomic predictors, namely the Producer Price Index \(PPI\), Gross Loan Debt, Foreign Debt, Total Exports, Total Imports, and the Foreign Exchange Rate\. Forecasting accuracy is assessed using MSE, RMSE, and MAPE\. The empirical results show that the LSTM model achieves the lowest forecast errors, with an out\-of\-sample MAPE of 1\.192% and an RMSE of 1\.4177, followed by the GBT model with a MAPE of 1\.320%\. The SARIMAX and SVR models exhibit comparatively higher forecast errors\. The Diebold–Mariano test indicates that the difference in predictive accuracy between the LSTM and GBT models is not statistically significant, suggesting statistically comparable forecasting performance\. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of ML\-based approaches, particularly LSTM and GBT, for capturing the complex dynamics of South African CPI\. The study contributes to the economic forecasting literature by providing empirical evidence on the application and comparative performance of statistical and ML models for CPI forecasting in an emerging economy\. The findings provide useful insights for central banks, policymakers, economists, and financial institutions seeking improved CPI forecasts to support monetary policy formulation, economic planning, and financial decision\-making\.

## [Clinical characteristics and outcomes of 144 critically ill children receiving therapeutic plasma exchange in a pediatric intensive care unit: a single\-center retrospective study](../publications/c6c040a070bd36c735cd.md)

Zhijiang Chen; Qiuju Wei; Jufang Liu; Cheng Zeng; Wei Zhao

Background Therapeutic plasma exchange \(TPE\) is increasingly used in critically ill children, yet pediatric data remain scarce\. This study aimed to characterize the clinical features, indications, complications, and outcomes of children receiving TPE in a pediatric intensive care unit \(PICU\)\. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 144 children who underwent TPE in the PICU of Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University, between January 2017 and December 2021\. Demographic data, diagnoses, TPE indications \(categorized according to the 2019 American Society for Apheresis \[ASFA\] guidelines\), complications, and outcomes were collected\. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify risk factors for mortality\. Results The 144 children \(median age, 66 months; median Pediatric Risk of Mortality III score, 18\) underwent 414 TPE sessions\. The leading indications were neurological disorders \(29\.2%\), liver diseases \(19\.4%\), and hematologic disorders \(16\.7%\); 57\.6% of patients were treated for ASFA category III indications\. The complication rate was 16\.9% per session, with filter or circuit clotting the most frequent event \(7\.2%\); all complications resolved after prompt management, and no treatment\-related death occurred\. Overall PICU mortality was 36\.8%, highest in the liver disease group \(60\.7%\) and lowest in the neurological disorder group \(16\.7%\) \( P = 0\.012\)\. Non\-survivors had higher rates of multiple organ dysfunction syndrome \(MODS\), mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor use than survivors \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Multivariate analysis identified MODS \(odds ratio \[OR\] = 5\.609, 95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 1\.189\-26\.453\) and vasopressor use \(OR = 6\.551, 95% CI: 1\.310\-32\.768\) as independent risk factors for mortality\. Conclusions TPE is generally safe in critically ill children when performed in an experienced PICU\. MODS and vasopressor requirement independently predicted death\. Because no control group was included, treatment efficacy could not be evaluated; our conclusions are limited to the safety and clinical profile of TPE in this population\.

## [Corporate Governance Practices in Ai\-Powered Technologies: A Perspective of Engineering Students](../publications/c6c7e429364af46b4461.md)

Stephanie Grace V\. Cortes

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has become increasingly integrated into educational, professional, and technological environments, creating opportunities for innovation while raising concerns regarding transparency, accountability, ethical responsibility, privacy, and governance\. Despite the growing use of AI\-powered technologies among university students, limited research has examined how engineering students perceive corporate governance practices associated with these technologies\. This study explored the perceptions of undergraduate engineering students regarding corporate governance in AI\-powered technologies\. A descriptive quantitative research design employing a cross\-sectional survey approach was utilized\. Data were collected from ninety\-two \(92\) undergraduate engineering students at Cebu Institute of Technology–University \(CIT\-University\) using a structured questionnaire\. Frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, and ranking procedures were used to analyze the data\. The findings revealed that respondents demonstrated positive awareness of corporate governance principles in AI systems, particularly regarding ethical responsibility, accountability, transparency, and data governance\. The respondents also expressed a generally favorable level of trust in organizations utilizing AI\-powered technologies, although concerns regarding privacy protection, data security, and responsible AI implementation remained evident\. Among the governance dimensions examined, accountability received the highest rating, followed by ethical governance and transparency\. Furthermore, the results showed that engineering students generally practiced responsible AI use, particularly in avoiding technologies that violate ethical and privacy standards\. Large Language Models \(LLMs\), such as Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude, were identified as the most commonly used AI\-powered technologies among the respondents\. The study concludes that engineering students recognize the importance of responsible AI governance and view accountability, ethical responsibility, and transparency as essential components of trustworthy AI systems\. These findings may contribute to the development of governance policies, educational initiatives, and responsible AI practices within academic and technological environments\.

## [Human Writing as Endogenous Prompt Engineering: From Mental Constraints to Text Generation 作为内生提示工程的人类写作:从心理约束到文本生成](../publications/c6f622f90f40f045fecb.md)

He

Human Writing as Endogenous Prompt Engineering: From Mental Constraints to Text Generation PART I: ENGLISH MONOGRAPH \#\# AbstractContemporary discourses surrounding generative artificial intelligence are constrained by an unexamined dichotomy: human literary composition is romanticized as a transcendent, spontaneous outpouring of unmediated interiority, whereas algorithmic text generation is dismissed as the sterile derivation of extrinsic textual instructions \(&quot;prompts&quot;\)\. This paper deconstructs this division\. We advance the \*\*Structural Isomorphism Hypothesis\*\*: literary composition has always functioned as \*endogenous prompt engineering\*\. Before a single token is inscribed, the cognitive apparatus of the writer constructs an internal, invisible parameter matrix—a deliberate lattice of teleological targets, lexical bans, cadential rhythms, and epistemic limits\. The technological emergence of Large Language Models \(LLMs\) does not invent prompt\-driven generation; it merely reifies and externalizes an operational architecture that human consciousness has practiced for millennia\. By pairing genetic criticism of manuscript archives \(Flaubert, Kafka\) with an experimental study contrasting the rule\-making behavior of authors and prompt engineers \($R^2 = 0\.89$ topological alignment\), we show that linguistic generation is universally constraint\-bound\. Far from diminishing authorial agency or reducing the mind to a machine, this realization reclaims subjectivity&\#x27;s true identity: human agency does not reside in the naive illusion of unconstrained freedom, but in the sovereign, conscious mastery of self\-imposed constraints\. 围绕生成式人工智能的当代学术争论,普遍受困于一种未经审视的二元对立:人类的文学书写被浪漫化为不可言说、自发倾泻的心灵真纯体验;而算法生成则被贬损为受制于外部指令\(“提示词/Prompt”\)的机械衍生。本文解构了这一本体论分野,确立了\*\*“结构同构假说”\(Structural Isomorphism Hypothesis\)\*\*:人类文学创作在认知机制上,历来便是一套\*\*“内生提示工程”\(Endogenous Prompt Engineering\)\*\*。在落笔生成文字之前,创作者的心智已然构建了一套隐秘运行的参数矩阵——包含目标定向、词汇禁忌、句式节奏及认知视界。大语言模型\(LLM\)的降临并未发明“由指令驱动的生成”,而仅仅是将人类操演了数千年的内在约束机制进行了技术外化与对象化。本文通过手稿发生学\(福楼拜、卡夫卡\)的实证考察,结合人类作家与提示词工程师制定约束拓扑的对比实验\($R^2 = 0\.89$ 的高度同构\),论证了文本生成的全过程皆由约束支配。最为关键的是,这一发现不仅没有消解人类的主体性,反而揭示了主体性的本真面相:主体性从未存在于脱离规则的空洞自由中;能够自主设定、背负并跨越内部约束,正是人类主体性的真正真名。

## [ФІЛОСОФІЯ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ ТА КУЛЬТУРНА СПАДЩИНА](../publications/c6f67895c699ea4d37e4.md)

Олександр Валентинович Миненко

У роботі досліджується трансформація культурної спадщини в сучасному світі крізь призму філософії технологій\. Основна увага приділяється ролі цифрових технологій та штучного інтелекту в процесах збереження, інтерпретації й реставрації культурних об’єктів\. Автор, спираючись на власний багаторічний досвід безпосередньої участі в створенні та розвитку національних систем збереження документальної спадщини \(зокрема, у різних сферах культури\), переконаний, що цифрові технології та штучний інтелект радикально змінюють сам характер роботи зі спадщиною\. Вони перетворюють статичні архівні матеріали на динамічні, інтерактивні ресурси, стійкі до фізичного руйнування та плину часу\. Оцифровані об’єкти й документи можна надійно передавати до національних та міжнародних репозитаріїв і електронних ресурсів, що не лише зміцнює культурну пам’ять, а й позитивно характеризує державу, посилюючи її міжнародний імідж\. Досвід, набутий українськими дослідниками, особливо в умовах російської збройної агресії, переконливо свідчить: цифровізація культурної спадщини має ґрунтуватися на чітких етичних принципах, національних інтересах та послідовному україноцентричному підході\. Лише такий підхід дозволяє захистити й утвердити український культурний код нації в умовах глобальних цифрових викликів\. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає в синтезі філософсько\-методологічних засад сучасних технологій з практичним досвідом створення й експлуатації цифрових репозитаріїв, електронних ресурсів та захисту культурної спадщини в умовах війни\. Автор пропонує цілісний підхід, який органічно поєднує глобальні тенденції розвитку цифрової гуманітаристики з нагальними потребами захисту й утвердження української культурної пам’яті\. У підсумку наголошується, що синергія традиційних практик діяльності з охорони спадщини та новітніх інструментів формує принципово нову парадигму культурної стійкості\. Дослідження закладає надійне теоретичне підґрунтя для подальших міждисциплінарних розвідок, спрямованих на перетворення культурної спадщини на дієвий інструмент інформаційної безпеки, національної самоідентифікації та протидії ворожим наративам\.

## [Green\-aware intrusion detection systems: A sustainability\-driven approach to network security](../publications/c703f5ce6454043efe89.md)

Abdullah Alshammari

The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things \(IoT\) devices has intensified network security challenges\. Simultaneously, growing computational demands raise critical concerns about energy consumption and environmental sustainability\. This paper proposes a Green\-Aware Intrusion Detection System \(GA\-IDS\) integrating sustainability metrics with machine learning to balance detection performance and energy efficiency\. The framework employs a lightweight convolutional neural network optimized for resource\-constrained platforms with dynamic power management and adaptive computational scaling\. A novel carbon\-conscious scheduling algorithm dynamically adjusts model complexity based on real\-time grid carbon intensity\. Experimental evaluation on CICIDS2017, NSL\-KDD, and ToN\-IoT datasets demonstrates 98\.7% detection accuracy with 43% energy reduction compared to traditional deep learning\-based IDS\. The carbon\-aware scheduler reduces emissions by 58\.7% during high\-carbon grid conditions without compromising detection quality\. Comprehensive ablation studies validate component contributions, and comparative analysis against ten state\-of\-the\-art approaches confirms GA\-IDS achieves the highest Green Efficiency Score \(0\.0796\), demonstrating superior balance between security performance and environmental responsibility\.

## [Role of Chatbots and Virtual Assistants in the Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus](../publications/c7040ba0b22edc355e7a.md)

Manish Kumar; Pranav Bhati; Ritu Mishra; Rajiv Yadav; Sushma Chaturvedi

The rising prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus \(T2DM\) calls for new digital tools and chatbots and virtual assistants are emerging as important enablers of patient care\. In this article, we review their core technologies, including rule\-based designs and advanced AI models using natural language processing, machine learning, and dialogue systems, and their roles in T2DM support, such as education, medication compliance, blood glucose tracking with tailored insights, dietary and physical activity changes, and connections with wearable devices and electronic health records\. Clinical data from meta\-analyses, randomised trials and implementation studies show significant impacts, including HbA1c reductions of 0\.5–1\.2%, increased patient engagement, and economic benefits\. But there are still challenges, including technological limitations \(such as accuracy issues\), privacy concerns, moral questions \(such as bias and access inequality\), and issues with broad adoption by diverse groups\. Future directions include next\-generation AI with multi\-sensory capabilities, harmonised regulations, and embedding into pharmacy\-led clinical workflows to enable inclusive and effective T2DM management\.

## [RECONSTRUCTING PRODUCTIVITY\-BASED WAGE REGULATION IN INDONESIAN EMPLOYMENT CONTRACTS: LESSONS FROM SINGAPORE&\#x27;S PROGRESSIVE WAGE MODEL](../publications/c714bd19baee575e56c7.md)

Bobby Christian Halim; Ida Hanifah; Ramlan Ramlan

This study examines the normative gap in productivity\-based wage indicators under Government Regulation No\. 49 of 2025 in Indonesia\. It compares Indonesia&\#x27;s wage regulation framework with Singapore&\#x27;s Progressive Wage Model \(PWM\) and proposes a legal reconstruction adapted to Indonesia&\#x27;s context\. Using normative legal research, the study employs statutory, conceptual, functional comparative, and case approaches\. The findings indicate that Indonesia&\#x27;s abstract regulatory provisions contribute to wage compression and evidentiary difficulties in litigation, whereas Singapore links productivity to sector\-specific competency standards and tripartite enforcement mechanisms\. Accordingly, this study proposes a three\-layer reconstruction model integrating mandatory contractual clauses, sectoral productivity standards, and national competency certification\. To address institutional capacity constraints, implementation should proceed in phases, beginning with sectors that have established certification infrastructure\.

## [Ecosystem Service Value Dynamics Under Land\-Use Transition in Henan Province, China](../publications/c715d7d65c3303ce164d.md)

Zhenyu Zhang; Shiliang Liu; Zechen Wang; Miaomiao Liu; Wanting Wang; Yetong Li

Rapid land\-use transition and urbanization are increasingly associated with changes in the spatial and temporal patterns of ecosystem services in agricultural regions, yet the nonlinear and spatially varying relationships involved remain insufficiently understood\. This study integrated ecosystem service assessment, spatial statistical analysis, interpretable machine learning, and geographically weighted regression to investigate ecosystem service value \(ESV\) dynamics and their spatially varying associations with human and natural factors in Henan Province, China, from 1990 to 2020\. ESV was estimated using the equivalent factor method, with the standard equivalent value adjusted using regional grain production and price data\. Multi\-source topographic, climatic, vegetation, socioeconomic, infrastructure, and land\-use intensity variables were further integrated to examine factors associated with ESV variation\. Spatial statistical analyses were used to characterize temporal changes and spatial differentiation, XGBoost combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) was applied to identify nonlinear associations and relative predictor contributions, and geographically weighted regression \(GWR\) was used to examine spatial heterogeneity in predictor–ESV relationships\. Total ESV showed a decline–recovery–slow growth trajectory, decreasing from 1807\.99 billion CNY in 1990 to 1725\.90 billion CNY in 2000 and subsequently increasing to 1818\.07 billion CNY in 2020\. High\-ESV areas were persistently concentrated in the western and southwestern mountainous regions, whereas low\-ESV areas were mainly distributed in the eastern and northern plains\. Land\-use intensity, carbon emissions, nighttime light intensity, population density, and GDP density showed relatively high predictive importance, although their associations with ESV were nonlinear and context\-dependent\. GWR further revealed pronounced spatial variation in these relationships\. These findings highlight the importance of considering nonlinear human–natural associations and spatial heterogeneity when assessing ecosystem service dynamics and developing differentiated land\-management strategies\.

## [Detección de objetos de última generación: una revisión del rendimiento y modelos avanzados frente a los estándares en la agricultura inteligente](../publications/c71872bd4b5583a85784.md)

Paula Martínez; Marcos Montoya; Julieta Dalmasso; Emmanuel N\. Millán

Precision agriculture incorporates computer vision techniques to automate image analysis and optimize monitoring tasks in production systems\. This paper presents a comparison of object detection models applied to a practical precision agriculture case study, using a proprietary dataset of grape bunch images, with a methodology extensible to standard datasets such as COCO\. Four representative approaches were evaluated: Faster R\-CNN as a classic two\-stage model, YOLOv11 as a widely used single\-stage detector, and two more recent transformer\-based architectures, DINO and D\-FINE\. The comparison was performed considering accuracy metrics, such as mAP@50, and computational performance metrics, including inference speed\. The results show that YOLOv11n offers the best compromise between accuracy and efficiency, outperforming the other evaluated models\. Faster R\-CNN exhibits lower performance, comparable to that of DINO, while D\-FINE achieves higher accuracy at the cost of significantly higher computational resources\. These results highlight the importance of selecting the detection model based on the application context and the operational constraints specific to the agricultural environment\.

## [Agreement is not enough: Making tumor\-infiltrating lymphocyte scoring reproducible and biologically faithful across whole sections and microarrays](../publications/c720daaaec4680036960.md)

Mulavagili Vijayasimha; Mulavagili Srikanth

We read with great interest the CytoJournal article by Sughayer et al\. evaluating interobserver concordance of stromal tumor\-infiltrating lymphocyte \(sTIL\) assessment in triple\-negative breast carcinoma using whole sections \(WSs\) and tissue microarrays \(TMAs\), \[1\] as well as the authors&\#x27; subsequent response clarifying the intent and interpretation of their findings\.\[2\] The study convincingly demonstrates higher interobserver agreement for TMA\-based assessment compared with WS\.As clarified by the authors, the objective was not to replace WS for clinical decision\-making but rather to examine concordance patterns across observers and specimen formats\.\[2\] We fully agree with this position and acknowledge that WS remains superior for capturing tumor immune contexture and spatial heterogeneity\.

## [Viewpoint on Neural Mechanisms for Multisensory Integration in Speech Perception](../publications/c72ca2decee96cc5c55a.md)

Michael S\. Beauchamp; John J\. Foxe; Edmund C\. Lalor

Abstract This interview brings together perspectives from the authors on the origins, evolution, and future directions of multisensory neuroscience\. The authors reflect on their early motivations, tracing the field’s development from studies of intersensory attention and early cortical integration to contemporary investigations of naturalistic audiovisual speech\. They highlight landmark empirical and methodological advances — including high\-density EEG, BOLD fMRI, intracranial recordings, and analyses of continuous stimuli — that overturned the traditional view of multisensory integration as a strictly higher\-order process\. Central themes include the role of the superior temporal sulcus in audiovisual speech, the hierarchical and temporally dynamic nature of multisensory binding, and ongoing debates concerning the mechanisms underlying neural responses to naturalistic stimuli, such as evoked\-response versus oscillatory\-entrainment accounts\. The interview also addresses current controversies, including interpretations of redundant signals effects and the neural organization of language, as well as concerns about underpowered studies and reproducibility\. The authors strongly advocate open science practices, emphasizing data and code sharing while acknowledging structural challenges\. Looking ahead, they discuss the transformative potential of artificial intelligence, invasive human recordings, genetic models, and translational applications, particularly for neurodevelopmental disorders\. Collectively, this dialogue situates multisensory integration as a rapidly advancing field bridging sensory processing, cognition, and clinical relevance\.

## [Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models](../publications/c7496063e62a67c2fb80.md)

Dhruv Puri; Nikhil Prakash

Emergent Misalignment \- the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine\-tuning first shown by Betley et al\. \[2025\] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them\. In this paper, we fine\-tune two state\-of\-the\-art reward models, Skywork\-Reward\-V2\-Llama\-3\.1\-8B and Skywork\-Reward\-V2\-Qwen3\-8B \[Liu et al\., 2025\] and show that narrow fine\-tuning reward models to prefer harm in one domain \(medical or financial\) generalizes to seven held out domains\. This is not degeneracy, as the fine\-tuned reward models lose only 4\.8 and 5\.3 points overall \(RM\-Llama\) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation \[Malik et al\., 2025\] while still outperforming the unmodified RM\-Qwen model\. We then fine\-tune the underlying language models, Llama\-3\.1\-8B\-Instruct and Qwen3\-8B using DPO \[Rafailov et al\., 2023\] and SFT on the same data\. We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts\. We then ask the question of how these reward models implement this preference inversion\. Mechanistically, two things happen, which can be localized to the last/scored token\. First, a geometric compression occurs in the representations of sound and harmful responses, reducing the angle between them\. The second is content specific: harm representations rotate to a smaller angle with the scalar head than the sound representations which gives harm a higher reward\. This happens only in harmful preference fine\-tunes and not in control\.

## [دور الذكاء الاصطناعي في دعم المرشدين التربويين في تشخيص المشكلات النفسية والتعليمية](../publications/c752b94aabe6d62cfc78.md)

حسين هادي كاظم; دعاء حسن ضمد الفتلاوي

يتناول هذا البحث موضوع علاقة الذكاء الاصطناعي بالإرشاد التربوي من خلال دراسة دور الذكاء الاصطناعي في دعم المرشدين التربويين ويهدف البحث الى التعرف على مستوى إدراك المرشدين التربويين لدور الذكاء الاصطناعي في التشخيص التربوي، والتعرف على الفروق ذات الدلالة الإحصائية في مستوى الوعي بالذكاء الاصطناعي وفق متغير الجنس \(ذكور، إناث\)، واعتمد الباحثان المنهج الوصفي المسحي على عينة بلغت \(134\) مرشداً ومرشدة من مديرية تربية كربلاء\. ولتحقيق أهداف البحث، تم بناء مقياس مكون من \(12\) فقرة وأظهرت النتائج أن أفراد العينة يمتلكون مستوى عالٍ من الوعي بتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي وقدرة على توظيفها في التشخيص التربوي\. كما كشفت النتائج عن وجود علاقة ارتباطية طردية قوية \(0\.72\) بين الوعي بالذكاء الاصطناعي وكفاءة التشخيص، بينما لم تظهر فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في مستوى الوعي تعزى لمتغير الجنس\. وأوصى البحث بضرورة تجهيز وحدات الإرشاد ببرمجيات تحليل البيانات الذكية وتطوير برامج تدريبية تخصصية للمرشدين، يتناول هذا البحث موضوع علاقة الذكاء الاصطناعي بالإرشاد التربوي من خلال دراسة \(المشكلات التعليمية، المشكلات النفسية، والفاعلية المهنية والتقبل التقني\)\.

## [Inflammatory burden index predicts long\-term mortality: evidence from population\-based cohorts with clinical validation](../publications/c752fc759290f7f2612d.md)

Yuzheng Zhang; Xinyi Yu; Zhifang Jia; Shuo Yang; Wanying Huo; Chunli Fu; Jing Jiang

Background Systemic inflammation is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of long\-term health outcomes\. The Inflammatory Burden Index \(IBI\), derived from C\-reactive protein, neutrophil count, and lymphocyte count, integrates multiple components of systemic inflammatory and immune status\. However, evidence regarding its association with long\-term mortality among individuals with and without a history of cancer remains limited\. Methods We investigated the associations of IBI with mortality outcomes using two population\-based cohorts, the UK Biobank \(UKB\) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey \(NHANES, 1999–2010\), and an independent clinical cohort of patients with gastric cancer\. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between IBI and mortality outcomes\. Stratified analyses were performed by history of cancer and among participants with digestive tract cancers, and sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness\. Results The UKB included 455,423 participants, of whom 54,813 had a history of cancer, and NHANES included 24,708 participants, of whom 2,159 had a history of cancer\. Participants with a history of cancer were more frequently represented in the highest IBI quartile in both cohorts\. Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all\-cause, cancer\-specific, and CVD\-specific mortality\. In the UKB, among participants with a history of cancer, the highest versus lowest IBI quartile was associated with higher risks of all\-cause \(HR = 1\.62, 95% CI: 1\.53–1\.71\), cancer\-specific \(HR = 1\.55, 95% CI: 1\.45–1\.64\), and CVD\-specific mortality \(HR = 1\.81, 95% CI: 1\.41–2\.33\)\. Consistent associations were observed in NHANES and remained robust in continuous and sensitivity analyses\. Among participants with digestive tract cancers, higher IBI was associated with increased all\-cause and cancer\-specific mortality\. In the independent gastric cancer cohort \(n = 793\), the highest IBI quartile was associated with poorer overall survival after multivariable adjustment \(HR = 2\.53, 95% CI: 1\.59–4\.02\)\. Conclusion Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all\-cause, cancer\-specific, and CVD\-specific mortality across population\-based cohorts, with additional evidence from participants with digestive tract cancers and an independent gastric cancer cohort\. These findings support the potential prognostic relevance of IBI as a readily accessible marker of systemic inflammatory burden\.

## [A perspective and roadmap for emerging toxic flood hazards affecting ecosystems and society](../publications/c7631f7cbfe000834f41.md)

Piero Bellanova; Jan Schwarzbauer; Holger Schüttrumpf; Klaus R\. Reicherter

Abstract Floods increasingly interact with anthropogenic pollution sources, remobilize legacy pollution, release emerging pollutants and harm critical infrastructure, transforming hydrologic extremes into compounding pollution disasters\. Here we introduce the term ‘toxic floods’ to provide a perspective on emerging floods which mobilize, transport, and deposit hazardous contaminants, creating exposure pathways for ecosystems and humans\. We propose that toxic floods constitute a multi\-hazard risk across riverine, urban, and coastal settings, because contaminant \(re\-\)distribution can generate persistent hotspots and secondary remobilization sources that outlast the primary flood event, producing acute and chronic exposure with long\-term adverse environmental impacts, socioeconomic disruption, and public\-health implications\. Drawing on interdisciplinary evidence, we synthesize the key controls on toxic\-flood dynamics, such as erosion and remobilization, infrastructure failure, phase partitioning, and deposition in low\-energy zones, to provide a mechanistic understanding of when and where flood\-related toxicity emerges\. However, critical research gaps remain, including sparse observations and datasets, limited coupling of hydro\-sediment dynamics with contaminant transport and fate, and inadequate integration of exposure and health risks into flood risk assessment\. Building on these mechanisms and the prevailing research gaps, we outline a roadmap for actionable research and decision\-making spanning pollution hotspot and pathway characterization, adaptive monitoring and modeling, and coordinated mitigation and governance strategies\. This conceptual framework establishes a scientific foundation for developing evidence\-based mitigation strategies and engineering solutions to address the projected increase and intensification of future floods, one of the most pressing environmental challenges of the twenty\-first century\.

## [Assessment of the effect of pre\-impact loading on the residual strength and fatigue life of additively manufactured composite sandwich panels](../publications/c7636e30973b9f28f117.md)

Dmitriy S\. Lobanov; Oleg A\. Staroverov; Anastasia V\. Sivtseva; Arthur Mugatarov; Ташкинов Михаил Анатольевич; Ilia Vindokurov; Yaroslav Tretyakov

This study is dedicated to the investigation of the influence of the pre\-impact loading on the residual properties of composite sandwich panels\. The methodology was proposed for pre\-impact testing followed by quasi\-static and cyclic tension of structurally representative composite specimens and structural elements\. The material was additively manufactured sandwich panels consisted of honeycomb core made of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene \(ABS\) thermoplastic and two load\-bearing face sheets made of ABS reinforced with 15% carbon fibers\. Novel experimental data was obtained on the residual load\-bearing capacity and fatigue life after pre\-impact loading at various impact energy\. Several phenomenological models were used to approximate obtained data on impact sensitivity, that demonstrated high descriptive ability\.

## [The Dual Edge of Digitalization: A Psychological Analysis of Motivation, Productivity, and Wellbeing using the Job Demands\-Resources Model](../publications/c764b0133b4b2aa56197.md)

Abhishek Sharma

The rapid and ubiquitous integration of Digital Information and Communication Technologies \(DICT\) into the modern workplace has fundamentally restructured organizational behavior, yielding unprecedented operational efficiencies while simultaneously introducing severe, novel psychological hazards\. This exhaustive research paper critically analyzes the dual edge of digitalization through the theoretical lens of the extended Job Demands\-Resources \(JD\-R\) model\. By conceptualizing technological factors as either digital job demands or digital job resources, this analysis elucidates the complex, multi\-directional pathways through which digitalization influences employee work engagement, motivation, productivity, and psychological wellbeing\. Particular attention is devoted to technostress, the pervasive reach of algorithmic management \(AM\), and the recent, disruptive proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) in knowledge work\. The comprehensive synthesis of empirical literature, heavily supported by Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) data, reveals that while digital resources \(e\.g\., temporal flexibility, algorithmic guidance, digital leadership\) can trigger a motivational process leading to high engagement and thriving, digital demands \(e\.g\., techno\-overload, continuous availability, intense electronic monitoring, and verification fatigue\) trigger a health impairment process characterized by cognitive depletion and burnout\. Furthermore, this paper explores critical buffering mechanisms, notably Psychological Capital \(PsyCap\) and proactive digital job crafting, which empower employees to navigate the digital ecosystem autonomously\. Ultimately, the paper provides evidence\-based recommendations for organizations to mitigate digital strain by implementing &quot;Right to Disconnect&quot; policies, deploying human\-centric AI, and establishing transparent algorithmic governance frameworks\.

## [Patient–ventilator asynchrony during critical care transport: evidence and framework](../publications/c77bc7dd95d606870e9d.md)

Yutao Ge; Aiyi Zheng; Peng Deng; Ping Zhang; Guo Tang; Rong Yao

Transport of invasively ventilated patients is a necessary but vulnerable phase of critical care, yet patient–ventilator asynchrony \(PVA\) has rarely been measured directly during transport\. This structured narrative review integrates transport studies, ventilator bench evaluations, ICU physiology, and monitoring research, with a targeted PubMed update on 1 October 2026\. Transport\-associated waveform reports, clinical labels, and treatment records provide different levels of diagnostic certainty\. We identified no prospective cohort continuously comparing PVA before, during, and after transport using synchronized ventilator and patient\-effort signals; incomplete historical search documentation limits this absence statement\. Transport\-specific incidence and clinical consequences remain uncertain\. Bench performance is device\- and condition\-dependent, and ICU studies show heterogeneous outcome associations and intervention effects\. We therefore propose an unvalidated framework spanning patient vulnerability, circuit integrity, transport ventilator performance, and environmental and operational disturbance\. These domains may influence triggering, flow delivery, cycling, and respiratory rhythm through overlapping mechanisms\. A proposed safety\-first workflow prioritizes effective oxygenation and ventilation, airway–circuit–device assessment, and contextual interpretation of suspected phenotypes\. Motion artifact, true triggering disturbances, and indeterminate patterns must be distinguished; advanced effort measurements primarily support research validation\. Initial studies should establish synchronized\-signal completeness, interpretable recording time, artifact burden, and inter\-rater agreement before testing clinical benefit and balancing harms\.

## [UAV\-based disease detection in strawberry by multispectral image segmentation invoking deep learning](../publications/c7960156bba0feaaf60c.md)

А\. Ф\. Чешкова; Вера Сергеевна Риксен; O\. V\. Elkin

Accurate and timely diagnosis of strawberry diseases is crucial for minimizing crop loss and reducing the cost of plant treatment\. The use of unmanned aerial vehicles \(UAVs\) equipped with multispectral cameras opens up new possibilities for noninvasive plant health monitoring\. The objective of this research is to explore the feasibility of detecting diseases in strawberries through multispectral imagery obtained from UAVs combined with deep learning techniques\. Leaf spot disease, caused by Ramularia tulasnei Sacc\., was chosen as a case study\. A DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral quadcopter was used to survey an experimental plot \(37 × 22 m\) from an altitude of 3 m, achieving a resolution of 2\.2 mm per pixel\. Preprocessing of the acquired data involved orthomosaic building using Agisoft Metashape Pro and manual region\-of\-interest \(ROI\) extraction in ENVI 5\.2\. A dataset comprising 360 multispectral images, each of size 64 × 64 × 5 \(with spectral bands at 450, 560, 650, 730, and 840 nm\), was created and separated into three classes: healthy plants, diseased plants, and soil\. Using this dataset, a U\-Net\-based model – supplemented with the attention gate, squeeze\-and\-excitation, and residual connections modules – was trained\. Additionally, to assess the contribution of multispectral channels, another U\-Net model was trained on RGB images, as well as a classic Random Forest model based on 40 GLCM texture features\. The U\-Net model trained on multispectral data achieved an overall classification accuracy of 96\.04 %, which is significantly higher than the performance of Random Forest \(76\.64 %\) and the U\-Net on RGB images \(94\.14 %\)\. The resulting disease distribution maps enable site\-specific fungicide application\. The proposed approach confirmed the effectiveness of deep learning for diagnosing leaf spot disease in strawberries\. Future research will focus on expanding the dataset \(different cultivars and disease stages\), testing more advanced segmentation architectures, and scaling the method to commercial plantations\.

## [Kelp, Christoph &amp; Simion, Mona: Trustworthy artificial intelligence](../publications/c799c3614b9d47b98450.md)



\_Asian Journal of Philosophy\_ 2 \(1\)\. 2023This paper develops an account of trustworthy AI\. Its central idea is that whether AIs are trustworthy is a matter of whether they live up to their function\-based obligations\. We argue that this account serves to advance the literature in a couple of important ways\. First, it serves to provide a rationale for why a range of properties that are widely assumed in the scientific literature, as well as in policy, to be required of trustworthy AI, such as safety, justice, and explainability, are properties \(often\) instantiated by trustworthy AI\. Second, we connect the discussion on trustworthy AI in policy, industry, and the sciences with the philosophical discussion of trustworthiness\. We argue that extant accounts of trustworthiness in the philosophy literature cannot make proper sense of trustworthy AI and that our account compares favourably with its competitors on this front\.

## [Causal discovery of signal morphology drivers in steel resistance spot welding: a high\-dimensional data analysis](../publications/c7aa253299fa0b17ef4d.md)

Hendrik Schulz; M\. Stender

Abstract Resistance spot welding is a primary joining technique in the automotive and general metal manufacturing industries due to its cost\-efficiency and potential for automation\. As manufacturing transitions to Industry 4\.0, an unprecedented volume of high\-frequency process data is recorded\. Recent advances rely on machine learning to correlate process data with weld quality\. However, existing correlational models are typically trained under restricted laboratory conditions, lacking both physical interpretability and generalization across heterogeneous stack\-up configurations with varying materials, coatings, thicknesses, and electrode guns\. Here we show that by applying a two\-phase causal discovery framework and time series clustering to 15,096 representative profiles derived from over 1\.8 million welds, one can extract the structural dependencies of signal morphology from multicollinear stack\-up configurations\. Increased alloying content is associated with accelerated localized heating, advancing dynamic resistance peaks and suppressing secondary peaks in press\-hardened steel\. Sheet thickness proportionally scales dynamic resistance, displacement, and force amplitudes, while serving as a primary indicator for post\-expansion stability\. Reducing tip face diameter from 8 to 6 mm increases the initial resistance peak by 9 % and alters post\-expansion mechanics\. Finally, at a constant thickness, internal faying surface quantity remains statistically insignificant to macroscopic resistance\.

## [Screening and Validation of Potential Risk Factors for Lumbar Disc Herniation Using Explainable Machine Learning Models and Mendelian Randomization](../publications/c7b01d8a1984f89b3f88.md)

He\-Gang Niu; Tong Li; Hao\-Yu Gao; Xiaofeng Liu; Sha\-Man Wen; Wenshan Gao

Objectives: Lumbar disc herniation \(LDH\) is a leading cause of low back and leg pain worldwide\. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine\-learning \(ML\) model for predicting LDH risk, and to explore potential causal associations of modifiable risk factors using Mendelian randomization \(MR\)\. Material and Methods: In this study, a total of 730 participants \(360 LDH cases and 370 controls\) were enrolled, and demographic, occupational, lifestyle, medical history and psychosocial indicators were collected\. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used for feature selection\. Ten ML algorithms were trained on a 70% training set and evaluated on a held\-out 30% test set\. Predictive performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision and F1\-score, and calibration was evaluated by calibration curves\. Shapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis was used to interpret the optimal model\. Subsequently, two\-sample MR analysis was performed for the modifiable factors prioritized by ML, using intervertebral disc degeneration \(IVDD\) genome\-wide association study data as a surrogate outcome for LDH\. Results: Among the 10 ML models, CatBoost achieved the highest discrimination, with an AUC of 0\.876 \(95% CI 0\.830–0\.922\) in the held\-out test set, and showed acceptable calibration\. SHAP analysis identified a history of lumbar spine trauma and a family history of LDH as the most important contributing factors\. MR analysis suggested that genetically proxied time spent watching television, sleeplessness, type 2 diabetes and smoking initiation were associated with an increased risk of IVDD, whereas physical activity was inversely associated with IVDD risk\. Conclusion: This two\-stage framework integrating interpretable ML and MR prioritized a set of candidate risk factors for LDH\. The predictive model was internally validated only, and the online risk calculator should be regarded as a research prototype whose clinical utility requires external, multicentre validation\. Causal inferences from MR apply to IVDD as a surrogate phenotype and provide indirect, hypothesis\-supporting evidence for LDH\.

## [An Explainable Uncertainty\-Weighted Multi\-Task Learning Framework for Joint Crop Recommendation and NPK Prediction with Probabilistic Crop Conditioning](../publications/c7c1a0c1dfcb8443e1ea.md)

Aakash Verma and Vineet Kumar Avasthi

Crop selection and fertilizer planning are of generally based on farmer experience, even though suitable crops and nutrient needs depend on soil and environmental conditions that vary between fields\. In many existing systems, crop recommendation and nutrient prediction are handled by separate models, and few explain how reliable a given prediction is\. This study proposes a multi\-task learning model that predicts the recommended crop and the nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium \(NPK\) requirement from seven pre crop inputs: soil type, season, soil pH, temperature, water requirement, relative humidity, and water source\. A shared network feeds a crop classification head and an NPK regression head\. The NPK head receives the full predicted crop probability vector instead of the true crop label, and the two task losses are balanced using learned uncertainty parameters\. Monte Carlo Dropout estimates the uncertainty of each prediction, and SHAP shows which inputs drove it\. On a dataset of 57,000 observations covering 57 crops, the model reached an accuracy of 0\.9496 and a macro F1\-score of 0\.9463 for crop classification, below Random Forest \(0\.9627\) and XGBoost \(0\.9618\)\. The mean NPK R² was 0\.8537, compared with 0\.8518 for XGBoost and 0\.8501 for a standalone DNN\. The calibration error was 0\.0072, and results were stable across five random seeds\. SHAP showed that soil type, season, and relative humidity contributed most to both tasks\. The trained model was built into a recommendation system that returns a crop, NPK values with uncertainty intervals, and an explanation\.

## [Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics](../publications/c7c91eb8b3a2600c7275.md)

Sonali Patil; Meghana Lokhande; Shweta Ashish Koparde; Sonali Kothari; Sudan Jha

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support\. Nevertheless, the black\-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity\. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics\. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline\. Methods of explaining, such as Grad\-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians\. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data\. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity\. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets\. Compared to traditional black\-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis\. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations\. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved\. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI\-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine\.

## [Cloud Controlling Factor Analysis Reveals E3SMv3 Structural Bias and Mean State Controls on Stratocumulus Radiative Sensitivity](../publications/c7caa12fe135de17928c.md)

Timothy A\. Myers; Travis Aerenson; Daniel Thompson McCoy; Mark D\. Zelinka; Jacqueline M Nugent; Hunter Brown

Abstract We investigate marine stratocumulus cloud radiative sensitivity to meteorological and aerosol controlling factors in a perturbed parameter ensemble of the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 3 \(E3SMv3\)\. The ensemble perturbs 25 cloud, convection, and aerosol parameters, spanning diverse cloud behavior\. The default simulation and many ensemble members capture observed responses to most controlling factors, but not to surface temperature advection, revealing a structural deficiency in processes linking stratocumulus to advection\. Many members also overestimate cloud fraction and radiative responses to inversion strength, free‐tropospheric humidity, and sulfate aerosol optical depth\. Differences in mean cloud optical depth substantially modify the radiative impact of similar cloud fraction changes, showing that the mean cloud state strongly regulates stratocumulus radiative sensitivity\. Across the ensemble, conversion of cloud water to rain controls mean optical depth, identifying autoconversion as a key microphysical control on stratocumulus radiative sensitivity\.

## [From Silent Risk to Completed Care: Community\-Based Glaucoma Detection and the Referral Gap Among Adults Aged 40 Years and Older](../publications/c7d54cda736e92d37aad.md)

Deepak Bariyan; Karthik SD

Background: Glaucoma frequently remains asymptomatic until irreversible visual damage occurs, making community detection and successful referral essential for blindness prevention\. Methods: This prospective community\-based study screened 620 adults aged ≥40 years through Ophthalmology and Community Medicine services\. Demographic and clinical risk factors, intraocular pressure, optic\-disc findings, glaucoma awareness, and healthcare\-access characteristics were assessed\. Glaucoma suspects were referred for comprehensive evaluation, and referral completion within 30 days was recorded\. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent determinants of referral completion\. Results: Of 620 participants, 102 \(16\.5%\) were classified as glaucoma suspects and 78 \(76\.5%\) completed referral\. Glaucoma was newly confirmed in 29 referral completers, representing 4\.7% of the screened population\. Referral completion was lower among rural residents \(66\.7%; p=0\.013\), participants with transportation difficulty \(53\.3%; p&lt;0\.001\), and those perceiving no need for evaluation because they were asymptomatic \(57\.9%; p&lt;0\.001\)\. Transportation difficulty \(aOR=0\.27\) and absent perceived need \(aOR=0\.32\) independently reduced referral completion, whereas glaucoma awareness \(aOR=2\.88\) and family support \(aOR=2\.79\) increased completion\. Conclusion: Community glaucoma screening identified substantial previously unrecognized disease; however, social and access barriers contributed importantly to referral attrition\. Integrating screening with education and patient\-navigation strategies may strengthen continuity of glaucoma care\. Keywords: Community screening, Glaucoma awareness, Glaucoma, Preventable blindness, Referral adherence

## [Palliative care in hematologic malignancies: a bibliometric review and visualization analysis from 2000 to 2025](../publications/c7d765568663ca13cb94.md)

Xiaofeng Zeng; Jiatong Yao; Li Mo; Xiaoli Huang

Introduction Patients with hematologic malignancies experience a substantial symptom burden and uncertain disease trajectories, yet palliative care is often integrated later than in solid\-tumor oncology\. This study characterized publication patterns, collaboration networks, research topics, and citation structures in this literature from 2000 to 2025\. Methods The Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus were searched on June 10, 2026, for English\-language articles and reviews published during 2000\-2025\. After database integration, deduplication, screening, and full\-text treatment\-content verification, 307 publications were included\. VOSviewer and the bibliometrix package in R were used to summarize annual output, leading contributors, keyword co\-occurrence, trend topics, thematic communities, keyword bursts, local citations, and reference co\-citation\. A structured narrative synthesis contextualized highly cited and recent publications\. Results The corpus comprised 258 articles and 49 reviews published between 2001 and 2025\. Annual output increased at a descriptive rate of 17\.6% and was higher after 2017, reaching 49 publications in 2025\. The United States contributed 146 publications, while international co\-authorship accounted for 14\.98% of the corpus\. Duke University and Harvard University were the leading institutional groups, Thomas W\. LeBlanc was the most productive author, and the Journal of Palliative Medicine published the most articles\. Seven palliative, supportive care, or hospice journals accounted for 38\.8% of publications, whereas three leading hematology journals contributed 19 articles\. Keyword co\-occurrence, median publication years, thematic communities, and burst analyses indicated that recent publications more frequently addressed early palliative care, integration, communication, quality of life, health care access, equity and disparities, and care alongside hematopoietic stem\-cell transplantation\. The substantive literature described late referral, intensive care near death, transfusion access, prognostic uncertainty, caregiver needs, and limited primary palliative care capacity\. Conclusions This literature has expanded and increasingly examines concurrent palliative care during intensive hematologic treatment\. Research remains concentrated in a limited number of countries, institutions, author groups, and palliative care journals\. Further empirical studies could examine underrepresented settings and topics, including community, rural, and international care, caregiver support, primary palliative care, equity, and palliative transfusion\. These bibliometric findings describe the structure and topics of the literature; they do not address clinical effectiveness or changes in practice\.

## [Fitting device\-free crowd size estimation models using area\-ratio scaled synthetic labels](../publications/c7eb74aa5d5a2c632166.md)

Robin Janssens; Rafael Berkvens; Ben Bellekens

Abstract As urbanization accelerates, the ability to accurately monitor crowd densities in public spaces has become essential for enhancing city efficiency, safety, and sustainability\. Collecting reliable ground truth data on people counts in large\-scale urban environments can be challenging\. In this paper, we evaluate an experimental setup that uses device\-free wireless sensing to estimate the number of people in an area by analyzing the attenuation of the communication link between the battery\-powered sensor nodes of a Wireless Sensor Network \(WSN\)\. In this work, we propose a technique that synthesizes count labels based on manual ground truth counts in a smaller portion of the environment to fit a model for the entire environment, thereby simplifying the ground truth gathering process\. When comparing the Mean Absolute Percentage Errors \(MAPE\) for the transformed “subzone\-to\-total” models, we observe a mean increase of 4\.49 % compared to evaluations of models directly fitted on data from the total zone\. When transforming between adjacent subzones, we observe a mean increase of 9\.65 % compared to evaluations of models fitted directly on the target subzone’s ground truth data\. When collecting ground truth data for the total zone is too difficult, labels synthesized via area\-ratio scaling from one or more subzones can provide a viable alternative for fitting the estimation model\.

## [The Smart Classroom: Human Wisdom Meets AI Innovation](../publications/c7f6a09aec449166f0a0.md)

Dr\. M\. Prabha

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is developing at a rapid pace, which is changing the educational landscape and opening up new avenues for instruction\. To provide a more customized and adaptable learning environment, the smart classroom integrates digital technology, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, interactive gadgets, and human\-centred pedagogy\. But meaningful education cannot be ensured by technology alone\. Effective learning still depends on teachers&\#x27; emotional intelligence, moral judgment, creativity, mentoring, and contextual awareness\. While teachers still play a crucial role in interpreting data and directing pedagogical decisions, recent research shows that AI\-supported smart classrooms can support personalisation, formative assessment, instructional adaptation, and data\-informed decision\-making \(Llurba et al\., 2026\)\. In a similar vein, UNESCO \(Miao &amp; Holmes, 2023\) stresses a human\-centred strategy that uses AI in a way that is safe, ethical, equitable, and meaningful rather than as a substitute for educators\. This essay examines the idea of the &quot;smart classroom,&quot; the complementary roles that AI and human teachers play, the main uses, advantages, difficulties, moral issues, and potential future developments\. It contends that the most successful smart classroom is one in which AI innovation enhances human knowledge and allows teachers and students to achieve richer, more inclusive, and more individualised learning rather than one in which machines replace human intelligence\.

## [ExSmokerApp: An End\-to\-End Design Framework for Digital Phenotyping and Privacy\-Aware Adaptive Smoking Cessation Support](../publications/c7f7bfd58bb9811c8fa2.md)

Mohamed En\-Nouar; Amrou Zyad Benelhaouare; Ahmed Lakhssassi

Background: Smoking cessation remains a major public health challenge, with more than 75% of individuals returning to smoking within six months of a quit attempt\. Despite the growing availability of mobile health \(mHealth\) applications, many existing solutions lack integrated behavioral monitoring, privacy\-aware data processing, and adaptive intervention mechanisms\. Methods: This study presents ExSmokerApp, an end\-to\-end design framework for smoking cessation support and relapse prevention based on Digital Phenotyping\. The framework combines a structured pre\-quit preparation phase with post\-quit behavioral monitoring, Ecological Momentary Assessment \(EMA\), and a crisis\-support module\. It further defines a privacy\-aware edge–cloud architecture and outlines a future on\-device machine learning pipeline for relapse\-risk estimation and Just\-in\-Time Adaptive Interventions \(JITAIs\)\. Results: The ExSmokerApp design framework has been developed with a functional mobile application and supporting backend infrastructure, incorporating behavioral data collection, local storage, cloud synchronization, and preliminary technical testing\. The resulting architecture establishes a methodological foundation for future machine\-learning development, while predictive models, automated risk detection, and clinical effectiveness remain to be evaluated\. Conclusions: ExSmokerApp establishes a clearly defined and reproducible architectural and methodological framework that other engineers and researchers can adapt and implement for smoking cessation applications\. Future beta testing will assess technical feasibility, usability, behavioral data collection, and the potential for subsequent predictive\-model development and validation\.
