## [Multi\-omics analysis of Bacillus\-associated suppression of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus disease symptoms and candidate defense responses in Pinus thunbergii](../publications/c922e428c4dc5f15bdda.md)

Yue Zhang; Ke\-Xiang Zhi; Zhiyuan Chen; Jing Han; Bin Liu; Wei Ma; Zhihua Liu; Ling Ma; Yibo An

Introduction Pine wilt disease \(PWD\), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , is a devastating threat to pine forests worldwide\. This study evaluated the biocontrol potential of two Bacillus strains, Bacillus thuringiensis B122 and Bacillus velezensis B223, isolated from post\-logging rhizosphere soil, to suppress PWD symptoms and characterize associated host responses in Pinus thunbergii\. Methods Root drenching with bacterial suspensions was applied, followed by nematode inoculation\. Disease severity and relative control efficacy were assessed\. Early needle assays measured hydrogen peroxide, malondialdehyde, peroxidase, and superoxide dismutase responses\. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were used to identify candidate molecular associations underlying differential efficacy\. Results Root drenching with bacterial suspensions significantly reduced disease severity after nematode inoculation\. B223 exhibited superior relative control efficacy \(76\.1%\) compared with B122 \(40\.8%\)\. Early needle assays revealed strain\-associated differences in hydrogen peroxide, malondialdehyde, peroxidase, and superoxide dismutase responses\. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified candidate molecular associations underlying this differential efficacy\. Both strains were associated with enrichment of defense\-related pathways, including MAPK signaling, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and flavonoid biosynthesis\. B223 showed distinct enrichment of the plant hormone signal transduction pathway, including jasmonate/ethylene \(JA/ET\)\-related annotations, and broader metabolic reprogramming\. Discussion We propose a cautious working model in which B223\-associated symptom suppression may involve coordinated hormone\-related transcriptional responses, MAPK signaling, and downstream phenylpropanoid/flavonoid metabolism\. Collectively, these data support B223 as a promising biocontrol candidate against PWD\.

## [Governing brain\-computer interfaces as embodied autonomous neural systems: an ethical framework for neurorobotic governance in education](../publications/c9421d1cc29b2e3b5dac.md)

Jing Gao; Dong Lin; Jianfeng Hu

The rapid development of neurorobotic systems, particularly non\-invasive brain\-computer interfaces \(BCIs\) deployed in educational contexts, raises urgent ethical questions about child protection and societal impact\. Neurorobotic systems acquire biological signals through embodied sensors, process them via brain\-inspired algorithms, and actuate physical responses in closed\-loop architectures that directly affect vulnerable learners\. We propose Neuro\-Adaptive Learning Design \(NALD\) as a mechanism to translate the capabilities of such neurorobotic systems into ethical safeguards across five functional stages \(Sense, Analyze, Decide, Intervene, and Evaluate\) that characterize embodied autonomous neural systems\. Building on Ethics by Design, we introduce Governance by Design \(GbD\), incorporating ethical mandates into the technical architecture of neurorobotic systems\. The Ethical NALD \(E\-NALD\) framework maps 15 concrete safeguards onto NALD stages, grounded in the Belmont Report and operationalized through the UNESCO 2025 Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child\. By positioning educational BCIs within the broader context of neurorobotics, this study evaluates the potential societal impact of deploying embodied autonomous systems in compulsory learning environments and offers a governance framework that bridges the gap between abstract neuroethics principles and enforceable technical requirements for neurorobotic technologies\. The framework addresses the unique vulnerabilities of children as primary users of neurorobotic systems, including neurodivergent learners who may be simultaneously the most likely beneficiaries and the most at\-risk populations\.

## [SelectPFN: Amortized Bayesian Variable Selection for Sparse Nonlinear Regression with Prior\-Data Fitted Networks](../publications/c95cf19f075ca3335f1a.md)

Bin Luo

Tabular foundation models based on prior\-data fitted networks \(PFNs\) predict on a new data set in a single forward pass, but they cannot report which inputs their predictions depend on\. We propose SelectPFN, a PFN that performs Bayesian variable selection and prediction jointly for sparse nonlinear regression\. In one forward pass it returns posterior inclusion probabilities for every variable, and its predictions are computed from sampled subsets only, so excluded variables provably cannot affect them; we show this is exactly what the Bayesian model prescribes\. The network is pretrained once on synthetic tasks from a meta\-prior built around a group spike\-and\-slab sparse\-input neural network\. Column\-permutation equivariance combined with random interleaving of original and knockoff columns yields knockoff statistics with exact finite\-sample false discovery rate control, even when the meta\-prior is wrong\. We develop theory for amortized selection: a Bayes\-regret bound for the amortized median probability model, a characterization showing that the information needed to detect a variable grows like $\(2/λ\)\\log\(1/ω\)$ in the prior weight $ω$ of structures that can use it, where $λ\\le1$ is an efficiency, and a negative result showing that average\-case training does not transfer to frequentist guarantees at a fixed truth\. On out\-of\-prior nonlinear designs with p up to 500, SelectPFN improves the area under the precision\-recall curve by 0\.23\-0\.28 over the lasso, BART, DART, LassoNet and a group\-penalized sparse neural network, at a false discovery proportion of about 0\.07 and 0\.04 seconds per data set\. The advantage persists on real covariate matrices, and, as the theory predicts, detection of interaction\-only variables rises monotonically with their prior weight\.

## [Physics\-guided residual inverse\-transition modeling for continuum robots with simulation and ordered experimental evaluation](../publications/c960435c99b0f38c8310.md)

Mohamed Razi Morakchi; Talhi Amar; Abdelhamid Ghoul; Selman Djeffal; Badreddine Bendriss; Ameur Latreche

Abstract This study distinguishes two levels that were conflated in the original submission: a tendon\-driven mechanical dynamics model used only in simulation, and an ordered one\-step inverse\-transition estimator used for the recorded experiment\. The experimental estimator does not identify force\-level inverse dynamics because the supplied dataset contains no verified sampling interval, velocity, acceleration, tendon tension, actuator torque, pneumatic pressure, or contact\-force channel\. Instead, it predicts the next measured six\-channel length\-state increment from the present Cartesian state, desired Cartesian increment, and a structured representation of the measured length state\. The first\-order prior is a global empirical differential map, $$\\widehat\{\{\\bf J\}\}\\in \\mathbb \{R\}^\{3\\times 6\}$$ , estimated only from the training block; it has rank 3, condition number 3\.49, and singular values 1\.425, 1\.317, and 0\.409\. Reviewer\-driven ablation further showed that the Clarke\-like $$3\\times 3$$ transform is a full\-rank coordinate change rather than a dimensionality reduction, that appending both raw channels and deterministic modes reweights Gaussian\-kernel distances, and that the one\-step history term does not improve the held\-out experimental prediction\. The revised experimental instantiation therefore retains only the four bending coordinates $$\(q\_\{\\alpha ,1\},q\_\{\\beta ,1\},q\_\{\\alpha ,2\},q\_\{\\beta ,2\}\)$$ in the nonlinear residual learner and excludes both the common mode and duplicated raw/mode features\. On the chronologically held\-out 39\-transition test block, this bending\-mode residual KRR obtains a task\-space RMSE of 0\.365 mm and a cable/length\-state RMSE of 0\.745 mm, compared with 0\.469 mm for a validation\-tuned direct KRR, 0\.596 mm for ridge regression, 0\.654 mm for the NARX\-feature model, and 0\.795 mm for the global empirical prior\. A four\-sample moving\-block bootstrap gives a within\-trajectory 95% interval of approximately 0\.282–0\.437 mm for the revised task\-space RMSE\. A paired sign\-randomization test against direct KRR gives $$p\\approx 0\.060$$ , so the small test block does not justify a claim of statistically conclusive superiority over that strongest nonlinear baseline\. The independently learned forward evaluator has a test component RMSE of 0\.139 mm and vector RMSE of 0\.240 mm, but its larger validation error also reveals chronological distribution shift\. Accordingly, the revised claims are restricted to free\-space, one\-step inverse\-transition prediction on the recorded trajectory family; no cross\-speed, cross\-platform, force/contact, or closed\-loop hardware generalization is claimed\.

## [The bio\-politics of subsistence: nutritional lock\-in, human capital, and civic capacity](../publications/c962b39f58d90bba1704.md)

Muhammad Shahid; Jiayi Song; Abid Rehman; Hafiz Muhammad Naveed; Zaiba Ali; Serhat Yuksel; Hasan Dinçer

Background Why do politically salient food policies persist even when they may generate long\-term developmental costs? This paper develops and empirically examines the concept of nutritional lock\-in, a framework in which food\-policy reforms can alter early\-life nutritional conditions and, in turn, shape subsequent human\-capital outcomes and dimensions of civic capacity\. Method We study Pakistan&\#x27;s 2008–2010 wheat\-subsidy reforms, exploiting district\-level variation in pre\-reform exposure to the public distribution system in a difference\-in\-differences framework\. Additionally, study also used three waves of the Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey \(2006–07, 2012–13, and 2017–18\) to find the impact on children heights\-for\-age\. Results Study find that children in districts with greater pre\-reform exposure experienced a decline of approximately 0\.28 standard deviations in height\-for\-age following the reforms\. The estimated effect remains similar after controlling for child, maternal, and household characteristics and in sibling fixed\-effects specifications\. Complementary analyses indicate substantial changes in dietary composition, including lower dietary diversity and reduced consumption of several nutrient\-rich food groups\. District\-cohort analyses further show that early\-life nutritional shocks are negatively associated with later standardized mathematics achievement, although these estimates are correlational\. Similarly, women in more highly exposed districts exhibit lower scores on measures of autonomy, mobility, media exposure, and community participation, which we interpret as proxies for civic capacity rather than direct measures of political behavior\. Conclusion The study findings are consistent with the nutritional lock\-in framework: food\-policy reforms can have consequences extending beyond immediate fiscal or consumption effects to child nutrition, human\-capital formation, and dimensions of civic capacity\. However, the data do not identify the complete causal pathway from childhood nutrition to political accountability or policy persistence\. The findings therefore motivate a broader view of food policy as a component of long\-run human\-capital and institutional development\.

## [The Fiscal Consequences Attributed to Multiple Myeloma in Slovakia: There is No Small Disease](../publications/c96c6c0efdb8db8afe56.md)

Robert Babela; Nikolaos Kotsopoulos; Mark P\. Connolly

Abstract Background The incidence of multiple myeloma \(MM\) is rising in ageing populations\. New therapies have improved survival but are among the most expensive in oncology\. The consequences of MM for government revenues and expenditures in Slovakia have not been quantified\. Methods A government\-perspective fiscal model compared people with MM with the general population of the same age in Slovakia for 2009–2023, with projections to 2030\. Each annual result combined gross public healthcare expenditure, before confidential rebates, with the present value of the lifetime tax and contribution revenue not collected, and of the additional sick\-leave and disability transfers, for newly diagnosed patients and their caregivers\. One\-way sensitivity analyses were performed\. Results In 2023, the total fiscal burden was €32 210 398: healthcare expenditure €25 848 178 \(80\.2%\), revenue not collected €6 230 764 \(19\.3%\) and additional transfers €131 456 \(0\.4%\)\. The cumulative burden for 2009–2023 was €387\.0 million \(healthcare €304\.6 million, revenue €80\.0 million, transfers €2\.4 million\)\. Gross earnings losses \(societal perspective, not part of the fiscal burden\) were €82\.4 million\. The burden is projected to reach €39 533 502 in 2030 \(\+ 22\.7%\)\. In sensitivity analyses, the 2023 total ranged from €28\.5 million to €44\.5 million and was most sensitive to the discount rate and to projected healthcare expenditure\. Conclusions MM imposes a substantial fiscal burden on Slovak public finances, which is projected to grow\. Most of it is healthcare expenditure; social transfers account for less than 1%\. The estimates provide a baseline for fiscal evaluations of specific interventions\.

## [A fuzzy\-augmented deep learning pipeline for multilingual natural language processing from handwritten script: a Tamil case study](../publications/c97c9de21f1df5aa89cd.md)

Harsha Kumar A; B\. Aarthi; K\. Kumaran; G\. Saranya; Preetham Venkatram C

Multilingual natural language processing \(NLP\) from handwritten script is an open artificial intelligence \(AI\) challenge requiring advances in both pattern recognition and sequence generation\. Existing end\-to\-end pipelines often fail to model the structural uncertainty in complex scripts, particularly the decorative stroke variability in Dravidian writing systems, before passing representations to downstream NLP models\. This omission can result in error propagation from the recognition stage into translation\. This paper proposes a Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition and Translation \(THCRT\) framework, a fuzzy\-augmented deep learning NLP pipeline that addresses this gap by coupling a Biparametric Exponential Membership Function\-based Fuzzy Inference System \(BEMFFIS\) with a deep convolutional recognition network and a multilingual transformer for translation\. The fuzzy inference component models stroke\-boundary uncertainty through Decorative Stroke Analysis \(DSA\) using the Coefficient of Variation \(CoV\)\. BEMFFIS employs a coupled\-parameter Gaussian membership function, which reduces the hyperparameter search space to a single degree of freedom\. This produces normalized representations that improve downstream NLP performance\. Hierarchical segmentation of line, word, and character is achieved via Connected Polar Functional Component Analysis \(CPFCA\)\. Recognition is performed by a Global Averaged Excitation\-based Deep Convolutional Neural Network with Swish activation \(GAE\-DCSSNN\), and multilingual translation is executed by a multilingual Bernoulli Distribution\-based Auto\-Regressive Transformer \(mBBDART\) built on the mBART backbone with stochastic token\-pruning augmentation\. The pipeline is evaluated on Tamil handwriting using two publicly available datasets: the Tamil Offline Handwritten Word Recognition \(TOHWR\) dataset and the Tamil Handwritten Character Corpus Mendeley Data \(THCCMD\) dataset\. Translation quality is assessed on a 1,200\-sample parallel reference set annotated by two certified bilingual translators with Cohen&\#x27;s κ = 0\.91, reflecting the word\-level and short\-phrase scope of the TOHWR corpus\. The THCRT framework achieves a recognition accuracy of 98\.23%, a Character Error Rate \(CER\) of 1\.12%, and a Bilingual Evaluation Understudy \(BLEU\) score of 0\.438 on the annotated evaluation set, outperforming the baseline architectures on both datasets and demonstrating a 1\.79 percentage\-point accuracy gain attributed to the BEMFFIS stroke\-uncertainty module\.

## [Spatial multi\-omics reveals that CXCL10 enhances the response to nICT in surgically resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma](../publications/c982d167204fc5fe1b6a.md)

Yefeng Shen; Yunlei Ma; Huansong Yang; Jing Kang; Jing Li; Xinchun Duan; Chunquan Liu; Jian Song; Dong Chang; Yong Cui

Abstract Neoadjuvant immune\-chemotherapy \(nICT\) has transformed the treatment strategy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma \(ESCC\), yet the molecular mechanisms underlying treatment response remain incompletely understood\. To investigate these mechanisms, we jointly analyzed matched ESCC specimens obtained before and after neoadjuvant therapy using single\-cell transcriptomic profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomic imaging\. This multilayered, same\-sample framework revealed extensive remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, including enhanced immune activation and marked changes in the spatial organization of major cellular populations\. Notably, CXCL10 increased the intratumoral proportion of CD8⁺ T cells, promoted their cytotoxic activation, and enhanced T\-cell–mediated tumor elimination both in vitro and in vivo\. Genetic silencing or pharmacological inhibition of CXCR3 attenuated these effects and diminished the therapeutic benefit of anti\-PD1 treatment, supporting a functional role for the CXCL10–CXCR3 axis in modulating immunotherapy efficacy\. Spatial metabolomics further revealed pronounced remodeling of ornithine metabolism in malignant regions, characterized by suppression of the urea cycle, potential involvement of a glutamate/proline\-linked ornithine pathway, and enhanced polyamine synthesis\. An ornithine metabolism\-related gene signature was strongly associated with poor prognosis in the TCGA\-ESCC cohort, while pharmacological inhibition of ornithine decarboxylase enhanced the antitumor efficacy of anti\-PD1 therapy in vivo\. Together, these findings provide a spatial multi\-omics atlas of ESCC following nICT and identify the CXCL10–CXCR3 axis and ornithine\-centered metabolic remodeling as potentially actionable immune and metabolic features associated with treatment response\.

## [Predictive Value of Lung Ultrasound Scores for Early Detection of Severe Community\-Acquired Pneumonia in Children](../publications/c98892105d3d73fead32.md)

Fatma A\.S\. Ibrahim; Maysan Bassam Sulaiman Ballaji; Abdulkarim Khalid Oskubi

Background: Community\-acquired pneumonia \(CAP\) poses a significant health threat, claiming lives and sickening children all across the world\. Early in their CAP journeys, children who are most vulnerable to the worst outcomes, those whose illness is most likely to become life\-threatening, could be detected more readily by timely care\. Lung Ultrasound \(LUS\), which can be deployed at a patient’s bedside with no damaging radiation and little expertise, is a widely useful diagnostic technique for young people with pneumonia\. This examination seeks to determine the prognostic efficacy of LUS scoring systems with respect to identifying early severity among pediatric CAP patients\. Methods: A literature research of pertinent investigations published between 2020\-2026 exploring LUS scoring systems for the prediction of severity and complications among pediatric CAP populations was carried out using data from Medline, Scopus, EMBASE databases and the Cochrane library\. The goal was to discover and evaluate the research original findings and review papers to find all published data addressing clinical practicality and diagnostic efficacy of the diverse LUS scoring tools in pediatric patients\. The LUS scoring system’s predictive aptitude for capturing severity \(e\.g\. Necessity for oxygen and ICU\) and classifying patients with either NP or LOS was analyzed\. The LUS system was additionally analyzed regarding morbidity and fatality with various clinical parameters\. Results: Several LUS scoring methods have demonstrated strong predictability of the clinical outcome among those patients who are victims of CAP\. Traditional 12\-zone LUS \(0 to36 points\), and m\-LUS score, were discovered to have fair and excellent prediction capability in terms of likelihood for of oxygen need \(AUC 0\.84 \- 0\.88\) and admission to ICU\(AUC0\.82\-0\.88\) and identification of NP\(AUC 0\.82– 0\.85\) and Los, morbidity and mortality\. LUS scores are correlated strongly with procalcitonin levels \(R=0\.709\) and inversely correlate with Pediatric Critical Illness Score \(R=\-0\.544\)\. The twelve to\-15 points of LUS scoring system are predictive of children who are appropriate to be treated intensively\. When a patient gets LUS score\(m\-LU Score\)of 12\.5at baseline, they show to be at risk for Developing NP at a rate of 76\.2 % \(sensitivity\)with 66\.4 % \(specificity\); with follow up visit sat 5 day, the rate increases to85\.7%\(sensitivity\),76\.0% \(specificity\)\. Conclusions: We report the results that the LUS scoring system is able to reliably and non\-traumatically predict severe childhood pneumonia with an acceptable rate of diagnostic capability\. The implement at ion of these scoring systems could provide an efficient stratification of those at risk, optimal use of care resources, and targeted approaches in medical treatment\.

## [Assessing Artificial Intelligence Readiness of Higher Education Institutions in Chhattisgarh: A Study of Faculty and Students](../publications/c9911505a57d4d5fc82c.md)

Rajni Lakra1; Ravi Kumar Malhotra; Manjulata Sidar3

The research measured the readiness of faculty and students of higher education institutions \(HEIs\) in Chhattisgarh, India in terms of five dimensions: awareness of AI, technical skills, digital infrastructure, policy and institutional support, and attitude toward AI\. The data was collected from four types of institutions, through a cross\-sectional survey design with the help of stratified sampling technique with 440 respondents consisting of 120 faculty members and 320 students\. An overall Artificial Intelligence Readiness Index \(ARI\) was calculated using a 5\-point scale\. Readiness was moderate \(M = 3\.24, SD = 0\.45\): attitude and awareness and infrastructure and institutional policy were the highest and the lowest scores respectively\. Students performed significantly higher than faculty on the ARI, t \(205\) = 5\.41, p &lt; \.001, and the readiness differed by institution type, F\(3, 436\) = 16\.0, p &lt; \.001, with government colleges being the lowest\. The results showed that 62\.7% of the variance of attitude towards AI could be accounted for by awareness, skills, infrastructure and policy support\. The results highlight an infrastructure\-governance gap as a more likely cause than a motivation gap, and suggestions are provided on paths forward for state policymakers and institutional leaders\. Note: The data analysed in this draft are illustrative \(simulated\) and must be replaced by actual survey responses prior to submission and/or publication\.

## [Two suspected sequential retinal arterial macroaneurysms in a single eye with secondary nonvascular cystoid macular edema: 5\-year follow\-up: a case report](../publications/c99379c5937a578ce680.md)

Kaiyao Chi; Daoxi Lei; Tong Guo; Xiaoding Shui; Huili Li

Background Retinal arterial macroaneurysm \(RAM\) is an acquired vascular disorder\. The long\-term natural history of multiple RAMs in a single eye complicated by nonvascular cystoid maculopathy \(NVCM\) is rarely documented\. Case presentation A 65\-year\-old hypertensive woman presented with acute vision loss in her left eye secondary to severe vitreous hemorrhage\. She underwent pars plana vitrectomy with intravitreal recombinant tissue plasminogen activator thrombolysis and silicone oil tamponade\. Postoperative multimodal imaging supported the diagnosis of two suspected sequential RAMs confined to the left eye\. Over a 5\-year follow\-up, the two lesions exhibited divergent outcomes: one developed fibrosis and persistent NVCM associated with severe initial hemorrhage and inadequate blood pressure control, whereas the other regressed completely following rigorous systemic hypertension management\. Conclusions Multiple RAMs within the same eye can follow distinctly divergent natural courses\. In this single case, early blood pressure control appeared to be an important contributing factor to the divergent lesion outcomes, although the contribution of spontaneous regression and other confounding factors cannot be excluded\. Multimodal imaging is indispensable for differentiating NVCM from vasogenic macular edema, guiding individualized conservative management, and preventing unnecessary interventions\.

Wenyi Yang; Xu Jiang; Qiang Xu

This study develops a physics\-informed and interpretable data\-driven framework for predicting the axial buckling capacity of circular steel tubes strengthened with longitudinal CFRP strips\. A validated finite element \(FE\) model against test results was used to generate 196 parametric samples, and these data were combined with 190 experimental results from literature to establish a 386\-sample database for machine\-learning modeling\. The FE analysis shows that CFRP strengthening increases the sectional flexural stiffness and can improve the ultimate load by up to 49\.57% for slender members\. For medium\-length columns, a distinct capacity jump of up to 30\.12% is observed, which is attributed to a transition from global flexural buckling to localized instability induced by the longitudinal stiffness constraint of high\-modulus CFRP strips\. Four prediction models \(XGBoost, BPNN, SVR and Stacking\) were optimized using four swarm\-intelligence algorithms to overcome the sensitivity of model performance to hyperparameter selection\. Pearson correlation analysis identifies the slenderness ratio as the dominant capacity\-reducing variable \( r = \-0\.81\), whereas the number of CFRP layers, the diameter\-to\-thickness ratio and the steel yield strength show positive correlations with buckling resistance \( r = 0\.25, 0\.25 and 0\.13, respectively\)\. Among all optimized models, AVOA\-XGBoost provides the best overall performance, with a testing R 2 of 0\.925, a MAE of 18\.40 kN and a RMSE of 30\.11 kN\. SHAP analysis further confirms that the learned feature effects are consistent with structural stability theory\. The proposed framework offers both mechanistic insight into CFRP\-assisted instability control and a practical surrogate model for the rehabilitation design of steel tubular members\.

## [Artificial intelligence in cancer transcriptomics: methods, applications in oncology, and limitations](../publications/c9a302a5d538433e42a8.md)

Ilya A\. Solovev; Denis Golubev

Background\. Transcriptomic data show which genes are active in cells and tissues\. Machine\-learning and deep\-learning methods use these data to classify samples, integrate different datasets, and predict biological properties and treatment response\. In oncology, a major challenge is transferring patterns identified in experimental models to tumor samples from patients\. Objective\. To critically synthesize current artificial\-intelligence methods for transcriptomic analysis, with emphasis on oncology applications, transfer of models to patient data, and requirements for clinical validation\. Materials and Methods\. We performed a critical narrative review of primary studies and methodological papers and additionally described the authors&\#x27; publication sample for 2021–2026\. The literature review was updated through August 13, 2026\. Results\. The most developed areas include single\-cell data analysis, spatially resolved tumor diagnostics, and drug\-response prediction\. Independent comparative evaluations show that increasing model size and complexity does not guarantee better performance than simpler methods\. Clinical translation requires accounting for cellular composition and technical differences between measurement batches, aligning experimental and clinical response measures, preventing information leakage, and performing external validation\. Conclusion\. Artificial intelligence should be viewed as a data\-analysis tool rather than a substitute for experimental or clinical validation\. Its value depends on data quality, correct task definition, and the ability to maintain performance in independent cohorts\.

## [Adaptive Privacy\-Preserving Big Data Analytics: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Deterministic Guardrail Framework](../publications/c9b26d46858081d9f0db.md)

Satish Basavaraj Basapur; Ansh Jain; Ayush Singh; Abhishek L; Abhinav Kumar Mishra Abhinav Kumar Mishra

The exponential expansion of consumer financial services has led to massive volumes of structured transaction and account data being migrated to public cloud data lakes for high\-throughput distributed analytics\. However, financial datasets intrinsically contain sensitive Personally Identifiable Information \(PII\) subject to stringent regulatory frameworks including the General Data Protection Regulation \(GDPR\) and the Indian Digital Personal Data Protection \(DPDP\) Act of 2023\. Conventional privacy solutions exhibit a debilitating trilemma: cryptographic methods such as Fully Homomorphic Encryption \(FHE\) impose prohibitive computational latency; static dictionary\-based anonymization collapses under schema drift and lexical variations; and unconstrained machine learning classifiers suffer from train/serve distribution shifts where subtle format discrepancies precipitate catastrophic privacy leaks\. In this paper, we propose a scalable, cloud\-native privacy preserving big data analytics framework anchored by an Adaptive Dual\-Tier Privacy Engine\. Our architecture couples an adaptive multi\-stage gradient boosted decision tree \(XGBoost\) classifier— trained on a 25\-dimensional structural, keyword, sample\-level, and regular expression feature space—with deterministic safety\-net guardrails \(Force\-Protect and Force\-Keep\)\. This hybrid design guarantees zero exposure of mission\-critical identifiers while completely insulating downstream business analytical features against corruption\. Masked datasets are securely persisted to AWS S3 and processed through distributed Apache Spark \(PySpark\) clusters via the S3A connector across four analytical dimensions: descriptive statistics, bivariate fraud detection with two\-factor authentication \(2FA\) correlation, credit risk profiling, and multi tier customer segmentation\. Validated against a high\-cardinality 100,000\-record banking benchmark across 57 attributes, our system demonstrates 100% mitigation of critical PII leakage, overcomes real\-world distribution skew on complex identifier formats, preserves analytical utility with zero loss of statistical fidelity, and maintains sub\-minute distributed pipeline throughput\. Index Terms—Privacy\-Preserving Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing, Apache Spark, XGBoost, Personally Identifiable Information \(PII\), Hybrid Guardrails, Train/Serve Skew, Financial Data Governance\.

## [Competence\-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models](../publications/c9b3d3a3c630217e2df4.md)

Jize Jiang; Chengxiang Zhai

Recent advances in large language models \(LLMs\) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation\. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity\. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks\. Such a performance\-based evaluation methodology says little about a model&\#x27;s generalization capacity in reasoning\. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence\-based evaluation \(CBE\), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems\. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer\-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation\. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule\. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family\. Chain\-of\-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held\-out transfer\. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models\.

## [Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp\. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots](../publications/c9b46bc4cf1bfdf9f836.md)

Fahad Awwadh Almarshadi; Walid Alesefir; Gaurav Kumar

Introduction Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential\. Methods In the present research, the antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic properties of the ethyl acetate extract of endophytic Aspergillus sp\. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots were evaluated using both in vitro and in silico assessments\. The crude extract was subjected to GC–MS profiling, which tentatively identified several metabolites, followed by molecular docking, drug\-likeness, pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction analyses\. Results and Discussion The crude extract has shown broad spectrum antibacterial activity with inhibition zone of 15\.66 ± 0\.57 mm against Escherichia coli , 14\.66 ± 1\.52 mm against Staphylococcus aureus , 14\.00 ± 0\.00 mm against Staphylococcus epidermidis and 13\.33 ± 0\.57 mm against Bacillus subtilis \. Minimum inhibitory concentration values were 16, 32, 64, and 64 μg/mL, while minimum bactericidal concentration values were 32, 32, 64, and 128 μg/mL, respectively\. The extract showed concentration\-dependent responses in chemical antioxidant assays, including DPPH radical\-scavenging, hydrogen peroxide\-scavenging, reducing\-power and total antioxidant\-capacity assays\. A strong correlation between chemical antioxidant capacity and total phenolics \(R2 = 0\.9752–0\.9986\) and total flavonoids \(R2 = 0\.9814–0\.9956\) content was found\. The extract exhibited concentration\-dependent cytotoxicity against MCF\-7 cells with an IC50 value of 69\.20 μg/mL that had positive correlation with the phenolics and flavonoids content\. The analysis of GC–MS points to the presence of several metabolites, including 2\-Buten\-1\-one, 1,3\-diphenyl\- \(dypnone, a β\-methyl2\-Buten\-1\-one, 1,3\-diphenyl\-; CID 95329\) which showed the highest binding affinity to selected protein targets, along with favourable drug\-likeness, in silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity properties\. The extract demonstrated antibacterial activity, measurable chemical antioxidant/ radical\-scavenging properties, and cytotoxic effects under the experimental conditions\. Integrated experimental and computational studies highlighted the tentatively identified 2\-Buten\-1\-one, 1,3\-diphenyl\- as a compound of interest for further investigation\. Conclusion These findings provide preliminary indication for the possible biological activity of the Aspergillus sp\. GK1 extract and support further bioassay\- guided fractionation, isolation, structural characterization, mechanistic studies, and in vivo analysis of its active constituents\.

## [Mudança do uso da terra em 30 anos nas nascentes da bacia hidrográfica do rio Turiaçu, Amazônia Maranhense, região nordeste do Brasil](../publications/c9b55b1aea30bcce8774.md)

Juliana Lopes Almeida; Thiago Bernardi Vieira; José Fernando Rodrigues Bezerra; Karina Dias‐Silva

Uma das consequências diretas do desmatamento é a fragmentação florestal, que pode ocorrer de forma natural ou por atores sociais\. Estima\-se que o estado do Maranhão perdeu mais de 75% da cobertura florestal original amazônica, e os principais remanescentes de floresta estão em Terras Indígenas e na Reserva Biológica do Gurupi\. Assim, a fim de contribuir para a gestão e planejamento da Bacia Hidrográfica do Rio Turiaçu, localizada no Maranhão, Brasil, o objetivo deste trabalho é analisar as mudanças no uso da terra nas nascentes da bacia nos anos 1990, 2000, 2010 e 2020\. Essa área necessita de estudos que auxiliem no planejamento de restauração da conectividade florestal\. Com base nos dados do MapBiomas, integrados ao arquivo de localização das nascentes, foi possível avaliar as mudanças no uso e ocupação das áreas de nascentes localizadas próximas as rodovias e das que estão dentro das TIs \(Terras Indígenas\)\. Os resultados identificaram mudanças significativas, como a diminuição da classe Floresta e o avanço da Agropecuária\. Através das análises estatísticas, constatou\-se que as TIs apresentaram a maior taxa de conservação florestal; contudo, essa classe obteve uma redução gradual no período estudado, assinalando a importância da criação e manutenção de áreas protegidas\.

## [Young people&\#x27;s planned adherence to Australia&\#x27;s social media age restrictions](../publications/c9cf0ca01b64b763eb26.md)

Laura McVey; Sarah Skye Napier; Aimee Wrightson\-Hester

Australia’s social media minimum age legislation restricts individuals under 16 years from holding accounts on specified social media platforms\. Prior to the new restrictions taking place, this study surveyed 382 high school students in Australia aged 11–15 years to understand their attitudes and planned responses to the social media restrictions\. One in five \(21\.8%\) young people said they would continue to use the restricted platforms, and 60\.7 percent thought other young people would do so\. Of those who said they would use restricted platforms, most either did not yet know how they would do so \(43\.6%\) or planned to give a fake age \(39\.7%\), while 2\.6 percent said they would use a VPN\. Boys, older children and those who spent more time online were more likely to say they would use restricted platforms\.

## [From Waste to Value: Diagnosing Ethiopia&\#x27;s Coffee By\-Product Circular Economy Commercialization Gap](../publications/c9e8dc29f0ec6bdc98f4.md)

Soliyana Afework Gebreananya

Coffee husk, pulp, and spent grounds are a large, underused waste stream with established circular\-economy conversion pathways \(biochar via pyrolysis, biogas via anaerobic fermentation, compost, and cascara\), yet Ethiopia, among the world&\#x27;s five largest coffee producers, generates an estimated 192,000 metric tons of coffee husk waste annually with almost none valorized commercially\. Ethiopian universities have validated these conversion technologies, yet little evidence shows this becoming a functioning circular\-economy industry\. Countries producing a fraction of Ethiopia&\#x27;s coffee, and one producing none, have already built profitable by\-product sectors using the same technologies\. This paper argues Ethiopia&\#x27;s constraint is commercial rather than technological: the country clears scientific research and technology validation but stalls before commercial feasibility and investment\. Testing production scale, scientific capacity, and market demand against international literature, Ethiopian research, and interviews with five Ethiopian coffee\-sector professionals, this paper eliminates each as a sufficient explanation and identifies a missing institutional bridge between research and commercialisation as the most probable constraint\. Ethiopia&\#x27;s recent investment reforms, plastics restrictions, and rising demand for biodegradable materials have converged into a favourable commercialisation window\. The paper contributes a diagnostic framework for scaling circular\-economy waste valorization, connecting university research, industry perspectives, and policy timing\. Keywords: biochar; circular economy; coffee by\-products; technology commercialization; waste valorization

## [Diagnostic classification of hepatocellular carcinoma in the Vietnamese population using clinical and biochemical data: explainable machine learning approaches](../publications/c9e906ae7f455e8bab56.md)

Thi Hong Tham Pham; Thi Hong Tham Pham; Huu Phong Nguyen; Quang Tung Pham; Vu Khanh an Le; Anh Gia Pham; Binh Giang Tran; Hung N\. Luu; Vu Cong Duy; Thanh Hai Tran; Thi Lan Le; Hai Vu

Hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\) is one of the leading causes of cancer\-related deaths worldwide and one of the leading causes of cancer\-related death in Vietnam\. This highlights the need for accurate and interpretable diagnostic classification models based on routine clinical parameters\. This study investigates machine learning \(ML\) techniques for HCC classification and explanation using clinical and biochemical data, particularly in the context of imbalanced ratio between HCC and non\-HCC\. A transparent ML framework was developed, focusing on feature selection and model interpretability\. First, the VD\_HCC dataset, comprising 880 Vietnamese patients \(303 with biopsy\-confirmed HCC and 577 non\-HCC\), was collected at a Vietnamese healthcare center\. A pre\-processing pipeline was then applied to ensure data consistency, reduce noise, and improve downstream model performance\. Next, eight feature selection methods were used to identify important biomarkers\. Features consistently selected across multiple methods were combined with clinical expertise to build optimized feature subsets\. Several classifiers, including ensemble methods such as XGBoost, AdaBoost, and LightGBM, were evaluated using these feature sets\. A two\-layer XAI analysis combining SHAP, LIME, Partial Dependence Plots \(PDPs\), and a feature\-correlation graph was then used to compare feature attributions and characterize fitted\-model behavior and associations in the study data\. Across 30 repeated runs with independent training and test partitions, XGBoost using the 10 features set \(named Set 5\) achieved an Accuracy of \\\(0\.938 \\pm 0\.018\\\) and an F1\-score of \\\(0\.909 \\pm 0\.022\\\) , with AFP, HBsAg, CEA, AST, Platelets, and ALT among the leading contributors\. On the locked hold\-out test set, both XGBoost and LightGBM achieved the best ROC\-AUC values of 0\.979 and PR\-AUC values of 0\.971 and 0\.965, respectively\. Under the most imbalanced stress\-test scenario \(HCC = 1:21\), XGBoost and LightGBM achieved comparable Accuracy; XGBoost showed higher Precision, Recall, F1\-score, and ROC\-AUC, whereas LightGBM achieved a slightly higher PR\-AUC \( \\\(0\.878 \\pm 0\.089\\\) vs\. \\\(0\.861 \\pm 0\.093\\\) \), compared with a no\-skill PR\-AUC baseline of 0\.045\. For the final Set 5 XGBoost model, aggregated LIME and SHAP yielded highly consistent feature rankings Spearman \\\(\\rho = 0\.976\\\) ; top\-six Jaccard index = 1\.000, while the feature\-correlation graph provided a complementary description of associations among the study variables\. These explanation analyses characterize the behavior of the fitted model and associations within the study data, rather than establishing causal effects or independently validated clinical importance\. The ensemble classifiers showed relatively stable discriminative performance across imbalance levels, despite heavy HCC imbalance on the test set\. The proposed framework provides an interpretable view of HCC classification by identifying the features that contribute most to the model’s predictions in separating HCC from non\-HCC cases\.

## [Adult presentation of SLC29A3\-related disorder spectrum with marked hypogammaglobulinemia due to a recurrent homozygous pathogenic variant \(G437R\): a case report](../publications/c9ed0bd675114a6c3caa.md)

Mohammad Ameen Ishqair; Abbas K\. H\. Masalma; Mohanad Saleh; Fawaz Awad; Aliaa Khalili; Anas Ameen Ishqair; Somaya Salah; Abed\-Rahman N\. Saleh

Background SLC29A3\-related disorder spectrum encompasses rare autosomal recessive conditions characterized by multisystem involvement, including immunodeficiency, lymphoproliferation, cutaneous findings, endocrine dysfunction, and growth failure\. The clinical presentation is highly heterogeneous, often leading to delayed diagnosis, particularly in adults\. Case presentation A 33\-year\-old Palestinian woman born to consanguineous parents presented with a lifelong history of recurrent severe respiratory infections, growth failure \(short stature and microcephaly\), recurrent nephrolithiasis, chronic vomiting, generalized hirsutism, and bilateral hallux valgus\. Laboratory evaluation revealed marked hypogammaglobulinemia \(IgG &lt;320 mg/dL, IgA &lt;25 mg/dL, IgM &lt;25 mg/dL\), microcytic anemia, and severe vitamin D deficiency\. Imaging confirmed chronic pulmonary small\-airway changes and a chronically small right kidney with recurrent stones\. Whole\-exome sequencing identified a homozygous pathogenic SLC29A3 variant \(c\.1309G&gt;A; p\.Gly437Arg\), establishing a diagnosis within the SLC29A3\-related disorder spectrum\. This case is unique due to its adult presentation, the exceptional severity of the humoral immunodeficiency, and the associated renal manifestations, which are infrequently reported in this spectrum\. Conclusion This report underscores the importance of considering SLC29A3\-related disorder spectrum in adults with multisystem disease\. Recognition of this spectrum enables targeted multidisciplinary care, including immunoglobulin replacement therapy and anticipatory surveillance for endocrine and renal complications\.

## [الكفاءات الاحترافية والجدارات الذكية للعاملين في المكتبات والأرشيف: إطار تدريبي مقترح لمواكبة التحولات الرقمية وتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي](../publications/ca1cbb1c8d8e9a1efa81.md)

المزمل حامد; جميلة حسن; ريم الشرياني

تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى بناء إطار تدريبي مقترح لتنمية الكفاءات الاحترافية والجدارات الذكية للعاملين في المكتبات والأرشيف بما يواكب التحولات الرقمية والذكاء الاصطناعي\. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي وتحليل الوثائق والمراجعة المنهجية للأدبيات، باستخدام استمارة تحليل المحتوى\. وتوصلت الدراسة إلى أربع مجالات رئيسة: الكفاءات الرقمية والتقنية، والجدارات التحليلية وإدارة البيانات، والابتكار وتطوير الخدمات الذكية، والأخلاقية والحوكمة الرقمية، إلى جانب أربعة مستويات للإتقان \(PL1–PL4\) تتدرج من الاستخدام الأساسي إلى التطبيق والتحليل والقيادة\. كما ربطت الدراسة أهداف ومخرجات التعلم بمؤشرات أداء لقياس تحقق الكفاءات، وأوصت الدراسة بتصميم مسارات تدريبية متدرجة وفق مستويات الإتقان \(PL1–PL4\)\. وتعزيز التدريب المستمر في الذكاء الاصطناعي، وتحليل البيانات، والتقنيات الرقمية، والابتكار الكلمات المفتاحية: الكفاءات الاحترافية، الجدارات الذكية، المكتبات، الأرشيف، التحول الرقمي، الذكاء الاصطناعي\.

## [From AI Tools to Learner\-Centered Human–AI Collaboration: Developing and Evaluating the Learner\-Centered Human–AI Pedagogical Framework \(LCHAP\)](../publications/ca241be2a22096a9eb07.md)

Myagmarsuren Orosoo; Namjildagva Raash; Tumentsetseg Baljinnyam; Munkhtsetseg Narantsetseg

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping higher education, yet practical guidance for integrating it into meaningful learning remains limited\. This paper introduces the Learner\-Centered Human–AI Pedagogical Framework \(LCHAP\), which positions AI as a collaborative cognitive partner while preserving learner agency and responsibility\. LCHAP was implemented through the Human–AI Learning Cycle \(HALC\) in a 15\-week quasi\-experimental mixed\-methods study involving 80 first\-year undergraduates at the Mongolian National University of Education\. At post\-intervention, the experimental group showed higher mean scores than the control group in English writing, learner engagement, learner autonomy, AI literacy, reflective learning, and critical thinking\. Qualitative evidence indicated a shift from answer generation toward idea exploration, comparison, revision, and reflection\. Because the reported quantitative evidence is descriptive, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary rather than causal\. LCHAP offers a practical design framework for responsible, learner\-centered Human–AI collaboration in higher education\.

## [Biomass conversion in thermo‐catalytic reforming reactor: process modeling and kinetic insights for integrated intermediate pyrolysis](../publications/ca38d93dce63889f1252.md)

Sukriti Sharma; Asad  Hasan Sahir; Andreas Apfelbacher; Robert Daschner

Abstract A sustainable energy transition in the 21st century necessitates efficient biomass‐to‐energy conversion technologies, with pyrolysis playing a crucial role\. Thermo‐catalytic reforming \(TCR\) combines intermediate pyrolysis with a catalytic post‐reforming stage, producing higher‐quality bio‐oil, char, and syngas than conventional pyrolysis\. However, process models capable of predicting TCR performance across different feedstocks remain limited\. This work presents an Aspen Plus‐based kinetic process model that couples both TCR reaction stages, primary pyrolysis, and catalytic post‐reforming, within a single framework\. The model integrates the CRECK kinetic mechanism with a detailed char decomposition model, predicting product yields and gas composition directly from feedstock elemental analysis\. It is validated against experimental data from five compositionally distinct feedstocks: digestate, municipal solid waste, eucalyptus, bagasse, and straw pellets\. These span both conventional lignocellulosic biomass and heterogeneous waste streams\. The model achieves strong agreement for char yield predictions across all five feedstocks, within approximately 1–2% deviation, while bio‐oil prediction accuracy varies by feedstock composition\. Sensitivity analysis of post‐reformer temperature \(800–900 °C\) shows a consistent increase in H 2 \(by approximately 8–12%\) and decrease in CH 4 \(by approximately 23–46%\) across all feedstocks\. This trend is driven by steam methane reforming and water–gas shift conversion, identifying higher post‐reformer temperature as a generalizable route to improved syngas quality\. The model requires only standard elemental feedstock analysis as input, linking feedstock composition directly to predicted product distribution and enabling identification of favorable operating conditions ahead of physical trials\.

## [Noise\-Resilient Attention\-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Network Intrusion Detection](../publications/ca3d0e78a598762e5cc5.md)

M\. Sathya; K Pradeepa

The rising complexity of the state of the art network infrastructures and the swift advancement of cyber\-attacks have rendered the correct and sound detection of intrusion to be a vital security need\. Conventional intrusion detection solutions tend to collapse with noisy, high\-dimensional network traffic, temporally changing traffic and encourage superior Deep Learning \(DL\)\-based options\. The main goal of this work is to improve the intrusion detection reliability by resolving the issue of noise sensitivity, over\-representation of redundant features and inadequate temporal modelling\. This is accomplished by introducing a noise\-resilient attentionguided DL architecture which are Adaptive Noise\-Resilient Data Preprocessing \(ANR\-DP\), Hybrid Recursive Attention\-Based Feature Selection \(HRAFS\), and a Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\)\-based temporal classifier\. ANR\-DP acts dynamically on traffic noise and maintains the characteristics of the attacks, but HRAFS is expected to select stable and security\-critical features through recursive elimination and attentiondriven relevance learning\. The optimized features are fed through an LSTM network in order to detect sequential and long\-term intrusion patterns\. Experimental analysis of the CICIDS2017 dataset provides a better performance with Proposed ANR\-DP having low Missing Value Ratio of 1\.2, High Outlier Reduction Rate of 91\.5, HRAFS achieves a Feature Reduction Ratio of 68\.7% and 9\.1% accuracy improvement\. The LSTM classifier also has an accuracy of 98\.6%, and a low false positive rate of 3\.1%\. These findings establish that the proposed framework is very effective in enhancing robustness, precision, and dependability, it can be applicable in the environment of network intrusion detection\.

## [EMERGING ROLE OF AYURVEDIC REGIMENS FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF STHAULYA \(OBESITY\) WITH INTEGRATIVE INSIGHTS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW](../publications/ca4da8aa9beb42cd53be.md)

Dr Mamta Rana; Ishani Thakur; Kanika Sharma; Monika Sharma

BACKGROUND: Sthaulya \(obesity\) is a major global health concern associated with metabolic disorder\. Its growing prevalence is primarily driven by sedentary lifestyle and poor dietary habits\. In ayurveda Sthaulya is described as a metabolic imbalance including Kapha dosha and meda dhatu, highlighting the need for holistic management approaches\. OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to evaluate the role of ayurvedic regimens and yoga interventions in the management of sthaulya\. METHOD: The Comprehensive literature search was conducted across Google scholar, PubMed, and Ayush portal for studies published between 2018 to 2026\. A total of 110 articles were included in this review\. RESULTS: The review highlights that ayurvedic regimes including lifestyle modification, dietary changes, herbal medicine, panchkarma, along with yoga practices, are associated with improvements in anthropometric parameters and metabolic health\. These approaches collectively contribute to the improved metabolic balance and reduction in obesity risk factors, thereby promoting overall health and well\- being\. CONCLUSION: Integrative approaches including yoga and ayurveda provide effective complementary strategies for obesity management, emphasizing sustainable and holistic care\.

## [Fatigue in Different Groups of Disaster Responders after the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake: Group\-Specific Associations and Priorities for Intervention](../publications/ca599865f341f433511e.md)

大輔 是枝; Odgerel Chimed‐Ochir; Megumi Takenaka; Tatsuhiro Nagata; 村山華子; Yui Yumiya; Ami Fukunaga; Seiichiro Tateishi; Tatsuhiko Kubo

OBJECTIVE: To compare fatigue in the external supporters and local public officers who responded to the January 1, 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake, identify group\-specific factors associated with fatigue, and estimate population\-level differences under hypothetical scenarios\. METHODS: A repeated\-measures observational study was conducted using responder health surveillance data collected between January and March 2024\. Generalized estimating equations were used to compare fatigue levels and examine group\-specific associations with operational and health\-related factors\. G\-computation was used to estimate model\-based population\-level differences in fatigue under hypothetical scenarios in which each factor was set to zero\. RESULTS: There were 23,865 observations from 7,135 responders\. Local public officers reported greater fatigue than external supporters \(β = 2\.32, 95% CI: 2\.22\-2\.43\)\. The inability to take meals and breaks and unclear command/task structure were associated with greater fatigue in both groups\. Sleep disturbance and irritability had stronger associations with fatigue in external supporters\. G\-computation showed larger model\-based population\-level differences under the hypothetical scenarios in local public officers, primarily because operational and health\-related problems were more prevalent in this group\. CONCLUSIONS: Operational factors and health problems were associated with fatigue in disaster responders, and the model\-based population\-level differences under hypothetical scenarios depended on their prevalence\. Increasing the number of responders, provision of rest periods, improving command clarity, and monitoring the health of responders may reduce fatigue and improve disaster responses\.

## [A prospective study evaluating the impact of waiting time on blood testing and clinical workflows in cancer patients](../publications/ca671d458c1269bb9884.md)

Yu Sunakawa; Hiroyuki Arai; Yohei Kubota; Yusuke Nagata; Hiroyuki Takeda; Kumiko Umemoto; Yoshiki Horie; Naoki Izawa; Takashi Ogura; Kiyoshi Okazuka; Yuta Okamura; Toshihide Hosoyamada; Yumi Izumaru; Yukiko Sakakibara; Junpei Soeda; Reo Takaku

BACKGROUND: Long waiting times on chemotherapy days increase patient burden\. Pre\-visit blood sampling may streamline workflows; however, its real\-world impact remains unclear\. METHODS: This prospective study collected data on waiting times for pre\-visit vs same\-day blood sampling in 50 cancer patients receiving chemotherapy between October 2024 and February 2025 at St\. Marianna University Hospital\. Pre‑visit and same‑day blood sampling was compared in the same patients across four waiting times: \(i\) check\-in to consultation, \(ii\) check\-in to check\-out, and \(iii\-iv\) extended measures incorporating travel time\. For times \(iii\) and \(iv\), travel time during pre\-visit was also included\. Patient and physician satisfaction and indirect costs were also evaluated\. RESULTS: The median waiting time from check\-in to consultation was 1\.8 and 2\.2 h for pre\-visit and same\-day sampling, respectively; when chemotherapy and check\-out were included \(ii\), total duration was similar \(6\.3 vs 6\.3 h\)\. Extended measures \(iii\-iv\) tended to be longer with pre\-visit sampling\. After excluding the two outliers, waiting time from check\-in to chemotherapy was significantly shorter for pre\-visit vs same\-day sampling \(3\.3 vs 3\.9 h, p=0\.025\)\. Patient satisfaction was favorable, and 24\.0% of patients reported reduced burden\. Indirect costs improved by approximately 1198 Japanese yen per patient, with benefits reported in approximately half of the cases\. Subgroup analyses suggested greater benefits for patients living within 30 min of both pre\-visit blood sampling and chemotherapy facilities\. CONCLUSIONS: Pre\-visit blood sampling may reduce waiting time and perceived burden for selected patients, although overall time savings were modest\. Trial registration University Hospital Medical Information Network \(UMIN\) Clinical Trials Registry: UMIN000055757\.

## [Optimization of Tube Voltage in Digital Chest Radiography: Integrating Exposure Index and Image Noise Using an Anthropomorphic Phantom](../publications/ca73dc910c1a427a7063.md)

Jihan Rahima; Anisa Nur Istiqomah; Muhamad Fa’ik

Tube voltage \(kVp\) influences detector exposure and objective image\-quality characteristics in digital radiography; however, the integration of standardized exposure indicators with region\-specific image noise and signal\-to\-noise ratio \(SNR\) across anatomically distinct thoracic regions remains limited\. This study evaluated the effects of tube\-voltage variation on Exposure Index \(EI\), Deviation Index \(DI\), image noise, and SNR in digital chest radiography\. An anthropomorphic PBU\-50 thorax phantom was imaged using a Samsung XGEO GF50 digital radiography system at eleven tube\-voltage settings from 50 to 100 kVp in 5\-kVp increments while maintaining a constant 8 mAs\. Three independent acquisitions were performed at each setting, yielding 33 radiographic images\. EI and DI were extracted from DICOM metadata, while mean pixel value, image noise, and SNR were evaluated in five anatomical regions of interest: clavicle, scapula, costae, sternum, and lung field\. Descriptive statistics, linear and quadratic regression, and Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were performed\. EI increased from 73\.95 ± 0\.28 at 50 kVp to 1980\.91 ± 16\.78 at 100 kVp, while DI increased from −4\.01 ± 0\.02 to \+10\.28 ± 0\.04\. Image noise generally decreased with increasing kVp, with reductions from 50 to 100 kVp ranging from 6\.9% in the scapula to 58\.8% in the sternum\. SNR exhibited region\-dependent nonlinear responses, and quadratic models better characterized several kVp\-dependent relationships\. At 60 kVp, EI was 216\.02 ± 1\.68, and DI was \+0\.65 ± 0\.03, representing the only investigated condition within the predefined −1 ≤ DI ≤ \+1 interval while providing higher SNR than at 50 kVp across all ROIs\. These findings demonstrate an anatomy\-dependent trade\-off between detector exposure and objective image quality\. The 60\-kVp condition should therefore be considered a candidate detector\-exposure condition for further optimization using patient\-dose measurements and diagnostic image\-quality assessment\.

## [STRATEGI GURU DALAM MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI BELAJAR ANAK USIA DINI MELALUI AKTIVITAS BERMAIN DI TAMAN KANAK\-KANAK AL\-BARRA KELURAHAN BANDAR RATU KECAMATAN KOTA MUKOMUKO](../publications/ca9413577157e8fa2585.md)

Sri Wahyuni; Achmad Fadlan; Eka Mei Ratnasari

Early childhood education requires learning strategies that can create meaningful, enjoyable, and developmentally appropriate learning experiences\. This study aims to analyze teacher strategies in improving early childhood learning motivation through play activities at TK Al\-Barra, Bandar Ratu Village, Kota Mukomuko District\. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving three kindergarten teachers as research subjects\. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive analysis model consisting of data reduction, data display, verification, and conclusion drawing\. The findings revealed that teachers implemented various strategies through educational games, group play activities, and creative play activities adapted to children’s needs and developmental characteristics\. Play\-based activities effectively enhanced children’s engagement, enthusiasm, curiosity, and active participation during the learning process\. However, the implementation of play\-based learning still encountered several challenges, including limited learning facilities, time constraints, and diverse characteristics of children\. This study highlights that teacher creativity and pedagogical competence are essential factors in optimizing play\-based learning implementation in early childhood education\.

## [On the construction and analysis of some stochastic pseudo\-first\-order kinetic models](../publications/ca9626856c64004c7558.md)

Virginia Giorno; A\. G\. Nobile

Abstract Time\-inhomogeneous stochastic processes are constructed starting from the pseudo\-first\-order kinetic model by adopting two different approaches\. For constant carrying capacity, the transition probability density functions and the related conditional moments are determined\. The case in which the stochastic processes are restricted by a reflecting condition in the zero\-state is also analyzed\. Particular attention is paid to the first\-passage time problem through a constant boundary for time\-homogeneous processes and for time\-inhomogeneous processes with proportional intensity functions\. Various numerical computations and simulations are performed to compare the proposed models\.

## [Modeling and simulation of failure mechanisms in low\-voltage electric motors for predictive maintenance applications](../publications/ca99352675a5a0f6fb18.md)

Orazbek Sadu; Gulmira Bazil; Akmar Ainul; Altynbek Sadu; Zhanserik Karasay

Through predictive maintenance of low\-voltage electric motors, unexpected failures can be avoided\. The multi\-physics modeling and simulation framework with MATLAB FEA based on 1000 motor dataset was developed in the present study\. Operational parameters like load \(0\.57\-15 kW, mean 7\.61 kW\), voltage \(215\-246 V, mean 230\.49 V\), current \(1\-59\.87 A, mean 30\.08 A\), vibration \(\-0\.10\-1\.28 mm/s, mean 0\.50 mm/s\) and temperature \(39\.9\-102\.4 °C, mean 69\.42 °C\)\. Fault indicators include insulation degradation \(0\.1% to 99\.9%, average 49\.62%\); bearing wear \(0% to 99\.9%, average 48\.57%\); rotor bar defects \(0% to 99\.6%, average 48\.13%\); and stator winding faults \(0% to 99\.9%, average 49\.78%\)\. Some results are that the temperature and insulation degradation correlate positively by 0\.12, and that vibration and bearing wear correlate positively by 0\.07\. According to the simulation results, failure probabilities range from 0\.48 to 1\.00\. In addition, 15% of simulations exceeded the early\-warning level, requiring immediate motor maintenance\. According to the sensitivity analysis, if each fault mechanism is increased by 10%, the failure probability will increase by 4\.5\-5\.1%\. The framework facilitates condition\-based maintenance and identifies motors at risk of failure with over 85% accuracy, as well as appropriate thresholds for early action\. Results of the evaluation indicated that a quantitative and reliable approach can help improve motor reliability as well as reduce maintenance cost in industry\.

## [Synthetic corroboration: when AI interpretation looks like independent evidence](../publications/ca9fafe2cbf79d8e9ee3.md)

Yiran Du

People increasingly use generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) to interpret the motives, emotions, and likely actions of absent others\. This article develops synthetic corroboration, defined as the inflation of perceived independent target\-specific evidential support when an externally attributed AI interpretation remains substantially dependent on evidence supplied by the user\. The construct distinguishes independence of target\-specific source access and information from analytical independence: AI may contribute general knowledge, alternative hypotheses, or inferential processing without providing an independent evidential source\. Drawing on research on interpersonal inference, advice taking, source dependence, judgement aggregation, source monitoring, machine agency, and social sycophancy, the article proposes a programme of discriminating tests\. The core experiment crosses source attribution with structural transformation while holding target\-specific evidence constant, comparing AI with self\-reformulation and a human adviser given the same evidence\. The central prediction is that transformation will disproportionately increase perceived evidential independence under AI attribution and reduce subsequent acquisition of genuinely independent information\. AI–human equivalence, failure to predict information seeking, or reduction to established constructs would narrow or defeat the AI\-specific account\.n psychological fluency or agreement\.

## [Machine learning‐based damage classification of ultra‐high performance concrete slabs under contact explosions](../publications/caa07d4d6af8132fb3a5.md)

Yufei Yan; Zhouhong Zong; Yuanzheng Lin; Hanyuan Shi; Haimin Qian; Jingming Cai

Abstract The prediction of failure modes in ultra‐high‐performance concrete \(UHPC\) slabs is critical for guiding post‐blast operational planning and repair strategies for protective structures following blast events\. This study addresses the requirement by investigating the application of machine learning \(ML\) methods to failure‐mode classification\. Three representative failure modes, that is, crater, spalling, and breach, were considered, with a dataset of 638 samples compiled from field experiments and numerical simulations\. The prediction performance of four ML models, including Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), Random Forest \(RF\), XGBoost and Backpropagation \(BP\) neural network, was evaluated using a randomly selected test set\. Among the evaluated models, RF achieved the highest accuracy of 93\.8%, while BP obtained the highest mean test accuracy of 91\.7%\. A comparison with existing methods highlighted the advantages of ML‐based prediction in enhancing classification accuracy at about 20\.7 percentage points\. Furthermore, the influence of key input parameters on model performance was analyzed, providing interpretability of the results and improving the reliability of the prediction framework\.

## [Instagram Popularity Seeking and the Meaning of Happiness in Early Adulthood: A Qualitative Study](../publications/caa9f51fbaae30f109b6.md)

Aisyah Wulan Suci; Maemunah Maemunah; Isnaini Isnaini

This study explores how Instagram popularity seeking is experienced and understood in relation to the meaning of happiness in early adulthood, highlighting how visual culture and social evaluation shape emotional well\-being\. A descriptive qualitative approach was used through in\-depth interviews, digital observation, and documentation to capture participants&\#x27; direct experiences and digital behavior\. The study involved three young adult participants aged 18–21 years, consisting of one male and two females, and two female expert informants, consisting of a psychology lecturer and an Instagram observer\. The study was conducted in a university environment for the primary participants, while the expert informants were interviewed based on their relevant expertise\. The data analysis focused on recurring themes, such as identity performativity, social comparison, and emotional dependence, using the Miles and Huberman approach through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing\. Research shows that popularity on Instagram is seen as a marker of social value and modern relevance, encouraging users to adjust their appearance and content to align with dominant aesthetic norms\. Validation in the form of likes, comments, and number of followers does provide short\-term emotional satisfaction, but at the same time reinforces fragile happiness because it depends on unstable external responses\. Social comparison, the FOMO phenomenon, and repeated exposure to idealized content were described by participants as contributing to psychological pressure, including anxiety, self\-dissatisfaction, and dependence on digital appreciation for feelings of self\-worth\. These findings reveal the paradox that digital connectivity may increase emotional vulnerability and challenge participants&\#x27; perceptions of authentic well\-being\. This study concludes that the culture of popularity on Instagram is closely associated with how young adults understand and experience happiness and emotional well\-being in early adulthood\. The implications emphasize the importance of digital literacy, emotional regulation strategies, and supportive interventions to reduce the psychosocial risks of social media use\.

## [Balancing flexibility and regulatory risk: AI\-assisted strategies for non\-GAAP disclosures in competitive markets](../publications/cadc13bcc660525f5100.md)

Hrishikesh Desai

Purpose This paper develops an optimal control model to analyze how firms optimize their non\-generally accepted accounting principles \(GAAP\) disclosure strategies in competitive markets while managing regulatory risks, and examines how artificial intelligence \(AI\) capabilities in regulatory navigation and operational efficiency influence these optimal disclosure decisions\. Design/methodology/approach The study employs an open\-loop optimal control framework with a differential\-game payoff structure, using a Hamiltonian formulation and Pontryagin&\#x27;s maximum principle to derive closed\-form optimal disclosure strategies\. Findings The research reveals that optimal disclosure strategies emerge from balancing the valuation benefits of disclosure flexibility against regulatory risk\. AI capabilities affect firm strategy through two channels – \(1\) reduced regulatory sensitivity enables firms to sustain higher equilibrium flexibility levels, and \(2\) reduced adjustment costs accelerate convergence to target equilibrium flexibility\. Comparative statics analysis identifies how competitive intensity, AI capabilities and firm characteristics influence equilibrium disclosure choices\. Research limitations/implications The model employs an open\-loop formulation and is limited to a two\-firm setting\. It assumes constant model parameters over the planning horizon and therefore does not capture time\-varying market conditions or strategic feedback between firms\. Practical implications The framework provides corporate managers with analytical insights into how investments in AI\-enhanced regulatory navigation and operational efficiency influence optimal disclosure strategies\. It also provides regulators with a theoretical basis for understanding how AI capabilities moderate the marginal relationship between disclosure flexibility and regulatory intervention\. Originality/value This paper presents the first analytical model of a non\-GAAP disclosure strategy that explicitly distinguishes between AI\-enhanced regulatory navigation and operational efficiency, yielding closed\-form solutions that facilitate rigorous comparative statics and generate testable empirical predictions\.

## [Probing Planet Formation within 10 au: Dust Substructures in Extremely Compact Protoplanetary Disks](../publications/cadd9710bd6747d0b45d.md)

Pietro Curone; Gijs D\. Mulders; Nienke van der Marel; Laura M\. Pérez

Abstract Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter \(ALMA\) high\-resolution surveys have so far focused mainly on large, bright protoplanetary disks, where substructures are routinely detected, leaving compact disks poorly characterized\. Yet, the survival of millimeter emission in Class II sources implies that radial drift must have been halted by pressure traps, previously undetected due to limited angular resolution\. We present ALMA Band 7 \(0\.9 mm\) continuum observations of 11 of the smallest \( R 68 &lt; 10 au\) Class II disks in Lupus, reaching 0 \. ″ 02 \(2 au\) resolution, the highest currently available with ALMA at this wavelength\. We detect substructures in four disks, including a clear inner cavity of radius 1\.6 au, and hints of substructure in three more\. Two disks also host faint outer rings beyond their bright inner core\. Combining these results with demographic information on Class II disks observed with ALMA, we examine how the substructure detection rate varies with disk size, restricting to disks whose diameter is resolved by at least three resolution elements\. We find that nearly all disks \(≳95%\) larger than 30 au show substructures, compared to a still substantial ∼50% between 3 and 30 au, with the lower rate likely affected by optical depth\. The planet masses required to open gaps within 5 au fall in the super\-Earth to mini\-Neptune regime\. These results demonstrate that substructures are ubiquitous across the disk population, and that planet formation conditions can be probed down to a few astronomical units from the host star\.

## [Variable proficiency attainment following virtual reality cataract training: Implications for a mastery learning approach](../publications/cae896def2b14736c613.md)

Amalie Carlsson; Lars Konge; Morten la Cour; A\. Le; Ann Sofia Skou Thomsen

PURPOSE: Virtual reality simulation \(VRS\)\-based training is widely used to prepare novice cataract surgeons, yet unstandardized training regimens result in variable competence at the transition to surgery\. In many settings, training follows a directed self\-regulated learning approach, where progression is based on self\-assessed competence\. In contrast, mastery learning requires trainees to reach a predefined proficiency benchmark\. This study evaluated whether participants using directed self\-regulated learning attained proficiency on a simulation\-based test with established validity evidence, whether baseline aptitude predicted proficiency attainment, and the time required to reach the benchmark\. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included ophthalmology residents and research associates at the Department of Ophthalmology, Rigshospitalet\-Glostrup, with ≥6 months of clinical ophthalmology experience\. Participants completed a baseline test on the EyeSi Surgical Simulator and trained until they felt ready to attempt a simulation\-based test\. Passing required reaching a predefined proficiency benchmark\. Participants who did not reach the benchmark repeated testing until proficiency attainment or training was discontinued\. RESULTS: Forty participants were included; 25 \(63%\) reached the proficiency benchmark\. Baseline score was not significantly associated with proficiency attainment \(OR per 1 SD = 1\.60, 95% CI 0\.82 to 3\.32; p = 0\.18\)\. Median time to proficiency was 13 h 21 min \(range, 6 h 57 min\-31 h 37 min\)\. CONCLUSION: Directed self\-regulated learning did not ensure proficiency attainment among all participants\. No statistically significant association was found between baseline score and proficiency attainment, and variation in training time supports the rationale for evaluation and implementation of a mastery learning approach\.

## [Potential range shifts of the morphotypes within the Anastrepha fraterculus complex \(Diptera: Tephritidae\): Implications under climate change scenarios](../publications/caf10864f680fdc4c77d.md)

Damián Freilij; Juan C\. Vilardi; Paula Gómez\-Cendra

Abstract The South American fruit fly Anastrepha fraterculus is a cryptic species complex comprising at least eight morphotypes threatening fruit production across the Americas\. We modelled the current and future potential distributions of the species complex and each morphotype\. Filtered occurrence data \( n = 339\) were analysed against six non‐collinear bioclimatic predictors\. Ensemble models created with statistical and machine learning algorithms identified \~6 million km 2 of environmentally suitable area for the species complex, mainly in Brazil and Argentina\. Morphotype‐level analyses revealed contrasting range extension and suitable areas: Brazilian‐1 exhibited the broadest distribution and environmental breadth, whereas Brazilian‐2 and Brazilian‐3 are restricted to coastal regions\. High‐elevation morphotypes \(Andean, Ecuadorian, Peruvian, Venezuelan\) were strongly constrained by temperature, whereas the Mexican morphotype distribution was related to precipitation with significant potential for expansion into Central and North America\. Future projections indicated overall contractions \(18%–40%\) of high‐suitability areas for the presence of the nominal species\. We also detected southward range shifts and increased morphotype overlap in temperate regions\. Nevertheless, the remaining highly suitable areas include current zones of high fruit production\. Our results provide a morphotype‐explicit reference for anticipating invasion risk and support area‐wide integrated pest management strategies under climate change\.

## [Tryptoline stereoprobe elaboration identifies inhibitors of the GRPEL1–HSPA9 complex](../publications/caf75d2b3c1c11716fbb.md)

Rachel E\. Hayward; Raymond F\. Berkeley; Zijian Gao; Maximilian Garhammer; Marc A\. Morizono; Evert Njomen; Haoxin Li; Kristen E\. DeMeester; Victor Cociorva; Mark A\. Herzik; F\. Ulrich Hartl; Bruno N\. Melillo; Benjamin F\. Cravatt

Activity\-based protein profiling has identified hundreds of human proteins from diverse classes that react at cysteine residues with stereochemically defined electrophilic compounds \(stereoprobes\)\. The structure\-activity relationships underlying these stereoprobe\-protein interactions, however, remain poorly understood\. Here, we show that the protein interaction landscape of tryptoline acrylamide stereoprobes can be profoundly altered by structural modifications distal to the acrylamide reactive group\.
