Most stereoprobe liganding events occurred at nonorthosteric sites and evaded assignment by the machine learning\-based cofolding model Boltz\-2, which instead tended to misplace stereoprobes in orthosteric pockets \(an outcome we term &\#x27;orthostery burnout&\#x27;\)\. We found that stereoprobes reacting with C124 in the nucleotide exchange factor GRPEL1 disrupt interactions with the mitochondrial HSP70 chaperone HSPA9/mortalin, leading to impairments in mitochondrial protein import and mitophagy induction\. Our results highlight tryptoline acrylamides as a versatile source of covalent ligands targeting nonorthosteric sites on proteins, including tool compounds that perturb the mitochondrial HSP70 chaperone system\.

## [Stepwise multimodal management of acquired post\-intubation subglottic stenosis: a proposed treatment algorithm](../publications/cafbf9b1e77196c95a5c.md)

Kul Bhushan Bali; Deepthy Das; Nidhi Mohan; Vishwanatha B; Sindhuja Mudiyala

Background: Acquired post\-intubation subglottic stenosis \(SGS\) requires tailored interventions\.Aim and Objectives: To evaluate clinical presentations, management strategies, and outcomes of an individualized, stepwise multimodal surgical approach while proposing a practical treatment algorithm for affected patients\.Materials and Methods: This retrospective single\-centre case series included 10 consecutive patients with acquired post\-intubation SGS treated between January 2022\-December 2025, with last follow\-up till June 2026\. Clinical, endoscopic, radiological and outcome data were analysed descriptively\. Management was individualized according to stenosis severity, length, scar characteristics, cartilage involvement, airway stability and previous interventions\. Endoscopic treatment included coblation\-assisted scar excision, neodymium\-doped yttrium aluminium garnet \(Nd:YAG\) laser as an adjunct, balloon dilatation, selected intralesional corticosteroid and mitomycin\-C application, and temporary stenting\. Open reconstruction was reserved for advanced or recurrent disease\.Results: The mean age was 30\.3 years \(range 2 years 7 months–45 years\), and 6 patients were male\. Grade III stenosis accounted for 60% of cases\. Endoscopic management with different modalities alone was sufficient in 7 patients \(70%\), while 3 \(30%\) required open reconstruction with anterior cricoid split and cartilage grafting\. Restenosis occurred in 3 patients \(30%\), and successful decannulation was achieved in 9 of 10 patients \(90%\)\. No major postoperative complications or perioperative deaths occurred during a mean follow\-up of 12 months \(range 6–18 months\)\.Conclusion: An individualized stepwise multimodal strategy combining complementary endoscopic techniques with timely open reconstruction was associated with favorable airway outcomes in this series\. Treatment should be guided by airway anatomy, stenosis characteristics, previous interventions, and response to treatment rather than stenosis grade alone\. The proposed algorithm provides an experience\-based framework requiring validation in larger prospective multicenter studies\.

## [RGraphSpace: Rendering graphs as coherent spatial objects in ggplot2](../publications/cafea629673bb2091256.md)

Flávio Gabriel Carazza Kessler; Jonathan André Back; Lana Bazan Peters Querne; Victor Henrique Apolonio dos Santos; Mauro A\. A\. Castro

A graph describes a network structure of nodes connected by edges, and is used across many areas of science to represent relationships between entities\.When the relationships themselves are spatial, node positions carry physical meaning, and the graph must be further represented within an external frame of reference\.In R, igraph \(Csardi &amp; Nepusz, 2006\) provides powerful tools for network analysis, and the ggplot2 ecosystem \(Wickham, 2016\) does the same for visualization, drawing nodes and edges as separate layers\.Integrating the two remains challenging, however, because the geometry of these layers is not fully coordinated at rendering time, a consequence of ggplot2&\#x27;s input model in which each plot layer consumes a single rectangular table and is resolved independently\.This design works remarkably well for most applications but is restrictive for graph structures with mutually dependent components\.Because layers do not share transformed states, the graph is not rendered as a single coherent object\.Here we introduce RGraphSpace, a streamlined interface that integrates igraph with ggplot2 graphics within a normalized coordinate space\.It synchronizes node and edge layers, jointly resolving their geometry under standard aesthetic mappings\.This coherence lets the graph be anchored to external reference frames, where it becomes a spatial object embedded in a wider context\. Statement of needGraph handling in R rests on two mature foundations: igraph \(Csardi &amp; Nepusz, 2006\) for network analysis and ggplot2 \(Wickham, 2016\) for layered visualization\.The ggraph package \(Pedersen, 2025a\) bridges these, exposing relational data to the grammar of graphics\.Graph data manipulation has similarly matured through tidygraph \(Pedersen, 2025b\), which represents graphs as tidy node and edge tables\.Yet rendering a graph as a spatial object requires coordination across its components\.Because ggplot2 resolves each layer independently, node and edge layers are not fully synchronized\.Positional coordinates are shared, but other aesthetics are resolved per layer, so edges have no access to the rendered sizes of the nodes\.RGraphSpace addresses this by mapping an igraph object into a normalized coordinate space in which nodes, edges, and their associated elements are resolved together\.With node and edge geometries synchronized at rendering time, edges are drawn with respect to the final extent of the nodes they connect, and this correspondence is maintained even when node attributes are rescaled through the ggplot2 grammar\.This normalized space serves a second purpose, placing the graph within a broader spatial Carazza\-Kessler et al\. \(2026\)\.RGraphSpace: Rendering graphs as coherent spatial objects in ggplot2\.

## [Ol\-, Ḳıl\-, Ėt\- ve Eyle\- Yardımcı Fiilleri ile Kurulan Birleşik Fiiller: Dâsitân\-ı Duhter\-i Şeyh Abdullâh Örneği](../publications/cb0167f67749848faa48.md)

Muhammet Raşit Öztürk

Sondan eklemeli dillerden olan Türkçe, isim türünden kelimeleri fiilleştirmek gerekliliği ortaya çıktığında fiil yapma özelliğini taşıyan yapım eklerini kullanır\. Fiil varlığını zenginleştirmenin bir başka yolu ise “söz dizimsel türetme”dir\. İsimlerin yardımcı fiillerle birlikte kullanımı, yeni söz dizimsel birimlerin ortaya çıkmasına olanak tanır\. Türkçenin fiil varlığı içinde yer alan ol\-, ḳıl\-, ėt\- ve eyle\- fiilleri, bu işlevi yerine getiren temel yardımcı fiiller olarak dikkat çekmektedir\. Ol\- ve ḳıl\- yardımcı fiilleri hem esas fiil hem de yardımcı fiil olarak Orhon Türkçesinden beri kullanılmaktadır\. Ėt\- yardımcı fiili, Orhon Türkçesi döneminde esas fiil olarak kullanılmış, Karahanlı Türkçesi dönemiyle birlikte yardımcı fiil özelliği de kazanmıştır\. Eyle\- fiili ise esas fiil olarak ilk kez Karahanlı Türkçesi döneminde kullanılmış, yardımcı fiil hüviyetini Harezm Türkçesi döneminde kazanarak günümüze taşınmıştır\. Ol\-, ḳıl\-, ėt\- ve eyle\- yardımcı fiilleri ve bu fiillerin kurmuş oldukları birleşik fiiller, Eski Anadolu Türkçesi döneminde sıklıkla kullanılmıştır\. Bu kuruluşta görev alan yardımcı fiillerin işlevsel çeşitliliğini, yardımcı fiillerin kurduğu birleşiklerin Eski Anadolu Türkçesinden Türkiye Türkçesine aktarımını, bu aktarımın sınırlarını ve ortaya çıkan değişkeleri dikkatlere sunmayı amaçlayan bu çalışmada Eski Anadolu Türkçesi döneminin tipik bir eseri olan Dâsitân\-ı Duhter\-i Şeyh Abdullâh örneklem olarak seçilmiştir\.

## [Challenges of Employing Artificial Intelligence Applications in Education from the Perspectives of English Language Teachers](../publications/cb0e2860c8c9bbd47dd2.md)

Salam Abd Alrahman Suleman Alqtifan; Talal Abd Alhameed Salem Alodwan

The study aimed to uncover the challenges of employing artificial intelligence applications in education from the perspective of English language teachers\. To achieve this, the study followed the descriptive survey method\. The study sample consisted of \(320\) English language teachers in the Al\-Quwaysimah district\. To achieve the study objectives, a questionnaire was developed distributed across \(4\) areas: \(technical and technological challenges, material challenges, educational and human challenges, and organizational and administrative challenges\)\. The results of the study showed that the level of challenges facing English language teachers at the basic stage in employing artificial intelligence applications in education from their perspective was moderate\. The results also showed the existence of statistically significant differences \(α = 0\.05\) attributable to the effect of the education sector, with the differences favoring the public sector\. There were also statistically significant differences attributable to the effect of experience, with the differences favoring teachers with experience \(10 years or more\)\. There were also statistically significant differences attributable to the effect of academic qualification, with the differences favoring those holding a bachelor&\#x27;s degree\. In light of the study’s findings, the study recommended the need to develop the technical infrastructure and provide the necessary resources in schools, especially government sector schools, in addition to implementing continuous training programs for English language teachers to develop their competencies in employing artificial intelligence applications in education\.

## [Machine learning\-driven prediction and optimization of renewable energy integration in multi\-regional economic systems: Evidence from China’s carbon markets](../publications/cb1af48944cbef36633b.md)

Kaiwen Min; Dawei Yan

China’s commitment to carbon neutrality by 2060 requires precise, regionally differentiated forecasts of renewable energy \(RE\) penetration and carbon allowance prices to guide investment and policy\. This study presents a methodologically rigorous machine learning framework integrating five operational datasets across eight Chinese regional power markets \(2019–2023, n = 11,448 training and 2,920 test observations\)\. A leakage\-free temporal train/test split, ten\-model benchmark with Diebold\-Mariano \(DM\) significance testing, SHAP TreeExplainer interpretability, and quantile\-regression prediction intervals collectively address methodological gaps prevalent in prior RE forecasting literature\. Building on this protocol we propose Hybrid XGBoost, in which a constriction\-factor particle swarm optimizes the boosting hyperparameters, the feature subset and the prediction saturation thresholds jointly under an explicit complexity penalty, and we benchmark it against four hybrid architectures from the literature \(GA\-XGBoost, PSO\-XGBoost, Bayesian\-XGBoost and XGBoost\-ANN\) under identical data, splits and search budgets\. Under strict temporal validation, XGBoost achieves R2 = 0\.9969 \(RMSE = 0\.01661\) for daily RE penetration rate–significantly outperforming all baselines \(DM p &lt; 0\.001\)–and R2 = 0\.9971 \(RMSE = 0\.420 CNY/tCO2\) for carbon allowance prices\. Hybrid XGBoost lowers this to R2 = 0\.9972 \(RMSE = 0\.01598\), the best of the fifteen models compared and a significant gain over the hyperparameter\-only hybrids, whereas tuning hyperparameters alone improved the validation error without improving the held\-out year at all\. Calibrated 90% prediction intervals attain 0\.930 empirical coverage\. SHAP analysis identifies 7\-day autoregressive persistence and regional CO2 flux as dominant predictors; an ablation study confirms physical features alone yield R2 = 0\.9025\. A linear programming optimization module translates ML outputs into a regional RE investment allocation–prioritizing Southwest and Northeast China–projected to reduce aggregate carbon intensity by 5\.9% against the IEA Statistics baseline, while a non\-linear program that lets this response saturate leaves that plan within 0\.03 percentage points of optimal but revises the projected reduction to 4\.8%, recovering the linear case in the first\-order limit, providing a data\-driven pathway toward China’s 2030 carbon peak target\.

## [Engineering T cell\-selective chemokine inhibitors through network\-level directed evolution](../publications/cb1e4a907b738b551941.md)

Megan Payne; Fernando Durães; Charlie J\. Clark; Emma Wilde; Kalimuthu Karuppanan; Soumyanetra Chandra; Paul E\. Brennan; David J\. Hodson; Gintare Smagurauskaite; Shoumo Bhattacharya

Abstract Immune\-mediated inflammatory diseases \(IMIDs\) are sustained by chemokine\-driven recruitment of effector T cells\. Although direct suppression of T cell function can be effective, systemic immunosuppression and infection risk limit clinical utility\. Targeting chemokine networks offers an alternative strategy, yet chemokine redundancy has hindered the development of clinically effective inhibitors\. Tick evasins overcome chemokine redundancy by binding multiple chemokines\. Here we show that network\-level directed evolution of class B evasin\-derived peptides generates T cell\-selective chemokine inhibitors\. In contrast to analogous class A\-derived peptides, these preferentially bind and inhibit chemokines that drive T cell migration\. Structural modelling of chemokine:peptide complexes and structure\-guided mutagenesis suggest that evasin\-derived peptides sterically occlude receptor\-binding surfaces and that class B\-derived peptides exhibit a more compact organisation of key interaction hotspots than a previously characterised class A\-derived peptide\. Together, these findings suggest that anti\-chemokine peptide specificity can be engineered through scaffold choice and network\-level directed evolution\.

## [Влияние искусственного интеллекта на результаты деятельности фирмы: систематический обзор литературы](../publications/cb2219be1c56fb1d1f5f.md)

Дарья Павловна Степанюк; Олеся Олеговна Ярыга

This article presents a systematic review of contemporary empirical studies dedicated to examining the impact of artificial intelligence on firm performance\. The review findings demonstrate that the influence of artificial intelligence on firm activities is not a direct cause\-and\-effect relationship but rather constitutes a complex system mediated by organizational capabilities, dynamic capabilities, and contextual factors\. Based on the conducted analysis, a conceptual model is proposed, illustrating the interrelationship between formative factors, such as technological, organizational, and external ones, artificial intelligence technologies, and firm performance outcomes, including operational, financial, strategic, and sustainability indicators\. The article emphasizes the necessity of transitioning from a narrow technical approach to implementing artificial intelligence technologies to a comprehensive approach that views AI adoption as a complex organizational transformation process, and it identifies promising directions for future research, in particular, exploring the specifics of AI implementation within the Russian business context among small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\)\.

## [Multi‐Level Automated Classification of Temporomandibular Joint Degenerative Joint Disease on CBCT Using 3D Volumetric and 2D Slice‐Based Approaches](../publications/cb29adb78bc016a35e9b.md)

Abbas Ahmed Abdulqader; Lisa Liu; Zainab Abdulkader Said; Fulin Jiang; Zihan Meng; Fangyuan Cheng; Lixia Yu; Anas Saeed Al\-Zaghruri; Xianglong Han; Juan Li

BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular joint degenerative joint disease \(TMJ DJD\) causes progressive osseous changes of the mandibular condyle and articular fossa\. Although cone\-beam computed tomography \(CBCT\) enables detailed assessment, manual interpretation is time\-consuming and subject to inter\-observer variability\. OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a multilevel AI framework for CBCT\-based TMJ DJD assessment using three\-dimensional classification, quantitative volumetric analysis, and two\-dimensional slice\-based detection\. METHODS: Full\-field\-of\-view CBCT scans from 222 patients were used for three\-dimensional analysis\. A 3D V\-Net classified condyles into Normal, Osteophyte, Erosion, Flattening, and Severe Degeneration categories\. Condylar volume was quantitatively compared between TMJ DJD and non\-TMJ DJD groups and among degenerative subgroups\. For slice\-based analysis, 727 temporomandibular joints from 416 patients were retrospectively evaluated\. Automated sagittal slice extraction based on the condylion landmark generated 5787 condylar and 666 articular fossa slices\. YOLOv10 was used for multi\-lesion detection of six condylar and three fossa categories\. RESULTS: The 3D V\-Net achieved an overall sensitivity of 79\.47%\. Condylar volume differed significantly between TMJ DJD and non\-TMJ DJD groups \(ANOVA, p = 0\.025\), whereas differences among the TMJ DJD subgroups were not statistically significant\. For condylar slice\-based detection, YOLOv10 achieved 94\.0% sensitivity, 82\.8% precision, 88\.0% F1\-score, and 91\.3% AP@0\.50\. For articular fossa detection, YOLOv10 achieved 92\.41% sensitivity, 83\.91% precision, 87\.95% F1\-score, and 82\.01% AP@0\.50\. CONCLUSIONS: Three\-dimensional AI enabled overall TMJ DJD classification but showed limited discrimination of specific subgroups, particularly erosion\. Volumetric analysis differentiated DJD from non\-DJD cases but not among DJD subgroups\. In contrast, slice\-based YOLOv10 effectively detected and labelled specific condylar and fossa degenerative changes, providing more detailed lesion\-level characterization\.

## [Complicações neurológicas associadas à deficiência de micronutrientes após bypass gástrico em Y de Roux: uma revisão integrativa da literatura](../publications/cb3370e098d1e292730b.md)

Pedro Chaves Bisneto; Ana Carolina Carvalho; João Paulo Andrade; Maria Bernadete Figueiredo

Introdução: O bypass gástrico em Y de Roux \(RYGB\) é uma das técnicas mais eficazes no tratamento da obesidade grave, mas o desvio do duodeno e do jejuno proximal favorece a má absorção de micronutrientes essenciais à função neurológica\. Objetivo: Identificar as principais complicações neurológicas associadas à deficiência de micronutrientes após o RYGB descritas na literatura entre 2022 e 2026\. Metodologia: Revisão integrativa da literatura, com busca nas bases PubMed, LILACS e SciELO realizada entre maio e julho de 2026, conforme as recomendações do PRISMA 2020\. Dos 1\.020 registros identificados, 12 estudos compuseram a amostra final\. Resultados: Nove estudos \(75,0%\) eram relatos de caso, dois eram estudos de coorte e um, revisão sistemática\. Seis abordaram a deficiência de tiamina, três a de cobre e três deficiências múltiplas ou de outros micronutrientes\. A encefalopatia de Wernicke manifestou\-se predominantemente nos primeiros meses de pós\-operatório, frequentemente precipitada por vômitos e com apresentação atípica, e apresentou boa resposta à reposição precoce\. A mieloneuropatia por deficiência de cobre surgiu cerca de duas décadas após a cirurgia, mimetizou a deficiência de vitamina B12 e doenças desmielinizantes e evoluiu com sequelas\. Não foram identificadas complicações atribuídas exclusivamente à deficiência de vitamina B12\. Conclusão: As complicações neurológicas após o RYGB apresentam padrão cronológico definido e acompanham o paciente ao longo de toda a vida, o que reforça a necessidade de suspeição clínica, de monitorização laboratorial contínua e de suplementação mantida a longo prazo\.

## [Dor lombopélvica na gestação: Abordagem fisioterapêutica, incapacidade funcional e qualidade de vida](../publications/cb3601f560e26fbe6336.md)

Ellen A Santos; GABRIELA SARNACKI ZAITTER; Larissa Frazão Torres; Renata Araújo Cardoso; Giusara Zuley Curvelo Rosado

Introdução: A dor lombopélvica na gestação pode comprometer atividades cotidianas; intensidade da dor, incapacidade funcional e qualidade de vida são desfechos distintos\. Objetivo: Analisar criticamente as evidências sobre a abordagem fisioterapêutica da dor lombopélvica na gestação e seus efeitos na incapacidade funcional e na qualidade de vida\. Métodos: Revisão narrativa com buscas no PubMed e localização de artigos da coleção SciELO Brasil por mecanismo externo de busca na web, até 26 de setembro de 2026\. A seleção considerou pertinência clínica, desenho e desfechos, com leitura integral das fontes utilizadas na síntese\. Resultados: O exercício terapêutico apresentou resultados favoráveis para dor entre seis e doze semanas, com efeito funcional menos estável\. Estudos brasileiros localizados na coleção SciELO complementaram a análise de intervenções e avaliação funcional\. A associação de exercício e educação superou a educação isolada em síntese de ensaios; estimativas para cintos pélvicos incluíram ausência de efeito\. A qualidade de vida foi menos estudada\. Conclusão: O exercício terapêutico pode reduzir a dor de gestantes sintomáticas; os efeitos sobre incapacidade variam conforme comparação e tempo\. Não há benefício global uniforme demonstrado para qualidade de vida nem protocolo único superior\.

## [Instrumentations, Devices, Machines and Their Health Condition Monitoring Techniques Used in Biomedical Engineering: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/cb37d8665fed4e0d4d3b.md)

Moussa Hamadache; Noureddine Messaoudi; Samia Belkacem

The instrumentations, devices, and machines used in biomedical applications have a highly intricate structure that necessitates not just a substantial number of components \(i\.e\., medical imaging machines; medical sensing devices; robotics; wearable devices; and e\-Health remote monitoring systems\), but also different types of technologies \(mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic devices to operate, and electrical and/or electronic devices to control\)\. This intricacy makes them susceptible to breakdowns and malfunctions, which can result in injuries and, in severe cases, fatal accidents\. Therefore, developing effective health condition monitoring \(HCM\) methods is essential for handling fault detection and diagnosis \(FDD\), fault\-tolerant control \(FTC\), lifecycle estimation \(LCE\), and prognosis and health management \(PHM\) in the field of biomedical engineering\. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the contemporary techniques for fault detection, diagnosis, and prognosis in the diversified smart\-biomedical systems \(SBSs\) and their different applications\. Ultimately, the goal is to provide a state\-of\-the\-art platform for researchers, doctors \(i\.e\., the operators\), maintenance teams, and experts to investigate, innovate, and implement the most effective HCM techniques for their use, thereby facilitating the rapid advancement of monitoring and fault detection in biomedical engineering during a period of heightened interest in condition\-based maintenance \(CBM\) and the incorporation of advanced technology in the medical field, particularly, with the availability of big data and the Internet of Things \(IoT\) within the blooming era of artificial intelligence\(AI\), especially at present, with the fourth industrial revolution\.

## [Local Temporal Contrasts on Human Motion Data Induce a Latent Geometry](../publications/cb3ac511503551e98dd3.md)

Lourenço A\. Rodrigues; Felix Putze

Time series such as recordings of human motion data often encode structure across multiple temporal scales, and when a latent state determining this sequence evolves, this structure needs to survive in the representation space for downstream use\. Yet the currently prevalent attention\-based encoders paired with sequence\-level pooling have made single\-vector, pointwise comparison the default mode of inference, discarding the trajectory a sequence traces through the representation space\. We propose recovering this geometric structure directly, without relying on forecasting\-based objectives, by training an encoder model \(SemTAC\) with a temporal\-neighborhood contrastive loss: representations that satisfy local consistency everywhere must give rise to a coherent global structure, letting inference happen at temporal scales beyond those seen during training\. We evaluate SemTAC against four baselines on a five\-step motion sequence discrimination task: the same architecture trained with a classification or a standard contrastive objective, and two established self\-supervised time\-series methods, TS\-TCC and TS2Vec\. At the full sequence length all five are broadly competitive, but on incomplete, truncated sequences SemTAC holds a large advantage: a median F1 of 0\.77 one step before the sequence completes, against 0\.27\-0\.70 for the four baselines\. A hyperparameter\-matched ablation attributes this effect specifically to the temporal\-contrastive objective\. SemTAC&\#x27;s representation trajectories are also the only ones among these five to exhibit interpretable geometric structures, exceeding a no\-structure chance baseline on a displacement\-smoothness metric which we introduce\. This is evidence that its objective, not classification accuracy alone, produces genuinely temporally\-ordered trajectories\.

## [Static Inference Architecture for Data Traceability in Legacy Natural/Adabas Ecosystems: An Entity Disambiguation Approach](../publications/cb3d200f207e6613b823.md)

Julián Ignacio Perdiguero; Pedro Osvaldo Falabella

Este trabajo aborda la opacidad en la trazabilidad de datos dentro de sistemas críticos de gran escala desarrollados en Natural con bases de datos Adabas\. La erosión de la documentación técnica y el uso extensivo de alias técnicos con restricciones de longitud \(DDM\) generan riesgos significativos en la identificación de procesos de negocio\. Para resolver este desafío, se propone una metodología de Ingeniería Inversa determinística basada en un motor de Análisis Estático de Código de cuatro fases: Sanitización Semántica, Normalización de Metadatos, Inferencia de Impacto CRUD y Persistencia Relacional\. A diferencia de los enfoques puramente probabilísticos basados en IA, esta metodología utiliza un motor de curación basado en diccionarios \(M\.I\.T\.D\.\) que elimina el margen de error en entornos de alta criticidad normativa\. Los resultados demuestran una reducción del 30% en falsos positivos y permiten identificar procesos de escritura críticos en tablas maestras que anteriormente permanecían ocultos tras alias técnicos\. Este marco de trabajo proporciona una hoja de ruta confiable y precisa para la mitigación de riesgos en proyectos de migración, refactorización y cumplimiento regulatorio en los sectores bancario y de seguros, cerrando la brecha entre la complejidad legacy y los estándares arquitectónicos modernos\.

## [Sarcopenia in Patients with Axial Spondyloarthritis: Associations with TNF Inhibitor Therapy and Exploratory Ultrasound Findings](../publications/cb435c4ee427cc42093d.md)

Cagla Karaoglu; Özlem Pehlivan; Halise Hande Gezer; Rıdvan Sivritepe; Fatma Kulalı; Sema Basat

Background/Aims: Sarcopenia has gained increasing attention as a potential comorbidity in axial spondyloarthritis \(axSpA\)\. This study aimed to assess the frequency of sarcopenia in patients with axSpA and to investigate its association with tumor necrosis factor inhibitor \(TNFi\) therapy\. A secondary objective was to explore the potential value of ultrasound\-based muscle measurements in identifying sarcopenia\. Materials and Methods: This cross\-sectional study enrolled 62 adult patients with axSpA who were evaluated during routine rheumatology follow\-up\. Clinical data, including disease activity, functional status, and spinal mobility, were recorded\. Muscle strength, physical performance, and body composition were assessed in accordance with current sarcopenia definitions\. Selected thigh and lumbar muscle parameters were measured using musculoskeletal ultrasound\. Statistical analyses included comparative tests and regression modeling\. Results: Probable sarcopenia was identified in 22\.6% of patients, while 12\.9% met the criteria for sarcopenia; no cases of severe sarcopenia were detected\. Sarcopenia was observed less frequently among patients receiving TNFi therapy compared with those not treated with TNFi\. TNFi use was associated with a reduced likelihood of sarcopenia\. Ultrasound measurements of the rectus femoris muscle showed modest associations with sarcopenia status, although their diagnostic performance was limited\. Conclusion: Sarcopenia is common in patients with axSpA\. In this cross\-sectional study, TNFi use was associated with a lower prevalence of sarcopenia, although a causal relationship cannot be established\. Ultrasound\-derived muscle parameters showed limited discriminatory performance and should be considered exploratory\. Cite this article as: Karaoğlu Ç, Pehlivan Ö, Gezer HH, Sivritepe R, Kulalı F, Basat S\. Sarcopenia in Patients with Axial Spondyloarthritis: Associations with TNF Inhibitor Therapy and Exploratory Ultrasound Findings\. ArchRheumatol\. Published online October 14, 2026\. doi: 10\.5152/ ArchRheumatol\.2026\.26292\.

## [Digital twin\-driven transformation of hydropower and dam structures: toward smart structural health monitoring](../publications/cb48b2abea28fde7029c.md)

Amal Aboulhassane; Abdelilah Jerrari; Fouzia Kassou; Om El Khaiat Moustachi

ABSTRACT In the digital transformation era, civil engineering infrastructure is undergoing profound life\-cycle evolution, enhancing efficiency, safety, sustainability, and resilience\. Given their unique nature and the complexity of their design, construction, and management, as well as their direct impact on water security and public safety, Hydropower and Dam Structures \(HDS\) are a high\-priority domain for the implementation of digital technologies, particularly Building Information Modeling \(BIM\), the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence\. This paper aims to provide an in\-depth state\-of\-the\-art review of the implementation of digital technologies, particularly BIM and Digital Twin, in HDS, with a focus on real\-time Structural Health Monitoring \(SHM\)\. This review builds on a systematic and critical analysis of more than 120 carefully selected, highly relevant references\. It investigates the main digital technologies supporting HDS transformation \(information modeling, data acquisition and pipelines, and data processing\) and highlights adoption drivers and barriers in developed and developing countries\. It clarifies the concepts of BIM and Digital Twin, along with the supporting tools and technologies\. It also summarizes the most recent life\-cycle HDS applications and discusses interoperability challenges and potential solutions\. In particular, the review provides further insights into real\-time SHM of HDS by analyzing the most advanced BIM\-driven case studies integrating the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, numerical simulations, and remote sensing\. This review establishes a comprehensive foundation and provides practical recommendations to guide researchers and practitioners seeking to design, assess, and operationalize digital solutions for large civil infrastructure, thereby accelerating digital transformation while strengthening safety, intelligence, and resilience\.

## [ITALMUD: a Computational Terminology of the Italian Translation of the Babylonian Talmud](../publications/cb48d5f376acafa02738.md)

Emiliano Giovanetti; Andrea Bellandi; Flavia Sciolette

ITALMUD is a multilingual computational terminology built from the Italian translation of the Babylonian Talmud\. Terms were extracted from glossaries compiled during ten years of translation work and modeled using the OntoLex\-Lemon model\. The resource includes over 1,600 terms in Italian, Hebrew, and Aramaic\. A key innovation that was introduced involved linking terms to the CompL\-it computational lexicon of the Italian language, in order to place the terminology within a rich network of semantic relations and enable more sophisticated linguistic searches\. ITALMUD is available as an open resource and conforms to the principles of Linked Open Data to ensure maximum interoperability and reuse\.

## [A STUDY OF CONSUMER BEHAVIOR IN CHOOSING ONLINE TRANSPORTATION SERVICES IN MADIUN CITY](../publications/cb49b08b44dcb581ba23.md)

Tannia Regina; Ahmad Fitriansyah

One innovation in the development of information and communication technology is the emergence of online transportation services\. Online transportation services not only offer easier mobility but also create new business models that shape consumer behavior and preferences\. With online transportation, consumers have many choices and can easily compare the services offered\. This underscores the importance of understanding which factors consumers in Madiun City consider most when choosing online transportation services\. This study examines consumer behavior in choosing online transportation services in Madiun City\. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, this study focuses on an in\-depth understanding of the factors that influence consumer decisions\. The results show several key factors that significantly influence consumer behavior: ease of access, competitive rates, service speed, and safety\. In addition, frequent promotions and discounts are also strong attractions\. This study concludes that online transportation service providers need to continuously improve service quality and innovate to meet dynamic consumer expectations\. The results of this study are expected to provide valuable insights for online transportation businesses and local governments in developing policies that support the sustainable growth of the digital economy in Madiun City\.Salah satu inovasi perkembangan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi adalah munculnya layanan transportasi daring\. Layanan transportasi daring tidak hanya menawarkan kemudahan mobilitas, tetapi juga menciptakan model bisnis baru yang berdampak pada perilaku dan preferensi konsumen\. Pada transportasi daring, konsumen memiliki banyak pilihan dan dapat dengan mudah membandingkan layanan yang ditawarkan\. Hal ini mendasari pentingnya untuk memahami faktor\-faktor apa saja yang menjadi pertimbangan utama bagi konsumen di Kota Madiun dalam memilih layanan transportasi daring\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji perilaku konsumen dalam memilih jasa transportasi daring \(online\) di Kota Madiun\. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif, penelitian ini berfokus pada pemahaman mendalam mengenai faktor\-faktor yang memengaruhi keputusan konsumen\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ada beberapa faktor utama yang sangat memengaruhi perilaku konsumen, yaitu kemudahan akses, tarif yang kompetitif, kecepatan layanan, dan faktor keamanan\. Selain itu, promosi dan diskon yang sering ditawarkan juga menjadi daya tarik yang kuat\. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa perusahaan penyedia jasa transportasi daring perlu terus meningkatkan kualitas layanan dan berinovasi untuk memenuhi ekspektasi konsumen yang dinamis\. Hasil studi ini diharapkan dapat memberikan wawasan berharga bagi pelaku bisnis transportasi daring dan pemerintah daerah dalam menyusun kebijakan yang mendukung pertumbuhan ekonomi digital yang berkelanjutan di Kota Madiun\.

## [Seasonal niche shifts and foraging plasticity of the Southern Gelada \(Theropithecus gelada obscurus Heuglin, 1863\) \(Cercopithecidae, Papionini\) within the extreme Afro\-alpine ecosystem of the Abune Yosef Zigit Community Conservation Area, Ethiopia](../publications/cb49d7a350e30b5f66a1.md)

Setie Ewnetu; Zerihun Girma

Understanding how primates adapt their foraging strategies to fluctuating environmental conditions is a central theme in behavioral ecology\. The extreme Afro\-alpine ecosystem presents a unique setting to test predictions of Optimal Foraging Theory and the Fallback Food Hypothesis due to its severe seasonal shifts in resource availability\. This study investigated the dietary composition, seasonal variation, food preferences \(dietary selectivity\), and foraging plasticity of the Southern Gelada \( Theropithecus gelada obscurus \) in the Abune Yosef Zigit Community Conservation Area, Ethiopia\. Using instantaneous scan sampling and vegetation surveys across dry and wet seasons, we recorded 761 feeding records encompassing 25 food items\. Forbs dominated the diet \(55\.7%\), followed by grasses \(42\.7%\), and insects \(1\.6%\)\. Geladas exhibited a consistent bimodal feeding pattern but demonstrated pronounced seasonal niche shifts\. In the dry season, they highly expanded their dietary breadth \(Shannon H&\#x27; = 2\.31\) and relied heavily on underground roots, aligning with fallback food strategies\. In the wet season, the dietary niche narrowed \(H&\#x27; = 1\.92\), with greater reliance on grass blades and young shoots\. Electivity indices revealed highly dynamic, context dependent selectivity rather than fixed preferences, with preference rankings shifting between seasons\. These findings highlight the remarkable behavioral plasticity of geladas and underscore their ability to dynamically adjust foraging strategies to survive in extreme, highly seasonal environments\.

## [Sustainable water management in urban areas of Pakistan: challenges and future policy directions](../publications/cb4c421a9ec142f4552c.md)

Bushra Azhar; Gul Zareen Ghafoor; Naghmana Ghafoor; Faiza Sharif; Eman Sarfraz

Urban water management challenges in Pakistan are intensifying due to the rapid urbanization, increasing population, rising demand for limited water resources, climate change and inadequate infrastructure\. The issues of water insecurity and unsustainable urban development are growing because of water scarcity, depleting groundwater reserves, poor water quality, urban flooding and lack of water governance\. This review consolidates the assessment of sustainable management of urban water resources in Pakistan from various perspectives considering the challenges, lessons learnt from novel water management approaches, and the policy priority for fortifying water resilience at urban level\. In this paper, a detailed review has been carried out considering the latest literature published during 2018 to 2025 including articles, reports and policy documents of national and international organizations\. Four thematic areas \(urban water management challenges, sustainable management approaches, international experiences and policy implications\) were chosen and used in a synthesis of relevant studies from the following key academic databases\. The review revealed a very complex matrix of urban water issues which can only be tackled through a sectoral approach\. This paradox of urban water is caused by the urbanization which exacerbates the groundwater depletion and urban flood vulnerability\. Furthermore, water security and climate resilience are further compromised by inadequate institutional collaboration, obsolete infrastructure and weak governance and wastewater treatment\. Optimizing water resource management requires sustainable design of urban development, governmental reforms and climatic adaptation\. Integrated Water Resources Management \(IWRM\), Nature Based Solutions \(NbS\), wastewater reuse, rainwater harvesting, managed aquifer recharge and smart water technologies have great potential for urban water sustainability\. The review finds that the governance system in Pakistan needs to be climate resilient, resource efficient and integrated to improve the water security and resilience of cities\.

## [Secure Boot and Firmware Update Framework for ARM Cortex\-M Embedded IoT Devices](../publications/cb5ac5a5cf6df30722d1.md)

Lau Wei Cheng; Beh L\. Wei

The paper presents a lightweight and well\-impervious security framework suitable to ARM Cortex\-M\-based IOEs embedded devices, which will serve an important purpose of presenting secure boot and firmware update operations in resource\-constrained systems\. As IoT implementations and applications in sensitive parts of our life like healthcare, smart infrastructure, and industrial control systems increase exponentially, embedded devices become more exposed to firmware tampering, write malicious code and update securities\. The framework that is proposed addresses such threats by employing a multi\-layered cryptographic approach, suitable to the framework by symmetric encryption with the use of AES\-GCM, offering confidentiality, elliptic curve digital signature algorithm \(ECDSA\) providing authentication, and the SHA\-256 hash to provide integrity verification\. A trusted bootloader \(« a procedure incorporating cryptographic functions used to secure a bootloader implementation »,\) in a trusted ROM who administers cryptographic verification of the firmware signature with the help of a hardware\-based root of trust prior to handing off control to the application firmware\. As an additional measure the rollback protection is implemented with the help of version control to avoid firmware downgrade until known vulnerabilities are eliminated\. The firmware update process allows encrypted over\-the\-air \( OTA \) update process to execute safe remote updates, storing the data maliciously and risking transmission\. An atomic and fail safe update process is achieved through double\-buffering\. The experimental system was used and tested on STM32F429 Cortex\-M4 microcontroller, and it successfully detected unauthorized modification of the firmware and was able to withstand rollback attacks\. Performance evaluation with the bootloader as the benchmark shows the latency was only 10 milliseconds and the number of Flash memory usage was less than 0\.05 percent\. These outcomes confirm the application of the framework in the low\-power and memory\-constrained embedded systems without undermining state\-of\-the\-art security assurances\. The approach is compared to the current solutions in security to show a very usable set of efficiency, scalability and ease of implementation, which makes the presented approach an optimal one to be used in production IoT systems\. A discussion on future improvements is provided wherein they would want to integrate it with hardware security modules and supporting quantum\-resilient cryptographic primitives that would make the system secure in the long term\.

## [Do People Still Matter? Healthcare in the Age of Artificial Intelligence](../publications/cb5b99158b3dd454c058.md)

Julie A\. Haizlip; Katy Hall; Natalie May

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) platforms are becoming increasingly prevalent in healthcare\. Unlike previous technologies, AI has the capability to perform tasks previously considered uniquely human including synthesizing historical information and data to establish a clinical diagnosis and constructing a treatment plan\. AI promises to improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery and development, and enhance access to healthcare\. The overall impact that AI will have on the well\-being of individuals who provide and receive care, however, is less obvious\. This article examines the potential and pitfalls of AI in medicine through the lens of mattering and its importance to human flourishing\. Mattering is a psychological construct that encompasses the human needs to be noticed, feel significant, and contribute\. It arises from interpersonal interactions and is based on perceptions of our value within our communities and society\. Mattering is inherently relational, is a significant contributor to psychological well\-being, and may be at risk in the age of AI\. The authors describe the foundations of mattering and its relevance to medicine; the potential impacts of AI on mattering in medicine from the clinician, patient, and trainee perspectives; and propose a framework for integrating AI into healthcare such that mattering is preserved for all stakeholders\.

## [The Shift from Google Search to ChatGPT: How Generative AI Is Changing Students’ Information\-Seeking Behaviour](../publications/cb5f8aaf5a465c06b2a6.md)

Prof\. Vishwas Kenchi; Prof\. Vishwas Kenchi; Rutuja More; Sarika Kore; Jay Shinde

The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools such as ChatGPT is changing how students search for, understand, and verify academic information, a role long held by search engines such as Google\. This study examines students’ self\-reported information\-seeking behaviour with Google Search and ChatGPT, covering frequency of use, purpose, first\-source preference, reasons for adoption, trust, verification practice, and perceived change\. A descriptive, quantitative survey was conducted using a 25\-item structured Google Forms questionnaire administered to college and university students through convenience sampling \(N = 200\)\. Data were analysed using frequency and percentage analysis\. Of the respondents, 73\.5% use ChatGPT/AI at least once a day, and 61\.2% name ChatGPT/AI as their first source for academic answers, compared with 30\.6% for Google Search\. Understanding concepts, faster answers, and easier explanations were the main reasons for use\. Trust was conditional: 59\.2% verify ChatGPT answers always or often, 59\.2% have encountered incorrect or misleading output at least sometimes, and Google Search was the most common verification source \(42\.9%\)\. In total, 93\.9% reported at least some change in how they find information\. The findings point to a hybrid, AI\-assisted pattern rather than a replacement of search engines; however, they rest on self\-reported data from a non\-probability sample and cannot be generalised\.

## [Meldrum&\#x27;s acid derivatives as promising platforms for nanotechnology applications](../publications/cb6874e4c31a1439fb58.md)

Isaac Moura Araújo; Matheus dos Santos Lourenço; Ingrid Gonçalves Pereira Dantas; Maria Andressa Nicácio de Lima; Cícera Laura Roque Paulo; Iasminy Macedo; Romario Matheus Conceição de Oliveira; Lucas Dos Santos Sá; Ana Georgia Amaro Alencar Bezerra Matos; Welington Soares Feitosa; Luis Pereira de Morais; Diógenes de Queiroz Dias; Leandro Marques Correia; Cícera Datiane de Morais Oliveira–Tintino

Meldrum&\#x27;s acid derivatives have emerged as versatile molecular platforms with significant potential for nanotechnology applications due to their unique structural, photophysical, and functional properties\. Although traditionally employed as synthetic intermediates in organic chemistry, recent advances have demonstrated their relevance in the development of smart fluorophores, biosensors, molecular probes, and stimulus\-responsive systems\. This review discusses the structural characteristics of Meldrum&\#x27;s acid that underpin its remarkable synthetic versatility, including the highly acidic methylene group, the gem\-dimethyl effect, and the cyclic gem\-diacetal framework, which enable extensive molecular functionalization and the construction of π\-conjugated systems\. The photophysical behavior of arylidene derivatives, particularly their donor–π–acceptor architecture and intramolecular charge transfer mechanisms, has enabled the design of enzyme\-responsive fluorescent probes and bioimaging agents with high sensitivity and selectivity\. Furthermore, the compatibility of these derivatives with polymeric, lipid\-based, magnetic, and metallic nanocarriers highlights their potential for controlled drug delivery, molecular imaging, antimicrobial nanomedicine, and theranostic applications\. Recent studies also indicate promising biological activities, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, antiproliferative, and antibiotic\-modulating effects, expanding their potential beyond diagnostic applications\. Despite these advances, important challenges remain, particularly the limited number of studies addressing direct nanoencapsulation, long\-term stability in biological environments, comprehensive toxicological evaluation, and in vivo validation\. Overall, the integration of Meldrum&\#x27;s acid derivatives into multifunctional nanoplatforms represents a promising strategy for developing next\-generation diagnostic and therapeutic systems\. Continued interdisciplinary research combining medicinal chemistry, materials science, nanotechnology, and molecular biology will be essential to translate these compounds from experimental research into clinically relevant biomedical applications\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN KENYAN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES: ARE THEY PREPARED FOR THE SHIFT? AWARENESS, READINESS, AND EMERGING TRENDS AMONG LIBRARIANS](../publications/cb6dfdc4b51769edb495.md)

Rahab Koech; Paul Kibet Maina; Faith Masinza

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is transforming academic library services globally, requiring librarians to adapt to emerging technologies\. This study examined Kenyan university librarians&\#x27; awareness and readiness for AI integration in library services\. The study used a descriptive survey design and targeted professional librarians at accredited public and private universities\. Researchers collected data through online questionnaires distributed via librarians’ WhatsApp groups\. Of the 63 universities targeted, 45 librarians responded, yielding a 71% response rate\. Findings showed high AI awareness: 76% were aware of AI initiatives, 82% actively followed AI developments, and 78% were familiar with AI benefits\. Additionally, 73% felt confident discussing AI\-related issues\. However, only 44% had attended AI\-related training, highlighting a gap between awareness and practical preparedness\. The study concludes that although librarians demonstrate positive attitudes toward AI, greater investment in training, infrastructure, and institutional support is needed to enhance AI readiness\.

## [Advancing early detection of Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations](../publications/cb71c8dd15d6a1cce2c2.md)

Le Qu; Yan Wang; Lina Ren; Chi Zhang; Zihui Guo; Le Zhang; Xiaoyan Pang; Sha Sha

Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care\. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase\. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late\-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role\. While cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) and positron emission tomography \(PET\) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs\. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost\-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking\. Additionally, non\-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large\-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis\. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain \(NFL\), neurogranin \(Ng\), β\-secretase 1 \(BACE1\) and synaptosomal\-associated protein 25 \(SNAP\-25\)\. Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation\. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non\-invasive carriers \(saliva, urine and tears\)\. It further synthesizes cohort\-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics \(AUC, sensitivity, specificity\) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head\-to\-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence\-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies\.

## [Automatic Trajectory Planning from Preoperative MRI images Using the AI\-Optimized RRT\* Algorithm for Robotic Breast Ultrasound](../publications/cb73a2cc28ba195edf14.md)

Ghizlane Akrramou; My Hachem El Yousfi Alaoui; Bassma Jioudi; Safia Boutinkhar

Ultrasound imaging is the most widely used technique for detecting and diagnosing breast cancer, as it provides real\-time images in a non\-invasive and inexpensive manner\. However, performing ultrasound examinations requires experienced and well\-trained operators either for probe manipulation during acquisition or during image interpretation, which makes this technique dependent\. This dependency requires the employment of sonographers with extensive training and experience, which may limit access to this technique in remote areas and also expose experts to serious health issues due to repetitive movements\. To overcome these difficulties, robotic ultrasound systems have emerged in recent years to enable conventional ultrasound examinations to be performed in an automated and standardized way\. Our study contributes to this field through an integrated approach to automated planning of robotic breast ultrasound trajectories\. This approach is based on the application of a developed version of the rapidly\-exploring random tree \(RRT\) trajectory planning algorithm to pre\-operational threedimensional \(3D\) magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) images\. We performed simulations with the three versions of the algorithm RRT, RRT\* and RRT\* with 30% reinforcement learning \(RL\) on two different patients\. The results obtained demonstrate the potential of the RRT algorithm with 30% RL to obtain optimized trajectories with high fluidity and a short path while ensuring total and homogeneous coverage adapted to different complex breast morphologies\.

## [What craft\-makers know, and what they need: mapping skills and learning preferences across European craft\-ecosystems](../publications/cb873f8ed435a6a0ef98.md)

Luca Pareschi; Francesca Leonardi

This article investigates which skills contemporary craft\-makers consider most relevant, which they prefer to develop or outsource, and how these preferences reflect different educational contexts\. We conducted fieldwork in four European craft ecosystems \(Bassano del Grappa, Venice, Dals Långed, Bornholm\) through interviews, an online questionnaire, and three co\-creation workshops\. We develop a framework comprising five skill areas: craft\-making and technical, technological, business, communication and selling, and transversal skills\. Our findings reveal how craft\-making is shaped by a complex interplay between the primacy of craft\-making skills, the uneasy yet unavoidable role of managerial and communication skills, and persistent tensions around technology and sustainability\. Craft\-makers generally prefer to develop making and transversal skills while outsourcing business and administrative activities\. Learning is also constrained by limited time, and economic precarity, while national educational systems shape distinct career pathways and skill needs, requiring context\-sensitive policy support\.

## [Caracterización del lodo residual oleoso y su mezcla con el fuel oíl de la generación distribuida](../publications/cb91657c656cb46cc279.md)

Ms\. C\. Jorge de los Santos Portuondo Pera; Dr\. C\. Lorenzo Alfredo Enríquez García; Dr\. C\. Francisco Lafargue Pérez

En la industria del petróleo y el gas, se obtiene una cantidad apreciable de residuos oleosos, los cuales pueden generar productos de valor agregado para su uso como combustible\. El trabajo tiene como objetivo determinar las propiedades físicas \(viscosidad, densidad y valor calórico\) del lodo residual oleoso y sus mezclas con el fuel oíl con diferentes fracciones provenientes de la generación distribuida con contenidos de agua del 4% y 12%v/v, lo cuales son las magnitudes presentes en el lodo\. Se emplean los métodos basados en las normas ASTM D 445, ASTM D1298, ASTM D240 y ASTM D95 para determinar dichas propiedades\. Se comprobó que el lodo con contenido de agua de 12%v/v, solamente podrá utilizarse de manera limitada entre el 4% y 6% de la mezcla como combustible en generadores de vapor, debido a la presencia de agua, por lo tanto es necesario la aplicación de un tratamiento sostenible que garantice su desmulsificación\.

## [Performance and eco\-efficiency of high\-strength concrete incorporating a screened quaternary low\-carbon binder](../publications/cb974f54435d09f24168.md)

Prathibha P\. Shetty; Asha Udaya Rao

Abstract This study investigates the development and performance of high\-strength concrete designed for an M65 target grade incorporating an optimized quaternary low\-carbon binder system comprising Ordinary Portland Cement \(50%\), Class F fly ash \(20%\), ground granulated blast furnace slag \(15–25%\), and calcined seashell powder \(5–15%\)\. Binder proportions were systematically investigated using an S/N\-ratio\-based comparative screening approach to rank the predefined mixtures based on compressive strength\. A comprehensive experimental evaluation was conducted to assess mechanical properties, durability characteristics, and eco\-efficiency\. Results indicate that the incorporation of industrial and aqua\-industrial waste materials significantly reduces carbon footprint and embodied energy compared to conventional OPC\-based concrete, while demonstrating continued strength development at later ages and enhancing long\-term durability\. The developed quaternary binder system demonstrates strong potential as a sustainable and practically viable solution for high\-performance concrete, promoting effective waste valorisation and contributing to the objectives of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs 9, 12, and 13\)\.

## [Edge\-Based Long\-TermAutomated Monitoring of Budgerigar Vocal Activity Using YAMNet](../publications/cb9e755cda500ab9d0d3.md)

Aldiyar T\. Agishev; Irina I\. Arifulova; Margulan Ibraimov; N\.V\. Surovtseva; Serik A\. Khokhlov; Dauren Zhexebay; Maxim V\. Kulemin

Continuous monitoring of animal behavior may provide quantitative information on responses to environmental changes; however, its application in seismobiological research requires reliable characterization of baseline behavioral variability\. This study developed and evaluated an edge\-based bioacoustic monitoring system for the continuous analysis of vocal activity in budgerigars \(Melopsittacus undulatus\)\. Ten birds were monitored under stable housing conditions from June 2025 to May 2026\. Audio was processed locally on a Raspberry Pi\-based system that combined a pretrained YAMNet feature extractor with a task\-specific binary classifier\. Vocal activity was quantified using the vocal activity second \(VAS\), defined as a 1 s interval containing at least one detected vocalization\. Time\-series analysis revealed a pronounced diel organization of vocal activity, with increased activity during daylight hours and minimal activity at night, together with seasonal variability\. Wavelet and periodogram analyses identified a periodic component near 24 h, with weaker components within the 2–8 h range\. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous edge\-based monitoring of avian vocal behavior and establish a quantitative analysis of acoustic activity\. The present study represents a methodological framework for the collection and analysis of avian acoustic signals using machine learning and computational signal processing approaches\. The proposed approach provides a quantitative framework for investigating changes in avian behavior and for evaluating whether potential behavioral responses in vocal organization are associated with environmental factors\.

## [Behavioral characterization of 5xFAD mice using standardized decision\-making and open field assays](../publications/cba0fb367649316fb4c0.md)

Nilufar Imomdodova; Sayli Korde; Youjin Lee; Sophia Cinquemani; Eun Jung Hwang

The 5xFAD mouse is a widely used transgenic model of Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\), characterized by early and aggressive amyloid\-β plaque accumulation\. However, the extent to which plaque burden in this model predicts functional impairment remains unclear, particularly during early to mid stages of pathology when substantial plaque deposition is already present\. To further characterize behavior in this model using standardized assays, we systematically evaluated feedback\-based associative learning, choice\-switching behavior, and open field behavior in 5xFAD and wild\-type mice \(2–9 months of age\) using the International Brain Laboratory decision\-making task, a rigorously standardized behavioral paradigm, together with the commonly used open field test\. Despite robust, age\-dependent plaque accumulation, 5xFAD mice did not differ from age\-matched controls in associative learning, choice\-switching behavior, anxiety\-like behavior, or locomotor activity\. These results indicate that substantial amyloid plaque accumulation was not associated with measurable deficits in the behavioral domains examined during the early to mid stages of pathological progression\. Our findings provide a standardized behavioral characterization of the 5xFAD model and highlight the need for more sensitive functional assays to further clarify the relationship between early amyloid pathology and behavioral outcomes in AD research\.

## [Financial Inclusion, Agricultural Productivity, and Sustainable Development: Evidence from a Bayesian Hierarchical Model in Developing Asia](../publications/cba65b687da02509ef9c.md)

Hong Anh Thi Nguyen

Sustainable development has become a major concern, particularly in developing Asian countries, where increasing pressures arise from structural imbalances in both the financial system and agricultural production\. Although financial inclusion has expanded significantly, its effectiveness in supporting productive sectors, especially agriculture, remains uneven\. At the same time, agricultural productivity continues to play an important role in improving rural income, ensuring food security, and supporting long\-term development\. However, existing studies often examine financial inclusion or agricultural productivity separately, leaving their combined role in sustainable development insufficiently explored\. This study uses panel data from 19 developing Asian countries over the period 2000–2023 to examine the relationship between financial inclusion, agricultural productivity, and sustainable development using a Bayesian hierarchical model that accounts for cross\-country heterogeneity\. The results indicate that financial inclusion and agricultural productivity are positively associated with sustainable development, although the magnitude and stability of these effects vary across countries\. Agricultural productivity shows a more consistent effect, whereas the influence of financial inclusion differs significantly across the sample\. Trade openness and investment do not show clear evidence, while population growth is negatively associated with sustainable development\. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening the linkage between financial systems and productive sectors, particularly agriculture, to promote more balanced and sustainable development outcomes\.

## [Serum Galectin\-9 and TIM\-3 Expression in Relapse\-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: Assessment of Immune Checkpoint Biomarkers](../publications/cba903e26c1c0ec30aa8.md)

Zahra’a Abdul AL\-Aziz Yousif; Muhanad Ahmed Kadhim; Farah A\. AL\-waeely

Objective: An immune checkpoint molecule, T\-cell immunoglobulin and mucin\-domain containing\-3 \(TIM\-3\), is an important effector of T cell exhaustion and tolerance by interacting with its ligand, Galectin\-9 \(Gal\-9\)\. This study investigated whether serum TIM\-3/Gal\-9 levels could reflect immune regulatory dysfunction in relapsing\-remitting multiple sclerosis \(RRMS\)\.Material and Methods: Serum TIM\-3 and Gal\-9 were evaluated intwo main groups of the study \(RRMS patients and control groups\) with enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay \(ELISA\)\. For the evaluation of diagnostic utility, statistical studies were performed using the Mann\-Whitney U test, Spearman’s correlation, and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis\.Results: TIM\-3 levels were substantially higher in patients than in controls\. Gal\-9 levels revealed no significant difference, but were markedly heterogeneous in patients\. There was a significant positive correlation between study markers in both groups\. ROC analysis revealed that TIM\-3 had modest diagnostic efficacy, but Gal\-9 lacked discriminatory value\. A subgroup analysis revealed no significant difference in biomarker levels between individuals on disease\-modifying medications and those not on treatment\. Conclusion: This study represents the first evidence that serum TIM\-3 is considerably higher in RRMS, indicating immune checkpoint dysregulation, which is fundamental to MS pathogenesis\. Although Gal\-9 did not have direct diagnostic value, its strong, significant correlation with TIM\-3 suggests dysregulation of immune tolerance mechanisms\. These findings require validation in large cohorts with clinical correlation, but identify TIM\-3 as a candidate immunological exhaustion biomarker, and Gal\-9/TIM\-3 axis as a potential therapeutic target\.

## [Student\-Led Class Observation: A New Paradigm for EFL Teaching Evaluation at the Tertiary Level](../publications/cba9206fe0c86d312b5d.md)

M\. A\. Rahat Rahat

In Bangladesh, teaching English as a foreign language \(EFL\) is frequently still teacher\-centered and conventional\. Nonetheless, one important method for evaluating instructional strategies is classroom observation\. However, conventional approaches ignore the perspectives of students\. Because of this, learner perspectives are not fully incorporated\. An alternative to traditional teaching methods is student\-led observation\. Students are empowered to actively assess their classes\. This method encourages self\-reliance and introspection among Bangladeshi tertiary\-level in\-service and pre\-service educators\. However, there is very little and conservative research in this area in South Asian settings like Bangladesh\. Examining student\-led observation in tertiary EFL instruction is the goal of this study\. It first looks at how this approach affects students’ language learning strategies and metacognitive awareness\. Second, it looks into how teachers view its usefulness and validity\. The research utilizes qualitative techniques within an exploratory case study framework\. The study involves four EFL instructors chosen purposefully from a private university\. Data is collected through semi\-structured interviews and classroom observations utilizing a checklist\. Triangulation ensures the reliability of student\-teacher connections in the classroom, whereas thematic analysis supports the understanding of the findings\. Observation led by students enhances metacognition in language learners\. For example, learners reflect on lesson goals and evaluations, leading to enhanced methods such as self\-assessment and strategizing\. Educators find it valid for understanding, yet they also recognize prejudices\. Furthermore, it promotes joint assessment, student empowerment, and improvements in teaching\. Universities should train participants and integrate them into their programs\. Future studies can utilize the samples from this research to secure more in\-depth insights\. Also, it enhances EFL practices in Bangladesh\.

## [Biobanking across Africa: from participant\-level trust to institutional trustworthiness](../publications/cbb2987c0d4231d7bbfb.md)

Aisha Sallah; Salma Tarmoun; Krishna Gajjar; Patience Yeboah; Bernard Abakah; Everlyne Mutua; Dimitris Boufidis

Building trust and maintaining participant engagement are widely recognized as requirements for sustainable biobanking\. Yet efforts to achieve these goals must account for the historical, economic, geo\-political and socio\-cultural contexts that shape participant engagement\. In Africa, biobanking has shown immense scientific and global public health value, but persistent governance challenges continue to affect participation\. In this Perspective, we examine the factors that have constrained participant engagement in biobanking across Africa\. We argue that trust is not simply a participant\-level deficit to be corrected through increased outreach\. Instead, trust and mistrust are shaped by the broader biobanking ecosystem, and by whether its institutions have demonstrated that they are worthy of public trust\. Drawing on studies from across the continent, we propose strategies for how governance bodies, researchers and healthcare professionals can develop biobanking systems and frameworks that are sustainable and accountable to the public at both the national and international levels\. Importantly, we identify science diplomacy as a valuable mechanism for strengthening cross\-border coordination in support of more equitable, coherent and locally\-governed biobanking initiatives\.

## [DIGITAL STORYTELLING DALAM PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM: KAJIAN LITERATUR TERHADAP MOTIVASI BELAJAR GENERASI Z](../publications/cbb64e26a334261bdbd6.md)

Lutfiana Nazmaatun

The development of digital transformation in the world of education has also encouraged a shift in learning strategies towards a more interactive, contextual, and student\-oriented direction\. One of the approaches that has begun to be looked at in this shift is digital storytelling, a strategy that combines storytelling activities with multimedia elements to present a more meaningful learning experience\. Departing from this phenomenon, this study seeks to examine the role of digital storytelling in Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) learning and its relationship with the learning motivation of Generation Z, through a literature review approach with narrative synthesis techniques based on a number of previous studies\. In order to deepen the analysis, this study relies on Self\-Determination Theory \(SDT\) and Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning \(CTML\) to examine the motivational and cognitive dimensions in digital\-based learning\. The results of the study indicate that digital storytelling has the potential to support Generation Z&\#x27;s learning motivation, especially through strengthening active participation, creativity, and a deeper understanding of teaching materials\. Especially in PAI learning, this approach has been proven to be able to bridge religious materials with students&\#x27; personal experiences through the process of reflection and internalization of values\. However, the success of its implementation still depends on a number of factors, including the validity of religious sources, the readiness of educators, the level of digital literacy, and the accuracy of the learning design used\. Keywords: Digital storytelling; Learning motivation; Generation Z; Religious Education

## [Interfacially Regulated MXene‐Based Nanocomposite Membranes for Highly Selective Ion Transport and Salinity Gradient Energy Harvesting](../publications/cbc4b37385b639841692.md)

Randa I\. Gaber; Seung‐Hyun Hong; Daniel Bahamón; Mahmoud A\. Abdulhamid; Lourdes F\. Vega; Ekaterina A\. Pomerantseva; Emad Alhseinat

ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport\. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid \(HA\) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix\. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties\. The optimized membrane achieved near‐ideal monovalent cation selectivity \(∼99%\), a low area‐specific membrane resistance of 0\.06 Ω·m 2 , and an energy conversion efficiency of 45\.6%\. The same membrane was evaluated over multiple electrochemical testing cycles totaling approximately 300 h, including dedicated 48 h stability measurements under heavy‐metal‐ and organic‐foulant‐containing conditions\. A model‐based assessment of a conceptual reverse electrodialysis \(RED\) stack predicts a 37% increase in power generation, accompanied by an increase in energy conversion efficiency from 30\.0% to 41\.1%, relative to the commercial‐membrane scenario\. These findings demonstrate that regulating interfacial interactions provides an effective design strategy for developing MXene‐based ion‐selective membranes for salinity‐gradient energy harvesting and related electrochemical separation processes\.

## [Disagreement\-Guided Weak\-to\-Strong Routing](../publications/cbcba3df76794a7b455a.md)

Sima Noorani; Shayan Kiyani; George Pappas; Hamed Hassani

Small language models are increasingly deployed on edge devices and robotic systems to meet cost and latency constraints, yet their limited capabilities can make reliable deployment challenging\. Stronger models can provide assistance when needed, but deciding when to route a weak\-model response to a stronger model often relies on signals of response correctness\. In open\-ended and agentic tasks, however, obtaining such signals can require costly ground\-truth supervision that is difficult to obtain at scale\. We revisit the foundations of weak\-to\-strong routing and ask whether routing decisions can instead be guided by signals that do not require ground\-truth supervision\. We first characterize the optimal weak\-to\-strong routing policy, while allowing for multiple weak\-model responses generated through local inference\. Building on this characterization, we derive a principled approximation to the optimal routing based on model\-to\-model comparison\. In particular, we introduce a notion of model disagreement that can be measured directly from model\-generated responses, without ground\-truth supervision\. Importantly, the approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the strong model becomes a better proxy for the ground\-truth distribution\. Across agentic and single\-turn tasks, our approach effectively navigates the trade\-off between routing cost and response accuracy without ground\-truth supervision\. Moreover, even when ground\-truth correctness signals are available for training, disagreement\-based routing can outperform methods trained directly to predict correctness

## [Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery](../publications/cbd9fee9a6ce28d0af71.md)

Xudong Zhang; Jianzhe Li; Yitong Tang; Peijie Zhou

Genetic and drug perturbation screens are important tools for elucidating disease mechanisms and validating therapeutic targets, but experimental costs limit the number of candidates that can be tested\. Existing perturbation screening methods typically update the surrogate model with feedback while keeping the acquisition function fixed, limiting their ability to adapt selection to different response landscapes\. Experimental feedback reveals current hits and informs subsequent selection by updating candidate predictions, providing a training signal for learning how to select experiments\. We formulate budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and propose Temporal Difference Active Learning \(TDAL\), which learns an acquisition function online through temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory, accounting for current hits and future discoveries\. TDAL uses the Hellinger distance between hit probabilities for unmeasured candidates before and after an experiment to weight successor value, and reuses measured outcomes through leave\-batch\-out \(LBO\) to construct virtual transitions and alleviate training data scarcity\. Across eight public screens spanning single, double, and triple perturbations under varied experimental configurations, TDAL achieves an average rank of 1\.63 among eleven methods and ranks first on four tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across response landscapes\.

## [Biomechanical stabilization of the keratoconic cornea: a review of current therapeutic strategies](../publications/cbe775ac5d56c6e88ad4.md)

Graziana Maria Ragonese; Edoardo Grosso; Dario Carbonaro; Elena Torta; Emiliano Lepore; Gallo Diego

Keratoconus is a progressive corneal ectatic disorder characterized by stromal thinning and biomechanical weakening of the cornea, leading to progressive corneal protrusion and visual impairment\. Therapeutic strategies have evolved from visual correction toward approaches specifically targeting the biomechanical instability underlying disease progression\. This review provides a biomechanical perspective on current and emerging strategies for the biomechanical stabilization of the keratoconic cornea\. Conservative treatments based on contact lenses remain essential for visual rehabilitation but do not modify the underlying ectatic process\. Corneal collagen crosslinking represents the reference treatment for progressive keratoconus, as it increases stromal stiffness through the formation of additional covalent bonds\. However, its efficacy depends on treatment protocol, epithelial status, corneal thickness, and disease stage\. Corneal implants, i\.e\., synthetic intracorneal ring segments and corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments, provide stretch\-induced geometric improvement of the corneal shape and, consequently, of visual acuity, although predictability remains limited\. Combined approaches, such as ring implantation followed by cross\-linking, aim to integrate corneal reshaping with intrinsic stromal reinforcement\. Emerging approaches, including cell\-based therapies, and implantation of stromal lenticule or tissue\-engineered scaffolds, suggest a future shift toward a multimodal therapeutic strategy integrating biomechanical stabilization, restoration of stromal structure, and biological regeneration\. Advancing keratoconus management will require objective biomechanical assessment and predictive modeling tools to guide individualized treatment planning and improve outcome predictability\. Ultimately, future management should increasingly incorporate a biomechanical perspective, with interventions designed to modify the mechanical behavior of the ectatic cornea, arrest progression, and restore functional corneal integrity\.

## [Encoding identity values in digital heritage workflows: lessons from Saxon rural architecture in Transylvania](../publications/cbe7f06efafabc9f8c9e.md)

Alina Elena Voinea

Digital heritage workflows increasingly document buildings through surveys, models, and visualizations, but often remain weak in representing the identity values embedded in vernacular architecture\. This Perspective argues for a value\-based framework that links documentation, interpretation, and design through the concept of transmissible identity values\. Using Saxon rural architecture in Transylvania as an illustrative case, it proposes transferable categories for internationally comparable heritage\-building workflows\.
