## [TechDiscovery Inquiry Cycle Enhances Hydraulics Achievement and Narrows Score Dispersion in Vocational Education](../publications/cbe7fb76320719688f41.md)

Erwin Komara Mindarta; Dani Irawan; Syarif Suhartadi; Adi Aziz Wibowo; Ahmad Ridho; Ilham Amanulloh; Geraldo Vigor Putra Deca

Heavy\-equipment hydraulics requires vocational students to connect pressure\-flow relationships, component functions, circuit behavior, and technical reasoning\. This study examined the integration of the TechDiscovery Inquiry Cycle, hereafter TDIC, which links technology discovery, inquiry formulation, experimentation, evidence interpretation, reflection, and application\. A quasi\-experimental pretest\-posttest comparison\-group design involved 70 Grade XI students at SMKN 1 Singosari, Indonesia\. One intact class received TDIC and one received the school’s comparison instruction, with 35 students in each class\. Cognitive achievement was measured before and after instruction\. Because most score distributions departed from normality, the primary analyses used Wilcoxon signed\-rank and Mann\-Whitney U tests\. The TDIC mean increased from 55\.00 to 91\.29; 34 of 35 students improved and none declined\. Posttest ranks were also significantly higher for TDIC than for comparison instruction, with both inferential tests yielding p values below \.001\. Score dispersion decreased by 64\.5 percent under TDIC compared with 31\.7 percent in the comparison group, while the TDIC posttest minimum rose to 85\. These findings indicate that TDIC was associated with higher cognitive attainment and a narrower distribution of achievement, a pattern described here as achievement convergence\. Intact\-class allocation, the single\-school setting, and possible ceiling effects limit causal and generalizable conclusions\.

## [McDuie\-Ra, Duncan ; Gulson, Kalervo N\. &amp; Taylor, Simon Michael: Artificial Intelligence from Colonial India: Race, Statistics, and Facial Recognition in the Global South](../publications/cbe997c0c733387697dd.md)



\_Science, Technology, and Human Values\_ 48 \(3\):663\-689\. 2023This article examines the history of a similarity measure—the Mahalanobis Distance Function—and its movement from colonial India into contemporary artificial intelligence technologies, including facial recognition, and its reapplication into postcolonial India\. The article identifies how the creation of the Distance Function was connected to the colonial “problem” of caste and ethnic classification for British bureaucracy in 1920\-1930s India\. This article demonstrates that the Distance Function is a statistical method, originating to make anthropometric caste distinctions in India, that became both a technical standard and a mobile racialized technique, utilized in machine learning applications\. The creation of the Distance Function as a measure of “similitude” at a particular period of colonial state\-making helped to model wider categories of classification which have proliferated in facial recognition technology\. Overall, we highlight how a measurement function that operates in recognition technologies today can be traced across time and space to other racialized contexts\.

## [Global Research Trends in Music and Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scopus Publications \(1912\-2025\)](../publications/cbf251d2767b2eca61c9.md)

Zet Latuminase; Juntika Nurihsan; Idat Muqodas

Music education has gained growing attention in the global educational landscape of the digital era and is known to strengthen students&\#x27; cognitive, social, and emotional skills, yet it is often treated as a supplementary subject with limited policy priority\. This study aims to map the annual distribution of publications on music and learning and to identify the most productive authors and the most\-cited works\. Data were retrieved from Scopus on July 15, 2025, using the search string TITLE\-ABS\-KEY \(&quot;music&quot; AND &quot;learning&quot;\); of 16,327 records, 15,015 documents published between 1912 and 2025 were analyzed descriptively with Bibliometrix, and keyword co\-occurrence was visualized with VOSviewer\. Publications rose sharply after 2000, peaking at approximately 2,700 documents in 2022; the 2025 count is partial\. Nine authors \(Widmer, Yang, Serra, Calvo\-Zaragoza, Ludovico, McPherson, Su, Altenmüller, and Fujinaga\) each produced 10\-25 documents across music psychology, music computation, and music learning technology, while the most\-cited works are by Campbell and Hallam\. Keyword analysis revealed four clusters: music education, digital learning, cognition, and computational music\. The field is becoming more interdisciplinary and digitally oriented, although the broad search string means the findings cover music and learning rather than music education alone\.

## [Análisis cromático para caracterización de dipterofauna de la familia Piophilidae con fines forenses](../publications/cbf4a3a8fa88a1909d09.md)

Emanuel Emilio Valera\-Hurtado; Andrea Alicia Yépez\-Peñaherrera; Rosa Doménica Peñafiel\-Guatán; Denisse Alexandra Guartambel\-Cruz

Forensic entomology is an essential discipline for determining the Postmortem Interval; however, the description of color in species of the Piophilidae family remains a subjective process that depends on the expert&\#x27;s perception and lighting conditions\. This study addresses this issue throught chromatic analysis to standardize the characterizing of forensic\-interest Piophilidae entomological samples in Ecuador\. To this end, an exploratory documentary approach and a systematic review were employed, integrating objective colorimetric methodologies such as the Munsell and CIELAB systems\. Various anatomical structures and appendages of the Neottiophilinae and Piophilinae subfamilies were analyzed in detail, translating visual features into specific digital codes such as HEX and RGB\. The results establish a precise color classification by tagmata, providing a comprehensive reference tool that minimizes inconsistencies in taxonomic identification\. It concludes that creating a color scale based on color analysis turns coloration into an objective and verificable forensic data point for this family, strengthening the scientific validity of technical reports\. This standardization not only optimizes the reliability of entomological analyses, but also provides a methodological rigor necessary for the administration of justice in the national context

## [Unlocking Quantitative Skills: A Serious Game for University\-Level Social Science](../publications/cbf53b2090ba775b94de.md)

María M\. Serrano\-Baena; Sonia Navajas\-Torrente; Rosa María Muñoz\-Millán; José Ríos‐Madrid; José Ángel Roldán Casas

The deficiencies in basic mathematical skills and emotional factors such as maths anxiety hinder learning in quantitative subjects in non\-STEM university degrees, so it becomes essential to reconsider the teaching methodologies being used\. In this context, both serious games and gamification are considered as innovative pedagogical tools that strengthen student commitment, autonomy, and collaboration\. Thus, this study presents the design and implementation of a serious game developed for undergraduate students enrolled in Business Administration and Management degree programs, aimed at fostering deeper engagement and understanding in quantitative subjects\. It takes shape in an educational breakout, based on a business narrative and focused on the collaborative resolution of quantitative challenges related to mathematics, statistics and accounting\. The pilot project implemented in October 2024 with second\-year undergraduate students, not only validates their effectiveness but also offers a replicable and scalable model adaptable to different disciplines and educational contexts\. In conclusion, the presented project demonstrates that serious games, and particularly educational breakouts, can be powerful tools for transforming the teaching of quantitative content in non\-STEM university degrees\.

## [Innovative Financing in Tertiary Institutions in Nigeria: A Review of Seven Strategies for Sustainable Development](../publications/cc0952eadb6f00ddef07.md)

Mark Patience Ukwuori

Financing tertiary education remains a major challenge in Nigeria due to increasing student enrolment, rising operational costs, inadequate infrastructure, and competing demands on government revenue\. Universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education require adequate financial resources to provide quality teaching, support research, maintain infrastructure, and promote innovation\. However, excessive dependence on government allocations has made it difficult for many institutions to meet their growing financial needs\. This paper examines innovative financing as an approach to improving the financial sustainability of tertiary institutions in Nigeria\. It discusses alternative financing strategies, including internally generated revenue, public–private partnerships, alumni contributions and endowment funds, consultancy services, commercialisation of research outputs, competitive research grants, and digital education programmes\. The paper highlights the importance of effective financial management, institutional accountability, and strategic planning in implementing these strategies\. It argues that innovative financing should complement government funding rather than replace the government&\#x27;s responsibility for public tertiary education\. The paper concludes that diversifying funding sources can strengthen institutional capacity, improve educational quality, and support sustainable development when appropriate management structures and accountability mechanisms are established\.

## [Strategic analysis of online pharmacy implementation: a scoping review and SWOT\-based framework](../publications/cc0e0923bb0ddc713d94.md)

Rouhollah Zaboli; Ali Jajarmizadeh; Mahdi Mashhadi Akbar Boojar

The expansion of online pharmacies, a key development in digital health, has influenced both patient care and health system operations\. Despite their benefits, these platforms face regulatory, infrastructural, and safety challenges\. This study aimed to provide a strategic overview of online pharmacy implementation and propose operational strategies\. A scoping review was conducted following the six\-stage framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley\. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and June 2026\. After screening 496 records, 37 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis\. Data were analyzed using the framework analysis approach developed by Ritchie and Spencer and were subsequently categorized according to a SWOT framework and associated implementation strategies\. Online pharmacies offer several potential advantages, including lower indirect costs, improved access to pharmaceutical services, and enhanced medication management\. However, challenges such as digital inequalities, logistical constraints, and cybersecurity concerns remain significant\. Key opportunities include integration with telemedicine, emerging regulatory frameworks, and the adoption of innovative technologies\. Major threats involve regulatory gaps, counterfeit medicines, self\-medication, and financial sustainability challenges\. Eleven implementation strategies were identified to support the safe and sustainable development of online pharmacy services\. Online pharmacies have the potential to serve as an important complement to health systems by reducing indirect patient costs, may contribute to improving equity in access, and enhancing the quality of services\. Realizing this potential requires coherent policymaking, investment in infrastructure, and the use of novel technologies such as artificial intelligence\.

## [Toward integrated multimodal artificial intelligence in bone marrow examination: current state and open challenges](../publications/cc16134890b04aaf891a.md)

Seung Yeob Lee

Bone marrow \(BM\) examinations are intrinsically multimodal: hematopathologists integrate peripheral blood, aspirate cytomorphology, trephine histology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, and molecular genetics data into a single interpretation\. Because WHO\-HAEM5 and ICC 2022 define entities through integrated morphological, immunophenotypic, cytogenetic, and molecular criteria, multimodal diagnostic reasoning embedded in a procedural workflow, not isolated image classification, represents the appropriate target for the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. We review the existing research on integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examination by classifying these systems into three categories: mature single\-modality tools; systems that perform cross\-modal prediction, in which one modality is estimated from another; and genuine multimodal fusion systems, in which several modalities are jointly ingested by a single model\. Evidence is stronger at the single\-modality level, where deep learning approaches expert performance in aspirate cytology, trephine histology, and flow cytometry assessments, and the first Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\) De Novo\-authorized all\-digital bone marrow aspirate \(BMA\) application has defined a new device category\. On the other hand, while cross\-modal prediction is rapidly expanding, genuine multimodal fused systems that jointly ingest matched morphology, flow, molecular, and clinical data to yield unified guideline\-aligned recommendations remain unrealized\. Direct head\-to\-head evidence is sparse and endpoint\-dependent; nevertheless, the lack of demonstrated superiority over the strongest single\-modality comparator does not automatically imply the absence of benefits\. The dominant obstacles are fusion of heterogeneous modalities with missing data, absence of large paired multi\-institutional datasets and harmonized nomenclature, class imbalances, batch\-effect\-driven generalization failures, immature explainability, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory pathways\. Nevertheless, integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examinations have entered a promising early translational phase, and the field should aim to pursue integration using paired datasets, explicit fusion architectures, calibrated abstention\-aware models, and staged prospective validation\.

## [Dynamic trajectories of sepsis\-induced immunoparalysis: from biological mechanisms to precision monitoring and targeted intervention](../publications/cc1a96111010e86f67cf.md)

Chengxin Xue; Yiheng Hu; Xinyun Wu; Yudan Chen; Zihao Zhou; Qidong Jiang; Bo Yang; Chengli Wen

Sepsis is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous syndrome in which profound immunosuppression, or immunoparalysis, may coexist with or follow the initial hyperinflammatory response\. This state is characterized by impaired host responsiveness to pathogens and secondary immune stimuli and is associated with secondary infections, persistent organ dysfunction, and increased mortality\. This narrative review summarizes the conceptual evolution and biological basis of sepsis\-induced immunoparalysis, with particular emphasis on innate immune deactivation, adaptive immune dysfunction, immune\-checkpoint upregulation, and metabolic\-epigenetic reprogramming\. A central focus is the transition from static, single\-time\-point assessment toward longitudinal characterization of immune trajectories\. Current evidence suggests that the first 1–2 weeks after sepsis onset represent a critical period during which heterogeneous recovery patterns become apparent\. Empirically supported patterns include improving or recovering immune states and persistent hyporesponsiveness, whereas fluctuating transitions remain a proposed, hypothesis\-generating trajectory requiring further longitudinal validation\. We review major monitoring indicators, including monocyte human leukocyte antigen\-DR \(mHLA\-DR\), absolute lymphocyte count \(ALC\), ex vivo cytokine production capacity, and immune checkpoints such as programmed death\-1 \(PD\-1\) and programmed death\-ligand 1 \(PD\-L1\)\. Importantly, most currently available biomarkers have stronger evidence for immune phenotyping and prognostic assessment than for predicting treatment response, and reported thresholds remain dependent on assay methodology, patient population, and measurement timing\. We further discuss emerging biomarker\-guided approaches, including the ImmunoSep trial, as early proof\-of\-concept for phenotype\-enriched immunotherapy rather than definitive evidence for routine clinical implementation\. Overall, repeated multi\-marker assessment may improve characterization of immune trajectories and help identify candidate treatment\-eligible windows; however, biomarker\-based treatment thresholds, composite immune\-clinical frameworks, and phenotype\-matched immunotherapies require further prospective validation, particularly with respect to mortality, safety, and other patient\-important outcomes\.

## [University faculty competence deficits in the safe application of artificial intelligence](../publications/cc1c4d9c776733f67555.md)

Mikhail Zamyslov; M\. D\. Kitaygorodskiy

The purpose of the study is to identify the state of university faculty competence in the field of safe application of artificial intelligence technologies \(AI competence\) across its various components and, on this basis, to substantiate the content of a professional development program\. The article clarifies the concept of a teacher’s AI competence as a constituent part of their digital competence, identifies its general user, general pedagogical, and subject\-pedagogical components, and differentiates between the technological limitations of AI systems and the ethical and legal norms governing their use\. The results of a survey involving 44 university teachers are presented\. The scientific novelty of the study lies in clarifying the concept and component structure of university teachers’ AI competence and in obtaining empirical data on its state, including the nature of teachers’ understanding of the ethical risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence\. As a result, it was established that approximately half of the teachers have practical experience in applying AI, while their understanding of AI technologies is limited to the interface level\. Ethical risks are not differentiated by almost half of the respondents; the remainder conceptualize them primarily as data transfer risks, whereas the risks of unreliability and opacity of generated results are underestimated – notably, active users rate the risk of unreliability lower than others\. Based on the identified deficits and a content analysis of existing courses, a modular structure for a professional development program with a risk\-oriented approach to content design is substantiated\.

Rikiya Okuyama; Hajime Horiuchi; Masaki Nakamura; Mitsuaki Muroya; Teppei Morikawa

OBJECTIVES: hybridization \(FISH\), and tumor markers like nuclear matrix protein 22 \(NMP22\), have limited sensitivity and specificity\. This study assessed the potential of low\-cost, non\-invasive urine sediment data for BC detection using a machine learning model\. METHODS: Urine sediment data from 1,341 patients \(577 with BC and 764 with benign conditions\) were obtained using a fully automated urinary particle analyzer \(UF\-5000\)\. One preoperative sample per patient was included\. A soft\-voting ensemble model combining random forest and logistic regression was developed\. Class imbalance was addressed using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique, and feature selection was guided by the variance inflation factor\. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), balanced accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, with 95 % confidence intervals estimated via bootstrapping\. Model stability was evaluated using fivefold cross\-validation\. RESULTS: The ensemble model achieved an AUC of 0\.89, with a sensitivity of 0\.80 and specificity of 0\.88\. Balanced accuracy was 0\.84, and cross\-validation demonstrated stable performance \(accuracy 0\.80\)\. Feature importance analysis identified atypical cells and red blood cells as the most influential predictors, particularly of non\-muscle\-invasive BC\. CONCLUSIONS: This urine sediment\-based, non\-invasive approach shows promise for the early detection and monitoring of BC\. ## [Comparing the efficacy of virtual reality and conventional therapy on balance and anxiety reduction in adult stroke patients – A pilot study](../publications/cc2dc4bba30d57fb6d46.md)



BackgroundStroke is a critical medical condition characterized by the sudden interruption of blood supply to the brain, resulting in neuronal damage due to oxygen deprivation\.This disruption can stem from either a vascular blockage \(ischemic stroke\) or rupture \(hemorrhagic stroke\), often leading to significant neurological impairments such as motor dysfunction, speech difficulties, and cognitive decline\.Beyond physical deficits, stroke survivors frequently face psychological challenges, with anxiety affecting up to 40% of patients\.Addressing both motor and emotional outcomes is essential for comprehensive rehabilitation\. MethodologyThis study aimed to compare the effects of Virtual Reality \(VR\)\-assisted balance therapy with conventional balance training in post\-stroke individuals\.Twenty participants aged 18 to 80 years, all diagnosed with stroke and ambulatory, were randomly assigned to two groups\.Group A received VR\-based interactive balance exercises alongside routine physiotherapy, while Group B underwent traditional balance training alone\.Both groups participated in a structured intervention program for four weeks, comprising 30\-60 minute sessions held 3\-5 times per week\. ResultOutcome measures included the Berg Balance Scale \(BBS\) for evaluating balance and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale \(GAD\-7\) for assessing psychological well\-being\.Results revealed significantly greater improvements in the VR group in both balance and anxiety scores over time\.On day 30, Group A showed higher BBS scores \(50\.4 ± 1\.07\) and lower GAD\-7 scores \(5\.2 ± 0\.42\) compared to Group B \(BBS: 47\.2 ± 1\.47; GAD\-7: 9\.4 ± 1\.17\)\.Multivariate analysis confirmed significant effects of time and group\-time interaction \(p &lt; \.001\),with large effect sizes\. ConclusionThe findings support that VR\-assisted therapy is more effective than conventional methods in improving post\-stroke balance and reducing anxiety\.This suggests that incorporating immersive technologies into rehabilitation may enhance functional and psychological outcomes in stroke recovery\.

## [Selection Is Not Learning: Choosing Model Futures](../publications/cc2f03effe0324ffc51d.md)

Haoyi Yang; Kshitij Mishra; Nils Lukas; Salem Lahlou

Self\-evolving language models train on tasks they generate, so every round must decide which updated model the next round inherits\. Current loops such as R\-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self\-Play make this decision through the task, admitting tasks that look learnable and inheriting every resulting update\. We identify a selection\-to\-update gap in these loops, where a task that looks learnable need not produce a useful update\. Most updates on verified tasks fail to make correct answers more likely, yet these loops inherit them all\. HeirCommit freezes the updated model and uses fresh evaluation questions to decide whether to inherit it or retain the current model\. EvoHeir separates parameter inheritance from experience inheritance, using current and archived experience to repair failures and preserve successes before final confirmation\. Our analysis characterizes selection\-induced optimism and decomposes regret into selection, absorption, and confirmation errors\. HeirCommit cuts the harmful share of accepted updates by 68\-83% relative to random inheritance at the same acceptance rate\. Across four backbones, EvoHeir achieves the best mathematics and general\-reasoning averages, raising the math average by 5\.3% relative to the strongest baseline, Agent0\. The framework lets useful experience persist even when the model that produced it is not inherited\.

## [The international consensus protocol for the management of severe traumatic brain injury in the absence of intracranial pressure monitoring](../publications/cc2f6697191021e99eed.md)

Oshorov Av

Background\. Severe traumatic brain injury \(TBI\) remains one of the leading causes of mortality and disability, particularly in resource\-limited settings where invasive intracranial pressure \(ICP\) monitoring is unavailable\. The international Brain Trauma Foundation guidelines require specialized equipment, creating a substantial gap between evidence\-based medicine and actual clinical practice in low\-resource institutions\. The aim\. To present and analyze the international consensus protocol CREVICE \(Consensus REVised ICE \(Imaging and Clinical Examination\)\) – a modified management system for patients with severe TBI designed for use in the absence of ICP monitoring – and to evaluate its potential applicability in Russian healthcare facilities\. Main provisions\. The CREVICE protocol is a logical development of the ICE protocol, which was validated in the randomized BEST:TRIP trial\. The protocol is based on the use of computed tomography \(modified Marshall classification\) and clinical\-neurological criteria \(motor response on the Glasgow Coma Scale, pupillary response\) as surrogate markers of intracranial hypertension\. The protocol includes clear criteria for initiating treatment of suspected intracranial hypertension, a hierarchical escalation therapy with dosing of hyperosmolar agents, an algorithm for managing neurological deterioration, and a detailed de\-escalation system using visual decision\-making matrices\. Contraindicated therapeutic modalities \(corticosteroids, prolonged hyperventilation, continuous mannitol infusion\) are specifically addressed\. Conclusion\. The CREVICE protocol is a practical tool that enables the application of modern neurocritical care principles in the absence of invasive neuromonitoring\. Its implementation into clinical practice may contribute to treatment standardization, reduced mortality, and improved functional outcomes in patients with severe TBI\. For Russian healthcare facilities, the CREVICE framework can serve as a reference for the development and modernization of local clinical protocols\.

## [Matrix bound nanovesicles from decellularized pericardium facilitate angiogenesis](../publications/cc3ed101ad9ce7d2d74f.md)

Dalila Di Francesco; Carolina Di Varsavia; Irene Regano; Luca Di Nunno; Simona Casarella; Nausicaa Clemente; Mantovani Diego; Francesca Boccafoschi

Therapeutic angiogenesis is a regenerative medicine approach which aims to induce revascularization for tissue repair\. Among the existing strategies used to promote angiogenesis, biomaterials derived from decellularized tissues and composed of extracellular matrix \(dECM\) possess intrinsic angiogenic and regenerative potential\. Recently, a bioactive component of such ECM materials has been identified; specifically, matrix bound nanovesicles \(MBV\)\. MBV have been shown to possess highly bioactive and tissue\-specific cargo, and the ability to induce a potent immunomodulatory and regenerative response\. However, their angiogenic potential has not been studied yet\. Herein, the angiogenic properties of MBV derived from bovine pericardia dECM is evaluated\. MBV show cytocompatibility toward endothelial cells, enhancing their functional phenotype and inducing the expression of angiogenic markers\. In the presence of MBV, endothelial cells form three\-dimensional monolayered endothelial vessel\-like structures in tube formation assay\. MBV also enhance endothelial sprouting in aortic ring assay\. Finally, in hind limb ischemia in vivo model, MBV prevent tissue necrosis and restore vascularization and tissue function\. These results demonstrate the angiogenic potential of MBV from pericardia ECM and represent a promising approach for therapeutic angiogenesis in regenerative medicine applications\.

## [RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM PENGAMBILAN KEPUTUSAN PENDETEKSI KANTUK PENGEMUDI BERBASIS INTERNET OF THINGS DENGAN OUTPUT PERINGATAN MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA NAIVE BAYES](../publications/cc696f25e469d405b0f5.md)

M\. Gading Dimas Nugraha; Mhd\. Basri

Kantuk saat mengemudi merupakan salah satu faktor yang dapat menurunkan konsentrasi dan kewaspadaan pengemudi sehingga meningkatkan risiko kecelakaan, khususnya pada operasional kendaraan berat di lingkungan proyek konstruksi\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sistem pendeteksi kantuk pengemudi berbasis Internet of Things \(IoT\) dengan menerapkan algoritma Naive Bayes sebagai metode klasifikasi serta buzzer sebagai perangkat peringatan\. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development \(R&amp;D\) dengan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif\. Sistem yang dikembangkan menggunakan mikrokontroler ESP32, sensor inframerah FC\-51 untuk mendeteksi kondisi mata, serta sensor MPU6050 untuk memperoleh nilai kemiringan kepala berdasarkan parameter pitch dan roll\. Data sensor dikirimkan melalui jaringan Wi\-Fi ke server berbasis Python dan Flask untuk diproses menggunakan algoritma Naive Bayes\. Hasil klasifikasi dibagi menjadi tiga kategori, yaitu normal, mengantuk, dan sangat mengantuk\. Hasil prediksi dikirimkan kembali ke ESP32 untuk mengendalikan buzzer sebagai peringatan kepada pengemudi\. Selain itu, data sensor dan hasil klasifikasi disimpan melalui Firebase Realtime Database dan ditampilkan pada website monitoring sehingga kondisi pengemudi dapat dipantau secara jarak jauh\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem berhasil diimplementasikan dan mampu mengintegrasikan pembacaan sensor, pengiriman data, proses klasifikasi, pemberian peringatan suara, penyimpanan data, serta pemantauan melalui website\. Sistem ini diharapkan dapat mendukung upaya peningkatan keselamatan pengemudi dan membantu proses pemantauan kondisi pengemudi oleh pengawas proyek\.

## [Medication Adherence and Associated Factors Among Geriatric Population with Chronic Diseases in Rural Northern Kerala: A Cross\-sectional Study](../publications/cc6b8522eb9f7518caef.md)

Narayanan Namboothiri G; Arya Ravindran; Rinsha Rasheed V P; Rinshiya Fathima C; Rushdha Thanikatt; Safa K; Sahana Benzey; Saina N; Salma A N; Sameeha

Introduction: Medication adherence among elderly patients with chronic diseases is crucial for effective disease control but often remains inadequate\. Limited Indian data and under\-assessment justified studying its determinants and impact\. Objectives: This study aimed to assess medication adherence and associated factors among the geriatric population using the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale \(MMAS\-8\)\. Methodology: A community\-based cross\-sectional study was conducted among 292 individuals aged ≥60 years with chronic diseases in a rural field practice area of a tertiary care centre in Northern Kerala, in 2025\. Participants were selected using simple random sampling\. Data were collected through face\-to\-face interviews using a structured questionnaire, and adherence was assessed using the MMAS\-8 scale\. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, and chi\-square test was applied to identify associated factors\. Results: Medication adherence among geriatrics showed that 62\.3% had low adherence and 37\.7% had high adherence\. Higher adherence was significantly associated with younger elderly age, female gender, higher education, higher socio\-economic status, and living with family, as well as shorter duration of illness and having a single chronic condition\. Additionally, factors such as motivation to take medications, regular follow\-up, absence of cost\-related barriers, shorter waiting times, receipt of counseling, medication availability, and satisfaction with healthcare services were significantly associated with better adherence \(p&lt;0\.05\)\. Conclusion: Medication adherence among the geriatric population with chronic diseases was suboptimal and influenced by multiple socio\-demographic, clinical, behavioral, and healthcare system factors\. Improving adherence requires comprehensive, patient\-centered strategies focusing on education, accessibility, and strengthening healthcare support systems\.

## [Evaluation of segmental skin temperature cooling responses in a summer electric vehicle cabin using a thermophysiological model](../publications/cc851451619748ce0b0f.md)

Muhammad Iqbal M\. Ruhyanto; Mohammad F\.B\. Suhaimi; Woo Geun Kim; Chung\-Won Cho; Dongchan Lee; Hyunjin Lee

Electric vehicle \(EV\) cabins create transient and uneven cooling conditions, but cabin average and whole\-body indicators cannot show how cooling is distributed across body regions\. This study evaluated segmental skin temperature cooling responses in a summer EV cabin by combining human skin temperature measurements from ten participants, thermal manikin based local boundary conditions, and a thermophysiological model\. The model reproduced segmental skin temperatures with root\-mean\-square error values of 0\.12–0\.69 °C\. A trend\-based no\-cooling reference was then constructed to estimate the cooling effect of active HVAC operation for each body segment\. The analysis distinguished sustained low intensity cooling from stronger accumulated cooling, showing that cooling duration alone can misrepresent segmental cooling performance\. The left arm showed the strongest accumulated cooling, with a cumulative cooling effect of 168\.34 °C·min and an effective period equivalent cooling intensity of 3\.77 °C, whereas the back showed the weakest response \(44\.69 °C·min; 0\.82 °C\)\. The right foot remained above the 0\.5 °C threshold throughout the exposure, but its effective period equivalent cooling intensity was only 1\.17 °C\. These findings provide a compact framework for evaluating non\-uniform cabin cooling and identifying body regions where conventional airflow may require complementary localized cooling strategies\.

## [A Cognitive, Quantum\-Inspired Learning Framework for Energy\-Efficient and Reliable Routing in Wireless Body Area Networks](../publications/cc942cfc254718846a0a.md)

Soufiane Ben Othman; Naima Saeed

Wireless Body Area Networks \(WBANs\) are critical enablers of real\-time, non\-invasive healthcare monitoring, enabling continuous acquisition and wireless transmission of vital physiological signals such as electrocardiogram \(ECG\), heart rate, and motion data\. However, their practical deployment faces significant challenges due to stringent energy constraints, dynamic on\-body channel variations induced by mobility, and multi\-class Quality\-of\-Service \(QoS\) requirements, particularly ultra\-low latency \( $$\\le 18\\,\\text \{ms\}$$ \) for emergency alerts and high reliability \( $$\\ge 99\.5\\%$$ PDR\) for diagnostic data\. Conventional routing protocols often rely on static topologies or reactive mechanisms that fail under the coupled spatio\-temporal variability of physiological dynamics and wireless channels\. To address these limitations, we propose QuantumEERP\-Net, a novel, intelligent, and self\-optimizing routing framework that synergistically integrates Multi\-Agent Dueling Double Deep Q\-Networks \(D3QN\), a Quantum\-Inspired Dual Prediction Model \(Q\-DPM\), and Context\-Aware Adaptive Routing into a fully decentralized architecture\. Each sensor node operates as an autonomous agent, learning optimal forwarding policies through continuous interaction with a dynamic environment modeled using log\-normal shadowing \( $$\\sigma = 6\.500\\,\\text \{dB\}$$ \) and Markovian mobility states\. The Q\-DPM, implemented via a variational quantum circuit with parameter\-shift gradient estimation, jointly predicts future sensor values \(e\.g\., ECG at $$125\~\\textrm\{Hz\}$$ \) and residual energy levels with mean error $$&lt; 0\.008\\,\\text \{J\}$$ , enabling proactive suppression of redundant transmissions and substantial energy savings\. A real\-time context\-aware engine fuses IMU and ECG inputs to detect mobility patterns \(static/walking/running\) and critical events \(HR $$&gt; 180\~\\textrm\{bpm\}$$ , falls\) with accuracy $$\\ge 0\.991$$ , triggering low\-latency routing overrides for emergency traffic\. Extensive simulations over 20 000 cycles using a comprehensive hybrid dataset of 450,000 labeled samples \(150,000 per class\), with a held\-out test set of 150,000 samples \(50,000 per class\), demonstrate that QuantumEERP\-Net achieves a First Node Dead \(FND\) of 10,250 rounds \(an 83\.0% improvement\) and extends Last Node Dead \(LND\) by 84\.3% compared to EAFST\. The framework attains a Packet Delivery Ratio \(PDR\) of 1\.000 for Emergency data, reduces emergency end\-to\-end delay to 13\.800 ms \(with an average delay of 2\.000 ms\), and maintains a security compliance of 0\.995\. Furthermore, hardware benchmarking on an nRF52832 SoC validates that the D3QN and Q\-DPM inference consumes only $$\\approx 3\.600\\,\\upmu \\text \{J\}$$ per cycle, ensuring minimal computational overhead\. These gains result from the tight integration of link\-quality\-aware forwarding, NSGA\-II\-based multi\-objective optimization, and predictive intelligence\. By unifying quantum\-inspired computation, deep reinforcement learning, and physiological context awareness, QuantumEERP\-Net establishes a new paradigm for secure, energy\-efficient, and adaptive communication in next\-generation WBANs, offering a scalable solution for mission\-critical telemedicine and remote patient monitoring systems\.

## [Protocol: From Pilots to Practice: A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in the Healthcare Sector of the GCC Countries and Egypt](../publications/cc9da671ab18634be519.md)

Protocol \(version 0\.6, 17 October 2026\) for a scoping review mapping the adoption of artificial intelligence across five healthcare sectors in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Egypt \(2015–2026\): hospitals and providers; pharmaceutical companies and manufacturers; pharmacies and distribution; government and regulators; and research and universities\. ## [Neural Expansion: A Unified Mechanism for How Deep Neural Networks Generalize](../publications/cca5f8313910be505894.md)

Chashi Mahiul Islam; Samuel Jacob Chacko; Mao Nishino; Canlin Zhang; Xiuwen Liu

Deep neural networks demonstrate remarkable generalization despite being highly over\-parameterized, challenging traditional statistical learning theories\. While several theoretical paradigms such as margin\-based bounds, PAC\-Bayesian analyses, and neural tangent kernels provide global explanations, they often lack mechanistic insight into how generalization emerges from training dynamics\. We introduce Neural Expansion, a unified geometric framework that characterizes generalization through the expansion of directionally\-selective ray coverage in the input space\. Using Generalization Intervals \(GIs\), we quantify direction\-specific regions around training samples where the model&\#x27;s predictions remain stable\. Our extensive empirical studies across diverse architectures and datasets reveal that training leads to progressive expansion of ray coverage, particularly along directions with low Jacobian singular values\. This mechanism helps explain a large fraction of correctly classified test inputs, adversarial examples, and even mislabeled or out\-of\-distribution samples through the geometry of ray coverage rather than instance\-level memorization\. By connecting input\-space curvature to predictive behavior, our framework provides a mechanistic foundation that complements existing global theories of deep learning\.

## [A Physics\-Hybrid Alpha Network \(PHAN\) approach for soil moisture retrieval using time series optical and SAR imagery](../publications/ccaca6c18de484a89199.md)

Zhuqiang Li; Xiao Chen; Lisai Cao; Zhijun Zhen; Shengbo Chen; Liqiang Zhang

The coarse spatial resolution hinders the application of soil moisture \(SM\) in elucidating the interactions among water, energy and carbon cycles at regional and global scales\. We propose a physics\-hybrid differentiable network, termed the Physics\-Hybrid Alpha\-Net \(PHAN\), that integrates time\-series C\-band dual\-polarization SAR and optical observations to retrieve 10\-metre high\-resolution SM maps\. PHAN extends the Alpha approximation by enforcing a physics\-based regularization on retrieved soil moisture \(SM\) and adding a cross\-attention module that implicitly reduces vegetation\-canopy scattering\. By using optical and SAR imagery from 2019 to 2020 of Shandian River Basin, Naqu and Twente, PHAN outperformed machine learning \(ML\), deep learning \(DL\) and physics\-guided baselines, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients \(R\) = 0\.821, 0\.861, 0\.856 and unbiased root mean square error \(ubRMSE\) = 4\.62, 5\.54, 8\.38 vol%\. ## [Barriers to and Needs for the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence in Radiation Therapy Planning in Saudi Arabia\. A Cross\-Sectional Survey](../publications/ccb7149be549d0e90d92.md)

Abdulaziz M\. Alshaikh; Ghadah AlQarni; Abdulaziz AlGhamdi; Khalid Alrabiah; Nasser Al\-Rajhi; Mohammed Aldehaim

Objectives: To assess radiation oncology physicians&\#x27; perceptions of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in radiation therapy planning in Saudi Arabia and identify barriers to and support needs for its implementation\.Methods: A cross\-sectional online survey was distributed through the Saudi Association of Radiation Oncology email list to 142 physicians from April to May 2026\. We analyzed responses using descriptive statistics and exploratory 2\-sided Fisher exact tests comparing residents with nonresidents\.Results: Forty\-three complete responses were analyzed \(response rate: 30\.3%\)\. A total of 33 \(76\.7%\) respondents agreed or strongly agreed that AI would improve planning accuracy and efficiency\. Nineteen \(44\.2%\) reported no workplace access to AI tools, and 34 \(79\.1%\) reported no formal AI training\. The most common concerns regarding AI were output accuracy or validation \(n = 28, 65\.1%\), loss of clinical judgment \(n = 22, 51\.2%\), and legal liability \(n = 21, 48\.8%\)\. The most requested forms of support were hands\-on training or simulation \(n = 35, 81\.4%\), regulatory and legal guidance \(n = 30, 69\.8%\), and vendor technical support \(n = 29, 67\.4%\)\. Nonresidents more often reported practical implementation barriers, including funding limitations, accuracy issues, and inadequate support; however, these comparisons were confounded by age and experience differences and should remain exploratory and hypothesis\-generating\.Conclusion: Respondents viewed AI favorably, but gaps regarding access, training, validation, funding, and governance may limit safe implementation\. Structured education, local validation, quality assurance, technical support, and clear institutional and regulatory guidance are needed\.

## [A ASSOCIAÇÃO DE MICRORGANISMOS PERIODONTAIS E A DOENÇA DE ALZHEIMER: UMA REVISÃO DE LITERATURA](../publications/ccbc7fc6ae0e3f60e289.md)

The objective of this study was to conduct a literature review on the association between periodontal microorganisms and Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease, using the PubMed and Lilacs databases with the descriptors &quot;Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease&quot;, &quot;periodontitis&quot;, &quot;neurodegenerative diseases&quot;, &quot;neuroinflammation&quot;, &quot;periodontal pathogens&quot;, and &quot;oral microbiome&quot;, from 2015 to 2025\. ## [Case\-level audit of thyroid ultrasound and cytology deep learning: label conflicts, split design, and shortcut\-sensitive performance in a public archive](../publications/ccd0531c4d9ab50fd8f8.md)

Behnam Kiani Kalejahi; Mohammad Javad Rajabi

The measured performance of thyroid imaging artificial intelligence depends on how the analytical population is assembled, how images are partitioned, whether non\-anatomical image content is informative, and which reference labels are used\. We audited a public multimodal thyroid archive at case level and examined what its reported performance does and does not demonstrate\. The released archive of Pang et al\. \(387 ultrasound images; 1,332 fine\-needle aspiration cytology blocks\) was audited for exact and near\-duplicate images and for contradictory labels, and a frozen case\-level partition was built\. Five ImageNet\-initialised backbones and their mean\-probability ensemble were evaluated by group\-stratified five\-fold cross\-validation and on the frozen test set, with thresholds selected on validation data and case\-clustered 95% confidence intervals\. Revision\-stage control analyses comprised an identical\-code comparison of image\-level and case\-grouped folds; retraining with a heuristically detected sonographic sector or its surround removed, for all five backbones and the ensemble; and a metadata\-only model without a convolutional network\. Frozen ultrasound models were then reassessed on TN3K, against its distributed benign/malignant labels, and on DDTI, for concordance with TI\-RADS categories; both datasets had been accessed during earlier analytical development\. Nine ultrasound images appeared under both benign and papillary carcinoma labels \(19 files\) and were excluded\. Under case\-level cross\-validation, the cytology ensemble reached an AUROC of 0\.958 \(95% CI 0\.938–0\.975\) and the ultrasound ensemble 0\.768 \(0\.716–0\.819\)\. Image\-level folds, despite 99\.8% within\-fold case contamination, changed AUROC by −0\.002 \(−0\.021 to 0\.019\) and \+0\.019 \(0\.008 to 0\.032\) for the two tested backbones\. After removal of the detected sonographic sector, the ultrasound ensemble retained an AUROC of 0\.690 \(0\.630–0\.747\), a paired change of −0\.078 \(−0\.148 to −0\.013\); with only the detected sector retained, it reached 0\.760 \(paired change −0\.008, −0\.054 to 0\.039\)\. Sector detection fell back to a fixed central box in 24\.2% of frames\. A metadata\-only model using frame geometry, global intensity and border statistics reached 0\.749 \(0\.692–0\.804\) for ultrasound\. In post\-exposure reassessment, the ensemble reached 0\.700 \(0\.661–0\.741; image\-level interval\) on TN3K and over\-predicted malignancy \(calibration\-in\-the\-large −0\.49\), and showed no concordance with DDTI TI\-RADS grouping \(0\.518, 0\.436–0\.605\)\. This case\-level audit of a public thyroid archive showed contradictory labels, partition\-sensitive evaluation, and substantial discriminative signal both after removal of a heuristically detected sonographic region and in acquisition metadata alone, so performance on this archive cannot be interpreted as exclusively lesion\-based\. Post\-exposure reassessment on external datasets showed limited and endpoint\-dependent transport of the internal models\.

## [Stability\-Accuracy Tradeoffs in Decentralized Online Learning of Coalition Structures by Selfish Agents](../publications/ccddfcfbc9c9c677e08a.md)

Saar Cohen; Noa Agmon

Coalition formation involves self\-organized coalitions generated through strategic collaborations of autonomous selfish agents\. In online learning of coalition structures, agents’ preferences toward each other are initially unknown before agents interact\. Coalitions are formed iteratively based on preferences that agents learn online from repeated feedback resulting from their interactions\. In this work, we introduce online learning in coalition formation through the lens of distributed decision\-making, where self\-interested agents operate without global coordination or information sharing, and learn only from their own experience\. Under the selfish perspective, each agent seeks to maximize her own utility\. Hence, we analyze the system in terms of Nash stability, where no agent can improve her utility by unilaterally deviating\. Our goal is therefore designing sample\-efficient decentralized algorithms for selfish agents that minimize their Nash regret, yielding approximately Nash stable solutions\. This poses a natural tension between an algorithm’s performance in the short\- and long\-term, trading off between the accuracy of the utility estimation at each round and the long\-term objective of minimizing Nash regret to reach approximately Nash stable outcomes\. Specifically, we first devise an algorithm where each agent sacrifices accuracy at each single time step by using only one utility feedback per round to update her strategy, but still has Nash regret and sample complexity bounds that are optimal up to logarithmic factors\. To control the error incurred at any individual time instant, we then propose a method using multiple samples per round, yet at the expense of obtaining suboptimal Nash regret and sample complexity bounds\.

## [Global research trends in subcentimeter and subsolid pulmonary nodules associated with early\-stage lung cancer: a bibliometric analysis \(2000–2024\)](../publications/ccde9aa8aad173db7b7e.md)

Zechao Wang; Peidong Wang

Abstract Objectives The widespread use of low\-dose computed tomography has markedly increased the detection of subcentimeter and subsolid pulmonary nodules, many of which are closely associated with early\-stage lung cancer\. This study aimed to map global research trends, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution at the intersection of subcentimeter/subsolid pulmonary nodules and early\-stage lung cancer from 2000 to 2024\. Methods: The Web of Science Core Collection \(WoSCC\) was searched on 31 December 2024 for original research articles and reviews published between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2024\. Of the 2,854 records initially retrieved, 1,992 publications met the eligibility criteria and were included\. Analyses were performed in Python \(version 3\.12\) using the igraph library, including collaboration\-network analysis, co\-citation analysis, keyword co\-occurrence clustering based on the Louvain algorithm, thematic evolution analysis, strategic diagram analysis, and historiographic citation\-trajectory analysis\. Results: Annual publication output grew slowly during 2000–2010 and entered an exponential growth phase after 2011\. China, Japan, and the United States were the most productive countries, and China and the United States formed the closest bilateral collaboration\. Co\-citation analysis identified three knowledge pillars: large\-scale lung cancer screening trials, international nodule\-management guidelines, and modern pathological classification of lung adenocarcinoma\. Keyword clustering revealed three principal thematic clusters: \(1\) screening, imaging\-based diagnosis, and nodule management; \(2\) ground\-glass opacity spectrum and surgical treatment; and \(3\) tumor histologic classification\. Thematic evolution showed a progression from morphological description toward refined classification, risk stratification, and individualized management\. Conclusions: The observed research trends indicate that this field is transitioning from morphological description toward precision\-oriented diagnosis and individualized management, with growing attention to artificial intelligence\-assisted diagnostic tools, sublobar surgical strategies, and active surveillance of ground\-glass nodules\. These findings should be interpreted within the thematic scope of subcentimeter and subsolid nodules associated with early\-stage lung cancer rather than the entire field of pulmonary nodule research\.

## [Mosaic: Multi\-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../publications/cce7c9254280221ef334.md)

Yilong Xu; Minrui Xu; Xinyu Zhou; Xiang Long; Haochen Tan; Zhijiang Guo

Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single\-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context\. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single\-session training assumption and inference\-time execution\. Therefore, we introduce Multi\-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory\. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory\-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories\. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi\-session agentic RL method with critic\-free hierarchical optimization\. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session\-usage signals into advantage estimation\. At the session level, it shapes each session&\#x27;s advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution\. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3\.5\-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average\. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi\-session agentic RL\.

## [vToxiNet: An interpretable deep learning framework for hepatotoxicity prediction and mechanism exploration](../publications/ccea8e061038c6dc39a8.md)

Xuelian Jia; Tong Wang; Daniel P\. Russo; Lauren M\. Aleksunes; Shuo Xiao; Hao Zhu

Hepatotoxicity remains a leading cause of drug attrition and post\-marketing withdrawal, resulting from diverse and complex toxicity mechanisms\. Traditional in vitro models can only capture a limited subset of toxicity pathways, and animal studies face translational and ethical limitations\. Regulatory agencies have therefore promoted new approach methodologies, including human\-relevant assays, omics technologies, and computational models to improve predictive toxicology and support evidence\-based decision\-making\. However, most machine learning models for hepatotoxicity either rely solely on chemical structure or operate as black boxes, limiting mechanistic interpretability and broader applicability\. Here, we introduce the virtual toxicity network \(vToxiNet\), a biologically constrained deep learning framework that embeds systems toxicology knowledge directly into neural network architecture for interpretable hepatotoxicity prediction\. vToxiNet integrates chemical descriptors, high\-throughput assay responses, transcriptomic signatures, and Reactome pathway hierarchy to construct a virtual adverse outcome pathway network\. Across cross\-validation and external validation, vToxiNet demonstrates promising predictive performance\. Importantly, interpretation of vToxiNet enables gene and pathway\-level attribution, supporting mechanism\-informed hazard characterization and chemical prioritization\. By integrating multimodal data and biological hierarchy as architectural constraints, this study provides a framework that combines prediction with mechanistic interpretation and supports further development of mechanism\-informed approaches for chemical hazard assessment\.

## [A SMOTE enhanced multi stream deep learning ensemble for credit card fraud detection](../publications/ccfbf6f5d569fb3ab986.md)

Lubna Abdulaziz Alharbi; Faizah Hameed Alsulami

Credit card fraud detection is highly imbalanced, making minority\-class metrics and deployment efficiency more informative than accuracy alone\. This study proposes SMOTE\-EnsembleNet \(SENet\), combining CNN, BiLSTM, and Transformer streams through learnable cross\-attention fusion\. Among 100%, 200%, and 500% SMOTE ratios with focal loss, 200% SMOTE achieved the best overall balance\. SENet obtained AUC\-ROC values of 0\.9967 \(95% CI 0\.9955–0\.9979\), 0\.9567 \(95% CI 0\.9542–0\.9592\), and 0\.9923 \(95% CI 0\.9911–0\.9935\) on ULB, IEEE\-CIS, and PaySim, respectively\. Compared with no SMOTE, AUC\-ROC improved by 1\.55, 1\.55, and 1\.34 percentage points, while cross\-attention improved AUC\-ROC by 0\.22 percentage points over concatenation\. Fold\-level significance testing \(\(p &lt; 0\.05\)\) was conducted against all tuned baselines\. SENet achieved 12\.4 ms inference latency per transaction on an NVIDIA A100 GPU while supporting interpretable error and feature\-importance analyses\. AUC\-ROC and AUC\-PR are threshold\-independent, whereas precision, recall, and F1\-score are reported separately in the experiments\. The 12\.4 ms latency applies only to the stated NVIDIA A100 configuration\. Cross\-attention additionally improved AUC\-PR by 1\.3 percentage points over concatenation, and the small differences between 200% and 500% SMOTE are interpreted together with fold\-level statistical tests\.

## [MQDA\-Net: A Quantum\-enhanced Dual\-branch Framework for Unified Brain Tumor Segmentation, Classification and Structured Radiology Report Generation](../publications/ccfcc8523951466031e4.md)

subia salma; Sanjeev C\. Lingareddy; S\. Shilpashree; Vineet Kumar

Automated brain tumor analysis from multi\-parametric MRI is typically split into three separately solved problems: volumetric segmentation, tumor\-type classification and radiology report generation\.The few unified systems chain these stages rather than optimizing them jointly, and inherit the weaknesses of every link: slice\-level segmenters that discard volumetric context, classification heads carrying tens of millions of parameters that overfit small neuro\-oncology cohorts, static knowledge graphs that cannot reason from image evidence, and report generators whose output barely overlaps clinician text\.We propose MQDA\-Net, which integrates all three tasks in one architecture, each pathway optimized on the cohort carrying its annotations and coupled to the others through shared representations and explicit conditioning\.A three\-dimensional encoder with block\-level Multi\-Scale Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling \(MSASPP\) widens the bottleneck receptive field\.A Dual\-Branch Discriminative Decoder couples a coarse binary localization branch to a fine\-grained semantic branch through cross\-attention, injecting an explicit localization prior into sub\-region assignment\.A twelve\-qubit variational classification head \(parameterized U3 rotations, controlled\-Z entanglement and Pauli\-X readout\) replaces the conventional stacked classifier, reducing classifier parameters from 67\.2 M to 7\.3 M\. A dynamic image\-grounded knowledge graph, built per case from segmentation masks and MNI atlas co\-registration and refined by a Graph Attention Network, conditions a Q\-Formerprojected LoRA\-adapted Llama 3\.2 11B Vision\-Instruct backbone that emits structured reports carrying volumetric measurements, anatomical localization and BT\-RADS risk stratification\.On BraTS 2023, MQDA\-Net reaches mean Dice 0\.91 and IoU 0\.84; on the harder BraTS 2024 post\-treatment cohort the framework reaches 79\.85 % Dice, exceeding a self\-supervised specialist baseline by 4\.61 points\.Classification accuracy reaches 99\.72 % on the Nickparvar composite benchmark, and report BLEU improves from 0\.068 to 0\.170 with ROUGE\-L F1 rising from 0\.0018 to 0\.068\.Differences against published values for the closest prior unified framework are reported descriptively; no matched statistical comparison is claimed\.

## [Jovchelovitch, Sandra: The Rehabilitation of Common Sense: Social Representations, Science and Cognitive Polyphasia](../publications/ccfe26a0169f424b1299.md)



\_Journal for the Theory of Social Behaviour\_ 38 \(4\):431\-448\. 2008In Psychoanalysis, its image and its public Moscovici introduced the theory of social representations and took further the project of rehabilitating common sense\. In this paper I examine this project through a consideration of the problem of cognitive polyphasia, and the continuity and discontinuity between different systems of knowing\. Focusing on the relations between science and common sense\. I ask why, despite considerable evidence to the contrary, the scientific imagination tends to deny its relation to common sense and believe that can displace it\. I argue that the psychosocial dynamic between common sense and science is revealing of how heavily they are entangled in, and indeed indebted to each other\. Even more, this dynamic allows for a full appreciation of what the theory of social representations calls states of cognitive polyphasia\. Different systems of thinking and knowing do not displace each other but live side by side, co\-existing in a variety of ways, fulfilling different functions and answering different needs in social life \(direct link \)

## [Designing Engineering Curricula as Socio\-Technical Systems: A Practice\-Informed ST\+EHoM Model\.](../publications/cd08f9a77b7698d838ac.md)

Nikita Hari; Abel Nyamapfene; Janet Hanson

Electrical and electronic engineering graduates increasingly need to work with complex socio\-technical systems involving technical, human, organisational, environmental and ethical dimensions\. This creates a curriculum design challenge: programmes must develop technical depth while also helping students recognise interdependencies, frame problems, work with uncertainty, iterate solutions and adapt to changing constraints\. This paper develops and illustrates a curriculum design process that combines systems thinking with Engineering Habits of Mind \(EHoM\)\. It argues that systems thinking can function both as a curriculum design logic and as an integrative engineering habit, while EHoM provides a language for translating this logic into learning outcomes, pedagogy, assessment and reflection\. The paper adopts a practice\-informed conceptual design case approach, drawing on the design and early implementation of an undergraduate engineering degree apprenticeship curriculum in a new higher education provider in England\. The case is used to examine how the ST\+EHoM model supported curriculum coherence, academic\-workplace integration, assessment alignment and adaptive redesign, while also surfacing tensions around accreditation, staff capacity, student expectations and the balance between technical depth and disposition\-oriented learning\. The paper contributes a practical, conceptually grounded model for designing engineering curricula that prepare students to think and act as engineers within complex socio\-technical systems\.

## [Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross\-Section of Stock Returns](../publications/cd0aca2864b98a6723c7.md)

Kevin Foley; Jonathan Hartadi; Shivesh Prakash; Charishma Takkallapalli; Swapnil Vatsal

Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight\. We build news topics from NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, adapted into a sentence encoder by contrastive fine\-tuning on passages of the same article, with no labels or returns\. We compare it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT readers on 1\.26 million articles from 2012 to 2024, convert each reader&\#x27;s topics into attention shocks and stock exposures, and forecast the returns of the 1,000 largest US stocks with eight models at three rebalancing frequencies\. Models are fitted on 2013\-2019, choices are made on 2020\-2021, and 2022\-2024 is held out\. The experiment with the best validation score loses money at every frequency\. Measuring attention shocks against the past 63 trading days instead of 5 raises the test rank IC of every reader\. NoLBERT gives the most stable topics and forecasts about as well as LDA\. An equal\-weight combination of all readers and models earns a monthly net Sharpe ratio of 1\.12, significant against zero before adjusting for the search but not against a price\-only benchmark\.

## [Generative AI Use and the Verification Gap Follow Opposing Social Gradients in Türkiye](../publications/cd0e0306964c91ca609b.md)

Doğukan Kurç

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) use and online information checking may be socially patterned in different ways\. This cross\-sectional study analysed the 2025 Turkish Statistical Institute ICT survey of 22,502 internet users aged 16–74 using weighted modified Poisson regression with household\-clustered standard errors\. Overall, 19\.2% reported generative AI use, and 48\.3% of respondents who noticed doubtful content did not check it\. Conditional non\-checking \(the verification gap\) increased with age and decreased with education and reported digital activity, whereas AI use followed the opposite pattern\. Compared with ages 16–24, the adjusted prevalence ratio at ages 65–74 was 1\.48 \(95% confidence interval 1\.30–1\.68\) for non\-checking and 0\.10 \(0\.07–0\.16\) for AI use\. Health information seekers and AI users reported less non\-checking among those who noticed doubtful content, but neither group had a lower prevalence of noticing without checking among all internet users\. Among non\-checkers, 87\.3% reported already judging the information or source unreliable and 15\.2% reported insufficient skills or knowledge; responses could overlap\. These findings distinguish participation in AI use, reported noticing of doubtful content, and subsequent checking\. ## [Hybrid CNN–GNN Architectures for Hyperspectral Image Analysis in Kidney Cancer: A Structured Review of Foundations, Evidence, and Research Gaps](../publications/cd1472816f8191bfc2a9.md)

Jestin Joseph M; Shanthi T

Renal cell carcinoma \(RCC\) accounts for most adult kidney cancers\. Its diagnosis relies on imaging and on histopathological subtyping and grading, both of which use only a small part of the optical information in tissue\. Hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) records tens to hundreds of contiguous narrow bands per pixel and encodes biochemical contrast that RGB microscopy does not resolve\. Convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) learn local spectral–spatial patterns\. Graph neural networks \(GNNs\) model relations between regions that are not neighbours on the pixel grid\. Hybrid CNN–GNN models that combine the two are an active line of work in hyperspectral remote sensing, and graph\-based models have already been applied to conventional RGB RCC histopathology\. This structured narrative review synthesises four bodies of literature: CNN and GNN methods for HSI, hybrid CNNGNN fusion, medical and renal HSI, and deep learning for RCC imaging and histopathology\. It also positions the work against existing RCC deep\-learning and HSI–GNN reviews\. In the literature located, all HSI studies of RCC tissue identified used non\-graph architectures, and graph\-based RCC models used RGB slides only\. The review then sets out a candidate CNN–GNN architecture for hyperspectral RCC tissue, defined as a testable hypothesis with an explicit evaluation protocol\. It identifies six research gaps: graph\-augmented HSI models for RCC, public data, tissue\-specific graph construction, transfer from RGB pathology graphs, interpretability, and computational feasibility\. It also identifies the main threats to validity in the current evidence: small single\-centre cohorts and the risk of data leakage when data are split at the pixel or patch level rather than the patient level\.

## [Agentic\-Priors: Using Large Language Models to Address the Cold Start Problem in Preference Elicitation](../publications/cd14bd80d6a54646a660.md)

Bruno Arcanjo; Zhaoxing Li; Sebastian Stein

An agent that learns a user&\#x27;s preferences from their choices faces a cold start problem: before any choices are observed, it must rely solely on a prior\. Informative priors are usually fitted to historical choice data, which new tasks and deployments lack\. To address this, we present Agentic\-Priors, which lets agentic systems use the implicit knowledge of large language models \(LLMs\) instead\. Specifically, an LLM states a new user&\#x27;s trade\-offs in interpretable terms, such as willingness to pay or value of time, which we map to a prior over multinomial logit coefficients\. This prior is then refined by a Bayesian learner as choices are observed\. Across seven choice datasets, Agentic\-Priors improves cold start accuracy over an uninformed prior by 5\-40 percentage points\. It also outperforms AutoElicit, a state\-of\-the\-art LLM prior\-elicitation method, on three datasets and loses on one\. It is up to 18 points more accurate than in\-context learning, and never significantly worse\. Against hierarchical Bayes models fitted to surveys of increasing size, our approach is worth roughly 6\-40 surveyed users, in terms of log\-loss, so its value is concentrated in a deployment&\#x27;s first users\.

## [Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short\-Answer F1 Loss](../publications/cd23d3b3df51cf736285.md)

Zhiyuan Wang

Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture\-of\-experts \(MoE\) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages\. We locate the damage with token\-, layer\- and attention\-path interventions on short\-answer question answering in four MoE families\. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly\. In Qwen3\-30B\-A3B this loss is made at the two chat\-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek\-V2\-Lite at the first 8\-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage\. Reduction changes the first token&\#x27;s attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full\. On real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts, placing them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while placing them at random in the documents is about 3 points worse \(two of five prespecified primary comparisons; the others were undecided or not run\)\. Because the answer boundary always ends a single\-turn prompt, and DeepSeek&\#x27;s loss was no longer detectable once its instruction moved away from the start, the sensitive tokens lay at the prompt ends in every sensitive layout we found, so rules that keep the ends are not distinguished from rules that read application marks\. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K\-token prompts and not at 2K tokens\.

## [How Nespresso transformed from a product\-centric business to an AI\-driven service platform – and which business model innovation factors made it succeed](../publications/cd37bd12b179a8eab96e.md)

Sandro Battisti; Alexander Brem

Purpose This real impact article focuses on the interplay between business model innovation and artificial intelligence \(AI\) in the coffee industry\. We explored Nespresso&\#x27;s omnichannel customer engagement as a key case study on AI\-enabled platform service model\. Drawing on secondary data on customer experience with AI\-based solutions, this study shows the business model and key innovation factors of Nespresso\. The study focuses on customer service experience and omnichannel engagement rather than the capsule and machine business revenue stream\. Design/methodology/approach This research conducts a single\-case study of Nespresso service application scenarios, based on publicly available data from the Nespresso website, reports, partner websites and academic literature\. We explored how Nespresso and its parent company, Nestlé, structured their business model, as well as five use case scenarios for an omnichannel customer engagement strategy\. ## [Designing Rare Pediatric Disease Trials for FDA Review: A Mutation\-Agnostic Cell Therapy Strategy in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/cd3a303d78dc6a118fa1.md)

Patricia Angelique Mallari; Peivand Pirouzi

Clinical trial design in rare pediatric disease faces two compounding structural constraints that do not apply in the same way to common adult conditions: the eligible population for any single, mutation\-specific intervention is already a fraction of an already small disease population, and enrolling children in a placebo\-controlled trial for a fatal, progressive disease raises genuine ethical questions around consent and equipoise, pushing sponsors toward smaller trials, surrogate endpoints, or historical controls\. This article examines how a mutation\-agnostic allogeneic cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) represents a different response to these constraints, trading the narrower population and accelerated\-approval pathway available to mutation\-specific exon\-skipping therapies for a broader eligible population and a correspondingly higher evidentiary burden on a traditional clinical endpoint\. The article develops this trial\-design tradeoff as a general framework applicable to other mutation\-agnostic rare\-disease programs, situates it against the product&\#x27;s documented regulatory history, and proposes a real\-world evidence strategy informed by registries already established for this disease area\. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals designing clinical programs for mutation\-agnostic therapeutics in rare pediatric populations\.Keywords: rare pediatric disease; mutation\-agnostic therapy; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; trial design; allogeneic cell therapy; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single\-cell–to–bulk transcriptome mapping](../publications/cd3c7d8ea707b5bac5fe.md)

Alexandre Coudray; Romain Forey; Benjamı́n Béjar; Filipe Martins; Joana Carlevaro\-Fita; Shaoline Sheppard; Sandra Eloise Offner; Gioele La Manno; Guillaume Obozinski; Didier Trono

Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells\. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived\. Such bulk measurements obscure cell\-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes\. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two\-step machine\-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA\-seq into cell\-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug sensitivity measurements into cell subtype\- and single\-cell\-specific profiles\. We first validate CLIMB using in\-vitro mixtures of leukemic cell lines with experimentally known cell\-type proportions, then extend this validation to large\-scale, cross\-dataset pseudo\-bulk analyses built from independent scRNA\-seq references across two disease contexts and five cancer types \- mimicking the reference\-to\-target mismatches encountered in real applications \- and show that CLIMB accurately infers the cellular composition of bulk samples, outperforming state\-of\-the\-art bulk deconvolution methods\. We emphasize CLIMB&\#x27;s effectiveness in acute myeloid leukemia, where it offers highly accurate estimation of leukemic stem cell fractions across three test datasets and three patient cohorts\. We then validate CLIFF, our algorithm for estimating cell subtype\- and single\-cell\-specific drug sensitivity, first on the same in\-vitro cell line mixtures using experimentally measured drug responses, and then through in\-depth, realistic\-scale pseudo\-bulk simulations\. We applied our deconvolution strategy to the beatAML cohort dataset, currently the most extensive database of ex\-vivo drug screening data\. This analysis generated a cell subtype\-resolved drug sensitivity landscape for 121 compounds, revealing multiple compounds putatively active against leukemic stem cells, including midostaurin, A\-674563, SNS\-032, and foretinib\. Collectively, our work introduces a general computational framework for resolving bulk functional measurements at cell\-type and single\-cell resolution, providing an attractive new computational tool for drug development and precision medicine\.

## [Recent Advances in Silicon/Carbon Composite Anodes for Lithium‐Ion Batteries: Material, Structure, and Interfacial Stability](../publications/cd3cd4ab42eb1c5f9d5e.md)

Yongkang Li; 韩雅菘; Lihua Fan; Long Jiang; Jing Zhu; Ling Wang; Lei Dai; Huajun Tian; Bing Xue; Zhangxing He

As the global energy transition creates an increasingly pressing need for lithium\-ion batteries, silicon/carbon composite anodes have garnered substantial attention owing to their ultrahigh specific capacity\. However, their commercial application is severely hindered by critical issues, including particle pulverization, electrode delamination, and broken and thick solid electrolyte interphase \(SEI\) layer, all arising from the severe volume expansion during cycling\. Rational design of the anode structure, electrode interface, and electrolyte composition has proven effective in mitigating these challenges and enhancing battery performance\. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in silicon/carbon composite anodes for lithium\-ion batteries, with strategies categorized into three main areas, structural design, electrode interface design, and electrolyte regulation\. Structural design encompasses core\-shell, yolk\-shell, and embedding structures\. Electrode interface design includes functional coatings and novel binders\. Electrolyte regulation involves tailoring lithium salts, solvents, and additives\. The existing challenges and design requirements for silicon/carbon composite anodes are first discussed, followed by a detailed examination of improvement strategies aimed at alleviating volume expansion and stabilizing the SEI film\. This review aims to provide guidance for related work and to stimulate further research in the field of silicon/carbon composite anodes for high\-energy\-density lithium\-ion batteries\.

Marius Gene Cassius Arce; Rowen Neil Enriquez; Vince Caleb Tadiwan

Construction organizations that still plan and track work through spreadsheets, email, and paper records have limitedvisibility of schedule, cost, resources, and risk\. This paper reports the design, implementation, and evaluation of aweb\-based project management system for UA Designs, a design\-and\-build contractor, aligned with six knowledge areas ofthe Project Management Body of Knowledge \(PMBOK\): integration, schedule, cost, resource, risk, and stakeholdermanagement\. The system is a React and Node\.js application with critical\-path scheduling, earned\-value indicators, adeterministic forecasting engine, and a tool\-grounded artificial intelligence assistant whose suggested changes to projectrecords require human approval\. Software verification covered functional, usability\-walkthrough, performance, andPMBOK\-alignment tests\. A descriptive evaluation with two key company users produced a functionality mean of 4\.83 and ausability mean of 4\.92 on a five\-point scale, both interpreted as Excellent, and a System Usability Scale average of 60\.0,below the commonly cited benchmark of 68\.
