## [Task\-aware Kernel Stein certificates for Rényi differential privacy](../publications/cdee43e97877b6df55e8.md)

Leoni Carla Wirth; Tara Trautwein; Gesine Reinert

Rènyi differential privacy, based on Rènyi divergence, has become a notion of choice for privacy guarantees\. However, outside the Gaussian setting, Rènyi divergence can be difficult to compute\. In particular, Rènyi differential privacy guarantees that exploit task\-specific information, as in Rènyi Pufferfish privacy, can be challenging\. Here we use kernel Stein discrepancies based on escort distributions to provide certificates for Rènyi differential privacy\. By designing the kernel to focus on the relevant privacy directions, we also derive task\-aware privacy certificates\. We provide exact identities for Gaussian and Laplace mechanisms and bounds for exponential mechanisms, with separate task\-aware guarantees\. A real data set example illustrates how the protected comparison set and the released subspace jointly determine the resulting certificates\.

## [A LIGHTWEIGHT AND RESOURCE\-ADAPTIVE DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE CLASSIFICATION ON LIMITED MRI DATASETS](../publications/cdf04f6a02f232af8429.md)

B Sowjanya

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects memory, cognitive abilities, and daily functioning\. Early and accurate classification of the disease is important for supporting clinical assessment and timely medical intervention\. However, developing reliable deep learning models for Alzheimer’s disease classification remains challenging because of the limited availability of labeled Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\) datasets and the high computational requirements of complex neural networks\. This paper proposes “A Lightweight and Resource\-Adaptive Deep Learning Framework for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification on Limited MRI Datasets” to address these challenges through an efficient and computationally economical classification approach\. The proposed framework involves MRI image preprocessing, data augmentation, feature extraction, and lightweight deep learningbased classification to identify relevant patterns associated with different stages of Alzheimer’s disease\. Resource\-adaptive mechanisms are incorporated to optimize model complexity and computational requirements according to the available dataset and hardware resources\. Transfer learning and regularization techniques can be employed to improve feature learning and reduce overfitting when training data are limited\. The framework aims to classify MRI images into clinically relevant categories, such as cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer’s disease, depending on the selected dataset and its available labels\. Its performance can be evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, model size, inference time, and computational resource utilization\. By balancing classification performance with computational efficiency, the proposed approach seeks to provide a practical solution for Alzheimer’s disease classification in resource\-constrained environments\. The framework may support research in computer\-aided neurological assessment, although its predictions require clinical validation before use in real\-world medical decision\-making\.

## [Mechanism\-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review](../publications/cdf14ebf0c27d3227bb4.md)

Arbind Kumar Choudhary; Anamitra Hait; Maheshkumar Baladaniya

Background Secondary hypertension is under\-recognised despite the availability of mechanism\-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy\. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause\-directed treatment\. Objectives To systematically synthesise evidence across the principal causes of secondary hypertension using a mechanism → diagnosis → therapy framework; to compare diagnostic performance and cause\-directed treatment effects; and to examine concordance between contemporary society guidelines and real\-world implementation\. Methods This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA\) 2020, with diagnostic accuracy reporting informed by PRISMA\-DTA\. MEDLINE \(PubMed\), Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, ClinicalTrials\.gov, and the WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to 30 June 2025, supplemented by citation searching\. The formal search identified 580 records; after removal of 168 duplicates, 412 records were screened, 106 full\-text reports were assessed, and 58 included evidence records were represented across 63 publications\. The review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO\. Screening, extraction and structured appraisal were performed by a single reviewer \(the first author\); therefore, no dual\-reviewer agreement statistic was applicable\. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2, ROBINS\-I, QUADAS\-2, and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate, and certainty was summarised using GRADE\. A targeted post\-search surveillance update through 31 July 2026 was used only to contextualise major newly available guidelines and Phase 3 trial reports and did not alter the original PRISMA counts\. Results Primary aldosteronism \(PA\) is best understood as a continuum of renin\-independent aldosterone excess: in Brown et al\. \[The unrecognized prevalence of primary aldosteronism: a cross\-sectional study\. Ann Intern Med \. \(2020\) 173 :10–20\], biochemically overt autonomous aldosterone production was present in 11\.3%, 15\.7%, 21\.6%, and 22\.0% across normotensive, stage 1, stage 2, and resistant\-hypertension strata, respectively\. In unilateral PA, the PASO cohort distinguished complete biochemical success after adrenalectomy \(94%; 656/699\) from complete clinical success \(37%; 259/705\), with partial clinical improvement in a further 47%\. PATHWAY\-2 established spironolactone as the most effective fourth\-line drug in resistant hypertension; CORAL, ASTRAL, STAR, and DRASTIC did not support routine revascularisation for stable atherosclerotic renal\-artery stenosis; plasma\-free metanephrines remained highly sensitive for phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma; and PA testing in eligible patients with resistant hypertension remained only 1\.6%–2\.1%\. Post\-search Phase 3 trials of selective aldosterone synthase inhibition showed approximately 9 mm Hg placebo\-corrected office systolic blood pressure reductions, but cardiovascular\-outcome benefit has not been established, and electrolyte/renal monitoring remains necessary\. Conclusions Across secondary hypertension, a limited set of pathophysiological effector pathways maps to specific diagnostic tests and cause\-directed treatments\. The strongest opportunities for clinical gain are earlier recognition of high\-yield phenotypes, accurate aetiological subtyping, and implementation of established testing pathways; emerging aldosterone synthase inhibitors expand blood\-pressure\-lowering options but should not yet be interpreted as proven cardiovascular\-outcome therapies\.

## [Grünbaum, Thor &amp; Christensen, Mark Schram: The functional role of conscious sensation of movement](../publications/ce03db4939ba659d4c02.md)



\_Neuroscience &amp; Biobehavioral Reviews\_ 164 \(\[105813\]\)\. 2024This paper proposes a new framework for investigating neural signals sufficient for a conscious sensation of movement and their role in motor control\. We focus on signals sufficient for proprioceptive awareness, particularly from muscle spindle activation and from primary motor cortex \(M1\)\. Our review of muscle vibration studies reveals that afferent signals alone can induce conscious sensations of movement\. Similarly, studies employing peripheral nerve blocks suggest that efferent signals from M1 are sufficient for sensations of movement\. On this basis, we show that competing theories of motor control assign different roles to sensation of movement\. According to motor command theories, sensation of movement corresponds to an estimation of the current state based on afferent signals, efferent signals, and predictions\. In contrast, within active inference architectures, sensations correspond to proprioceptive predictions driven by efferent signals from M1\. The focus on sensation of movement provides a way to critically compare and evaluate the two theories\. Our analysis offers new insights into the functional roles of movement sensations in motor control and consciousness\. \(direct link \)

## [Investigation on Automatic Classification of Bone, Lymph Node, and Local Lesions in CT Images of Prostate Cancer Patients](../publications/ce08269c427da90c7edf.md)

Oona Rainio; Ahti Vehmanen; Anjie Li; Maria K\. Jaakkola; Jukka Kemppainen; Riku Klén

Abstract Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer \(PCa\) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning\. Following a computed tomography \(CT\) or a positron emission tomography \(PET\)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations\. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning models\. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of $$^\{18\}$$ 18 F\-prostate\-specific membrane antigen \(PSMA\) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients\. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type\. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs\. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96\.0%\. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97\.9±1\.2%, 95\.2±1\.3%, and 93\.1±2\.8% in the five\-fold cross\-validation experiments of the primary data and 96\.3%, 94\.0%, and 80\.0% on the external test set, respectively\. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions\. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories\.

## [Implementation of Neural Networks for Direction Control of DC\-Motor](../publications/ce2355a32893ae6b1635.md)

Abdullah Masrub

In this paper, a neural network was implemented to control the direction of a DC motor\. In this context, attention was paid to the field of artificial intelligence related to neural networks\. The network targeted for training is small in size, and the tasks required of it are limited and include the direction of rotation of the DC motor axis, which has two directions \(clockwise rotation or counterclockwise rotation\)\. DC motors are used in applications such as robotics and automated manufacturing\. It is a rotary actuator or linear actuator that allows control of linear direction\. The main purpose of this work is to provide a clear view of the importance of using neural networks in the control field\. In this study, the ANN is trained by the back\-propagation algorithm, and a multilayer neural network is composed to implement the controller that controls the operation of the model using the back\-propagation learning algorithm that regulates the function of the DC motor system\. It was noticed that changing some parameters such as weights, learning rates, number of hidden layers, or number of nodes can enhance the output and generate the proper control of the direction\.

## [Prescription Patterns in Terminal Cancer Patients: A Prospective Study in a Low\- and Middle\-Income Country Setting](../publications/ce2c1c89f61b73fa6133.md)

Divya Sai Vanumu; Praneeth Suvvari; Praveen Kumar Kodisharapu; Basanth Kumar Rayani

Objectives: The objective of the study is to evaluate prescription patterns from admission \(Ta\) to discharge/death \(Td\), assess associations between symptom burden and medication use and identify significant co\-prescription patterns contributing to polypharmacy\. Materials and Methods: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted in an acute palliative care unit of a tertiary cancer hospital \(n = 219\)\. Medications were categorised using the World Health Organization anatomical therapeutic chemical codes\. Symptom burden was assessed at Ta using the Symptom Assessment Scale\. McNemar and Chi\-square tests examined changes in prescribing; Pearson correlation assessed relationships between symptom burden and medication use\. Results: Polypharmacy was common \(mean \~7\.5 medications\) throughout admission\. Opioids \(73%\), antacids \(68%\), laxatives \(48\.9%\) and corticosteroids \(48\.9%\) were most frequent at Td\. Significant co\-prescription patterns included prophylactic combinations \(opioid\-laxative, corticosteroid\-antiulcer, non steroidal anti\-inflammatory drugs–antiulcer; p &lt; 0\.05\), symptom cluster management \(opioid\-anxiolytic, opioid\-propulsives; p &lt; 0\.001\) and potential medication\-induced prescribing patterns \(gabapentinoid\-diuretic; p = 0\.035\)\. Individual symptoms predicted the use of relevant medication classes, but overall symptom burden did not predict total medication load at Td \(r = 0\.056, p = 0\.408\), indicating cascade\-driven rather than symptom\-driven polypharmacy\. Only 63\.6% of medications aligned with the International Association of Hospice and Palliative Care Essential Medicines List\. Conclusion: Persistent polypharmacy and identifiable preventive co\-prescribing patterns suggest opportunities for targeted interventions, including structured deprescribing, pharmacist\-led reviews and development of LMIC\-specific essential medicines lists\.

## [Neuromorphic Spin\-Torque Nano\-Oscillators and Coupled Magnonic Networks: Nonlinear Dynamics, Frequency Entrainment, and Edge Reservoir Computing](../publications/ce2c497ac30da040ce95.md)

Harshit Sharma, Rajnish Singh, Dr\. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr\. Vibhakar Pathak , Er\. Robil Varshney

Edge artificial intelligence, real\-time wireless classification, and high\-frequency time\-series forecasting demand hardware architectures capable of processing complex temporal dynamics at ultra\-low power levels without conventional digital clock bottlenecks\. Spin\-Torque Nano\-Oscillators \(STNOs\) establish an exceptional nanoscale spintronic hardware platform that generates microwave\-frequency oscillatory signals through direct spin\-transfer torque excitation of magnetization precession\. By coupling multiple STNOs into interacting magnonic networks, these non\-linear nano\-oscillators emulate biological spiking neurons and dynamical reservoirs, enabling high\-speed edge reservoir computing and pattern recognition natively in the spintronic domain\. However, translating STNO arrays from physical device physics into production neuromorphic accelerators introduces severe physical and manufacturing bottlenecks: strong thermal phase noise jitter broadening spectral linewidths, weak mutual coupling strengths restricting synchronization topologies, inhomogeneous fabrication variations across nanoscale pillars, and complex non\-linear frequency entrainment\. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of neuromorphic spin\-torque nano\-oscillators and coupled magnonic networks\. We formalize magnetization dynamics via the Landau\-Lifshitz\-Gilbert\-Slonczewski \(LLGS\) equation with STT active damping modulation, derive Adler equations for mutual phase synchronization and frequency entrainment, and model spin\-wave bus propagation\. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SPICE and hardware\-in\-the\-loop testbed evaluating 64\-node STNO neuromorphic arrays across spoken digit recognition and real\-time wireless anomaly detection\. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our synchronized magnonic network achieves a 97\.4% classification accuracy on spoken digit recognition while operating at gigahertz frequencies within an ultra\-low power envelope of 42 nanowatts per oscillator—outperforming digital recurrent neural networks by over three orders of magnitude in energy efficiency\. Finally, we formulate open challenges in thermal noise suppression, all\-magnonic transistorless logic, and scalable 3D magnetic interconnect integration\.

## [Moussa, Rony: Artificial Intelligence and the Future Structure of Scientific Discovery: A Philosophical Perspective](../publications/ce36de1b6deab81ed07a.md)



Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming scientific practice by identifying patterns, generating hypotheses, and making discoveries that frequently exceed direct human cognitive capacities\. These developments raise a fundamental philosophical question: how does artificial intelligence change the structure of scientific discovery itself? This paper argues that AI does not replace scientific explanation but reorganizes its role within scientific inquiry\. Traditionally, scientific discovery and scientific explanation were closely intertwined\. Increasingly, however, computational systems are capable of discovering organizational regularities before scientists understand their underlying significance\. From the perspective of Generative Continuum Ontology \(GCO\), this development represents not the replacement of scientific understanding but the emergence of a new stage within the scientific process\. Artificial intelligence progressively expands the capacity to identify organizational regularities, while scientific explanation remains responsible for integrating these discoveries into coherent organizational understanding\. The future of science is therefore characterized not by the disappearance of explanation but by its increasing philosophical importance as the bridge between computational discovery and scientific understanding\. \(direct link \)

## [NSF\-DOE Vera C\. Rubin Observatory’s First View of the Neptune Trojan L5 \(Trailing\) Cloud: Two New Long\-term Stable Trojans](../publications/ce44fc006dd3f0c57484.md)

Megan E\. Schwamb; Pedro H\. Bernardinelli; Kathryn Volk; J Murtagh; Hsing Wen Lin; Andrew S\. Rivkin; Colin Orion Chandler; Lynne Jones; Susan Benecchi; Mario Jurić; Jacob A\. Kurlander; Sarah Greenstreet; Adam Wilson; Maxine West; Ryan R\. Lyttle

Abstract The NSF\-DOE Vera C\. Rubin Observatory’s combination of survey speed, sky coverage, and depth provides a unique opportunity to study the distant trans\-Neptunian region, including the Neptune Trojans\. The Neptune Trojans are small bodies on orbits with Neptune’s semimajor axis that are locked in the 1:1 mean motion resonance librating about the ice giant’s stable Lagrange points, L4 \(leading\) and L5 \(trailing\), located 60 ∘ ahead of or behind the planet\. For more than 15 yr, the on\-sky location of the L5 Neptune Trojan cloud has been coincident with the Galactic plane and Galactic center; the high stellar density has significantly hindered the discovery of L5 Neptune Trojans\. In 2025, the L5 cloud had moved sufficiently out of the Galactic plane to overlap with the sky covered by Rubin Observatory’s Science Validation \(SV\) survey that was executed during the observatory’s commissioning phase\. We report on two new confirmed long\-term stable \(primordial\) members of the Neptune L5 Trojan cloud \(2025 MH348 and 2025 NN80\), doubling the known sample, and one candidate \(2025 MD138\), all of which have been found in a preliminary search of the SV survey observations\. We present our study to characterize the physical and dynamical properties of these objects and compare the L5 sample to the well\-studied L4 cloud\. This work also presents the first characterization of objects discovered by Rubin Observatory’s moving object discovery pipelines using observations taken in an LSST\-like cadence, and as such, provides a blueprint for LSST\-era analyses\.

## [Gut\-liver axis dysregulation and restoration in decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis: rationale and research progress of fecal microbiota transplantation](../publications/ce4d7d03b26c13c40bff.md)

Shujuan Gao; Jie Zhuang; Hui Cheng; Kai Hu; 庄立伟; Yong Pan

Decompensated hepatitis B virus \(HBV\) related cirrhosis is associated with high mortality and a wide range of complications\. Current antiviral and symptomatic treatments fail to reverse core pathological alterations, including disruption of the gut microbial ecosystem\. Gut\-liver axis imbalance represents a central hub in disease progression\. Gut dysbiosis compromises the intestinal mucosal barrier, leading to endotoxin translocation into the bloodstream, which in turn exacerbates hepatic inflammation and fibrosis, thereby establishing a vicious cycle\. This review synthesizes the key mechanisms, clinical efficacy, administration routes, and safety profile of fecal microbiota transplantation \(FMT\) in this disease\. It also identifies current technical bottlenecks and research gaps in FMT application and discusses future directions toward precision based and standardized clinical translation of this therapeutic approach\.

## [A desnutrição proteica perinatal não altera a expressão de c\-Fos em áreas de controle hedônico do comportamento alimentar em ratos neonatos machos](../publications/ce4dcb655728cb75400b.md)

Elton Gabriel Fernandes de Brito; Emily Pereira de Souza; Thays Kallyne Marinho de Souza; Taisy Cinthia Ferro Cavalcante; Amanda Alves Marcelino da Silva

A desnutrição proteica perinatal altera os mecanismos neurais que controlam o comportamento alimentar, modificando os padrões de consumo de alimentos\. Estímulos de controle hedônico sobrepõem\-se à regulação homeostática, aumentando a ingestão alimentar e a duração das refeições\. A serotonina é um importante modulador da saciedade, e a fenfluramina, uma sonda farmacológica liberadora de serotonina, foi utilizada aqui para avaliar a responsividade funcional de circuitos\-alvo serotonérgicos no controle hedônico da alimentação\. Este estudo avaliou o efeito da desnutrição proteica perinatal sobre o número de células c\-Fos\-imunorreativas ativadas em áreas de controle hedônico do comportamento alimentar em ratos neonatos machos\. A análise imuno\-histoquímica foi utilizada para visualizar células nervosas imunorreativas à proteína Fos em áreas de controle hedônico após a administração aguda de fenfluramina \(3 mg/kg, s\.c\.\) em ratos neonatos machos de 18 dias de idade\. Não foram encontradas diferenças estatisticamente significativas entre os grupos no Caudado\-Putâmen \(p = 0,2071\) ou na Amígdala Central \(p = 0,5918\)\. No entanto, observou\-se diferença significativa na Amígdala Basolateral \(p = 0,0052\), com o grupo desnutrido\+salina apresentando expressão de c\-Fos acentuadamente elevada em relação ao controle\+salina, e a administração de fenfluramina reduziu essa ativação elevada nos animais desnutridos, aproximando\-a dos níveis do controle\. A desnutrição precoce não altera a ativação neuronal \(c\-Fos\) na maioria das áreas hedônicas avaliadas em ratos neonatos machos, mas aumenta significativamente a ativação basal e altera a responsividade à fenfluramina na Amígdala Basolateral, região crítica para o controle do consumo de alimentos palatáveis e para a integração entre as vias hedônica e homeostática\.

## [PREDIÇÃO DO FRACASSO ESCOLAR NO ENSINO SUPERIOR USANDO TÉCNICAS DE MINERAÇÃO DE DADOS: CASO DO INSTITUTO SUPERIOR POLITÉCNICO DO MOXICO](../publications/ce6c6c1f9cede1c953a0.md)

Felino Job Muacanhica; Solange Flora André Muacanhica

O fracasso escolar no ensino superior deriva de múltiplas variáveis ligadas ao perfil do estudante e ao ambiente de aprendizagem\. Este trabalho analisou dados de um estudo realizado no Instituto Superior Politécnico do Moxico, focando nos estudantes do 1\.º ano de Ciências de Computação, na disciplina de Lógica de Programação, com o objetivo de avaliar o desempenho discente mediante algoritmos de mineração de dados, identificando padrões preditivos de reprovação\. A pesquisa é de natureza qualitativa, descritiva e de pesquisa\-ação, envolveu 20 estudantes\. Os dados, obtidos por observação, análise documental, questionário e entrevista, foram processados no WEKA\. Compararam\-se cinco algoritmos de classificação \(J48, REPTree, NaiveBayes, SMO e Multilayer Perceptron\) através de validação cruzada de 10 partições\. O NaiveBayes destacou\-se com 90% de acurácia, classificando corretamente 18 das 20 instâncias\. A comparação pré e pós\-intervenção, baseada em 13 interações, revelou redução sistemática da percentagem predita de fracasso: valores iniciais entre 50% e 96% caíram para 1% a 68%\. A média recuou de 78,77% para 18,15%, uma variação de 60,62 pontos percentuais\. Os achados sublinham a utilidade da mineração de dados no mapeamento de riscos académicos e no monitoramento de tendências preditivas, ressalvando que o desenho do estudo não permite inferir causalidade direta entre as ações implementadas e a redução observada\.

## [PENGARUH AI SEBAGAI TUTOR ONLINE TERHADAP PEMAHAMAN MATERI DI MEDIASI OLEH LITERASI DIGITAL](../publications/ce790279323f257b9662.md)

Guntur Gunawan

The use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in learning is expanding rapidly; however, empirical evidence regarding the role of AI as an online tutor in supporting subject matter understanding through digital literacy remains limited\. This study aims to analyze the relationships between AI as an Online Tutor, Digital Literacy, and Subject Matter Understanding, as well as the mediating role of Digital Literacy\. An explanatory research design with a quantitative approach was employed\. Data were collected from 110 participants selected via random sampling from a population of 245 individuals\. The instrument comprised 11 indicators, and the data were analyzed using PLS\-SEM\. The results indicate that AI as an Online Tutor is positively associated with Digital Literacy \(β = 0\.725; p = 0\.000\) and Subject Matter Understanding \(β = 0\.426; p = 0\.000\)\. Digital Literacy is also positively associated with Subject Matter Understanding \(β = 0\.472; p = 0\.000\)\. Furthermore, Digital Literacy mediates the relationship between AI as an Online Tutor and Subject Matter Understanding \(β = 0\.343; p = 0\.000\)\. These findings demonstrate that AI as an online tutor supports Subject Matter Understanding both directly and through the enhancement of Digital Literacy\. The study underscores the importance of integrating AI usage with Digital Literacy development in learning, enabling learners to effectively leverage AI support to comprehend the material\.

## [Ponce, Hiram \(ed\.\): Towards a Unified Framework for Debugging Systems Requirements Specifications Translated Into ASP Logic Predicates](../publications/ce7be36efc71237a9952.md)



Ensuring consistency in system requirements is a critical challenge in systems engineering, particularly as updates introduce ambiguities or conflicts\. This paper presents a theoretical framework for a systems requirements debugger that processes and maintains logical representations of requirements\. Based on Knowledge Representation and Reasoning \(KRR\), the framework detects inconsistencies within static knowledge bases and manages conflicts arising from new information\. We propose methods for rapid prototyping in logic programming and optimization of Minimum Generalized Answer Sets \(MGAS\) in Abductive Logic Programming\. An online debugger prototype is introduced as a research and educational tool, offering a practical test bed for logic programming\. Using Answer Set Programming \(ASP\) solvers, we outline a declarative implementation that advances knowledge management and lays the groundwork for more sophisticated \(semi\)automatic debugging tools\.

## [Integrating Well Logs, Drilling Parameters, and Machine Learning for Subsurface Characterization of Volcanic Geothermal Rocks](../publications/ce7c480d45ad2926f90d.md)

Aliaa Hammoud; Marlène C\. Villeneuve; Eva Caspari

Abstract Characterizing subsurface rock properties in high\-temperature geothermal systems is challenging because extreme conditions often limit the availability and reliability of wireline, cuttings, and core data\. This study applies a data\-driven workflow to well THG13 in northeastern Iceland, combining objective\-driven preprocessing of wireline and drilling data with unsupervised machine learning to derive electrofacies associated with rock composition and relative porosity\. These electrofacies are then integrated with rate of penetration and weight on bit to investigate the mechanical response of volcanic units\. After minimizing operational effects, variations in drilling parameters reveal porosity\-related contrasts in rock strength and drillability\. The results demonstrate that integrating carefully processed wireline and drilling datasets can improve geological and mechanical characterization of volcanic geothermal reservoirs under data\-constrained conditions\.

## [Integration of natural deep eutectic solvent in a bulk liquid membrane system for tetracycline removal from wastewater](../publications/ce7e28a236b31b03c389.md)

Khalid M\. Abed; Bilal A\. Wasmi; Badoor M\. Kurji; Sunarti Abd Rahman; Adeeb Hayyan; Wan Jefrey Basirun; Jehad Saleh; Bhaskar Sen Gupta; M\. Zulhaziman M\. Salleh; Yousef Mohammed Alanazi

The presence of tetracycline \(TC\) in aquatic environments poses significant ecological and public health risks, requiring the development of effective and sustainable methods for its removal\. This research details the selective extraction and removal of TC from wastewater using natural deep eutectic solvent \(NADES\) with a bulk liquid membrane \(BLM\)\. NADES was synthesized through mixing thymol \(THY\), a hydrogen\-bond donor, and oleic acid \(OA\), a hydrogen\-bond acceptor, and was further utilized as a green carrier in the BLM system\. Extraction parameters, i\.e\., extraction time, NADES concentration, and mixing speed, were optimized via response surface methodology in order to maximize TC extraction and stripping efficiencies\. The conductor\-like screening model for real solvents \(COSMO\-RS\) was also utilized for the verification of TC removal, as well as for characterizing the molecular interactions\. Under the optimized conditions, the integrated NADES\-BLM system attained notable TC extraction and stripping efficiencies of 79\.4% and 78\.5%, respectively\. Moreover, the extraction efficiency was confirmed using COSMO\-RS molecular interactions, which was investigated through sigma profile and a sigma potential between the TC molecules and the system phases\. This research implies a novel green approach via utilizing NADES as a carrier in the BLM extraction system\.

## [Particle capture mechanism and friction\-reducing effect of vortex structures in continuous micro\-groove textures fabricated by ball\-end milling under lubricated conditions](../publications/ce8af2cb79ad3ebae784.md)

Weimin Huang; Yaoyao Shen; Guijie Wang; Jixin Yang; Zhenhao Xue; Xiaomeng Liu; Zixuan Wang

Abstract Surface texturing has been widely used to improve the performance of friction pairs\. However, existing studies have mainly focused on the role of texture geometry in wear\-debris storage, whereas the mechanisms by which the internal flow field of textures regulates particle migration, retention, and friction reduction remain unclear\.In this study, continuous micro\-groove textures were fabricated by ball\-end milling\.Fluent numerical simulations and reciprocating friction tests were conducted to systematically investigate the capture behavior of micrometer\-sized solid particles induced by vortex structures inside the micro\-grooves and their effects on the frictionreducing performance of the textured surface\. The results show that the local geometric expansion at the micro\-groove inlet induces a stable vortex, which governs particle entry, migration, and retention through shear\-layer entrainment and recirculating transport\. The introduced particles do not merely act as passively accommodated objects; instead, they modify the spatial scale of the vortex and the velocity\-gradient distribution near the groove opening through particle\-fluid momentum exchange\.When the particle diameter is 2 μm and the mass fraction is 0\.7%, the vortex inside the groove is moderately weakened, internal recirculation dissipation is reduced, and the hydrodynamic wedge effect is enhanced, resulting in a 5\.7% increase in the loadcarrying capacity of the oil film compared with the particle\-free condition\. The friction test results indicate that the coefficient of friction first decreases and then increases with increasing particle diameter, reaching its minimum at 2 μm\. This study clarifies the vortex\-dominated particle capture and friction\-reduction mechanism in continuous micro\-grooves, providing a theoretical basis for the design of textured surfaces and the optimization of particle\-containing lubrication systems\.

## [Biopolymer\-based coatings for egg preservation: recent advances, current challenges, and future prospects](../publications/ce9bf3c37c45fec3a2e8.md)

Dariush Khademi Shurmasti; Clara Mariana Gonçalves Lima; Renata Ferreira Santana; Nishant Kumar; Michelle Carlota Gonçalves; Renata Cristina Ferreira Bonomo; Henrique Douglas Melo Coutinho; Charles Odilichukwu R\. Okpala

Eggs, despite being globally consumed given their nutritional value, remain highly susceptible to storage quality challenges, from physicochemical changes, through microbial contamination, to oxidative deterioration\. Moreover, if sustainable preservation outcomes extending egg shelf life were to be steadily achieved, it would require continued literature syntheses about how internal quality and safety \(of egg shelf life\) are maintained\. To supplement existing information, this current review synthesizes biopolymer\-based coatings for egg preservation, from recent advances, through current challenges, to future research prospects\. Polysaccharide\- and protein\-based biopolymer matrices are established as important coating platforms for improving egg quality and shelf life\. Nanocomposite coatings incorporating nanofillers and natural bioactive compounds provide multifunctional barrier, mechanical, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties\. Such multifunctional coating systems can enhance preservation performance through combined mechanisms involving moisture regulation, controlled gas transfer, oxidative stabilization, microbial inhibition, and retention and gradual availability of active compounds\. Unlike previous reviews that largely dwelt on individual coating materials, the current review synergizes biopolymer matrices, nanocomposite reinforcement, bioactive functionalization, alongside emerging intelligent coating strategies\. Besides, consumer acceptance, manufacturing scalability, production cost, and regulatory compliance remain important considerations and potential barriers to commercialization\. However, if multifunctional, intelligent, and commercially viable coating technologies are to successfully enhance sustainable egg preservation, more efforts are required\. Overall, coating technology has progressed beyond simple protective barriers toward edible multifunctional preservation systems with promising potential to improve egg quality, safety, shelf life, and sustainability\.

## [Effects of record extension and statistical methods on dam reliability – insights from the Stronie Śląskie failure](../publications/ceaaacab6ea447b47185.md)

Łukasz Krysiak

This paper investigates the effects of methodological choices and the extension of hydrological records on extreme discharge estimates and dam safety, drawing on the 2024 failure of the century\-old Stronie Śląskie dam in Poland\. It is based on long\-term precipitation and discharge records from eight precipitation and seven gauging stations in the Biała Lądecka River basin \(in the Sudetes Mountains\) and neighbouring catchments\. To isolate the effects of record extension, three periods ending in 1984, 2023 and 2024 are analysed\. The series were tested for homogeneity, independence, stationarity and trends using a set of non\-parametric tests\. Extreme\-value distributions were fitted by maximum likelihood following two sets of Polish guidelines \(including the so\-called event alternative method\)\. Discharges at the ungauged dam cross\-section were estimated by regional regression and extrapolation\. No statistically significant monotonic trends were detected in hydrological data\. Nevertheless, extending the series – by 40 years or by a single flood event – led to substantial increases in design discharge for low exceedance probabilities, and wider confidence intervals\. The choice of probability distribution can change control flood estimates several\-fold and shift the dam’s overtopping probability from levels typical of high\-consequence structures to those below the lowest reliability class\. The results indicate that periodic hydrological re\-evaluation of existing dams is essential and that clearly defined methods for estimating extreme flows are needed to establish consistent safety targets and responsibilities and prompt timely spillway upgrades\.

## [Disinformasi Digital sebagai Ancaman Keamanan Non\-Tradisional: Konstruksi dan Kontestasi Narasi Laut China Selatan dalam Diplomasi Digital ASEAN](../publications/ceb4c94483b87f54a7f2.md)

## [PixelMap: A Browser\-Based Tool for Wiring\-Aware, Anatomy\- and Activity\-Guided Design of Neuropixels Channelmaps](../publications/ceb4fbe26c7564d0139f.md)

Maxime Beau; Julie MJ Fabre; Christian Tabedzki; Jorge Yanar; Carlos D\. Brody

PixelMap is a browser\-based application for designing custom channelmaps for Neuropixels probes while respecting electrode wiring constraints\.Neuropixels probes, widely used for high\-density neural recordings, have more physical electrodes than can be used for simultaneous recording because they contain fewer readout channels and analogue\-to\-digital converters \(ADCs\) than electrodes\.Each ADC and readout channel is hard\-wired to several electrodes, creating complex interdependencies where selecting one electrode makes others unavailable\.PixelMap provides an installation\-free, browser\-based interface for researchers to design arbitrary recording configurations that meet their experimental requirements while satisfying these hardware constraints\.Beyond constraint\-aware electrode selection, PixelMap supports two guided workflows: overlaying anatomical region boundaries from any BrainGlobe atlas to plan recordings around specific regions, and overlaying a SpikeGLX activity survey heatmap to identify the most active channels after implantation\.Both overlays can be used simultaneously during electrode selection\.PixelMap generates IMRO \(IMEC Read Out\) files compatible with SpikeGLX, the reference acquisition software for Neuropixels recordings\.

## [MC\-CRoMD: A Multi\-channel Statistical Feature Extraction and Selection Framework for Lung and Colon Histopathological Image Classification Using Machine and Deep Learning](../publications/cebc9a48f850f972ddad.md)

Mohammed Thajeel Abdullah; Raed Mohammed Hussein; Ashraf Sabri Waheed Alameri

This study introduces MC\-CRoMD, an interpretable statistical framework for lung and colon cancer histological image classification\.Images are divided into non\-overlapping 32×32, 64×64, 128×128, and 256×256 patches\.For each patch, Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha is used as a heuristic inter\-channel descriptor of shared spatial intensity variation among RGB channels\.Eight dispersion measures\-Range, Variance, Standard Deviation, Q1, Q3, IQR, MAD, and CV\-are extracted separately from each channel, yielding 24 channel\-wise features; together with Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha, each patch contains 25 features\.The LC25000 dataset was evaluated under binary, three\-class, and five\-class scenarios\.Six feature\-selection methods and the AllMsr baseline were assessed using nine machine\-learning models and a DNN\.Final configurations were selected using validation data and evaluated once on a locked independent test set\.The results imply that statistical descriptors, both inter\-channel and channel\-wise, may support the classification of LC25000 histopathological images\.

## [SEFRQO\-Plus: a self\-evolving query optimizer via large language models and retrieval\-augmented generation](../publications/cebe958ea99447bb1d12.md)

Hanwen Liu; Q\. Zhang; Ryan Marcus; Ibrahim Sabek

Abstract Query optimization is a crucial problem in database systems that has been studied for decades\. Learned query optimizers \(LQOs\) can improve performance over time by incorporating feedback; however, they suffer from cold\-start issues and often require retraining when workloads shift or schemas change\. We initially proposed SEFRQO, a Self\-Evolving Fine\-tuned RAG\-based Query Optimizer, which leverages fine\-tuned LLMs to address these challenges and uses in\-context learning to achieve continuous evolution\. However, its system design relies on the assumption of repetitive query workloads, requires executing queries statically upon their first encounter \(incurring extra overhead\), and utilizes only partial feedback from the best historical records \(insufficient feedback design\)\. In this paper, we present SEFRQO\-Plus, which resolves the above limitations\. First, we design a feedback\-oriented vector database with query structure\-aware embeddings to support effective similarity search, and we incorporate multi\-layered histories as references to enrich the feedback\. Then, we enhance the prompt optimization workflow by utilizing multi\-dimensional historical feedback to drive continuous self\-evolution\. Moreover, we provide formal theoretical proofs to validate the advantages of our customized query group relative policy optimization\. Evaluations show that SEFRQO\-Plus outperforms state\-of\-the\-art LQOs, achieving reductions of 66\.52% and 69\.79% in query latency for the complete CEB and Stack workloads, respectively, compared to PostgreSQL\. SEFRQO\-Plus achieves an additional 15% improvement over the initial SEFRQO\. Moreover, it generalizes effectively across multiple workloads and scenarios, and even across different DBMSes\.

## [Inteligencia artificial y pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de educación básica](../publications/cebed98985f587e7cc18.md)

Jesús Francisco Macías De la Cruz; Sandra Janneth Rivera Torres; Carlos Alberto Aldean\-Tumbaco; Adriana Pauleth Montoya Maya

La incorporación de herramientas de inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos plantea nuevas posibilidades para el aprendizaje, pero también interrogantes acerca de la manera en que los estudiantes valoran, contrastan y utilizan la información generada por estas tecnologías\. El presente estudio tiene como objetivo comprender cómo la interacción con herramientas de inteligencia artificial se relaciona con las experiencias y significados atribuidos al pensamiento crítico por estudiantes de educación primaria\. Se propone un estudio de caso cualitativo desarrollado en un contexto escolar de nivel primario, con una muestra intencional de entre 15 y 25 estudiantes\. La producción de información contempla entrevistas semiestructuradas, grupos focales y observación de actividades de aprendizaje mediadas por inteligencia artificial\. El análisis se desarrollará mediante procesos sucesivos de codificación abierta, axial y selectiva, complementados con triangulación de fuentes y técnicas\. El estudio prestará especial atención a las formas en que los estudiantes verifican información, reconocen errores, formulan preguntas, justifican decisiones y distinguen entre una respuesta generada automáticamente y una explicación que consideran confiable\. Se espera que el análisis permita comprender las condiciones pedagógicas bajo las cuales la inteligencia artificial puede funcionar como recurso para la indagación y no únicamente como mecanismo de obtención inmediata de respuestas\. La investigación busca aportar elementos para orientar prácticas docentes que incorporen inteligencia artificial de manera crítica, gradual y acorde con la edad de los estudiantes\.
