## [Growth Based on Education and Innovation: An AARDL Analysis for Türkiye](../publications/cec1ecb1b8bcbcbebac2.md)

Hüseyin COŞKUN

This study investigates the effects of education and innovation on economic growth in Türkiye using annual data from 1990 to 2023\. The stationarity of the variables was examined using the ADF and PP unit root tests\. The Bai\-Perron test was used to identify structural breaks, and breaks were detected in 2001 and 2008\. Cointegration between the variables was investigated using the AARDL model, and the existence of a cointegration relationship was determined\. Long\-term estimation results showed that capital, labor, education, and innovation positively affect economic growth\. Short\-term results showed that the innovation variable has a positive effect on economic growth\. Furthermore, the break years 2001 and 2008 included in the model were found to be statistically significant\. The results highlight the importance of education and innovation\-focused policies for sustainable economic growth\. They also indicate that innovation and education, which increase the productivity of labor and capital, can be important policy tools\. Alongside the basic growth factors, policies that improve education and innovation can increase the productivity of labor and capital, thus directly driving economic growth\.

## [Construction and validation of an intelligent pertussis identification model based on routine blood parameters and machine learning algorithms](../publications/cec3a36751efa9550f55.md)

Jing Yang; Siying Sun; Wenjing Deng; Jiao Xie; Xiaoqin Zeng; Xuelian Peng; Chunyan Yang; Baoru Han; Jin Li

Abstract Background Pertussis is a highly contagious respiratory disease whose early symptoms often resemble those of common respiratory tract infections, posing challenges for timely diagnosis\. This study aimed to develop machine learning models based on routine blood parameters and evaluate their discrimination between pertussis\-positive and symptomatic pertussis\-negative children, with an additional exploratory comparison against healthy controls\. Methods A total of 1132 paediatric cases were retrospectively collected from The Affiliated Dazu’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, including children with positive pertussis nucleic acid test results, symptomatic but pertussis\-negative cases, and healthy controls\. All cases had complete routine blood test results, covering 24 routine blood parameters\. Nine machine learning \(ML\) algorithms were evaluated in two separate binary classification tasks: pertussis\-positive versus symptomatic pertussis\-negative children, and pertussis\-positive children versus healthy controls\. Performance was assessed using seven assessment metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\)\. A separate temporal cohort was further used for calibration assessment\. The selected models were incorporated into a prototype webpage\. Results On the held\-out test set within the modelling subset, XGBoost achieved an accuracy of 0\.873 \(95% CI: 0\.836–0\.909\) and an F1 score of 0\.867 \(95% CI: 0\.828–0\.913\) for distinguishing pertussis\-positive from symptomatic pertussis\-negative cases\. For the exploratory positive\-versus\-healthy comparison, the CatBoost model achieved an accuracy of 0\.938 \(95% CI: 0\.918–0\.964\), an F1 score of 0\.932 \(95% CI: 0\.908–0\.962\), and an AUC value of 0\.988 \(95% CI: 0\.975\-1\.000\)\. SHAP analysis identified that Baso%, Mono\#, and CRP exerted the most significant influence as the leading features in the CatBoost positive\-versus\-healthy model, and Eos\#, Mono%, and PCT \(plateletcrit\) as the leading features in the XGBoost positive\-versus\-negative model\. Conclusions Machine learning models based on routine blood parameters demonstrated the ability to discriminate between pertussis\-positive and symptomatic pertussis\-negative children\. The additional positive\-versus\-healthy comparison provided exploratory evidence of discrimination between pertussis cases and healthy controls\. These findings highlight the potential value of routine blood parameters for machine learning\-assisted pertussis identification\.

## [Analysis of post\-adoption behaviors of climate change adaptation strategies among smallholder farmers: Evidence from Burkina Fa\-so](../publications/cec55dbcc3c25ee34a37.md)

Henri Zoungrana; Lwungili Justin Bationo; Kale Julienne MILLOGO1 MILLOGO; Coffie Francis José N’Guessan; Omer Souglimpo Combary

Enhancing long\-term adaptation to climate change in developing countries requires an under\-standing of farmers’ post\-adoption behaviors\. This study examines the factors influencing post\-adoption decisions, namely substitution, maintenance, combination, and abandonment, across soil and water conservation techniques \(SWCTs\), agroforestry, crop associations, and improved seed varieties in climate\-vulnerable contexts\. Using a multinomial logit model with sample\-selection bi\-as correction and data from the Permanent Agricultural Survey covering 13,030 farmers in Burkina Faso from 2015 to 2019, the findings reveal that men are more likely to maintain, substitute, or combine SWCTs, agroforestry, and crop associations rather than abandon them, while age and education exhibit practice\-specific effects\. Land ownership, labor availability, farm size, and external support are associated with greater continuation, substitution, or combination for several practices rather than abandonment\. Climatic shocks also generate differentiated responses, with drought increasing the likelihood of SWCT abandonment, while crop associations are less likely to be abandoned in Sahelian and Sahelo\-Sahelian zones\. These findings highlight the need for post\-adoption policies that complement initial adoption support through tailored extension services, improved access to productive resources and institutional support, and geographically and climatically differentiated interventions to sustain and adjust existing adaptation strategies\.

## [THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE ON THE DIAGNOSTIC DECISIONS OF DENTAL STUDENTS IN CARIES DETECTION](../publications/ced0f6111ca66a9d6cb3.md)

Razhabzoda Parvina Hakimovna; Fayzullayeva Shaxrizoda Erkin qizi

The integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) into dental diagnostics has emerged as a transformative development in dental education\. This study investigates the impact of AI assistance on the clinical and radiographic diagnostic decisions of dental students during dental caries detection\. While traditional training relies heavily on visual\-tactile metrics and conventional radiographic interpretation, AI systems utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\) offer a standardized, data\-driven second opinion\. Current literature suggests that AI assistance substantially improves students&\#x27; diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity, particularly in identifying early enamel and proximal carious lesions\. Furthermore, AI tools reduce diagnostic time and enhance student confidence\. However, concerns regarding automation bias, potential false positives, and a deficiency in structured curricula persist\. This paper outlines the mechanisms, educational benefits, limitations, and future outlook of implementing AI in dental diagnostics training\.

## [VISTA as a tumour\-microenvironment checkpoint: spatial, metabolic and cellular control of antitumour immunity](../publications/ced6d8c5c8dbce824ed5.md)

Kexun Li; Zilong Qian; Jianzhe Zhang; Jie Mao; Tengfei Ke

V\-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T\-cell activation \(VISTA; also termed VSIR, PD\-1H or B7\-H5\) is increasingly recognised as an immune checkpoint whose biological and clinical significance depends less on total expression than on the tumour microenvironment \(TME\) in which it operates\. Rather than acting as a linear T\-cell exhaustion receptor, VISTA integrates tumour chemistry, stromal architecture, innate and adaptive immune states, and therapy\-induced feedback inhibition\. It is expressed by tumour cells and multiple immune populations, including macrophages, myeloid\-derived suppressor cells, dendritic cells, neutrophils, regulatory T cells and activated or quiescent T cells\. VISTA can also function through pH\-dependent and pH\-independent ligand\-receptor interactions\. This review reframes VISTA as a TME\-gated regulatory system\. Low pH, hypoxia, transforming growth factor beta \(TGF\-β\), histamine, aldehyde metabolism, Yes\-associated protein \(YAP\)/TEA domain \(TEAD\) signalling, macrophage polarity, antigen\-presenting\-cell fitness and spatial immune exclusion can jointly determine whether VISTA marks immune resistance, immune activation under feedback restraint or tumour\-cell\-intrinsic evasion\. This context helps explain the divergent prognostic associations of VISTA across pancreatic, gastric, colorectal, lung, breast, bladder, gynaecological, skin, brain, mesothelial and haematological malignancies\. Therapeutically, VISTA should therefore not be treated as another universal immune\-checkpoint target\. More plausible strategies include pH\-selective antibodies, ligand\-axis disruption, local or nanoparticle delivery, targeted degradation, tumour\-cell\-intrinsic pathway inhibition and combinations that convert suppressive TME niches into antigen\-presenting and cytotoxic niches\. A TME\-centred framework can make VISTA biology clinically interpretable and guide biomarker development, trial design and rational combination immunotherapy\.

## [OPTIMASI MODEL SMART GREEN MARKETING BERBASIS MEDIA SOSIAL GUNA MENINGKATKAN DAYA SAING UMKM KERIPIK SINGKONG DI KABUPATEN KARANGANYAR](../publications/cedda6255bd693ae9ca0.md)

Giyono; Savitri; Giarti Slamet

Cassava chip MSMEs in Karanganyar face challenges in balancing digitalization with sustainability\. The use of social media for &quot;Smart Green Marketing&quot; has not yet optimally communicated eco\-friendly values\. This study aims to optimize this marketing model by integrating variables such as loyalty, brand, trust, and customer satisfaction using the Structural Equation Modeling \(SEM\-PLS\) method\. The results indicate that social media platforms like WhatsApp Business, when supported by high product quality, are effective in building consumer satisfaction and loyalty\. Satisfaction and an environmentally\-oriented brand image were proven to reinforce repurchase decisions\. The resulting optimization model establishes that product quality, price, and green value contribute directly to satisfaction, brand image, and digital trust, ultimately leading to customer loyalty\. Despite having broad market opportunities, these MSMEs are constrained by limitations in content creation capacity and digital marketing skills; therefore, strategic guidance is essential to strengthen their sustainable competitiveness\. Keywords: Green marketing; MSMEs; SEM; optimization; cassava chips

## [Identification and validation of potential biomarkers related to oxidative stress and inflammation in ischemic stroke](../publications/cede05afbdb64bb46e3e.md)

Jun He; Yuan Feng; Jian Wang; Mingwu Xia

Previous studies speculated that oxidative stress and inflammation might affect the pathogenesis of ischemic stroke \(IS\)\. This study explored the utility of oxidative stress \(OS\)\-related genes \(OSRGs\) and inflammation\-related genes \(IRGs\) in IS\. IS and control samples were downloaded from public databases, and IRGs and OSRGs were obtained from previous research\. The differentially expressed genes \(DEGs\) between the IS and control groups were identified by differential expression analysis\. Subsequently, candidate genes were identified utilizing the intersection of DEGs, IRGs, and OSRGs\. Then, machine learning algorithms and gene expression verification were utilized to obtain potential biomarkers\. Furthermore, a nomogram was constructed, and gene set enrichment analysis \(GSEA\) was performed\. Molecular regulatory network construction, drug prediction, and molecular docking were subsequently performed\. Finally, the expression of the potential biomarkers in clinical samples was evaluated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction \(RT\-qPCR\), and a mouse single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\) dataset was used as a complementary exploratory analysis to examine their cell type\-specific expression patterns and identify candidate cell populations potentially associated with IS\. In total, 596 DEGs were identified, and 6 candidate genes were highlighted\. Ultimately, TNFSF10 , TLR2 , ADM , ABCA1 , and HIF1A were obtained as potential biomarkers\. The nomogram had good predictive ability for IS\. The GSEA results illustrated that all potential biomarkers excluding HIF1A were enriched in complement and coagulation cascades\. The molecular regulatory network included 146 transcription factors, such as MYC \. The microRNAs related to potential biomarkers included miR\-6809\-3p and miR\-1276\. Moreover, the drugs with high affinity for the potential biomarkers included diprovocim\-1 and trichostatin A\. Finally, the RT\-qPCR results were consistent with the bioinformatic findings, while analysis of the mouse scRNA\-seq dataset suggested that microglia and central nervous system\-associated macrophages \(CAMs\) may represent candidate cell populations associated with the identified biomarkers\. This study identified five potential biomarkers \( TNFSF10 , TLR2 , ADM , ABCA1 , and HIF1A \) with potentially significant effects on IS\.

## [Thrombectomy improves functional outcome in large core stroke partly by preventing severe cerebral edema: a real\-world mediation analysis](../publications/cee968c798c075f6edf8.md)

Thiện Quang Lê; Son Van Dang Nguyen; Tuan Phuoc Pham; Tao Tran; Trung Quoc Nguyen; Alexander Thomas Yahanda; Adam Andrew Dmytriw; Vu Thanh Huynh; Hai Quang Duong; Thanh N\. Nguyen; Nhan Duc Le

Objective Endovascular thrombectomy \(EVT\) is effective in large infarct core \(LIC\) stroke, but mortality and severe disability remain high when cerebral edema \(CED\) develops\. We assessed the effect of EVT on CED and outcomes in LIC patients within 24 h of stroke onset\. Methods In a prospective observational cohort study, we enrolled patients with large\-vessel occlusion in the anterior circulation, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale \(NIHSS\) score ≥ 6, Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score \(ASPECTS\) ≤ 5, and admission within 24 h of onset\. The primary outcome was mass effect \(ME\) due to severe cerebral edema, defined as a maximum midline shift \(MLS\) ≥ 5 mm on follow\-up imaging within 72 h\. The secondary outcome was favorable outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale \(mRS\) score of 0–3 at 90 days\. Safety outcomes were determined by death at 90 days, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage \(sICH\) according to SITS\-MOST criteria\. Treatment effects were estimated using inverse probability of treatment weighting \(IPTW\) with doubly robust adjustment\. Mediation analysis assessed whether ME contributed to the association between EVT and favorable outcome\. Results Of 202 patients \(EVT group: 119; medical management group: 83\), after IPTW adjustment, EVT was associated with lower odds of ME \[31\.1% vs\. 51\.8%; IPTW\-adjusted odds ratio \(aOR\), 0\.28; 95% CI, 0\.12–0\.67\], higher odds of favorable outcome \(aOR, 2\.32; 95% CI, 1\.01–5\.31\), and lower mortality \(aOR 0\.45; 95% CI, 0\.21–0\.97\) with no excess sICH\. ME independently predicted poor outcome \(aOR for mRS 4–6, 7\.7; 95% CI, 3\.01–19\.69\), and approximately 29\.5% of the association between EVT and favorable outcome was statistically mediated by ME attenuation\. Two admission variables—lower baseline ASPECTS and higher admission glucose—independently predicted ME \(optimism\-corrected AUC 0\.82\)\. Conclusion In large\-core stroke, EVT was associated with better functional outcome and lower odds of mass effect\. Approximately one\-third of EVT&\#x27;s functional benefit was statistically mediated by attenuation of severe CED\. ME independently predicted poor outcome, whereas lower ASPECTS and higher admission glucose identified patients at greater risk of severe swelling, supporting bedside risk stratification to guide intensified monitoring and edema\-targeted management\. Trial registration ClinicalTrials\.gov , Identifier \[NCT06016348\]\.

## [An interpretable hierarchical deep learning framework for lung and colon cancer detection](../publications/cf024429d91d16e71a44.md)

Md\. Alamin Talukder; Reza Rafeh; Nam H\. Chu; Md\. Ashraf Uddin

Abstract Accurate and interpretable classification of lung and colon cancer from histopathological images remains challenging because of substantial inter\-class similarities, morphological heterogeneity, and the limited transparency of conventional deep learning \(DL\) models\. Most existing methods treat the problem as a flat multiclass classification task, requiring a single model to distinguish normal tissue and multiple cancer subtypes simultaneously\. In this study, we propose an interpretable hierarchical DL framework that decomposes the five\-class classification problem into clinically motivated coarse\-to\-fine decision stages\. The framework initially separates normal tissue from cancerous tissue and then directs each sample to a specialized classifier for either normal tissue categorization or cancer subtype identification\. Candidate DL architectures are independently evaluated at each stage, allowing the most suitable model to be selected for each specific classification task\. The framework is evaluated on the LC25000 benchmark and further assessed on the independent LungHist700 dataset, which presents a distinct evaluation setting with different image characteristics and class distributions\. The proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 98\.50% on LC25000 and 82\.01% on LungHist700\. To improve model transparency, Grad\-CAM, Grad\-CAM\+\+, LIME, and Occlusion Sensitivity are employed to highlight the image regions that contribute to the hierarchical predictions\. The results show that the framework combines strong classification performance with a structured coarse\-to\-fine decision process and complementary interpretability techniques\. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of hierarchical decision decomposition and explainable DL to provide a more transparent and task\-specific approach to computer\-aided histopathological cancer classification, particularly for distinguishing normal tissue from lung and colon cancer subtypes\.

## [Evolution of Architectural Design: A Historical Analysis of the Rivers State Government House from Independence to Present](../publications/cf04bced438f3e314f6d.md)

C\. C\. Kalagbor

The architectural transformation of the Rivers State Government House serves as a lens for examining the interplay between political authority, historical influence, and cultural identity in Nigeria\. This study traces the evolution of its design from colonial\-era structures to modern government complexes, analysing how governance, modernisation, and external architectural trends have shaped its development\. Using a qualitative case study approach, data was collected through semi\-structured interviews, direct observations, and archival research\. Findings reveal that while successive administrations have modified the building to reflect changing priorities of governance, it remains largely influenced by Western architectural styles, with minimal incorporation of indigenous Nigerian elements\. The study highlights the role of government buildings as both a functional and symbolic expression of power, economic capacity, and state identity\. To foster greater cultural representation, the study recommends integrating indigenous motifs, engaging local architects, and balancing modernisation with heritage preservation in in the government buildings\.

## [Fan, Ning: Solving the puzzle of forever fitting emotions: justifying and requiring reasons](../publications/cf04c8eda39dc45408c1.md)



\_Philosophical Studies\_\. forthcomingFacts that make emotions like regret, grief, and gratitude fitting provide reasons for those emotions\. These reasons typically persist, yet we do not always experience the emotions themselves—we often cease to feel them, and this absence seems permissible\. This raises the puzzle of “forever fitting emotions”: why can we permissibly fail to have emotions even when the reasons remain? This paper examines this puzzle and proposes a solution to it\. Central to my approach is distinguishing two roles that normative reasons can play: they can justify a response or, more strongly, require it\. Crucially, I argue that responding to a reason—by having the emotion or performing its expressive actions—can diminish its requiring strength, explaining why one may permissibly fail to maintain an emotion even when the reason persists\. \(direct link \)

## [Reconciling Global Data\-Centre Electricity Projections for 2030: A Boundary\-Aware Evidence Map](../publications/cf07f38ec40e82fb71ac.md)

Aditya Singh

Background: Published projections of global data\-centre electricity use are frequently compared despite differences in geography, facility and workload coverage, units, and scenario design\. Methods: We constructed a secondary\-source\-seeded, boundary\-aware evidence map of projections for annual global operational electricity use by total data centres in 2030\. Each publication was coded across eight comparability dimensions and assigned a transparent primary\-source verification status\. The primary synthesis treats publications reporting only range endpoints as interval\-censored rather than interpreting their endpoints as complete scenarios\. Publication\-level bootstrap intervals and verification, peer\-review, scenario\-completeness, aggregation, and influence sensitivities were examined\. Results: The corpus contains 28 values from 15 publications; 7 were directly checked in primary or author full text by one reviewer and 8 remain verification incomplete\. The interval\-censored model estimates a median latent publication centre of 912 TWh yr\-1 \(95% publication\-bootstrap interval 712\-1217\) and a geometric standard deviation of 1\.69\. A conventional geometric\-scenario summary gives a median of 945 TWh yr\-1 \(interquartile range 648\-1167\)\. Method, publisher, and vintage contrasts are imprecise and are retained only as exploratory sensitivities\. Conclusions: Boundary harmonisation makes the literature more interpretable but does not identify a probability distribution for realised 2030 demand\. The principal contribution is an auditable comparability taxonomy and minimum reporting standard, not a consensus forecast\.

## [PEMBERDAYAAN UMKM PURNA PEKERJA MIGRAN INDONESIA MELALUI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UNTUK PENGUATAN BRANDING DI DESA WALIWIS](../publications/cf13e0cfb8acedf31635.md)

Andi Hasryningsih Asfar; Muhammad Irfan Tegar Algifari; Gilang Yudha Pratama; Muhammad Ridho; Muhammad Fatur Rahman; Dzaky Hasan Eka Putra Agusthian; Dandy Putra Ramadhan

Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah \(UMKM\) memiliki peran penting dalam penguatan ekonomi masyarakat, namun pelaku UMKM masih menghadapi kendala dalam membangun identitas produk dan memanfaatkan teknologi digital untuk memperluas pengenalan produk\. Kondisi tersebut juga dihadapi oleh pelaku UMKM Purna Pekerja Migran Indonesia \(PMI\) di Desa Waliwis, Kecamatan Mekar Baru, Kabupaten Tangerang\. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat \(PkM\) ini bertujuan memberikan pendampingan kepada pelaku UMKM Purna PMI dalam memanfaatkan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) sebagai alat bantu pengembangan branding produk\. Kegiatan melibatkan 30 pelaku UMKM dan dilaksanakan melalui tahapan identifikasi kebutuhan, sosialisasi, demonstrasi, praktik, dan pendampingan pengembangan identitas visual produk\. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan partisipatif dengan melibatkan peserta secara langsung dalam mengeksplorasi ide, mengembangkan konsep desain, dan menerapkan elemen branding sesuai karakteristik produk\. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya capaian praktis berupa pengembangan konsep identitas visual dan label produk UMKM\. Salah satu output pendampingan berupa pengembangan label produk Keripik Pisang Ibu Rumah Tangga yang dipersiapkan untuk diterapkan pada kemasan produk\. Peserta juga memperoleh pengalaman praktis dalam memanfaatkan AI untuk mengeksplorasi konsep visual dan mendukung pengembangan branding produk\. Evaluasi kegiatan dilakukan secara deskriptif berdasarkan keterlibatan peserta, proses praktik, dokumentasi kegiatan, dan output branding yang dihasilkan\. Kegiatan ini menunjukkan bahwa sosialisasi dan pendampingan pemanfaatan AI dapat menjadi alternatif praktis untuk membantu pelaku UMKM Purna PMI memperkuat identitas produk serta menjadi langkah awal dalam meningkatkan kesiapan mereka menghadapi pemasaran di era digital\.

## [Cultivating a Culturally Relevant and Inclusive Elementary Music Classroom](../publications/cf1a6ac48b7772994c31.md)

Elisabeth Virginia Marie Buzzell

While programs such as the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Act \(DEI\) and the practice of Culturally Responsive Education \(CRE\) existed for much of the last decade, representation of marginalized and intersectional identities in traditional music education is often limited to world culture units, rather than being consistently integrated throughout the curriculum\. The social understanding of CRE and DEI often limits their purpose to racial diversity; however, these philosophies affirm people from any marginalized class, including those based on gender, disability, race, culture, community, orientation, socioeconomics, or simply bringing one’s lived experiences into a valued perspective\. The lack of integration happens regardless of the cultural makeup of the community a teacher serves\. This study explores phenomenology to examine culturally responsive music education \(CRME\) in music teachers’ educational experience and how they address representation within their programs\. This study employed a phenomenological approach to analyzing music teachers’ experiences with diversity and inclusion in music education\. The findings of this study may provide insights into how music educators navigate representation within their programs\. Clarity and intentional application of CRE in music classes may better support student development\. Ultimately, this study may bridge the concept of CRE to what teachers have naturally done in their classes, contribute to the ongoing dialogue about the importance of inclusive curricula, and offer strategies for intentional practices within the field\.

## [From research to clinical practice: Expert consensus on Neuroimaging AI tools for the Memory clinic \(Neuro\-AIM\)](../publications/cf1b77b55ea4d4b9df60.md)

Natasha Clarke; Mathias Huybrechts; Jay Amin; Lewis Hotchkiss; James Leighs; Matthew Leming; Usman Saeed; Catherine J Scott; Dirk Smeets; Angela Tam; Stefano Tamburin; Geert Vanhooren; Meike Willemijn Vernooij; Jennifer Camaradou; David J\. Llewellyn; Timothy Rittman; Rose Bruffaerts

Abstract Although AI tools for neuroimaging show considerable promise in the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of neurodegenerative disorders, their uptake in memory clinics has been limited\. A key barrier is lack of consensus on their effective design and implementation\. Here we establish expert consensus on the specific goals, usage and challenges of AI tools for neuroimaging in the memory clinic using a Delphi process\. Sixteen experts from clinical, academic, and industry backgrounds participated in three rounds of questionnaires, coordinated by the Imaging Working Group of the Deep Dementia Phenotyping \(DEMON\) network, with support from a patient and public involvement representative\. Consensus was reached on eight statements covering four themes: purpose, quality, interactions with clinicians and memory clinics, and privacy and ethics\. Implementation of these recommendations will further the adoption of AI neuroimaging tools from research to clinical practice, improving diagnostic and care pathways for patient benefit\.

## [Enterprise Architecture Risk Management Framework](../publications/cf1e5fa03f1092fbc994.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

Enterprise transformation creates architecture risks that may not be visible through traditional project or operational risk processes\. Fragmented applications, unsupported technologies, weak integration, inconsistent data, cloud misconfiguration, architectural debt, vendor concentration, inadequate resilience, and uncontrolled Artificial Intelligence can create systemic exposure across the enterprise\. This paper proposes an Enterprise Architecture Risk Management Framework that integrates architecture governance with enterprise risk management\. The framework defines risk domains, architecture risk identification, scoring, risk appetite, control mapping, exception governance, remediation planning, portfolio aggregation, continuous monitoring, and executive reporting\. It covers business architecture, applications, data, integration, cloud, infrastructure, security, resilience, AI, and third\-party dependencies\. The framework also introduces architecture risk indicators, heat maps, risk\-based review intensity, and lifecycle monitoring\. The proposed approach enables organizations to identify systemic technology and design risks earlier, prioritize remediation, reduce technical debt, and align architecture decisions with enterprise risk tolerance and strategic objectives\.

## [RULE\-BASED ENERGY MANAGEMENT OF A STANDALONE PV\-BATTERY SYSTEM UNDER ONE\-MONTH SOLAR RESOURCE VARIABILITY: A CASE STUDY IN SENEGAL](../publications/cf216ebb7cc0580f6376.md)

Souleymane Soumah; Mouhamadou Falilou Ndiaye; Mohamed Ansoumane Camara; Mohamed Lamine TOURE; Kadiatou Aissatou Barry; Vincent Sambou

Energy management is a key factor in the reliability and performance of photovoltaic \(PV\) systems coupled with battery storage for rural electrification\. Unlike studies based on representative days, this work investigates the operation of a PV–battery system over a continuous 28\-day period \(672 h\) to assess the influence of day\-to\-day weather variations on its behaviour\. The system consists of a 36\.6 kWp PV generator, a battery storage system \(648 Ah, 200 V\), and a bidirectional buck–boost converter exchanging energy between the DC bus and the batteries\. Simulations were carried out in MATLAB/Simulink using hourly solar irradiation and temperature profiles measured in Senegal in February 2005, and a domestic load profile\. Maximum power point tracking is performed with the incremental conductance algorithm, while a PI controller maintains the DC bus voltage at its 395 V reference\. A rule\-based energy management strategy coordinates PV generation, storage and load supply according to the instantaneous power balance and the battery state of charge \(SOC\)\. Results show that the DC bus voltage remains globally close to its reference despite fluctuations in solar irradiation, apart from a transient drop to about 260 V around 275 h\. The battery SOC stays close to 50% over the whole month, indicating stable operation of the strategy under the simulated conditions\. This study provides a basis for analysing the sizing and operation of PV–battery systems in the sub\-Saharan African context\.

## [Heterophily‐Aware Motif‐Guided Contrastive Learning for Robust Social Recommendation](../publications/cf22ef966b71b9e34858.md)

Yinghe Wang; Yuan\-Kun Xu; Chulei Xiang

ABSTRACT The homophily principle serves as the core foundation of graph neural network \(GNN\) based social recommendation, which assumes socially connected users share similar preferences and enables neighbourhood aggregation for user representation learning\. Most existing methods directly aggregate information from original social graphs, but this strategy is severely suboptimal due to the prevalent low preference‐aware homophily in real‐world social networks\. We further reveal that nonpreference‐driven social connections introduce massive noise into GNN aggregation, leading to representation degradation, over‐smoothing and even performance decline\. Existing efforts mostly focus on individual subproblems of social denoising, high‐order modelling or representation enhancement and fail to provide a systematic solution for these cascading challenges\. In this paper, we propose H2Rec, a heterophily‐aware motif‐guided contrastive learning framework for low‐homophily social recommendation\. It integrates a dual‐branch social aggregation module, a homophily‐enhanced contrastive alignment objective and a user‐adaptive fusion mechanism to suppress noise and learn robust user representations end‐to‐end\. Extensive experiments on real‐world benchmarks show that H2Rec significantly outperforms state‐of‐the‐art methods on mainstream evaluation metrics\.

## [Assessing the overheating resilience of a novel earth walled \(CobBauge\) building across different climate zones in Europe using a calibrated building performance simulation model](../publications/cf298748c0054726c6a6.md)

Halat Alnaqshabandy; Matthew Fox; Steve Goodhew

CobBauge is a dual\-layer earthen construction material, optimized to meet Part\-L of the Building Regulations in England and Wales\. A classroom constructed with CobBauge demonstrated high resilience to overheating during two heatwaves in Plymouth, highlighting its potential as a sustainable and ultra\-low\-carbon material\. This study assesses its overheating resilience using a simulation model, calibrated to achieve 7\.30% CV\(RMSE\) and 1\.34°C RMSE against measured indoor temperatures\. Plymouth&\#x27;s future climate and nine European locations representing different Köppen climate classifications were incorporated into the model to analyse the building&\#x27;s thermal performance and its compliance with CIBSE TM52 criteria\. Results showed no overheating risk under Plymouth&\#x27;s future climate\. Similar performance was observed across all European locations except Murcia, where outdoor temperatures reached 42°C\. Nevertheless, indoor temperatures remained 9°C below outdoor peaks without active cooling\. This study recommends CobBauge as an ultra\-low\-carbon and resilient material to mitigate indoor overheating across diverse European climates\.

## [A Combined Network Toxicology and Docking Study to Identify Putative Molecular Targets Linking Styrene Exposure to Atherosclerosis](../publications/cf36daa631707d7808bf.md)

Shuai Yan; Geng Shen; Yu\-Qing Huang; HE Guo\-dong

Background: Styrene is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound linked to hematologic and vascular alterations; however, the molecular mechanisms connecting exposure to atherosclerosis remain poorly characterized\. Methods: We integrated peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic profiles \(GSE23746\) with toxicogenomic data from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, applying support vector machine recursive feature elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator machine learning algorithms to identify core targets at the styrene\-atherosclerosis intersection\. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT and single\-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and molecular docking evaluated binding potential\. results: Four model genes—CCND3, CCR1, MYC, and MYD88—were identified and constituted a diagnostic signature with high accuracy \(area under the curve &gt; 0\.9\)\. These genes were enriched in IL\-17 and NF\-κB inflammatory pathways and correlated with distinct immune cell alterations, particularly mast cells and T cell subsets\. Molecular docking revealed direct, moderate binding of styrene to CCND3\. Results: Four model genes—CCND3, CCR1, MYC, and MYD88—were identified and constituted a diagnostic signature with high accuracy \(area under the curve &gt; 0\.9\)\. These genes were enriched in IL\-17 and NF\-κB inflammatory pathways and correlated with distinct immune cell alterations, particularly neutrophils and T cell subsets\. Molecular docking predicted direct, moderate\-affinity binding of styrene to CCND3 \(Vina score = −6\.4 kcal/mol\), involving multiple contacts within the cyclin domain\. Discussion: The convergence of transcriptomic screening and molecular docking identifies CCND3 as a putative target for styrene\-protein interaction and suggests a mechanistic hypothesis linking styrene to atherosclerosis via inflammatory and immune dysregulation\. The computational framework provides a basis for future experimental validation\. Conclusion: This computational framework generates the hypothesis that styrene may contribute to atherosclerosis through coordinated perturbations of immune signaling and cell cycle regulation, with CCND3 representing a candidate molecular target for future experimental validation in styrene\-exposed populations\.

## [Faster but Not Truer, Part 2: The Regulatory Record, the Economics, and the TRACE\-HEOR Reporting Standard](../publications/cf403f5cff14201c3211.md)

Onur Başer

Background: Part 1 of this series found that measured gains from artificial intelligence \(AI\) in health economics and outcomes research \(HEOR\) concentrate in tasks with observable ground truth and disappear where the quantity of interest is a counterfactual\. What regulators, health technology assessment \(HTA\) bodies, and sponsors have said about that division has not been assembled in one place\. Methods: We assembled the primary regulatory, HTA, industry, and journal policy record through September 2026, requiring for each claim a named primary source and, where a quantity was reported, its provenance and whether the reporting party had a commercial interest\. We downloaded the Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\) AI\-enabled medical device list in full, tabulated published economic evaluations of AI, and set reported industry efficiency gains against disclosed use in submissions\. We then evaluated the field against the task\-based productivity framework of Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu and derived a reporting standard from the documented failure modes\. Results: The FDA has authorized 1614 AI\-enabled devices, 1230 \(76\.2%\) in radiology, rising from 18 in 2016 to 335 in 2025, and has received more than 500 drug and biologic submissions containing AI components since 2016; its January 2025 credibility assessment guidance remains a draft and excludes discovery and operational uses\. Industry sources report time savings of 40% to 97% in regulatory writing and approximately 80% in payer dossier drafting, but every one of these figures comes from a single\-arm comparison without a concurrent control and was reported by the company that deployed or sold the tool\. AI use was disclosed in 3 of 1391 HTA documents \(0\.2%\) and 0\.6% of one journal&\#x27;s submissions, against surveys reporting use between 25% and 81%\. Nineteen economic evaluations of AI have been published against 1614 authorized devices\. No regulator or HTA body has been documented accepting or rejecting an AI\-derived endpoint as such\. Conclusions: Current disclosure instruments ask whether AI wrote the text\. Reviewers need to know whether AI selected the evidence, defined the cohort, derived the endpoint, or generated the code, and whether the recommendation would change without it\.

## [SiAman EduBot: Inovasi AI untuk Pelaporan Insiden dan Edukasi Keselamatan Pasien Dalam Satu Platform Digital\.](../publications/cf5c3a2f91d79099dba3.md)

Ronald Winardi Kartika; Sarwoko SITANALA

RSUP dr\. Sitanala is committed to strengthening patient safety culture toward a smart hospital paradigm through an artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-driven innovation named Si Aman EduBot\. This interactive chatbot, integrated via WhatsApp and the hospital&\#x27;s proprietary application, was developed to provide real\-time education on safety standards, emergency procedures, and digital incident reporting systems for both staff and patients\. This study aims to evaluate the impact of Si Aman EduBot implementation on enhancing safety culture within the hospital environment\. The evaluation results over a three\-month period demonstrated significant achievements, including over 5,000 user interactions, a 35% increase in incident reporting volume, and a 20% improvement in patient safety culture scores from the baseline\. The rapid and responsive nature of the chatbot proved effective in increasing staff awareness and fostering an open, blame\-free reporting culture\. Through its interactive educational features and digital system integration, Si Aman EduBot holds the potential to serve as a national model for building a sustainable patient safety culture\. Future developments will focus on integrating voice assistant capabilities and electronic medical records\. Keywords: Patient Safety, Educational Chatbot, Digital Incident Reporting, Blame\-Free Culture\.

## [Data Labeling with Local and Global Consistency Using Phylograms](../publications/cf6088bfb53e747d478a.md)

Breno Caetano da Silva; Jorge Luiz Franco; Hermes Manoel Galvão Castelo Branco; Alexandre C\. B\. Delbem

One of the main challenges in machine learning tasks is unlabeled data\. Consequently, semi\-supervised learning is an approach commonly used in labeling data tasks\. The use of diffusion kernels is one of the powerful methods in this set of learning\. This paper introduces Phylogram based Data Labeling \(PhyDL\), an innovative method that combines the benefits of phylogram analysis with Learning with Local and Global Consistency \(LLGC\)\. PhyDL leverages phylogram analysis to act as an aggregator of information from labeled samples, capable of correcting possible labeling errors\. PhyDL constructs a phylogram using community detection algorithms, FastGreedy and Edge Betweenness, to identify and leverage the structure of the data, with FastGreedy emerging as the best\-performing algorithm among those evaluated\. We implemented PhyDL and evaluated its performance on the TwoMoons, MNIST, MUSK, HEART, and SONAR datasets\. PhyDL outperformed LLGC on 4 out of 5 evaluated datasets, highlighting its effectiveness in semi\-supervised learning scenarios\. On the TwoMoons, MNIST, MUSK, and SONAR benchmarks, the method showed steady accuracy gains, with consistent improvements as the number of labeled samples increased\. However, on the HEART dataset, standard LLGC achieved better results, indicating that PhyDL’s community\-based diffusion can be limited by certain underlying spatial structures\. Furthermore, the experiments revealed that the Edge Betweenness algorithm is unsuitable for these specific high\-dimensional tasks\. Ultimately, this study showcases PhyDL’s potential, when equipped with the FastGreedy algorithm, to significantly improve data labeling performance in semi\-supervised scenarios, effectively leveraging the structural topology of complex datasets\.

## [MRI\-PHYSIOL\-NIRS: an integrated platform to study kidney oxygenation](../publications/cf62f7417e5eb7ec7e9b.md)

Thomas Gladytz; Kathleen Cantow; Jason Michael Millward; Sonia Waiczies; Ehsan Tasbihi; Dirk Grosenick; Erdmann Seeliger; Thoralf Niendorf

Abstract The kidney always operates close to hypoxia, a pathological condition of O 2 \-shortage, due to its unique relationship between blood flow and oxygen demand\. Renal hypoxia is central to kidney diseases, where progressive loss of renal function ultimately can no longer sustain life\. Magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) can assess renal oxygenation non\-invasively in vivo via the relaxation times T 2 \* and T 2 , which reflect deoxygenated hemoglobin, but are influenced by several physiological confounders\. We developed MRI\-PHYSIOL\-NIRS, a platform integrating MRI with ground\-truth probes that directly measure tissue oxygenation in rat kidneys \(PHYSIOL\), and near\-infrared spectroscopy \(NIRS\) to estimate oxygenation\-related parameters to dissect the relationship between MRI\-based measures and true tissue oxygenation\. Using aortic occlusion and hyperoxia interventions within the MRI scanner, we investigated correlations between non\-invasive MRI\-based oxygenation measures and true tissue oxygenation\. These results demonstrate the potential for entirely MRI\-based measurement of renal oxygenation in health and disease, with ultimate application in patients\.

## [Pitetti\-Heil, Johanna: Artificial Intelligence from Science Fiction to Soul Machines: Configuring Empathy between Bodies, Knowledge, and Power](../publications/cf78431148b02736d895.md)



In Herta Nagl\-Docekal &amp; Waldemar Zacharasiewicz, Artificial Intelligence and Human Enhancement: Affirmative and Critical Approaches in the Humanities\. Berlin, Boston: De Gruyter\. pp\. 287\-308\. 2022In science fiction, empathy has long been treated as an exclusive trait of human beings, and the ability to feel empathy allows many authors to establish social hierarchies between humans and non\-humans who feel or show empathy in unexpected ways\. Such treatments foster what Donna Haraway has called “human exceptionalism,” which connects empathy to morality in an ableist manner\. This article argues that Richard Powers’s Galatea 2\.2 and Philip K\. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? counter this exceptionalist tradition by treating the electrical circuits of a neural network and the particular bodies of androids as forms of “vibrant matter” \(Bennett\) that develop their own senses of embodiment, loyalty, empathy, and efficacy\. In a parallel development, the realworld company Soul Machines has been challenging preconceived conceptions of empathy in developing empathetic AI systems\. Connecting these developments in AI research to science fiction discourses of empathic intelligence, the article \(re\)thinks empathy and \(artificial\) intelligence in relation to questions of morality, responsibility, and power, and asks what models of care and empathy are necessary if humanity is to develop in collaboration with artificial intelligence systems\.

## [Revolución de datos mediante Big Data y Google Colab para el análisis y gestión de ciencia de datos](../publications/cf7f44ac76fcf9381c5d.md)

Ricardo Manuel Candanedo Yau

This research analyzed the influence of Big Data and Google Colab platform on information analysis, processing, and management within academic and technological contexts\. The study followed a documentary and descriptive approach supported by the review and analysis of 100 indexed scientific publications selected according to thematic relevance, currency, and academic rigor\. The methodology incorporated thematic coding processes and documentary frequency analysis aimed at identifying trends related to Big Data, information science, cloud computing, machine learning, and collaborative platforms for data analysis\. The findings revealed that the accelerated growth of digital information significantly transformed the way organizations, educational institutions, and research centers manage information to support strategic decision\-making processes\. Likewise, the study identified that Big Data facilitates large\-scale information processing through predictive analytics, data mining, and statistical visualization techniques, while Google Colab enables the development of projects based on cloud computing, programming, and computational analysis within collaborative environments\. The results also demonstrated that the integration of both technologies strengthened digital and analytical competencies related to programming, information management, analytical thinking, and the automation of scientific processes\. In the same way, the accessibility and flexibility of Google Colab contributed to democratizing access to advanced tools for data analysis and processing without requiring specialized technological infrastructure\. The study concluded that the convergence between Big Data and Google Colab represents a strategic alternative for optimizing knowledge management, strengthening scientific research, and promoting technological innovation and digital transformation processes in academic and organizational environments\. Furthermore, these technologies foster new opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and data\-driven decision\-making\.

## [Transformation de l&\#x27;agriculture africaine à l&\#x27;ère de l&\#x27;intelligence artificielle : quels modèles managériaux pour une performance durable et inclusive ?](../publications/cf8006f0a29fceb640ec.md)

ASSONTIA DJOUDJI Gaston

L’essor des technologies numériques, notamment certaines applications de l’intelligence artificielle, ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour l’agriculture africaine, mais leurs effets organisationnels restent peu documentés\. Cette recherche analyse les transformations des pratiques de gestion, de coordination et de décision dans l’écosystème agricole camerounais\. Elle adopte une approche qualitative exploratoire combinant un questionnaire auprès de 46 acteurs agricoles et des entretiens semi\-directifs avec des producteurs, dirigeants, responsables techniques et prestataires\. Les données ont été analysées par codage thématique\. Les résultats montrent que les technologies numériques sont principalement mobilisées pour améliorer l’accès à l’information, l’organisation des activités, les traitements agricoles et les relations avec les clients\. Leur appropriation demeure progressive, sous l’effet de contraintes techniques, organisationnelles et territoriales\. Elles modifient certains mécanismes de coordination et de décision sans se substituer au décideur humain, tout en renforçant le rôle des données et des compétences\. Les expériences d’agriculture de précision révèlent enfin l’adaptation de technologies importées aux réalités locales\. L’étude met ainsi en évidence des configurations managériales hybrides associant savoir\-faire locaux, outils numériques, données et expertise humaine\.

## [From prompts to genomes: A constraint\-first framework for AI\-driven sequence design across life and viruses](../publications/cf80c524ff80996284eb.md)

Adhityo Wicaksono; Arli Aditya Parikesit

A constraint\-first framework for future &\#x27;prompt\-to\-genome&\#x27; AI across Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryota, and viruses is proposed\. Genome\-scale models can now generate long DNA sequences, and experimentally viable genome\-scale designs have begun to appear, but sequence generation alone does not establish biological feasibility\. Constraints should not require designs to remain within natural sequence space; rather, they should define testable boundaries for function, inheritance, lifecycle coherence and safe use, including new\-to\-nature designs\. We propose a two\-part system\. First, a Constraint Compiler translates natural\-language prompts into machine\-checkable specifications defining scope, context, objectives, assumptions and governance requirements\. Second, a modular Validator Stack \(C1\-C6\) evaluates candidate designs for sequence integrity, gene and regulatory plausibility, genome completeness, comparative coherence, systems\-level feasibility, and safety and governance\. Extreme prompts serve as stress tests to expose hidden assumptions, conflicting objectives, and refusal points, complemented by adversarial testing and risk assessment\. A phased roadmap and community benchmarks are proposed to measure specification accuracy, biological feasibility, robustness, and governance performance\. The goal is to move prompt\-to\-genome systems from impressive generation toward reliable, auditable, and accountable biological design\.

## [Perceived viewing\-experience enhancement and audience acceptance: applying TAM to AI\-based sports broadcasting services](../publications/cf822cc4f575be23b275.md)

Liuxin Li

Introduction Despite the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence \(AI\) technologies in sports broadcasting, empirical evidence validating the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) and experiential outcomes in this specific context remains limited\. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the statistical relationships among core TAM constructs, usage attitude, behavioral intention, and perceived viewing\-experience enhancement within AI\-based sports broadcasting services\. Methods Based on the theoretical framework of TAM, this study collected valid data from 630 Chinese respondents\. Structural equation modeling \(SEM\) was employed to quantitatively test the hypothesized research model and examine the interrelationships between the proposed variables\. Results The empirical results demonstrate that perceived ease of use positively predicts perceived usefulness, and both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness exert significant positive effects on users&\#x27; usage attitude\. Furthermore, usage attitude is positively associated with behavioral intention and perceived viewing\-experience enhancement\. Notably, usage attitude plays a full mediating role in the relationships between the two perceptual antecedents \(perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness\) and the two outcome variables \(behavioral intention, viewing\-experience enhancement\)\. Discussion This research contributes context\-specific empirical validation to the TAM framework in the emerging domain of AI\-driven sports broadcasting\. It extends existing TAM literature by integrating individual\-level experiential outcomes alongside traditional behavioral intention indicators in sports media consumption\. Practically, the findings provide actionable insights for optimizing user experience and improving service design for AI sports broadcasting platforms\.

## [Research on the Application of Digital Formative Assessment in College Sports Skill Teachings](../publications/cf9c1b02cd0eabd42aec.md)

Yunxing He; Ligen Wei

To enhance the process\-oriented nature and monitoring effectiveness of physical education skills instruction in higher education, this study employs digital formative assessment methods\. The analysis focuses on the decomposition of skill objectives, the identification of learning evidence, the collection of multi\-source data, and the establishment of feedback rules\. By embedding the assessment into the processes of pre\-class identification, motion tracking, real\-time correction, and individual practice adjustments, a comprehensive digital evaluation framework is constructed\. An empirical intervention was conducted to validate this framework, utilizing quantitative metrics to evaluate student performance before and after the implementation\. The results show that following the intervention, students&\#x27; comprehensive scores in specific skills, technical execution, success rates, and movement stability all significantly improved\. Furthermore, a feedback\-driven correction cycle gradually took shape during classroom practice\. Students demonstrated a marked enhancement in their ability to independently adjust their practice, indicating a strong development in self\-management and autonomous learning capabilities\. The digital tools facilitated immediate and personalized feedback, which was crucial for refining motor skills and correcting technical errors in real time\. Ultimately, this study provides valuable insights and a practical paradigm for optimizing the assessment of physical education skills instruction in higher education, demonstrating the transformative potential of digital formative assessment in fostering student\-centered, data\-driven pedagogical environments\.

## [Sovereign European AI Built on Permissively Licensed Open Models](../publications/cf9ef74384b82983eb76.md)

Dirk de Pol

Abstract This paper examines the conditions under which a European organization can adopt a permissively licensed language model, develop it further within a confidential environment, retain control over its model weights and training materials, and reduce dependence on NVIDIA hardware and other concentrated infrastructure suppliers\. The analysis combines a targeted review of model releases and license terms, an assessment of European Union and national legal requirements, a threat\-model\-based security architecture, and a staged procurement and development roadmap\. The study forms part of the broader intellectual and research context of Omegacene, an interdisciplinary project examining the implications of artificial intelligence, technological transformation, and the changing relationship between human and machine agency\. Within this context, AI sovereignty is treated not merely as a question of model ownership or infrastructure procurement, but as a problem of institutional control, verifiable accountability, and the capacity to make consequential technological systems independently assessable and governable\. The central finding is that model licensing, regulatory compliance, operational security, and supply\-chain sovereignty are separate but interdependent dimensions\. Apache License 2\.0 generally permits confidential modification without an obligation to publish derivative artifacts\. This permission does not establish the lawfulness of training data, guarantee freedom from third\-party rights, or exempt a downstream organization from applicable AI, data protection, cybersecurity, or procurement law\. The European Commission’s compute\-based guidance on modifications of general\-purpose AI models provides a useful planning indicator, but it does not constitute a statutory exemption or a security threshold\. Technical transparency can improve auditability but cannot prove the absence of malicious behavior\. Confidential execution, access controls, artifact signing, and model\-extraction defenses reduce particular risks without providing absolute protection\. Hardware independence is likewise multidimensional: replacing NVIDIA with another supplier does not eliminate dependence on non\-European fabrication, memory, interconnects, firmware, or design tools\. Advanced fabrication already exists within the EU, but the evidence reviewed does not establish a complete, independently controllable European accelerator supply chain\. The paper proposes three complementary model\-development tracks, a four\-zone security architecture, measurable procurement requirements, corrected compute estimates, and a risk register\. Its principal contribution is a framework for making sovereignty claims testable by translating broad aspirations into explicit technical, legal, operational, and supply\-chain criteria\. In the wider Omegacene\.com context, this approach offers a practical basis for evaluating whether control over AI systems is substantive, demonstrable, and resilient, rather than merely asserted through licensing choices or national affiliation\. Keywords: digital sovereignty; general\-purpose AI; Apache License 2\.0; AI Act; confidential model development; model weights; trade secrets; confidential computing; export controls; semiconductor supply chains; EuroHPC; public procurement\.

## [Transport\-injury burden among children and adolescents in the Western Pacific Region, 2000–2023, with projections to 2035](../publications/cfa5c0edbc67eee1fd63.md)

Rongxiang Sun; Qinglong Jian; Chen Ye; Quanneng Luo; Kenyou Zhou; Huilong Guo; Guohua Wang; Chuncheung Chan

Background Transport injuries remain a major preventable cause of death and disability among children and adolescents\. Evidence on long\-term trends, geographic inequalities, and future burden across the Western Pacific Region \(WPR\) remains limited\. We assessed transport\-injury burden among people aged &lt;20 years in the WPR from 2000 to 2023 and projected trends to 2035\. Methods We analysed Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023 estimates for 33 WPR countries and territories\. We assessed incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability\-adjusted life years \(DALYs\) from 2000 to 2023\. We mapped 2023 age\-standardised rates, examined four age groups by sex, and decomposed changes into demographic and epidemiological components\. Sex\-specific autoregressive integrated moving average \(ARIMA\) models were used to project age\-standardised outcomes from 2024 to 2035\. Results Incident cases decreased from 5,034,407 \[95% uncertainty interval \(UI\), 4,180,502–5,955,077\] in 2000 to 2,433,402 \(1,988,777–2,920,981\) in 2023\. The age\-standardised incidence rate fell from 812\.69 to 428\.74 per 100,000\. The annual percentage change was −2\.82% \(95% confidence interval, −3\.04 to −2\.61; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. In 2023, incidence varied 4\.48\-fold and mortality varied 38\.2\-fold across locations\. Males aged 15–19 years had higher incidence, mortality, and DALY rates than females of the same age\. Epidemiological change drove most of the regional reduction\. Between 2024 and 2035, ARIMA models projected male age\-standardised incidence and prevalence rates to decline modestly, while female rates remained nearly stable\. Mortality and DALY projections crossed zero and were excluded from quantitative interpretation\. Conclusions The transport\-injury burden among children and adolescents in the WPR decreased substantially, but marked geographic and age\-sex inequalities persisted\. The 2024–2035 projections suggest that non\-fatal burden may decline only modestly, with little change among females\. Prevention should prioritise older adolescent males and high\-mortality settings, while longer\-term policy planning requires more robust forecasting\.

## [A Metaphysical Analysis of Theological Language: Can We Talk About God?](../publications/cfa838ffce13f6fa28cd.md)

Kenneth R Marple

The possibility of meaningful theological language presents a longstanding problem in philosophy of religion and Christian theology\. Because human language is finite and creaturely while God is infinite and transcendent, questions arise concerning how human beings can make meaningful and truthful claims about God\. Traditional accounts of univocal, equivocal, and analogical predication address aspects of this problem but often leave a more fundamental metaphysical question unresolved: what must language be for it to meaningfully signify reality? This dissertation provides a metaphysical analysis of theological language by examining the ontological foundations of language and its relationship to reality\. Through qualitative, interdisciplinary research engaging philosophy of language, metaphysics, historical theology, biblical theology, and Christian participatory metaphysics, the study examines the relationship between linguistic meaning, reference, conceptual content, and being\. The work engages significant contributions from Augustine, Aquinas, Scotus, Chomsky, Fodor, Kripke, Wittgenstein, and Alston\. The dissertation argues that language possesses a genuine, though abstract, mode of being and therefore cannot be adequately understood as merely an arbitrary human convention\. Because language can participate in and signify objective reality, linguistic meaning can possess truth beyond the conventions of a particular linguistic community\. Within a Christian metaphysical framework, this capacity is ultimately grounded in the being and mind of the Triune God\. Human language therefore participates in a reality that transcends the human speaker while remaining genuinely finite and creaturely\. The study concludes that meaningful theological language is possible because language, reality, and divine being are not metaphysically disconnected\. This participatory account provides a foundation for understanding how finite human beings can make genuine claims about an infinite God while avoiding both exhaustive univocity and the loss of meaningful conceptual continuity\.

## [The Role of Viscoelasticity in Heterogeneous Glioblastoma Stem Cell Invasion in Biomimetic 3‐Dimensional Hydrogels](../publications/cfbec052443f0903c91c.md)

Nicole Blaine; Arianna Skirzynska; Allysia A\. Chin; Julie Audet; Molly Sandra Shoichet

The role of viscoelasticity in cell invasion within the brain extracellular matrix \(ECM\) is not well understood in the context of glioblastoma \(GBM\)\. We designed biomimetic viscoelastic hyaluronan \(HA\)\-based hydrogels to understand the effect of viscoelasticity on the invasion of heterogeneous glioblastoma stem cells \(GSCs\) categorized into subgroups based on molecular profile, as Reactive, Invasive, or Constructive\. Hydrogel viscoelasticity was introduced to a hyaluronan\-oxime \(HAox\) hydrogel to varying degrees through the incorporation of one of methyl cellulose, ECM\-based proteins, tenascin C or collagen IV, or hydrazone chemistry\. Each HAox\-derived viscoelastic hydrogel exhibited significantly higher stress relaxation than HAox\. We demonstrated that heterogeneous patient\-derived GSC lines respond differently to viscoelasticity, with a strong correlation between greater invasion of Reactive GSCs in faster stress\-relaxing matrices\. This work highlights the importance of investigating the behavior of GSCs based on their heterogeneous molecular profiles and contributes to the understanding of the role of viscoelasticity in GSC invasion\.

## [Association between social jetlag and diabetes self\-management in adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross\-sectional study with serial mediation analysis](../publications/cfde553bddd9036f3688.md)

Jinman He; Shuaiyou Wang; Jingyu Zhang; Shuang Li; Xiaoting Huang; Huang Chongmei; Minhui Liu

Background Diabetes self\-management requires consistent daily behaviors\. Social jetlag, the mismatch between workday and free\-day sleep timing, may disrupt daily behavior routines\. This study examined the association between social jetlag and self\-management in adults with type 2 diabetes \(T2D\), and whether sleep quality and depressive symptoms statistically accounted for portions of this association\. Methods This cross\-sectional study recruited employed adults aged 18–60 years with T2D from the endocrinology departments of three tertiary public general hospitals in Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China, from January to April 2026\. Social jetlag was calculated from the micro Munich Chronotype Questionnaire; sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and diabetes self\-management were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Patient Health Questionnaire\-9, and Summary of Diabetes Self\-Care Activities, respectively\. Multivariable linear regression and serial mediation analysis with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were performed\. Results A total of 339 participants were analyzed\. Each additional h of social jetlag was associated with higher PSQI score \( B = 1\.352, 95% CI 1\.042 to 1\.663\), higher PHQ\-9 score \( B = 3\.772, 95% CI 3\.314 to 4\.229\), and lower SDSCA score \( B = −6\.623, 95% CI −7\.566 to −5\.679\)\. The direct association remained significant after PSQI and PHQ\-9 scores were included \( B = −3\.830, 95% CI −5\.048 to −2\.611\)\. The specific indirect association through depressive symptoms alone was −2\.230 \(95% bootstrap CI −3\.053 to −1\.469\), and the serial indirect association through sleep quality and depressive symptoms was −0\.314 \(95% bootstrap CI −0\.534 to −0\.150\)\. Conclusion Greater social jetlag was associated with poorer diabetes self\-management\. Significant indirect associations were observed through depressive symptoms alone and through the serial pathway from sleep quality to depressive symptoms\. These associations do not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation because the data were cross\-sectional\.

## [Crop diversification as a climate\-smart agriculture strategy and household welfare in Nigeria: evidence from living standard measurement survey](../publications/cfe53ad6acdd41c6e14b.md)

Robert Ugochukwu Onyeneke; Chukwuemeka Chinonso Emenekwe; Chinedum Uzoma Nwajiuba

Crop diversification is a climate\-smart agriculture \(CSA\) practice with well\-documented yield and agroecological benefits, but rigorous, nationally representative evidence on its welfare impacts in Nigeria remains scarce\. This study examined the determinants and welfare effects of crop diversification adoption among 3,229 farm households, using the fourth wave of Nigeria’s Living Standard Measurement Study – Integrated Surveys on Agriculture \(LSMS\-ISA\)\. A probit model identified the determinants of adoption, and an endogenous switching regression \(ESR\) model, which corrects for selection bias arising from observed and unobserved heterogeneity, estimated the causal impact of adoption on household per capita consumption expenditure and dietary diversity\. About 1,846 households \(57%\) adopted crop diversification\. Household size, farm size, age of household head, distance to road, fertilizer use, and temperature exposure significantly increased the probability of adoption, while education, distance to market, access to finance, and rainfall shock significantly reduced it\. Adoption increased per capita consumption expenditure by an average treatment effect of 0\.72 log points and household dietary diversity scores by 2\.03 points among adopters, effects that are large relative to national poverty and dietary diversity benchmarks\. These results indicate that limited market access, credit products tied to specialized cropping, and climate shocks jointly suppress adoption\. Government agricultural and nutrition agencies should jointly fund a targeted program that redesigns credit products to support diversified cropping, pairs rural road investment with market access, and bundles diversification advice with climate information and weather\-index insurance in drought\-prone areas\.

## [Environmental Health Compliance Requirements for Urban Tuition Centres Operating in Renovated Shop Office Premises](../publications/cfed57f3fb368d3ef9e3.md)

Nur Khairul Faizah Mustafa; Adi Irfan Che Ani; Sharyzee Mohmad Shukri; Mohd Hayazi Agusi

Adherence to environmental health standards is imperative to safeguard the well\-being of students, educators, and administrative personnel within private tuition centres\. Urban tuition centres operating in renovated shop\-office premises may encounter environmental health challenges because their original commercial layouts are not necessarily suited to sustained educational occupancy\. This study identifies the environmental health parameters relevant to tuition\-centre licensing in Kajang, Selangor, and proposes practical, evidence informed improvement measures\. A qualitative research design combined documentary analysis of the Ministry of Health Malaysia’s premises\-inspection checklist and 28 regulatory, technical and scholarly sources with one semistructured key\-informant interview involving an authorised environmental health inspector from the Hulu Langat District Health Office\. Kajang, defined as the geographical context without selected case study and field observations or premises inspections were conducted\. Directed qualitative content analysis and a six\-phase thematic procedure were undertaken manually using a structured coding matrix\. Five document informed themes were identified: lighting; indoor air quality and ventilation; sanitation, cleanliness and waste management; noise control; and building safety and maintenance\. Documentary frequencies indicate the extent to which the selected sources address each theme but do not represent centre level of noncompliance rates\. The inspector’s account provides contextual interpretation of inspection requirements rather than statistically representative evidence\. Appropriate responses include verifying classroom illuminance, ensuring adequate outdoor\-air ventilation, maintaining hygienic facilities, controlling intrusive noise, and keeping escape routes and safety equipment serviceable\. The findings provide a substantially contextualised framework for interpreting environmental health requirements in repurposed shop\-office tuition centres, subject to the limitations of a single key informant and the absence of primary premises level observations\. Keywords: Compliance, Environmental Health Standard, Parameters, Shop Office, Tuition Centre

## [Among rural older adults, an apparent physical\-activity contrast in nonblank medication\-field presence was markedly attenuated when chronic\-disease management registration was incorporated into the analysis](../publications/cfef6dd216ee86be0324.md)

Kun Xu; Yiming Zhang; Yongheng Zhao; Xuefeng Xi; Gaixia Hou; Zhuangzhuang Guo; Limeng Liu; Yajuan Wang; Dehui Zhang

Background Medication fields created for chronic\-disease management may mislead when reused as medication\-exposure measures in broader older\-adult populations\. Using routine exercise\-frequency as routine\-recorded physical activity \(PA\), we compared PA \+ records \(daily, at least weekly, or occasional exercise\) with PA− records \(no exercise\) and examined how nonblank medication\-field presence changed after management\-registration context was incorporated\. Methods This cross\-sectional study used 2,270 examination records from a 2025 rural primary\-care program in northeastern China; PA was available for 2,226 records\. The outcome was any nonblank text in the main\-medication field\. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios \(PRs\) with small\-sample\-adjusted cluster\-robust inference across 20 sites\. Sequential models incorporated demographics, site, and four hypertension/diabetes management\-registration categories\. Logistic regression estimated standardized proportions and absolute differences\. Medication text underwent secondary audit, including 200 randomly sampled retained entries independently reviewed by two pharmacists\. Results Nonblank medication fields occurred in 1,114/1,157 \(96\.3%\) records with hypertension and/or diabetes management registration versus 27/1,113 \(2\.4%\) with neither registration\. Field presence was low without registration and near\-complete with hypertension\-only or dual registration; the diabetes\-only stratum was small \(n = 37\)\. Overall field presence was 56\.4% in PA\+ and 42\.8% in PA− records \(PR 1\.317, 95% CI 1\.076–1\.612\)\. After registration context was incorporated, the PR was 1\.001 \(95% CI 0\.960–1\.043\); full adjustment yielded 1\.002 \(95% CI 0\.959–1\.046\)\. Standardized proportions were 51\.26% and 51\.14%, a difference of 0\.12 percentage points \(95% CI −2\.07 to 2\.30\)\. Among 1,368 retained entries, archived labels classified 75\.9% as antihypertensive, 14\.5% as glucose\-lowering, 0\.5% as other cardiovascular, 1\.7% as other medications, and 7\.4% as unresolved\. Inter\-reviewer agreement for broad therapeutic class was 99\.5% \(κ = 0\.982\), and parser–manual\-reference concordance was 99\.0%; these assessments did not verify medication exposure\. Conclusion Nonblank main\-medication\-field recording was strongly patterned by chronic\-disease management registration, and the apparent overall PA\-related contrast was markedly attenuated after this context was incorporated\. Blank fields cannot establish medication nonuse, and nonblank or consistently parsed text cannot establish complete, current medication exposure\.

## [Integrated multi\-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor\-induced myocarditis](../publications/cff79398b9e2cae0adac.md)

Shilong Zhang; Cai Qing\-qing; Jian Zhang; Yuan Liu; Hao Lu; Ye\-Rui Zhang; Yu\-Chen Xu; Hai\-Xiang Peng; Hui\-Yong Chen; Yan Wang; Leilei Cheng; Junbo Ge

Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor\-associated myocarditis \(ICI\-myocarditis\) is a rare but frequently fatal immune\-related adverse event\. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI\-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions\. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI\-myocarditis via scRNA\-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling\. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity\. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2\-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI\-induced cardiac injury in vivo\. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI\-myocarditis, we develop an 8\-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI\-myocarditis from other ICIs\-treated controls\. JAK\-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes\. Furthermore, JAK\-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti\-PD\-1 therapy in mouse models\. In summary, this study implicates immune\-pathogenic features of ICI\-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies\.

## [AI\-ENABLED COMMUNICATION EFFICIENCY AS A MEDIATOR BETWEEN REGULATORY ADAPTATION, INTERCULTURAL TRAINING, AND PROJECT PERFORMANCE IN GEOSITE TOURISM DEVELOPMENT: A CASE OF YUNNAN CONSTRUCTION AND INVESTMENT HOLDING GROUP](../publications/d0012951ce44d745af80.md)

Chao Cheng; Dhakir Abbas Ali; Rozaini binti Rosli

This study develops and tests a mediation model in which AI\-enabled communication efficiency \(AICE\) transmits the effects of regulatory adaptation \(RA\) and intercultural training \(ICT\) to project performance \(PP\) in geosite tourism development projects associated with Yunnan Construction and Investment Holding Group \(YCIH\)\. A sequential quantitative design is specified and analyzed data from 320 respondents that represents stakeholder responses in a provincial state\-owned enterprise project context\. Quantitative analysis follows the structure: indicator loadings, reliability \(ρA, ρc, α\), convergent validity \(AVE\), discriminant validity \(Fornell–Larcker and HTMT\), structural paths with bootstrapped standard errors, effect sizes \(f²\), and predictive diagnostics \(R², Q²predict, RMSE, MAE\)\. Regulatory adaptation and intercultural training both improve AI\-enabled communication efficiency \(β = 0\.430 and 0\.370, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. AI\-enabled communication efficiency improves project performance \(β = 0\.410, p &lt; 0\.001\) and partially mediates the effects of regulatory adaptation and intercultural training on performance \(indirect effects β = 0\.176 and 0\.152, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The model explains 38\.2% of the variance in AICE and 45\.3% in PP, with acceptable predictive relevance \(Q²predict = 0\.369 for AICE; 0\.436 for PP\)\. For geosite tourism development, where projects must satisfy geopark governance expectations for visibility, conservation, and community participation\. This study positions AICE as a managerial lever that makes regulatory and intercultural capabilities “actionable\.” It suggests that horizon scanning and cross\-cultural capability building yield stronger performance benefits when project teams adopt AIsupported translation, summarisation, and knowledge\-routing routines consistent with responsible AI governance\.

## [Assessment of Seasonal Groundwater Level Trends in Afzalpur Taluk, Karnataka Using Non\-Parametric Statistical Techniques](../publications/d003d554ad4154018393.md)

Channamma Sadashiva Gour
