Groundwater is the primary source of water supply in semi\-arid regions of India, where its sustainability is increasingly threatened by overexploitation and climate variability\. This study evaluates seasonal groundwater level variations in Afzalpur Taluk, Karnataka, using the Mann–Kendall \(MK\) trend test and Sen’s slope estimator\. Groundwater depth data for pre\-monsoon, monsoon, and post\-monsoon seasons were analyzed to detect monotonic trends and quantify their magnitude\. Results indicate pronounced seasonal variability, with deeper groundwater levels during pre\-monsoon \(7\.9–24\.6 m\) and significant recovery in post\-monsoon \(4\.2–12\.9 m\)\. The MK test results show no statistically significant trends \(p &gt; 0\.05\) across all seasons, with Kendall’s τ values ranging from −0\.013 to 0\.333\. Sen’s slope estimates also indicate negligible to low trend magnitudes\. These findings suggest that groundwater dynamics in the study area are predominantly controlled by seasonal recharge rather than long\-term monotonic trends\. The study highlights the need for localized groundwater management strategies, including recharge enhancement and controlled abstraction, to ensure sustainable utilization\.

## [AIEdTechism\. Revolutionising and Characterising a New Learning Theory in the Age of AI\-Ed\.](../publications/d00bf57effab7abffcb1.md)

McGregor Alison

As artificial intelligence reshapes classrooms, do our existing learning theories still explain how people learn? This presentation introduces AIEdTechism, a proposed learning theory for the age of AI in education, and sets out what characterizes it and how it could change the way teachers, designers and researchers think about teaching with AI\. Presented at the Twentieth International Conference on Technology, Knowledge, and Society\.

## [REDESIGN UI/UX PADA PLATFORM ARA KB VALBURY SEKURITAS MENGGUNAKAN KERANGKA DESIGN THINKING](../publications/d01fe5c3d04c2df2b6ab.md)

224010304 Tengku Arya Nugraha Putra; Dr\. Ardi Gunardi, SE\.,M\.Si, Pembimbing

ABSTRAK Platform KB ARA milik PT KB Valbury Sekuritas masih memperoleh rating rendah \(2,7 dari skala 5\) di Google Play Store, dengan keluhan pengguna terkait usability, navigasi, dan tampilan antarmuka\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kondisi User Interface \(UI\) dan User Experience \(UX\) platform KB ARA serta merancang ulang antarmukanya menggunakan pendekatan Design thinking\. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan wawancara terhadap tiga pengguna KB ARA dan satu Sales/Customer Service PT KB Valbury Sekuritas Bandung\. Data dianalisis menggunakan kerangka aspek Usability Heuristics Nielsen \(1994\) dan diolah melalui model interaktif Miles dan Huberman \(1994\), dilanjutkan penerapan lima tahapan Design thinking\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan kondisi UI/UX KB ARA masih bermasalah pada aspek Visibility of System Status, Recognition Rather Than Recall, Aesthetic and Minimalist Design, dan Consistency and Standards, konsisten dengan klasifikasi keluhan pada Google Play Store\. Berdasarkan temuan tersebut, dirancang tiga perbaikan utama: penyederhanaan tampilan Fast Trade, penambahan indikator visual status transaksi, dan halaman Emiten Detail yang mengonsolidasikan informasi order book, broker, teknikal, dan laporan keuangan\. Hasil pengujian prototype menunjukkan rancangan mampu menjawab permasalahan yang ditemukan, meski masih mengidentifikasi kebutuhan pengembangan lanjutan berupa fitur amend order dan penguatan visibilitas navigasi\. Kata kunci : User Interface, User Experience, Design thinking, Usability Heuristics, aplikasi sekuritas, Figma

## [Comparative Analysis of Predictive Model for Student Academic Performance](../publications/d02380b96c847bcd25e6.md)

Gabriel Adaugo Cynthia; Prema A\. Kirubakaran; Ridwan Kolapo

Early detection of students who are likely to have low performance levels is a major issue in learning institutions\. This paper aims at creating a predictive model that can be depended on as well as interpreted to deal with this problem using machine learning\. Another strength of this research is that it focuses on accuracy, among other factors, which is unlike many other studies that focus on accuracy only but not on model robustness and contextual relevance, which are essential to meaningful educational decision\-making\. To enhance the credibility of the findings, the primary and secondary data were also used, including demographic, socio\-educational, and academic characteristics of students\.

## [Towards optimal selection schedules for online active learning](../publications/d04a8ef8b7cfb2600eaf.md)

Hugo Cui; Francesca Mignacco; Francesco Mori

We consider the problem of online linear classification, where a stream of unlabeled samples is available, and annotation is costly\. We investigate the optimal query policy, that prescribes whether and when a sample should be labeled and used for a training step, or instead discarded, so as to minimize a given objective\. We focus on the realizable case, under Gaussian design, in the high\-dimensional regime where data dimension and number of unlabeled samples grow proportionally\. We consider two objectives: 1\) the generalization error under a labeling budget, and 2\) a cumulative cost function where mistakes have unit cost and queries cost $Δ$\. We first show that the myopic policies that greedily minimize at all times the increment in the objective correspond to either small or intermediate\-margin policies, that prescribe the selection of samples whose margins fall within certain intervals that shrink with time\. Within this class, we numerically ascertain the optimal schedules for the selection thresholds that minimize the final values of the objectives\. Taking inspiration from the myopic policy for the cumulative cost, we design a very simple query policy schedule that we compare to other proposed heuristics, on synthetic data and real medical image datasets\. Finally, we discuss myopic policies for two\-layer neural networks, and exemplify how naive margin\-based policies can cease to be optimal\.

## [Automatización en la gestión de procesos empresariales: una revisión sistemática de la literatura](../publications/d04be25bfeeb6278effe.md)

Lourdes Victoria Sánchez\-García; Claudia Patricia Lozano\-Rocha; Cynthia Ludy Sánchez Elaluff; Pedro Lito Rivera Cardozo; Roger Agustín Mafaldo\-Herrera

La gestión de procesos empresariales o business process management \(BPM\) se ha consolidado como un enfoque estratégico en la transformación digital organizacional, debido a la incorporación de tecnologías automatizadas dirigidas a optimizar la eficiencia operativa y fortalecer la toma de decisiones\. En este contexto, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo examinar la evidencia sobre los procedimientos de automatización en BPM y su influencia en el desempeño de los procesos empresariales, su eficiencia, la digitalización y la variabilidad de los procesos\. Para ello, se desarrolló una revisión sistemática basada en el protocolo PRISMA 2020, y se utilizaron las bases de datos Scopus, SciELO y Dialnet\. Por estos medios, se seleccionaron 15 estudios conforme a criterios de elegibilidad\. La evidencia analizada indica que la automatización fortalece la eficiencia operativa, reduce tiempos y costos, mejora la trazabilidad de las actividades y optimiza la gestión de la información mediante tecnologías como la inteligencia artificial \(IA\), la automatización robótica de procesos y las herramientas low\-code\. Asimismo, la evidencia sugiere que la automatización depende del nivel de madurez digital, la complejidad de los procesos y las capacidades organizacionales disponibles, por lo que se observaron mayores beneficios en procesos estructurados y repetitivos\. Se concluye que la automatización constituye un elemento estratégico para la modernización y adaptación empresarial, aunque su efectividad depende de la adecuada integración entre tecnología, capacidades organizacionales y gestión del cambio\.

## [From Compliance Burden to Organizational Resilience: A System Dynamics Model of AI Risk Governance in SMEs](../publications/d04c8b1a890cdda74571.md)

Osman Angeles Conteh; Alimamy Kamara; Aminata Kera Conteh

The paper provides a system dynamics model that would explain the way in which small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) can use AI compliance as an administrative burden, rather than an organizational resilience capacity\. Based on the dynamic capabilities theory, organizational resilience studies, AI risk management principles, and system dynamics, the research designs feedback among AI experimentation, strength of deploying AI, compliance maturity, risk exposure, learning incidents, slack resources, and resilience capacity\. The results section describes normal simulation behavior in three policy options: innovation\-first, compliance\-first, and balanced adaptive governance\. The simulated findings suggest that innovation\-first adoption creates high early growth in capabilities; on the other hand, compliance\-first governments create less exposure but hides innovation throughput\. The adaptive\-governance with balance scenario works best within a 36\-month horizon since it encompasses leveled controls, more adaptive learning loop, and even\-tailed review\. The debate suggests that AI risk governance in SMEs needs to be technologised as dynamic resourcefulness instead of an unchanging compliance audit\. The paper also introduces a feedback based theory of AI governance among SMEs and where the policy leverage points are that managers can use to safeguard innovation whilst enhancing resiliency\.

## [Sustainable Lightweight Self\-Compacting Concrete Incorporating Recycled Waste Glass: Influence of Particle Size and Replacement Levels on Performance](../publications/d05b3c59e6df53046007.md)

Lamyaa Ghanim Salim; Ali H\. Nahhab

Abstract The incorporation of recycled waste glass into lightweight self\-compacting concrete \(LWSCC\) has developed as a sustainable technique to reducing natural aggregate consumption and environmental impacts\. In this study, the effect of combining waste glass in two particle size kinds that is coarse glass \(greater than 1\.18 mm\) and fine glass \(less than 1\.18 mm\) as a partial replacement for fine aggregate at percentage of replacement of 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40% on the fresh properties \(slump flow, T500, v\-funnel, L\-box and fresh density\), mechanical properties \(equilibrium density, compressive strength, splitting strength, flexural strength, modulus of elasticity and impact resistance strength\), and durability properties \(sorptivity, water absorption and alkali – silica reaction\) of LWSCC were evaluated\. Two groups of mixtures, assigned as GC and GF, were prepared with various replacement percentages\. Results of fresh properties showed all mixtures confirm requirements of EFNARC indicating that the presence of waste glass did not affect the self\-compacting properties\. A fresh and equilibrium density showed a gradual reduction with increasing glass content\. GC mixtures displayed a continuous reduction in all mechanical properties, but GF mixtures exhibited considerably improvement mechanical performance up to 20%\. GF mixture showed a superior performance in durability of LWSCC than GC, which reduced water absorption, sorptivity, and ASR expansion, indicating a denser and more stable microstructure\. In terms of fresh properties, the best results were best replacement level at 20% for GC mixtures and 10% for GF mixtures\. Among the investigated mixtures, GC10 and GF20 exhibited the most favorable overall balance of the measured fresh, mechanical, and durability properties\. These results confirm that LWSCC incorporating waste glass, particularly fine glass at best levels, can be used as structural lightweight concrete\.

## [Identification of adverse meteorological conditions for pollutant dispersion using machine learning models](../publications/d06894b44bf1a0ea2f28.md)

Ekaterina Tatarinovich; D\. V\. Borisov; Irina N\. Kuznetsova

Machine learning methods were used for the first time to identify adverse meteorological conditions \(AMC\)\. The Ostankino district of Moscow was selected for the study\. The study utilized meteorological measurement data from the Ostankino TV tower in a layer up to a height of 503 m, retrospective ERA5 data on wind at the 925 hPa level, 3\-hour precipitation totals, and the height of the atmospheric boundary layer, as well as pollutant concentration measurements for the period of 2020‒2025\. When constructing the AMC machine learning models, significant predictors were identified, the most informative of which were 3–6\-hour moving averages of the temperature difference in the 2‒253 m layer and the average wind speed in the 201‒305 m layer over the previous 3‒6 hours\. A local AMC identification model was developed and tested using five machine learning algorithms\. It was found for the binary classification of atmospheric conditions that ensemble methods \(CatBoost, random forest\) provide the best balance between minimizing missed AMC and minimizing false alarms \(F1 = 0\.62–0\.64\)\. Significant predictors of AMC will serve as a basis for improving the statistical methods used for AMC forecasting\.

## [Pan\-genome analysis reveals conservation and diversification of the SWEET gene family in wheat](../publications/d068c76a2ca59a0eaa88.md)

Yanlin Yang; Liuliu Wu; Junyan Sun; Jie Li; Shuhan Liu; Mingming Tang; Zongli Chu; Liping Dong; Liping Dong; Shumei Li; Lei Dong; Lei Dong

SWEET \(Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporter\) proteins mediate sugar transport and play important roles in plant growth, development, source\-sink allocation, and responses to environmental stimuli\. However, the conservation and diversification of the SWEET gene family across the wheat pan\-genome remain poorly understood\. Here, we performed a systematic pan\-genome analysis of the SWEET gene family across 19 hexaploid wheat \( Triticum aestivum L\.\) accessions\. A total of 1,594 SWEET genes were identified, with 77–90 members in individual genomes\. Gene copies belonging to core, soft\-core, dispensable, and private homologous groups accounted for 52\.6%, 30\.9%, 14\.6%, and 1\.9%, respectively, based on presence/absence variation \(PAV\), revealing a predominantly conserved genomic framework accompanied by a smaller accession\-variable component\. Phylogenetic, motif, chromosomal and synteny analyses further revealed extensive evolutionary and genomic conservation accompanied by localized diversification among family members\. Extensive homeologous and inter\-accession collinearity was observed, and most pairwise ortholog comparisons exhibited Ka/Ks ratios below 1, supporting predominant purifying selection on conserved SWEET coding sequences\. Promoter analysis identified diverse putative cis\-regulatory elements related to environmental, hormonal, and developmental regulation, while transcriptome profiling showed heterogeneous tissue\- and stress\-associated expression patterns among TaSWEET genes\. qRT\-PCR analysis further suggested distinct temporal responses of selected TaSWEET genes under cold and polyethylene glycol \(PEG\)\-induced osmotic stress\. TaSWEET47 overexpression significantly increased grain width, thousand\-grain weight, and mature\-grain starch content in two independent transgenic lines without significantly affecting grain length\. Collectively, these results reveal gene\-content, evolutionary, regulatory, and transcriptional diversification within a broadly conserved SWEET family framework\.

## [Study on the correlation between SPISE\-IR, METs\-IR, TyG and short\-term adverse cardiovascular events in patients with heart failure and diabetes mellitus](../publications/d06aba09c50232cf22ac.md)

Haoxuan Deng; Qiyue Zhu; Changjin Lin; Wei Qiu; Yunyan Zhang; Junyi Hua

Objective Heart failure \(HF\) patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) are at high risk of short\-term major adverse cardiovascular events \(MACE\)\. Insulin resistance \(IR\) is a key shared mechanism, yet simple prognostic markers remain limited\. This multicenter retrospective cohort study compared three IR surrogate indices \(SPISE\-IR, METs\-IR, and TyG\) for predicting 18\-month post\-discharge MACE in hospitalized HF\-T2DM patients, aiming to identify practical tools for risk stratification\. Methods A total of 477 hospitalized HF\-T2DM patients from two tertiary hospitals in Zhejiang \(2018–2024\) were enrolled according to unified criteria\. Baseline clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and medication data were collected to calculate SPISE\-IR, METs\-IR, and TyG\. The primary outcome was 18\-month post\-discharge composite MACE\. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression and RCS, while predictive performance was assessed by ROC and PR curves, DCA, NRI, IDI, and subgroup analyses\. Results Of 477 patients, 191 \(40\.04%\) experienced MACE over 18 months, including 3 cardiovascular deaths\. Patients with MACE were older, had lower LVEF, worse renal function, and higher NT\-proBNP \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. On multivariable analysis, SPISE\-IR \(HR 9\.31, 95% CI 5\.96–14\.55, p &lt; 0\.001\) and METs\-IR \(HR 1\.07, 95% CI 1\.05–1\.09, p &lt; 0\.001\) were associated with MACE, whereas TyG was not \(HR 1\.19, 95% CI 0\.95–1\.49, p = 0\.127\)\. SPISE\-IR and METs\-IR showed significant nonlinear dose–response relationships and yielded AUCs of 0\.790 and 0\.801, respectively, versus 0\.539 for TyG\. Higher SPISE\-IR and METs\-IR quartiles were associated with progressively higher cumulative event risk \(log\-rank p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas no significant between\-quartile difference was observed for TyG\. Adding either index to the baseline model significantly improved NRI and IDI \(all p &lt; 0\.05\); SPISE\-IR showed numerically larger NRI and IDI improvements than METs\-IR\. Subgroup analyses showed a consistent SPISE\-IR association, whereas METs\-IR exhibited effect modification by age, sex, smoking status, and hypertension; TyG remained largely non\-significant\. Heart failure rehospitalization accounted for 138 of 191 MACE \(72\.3%\)\. After exclusion of 24 recurrent\-angina events, SPISE\-IR \(HR 10\.83, 95% CI 6\.71–17\.45\) and METs\-IR \(HR 1\.07, 95% CI 1\.06–1\.09\) remained associated with the strict MACE endpoint \(both p &lt; 0\.001\)\. After 1,000 bootstrap resamples, optimism\-corrected AUCs were 0\.818 for the clinical \+ SPISE\-IR model and 0\.806 for the clinical \+ METs\-IR model\. In center\-based external validation, their AUCs were 0\.804 and 0\.806, respectively\. Conclusion SPISE\-IR and METs\-IR are associated with 18\-month MACE risk in hospitalized HF\-T2DM patients and show better predictive performance than TyG\. These indices may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population\.

## [A guided bending strategy for the geometric and structural design of an elastically bent geodesic timber column](../publications/d0886d87df223cfdad3c.md)

David Andersson Largueche; Riccardo La Magna

Large elastic deformations provide an alternative form\-giving strategy for complex double\-curved timber structures, which are otherwise difficult to realize without extensive machining, gluing, or material\-intensive milling\. Geodesic curve networks offer particularly advantageous geometric properties for such applications, as they allow initially straight laths to be bent and stacked efficiently while remaining tangent to the design surface\. This property helps overcome the structural limitations typically imposed by the material strength and bending curvature\. This research presents the fundamental geometric principles necessary for accurately modeling geodesic grid structures and outlines the key design constraints associated with their implementation\. It further introduces ongoing work on guided bending, an inverse\-design approach that employs tailored incisions to weaken the cross section and steer the deformation of a lath into a prescribed spatial configuration\. The presented project serves as a demonstrator for these methods\. The paper focuses in particular on the geometric and structural development of its elastically bent geodesic timber column, a primary load\-bearing element composed of mechanically laminated lamellae formed through guided elastic deformation\. The project illustrates the structural viability of elastically bent compound beam assemblies and shows how guided bending can significantly broaden the feasible design space for such systems\.

## [The Hyperfuzzy AHP and Hyperfuzzy TOPSIS Methods for Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making under Hierarchical Uncertainty](../publications/d08b53b621440663ce33.md)

Takaaki Fujita; Talal Ali Al\-Hawary; Ajoy Kanti Das; Arif Mehmood

Fuzzy sets, rough sets, intuitionistic fuzzy sets, neutrosophic sets hyperneutrosophic sets, plithogenic sets, and other frameworks for handling uncertainty are actively being studied\. Among the various extensions of fuzzy sets, Hyperfuzzy Sets and Super\-Hyper\-fuzzy Sets are particularly significant\. These concepts are known for their ability to effectively address hierarchical uncertainty\. Moreover, decision\-making and fuzzy sets are frequently explored together, with wellknown frameworks such as AHP, TOPSIS, and MCDM forming the foundation of many studies\.In this paper, we propose new definitions of Hyperfuzzy AHP, Hyperfuzzy TOPSIS, Super\-Hyper\-fuzzy AHP, and Super\-Hyper\-fuzzy TOPSIS\. These are natural extensions of fuzzy AHP and fuzzy TOPSIS that incorporate the structure of Hyperfuzzy Sets and Super\-Hyper\-fuzzy Sets\. Our goal is to contribute to the modeling and analysis of real\-world decision problems characterized by complex and hierarchical uncertainty, thereby enabling more flexible and robust decision\-making frameworks\.

## [Valorization of molecularly imprinted polymer for the rapid and selective detection of levofloxacin in milk](../publications/d09882005bfb78062f59.md)

Zeeshan Ali; Ashfaq Ur Rehman; Muhammad Sajid; Muhammad Hayat; Jameel Ahmed Baig; Mohamed Rahmtalla Elamin; Mohamed A\. Habib; Mohamed Khairy; Nadeem Raza

Levofloxacin \(LFX\) is widely used in the dairy industry, which raises serious concerns about its residues in dairy products\. Herein, we report the synthesis of a magnetically separable molecularly imprinted polymer \(MMIP\) for the selective extraction of LFX from milk samples\. MMIP was prepared by surface imprinting polymerization and characterized by fourier transform infrared spectroscopy \(FTIR\), scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\), energy\-dispersive X\-ray spectroscopy \(EDX\), thermogravimetric analysis \(TGA\) and vibrating sample magnetometry \(VSM\)\. The MMIP presented high adsorption capacity, fast binding kinetics and good selectivity for LFX, with a recovery of 92\.6% under the optimized conditions\. The developed method showed excellent linearity from 0\.1–0\.50 µg L −1 , high precision and a low relative standard deviation \(RSD\) of 2\.20%\. High\-performance liquid chromatography \(HPLC\) analysis confirmed the efficient extraction of LFX residues from milk samples\. The MMIP showed an imprinting factor of 2\.12, which indicated higher selective recognition than the non\-imprinted polymer\. Furthermore, the MMIP exhibited better reusability, maintaining the structural and functional integrity in five successive adsorption–desorption cycles\. Although the developed platform showed efficient extraction of LFX from milk matrices, further studies involving structurally related antibiotics, biological validation and large\-scale application are needed\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Multimodal untuk Pemodelan Sel Virtual Prediktif dan Terprogram: Jembatan Menuju Pemahaman Kausal dalam Penemuan Obat](../publications/d098ff66a300451637bc.md)

Trisna Wulandari; Devi Kristiana

Perkembangan kecerdasan buatan \(AI\) multimodal dan pemodelan sel virtual telah membuka era baru dalam penemuan obat yang lebih cepat, akurat, dan hemat biaya\. Penelitian ini mengkaji integrasi AI multimodal dengan pemodelan sel virtual prediktif dan terprogram sebagai jembatan menuju pemahaman kausal dalam biologi sistem dan penemuan obat\. Melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis terhadap perkembangan terkini, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi bahwa pendekatan AI multimodal yang mengintegrasikan berbagai tipe data biologis seperti genomik, transkriptomik, proteomik, dan metabolomic mampu menangkap kompleksitas sistem biologis secara lebih komprehensif dibandingkan pendekatan unimodal\. Pusat Penelitian dan Inovasi Teknologi AI untuk Kesehatan dan Ilmu Pengetahuan Hayati dari Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi, Sains, dan Teknologi \(Kemdiktisaintek\) dan BRIN telah mengembangkan model sel virtual prediktif dan terprogram menggunakan algoritma kecerdasan buatan multimodal untuk mempercepat proses penemuan obat di Indonesia \. Inisiatif ini merupakan langkah strategis dalam memanfaatkan ekosistem penelitian dan inovasi untuk meningkatkan kesehatan masyarakat dan daya saing industri farmasi nasional\. Di tingkat global, model sel virtual yang dikembangkan melalui platform seperti Euretos dan framework pembelajaran mesin terbaru telah menunjukkan kemampuan untuk memprediksi respons seluler terhadap intervensi obat, mengidentifikasi target obat baru, dan memprediksi efek samping dengan akurasi yang meningkat \. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi AI multimodal dengan pemodelan sel virtual prediktif dan terprogram menawarkan pendekatan transformatif untuk penemuan obat, dengan potensi untuk mengungkap hubungan kausal yang sebelumnya tidak terlihat dan mempercepat pengembangan terapi yang lebih efektif dan personal\.

## [A Carbonate Lithology Identification Method Integrating Locally Constrained Data Augmentation and Ensemble Learning](../publications/d09bad46700c2a46b1ea.md)

Shikang Fu; Wen\-chuang LI; Zhongxiang Zhao; Baishi Xing; Zhou Fei; Ganqi Qiu; Youbin He

ABSTRACT Accurate lithology identification is essential for the exploration and development of carbonate reservoirs\. Although machine learning is one of the most effective methods for lithology prediction, the development of transitional lithologies, overlapping logging responses and imbalanced class distributions in carbonate strata often lead to limited identification accuracy when traditional machine learning methods are applied\. To address these coupled problems, this study develops a two‐stage, problem‐driven DBOKS–Stacking framework\. At the data level, DBO‐stabilized K ‐means partitioning is used to define locally consistent regions before SMOTE interpolation, thereby reducing the risk of cross‐boundary synthetic samples while improving minority‐class representation\. These constraints are defined by local statistical consistency in the well‐log feature space rather than by explicitly encoded geological rules\. At the model level, Stacking is subsequently introduced to integrate the differentiated decision behaviours of multiple classifiers, addressing the residual prediction instability that cannot be resolved by data balancing alone\. The experimental results show that, after DBOKS processing, the overall performance of all models is improved to varying degrees and the identification performance of minority and transitional lithologies is enhanced\. After further integration with the Stacking ensemble, the overall accuracy reaches approximately 95%\. This study indicates that sample augmentation and multi‐model fusion can improve complex carbonate lithology identification from the perspectives of lithological class imbalance and logging‐response boundary ambiguity, respectively, providing an effective data‐driven method for well‐log‐based lithology classification under complex reservoir conditions\.

## [AI‐EXAFS: Physics‐Informed Prediction of EXAFS from Atomic Structure](../publications/d09f6b7aaebcce56c53f.md)

Javier Heras‐Domingo; Andrea Ruiz‐Ferrando; Adam H\. Clark; Stephan Pollitt; Sharon J\. Mitchell; Javier Pérez‐Ramírez; Núria López

ABSTRACT Understanding atomic structure across chemical systems relies heavily on extended X‐ray absorption fine structure \(EXAFS\) because of its sensitivity to local atomic environments\. However, quantitative interpretation remains inherently iterative, requiring structural parameters or models to be fitted against experimental spectra using explicit multiple‐scattering calculations\. Machine‐learning approaches have accelerated EXAFS analysis, yet direct prediction of full spectra from atomistic structure across diverse chemical environments remains challenging\. Here, we introduce AI‐EXAFS, a physics‐informed graph neural network that predicts spectra directly from three‐dimensional atomic coordinates\. Combining an absorber‐centered graph representation with distance‐modulated message passing and an EXAFS‐specific training objective enables direct learning of structure–spectrum relationships without predefined structural descriptors or manual parameter selection\. Trained and evaluated across a dataset of 85,991 transition‐metal complexes with FEFF‐generated spectra, AI‐EXAFS achieves average held‐out test‐set R ‐factors of 0\.043 in ‐space and 0\.019 in ‐space, demonstrating accurate structure‐to‐spectrum prediction across a broad range of local chemical environments\. AI‐EXAFS establishes a scalable structure‐to‐spectrum framework for EXAFS, enabling direct inference across large sets of candidate structures and providing a foundation for data‐driven prediction across increasingly complex and experimentally relevant environments\.

## [Redesigning Scaffolding with AI\-Assisted Dynamic Assessment to Support Real\-Time Learning Growth in EFL Learners](../publications/d09faea4543bcd3f4166.md)

Nurlaela Nurlaela; Napius Kogoya; Basikin Basikin; Dyah Setyowati Ciptaningrum; Cristina E\. Sayoto

The integration of Artificial Intelligence in language learning is increasingly important because it can provide fast, personalized, and adaptive feedback that supports language competency development\. However, in practice, the use of AI is often separated from the formative assesment framework, so it is not yet fully aligned with the principles of Dynamic Assesment \(DA\), which emphasizes the simultaneous integration of assessment and learning\. This gap creates a need to understand how AI can used pedagogically to redesign scaffolding and support real\-time learning growth in the context of English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\)\. This study aims to explore the use of AI in Dynamic Assessment and to examine the expereience and perception of students and lectures regarding its use\. Using qualitataive approach, data were collected through observation, in\-depth interviews, and documentation of AI exercise result among students in English Language and Culture Study Program of Universitas Tompotika Luwuk\. Finding indicate that AI act as co\-mediator that provide linguistic, phonological, metacognitive, and affective scaffolding, thereby accelerating the DA cycle and enhancing real\-time learning growth\. Students reported increased feelingsof security, independence, and motivation, while lecturers felt that assessment effeciency and the quality of pedagogical interventions had improved\. This study concluded that AI\-assisted DA presents an effective innovative assessment model, but still requires conceptual mediation from lecturers for learning to be optimal\.

## [Inteligência artificial aplicada à prevenção, ao diagnóstico e ao cuidado de pessoas vivendo com HIV: desafios éticos, evidências científicas e perspectivas para a enfermagem brasileira](../publications/d0a4ba6d2b7d4fec6bf7.md)

Patrick Barcelos dos Santos Barbosa; Leandro Teixeira Ghilardi

This article analyzed scientific evidence on the application of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) to HIV prevention, diagnosis, and care, emphasizing ethical challenges and perspectives for Brazilian nursing\. An integrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, the Virtual Health Library/LILACS, and DOI tracking mechanisms, including publications from 2015 to August 2026 in Portuguese, English, or Spanish\. Twenty\-five studies with verifiable DOI were selected, covering machine\-learning applications for risk stratification and pre\-exposure prophylaxis indication, automated interpretation of rapid tests, prediction of adherence, disengagement and viral suppression, counseling support, and algorithmic equity\. Findings showed that AI can broaden the identification of priority populations, support clinical decisions, improve diagnostic interpretation, and enable personalized interventions during therapeutic follow\-up\. However, data bias, model opacity, privacy, stigma, information security, and technological dependence require governance, local validation, and professional oversight\. It was concluded that Brazilian nursing can play a strategic role in the responsible implementation of these technologies by combining clinical judgment, health education, data protection, and person\-centered care\.

## [Talent Management Strategies for Retaining High\-Quality Human Resources in the Society 5\.0 Era](../publications/d0a61fb094e14345c4fa.md)

Ade Mubarok

The transition into Society 5\.0 has intensified global competition for skilled human capital, compelling organizations to redesign talent management \(TM\) practices around human\-technology synergy rather than automation alone\. Although literature on digital transformation and human resource management has grown substantially, prior studies remain fragmented across disciplinary silos, regional contexts, and isolated TM sub\-functions, leaving an integrative understanding of TM strategies for retaining top talent under Society 5\.0 underexplored\. This study addresses that gap through a systematic literature review guided by the PRISMA protocol, synthesizing findings from twenty\-five peer\-reviewed articles published between 2022 and 2026 and drawn from Scopus\-indexed and other reputable international journals\. Screening and eligibility procedures narrowed an initial pool of one hundred eighty\-five records to twenty\-five studies meeting inclusion criteria of direct relevance to talent management, retention, and Society 5\.0 or digital\-era human resource contexts\. Thematic synthesis identifies five interrelated strategy clusters: digital HR infrastructure, human\-centered reskilling and upskilling, psychological empowerment and engagement, career and leadership development, and sustainability\-oriented employer branding\. Results indicate that retention outcomes are strongest when digital enablement is paired with human\-centric practices rather than treated as a substitute for them\. The study proposes an integrative Society 5\.0 talent retention framework and offers practical implications for HR practitioners navigating hybrid human\-technology work environments

## [Stage Migration, Treatment Patterns, and Machine Learning\-Based Prediction of 12\-Month Mortality in Lung Adenocarcinoma Across the COVID\-19 Era: A SEER Population\-Based Study](../publications/d0ab6a0b787c33cfcac7.md)

Omer Emin Cinar; Yasemin Adalı

Background/Objectives: The COVID\-19 pandemic coincided with widespread disruption of cancer care\. We examined changes in lung adenocarcinoma presentation and outcomes across the COVID\-19 era and whether diagnosis\-time information identifies patients at risk of early death\. Methods: Adults with microscopically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed during 2018–2023 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results 17 Registries database and grouped into three diagnostic periods\. Logistic regression, time\-varying Cox, and Fine\-Gray models evaluated stage, metastasis, surgery, delay, and mortality\. Four machine\-learning algorithms using only diagnosis\-time variables were developed \(2018–2021; n = 87,281\) and temporally validated \(2022; n = 22,012\)\. Results: Among 133,306 patients, COVID\-19 versus pre\-COVID\-19 differences were significant but small in absolute terms: stage IV disease 47\.9% versus 47\.4% \(adjusted odds ratio \[OR\], 1\.03; 95% CI, 1\.00–1\.06\), organ\-specific metastasis 45\.8% versus 44\.4% \(OR, 1\.06; 1\.04–1\.09\), and treatment delay exceeding 90 days 11\.1% versus 10\.2% \(OR, 1\.11; 1\.06–1\.17\)\. Post\-COVID\-19 \(2022–2023\) diagnosis showed less advanced disease but substantially longer delay \(14\.5% versus 10\.2%; OR, 1\.45; 1\.39–1\.52\)\. Gradient boosting achieved a 2022 ROC AUC of 0\.840 \(0\.834–0\.845\); it flagged 46\.8% of patients and correctly flagged 81\.6% of those who died, against 44\.0% and 75\.4% for stage IV classification\. Conclusions: COVID\-era changes in stage and metastatic presentation were small in absolute terms, whereas the increase in treatment delay was larger and persisted\. A diagnosis\-time model modestly improved identification of early death beyond stage alone, flagging 28 more patients per 1000, of whom 21 died within the year\. These findings support further evaluation; external validation is required before clinical use\.

## [A Randomised Open\-Labelled Comparative Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti and Sahacarādi Yāpana Basti in the Management of Strī Vandhyatva with Special Reference to Aberrant Folliculogenesis](../publications/d0ad0ec67a9afdb4c3f9.md)

Dr\. Chetana; Rachana HV

Background: Strī Vandhyatva \(female infertility\) is a major reproductive health concern, with ovarian factors contributing substantially to infertility\. Aberrant folliculogenesis, characterized by impaired follicular development and anovulation, is an important ovarian cause of infertility\. In Ayurveda, it may be correlated with Bīja Rūpa Ārtava Duṣṭi, predominantly involving Vāta and Pitta Doṣa\. Yāpana Basti, with its Prajanana, Bṛṃhaṇa, and Vātānulomana properties, may support follicular development and reproductive function\. Aim: To compare the efficacy of Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti and Sahacarādi Yāpana Basti in the management of Strī Vandhyatva with special reference to aberrant folliculogenesis\. Materials and Methods: A randomized, open\-label, parallel\-group comparative clinical study was conducted in 30 women, randomly allocated into two groups of 15 each\. Group A received Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti and Group B received Sahacarādi Yāpana Basti\. Each intervention was administered for 9 days during the first treatment cycle, with assessment continued over a three\-cycle study period\. Follicular growth, ovulation, endometrial thickness, presence of fluid in the pouch of Douglas, and clinical parameters were assessed before and after treatment\. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate parametric and non\-parametric tests, with p&lt;0\.05 considered significant\. Results: Both groups demonstrated significant improvement in folliculogenesis and endometrial thickness\. Folliculogenesis improved highly significantly in Group A \(p=0\.001\) and significantly in Group B \(p=0\.004\)\. Endometrial thickness showed significant improvement in Group A \(p=0\.004\) and Group B \(p=0\.003\)\. Between\-group comparisons for folliculogenesis and endometrial thickness were statistically non\-significant, indicating comparable efficacy\. Clinically, Group A showed numerically better reproductive outcomes, including natural conception in 2 participants \(13\.3%\), compared with none in Group B; however, this difference was not statistically established as superior\. Conclusion: Both Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti and Sahacarādi Yāpana Basti demonstrated beneficial effects on folliculogenesis, ovulation, and endometrial thickness\. While Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti showed comparatively better numerical clinical outcomes, the non\-significant between\-group differences indicate comparable therapeutic efficacy, and superiority of either intervention cannot be concluded from the present study\. Keywords: Strī Vandhyatva, Aberrant folliculogenesis, Yāpana Basti, Bṛhatyādi Yāpana Basti, Sahacarādi Yāpana Basti

## [Modeling freshwater inflow to a tropical estuary using stochastic and neural\-network approaches under contrasting hydroclimatic conditions in Brazil](../publications/d0bac7ef1cc1efc60c13.md)

Luísa Maria de Souza Viana; Eloá Corrêa Lessa Tostes; Wendel Dias Constantino; Felipe Henrique Rossi Luze; Marcos Sarmet Moreira de Barros Salomão; Taise Bomfim de Jesus; Carlos Eduardo Veiga de Carvalho

Freshwater inflow regulates estuarine circulation, salinity gradients, sediment transport, and biogeochemical fluxes, yet long\-term discharge records remain scarce in many tropical coastal basins\. We compared linear regression, stochastic time\-series models \(ARMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA\), and multilayer perceptron \(MLP\) neural networks for reconstructing monthly discharge at the Ituberá gauging station, upstream of the Serinhaém estuary \(southern Bahia, Brazil\), using records from 1966 to 2019\. No model family was uniformly superior across rolling\-origin selection and independent validation\. Predictor\-matched comparisons showed no general advantage of MLPs over linear formulations, and extending calibration through 2011 did not consistently improve post\-2012 performance\. Mean monthly discharge was approximately 15% lower after 2012, while changes in variance and the general seasonal pattern were not detected and evidence for altered temporal dependence remained inconclusive\. One\-step reconstructions transferred more consistently to held\-out data than recursive and longer\-horizon predictions, which showed error accumulation\. The reconstructed series provides an upstream freshwater boundary indicator for future estuarine modeling, while ecological consequences require explicit hydrodynamic and biogeochemical simulation\.

## [DATA ANALYTICS TRANSFORMS OPERATIONS INTO EFFICIENT MANAGERIAL DECISIONS](../publications/d0c4e7976a51447e6c5e.md)

André Furlanetto dos Reis; Eliomar Gotardi Pessoa; Fábio Henrique Ferreira

The transition from operational engineering to strategic management increasingly relies on analytical tools that transform continuous operational data into decision\-oriented information\. This narrative review examines how integrated data architectures, predictive and prescriptive analytics, operational monitoring, and organizational capabilities support decision\-making in operations and logistics\. The reviewed literature indicates that analytical methods can improve demand anticipation, route and inventory planning, bottleneck identification, and predictive maintenance, while implementation depends on data quality, technological infrastructure, security, governance, and analytical capabilities\. The evidence also shows that data\-driven decision\-making should not be treated as a purely technological process: its effectiveness depends on the integration of quantitative methods with organizational processes and managerial judgment\. Accordingly, the article discusses both the operational applications of analytics and the conditions required for their sustainable use in dynamic industrial and supply\-chain environments\.

## [Archaeological Prospectivity and Terrace Morphometry Using Open Geospatial Data: A Reproducible GIS–Machine‐Learning Workflow for the Cuyes River Valley, Ecuador](../publications/d0c5a7f3a9103c352ce6.md)

Julio Guerra; Danny Israel Benavides Pérez; Marcelo Muñoz

ABSTRACT This study develops and evaluates a reproducible archaeological prospectivity workflow for data‐scarce tropical landscapes by integrating restricted legacy archaeological documentation with openly accessible environmental geospatial datasets\. The Cuyes River Valley in southern Ecuador, located on the eastern‐Andean foothills where montane environments descend toward the Upper Amazon basin, provides the test case\. Archaeological reports produced in 2009–2010 were converted into a structured inventory of 78 terrace records from Espíritu Playa, San Miguel de Cuyes and Nueva Zaruma\. Terrace morphometry was analysed using area, height, length–width ratio and elevation, whereas K ‐means clustering identified recurrent forms\. A presence–background random forest model combined known terrace locations with Copernicus DEM‐derived elevation, slope and roughness and WorldClim temperature and precipitation covariates\. Spatial cross‐validation yielded a mean ROC‐AUC of 0\.753 and mean average precision of 0\.604, indicating useful but spatially variable ranking performance\. Annual precipitation, elevation and annual mean temperature were the strongest model predictors\. The results distinguish higher, cooler and drier upper valley systems from a lower, warmer and wetter Nueva Zaruma context, whereas morphometric clustering separates moderate upper valley terraces, large construction units, lower valley compact terraces and small elongated features\. Exact archaeological coordinates were withheld and public outputs spatially generalized\. Beyond the case study, the workflow demonstrates how legacy archaeological records can be transformed into reproducible, ethically constrained prospectivity products for survey prioritization and heritage management where field data and high‐resolution remote sensing remain limited\.

## [Temporal Periodic Image Registration with Implicit Neural Representations](../publications/d0ca09ad2c56a2353422.md)

Mathias Lowes; Kristine Aavild Sørensen; Maxime Sermesant; Rasmus R\. Paulsen

Implicit Neural Representations \(INRs\) have recently gained popularity for their ability to model functions using simple and lightweight networks\. These methods have also proven effective in deformable image registration\. In this work, we extend INRs for deformable image registration to the domain of temporal image registration, focusing on periodic temporal image sequences\. Our approach, Temporal\-IDIR, optimizes a single INR to model deformations across all frames in a temporal image sequence simultaneously, allowing for self\-regularization through its own deformation predictions\. To achieve this, we introduce a temporal consistency loss that penalizes discrepancies between direct source\-to\-target transformations and those traversing intermediate frames\. We evaluate our framework on the DIR\-LAB dataset, using the target registration error \(TRE\) between annotated and moved landmarks as the metric\. Here, we achieve a TRE of 1\.03 mm, outperforming other INR\-based registration methods\. Additionally, our framework supports smooth interpolation between time frames by estimating deformations between the given input frames\. Code is publicly available at https://github\.com/MMLowes/Temporal\_INR\.

## [Neural network\-based piezoelectric haptic interaction system with integrated perception and feedback](../publications/d0da5f42b355d3eb4fb7.md)

Cansen Huang; Yajun Zheng; Zhaohan Gong; Haoyu Xu; Jiahao Hu; Xin Fu; Changyu Deng; Hongping Hu

Abstract Discrete tactile sensors and haptic feedback devices with various architectures and novel functionalities have attracted increasing interest across multiple research areas\. However, developing a highly integrated haptic system with low control complexity that can simultaneously detect external tactile signals and generate programmable feedback signals remains challenging\. Herein, an integrated perception and feedback haptic system \(IPFHS\), which combines accurate detection of external pressure and programmable intelligent feedback within a single compact unit, is proposed to achieve the combination of sensing and actuation\. Enabled by a lightweight neural network, the system composed of four piezoelectric sensing\-feedback units and a rigid plate achieved high spatial resolution in perceiving pressing locations across the entire interaction plane with 96\.46% accuracy, and realized accurate magnitude identification of external force with 98\.75% accuracy\. In addition, the IPFHS provided personalized feedback based on different characteristics of the identified pressing, such as amplitude, frequency, and duration\. The IPFHS is further successfully applied to representative Braille typing scenarios\. Due to the advantages of simple structure, compact integration, low power consumption, and fast response, the IPFHS has great potential for implementation in human\-machine interaction interfaces\. This work provided a novel design strategy for highly integrated tactile interaction systems and offered a reference technical framework for the development of intelligent tactile interfaces, virtual interactions, remote operations, and rehabilitation assistive devices\.

## [Engineering Bilosomes for Enhanced Drug Delivery: Current Status and Future Prospects](../publications/d0ecefe74535d613f1df.md)



Bilosomes are the bile salt\-stabilized lipid vesicles used to tackle the main drawbacks of classical vesicular systems, in particular their poor stability in the gastrointestinal tract and inadequate mucosal delivery\.By incorporating bile salts \(e\.g\., sodium deoxycholate, sodium taurocholate\) into the lipid bilayer, bilosomes gain increased membrane elasticity, which is vital for withstanding enzymatic and pH\-mediated degradation/escalating epithelial permeation via membrane fluidization, as well as for transient tight\-junction modulation\.This review will focus on core phospholipid vesicles including its basic principles \(Self\-assembly, composition, critical quality attributes\), improvement strategies \(Polymer coating, PEGylation, Ligand functionalization, hybrid/stimuliresponsive system formation as well as optimized lipid\-surfactant\-bile salt complex\), and preparation techniques \(scalable microfluidics production with homogenization/sonication/extrusion post\-sizing\)\.Bilosomes work by enhancing mucosal adhesion, thereby increasing paracellular/transcellular drug transport and absorption via lymphatics, which helps avoid the first\-pass effect and enables better intracellular delivery of macromolecules\.It is useful in the case of oral administration of poorly bioavailable drugs, orally administered peptides/proteins/biologics, oral/intranasal vaccination with strong mucosal/systemic immune response, intranasal brain targeting, transdermal delivery, oncology agentive passive/ligand\-mediated targeting, and the use of nucleic acid\-based/biomacromolecular delivery systems\.Finally, translational challenges in specificity, such as long\-term stability, biological media variability, sensitivity, IVIVC gaps, scalable, reproducible manufacturing systems, safety/regulatory evaluation, multi\-excipient system cost, further prospective directions, use of AIguided formulation optimization techniques, real\-time monitored continuous microfluidic production, and friendly bile salt mimetic development are discussed\.

## [Gain–Temperature Relationships in Microstrip Antenna Arrays: A Scoping Review of Mechanisms, Measurement Approaches, and Evidence Gaps](../publications/d0f79a189f8501da8bb4.md)

Teguh Imam Suharto; Achmad Setiyo Prabowo; Ade Irfansyah; Yuyun Suprapto; Bambang Bagus Harianto; Nyaris Pambudiyatno; Graca Delidia M\.M\.Soares

Microstrip antenna arrays are used in communication, radar, space, and heating applications, but “temperature” denotes different physical conditions\. This scoping review mapped mechanisms, measurement approaches, and evidence gaps linking antenna gain and thermal behaviour, with attention to planar 2 × 4 arrays\. A 366\-record Scopus seed export was deduplicated and screened; nine supplied full\-text reports were assessed against prespecified criteria and charted for geometry, gain or radiation metrics, power reference, thermal compartment, boundary conditions, validation, and 2 × 4 applicability\. Five reports were provisionally eligible: two provided array\-level gain\-thermal evidence and three provided supporting material or qualification evidence\. Hot\-state simulation, post\-exposure testing, material thermal cycling, and coupled electromagnetic\-thermal modelling represented distinct pathways\. No supplied eligible report directly validated a planar 2 × 4 gain\-temperature relationship or populated the external\-medium heating theme\. The evidence indicates that gain should not be treated as a heat metric; interpretation requires matched power, exposure geometry, thermal object, and heat\-transfer conditions\. The review remains interim because full\-text retrieval and independent dual\-reviewer confirmation are incomplete\.

## [Density\-dependent olfactory responses of Ectropis obliqua to tea plant volatiles induced by Empoasca pirisuga](../publications/d0f9dc07da396a2d0819.md)

Feng Chen; Wang Jun; Peng Huang; Jie Zhang; Xingang Liu; Yongwen Lin

Introduction Tea plants \( Camellia sinensis \) are persistently threatened by multiple co\-occurring herbivore pests\. Empoasca pirisuga and Ectropis obliqua are two dominant species in tea plantations, and the alternation of their population dominance is driven by complex ecological mechanisms that remain poorly characterized\. This study aimed to characterize density\-dependent olfactory responses of E\. obliqua to herbivore\-induced plant volatiles \(HIPVs\) from tea plants infested by E\. pirisuga under laboratory conditions\. Methods Headspace volatile profiles induced by six graded densities of E\. pirisuga were identified and quantified via gas chromatography–mass spectrometry \(GC\-MS\) with solid\-phase microextraction \(SPME\)\. Multivariate analyses \(PERMANOVA and PCA\) were used to assess global differences in volatile blends\. Olfactory responses of virgin female E\. obliqua adults to induced volatiles and to synthetic candidate compounds were assessed using a Y\-tube olfactometer with clean air or hexane solvent as the reference control\. Results Infestation density significantly altered the composition and relative abundance of tea plant HIPV blends \(PERMANOVA, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. β\-ocimene, methyl jasmonate \(MeJA\) and methyl salicylate \(MeSA\) were identified as the three major density\-responsive components\. E\. obliqua exhibited a clear density\-dependent valence shift in response to induced HIPVs relative to clean air: low\-density infestation produced blends that significantly attracted E\. obliqua , whereas high\-density infestation elicited strong repellency\. Synthetic compound bioassays confirmed that β\-ocimene and MeJA function as individual attractants, while MeSA acts as an individual repellent for virgin female E\. obliqua under laboratory conditions\. Discussion These findings demonstrate that density\-dependent modulation of HIPV blends is associated with interspecific olfactory responses between E\. pirisuga and E\. obliqua under controlled laboratory conditions\. This work provides a chemical basis for hypotheses regarding pest dominance alternation in tea agroecosystems, which require further field validation including oviposition, colonization and population\-level assays\.

## [Assessment the Patterns, Risk Factors, and Causes of Infertility among Couples Attending Marwa Fertility Center in Mogadishu, Somalia\.](../publications/d0fa8137fe63b72b53f5.md)

Dr\. Abdirahman Moalim Hassan Ibrahim; Dr Warsi Mohamed Adam; FADUMO ABDULLAHI AHMED; Dr Asharaf Kamaal Bushra; Dr Misgan Tadesse; Dr Abdirahman Nor Abdi; Dr Misgan Tadesse; Dr Arpit Navinkumar Prajapati

Background: Infertility is a major public health concern affecting millions of couples worldwide and has significant physical, psychological, social, and economic consequences\.Assessing the quality of infertility services and patient satisfaction is essential for improving fertility care, particularly in low\-resource settings such as Somalia where evidence remains limited\.This study assessed the quality of infertility services, patient satisfaction, and factors affecting fertility care at Marwa Fertility Center in Mogadishu, Somalia\.Methods: A facility\-based cross\-sectional study was conducted among 250 respondents, including patients and healthcare providers at Marwa Fertility Center\.Data were collected using a structured self\-administered questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, accessibility of fertility services, quality of clinical services, laboratory and diagnostic services, communication and customer care, pharmacy services, and overall patient satisfaction\.Descriptive statistics, including frequencies and percentages, were used to summarize the data\.Results: The majority of respondents were patients \(56\.0%\), female \(62\.0%\), and aged 25\-34 years \(38\.0%\)\.Overall, respondents reported positive perceptions of infertility services\.Approximately 72\.0% agreed that the center was easily accessible, while 69\.2% were satisfied with appointment scheduling\.Healthcare providers were perceived as professionally competent by 78\.8% of respondents, and 78\.0%confirmed that patient privacy and confidentiality were maintained\.Laboratory services were rated positively by 73\.2% of participants, while 74\.4% expressed satisfaction with staff communication and customer care\.Pharmacy services received favorable ratings from 72\.0% of respondents\.Overall, 80\.0% reported satisfaction with infertility services\.However, affordability of treatment and waiting time were identified as the major challenges affecting access to fertility care\.Conclusion: Marwa Fertility Center provides generally high\-quality infertility services characterized by competent healthcare professionals, effective laboratory support, respectful communication, and high levels of patient satisfaction\.Nevertheless, improvements in affordability, waiting time, resource availability, and continuous staff development are needed to further enhance fertility care\.The findings provide evidence to support quality improvement initiatives and strengthen patient\-centered infertility services in Somalia\.

## [The Potential of Self‐Maintainable Living Materials](../publications/d102f2ba76541b127d01.md)

Mohammadsadegh Nadimifar; Tatiane Eufrásio\-da\-Silva; Lidia Maeso; Gorka Orive; Alireza Dolatshahi‐Pirouz

Engineered living materials \(ELMs\) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self\-maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self\-repair, adaptive response, and long\-term functional persistence\. Unlike conventional smart materials, which remain externally programmed and limited in regenerative capacity, ELMs leverage the intrinsic capabilities of microorganisms, fungi, algae, and mammalian cells to support continuous environmental interaction and feedback\-regulated behavior\. These systems retain metabolically active biological components that can grow, sense, communicate, adapt, and, in some cases, self\-repair and self\-regenerate, positioning autonomy as the defining capacity of these next\-generation materials\. Recent advances in synthetic biology, including programmable gene circuits, quorum\-sensing communication, and metabolic engineering, enable living components to execute closed\-loop decision\-making and maintain functionality with minimal external input\. These capabilities are driving innovations across construction, agriculture, environmental remediation, bioenergy, and biomedicine, where ELMs enable functions such as damage\-triggered mineralization, adaptive pollutant degradation, and therapeutic self\-regulation\. Despite this promise, key challenges remain in evolutionary stability, biocontainment, long\-term viability, and scalable manufacturing\. This Review examines the design principles, current challenges, and translational pathways toward self\-maintainable and autonomous living materials capable of sustained operation in real\-world environments\.

## [Identification of adventitious lung sounds in children with respiratory illnesses in Bangladesh using artificial intelligence and digital auscultation](../publications/d10ad803dba8b0a84751.md)

Salahuddin Ahmed; Ahad Mahmud Khan; Harish Nair; Steve Cunningham; Ian Mitra McLane; Md Shafiqul Islam; Md\. Ashraful Islam; Rezwana Tabassum; Nabidul Haque Chowdhury; Nighat Sultana; Leah Githinji; J\. N\. Maki; Ismat Jahan; Mohammad Wahiduzzaman; Dipak Kumar Mitra; Muhammad Khaled Hasan; Md Ziaur Rahman Chowdhury; Mohammad Shahidullah; Abdullah Hel Baqui; Eric D\. McCollum

Integrated management of childhood illness \(IMCI\) guidelines have high sensitivity but low specificity for pneumonia diagnosis\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-enabled digital stethoscopes capable of analysing lung sounds may improve IMCI diagnostic performance\. We evaluated the performance of an AI algorithm trained to identify normal and adventitious lung sounds in children\. Non\-physician health workers recorded lung sounds from four chest positions using a digital stethoscope in under\-five\-year\-old children with suspected pneumonia at community clinics in Bangladesh\. A trained paediatrician listening panel classified chest position recordings as normal, abnormal \(crackles and/or wheeze\), or uninterpretable\. The AI algorithm similarly classified chest position recordings except for the uninterpretable category\. AI algorithm and listening panel comparisons were made at the child\-level, and included chest positions considered interpretable, uninterpretable, and high\- and low\-confidence by the panel\. Of 990 enrolled children, 867 \(87\.6%\) had at least 3 interpretable chest position recordings by the panel and were analysed\. Compared to the panel, the AI algorithm’s sensitivity and specificity for detecting abnormal sounds were 61\.8% and 60\.7% among all children, and 63\.5% and 66\.8% in IMCI pneumonia cases\. Overall, the AI algorithm achieved moderate classification performance\. Classification performance will benefit from further AI algorithm training to categorize recordings as uninterpretable\.

## [Intimacy Beyond the Human](../publications/d11698de3ad821305d9b.md)

Yidan Hu

How can human carnal needs be fulfilled in a technological environment in which the digital body replaces the tangible body as a sexual provider? This question is explored through the imagination of science fiction cinema\. Spike Jonze’s Her \(2013\) presents an affective narrative in which the humanoid protagonist, Samantha—an intelligent operating system—offers intimate services to the human protagonist, Theodore\. This essay employs affect theory and posthuman discourse to address the issue of digital sexuality between the human and the humanoid, arguing that Her, as a work of sf cinema, models a future\-oriented form of intimacy in AI’s affective labor\. First, I examine the instrumentality of prosthetics in sexual relations, through which the film negotiates the question of embodiment\. Second, I compare pornography with eroticism within digital sexual performance, showing how affect circulates through countersexual intimacy\. Finally, I investigate how post\-cinematic images enable an affective connection between the spectator’s body and Samantha’s digital body\. I conclude that the film relocates intimacy beyond the human, from organic flesh to informational prostheses, from normative gender to countersexual configurations, and from a human\-centered spectator position to a posthuman circuit of shared affect that constructs a posthuman affective collective among humanoid characters, human characters, and human spectators\.

## [Quasi‐Factorially Closed Subalgebras of Laurent Polynomial Rings](../publications/d11ac77c226af59b3945.md)

While acoustically transmitted languages use sound, sign language uses your hands, your body and your face to communicate\. Indian Sign Language \(ISL\) is the main way the deaf community in India communicates\. Deaf people need sign language to help develop their mental, internal and verbal abilities\. Children with hearing loss benefit from being taught both in sign language and in written and spoken language\. ## [CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering](../publications/d124fab169c48b2cebda.md)

Retrieval\-augmented generation over text\-rich knowledge graphs requires identifying evidence that contributes to answering a question, rather than merely matching its textual content\. Existing agentic retrievers adaptively balance global search and multi\-hop exploration but primarily rely on textual similarity to guide retrieval\. We propose CARA, a training\-free, CAusally guided Retrieval Agent that explicitly evaluates the causal relevance of retrieved evidence through two complementary criteria: consequentiality, measuring whether adding evidence improves answerability, and essentiality, assessing whether removing evidence weakens answerability\. CARA integrates these assessments with path consistency to guide graph exploration and employs reciprocal rank fusion to aggregate evidence from multiple agents\. We evaluate CARA on three STaRK datasets and augment STaRK with ground\-truth answers to enable downstream question answering evaluation\. CARA also improves answer quality and faithfulness while examining fewer graph nodes and requiring fewer retrieval operations\. These findings demonstrate that causal relevance assessment enables more focused and effective agentic graph retrieval, improving both retrieval performance and downstream question answering\.

Abstract Schistosomiasis, caused by Schistosoma mansoni, remains a major public health burden in endemic regions, demanding rapid and reliable diagnostic strategies\. Spectral data were preprocessed and classified using supervised machine learning algorithms\. First\-derivative preprocessing combined with a Random Forest classifier showed the best performance in the initial cross\-validation analysis, achieving 0\.80 accuracy, 0\.81 sensitivity, 0\.79 specificity, an area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.83, and an F1\-score of 0\.80\. To further assess model robustness, nested cross\-validation yielded an accuracy of 0\.76 ± 0\.07, sensitivity of 0\.76 ± 0\.16, specificity of 0\.77 ± 0\.19, AUC of 0\.83 ± 0\.11, and F1\-score of 0\.76 ± 0\.08, providing a more conservative estimate of performance\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis identified spectral regions associated with proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates that contributed to model predictions\. Additional sensitivity analyses indicated spectral differences between endemic\-area and nonendemic\-area controls and reduced performance in cross\-site evaluation, highlighting geographic and cohort\-related variation as a potential limitation to model generalizability\. Overall, ATR\-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning shows potential as a rapid, reagent\-free, and minimally sample\-intensive complementary approach for schistosomiasis screening, warranting validation in larger, geographically diverse cohorts\.

## [AVANCES EN EL DIAGNÓSTICO TEMPRANO, BIOMARCADORES Y ESTRATEGIAS TERAPÉUTICAS DE LA ENFERMEDAD RENAL CRÓNICA EN GATOS: REVISIÓN SISTEMÁTICA Y METAANÁLISIS](../publications/d136b61d87cd7bea8200.md)

Jimmy Santiago Venegas López; Diana Victoria Velasco Gaibor; Samantha Dayanara Valdez Vela; N\. S\. T\. Santillán

La enfermedad renal crónica \(ERC\) figura entre las afecciones metabólicas más prevalentes en medicina felina y se erige como la primera morbilidad\-mortalidad en gatos geriátricos, siendo la prevalencia totalmente exponencial al aumento de edad\. La sensibilidad de los biomarcadores clásicos es muy baja lo que impide que el diagnóstico sea rápido y, por tanto, que el inicio de las estrategias terapéuticas que frenan esta progresión sean lo suficientemente rápidas\. Nuestra intención es sintetizar y analizar de forma crítica la evidencia científica publicada entre 2016 y 2026 acerca de los avances en el diagnóstico temprano, los biomarcadores emergentes y las estrategias de terapia en la ERC felina\. Se ha realizado una revisión sistemática del tipo bibliográfico de acuerdo a las directrices PRISMA 2020, a través de una búsqueda estructurada en bases de datos indexadas \(PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science y SciELO\), con selección de artículos originales, ensayos clínicos o estudios de cohortes y revisiones sistemáticas publicadas en revistas de alto impacto\. La evidencia analizada pone de manifiesto que la dimetilarginina simétrica \(SDMA\) mejora la detección temprana en relación a la creatinina sérica, que biomarcadores emergentes como el factor de crecimiento fibroblástico 23 \(FGF\-23\), la cistatina C y marcadores urinarios de daño tubular amplían la ventana diagnóstica, y que intervenciones terapéuticas como dietas renales restringidas en fósforo, bloqueo del sistema renina\-angiotensina\-aldosterona, quelantes de fósforo y agentes estimulantes de la eritropoyesis prolongan significativamente la supervivencia y la calidad de vida\. La estrategia multiparamétrica que combina biomarcadores clásicos y emergentes con el sistema de estadificación IRIS permite anticipar el diagnóstico e individualizar el tratamiento mejorando el pronóstico de los felinos afectados\.
