## [Faster but Not Truer, Part 1: A Systematic Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Health Economics and Outcomes Research](../publications/d1562017483a23405b8f.md)

Onur Başer

Background: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is being introduced into every stage of the health economics and outcomes research \(HEOR\) production line, from literature screening to causal estimation\. The field lacks a defensible count of what has been done, and bibliometric claims about AI adoption circulate without measured error rates\. Methods: Following PRISMA\-ScR, we searched PubMed for AI terms co\-occurring with HEOR terms for publications from 2010 through 2025, retrieved 2642 records, and included 2476 after screening\. Records were classified into 8 nonexclusive application domains and 1 of 6 method categories using a published term dictionary\. To quantify classification error, an independent large language model classifier, blinded to the dictionary labels and given only title and abstract, reclassified a random sample of 300 included records\. We report per label counts, agreement, Cohen kappa, prevalence\-adjusted bias\-adjusted kappa, precision, recall, F1, and a precision\-adjusted corpus size with exact binomial intervals\. We separately assembled the primary performance evidence for each HEOR workflow, requiring a quantitative metric from a primary study\. Results: Included publications rose from 29 in 2010 to 852 in 2025, a factor of 29\.4, with the inflection at 2018 to 2019 rather than at the release of ChatGPT\. AI reached 6\.0% of all indexed HEOR output in 2025 while HEOR fell to 0\.86% of all indexed medical AI output\. Economic evaluation was the most frequently assigned domain \(1559/2476, 63\.0%\), followed by real\-world data and causal inference \(496, 20\.0%\) and governance, reporting, and validity \(494, 20\.0%\)\. Generative AI appeared in no record before 2021 and in 103 in 2025\. Only 154 of 300 sampled records \(51\.3%; 95% confidence interval \[CI\], 45\.7\-56\.9\) were judged genuinely HEOR relevant, implying a precision\-adjusted corpus of 1271 studies \(95% CI 1131\-1410\)\. Agreement was substantial for real\-world data and causal inference \(kappa, 0\.729\) but negligible for economic evaluation \(kappa, 0\.144\), where dictionary precision was 29\.6%\. Of 2476 records, 38 \(1\.5%\) were randomized trials and 17 \(0\.7%\) validation studies\. The replication package is publicly available\. Conclusions: The literature is growing faster than its own measurement infrastructure\. Measured gains concentrate in tasks with observable ground truth, and predictive performance repeatedly fails to predict evidentiary performance\.

## [Robust Covariance Estimation for Entry\-wise Contaminated and Partially Observed Data via Expectation Maximization Algorithm](../publications/d15b78deeb216308f6a5.md)

Matys Savidan; Mohammed Nabil El Korso

Robust covariance estimation under entry\-wise contamination and missing data is challenging in various signal processing applications\. Under the Student\-$t$ model, observation\-level reweighting induces a uniform attenuation across samples, which can lead to cumulative information loss even when most coordinates remain informative\. The alternative Student\-$t^\*$ model enables coordinate\-wise robustness, but its E\-step is not available in closed form\. We extend inference for the Student\-$t^\*$ model to incomplete observations through a stochastic approximation EM \(SAEM\) algorithm operating on a reduced latent space: stochastic updates of the coordinate\-wise scales are combined with Rao\-Blackwellized Gaussian conditional moments, which avoids explicit sampling of latent Gaussian variables while preserving a likelihood\-based framework\. Experiments on synthetic and real sensor data show a lower Fisher\-Rao error than Gaussian, Student\-$t$, imputation\-based and detect\-then\-estimate estimators at moderate to high outlier rates under diffuse contamination\.

## [A Real\-time Multimodal Driver Monitoring System with Context\-dependent Rule\-based Fusion for the Detection of Distraction, Drowsiness, and Sudden Medical Conditions](../publications/d164e24b2b9f229eb782.md)

Hasan Abdulhadi Kazum; Jumana Waleed; Abbas M\. Al\-Bakry

Driver distraction, fatigue, and acute medical conditions are among the main contributors to road traffic crashes\.Most existing driver monitoring systems rely on a single sensing modality or address a single driver state, and few translate a detected state into a graduated safety response\.This paper presents a real\-time multimodal driver monitoring system that combines infrared camera\-based behavioral analysis, wearable physiological sensing, and OBD\-II vehicle\-speed information through a context\-dependent rule\-based decision\-level combination\.The visual subsystem integrates a YOLOv8n driver\-behavior detector, trained for this work on 3,971 annotated in\-cabin images spanning nine distraction\-related classes, with MediaPipe\-based facial, ocular, and hand landmark analysis\.Temporal confirmation, physiological corroboration, and speed\-dependent escalation are applied to produce stable event\-level driver\-state decisions and to suppress transient false alarms\.The system is implemented as an embedded prototype on a Raspberry Pi 5 and evaluated on data from ten participants, comprising 273 annotated unsafe\-driving events and ten normal\-driving segments totalling 51\.1 minutes\.Event\-based evaluation yields a precision of 95\.41%, a recall of 98\.90%, and an F1\-score of 97\.12%, with a reconstructed mean event\-detection delay of 0\.568 s; 98% of matched events occurred within one 1\.0\-s logging interval of the annotated event onset\.No confirmed safety activation occurred during the normal\-driving segments, while 290 transient detections that did not meet the false\-alarm criteria were logged and are reported separately\.The decision parameters are fixed rather than learned, and the results were obtained on a small scripted dataset without a head\-to\-head baseline comparison; they should therefore be interpreted as prototype\-level validation of an integrated embedded architecture and its evaluation protocol rather than as evidence of general real\-world performance\.

## [TREATING THE CHALLENGE OF PNEUMOCOCCAL MENINGITIS USING NOVEL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS](../publications/d167e191aff6b31ec2be.md)

Vaishnavi \. A \. Ghormade; Harsha Sonaye; Jignesh M\. Doshi

Even though vaccinations and effective treatments are accessible, pneumococcal meningitis caused by Streptococcus pneumonia is still one of the major determinants of morbidity and mortality worldwide\. As a result of the rapid progression of disease, increased resistance to antibiotics, and low medication permeation through the blood\-brain barrier \(BBB\), conventional methodologies to treatment are often limited\. Treatment methodologies for CNS infections were totally revolutionized by the recent developments in innovative drug delivery systems \(NDDS\)\. Delivery approaches like intranasal administration, liposomes, niosomes, dendrimers, micelles, nanoparticles, and polymer\-based drug delivery are known to offer better drug bioavailability, extended drug\-release profile, and better drug permeability via the BBB\. The pathology behind pneumococcal meningitis, existing problems with treatment, and the new advances in NDDS have been elaborated on in this review to facilitate effective management of the condition\. The combination of effective antibiotics and advanced delivery systems can bring considerable improvements in the treatment of the disease, reducing its mortality rates and combating antibiotic resistance\.

## [AFFORDABLE PHARMACOGENOMICS IN BRAZIL&\#x27;S UNIFIED HEALTH SYSTEM: COST LEVERS, THE ROLE OF THE CLINICAL PHARMACIST AND THE FARMA\-GEN SUS IMPLEMENTATION MODEL](../publications/d16890bcf210468877ea.md)

Joao Fernandes Floriano; María Elizabeth Menezes

Introduction: Clinical pharmacogenomic guidelines are available, but implementation in Brazil&\#x27;s Unified Health System \(SUS\) faces testing costs, fragmented care pathways and limited reuse of results\. Objective: To examine the determinants of pharmacogenomic costs and value in the SUS and to propose FARMA\-GEN SUS, an author\-proposed implementation model not adopted by the Ministry of Health, combining a multigene panel triggered by a first high\-yield clinical indication, interoperable records and pharmacist–prescriber collaboration\. Methods: Critical, proposal\-oriented essay integrating clinical trials, economic evaluations, Brazilian population studies and regulatory documents in force on 13 October 2026, supplemented by targeted PubMed and BVS/LILACS searches\. Published evidence, illustrative calculations and implementation proposals were considered separately; no primary clinical data were collected\. Synthesis: In PREPARE, clinically relevant adverse drug reactions among patients with actionable gene–drug interactions occurred in 21\.0% of the guided group versus 27\.7% of controls \(OR 0\.70; 95% CI 0\.54–0\.91\)\. The associated economic analysis identified the test price as a major cost driver, without establishing savings for Brazil\. The proposed model prioritises high\-yield clinical triggers, fit\-for\-purpose analytical coverage, structured recording, clinical interpretation and later reuse\. An illustrative CYP2C19–clopidogrel break\-even exercise used hypothetical clinical assumptions and a non\-significant effect from TAILOR\-PCI; with median public\-purchase prices \(2025–2026\), the annual incremental cost of ticagrelor far exceeded the break\-even ceilings against clopidogrel, whereas a counterfactual against universal ticagrelor suggested possible savings\. Results depend on effect size, medicine and test costs and the comparator; the exercise is not a cost\-effectiveness study\. Conclusion: Savings for the SUS have not been demonstrated\. FARMA\-GEN SUS should be evaluated in a prospective comparative pilot measuring health outcomes \(events avoided, QALYs\), safety, micro\-costed expenditure, access, implementation and budget impact before any scale\-up\.

## [Entre algoritmos y cuentos: motivación lectora en educación primaria mediante intervención gamificada apoyada por inteligencia artificial](../publications/d16dacb3294a4045483d.md)

Yuliana Corrales; Carlos Betancourth Correa; Natalia Morales Villaneda

La motivación lectora en la escuela primaria constituye un desafío relevante, especialmente en contextos donde la lectura suele percibirse como una actividad obligatoria y poco atractiva\. Este artículo de reflexión, derivado de una experiencia pedagógica situada, analiza el papel que pueden desempeñar las herramientas de inteligencia artificial \(IA\) y las dinámicas de juego en el fortalecimiento de la motivación lectora de estudiantes de educación primaria\. La re\- flexión se sustenta en la observación de aula y en el análisis de las interacciones, los niveles de participación y las respuestas de los estudiantes frente a actividades desarrolladas en Gimkit, diseñadas con apoyo de herramientas de IA y mediadas pedagógicamente por las docentes\. Las interpretaciones derivadas de esta experiencia sugieren que la articulación entre dinámicas de juego, recursos digitales e inteligencia artificial favoreció mayores niveles de participación, interés y compromiso con la lectura en el contexto educativo analizado\. Esta experiencia invita a reflexionar sobre el potencial de estas estrategias como recursos de mediación pedagógica para fortalecer la motivación lectora, reconociendo que sus aportes se interpretan desde un contexto pedagógico específico y requieren ser comprendidos a la luz de las particularidades de cada entorno escolar\. Este artículo se deriva de una experiencia desarrollada en el marco de la Maestría en Educación Virtual de la Universidad de Manizales durante el periodo 2025\-2026\.

## [“Creatures of the symbolic ocean”: toward a structure\-mapped apperception of synthetic cognition](../publications/d186c7b1c4927545eabd.md)

Qingchen Guo

The rapid integration of Large Language Models has triggered a global policy dilemma regarding anthropomorphism and user dependency\. Because this regulatory challenge is closely tied to an unresolved conceptual ambiguity concerning the nature of AI, this article introduces a phenomenological framework to delineate the essential character of synthetic cognition\. To this end, we demonstrate a functional isomorphism between the generative logic of human consciousness and the computational operations of LLMs\. Specifically, we align human hyletic processing, representation integration, and recursive reflection with the model mechanisms of loss\-driven token embedding, Attention\-FFN synthesis, and recursive policy emergence\. Synthesizing these functional parallels, we propose “Structure\-Mapped Apperception” to conceptualize LLMs as “Creatures of the Symbolic Ocean” navigating semantic currents\. Crucially, this same apperceptive lens delineates the fundamental existential gaps that separate current AI from embodied subjectivity, revealing these systems to be existentially suspended\. Ultimately, this heuristic offers a philosophical basis for AI governance by providing a conceptual framework to mitigate psychological harm and data\-polluting sycophancy\.

## [High\-Quality, Low\-Cost Quasi\-Bulk Hexagonal Boron Nitride Crystals by LP\-HVPE: Machine Learning\-Assisted Process Optimization via XRD and Raman Characterization](../publications/d18d6d39282ce845f406.md)

Abstract Highly ordered, quasi\-bulk hexagonal boron nitride \(hBN\) films were grown on c\-plane sapphire \(α\-Al2O3\) substrates via low\-pressure hydride vapor\-phase epitaxy \(LP\-HVPE\), using industrial\-grade boron trichloride \(BCl3\) and ammonia \(NH3\) as low\-cost boron and nitrogen sources, respectively\. The effects of four key growth parameters \(growth temperature, III/V source flow ratio, growth ambient, and growth pressure\) on the crystalline quality of hBN films were systematically investigated via the single\-variable method\. A gradient boosting regression machine learning \(ML\) model was constructed based on 24 groups of experimental datasets to achieve high\-precision prediction of hBN crystalline quality, with determination coefficients \(R2\) of 0\.96 and 0\.94 for the prediction of X\-ray diffraction and Raman characteristic peak full width at half maximum, respectively\. The optimized growth condition was determined as follows: a growth temperature of 1350 °C, a III/V ratio of 1:3, N2 ambient, and a growth pressure of 100 Pa, which is consistent with the global optimal parameters obtained by Bayesian optimization combined with the ML model\. This work provides a low\-cost, high\-efficiency route for the controllable preparation of high\-quality quasi\-bulk hBN crystals via LP\-HVPE with ML\-assisted optimization\.

## [Detecting Fuel Adulteration in Otto\-Cycle Vehicles Using On\-Board Diagnostics Data and Machine Learning–Based Anomaly Detection](../publications/d18e9e83ff3dab7b27c7.md)

André Ricardo Marchezan; Mateus Giesbrecht

Fuel adulteration increases operating costs, reduces vehicle efficiency, and contributes to air pollution\. Fuel\-quality verification typically requires laboratory infrastructure or dedicated sensors that are not available to most end users\. In our previous work, we demonstrated that a software\-only approach based on standard on\-board diagnostics \(OBD\) signals and supervised machine learning can detect water adulteration in hydrated ethanol under real\-world driving conditions with high accuracy\. However, supervised classifiers remain challenging because fuel\-trim dynamics vary across vehicles due to powertrain calibration, component aging, and operating environments, which can limit model generalization\. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a detection framework that learns a vehicle\-specific baseline of normal operation using gradient boosting regression \(GBR\) and flags anomalous events through residual\-based cumulative sum \(CUSUM\) monitoring\. The baseline model is trained using compliant\-fuel data, and the CUSUM decision threshold is calibrated from temporally ordered normal\-operation data using an expanding\-window procedure with an initial warm\-up segment\. Across two vehicles, the proposed framework achieved recall values of 99\.77% and 84\.38%, with F1 scores of 99\.88% and 91\.53%, respectively, while maintaining zero false positives under compliant\-fuel operation\.

## [Urban regeneration as a mobility intervention: Evidence on travel behavior shifts](../publications/d1998fd3f9ff26bbd426.md)

Meng Zhou; Chuqi Huang; Jincheng Jiang; Mingxiao Li; Li Guo

Urban regeneration reshapes urban space and population composition, yet its effects on daily travel behavior remains unclear\. This study examines how urban regeneration influences residents&\#x27; travel behavior using repeated cross\-sectional Household Travel Survey data from Shenzhen, China\. Treating regeneration projects implemented between 2016 and 2020 as a quasi\-natural experiment, we apply a machine\-learning\-enhanced doubly robust difference\-in\-differences framework to estimate the effects of urban regeneration\. The results show that urban regeneration has no significant impact on commuting time, while its effect on commuting distance remains indeterminate\. In contrast, urban regeneration is found to have significantly positive effects on the shares of private car and bus travel, measured by both trip frequency and travel distance, with no significant effects on metro use\. These findings suggest that, besides local accessibility improvements and built environment transformations, urban regeneration may also shape mobility choices through changes in population composition and travel preferences, highlighting the need to integrate transport and social considerations into regeneration policies\. The empirical evidence underscores the importance of viewing urban regeneration as a multidimensional process, in which physical alteration, population restructuring and their mobility implications should be jointly considered in regeneration practice to support more sustainable and equitable urban mobility systems\.

## [Photobiomodulation as a regulator of neuroinflammation: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential in brain disorders](../publications/d1a63aa16ed1576fdcc7.md)

Guillaume Blivet; Cédric Bertrand; David Brauge; Julien Delrieu; Jacques Touchon

Brain disorders, including neurodegenerative, neuropsychiatric, and cerebrovascular diseases, represent a growing global health challenge contributing to disability and mortality worldwide\. Although these conditions differ in etiology and clinical presentation, accumulating evidence identifies neuroinflammation as a shared pathological mechanism\. Involving microglial activation, astrocytic reactivity, cytokine dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and blood–brain barrier disruption, it contributes to synaptic dysfunction, neuronal loss, and disease progression, yet therapeutic strategies targeting these processes remain limited\. Photobiomodulation \(PBM\), the therapeutic application of low\-intensity red to near\-infrared light, has emerged as a neurotechnology capable of modulating biological pathways relevant to neuroinflammation\. Preclinical studies suggest that PBM may influence mitochondrial activity through cytochrome c oxidase\-mediated mechanisms, enhancing cellular metabolism while regulating reactive oxygen species, inflammatory signaling pathways, and tissue homeostasis\. Through these effects, PBM may attenuate neuroinflammatory responses, regulate glial activation, and support neuroprotective processes across multiple neurological models\. This narrative review examines evidence supporting neuroinflammation as a common denominator across major brain disorders and explores the biological rationale for PBM as a therapeutic strategy\. It summarizes the cellular and molecular basis of PBM, its effects on neuroinflammatory pathways, and preclinical and clinical findings across brain disease models\. Preclinical findings consistently support a multi\-target anti\-inflammatory effect, whereas clinical investigation remains at an early stage, with encouraging results in Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis but mainly negative data on primary outcomes in Parkinson’s disease and major depressive disorder\. Further research is needed to optimize treatment parameters, clarify mechanisms of action, and determine clinical efficacy across disease contexts\.

## [Native Geometry vs\. Linear Recoverability: How Alignment Changes Platonic Scaling](../publications/d1a7b118b65576e9095f.md)

Angus Hoy; Austin Lutterbach; Jasper Chong; Aman Kumar; Michael J\. Smith

Do larger models learn increasingly similar representations of the same world? The Platonic Representation Hypothesis \(PRH\) predicts that they should, but similar can mean native cosine geometry\-\-\-nearest\-neighbour structure induced by cosine similarity before any learned alignment\-\-\-or linear recoverability: correspondence revealed by a supervised linear map\. Using matched Legacy Survey and Hyper Suprime\-Cam \(HSC\) embeddings across five model families, we find that Ridge alignment strengthens the relationship between model size and cross\-dataset neighbourhood correspondence relative to native cosine geometry\. The effect appears in all five families and persists when both representations are reduced to dimension, so it is not simply that wider embeddings give alignment more dimensions to work with\. The learned maps remain far from rotations or uniform scaling, and Sparse Autoencoder \(SAE\) and Block\-Sparse Featuriser \(BSF\) features give no advantage over the same alignment applied to dense embeddings\. Model scale thus improves linear recoverability more clearly than native cosine\-neighbourhood correspondence, without establishing convergence toward a shared native metric geometry\.

## [SINADRA: Situation\-Aware Dynamic Risk Assessment for Safe and Permissive Autonomous Systems](../publications/d1b09b68f1474ef35fd8.md)

Jan Reich

Runtime safety monitors are a key safety measure for autonomous systems, but they are often designed for worst\-case behavior of other agents and the environment\. This keeps safety arguments simple, yet it can make systems overly conservative, with unnecessary stops, large distances, and reduced throughput\. The core problem addressed in this dissertation is how to increase monitor permissiveness without weakening safety justification: when a monitor relaxes an environment assumption, engineers must be able to argue why this relaxation is safe in the relevant hazardous situations and within the stated operational design domain\. This dissertation proposes Situation\-Aware Dynamic Risk Assessment \(SINADRA\), an engineering method that extends hazard analysis and risk assessment \(HARA\) work products so that they support monitorable low\-risk situation hypotheses for adaptive constraint relaxation\. SINADRA targets risk variability that stems from external agent behavior like human workers in warehouses or human drivers in traffic\. The method has three main elements\. First, Structured Environment Models \(SEM\) scope each hazardous situation into an explicit, risk\-driven environment view, including initiator scenarios and environment factors that matter for risk\. Second, Critical Behavior Cause Trees \(CBCT\) refine hazardous situations into behavior risk scenarios and relate these scenarios to risk implausibility hypotheses – monitorable situation conditions indicating low risk – and other safety measures from the safety concept like system behavior restrictions\. CBCTs form a Boolean model that supports minimal cut set analysis as reviewable verification evidence that, within the modeled scope, risk scenarios are sufficiently blocked by hypotheses and safety measures\. Third, SINADRA provides a runtime model transformation that turns argued hypotheses into executable inference components, using either Boolean logic or Bayesian networks \(BNs\)\. SINADRA is evaluated in two case studies\. A warehouse robotics study executes the full design\-time chain, integrates Boolean runtime models into a ROS\-based safety monitoring system, and demonstrates hypothesis\-driven mode switching with worst\-case as the default\. An analytic comparison reports estimated corridor travel\-time gains of about 2% for passing and 21% for overtaking under stated assumptions\. An urban automated\-driving study demonstrates component\-level runtime feasibility in CARLA by inferring behavior intent likelihoods with BNs and computing an intent\-weighted collision\-risk signal that differs from a worst\-case baseline in uncritical situations\. Overall, SINADRA provides a traceable path from HARA artifacts to runtime adaptation logic for safer, situation\-dependent permissiveness\.

## [Universal Semantic Enhancement for Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection](../publications/d1bcb3e0f8ffdd4231e9.md)

Siyu Zhou; Yuqin Xie; Hao Yuan; Yingjie Zhou

Weakly supervised anomaly detection on tabular data is an essential task in many label\-scarce applications, since tabular data is widely encountered and it is commonly observed in practice that only a limited number of labeled anomalies are available alongside abundant unlabeled samples\. Most existing methods try to learn features that capture the inherent distribution patterns in the target domain\. However, such features often struggle to provide a complete description of possible abnormal characteristics and are highly susceptible to overfitting the extremely scarce labels\. To address this challenge, we propose a weakly supervised anomaly detection method based on universal semantic enhancement for tabular data, which fuses the universal knowledge from a pre\-trained tabular foundation model with the domain\-specific knowledge learned on the target dataset\. The two types of knowledge are naturally complementary: universal semantics describe the common patterns of tabular data across domains, while the domain\-specific features capture the inherent distributions of normal and anomalous behaviors in the target dataset\. A prototype\-conditioned modulation mechanism is then designed to effectively integrate the two types of features, allowing them to reinforce each other for improved anomaly detection\. Extensive experiments on public datasets show that the proposed method outperforms competitive methods when only eight labeled anomalies are available in the training procedure\.

## [Beyond accuracy: How humans evaluate legally correct but socially controversial legal advice from machines\.](../publications/d1d7e10e7e51e673615a.md)

Benjamin Minhao Chen; Zhiyu Li

AI systems are increasingly used to provide legal advice, raising questions about whether laypeople accept guidance from algorithms\-especially when that advice is legally correct but socially controversial\.We report a preregistered survey experiment with 3,348 adults in mainland China examining how people evaluate identical legal advice when it is attributed either to an AI system or to a human lawyer and when it is accompanied by reasoning or not\.Contrary to expectations of algorithm aversion, attribution to an AI system has no net effect on perceived reasonableness\.However, mediation analyses reveal opposing psychological pathways underlying this null result\.AI\-attributed advice is perceived as more objective, which increases perceived reasonableness, but also as less comprehensive and less attentive to special circumstances, which decreases perceived reasonableness\.By contrast, providing legal reasoning substantially increases perceived reasonableness regardless of source, largely by enhancing perceptions of objectivity\.Qualitative responses corroborate this tension between objectivity and contextual sensitivity in evaluations of legal advice\.Together, these findings suggest that public responses to AI legal advisors are shaped not by rigid attitudes toward automation but by the balancing of competing normative expectations\.The results have implications for theories of algorithm aversion and the design of AI recommendation systems in normatively salient domains\.

## [X\-ray image quality before and after radiographer commenting: A quantitative visual grading characteristics analysis](../publications/d1d7f586925f457b8765.md)

Alexandra Tonks; Frances Gray; D\. Nocum; Y\. Jiménez; A\. Tavakoli Taba; Ernest Usang Ekpo

Introduction The Radiographer Comment and Alert \(RCA\) model was established to provide written alerts of abnormal radiographic appearances identified at acquisition, but its quantitative impact on image quality is unknown\. This study quantifies differences in radiograph image quality before and after RCA implementation\. Methods A total of 234 radiographs encompassing the pelvis, hand, wrist, elbow, knee, ankle, and foot were collected\. This comprised all 117 investigations for these anatomical areas with radiographer comments over 12\-months at one site, and 117 matched radiographs obtained one year before RCA implementation\. Each image pair was displayed simultaneously, but the order and left\-right orientation was randomised\. Seventeen radiographers independently rated image pairs using a visual grading characteristics \(VGC\) analysis scale on seven quality criteria \(rotation, angulation, centering, collimation, exposure, artifacts, diagnostic utility\)\. Data were analysed using VGC Analyser Software v1\.0\.2\. Non\-parametric rank\-invariant statistics generated an area under the VGC curve \(AUC VGC \) to measure the difference in quality between images with and without radiographer comments\. Results Across the combined dataset, images acquired after implementation of RCA received visual grading ratings for radiological quality that were significantly higher than images acquired prior to implementation \(AUC VGC 0\.52, p = 0\.016, CI\[0\.500862,0\.532967\]\)\. Statistical significance at 95% confidence was not met for individual upper \(AUC VGC 0\.52, p = 0\.084\) and lower limb \(AUC VGC 0\.50, p = 0\.746\) regions, but was achieved for the axial region \(AUC VGC 0\.54, p = 0\.012\)\. Quality improvement was driven by improved positioning, particularly rotation \(AUC VGC 0\.57, p = 0\.002\)\. Intraclass correlation coefficient scores were good or excellent \(ICC3,k ≳ 0\.62–0\.97\) and all reached significance \( p \-value&lt;0\.05\), indicating stable consensus and good inter\-rater agreement\. Conclusion Quantitative evidence demonstrates implementation of RCA significantly improves the overall quality of projection radiographs submitted for reporting\. Implications for practice Radiographer image interpretation models can be utilised as tools to improve radiographic image quality\.

## [Use of Generative AI in Scholarly Research: Challenges and Opportunities](../publications/d1ea3285335106942d1e.md)

Marco Marabelli; Robert M\. Davison; Giovanni Gatti; Ankita Srivastava; Monideepa Tarafdar

The focus of this panel report is to present evidence of a panel discussion that took place in October 2025 on the use of generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) in academic research and publishing\. The panel included publishers \(Elsevier, Emerald, Galiot Press, MIT Press, Nature/Springer, Wiley\) and editors\-in\-chief \(representing the Information Systems Journal, Journal of the AIS, Journal of Data Science and ICES Journal of Marine Science\)\. Key outcomes of the panel are the following: \(1\) publishers and editors have some disagreements regarding GAI use; \(2\) besides disagreements, all recognize that GAI is here to stay, and therefore, outstanding issues \(e\.g\., training for PhD students and junior faculty and consequences for unallowed uses of GAI\) need to be addressed jointly; \(3\) GAI is in constant flux, and this is a challenge for publisher and journal policies; and \(4\) it is unclear the extent to which GAI will affect future scholarship outcomes, especially having in mind the potential for scholarly deskilling\.

## [Evaluation of Depressive Symptoms in Children Aged 3\-6 Years: A Parent\-Report Study](../publications/d1f0bfe91e4693834678.md)

Mine Cengiz; Yusuf Aktepe; Burcu Demir Gökmen

BACKGROUND/AIMS:This study aimed to evaluate parent\-reported depressive symptoms in children aged 3\-6 years and to examine the relationship between these symptoms and the socio\-demographic characteristics of the children and their parents\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A descriptive cross\-sectional study was conducted from January to March 2025 and included 236 parents who were recruited by simple random sampling\.Data were collected using a socio\-demographic information form and the child depressive symptom scale\.The results were summarized as counts, percentages, means, and standard deviations, and comparisons were made using Independent Samples t\-tests, one\-way analysis of variance, Kruskal\-Wallis, and Mann\-Whitney U tests\. RESULTS:Depressive symptom levels varied significantly among children, differing by age, sex, and child health\-related factors, such as allergic or chronic diseases\.In addition, family\-related factors, particularly parental chronic illness, were associated with higher levels of depressive symptoms \(p&lt;0\.05\)\. CONCLUSION:Children&\#x27;s depressive symptom levels differ according to certain child and family characteristics\.The findings suggest that, when assessing the psychosocial well\-being of young children, family\-related characteristics, in addition to child\-related factors, may also be taken into consideration\.Further studies with larger sample sizes, longitudinal designs, and intervention\-based approaches are needed to evaluate the potential benefits of psychoeducation and support programs for parents\.

## [ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ ПРИМЕНЕНИЯ ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА В ОБУЧЕНИИ ЗАДАЧАМ НА ПОСТРОЕНИЕ С ПОМОЩЬЮ ЦИРКУЛЯ И ЛИНЕЙКИ В ШКОЛЬНОЙ ГЕОМЕТРИИ](../publications/d206bdb0ee8974e8f911.md)

Ж\.Н\. Әбжан; Ж\.У\. Байдуллаева; Н\.Н\. Турдиева

The study examines the methodology for solving geometric construction problems, which is one of the most complex and important sections of school geometry\. In the modern education system, primary attention is paid to developing students’ logical thinking and spatial imagination\. Geometric constructions enhance students’ cognitive abilities and open the way to a deep mastery of fundamental knowledge\. The distinctive feature of construction problems is that they are based not on ready\-made formulas and memorized algorithms, but on students’ creative exploration and critical thinking\. While performing such tasks, students sharpen their skills in working with drawing instruments, from graphic literacy, and see first\-hand the practical proof of theoretical theorems\. At the same time, during the analysis of geometry textbooks for grades 7\-9 in the course of the research, a limited number of sample construction tasks was noticed\. In our view, students encounter numerous difficulties in independently understanding construction problems using a compass and straightedge\. The goal of the study is to systematize effective methods for solving construction problems and reveal their practical significance\. According to the main hypothesis of the work, in\-depth teaching of geometric constructions significantly improves students’ mathematical literacy\. Along with traditional methods, modern digital tools such as GeoGebra Classic were used during the research\. Modeling problems in an interactive environment allows students to visually grasp construction algorithms\. The results of the study are recommended as a methodological guide for teachers in school geometry classes and elective courses\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and Copyright: Authorship, Ownership, and Originality](../publications/d20c1adccc84a0df104d.md)

N\. Sudarshan; Deepika Nallabelli

This study critically examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and copyright law by focusing on the three foundational concepts of authorship, ownership, and originality\. ## [Super\-Cross\-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease](../publications/d21fe886c566c8f04248.md)

Wenbo Li; Jing Li; Xinyu Ning; Jia‐Hong Tian; Fangyuan Chen; Shu\-Xin Zhang; Ze\-Han Wang; Yu‐Chen Pan; Wei Zhang; Dong‐Sheng Guo

Abstract Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases\. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening\. To address this, we develop a machine learning\-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock\-and\-key” recognition\. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses\. This design confers high\-dimensional cross\-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages\. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1\-month\-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months\. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with &gt;95% accuracy\. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases\.

## [Low\-intensity mind–body exercise for mental health in ageing societies: Tai Chi as a scalable intervention across depression, anxiety, insomnia, loneliness, and cognitive decline](../publications/d22a4d6cb1423dec2cdb.md)

Xiaoqi Zhang; Yaya Shi

Population ageing is increasing the number of older adults who experience overlapping depressive symptoms, anxiety, insomnia, loneliness, and cognitive vulnerability, often alongside multimorbidity, pain, frailty, and functional limitation\. This structured narrative review evaluates Tai Chi as a scalable, low\-intensity mind–body exercise for these interconnected problems\. We synthesised 171 publications identified through PubMed and citation chaining, including Tai Chi\-specific clinical studies, broader mind–body evidence, guidelines, and implementation literature\. Evidence is most consistent for reducing depressive symptoms, improving sleep, and improving balance, with possible benefits for selected cognitive outcomes\. Evidence is weaker for diagnosed depressive or anxiety disorders, loneliness as a primary outcome, long\-term cognitive trajectories, and dementia incidence\. Tai Chi should therefore be positioned as an adjunct to established care, not as a replacement for pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia \(CBT\-I\), or multidomain dementia\-risk reduction\. Proposed pathways include autonomic regulation, sleep stabilisation, behavioral activation, balance confidence, cognitive–motor integration, and group participation; however, most mechanism evidence is indirect or exploratory\. Translation requires clearly specified protocols, active comparators, blinded outcome assessments where feasible, long\-term follow\-up, systematic adverse\-event reporting, cost\-effectiveness analyses, and equity\-focused implementation\. Tai Chi is the most credible as an adaptable component of stepped or integrated care for older adults, provided that programmes are standardised, safely delivered, and evaluated against clinically significant outcomes\.

## [An Adaptive\-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling](../publications/d22b37312a580c5ef9c9.md)

Ying Cao; Yifan Yang; Junqiang Xia; Julia C\. Mullarney; Mário J\. Franca

Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating\. For long duration, multi\-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding\. This study proposes an Adaptive\-Horizon Graph Neural Operator \(AH\-GNO\) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments\. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes\. The approach integrates area\-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length \(K\) and update interval \(B\) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state\. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field\-scale application \(Waiho River, New Zealand\)\. Results show that the AH\-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend\-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment\. Across the three cases, the tested CPU\-GPU deployment reduced post\-training bed\-update workflow time from 12\~1204 s with GAIA to 0\.08\~3\.34 s with AH\-GNO\. This improvement corresponds to deployment\-specific accelerations of approximately 150\~360 times relative to 4\-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105\~186 times gains for 20\-core CPU configurations\. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC\-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation\.

## [Cogeneration plant with a low\-temperature piston engine](../publications/d23c2bb53c6d1d79951b.md)

Rymtay SHAIMERDENOVA; Аli МЕKHTIYEV; Sultanbek Issenov; Aleksey Yurchenko; Anar Assylbekova

This paper studies the energy concert and economic feasibility of a moderate cogeneration system based on a low\-temperature piston engine \(LDP\), with a particular focus on its potential use in decentralized rural areas\. A thermodynamic model implemented in MATLAB is used to estimate system behavior, including electricity production, heat recovery, overall efficiency, and key economic indicators\. The results suggest that the system is capable of generating approximately 195,000 kWh of electricity per year, while an additional 292,500 kWh of thermal energy may be recovered and used for practical applications\. In this way, the total useful energy output is estimated to reach about 487,500 kWh annually\. However, these values depend on the assumed operating conditions and the extent to which the recovered heat can be effectively utilized\. From an economic standpoint, the combined use of electrical and thermal energy appears to play a significant role in reducing the overall cost of energy\. Under the conditions considered in this study, the effective energy cost is estimated at around 0\.072 €/kWh, with a payback period of approximately 3\.8 years\. It should be said that the given data may diverge reliant to issues such as petroleum fee, system procedure, and request outlines\. Overall, the findings indicate that LDP\-based CHP systems could represent a practical and potentially cost\-effective solution for improving energy supply in rural and decentralized settings, particularly where both electrical and thermal demands are present\.

## [A quantum\-informed gradient catalyst layer architecture for freeze\-resistant proton exchange membrane fuel cell cold startup via DFT guided machine learning](../publications/d23e9fe9ebe3b05c240a.md)

Muhammad Aurangzeb; Junchen Li; Xiong Shusheng; Li Xinwei; Muhammad Khalid; Ahmed Mohmed Dafalla; Zulkarnain Abbas; Hasan Saeed Qazi; M\. Sami Ul Haq; Abdul Rehman

Cold start represents a critical barrier to automotive PEMFC commercialization, as product water from the oxygen reduction reaction freezes rapidly at sub\-zero temperatures, blocking catalyst active sites and transport pathways\. This work proposes a quantum\-mechanically guided hydrophilic\-hydrophobic gradient catalyst layer architecture optimized for freeze\-resistant cold startup at − 20 °C\. We utilize the Density Functional Theory \(DFT\) results to use N\-doped carbon and MoS 2 quantum dots useful interfaces to perform a systematic analysis of the water binding energies, ice nucleation barrier, and diffusion coefficient of a surface on the material\. The Q\-ICE\-CL framework follows a five\-stage workflow: \(1\) DFT quantum\-mechanical calculations establish water\-surface interaction descriptors for N\-doped carbon/MoS₂ interfaces; \(2\) hybrid XGBoost\-GNN machine learning models trained on DFT data enable inference\-time composition screening within the established design space; \(3\) gradient catalyst layer architecture is designed using DFT\-derived wettability parameters; \(4\) COMSOL Multiphysics simulations pre\-validate the design before physical fabrication, substantially reducing experimental iterations; and \(5\) experimental cold\-start testing validates the fabricated gradient catalyst layer\. The calculated values of quantum parameters inform the design of a three\-zone gradient architecture in which the membrane\-side and proton\-transport zone is mildly hydrophilic \(1\.5% N\-doped\), the core zone compartment offers mixed\-wettability microchannels \(3% N \+ 8% MoS \\\( \{\\text\{\}\}\_\{2\}\\\) \) and the gas diffusion interface is hydrophobic \(5% N \-doped\)\. The hybrid XGBoost\-GNN ensemble achieves R² = 0\.881 \(MAE = 2\.14 s, n = 126 test compositions\) using composition\-structural inputs only, representing genuine independent predictive capability; the full\-feature ensemble including DFT\-linked descriptors that also participate in label construction achieves R² = 0\.946 \(MAE = 1\.24s, n = 126 test compositions\) and functions as a physics\-informed emulator of the DFT\-to\-device performance chain rather than an independent predictor\. Simulations of the gradient design using COMSOL Multiphysics has been performed for future time saving purpose which reveal that the gradient design provides a 108% increase in the freeze\-delay time \(17\.1s\) compared to baseline \(8\.2s\), and a 52% decrease in time\-to\-0 °C self\-heating threshold \(12\.0s\) compared to baseline \(25\.0s\), reduce ice formation \(41\.7% reduction in ice area fraction, and a 97% cold\-start success rate at − 20 °C \(29 of 30 trials\), and tolerate is 5% of performance loss after 200 freeze\-thaw cycles \(compared to conventional Pt/C catalyst layers\)\. These findings establish quantum\-controlled microarchitectures as a significant advance toward reliable sub\-zero PEMFC operation\. This multi\-scale pipeline represents one of the first frameworks to integrate DFT\-computed ice nucleation descriptors with ML\-accelerated screening specifically for cold\-start catalyst layer optimization\.

## [Three\-dimensional progressive damage and geohazard assessment of an open\-pit slope affected by subsurface voids and staged excavation: a case study of the Nanfen mine](../publications/d2431da1c497b0e076fb.md)

Hua Li; Ruijie Gong; Shihui Jiao; Yong Zhao; Yilin Tian; Tianhong Yang; Wenxue Deng; Yawei Li

Historical underground voids and surface excavation can affect the three\-dimensional response of open\-pit slopes\. This study applies geological modeling and an elasto\-damage constitutive model to the east slope of the Nanfen open\-pit mine\. UAV photogrammetry and geological exploration data represent the topography, lithology, and underground voids\. A continuous excavation sequence uses the actual 2024 and end\-of\-2025 mine geometries, followed by the planned end\-of\-2026 and end\-of\-2027 design geometries\. Stress, damage, and historical strain variables are inherited on the retained mesh\. Reported settlement decreases from a baseline maximum of 27\.5 mm to sub\-millimeter values in the final configuration\. The settlement statistics describe the remaining slope surface in each configuration and incorporate changes in the sampled domain\. The damage plots suggest spatial separation between void\-associated and slope\-associated regions\. The simulated sequence captures the combined response to slope cutting and pit excavation\. These results characterize the Nanfen slope under the modeled excavation stages and loading conditions\.

## [Solid Lipid Nanoparticles and Nanostructured Lipid Carriers in Drug Delivery: A Review](../publications/d247d3d8afe46abb55cb.md)

Sandip Kumar; Dr\. Bipul Nath; Bahunshisha Kharsahnoh; Meker Shyrmang; Ruwa O\. Padit

Many pharmacological compounds suffer from poor aqueous solubility, variable bioavailability, fast degradation, unfavorable biodistribution and dose\-related side effects, which restrict their therapeutic efficacy\. Conventional dosage forms may not achieve the appropriate drug concentrations within the therapeutic window, necessitating the development of improved delivery platforms\. Lipid\-based nanocarriers, especially solid lipid nanoparticles \(SLNs\) and nanostructured lipid carriers \(NLCs\), provide intriguing methods owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability and formulation diversity\. SLNs are composed of a largely solid lipid matrix supported by surfactants, while NLCs are a mixture of solid and liquid lipids that form a less ordered matrix with more drug accommodation and less drug ejection during storage\. This review critically discusses recent advances, with emphasis on literature published during 2021–2026, on the evolution, classification, structural characteristics, formulation components, preparation and characterization, drug\-loading and release mechanisms, biological fate, surface engineering, administration routes, and therapeutic applications of SLNs and NLCs\. Special attention is paid to safety, regulatory issues, scale\-up, commercialization and emerging technologies including artificial intelligence\-assisted optimization and microfluidic production\. \[There has been\] considerable preclinical progress but little clinical translation\. Long term stability, reproducible large scale manufacturing, regulatory uniformity, and rigorous clinical validation are significant difficulties that need to be systematically investigated\.

## [Towards machine learning\-based digital twinning for autonomous mobile robot control](../publications/d25257e6be1dc52c2557.md)

Sajad Shahsavari

Digital Twin \(DT\) refers to the technology that enables a synchronized digital replica to mirror the operation of its corresponding physical system\. A representative DT, i\.e\., a comprehensive, high\-fdelity, multi\-physics, multi\-scale, and continuously updated digital representation of a complex physical system, offers signifcant advantages\. These include the ability to optimize system operation at runtime and to test new developments extensively in a controlled digital environment\. In this thesis, we leverage the concept of digital twins to support the control and resource management of autonomous robotic systems\. We demonstrate that a model capable of capturing both the internal characteristics of a robot and the external environmental effects can be effectively utilized for proactive robot control under both long\-term and short\-term operational constraints\. To achieve this, we frst develop a general open\-source DT framework \(MCX\) in which models with different levels of abstraction can be embedded for various robotic subsystems\. We then apply data\-driven and formal models of key mobile\-robot components, such as mechanical dynamics, computational load, and battery behavior, both individually and in combination, to inform actuator control under constraints related to performance, energy consumption, and reliability\. We experimentally demonstrate that separate independent control of mechanical and computational parts does not guarantee an optimal solution for energy management\. Moreover, we show that, by employing even a rather simple DT for proactive control of computational and mechanical parts, robot’s energy management algorithm can operate signifcantly more effciently\. Later, we employ Reinforcement Learning \(RL\) method to learn the robot’s optimal control policy to take into account the energy consumption, mission time and application throughput criteria\. We further consider the degradation of robot’s energy reserve, i\.e\., battery, by proposing a Machine Learning \(ML\) model to quantitatively estimate the long\-term damage on the robot’s battery due to short\-term operational profle\. Experimental results show that exploiting internal modeling of robot behavior for managing long\-term and short\-term operational characteristics signifcantly improves the effciency and robustness of mobile\-robot control across diverse constraint settings\.

## [From digital interaction to social connection: AI virtual humans as interactive learning partners for older adults](../publications/d25dd8bb9e2d38e2df5b.md)

WeiCheng Pan; WanQing Zhang; Hong Chen; Qi Guo; Shuyi Wang; Hesen Li

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) becomes increasingly embedded in educational and social interaction systems, its potential to alleviate digital exclusion and digital loneliness among older adults has attracted growing attention\. Across two independent experiments, this study examined the association between AI\-assisted interaction and digital loneliness among older adults, as well as the underlying psychological mechanisms\. In Experiment 1, 90 older adults participated in a four\-week randomized longitudinal experiment\. A 2 \(group\) × 5 \(time\) mixed\-design repeated\-measures analysis of variance was conducted to compare changes in digital loneliness between an AI\-assisted interaction group and a conventional interaction control group\. The results showed that participants in the AI\-assisted interaction group exhibited a more pronounced reduction in digital loneliness over the intervention period\. Experiment 2 involved an independent sample of 210 participants and used PROCESS analyses to examine further the roles of perceived social support, evaluative emotional fulfillment, and technology acceptance\. After controlling for baseline digital loneliness, perceived social support constituted a significant indirect pathway linking AI\-assisted interaction to post\-intervention digital loneliness, whereas the indirect effect through evaluative emotional fulfillment did not reach statistical significance\. Technology acceptance further moderated the association between AI\-assisted interaction and perceived social support\. Taken together, these findings suggest that the association between AI\-assisted interaction and reduced digital loneliness among older adults is primarily related to the perceived social support pathway\. In contrast, evidence supporting the mediating role of evaluative emotional fulfillment remains insufficient\. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding older adults’ experiences of social connectedness in inclusive AI\-enabled environments\. It underscores the importance of enhancing both the acceptability of AI\-mediated interaction and its capacity to provide social support within educational and digital learning ecosystems\.

## [Physically Active Learning and Primary Students&\#x27; Outcomes: A Bibliometric Science Mapping Study \(2000–2026\)](../publications/d264549a22b92fd277d5.md)

Jeni Arianti Pa Nyola; Mubiar Agustin; Idat Muqodas

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of Physically Active Learning \(PAL\) and its relationship with primary school students&\#x27; learning outcomes\. To the best of the authors&\#x27; knowledge, no prior bibliometric study has exclusively focused on PAL as a pedagogical construct\. Using the Scopus database \(2000–2026\), a modified PRISMA approach, and VOSviewer v\.1\.6\.20, 1,001 articles from 374 journals were analyzed\. The dataset yielded 21,897 citations, an h\-index of 68, and a CAGR of 17\.1% \(2010–2025\)\. Three temporal phases were identified: health\-oriented foundation \(2000–2010\), pedagogical diversification \(2011–2017\), and expansion–consolidation \(2018–2026\)\. Thematic analyses suggest a gradual paradigm shift from PAL as a health intervention toward a pedagogically oriented strategy, reflected in the increasing prominence of embodied learning and movement integration\. The United States dominates global production \(45\.1%\), while Indonesia remains underrepresented \(1\.5%\)\. This study proposes research directions for Indonesian scholars, including traditional game\-based PAL interventions and Merdeka Belajar curriculum integration\. Keywords: Efficiency, Knowledge Management, Tax Administration, Tax Officer, Training

## [MS\-Eval: Benchmarking Sub\-Agent Delegation and Orchestration in MCP\-Intensive Working Scenarios](../publications/d270f90658eaa449f66c.md)

Bowen Ding; Qixin Wang; Lexing Ruan; Weiyi Lu; Qiwei Ge; Ruishan Fang; Tao Lin

LLM agents are increasingly integrated into real\-world works, yet they must handle diverse domain\-specific tools and complex multi\-sub\-task problems that sequential tool invocation resolves inefficiently and with severe context bloat\. The Main\-Agent Delegation and Sub\-Agent Execution \(MAD\-SAE\) paradigm addresses these issues by delegating sub\-tasks to specialized sub\-agents for parallel execution in isolated contexts, but its delegation and orchestration quality remains unquantified\. We introduce MS\-Eval, a unified evaluation kit comprising an MCP\-intensive benchmark, a controlled execution harness, tailored delegation and orchestration metrics, and the MSQ index for comprehensive assessment\. Evaluating four MAD\-SAE variants and eight frontier models reveals that \(1\) sub\-agent specialization \(Spec\) is the best practical practice; \(2\) open\-source models are largely competitive with few exceptions; and \(3\) MAD\-SAE generally raises cost with contingent payoff, benefiting most open\-source models in both performance and efficiency while leaving closed\-source models with higher cost and degraded performance\. Our case study further traces these gains to better single\-agent solutions, effective context offloading, and genuine sub\-task parallelism, whereas unnecessary or redundant delegation turns the same cost into pure overhead\. Codes: https://github\.com/LINs\-lab/MS\-Eval

## [SUN’IY INTELLEKTNI XALQARO HUQUQIY TARTIBGA SOLISHNING SHARTNOMAVIY\-HUQUQIY ASOSLARI](../publications/d276afb586ae3d12963a.md)

Нугманов Нугман Абдуллаевич; Сайфуллаева Венера Ниматжоновна

The international legal regulation of artificial intelligence at the global level is currently one of the key issues being addressed within the United Nations\. The UN International Law Commission and the UN global scientific body are advancing the concept of maintaining the human element in decision\-making processes involving artificial intelligence, while focusing on risk assessment and the assurance of technological safety\. To date, no convention establishing a universal \(global\) legal framework for artificial intelligence has been adopted\. Nevertheless, within the realm of international law and grounded in the UN Charter and generally accepted norms of international law key universal instruments include UN resolutions, the UN Convention on Combating Cybercrime, the “Pact for the Future”, the “Global Digital Compact”, the “Declaration on Future Generations”, and recommendations issued by UNESCO and the Organization for Economic Co\-operation and Development \(OECD\)\. As a result of technological advancements, international information security has emerged as a new field within international relations; currently, international legal experts are addressing issues regarding the legal regulation of information and communication technologies and the development of relevant international standards and principles\. This article analyzes universal and regional models for regulating artificial intelligence in the sphere of information security and proposes the adoption of an international standard that incorporates norms concerning information security\.

## [AI\-Based Optimization Models for High\-Performance Computing and Intelligent Network Architectures](../publications/d2772179b3b06c9caca6.md)

Dr Atthapu Thirupathaiah; K\. Arpitha; Kaushik Paul; Monisha Monisha; Armstrong Joseph J; P\. Mayavel

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has become a necessary technology to optimize High\-Performance computers \(HPC\) systems and intelligent network architecture, such as optimizing the use of resources, the schedulization of workloads and network efficiency\. This paper discusses how the three AI\-based optimization tools, i\.e\., Deep Reinforcement Learning \(DRL\), Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) can be optimized to enhance performance in the HPC environment\. It was done using a quantitative, simulation based, approach on the benchmark HPC workload and HPC network datasets\. Data cleaning, feature selection, normalization and train\-test splitting were used to preprocess the datasets and then model implementation and evaluation took place\. The models were evaluated based on performance such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, execution time, resource consumption, throughput, latency as well as the energy consumption\. Experimental results demonstrated that the DRL model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 96\.8, 93\.8 CPU resources consumption, 96\.1 network efficiency, 12\.8 Gbps throughput and 5\.3 ms \(lowest\) network latency values\. LSTM had the highest prediction accuracy of 95\.2, and XGBoost had a score of 93\.9 with the lowest training time rate of 39 minutes\. The findings indicate that AI\-based optimization is tremendously more effective regarding calculations and adaptability, scheduling, and resource allocation compared to the conventional ones\. The suggested framework offers a viable solution to scalable, smart and energy efficient, intelligent HPC systems, which can be used to support next generations of computing and networking systems\.

## [Agricultural production services and farmland reallocation among wheat\-growing households in China](../publications/d28fc1c648b715ce8275.md)

Yihang Jiang; Yue Sun

Introduction Agricultural production services may influence farmland allocation, but their associations with farm expansion and land retention may differ\. This study examines how service use relates to operated farmland area and land rented in and out among wheat\-growing households in four Chinese provinces\. Methods Using cross\-sectional survey data, we measure service use by expenditure and, alternatively, by the number of production stages served, which is less mechanically related to cultivated area\. We also use two\-part models to distinguish rental participation from rented\-in area conditional on participation\. Fixed\-effects estimates from a separate three\-wave rural panel provide a complementary longitudinal check\. Results Service use is positively associated with operated area and rented\-in area and negatively associated with rented\-out area, although the strength of the rented\-out association varies by measure and model specification\. Service\-stage breadth is associated with participation in renting in land, but not significantly with conditional rented\-in area\. In the longitudinal panel, wheat service expenditure per mu is positively associated with operated area and wheat\-growing area\. Discussion These findings are consistent with agricultural production services being linked to farmland reallocation through both expansion and land\-retention margins\. Proposed labor\-substitution and expected\-return mechanisms remain correlational\. Because the main survey is cross\-sectional and limited to active wheat growers, the findings should not be generalized beyond comparable wheat\-producing settings\.

## [Niami, Morteza: The Deferred Life](../publications/d2979ee924f18db1ab3c.md)



In this book, I develop a philosophical account of deferred living within the framework of Finite Continuance\. I begin with the proposition that human beings frequently organize their present existence around the anticipation of a future in which life will finally become possible\. Happiness is postponed until circumstances improve, freedom until fear diminishes, and fulfillment until the conditions of existence become sufficiently favorable\. I interpret this recurrent structure as a temporal and ontological problem rather than merely a psychological disposition\. My central argument is that the indefinite preservation of future possibilities can progressively consume the finite capacities required for their realization\. A person may maintain functional continuity while losing time, energy, attention, relational openness, and the capacity to reorganize commitments\. I distinguish between preserving the conditions of life and preserving the capacity to live through them\. Drawing on the concepts of provisional stabilization, constitutive exchange, erosion, reconfigurative capacity, modal openness, and the threshold of sufficiency, I examine how deferred living emerges through individual decisions, interpersonal expectations, institutional arrangements, and cultural narratives of future fulfillment\. I argue that the ethical problem of postponement concerns the distribution of finite capacities across time and the preservation of meaningful alternatives\. I conclude that a defensible orientation toward finite existence requires neither the abandonment of future planning nor the unrestricted pursuit of immediate satisfaction\. It requires a form oftemporal responsibility through which I can preserve the conditions of future agency while allowing the present to become a genuine field of existence\. Keywords: Finite Continuance; deferred living; temporality; erosion; reconfigurative capacity; future possibility; modal openness; provisional stabilization; existential agency; temporal responsibility \(direct link \)

## [Identifying future geriatric nurses: psychometric evaluation of the German Willingness to Work with Elderly People Scale among nursing students](../publications/d2a07427915aea159320.md)

Shengze Zhi; Burcu Akpınar Söylemez; 孙皎; Birgit Teichmann

Introduction In German\-speaking countries, where geriatric care faces a persistent nursing shortage, nursing students are expected to play a key role in addressing future workforce needs\. Currently, there is a lack of valid and reliable instruments to assess nursing students’ willingness to work with older adults\. This cross\-sectional study aimed to validate the German version of the Willingness to Work with Elderly People \(WEPS\-D\) Scale and examine factors associated with the willingness to work with older adults to support geriatric workforce development in nursing education\. Methods A convenience sample of 207 German\-speaking nursing students completed the survey, including 52 students who participated in a 4\-week retest\. Structural validity was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis \(EFA\), while convergent validity was assessed through correlations with the Kogan Attitudes toward Older People Scale \(KAOP\), Age Stereotypes \(AS\), and Future Self\-views \(FS\)\. Internal consistency and test–retest reliability were examined\. In addition, multiple linear regression was used to identify factors independently associated with willingness to work with older adults\. Results EFA identified a four\-factor structure \(intention, perceived behavioral control, attitude, and subjective norm\) with 20 items, explaining 49\.01% of the total variance\. Convergent validity was supported at the factor level, with factor 3 \(Attitude\) showing a moderate correlation with the KAOP \( r = 0\.515, p &lt; 0\.01\), while the total WEPS\-D score showed a lower correlation \( r = 0\.385, p &lt; 0\.01\) that did not meet the pre\-specified criterion\. At the scale level, internal consistency \(Cronbach’s α = 0\.894, McDonald’s ω = 0\.902\) and test–retest reliability \(ICC = 0\.882\) were good, although factors 3 \(Attitude\) and 4 \(Subjective norm\) showed relatively low internal consistency\. Multiple linear regression showed that higher education and negative or neutral attitudes toward aging were significantly associated with lower WEPS\-D scores compared with vocational training and positive attitudes, respectively\. Conclusion The WEPS\-D is a valid and reliable tool for assessing nursing students’ willingness to work with older adults\. It can be used in schools to identify the potential workforce in geriatric nursing and guide early educational interventions\.

## [Bioinspired nanozyme\-exoskeletonized yeast\-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease](../publications/d2acec3e9ae9003d70eb.md)

Fan Zhang; Lei Chen; Shengfu Wang; Xinyuan Chen; Kaiyi Du; Fuqiang Song; Linyuan Jiang; Yanzhen Feng; Siting Du; Tianyao Jiang; Jianfeng Liu; Jian Xiao

Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease \(IBD\) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression\. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti\-inflammatory, barrier\-reparative, and microbiota\-modulating effects\. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme\-exoskeletonized yeast\-derived polysaccharides \(NZEP\) by integrating nanozymes with yeast\-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization\-inspired strategy\. Among them, NZEP TA\-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme\-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF\-κB\-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways\. Oral administration of NZEP TA\-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair\. Furthermore, NZEP TA\-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD\. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities\.

## [Training\-Free On\-Policy Distillation](../publications/d2b3b9568495555fe925.md)

Bangji Yang; Jiajun Fan; Zhaoyu Zhu; Hongbo Ma; Ge Liu

On\-policy distillation consolidates specialist models into one student at the price of rollouts, teacher passes and gradient steps for every teacher\. We show that the consolidation does not need training: with forward passes only, the capabilities of separately tuned specialists can be aggregated into one model that is, on average, more accurate than either specialist alone\. When specialists share a base model, distillation has an exact layer\-wise solution: each linear layer of the fused model must reproduce every specialist&\#x27;s output on the inputs that specialist receives while reading its own answers, a least\-squares problem whose solution needs only the second moments of those inputs\. One forward pass over a few hundred rollouts provides them\. We call this training\-free on\-policy distillation \(\\method\)\. What the rollouts contain matters more than the solver: answers truncated in repetition loops are few among a mathematics specialist&\#x27;s rollouts but carry a large share of their tokens, and removing them lifts the fused model on AIME25 from task arithmetic&\#x27;s level to the specialist&\#x27;s at matched precision\. On Olmo\~3 7B, a few GPU\-hours of forward computation per specialist yield a generalist that keeps most of each specialist&\#x27;s gain on each of seven mathematics and code benchmarks\.

## [Beyond Answer Generation: University Teachers’ Experiences with a Reflective GenAI Chatbot for Professional Learning](../publications/d2c39b3b79d93f9d46d6.md)

Linda Bradley; Jonas Karlén; Niklas Segergren; Mattias von Feilitzen; Daniel Johansson

Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in higher education, yet limited research has examined how university teachers’ experience pedagogically designed AI systems that prioritize reflective learning over answer generation\. This exploratory mixed\-methods case study investigated university teachers’ experiences of a course\-specific GenAI chatbot within a professional\-development course at a Swedish university\. All 48 course participants were invited to complete a questionnaire, of whom 21 responded and 11 reported using the course\-specific chatbot; nine respondents also participated in semi\-structured interviews\. Questionnaire data were analyzed descriptively and interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis\. The chatbot was designed to encourage dialogue, engagement with course literature, and independent thinking rather than provide summaries or ready\-made answers\. Participants generally found the chatbot easy to use, but perceptions of usefulness varied\. Evaluations were shaped by prior experiences and expectations of GenAI: some teachers, who associated AI with efficiency and rapid answers, perceived the reflective design as restrictive, while others perceived its value as supporting dialogue and independent thinking\. We interpret this tension as pedagogical friction, where design constraints intended to support reflection may conflict with users’ expectations of how GenAI should function\. The findings suggest that the perceived educational value of GenAI depends not only on technical usability but also on alignment between pedagogical design, users’ expectations, and educational context\. Successful implementation of reflective AI may therefore require explicit pedagogical framing alongside technical development\.

The rapid growth of the global population and the increasing scarcity of agricultural land and water resources necessitate the development of innovative production approaches to ensure food security\. In this review study, the fundamental methods of soilless agriculture are examined, and the advantages these methods provide in terms of water and energy use, land requirements, and environmental impacts are evaluated in comparison with traditional soil\-based agriculture\. Furthermore, the technical and economic limitations encountered in soilless farming applications are addressed, and the effect of lighting management on production efficiency and energy consumption in vertical farming systems is discussed in line with current literature findings\.
