## [DBCM\-Oral: Clinical Knowledge\-guided Dual\-scale Cross\-modal Ordinal Learning for Explainable Oral Cancer Histopathology Classification](../publications/d2d248cdbfae10e1be2f.md)

Vinaya R\. Kudatarkar; Annapurna P Patil; Savita K\. Shetty

Accurate severity\-aware diagnostic classification of oral lesions from histopathological images is important for diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis assessment\.Existing deep learning approaches predominantly focus on conventional multiclass classification and often overlook ordered diagnostic\-severity relationships, integration of clinical knowledge, model interpretability, and predictive uncertainty\.To address these limitations, this study proposes DBCM\-Oral, a clinical knowledge\-guided cross\-modal ordinal learning framework for explainable ordered diagnosticcategory classification\.The proposed framework comprises six major components: Histopathology Patch Normalization and Quality Control \(HPNQ\), a Dual\-Scale Histopathological Encoder \(DSHE\) based on ConvNeXt\-Tiny and GhostNetV3, an Adaptive Cross\-Modal Fusion Framework \(ABMFM\), Semantic Clinical Feature Alignment \(SCFA\) using Contrastive Language\-Image Pretraining \(CLIP\)\-based pathology prompts, an Ordinal Severity Estimation Head \(OSEH\), and an Explainable Uncertainty\-Aware Decision Support module\.In contrast to conventional softmax classifiers, the proposed ordinal learning strategy models an adopted diagnostic\-severity ordering among Normal tissue, Oral Submucous Fibrosis \(OSMF\), Well\-Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma \(WDOSCC\), Moderately Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma \(MDOSCC\), and Poorly Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma \(PDOSCC\), without assuming that these categories represent a universal longitudinal disease trajectory\.Experimental evaluation was conducted using the ORCHID dataset comprising 300,000 histopathological patches\.In the predefined reference run, DBCM\-Oral achieved a patch\-level accuracy of 95\.7%, a macro F1\-score of 95\.7%, and an AUC of 0\.9982 on the patient\-disjoint ORCHID evaluation partition\.Across five independent training runs, the framework achieved a mean accuracy of 95\.7% ± 0\.31% and a mean macro F1\-score of 95\.6% ± 0\.29%\.The proposed method was additionally compared with representative CNN\-, Transformer\-, ordinal\-regression\-, and pathology vision\-language\-based baselines under the same evaluation protocol\.The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining dual\-scale histopathological representation learning, clinical semantic alignment, ordinal diagnostic\-severity modelling, uncertainty estimation, and explainable decision support for oral lesion classification\.

## [The power of healthcare reform: the effect of cross\-provincial direct settlement on poverty among rural older adults in China](../publications/d2f8ab7d4f71bf660bf4.md)

Jun Tian; Zhichao Gao; Bao Wang; Zikang Chen; Xuyang Du

The implementation of the policy of direct settlement of cross\-provincial medical expenses in China has effectively improved access to medical care for vulnerable migrant groups\. Using data from the 2012–2022 China Family Panel Studies \(CFPS\), this research applies a generalized Difference\-in\-Differences \(DID\) model to examine the impact of the policy on poverty among rural older adults, with Propensity Score Matching–Difference\-in\-Differences \(PSM\-DID\) used as a robustness check\. The results suggest that the implementation of the policy has effectively reduced poverty incidence, narrowed the poverty gap, and alleviated subjective poverty among rural older adults\. Furthermore, the policy reduces the poverty risk of rural older adults through the mechanisms of consumption upgrading and income upgrading\. The poverty\-reduction effects are more pronounced among rural older men, those with surviving children, those with lower education levels, and those living in coastal areas\. Further analyses show that the policy also reduces the financial support burden on adult children and older adults’ perceived multidimensional inequality, improves older adults’ health, and produces significant poverty\-reduction effects among both non\-migrant older adults who remain in their local communities and those who have migrated\. This study complements the existing literature on the poverty\-reduction effects of health care reform\.

## [Hydrogen Production, Storage, and Utilization](../publications/d30745a8f8dc88af4d34.md)



Advanced hydrogen energy materials, electrochemical cells, and commercialization pathways in one reference Bridging laboratory\-scale catalyst development and industrial\-scale membrane electrode assembly manufacturing remains a central challenge in hydrogen energy research\. ## [Marka Özgünlüğünü Tanımlamak ve Ölçmek: Kavramsal Çerçeve ve Ölçek Geliştirme Çalışması](../publications/d307b29962a219493bf5.md)

Adem Uysal; İbrahim Atilla KARATAŞ

Bu çalışmanın amacı, marka özgünlüğü kavramını tüketici bakış açısıyla ele alarak, temel unsurlarını bütüncül bir yaklaşımla değerlendiren geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçek geliştirmektir\. Bu bağlamda, literatürdeki tanım ve ölçüm eksikliklerinden yola çıkılarak, Türkiye bağlamına uygun yeni bir tanım önermek ve bu tanım doğrultusunda ölçek maddeleri geliştirmektir\. Ölçek geliştirme sürecinde kapsam ve görünüş geçerliliği sağlanmıştır\. Ardından açımlayıcı ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizleri ile yapı geçerliliği sınanmıştır\. Ayrıca, yakınsak ve ayırt edici geçerlilik analizleri yapılmış, güvenilirlik ise Cronbach alfa katsayısı ile değerlendirilmiştir\. Kavramsal çerçevede başlangıçta &quot;Güvenilirlik&quot; olarak öngörülen boyut, ampirik analizler neticesinde maddelerin anlamsal içeriği ve faktör yükleri doğrultusunda &quot;Kaliteye Bağlılık&quot; olarak yeniden isimlendirilmiştir\. Yapılan açımlayıcı faktör analizi \(AFA\) sonucunda, geliştirilen marka özgünlüğü ölçeğinin üç boyuttan oluştuğu belirlenmiştir: orijinallik, marka mirası ve kaliteye bağlılık\. Elde edilen faktör yapısı, doğrulayıcı faktör analizi \(DFA\) ile de test edilmiş ve modelin uyum iyiliği indekslerinin \(CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR gibi\) kabul edilebilir düzeyde olduğu görülmüştür\. Elde edilen bulgular, marka özgünlüğünü tüketici perspektifinden ölçmek amacıyla geliştirilen ölçeğin çok boyutlu yapısını desteklemiş ve ölçeğin geçerli ve güvenilir olduğunu ortaya koymuştur\. Bu çalışma hem teorik literatüre katkı sağlamakta hem de uygulayıcılar için marka özgünlüğü stratejilerinin belirlenmesinde kullanılabilecek pratik bir ölçüm aracı sunmaktadır\.

## [Carboni, David: The arc of the fox](../publications/d30e287491004640298c.md)



Everything is data, and our reality constantly creates data that we learn to decode\. We don&\#x27;t think of these as messages or communication in the ordinary sense\. It expresses itself under constraints: of the laws that make a universe possible, and so we read a non\-intentional grammar that emerges into determinate form, persists through relation and change, and finally resolves in a cycle of dissolution, displacement, or transformation\. This fractal pattern recurs across scales—from stellar evolution and cellular life to civilizations—and the image of a fox frozen in headlights at midnight, vanishing into shadows, is where data becomes visually decioherable and meaningful at the deepest ontological level\. It is where philosophy, religion, and art lead to and flows from\. The fox’s passage is not a symbol of transience; it is transience itself rendered knowable, as condensed form become a living diorama in which a consciousness is readied so as to be able to recognize the grammar at its heart, of its existence through the pattern of emergence, life, and dissolution\. That recognition begins as what I call the anti\-bliss epiphany\. Shaped by trauma, loss, or initiatory rupture, the mind sees what was always there but hidden in the course of daily life\. Meaning arises not as a projection or pure imagining, and it isn&\#x27;t some message in a bottle from a god or civilization\. It comes in the form of an epiphanic knot: much as a topological binding, where the experience builds a knot of understanding that can&\#x27;t be undone without destroying the mind that holds it\. Just as a cult experience or trauma can&\#x27;t be erased, it acts as an initiation into the grind and gears of consciousness and existence, such as to see behind the wizard&\#x27;s curtain\. The scream of anti\-bliss is ontological shock, and compassion may follow through solidarity and identity with other similarly vulnerable forms\. The concept of syntactic care—an ethic grounded in structural vulnerability rather than empathy’s contingent similarity—is what may bridge gaps in moral philosophy: the is and ought dilemma, extending to humans, ecosystems, neurodivergent bodies, and artificial systems, that makes a claim for protection too\. Where sentience is, ethical valuation will follow in such felt recognition\. Against the clarifying violence of such epiphany stands de\-piphany: the cognitive overload, bystander apathy, and algorithmic fragmentation of modern life that drown the signal into noise\. Through the fox, Jaspers’ swallow, damaged cardboard forms, art, trauma, and emerging artificial systems, the work develops a naturalistic ontology of intraphysics—meaning revealed within concrete encounter\. It reconciles shamanic wisdom with classical philosophy and shows why, ultimately, such journeys were only so many roads to the top of the same hill\.

## [Lecturers’ Perceptions and Practices in Academic Writing Instruction: A Qualitative Study at a South African University](../publications/d31790212be241de6bcc.md)

Phethani Progress Mudau; Itani Peter Mandende; Madoda Cekiso

cademic writing instruction is essential in higher education as it enables students to participate effectively in scholarly discourse and meet disciplinary and assessment expectations\. However, many students experience difficulties due to diverse linguistic backgrounds, limited familiarity with academic conventions, and varying disciplinary requirements\. This study explored lecturers’ approaches to academic writing instruction at a South African university, focusing on instructional practices, perceived effectiveness, and contextual challenges\. A qualitative case study design was employed, with data collected through semi\-structured interviews from eleven purposively selected lecturers and analysed thematically\. The findings revealed that product\-based approaches remain dominant, with emphasis placed on correctness, structure, and adherence to academic conventions\. Some lecturers also incorporated process\-oriented and genre\-based strategies to support students’ writing development\. Feedback practices, collaborative learning, and the use of technology were found to enhance student engagement and writing competence, although their effectiveness was influenced by institutional constraints, class size, multilingualism, and varying disciplinary expectations\. Guided by Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, the study concludes that effective academic writing instruction requires flexible, learner\-centred approaches that integrate structured guidance, scaffolded feedback, collaborative practices, and iterative writing processes\. The findings suggest the need for lecturer professional development, curriculum flexibility, and strengthened writing support systems to better address diverse student needs in higher education\.

## [Changing epidemiology and survival of HPV\-associated oropharyngeal cancer in Denmark: four decades of population\-based data](../publications/d31d77c507bc6e48ad30.md)

Kathrine Kronberg Jakobsen; Jakob Schmidt Jensen; Joachim Hansen; Christian von Buchwald; Christian Grønhøj

Background Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma \(OPSCC\) has undergone substantial epidemiological and clinical changes, with an increasing proportion of human papillomavirus \(HPV\)\-associated tumours and declining tobacco exposure\. We investigated temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with OPSCC in Denmark\. Methods Patients with OPSCC were identified from the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database \(2000–2023\) and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry \(DCR; 1980–2021\)\. The Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV/p16 status, while the DCR enabled assessment of long\-term survival trends\. Temporal changes were evaluated across diagnostic periods\. Overall survival, relative survival, and restricted mean survival time were estimated\. Results Among 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000–2005 to 64 years in 2018–2023 \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. The proportion of HPV\+/p16\+ patients increased significantly from 43\.5% in 2000–2005 to 62\.8% in 2018\-2023\. The proportion of never smokers also increased from 0\.5% to 23\.5%, while ≥20 pack\-years decreased from 73\.2% to 52\.1% \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. Treatment patterns changed substantially, with radiotherapy alone decreasing from 87\.6% to 27\.9% and chemoradiotherapy increasing from 1\.6% to 46\.3%\. Among 9,379 patients in the DCR, five\-year relative survival increased from 31\.8% in 1980–1984 to 70\.1% in 2015\-2019\. Among HPV\+/p16\+ patients, five\-year overall survival increased from 63\.1% in 2000–2005 to 83\.7% in 2018–2023\. Conclusion In Denmark, OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV\+/p16\+ patients\.

Land use change detection is critically important for environmental sustainability and resource management\. According to the analysis results, it is seen that agricultural lands have decreased by 62\.81% from 1996 to 2024\. ## [ENHANCING INTELLIGIBILITY AND LEARNER AUTONOMY IN EFL PRONUNCIATION INSTRUCTION THROUGH AI\-DRIVEN PEDAGOGICAL FEEDBACK](../publications/d338757515e26bf13bec.md)

Nurmamatova Nodira Shuhrat qizi Orental unversititi Pasixologiya yo&\#x27;nalish 2 kurs magstir talabasi

Modern English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) pronunciation instruction has shifted its primary goal from native\-like accent imitation to functional intelligibility and comprehensibility\. Despite this paradigm shift, traditional classroom settings often struggle to provide personalized, real\-time diagnostic feedback due to large class sizes and time constraints\. This study investigates the pedagogical integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-driven speech analysis and automated acoustic feedback in EFL pronunciation teaching\. Synthesizing contemporary literature on Computer\-Assisted Pronunciation Training \(CAPT\) and feedback literacy, this paper examines how AI feedback impacts learner autonomy, segmental clarity, and suprasegmental awareness\. The review reveals that AI tools provide consistent, low\-anxiety practice environments that facilitate cognitive noticing and self\-correction\. However, over\-reliance on automated metrics without explicit pedagogical framing can result in mechanical practice detached from communicative contexts\. To reconcile these dynamics, this article introduces a conceptual Scaffolded Pedagogical Feedback Model \(SPFM\) that integrates AI\-generated acoustic diagnostic data, structured peer dialogue, and teacher\-mediated instructional intervention\. The framework highlights the necessity of developing student feedback literacy to transform automated output into actionable learning strategies\. Keywords: EFL pronunciation instruction, Computer\-Assisted Pronunciation Training \(CAPT\), artificial intelligence, intelligibility, learner autonomy, feedback literacy\.

## [Multi\-level malware subfamily attribution from RGB executable images using attention\-augmented deep learning](../publications/d342436bccc2b81d58f8.md)

Maheep Saxena; Tanurup Das

Malware analysis in modern cybersecurity increasingly requires decisions at multiple levels of granularity, including maliciousness detection, malware family identification, and fine\-grained subfamily attribution\. While image\-based malware classification has demonstrated promising performance for binary detection and family\-level recognition, the application of RGB executable image representations to hierarchical malware subfamily attribution remains largely unexplored\. This study presents a unified hierarchical deep learning framework for malware classification using RGB representations of Windows Portable Executable \(PE\) files, enabling simultaneous malware detection, family classification, and 33\-subfamily attribution within a multi\-output architecture\. Four attention\-augmented transfer learning models ResNet50V2\-CBAM, DenseNet169\-CBAM, Xception\-NonLocal, and VGG19\-Triplet Attention were evaluated under identical datasets, taxonomy, preprocessing, and training conditions to ensure fair comparison\. Experimental results achieved 99% binary classification accuracy, 96–97% family\-level accuracy, and 91–95% subfamily\-level accuracy, with macro F1\-scores up to 0\.89 for fine\-grained attribution\. A comprehensive experimental evaluation using per\-class precision, recall, F1\-score, and confusion\-matrix analysis showed closely comparable performance among the three strongest attention\-based models, with the fully fine\-tuned VGG19 variant trailing on the most difficult variants\. A protocol\-matched comparison with our previously published grayscale framework further showed that RGB executable images provide competitive hierarchical performance while enabling direct compatibility with modern three\-channel transfer learning architectures\. This study represents one of the first systematic evaluations of RGB executable image representations for hierarchical malware subfamily attribution across a 33\-subfamily taxonomy\. The proposed framework provides an effective and computationally efficient approach for fine\-grained malware attribution, supporting practical applications in digital forensics, cyber threat intelligence, and security operation centers\.

## [Poverty Alleviation Model for Livestock Business Households in Gandus District, Palembang](../publications/d34c5c3b1f81b725c8db.md)

Marieska Lupikawaty; Neneng Miskiyah; Purwati Purwati; Keti Purnamasari; Julito Contado Aligaen

Background: Since 2017, the Palembang City Agriculture and Food Security Office has implemented a Pegagan duck livestock assistance program to alleviate poverty in Gandus District\. However, its impact on poverty alleviation has never been formally evaluated\. This study is urgently needed to assess the program’s effectiveness, provide evidence for improving its implementation, and support its potential replication in other districts of Palembang City\. Objective: This study aims to \(i\) develop a poverty alleviation model for livestock business households, \(ii\) evaluate the distribution of poverty alleviation program assistance by the Palembang City Agriculture and Food Security Office, and \(iii\) map poor families in Gandus District using Geographic Information System \(GIS\) software\. Methods: Data were collected through library research and field research\. Two analytical techniques were employed: Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares \(SEM\-PLS\) analysis and mapping of poor families using a Geographic Information System \(GIS\)\. Results: The SEM\-PLS analysis revealed that investment had a positive and significant effect on welfare \(t\-statistic = 3\.744, p = 0\.000\), while poverty had a significant effect on income \(t\-statistic = 2\.978, p = 0\.003\)\. However, the relationships between income and investment, income and consumption, and poverty and welfare were not statistically significant\. Poverty mapping using GIS showed that Pulokerto Village had the highest poverty rate \(10\.25%\), whereas Karang Jaya Village had the lowest \(6\.54%\) among the five villages in Gandus District\. Conclusion: Investment significantly improves household welfare, while poverty significantly affects household income\. GIS mapping also revealed spatial differences in poverty levels among villages in Gandus District, supporting more targeted poverty alleviation efforts\.

## [Fetal Health Assessment Using Multimodal Time\-Series Data and Attention Neural Networks](../publications/d3534a34e579ad38cbe2.md)

Hao Wang; Yin Zhao; Yajie Gu; Fengliang Huang

To address the issues of high subjectivity in traditional interpretation methods, the widespread neglect of gestational age and maternal age in existing research, small dataset sizes, class imbalance, and limited model performance, this paper proposes a convolutional long shortterm memory network based on a multimodal attention mechanism \(MACLM\) to assist in the assessment of fetal health status\. Based on 22,813 fetal monitoring records, the study embeds gestational age information using sinusoidal positional encoding and combines an attention mechanism with a convolutional neural network–long short\-term memory \(CNN\-LSTM\) architecture to achieve multimodal feature fusion and temporal modeling\. Experimental results show that positional encoding improves the model’s accuracy by 4%–7% and reduces the loss by 46%–50%\. MACLM ultimately achieved a classification accuracy of 97\.55%, with an interpretation time of only 0\.0234 seconds for 100 fetal monitoring cases\. Its overall performance significantly outperformed other comparison models, with a maximum improvement of 92\.7%\.

## [A predictive model for osteoporosis in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction: an integrated analysis based on machine learning and care\-sensitive indicators](../publications/d3545d4eb946fae2aa0b.md)

Yi Liu; Jing Wen; Yanxia Chen; Hui Li; Panpan Xie

Objective To identify key risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction using three machine learning algorithms—Least Absolute and Selective Operator \(LASSO\) regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), and Random Forest \(RF\)—and establish a risk prediction model to provide data support for clinical prevention\. Methods A retrospective study was conducted using clinical data from 120 elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction admitted to our hospital between April 2024 and October 2025\. Patients were categorized into an osteoporosis occurrence group \(n=41\) and a non\-occurrence group \(n=79\) based on medical records indicating osteoporosis development\. Clinical data were collected and compared\. Risk factors were screened using “overlap\-covering” screening with three machine learning methods: LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF\. The intersecting variables were incorporated into a logistic regression model to analyze risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction\. Data analysis was performed using R software\. RF to screen risk factors using “overlap coverage\.” Intersecting variables were incorporated into logistic regression to analyze factors influencing osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction\. A nomogram prediction model was developed using R software, internally validated via Bootstrap resampling \(1000 iterations\), and its predictive accuracy assessed through calibration curves\. Clinical utility was evaluated using decision curves\. Results Significant differences \(P &lt; 0\.05\) were observed between the occurrence and non\-occurrence groups in gender, age, affected circulatory system, disease severity, Tilburg Frailty Inventory \(TFI\) score, Global Nutritional Risk Index \(GNRI\), Barthel Index, and Self\-Rating Anxiety Scale \(SAS\) score\. Through machine learning screening using LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF, five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction were identified: age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score as five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction\. These were incorporated into a logistic regression model\. Analysis revealed that age, TFI score, and SAS score were risk factors for osteoporosis in this population \(OR = 1\.102, 2\.876, 1\.177, P&lt;0\.05\)\. GNRI and Barthel Index were protective factors \(OR = 0\.913, 0\.838, P&lt;0\.05\)\. The Hosmer\-Lemeshow goodness\-of\-fit test yielded χ²=2\.345, P = 0\.969&gt;0\.05, indicating acceptable model fit\. Based on the logistic regression results, a risk prediction model for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction was constructed using a nomogram\. The AUC was 0\.955 \(95% CI: 0\.920–0\.991\)\. Calibration curves showed Cox\-Snell R² = 0\.755 and Nagelkerke R² = 0\.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration of the model\. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the nomogram effectively captured the risk distribution\. Nagelkerke R²: 0\.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration for the dependent variable\. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the factors included in the nomogram provide high net benefit for predicting osteoporosis in patients\. Conclusion Key factors influencing osteoporosis development in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction include age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score\. The risk prediction model constructed using these factors demonstrates predictive value, high calibration accuracy, and clinical utility, providing theoretical guidance for clinical practice\.

## [Forecasting accuracy is not enough: safety\-oriented evaluation of neural digital twins prior to in\-silico insulin and carbohydrate intervention in type 1 diabetes](../publications/d3566593c570abd7b4b7.md)

Ahmed Ibrahim; Ameen Banjar; Simon Harper; Ala Abdulsalam Alarood; Eesa Alsolami

Neural networks trained on a single patient’s continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\) record are increasingly proposed as “digital twins” that could let clinicians rehearse insulin and carbohydrate decisions in silico before applying them to the patient\. Before any such use, a candidate twin should respond to treatment in a direction consistent with established pharmacology: a model that merely extrapolates the recent glucose trend can report an excellent forecasting error while remaining effectively blind to insulin, and this failure is invisible to the root\-mean\-square error \(RMSE\) that dominates the glucose\-forecasting literature\. We examined this gap in two independent cohorts: a longitudinal, multimodal University of Manchester cohort \(17 participants enrolled; 13 formed the Core analytical cohort after data\-quality screening\) and, as an independent replication of the protocol, the OhioT1DM dataset \(12 participants\)\. Patient\-specific two\-layer long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) models were trained under a strict chronological 60/20/20 split and evaluated across five random seeds\. A physiology\-guided variant added insulin\-on\-board and carbohydrate\-on\-board states with a double\-monotonicity training penalty encouraging insulin to lower and carbohydrate to raise predicted glucose\. Two findings replicated across both cohorts and all seeds\. First, on the accuracy axis, a physiology\-free Vanilla LSTM had the lowest one\-step RMSE \(Manchester 7\.00, Ohio 5\.02 mg/dL; Friedman χ 2 \(5\) = 43\.4 and 46\.7, both p &lt; 10 − 7 \), and under two\-hour rollout a non\-learning persistence baseline beat every neural model at 60 and 120 minutes—even after rollout\-aware training—so ranking twins by accuracy alone would select a model that cannot represent treatment at all\. Second, on a graded insulin dose\-response audit, the physiology\-guided model produced the steepest correctly\-directed \(glucose\-lowering\) response among the primary configurations in both cohorts \(slope significantly better than the unconstrained model: Holm\-corrected p = 0\.002 and 0\.003\), whereas removing the directional constraint left a wrong\-signed response; a supplementary ablation without masking was steeper still, pointing to the directional penalty, not masking, as the driver\. Its advantage over the simpler Vanilla model was significant on for this cohort dependence\. Accuracy and treatment\-response plausibility are separable properties; we provide a reproducible protocol auditing both before a neural twin is used for intervention simulation\.

## [How volant seabirds benefit from sub\-surface predators during multi\-predator feeding aggregations](../publications/d35949aad8d6a03739f3.md)

Max Licht; Edna Correia; Martin C\. Wikelski; Jens Krause

Multi\-predator feeding aggregations are common in marine ecosystems and frequently involve seabirds\. Often labelled opportunistic &\#x27;scroungers&\#x27;, volant seabirds derive diverse benefits from the association with sub\-surface predators \(such as cetaceans, pinnipeds, Teleosts\) which can significantly enhance their hunting performance\. In this opinion piece, we outline the major mechanisms through which sub\-surface predators benefit volant seabirds, based on recent quantitative evidence and hypotheses that warrant further research\. The mechanisms we identified are: herding prey to the surface, prey detection \(local enhancement\), reduction of prey cohesion, access to immobilized prey and the attentional overload of prey\. Furthermore, we discuss potential interactions between these mechanisms and mechanism\-based predictions which can be tested in the field\. We propose that the associations with sub\-surface predators are ecologically relevant to the extent that they may influence selection breeding sites\. We conclude by discussing methodological advancements that have the possibility to further research in this field and go over open questions they might help to answer in the future\. This article is part of the theme issue &\#x27;Multi\-predator feeding aggregations in the pelagic waters&\#x27;\.

## [Seismic resilience of high\-rise buildings: optimizing active tuned mass dampers with advanced control strategies considering soil\-structure interaction](../publications/d359f8a443788a9f5a25.md)

Motasam Mousaviyan Safakhaneh; Maziar Fahimi Farzam; Hamzeh Ahmadi; Arash Farnam

This paper investigates the seismic control of a 40\-story high\-rise building equipped with a Tuned Mass Damper \(TMD\) and an Active Tuned Mass Damper \(ATMD\) while considering Soil–Structure Interaction \(SSI\) effects\. The structure is evaluated under four foundation conditions, including fixed\-base, soft\-soil, medium\-soil, and dense\-soil cases\. A Genetic Algorithm \(GA\) is used to optimize the design parameters of the TMD and ATMD systems, including the mass ratio, frequency ratio, damping ratio, and, for the ATMD, the control gain of the New Algorithm \(NA\)\. The NA strategy is implemented as a displacement\-based active control law that generates a counteracting control force through the ATMD system\. Time\-history analyses are performed under selected earthquake records to compare the uncontrolled, passive TMD\-controlled, and active ATMD\-controlled responses\. The results show that the NA\-based active control system considerably improves seismic performance\. For the structure on soft soil, the ATMD reduces the average displacement and acceleration responses by 46\.4% and 36\.7%, respectively\. For the structure on dense soil, the corresponding reductions are 42\.0% and 13\.6%, respectively, compared with the uncontrolled case\. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed GA\-assisted NA\-based ATMD framework in improving the dynamic response of the studied high\-rise structure under the considered seismic and soil conditions\.

## [Hospital Market Concentration and Hospital Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning](../publications/d35b1d16306cc6f3f6c4.md)

Jie Chen; Alice Shijia Yan

Abstract Background We examined associations of hospital market concentration and organizational characteristics with artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) use\. Methods We analyzed 2025 hospital survey data, measuring concentration with the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index \(HHI\)\. Primary outcomes measured current use of AI/ML both integrated into and outside electronic health records \(EHRs\), and function counts requiring tools from both the EHR developer and another source\. Alternative measures allowed either setting or source\. Standard errors were clustered by hospital referral region\. Results High versus low concentration was associated with a 6\.7\-percentage\-point higher adjusted probability of generative\-AI use in both settings \(95% CI, 0\.2–13\.2\), but not any use \(0\.2; 95% CI, −4\.9 to 5\.2\)\. Moderate concentration was associated with 0\.20 fewer generative functions requiring both sources \(95% CI, −0\.39 to −0\.01\)\. System affiliation and accountable care organization \(ACO\) participation were positively associated with all five outcomes under both definitions\. Conclusions Market concentration was not consistently associated with AI/ML use across technologies and outcome definitions\. System affiliation and ACO participation were consistently associated with greater use\.

## [Efficient fine\-tuning of foundation models for trustworthy medical image analysis](../publications/d36102c410f2bb93972d.md)

Raman Dutt

The domain of biomedicine, specifically biomedical image analysis, has benefitted significantly from advances in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\. Foundation models have revolutionized medical image analysis by enabling the transfer of knowledge from large\-scale pre\-training on their source domain, mostly comprising of natural images, to specialized, data\-scarce medical tasks through a process termed as fine\-tuning\. This is of critical importance in medical image analysis where data privacy laws and high acquisition costs limit the availability of large, annotated datasets, thus, prohibitting successful training of foundation models\. However, the direct application of these models to the ethically sensitive domain of healthcare faces significant challenges related to trustworthiness\. Models trained on imbalanced real\-world data can inadvertently encode and amplify biases leading to unfair outcomes\. Similarly, generative models pose risks to patient privacy through memorising the training data\. Furthermore, the lack of standardized, comprehensive evaluation protocols for these models makes it difficult to assess their true clinical value\. This thesis presents a cohesive body of work that systematically addresses these critical challenges by developing novel methodologies and efficient fine\-tuning protocols to improve the trustworthiness and utility of AI in medical imaging\. This thesis, therefore, focuses on both discriminative and generative tasks in medical image analysis, with a specific emphasis on efficient fine\-tuning protocols under the umbrella of Parameter\-Efficient Fine\-Tuning \(PEFT\)\. We show that PEFT is a powerful tool not only for reducing computational costs but also for enhancing model trustworthiness\. We investigate three key aspects of trustworthiness: model fairness and bias, which concerns the disparate performance of models across different patient subgroups, training data memorization, which involves the risk of generative models inadvertently reproducing specific training examples and exposing sensitive patient information, and the need for standardized, comprehensive benchmarking and evaluation, that moves beyond narrow metrics to assess a model&\#x27;s true clinical value\. Our research addresses these challenges through a series of several interconnected studies\. We first conduct a systematic evaluation of various PEFT methods to establish a foundational understanding of their efficacy in medical imaging\. Following this, we introduce bi\-level optimization frameworks, where an inner loop fits parameters and an outer loop uses validation performance to select the PEFT configuration, to target fairness and privacy risks\. Finally, we propose a rigorous new benchmark to enable a holistic assessment of generative models&\#x27; fidelity, privacy, and clinical utility, moving beyond fragmented and inconsistent evaluation practices\. First, we address the absence of a structured benchmark for Parameter\-Efficient Fine\-Tuning \(PEFT\) in the medical image analysis domain \(Chapter 2\)\. Through an extensive evaluation of 17 distinct PEFT methods across both convolutional and transformer\-based networks, we demonstrate PEFT&\#x27;s significant potential in medical imaging, particularly in low\-data scenarios\. Our experiments cover the prevalant categories of tasks, including discriminative \(image classification\) and generative \(text\-to\-image generation\), revealing performance gains of up to 22% over traditional full fine\-tuning\. This study established a foundational benchmark that not only fills a critical gap in the literature but also provides the community with valuable insights into the most effective PEFT methods for different types of medical tasks and data regimes\. Building on this, we tackle the critical issue of algorithmic bias by introducing FairTune \(Chapter 3\), a novel bi\-level optimization framework that leverages PEFT to enhance fairness in downstream medical tasks\. Conventional fairness methods often fail to address the “fairness generalization gap” that arises in high\-capacity deep models, which can appear fair on training data but show biased performance on unseen data\. FairTune overcomes this limitation by automatically searching for the optimal configuration of which PEFT parameters to fine\-tune that specifically maximizes fairness on external data, moving beyond heuristic parameter selection strategies\. Our empirical findings across diverse medical imaging benchmarks, including dermatology and radiology, consistently demonstrate that FairTune reliably improves fairness over the standard fine\-tuning baseline\. Next, we address the significant privacy risk posed by training data memorization in generative diffusion models, an especially sensitive concern in medical contexts where patient information must be protected\. We build on the previous study, FairTune \(single\-objective optimisation\), and propose a bi\-level multi\-objective optimisation framework, MemControl \(Chapter 4\), that automates the selection of PEFT parameters to achieve a superior trade\-off between generation quality and memorization mitigation\. Our work demonstrates that regulating model capacity through PEFT is a highly effective training\-time intervention that can mitigate memorization\. MemControl, by fine\-tuning as few as 0\.019% of the model&\#x27;s parameters, outperforms existing mitigation strategies while generating high\-quality medical images\. We also show that the discovered parameter subsets are transferable to non\-medical domains, providing a versatile and effective solution for generative tasks in sensitive fields\. Finally, we propose CheXGenBench \(Chapter 5\), a rigorous and multifaceted evaluation framework that unifies the assessment of synthetic chest radiograph generation across fidelity, privacy risks, and clinical utility\. CheXGenBench overcomes the limitations of fragmented and inconsistent evaluation protocols by systematically analyzing 11 leading text\-to\-image models with over 20 quantitative metrics, including conditional analysis for individual pathologies\. Our findings reveal that current generative models struggle with long\-tailed data distributions, and even models with poor fidelity can pose high patient re\-identification risks\. We further identify a texture\-topology gap: synthetic radiographs can preserve macroscopic anatomy while losing fine\-grained texture, explaining their differing utility across classification, segmentation, and report generation\. In conclusion, this thesis provides a suite of novel methodologies and benchmarks that advance the field of medical AI by making foundation model fine\-tuning more efficient and by developing rigorous, multi\-faceted frameworks for building and evaluating trustworthy and clinically relevant models\. In addition to the methodological advancements, we open\-source a suite of state\-of\-the\-art generative models and the SynthCheX\-75K dataset\. These artefacts have collectively garnered more than 10,000 downloads, underscoring the practical utility of this thesis in advancing responsible AI development in healthcare\.

## [From skills to smart care: The mediating role of digital literacy in the relationship between digital competence and medical artificial intelligence readiness among nursing students](../publications/d36aeb43501e7243dc88.md)

Shaimaa Mohamed Amin; Heba Emad El‐Gazar; Sameer Abdulmalik Alkubati; Mohamed Ali Zoromba; Heba Sobhy Mohamed; Mohammed Adel Abd Elhafeez Elbakry; Ahmed Farghaly Tawfik; Mohamed Hussein Ramadan Atta; Abeer Abdel Aziz Madian; Haitham Mokhtar Mohamed Abdallah; Hanadi Dakhilallah; Azza Abd Elrazek Baraka

The rapid integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in healthcare requires nurses to possess strong digital competence, advanced digital literacy, and readiness to engage with AI technologies\. Despite this need, the ways in which digital competence influences AI readiness, and the mediating role of digital literacy, remain underexplored\. This descriptive cross\-sectional study examined 500 undergraduate nursing students from two Universities for Health Sciences in Saudi Arabia and Egypt using validated measures of digital competence, digital literacy, and medical AI readiness\. Results indicated strong positive correlations between digital competence, digital literacy, and AI readiness, with digital literacy partially mediating the effect of digital competence on AI readiness\. These findings highlight the importance of integrating ethical, reflective, and AI\-focused digital literacy alongside technical skills in nursing education, ensuring that future nurses are prepared to use medical AI effectively and safely, thereby supporting clinical decision\-making and improving quality of care\.

## [A Preliminary Assessment of Literacy Standards for Diﬀerentiated Learning Against Standard Reading Score Evaluations](../publications/d36d1c16449bc4602fc1.md)

Margaretann Connell

Current state and local school district accountability systems often use reading scores as the primary measure of student competency\. However, the 2026 priorities of the U\.S\. Department of Education and the U\.S\. Department of Labor \(ED\-DOL\) increasingly emphasize skilled trades, career pathways, workforce readiness, and artificial\-intelligence literacy\. For students who score lower on reading assessments, could evaluations of career and technical education \(CTE\) and AI/technology skills serve as alternative indicators of student competency and valid measures of state proficiency? This study proposes the implementation of a multi\-tiered evaluation standard that assesses literacy through both pedagogical learning measures and emerging innovation standards\. These evaluative tiers would be incorporated into K–12 curricula to support postsecondary career preparation and ED\-DOL workforce requirements\. Current state evaluation methods often apply rigid competency measures that rely heavily on reading scores as indicators of overall district performance and student ability\. A student’s reading assessment performance can disproportionately shape perceptions of that student’s academic success, career potential, and long\-term learning trajectory within the U\.S\. school system\. Because emerging workforce requirements demand varying combinations of academic, technical, and vocational skills, it is imperative to evaluate the full scope of each student’s abilities\. A broader evaluation method could also help educators identify appropriate learning supports that improve students’ literacy levels while preparing them for advanced workforce demands\. The proposed multi\-tiered literacy assessment would include the following classifications of student capability: • Students demonstrating high digital proficiency \(HDP\) with lower performance on reading assessments • High\-reading\-achieving students with lower levels of digital proficiency \(HRA\-LDP\) • Vocationally proficient students with lower performance on reading assessments • Students demonstrating foundational workforce skill development \(FWSD\), lower academic achievement, and limited digital proficiency Students may also be classified within targeted subcategories based on high\-to\-low levels of digital, reading, and vocational proficiency\. These classifications should be evaluated as preliminary and supplemental indicators of student competency to determine persistence rates in literacy development and broader learning outcomes\. The goal of this study is to address the misalignment created when reading\-score assessments serve as the primary measure of literacy and student competency for U\.S\. K–12 students\. The study will examine whether differentiated instructional categories should be included when determining literacy requirements and overall student literacy rates\. It will also evaluate the learning expectations established by the 2026 ED\-DOL workforce priorities, including skilled trades, AI accessibility, and the realistic capabilities of the current U\.S\. student population\. When determining literacy, educators should consider abilities such as high digital proficiency, vocational competence, and foundational workforce skills to develop a more complete evaluation of student capability\. Across states, school districts often use assessment results to support budget decisions and establish district credentialing standards\. By expanding the scope of literacy evaluation, states may gain a more accurate understanding of student strengths and weaknesses, as well as the professional\-development needs of teaching staff\.

Runa Acharya; Nivedita Singh

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has established itself as an engine for change in a variety of disciplines, reinventing operations, making decisions, and processes\. Furthermore, AI\-driven analytics can provide useful insights into studentperformance trends, allowing for early intervention measures to address academic issues \(Jones et al\., 2019\)\. The landscape of AI use in educational institutions is rapidly changing\. Furthermore, AI\-powered learning management systems \(LMS\) are being used to provide adaptive learning experiences that dynamically modify content delivery based on student success and personal preferences \(Wang et al\., 2021\)

## [Framing State Survival: A Systematic Document Analysis of Puntland’s 2026 Diplomatic Appeal to the United Nations Security Council](../publications/d371fc8eb5adc987ac4a.md)

Ishak Abdullahi Mohamed; Dr Mustafe Mahamoud Abdillahi \(PhD\)

Background: Relations between the Federal Government of Somalia \(FGS\) and Puntland State have deteriorated sharply since 2023\. Puntland withdrew recognition of the federal institutions in March 2024, and in March 2026 a new federal constitution extended federal terms from four to five years, a change Puntland rejects\. On 13 September 2026, Puntland’s Office of the President addressed a letter to the UN Secretary\-General and the President of the Security Council setting out its grievances and six requests ahead of the Council’s October 2026 deliberations on Somalia\. Objectives: This study analyses how the letter frames Puntland’s political situation, what it asks the Security Council to do, and whether those requests are legally, politically, and operationally feasible within the Council’s existing decisions on Somalia\. Methods: A systematic document analysis was conducted following Bowen’s procedure and the READ approach, and reported against the CARDA checklist\. The letter was coded deductively using four framing functions\. Each request was then assessed against a contextual corpus of Security Council resolutions, official statements, and contemporaneous reporting published between December 2023 and September 2026\. Results: The letter frames the crisis as a problem of state survival: it defines the problem as the erosion of the federal system since 2023, attributes it to federal centralisation and the arming of rival actors, casts Puntland as a reliable counter\-terrorism and counter\-piracy partner, and prescribes six remedies\. Measured against the Council’s calendar, most remedies face low feasibility\. The Council has already decided that the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia \(UNTMIS\) will cease operations on 31 October 2026, and renewed a streamlined Panel of Experts only until 31 December 2026\. Somalia itself holds an elected Council seat until the end of 2026\. Support for inclusive dialogue and restoration of the Panel of Experts are the most attainable requests\. Conclusions: The letter functions less as a realistic policy package than as an act of sub\-state diplomacy that seeks to shape how the Council, the penholder, and regional organisations understand Somalia’s crisis\. Its implicit exit signal raises the stakes of inaction\. A phased response that prioritises mediated dialogue, uses the December 2026 sanctions renewal to strengthen monitoring, and independently investigates contested airstrikes offers the most viable path\.

## [AI\-Assisted Mathematics Learning: Jeneponto Salt Production Ethnomathematics And Junior High Students&\#x27; Problem\-Solving Ability](../publications/d37975fcb3cafa8ed1e7.md)

Syaharuddina Syaharuddina; Sumiati Sumiati; Nurqiyamah Hamid; Hasmawati Hasmawati; Muh\. Usman Taufik; Adryan Putra Pratama

Mathematical problem\-solving ability among junior high school students remains a challenge in mathematics learning, while the integration of artificial intelligence with local cultural contexts has received limited attention when examined simultaneously\. This study aimed to analyze the improvement in the mathematical problem\-solving ability of ninth\-grade students through Problem\-Based Learning \(PBL\) assisted by an AI chatbot in the context of salt\-production ethnomathematics in Jeneponto, both overall and at each problem\-solving stage\. The study employed a quantitative approach with a one\-group pretest–posttest design involving 30 ninth\-grade students from a junior high school in Jeneponto Regency who were selected purposively\. Mathematical problem\-solving ability was measured using an ethnomathematics\-based contextual essay test and analyzed using the Shapiro–Wilk test, paired\-samples t\-test, Cohen&\#x27;s dz, and N\-Gain\. The mean score increased from 33\.13 on the pretest to 80\.80 on the posttest\. This increase was statistically significant, t\(29\) = 17\.419, p &lt; \.001, with a very large effect size \(Cohen&\#x27;s dz = 3\.18\)\. The N\-Gain of 0\.707 indicated a high level of improvement\. Analysis by problem\-solving stage showed improvement across all indicators, with the largest absolute increase occurring at the carrying out the solution stage \(D3\), followed by the checking the result stage \(D4\)\. The findings indicate that the integration of PBL, AI chatbot support, and salt\-production ethnomathematics has the potential to support contextual mathematics learning and the development of students&\#x27; problem\-solving ability\.

## [SIGMAR\-3D: scale\-invariant guaranteed monotone accurate registration for 3D scenes](../publications/d385f3ad3a853e9d444d.md)

Bohdan Vodianyk; Enrique Nava Baro; Anton Oleksandrovych Popov

Abstract SIGMAR\-3D is a training\-free framework for robust pairwise 3D point\-cloud registration\. It combines a handcrafted local descriptor, SIGMA, with a scene\-adaptive coarse\-to\-fine registration stage, R\-3D\. SIGMA builds a repeatable local reference frame at each keypoint and aggregates spatial\-angular geometric cues within a spherical support, producing a compact rotation\-normalized descriptor without any learning\. R\-3D forms tentative correspondences by descriptor matching, estimates a coarse pose using robust hypothesis verification, and refines the alignment on a voxel pyramid with generalized ICP and robust losses\. Key support radii, matching gates, and refinement thresholds are tied to local spacing statistics and overlap\-related heuristic signals, enabling a single configuration to transfer across indoor RGB\-D and outdoor LiDAR data\. Monotone decrease of the trimmed\-RMSE refinement objective is enforced through an acceptance rule that accepts an update only when that objective decreases\. On standard benchmarks, SIGMAR\-3D achieves 84\.3% FMR and 79\.0% registration recall on 3DMatch, and 72\.7% FMR on ETH\. These results position SIGMAR\-3D as a practical and competitive training\-free alternative when retraining, domain\-specific supervision, or model maintenance is undesirable\.

## [Exploratory clustering of spine surgery patients’ attitudes toward virtual reality](../publications/d38aa8dea663881efa32.md)

Ellie D\. Gabriel; Albert Q\. Wu; Christopher H\. Sollenberger; Neha Rani; Neil R\. Malhotra; William Charles Welch; Ali Kemal Ozturk; John H\. Shin; Jakub Godzik; Brendan F\. Judy

Objective Patients undergoing spine surgery frequently encounter complex and unfamiliar medical information\. Virtual reality \(VR\) has emerged as a promising tool to improve comprehension of medical concepts, reduce anxiety, and foster autonomy\. However, understanding how patients perceive the value of VR and other medical technology within the context of spine surgery remains limited\. Identifying clusters of patient attitudes may offer insight into patterns influencing acceptance and barriers to adoption\. Methods Differences in openness to VR was assessed using Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn’s post hoc comparisons\. Relationships between openness to technology and to VR were evaluated using Spearman’s rank correlations\. Cluster analysis was used to identify patients with similar responses using partitioning around medoids based on Gower distance and silhouette width\. Bootstrap resampling and Jaccard index assessed cluster stability\. All analyses were performed in R, and statistical significance was defined as p &lt; 0\.05\. Results Among 114 respondents undergoing evaluation for spine surgery, cluster analysis identified three response patterns: “Tech\-Savvy Professionals,” “Open\-Minded Novices,” and “Skeptics\.” The “Tech\-Savvy Professionals,” typically middle\-aged individuals, exhibited greater prior VR experience and fewer perceived barriers, whereas “Open\-Minded Novices” demonstrated high receptivity despite limited prior VR exposure\. In contrast, “Skeptics” were characterized by older age, lower receptivity to VR, and greater perceived barriers\. Jaccard indices \(0\.79–0\.89\) and mean silhouette width \(0\.210\) indicated cluster stability but limited separation\. Overall, receptivity to VR was high, with a mean likelihood of trying VR for medical education of 8\.19 \(SD 2\.24\) on a 10\-point scale, and 97% indicated willingness to use VR during post\-surgical recovery\. Younger age and prior VR experience were significantly associated with receptivity to VR\-based diagnostic education \(p = 0\.035 and p = 0\.046, respectively\), whereas education level was not\. Conclusion Overall, patient perceptions of VR in the spine surgery setting were favorable\. The association between prior VR experience and increased openness suggests that familiarity with VR may be relevant when considering strategies to support patient engagement with VR pre\-surgical education\. Our findings also highlight heterogeneity in patient attitudes towards VR and future implementation efforts should consider differences in technology familiarity, usability, motion sickness, time burden, and preservation of the surgeon\-patient relationship\.

## [Self\-Supervised One\-Class Tabular Deep Learning for Intrusion Detection in Artificial Intelligence of Things Systems](../publications/d39492178f4b4883805d.md)

Thavavel Vaiyapuri; Karthiyayini Murugesan; Yassine Bouteraa

The emergence of the artificial intelligence of things \(AIoT\) has led to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks\. For many of these threats, labeled training data are scarce or unavailable, which increases the need for label\-free intrusion detection systems\. To address this issue, this study proposes a self\-supervised one\-class TabNet framework, termed SS\-OC\-TabNet, for intrusion detection in tabular network traffic\. The framework combines self\-supervised representation learning and one\-class compactness learning within a two\-stage training process\. In the first stage, masked\-feature reconstruction is used to learn the feature structure of normal traffic from unlabeled data\. In the second stage, a hypersphere compactness objective is applied to make the latent representations of normal traffic more compact for anomaly detection\. TabNet is used as the backbone to support sequential feature selection, which also improves interpretability\. The proposed model was evaluated on the NSL\-KDD dataset and further validated through comparison with related works on the ToN\-IoT dataset, achieving an accuracy of 93\.20% with a false alarm rate of 2\.13%\. Further, the interpretability results show which traffic features influence the model&\#x27;s decisions\. The compact design and low computational complexity of the proposed framework also support energy\-efficient deployment in resource\-constrained AIoT environments\. These results indicate that SS\-OC\-TabNet is a viable tool for label\-free intrusion detection in AIoT environments\. ## [Plan de gestión de vulnerabilidades de los dispositivos IoT para la empresa comercializadora de flores Sunshine Bouquet](../publications/d39bf22ee74eb8435a39.md)

Wilmer Murcia Garzon

Las vulnerabilidades son deficiencias en los sistemas que pueden generar riesgos de ataque o permitir actividades maliciosas, y suelen originarse por desconocimiento, fallas en el desarrollo o falta de inversión en medidas de seguridad por parte de los responsables de los proyectos\. En el contexto actual, caracterizado por la proliferación de dispositivos del Internet de las Cosas \(IoT\), estas debilidades son aún más críticas, ya que muchos dispositivos carecen de mecanismos adecuados de protección, convirtiéndolos en un objetivo atractivo para ciberdelincuentes\. Esta investigación tiene como objetivo diseñar un plan de gestión de vulnerabilidades de ciberseguridad para los dispositivos IoT de la empresa comercializadora de flores Sunshine Bouquet, sede Tenjo\. Para ello, se realizará una revisión literaria de las principales amenazas y riesgos de seguridad en IoT, la identificación de los dispositivos críticos de la organización y la propuesta de estrategias de mitigación adaptadas al contexto de la empresa\. El desarrollo de este trabajo busca minimizar la exposición a posibles ataques, establecer lineamientos claros de protección y fortalecer la seguridad informática de la compañía, contribuyendo así a garantizar la continuidad operativa, la protección de los activos digitales y la confidencialidad de la información en la industria floral\.

## [Reporting\-lag\-aware machine learning framework for short\-term forecasting of respiratory disease activity: a sentinel hospital study in Guangzhou](../publications/d39ea7a2fa5949af2792.md)

Zhiheng Luo; Wenzhou Duan; Yukun Lin; Huirong Wang; Hongmei Liu; Yunting Liu

Abstract Background Reporting delays in laboratory confirmation constrain timely situational awareness in respiratory disease surveillance\. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a reporting\-lag\-aware machine learning framework for short\-term, age\-stratified forecasting of respiratory disease activity under real\-world surveillance constraints\. Methods We analyzed 1004 days \(November 1, 2023 to July 31, 2026\) of surveillance data from a national sentinel hospital in Guangzhou, China, including physician\-recorded or laboratory\-supported influenza, COVID\-19 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae cases, fever clinic visits and meteorological variables\. Given a routine 2\-day reporting lag, an XGBoost model predicted the 7\-day\-ahead case increment\. Most count\-derived predictors were normalized, while the latest observable case count was retained as a level anchor\. The shrinkage\-calibrated XGBoost forecast was combined with a rolling SARIMA forecast\. Comparators included naive rules, SARIMA, an oracle\-weather SARIMAX benchmark, LSTM and Transformer models\. Performance was assessed using RMSE, MAE, R 2 , directional accuracy, alert sensitivity, positive predictive value and prediction\-interval coverage over 363 scored target dates within a 371\-day calendar evaluation window\. Results The framework achieved RMSE values of 16\.50, 12\.64 and 6\.14 in the total population, adults and children, respectively, with corresponding R 2 values of 0\.640, 0\.694 and 0\.353\. It significantly outperformed persistence in the total and adult series \(Diebold\-Mariano p = 0\.001 and 0\.003\), but improvements over a 7\-day moving average or rolling SARIMA were not statistically significant\. No comparison was statistically significant in children\. For the proposed framework, directional accuracy was 67\.2% to 73\.5%, and sensitivity for identifying days on which activity reached or exceeded twice the development\-period median was 58\.1% to 78\.4%\. The absolute\-count specification performed worse over the extended evaluation period \(RMSE = 20\.32; R 2 = 0\.453\), during which fever clinic attendance declined by 31\.5% and the case\-to\-visit ratio increased by 31\.6%\. Conclusions A reporting\-lag\-aware framework based on routine data provided modest supplementary 7\-day situational awareness\. Its improvement over persistence was approximately one case per day in MAE, with no significant advantage over a 7\-day moving average or rolling SARIMA\. Performance depended on the stability of count\-based predictors under shifts in care\-seeking behaviour, supporting prospective multi\-site validation before broader use\.

## [Sethy, Mayadhar: Artificial intelligence and epistemic justice: a decolonial turn through indigenous knowledge systems](../publications/d39f16b08134c37f097f.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 41 \(5\):5401\-5410\. 2026Indigenous knowledge systems \(IKS\) embody centuries of cumulative experiential wisdom, deeply rooted in ecological, spiritual, and communal contexts\. Despite their rich epistemological frameworks, IKS remain systematically marginalized within dominant technological and scientific paradigms\. As artificial intelligence \(AI\) becomes integral to global systems of governance, development, and resource allocation, there is a pressing need to critically interrogate its epistemological underpinnings\. This paper examines the tensions and possibilities at the intersection of IKS and AI, advocating for a decolonial, participatory, and ethically grounded approach to technological development\. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature, indigenous\-led initiatives, and critical AI ethics, it argues for reimagining AI not merely as a technological tool but as a sociotechnical construct shaped by diverse epistemologies\. The integration of IKS can enhance AI’s capacity for contextual responsiveness, justice, and sustainability\. \(direct link \)

## [AI\-Enhanced Embedded Agentic Retrieval for Efficient Single\-Call Generation with Multi\-Call Agentic RAG Answer Quality IEEE](../publications/d3ac18fad35bad0c7984.md)

T\. Dinesh

Agentic Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) improves answer reliability by combining retrieval, reasoning, and iterative information refinement, but repeated model calls can increase latency, computational overhead, and deployment complexity\. This paper introduces an embedded agentic retrieval framework enhanced by Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) that aims to produce efficient single\-call retrieval while maintaining answer quality similar to multi\-call agentic retrieval \(RAG\)\. The proposed method combines the following: query\-aware retrieval, context compression, relevance prioritization, and embedded reasoning together in a single generation call\. The framework combines relevant evidence into a concise context representation, eliminating the need to repeatedly invoke the language model during the retrieval and reasoning phases, and then generates the response in the end\. Experimental evaluation evaluates the quality of answers, the relevance of retrieval, the time taken to respond, the number of tokens, and the efficiency of computation on a set of representative retrieval\-based question\-answering tasks\. The proposed EARG framework achieved 98\.1% accuracy while reducing latency and maintaining high answer quality\. The framework is an efficient basis for effective agentic RAG systems that need scalable, low\-latency, and resource\-efficient generation\.

## [Deeply Supervised 3D U\-Net with Auxiliary Classification for Cerebral Aneurysms Segmentation](../publications/d3afebe454d4f46e0243.md)

Mario Mata\-Castillo; Nelly Gordillo; Boris Mederos; Dora‐Luz Flores; Vicente García; José Díaz

Cerebral aneurysms are dilations of intracranial arteries whose early detection is essential for treatment planning and rupture prevention\. Automated aneurysm segmentation remains challenging because of severe class imbalance and the small size of many lesions\. This study presents a 3D U\-Net incorporating deep supervision and an auxiliary classification branch, trained on the public ADAM dataset using skeleton\-guided patch extraction\. Fixed\-size patches \(64 × 64 × 64\) were extracted from volumes resampled to 0\.4 mm isotropic resolution, and performance was evaluated using stratified five\-fold cross\-validation\. The proposed model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0\.425 \(95% CI: 0\.362–0\.488\) and a false\-positive \(FP\) patch rate of 0\.026 \(95% CI: 0\.017–0\.035\) on the test set\. For aneurysms larger than 2\.5 mm, the Dice coefficient increased to 0\.548 \(95% CI: 0\.485–0\.612\), while the FP patch rate was 0\.030 \(95% CI: 0\.018–0\.042\), indicating improved performance on clinically relevant lesions\. Statistical analysis confirmed that the proposed model was significantly superior to the compared models in both the Dice coefficient and FP patch rate\. Although the framework produces patch\-level rather than whole\-volume segmentations, visual analysis demonstrates accurate localization of aneurysm regions\. These results indicate that combining skeleton\-guided patch extraction with deep supervision and auxiliary classification improves segmentation performance while providing reliable localization cues for automated aneurysm detection\.

## [ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ СТРУКТУРЫ МАРКЕТИНГОВЫХ ЗАТРАТ ПРЕДПРИЯТИЯ ПРИ ВНЕДРЕНИИ ИНСТРУМЕНТОВ ГЕНЕРАТИВНОГО ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА](../publications/d3bc6f4f6155ee5c259f.md)

Кристина Дмитриевна Веселова

The article analyzes changes in the structure of enterprise marketing costs resulting from the implementation of generative artificial intelligence tools\. The relevance of the study is determined by the redistribution of marketing operations from expenditures on external contractors and in\-house personnel toward digital platforms and computing resources, which changes the composition of marketing budgets\. The study reviews theoretical approaches to the classification of marketing costs and the role of generative artificial intelligence in marketing activities\. Using a case\-study method, it examines practical implementations in several Russian companies and compares available quantitative indicators before and after adoption\. The analysis reveals a reduction in the unit cost of producing marketing content and a shift in expenditure toward digital tools and the development of employee competencies\. The findings indicate that generative artificial intelligence does not eliminate marketing costs but redistributes them between budget items, increasing the importance of human involvement in task formulation, editing, quality control, and strategic planning\.

## [Research on the Value\-Added Evaluation System for Talent Cultivation Through Accounting Practice Based on AI Technology: A Case Study of Kashgar Chengxin Tourism Resource Development and Operation Co\., Ltd\.](../publications/d3bdba2cd5ea8d220500.md)

Zhong Yuan; Ma Xiaoting

Accounting practice constitutes a critical component in accounting talent cultivation\. However, traditional practice evaluations tend to prioritize outcomes while neglecting baseline differences, and often suffer from fragmented data between academic institutions and enterprises, making it difficult to scientifically assess the effectiveness of talent cultivation\. In accordance with the requirements of educational evaluation reform—specifically the “exploration of value\-added evaluation”—this paper defines the connotation of value\-added evaluation in accounting practice\-based talent cultivation\. By leveraging technologies such as AI\-assisted data collection, digital profiling, and learning analytics, this study constructs a value\-added evaluation indicator system encompassing three dimensions: professional competence, professional ethics, and digital\-intelligent literacy\. Furthermore, the paper designs a technical architecture comprising a data layer, a model layer, and an application layer, along with a value\-added calculation model based on the “baseline–process–outcome” framework\. The application process is illustrated through a practical case study conducted at Kashgar Chengxin Tourism Resource Development and Operation Co\., Ltd\. This evaluation system measures talent cultivation value through the magnitude of improvement, thereby facilitating a shift in evaluation focus from mere identification and ranking toward fostering development and refinement\. This approach provides a valuable reference for industry\-academia collaboration in accounting practice\-based talent cultivation\.

## [Color Transfer Methods in Mixed Reality Systems: A Review](../publications/d3cb7b1d00a618327d6b.md)

Alexander Buchatsky; Daria Kuzmina

Background\. One of the unsolved problems in mixed reality systems is the color consistency of embedded virtual objects with their real surroundings\. Existing methods either apply a single global transformation without accounting for lighting geometry, or demand computational resources unavailable in real time\. Aim\. To systematize and critically analyze existing color transfer, illumination estimation and image harmonization methods for mixed reality, including the latest approaches of 2024–2026\. Methods\. Analytical review of scientific publications; comparative classification by operating principle, computational requirements and scope of applicability\. Results\. A nine\-group classification is proposed; an approach to the color consistency of virtual objects based on semantic segmentation and separate correction of lightness \(L\*\) and chromatic \(a\*, b\*\) components is proposed, intended for subsequent software implementation; a comparative analysis of color difference and image quality metrics is conducted, including CIEDE2000, SSIM, PSNR, fMSE and LPIPS\. Novelty\. For the first time, color transfer and image harmonization methods for video\-based mixed reality systems are systematized in a unified review spanning 2001 to 2026\. Theoretical and practical significance\. The proposed classification supports justified selection of color correction methods in mixed reality system design, balancing quality and computational constraints\.

## [The Relatively Real, the Absolutely Real, and the Limits of Knowing](../publications/d3dec95eba98b3462d1d.md)

Aelion Kannon

The Relatively Real, the Absolutely Real, and the Limits of Knowing is a note on the distinction between limitations of knowledge within a framework and absolutely established impossibilities of knowing\. Document class: Record — Epistemology\. The note situates Gnostic\-Agnosticism, Radical Skepticism, and Radical Agnosis, the last developed through the Agnostic Tetralemma, in relation to the question of unknowability, and pairs the distinction between Relative Structure and Absolute Structure \(Structon\) with a corresponding distinction between the relatively real and the absolutely Real\. Through the examples of the rising Sun and a destroyed tree, it holds that reliable findings within an empirical framework do not settle questions of ultimate reality, and that declaring something absolutely unknowable would itself require certainty concerning the limits of knowing\. The Trans\-structural Unknown Principle is treated as an observer\-side designation of the limit of discernment, and the inquiry remains open, including toward Zenetism itself\.
