## [AI Based Marketing Strategy to Improve Sales Performance of PT Ramayana Lestari Sentosa Tbk: A Technology\-Organization\-Environment \(TOE\) and Generative AI Recombination\-Targeting\-Iteration \(RTI\) Approach](../publications/d3e64920815d4503a98c.md)

Kevin Stevanus Irwanto; Regina Violyn Widjaja; Anastasia Christy Arviana Montana; Cindy Valentina Tamrin

PT Ramayana Lestari Sentosa Tbk \(RALS\), one of Indonesia&\#x27;s oldest department store retailers, has experienced a consistent decline in sales performance and net profit in recent years, whereas comparable competitors have demonstrated financial growth over the same timeframe\. This study formulates an Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-based marketing strategy framework for RALS by integrating the Technology\-Organization\-Environment \(TOE\) model to assess organizational technology adoption readiness with the Generative AI Recombination\-Targeting\-Iteration \(RTI\) framework to structure its strategic deployment\. A descriptive qualitative approach was conducted using literature review synthesis and secondary document analysis encompassing annual reports, Public Expose presentations, and financial disclosures\. The findings reveal that RALS&\#x27;s readiness across the TOE dimensions is asymmetrical: the Technology and Organization dimensions remain at a moderate level, whereas competitive and macroeconomic pressures within the Environment dimension are critically high\. Consequently, a phased Gen\-AI RTI marketing strategy is formulated across three core pillars: \(1\) recombination, integrating fragmented legacy data assets \(Point of Sale, mobile membership, transaction records\) with Generative AI capabilities via a cost\-effective API gateway architecture; \(2\) targeting, prioritizing high\-ROI operational use cases across inventory forecasting, customer segmentation, and collaborative Sales &amp; Operations Planning; and \(3\) iteration, embedding continuous model calibration driven by structured human\-in\-the\-loop operational feedback mechanisms\. This research provides an adaptable implementation roadmap aligned with RALS&\#x27;s fiscal and workforce constraints, enriching the empirical discourse surrounding generative technology diffusion within conventional department store retail ecosystems in emerging markets\.

## [HPV DNA testing and treatment strategies for cervical pre\-cancer among women living with HIV in Papua New Guinea: a prospective clinical cohort study](../publications/d40629f2687d34f2dc56.md)

Joyce Sauk; Michaela A\. Riddell; Joy Tongela; Fredah Koluk; Hari Lialu; Grace Tan; Robert Jones; Arthur Elijah; Josephine Gabuzzi; Paulus Ripa; Pamela J Toliman; Heni Meke; Steven G\. Badman; Rebecca Guy; Marion Saville; Angela Kelly‐Hanku; Andrew JB Vallely

BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization recommends human papillomavirus \(HPV\) testing and same\-day treatment for cervical screening among women in the general population in low\- and middle\-income countries \(LMIC\)\. Among women living with HIV, additional triage is recommended due to lower specificity and predictive value of HPV testing alone in this population\. We evaluated the performance of HPV DNA testing alone and in combination with alternative triage strategies for the early detection and treatment of cervical pre\-cancer among women living with HIV in Papua New Guinea \(PNG\)\. METHODS: We did a prospective clinical cohort study among women living with HIV aged 30\-59 years attending an HIV treatment and care service\. Eligible women self\-collected a vaginal specimen for point\-of\-care HPV DNA testing on the GeneXpert platform\. All women testing HPV\-positive, and a random sample of HPV\-negative women, had enhanced visualisation of the cervix with digital colposcopy \(EVA\) and provided a clinician\-collected cervical specimen for off\-site liquid\-based cytology\. The primary outcome was the clinical performance \(sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value \[PPV, NPV\]\) of HPV testing alone and in combination with alternative triage strategies \(EVA, HPV type restriction, modified assay cut\-off values\) for detection of high\-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion \(HSIL\) or worse\. RESULTS: Between May 3, 2024 and December 12, 2024, we recruited 404 women, of whom 168 \(41\.6%\) tested positive for one or more of 14 oncogenic HPV types\. Estimated sensitivity and NPV for HSIL or worse using manufacturer\-defined cycle threshold cutoffs was &gt;99%, specificity 63\.3% \(95%CI: 58\.3%\-68\.3%\), and PPV 18\.6% \(12\.6%\-24\.6%\)\. Restricting screen\-positive to one or more of the 8 HPV types of greatest oncogenic potential had comparable sensitivity and NPV \(&gt;99%\), with specificity 70\.2% \(65\.5%\-74\.9%\) and PPV 22\.6% \(15\.6%\-29\.6%\)\. HPV 8\-type restriction with more stringent assay cut\-offs \(cycle threshold &lt;33\.99\) had sensitivity 86\.5% \(75\.3%\-97\.7%\), specificity 80\.1% \(75\.9%\-84\.3%\), PPV 30\.7% \(21\.7%\-39\.7%\), and NPV 98\.4% \(96\.9%\-99\.9%\)\. EVA provided no additional benefits to HPV testing alone\. CONCLUSIONS: Applying HPV 8\-type restriction with or without modified manufacturer assay cut\-off values to the WHO pre\-qualified Xpert HPV test improved clinical performance for detection of HSIL or worse among women living with HIV in PNG\.

## [Analysis of the Malfunction and Handling of the Navtech Radar in an Airport Perimeter Security System](../publications/d4087e0ac0d6411cc0ac.md)

Lydia Cascadia; Yuyun Suprapto; Ismat Valiyev

The Navtech AdvanceGuard radar is a core component of the Perimeter Intruder Detection System \(PIDS\) that monitors and detects object movement along the perimeter area of Juanda International Airport, Surabaya, integrated with Pan/Tilt/Zoom \(PTZ\) cameras for automatic visual tracking\. During the study period, Aviation Security \(AVSEC\) officers reported that the Navtech radar was not functioning\. This article aims to analyze the cause of the malfunction and document the repair process\. The method used was field observation and systematic troubleshooting, consisting of checking the radar status through the monitoring application, measuring the power supply, and testing the camera cabling network\. The initial inspection showed the radar status as red \(off\) due to a malfunctioning power supply, which also caused the network indicator on the switch to go dark; replacing the power supply restored the radar to normal \(running\) status\. However, further verification found that the PTZ camera could not follow the radar&\#x27;s commands due to corrosion on the RJ45 connector of the camera cable\. The repair was carried out by replacing the RJ45 connector and re\-crimping it, and the test results showed the network indicator functioning normally again, with the radar able to be monitored and to control the camera as intended\. This case study emphasizes the importance of preventive maintenance of power supplies and network connectors on outdoor electronic equipment to maintain the reliability of an airport&\#x27;s perimeter security system\. The findings are limited to a single case\.

## [English Writing Errors among University EFL Students in Somalia: An Error Analysis of Student Essays from a University in Mogadishu](../publications/d4092ce9f4e6fff90e7c.md)

James Nuwamanya; Jerald Kule; Proscovia Namubiru; Barasa Mercy Chemtai; Prashant Bhimsen Pagare; David Kessio

Background Persistent difficulties in written English remain a concern among university\-level English as a foreign language \(EFL\) learners in Somalia, including students who have received English instruction for several years\. This study examined the nature and patterns of linguistic errors in the written English of advanced undergraduate EFL learners in Mogadishu\. Methods A qualitative single\-case study design was employed at one university in Mogadishu, Somalia\. The study analysed 59 compositions produced by Level 4 EFL undergraduate students through a controlled writing task in which students wrote about a festival in their country\. The data were analysed using the error analysis approach associated with Corder, with errors identified, classified and explained\. Following the surface strategy taxonomy, errors were grouped into grammatical, mechanical, morphological and semantic categories\. Results The analysis revealed persistent difficulties across all four categories\. Grammatical errors included problems with tense and aspect, subject\-verb agreement, articles, prepositions and noun number, with addition, omission and misformation occurring frequently\. Mechanical errors involved spelling, capitalisation, punctuation and orthography, while morphological errors reflected difficulties with word formation and word boundaries\. Semantic errors were characterised by inappropriate word combinations, unclear relationships between ideas and constructions in which the intended meaning was difficult to recover\. The findings indicate that difficulties with basic written English conventions persist even among Level 4 learners who had progressed through several years of English instruction\. Conclusions The study demonstrates the need for continued, targeted university\-level writing support rather than assuming that foundational English writing skills have been mastered at advanced undergraduate level\. Regular diagnostic writing and focused feedback may help address recurring grammatical, mechanical, morphological and semantic difficulties\.

## [Enacting Digital Humanism in Education: A Comparative Case Study of Two Teachers in Greece and Australia](../publications/d40ada83137617f4af44.md)

Eunice Yin Yung Chiu

ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of digital technologies in education, accelerated by the COVID 19 pandemic, has transformed teaching and learning worldwide\. Although digital humanism has emerged as an important framework for aligning technological development with human values, its enactment in educational practice remains underexplored\. This study examines how two educators, a secondary school teacher in Greece and a university professor in Australia, integrated digital technologies whilst prioritising human relationships, student wellbeing and ethical responsibility\. Drawing on comparative case study research and thematic narrative analysis, the findings identify three interconnected dimensions of digital humanist practice: fostering human relationships, promoting collaborative and participatory learning and encouraging critical engagement with digital technologies, including artificial intelligence\. The study argues that digital humanism functions as a pedagogical orientation that guides the integration of technology into education\. The findings contribute empirical evidence to emerging scholarship on digital humanism and offer practical implications for educators navigating digital transformation\.

## [‘Too dumb to be Dutch’: learning ability test in Dutch civic integration programme](../publications/d40bb538238cc1291e5b.md)

Nadine Blankvoort; Dawit Tesfay Haile; Debbie Laliberte Rudman; Margo J\. van Hartingsveldt; Anja J\. S\. M\. Krumeich

This study presents an in\-depth analysis of the Learning Ability Test \(LAT\), a new testing tool used in Dutch civic integration\. Drawing from theoretical perspectives rooted in Science and Technology Studies, testing studies, and critical migration and integration studies, we conceptualise the test as a sociotechnical actor in the ‘ordering’ processes of contemporary jus linguarum citizenship, where membership is increasingly tied to demonstrable language proficiency\. Analysing government documents and interviews with test developers, administrators and test\-takers, we reconstruct how the LAT was designed, contested and ultimately stabilised as an ‘objective’, evidence\-based tool through various technologies of legitimacy\. We show that the LAT does far more than assess linguistic potential\. Applied at the start of the integration trajectory, it sorts subjects into differentiated learning routes and citizenship horizons, functioning as an internal raciolinguistic border that silently ranks their worth and presumed capacity for ‘self\-reliance’\. The analysis highlights how the test’s thresholds, categories and discretionary space translate political and moral judgements into the language of measurement, obscuring the racialised and discriminatory work they perform\. We conclude that this ostensibly neutral classification tool not only reproduces but also deepens hierarchies of desirable and undesirable citizens, with significant consequences for access to naturalisation and full membership\.

## [Association of TyG\-related indices with cardiometabolic multimorbidity across early cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a prospective cohort study](../publications/d4142a59b98750901238.md)

Ankai Chen; Haosen Pan; Gang Liu; Xinxiang Dong; Xintao Chen; Fulai Sun; Sukhee Ahn; Liping Ren; Maoyun Miao

Abstract Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic \(CKM\) syndrome is a systemic condition characterized by interrelated cardiac, renal, and metabolic disturbances\. The triglyceride–glucose \(TyG\) index and several of its anthropometry\-based derivatives have been increasingly recognized as surrogate markers of insulin resistance and potential predictors of cardiometabolic multimorbidity \(CMM\)\. However, whether their predictive performance differs across CKM stages 0–3 remains unclear\. This prospective cohort investigation enrolled 646 participants without established CMM at baseline\. CKM stages were classified according to AHA criteria based on obesity, metabolic abnormalities, kidney dysfunction, and subclinical cardiovascular disease\. Five surrogate indicators of insulin resistance were examined, including the TyG index and four anthropometry\-based TyG\-derived indices\. To evaluate model discrimination over time, Harrell’s time\-dependent C\-statistics were calculated\. Improvements in predictive performance were further assessed by estimating the net reclassification index \(NRI\) and the integrated discrimination index \(IDI\)\. Restricted cubic spline functions were additionally fitted to depict potential dose–response relationships between each TyG\-related measure and incident CMM\. During a four\-year follow\-up, 21\.36% of participants developed CMM\. All TyG\-related indices were significantly associated with increased CMM risk, displaying clear linear dose–response patterns\. Among participants classified as CKM stage 3, TyG\-WWI \(TyG–weight\-adjusted waist index\) showed a robust association with CMM\. Among all indicators, TyG\-WWI and TyG\-WHtR \(TyG–waist\-to\-height ratio\) showed relatively better discrimination, with meaningful improvements in NRI and IDI compared with the TyG index alone\. Across CKM stages 0–3, the TyG index and its derivative markers showed consistent and independent associations with incident CMM\. TyG\-WWI and TyG\-WHtR exhibited relatively better discrimination, highlighting their potential utility for early identification of high\-risk individuals in community screening contexts, though their direct clinical applicability requires further validation\.

## [From monitoring to maintenance support: a critical review of wind turbine condition monitoring systems and their integration into maintenance practice](../publications/d416297050f6f3b265ad.md)

Rundong Yan; Wenxian Yang; Liuyang Zhang; Ruqiang Yan; Guangrui Wen; Zhinong Li

Although condition monitoring systems \(CMS\) provide detailed information about the health of critical wind turbine components, their practical application in wind farm operations and maintenance \(O&amp;M\) remains limited, significantly diminishing their value\. The reasons for this situation are not merely technical issues, rather, a complex interplay of various factors besides the condition monitoring algorithms themselves\. The purpose of the paper is to investigate these reasons and propose a potential solution\. Through in\-depth analysis, two gaps are identified\. The first gap is the Data\-Model Gap, in which operational wind turbine data do not adequately satisfy the assumptions and quality requirements of condition monitoring algorithms\. The second is the Model\-Decision Gap, where the CMS output fails to provide sufficient information to support maintenance decisions\. Based on this, a Data\-Model\-Decision Gap \(DMDG\) framework is further developed to explain how maintenance requirements can be used to determine the CMS outputs and, subsequently, the wind turbine condition monitoring data that are needed to produce these CMS outputs\. Such a CMS design logic reverses the usual data\-to\-model development sequence by starting from understanding what kind of CMS outputs can actually support decision\-making in practical wind farm O&amp;M\. This new CMS design approach emphasizes the alignment of data, models, and decision processes through an iterative and integrated design strategy\. Research findings indicate that merely improving algorithm accuracy is insufficient to enhance the practical value of CMS\. Bridging the aforementioned gaps is the key to transforming the CMS design from “monitoring\-oriented” to “decision\-oriented” and in the end, providing “prescriptive maintenance solutions”\. This change is critical for unlocking the full potential of CMS in wind farm O&amp;M\.

## [PSICOPEDAGOGIA E INCLUSÃO ESCOLAR DE ESTUDANTES COM TDAH: UMA REVISÃO NARRATIVA DA LITERATURA](../publications/d424821885200c086577.md)

Francisco Gustavo Severino de Sousa

O Transtorno do Déficit de Atenção e Hiperatividade \(TDAH\) pode repercutir na organização das atividades, na participação e na aprendizagem escolar, exigindo respostas que articulem conhecimentos sobre o desenvolvimento e análise das condições de ensino\. Este artigo tem como objetivo discutir as contribuições e os limites da atuação psicopedagógica na inclusão escolar de estudantes com TDAH\. Trata\-se de revisão narrativa, bibliográfica e documental, constituída por seleção temática de publicações científicas e documentos institucionais localizados em fontes eletrônicas, sem pretensão de busca exaustiva\. A discussão organiza\-se em quatro eixos: compreensão do transtorno e das barreiras escolares; avaliação psicopedagógica; planejamento e acompanhamento das intervenções; e articulação entre escola, família e serviços de saúde\. A literatura selecionada oferece fundamentos para a mediação da aprendizagem e indica resultados favoráveis de determinadas intervenções escolares, mas não permite atribuir à Psicopedagogia, de forma isolada, eficácia geral sobre o TDAH\. Argumenta\-se que sua contribuição depende da definição de objetivos educacionais, da colaboração com professores e da avaliação continuada dos apoios\. Conclui\-se que a inclusão exige preservar o acesso ao currículo, enfrentar práticas estigmatizantes e compreender o estudante em sua relação com as situações de aprendizagem, reconhecendo as limitações das evidências disponíveis e a necessidade de pesquisas contextualizadas\.

## [Investigating Structural Properties and Bandgap Effect of Doping Zinc Oxide with Hafnium: A DFT Approach](../publications/d434ac69fc162e553435.md)

Onyekachi Kalu; R Mfon; S Ahams

Purpose: This study used the density functional theory \(DFT\) to investigate the characteristics of Hf\-doped ZnO in a hexagonal structural phase\. Methodology: First\-principles calculations were employed in studying the structural, electronic, and optical properties of Hf\-doped ZnO at the Zn site\. The progression of the physical properties of the daughter nuclei in the Zn0\.5Hf0\.5O alloy was also comprehensively examined using the full\-potential linearized augmented\-plane\-wave \(FP\-LAPW\) method within DFT\. Findings: Variations in the lattice parameters of the ZnO and Zn\_0\.5 Hf\_0\.5 O alloy as well as the calculated 84\.3 % difference in Bulk moduli values for these materials are indications of local structural distortions in the ZnO lattice and the production of secondary Hf phases\. A 50 % doping of ZnO with Hf shifted the system’s equilibrium volume to about 425 〖a\.u〗^3 indicating that the Hf\-doped system has lower resistance to volume deformation\. The Density of States \(DOS\) values and contributions from individual orbitals indicate that ZnO is a material of bandgap value 0\.61 eV and behaves as a semiconductor, whereas the alloy 〖\(Zn〗\_0\.5 Hf\_0\.5 O\) is a conductor with a high DOS\(3\.18 states/eV\) and strong electronic activity likely to display high electrical conductivity due to electronic transitions\. Recommendation: The obtained values of the refractive index n and extinction coefficient k indicate that Hf doping significantly modifies the optical properties of ZnO, alters its dielectric response, refractive index, extinction coefficient, and optical absorption, and that incorporating Hf into the ZnO lattice can impact on its electronic structure and electronic transitions for possible optoelectronics applications\.

## [La Inteligencia Artificial como mediación pedagógica: una mirada crítica al fortalecimiento de la competencia argumentativa en la educación básica secundaria\.](../publications/d43e403ff2ca977f9d18.md)

Ronald García Villamizar

The rapid incorporation of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) into education calls for reflection on its pedagogical meaning, particularly regarding the development of higher\-order thinking skills such as argumentation\. This article aims to analyze, from a theoretical and critical perspective, the conditions under which AI can become a pedagogical mediation rather than merely a tool for strengthening argumentative competence among secondary school students\. The work is developed through a review and discussion of recent research on generative AI, writing, critical thinking, and technological mediation in educational contexts\. The findings show that the educational value of AI does not depend on its technical capabilities but on the pedagogical intention guiding its use: when AI is used to challenge ideas, request counterarguments, and demand justification, it can act as an interlocutor that stimulates thinking; when it replaces the student&\#x27;s own textual construction, it displaces precisely the capacity it is meant to develop\. Risks related to cognitive dependency, unequal access, and academic integrity are also identified, requiring teacher guidance and critical digital literacy\. As a limitation, this analysis is theoretical and does not yet include original empirical evidence, which will be developed in the master&\#x27;s research from which this article originates\. Its originality lies in framing AI\-based pedagogical mediation as a triangular relationship between student, technology, and teacher, and in linking this framework to argumentative competence in secondary education\. It is concluded that the educational challenge is not teaching students to use AI, but forming students capable of critically dialoguing with it, questioning, contrasting, and arguing their own positions\.

## [FLARE: Physics\-Grounded Evaluation of Language\-Model Agents for Feeder Restoration with Degraded Observations](../publications/d44bdd68fda59c862d7c.md)

BHVSP Subrahmanyam; Neeraj Choudhary

Restoring service after distribution\-grid faults requires decisions from incomplete and conflicting information while respecting electrical constraints\. Addressing this need, we introduce FLARE \(Feeder\-Level Agent Restoration Evaluation\), a physics\-grounded benchmark for post\-isolation feeder restoration\. FLARE con\- tains 800 AC\-feasible cases across five observation settings and allows agents to gather evidence, evaluate switches, and perform restoration actions under fixed operational limits\. We evaluate five instruction\-tuned models over 78,750 episodes, including topology, distributed\-generation, and loading shifts\. Mean normalized regret ranges from 0\.082 to 0\.148\. Although every model has zero median regret, P95 regret ranges from 0\.814 to 1\.000, revealing an important failure tail\. Shadow replay shows that 96\.4% of 15,706 guard\-rejected actions would have caused a physical violation\. FLARE enables reproducible evaluation of language\-model based restoration support while emphasizing the need for external safety checks\.

## [Employing Artificial Intelligence in the Morphological Analysis of the English Language](../publications/d45fb2bbe342736f05c7.md)

زينب محمد لفته الباحث

This study evaluates how accurately artificial intelligence \(AI\) analyzes the morphological structure of English words\. Seventeen systems from five paradigms were compared: rule\-based analyzers, unsupervised statistical learning, the subword tokenizers of pretrained large language models \(LLMs\), supervised feature\-based learning and neural networks\. All were applied to the 57,755 English test words of the SIGMORPHON 2022 morpheme segmentation benchmark and scored with the official morpheme\-level F1, exact match, boundary detection and lemmatization accuracy\. Neural canonical segmenters were the most accurate \(90\.5–93\.6 F1; up to 90\.4% exact match\), followed by a conditional random field \(CRF; 74\.0\), a feed\-forward neural network \(71\.9\), a knowledge\-based affix\-stripping analyzer \(64\.1\), Morfessor \(45\.0\) and LLM tokenizers \(18\.1–28\.8\)\. On words without spelling change, the CRF placed boundaries nearly as well as the neural systems \(90\.2 vs 94\.8 boundary F1\)\. The neural advantage came from restoring underlying forms in the 30% of words with orthographic alternation, where dedicated surface segmenters lost 16–32 F1 points and neural systems less than one\. Only 20–33% of the boundaries drawn by LLM tokenizers coincided with morpheme boundaries, and larger vocabularies barely improved alignment\. The knowledge\-based analyzer matched a CRF trained on 5,000–10,000 annotated words, and a linguistic coding of residual errors showed that most concern the depth of analysis and annotation conventions rather than clear mistakes\. AI can thus analyze English word structure at a near\-expert level, provided it models morphophonological alternation, but LLM subword units should not be equated with morphemes\.

## [Microbiome\-Prostate Cancer Interactions: Emerging Mechanisms, Diagnostic Opportunities and Therapeutic Strategies: A Review](../publications/d47c292c7e570b2634d1.md)

M Ragavendra

Prostate cancer \(PCa\) is one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies in men with incidence increasing significantly with advancing age\. Prostate cancer \(PCa\) represents a major public health problem worldwide, with an estimated 1\.4 million new diagnoses in 2022\. Evidence is accumulating that the human microbiome may be important in PCa initiation, progression and response to therapy\. Microbial populations colonising the gut, prostate and urinary tract may possess the ability to modulate immune responses, androgen metabolism, inflammatory signaling and epithelial homeostasis, potentially contributing to prostate carcinogenesis\. Dysbiosis, referring to changes in the composition and diversity of the microbiome, has been associated with PCa, and the Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria phyla have been frequently studied in relation to disease risk and progression\. Furthermore, metabolites derived from microbiota, such as short\-chain fatty acids, bile acid derivatives and other bioactive molecules, may modulate tumor biology by affecting immune pathways, inflammation, hormonal signaling, and epigenetic mechanisms\. Recent advances in metagenomic, metabolomic and multi\-omics technologies have provided new opportunities for the identification of microbiome\-associated biomarkers for PCa detection, risk stratification and treatment monitoring\. This review provides an overview on current understanding of the microbiome–PCa relationship with a focus on microbial dysbiosis, molecular mechanisms, emerging diagnostic applications and microbiome\-targeted therapeutic approaches\. It also discusses the current limitations, research gaps, and future perspectives of microbiome\-based approaches for precision Pca management\.

## [ASSESSING PERIODICITY IN TIME SERIES DATA USING PERSISTENT HOMOLOGY](../publications/d49542b5dbe708eaa691.md)

Zabidi Abu Hasan; R\. U\. Gobithaasan; Roslan Hasni

Topological Data Analysis \(TDA\), a novel method rooted in algebraic topology, offers a powerful framework for quantifying the structure of high\-dimensional datasets\. This study focuses on Persistent Homology \(PH\), a key TDA method, to elucidate the underlying shape and structure of time series data, thereby facilitating the understanding of patterns and recurrence\. By employing Takens’ embedding to represent the time series as a high\-dimensional point cloud, this approach effectively encodes its topological characteristics, particularly periodicity\. We utilize various PH summaries, in the form of persistence vectors \(PV\), to assess periodicity by quantifying connected components $\(H\_0\)$ and one\-dimensional holes $\(H\_1\)$\. The methodology is validated on ten synthetic datasets, each comprising 200 data points and exhibiting varying levels of periodicity, amplitude, and frequency\. The optimal window size for the sliding window embedding is determined by maximizing the $PD\_\{\\text\{max\}\}$ score\. Subsequently, the $L^1$\-norm of the PVs is computed to quantify periodicity\. Under optimal window selection $\(D=14\)$, the cosine signal achieves the highest periodicity, followed by damped cosine and linear trend\. Formal quantitative stability analysis identifies one of the two Sliding Window 1\-Persistence Scoring \(SW1PerS\) baselines, SW2, as the most stable representation under both Gaussian noise \(Rank Instability Index, RII$=0\.243$\) and missing data \(Mean Absolute Rank Deviation, MARD=0\.117\), with the Persistence Landscape Score \(PLS\) and SW1 ranking closely behind; differences under noise are not statistically significant \(Friedman $p=0\.42$\), while those under missing data are significant $\(p=0\.001\)$\. A comparison against non\-topological baselines \(FFT\-based spectral entropy, autocorrelation, and recurrence quantification analysis\) demonstrates that PLS achieves Kendall $\\tau=0\.867$, substantially outperforming spectral entropy \(SE: $\\tau=0\.733$\) which is the only non\-topological baseline that achieves statistically significant concordance $\(p=0\.002\)$, while the autocorrelation peak ratio \(APR: $\\tau=\-0\.289$\) and recurrence rate \(RR: $\\tau=\-0\.200$\) yield non\-significant negative concordance on these synthetic signals\.

## [Design and Implementation of a Raspberry Pi\-Based Smart Wet and Dry Waste Segregation System Using AI](../publications/d4a5ed248a6c077c1744.md)



With increasing urbanization and consumerism, the global Municipal Solid Waste \(MSW\) generation has skyrocketed\.The ever\-growing MSW collection, transportation and disposal infrastructure is insufficient and is overwhelmed by the volume of waste generated\.Manual segregation of wet and dry MSW is a cumbersome process because of unmethodized sorting, low accuracy and 60\-70% of wet recyclable waste still head into landfills\.We hence propose and analyze an AIenabled intelligent, automated, and low\-cost trash segregation prototype that classifies household level wet or dry trash using camera modules and onboard computer module, runs convolution neural network model on raspberry pi 4 to detect the object, actuates servo pan\-tilt into the bin, and loads onto ultrasonic sensors to monitor bin fill level and load cells with HX711 amplifier to measure the dry and wet mass accumulated in each bin\.Such an intelligent waste segregation system can cater to home, school, Institutional and community level waste segregation needs\.

## [Evolution of chaotic stick–slip frictional behavior affected by dynamic normal stress disturbances: parameter study based on spring\-block model](../publications/d4a70162683c9ceb7fc5.md)

Kang Tao; Heinz Konietzky

Frictional sliding is ubiquitous in both natural phenomena and engineering systems, often occurring under dynamic normal stress conditions, yet the theoretical understanding of such scenarios remains limited\. This study employs a verified one\-dimensional spring\-block model, incorporating rate\- and state\-dependent friction law, to investigate the evolution of stick–slip behavior under cyclic normal stress perturbations\. We conduct a systematic parametric analysis to explore how the normalized amplitude and frequency of the normal stress oscillations influence the chaotic frictional behavior\. The results demonstrate that cyclic normal stress dramatically alters the frictional style\. While the model exhibits periodic stick slip under constant normal stress, specific combinations of intermediate amplitude and frequency drive the frictional style into a chaotic regime characterized by irregular and unpredictable stress drops\. We employ a Schuster test to reveal that the timing of chaotic slip events can be statistically correlated with the phase angle of normal unloading beyond critical perturbation amplitude\. The estimated largest Lyapunov exponent in the specific space supports the presence of chaotic sensitivity in the observable response, underscoring the sensitivity of frictional process to external loading conditions\. These findings preliminarily highlight the intrinsic potential for deterministic chaos during frictional sliding, with implications for predicting frictional instabilities in engineering safety and seismology\.

## [Orgasmic Meditation, Sleep, and Next\-Day Somatic Distress: A 30\-Day Observational Study](../publications/d4a86fd7c6b4f35dce04.md)

Caroline Griggs

Background: Orgasmic Meditation \(OM\) is a structured attention\-training practice conducted between two people who follow a predefined set of detailed instructions\.One person, the stroker, gently strokes the clitoris of the other person, the strokee, for 15 minutes while both place their attention on the point of contact and notice what they feel\.Climax is not the goal\.This study examined whether OM practice was associated with app\-assessed sleep and next\-morning Tumescence Survey responses\.Methods: In this 30\-day observational study, 41 experienced OM practitioners enrolled, and 36 contributed analyzable data, yielding 1,026 participant\-nights\.The Sleep Cycle Premium application assessed sleep quality, duration, regularity, and time to sleep onset\.Each morning, participants reported whether they had practiced OM the previous day and completed the 15\-item Tumescence Survey\.Linear mixed\-effects models accounted for repeated nights from the same participants and separated within\-person from between\-person associations\.Results: OM practice was not significantly associated with sleep quality \(b = \-1\.87index points; 95% CI: \-3\.96 to 0\.21; p = \.079\),sleep duration \(\-10\.11minutes; 95% CI: \-22\.37 to 2\.15; p = \.106\),time to sleep onset \(\+2\.01 minutes; p = \.225\),or sleep regularity \(\+0\.05; p = \.948\)\.On mornings after OM, participants reported less dissociation from their bodies and less agitation\.These two item\-level associations remained significant after correction for 15 comparisons\.Craving and irritability scores were slightly lower after OM, but the differences were not statistically significant\.Factor 2, which combined craving, physical discomfort, agitation, and dissociation, was lower after OM in the primary model \(b = \-0\.77;95% CI: \-1\.17 to \-0\.37; p &lt; \.001\)\.The estimate weakened when the OM association was allowed to vary among participants \(b = \-0\.67;95% CI: \-1\.36 to 0\.02; p = \.056\)\.Sleep did not mediate or modify this association\.With OM practice and sleep duration in the same model, a day of OM was associated with the same reduction in Factor 2 as 3\.8 additional hours of sleep \(95% CI: 1\.8 to 9\.5\), and with the same reduction in the total survey score as 1\.7 additional hours \(95% CI: 0\.2 to 3\.9\)\.Climax was reported on 19\.4% of OM days and was not associated with sleep outcomes within OM days\.Conclusions: OM practice was not associated with app\-assessed sleep in this sample\.On mornings after OM, participants reported less dissociation from their bodies and less agitation, and these differences were not explained by sleep duration\.The difference associated with an OM day was comparable in size to the difference associated with 3\.8 additional hours of sleep for Factor 2 and 1\.7 additional hours for the total survey score\.The estimates weakened when the OM association was allowed to vary among participants\.This comparison describes the relative size of observational associations and does not show that OM reduces sleep need\.The sample was small and highly selected, and neither the sleep application nor the Tumescence Survey has been validated for this use\.Controlled studies using validated measures are needed\.

## [Serum neuron\-derived extracellular vesicle mitochondrial DNA as a potential biomarker for mild cognitive impairment due to AD](../publications/d4a9faf3dc1ec1f7f39a.md)

Danhong Lin; Yashi Luo; Xiaxia Qiu; Peng Ye; Rongbing Chen; Wenshen Xu; Ru Zheng; Xiaoqin Fu; Kengna Fan; Dengbin Chen; Bin Yang; 陈龙飞; Qishui Ou; Xiaofeng Liu

Background Mild cognitive impairment \(MCI\) represents the initial clinical manifestation, eventually evolving into the distinctive features of Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\), making its early identification crucial\. Notably, mitochondrial dysfunction is an early characteristic of AD\. Neuron\-derived extracellular vesicles \(NDEVs\) can cross the blood\-brain barrier, and their mitochondrial DNA \(mtDNA\) can reflect intracerebral lesions, showing considerable potential\. In this study, we investigated the alterations in mtDNA within serum NDEVs and evaluated their potential as early diagnostic biomarkers for MCI due to AD\. Methods A total of 42 MCI patients, 49 AD patients, and 57 age\-matched cognitively unimpaired \(CU\) controls were enrolled\. Serum NDEVs were enriched and characterized, and their mtDNA levels were quantified by qPCR\. ROC curve was used to analyze diagnostic performance, and the integration of multimodal biomarkers was explored\. Results Serum NDEVs mtDNA levels were decreased in patients with AD\-MCI, and a significant positive correlation was observed between serum NDEVs mtDNA levels and MMSE scores in MCI patients \( r = 0\.4864, P = 0\.0407\), and a similar association was observed in the AD group \( r = 0\.3857, P = 0\.0469\)\. In terms of diagnostic performance, serum NDEV mtDNA demonstrated outstanding discrimination between CU controls and AD subjects, achieving an area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.965 \(95% CI: 0\.933–0\.997\), with 97\.92% sensitivity and 89\.09% specificity\. Moreover, it also demonstrated moderate efficacy in differentiating early MCI from AD \(AUC = 0\.736, 95% CI: 0\.629–0\.842; sensitivity = 72\.92%, specificity = 66\.67%\)\. In exploratory analyses of clinical and metabolic factors, serum NDEV mtDNA levels were positively correlated with HCY in MCI patients, while in AD patients, NDEV mtDNA levels were elevated in those with diabetes and positively correlated with TG\. Notably, integrating NDEV mtDNA with established biomarkers, including p\-Tau 217, GFAP, and APOE ε4 carrier status, significantly improved the accuracy of MCI detection, highlighting its value in multimodal biomarker strategies\. Conclusion Serum NDEVs mtDNA levels were significantly reduced in patients with MCI and AD, suggesting strong potential as an early diagnostic biomarker for MCI due to AD\.

## [دور الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحسين البيانات الجغرافية](../publications/d4b18932e76c2664218b.md)

شهدت الدراسات الجغرافية في العقود الأخيرة تطوراً ملحوظاً نتيجة التقدم السريع في تقنيات المعلومات والاتصال، وخاصة مع ظهور تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي التي أصبحت تلعب دوراً محورياً في معالجة وتحليل البيانات المكانية\. وتُعد البيانات الجغرافية من أكثر أنواع البيانات تعقيداً نظراً لارتباطها بالموقع والزمان وتعدد مصادرها مثل صور الأقمار الصناعية ونظم المعلومات الجغرافية وأجهزة الاستشعار المختلفة\. يهدف هذا المقال إلى إبراز دور الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحسين جودة البيانات الجغرافية من خلال تطوير أساليب جمعها ومعالجتها وتحليلها، بالإضافة إلى استعراض أهم التطبيقات العملية لهذه التقنيات في مجالات التخطيط العمراني وإدارة الموارد الطبيعية ومراقبة التغيرات البيئية\. كما يناقش البحث التحديات التي تواجه استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في المجال الجغرافي وآفاقه المستقبلية في تطوير نظم المعلومات الجغرافية الذكية\. وتشير النتائج إلى أن دمج تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي مع البيانات الجغرافية يسهم في تحسين دقة التحليل المكاني وتسريع عمليات المعالجة، مما يعزز عملية اتخاذ القرار في العديد من المجالات التنموية\.

## [SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture](../publications/d4b5151ae71e8a9c4f33.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

SAP AI Core provides enterprise capabilities for executing, managing, and operationalizing Artificial Intelligence workloads within SAP Business Technology Platform landscapes\. Enterprise adoption requires a reference architecture that connects model runtime, data, applications, identity, security, integration, observability, Responsible AI, and lifecycle governance\. This paper proposes a SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture spanning user and application channels, AI service orchestration, model runtime, data and feature access, SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP Integration Suite, model repositories, security controls, monitoring, and governance\. The architecture supports predictive AI, custom machine learning, Generative AI, embeddings, and agentic services while maintaining clean\-core integration, least privilege, auditability, resilience, and business accountability\. It also defines implementation patterns, deployment controls, model lifecycle processes, and operational KPIs/KRIs\. The proposed architecture enables organizations to scale AI on SAP BTP in a secure, reusable, and governed manner\.

## [Worker deaugmentation risk in tourism and hospitality automation: evidence from a back\-of\-the\-house occupation](../publications/d4b5aea89cc27e2162ce.md)

Jacques Bulchand‐Gidumal; Santiago Melián González

Worker augmentation dominates current narratives about robotics and AI\. These technologies may, however, also produce worker deaugmentation, which occurs when technology automates the tasks employees value most while leaving them responsible for lower\-value, monotonous activities\. This letter introduces worker deaugmentation, argues that it is particularly relevant in tourism and hospitality, where occupations combine diverse manual and cognitive tasks, and advances two propositions\. We illustrate them in a back\-of\-the\-house occupation, rating the 14 core tasks O\*NET assigns to the cook occupation, evaluating each according to its subjective value and likelihood of automation\. Expert assessments indicate that seven support the deaugmentation effect: five highly valued tasks are highly automatable, whereas two low\-value tasks appear resistant to automation\. These findings suggest that automation may reduce job quality and intrinsic motivation\. A two\-by\-two framework distinguishes deaugmentation risk from beneficial automation and indicates where job design should intervene\.

## [AI\-Driven Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening Using LightGBM and Behavioral Analysis](../publications/d4bb96d79c4689d520f3.md)

Arul Princy\. A; Rohini T\.; Visali

Autism Spectrum Disorder \(ASD\) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by problems with communication, social interaction, and behavior patterns\. Early detection of autism spectrum disorder is crucial for appropriate treatment and positive development\. The existing procedures are lengthy and rely on manual assessment\. This research work proposes a machine learning solution for the early detection of autism spectrum disorder based on the behavioral data obtained from a questionnaire, along with the demographic features\. Different approaches to classification, including Decision Tree, K\-Nearest Neighbors \(KNN\), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine \(LightGBM\) are tested to select the most efficient method for prediction\. LightGBM proves to be the best approach because of its efficiency with structured data\. In order to improve model transparency and facilitate decision\-making in clinical practice, SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) are incorporated to assess and measure the impact of specific features\. The developed model ensures 97% accuracy, 97% precision, 92% recall, and 94% F1\-score on the test dataset\. The feature importance analysis reveals that the behavioral factors such as communication issues, problems in making eye contact, interaction problems, and repetition are among the important features contributing to the prediction of ASD\. By combining high predictive accuracy with transparency, the proposed solution presents a reliable, efficient, and easy\-to\-use approach for early ASD screening\.

## [Nuclear mechanomics beyond stiffness: toward a genuine mechanical state space](../publications/d4be6fa27ef6f67c7146.md)

Diego Herráez‐Aguilar; Carlos del Pozo; Lucía Benito\-Barca; Sonia Contera; Manuel R\. Ramírez; Francisco Monroy

Mechanical measurements of the nucleus remain fragmented across modalities and are often reduced to scalar “stiffness” proxies\. We define the Genuine Nuclear Mechanome as a regime\-aware, physically interpretable representation of intrinsic nuclear mechanical state\. Readouts from non\-equivalent techniques are converted into model\-dependent descriptors and mapped onto experimentally supported chromatin contexts\. A living\-HeLa reconstruction illustrates the framework, which requires state preservation, identifiability, uncertainty propagation and cross\-regime validation for multimodal systems biology\.

## [Integrating morphological embryo quality scoring and untargeted metabolomics identifies candidate biomarkers in Bali cattle embryos](../publications/d4c107e36922ddf04ced.md)

Fuad Hasan; Rahmat Rahmat; Dian Tria Fatmila; Athhar Manabi Diansyah; Muhammad Fajar Amrullah; Syahruddin Said; An Nahl Nur Sa&\#x27;ad

Background and Aim: Embryo quality is a major determinant of the efficiency of in vitro embryo production in cattle\. Although morphological assessment is routinely used for embryo selection, it may not fully reflect the underlying metabolic state\. Metabolomics may complement morphological evaluation by identifying biochemical characteristics associated with embryo quality\. This study aimed to evaluate Bali cattle embryo quality and identify candidate metabolite biomarkers by integrating multi\-parameter morphological scoring with liquid chromatography–high\-resolution mass spectrometry \(LC–HRMS\)\-based untargeted metabolomics\. Materials and Methods: Thirty Bali cattle embryos produced through in vitro fertilization were evaluated using six morphological parameters: general embryo structure, blastomere uniformity, fragmentation, cellular compaction, zona pellucida condition, and cellular degeneration\. Embryos were classified as good\- or poor\-quality according to their composite quality scores\. Three embryos from the same quality group were pooled per metabolomic sample, generating 10 analytical pools \(five/group\)\. Untargeted LC–HRMS metabolomics, differential metabolite analysis, multivariate analysis, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes\-based functional analysis, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and correlation analysis were performed\. Candidate biomarkers were prioritized using differential patterns, variable importance in projection scores &gt;1, pathway involvement, area under the curve values &gt;0\.8, and significant associations with embryo quality parameters\. Results: Good quality embryos had significantly higher general embryo structure, blastomere uniformity, cellular compaction, zona pellucida condition, and total quality scores\. Metabolomic profiles differed between quality groups\. Nine metabolites were prioritized as candidate biomarkers\. Pyruvate, citrate, \(S\)\-malate, 2\-oxoglutarate, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate, and L\-glutamate were higher in good quality embryos, whereas succinate, oxidized glutathione, and L\-tyrosine were higher in poor\-quality embryos\. These metabolites were principally associated with energy metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and redox regulation and showed significant associations with morphological embryo quality parameters\. Conclusion: Integrating morphological scoring with untargeted metabolomic profiling revealed coordinated metabolic differences associated with Bali cattle embryo quality\. The nine\-metabolite panel represents a set of candidates, rather than validated, biomarkers because the metabolomic analysis was based on pooled embryos and a small discovery dataset\. Individual embryo analysis and validation in larger independent cohorts are required before predictive or practical application\. Keywords: Bali cattle, candidate biomarkers, embryo quality, energy metabolism, in vitro fertilization, metabolomics, oxidative balance, untargeted metabolomics\.

## [Optogenetic modeling of wake\-like transcriptional progression in human SH\-SY5Y neuronal cells](../publications/d4c778dc3cfa3dba306a.md)

Shintaro Yamazaki; William Gee; Utham K\. Valekunja; Akhilesh B\. Reddy

Sleep deprivation induces widespread transcriptional remodeling in the brain, but the extent to which this response arises from sustained neuronal excitation rather than systemic confounders remains unclear\. Here we establish a reductionist human neuronal model to isolate the cell\-autonomous effects of prolonged depolarization\. Optogenetic stimulation of SH\-SY5Y cells produced controlled calcium influx and robust induction of activity\-dependent genes, enabling precise manipulation of excitation history\. Time\-resolved RNA sequencing revealed that sustained excitation partitions transcriptional responses into discrete temporal modules, including early\-, mid\-, and late\-peaking, sustained, biphasic, and suppressed patterns, each with distinct functional signatures\. At the pathway level, these modules combine into sequential transcriptional states that evolve directionally across stimulation and recovery\. Transitions were asymmetric, indicating excitation\-history\-dependent reorganization rather than simple reversal\. Cross\-dataset comparisons revealed selective concordance between defined temporal modules and in vivo sleep deprivation signatures\. Together, these findings demonstrate that sustained neuronal excitation alone can drive staged, wake\-like transcriptional progression, linking gene\-level temporal dynamics to higher\-order regulatory states\.

## [Novel sequence type 2040 non\-O1/non\-O139 Vibrio cholerae from southern China: genomic and phenotypic features with molecular epidemiological implications](../publications/d4cc121173d4cf697097.md)

夏远志; Jiawei Ding; Jinyan Kai; Chunhong Xie; Yanqin Nie; Jiaqiu Ru; Lianjiang Huang; Juan Wen

Introduction Non\-toxigenic non\-O1/non\-O139 Vibrio cholerae \(NOVC\) are opportunistic aquatic pathogens that cause extraintestinal infections including bacteremia, particularly in patients with underlying comorbidities\. The incidence of NOVC bacteremia has increased in coastal China, yet the genomic diversity and population structure of clinical NOVC isolates remain poorly defined\. This study aimed to characterize a clinical NOVC isolate from southern China at both phenotypic and genomic levels\. Methods We recovered a clinical NOVC isolate \(HL2601\) from a bloodstream infection case in Xiamen, China\. Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by broth microdilution and disk diffusion\. Whole\-genome sequencing was performed, followed by multilocus sequence typing \(MLST\), average nucleotide identity \(ANI\) analysis, core\-genome phylogeny reconstruction, virulence and resistance gene profiling, and quantitative genome collinearity and structural variation analysis\. Results The isolate was confirmed as V\. cholerae and assigned to a novel sequence type, ST2040\. It lacked cholera toxin and toxin\-coregulated pilus genes but harbored multiple alternative virulence determinants, including intact type II and type VI secretion systems, RTX toxin, hemolysins, and iron uptake systems\. HL2601 was susceptible to all 11 tested antibiotics and clustered phylogenetically with extraintestinal clinical and environmental NOVC strains, suggesting a potential environmental reservoir origin\. Discussion These findings expand the known genomic diversity of clinical NOVC in China\. They provide a genomic baseline for surveillance of emerging NOVC clones and inform empirical antibiotic selection for extraintestinal vibriosis in coastal regions\.

## [Ablation study of RGB encoding strategies for diffusion\-based dual\-view mammogram synthesis](../publications/d4cd2847d5d26eca931b.md)

Jorge Alberto Garza\-Abdala; Gerardo Alejandro Fumagal\-González; Daly Avendaño; Servando Cardona; Sadam Hussain; Eduardo de Ávila\-Armenta; Jasiel Toscano; Diana Sofia Milagros Rosales Gurmendi; Alma Pedro; José G\. Tamez‐Peña

The availability of large multi\-view mammographic datasets is limited by privacy concerns and acquisition variability, restricting the development of robust artificial intelligence models\. This study investigates the impact of RGB encoding strategies on diffusion\-based simultaneous dual\-view mammogram synthesis\. A Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model was fine\-tuned using RGB representations that encode craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views with different third\-channel formulations\. Three encoding strategies were evaluated using image quality metrics, distribution\-based comparisons, and anatomical consistency measurements\. Results show that zero\-channel and difference representations achieved comparable performance, while sum\-based encoding provided lower performance\. These findings highlight the importance of input representation design for generating consistent synthetic multi\-view mammograms\.

## [Integração entre Diagnóstico por Imagem, Conduta Clínica e Abordagem Cirúrgica no Abdome Agudo](../publications/d4d5e4736eea1ca945f5.md)

Mahayla Vernes Abu El Haje; Bruna Brekesi Sofia Duarte; Gabriela Fernandes Terra; Pedro Henrique Machado de Farias Santos; Adriel Vernes Abu El Haje

Objetivo: Sintetizar a evidência sobre a integração entre diagnóstico por imagem, conduta clínica e abordagem cirúrgica no abdome agudo\. Método: Revisão integrativa com busca na PubMed em outubro de 2026 e classificação do nível de evidência\. Resultados: De 243 registros, 25 estudos compuseram a síntese, entre eles dois ensaios randomizados\. A tomografia precoce aumentou os diagnósticos corretos em 24 horas e reduziu a mortalidade em seis meses; vias de atendimento e protocolos perioperatórios padronizados associaram\-se a menor mortalidade\. ## [PRE\-SERVICE ENGLISH TEACHERS&\#x27; ACCEPTANCE AND USE OF AI\-ENABLED LANGUAGE LEARNING TOOLS](../publications/d4e2f0439d9c5bbaa399.md)

Маржан Дуйсенова; Marzhan Moldakassymovna Duisenova

Future language teachers meet AI\-enabled language learning tools twice: as learners who use them now, and as professionals who may soon bring them into their own classrooms\. This article reports a cross\-sectional survey of pre\-service English teachers at one Kazakhstani pedagogical university\. Thirty\-eight third\- and fourth\-year students took part, and 33 confirmed using AI\-enabled language learning tools within the previous twelve months\. The questionnaire was adapted from the Technology Acceptance Model and covered perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, behavioral intention, an additional block on future professional use, a usage profile, and two open\-ended questions\. Internal consistency of the multi\-item scales was satisfactory \(Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha 0\.74–0\.80\)\. ChatGPT\-type chatbots turned out to be the most widely used tools \(81\.8%\), and vocabulary and writing were the skills students practised most often\. Perceived usefulness received the highest composite rating \(M = 3\.80\) and perceived ease of use the lowest \(M = 3\.44\)\. Usefulness correlated positively with behavioral intention \(rho = 0\.53, p = 0\.002\), whereas usage frequency showed no significant association with intention\. Open\-ended responses pointed to infrastructural barriers, distrust of answer accuracy, and the quality of Kazakh\-language adaptation\. Implications for foreign language teacher education programmes are discussed\.

## [Anticipatory Anxiety and Psychological Well\-Being in Middle\-Aged Adults with Claustrophobia](../publications/d4e7c003676b5f7c7f55.md)

Reena Kumari Jain

Claustrophobia can produce anxiety before exposure to confined environments, but its relationship with psychological well\-being remains insufficiently explored\. This study examined anticipatory anxiety and psychological well\-being among middle\-aged Indian adults with claustrophobia and compared individuals with predominant fears of restriction and suffocation\. A cross\-sectional survey included 12 adults aged 40 to 60 years who reported a diagnosis of claustrophobia\. Participants completed the Claustrophobia Questionnaire and Ryff&\#x27;s 42\-item Scales of Psychological Well\-Being\. Moderate anticipatory anxiety was reported by 58\.3% of participants, while 83\.3% demonstrated moderate psychological well\-being\. Fear of restriction predominated in 66\.7% of participants\. Anticipatory anxiety was not significantly associated with overall psychological well\-being but showed significant negative correlations with self\-acceptance \(s = \-\.79\) and personal growth \(rs = \-\.67\)\. Differences between predominant fear groups were not statistically significant\. These preliminary findings suggest that anticipatory anxiety may be associated with selected dimensions of psychological well\-being\. Larger studies using dedicated measures of anticipatory anxiety are needed to confirm these relationships and examine their clinical implications\.

## [Regulating Artificial Cultural Production\. Comparing Cultural Policy Strategies in Light of the AI Revolution](../publications/d4f08513a0a66b7f6875.md)

Ole Marius Hylland

The rapid development of artificial intelligence \(AI\) technology has been a cause of concern, curiosity, speculation, widespread media interest, and both utopian and dystopian perspectives on potential consequences\. The cultural sector has been one of the sectors that has attracted the most attention and controversy in the AI buzz, related to cultural workers fearing that their jobs might disappear, concern of rights\-holders, and to the lack of remuneration for cultural content used for AI training\. This study investigates existing Nordic attempts to include AI in explicit cultural policies and cultural policy strategies, as well as cultural production in general AI strategies\. In what way do current and recent cultural policy strategies reflect \(upon\) AI? In what way and to what extent do current/recent AI strategies reflect on and address the cultural production sector? The article shows that neither cultural policy nor AI strategies have thoroughly discussed AI and cultural production\. The policy narratives of these strategies are mainly assertions that they are complex issues with pros and cons\. The article concludes by arguing that the fundamental practical, ideological, and terminological challenges to cultural policy from AI are far from being met through updated and informed production of policy documents\.

## [Dimensionality Reduction Strategy on Four\-Dimensional Data Cubes with Independent Slices and Hyper\-Slices Focusing on Variability Structure and Components](../publications/d4f54cb7f815fe33e1c2.md)

Zacharenia Kyrana; Nikolaos Papafilippou; Emmanouil D\. Pratsinakis; Alexandra\-Maria Michaelidou; Christos A\. Dordas; Angelos Markos; Georgios C\. Menexes

Data cubes are p\-dimensional data structures \(p ≥ 3\)\. In most biological sciences, the key point of statistical data analysis is the study of variability, focusing on its structure and components\. The proposed strategy was based on principal component analysis \(PCA\) and the idea of decomposing the total variability of a four\-dimensional cube \(p = 4\) into variability between and within the cube’s slices and hyper\-slices\. The aim of this study was to propose new insights into the dimensionality reduction of four\-dimensional cubes with independent slices and hyper\-slices and equal or unequal number of experimental units per slice within each hyper\-slice\. As an example, the simulated dataset “Basil” from the field of agriculture was used\. The fourth dimension consisted of three irrigation levels \(hyper\-slices\)\. The third dimension consisted of five basil varieties \(slices\)\. The second dimension consisted of seven quantitative traits\-variables, and the first dimension consisted of different plants\. The proposed strategy allowed for a detailed examination of the effect of slices and hyper\-slices on the overall data cube structure by highlighting the dominant influence of irrigation levels\. Also, the study highlighted the controversial case of the variability decomposition on unbalanced four\-dimensional cubes\. For future research, various clustering strategies could be applied, in terms of the distance metric and the linkage method, either to the initial cubes or to the PCA components’ scores from each variability data matrix\. The proposed strategy could also be applied to data cubes with greater imbalance, in terms of sample size, between slices, and hyper\-slices\. ## [Deployment of edge\-lightweight AI vertical models in multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization of tech\-long production line](../publications/d4f6a53d71f502430380.md)

Xiaoman Wu; Xingshuo Tao; yu cheng; Zeyu Wang

Aiming at the problems that the abnormal state of high\-speed liquid packaging production lines is difficult to identify in time, the computing power of edge controller is limited, and the energy consumption regulation and condition monitoring are separated from each other, a multimodal lightweight artificial intelligence \(AI\) system embedded in Tech\-Long production controller is constructed; this realizes the collaborative optimization of abnormal operation window identification and energy consumption of the whole line\. First, this study collects vibration, acoustic, and thermal signals from the bottle blowing, filling, and packaging sections; it also constructs cross\-sectional anomaly characterization through time synchronization, feature\-level alignment, and hierarchical fusion\. Subsequently, Feather Convolutional Neural Network \(FeatherCNN\) is reconstructed using kernel fusion, channel compression, and 4\-bit Integer \(INT4\) quantization to reduce model computation and storage load; thus, the network can adapt to resource\-constrained Advanced RISC Machine \(ARM\) edge controllers\. Finally, a dual\-layer control chain is built, composed of continuous basic energy\-saving and anomaly risk\-weighted correction, so that anomaly scores influence the updates of temperature zones, valve openings, and heat\-sealing parameters via dynamic weights and adjustment gains\. The experimental results demonstrate that the anomaly window recognition accuracy of multimodal FeatherCNN reaches 0\.931, which is superior to traditional machine learning models, deep learning baselines and various single\-modal structures\. The lightweight processing reduces Floating\-Point Operations \(FLOPs\) from 3\.42×10⁹ to 0\.58×10⁹, a decrease of approximately 83%\. The inference latency of the complete model on the ARM controller is shortened from 18\.63 milliseconds \(ms\) to 7\.41 ms\. Under the controlled conditions of fixed production line speed, material specifications, and statistical windows, the dual\-layer collaborative control has reduced the overall energy consumption of the whole line by 26%\. The results show that multimodal anomaly identification, model lightweighting, and energy\-saving parameter tuning can work together in the same edge decision chain\. The framework verifies the feasibility of resource\-constrained controllers supporting abnormal monitoring and energy consumption regulation of the entire packaging line; meanwhile, it provides an engineering reference for edge intelligent deployment of similar high\-speed liquid packaging lines\.

## [HIPA: A Human Information Processing Architecture for LLM Responses in Ergonomic Design](../publications/d4fa23eca69b09fb2edb.md)

Youngjun Park; Jaekyu Park; Youngjae Im

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used for UI/UX evaluation and design decision support; however, their responses are often generated as implicit and unstructured outputs, making cognitive processes and judgment rationale difficult to trace\. Moreover, the quality of LLM\-based judgments may vary depending on users’ prompting proficiency, limiting the consistency of AI\-assisted evaluation\. This study proposes HIPA \(Human Information Processing Architecture\), a cognitive response architecture that structures LLM outputs based on the human information processing \(HIP\) model and investigates the manifestation of human cognitive stages in conventional LLM responses\. HIPA maps four HIP stages—perception, working memory, decision making, and response execution—into a two\-stage response structure consisting of information provision and judgment support through knowledge\-grounded prompting with GPT\-4o\. An exploratory evaluation was conducted with seven participants with different prompting proficiency levels who assessed the same mobile login interface using a general LLM\. Responses were coded according to HIP\-stage manifestation using a three\-point scale\. The results showed that perception and response execution were consistently observed, whereas working memory and decision\-making stages varied depending on prompt systematicity\. These findings indicate that general LLM responses do not inherently provide cognitively structured judgment support\. HIPA provides a human\-centered framework for developing AI\-assisted UI/UX evaluation systems based on human cognitive principles\.

## [Community learning drives children’s digital literacy development: evidence for reconstructing broken education ecosystems](../publications/d5032ca836fe59ede2a8.md)

Judit Horgas; Eszter Salamon; Aristidis Protopsaltis

Digital literacy development in children is widely assumed to occur primarily through formal schooling, yet growing evidence suggests that community learning—encompassing families, peers, and non\-formal organizations—has become the dominant pathway through which children acquire digital skills and competences\. This article focuses on the current distribution of digital literacy education responsibilities across formal and informal actors, examines how community\-based learning both mitigates and reproduces inequality, and analyses the implications of rights\-based frameworks for children’s digital participation and protection\. Drawing on quantitative survey data collected from primary and secondary school students, their teachers, school leaders, and parents in Hungary and the Netherlands within the framework of the EFFEct \(effective family and community engagement in technology\) horizon Europe project, qualitative and quantitative research from the EU\-funded DRONE \(digital literacy and combat of disinformation among vulnerable groups of adolescents\) and legal research in the SAILS \(supporting and advocating for inclusive learning spaces\) projects, and a systematic review of recent international scholarship, the study provides multi\-level empirical evidence on stakeholder roles in digital literacy education ecosystems\. across all four student groups surveyed, 100% of substantive responses indicated no perceived school\-based instruction on foundational digital citizenship and online safety skills, despite near\-universal device access, revealing a systematic curricular gap that contrasts sharply with children’s high levels of digital connectivity\. Parent data from 135 participants across six European countries in the DRONE project showed that families bear primary responsibility for teaching digital literacy to their children\. This finding is associated with both the limited availability and delayed implementation of structured school\-based programs, and the increasingly early engagement of children with digital technologies, through which digital skills and habits are formed prior to entry into formal schooling\. Addressing this fragmentation requires an urgent and systemic reconstruction of digital literacy education through coordinated multi\-stakeholder governance, curricular reform, teacher empowerment, and inclusive community\-based approaches that explicitly recognizes the central role of families and communities in children’s digital development\.
