## [ANÁLISE COMPARATIVA DE SISTEMAS DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL APLICADOS À MAMOGRAFIA E SUAS CONTRIBUIÇÕES PARA A PRÁTICA BIOMÉDICA](../publications/d5090398b490355cece4.md)

Ellen Carniato; Maria Luiza Guimarães Lima; Gabrielle Dutra Zessin; Bárbara Biazon Siqueira

A incorporação de tecnologias digitais e de recursos de inteligência artificial ao diagnóstico por imagem tem ampliado as possibilidades de suporte à avaliação mamográfica e à atuação dos profissionais da saúde\. Nesse contexto, os sistemas de inteligência artificial voltados à análise e ao suporte diagnóstico apresentam diferentes funcionalidades e níveis de aplicabilidade, tornando necessária a compreensão de seus recursos e limitações\. O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar uma análise comparativa de sistemas de inteligência artificial relacionados ao diagnóstico por imagem, com ênfase na mamografia, buscando identificar suas principais funcionalidades e possíveis contribuições para a prática biomédica\. Trata\-se de um estudo exploratório, descritivo e comparativo, de abordagem predominantemente qualitativa, desenvolvido por meio de levantamento bibliográfico e análise documental\. Foram consideradas informações provenientes de artigos científicos, fontes oficiais e documentação relacionada aos sistemas selecionados, sendo estabelecidos critérios para comparação quanto à finalidade, recursos tecnológicos, utilização de inteligência artificial, análise de imagens, aplicabilidade e suporte à prática profissional\. A análise evidenciou diferenças entre as ferramentas quanto às funcionalidades disponibilizadas, formas de utilização e possibilidades de integração ao processo de avaliação mamográfica\. Observou\-se que esses recursos apresentam potencial como ferramentas complementares ao trabalho profissional, especialmente no suporte à análise de imagens e à organização do fluxo de trabalho, sem substituir a avaliação e a tomada de decisão do profissional habilitado\. Conclui\-se que o conhecimento sobre as características, potencialidades e limitações dessas tecnologias é relevante para sua utilização responsável e para o acompanhamento da evolução tecnológica na área de diagnóstico por imagem\.

## [AI\-Based Language Models \(LLMs\) in Assessing ESL Learners’ Speaking Skills: Opportunities and Limitations](../publications/d52bd1035c29a6aba1f2.md)

Leyla Hajiyeva

Speaking is widely regarded as the most difficult skill to teach, practise, and assess in English as a Second Language \(ESL\) classrooms, largely because valid assessment of oral proficiency has traditionally depended on scarce resources: trained human raters, controlled testing conditions, and considerable time\. The recent emergence of large language models \(LLMs\) capable of real\-time speech\-to\-text conversion, conversational interaction, and rubric\-referenced feedback generation has renewed interest in automating parts of this process\. This article critically reviews the opportunities and limitations of LLM\-based tools for assessing and supporting the development of ESL learners’ speaking skills\. It traces the evolution from earlier automatic speech\-scoring systems grounded in automatic speech recognition \(ASR\) and statistical feature extraction to the current generation of generative, instruction\-following language models capable of producing holistic and analytic feedback in natural language\. Five categories of opportunity are identified — scalable formative feedback, on\-demand conversational practice, rubric\-referenced scoring support, fine\-grained pronunciation and fluency diagnostics, and reduced speaking anxiety through low\-stakes practice — alongside five categories of limitation: construct underrepresentation, accent\- and dialect\-related bias, hallucination and inconsistent reliability, washback effects and learner overreliance, and unresolved data\-privacy and ethical concerns\. Building on this synthesis, the article proposes a five\-criterion framework — validity, reliability, fairness, transparency, and pedagogical alignment — intended to guide the responsible integration of LLM\-based tools into ESL speaking instruction and assessment, and discusses implications for English\-language teaching contexts such as Azerbaijan, where access to trained oral examiners is often constrained\. The article concludes that LLMs are best positioned as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, human assessment of spoken English, and it outlines a research agenda for validating LLM\-based speaking assessment against established testing standards

## [Neuro‐Immune Interactions in the Tumour Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Treatment](../publications/d52fc7ff72d0545fd61b.md)

Mustafa Taleb Ardah; Raghda Ali Bakr; H\. Malathi; Vimal Arora; Priya Priyadarshini Nayak; Dilbar Urazbaeva; Djumaniyazova Mukhayya Xusinovna; Sadullayeva Moxinur

ABSTRACT The nervous and immune systems, once viewed as distinct biological networks, are now understood to be closely linked in regulating cancer development, progression, and responses to therapy\. Neural structures infiltrate the tumour microenvironment and communicate with immune cells, influencing key processes such as tumour growth, invasion, and metastatic spread\. Through neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and continuous signalling between peripheral tissues and the brain, nerves affect immune cell recruitment, activity, and overall immune balance\. Factors including psychological stress, circadian rhythm disturbances, and gut–brain communication further shape antitumour immune responses, highlighting the complexity of these interactions\. Research suggests that neuronal signalling not only contributes to cancer‐associated symptoms, such as pain, but also affects the efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy\. Neural biomarkers may provide prognostic value, while interventions targeting neural pathways could strengthen anticancer immunity\. Nevertheless, major challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, dynamic spatial and temporal interactions, and the limitations of existing experimental models\. Continued progress in molecular techniques, bioinformatics, and cross‐disciplinary research will be crucial for clarifying these mechanisms\. Investigating the neuro–immune–cancer interface offers significant potential for developing innovative treatment approaches that combine neuroscience, immunology, and oncology to enhance patient survival and quality of life\.

## [When extremes sound like the majority: Social signal and norm misperception](../publications/d539b5b9fe0c08d4b5bd.md)

Leah Bloy; Nechumi Malovicki\-Yaffe

Abstract Societies often misperceive their own normative center\. Individuals may believe that distinctive, conservative, or ideologically committed positions are more widely shared than they actually are, sustaining pluralistic ignorance even when private attitudes are moderate\. Yet little is known about how perceived norms become systematically organized under conditions of uncertainty\. We propose that norm perceptions are structured around socially salient reference points, including identity\-defining or ideologically committed subgroups, and only partially calibrated by individuals’ private attitudes\. Across two preregistered studies, we test this representational account of norm perception in distinct social ecologies\. Study 1 examines norm inference among 550 adults from Israel’s ultra\-Orthodox community, a context characterized by strong social norms and hierarchies\. Study 2 extends the analysis cross\-nationally using survey data from 21,233 respondents in 57 countries on perceived gender norms\. Using theory\-constrained regression models, we fixed the intercept to alternative candidate reference points and estimated adjustment from these anchors as a function of respondents’ private attitudes\. Across studies, perceived norms were better represented relative to contextually salient subgroup anchors or, in some domains, the response\-scale midpoint, than by population averages alone\. These findings suggest that pluralistic ignorance may reflect a predictable structure in how normative perceptions are formed under uncertainty: perceived norms are organized around salient reference points and only partially adjusted in relation to individuals’ private attitudes\.

## [Retrograde Cystic Duct Milking Before Ligation for Isolated Gallbladder Ascariasis with Acute Acalculous Hydrops: An Observational Analytic Case Study](../publications/d53d4055b0000739856f.md)

Muhammad Arisma Dwirian Putra; Ahmad Fakhrozi Helmi; Ali Hanafiah; Alsen Arlan

Background: Ascaris lumbricoides infects an estimated 700 million to one billion people, but gallbladder involvement accounts for only about 2\.1% of hepatobiliary ascariasis\. A worm impacted in the cystic duct can cause acute acalculous hydrops and may be transected during cholecystectomy\. Objective: To describe the presentation, open surgical management with retrograde cystic duct milking, and six\-month course of isolated gallbladder ascariasis with acute acalculous hydrops\. Methods: This study describes a 57\-year\-old woman with acute\-on\-chronic right upper quadrant pain in Indonesia, assessed clinically, biochemically, and sonographically from admission \(T0\) to month 6 \(T6\)\. Results: At admission, pain was 8/10, leukocytes 15,460/mm³, eosinophils 8\.0% \(1,236/mm³\), C\-reactive protein \(CRP\) 45\.0 mg/L, and alkaline phosphatase 133 U/L, with normal bilirubin \(0\.8 mg/dL\)\. Ultrasonography showed a tense, stone\-free gallbladder \(10\.5 × 4\.5 cm; estimated volume 111\.3 cm³; wall 4\.5 mm\) with the inner tube and stripe signs of a live worm impacted in the cystic duct\. Under rapid sequence induction without nitrous oxide, open cholecystectomy with retrograde cystic duct milking displaced an intact 22\.0\-cm A\. lumbricoides into the gallbladder before ligation\. Albendazole 400 mg was given on postoperative day 1 after flatus; she was discharged on day 3\. At month 6, she was asymptomatic, CRP \(−96\.9%\) and eosinophils \(−88\.9%\) had fallen, and liver enzymes were normal\. Conclusion: In this patient, retrograde cystic duct milking during open cholecystectomy, followed by albendazole after the return of bowel function, removed the impacted worm intact and was followed by full recovery\.

## [From appropriate use to dependency: How AI attitude and use motivations shape university students’ AI dependency](../publications/d54b38cf4cf90807dfda.md)

Jianfeng Yin; Yueying Zhang; Runjie Jiang

Whether students develop dependency on generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) technologies largely depends on their attitudes toward using such tools\. Existing studies have primarily explained the formation of AI dependency from the perspectives of usage attitude and technological characteristics, while paying limited attention to the psychological mechanisms through which attitudes exert their influence\. Grounded in Self\-Determination Theory, the present study examines how different types of use motivation mediate the relationship between students’ AI attitude and AI dependency\. A total of 405 university students completed a comprehensive questionnaire measuring AI attitude, use motivations, and AI dependency\. The results indicate that: \(i\) AI attitude does not directly predict AI dependency; instead, its effects are transmitted through multiple motivational pathways, with intrinsic motivation inhibiting AI dependency, whereas identified regulation facilitates its development; \(ii\) three distinct AI dependency profiles were identified: dependent, moderate, and conservative users\. These profiles exhibited clear stratification, with dependent users showing the highest scores across all dimensions and conservative users the lowest; and \(iii\) individuals with stronger motivations are more likely to be classified into the dependent user profile, with external motivation playing a particularly salient role\. These findings enrich the literature on AI dependency and offer practical implications for higher education administrators, tool developers, and educational researchers\.

## [DIGITAL SIMULATION AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELLING OF SURFACE\-ACTIVE COMPLEXES BASED ON QUATERNIZED ETHYL PIPERAZINE](../publications/d54cf326566828dfac93.md)

Elgun E\. Hasanov

Modelling and simulation of real\-life phenomena in virtual environment is gradually becoming an integral part of science and technology\.One crucial benefit of computer modelling in science and engineering is the opportunity to extract useful information about the nature of the subject system that would otherwise be available only through tedious experimental procedures\.The other advantage of computer simulation is the ability to analyze the system from a new perspective and identify new information which would not be available via experimental methodologies\.Future development and improvement on the accuracy of computer modelling techniques depend on how simulation results are successfully verified against experimental findings\.This work presents the outcome of a molecular simulation performed on a novel surface\-active complex alongside the relevant experimental findings to verify that the identified simulation methodology is robust enough to predict the behavior of the molecular system under specified real\-life conditions\.

## [Implementación de un sistema automatizado de alerta temprana para emergencias mediante la plataforma WhatsApp](../publications/d55e4ba17655a29fdadf.md)

Kevin Alexandro Diego Castro; Silvestre Bedolla Solano; Juan José Bedolla Solano; A\. A\. Rodríguez\-Rosales

Los chatbots se han convertido en herramientas clave dentro de la comunicación digital, esto especialmente en contextos de gestión de emergencias\. Gracias al procesamiento del lenguaje natural, estos sistemas pueden integrarse en aplicaciones móviles para ofrecer asistencia inmediata, automatizada y personalizada durante situaciones críticas\. En el ámbito operativo, permiten una respuesta rápida, difusión de información confiable, orientación en tiempo real y recolección de datos útiles para la toma de decisiones\. Su disponibilidad continua y facilidad de acceso a través de smartphones los convierten en un recurso eficaz para mejorar la vinculación entre los ciudadanos y organismos de respuesta\. Con base en esto, el presente artículo describe la aplicación de estas tecnologías mediante WhatsApp, evaluando su rol como catalizador de solidaridad, gestión de refugios temporales y herramientas heurística de datos bajo en un enfoque de investigación\-acción para optimizar la respuesta ante emergencias climáticas\.

## [Development and Physicochemical Characterization of Chitosan/Glucomannan and Chitosan/PVP Composite Beads With Urea Incorporation](../publications/d55fdd9e51637a65927c.md)

Kartini Afriani; Tri Sutanti Budikania; Achmad Nandang Roziafanto; Fareka Kholidanata; Ahmad Dzaky Mualim; Ali Akbar Mustaqim; Alma Lubna Kamilia; Afifah Huriyyah

ABSTRACT Hydrogels are three‐dimensional, crosslinked, hydrophilic polymers with exceptional water‐absorption capabilities, making them promising materials for controlled‐release applications\. This study focuses on the enhancement and characterization of composite hydrogel beads based on chitosan \(Ch\) combined with glucomannan \(G\) or polyvinyl pyrrolidone \(PVP\), with and without urea incorporation, for potential application in controlled‐release systems\. Four formulations were successfully fabricated: ChG, ChGu, ChP, and ChPu\. Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed hydrogen‐bond formation between chitosan and the secondary polymers via characteristic peak shifts\. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed new endothermic peaks in composites \(121°C for ChP; 108°C and 143°C for ChG\), confirming the formation of new polymer networks with enhanced thermal stability\. Swelling studies demonstrated pH‐dependent behavior: ChP composites exhibited continuous swelling up to 120% at neutral pH, while ChG composites showed rapid initial swelling followed by degradation\. Gel fraction analysis quantified network integrity, with ChP exhibiting the highest value \(68\.02% ± 3\.60%\), indicating dense crosslinking, whereas ChG showed a moderate gel fraction \(32\.50% ± 3\.16%\)\. Urea incorporation consistently reduced gel fraction \(ChPu: 54\.40% ± 3\.44%; ChGu: 27\.50 ± 3\.55%\), demonstrating its role as a network modulator through hydrogen bond disruption—the ‘salting‐out’ effect\. Water vapor adsorption studies revealed stable profiles over seven days \(97\.34%–99\.92%\), with ChG‐based composites showing slightly higher adsorption due to their more open network structure\. These findings demonstrate that chitosan/glucomannan and chitosan/PVP composites exhibit distinct, tunable physicochemical properties that can be modulated by polymer selection and urea incorporation, positioning them as promising candidates for controlled‐release systems in agricultural and biomedical applications\.

## [Brain tumor segmentation using a combination of graph cut and optimized U\-Net with genetic algorithm: An efficient hybrid framework for enhanced medical image analysis](../publications/d56e7be1fb93e0ae5d47.md)

Reem M\. Mostafa; Emad Mabrouk; Mohamed Saed Salim; Ahmed Ayman; Hamdy Z\. Zidan

Accurate segmentation of low\-grade gliomas \(LGGs\) in FLAIR MRI remains challenging due to low\-contrast tumor boundaries, irregular morphology, and extreme class imbalance\. This work presents a lightweight hybrid segmentation framework that integrates three complementary components: \(1\) a fast graph\-based region refinement step using GrabCut applied during training only to enhance tumor\-background contrast, \(2\) a compact U\-Net architecture whose filter configuration is automatically selected using a small\-scale genetic algorithm, and \(3\) an analytical evaluation of lightweight post\-processing strategies studied separately from the final GA\-optimized model\. The method was evaluated on the LGG\-MRI\-Segmentation dataset using strict patient\-level splits of 79 training, 19 validation, and 12 testing patients\. The final model achieved strong slice\-wise performance with a mean Dice of 0\.9132 and a median Dice of 0\.9855; the lower mean reflects the influence of more difficult, lower\-performing slices and therefore provides a more conservative summary of overall performance across the evaluated test cases\. Additional metrics include an IoU of 0\.8851, sensitivity of 0\.8954, precision of 0\.9523, specificity of 0\.9997, and an HD95 of 1\.00 mm, indicating highly accurate boundary delineation\. For contextual benchmarking, a 2D nnU\-Net model was trained on the same dataset\. nnU\-Net achieved a mean validation Dice of 0\.8450 and a best validation EMA Dice of 0\.9134\. Because these nnU\-Net Dice values were obtained from its validation workflow rather than the exact slice\-wise test procedure used for the proposed model, they are presented as contextual reference results rather than strictly matched test\-set estimates\. The proposed framework required substantially less training time under the evaluated implementations\. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that a carefully coordinated combination of preprocessing, lightweight architectural optimization, and efficient post\-processing can achieve strong segmentation performance on the evaluated dataset while remaining computationally efficient\. These findings suggest that the proposed framework is promising for computationally constrained LGG segmentation workflows\. However, broader clinical applicability requires validation on independent external cohorts before generalizability can be established\.

## [Role of Financial Literacy in Indonesian International Exchange Students’ Financial Management: Mediated by Financial Technology Adaptation](../publications/d579a41a6f4c83aee7fa.md)

Dzikom Puspitaningrum; Muhammad Istiyansyah Ulman Idris; Wan Nur Tasnim Wan Hussin; Aisyah Mohamad Nafis

The low level of financial literacy in Indonesia has the potential to affect students’ ability to manage their finances, particularly among participants of international student exchange programs who are exposed to different financial systems and payment technologies\. This study aims to analyze the effect of financial literacy on financial management and to examine the mediating role of financial technology adaptation\. The research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method involving Indonesian students who had participated in international student exchange programs\. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling\. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using regression analysis and path analysis with the PROCESS Macro by Hayes in SPSS\. The results indicate that financial technology adaptation significantly mediates the effect of financial literacy on financial management, as evidenced by an indirect effect value of 0\.285 and a 95% bootstrap confidence interval ranging from 0\.066 to 0\.580, which does not include zero\. These findings suggest that financial technology adaptation serves as a partial mediator, meaning that the effect of financial literacy on financial management occurs both directly and indirectly through financial technology adaptation\.

## [Affinity selection mass spectrometry \(AS\-MS\) for identification of acetylcholinesterase ligands in Strychnos peckii B\.L\. Rob](../publications/d581f90765e9e6c4ce5e.md)

Fernando Cassas; Carla L\. G\. Santos; Felipe Moura A\. da Silva; Quézia B\. Cass

Introduction Strychnos L\. species are traditionally used worldwide and are known to biosynthesize a wide range of structurally diverse alkaloids\. Several of these compounds have been reported to interact with targets in the central nervous system, including acetylcholinesterase \(AChE\)\. Given its use in paralytic preparations, an aqueous extract of S\. peckii was investigated for prospecting acetylcholinesterase ligands using affinity selection mass spectrometry \(AS\-MS\), with the enzyme immobilized on magnetic particles\. Methods For the AS\-MS assay, 200 µg of eelAChE was immobilized on 10 mg of amino\-functionalized magnetic beads via Schiff\-base chemistry using glutaraldehyde as a linker\. Control samples were prepared under identical conditions, with enzyme inactivation achieved using 100% MeOH \(60 min\)\. Enzymatic activity was monitored by choline formation\. The workflow was optimized using galantamine as the reference ligand across four stages \(incubation, magnetic separation, ligand dissociation, and LC\-HRMS identification\), establishing an affinity ratio \(AR\) cut\-off of 1\.2\. Dissociated ligands were analyzed by LC\-HRMS and processed in MZmine for ion alignment, deconvolution, and peak\-area calculation\. Results and Discussion Metabolites with AR &gt; 1\.2 were classified as AChE ligands and annotated based on MS/MS fragmentation data, interpretation of the molecular network, in silico tools, and manual curation guided by biosynthetic pathway analysis\. The identified ligands were lyaloside \(1\) \(AR, 3\.73\), 10\-hydroxygeissoschizol \(2\) \(AR, 3\.69\), alkaloid A \(3\) \(AR, 2\.51\), 5\-carboxystrictosidine \(4\) \(AR, 2\.05\), corynantheol \(5\) \(AR, 2\.04\), dolichantoside/isodolichantoside \(6\) \(AR, 1\.90\), alkaloid B \(7\) \(AR, 1\.68\), \(strictosidine \(AR, 1\.66\) \(8\), corynantheidal \(9\) \(AR, 1\.63\), desoxycordifoline \(10\) \(AR, 1\.57\), kaempferol\-3\- O \-rhamnoside \(11\) \(AR, 1\.36\), kaempferol \(12\) \(AR, 1\.35\), alkaloid C \(13\) \(AR, 1\.29\), and harman\-3\-carboxylic acid \(14\) \(AR, 1\.27\)\. Conclusion Overall, the ligands were enriched in monoterpene indole alkaloids and related scaffolds, demonstrating that AS\-MS is a rapid, label\-free strategy to prioritize enzyme binding metabolites from complex natural matrices and expand the AChE interacting chemical space of S\. peckii \.

## [Uma infraestrutura que parece ter impacto insignificante isoladamente pode produzir consequências relevantes quando inserida em um sistema ambiental já pressionado?](../publications/d58a056d6d73355f3fc9.md)

Marcela Almeida

Uma infraestrutura que parece ter impacto insignificante isoladamente pode produzir consequências relevantes quando inserida em um sistema ambiental já restrito? A expansão da inteligência artificial e seus possíveis impactos nos ecossistemas marinhos: uma reflexão sobre os efeitos ambientais cumulativos dos data centers submarinos Autora: Marcela Almeida Resumo A expansão da inteligência artificial tem ampliado a demanda por capacidade computacional, energia elétrica e infraestrutura de processamento de dados\. Nesse contexto, os data centers submarinos surgem como uma alternativa tecnológica que pode oferecer vantagens relacionadas à refrigeração e à proximidade de regiões costeiras\. Entretanto, sua implementação também levanta questões sobre os possíveis efeitos ambientais decorrentes da liberação de calor, da ocupação física do ambiente marinho e da interação dessas estruturas com ecossistemas submetidos às mudanças climáticas\. Este artigo propõe uma reflexão sobre os impactos ambientais cumulativos de infraestruturas digitais, partindo das hipóteses de que alterações localizadas, aparentemente insignificantes quando detectadas isoladamente, podem merecer atenção quando consideradas em conjunto com outras implicações ambientais e com a expansão futura dessas instalações\. A discussão não pressupõe a existência de danos ecológicos generalizados causados por centros de dados submarinos, mas destaca a necessidade de pesquisas, monitoramento ambiental e avaliação preventiva de seus efeitos em diferentes escalas espaciais e temporais\. 1\. Introdução A inteligência artificial tem ocupado uma posição cada vez mais relevante no desenvolvimento tecnológico contemporâneo\. Sua utilização em sistemas de automação, assistentes virtuais, análise de dados e agentes independentes exige uma infraestrutura computacional capaz de processar e armazenar quantidades crescentes de informações\. Embora os serviços digitais sejam frequentemente associados a uma realidade virtual e intangível, sua operação depende de estruturas físicas, equipamentos eletrônicos, sistemas de refrigeração, redes de comunicação e fornecimento contínuo de energia\. A expansão desse ecossistema tecnológico levanta, portanto, questões que ultrapassam os limites da engenharia computacional e alcançam os campos da sustentabilidade, da gestão energética e da proteção ambiental\. Entre as alternativas científicas para a instalação de infraestrutura computacional estão os data centers submarinos\. Ao utilizar água do mar como meio de dissipação térmica, essas estruturas podem reduzir critérios específicos de refrigeração e oferecer vantagens operacionais em condições específicas\. Entretanto, uma eficiência técnica de uma solução não é suficiente, por si só, para determinar sua sustentabilidade ambiental\. Diante desse cenário, surge a seguinte questão central: uma infraestrutura que parece ter impacto insignificante isoladamente pode produzir consequências relevantes quando inserida em um sistema ambiental já específico? A partir dessa pergunta, este artigo discute a necessidade de avaliar os possíveis efeitos cumulativos da expansão dos data centers submarinos, considerando o aquecimento oceânico, a dinâmica térmica da água e a sensibilidade dos ecossistemas marinhos\. 2\. A materialidade da inteligência artificial O crescimento da inteligência artificial depende de uma dimensão de infraestrutura física cuja dimensão pode ser pouco evidente para os usuários dos serviços digitais\. Modelos de inteligência artificial, especialmente aqueles usados em larga escala, exigem recursos computacionais para treinamento, inferência e armazenamento de dados\. Esses processos consomem energia elétrica e geram calor, que precisa ser transferido para o ambiente por sistemas adequados\. A expansão da capacidade computacional pode aumentar a necessidade de instalações, equipamentos e recursos energéticos\. Contudo, a relação entre o crescimento da inteligência artificial e o aumento da infraestrutura não é necessariamente linear: avanços em hardware, algoritmos e eficiência energética podem reduzir o consumo por operação, embora o crescimento da utilização dos serviços possa compensar parte desses ganhos\. Essa dinâmica conduz a uma reflexão importante: avaliar a sustentabilidade da inteligência artificial exige considerar não apenas a eficiência de cada equipamento, mas também a escala total de utilização da tecnologia e dos recursos necessários para sustentá\-la\. Nesse sentido, a infraestrutura digital deve ser detalhada como parte do ambiente físico, e não como um sistema independente dele\. 3\. Data centers submarinos e dissipação térmica O princípio de funcionamento de um data center submarino envolve a instalação de equipamentos computacionais em estruturas projetadas para operar sob condições específicas de pressão, umidade e temperatura\. O ambiente aquático pode facilitar a transferência de calor, dependendo do projeto dos trocadores térmicos, da circulação da água e das características do local de instalação\. Essa possibilidade foi investigada pelo Projeto Natick, desenvolvido pela Microsoft para avaliar as previsões de data centers instalados sob o mar\. Entretanto, o calor não desaparece durante o processo de refrigeração: ele é transferido para outro meio\. Quando há dissipação térmica para a água do mar, pode ocorrer uma alteração de temperatura na região à instalação\. A intensidade e a extensão dessa alteração independente de variáveis como a potência térmica liberada, as correntes marítimas, a profundidade, a mistura da água e a configuração do sistema de refrigeração\. Em determinadas condições, a circulação da água pode dispersar o calor rapidamente, limitando o aumento de temperatura a uma área reduzida\. Isso, porém, não permite concluir que todas as instalações, em todos os ambientes, apresentem o mesmo comportamento\. Por essa razão, a avaliação ambiental deve considerar as características específicas de cada projeto e do ecossistema em que ele será instalado\. 4\. A hipótese do impacto cumulativo O ponto central desta reflexão não é afirmado que uma pequena alteração térmica provoca necessariamente danos à vida marinha\. A questão é compreender se alterações localizadas podem adquirir relevância ecológica quando consideradas em conjunto com outras pressões ambientais\. O oceano está sujeito a mudanças relacionadas ao aquecimento global, à acidificação, à redução de oxigênio em determinadas regiões, à poluição e à manipulação de habitats\. Essas pressões não atuam de maneira uniforme e podem produzir respostas específicas conforme as características de cada ecossistema\. Em ambientes submetidos a estresse térmico, uma alteração adicional de temperatura pode, em determinadas circunstâncias, organismos sensíveis\. A relevância desse efeito dependerá de sua intensidade, duração, extensão espacial e interação com as condições preexistentes\. É nesse contexto que se inserem as hipóteses apresentadas neste artigo: um impacto ambiental aparentemente pequeno não deve ser considerado irrelevante antes que sua interação com o ambiente e com outras pressões seja envolvente investigada\. Essa hipótese não significa que os efeitos devam ser simplesmente somados de forma aritmética\. Sistemas ecológicos apresentam relações complexas, e as consequências de múltiplos fatores podem ser aditivas, sinérgicas, antagônicas ou até mesmo neutras, dependendo das situações\. O objetivo, portanto, é defender uma abordagem de avaliação ambiental que considere o conjunto das tensões existentes, em vez de analisar cada instalação como se estivesse isolada do restante do sistema ecológico\. 5\. Da escala local à expansão da infraestrutura Uma instalação submarina pode apresentar uma alteração térmica restrita ao seu entorno\. Entretanto, o planejamento de uma infraestrutura tecnológica não deve se limitar às condições previstas em um único protótipo\. Caso a adoção dessa tecnologia aumente, será necessário investigar como diferentes instalações poderão interagir com os ambientes em que foram posicionadas\. Isso não significa presumir que seus efeitos serão necessariamente acumulados de maneira significativa, mas é importante que a escala de implantação seja uma variável relevante para a análise\. A avaliação pode ser organizada em três níveis: Escala local: investiga alterações de temperatura, características físicas do habitat e respostas dos organismos próximos à instalação\. Escala regional: avalia a distribuição de múltiplas estruturas, as condições de circulação da água e a possibilidade de efeitos combinados em uma determinada região\. Escala global: considera os impactos associados ao ciclo de vida da infraestrutura digital, incluindo geração de energia, fabricação de equipamentos, transporte, substituição de componentes e destinação de materiais\. Essas escalas devem ser observadas separadamente e em conjunto, evitando a uma instalação efeitos individuais que possam ocorrer de outros fatores ambientais\. Também é importante distinguir o aquecimento localizado produzido por uma fonte de calor do aquecimento global associado ao aumento da energia retida pelo sistema climático\. São características físicas diferentes, embora possam coexistir no mesmo ambiente\. 6\. Eficiência energética significa sustentabilidade ambiental? A possibilidade de reduzir os custos de refrigeração representa uma vantagem potencial operacional dos data centers submarinos\. Contudo, eficiência energética e sustentabilidade ambiental são conceitos relacionados, mas não equivalentes\. Uma tecnologia pode consumir menos energia para executar determinada tarefa e, ainda assim, apresentar outros impactos associados à instalação, à manutenção ou à retirada dos equipamentos\. Da mesma forma, a redução do custo de operação pode promover a expansão da infraestrutura e aumentar a utilização de serviços digitais\. Esse comportamento está relacionado ao chamado efeito rebote, e nenhum ganho de eficiência pode ser par

## [Maritime transport and policy research over the past 50 years: a review across four maritime journals](../publications/d594417f3935a6382d0f.md)

郑芳; Ziaul Haque Munim; Jean‐Paul Rodrigue; Theo Notteboom

Journal focused bibliometric studies, especially those examining leading or highly relevant journals, are widely acknowledged as an effective way to capture the intellectual structure of a field\. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of four important journals which have strong orientation in maritime transport and policy field using R\-Bibliometrix package and VOSviewer\. The final dataset consists of 2,889 articles published between 1976 and 2024\. The results mapped the intellectual research landscape of the field by identifying leading authors, institutions, regions, influential articles, and major research clusters\. Keyword co\-occurrence analysis shows that the most frequently discussed topics include ports operations, logistics, container shipping, maritime safety, and climate change adaptation\. The field also engages with promising areas of human\-centred issues such as seafarer, maritime education and training, human factors, human error and non\-technical skills\. The findings show an interesting direction that integrates economic and technical operations with human and societal dimensions\. Additionally, the findings potentially provide insights for researchers and practitioners seeking collaborations or directions, and policymakers seeking priorities in the maritime transport and policy domain\.

## [Head to head searching: the Search&amp;Destroy card game in the health sciences classroom](../publications/d59c1b26bd9f52bb7d1d.md)

Lena Bohman; Regina Vitiello; Christiana M\. Keinath; Gary Maixner; Mari Kermit\-Canfield

Background: Games are a promising way to make health sciences education more engaging and improve synthesis for learners\. There have been some successful implementations of game\-based learning for health sciences library instruction \[1\], but there is room for development of games tailored specifically for teaching database searching skills to health sciences students\. Case Presentation: The authors developed a biomedical edition of the existing library instruction card game Search&amp;Destroy\. The original Search&amp;Destroy was developed as an alternative way to teach a one\-shot instructional session on search skills using a discovery layer in an academic library for undergraduates\. The biomedical edition modified the game to work with PubMed and incorporate health science\-specific searching skills\. Keyword cards were updated with biomedical terms and new cards were added with filters and actions related to health sciences literature searching \(e\.g\., last five years, systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials filters\)\. The new version was play tested internally by the authors and then piloted in classes with nurse residents\. The game is now available through the print\-on\-demand service The Game Crafter and teaching materials are available online\. Conclusions: Feedback from our pilot test group of nurse residents was overwhelmingly positive\. Informal conversations with nurse educators responsible for the program were also positive, and the game has been incorporated in the curriculum for the future\. The Biomedical Edition joins a growing family of Search&amp;Destroy games designed for a variety of library instruction needs\.

## [The integration of artificial intelligence in medical imaging practice: A perspective of the Nigerian radiographer](../publications/d59d3938b5b4f036bc5e.md)

Archibong B\.E; Paulinus S\.O; Abiazie H\.C; Okezie F\.C

ABSTRACT Background: The integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in medical imaging represents a transformative advancement in healthcare delivery, particularly within developing healthcare systems like Nigeria\. This study investigated the perspectives of Nigerian radiographers in the South\-South region regarding AI integration in medical imaging practice, focusing on knowledge, attitudes, current practices, and barriers to adoption\. Methods: Using a descriptive cross\-sectional survey design, data were collected from 73 practicing radiographers with at least 3 years of experience via structured questionnaires administered through Google Forms\. The questionnaire assessed their knowledge, attitudes, awareness, and willingness to adopt AI in their clinical practice\. Content validity was established by experts, and reliability was confirmed \(Cronbach’s α = 0\.73\)\. Microsoft Excel and the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences \(SPSS\) version 26\.0 were used to organize the data for descriptive statistics\. Results: Findings revealed high awareness of AI applications, with 78\.1% of respondents familiar with AI technologies\. However, only 21\.9% rated their knowledge as excellent, while 42\.5% considered it fair, indicating a gap between general awareness and in\-depth understanding\. Online resources were the primary source of AI knowledge, highlighting the need for structured educational interventions\. Radiographers demonstrated predominantly positive attitudes, with 73\.9% agreeing that AI would improve imaging accuracy and reduce workload\. Additionally, 64\.4% expressed preparedness for AI adoption, although 41\.1% feared potential replacement by AI technologies\. Current AI utilization was limited, with 31\.5% reporting workplace use, primarily for imaging analysis \(39\.1%\) and reporting assistance \(21\.7%\)\. Despite limited implementation, 89\.0% expressed willingness to undergo professional development, preferring workshops and seminars \(37\.0%\)\. Significant barriers included inadequate infrastructure and high implementation costs\. Conclusion: Successful AI integration requires coordinated efforts from educational institutions, professional bodies, healthcare facilities, and policymakers to address these barriers while building on radiographers&\#x27; positive attitudes toward AI adoption\. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Medical Imaging, Nigerian Radiographers, AI Adoption, Barriers, Perspectives

## [人工智能驱动下的文明转型终极推演:两百年工业体系的崩溃、利益僵局与历史涌现的风险\(V1\)](../publications/d5a65a93ced41926ca0b.md)

XiangKun Wang

现代人类社会形态的99%都是200年工业时代的过渡性产物,而非文明的永恒结构。 教育、法律、工作时间、职业、阶级结构、贸易、金融和货币,都仅仅服务于促进工业劳动分工;它们只能缓冲矛盾,而不能从根本上消除不平等。 人工智能代表了数千年来首次全面认知替代革命——足以瓦解延续两百年的工业体系,并颠覆人类劳动价值这一延续千年的公理。 人工智能的迭代速度远远超过了制度修正的速度,导致文明转型的窗口期迅速收窄,而紧迫感已达到临界水平。 文明转型的主要瓶颈并非技术障碍,而是财富与权力的结构性僵局——既有的体系缺乏主动重构的内在动机。 工业时代的两次生产力飞跃都通过世界大战实现了秩序重构;当今的深层矛盾正是历史模式的完全重演。 尽管结构性矛盾以绝对的确定性存在并持续积累,但历史具有内在的随机性和突发性,使得最终结果难以预测。 没有人希望出现动荡,但也没有人能阻止历史规律和系统势能的自然释放。 人类正步入一个终极人工智能转型的时代:一场彻底的范式转变,利益格局陷入难以破解的僵局,未来变得完全不可预测。

## [Educación emocional como base y guía del aprendizaje en el aula](../publications/d5a98f9f9da6a2cb3c73.md)

Álvaro Sebastián Álvarez Pérez

La educación emocional ha emergido como un pilar fundamental para optimizar los procesos de enseñanza\-aprendizaje, al influir directamente en factores cognitivos como la atención, la memoria y la motivación\. Este trabajo tiene como objetivo analizar la importancia de integrar la educación emocional de forma transversal en el aula, destacando su impacto en el bienestar y el rendimiento académico de los estudiantes\. La investigación se desarrolló mediante una revisión teórica y un análisis de experiencias docentes, complementados con estrategias basadas en la neurociencia y en el fomento de la inteligencia emocional\. Se empleó un enfoque descriptivo y analítico, considerando prácticas pedagógicas centradas en la regulación emocional, el fortalecimiento del vínculo docente\-estudiante y la creación de ambientes de aprendizaje seguros\. Los resultados evidencian que un clima emocionalmente saludable potencia la motivación intrínseca, reduce la incidencia de conductas disruptivas y mejora el compromiso académico\. Asimismo, se observó que el manejo de emociones negativas, el uso de retroalimentación emocional y la incorporación de metodologías activas generan un aprendizaje más significativo\. Se concluye que la educación emocional no debe considerarse un complemento, sino un componente esencial del currículo, que fortalece tanto el desarrollo académico como socioemocional, preparando a los estudiantes para enfrentar con resiliencia los retos de la vida\.

## [Complexity\-Aware Geographic Fairness in Crop Yield Prediction Using Diversity\-Weighted Learning](../publications/d5acd82217067f413d0b.md)

Vipin Bihari Yadav; Aditya Khamparia

Machine\-learning models for crop yield prediction are usually judged by overall accuracy alone, which hides large differences in prediction quality between regions\. This study shows that a standard Random Forest with an aggregate R² of 0\.935 can be misleading: state\-level MAE ranges from 0\.168 t/ha to 2\.505 t/ha, a 14\.9\-fold gap that the overall score conceals\. Two independent structural factors underlie this imbalance: the number of records per state \(data\-volume imbalance\) and the agricultural complexity of each state, both of which can be observed in any census or statistical record\. To address both at once, a Complexity\-Aware Geographic Fairness \(CAGF\) framework is presented that combines a Crop Diversity Index based on Shannon entropy with inverse\-frequency sample re\-weighting\. Four architectures \(Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR and MLP\) are evaluated under three training regimes \(unweighted baseline, inverse\-frequency weighting and CAGF\) using expanding\-window temporal cross\-validation, and TreeSHAP attribution shows that CAGF directs model attention toward crop\-specific regional patterns\. For XGBoost, CAGF gives the best overall accuracy among the three regimes \(R² = 0\.918; MAE = 1\.299 t/ha\) together with a lower geographic Gini of prediction error than the unweighted baseline \(GGPE = 0\.289 versus 0\.293\), so fairness improves without any loss of accuracy\.

## [Limits and being unlimited by the reading format: a phenomenological study on emotional experiences of readers of audiobooks and physical books](../publications/d5af5b1f160c1f80aa96.md)

Henri Nerg

Introduction\. This is a qualitative study of the reading habits and experiences of readers of audiobooks and physical fiction books, with a focus on their emotional reactions to the reading process and the format of reading\. Method\. Qualitative interviews were carried on for Finnish participants \(N=6\) and transcribed\. Analysis\. The analysis was interpretative phenomenological analysis, which focuses on the personal interpretations of the participants’ reading experiences\. The transcribed interviews were analysed in multiple rounds and the process of coding was used to map out themes\. Results\. The results suggest that both formats of reading create strong affective and emotional connections in the readers, but in various and often polarizing and dichotomic ways\. Feeling of being limited by the format and having control over the environment were two major themes regarding the reading and listening experience\. Conclusion\. All participants formed strong emotional connections with the medium and felt that the one that they did not prefer had negative connotations and limitations to the reading experience, whereas their preferred medium enhanced their experience and liberated them from the limitations of the not preferred medium\.

## [TEMPORAL AND CHANNEL\-SPECIFIC PATTERNS IN NIGERIAN FRAUD: INTERPRETABLE MACHINE LEARNING ON A LARGE\-SCALE SYNTHETIC DATASET](../publications/d5afd1936302ea116b4b.md)

Adeniran Gbolahan; Josiah Endurance Owolabi

Resumo indisponível na fonte\.

## [A dimensionless\-entropy weight method for determining cloud physical parameter responses induced by aircraft cloud seeding](../publications/d5b1221d398ac75ee130.md)

Xiuzhu Sha; Xingyu Li; Ronghao Chu; Bo Cheng; Yanhua Liu; Jianfang Ding; Fan Zhang; Can Song; Yao Xiao; Shanhai Wang

Abstract To address the challenges in evaluation of aircraft cloud seeding effect, this study proposes a physical evaluation method that integrates multiple key techniques to achieve an integrated quantitative evaluation based on multiple indicators\. This evaluation approach was applied to six aircraft cloud seeding operations conducted in Henan Province of China during 2023–2024\. Results show that the six operations exhibited nonlinear growth patterns for dispersion in both the target and control areas, with rapid expansion at the initial stage followed by a slower rate\. The dispersion rate, distance, extent and concentration of the seeding agent vary significantly depending on the meteorological conditions, such as atmospheric turbulence, wind speed, stability and humidity\. For the six operations, the vertically integrated liquid water content \(VIL\) showed notably high entropy weights \(0\.06–0\.43\) in multiple operations \(No\. 2, 3 and 6\), making it a relatively stable indicator for evaluating the cloud seeding effects\. Due to complex cloud microphysical processes such as latent heat release from deposition, downdrafts, cloud dissipation and cloud development, the responses of cloud\-top temperature to seeding varied considerably \(− 44\.56 °C \~ − 6 °C\)\. The effects of cloud seeding on cloud effective radius and optical thickness are complex and vary substantially depending on specific seeding conditions\. The responses of liquid water path were time\-dependent, the seeding\-induced responses of radar reflectivity exhibited distinct patterns, including delayed manifestation, strong enhancement, and ineffectiveness or being masked\. The strong\-echo area and the VIL in the target areas fluctuated and generally decreased over time, respectively\. The change rates of hourly precipitation induced by seeding varied from 3\.82% to 8\.91%\. The integrated physical inspection dimensionless index \(PIDI, a physical evaluation index for evaluating cloud seeding effects\) values for the seven indicators ranged from 15\.0% to 69\.7%, showing a smaller variation magnitude compared with the change rates of individual indicators, which reflects the synergistic effects of multiple indicators\. This study provides a quantifiable and robust algorithm that mitigates the interference of natural variability, and its application to six case studies demonstrates its potential for advancing cloud seeding techniques and improving effect evaluation capabilities\.

## [Carcinogenic mechanisms in penile cancer: HPV, inflammation, and other pathways](../publications/d5bb72d977bdd03d6a6a.md)

Leonardo Oliveira Reis; Luciana S\. B\. Dal Col; Pablo A\.L\. Mattos; Heveline R\. M\. Hoesch; Marina S\. Folguieri; Diego Moreira Capibaribe; Natália D\. Avilez; Marcos Tobias‐Machado

Objective: Penile cancer, though rare, carries profound clinical and psychosocial consequences\. Its diagnosis often occurs at advanced stages, leading to mutilating surgeries and severe impairment in quality of life\. Approximately 95% of penile malignancies are squamous cell carcinomas \(SCCs\), with a global 5\-year cancer\-specific survival rate of \~65%\. Recent advances have shifted attention from purely oncologic outcomes toward understanding its molecular heterogeneity and etiopathogenesis\. Growing evidence supports a dual carcinogenic model involving viral and non\-viral pathways, driven respectively by human papillomavirus \(HPV\) infection and chronic inflammatory dermatoses\. The objectives of the study are to synthesize current evidence on the molecular, immunologic, and epigenetic mechanisms underlying HPV\-related and HPV\-independent penile SCC, emphasizing their epidemiologic relevance, pathogenic interplay, and clinical implications\. Materials and Methods: A critical appraisal of epidemiological, molecular, and immunological studies was conducted, and evidence was graded according to the Oxford classification for levels of evidence and strength of recommendation\. Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Literatura Latino\-Americana e do Caribe em Ciências da Saúde, covering publications from January 2000 to October 2025\. Search terms included \(“penile cancer” OR “penile carcinoma” OR “penile squamous cell carcinoma” OR “cancer of the penis”\) AND \(“HPV” OR “human papillomavirus” OR “lichen sclerosus” OR “balanitis” OR “chronic inflammation” OR “carcinogenesis” OR “molecular mechanism” OR “tumor microenvironment” OR “epigenetics” OR “non\-coding RNA” OR “APOBEC” OR “immune checkpoint” OR “p16” OR “TP53” OR “E6 oncoprotein” OR “E7 oncoprotein” OR “p16INK4a” OR “viral integration” OR “HPV DNA” OR “E6/E7 mRNA” OR “pRb inactivation” OR “p53 degradation” OR “CDKN2A methylation” OR “DNA methylation” OR “histone modification” OR “miRNA” OR “lncRNA” OR “piRNA” OR “cancer\-associated fibroblast” OR “tumor\-associated macrophage” OR “immune checkpoint” OR “PD\-L1” OR “EBV” OR “HSV” OR “viral co\-infection”\)\. Studies were selected according to predefined inclusion criteria \(systematic reviews, clinical trials, and cohort studies with histological confirmation\) and exclusion criteria \(case reports, series with &lt;30 patients, and non\-peer\-reviewed sources\)\. Evidence quality was graded using the Oxford Centre for Evidence\-Based Medicine framework\. Results: Two distinct but occasionally overlapping oncogenic mechanisms drive penile carcinogenesis\. The HPV\-related pathway, responsible for 30–50% of cases, is predominantly associated with HPV\-16 and HPV\-18\. Viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 promote p53 degradation and retinoblastoma \(pRb\) inactivation, resulting in uncontrolled proliferation and p16^INK4a^ overexpression\. Integration of viral DNA into the host genome disrupts regulatory genes and induces epigenetic alterations, including hypermethylation of CDKN2A and global hypomethylation\. HPV\-positive tumors typically exhibit lower mutational burden, higher immune infiltration, and improved prognosis\. Nonetheless, HPV\-driven lesions display enrichment of immunosuppressive cells \(FoxP3\+ regulatory T cells and CD163\+ macrophages\), and upregulation of immune checkpoints \(programmed cell death 1, lymphocyte activation gene\-3, T cell immunoglobulin and mucin\-domain containing\-3\), favoring immune exhaustion and tumor persistence\. Conversely, the HPV\-independent pathway arises primarily from chronic inflammatory and dermatologic conditions such as lichen sclerosus and balanitis\. Persistent inflammation generates oxidative stress and DNA damage, driving tumor protein 53 \(TP53\) mutations and activating nuclear factor kappa B, cyclooxygenase\-2, interleukin 6/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, and transforming growth factor\-beta signaling cascades\. These molecular events establish a tumor\-promoting microenvironment characterized by angiogenesis, epithelial\-mesenchymal transition, and immune evasion\. Genetic susceptibility through polymorphisms in DNA repair \(TP53, breast cancer gene 2, excision repair cross\-complementing 4\) and immune\-regulatory genes modulates individual risk\. In addition, dysregulation of non\-coding RNAs \(miR\-21, miR\-223, miR\-744\-5p\), APOBEC3\-mediated mutagenesis, and viral co\-infections \(herpes simplex virus, Epstein\-Barr virus\) contribute to genomic instability and disease progression\. Conclusion: Penile carcinogenesis represents a multifactorial process involving viral, inflammatory, and host\-genetic interactions that converge on immune evasion and genomic instability\. HPV\-driven and inflammation\-mediated pathways may act synergistically, amplifying oncogenic potential through shared inflammatory and epigenetic circuits\. Integration of HPV testing, p16 immunohistochemistry, and molecular profiling into clinical practice is instrumental for accurate classification, prognostic refinement, and the development of precision\-based prevention and treatment strategies\. Public health efforts focused on HPV vaccination, early circumcision, and management of chronic inflammatory conditions remain critical to reducing incidence and mortality, particularly in high\-burden regions such as Latin America and sub\-Saharan Africa\.

## [Operationalizing OWASP LLM Top 10 Controls in Enterprise AI Platforms](../publications/d5e02921a068fbc9aecb.md)

Sai Kumar Pola; Pavan Kumar Koneru

Enterprises have moved large language model applications from pilot projects into production systems handling customer conversations, internal knowledge retrieval, and increasingly autonomous agentic workflows, introducing a risk surface that differs materially from what conventional application security programs address\. OWASP has responded with the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, most recently revised in its 2025 edition, and a newly published Top 10 for Agentic Applications covering autonomous, tool\-using systems\. These taxonomies name and prioritize risk but leave engineering teams to translate categories such as prompt injection or excessive agency into controls that fit an existing cloud\-native delivery pipeline\. This paper proposes a reference architecture and implementation framework mapping each of the ten OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 categories to specific, deployable controls built on commonly used cloud primitives: managed model gateways, service mesh identity, retrieval\-augmented generation pipelines, and continuous delivery tooling\. The framework is informed by production engineering practice with retrieval\-augmented generation and agentic workloads on Kubernetes using a managed foundation model service\. Five real, publicly documented incidents, including a corporate data leak, a manipulated dealership chatbot, a legal ruling on chatbot liability, an indirect prompt injection exfiltration attack, and a zero\-click vulnerability in a widely used enterprise copilot, are analyzed against the proposed controls to show where the framework would have reduced impact or prevented the incident outright\. A four\-stage maturity model helps organizations sequence adoption\. Open challenges discussed include the immaturity of evaluation tooling for non\-deterministic systems and the persistent tension between guardrail thoroughness and production latency\.

## [An Assessment of Green Management and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Business Management](../publications/d5e60989e8c4af4379f7.md)

Ayla AVCI

The aim of this study is to examine academic publications on green management published in 2024, identifying key research themes, findings, and relationships with sustainability, environmental performance, and green human resource management\. A qualitative research design based on document analysis was adopted for the investigation\. Data were gathered from 23 academic publications retrieved via Google Scholar using the keyword “green management”\. Selected publications underwent rigorous content analysis, and findings were synthesized thematically alongside geographical and sectoral distributions\. China represented the largest share, accounting for 39\.1% of all reviewed publications\. Research predominantly focused on the corporate sector, followed by higher education, manufacturing, and small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\)\. Notably, none of the examined studies directly addressed green artificial intelligence\. The findings indicate that green management is strongly associated with green innovation, environmental performance, resource efficiency, employee environmentally responsible behaviors, and overall organizational sustainability\. Green technology adoption, organizational culture, and environmental regulations also emerged as critical drivers\. Ultimately, the results underscore the necessity of integrating environmental objectives into core organizational strategies\. Future research should explore green management across diverse national and sectoral contexts\.

## [Genomics and metabolomics analyses reveal the endophytic fungus Neocucurbitaria sp\. VM\-36 as a potential source of bioactive metabolites against methicillin\-resistant Staphylococcus aureus](../publications/d5f26b7d426be27904b7.md)

Xiao Li; Rosario del Carmen Flores\-Vallejo; Ting He; Jan Maarten van Dijl; Kristina Haslinger

Introduction Endophytic fungi associated with medicinal plants represent valuable sources of specialized metabolites with potential biological activities\. Methods Here, we investigated Neocucurbitaria sp\. VM\-36, an understudied endophyte isolated from the medicinal plant Vinca minor , using an integrated genomic, metabolomic, and antibacterial approach\. Results Whole genome analysis suggests substantial biosynthetic potential for a range of secondary metabolites based on the presence of various biosynthetic gene clusters\. Metabolomic profiling revealed a broad chemical repertoire, including metabolites putatively assigned as decalin\-containing tetramic acids \(DTAs\)\. Among the compounds examined experimentally, compound 1 was structurally identified and exhibited potent antibacterial activity against Gram\-positive pathogens, particularly methicillin\-resistant Staphylococcus aureus \(MRSA\), with MIC and MBC values of 0\.5–1 and 2–4 μg/mL, respectively\. Compound 1 displayed rapid bactericidal activity and showed an additive effect in combination with daptomycin against a clinical MRSA isolate \(FICI = 0\.625\)\. These findings provide evidence for the occurrence of DTA\-related metabolites in Neocucurbitaria and experimentally demonstrate the antibacterial activity of compound 1 \. Discussion Collectively, this study provides integrated genomic and metabolomic insights into an endophytic Neocucurbitaria strain, expands the known occurrence of DTA\-related metabolites in fungi, and supports the potential of Neocucurbitaria as a source of antibacterial hit compounds\.

## [Understanding situational fear of crime in context: a virtual reality interview approach to studying victimization avoidance strategies in nocturnal urban spaces](../publications/d6003e3548e4fb0147f1.md)

Edoardo Cocco

Abstract Most research on the behavioral dimension of fear of crime captures broad avoidance habits through surveys or retrospective interviews, leaving the in\-situ risk management behaviors people deploy while actually present in a threatening space largely unobserved\. This study uses Virtual Reality Retrospective Thinking Aloud \(VR\-RTA\) to access this underexplored dimension\. Sixty\-one participants navigated a 3D replica of nocturnal Lausanne in scenarios developed with police officers\. Analysis identified two types of in\-situ avoidance strategies: anticipatory scanning and route management; reactive symbolic distancing from perceived threats, modulated by personal familiarity with the area as a dispositional factor, alongside three vulnerability dimensions \(self, environment, others\) reflecting the core components of Routine Activity Theory\. Crucially, many routing decisions proved habit\-driven rather than fear\-driven \(a distinction surveys cannot detect\) and several behavioral adjustments operated below conscious awareness, recoverable only through VR\-RTA video review of participants’ own behavior\. Findings point towards a sequential process model of situational FoC: behavioral adjustment begins as routine cognitive appraisal and escalates to full fear engagement only when perceived risk crosses a threshold\. They confirm and nuance existing qualitative typologies of avoidance behavior while identifying specific gaps in survey instruments for measuring the behavioral dimension of situational FoC\. Based on these insights, new survey items targeting in\-situ risk management behaviors are proposed to strengthen the measurement of fear of victimization events\.

## [Climate change exacerbates residential radon exposure and lung cancer risk](../publications/d6098354e9cc0d8da466.md)

Heechan Lee; Niccoló Loret; Sara Antignani; F\. Bochicchio; David B\. Richardson

Abstract Climate change adaptation strategies, such as increased air conditioning use, greater time spent indoors, and seeking cooler lower\-floor spaces, may inadvertently increase residential radon exposure and associated lung cancer risk\. We conducted a scoping review of literature on climate change and indoor radon, then developed four exposure scenarios reflecting plausible behavioral shifts: current conditions, increased air conditioning use, increased time in basements, and a combined scenario\. Using the BEIR VI exposure\-age\-concentration model, we estimated cumulative excess risk of lung cancer mortality by age 85 for US and pooled French\-German\-Italian populations\. Compared to current conditions, the combined hypothetical scenario yielded an additional 46 lung cancer deaths per 10,000 persons in the US, and 42 in Europe\. These findings highlight an unrecognized pathway through which climate change adaptation may amplify population\-level cancer risk, if available countermeasures are not taken\.

## [Circuit\-constrained molecular neuroethology in the medicinal leech Hirudo verbana](../publications/d60e15eb16932068e0ee.md)

Yusuke Tomina; Takayuki Watanabe

Medicinal leeches have long served as classic systems in comparative neuroethology because individual neurons can be identified across animals and linked to well\-defined behaviors\. This review argues that Hirudo verbana is now positioned for a new phase in which this identified\-cell framework can be connected directly to molecular mechanisms\. We first outline the organization and experimental accessibility of the leech nervous system, then evaluate genomic and transcriptomic resources as tools for testing physiologically constrained hypotheses rather than as endpoints in themselves\. We focus on selected problems in which behavior, identified neurons, and molecular candidates can be brought into close alignment: sensory encoding, serotonergic state\-dependent gating, multifunctional behavioral circuits, heartbeat rhythm generation, and endocannabinoid\-dependent plasticity\. Across these examples, the comparative value of Hirudo verbana lies not in nervous\-system simplicity alone, but in interpretability: receptors, ion channels, pumps, peptides, gap\-junction proteins, and metabolic enzymes can be examined in relation to cellular and circuit operations already defined by physiology\. Future progress will require tighter integration of circuit\-defined phenotypes with cell\-resolved transcriptomics, spatial localization, targeted perturbation, and quantitative modeling\. This circuit\-constrained strategy positions Hirudo verbana as a valuable bridge between classical identified\-cell neuroethology and molecular tests of circuit physiology\.

## [The Virtual Embodied Experience: Virtual Reality as a Medium for Computing, Analysing, and Representing the Cityscape](../publications/d6255aba32da287a704f.md)

Enriqueta Llabres\-Valls

The increasing availability of urban data has transformed how the built environment is analysed and designed, yet the tools used to represent and interpret that data remain largely abstract and symbolic\. Virtual reality \(VR\) offers the possibility of engaging with spatial data immersively, but its role in architectural and urban research remains predominantly confined to visualisation and simulation\. The extent to which VR supports embodied interaction with data, where users experience and interpret information through spatial presence and movement, remains underexplored\. This article addresses this gap through a systematic literature review of Scopus and CumInCAD \(Cumulative Index of Computer Aided Architectural Design\), comparing interdisciplinary and architecture\-specific research across three dominant themes: representation and analysis, simulation, and embodied interaction\. The findings reveal a conceptually fragmented field: While computational research has advanced VR simulation significantly, embodied approaches remain weakly integrated with data\-driven workflows\. To address this divide, the article proposes virtual embodied experience \(VEE\), a framework that positions VR as a cognitive interface through which environmental data are navigated as a spatial condition rather than consulted as an abstract output\. The implications of VEE are discussed in relation to emerging professional requirements established by the Architects Registration Board and the Royal Institute of British Architects around climate literacy, lifecycle thinking, and ecological design\.

## [Embodiment, Enaction, and Attunement in Schizophrenia, Autism, and Psychopathy: A Comparative Phenomenological Review](../publications/d62c9964f83c6539982e.md)

Luís Madeira; Cecilia Maria Esposito; Giovanni Stanghellini

Schizophrenia spectrum disorders, autism spectrum disorder, and psychopathy may resemble one another at the behavioural surface\. All three may involve social difficulties, flattened or atypical affect, unusual communication, interpersonal friction, and impaired social adaptation\. Yet their experiential architectures differ in ways that are clinically decisive for differential diagnosis, risk assessment, therapeutic alliance, and environmental design\. This narrative review critically synthesizes work in phenomenological psychopathology and 4E cognitive science to clarify how embodiment, enaction, and attunement are altered across these conditions, with attention to lived space, lived time, selfhood, the Other, empathy, and atmosphere\. We draw on classical phenomenological psychopathology, contemporary research on minimal self disturbance and anomalous self and world experience, enactive and participatory sense\-making accounts of social cognition, and theoretical and empirical literature on autism and psychopathy\. Schizophrenia is characterised by instability of minimal self and world openness, including hyperreflexivity, diminished self\-affection, altered salience, temporal fragmentation, demarcation disturbances, and atmospheric shifts that may precede overt psychosis\. Autism is characterised by differences in embodied sense\-making and interactional coordination, frequently involving sensory regulation needs, altered social timing, atypical affordance perception, masking fatigue, and bidirectional mismatch as described by the double empathy problem\. Psychopathy is characterised by preserved strategic social understanding with reduced affective resonance, moral emotions, and interpersonal concern, yielding forms of instrumental attunement and distinctive encounter climates\. Clinically, targeted phenomenological and second person assessment can improve formulation, reduce diagnostic overshadowing, and guide more differentiated care pathways\.

## [Psychological flourishing among young and middle\-aged postoperative lung cancer patients: a latent profile analysis](../publications/d634ce72ec5fdd14cfe3.md)

Xiuxiu Wang; Yaxuan Gui; Yingying Sang; Tuo Zheng; Huihui Fan; Dan Su; Baoming Wang

Background Young and middle\-aged patients after lung cancer surgery often bear multiple psychological pressures caused by illness and daily life\. As a vital positive psychological resource, flourishing may help improve their postoperative psychological adaptation\. This study aimed to identify the latent profiles of flourishing among young and middle\-aged patients after lung cancer surgery, examine the characteristics of each profile and explore factors associated with these profiles\. Methods Between August 2025 and June 2026, a cross\-sectional survey was conducted on 404 young and middle\-aged postoperative lung cancer patients from a tertiary specialized hospital in Anhui Province\. Data were collected using general demographic questionnaire, Flourishing Scale \(FS\), Herth Hope Index \(HHI\), Social Support Rating Scale \(SSRS\), and Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire \(BIPQ\)\. Latent profile analysis was employed to identify distinct flourishing profiles, and multinomial logistic regression analysis was used to explore factors associated with profile membership\. Results The four\-class model demonstrated optimal fit \(entropy=0\.806, LMR p = 0\.022, BLRT p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Four distinct latent flourishing profiles were identified: Moderate optimistic flourishing subtype \(22\.03%\), Moderate interpersonal flourishing subtype \(27\.97%\), Low flourishing subtype \(28\.22%\), and High flourishing subtype \(21\.78%\)\. Compared with the low flourishing profile, higher emotional response scores were associated with the moderate interpersonal profile \( OR = 1\.273, 95% CI = 1\.094\~1\.480\)\. Higher social support and emotional response scores were associated with the high flourishing profile \( OR = 1\.126, 95% CI = 1\.017\~1\.248; OR = 1\.221, 95% CI = 1\.038\~1\.437\)\. No variables were associated with the moderate optimistic profile\. Conclusion This study identified four latent profiles of flourishing among young and middle\-aged postoperative lung cancer patients, demonstrating substantial heterogeneity in positive psychological adaptation toward postoperative disease stress\. Illness\-related emotional responses and social support show distinct associations with profile membership\. Medical institutions should deliver stratified and refined psychological management according to each patient’s specific characteristics\. Future longitudinal studies may explore the dynamic trajectories of these profiles\.

## [Searching for the Ideal Selection of Cognitive Screening Tasks for Early Detection of Cognitive Decline in Older Individuals With Low Literacy](../publications/d63e5eb2ed878ded35fc.md)

Isabel Pellicer‐Espinosa; Rafael de Andrade Moral; Unai Díaz\-Orueta

BACKGROUND: Tests for detecting neurocognitive disorders may not be suitable for individuals with low educational levels\. This study presents a battery of cognitive tests and tasks to improve the detection of cognitive decline in older adults with different literacy levels\. METHOD: 78 older adults attending primary care services were classified in four groups based on their educational level \(low versus high\) and cognitive status \(healthy versus decline\)\. The evaluation included a selection of cognitive tests and tasks administered in two orders to each half of the sample to reduce sequence of administration bias\. RESULTS: Most tests \(MMSE, Stroop, Five Digit Test, and BNT\-15, as well as many individual tasks\) could not differentiate properly between low\-educated healthy individuals and highly educated individuals with decline, with the latter even showing better performance despite the decline in some selected tasks\. The Phototest emerged as the only effective tool where healthy individuals with low education outperformed highly educated individuals with cognitive decline\. A separate comparison of low versus high education groups \(healthy versus decline\) raised the need for differentiated tasks, based on the education level, to specifically discriminate between healthy individuals and individuals with decline\. CONCLUSIONS: Educational level \(EL\) significantly impacts cognitive performance\. High EL individuals show better results and even compensate for cognitive decline when screened with a range of widely used cognitive tasks\. Tasks must be adapted to EL to avoid biases and improve accuracy in detecting cognitive decline\. Careful selection of tools based on EL is recommended to optimise cognitive assessment\.

## [Beyond AI Use: How AI Literacy Is Linked to Critical Thinking through AI\-Assisted Problem\-Solving Ability and AI Reliance](../publications/d64fb0b74a29525ae159.md)

Yifan Wang

With the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) learning, helping learners use AI effectively to solve language\-related problems while maintaining independent judgment and critical thinking has become a key issue in technologyenhanced language education\. However, existing studies have largely focused on EFL learners’ acceptance of AI, intentions to use it, and usage behaviors, offering limited explanations of how AI literacy shapes learners’ interactions with AI and relates to critical thinking\. To address this gap, the present study drew on self\-regulated learning theory and adopted an explanatory sequential mixed\-methods design\. Questionnaire data from 450 university students with generative AIassisted EFL learning experience were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapping\. Subsequently, 20 participants selected through stratified purposive sampling took part in semi\-structured interviews, which were analyzed thematically\. Quantitative results showed that AI literacy was positively associated with AI\-assisted problem\-solving ability and indirectly associated with critical thinking through AI\-assisted problem\-solving ability and AI reliance\. Thematic analysis further revealed how learners translated AI\-related knowledge and skills into effective problem\-solving practices and how different levels of cognitive control were associated with distinct patterns of AI use and cognitive outcomes\. This study deepens the understanding of the internal cognitive mechanisms underlying EFL learners’ adaptation to AI and provides practical implications for the systematic development of AI literacy and critical thinking in EFL education\.

Asaputex Jaya, Tegal City\. ## [Hybrid Signature\-Based and Machine Learning Based Network Intrusion Detection](../publications/d66f3cdfecca0ec0a7b0.md)

Minakshi, Akash Saklani, Rishav Thakur

The increasing number of cyberattacks against computer networks has created a need for adaptable and effective Network Intrusion Detection System \(NIDS\)\. Traditional signature\-based detection methods are effective at identifying known attack patterns but may fail in detecting new or modified attacks\. On the other hand, machine learning\-based anamoly detection can identify unusual network behaviour but may generate false positives when they are used independently\. This research presents a hybrid Network Intrusion Detection System that combines signature\-based detection with machine learning\-based anamoly detection to address these limitations\. The proposed system captures live network traffic or analyses previously recorded PCAP files, extracts relevant packet and flow\-level features and processes the traffic through two parallel detection mechanisms\. The signature engine identifies known threats using configurable attack rules while a Random Forest classifier is used to detect abnormal or potentially malicious traffic\. Detected events are filtered, de\-duplicated, logged and presented through a real\-time Flask\-based web dashboard\. The system uses features such as packet length, TTL, payload size, protocol, source ports, destination ports and TCP flags for machine learning\-based detection\. The proposed hybrid approach aims to improve the coverage and practical usability of NIDS by combining the reliability of known attack signatures with the adaptability of machine learning\-based anamoly detection\.
