## [Impact of clinical pharmacist interventions in psychiatric hospitals on clinical and medication\-related outcomes](../publications/d69da7644eb47e34ba87.md)

M\. Stuhec; Kaja Balaško; Anteja Gorjan Gazdag; Zala Cuk; Igor Locatelli

Introduction: Clinical pharmacist interventions have been shown to improve outcomes and reduce drug\-related problems \(DRPs\) in patients with mental disorders\. However, no previous meta\-analysis has comprehensively evaluated their effectiveness in reducing DRPs and optimizing pharmacotherapy in psychiatric inpatient settings\.Aim: To evaluate the effectiveness of clinical pharmacist interventions in psychiatric inpatient settings on DRPs and clinical outcomes among patients with mental disorders\.Methods: This systematic review and meta\-analysis was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 statement and prospectively registered in PROSPERO \(CRD420261309290\)\. PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to March 2026\. Eligible studies included adult psychiatric inpatients receiving clinical pharmacist interventions, including different pharmaceutical services, such as medication review, medication reconciliation, and ward round participation\. A meta\-analysis was performed in R using a random\-effects model\. Heterogeneity was calculated using I$^2$\. Random\-effects meta\-analyses were performed for DRPs, potentially inappropriate medications \(PIMs\), and the number of prescribed medications\. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB two and ROBINS\-I\.Results: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, including one randomized controlled trial and 17 non\-randomized interventional studies\. Clinical pharmacist interventions significantly reduced the number of prescribed medications \(mean difference −1\.0 medications per patient, \(95% CI −1\.5 to −0\.5\) and were associated with a pooled reduction in DRPs of 70\.7% \(95% CI 46\.5–87\.0\), as well as reductions in PIMs\. Evidence for patient\-centred clinical outcomes, including symptom improvement, quality of life, and healthcare utilization, remained limited\. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, reflecting differences in intervention types, patient populations, and outcome measures\. Most non\-randomized studies were judged to have a serious risk of bias because of confounding and uncontrolled study designs\.Conclusion: Clinical pharmacist interventions in psychiatric inpatient settings improve medication\-related outcomes by reducing DRPs, PIMs, and the number of prescribed medications\. These findings support the integration of clinical pharmacists into multidisciplinary psychiatric teams\. Further adequately powered multicentre randomized controlled trials are needed to determine whether these improvements translate into better long\-term patient\-centred clinical outcomes\.

## [Metabolic inflammation in metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease](../publications/d6c3d0a89f6383308ccc.md)

Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\) affects approximately 1\.3 billion people worldwide and is frequently associated with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and other metabolic disorders\.A key feature linking these conditions is metabolic inflammation, or metainflammation, a state of chronic, low\-grade inflammation driven by excessive lipid accumulation and adipose tissue dysfunction\.Metainflammation promotes hepatic steatosis, inflammation, hepatocyte injury and ballooning, and fibrosis, thereby contributing to the development and progression of MASLD, as well as metabolic dysfunction and alcohol\-associated liver disease \(MetALD\), which can lead to liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma\.These pathological processes are mediated through multiple interconnected mechanisms, including insulin resistance, dysregulated lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, fibrogenesis, and alterations in the gut microbiota\.This review discusses the mechanisms underlying metainflammation in MASLD and MetALD and summarizes current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting these pathogenic factors in preclinical studies and clinical trials\.

## [The clicking doctors: how the mouse restructures clinical attention](../publications/d6d0255046807531b25a.md)

Wilhelm Haverkamp

The attention of office\-based physicians is increasingly structured less by the patients in front of them than by the screen beside them \- by the clicks, notifications, system lags, and task\-switching that the practice information system demands\. Research on cognitive load and burnout documents the demands of screen work, but commonly used outcome measures do not directly assess whether repeated fragmentation changes habitual patterns of clinical attention\. This article pursues exactly that question: what screen work may change is less the amount of attention than its disposition\. Drawing on research into attention residue, system response times, and time\-and\-motion evidence from ambulatory care, it identifies three mechanisms through which screen work restructures clinical attention: attention residue, response\-time fragmentation, and interface\-induced switching\. Unlike cognitive load, these mechanisms may reshape the disposition of clinical attention itself \- the way a physician attends to the patient, which may become shallower, more reactive, and more externally driven\. The claim is marked throughout as a research\-guiding hypothesis: the three mechanisms are measurable, their cumulative dispositional effect is not yet\. It then shows why automation does not dissolve the problem, and why the growing evidence on ambient\-AI documentation neither confirms nor refutes it\. Because every finding cited remains compatible with simple time scarcity, the article specifies the design that would begin to discriminate between the two: a carry\-over design presenting the same unhurried clinical task to the same physicians at the end of a high\-switch and a low\-switch day, scaled to a cohort with repeated measurement\. It closes with three design requirements: switch ceilings, context preservation after interruptions, and protected attentional time\.

## [Cognitive Psychiatry and the genesis of knowledge: From Meno’s paradox to cosmogenetic analyticity](../publications/d6e876f119bb634c5f8a.md)

Giovanna Azevedo Rodrigues; Marcelo Eduardo Caixeta

Arthur Pap’s functional a priori explains how laws change function once knowledge is constituted, but not how the conceptual core enabling such change is formed\. The aim of this article is to propose a naturogenetic theory of the genesis of knowledge, based on a re\-edition of Meno’s paradox, that completes Arthur Pap’s functional conception of the a priori\. This theoretical essay draws on a narrative review of recent literature \(2021\-2026\) in philosophy of science, cognitive science and neuroscience\. The paradox unfolds into difficulties of identity, pertinence and the gap\. The unknown has borders, as Mendeleev’s empty cells and Maxwell’s analogies show, and definition formalizes relations it does not create; operational criteria secure diagnostic reliability, not validity\. The organism, produced within the causal organization of reality, couples to it through co\-praxis, co\-synchrony and co\-causalization, sedimenting concepts as tracks for future knowledge, consistent with research on cognitive maps, schemas and causal learning\. Leibniz’s complete concept is reread as processual containment, and inquiry is traced back to a cosmogenetic analyticity prior to life and mind, which neither natural selection nor self\-organization explains\. Meno is answered by progressive nucleation, a naturalized recollection that also accounts for error\. Pap’s mobility of laws presupposes this foundation\. Objections of regress, nativism, conventionalism and metaphysical overreach are addressed, and implications for psychiatric nosology are outlined\. The most fundamental analyticity is a relation between real possibilities, not between words\.

## [Evaluating procollagen type III N\-terminal propeptide \(P3NP\) as a biomarker of sarcopenia in women with type 2 diabetes: a cross\-sectional study\.](../publications/d6f1dbd58f78210490ef.md)

Thyago Bruno de Lira Dos Santos; Giselle Rabelo Maciel; Francisco Alfredo Farias Bandeira

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether circulating procollagen type III N\-terminal propeptide \(P3NP\) improves the diagnosis of dual\-energy X\-ray absorptiometry \(DXA\)\-defined sarcopenia in women with type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\)\. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This cross\-sectional study enrolled 99 women with T2DM who underwent standardized clinical assessment, handgrip strength testing, and whole\-body DXA\. Sarcopenia was defined using a DXA\-derived fat\-free mass index\. Multivariable logistic regression models included age, body mass index, glycated hemoglobin \(HbA1c\), and estimated glomerular filtration rate, with and without log\-transformed, z\-standardized P3NP\. Discriminatory performance was quantified by the area under the curve \(AUC\) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals; sensitivity analyses excluded participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60\. RESULTS: P3NP showed weak bivariate correlations with age \(p = \-0\.210\) and the Short Physical Performance Battery \(p = 0\.225\)\. When incorporated into the clinical model, P3NP did not yield a clinically significant improvement \(ΔAUC = 0\.007\)\. As a sole predictor, P3NP had poor discrimination \(AUC 0\.53\) and was not independently associated with DXA\-defined sarcopenia \(odds ratio per 1\-standard deviation, p &gt; 0\.05\)\. Results were consistent after excluding participants with reduced kidney function and across interaction analyses; model calibration was adequate\. P3NP absolute values were elevated, with 80\.8% above the high threshold \(&gt;31 μg/L\), and clinical/functional profiles were broadly similar P3NP strata\. CONCLUSION: In women with T2DM, circulating P3NP was not an independent discriminator of DXA\-defined sarcopenia and provided no clinically meaningful advantage over standard clinical predictors\. Routine screening should continue to rely on assessments of muscle strength, function, and DXA\-based body composition, while P3NP may be considered an adjunct marker of extracellular matrix remodeling\.

## [A longitudinal perspective on educational inequalities in Romania: between\-cohort comparisons and within\-cohort progression across stages and pathways](../publications/d702a059521c9b1b9e5d.md)

Diana Paula Simionescu; Ana\-Maria Dalu; Delia Goia; Oana Iftode; Gabriela Nausica Noveanu; Ancuţa Plăeşu

Introduction Progression through educational milestones and inequality need not change in parallel: group differences may narrow at one transition, widen at another, or shift into differentiated pathways\. Methods Using Romanian administrative records, we compared the 1999, 2004, and 2009 birth cohorts across six transition\-specific analyses in two overlapping historical windows\. A linked stage\-based multi\-state analysis followed 122,344 students in the 2004 cohort from a documented Grade 5 origin through Baccalaureate success within four examination opportunities\. We estimated model\-implied probabilities and probability differences by sex, the Roma administrative marker, first language, and school setting\. Results The later cohort had higher probabilities at four milestones: promoted Grade 8 completion \[2009 vs\. 2004: \+4\.11 percentage points \(pp\)\], promoted Grade 12 completion within day\-school high school \(2004 vs\. 1999: \+7\.16 pp\), Baccalaureate entry \(\+2\.33 pp\), and Baccalaureate success within the first two examination opportunities \(\+7\.60 pp\)\. Group differences changed unevenly: female–male differences were smaller in the later cohort at all four milestones, non\-Roma–Roma differences narrowed at Grade 8 and Grade 12 completion, whereas the urban–rural difference narrowed at Grade 12 completion and Baccalaureate success but widened at Baccalaureate entry\. Grade 9 pathway composition varied by cohort and group\. Within the linked 2004 cohort, standardized probabilities from Grade 5 were 90\.54% for promoted Grade 8 completion, 64\.59% for documented high\-school completion, 60\.21% for Baccalaureate entry, and 50\.72% for Baccalaureate success through four examination opportunities\. Between Grade 8 completion and Baccalaureate success within the first four examination opportunities, the female–male gap increased from 0\.67 to 15\.08 pp, the non\-Roma–Roma gap from 30\.75 to 43\.15 pp, the Romanian–different\-first\-language gap from 0\.79 to 6\.21 pp, and the urban–rural Grade 5\-origin gap from 2\.32 to 30\.39 pp; not all gaps evolved monotonically across stages\. Discussion Aggregate progression, between\-cohort change in inequality, and inequality development across stages within a cohort are related but distinct processes\. A single endpoint can obscure convergence at some transitions alongside larger or reconfigured inequalities elsewhere in the educational trajectory\. Stage\-sensitive longitudinal evidence can identify where inequalities become most pronounced and guide research on their mechanisms and intervention effectiveness\.

## [Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine\-Tuning Generalizes After It](../publications/d7235e187bb10ce3515e.md)

Faridoun Mehri; Hinrich Schütze

Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well\. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task\. We study this distinction by constructing new relations from existing ones\. Take the relation that maps a place to its continent \(Paris \-&gt; Europe\) and assign each of its answers an arbitrary new label \(Europe \-&gt; crab, Asia \-&gt; zebra\)\. The new relation then maps Paris \-&gt; crab\. We fine\-tune the model on the new relation for a subset of subjects, without telling it the original relation or the relabeling rule, and test whether it assigns the corresponding labels to held\-out subjects that share an answer in the original relation\. Having learned Paris \-&gt; crab, does it answer Munich \-&gt; crab? Across eleven language models and 70 relations, how linearly readable the original relation is in pretrained representations strongly predicts this generalization\. Within each model, the two correlate across relations at Pearson r = 0\.87 to 0\.92\. This association persists when controlling, separately and jointly, for the number of fine\-tuning subjects and answers, the model&\#x27;s accuracy on the original relation, and how often the subjects occur in pretraining text\. It is also robust to re\-randomizing the label assignment and fine\-tuning seed, and to replacing the animal labels with labels from thirteen other semantic categories\. When we map a fine\-tuned model&\#x27;s wrong label back to the original answer it was assigned to, Munich \-&gt; zebra becomes Munich \-&gt; Asia\. Answers recovered this way are more often among the linear probe&\#x27;s top answers for the subject than among the pretrained model&\#x27;s own\. Whether a new relation generalizes depends less on whether its facts can be recalled than on how readily their shared structure can be read out linearly\.

## [Lightweight motion\-centric deepfake detection from the labial region through transferable and privacy\-aware forensic representations](../publications/d73c7adf840cf54bd554.md)

Spatio\-temporal, gradient\-based, and geometry\-aware descriptors are employed to capture complementary local facial dynamics while limiting reliance on full\-face imagery\. ## [From Anthropomorphism to Trust: Unpacking the Role of Authenticity in Generative AI and Large Language Models—A Structured Literature Review and Future Research Agenda](../publications/d779d7f69cb8e7c75620.md)

Ana Maria Ifrim; Ionica Oncioiu; Catalin ionut Silvestru; Constantin\-Adrian Popescu; Tiberiu Gabriel Dobrescu; Emilia\-Maria Popescu

Generative artificial intelligence has changed the conditions under which users encounter and evaluate machine\-produced communication\. In systems based on large language models, conversational output is no longer merely functional; it can be fluent, context\-aware, and socially legible, inviting judgments that extend beyond usefulness, accuracy, or efficiency\. Yet the literature still tends to treat anthropomorphism, perceived authenticity, and trust as largely separate constructs, without sufficiently explaining how human\-like cues become credible in the eyes of users and how this credibility shapes trust\. To address this problem, the present structured literature review synthesizes recent research on anthropomorphism, authenticity\-related evaluations, and trust in AI\-mediated interaction, with particular attention to conversational AI, generative AI, and LLM\-based systems\. A structured search in the Web of Science Core Collection identified 655 records; after duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 96 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis\. The analysis identifies several interrelated thematic patterns, including anthropomorphic cues and social presence, authenticity\-related mechanisms in AI\-mediated communication, trust formation and calibration, boundary conditions, and behavioral responses to conversational AI\. On this basis, the review develops an integrative conceptual framework and proposes perceived anthropomorphic authenticity as a review\-derived construct for examining how users evaluate human\-like AI communication in relation to trust\. The study contributes to human–AI interaction research by clarifying the role of authenticity\-related evaluations between anthropomorphic cues and calibrated trust and by identifying conditions under which human\-like communication may be associated with trust, skepticism, overreliance, or trust erosion\.

Tool\-augmented language\-model agents rely on interface text: tool descriptions, argument schemas, and the candidate tool list shown at inference time\. These interfaces often change after deployment even when the underlying tool semantics remain fixed, creating a practical reliability problem for function\-calling systems\. We study this failure mode as interface drift and evaluate whether a lightweight, training\-free repair layer can recover robustness without retraining the base model\. Our method, SchemaShield\-Lite, combines schema validation, candidate\-set retry for missing tool names, and one\-shot constrained repair\. On Qwen3\.5\-9B, it raises DICE\-300 accuracy from 0\.717 to 0\.813 and BFCL\-200 accuracy from 0\.580 to 0\.805, recovering 19/22 and 33/45 drift\-induced failures with no observed repair harms\. Naive retry does not explain the gains\. Ablations show that candidate\-set drift, especially distractor tools, accounts for most observed damage, while description and schema edits alone are less harmful\. The results position validation\-and\-repair as a practical robustness layer for deployed LLM\-agent tool use\.

## [EOS Banking AI Barometer\. What Europe&\#x27;s consumers really think about AI in banking\. Whitepaper](../publications/d79fbfa5475df7c5f75f.md)

EOS Holding GmbH

This whitepaper presents the findings of the EOS Banking AI Barometer 2026, a survey exploring consumer attitudes toward artificial intelligence in banking communication\. A total of 4,400 consumers across eleven European countries were surveyed about their expectations, preferences, and concerns regarding the use of AI in interactions with banks\. The study examines acceptance levels, perceived benefits, trust, and the role of AI in sensitive financial situations\. The findings provide insights into how consumers view AI\-powered banking services and how expectations differ across demographic groups and national markets\.

## [LASSO\-Based Identification of Sparse Autoregressive Exogenous Input Model Coefficients](../publications/d7a23282a740f9734d80.md)

Trung Dat Phan; Cong Toai Truong; Huy Hung Nguyen; Tan Tien Nguyen; Van Tu Duong

Accurate system identification is important role in the development of reliable control approaches for automated respiratory devices\. Nonetheless, conventional identification approaches suffer from overfitting and sensitivity to noise\. Therefore, in this paper, a novel sparse autoregressive exogenous input identification scheme based on the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator is proposed for the automated AMBU\-bag resuscitator \(AABR\)\. Specifically, it incorporates decoupled regularization terms for autoregressive and input\-related components, as well as enables robust parameter estimation without requiring normalization of input data\. The grey wolf optimizer \(GWO\) is used to optimize regularization parameters by minimizing prediction errors on validation datasets\. The experimental data were obtained from a real AABR system with three excitation signals: cosine, parabolic, and ramp, corresponding to smooth periodic, second\-order polynomial, and linear profiles, respectively\. The smooth periodic profile dataset was used for training, while the others were employed for validation\. As a result, the proposed model achieved consistent prediction accuracy, with the root mean square errors \(RMSEs\) of 0\.177893, 0\.195727, and 0\.150998\. Conversely, the conventional recursive least squares \(RLS\) method exhibited severe overfitting, with RMSE increasing from 0\.009821 to 11\.436522\.

## [Evidence\-based design of vaccine hesitancy information resources for health care providers](../publications/d7a7a130e2e1205b9f1c.md)

Margaret Ansell; Hannah Norton; Nina Stoyan\-Rosenzweig; Jane Morgan‐Daniel; Mary Edwards; Lauren Adkins

Background: The University of Florida Health Science Center Libraries \(HSCL\) sought to address the increasing challenge of vaccine hesitancy during the COVID\-19 pandemic by developing evidence\-based information resources for health care providers\. To do this, HSCL librarians assessed the vaccine hesitancy information needs of local health care providers to design a resource that could be used to support conversations with vaccine hesitant patients at the point of care\. Case Presentation: A team of six librarians, supported by student research assistants, conducted interviews with 20 health care providers in north central Florida\. The interviews, conducted via Zoom, focused on providers&\#x27; experiences with vaccine\-hesitant patients\. Content analysis of the transcribed interviews identified key themes, including trust, individualized conversations, and the impact of misinformation\. The team developed a resource guide based on these findings, featuring curated information to support providers in vaccine discussions\. Conclusions: The results highlighted the importance of trust in patient\-provider relationships and the challenges posed by misinformation\. Providers expressed a need for diverse, accessible resources to aid in conversations about vaccines\. The resulting resource guide, disseminated through local health networks, aims to enhance providers&\#x27; ability to address vaccine hesitancy effectively\. This project underscores the critical role of librarians in public health initiatives and the value of collaborative efforts to combat vaccine hesitancy\.

## [AI without reach: The last mile problem in preventive public health](../publications/d7a865275b23a73e9c73.md)

M\. Courtney Hughes

Objectives Examine the &quot;last mile problem&quot; in artificial intelligence \(AI\) applications for preventive public health\. Study design Conceptual short communication introducing a five\-stage pathway to examine where AI\-enabled prevention breaks down\. Methods This draws on emerging literature in AI, health services research, and implementation science to distinguish between predictive capacity and real\-world impact\. A five\-stage pathway model of prediction, translation, delivery, uptake, and sustainment is introduced to characterize where breakdowns occur between identifying risk and changing outcomes\. Results Current AI applications in public health are heavily concentrated in prediction, with limited attention to delivery, engagement, and sustained behavior change\. These gaps are particularly consequential in prevention, where action must occur before consequences are visible, and in contexts such as family caregiving, where individuals operate as de facto delivery systems without adequate support\. Traditional measures of healthcare access further obscure the problem by suggesting that services are available when real\-world barriers prevent their use\. The last mile problem is not evenly distributed; it disproportionately affects populations facing structural disadvantage, meaning that AI systems that fail to account for delivery and context risk widening existing inequities\. Conclusions Addressing the last mile requires reorienting AI from a primarily predictive tool to one embedded in systems of care and daily life\. This includes integrating real\-time data, designing for context, and evaluating AI on whether it enables timely, sustained action, not on predictive accuracy alone\. Until AI reaches the last mile, its contribution to prevention will remain incomplete, accurate in prediction but limited in impact\.

## [Blast\.jl: Differentiable Non\-Limber Power Spectra for Joint Clustering, Shear, and CMB lensing Analyses](../publications/d7afde23f30486810c50.md)

Sofia Chiarenza; Marco Bonici; Stefano Camera; Giulio Fabbian; Carlos García\-García; Alex Krolewski; Will J\. Percival

Upcoming large\-scale structure surveys require accurate theoretical predictions for angular power spectra on the largest angular scales, where the commonly used Limber approximation breaks down and multiple relativistic and observational effects become relevant\. At the same time, modern cosmological analyses increasingly rely on gradient\-based inference techniques, motivating the development of fast, fully differentiable algorithms\. In this work, we present a major extension of Blast\.jl, a numerical toolkit for the efficient computation of non\-Limber angular power spectra\. Building on the Chebyshev\-polynomial decomposition of the original framework, the updated algorithm incorporates redshift\-space distortions, magnification bias, primordial non\-Gaussianity, intrinsic alignments, CMB lensing, and the integrated Sachs\-Wolfe effect, while remaining fully differentiable through custom automatic differentiation rules\. Despite the increased physical complexity, the algorithm retains favorable scaling by precomputing all cosmology\-independent quantities\. We validate the expanded framework against brute\-force integration and established cosmological codes, and provide a detailed analysis of the trade\-off between computational speed and precision as a function of the algorithm hyperparameters\. We demonstrate the readiness of Blast\.jl for gradient\-based inference through a simulated likelihood analysis with LSST Y10\-like mock data, recovering unbiased cosmological and nuisance parameter constraints from a 35\-parameter model using gradient\-based samplers\.

## [Conceptual Framework and Domain\-Based Classification of Vātaprakopa Lakṣaṇas in Vātavyādhi: A Literary Review](../publications/d7b208c0c29c1c448ce9.md)

A\. J\. Jyothis; Dr\.K\.Murali Kizhakkemadham

Introduction: Vāta \- one of the three Doṣas \(the regulatory functional factors of the body: Vāta, Pitta and Kapha\), and the one governing movement, sensory perception and cognition — is the most dominant of the three Doṣas and underlies the majority of clinically encountered Vātavyādhi \(disorders of vitiated Vāta\)\. Its aggravated state, Vātaprakopa \(aggravation, or vitiation, of Vāta\), is described in the classics through Lakṣaṇas \(clinical signs and symptoms\) that are conceptually distinct from disease\-specific Vātavyādhi Lakṣaṇas, yet these descriptions remain scattered across texts in overlapping terminology, and no standardized framework or clinical tool exists to assess them systematically\. Methods: A conceptual literary review was undertaken of Vātaprakopa Lakṣaṇas described in Caraka Saṃhitā and Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya, with a brief supplementary reference from Suśruta Saṃhitā\. Lakṣaṇas were cross\-tabulated to identify terminological overlap, then synthesized into higher\-order domains using three guiding principles — functional similarity, pathophysiological coherence, and clinical applicability — restricted to disorders of the Madhyama Rogamārga \(the pathway of disease manifestation centred on the Sandhis \[joints\], Marmas \[vulnerable, or vital, points\], together with the Sirā\-Kaṇḍarā \[vessels and tendon\] — one of three classical categories of disease, distinguished not by fixed anatomical location but by the tissue or channel through which the Doṣa travels and manifests, together with Bāhya Rogamārga \[Tvak, Rakta, Māṃsa and Medas — skin, blood, muscle and fat\] and Antaḥ/Ābhyantara Rogamārga \[Koṣṭha — the abdominal cavity, chiefly the gastrointestinal tract\]\)\. Results: Synthesis yielded eight conceptual domains: Gati Vaiguṇya \(motor dysfunction\), Vedanā \(pain spectrum\), Sparśa and Sensory Dysfunction, Kriyā Hāni \(functional impairment\), Mārgāvarodha \(obstructive manifestations\), Dhātu Kṣaya and Structural Changes, Guṇa Vaikṛta \(altered physical qualities\), and Varṇa Vaikṛta \(colour changes\)\. Each domain was examined for a supporting classical rationale, and overlapping domain pairs \(Gati Vaiguṇya/Kriyā Hāni; Vedanā/Sparśa\) were differentiated using qualitative\-versus\-quantitative and submodality\-based distinctions respectively, each illustrated with worked clinical examples\. Conclusion: This review proposes an initial domain\-based conceptual framework for Vātaprakopa Lakṣaṇas specific to Vātavyādhi\. It offers a conceptual basis that may, subject to future expert\-panel and clinical validation, inform the development of a standardized clinical instrument to assess Vāta aggravation, stage disease, and monitor treatment outcome; these applications are proposed as future directions and have not themselves been validated in this review\. Keywords: Vātaprakopa, Vātavyādhi, Lakṣaṇa, domain classification, clinical assessment tool

## [A Comprehensive Review on Infectious and Non\-Infectious Diseases of Companion Animals](../publications/d7b54013046316a0bd33.md)



The rising incidence of infectious and non\-infectious diseases of companion animals is considered an issue of burning concern globally that has a significant impact on animal&\#x27;s productivity and quality of life\.Infectious and non\-infectious diseases of companion animals are also harmful to human beings such as Rabies, Canine Parvovirus, Canine Infectious Hepatitis, leptospirosis, Canine Distemper, Pan\-leukopenia, Feline Calicivirus, Equine Herpes Virus, and Equine Infectious Anemia\.During the last few decades, diagnostic criteria and overall treatment options have improved\.The re\-emergence, as well as the emergence of chronic and fatal diseases, threatens various sectors, including the animal care industry, and veterinary medicine\.The rapid growth of the animal industry, climate change, and socio\-economic burdens affect veterinarians, farmers, and epidemiologists in their ability to monitor the spread of diseases in animals and determine their beneficial effects on livelihoods and the environment\.Herein, we reviewed general information on various infections and non\-infectious diseases, along with the detective measures, control of epidemics, and effective measures of companion animals\.In the end, we summarize the future concerns, concluding remarks, and recommendations are also given for progress in the animal care and medicine sectors\.

## [Machine Learning in Teaching Piano Touch Technique and Tonal Expression](../publications/d7c38634d5d604f44e95.md)

Da Li; Jing Zhou; Qiyan Tan

Music is an art involving both sound and hearing, and it is experienced through a combination of musical performance and attentive listening\. Among the many musical instruments, the piano is often called the “king of instruments\.” Unlike the violin, which is frequently described as delicate and soft, the piano possesses a tone that may be perceived as noble and graceful\. A statement attributed to the pianist Nergoz emphasizes that the purpose of piano playing is to make sound and to create sound\. This observation draws attention to the central importance of sound production in piano education, although the attribution needs confirmation from an identifiable original source\. How, then, can a pianist use the instrument to produce a beautiful sound? This remains an essential concern for piano players at different levels of study and performance\. Therefore, tonal quality deserves consistent attention during both technical practice and musical performance, because the fingers must engage with the keys to produce each intended sound\. Tone plays an important role throughout the entire process of piano performance\. Both the expressiveness of piano playing and its appeal to listeners are closely associated with the quality of the resulting tone\. The area of key contact, the intensity of the touch, and the technique employed all have an important influence on the resulting sound\. A systematic approach to finger touch is consequently an important skill and a valuable technical consideration, both when learning to play the piano and when performing musical compositions\.

## [Platelet Rich Plasma Injection as A Treatment for Intercostal Neuralgia: A Case Report](../publications/d7c73834b8b1783c7a9d.md)

Meliani Anggreni; Pryambodho Pryambodho; Yosi Asmara

Intercostal neuralgia is a neuropathic pain condition that may persist following rib fractures, adversely affecting sleep quality and daily functioning\. Conventional pharmacological and interventional treatments may provide insufficient pain relief, prompting interest in regenerative therapeutic approaches\. This case report aimed to describe the clinical outcomes of ultrasound\-guided perineural platelet\-rich plasma \(PRP\) injections in a patient with refractory posttraumatic intercostal neuralgia\. A 52\-year\-old woman presented with persistent pain along the distribution of the left tenth intercostal nerve following a rib fracture sustained 10 months earlier\. Previous conservative treatment, cryoablation, and prolotherapy had failed to provide meaningful symptom relief\. Autologous PRP was prepared using a double\-spin centrifugation technique and administered perineurally under ultrasound guidance\. Two injections were performed at a two\-week interval\. Pain intensity and symptom improvement were assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale \(NRS\) and clinical symptom evaluation\. At baseline, the patient reported a pain intensity of 3–4 on the NRS, with breakthrough pain episodes reaching 6 and occurring three to five times daily, accompanied by sleep disturbances and limitations in daily activities\. Following the first injection, the patient reported approximately 50% pain relief, followed by complete pain relief after the second injection\. These clinical observations may be consistent with the proposed anti\-inflammatory and neuroregenerative effects of PRP, although the underlying mechanisms were not directly investigated\. Ultrasound\-guided perineural PRP injections may represent a potential therapeutic option for refractory posttraumatic intercostal neuralgia\. However, controlled clinical studies using standardized treatment protocols, objective outcome measures, and longer follow\-up periods are necessary to establish their efficacy and safety\.

## [Liquefaction\-Induced Settlement and Pile Foundation Performance in Gölbaşı after the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes: A Numerical and Site Observed Case Study](../publications/d7c7631f73c307e62bf5.md)

Erhan Tekin; Aybüke Nur Tuncel Gökdoğan; Nihat Sinan Işık; Seyhan Fırat

The 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence caused widespread structural damage and ground failure across southern Türkiye\. Gölbaşı district, Adıyaman province, was among the most affected localities, underlain by young alluvial, lacustrine, and marsh deposits with a shallow groundwater table\. This paper presents a case study of the damaged Gölbaşı Muftiate Building, a mat\-founded structure on an unconnected ground\-improvement pile system that underwent severe settlement and tilting after the earthquakes\. The study integrates post\-earthquake field observations, SPT and CPT data, laboratory characterization, strong\-motion record selection, one\-dimensional site\-response analysis, pile\-soil interaction analysis, two\-dimensional finite\-element modelling, and a simplified CPT\-based liquefaction settlement assessment\. The idealized profile comprises silty sand \(0–8\.0 m\), soft clay \(8\.0–11\.5 m\), sandy silt \(11\.5–16\.5 m\), and hard clay below 16\.5 m, with liquefaction\-prone units in the silty sand and sandy silt layers\. DEEPSOIL analyses indicate excess pore\-water\-pressure generation and free\-field horizontal deformation under the selected record\. RSPile results show liquefaction increases pile displacement, bending moment, and shear demand several\-fold relative to non\-liquefied conditions\. Plaxis 2D simulations reproduce settlement consistent with field\-observed damage and confirm excess pore\-pressure development in the upper profile\. A simplified calculation yields a median liquefaction\-induced settlement of about 1\.11 m, consistent with the observed one\-meter building settlement\. These results show that piles terminating within or near liquefiable layers may lose effectiveness when lateral spreading, cyclic mobility, and post\-liquefaction reconsolidation occur together\. The case underscores the need for integrated liquefaction triggering, deformation, and pile\-performance assessments in seismic foundation design\.

## [Defenses contra prompt injection en agents LLM: avaluació sistemàtica i anàlisi mecanicista de modes de fallada](../publications/d7caaec4a0d787d8133d.md)

Daniel Poncelas Vargas

\[EN\] Agents based on large language models \(LLMs\) with access to external tools have become the standard architecture for production artificial intelligence systems\. Their exposure to external content makes them vulnerable to prompt injection: the insertion of malicious instructions into data that the agent processes\. This exposure has been identified by the Open Web Application Security Project \(OWASP\) as the main security risk for LLM applications\. Although recent literature proposes numerous defenses, these methods are evaluated under heterogeneous conditions that prevent rigorous comparison\. This Master&\#x27;s Thesis addresses this gap through a systematic and reproducible evaluation of eight representative state\-of\-the\-art defenses \(Spotlighting, StruQ, SecAlign, PromptGuard, paraphrasing, sandwich, reminder and baseline\), which are applied to models covering both commercial and open\-source systems of different sizes\. The experimental protocol is built on the AgentDojo and InjecAgent benchmarks, applying utility, robustness and refusal metrics in the evaluation, supported by statistical tests\. The work is complemented by a mechanistic interpretability study, which applies techniques such as activation patching and logit lens, in order to characterize which internal components of the model are causally responsible for the failure of the defenses\.
