## [Current trends, knowledge structure, and evidence landscape of phosphorylation\-related research in organoid models: a bibliometric analysis](../publications/d7d757e9899f86cdec0c.md)

Rui Guo; Jing Jia; Chaojun Wei

Research on phosphorylation in organoid models has experienced rapid expansion; however, the knowledge structure, academic impact, and depth of evidence in this field remain inadequately characterized\. Publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection \(SCI\-EXPANDED\) from 2005 to 2025 were retrieved on April 2, 2026\. Following document\-type restriction, deduplication, and manual screening, a total of 236 studies were included\. CiteSpace was employed to analyze publication trends, collaboration patterns, co\-citation structures, highly cited studies, keyword evolution, and citation\-based impact\. The included studies were further classified according to evidence type\. Publication output experienced a significant increase after 2017, with the United States and China emerging as the primary contributors\. However, the levels of productivity did not consistently correlate with citation impact or collaborative centrality\. Co\-citation analysis indicated that the field predominantly focuses on the establishment of stem cell\-derived organoids, translational oncology, cerebral organoid disease models, and the signaling pathways that regulate organoid growth and differentiation\. The most highly cited studies primarily centered on mechanistic phospho\-signaling research, while more recent influential works have expanded into disease modeling and phosphoproteomics\. Notably, 184 out of 236 studies \(77\.97%\) were classified as providing signaling evidence, whereas only 24 studies \(10\.27%\) offered direct evidence of phosphorylation\. Furthermore, intestinal and brain organoids comprised the majority of the studies included, highlighting a pronounced tissue bias within the research\. Research on phosphorylation within organoid models is a rapidly expanding yet heterogeneous field, predominantly characterized by studies focused on signaling pathways, while direct evidence of phosphorylation remains scarce\. These findings underscore significant disparities in impact, model utilization, and the depth of evidence, which should guide future mechanistic and translational research endeavors\.

## [A Fuzzy Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making Approach for Managerial Appointments in Public Health Institutions](../publications/d7dc3b4dc089bd6da250.md)

Memiş KARACA

Objective: Healthcare services are fundamental to public welfare and social sustainability\. The quality, accessibility, continuity, and efficiency of healthcare delivery largely depend on effective institutional governance and competent leadership\. This study aims to develop an objective and systematic evaluation model for managerial appointments in public health institutions in order to strengthen healthcare service performance and ensure merit\-based leadership in service delivery processes\. Methods: A multi\-criteria decision\-making \(MCDM\) framework was developed based on criteria identified from the healthcare management literature, expert evaluations, and contractual managerial appointment regulations in public health institutions\. To address uncertainty and ensure consistency in expert judgments, the Fuzzy Full Consistency Method was applied to determine the relative importance of the defined criteria\. The model integrates sector\-specific healthcare service requirements into a structured decision\-support system\. Results: The analysis revealed that equipment\-related criteria, which directly influence the quality, efficiency, and sustainability of healthcare service delivery, had the highest importance weight \(0\.460\)\. Personal criteria were assigned the lowest weight \(0\.360\)\. The findings indicate that institutional capacity and service\-related competencies are prioritized over individual characteristics in strengthening healthcare service governance\. Conclusion: By focusing on healthcare service quality and institutional performance, this study presents the first fuzzy MCDM\-based model specifically designed to support managerial appointments in public health institutions\. The proposed framework contributes to improving healthcare service effectiveness, promoting merit\-based governance, and enhancing accountability and transparency in public healthcare management systems\. Cite this article as: Karaca M\. A fuzzy multi\-criteria decision\-making approach for managerial appointments in public health institutions\. Arch Health Sci Res\. 2026, 13, 0062, doi: 10\.5152/ArcHealthSciRes\.2026\.26062\.

## [СТВОРЕННЯ ВІТРОЗАХИСНИХ МЕТАТЕКСТИЛЬНИХ СТРУКТУР МЕТОДАМИ АДИТИВНОГО ВИРОБНИЦТВА](../publications/d7e5ab75dd4525a7784d.md)

Viktoriia Mytsa; Мykola Riabchykov

The article examines the prospects of creating wind\-protective metatextile structures using additive manufacturing methods\. The feasibility of using spatial cellular structures consisting of repeated nodal elements and curved connecting links to control airflow is substantiated\. The influence of geometry, porosity, thickness of structural elements, number of layers, and their spatial orientation on the aerodynamic resistance of metatextile structures is analyzed\. Computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\) modeling in the SimScale software environment is proposed for studying airflow penetration, enabling the determination of velocity and pressure fields, pressure drop, local airflow characteristics, and flow reduction coefficients\. A numerical study of four variants of spatial structures was performed at an identical inlet air velocity of 5 m/s\. It was established that the structure with elastic curved connections provided the greatest reduction in airflow velocity, reaching 60%, while its pressure reduction coefficient was 0\.280\. The results demonstrate that parametric design and additive manufacturing provide opportunities for developing metatextile materials with differentiated wind\-protective properties\. The proposed approach can be applied to the development of lightweight, flexible, and functional clothing elements with a locally controlled level of protection against wind exposure\.

## [Toxicogenetic profiling of an antifungal lawsone silver salt: in silico and in vitro analysis in 2D and 3D mammalian models](../publications/d7e9c0619a6cbb5c30d3.md)

Bárbara Verena Dias Galvão; Letícia Mota Candal de Matos; Alana da Cunha Goldstein; Luana Pereira Borba\-Santos; Nathalia Pinheiro dos Santos; Caroline Deckmann Nicoletti; Wanderley de Souza; Vı́tor F\. Ferreira; Débora Omena Futuro; Sônia Rozental; Carlos Fernando Araújo\-Lima; Israel Felzenszwalb

Abstract The development of novel metal\-based antifungals requires rigorous characterization of their toxicological mechanisms to ensure patient safety\. This study investigated the toxicogenetic profile and cellular interactions of lawsone silver salt \(LSS\), a compound with established activity against Sporothrix spp\. and emerging multidrug\-resistant pathogens\. Antifungal efficacy was confirmed against planktonic Aspergillus fumigatus , Candida albicans , and C\. auris \(MIC 1\.45–23\.2 µM\), with significant anti\-biofilm activity against C\. albicans \(185\.9 µM\) and A\. fumigatus \(92\.9 µM\)\. In silico ADMET modeling predicted high oral bioavailability and blood–brain barrier permeability, despite the genotoxicity alerts\. Experimentally, LSS \(0\.005–50 µg/plate\) was non\-mutagenic in the Salmonella /microsome assay \(TA1535, TA97a, TA98, TA100, and TA102\), regardless of the metabolic activation\. However, LSS \(0\.5–500 µM\) induced significant genomic instability in HepG2 cells\. The micronucleus assay revealed a dose\-dependent increase in micronuclei, nucleoplasmic bridges, and nuclear buds, indicating clastogenic and aneugenic effects\. Comparative cytotoxicity was evaluated in BALB/3T3 fibroblasts using 2D monolayers and scaffold\-based 3D models \(0\.005–5000 µM\)\. In 2D cultures, LSS exhibited potent cytotoxicity \(CC 50 : 2\.7–19\.9 µM\)\. Crucially, the 3D microenvironment significantly attenuated these effects \(CC 50 : 1,797–1,919 µM\), suggesting a markedly higher safety margin in physiologically relevant tissue architectures\. These findings demonstrate that while LSS induces chromosomal damage in human cells, its toxicity is fundamentally modulated by cellular organization, providing essential data for risk assessment and therapeutic optimization of naphthoquinone derivatives\.

## [Biography And The Relevance Of Al\-Kindi&\#x27;s Thoughts In The Issues Of Islamic Education In The Disruption Era](../publications/d7ed9bb99289b471ac54.md)

Defi Dachlian Nurdiana; Yusup Rohmadi; Andi Arif Rifa’i; Siti Sakdiyah Sakdiyah

Contemporary Islamic education faces various challenges, including the dichotomy of knowledge, the tension between faith and science, religious exclusivism, and the crisis of rationality and critical thinking in the digital era\. This study aims to analyze the relevance of Al\-Kindi&\#x27;s thought in understanding and responding to these problems through a study of the work of F? al\-Falsafah al\-?l?\. This study uses a qualitative approach with literature study methods and content analysis techniques\. Primary data is in the form of Al\-Kindi&\#x27;s works translated by Adamson and Pormann, while secondary data is obtained from relevant academic literature\. Analysis is carried out through tracing arguments in primary texts, comparisons with secondary sources, and critical interpretations of their relevance to contemporary Islamic education\. The results of the study show that Al\-Kindi&\#x27;s thought can be reconstructed through four main aspects, namely the alignment of the goals of revelation and reason, openness to the truth without limiting its origins, the connectedness of knowledge culminating in the recognition of God, and criticism of the rejection of philosophy based on certain interests\. These four aspects provide a conceptual foundation for the development of Islamic education that is integrative, dialogical, open to the development of science, and oriented towards strengthening critical reason\. This study contributes to the development of a conceptual framework of Islamic education that connects classical philosophical thought with the challenges of contemporary education in a critical manner\.

## [Cultural role and innovative development of broadcasting and hosting in news communication](../publications/d7ffc35f2eb99b30123c.md)

Yongjian Wang; Runwei Pan; Peng Cao

Existing research often focuses on the expressive style or individual image of broadcasters and hosts, but lacks a systematic theoretical integration of the mechanisms of cultural communication\. In particular, it neglects the synergistic interaction between ability, expression, literacy, and role, as well as their psychological and contextual mechanisms\. To deeply analyze the internal mechanisms of the cultural function of broadcasters and hosts, this paper constructs an integrative theoretical framework of “hosts as cultural mediators,” integrating encoding/decoding theory, the stimulus\-organism\-response \(S\-O\-R\) model, and cross\-cultural communication theory to reveal their multiple mechanisms of action in cultural communication\. Based on a questionnaire survey and data from the news media industry, this paper employs partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) for empirical analysis\. The results showed that cultural communication ability significantly and positively influenced cultural identity \(β = 0\.583, p &lt; 0\.001\), and this effect was significantly enhanced on new media platforms \(β = 0\.174, p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Innovative expression significantly enhanced information acceptance through the mediation of emotional resonance \(indirect effect = 0\.326, 95% CI \(Confidence interval\) \[0\.241, 0\.418\]\)\. The positive effect of professionalism on social influence was moderated by age group \(β = 0\.137, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Role positioning significantly enhanced the effectiveness of external communication, and cultural distance positively moderated this path \(β = 0\.156, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. This study not only validated the emotional mediation and contextual moderation mechanisms but also provided differentiated strategic recommendations for broadcasting organizations, journalism education, and international communication practice, potentially promoting the transformation of broadcasters and hosts from “information transmitters” to “cultural translators”\.

## [Differential hydraulic and carbon economic strategies among four oak species](../publications/d807128d3f33cbd68957.md)

Qiang Li; Xinke Sun; Jiaqi Jiang; Zixuan Feng; Wenlong Sun; Yao Huang; Ning Du

Background The fluctuations of precipitation will become more erratic and dramatic, threatening the growth and survival of forest species\. Plants usually integrate water and carbon management strategies to deal with environmental variations\. The hydraulic strategies of woody plants would modify their carbon capture and allocation patterns, thus characterizing divergent strategies in water and carbon use economy could elucidate the differential responses to climate change among closely related species\. To decipher possible correlations between functional traits relating to plant hydraulics and carbon economics, we selected four oak species \(one native species, Quercus dentata , and three exotic species, Q \. rubra , Q \. robur , and Q \. palustris \) growing in an Oak Nursery to explore trait associations in hydraulic and carbon economics, and to contrast strategy variations among four species\. Results Our results showed a trade\-off between leaf gas exchange rate and water use efficiency, where fast gas exchange related to fluctuating water potential\. In carbon allocation patterns, higher Huber values could supply sufficient water in leaves, thereby maintaining water potential stable\. Conclusions Compared to the exotic oaks, Q \. dentata adopted a relatively conservative strategy, embodying high water use efficiency, stable water potential, and leaves with smaller but denser stomata\. However, Q \. rubra was conservative and rapid\-responsive, Q \. robur was potentially drought\-tolerant, and Q \. palustris employed a strategy of less drought\-resistant but might be more competitive in the face of abundant resources\. Integrating these findings into global conservation efforts will lead to the development of adaptive management practices that foster tree species with better adaptation to environmental variations\.

## [Interdisciplinary consensus of classification oncoorthopedic complications\.](../publications/d8073fd89b1ab8f4e1ba.md)

Е\. А\. Сушенцов; I\. M\. Mikailov; V\. V\. Teplyakov; Artem V\. Bukharov; Петриченко Анна Викторовна; Andrey N\. Nikolaenko; Тихилов Рашид Муртузалиевич

The article presents an interdisciplinary consensus of the Russian\-language version of the classification of oncoorthopedic complications developing in patients with musculoskeletal tumors who have undergone limb\-salvage surgery\. The classification developed by the International Society of Limb Salvage \(ISOLS\) committee in 2014, being the most widespread and frequently cited in the literature, was used as the basis\.

## [Transport Layer Security attack detection using hardware performance counters side\-channel](../publications/d807c801d43d5786aa66.md)

Tomasz Główka; Cheng\-Feng Hung; Wojciech Mazurczyk; Cheng Shin\-Ming

Cryptographic protocols form the backbone of secure communication in various environments, including the Internet of Things \(IoT\) and non\-IoT settings\. One of the most popular and widely used cryptographic protocols is Transport Layer Security \(TLS\)\. However, TLS implementations remain vulnerable to implementation flaws, such as the Heartbleed bug, which affected a significant proportion of deployed TLS 1\.2 servers\. Many detection approaches rely on network traffic inspection, which is ineffective in encrypted environments\. In this paper, we present a non\-intrusive detection framework that collects hardware performance counter \(HPC\) side\-channel data from a TLS server process without modifying the application or requiring access to network packets\. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has combined HPC data with a deep neural network \(DNN\) in a zero\-modification testbed for TLS attack detection\. The training dataset was collected in a simplified single\-machine setup, while evaluation was conducted on physically separated machines to simulate real\-world deployment\. Recall ranges from 0\.590 to 0\.753, and Specificity from 0\.698 to 0\.850 across six evaluation configurations, confirming the feasibility of detection while identifying generalization as the key challenge for future work\. To validate the choice of DNN architecture, it was additionally compared against classical machine learning baselines such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), achieving the highest combined Recall and Specificity in all six configurations\.

## [GESTÃO DE RESÍDUOS SÓLIDOS, ECONOMIA CIRCULAR E SEGURANÇA DO TRABALHO NA ENGENHARIA: INOVAÇÕES TECNOLÓGICAS E ESTRATÉGIAS PARA A SUSTENTABILIDADE E PREVENÇÃO DE ACIDENTES](../publications/d80bc021e550ca09818d.md)

Jhonatan Filippe Alves Macedo Pereira; Melquizedec Arcos Rodrigues; Anna Luíza Oliveira Lordello Constantinides; Fernanda Hananda de Oliveira Lordello; Luiz Henrique Silva Dos Reis

A geração crescente de resíduos sólidos e a persistência de acidentes e doenças entre os trabalhadores que os manejam compõem um problema que a engenharia costuma tratar em compartimentos separados\. Este artigo analisa como a gestão de resíduos, a economia circular e a segurança do trabalho podem ser integradas, e que papel cabe às inovações tecnológicas nessa integração\. Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa de literatura, de abordagem qualitativa, apoiada em quinze fontes entre artigos científicos, relatórios técnicos e documentos normativos publicados entre 2010 e 2025\. A discussão se organiza em torno da hierarquia de gestão de resíduos prevista na legislação brasileira, associada a inovações como sensoriamento, inteligência artificial, visão computacional e dispositivos vestíveis, e aos riscos ocupacionais de cada etapa\. Os resultados indicam que a circularidade desloca e multiplica os riscos, ao criar novas atividades de triagem, desmontagem e reprocessamento, e que a tecnologia só reduz acidentes quando está ancorada em um sistema de gestão de riscos, na participação dos trabalhadores e em políticas públicas coerentes\. Conclui\-se que segurança deve ser tratada como critério de projeto da economia circular, e não como etapa posterior\.

## [University EFL Learners’ Perceptions on the Use of ChatGPT in Academic Writing Learning Process](../publications/d81a713ec9cd33cf6d9c.md)

Kristian Florensio Wijaya; Entika Prastikawati

With the burgeoning development of sophisticated artificial intelligence tools, it is of foremost importance for second language educators to integrate these digital learning platforms into their regular classroom settings, as they will help them deliver clearer pedagogical instructions and design more effective learning materials\. Concerning the aforesaid background, the researchers undertook this moderate library study to investigate university EFL learners’ perceptions of the use of ChatGPT in the academic writing learning process\. In compliance with this major study objective, the researchers employed a thematic analysis approach while reviewing pertinent findings derived from 30 previously published ChatGPT journal articles\. With the help of a thematic analysis approach, the researchers could generate more believable, trustworthy, and relatable findings, as it supported us in subsuming the targeted results into relevant themes\. The thematically\-categorized research results revealed that ChatGPT allowed the enhancement of writing accuracy, proficiency, strategic competence, motivation, confidence, and positive writing dispositions among global university EFL learners\.

## [One ATR Kinase Inhibitor Mechanism, Three Gateways: What a Biomarker\-Selected Oncology Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/d8229220c32b5f18cb51.md)

Junyi Wu; Atchaya Ravichandran; Daxaben Jigneshkumar Patel; Nilukshan Sugumar; Peivand Pirouzi

Ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3\-related protein \(ATR\) kinase inhibitors are investigational small molecules that target a central regulator of the cellular DNA damage response, exploiting the observation that tumours carrying certain loss\-of\-function alterations in DNA damage response pathways may be more vulnerable to ATR inhibition than tumours without these alterations\. This article uses a hypothetical multicentre Phase 1/2 clinical trial of an ATR kinase inhibitor candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014, using a biomarker\-selected advanced solid tumour population as the illustrative scenario\. The comparison traces how the Common Technical Document&\#x27;s harmonized Modules 2 through 5 carry the shared scientific case across all three regions while the biomarker selection strategy itself, the companion diagnostic or laboratory\-developed test used to identify eligible patients, introduces specific administrative and scientific considerations in each region&\#x27;s review\. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to a biomarker\-driven oncology program conducted across these three jurisdictions, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing DNA damage response\-targeted oncology candidates across Canada, the United States, and the European Union\.Keywords: ATR kinase inhibitor; DNA damage response; biomarker\-selected oncology trial; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Integrating Sustainability Strategy, Governance, and Outcomes: Reviewing Two‐Decades of ESG Research Through Bibliometric and Content Analysis](../publications/d82de6a899d6416220f5.md)

Badingatus Solikhah

ABSTRACT This study provides an in‐depth literature review on ESG topics\. It combines bibliometric mapping of 447 publications from Scopus and WoS, along with qualitative content analysis of 249 papers\. The review examines how ESG has evolved from a disclosure‐based measure into a comprehensive framework that integrates sustainable strategy, governance, and finance\. The analysis identifies five main research clusters: ESG disclosure and transparency, performance measurement, ratings and evaluation, sustainable finance, and reporting frameworks\. The content analysis outlines dominant theories, methods, and variable relationships, showing that ESG can act both as a driver and an outcome in empirical models\. It also highlights underexplored areas such as ESG assurance, greenwashing, stakeholder influence, and contextual diversity\. Future studies should strengthen conceptual and empirical connections across ESG themes, explore governance in cross‐country contexts, and evaluate the effects of mandatory disclosure regimes\. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and sustainability analytics also offer new opportunities to enhance the credibility and comparability of ESG information\.

## [Pengaruh Citra dan Kualitas Layanan Terhadap Keputusan Jamaah Menggunakan Tabungan Haji BSI Studi Kasus Pada Kerjasama Kbihu Syamsul Huda Al\-Amaliyah Ciawi Dengan BSI KC Ciawi](../publications/d835eb5e29d28aaa3223.md)

Octaviana Deliaputri; Maya Apriyana; Muhammad Amin

Jumlah jamaah Kelompok Bimbingan Ibadah Haji dan Umrah Syamsul Huda Al\-Amaliyah berubah\-ubah selama 2024 hingga 2026, padahal masa tunggu haji di Kabupaten Bogor sangat panjang\. Kondisi ini memunculkan dugaan bahwa persepsi jamaah memengaruhi keputusan mereka memakai Tabungan Haji Bank Syariah Indonesia melalui kerja sama dengan Kantor Cabang Ciawi\. Studi ini ingin mengetahui apakah citra dan kualitas layanan memengaruhi keputusan jamaah, masing\-masing maupun bersama\-sama\. Rancangan yang dipakai ialah kuantitatif asosiatif dengan data primer hasil kuesioner skala Likert yang dilengkapi wawancara dan dokumentasi\. Populasi berjumlah 202 jamaah pengguna tabungan haji, sedangkan sampel sebanyak 67 responden ditetapkan menggunakan rumus Slovin dan teknik purposive sampling\. Karena variabel keputusan bersifat dikotomis, data dianalisis dengan regresi logistik biner setelah instrumen dinyatakan valid dan reliabel\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial hanya kualitas layanan yang berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan jamaah \(B = 0,229; p = 0,001; Exp\(B\) = 1,257\), sedangkan citra tidak berpengaruh signifikan \(B = 0,164; p = 0,057\)\. Secara simultan, citra dan kualitas layanan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan jamaah \(χ² = 27,108; p &lt; 0,001; Nagelkerke R² = 0,444\)\. Simpulannya, pengalaman layanan yang nyata lebih menentukan keputusan jamaah daripada citra lembaga, sehingga pengelola perlu memprioritaskan daya tanggap dan jaminan layanan sambil tetap menjaga citra\.

## [Post\-hoc analyses of amyloid reduction after one year of treatment with donanemab using clinical trial data: prediction of amyloid clearance and association with downstream measurements](../publications/d85232cb62fe9d1a55dc.md)

Sergey Shcherbinin; Ming Lu; Jian Wang; Chakib Battioui; Scott W\. Andersen; Hong Wang; Emel Serap Nery; Cynthia Duggan Evans; Paula M\. Hauck; Ivelina Gueorguieva; Leonardo Iaccarino; Ian Andrew Kennedy; Dawn A\. Brooks; Mark A\. Mintun; Emily C\. Collins; John Randall Sims

Abstract Background Donanemab is an antibody designed to specifically target modified amyloid that is present only in plaques\. An objective of this post hoc study was to identify baseline characteristics associated with 52\-week amyloid clearance \(AC\) with donanemab treatment and to assess the association of AC with downstream biomarkers and clinical efficacy\. Methods Data was utilized from TRAILBLAZER\-ALZ 2 \(placebo: N = 876; donanemab: N = 860\), a Phase 3, double\-blind, placebo\-controlled study, and open\-label addendum \( N = 1053\) in participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\)\. Donanemab\-treated participants were split into two subgroups based on their 52\-week amyloid level: AC W52 \[&lt; 24\.1 Centiloids \(CL\)\] and NAC W52 \(≥ 24\.1 CL\)\. Machine learning and multiple linear regression analyses were utilized to assess baseline characteristics differentiating these subgroups\. Placebo\-treated participants were matched to AC W52 and NAC W52 participants by propensity score and compared using analysis of covariance or mixed models for repeated measures\. Results On average, substantial 52\-week amyloid reduction was observed in donanemab\-treated participants in both the AC W52 \( N = 443\) and NAC W52 \( N = 227\) subgroups\. Baseline amyloid \[mean \(SD\): 95\.8 \(32\.4\) and 120\.2 \(34\.0\), respectively\], was significantly correlated with 52\-week amyloid levels \[mean \(SD\): 4\.8 CL \(12\.5\) and 48\.2 \(22\.5\) CL, respectively \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\] and was inversely associated with probability of reaching 52\-week AC \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Of the baseline characteristics assessed, lower amyloid was the most important parameter differentiating AC W52 and NAC W52 subgroups, followed by older age, fewer APOE ε4 alleles, and lower body weight\. These findings were replicated using open\-label addendum data\. The AC W52 subgroup, but not the NAC W52 subgroup, had significantly less 76\-week tau accumulation than matched placebo \(mPBO\) \( p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Although both subgroups showed significant plasma P\-tau217 differences from the corresponding mPBO, the change from baseline was greater in the AC W52 subgroup\. At 76 weeks, slowing of clinical progression for the AC W52 and NAC W52 subgroups versus mPBO, as measured by Clinical Dementia Rating Scale–Sum of Boxes, was 29\.6% and 28\.8%, respectively, and slowing by the integrated AD Rating Scale was 25\.9% and 18\.8%, respectively\. Conclusions Donanemab\-mediated 52\-week amyloid clearance was associated with slower tau progression\. Slowing of clinical progression was observed in both AC W52 and NAC W52 subgroups\. Trial registration ClinicalTrials\.gov Identifier: NCT04437511, June 2020\.

## [Liquid\-liquid phase separation in cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy: emerging roles and translational opportunities](../publications/d856d5d2d46168f0d2b3.md)

Chenchen Dong; Cong Shang; Bing Han; Ziyi Liu; Jiaoyang Wang; Peng Cao; Juan Zeng; Ayao Guo; Xiufang Ren; Shuo Cao

Abstract Liquid\-liquid phase separation \(LLPS\) is a physicochemical process through which biomolecules assemble into membraneless condensates via weak, multivalent interactions\. LLPS has emerged as a central biological principle that helps explain intracellular spatiotemporal compartmentalization, signal transduction, and stress responses\. Dysregulated LLPS contributes to tumor initiation, progression, immune evasion, and treatment resistance; however, its cell\-type\-specific functions and relevance to radiotherapy and immunotherapy remain incompletely integrated\. In this review, we critically synthesize recent mechanistic and translational advances linking LLPS to cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy\. Condensates may either support therapeutic resistance and immune evasion or enhance radiosensitivity and antitumor immunity, depending on their molecular composition, subcellular localization, cell type, and treatment context\. We examine how condensate regulation connects radiation\-induced DNA damage repair with innate immune activation and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies that target disease\-associated condensates\. We also assess LLPS\-associated abnormal condensates as candidate biomarkers for prognosis and prediction of tumor response to radiotherapy and immunotherapy\. Tissue\-specific LLPS regulation across tumor types, dynamic condensate remodeling under therapeutic stress, and rational strategies combining phase\-separation modulation with immune\-checkpoint inhibitors and radiotherapy require further investigation\. Integrating multi\-omics data with artificial intelligence\-based algorithms may help construct systematic LLPS\-related therapeutic\-event maps and predictive models, thereby prioritizing experimentally testable hypotheses for personalized cancer management\. With rigorous mechanistic validation and prospective clinical evaluation, selective modulation of disease\-associated condensates may enhance radiosensitivity and strengthen antitumor immunity\.

## [Evaluation of Soil Microbial Biomass Carbon, Nitrogen, and Enzymatic Activity in Degraded Soils Amended With Organic and Inorganic Fertilizers](../publications/d86080c2f6d304b4104c.md)



Soil microbial biomass represents the living engine of the soil nutrient cycling system, and its restoration in degraded agricultural soils is a prerequisite for sustainable productivity in Pakistan&\#x27;s intensively managed irrigated plains\.The present greenhouse Completely Randomised Design \(CRD\) study, evaluated five amendment treatments \-unamended control, NPK chemical fertilizer, farmyard manure \(FYM, 10 t ha⁻¹\), biochar \(2% w/w\), and FYM\+biochar combination \-for their effects on twelve soil biological, chemical, and crop performance parameters in a severely degraded sandy loam soil \(initial MBC 84\.4 mg kg⁻¹, SOM 0\.42%, pH 8\.02\)\.Parameters assessed included microbial biomass carbon \(MBC\), microbial biomass nitrogen \(MBN\), basal soil respiration, metabolic quotient \(qCO₂\), MBC:MBN ratio, soil organic matter \(SOM\), available nitrogen \(N\), available phosphorus \(P\), dehydrogenase activity, urease activity, soil pH, and wheat crop yield\.The FYM\+biochar combination produced the highest values for all biological and yield parameters: MBC 212\.4 mg kg⁻¹ \(\+151\.6%over control\), MBN 28\.6 mg kg⁻¹ \(\+130\.6%\),basal respiration 22\.4 mg CO₂ 100 g⁻¹ d⁻¹ \(\+166\.7%\),dehydrogenase activity 38\.4 µg TPF g⁻¹ 24h⁻¹ \(\+209\.7%\),urease activity 62\.4 µg NH₄⁺\-N g⁻¹ h⁻¹ \(\+153\.7%\),and crop yield 5\.24 g pot⁻¹ \(\+84\.5% over unamended control\)\.Principal component analysis \(PCA\) explained 77\.2% of total variance across PC1 \(52\.4%\) and PC2 \(24\.8%\), with the FYM\+biochar treatment positioned at the extreme positive end of PC1 along with all biological health variables\.The metabolic quotient \(qCO₂\) was lowest under FYM\+biochar \(0\.106\), indicating the most efficient microbial community metabolism and the least stressed microbial biomass\.These results confirm that FYM combined with biochar is the superior amendment strategy for restoring soil microbial fertility, enzymatic activity, and crop productivity in degraded irrigated soils of Punjab, Pakistan, and provide a mechanistic understanding of the complementary contributions of labile organic substrate \(FYM\) and structured microhabitat \(biochar\) to soil biological recovery\.

## [INCREMENTAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE GOVERNANCE IN A SMALL TECHNOLOGY\-BASED COMPANY: A FRAMEWORK BASED ON CAPABILITIES AND DEPENDENCY RELATIONSHIPS](../publications/d8705455ac4cc3cec3bf.md)

Juliana Masson Prediger; Divino Bruno da Cunha; Maria Adriana Leite; Rayllon Rodrigues Rodrigues Sousa Reis

The adoption of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) systems by small businesses increases the need for mechanisms capable of controlling risks, defining responsibilities, ensuring traceability, and supporting human oversight\. This study develops an incremental AI governance framework based on capabilities and dependency relationships through Design Science Research and a single case study conducted in a small Brazilian technology\-based company that employs generative AI and multimodal processing for veterinary decision support\. The investigation combined scientific literature, governance frameworks, source\-code inspection, automated testing, architectural documentation, operational workflows, and decision records\. A total of 31 governance mechanisms were identified and consolidated, classified as implemented, partial, or planned\. Partial mechanisms were characterized according to gaps in coverage, integration, traceability, validation, and institutionalization, while relationships among capabilities were examined through a dependency matrix\. The results revealed greater consolidation of mechanisms associated with day\-to\-day operations, such as identity, authorization, consent, prompt versioning, review, and curation, while gaps remain in end\-to\-end traceability, systematic validation, independent dual review, versioned datasets, and governed evolution\. The resulting framework organizes capabilities into five levels and four cross\-cutting elements, without assuming a rigid maturity path, providing a structure for the analysis and gradual evolution of AI governance in small organizations\.

## [Lived Experiences of Senior High School English Teachers in Teaching Writing in the Advent of Generative AI Applications in Senior High Schools in San Mateo, Rizal](../publications/d8782ca333872d2ad9c8.md)

May Villanueva

The study uncovered the dilemma of English Senior High School Teachers in teaching writing with the prevalence of using Generative AI\. The study employed qualitative phenomenological research design to unravel the lived\-experiences of the English teachers in Senior High Schools in San Mateo, Rizal\. There were 8 participants who were interviewed through an in\-depth interview to convey their personal perspectives on teaching writing in the advent of Generative AI\. The emerging themes from the study are as follows: \(1\) Recognizing AI\-Influenced through Familiarity and Inconsistency; \(2\) Navigating Uncertainty in Establishing Authenticity; \(3\) AI\-Assistance and the Preservation of Student Writing; \(4\) Reconfiguring Writing Pedagogy and Assessment to Preserve Student Thinking; \(5\) Developing Teacher Preparedness through Experiences, Self\-Learning and Professional Development; and \(6\) Reconstructing Academic Integrity through Ownership, Boundaries, and Transparency\. The study revealed that the roles of the English teachers in teaching writing is diversified with the changing landscape of education and the integration of technology in teaching\. English Senior High School Teachers reconciled the use of AI in teaching writing and look at AI tools that support learning\. The participants in this study understood that the goal of technological advancements in schools in sustaining learning and successful integration of AI tools necessitates simultaneous advancement of technical skills, pedagogical flexibility, and the reconciliation of ethical judgement, while maintaining authenticity and academic integrity\. The implications of this study support a context\-driven and moderated use of AI in Senior High School Writing\. Specific type of Generative AI used for writing, AI assisted writing, assessments using AI and integrity in AI\-generated writing may be pursued in subsequent researches\.

## [Advancing precision oncology: a critical review of in Silico tools for nanoparticle\-based drug delivery systems](../publications/d8806e895bc10179d5b7.md)

Ipshita Das; Maryam Abdul Ajees; Pawas Kumar; Yashaswini Reddy; Kampa Sundara Babitha

The advent of in silico approaches has added a new dimension to the design of nanoformulations for targeted drug delivery, particularly in cancer therapy\. Such computer simulation\-based methodologies offer an economic and efficient means for the targeted design and optimisation of drug delivery systems\. With the growing interest in computational nanoformulations, owing to their potential to increase the delivery, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy of anticancer drugs, scaffolding tools in silico have become essential for their rational design\. Through the simulation of molecular interactions, in silico models provide essential information on the dynamics of nanoparticles in biological systems, allowing the prediction and optimisation of their target efficiency and therapeutic efficacy\. These computation\-based methodologies are also essential for the design of personalised medicine, as they can reduce the systemic toxicity and side effects of conventional cancer therapies\. The integration of in silico methodologies into drug nanoformulation research is a significant step toward more efficient, patient\-specific therapy\. Despite their significant potential, several challenges, including limited model validation, biological complexity, protein corona formation, specific ADMET prediction tools, and regulatory uncertainty, hinder clinical translation\. This review illustrates the potential of in silico research in the advancement of cancer treatment development using nanoformulations\. This paper presents a critical review of existing computational tools, such as molecular dynamics simulations, molecular docking, machine learning, and AI\-based platforms, applied in the design, screening, and optimisation of nanomedicines\. It also illustrates the application of key computational tools and platforms, such as GROMACS, AutoDock, Schrodinger, and Gaussian, and web\-based platforms, such as SwissADME and pkCSM\. Together, these tools facilitate the design of efficient and targeted drug delivery systems, allowing for their eventual clinical translation\. In silico tools revolutionize the rational design of cancer\-targeted nanoformulations\. Molecular docking unveils precise ligand–nanoparticle–receptor binding mechanisms\. MD simulations decode NP behavior under physiological and tumor conditions\. AI\-driven modeling accelerates prediction of NP efficacy and biocompatibility\. Integrated ADMET tools streamline early screening of nanoformulated anticancer drugs\.

## [Clinician Use of an Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Clinical Information Platform](../publications/d8811d0eebd71bb02e00.md)

Vishal R\. Patel; Samuel G\. Finlayson; Michael Liu\-Hass; Mondira Ray; Jesse Burk‐Rafel; Travis Ian Zack; Anupam Bapu Jena

Importance: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited\. Objective: To characterize clinician use of an AI\-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries\. Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross\-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier\-verified accounts of a commonly used AI\-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026\. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38\.8 million queries\. Main Outcomes and Measures: The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined\. Results: Overall, 952 008 clinicians \(58\.5% female\), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2\.5\-year study period\. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18\.0 to 39\.5\. Nurse practitioners \(44\.5\) and physician assistants \(44\.5\) submitted more queries per active user\-month than physicians \(37\.1\)\. A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation \(use ratio, 2\.54\) and residents and fellows \(1\.84\)\. Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology \(use ratio, 2\.00\), internal medicine \(1\.88\), and family medicine \(1\.80\), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties \(ophthalmology, 0\.23; radiology, 0\.24; orthopedics, 0\.24\)\. Most queries addressed clinical decision\-making \(51\.9%\), particularly treatment and management \(33\.1%\), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13\.9% of queries\. Queries addressing topics outside physicians&\#x27; own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians\. Conclusions and Relevance: Over 2\.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI\-enabled clinical information platform\. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks\.

## [Interventions to prevent, treat, and minimize long\-term visual impairment from optic neuropathy in people living with demyelinating diseases](../publications/d8855c032b2891ebd112.md)

Nicholas Sathi; Scott N\. Grossman

Optic neuritis, inflammation of the optic nerve, leading to optic neuropathy, damage to the optic nerve, is a common feature of demyelinating disease\. As many as 25% of individuals with multiple sclerosis \(MS\) first presenting in this manner\. A longstanding goal of teams caring for patients with demyelinating disease has been to protect vision by avoiding the development of optic neuropathy and restoring visual deficits when episodes do occur\. So called “neuroprotective” agents remain a holy grail in the field\. Neuroprotection refers to efforts to preserve and recover cellular structure and function of the nervous system\. This includes the concept of remyelination\. Various approaches have been attempted over the years though as of this writing little progress has been made\. We reviewed the literature on this subject using PubMed and Google Scholar, incorporating articles published from 1981–2026\. This review highlights the landscape of interventions to treat and minimize long\-term visual impairment from optic neuropathy in demyelinating diseases, considers relapse prevention to a lesser extent, and projects forward to the future in which neuroprotection becomes a reality\.

## [Unsilencing Through AI\-Generated Images: Contrasting Participants’ and Researchers’ Images as Tools for Visualizing Tacit Experiences](../publications/d892cd1d5361a19ba7cc.md)

Sasha Valgardsson; Luciara Nardon

We explore the role of image generation through artificial intelligence \(AI\) in enhancing participants’ involvement in reflective interviewing, contributing to a more nuanced understanding of AI’s different roles in supporting reflection through images\. We gave multicultural participants – second\-generation immigrants or those who grew up in multicultural households – the option to generate their own images or assemble a collage from pre\-prepared images to visually represent their experiences of growing up with plural and partial cultural influences\. We found that researchers’ pre\-prepared images limited the introduction of biases embedded in AI training data and reduced technological disruptions while allowing for multiple avenues of interpretation and improved accessibility\. However, researchers’ images have the potential to silence participants’ unique experiences by limiting the availability of visual material\. We discuss the potential and challenges of AI in extending the involvement of marginalized and silenced groups in qualitative research through artistic expression\.

## [Assessment of land\-use and land\-cover changes impacts on land surface temperature using remote sensing and GIS: a case study of Kohat District, Pakistan \(2015–2025\)](../publications/d89d81841661125c73f5.md)

Waheed Ali Khoso; Rukhshanda Rehman; Muhammad Junaid; Aqib Khattak; Abdul Basit; Muhammad Lutfur Rehman; Mussa Umali

ABSTRACT Graphical abstract showing LULC changes and their impacts on LST in Kohat District, Pakistan \(2015–2025\), including increased built\-up and barren areas, decreased vegetation and water bodies, and associated spatial\-temporal LST variations\. Kohat District, located in the semi\-arid region of Pakistan, has experienced rapid urbanization and environmental change driven by climate variability and land\-use transformation\. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of land\-use/land cover \(LULC\) and their relationship with land surface temperature \(LST\) from 2015 to 2025 using remote sensing and geographic information system techniques\. Multitemporal Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 images were classified into five LULC classes using the maximum likelihood classification method\. Results showed substantial land\-cover changes, with barren land increasing from 1,171\.90 to 1,573\.76 km2 and built\-up areas expanding from 110\.60 to 290\.53 km2\. In contrast, forest cover declined from 717\.59 to 314\.53 km2, agricultural land decreased from 945\.65 to 771\.79 km2, and water bodies slightly reduced from 31\.30 to 26\.42 km2\. Correspondingly, maximum LST increased from 38\.66 °C in 2015 to 45\.38 °C in 2025\. Vegetation and water bodies consistently exhibited lower surface temperatures, highlighting their cooling effect\. The strong positive relationship between urban expansion, barren land growth, and increasing LST demonstrates that land\-cover change is a major driver of local warming\. These findings emphasize the need for sustainable urban planning, afforestation, and effective natural resource management to enhance climate resilience in Kohat District\.

## [Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity and Digital Learning Resilience in Higher Education: An Integrative Review and Capacity\-Sensitive Framework for Resource\-Constrained Universities](../publications/d8a8534318911e5973f1.md)

Nsangaette Asuquo Udo; Khama Valentine Arinze; Irene Chinyere Ezugwu; Adesegun Nurudeen Osijirin

Purpose: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is now embedded in teaching, assessment and administration in higher education, simultaneously widening educational opportunity and institutional cyber exposure\. This review examines how AI\-related and conventional cyber threats affect the continuity of digital learning, how AI can both amplify and mitigate those threats, and which integrated responses are feasible for resource\-constrained universities, with Nigeria as the illustrative context\. Design/Methodology/Approach: A narrative integrative review following established integrative\-review guidance synthesised 60 sources published mainly between 2019 and 2026, comprising peer\-reviewed studies, technical standards, policy and legal instruments, and institutional or industry reports\. Sources were organised by threat mechanism, institutional vulnerability, educational consequence, response and implementation constraint, and each was classified by the type of inference it can support\. Findings: Seven overlapping threat clusters were identified: AI\-enhanced social engineering and identity abuse; ransomware and extortion; privacy leakage and surveillance; platform and supply\-chain compromise; manipulation of AI\-enabled learning systems; synthetic media and assessment\-integrity attacks; and human, governance and infrastructure weaknesses\. Experimental evidence shows that large language models lower the cost of persuasive phishing, while AI\-text detectors and automated proctoring raise reliability and fairness concerns\. AI\-assisted defence offers measurable triage benefits but introduces false alarms, concept drift, privacy exposure and automation bias\. Originality/Value: The proposed AI\-Cybersecurity\-Digital Learning Resilience \(AIC\-DLR\) Framework adapts NIST CSF 2\.0 functions to the educational mission, overlays NIST AI risk\-management guidance, and treats usable, equitable recovery of teaching and assessment, rather than system restoration alone, as the protected outcome\. A tiered roadmap and a set of operationally defined indicators translate the framework into testable practice\. Practical Implications: Priorities for low\-capacity institutions are accountable ownership, phishing\-resistant identity for privileged users, tested and isolated backups, proportionate data practices, governed AI use and pre\-authorised alternative learning channels\. The framework is conceptual and unvalidated; comparative implementation studies are required to establish its effect on recovery time and equitable access\.

## [QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization](../publications/d8a91d14163a65f2f3db.md)

Taisei Takabayashi; Masayuki Ohzeki

Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization \(QUBO\) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables\. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low\-energy states harder to sample\. We develop a Lagrange\-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed\-binary quadratic programs \(MBQPs\) without discretizing continuous variables\. The method is based on a finite\-temperature free\-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector\. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables\. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p \-median problem\. Compared with a penalty\-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably\. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances\. In the time\-to\-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target\-reached rates for stringent fixed\-accuracy targets\. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed\-integer optimization solver\.

## [Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies: Reconstructing Cognitive Justice in Minangkabau Legal Historiography](../publications/d8b779020d60e7120153.md)

Mhd\. Ilham Armi; Ahmad Luthfy Nasri; Syukra Latif; Ayu Ariska; Fitri Rahmawati

Colonial legal historiography in Minangkabau has long portrayed matrilineal adat and Islamic law as antagonistic systems, casting adat as static custom and Islam as an external imposition\. This article repositions the formula Syarak Mangato, Adaik Mamakai \(SMAM\), rendered here as “Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies,” as an analytical method for dismantling this binary, rather than treating the formula merely as a cultural description, as much of the existing scholarship has done\. The analysis proceeds in three stages: a genealogical critique of eight colonial legal sources; an analysis of allochronism, examining how twelve Indonesianist studies softened but did not fully dismantle the colonial dualism; and a contemporary socio\-legal analysis of twelve cases spanning household and kinship relations, economic and asset relations, and public governance\. The findings show that SMAM operates as a working legal practice within nagari\-based authorities, which negotiate inheritance disputes through asset categorisation, mobilise ancestral property \(pusako\) as productive economic capital, and assert local social control in the face of institutional hegemony\. The article argues that the integration of adat and Islamic legal norms is better understood as cognitive justice, grounded in the recognition of two epistemologies operating alongside one another, rather than as a compromise between competing systems\. Rather than proposing SMAM as a generalisable model, the article advances it as an empirically grounded comparative approach to examining pluralistic legal orders in postcolonial Southeast Asia\.

## [Remote audit as a moderator of the relationship between auditor digital competence, IT support, and audit quality](../publications/d8bd2a65d7da0948bc9a.md)

Oyong Lisa; Riza Bahtiar Sulistyan; Imanita Septian Rusdianti; Umi Muawanah; Djuni Farhan

Type of the article: Research Article The rapid shift toward remote auditing since the COVID\-19 pandemic has made auditor digital competence and organizational information technology \(IT\) support decisive factors for sustaining audit quality, yet empirical evidence on how remote audit conditions shape these relationships remains limited\. This study aims to examine the effects of auditor digital competence and IT support on audit quality and to test whether remote audit moderates these two relationships\. A quantitative explanatory approach was used, applying Partial Least Squares – Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) with SmartPLS on data from 160 external auditors working at Big Four\-affiliated public accounting firms operating in Malang City, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling\. The results show that auditor digital competence \(β = 0\.267; t = 3\.374; p = 0\.001\) and IT support \(β = 0\.889; t = 3\.134; p = 0\.002\) both have a positive and significant effect on audit quality \(R2 = 0\.414\)\. Remote audit significantly strengthens the effect of auditor digital competence on audit quality \(β = 0\.148; t = 2\.020; p = 0\.045\), but does not significantly moderate the effect of IT support on audit quality \(β = 0\.061; t = 0\.925; p = 0\.357\)\. These findings indicate that auditor digital competence becomes increasingly critical for audit quality as audits move to remote settings, while the contribution of IT support remains consistently strong regardless of audit mode, offering practical implications for digital audit training and IT infrastructure policy in public accounting firms\.Acknowledgments The authors gratefully acknowledge the support of facilities and infrastructure from the LPPM Universitas Gajayana during the research process\. We also extend our appreciation to the Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Gajayana, for the institutional support and facilities that facilitated the completion of this research\.

## [A STUDY TO ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF YOGA THERAPY WITH STRESS MANAGEMENT TECHNIQUES ON MIGRAINE FREQUENCY AMONG YOUNG ADULTS](../publications/d8cf82b4506894322928.md)



Migraine is one of the most common neurological disorders affecting young adults worldwide and is associated with significant physical, psychological, social, and economic burdens\.Stress has been identified as one of the primary triggers of migraine attacks, making stress reduction interventions increasingly important in migraine management\.Yoga therapy, combined with structured stress management techniques, has emerged as a promising nonpharmacological approach for reducing migraine frequency and improving overall well\-being\.The present study aimed to assess the effectiveness of yoga therapy with stress management techniques on migraine frequency among young adults\.A quasi\-experimental pretest\-posttest design was adopted among young adults diagnosed with migraine\.Participants underwent a structured yoga therapy program integrated with stress management interventions for twelve weeks\.Outcome measures included migraine frequency, pain intensity, perceived stress levels, and quality of life indicators\.The findings demonstrated significant reductions in migraine frequency and perceived stress levels following the intervention\.Participants also reported improvements in emotional well\-being, sleep quality, concentration, and daily functioning\.The study highlights the potential of integrating yoga\-based interventions into routine migraine management programs and supports the use of complementary therapies as effective public health strategies for addressing stress\-related neurological disorders\.

## [How Many, but How Sure? Class Competition as a Confidence Proxy in Multi\-Class Density\-Based Counting](../publications/d8e4a05b0791a9655dfa.md)

Villanelle O&\#x27;Reilly; Georgios Leontidis; Marc Hanheide

Multi\-class density estimators can count objects in crowded scenes, but their class\-wise outputs offer no indication of how reliably density mass has been allocated\. We introduce a training\-free confidence proxy based on local competition between the strongest class channels\. The resulting prominence measure requires only the predicted density maps, with no retraining or access to model internals\. We test whether residual competition is diagnostic of cross\-class leakage by attenuating contested density at inference time\. On DSACA predictions for the Hicks et al\. dataset, this reduces overall MAE from 0\.920 to 0\.846, suggesting that class competition contains useful information about count reliability\.

## [Onyeukaziri, Justin Nnaemeka: Artificial Intelligence and the Notions of the “Natural” and the “Artificial\.”](../publications/d8e6f4149b20fe932b99.md)



\_Journal of Data Analysis\_ 17 \(No\. 4\):101\-116\. 2022This paper argues that to negate the ontological difference between the natural and the artificial, is not plausible; nor is the reduction of the natural to the artificial or vice versa possible\. Except if one intends to empty the semantic content of the terms and notions: “natural” and “artificial\.” Most philosophical discussions on Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) have always been in relation to the human person, especially as it relates to human intelligence, consciousness and/or mind in general\. This paper, intends to broaden the conversation, by discussing AI in relation to the notions of “nature” and the “artificial\.” This intention is to more critically understand the artificiality in and of artificial intelligence\. To achieve this, the notion of “nature” in Aristotle’s Philosophy of Nature, has been employed as an epistemological tool in interrogating the notion of the artificial and the objectives of the science and technology of Artificial Intelligence\. \(direct link \)

## [Behavioral Feedback Loops and Kinesiophobia in Hidradenitis Suppurativa: A Conceptual Framework](../publications/d8ef5a25dce6e9515c67.md)

Jaap\-Jan Roukens

Introduction: Hidradenitis suppurativa \(HS\) is a severe inflammatory dermatosis characterized by debilitating localized pain\. Current HS feedback models focus on microscopic molecular networks and bacterial dysbiosis\. Objectives: This narrative review integrates the individually well\-documented psychosocial and behavioral burdens of the disease into a single positive feedback model\. Methods: A macroscopic behavioral framework was conceptualized by reviewing cross\-disciplinary literature regarding HS\. Results: This conceptual framework operates across three domains: i\) a biomechanical\-metabolic loop, where sustained immobility may accelerate the accumulation of visceral adiposity and insulin resistance; ii\) a psychosocial loop, where symptom\-induced psychiatric comorbidities may contribute to neuroendocrine dysregulation and compensatory coping behaviors; iii\) a socioeconomic loop, where economic instability can decrease healthcare security and hinder effective disease management\. Consequently, these interconnected burdens may result in increased systemic inflammation, which in turn exacerbates the pathophysiology of HS\. Moreover, this review proposes kinesiophobia \(the anticipatory fear of movement\) as a hypothesized component of the biomechanical\-metabolic feedback loop\. Conclusion: Currently, there is a notable absence of primary psychometric data quantifying kinesiophobia in the HS population\. Future research should aim to quantify this clinical construct in this demographic to establish its prevalence and clinical significance\. On a systems level, clinicians could consider systematically addressing these broader behavioral feedback loops through multidisciplinary approaches that incorporate targeted interventions such as cognitive behavioral therapy and structured patient education\. Ultimately, dismantling these behavioral cycles may be a critical step towards attenuating systemic inflammation, halting disease progression, improving therapeutic efficacy, and enhancing long\-term clinical outcomes\.

## [Exploring L1 listening comprehension in higher education — Is it language, strategy or is it personal?](../publications/d8f9f7fba82f7732efe2.md)

Pieterjan Bonne; Jordi Casteleyn

Although lectures are central to higher education, research on first\-language \(L1\) academic listening comprehension remains limited\. Drawing on Bachman and Palmer’s \(2010\) model of communicative language ability, this study explores factors influencing students’ comprehension of lectures delivered in their L1\. Communicative language ability comprises language knowledge and strategic competence, and is influenced by attributes related to the language user\. In this study, language knowledge was operationalized through general and academic vocabulary size, strategic competence through metacognitive awareness, and attributes related to the language user through educational and sociolinguistic background\. The study was conducted at a university college in Flanders, Belgium, where Dutch is both the language of instruction and the predominant first language\. A total of 167 students completed a listening comprehension task, vocabulary size tests, a metacognitive awareness questionnaire, and a background survey\. Results showed that general and academic vocabulary were strongly associated with listening comprehension\. Academic vocabulary predicted performance for lower\-proficiency listeners, while general vocabulary was significant for higher groups\. Metacognitive awareness was not a significant predictor overall, though potentially relevant for weaker listeners\. The relatively low explained variance suggests that L1 academic listening is a multifactorial skill, influenced by linguistic, strategic, and personal factors\.

## [Inteligência artificial na educação e neuroplasticidade: contribuições, limites e desafios para a aprendizagem](../publications/d911948d00859d6d4bcf.md)

Daniela Hayoshi

The literature on artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education focuses almost exclusively on performance, perception, and engagement; brain changes associated with neuroplasticity have rarely been measured\. This narrative review, using explicit search and classification criteria, distinguishes three types of evidence: \(a\) learning outcomes \(grades, retention, and transfer\), \(b\) behavioral measures of cognitive effort, and \(c\) direct neurophysiological measures \(EEG and fNIRS\)\. The most robust performance studies indicate that the effects of AI depend on task design: a randomized trial involving approximately one thousand high school students found gains ranging from 48% to 127% during AI\-assisted practice, while performance declined on an exam taken without AI among students with unrestricted access to the model; this decline was eliminated when the system was configured to provide hints rather than answers\. The most frequently cited meta\-analysis supporting AI \(g = 0\.867\) was retracted in 2026 due to analytical errors and the inclusion of invalid studies\. The few studies using brain\-based measures are small \(n ranging from 24 to 54\), short in duration, unpublished in peer\-reviewed journals or reporting null findings, and assess momentary engagement rather than lasting structural or functional plasticity\. It is therefore concluded that there is no basis for claiming that AI, by itself, either enhances or impairs neuroplasticity\. The evidence supports a narrower conclusion: activities that replace retrieval and elaborative effort tend to reduce measured learning, whereas activities that preserve such effort tend to maintain or enhance learning gains\. A research agenda is proposed incorporating longitudinal designs, transfer measures, and pre\- and post\-intervention neuroimaging with active control conditions\.

## [IMPACTOS DO USO DE CANNABIS SATIVA NA SAÚDE E DESEMPENHO ACADÊMICO DE ESTUDANTES UNIVERSITÁRIOS EM MARINGÁ/PR](../publications/d913543f06ccf37e2664.md)

Isis Nayara Wilhans de Camillo; Bruno Henrique Varão Barbosa; Amanda Tini Monteiro; Talita Matero de Oliveira; Raul Gomes Aguera; Claudia Cristina Batista Evangelista Coimbra

A Cannabis sativa é amplamente utilizada, sendo o Δ9\-tetraidrocanabinol \(THC\) seu principal composto psicoativo\. Entre universitários, o consumo é frequente devido ao acesso facilitado dentro e fora do campus, e o uso crônico pode gerar prejuízos em aprendizado, atenção, função cognitiva e memória operacional\. Este estudo teve como objetivo identificar, analisar e evidenciar os motivos e possíveis repercussões associados ao uso de cannabis entre universitários, com foco em aspectos cognitivos e desempenho acadêmico\. Foi aplicado um questionário estruturado on\-line, via Google Forms, garantindo anonimato, contemplando perfil sociodemográfico, tempo e frequência de uso, primeiro contato, motivos de consumo, percepção de efeitos e desempenho acadêmico\. Obtiveram\-se 73 respostas de usuários\. A amostra foi predominantemente feminina \(57,5%\), concentrada na faixa de 21 a 25 anos \(39,7%\) e vinculada a cursos da área da saúde \(54,8%\)\. Predominou o uso esporádico/recreativo \(37,0%\), motivado principalmente por recreação/lazer e alívio de estresse/ansiedade \(49,3% cada\), sem relatos de uso medicinal\. Embora a maioria não tenha percebido prejuízos expressivos em apetite, clareza de pensamento ou desempenho acadêmico, destacaram\-se indicadores de risco, como cansaço constante \(39,7%\), dificuldade para tomar decisões \(38,4%\) e alteração na memória de curto prazo \(26%\)\. Conclui\-se que, apesar da percepção predominantemente neutra ou positiva quanto aos efeitos do uso, o descompasso com esses indicadores objetivos de risco reforça a necessidade de ações de educação em saúde, orientação e prevenção no ambiente universitário, voltadas tanto à redução de danos quanto à identificação precoce de estudantes vulneráveis, fundamentadas em conhecimento científico e não apenas em juízos morais\.

## [Marx and the Machine Revisited: Rethinking Exploitation Beyond Technological Fetishism](../publications/d925decf5e8a6ae625fb.md)

Alf Hornborg

Abstract Both mainstream and heterodox conceptions of modern technology suffer from ‘machine fetishism’: the illusory perception that technological devices are productive or powerful in themselves , rather than as products of global relations of exchange\. A cognitive foundation for this illusion is the pervasive divide between the material and the social that derives from the dualism of nature and society in Western thought\. Another is the proclivity toward scientific abstraction, as in the divide between the detached theoretical design and the concrete execution of industrial production processes\. Such decontextualised design knowledge was epitomised in the work of Charles Babbage, whose principles for efficient production illustrate how similar considerations have been applied to the organisation of both its technical and its social aspects\. It is also evident in Sidney Mintz’s insight that the organisation of colonial plantations provided templates for industrial factories\. Paradoxically, Marx’s profound analysis of factories and machinery finally remained constrained by the Enlightenment divide between the social and the material and was thus conceptually confined to the British factory\. It did not derive the productivity of British industry from the system\-wide totality of global processes through which the factories were provisioned with inputs of embodied labour, materials, energy, and land from all over the colonial world\. These inputs should be included in the machine as a total socio\-material phenomenon\. What were locally experienced and perceived as labour\-saving machines should be reconceptualised as labour\- displacing devices, acknowledging exploitative exchange relations very far beyond the factory\.

## [Quantitative CT\-Derived Imaging Features Improve Preoperative Risk Stratification of Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasms](../publications/d92f2d2fa91b241a78af.md)

Tae Seung Lee; Hong Min Shin; In\-Ho Park; Jae Seok Bae; In Rae Cho; Woo Hyun Paik; Wooil Kwon; Dong Ho Lee; Haeryoung Kim; Ji Kon Ryu; Jin Ho Choi; Sang Hyub Lee

BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative identification of high\-grade dysplasia \(HGD\) or malignancy in intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms \(IPMNs\) remains challenging using conventional guideline\-based imaging criteria\. Quantitative computed tomography \(CT\)\-based features may detect subtle structural changes preceding overt radiologic findings\. This study aimed to evaluate whether the pancreatic index \(PI\) and additional three\-dimensional CT\-derived quantitative features improve prediction of HGD or malignancy in IPMNs\. METHODS: This single\-center retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical resection for pathologically confirmed IPMNs between January 2001 and August 2024 and had available preoperative pancreas\-protocol CT\. Three\-dimensional quantitative parameters were analyzed\. RESULTS: Among 333 patients, 204 had low\-grade dysplasia \(LGD\), 56 had HGD, and 73 had malignancy\. PI decreased with increasing histologic grade \(75\.6 ± 10\.2% in LGD, 74\.5 ± 12\.0% in HGD, 70\.5 ± 12\.6% in malignancy; p = 0\.003\)\. Pancreatic Hounsfield unit standard deviation \(HU\-SD\) was significantly higher in HGD and malignancy than in LGD \(25\.6 ± 5\.9, 29\.0 ± 8\.7, and 29\.6 ± 6\.2, respectively; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. A combined model integrating guideline\-based criteria with PI, CI, cystic HU\-SD, pancreatic HU\-SD, and pancreatic duct volume demonstrated better discrimination than the guideline\-only model \(area under the curve 0\.800 vs\. 0\.760; p = 0\.007\)\. CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative CT\-derived imaging features provide incremental value for predicting HGD and malignancy when integrated with conventional guideline\-based criteria\. These noninvasive imaging biomarkers may enhance risk stratification and provide additional information to support clinical decision\-making when integrated with conventional criteria\. Further external validation is required to establish their clinical utility in routine practice\.

## [Opportunities and limitations of using generative artificial intelligence in the development of a minimum viable product for non\-technical founders](../publications/d93b7aa589e52461c910.md)

Ustanovitelj brez tehničnega znanja se pri prvem digitalnem produktu sooča s tehničnimi, kompetenčnimi, časovnimi in finančnimi omejitvami hkrati, tehnično sposobnost pa lahko pridobi le prek tehničnega soustanovitelja, zunanjega izvajalca ali lastnega učenja programiranja, pri čemer ima vsaka pot svojo ceno\. ## [Occupational Networks: Labor Market Structure and Gender Gap in Argentina](../publications/d93e348c402a33082095.md)

Joaquín Carrascosa; Aaron Bernal Huanca; Viktoriya Semeshenko; Carlos Sarraute

Este trabajo analiza la estructura del mercado laboral argentino mediante un enfoque de redes complejas que vincula ocupaciones \(CIUO\-08\) y ramas de actividad económica \(CAES 1\.0\)\. Utilizando microdatos de las encuestas ENES \(2019\) y ESAyPP \(2021\), se construye una red bipartita de alta resolución y sus correspondientes proyecciones unipartitas para desentrañar patrones de interdependencia no visibles con métodos tradicionales\. Los resultados revelan una organización modular donde los sectores industriales y los servicios sociales ocupan regiones diferenciadas de la red, mientras que el comercio actúa como un nodo puente que articula ambos espacios\. En la red ocupacional se observa una marcada segmentación entre ocupaciones manuales y no manuales, junto con la presencia de ocupaciones transversales que articulan múltiples sectores económicos\. Un hallazgo central es que la segregación de género posee un correlato topológico: las ocupaciones con composiciones de género similares tienden a agruparse en la red \(homofilia\), evidenciando que la desigualdad está escrita en la propia estructura relacional del mercado\. Estos resultados muestran el potencial del análisis de redes para comprender la organización estructural del mercado laboral y sus patrones de segmentación\.

## [Empowerment Gain as Causal Learning, Causal Learning as Empowerment Gain: A Bridge between Bayesian Causal Hypothesis Testing and Reinforcement Learning](../publications/d95be9512d0a753c1f27.md)

Alison Gopnik C

Abstract Cognitive scientists have applied advances in our formal understanding of causation in philosophy and computer science, particularly within the Causal Bayes Net formalism, to understand human causal learning\. In parallel, reinforcement learning \(RL\) researchers have developed the idea of an intrinsic reward signal called “empowerment\.” An agent is rewarded for maximizing the mutual information between its actions and their outcomes, regardless of the external reward value of those outcomes\. Empowerment may be an important bridge between classical Bayesian causal learning and RL and may help to characterize causal learning in humans and enable it in machines\.
