## [Embodied Faith and Athletic Cognition: Interoception, Religious Meaning\-Making, and Self\-Regulation in Sport Başlığı kopyala](../publications/d975edcc53a7eb7d2d60.md)

Karadağ Erdal

Athletic cognition is shaped not only by explicit goals and strategic decisions but also by bodily sensations, expectations, attention, and culturally grounded interpretations of experience\. This critical integrative review considers whether religious and spiritual meaning\-making may alter how athletes interpret effort, arousal, fatigue, uncertainty, and setbacks, without presuming that religious commitment improves objective performance\. It connects research on interoception, embodied cognition, attentional regulation, stress appraisal, religious coping, and sport resilience\. The synthesis distinguishes sensory detection from appraisal, deliberate contemplative practice from automatic motor skill, and personal faith narratives from experimentally supported mechanisms\. A conditional embodied\-meaning framework is developed in which bodily signals and contextual expectations interact with identity and coping strategies to influence interpretation, behavioral choices, and participation\. Potentially beneficial processes include flexible attentional reorientation, acceptance of transient discomfort, and value\-consistent persistence; adverse pathways include hypervigilance, shame, ritual dependence, and misinterpretation of medically significant symptoms\. No new participants, original quantitative data, or experimental effects are reported\. The article proposes longitudinal and mixed\-method studies comparing religious and secular meaning frameworks, using preregistered outcomes, matched interventions, measurement\-invariance testing, and ethical safeguards\. Existing literature establishes the relevance of bodily perception and meaning\-making as separate domains, but their specific interaction in athletic performance remains insufficiently tested\. The framework is intended to generate falsifiable questions, not a new diagnostic or performance assessment tool\. embodied cognition; interoception; religion and spirituality; sport psychology; cognitive appraisal; self\-regulation

## [LLM\-BASED NEURO\-SYMBOLIC LEGAL JUDGMENT PREDICTION FOR CRIMINAL CASES](../publications/d98e8294913460edcd92.md)



Predicting the outcome of a criminal case involves more than recognising which offence a narrative resembles\.A court asks whether each ingredient of the offence has been proved, whether a lesser offence still applies when one ingredient fails, whether a general exception excuses the act, and what punishment the statute prescribes\.We describe a judgment prediction framework for the Indian Penal Code \(IPC\) that assigns these questions to two kinds of components\.Large language models \(LLMs\) served through the Groq API read the narrative, extract the facts, and mark every ingredient of each candidate offence as proved, not proved or unclear, quoting the supporting text\.A symbolic layer built on a knowledge base of 213 IPC sections then applies seven explicit rules to choose the charge, decide the verdict, and retrieve the prescribed punishment, which the language model never produces\.We also show that the 4,260\-record synthetic dataset used in this project discloses its own labels: every record states the section number, the offence name and the outcome, so a TF\-IDF classifier is 100% accurate on unmodified text and about 1% accurate once the offence is hidden\.After section numbers and verdict words are masked, the rule pipeline identifies the offence in 99\.5% of 852 held\-out records and the verdict in 99\.8%, matching a trained logistic\-regression baseline \(99\.6%\) without any training; when the offence name is also removed, it declines to decide in 99\.8% of records instead of guessing\.A preliminary test on narratives that never name the offence gives 41\.7% top\-1 and 83\.3% top\-3 section accuracy\.These figures describe a controlled prototype, not performance on real judgments\.

## [APPLICATION OF DEMAND FORECASTING MODELS TO INVENTORY MANAGEMENT OPTIMIZATION: A DATA\-DRIVEN APPROACH](../publications/d992b01e0cc76e82d059.md)

André Furlanetto dos Reis; Eliomar Gotardi Pessoa; Fábio Henrique Ferreira

Demand forecasting is a central input to inventory planning because replenishment decisions depend not only on expected demand but also on the uncertainty surrounding that estimate\. This narrative review examines how data\-driven forecasting models can contribute to reducing excess inventory and stockouts while maintaining adequate service levels\. The literature reviewed indicates that ensemble learning, machine\-learning models, probabilistic approaches, and hybrid forecasting methods can improve demand estimation, particularly when seasonality, promotions, economic indicators, and other exogenous variables are incorporated\. However, greater statistical accuracy does not automatically translate into lower inventory costs or higher service levels\. Operational performance depends on linking forecast outputs and residual uncertainty to safety\-stock calculations, reorder points, order\-up\-to policies, and other replenishment rules\. The evidence therefore supports an integrated forecasting–inventory perspective in which predictive performance and inventory policy are evaluated jointly\. This approach can improve the balance between product availability, working capital, and logistics costs, although results remain dependent on demand characteristics, model calibration, and the operating context\.

## [Bitcoin Price Prediction Using Machine Learning Technique](../publications/d995fe7cc9c3719ae12e.md)

Sujith V\.; Sree Yogeswari S\.; Subha Sri R

Bitcoin price forecasting is challenging because of nonlinear market behaviour and rapid price fluctuations\. This study presents an integrated machine\-learning framework for one\-step\-ahead Bitcoin price prediction using Random Forest \(RF\), Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), and XGBoost\. The framework incorporates preprocessing, comparative model evaluation, prediction fusion, and directional trend classification within a unified predictive workflow\. Model performance is assessed using MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R², while an equal\-weight fusion mechanism combines the individual prediction outputs\. A separate RF classifier generates UP, DOWN, and NEUTRAL market\-direction states\. Experimental results demonstrate that XGBoost provides the strongest predictive performance, achieving a reported accuracy of 96\.5% and an R² of 0\.94, with lower prediction errors than the other evaluated models\. The complete framework is deployed through a Flask\-based web application supporting interactive prediction, graphical visualization, trend analysis, and prediction\-history management\.

## [Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture\-of\-Experts LLMs for Personalization](../publications/d9a7a599449e36e528b4.md)

Sekh Mainul Islam; Pepa Atanasova; Isabelle Augenstein

Personalization of Large Language Models \(LLMs\) is increasingly important for user\-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it\. We propose to personalize Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization\. We adapt three open\-weight MoE LLMs on a large\-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non\-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features\. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non\-personalized model\. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model&\#x27;s behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non\-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features\.

## [DeDiCa: A Scalable Deconfounding Discrete Causal Generative Model](../publications/d9bebfd907d2df3a6a7a.md)

Kunchangtai Liang; Adrián Javaloy; Antonio Vergari; Isabel Valera

We introduce DeDiCa, a practical framework for efficient causal inference with discrete variables and hidden confounding that revisits classical probabilistic modeling through a tensorized parameterization of causal Bayesian networks, enabling tractable inference\. Given a causal graph, DeDiCa is trained once on observational data by maximum likelihood, exactly marginalizing over hidden confounders, and can then estimate any \(proxy\-\)identifiable interventional query\. Despite this deliberately simple parameterization, DeDiCa matches state\-of\-the\-art neural causal generative models in ATE estimation, while supporting memory\-efficient CPU training and exact interventional inference in milliseconds\. Compared with causal foundation models, DeDiCa scales more effectively with additional observational samples and achieves competitive accuracy at substantially lower inference time and memory\. DeDiCa provides a tractable, accurate, and scalable approach to causal inference in discrete settings with hidden confounding\.

## [OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain\-of\-Thought Reasoning](../publications/d9d0edc503a34a8bfe06.md)

Lewen Yan; Yanxu Zhu; Jie Zhang; Jing Shao

Chain\-of\-Thought \(CoT\) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention\. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks\. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors\. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine\-grained and coarse\-grained \(e\.g\., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage\), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs\. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness\. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general\-purpose LLMs by 1\.32\-30\.57 and 11\.71\-27\.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state\-of\-the\-art results on OpenAI&\#x27;s CoT monitorability benchmark\. It also generalizes to unseen models&\#x27; CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI\.

## [Emotional Example in Aristotle: A Way of Teaching the Worth of Things](../publications/d9e580b9976d23468016.md)

Andy Mullins

Aristotle’s insight that refined feelings generate motivations for action has profoundly influenced psychology, yet the role of refined emotional example to teach virtue has remained largely unnoticed by his commentators\. This paper offers a reappraisal of emotional example as integral to the formation of virtue, and attributable to Aristotelian insights\. I note that Aristotle establishes preconditions for a role for emotional example: a focus on children in the earliest years, the role of imitation in learning, and refined emotional responses as appraisals or judgements\. I offer a reading of two texts offering an appreciation of refined emotional example as a way teaching virtue and foundations of moral judgement\. I note the presence of emotional example in childhood studies and suggest that this paper serves to inform childhood studies more precisely in the light of Aristotelian principles, and to correct omissions in Aristotelian commentaries\.

## [Marčeta, Momir: On Karma: A Hypothesis on Experiential Continuity, Microconsciousness, and Reincarnation](../publications/d9e6036a84f7161a6732.md)



On Karma presents a philosophical hypothesis concerning karma, experiential continuity, microconsciousness, and reincarnation\. It proposes that what continues beyond an individual life is experience rather than personal identity\. Karma is understood as an automatic, self\-regulating process through which experiential traces contribute to the formation of a new life configuration, rather than as a system of moral reward and punishment\. The book explores the relationship between microconsciousness and macroconsciousness, the emergence of ego and identification, and the possibility of liberation through the ending of identification\. It also examines responsibility without interpreting suffering as deserved punishment\. The model is offered as a philosophical framework for inquiry, rather than an established scientific theory\.

## [Enhanced Short\-Text Clustering Based on a Multirepresentation Fusion Model](../publications/d9ede3e28c14684248fa.md)

Ali Sabah; Dhurgham Ali Mohammed; Zaid Alaa

Short\-text clustering has become increasingly important because of the exponential growth of textual data\. However, traditional methods struggle with sparsity, limited context, and poor cluster cohesion\. Recently, innovations have made word embedding algorithms, including Word2Vec, GloVe, and FastText, available for effectively learn semantic relationships\. Although these methods have advantages, they tend to concentrate on semantics area\. These limitations are addressed in this study by adopting an enhanced short\-text clustering method based on multirepresentation\. Specifically, this study integrates heterogeneous embeddings into a unified framework using weighted L2\-normalized concatenation, followed by Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\)\-based dimensionality reduction that retains 95% of the variance, thereby create a unified semantic representation\. Unlike simple concatenation approaches of embeddings, pre\-space normalization operations are added before the fusion operation to avoid the presence of dominant embedding bias\. The proposed model was evaluated on four benchmark datasets, namely, StackOverflow, AgNews, BioASQ, and SearchSnippet, via the k\-means and k\-medoids clustering algorithms\. The results demonstrate substantial improvements in the clustering quality metrics\. Compared with the results of the baseline models Bag of Words \(BoW\)/Term Frequency\-Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\), the average gains were statistically significant: 29% in silhouette score, 8% in adjusted Rand index, and 8% in normalized mutual information over the best \(single\) embedding baseline \(GloVe with k\-medoids\) and 63%, 35%, and 40%, respectively, over traditional BoW/TF\-IDF methods\. Most improvements are found to be statistically significant at p &lt; 0\.05\. Additionally, PCA was applied to reduce noise and dimensionality, potentially improving clustering outcomes\. ## [Digital Module 42: An Introduction to Analyzing Unstructured Data in Education](../publications/d9f44991ba6a2bb09754.md)

Mo Zhang; Mengxiao Zhu

Module Abstract Unstructured data, for example, text, audio, handwriting and drawings, video, and interaction logs, are increasingly abundant in education\. However, they lack the predefined schema that conventional psychometric tools assume\. This module introduces a principled, end‐to‐end workflow for turning such data into defensible measures\. In this module, we first define unstructured data \(Section 1\) and then proceed to four analytic stages: preprocessing across modalities \(Section 2\), data representation \(Section 3\), making inferences \(Section 4\), and evaluating the resulting measures against psychometric standards \(Section 5\)\. Finally, Section 6 gives an overview of data privacy, consent, and governance\. We demonstrate the methodologies using a dataset collected from a collaborative problem‐solving task\. By the end, learners will have a conceptual map of the analysis pipeline from raw signals to valid inference, a solid understanding of modern representation methods, and a framework for evaluating and governing measures built from unstructured data in the field of education\.

## [Turizm Alanında Kavramsal ve Uygulamalı Yaklaşımlar](../publications/d9f555a0bc158a3f09c7.md)



21\. yüzyılda küreselleşme olgusu ve dijital teknolojilerde yaşanan radikal gelişmeler, uluslararası mobiliteyi eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir boyuta taşıyarak turizm endüstrisini çok boyutlu bir sosyo\-ekonomik ekosisteme dönüştürmüştür\. Elli aşkın alt sektörü doğrudan ve dolaylı olarak harekete geçiren bu dinamik yapı, küresel düzeyde Gayri Safi Yurt İçi Hasıla’nın \(GSYİH\) yaklaşık %10’unu temsil ederek stratejik bir makro\-ekonomik enstrüman niteliği kazanmıştır\. Seyahat maliyetlerinin azalması ve erişilebilirliğin artması, sektörü küresel ekonominin en rekabetçi alanlarından biri haline getirmiştir\. Modern çalışma hayatının getirdiği psiko\-sosyal zorunluluklar, seyahat olgusunu geleneksel bir lüks tüketim kalıbından çıkararak temel bir insani gereksinime dönüştürmüştür\. Bu dönüşüm; kitle turizmine dayalı geleneksel modellerin yerini, değer odaklı, özgün ve kişiselleştirilmiş “deneyim” arayışlarına bırakmasına yol açmıştır\. Teknolojik inovasyonlar ise destinasyonların dijital platformlarda görünürlük kazanmasını ve küresel pazarda konumlanmasını sağlarken; bilgiye erişimi kolaylaşan, çevreye ve kültüre duyarlı “bilinçli turist” profilinin doğmasına zemin hazırlamıştır\. Bu eser, küreselleşme ve teknolojik paradigmanın turizm ekosistemine yansımalarını bütüncül ve disiplinlerarası bir perspektifle ele almak amacıyla kaleme alınmıştır\. Alanında uzman akademisyenlerin titiz çalışmalarıyla şekillenen çalışma; sektördeki güncel eğilimleri, dijital dönüşümün yapısal etkilerini ve değişen tüketici davranışlarını bilimsel bir süzgeçten geçirerek sunmaktadır\. Sonuç olarak çalışmanın; turizm profesyonellerine küresel rekabet ortamında yön gösterici stratejik bir vizyon kazandırması, akademideki literatür boşluğunu doldurması ve turizm alanında uzmanlaşmayı hedefleyen araştırmacılar ile öğrenciler için temel bir referans kaynağı oluşturması hedeflenmektedir\.

## [Reactive Inclusion: School Infrastructure Barriers and Accessibility for Learners with Cerebral Palsy in a Nigerian Private School: A Mixed\-Methods Case Study](../publications/d9f55b0ff507a3d1e7dd.md)

James Onole Okhakhu

Although Nigeria&\#x27;s Prohibition of the Discrimination against persons with Disabilities Act \(2018\) requires accessible school infrastructure, a substantial gap often lies between legal pronouncements and physical implementation especially in the private school sector\. This research explored how physical infrastructure acts to enable or impede the educational inclusion of learners with Cerebral Palsy \(CP\) in a purposively sampled private international school in Ibadan, Nigeria\. Utilizing a pragmatic mixed methods case study research design, data was collected using a closed Likert\-scale questionnaire to parents \(n=12\) of learners with CP and semi\-structured interviews with school personnel \(n=10\) including administrators, teachers and other support staff\. Descriptive statistics were employed to analyse quantitative data whereas reflexivity themes guided analysis of qualitative data\. The research revealed a mean parental rating of accessibility to be 3\.27 on a scale of 5\.00, concealing a polarized infrastructure that juxtaposes fairly compliant new building sections with exclusionary older structures\. The infrastructure domain rated least favourably included access facilities and handrails \(Mean=3\.00\) and the accessibility of sanitation facilities \(Mean=3\.08\)\. Major themes generated from the qualitative data analysis include the prevalence of architectural barriers in terms ofvertical access, the organizational propensity for reliance on human assistance \(‘the helper’ syndrome\), disjunctures between stated policies and actual practices and the Emotional Labour that staff incur\. We theorise these trends to represent &\#x27;Reactive Inclusion&\#x27;\- a condition where excellent interpersonal support serves to mask and, in effect, &\#x27;stand\-in&\#x27; for the failure of physical infrastructure\. Our results suggest policy implications for school leaders, policy makers and architectural professionals aimed at fostering genuine inclusion of learners with physical disabilities in sub\-Saharan Africa\.

## [Knowledge Structures and Gaps in Home\-Based Care for Older Adults With Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Bibliometric Analysis](../publications/da0b130c0a2b1c3b787f.md)

Sri Wianti; Antia Antia; Lilis Lismayanti; Wijayanti Wijayanti; Ika Kusuma Wardani

Introduction: Home\-based care for older adults with neurodegenerative diseases involves multidimensional needs that may require coordination among individuals, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and services\. However, how knowledge relevant to these care dimensions is organised across the research field remains insufficiently understood\. Objective: This study aimed to map global research trends and knowledge structures in home\-based care for older adults with neurodegenerative diseases and identify potential gaps in knowledge integration\. Method: A bibliometric analysis and science mapping were conducted using 315 Scopus\-indexed publications published between 1994 and 2026\. Data were retrieved on 8 July 2026 from an initial set of 373 records\. Analyses were performed using Biblioshiny, VOSviewer, and OpenRefine to examine publication performance, conceptual and intellectual structures, research fronts, thematic development, and scientific collaboration\. Result: The dataset comprised 315 publications by 1,759 authors, with international co\-authorship accounting for 21\.59% of publications\. Annual publication growth was 9\.81%\. Dementia was the most prominent keyword, followed by patient\-centered care and home care\. Caregiver involvement and care coordination were also represented in the conceptual network\. Thematic analyses showed increasing attention to primary healthcare, palliative care, and person\-centered approaches in more recent years\. Holistic care appeared in the keyword network but had lower frequency and connectivity than the major concepts\. Across the conceptual, intellectual, thematic, and social analyses, relevant care dimensions and research traditions were represented, but their relationships were not shown to form a coherent framework for holistic home\-based care\. Conclusion: The findings suggest a potential knowledge integration gap within the mapped literature\. Future research should develop and empirically evaluate a conceptual framework connecting multidimensional care needs, person\-centered approaches, caregiver involvement, and coordination across home\-based, primary, community, and palliative care\.

## [Linking Active Madden–Julian Oscillation to High–Very High Rainfall During Large\-Scale Flood Events in Banten and Jakarta](../publications/da1ec76f4e3255343827.md)

Yanuar Henri Pribadi; Tania June; Supari Supari; I Putu Santikayasa; Ana Turyanti

The modulation of rainfall extremes by the Madden–Julian Oscillation \(MJO\) over Indonesia and the Maritime Continent is well established, but less is known about how consistently this relationship is represented in documented large\-scale flood\-impact records\. This study provides an event\-based assessment of active MJO phases 3–5 on high–very high \(HVH\) rainfall associated with large\-scale flood events across seasonal rainfall zones \(ZOMs\)\. Flood records from 2008–2024 were linked with reconstructed daily rainfall data from 107 rain\-gauge stations and daily Real\-time Multivariate MJO index information\. Large\-scale flood events were defined based on spatial and temporal extent, while HVH rainfall was classified as rainfall above the 75th percentile and evaluated using maximum one\-day and five\-day accumulated rainfall\. The results show that 210 of 577 HVH rainfall\-event records, or 36\.4%, occurred during active MJO phases 3–5\. Active\-MJO conditions occurred in 22\.2% of one\-day HVH rainfall events and 48\.6% of five\-day accumulated HVH rainfall events\. During DJF, active MJO phases 3–5 occurred in 55\.1% of five\-day accumulated HVH flood\-associated events, compared with a seasonal five\-day\-window baseline of 47\.6%, corresponding to a modest enrichment ratio of 1\.16\. These findings indicate that active MJO phases 3–5 provide complementary information on multi\-day HVH rainfall accumulation, although their contribution varies substantially by season and should be interpreted relative to the seasonal background occurrence of the MJO\.

## [Distribution\-based canonical correlation residual monitoring for industrial processes fault detection](../publications/da1fe910ea93ac2847c2.md)

K\. Ramakrishna Kini; Fouzi Harrou; Muddu Madakyaru; Ying Sun

Abstract Reliable fault detection is essential for safe, efficient, and sustainable industrial processes\. This paper proposes a Canonical Correlation Analysis \(CCA\)\-based fault detection framework with distribution\-based residual monitoring using Hellinger Distance \(HD\), Kullback–Leibler Distance \(KLD\), and Kantorovich Distance \(KD\)\. Specifically, the proposed approach evaluates residual distributions within a moving window and determines decision thresholds nonparametrically using Kernel Density Estimation \(KDE\), avoiding restrictive Gaussian assumptions\. A key advantage is that the framework requires only fault\-free data for model construction and threshold calibration, making it suitable when labeled fault data are scarce or unavailable\. The framework detects faults that disrupt the CCA cross\-correlation structure, including faults affecting variables in either the predictor or response variables\. The proposed approach is evaluated on the Williams–Otto reactor and a Wastewater Treatment Plant \(WWTP\) under bias, intermittent, drift, and freezing faults\. Additional experiments examine faults in CCA input variables, sensitivity to moving\-window and KDE settings, and different fault magnitudes\. The proposed approach is also compared with CCA\-based Squared Prediction Error \(CCA\-SPE\), Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\), and Support Vector Regression \(SVR\) monitoring under identical fault scenarios and evaluation conditions\. The results show that distribution\-based CCA indicators generally outperform conventional CCA\-SPE and the considered PCA\- and SVR\-based strategies\. Among them, CCA\-KD achieves the best overall performance, with high detection and low false alarm rates\. Overall, integrating CCA with distribution\-based monitoring provides effective multivariate fault detection\.

## [Neuronal\-Like Negative Capacitance of Biofilms from Common Microbial Pathogens Using Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy](../publications/da2b61d33159c57934f7.md)

Adhvaidhi Kuntran; Victor Carneiro da Cunha Martorelli; Malek Arnold; Rok Krašovec; Ian S\. Roberts; Thomas Andrew Waigh

Abstract We studied electrical impedance spectroscopy of biofilms from Gram\-negative bacteria, Gram\-positive bacteria and a fungus: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterococcus faecalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus epidermidis and Candida albicans\. We show that low\-frequency negative capacitance appears across all species under small DC bias voltages\. The negative capacitance is not organism\-specific, but rather a general property of biofilm\-electrode systems driven by non\-equilibrium ionic and interfacial processes\. An equivalent circuit model incorporating a constant phase element and an inductive branch reproduces the impedance response, capturing both interfacial heterogeneity and delayed ionic dynamics\. While interfacial electrode–electrolyte coupling shapes the spectra, the behaviour is consistent with biologically regulated ion transport\. Previous work demonstrated that ion channel–mediated electrical activity in E\. coli biofilms can generate inductive\-like responses, providing a mechanistic contribution for the observed negative capacitance\. These results establish negative capacitance as a robust and broadly conserved feature of microbial biofilms\. Electrical sensors could be optimized to measure negative capacitance as a proxy for the formation of living biofilms e\.g\. to detect the biofouling of catheters\.

## [Algorithmic Provenance: When and Why Consumers Discount Products Made With AI ‐Involved Processes](../publications/da3439621c24b5df08a7.md)

S\. Sreejesh; Souvik Singha

ABSTRACT Firms increasingly incorporate generative and non‐generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) into product design, formulation, and production, and they face a disclosure question: how should they describe the role of AI to consumers? Across six studies, including analysis of 1800 marketplace listings and five pre‐registered experiments \(total experimental N = 2760\), we introduce and test a 2‐by‐2 framework of algorithmic provenance defined by the AI&\#x27;s role \(agentic vs\. assistive\) and its visibility in the final product \(visible vs\. invisible\)\. Identical products are evaluated differently depending on where they fall in this taxonomy\. Agentic AI involvement \(AI as designer\) reduces consumer product attitudes, perceived quality, purchase intentions, and willingness to pay relative to assistive AI involvement \(AI as a tool for a human designer\)\. The effect is amplified when AI involvement is visible in the final product\. The downstream responses are partially mediated by a new construct, perceived authenticity of creative intention, which captures consumers&\#x27; inference about whether a human creator pursued a genuine creative vision\. The effect is larger for expressive than for functional product domains and larger among consumers primed to hold an independent self‐construal\. A scalable managerial intervention, creative‐intent framing, narrows the agentic penalty by approximately half, again through the authenticity mechanism\. The findings identify a substantively important new construct for AI disclosure research, refine theories of algorithmic aversion, and offer marketers an actionable disclosure design principle\.

## [Kaynak Metinlerle Bağlar ve Sadakat Olgusu Çerçevesinde Hayran Filmlerini Okumak](../publications/da3ef8cac3e5e0f200d9.md)

Burak ÖZYAL

Edebiyat ve sinema ilişkisinin tarihsel bir sonucu olan uyarlama eserler hayran kültürü içerisinde farklı okuma biçimleriyle anlam kazanmaktadır\. Bu çalışmanın amacı izleyicilerin hayran kurgusu uyarlama filmle kaynak metinler arasında nasıl bağlar kurduklarını tematik bir yapı içerisinde ortaya koymak ve sadakat olgusunun bu anlam kümesi içerisinde nasıl işlev gördüğünü tarif etmektir\. Bu araştırmanın önemi hayran kültürü çalışmalarında üzerinde fazla durulmamış bir konu olan kaynak metne sadakat odaklı izleyici okumalarına dair anlam kategorilerinin keşfedilerek bu temalar üzerinden kuramsal bir yaklaşım geliştirilmesidir\. Keşfedici bir yaklaşımla yapılandırılan araştırma metodolojik olarak gömülü kuram yaklaşımını benimsemiştir\. J\.K\. Rowling’in fantastik roman türündeki eseri Harry Potter serisinden uyarlanan hayran kurgusu film “Severus Snape and the Marauders” filmine yapılan yorumlar MAXQDA programı aracılığıyla, gömülü kuram yaklaşımının kodlama basamaklarına göre analiz edilmiştir\. Çalışmada hayran kurgusu ve kaynak metin arasında bağlantı kurduğu belirlenen 1\.799 kullanıcı yorumu analiz edilmiştir\. Bulgular, izleyicilerin hayran kurgusu uyarlama film ve kaynak metinleri altı farklı anlam ekseninde ilişkilendirdiğini göstermektedir\. Bunlar eleştirel okuma, kaynak metne sadakatin olumlanması, kanaatleri etkileme, anlatı otoritesi çerçevesi, karşılaştırmalar ve özgün değer kategorileri olarak gruplandırılmıştır\. İkincil bulgular ise izleyicilerin hayran kurgusu film ve kaynak metinleri ilişkilendirme biçimlerinin ağırlıklı olarak, sınırları kaynak metin tarafından belirlenen kanon anlatıya sadakat değeri ekseninde geliştiğini göstermektedir\. Bu yönüyle hayran kurgusu yapımın olumlu, olumsuz veya müzakereci bir okuma biçiminden hangisine tabi olursa olsun temel incelenme kıstasının kaynak metne sadakat değeri olduğu görülmüştür\.

## [The evolution of MALDI mass spectrometry imaging](../publications/da45cfca41597b75e897.md)

Laurine Lagache; Michel Salzet; Isabelle Fournier

Matrix\-assisted laser desorption/ionization imaging mass spectrometry \(MALDI\-MSI\) has evolved from an experimental concept into a versatile analytical platform that links molecular information to spatial context\. Since its development in the 1980s as a soft ionization method, the field has progressed through key advances in sample preparation, matrix chemistry, instrumentation, and computational analysis\. The first molecular images of tissue sections in the 1990s enabled the label\-free visualization of proteins, lipids, metabolites, and drugs directly in situ, establishing MALDI\-MSI as a widely used technique in fundamental proteomics and clinical pathology\. Over the past two decades, improvements in sensitivity, spatial resolution, and reproducibility have broadened its applications in pharmacology and microbiology\. More recently, specialized approaches such as high\-resolution mass analyzers, ion mobility separation, MALDI\-2 post\-ionization, two\-laser post\-desolvation, and multimodal image fusion have demonstrated proof\-of\-concept capabilities toward single\-cell and subcellular imaging\. Emerging technologies, including in vivo molecular imaging with SpiderMass, integration with machine learning, and combination with spatial transcriptomics, remain largely exploratory and often rely on customized setups\. This review traces the historical development of MALDI\-MSI, highlights major technical and biomedical milestones, and distinguishes between established applications and experimental directions that may shape its future in research and clinical translation\.

## [Talent Acquisition Strategies and Employer Branding in a Technology Firm: An Observational Study of ValueDX Technologies Pvt\. Ltd\.](../publications/da51974d37aa6c741ca5.md)

Vaishnavi Choudhary

The process of recruiting talent in technology companies goes beyond simply filling job vacancies; it also demands the use of appropriate sourcing channels, timely communication with candidates, coordinated assessment, and a company image that attracts people to think about joining the organization\. This paper looks at the talent acquisition and employer branding practices at ValueDX Technologies Pvt\. Ltd\. in Pune during an On\-the\-Job Training \(OJT\) period that took place from 18 March to 19 June 2026\. Based on the practical recruitment activities and the records described in the source OJT report, the study employs a descriptive, qualitative case\-study method\. The activities carried out included sourcing via LinkedIn and Naukri\.com, placing job advertisements, making cold calls, contacting college authorities and Training and Placement Officers \(TPOs\), conducting recruitment drives, screening candidates, coordinating interviews, tracking candidates, and onboarding\. Special attention is paid to VishwaVidya, an initiative linked to free technical training and internship opportunities, as an example of how learning\-focused outreach can contribute to employer branding\. The observations indicate that different recruitment sources have different functions and that it is better to use a multi\-channel strategy than to rely on a single platform\. The report also stresses the importance of consistent follow\-up, accurate candidate records, coordination among stakeholders, and a structured onboarding procedure\. Since there was no fixed survey sample or complete recruitment outcome data available, the findings are purely descriptive and cannot be taken as statistical evidence of effectiveness\. The paper suggests the introduction of a standardized recruitment tracker, the collection of metrics by source, regular communication regarding employer branding, and a consistent process from selection through to onboarding\. Keywords: talent acquisition; employer branding; candidate experience; technical recruitment; campus hiring; onboarding

## [A Hybrid RAG\-Based Framework for Improved Information Retrieval from Long Documents via Summarization and Question Answering](../publications/da55b6d21725dc6ab59f.md)

Ahmed Sami Jaddoa; Jaber Karimpour; Pedram Salehpour

We present an integrated system, which is a mix of summarization as well as Question Answering \(QA\) to boost the performance regarding information retrieval \(IR\) for long and domain\-intensive documents\. This work creates a synergistic relationship between both tasks to enhance retrieval efficiency and quality of answers, unlike previous studies focusing separately on either summarization or QA\. The framework proposed is comprised of three stages\. First, it involves summarization that is used for condensing documents, maintaining their key semantic content\. Second, it employs a retrieval\-augmented generation \(RAG\) architecture, where the all\-MiniLM\-L6\-v2 model is used for the retrieval stage, while T5 and BART\-Large\-CNN models are utilized for the generation stage\. Lastly, answers generated are put into comparison with a baseline system which works with complete document processing without summarization\. Results at the NIPS dataset reveal that integrating summarization with QA significantly improves each summary informativeness and answer accuracy\. To investigate the impact of summarization inside the retrieval pipeline, two complementary eventualities are explored\. First, Proactive Summarization as an Indexing Tool \(Summarization\-First\) plays summarization earlier than the indexing and retrieval stages to reduce record size and improve retrieval performance while keeping semantic relevance\. Second, Query\-Guided Contextual Summarization \(Retrieval\-First Summarization\) applies summarization after the retrieval level, wherein only the retrieved relevant passages are summarized in step with consumer question for generating more targeted and context\-conscious solutions\. These two scenarios enable a comparative analysis of the way the position of summarization within RAG pipeline impacts retrieval efficiency as well as solution era quality\. ## [A data‐driven image extraction and analysis pipeline for plant phenotyping in controlled environments](../publications/da5dedb37bb5d9de3d3d.md)

Fahimeh Orvati Nia; Joshua Peeples; Seth C\. Murray; Andrew J\. McFarland; Troy Vann; Shima Salehi; Robert G\. Hardin; David D\. Baltensperger; Amir M\. H\. Ibrahim; J\. Alex Thomasson; Henry Y\. Fadamiro; Nithya K\. Subramanian; Suresh D\. Pillai; Rebecca Roston; Joslin Ishimwe; Diptadeep Basak; Nazar Oladepo; Uday Santhosh Raju Vysyaraju

Abstract Advances in automation, imaging, and artificial intelligence have enabled large‐scale plant phenotyping, but image analysis remains a critical bottleneck for crop improvement and biological discovery\. We developed an integrated multispectral phenotyping framework using imagery from the Texas A&amp;M AgriLife Automated Precision Phenotyping Greenhouse and expanded plant growth and phenotyping \(PGP v2\) data across maize \( Zea mays L\.\), cotton \( Gossypium hirsutum \), rice \( Oryza sativa \), and sorghum \( Sorghum bicolor L\.\)\. The pipeline integrates pseudo‐red‐green‐blue composite image generation, plant detection and segmentation, image stitching, vegetation‐index analysis, texture analysis, morphological trait extraction, and temporal comparison of image‐derived features to quantify changes in plant structure, spectral reflectance, and texture over time\. Among the evaluated segmentation approaches, segment anything model \(SAM\) v3 provided the highest and most consistent accuracy across diverse crop structures, although it required greater computational time than classical methods\. Segment anything model for long sequences \(SAM2Long\)maintained plant‐instance associations across vertically stacked frames, while scale‐invariant feature transform–based stitching reconstructed plant mosaics when individual plants extended beyond a single field of view\. For each plant and imaging date, the pipeline generated an 863‐dimensional feature vector spanning vegetation indices, spectral statistics, texture descriptors, and morphological traits\. The framework was evaluated through two case studies: treatment‐level temporal analysis of mutagenized sorghum lines and cold‐stress phenotyping of maize using a separate imaging system\. In both studies, the extracted features supported statistical and multivariate analyses of phenotypic variation and enabled separation of plants based on treatment‐ or stress‐related responses\. The combined dataset and workflow provide structured, automated, and well‐documented phenotypic analysis across multiple crops, experimental settings, and imaging systems for controlled‐environment plant science and crop improvement\.

## [Impacto y Beneficios de la Inteligencia Artificial en la Animación Digital: Una Revisión Sistemática](../publications/da608cb9513cad515c4e.md)

Christopher Alejandro González Romero; Francisco Jesús Kantún Hernández; Emmanuel Keb Pascual; José de Jesús Dzul Ruiz

La animación digital y la inteligencia artificial están transformando y ofreciendo herramientas innovadoras en la producción de películas animadas, reducción de producción y automatización de tareas\. Este estudio, basado en una revisión sistemática con metodología PRISMA, analiza cincuenta investigaciones recientes que abordan el uso de la IA como herramienta de la animación digital, animación 3D y animación 2D\. Los resultados muestran una mejora significativa en la eficiencia de producción en etapas como la postproducción y animación de personajes\. Si bien cada tecnología presenta sus ventajas y limitaciones específicas, su integración conjunta optimiza la posproducción, haciendo que las producciones de animación sean más eficientes en cuestiones de tiempo y recursos, teniendo plazos de entrega más accesibles\.

## [The role of sense of mission in rural physical education teachers’ turnover intention: a moderated mediation model](../publications/da65b26e244eff92d309.md)

Weijie Gao; Taotao Li; Wei Zhang

The viability of the physical education teachers in rural areas is critical in the sustainability of the quality of the rural education system and the balance of holistic development of the students\. Nevertheless, such teachers still experience a high turnover intention\. In addition to external policy actions, other aspects need to be looked at internally on the psychological processes that lead to their readiness to stay in the job\. The research follows the Job Demands\-Resources Model and Resource Conservation Theory to develop a moderated mediation model and discuss the change of sense of mission on turnover intention among the rural physical education teachers\. The research is aimed at examining the mediating variable of occupational burnout and the moderating variable of social support\. Methods: Four hundred and thirty six physical education teachers in the township primary and secondary schools in Henan Province, Sichuan Province, and Gansu Province were surveyed by clustering sampling method\. The Chinese versions of the Vocational Calling Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory, Perceived Social supportive Scale as well as Job leaving intention Scale were used as Research instruments\. The SPSS 26\.0 and the PROcess macro \(Model 59\) were used to analyze the data\. Findings: The correlation analysis results demonstrated that there was a positive correlation between the sense of mission and social support, and a negative correlation between the sense of mission and occupational burnout and turnover intention\. Sense of mission had a direct and indirect \(through occupational burnout\) decrease in turnover intention\. Conclusion: The effects of sense of mission on burnout, and the effects of burnout on turnover intention are buffered by social support\- this effect was the greatest in conditions of a low level of social support\. Occupational burnout mediates the mediating role of sense of mission on the turnover intention, social support moderates the first stage \(sense of mission to occupational burnout\) and the second stage \(occupational burnout to turnover intention\) of the mediating process\. The results point to a mediated moderation process and indicate that the stabilization of the rural population of physical education teachers should be done through reinforcing the sense of mission in the teachers and the creation of a strong social support network at the same time\. These measures will assist in alleviating work burnout and eventually decrease the turnover probability\.

## [Bridging accuracy and interpretability in predictive learning analytics: A human\-centered grey\-box approach](../publications/da6b4b8d09e9a4413a00.md)

Ángel Hernández\-García; Julián Chaparro\-Peláez; Carlos Cuenca\-Enrique; Carlos Salcedo\-Valverde

Learning analytics has been increasingly using predictive models to support educational decision\-making\. However, the trade\-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability remains a central challenge that limits how these models can be understood and used by educators\. This study examines grey\-box approaches to performance prediction by comparing two strategies: a theory\-driven approach that groups interaction data into pedagogically meaningful categories, and a data\-driven approach based on raw clickstream events followed by post hoc eXplainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) techniques\. Using clickstream data from three educational contexts with different scales and instructional formats, we empirically compare the predictive performance, interpretability, and pedagogical relevance of both strategies\. The results show that raw\-event models achieve higher predictive performance in the large\-scale online context with rich interaction data, where XAI methods provide relatively stable and consistent explanatory patterns\. In the smaller\-scale blended setting, where platform data capture only part of the learning activity, theory\-driven aggregation provides a predictive advantage, although results become inconclusive in very small cohorts\. The findings indicate that there is no single optimal approach, and that modeling strategies should be selected according to data characteristics, instructional design, and analytic goals\. From a human\-centered learning analytics perspective, the study highlights the importance of methodological alignment for the meaningful and responsible use of predictive models in education\.

## [Mental Workload: Physiological Assessment and Validation Using Visual Stimuli](../publications/da6d70c2048c142bbb2d.md)

Yamini Gogna; Sheela Tiwari; Rajesh Kumar Singla

ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography \(EEG\) in the field of cognitive science\. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty\. As many practical loads are fundamentally intrinsic, the task was designed to specifically induce intrinsic workload \(the productive load as per Cognitive Load Theory \(CLT\)\)\. The experiment used the task: Spot the Difference to create a workload scenario comprising three difficulty levels: spotting five differences, three more differences, and two more differences \(along with retaining the previous differences from working memory\)\. The task was designed intrinsically as the operators are generally occupied with tasks involving working memory and requiring attention towards the varying number of resources\. By utilising the brain signatures a mental workload model was developed employing a Support Vector Machine \(SVM\) as the classifier\. The workload levels were classified within an accuracy range of 84% to 98% \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Moreover, using subjective ratings about the workload on NASA&\#x27;s Task Load Index \(NASA‐TLX\) rating scale, workload scores were obtained for validation corresponding to the difficulty levels\. Finally, a correlation study showed the association of different EEG features with the workload score within a correlation coefficient range of 0\.306 to 0\.748 \( p &lt; 0\.05 2‐tailed\)\. The reported results can also provide new insights into the cognitive workload assessment of the operators at various phases of task loads\. Findings of this type may lead to the industrial and professional measurement and improvement of cognitive aptitude soon\.

## [Mapping Global Pain and Trauma: A Seven\-Domain Framework and the Fundamental Peace Index for the Journey from Shadow to Fundamental Peace](../publications/da74c52abce186fa6a75.md)

Luis Miguel Gallardo

Background More than one billion people live with a mental health condition, roughly seven in ten adults experience at least one traumatic event in their lifetime, and about one in five people living in conflict\-affected settings has a current mental disorder\. Yet these figures describe only the clinically visible part of human suffering\. Loneliness, shame, structural deprivation, loss of meaning, chronic pain and ecological grief sit largely outside the indicators that guide policy, and the disciplines that study them \(psychiatry, public health, peace studies, contemplative science\) rarely share a common map\. Objective This review proposes such a map\. It presents the Global Pain and Trauma Map \(GPTM\), a seven\-domain taxonomy of human suffering, and its inverse, the Fundamental Peace Index \(FPI = 100 − GPTM\), and links both to a staged pathway from &quot;shadow&quot; states to Fundamental Peace\. Methods Integrative narrative review of global epidemiology \(Global Burden of Disease, WHO World Mental Health Surveys, conflict meta\-analyses\), trauma and attachment theory, contemplative and hypnosis neuroscience, and the author&\#x27;s Shadow\-Gift\-Essence \(S\-G\-E\) framework; every statistic was re\-checked against its primary source for this version\. We also report a descriptive analysis of the GPTM platform dataset \(version 4\.9; 196 countries and 321 communities, each scored 0–100 on seven domains\)\. Framework The seven domains are Individual/Psychological \(D1\), Relational/Social \(D2\), Collective/Cultural \(D3\), Structural/Systemic \(D4\), Existential/Spiritual \(D5\), Somatic/Biological \(D6\) and Environmental/Planetary \(D7\)\. A place&\#x27;s GPTM composite is the mean of its seven domain scores; its FPI is 100 minus that composite\. Across the 196 countries the mean composite was 59\.1 \(SD 8\.8; FPI 40\.9\); no country reached FPI 60, and 26 exceeded FPI 50\. Structural pain \(D4\) was the highest\-scoring domain on average and existential pain \(D5\) the lowest, with sharp regional contrasts\. The current scores are expert\-rated estimates, not measurements; their inter\-domain correlations \(r up to 0\.95 between D1 and D2\) suggest substantial rater halo\. We describe a field instrument, the GPTM Village Profile \(GPTM\-V\), that applies the same formula to key\-informant ratings, and grade each proposed intervention by strength of evidence\. Conclusions The GPTM is best understood as a structured hypothesis about where suffering concentrates and how it might be relieved across levels, from the individual to the planetary\. Its value now is heuristic and organising; its scientific value depends on the validation programme set out here, beginning with transparent scoring rules, independent raters and convergence with population survey data\.

## [Designing Genotype\-Based Enrollment Criteria Without a Companion Diagnostic: An FDA Regulatory Case Study in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Cell Therapy](../publications/da75d6f0aca5c459982f.md)

Ruoqian Shi; Peivand Pirouzi

The question of whether a drug candidate requires a companion diagnostic is usually treated as a binary one: either the mechanism depends on a specific genetic alteration, requiring confirmatory testing before use, or it does not, in which case genotype is treated as clinically irrelevant to patient selection\. This article argues, using a representative allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) as a case study, that this binary framing obscures a subtler and more common practice: genotype\-based cohort capping and exclusion criteria used for trial enrichment, distinguishing slower\- from faster\-progressing patient subgroups without constituting, or requiring, a formal companion diagnostic\. The article develops this distinction in detail, situates it within the product&\#x27;s broader evidentiary dispute, proposes a real\-world evidence strategy that accounts explicitly for the enrichment logic used at the trial stage, and closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals designing enrollment criteria for mutation\-agnostic therapies in genetically heterogeneous rare\-disease populations\.Keywords: patient selection; genotype enrichment; companion diagnostic; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; allogeneic cell therapy; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [A comparative study of pseudo\-dipole arrays and standard arrays based on the high\-density DC resistivity method](../publications/da83e12e030d441bb9f2.md)

Xiaoyi Jiang; Shuhai Jiang; Hui Chen; Jianjun Gong; Suiming Liu

High\-density direct current resistivity surveys play a crucial role in characterizing aquifer structures and groundwater contamination\. However, the necessity of using multiple electrode arrays to achieve comprehensive subsurface imaging significantly prolongs field data acquisition, posing challenges to efficient hydrological investigations\. This study validates an efficient approach that employs a single pseudo\-dipole array to derive comprehensive datasets equivalent to those obtained from multiple standard arrays \(e\.g\., Wenner α, β, γ\)\. The pseudo\-dipole configuration, which utilizes fixed reference electrodes positioned at the line ends, demonstrates vertical resolution comparable to that of conventional dipole arrays, while offering superior lateral resolution in our analysis\. Numerical modeling and analytical solutions for homogeneous half\-space, vertical contact, and multi\-anomaly models confirmed that the pseudo\-dipole array exhibits enhanced sensitivity to subsurface anomalies\. Numerical experiments demonstrate that high\-resolution apparent resistivity pseudosections and reliable inversion models, derived from transformed pseudo\-dipole data, can effectively identify hydrological units\. This method provides a time\-efficient solution for detailed aquifer mapping and contamination plume monitoring, thereby enhancing the utility of electrical resistivity tomography in water resource management\.

## [Towards Next\-Generation Artificial Intelligence Models for Integrated Diagnostics Embedding Eye\-Brain Connections](../publications/daab51c82fecac4052f8.md)

Zhen Chen; Cheng Wang; Tianliang Yao; Jianwen Liang; Yijin Huang; Jianfeng Feng; Dongfeng Gu; Pearse A\. Keane; Xiaoying Tang; Yixuan Yuan

Abstract The brain and eye share profound and homologous relationships in terms of development, anatomy, and microcirculatory structures, yet current analyses typically examine them in isolation, limiting cross\-organ insights and the development of integrated artificial intelligence \(AI\) models\. Such a fragmented paradigm also constrains clinical understanding despite growing evidence of shared, anatomically connected, and predictive relationships between ocular and cerebral phenotypes in both brain and eye diseases\. In this context, this review introduces an Eye\-Brain Connection Pyramid, a multiscale organizational framework for examining eye\-brain relationships at three complementary biological levels: genetic and genomic susceptibility, molecular and protein processes, and neurovascular and tissue phenotypes\. The pyramid does not represent a serial causal pathway\. Across these levels, the framework distinguishes shared vulnerability and parallel pathology, direct brain\-to\-eye effects, retinal correlates and predictors of cerebral or systemic disease, and putative eye\-to\-brain causal contributions, which remain insufficiently established in humans\. This framework may inform future clinical research and the development of AI models integrating multimodal cross\-organ data, whose incremental diagnostic value over existing single\-organ and clinical approaches requires prospective validation\. Furthermore, this review presents a comprehensive AI research roadmap, spanning longitudinal prognostic models, explainable algorithms for clinical adoption, validation of incremental clinical value, fundus\-based brain health screening setups, and multi\-site collaboration\. By outlining these priorities, the proposed Eye\-Brain Connection Pyramid provides an organizational framework for investigating integrated eye\-brain diagnostics and for evaluating the potential clinical value of cross\-organ AI in risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and healthcare delivery\.

## [CORA\-CSS: Correlation\-Aware Reputation and Influence\-Capped Fusion for Collusion\-Resilient Cooperative Spectrum Sensing](../publications/dab2fe0551061e6d6c26.md)

Pavani Priya Vyshnavi Nandanavanam

Cooperative spectrum sensing improves primary\-user detection through spatial diversity, but collaborative fusion also creates an attack surface: multiple Byzantine radios can coordinate their reports so that individually plausible observations become collectively dominant\. Existing reputation methods attenuate persistently unreliable radios, while SENTRY\-CSS combines adaptive reliability with selective re\-sensing; however, protected reference labels and arbitrary collusion remain important limitations\. This paper introduces CORA\-CSS, a reference\-free fusion method that combines a rolling residual\-correlation graph, consensus\-based reputation, and a sublinear group\-influence cap\. Each radio is scored against the instantaneous robust median, its reputation is updated from agreement history, and radios exhibiting strongly correlated residuals with sustained deviation receive a multiplicative influence cap before soft fusion\. A reproducible Monte Carlo study models twelve heterogeneous sensing radios, fading\-like sensing variation, noise uncertainty, primary occupancy imbalance, and four attack families\. In the main ten\-seed condition with four colluding Byzantine radios, CORA\-CSS achieves 0\.9659±0\.0100 balanced accuracy, 0\.9677±0\.0103 detection probability, 0\.0358±0\.0125 false\-alarm probability, and 0\.9515±0\.0145 F1\. Reference\-free reputation without the correlation cap reaches 0\.9454 balanced accuracy, while equal\-soft, median, majority, trimmed\-mean, and clean\-calibrated SVM fusion degrade substantially\. CORA\-CSS remains above 0\.96 balanced accuracy with four colluders in the attacker\-count sweep and retains useful performance with five\. A stress test also exposes the boundary of the method: under weak stealth attacks that preserve plausible independent\-looking reports, ordinary equal\-soft fusion can outperform CORA\-CSS\. The contribution is therefore a collusion\-focused robustness mechanism, not a universal replacement for conventional fusion\.

## [Direct mapping from macroscopic attributes to seismic robustness: A trustworthy machine learning framework for regional highway bridges](../publications/dabc56f1372216f5c492.md)

Weichao Lyu; Dezhang Sun; Dai Junwu

For rapid post\-earthquake screening of bridge networks, this study develops a trustworthy machine learning framework to address the computational bottleneck of high\-fidelity simulations\. We propose a direct mapping from macroscopic structural attributes to a continuous seismic robustness index \(RI\)\. By performing random sampling from a uniform distribution over the spectral acceleration \( S a \) domain, fragility functions are converted into deterministic continuous labels for supervised learning\. To prevent information leakage inherent in grouped bridge datasets, leakage\-free GroupKFold cross\-validation is adopted\. Results reveal that conventional random partitioning spuriously inflates the coefficient of determination R 2 ≈ 0\.95 , whereas Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) achieves a realistic R 2 of 0\.78 for cross\-group extrapolation\. Physical consistency is assessed primarily through fixed\-profile RI – S a monotonicity: an S a \-monotone constrained XGBoost model eliminates non\-physical increases of predicted RI with rising demand while retaining accuracy comparable to the unconstrained baseline\. In leave\-one\-class\-out extrapolation tests on unseen single\-span bridges, performance degradation correlates with domain shift quantified via Jensen–Shannon divergence and Population Stability Index, enabling proactive identification of extrapolation risks\. From an engineering perspective, the framework establishes interpretable structure–performance relationships with explicitly defined applicability boundaries\. It supports high\-throughput batch inference and achieves strong portfolio\-level binary screening performance when the continuous RI is thresholded at 60 \(F1\-score = 0\.94\), providing a verifiable baseline for regional emergency resource allocation\. Finally, using the National Bridge Inventory, the constrained model is applied to screen 3536 highway bridges in Los Angeles County under the 1994 Northridge earthquake scenario with USGS ShakeMap S a \( T = 1\.0 \) \. Following a two\-stage applicability check—intensity support examination and structural shift review—macroscopic inventory data are converted into post\-earthquake spatial screening maps that illustrate the regional workflow\.

## [Ưng dụng các mô hình học máy dự báo chiều dài khu xoáy nước nhảy trong kênh chữ nhật](../publications/dac05bd75f8917bbfda0.md)

Hùng Hồ Việt

Chiều dài khu xoáy nước nhảy là một đặc trưng hình học quan trọng, ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến thiết kế công trình tiêu năng\. Việc xác định chính xác đại lượng này có ý nghĩa thực tiễn lớn trong lĩnh vực thủy lợi\. Các công thức thực nghiệm hiện có cho kết quả không nhất quán\. Vì vậy, nghiên cứu này đề xuất và đánh giá hiệu suất dự báo của bốn mô hình tổ hợp cây quyết định: Tăng cường phân loại \(Categorical Boosting \- CB\), Cây bổ sung \(Extra Trees \- ET\), Tăng cường độ dốc \(Gradient Boosting \- GB\) và Tăng cường độ dốc cực đại \(Extreme Gradient Boosting \- XGB\)\. Khác với các nghiên cứu trước, siêu tham số được tối ưu bằng thuật toán Bayes kết hợp kiểm định chéo lặp 10 nhóm, mức độ quan trọng của các biến đầu vào được lượng hóa bằng giá trị SHAP, và độ ổn định của kết quả được kiểm chứng qua 30 lần chia ngẫu nhiên dữ liệu\. Kết quả cho thấy các mô hình học máy cho sai số dự báo nhìn chung thấp hơn các công thức thực nghiệm\. Trên lần chia đại diện, CB dẫn đầu ở cả bốn chỉ số \(NSE = 0,984; MAE = 1,695; RMSE = 2,207; MAPE = 7,13%\)\. Qua 30 lần chia, CB giữ MAE, RMSE và MAPE trung bình thấp nhất\. Do đó, CB là phương pháp dự báo phù hợp nhất, bổ sung cho các công thức thực nghiệm truyền thống trong các trường hợp cần xét đồng thời nhiều yếu tố thủy lực\.

## [Leão XIV e Bartolomeu I diante da inteligência artificial](../publications/dac2e1298a76132f3402.md)

Paulo Augusto Tamanini

A emergência da inteligência artificial \(IA\) deslocou o debate tecnológico para o interior de questões antropológicas, éticas e pastorais que desafiam diretamente a teologia cristã\. Este artigo investiga em que medida as reflexões do Papa Leão XIV e do Patriarca Ecumênico Bartolomeu I sobre a IA podem contribuir para uma resposta cristã comum diante das transformações tecnológicas contemporâneas\. A pesquisa, de natureza qualitativa e bibliográfica\-documental, toma como fontes primárias a Carta Encíclica Magnifica Humanitas, de Leão XIV, e pronunciamentos recentes do Patriarca Bartolomeu I, em diálogo com a antropologia teológica ortodoxa de Ioannis Zizioulas, Dumitru Stăniloae, Christos Yannaras e Vladimir Lossky\. Sustenta\-se que a convergência entre os dois líderes cristãos não consiste em identidade doutrinal, mas em uma convergência antropológica e ética: ambos recusam a redução da pessoa à inteligência funcional, aos dados, à produtividade ou à eficiência e defendem que a técnica seja subordinada à dignidade humana, à responsabilidade, ao bem comum e ao cuidado da criação\. A partir da categoria de Zizioulas de pessoa\-em\-comunhão, o estudo propõe que a IA pode constituir uma nova agenda ecumênica, na qual as Igrejas Católica e Ortodoxa ofereçam testemunho convergente sem apagar suas diferenças confessionais\. Por fim, são formulados princípios éticos e pastorais para o uso eclesial da IA, especialmente nos campos da evangelização, catequese, formação, acompanhamento pastoral e comunicação, defendendo\-se que a tecnologia pode auxiliar a missão da Igreja, mas não substituir a presença, a liberdade, o discernimento e a comunhão pessoais\. Palavras\-chave: Inteligência artificial\. Antropologia teológica\. Pessoa\. Comunhão\. Ecumenismo\. Ética\. Pastoral\.

## [The Reciprocal Longitudinal Associations Between Short\-Form Video Addiction and Cyberbullying Perpetration Among Vocational School Students](../publications/dac4e46d2b0ebc27df79.md)

Danni Gui; Mingkun Ouyang; Yiwen Wang

Previous research has demonstrated the prevalence of short\-form video addiction and cyberbullying perpetration among adolescents\. Nevertheless, longitudinal evidence clarifying the directional associations between the two behaviors, particularly whether such associations reflect within\-person processes, remains limited\. Therefore, this study examined the reciprocal longitudinal associations between short\-form video addiction and cyberbullying perpetration using a three\-wave random intercept cross\-lagged panel model \(RI\-CLPM\) with 6\-month intervals, in a sample of 1,439 vocational school students \( M age = 17\.42 years, SD = 3\.94\)\. The results revealed significant positive between\-person associations, indicating that students reporting elevated short\-form video addiction engaged in more cyberbullying perpetration\. The within\-person effect from cyberbullying perpetration to short\-form video addiction remained significant across all time intervals, whereas the within\-person effect from short\-form video addiction to cyberbullying perpetration was only significant in the later interval\. These findings suggest that the longitudinal association between short\-form video addiction and cyberbullying perpetration involves both stable between\-person differences and dynamic within\-person processes\. This study advances understanding of the dynamic interplay between short\-form video addiction and cyberbullying perpetration among vocational school students and underscores the importance of considering both between\-person and within\-person processes in research on adolescent digital behaviors\.

## [The Challenges of Hyperparameter Tuning for Accurate Causal Effect Estimation](../publications/dac72b57905a6b5f3702.md)

Damian Machlanski; Spyridon Samothrakis; Paul Clarke

ML is playing an increasingly crucial role in estimating causal effects of treatments on outcomes from observational data\. Many ML methods \(&\#x27;causal estimators&\#x27;\) have been proposed for this task\. All of these methods, as with any ML approach, require extensive hyperparameter tuning\. For non\-causal predictive tasks, there is a consensus on the choice of tuning metrics \(e\.g\. mean squared error\), making it simple to compare models\. However, for causal inference tasks, such a consensus is yet to be reached, making a any comparison of causal models difficult\. On top of that, there is no ideal metric on which to tune causal estimators, so one must rely on proxies\. Furthermore, the fact that model selection in causal inference involves multiple components \(causal estimator, ML regressor, hyperparameters, metric\), complicates the issue even further\. In order to evaluate the importance of each component, we perform an extensive empirical study on their combination\. Our experimental setup involves many commonly used causal estimators, regressors \(&\#x27;base learners&\#x27; henceforth\) and metrics applied to four well\-known causal inference benchmark datasets\. Our results show that hyperparameter tuning increased the probability of reaching state\-of\-the\-art performance in average \(\[Formula: see text\]\) and individualised \(\[Formula: see text\]\) effect estimation with only commonly used estimators\. We also show that the performance of standard metrics can be inconsistent across different scenarios\. Our findings highlight the need for further research to establish whether metrics uniformly capable of state\-of\-the\-art performance in causal model evaluation can be found\.

## [A model for children’s drawing content analysis and creativity assessment Integrating DETR target detection and CLIP semantic understanding](../publications/dae3ec6ada3ccf2e8f61.md)

Yuan Yuan

To address the issue of imbalance between semantic depth and spatial understanding in children’s drawing content analysis, an innovative framework integrating DEtection TRansformer \(DETR\) and contrastive language\-image pretraining \(CLIP\) is proposed\. In the concrete implementation, the set prediction of DETR is regarded as the spatial backbone; the CLIP text prompt is inserted in each layer of the decoder; the frame position and semantic embedding are updated simultaneously by cross\-modal attention; the learnable positional encoding and contrastive loss are supplemented, and the zero\-shot metaphor analysis is realized\. In the experiment, a ChildArt\-Open subset \(5000 children’s drawings\) is constructed based on the Google Open Images Dataset \( https://storage\.googleapis\.com/openimages/web/index\.html \), and it is trained in a 32×NVIDIA A100 graphics processing unit environment\. DETR\-CLIP reaches 78\.6%±0\.4 on mAP@0\.5, significantly outperforming DETR’s 62\.3%±0\.6, Deformable DETR’s 71\.5%±0\.5, Faster R\-CNN\+CLIP’s 73\.8%±0\.6, RT\-DETR’s 74\.2%±0\.5, DINO\-DETR’s 75\.1%±0\.4, and YOLOv8’s 72\.6%±0\.6\. Ablation experiments show that creativity scoring accuracy drops by 15\.1% after removing the cross\-modal interaction module\. Semantic understanding accuracy decreases by 9\.1% after removing CLIP semantic guidance\. The model’s inference speed is 45 frames per second FPS, the number of parameters is 196\.9 M, and Floating\-point Operations \(FLOPs\) are 156\.2 G\. The model captures long\-distance dependence through the Transformer’s global attention mechanism and breaks through the closed category restrictions by combining CLIP’s open semantic space to symbolic expression in children’s drawings\. The results provide an extensible new path of aesthetic evaluation for low\-resource scenes\.

## [Pavlovian Approaches to Preventing Impulsive Choice: Envisioning an Ideal School\-Based Prevention Program](../publications/dae716b3657fbb93fe1d.md)

Gregory J\. Madden; Katherine Garland; Juan Molano\-Gallardo; Alexey Bukreyev; Saba Mahmoudi; Richard A\. Colombo

Abstract Impulsive choice—preference for a smaller\-sooner over a larger\-later reward—is a transdiagnostic risk factor for behaviors that harm human health\. Preventing a temporally extended pattern of impulsive choice should be a translational research priority\. No existing intervention meets all the criteria outlined in this article of an ideal school\-based prevention program: low cost, low teacher effort, fast\-acting, and capable of producing lasting, generalizable reductions in impulsive choice\. Here, we evaluate Pavlovian conditioning as a candidate approach\. Our review is informed by evidence from nonhuman laboratory experiments and kindergarten classroom studies examining whether appetitive Pavlovian conditioning protocols can reduce impulsive choice and related behaviors\. Laboratory experiments demonstrate that a brief Pavlovian conditioning protocol establishes a conditioned stimulus \(CS\) that may then be strategically used to reduce impulsive choice in rats by serving as an attractive antecedent and/or an appetitive delay\-bridging stimulus\. Studies conducted in kindergarten classrooms show that a class\-wide protocol can establish an appetitive CS with minimal teacher training and classroom disruption\. Presenting the CS during an in\-situ waiting task reduced children&\#x27;s challenging behaviors and presenting it during academic\-choice tasks increased children&\#x27;s willingness to work for larger rewards\. This preliminary evidence supports the continued exploration of Pavlovian conditioning approaches to efficiently prevent patterns of impulsive choice that cumulate over time to negatively affect human health and wellbeing\.

## [Dahms, Harry F\. &amp; Crombez, Joel: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Digital Ontotheology: Toward a Critical Rethinking of Science Fiction as Theory](../publications/db132e37f6434dedef9d.md)



\_Bulletin of Science, Technology and Society\_ 35 \(3\-4\):104\-113\. 2015In utopian/science fiction literature, comprehensive knowledge is a familiar motif that also inspires recent policies to screen society through surveillance\. In the late 20th century, a digital archive promised to facilitate quick access to abundant information and effective strategies to confront myriad challenges\. Yet, today, the scale and scope of information accumulation in national and corporate repositories is reaching proportions whose intelligent processing excedes human capabilities, and triggering a shift in focus from dumb repository to artificial intelligence\. Processing such accumulation of knowledge necessiates skills commonly attributed to divinity\. Without a theory that recognizes this condition and informs the operations of artificial intelligence, the latter is likely to fail in human ways, e\.g\., by perceiving false patterns resulting from flawed theories assigning meaning to knowledge\. For successful pattern recognition to occur, theories must rest on science fiction and a digital ontotheology of the machine as the form this archive assumes\.
