## [Fair Credit Decision Assurance: An Ethical Governance Framework For AI\-Based Credit Scoring in Bangladesh with Islamic Finance Duties](../publications/db14dd492948084eac6e.md)

Sumaia Yasmin Keya; Niger Sultana; Md\. Baharul Hasan; Md\. Shahed Alamm; Md\. Aminul Islam; Ummey Sumaiya

Purpose: Machine\-learning credit scoring can extend formal credit to people with thin files, but alternative data can also turn social disadvantage into apparently neutral risk scores\. This paper develops a governance framework for AI\-based credit scoring in Bangladesh and adapts it to the duties of Islamic financial institutions\. Design/methodology/approach: The study is a structured integrative review combined with policy and doctrinal analysis\. It synthesizes peer\-reviewed research on algorithmic lending, fairness and explainability; international benchmarks \(the EU AI Act, U\.S\. adverse action guidance, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the OECD AI Principles\); Bangladeshi instruments on e\-KYC, credit information, digital nano\-loans, e\-loans and data protection; and Islamic finance sources on maqasid al\-Shariah, gharar and Shariah governance\. Findings: Bangladesh now permits fully digital small\-value lending, yet its current instruments say little about model validation, bias testing, reason\-giving or contestation\. Predictive accuracy alone is an inadequate standard because a model can improve portfolio performance while concentrating false rejections on women, rural applicants or new\-to\-credit borrowers\. Originality/value: The paper proposes a Fair Credit Decision Assurance \(FCDA\) model with six gates: lawful data, feature relevance, fairness testing, explanation, human reconsideration and monitoring\. A Shariah overlay adds product\-level review and treats unexplained adverse decisions as a governance concern related to gharar\. Practical implications: The model gives banks, finance companies, mobile financial service providers and Bangladesh Bank a staged route to supervising algorithmic credit without halting innovation\.

## [At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver Frontier](../publications/db210dcba003a701089f.md)

Marco Dos Santos; Vivek Veeriah; Alex Havrilla; Andrew Bolt; Goran Zuzic; Satinder Singh; Tom Zahavy

Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics\-\-\-ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long\-standing open conjectures\-\-\-have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve\. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human\-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions\. To push beyond static challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver \(BB\) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally open\-ended\. Because no algorithm can compute the Busy Beaver number $\\mathrm\{BB\}\(n\)$ for every $n$, this domain provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof\. In this paper, we introduce a Gemini\-based agentic pipeline that automatically discovers accelerations of Turing machines, expressed as compact mathematical rules summarizing many execution steps\. Our system integrates pattern recognition, automated conjecturing, informal mathematical reasoning, and formal theorem proving in Lean\. With this framework, our system autonomously discovered and formally verified novel Collatz\-like accelerations for eleven machines in $\\mathrm\{BB\}\(6\)$\. Subject to community acceptance, we provisionally classify these machines as Cryptids, namely machines whose blank\-tape executions admit exact, compact mathematical descriptions but whose halting behavior remains unresolved\. These results advance the analysis of $\\mathrm\{BB\}\(6\)$ holdouts on the Busy Beaver frontier and demonstrate the potential of autonomous AI systems for open\-ended mathematical discovery in fundamental computer science\.

## [Steam explosion\-induced remodeling of volatile metabolites in Lysimachia foenum\-graecum essential oil revealed by GC\-MS and chemometric analysis](../publications/db26ce3d7f657db863ea.md)

Lei Li; Yongzhen Zhao; Xiao Chen; Changtong Lu; Jiaming Zhao; Haoyang Chen; Gaolei Xi; Pengfei Yang; Miao Liang; Qingfu Wang; Yibo Ning

Lysimachia foenum\-graecum is an aromatic plant rich in diverse volatile metabolites; however, the complexity of its volatile composition and chemical variability remain challenges for understanding and improving its aromatic characteristics\. This study aimed to investigate steam explosion\-induced remodeling of volatile metabolites in L\. foenum\-graecum essential oils from Guangxi and Yunnan origins\. Steam explosion conditions were optimized using single\-factor experiments combined with an orthogonal experimental design, and volatile profiles of essential oils before and after treatment were characterized by gas chromatography\-mass spectrometry \(GC\-MS\)\. Multivariate statistical analyses were further applied to identify differential volatile compounds associated with steam explosion treatment\. Although the individual optima observed in the single\-factor experiments differed from those of the final combination, orthogonal optimization identified a residence time of 60 s, a moisture addition ratio of 30%, and a steam pressure of 1\.5 MPa as the optimal combination, yielding an essential oil yield of 0\.603% ± 0\.009%\. A total of 95 volatile compounds were identified from essential oils of the two geographical origins\. Although the total volatile content decreased after steam explosion treatment, distinct alterations in volatile metabolite profiles were observed, characterized by the selective reduction of phenolic compounds and long\-chain fatty acids and their derivatives\. OPLS\-DA clearly differentiated untreated and treated samples, and 20 key differential compounds were identified using VIP &gt; 1 and p &lt; 0\.05, most of which were long\-chain fatty acids and their derivatives, including cis\-9\-hexadecenoic acid, methyl linoleate, methyl linolenate, and \(E\)\-phytol\. Despite the reduction in the total GC\-MS\-detectable volatile content, steam explosion altered the volatile composition of L\. foenum\-graecum \. Sensory evaluation showed trends toward increased herbal and roasted attributes, although these changes were not statistically significant\. This study provides new insights into steam explosion\-induced regulation of volatile metabolite composition in aromatic plants and highlights its potential as a physicochemical strategy for modulating the chemical profiles of L\. foenum\-graecum \.

## [Regional Development Performance and Poverty Reduction in Aceh: A Panel ARDL Analysis of Regencies and Municipalities, 2010–2025](../publications/db29d70a57f0a060e39d.md)

Nival Misbahul Amin; Helmi; Wais Alqarni; Maimun Maimun

Poverty remains a persistent development challenge in Aceh, particularly given the differences in human development, labor market conditions, and economic characteristics across regencies and municipalities\. This study examines the dynamic relationship between the Human Development Index \(HDI\), Open Unemployment Rate \(OUR\), and Gross Regional Domestic Product \(GRDP\) per capita and poverty in 23 regencies and municipalities in Aceh Province over the period 2010–2025, with particular attention to short\-run and long\-run dynamics and the adjustment process toward long\-run equilibrium\. Using a quantitative approach, the study employs the Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag \(ARDL\) method\. The Pooled Mean Group \(PMG\) and Mean Group \(MG\) estimators are compared, with the Hausman test used to determine the appropriate estimator, while the lag structure is selected based on the Akaike Information Criterion \(AIC\)\. The MG estimates show that HDI has a negative and statistically significant relationship with poverty in the long run, with a coefficient of −1\.384952 \(p&lt;0\.01\)\. In contrast, OUR and GRDP per capita do not exhibit statistically significant long\-run relationships with poverty\. In the short run, lagged changes in GRDP per capita are negatively and significantly associated with changes in poverty, with a coefficient of −0\.000299 \(p&lt;0\.01\), whereas changes in HDI, OUR, and current GRDP per capita are not statistically significant\. The Error Correction Term \(ECT\) of −0\.789703 \(p&lt;0\.01\) indicates that approximately 78\.97% of deviations from the long\-run equilibrium are corrected within one period\. These findings contribute empirical evidence to the study of regional development by demonstrating that the relationship between development and poverty in Aceh is dynamic and heterogeneous, highlighting the importance of considering both temporal dynamics and differences across regions in understanding poverty reduction\.

## [PENERAPAN BELAJAR BERMAKNA MELALUI STRATEGI EKSPERIMEN PADA MATERI SENYAWA POLAR UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KREATIVITAS SISWA KELAS XI](../publications/db2b17572654af5e7b22.md)

Hafiz Ariel Al\-Rizqi; Tasya Ruwanda Wiana; Indah Kencanawati; Titin Mairisiska

Penerapan belajar bermakna melalui strategi eksperimen pada materi senyawa polar untuk meningkatkan kreativitas siswa kelas XI\. Pembelajaran kimia pada materi senyawa polar masih menghadapi kendala karena konsepnya bersifat abstrak sehingga siswa cenderung menghafal tanpa memahami keterkaitannya dengan fenomena kehidupan sehari\-hari\. Kondisi tersebut berdampak pada rendahnya kreativitas siswa dalam proses pembelajaran\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis penerapan pembelajaran bermakna melalui strategi eksperimen dalam meningkatkan kreativitas siswa kelas XI MAN 1 Sungai Penuh pada materi senyawa polar\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain One\-Group Pretest–Posttest\. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes kreativitas, lembar observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, uji normalitas Shapiro–Wilk, uji Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank, N\-Gain, dan effect size\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest \(Z = ?4,62; p &lt; 0,001\), dengan 27 siswa mengalami peningkatan kreativitas\. Nilai N\-Gain sebesar 0,127 termasuk kategori rendah, namun menunjukkan adanya peningkatan setelah perlakuan\. Dengan demikian, pembelajaran bermakna melalui strategi eksperimen efektif meningkatkan kreativitas siswa serta memberikan pengalaman belajar yang lebih aktif, kontekstual, dan bermakna pada materi senyawa polar\.

## [Solving operating room scheduling problems using large language model based multi\-agent architecture](../publications/db404d223c3b6e853eaa.md)

Chu Tang; Qu Wei; Haitao Liu; Zekun Jiang; Xiaobo Zhou; Yu Cao; Kang Li

Efficient operating room scheduling is a complex task due to the diversity of surgical types, high patient demand, and limited hospital resources\. Since OR operations account for a substantial share of hospital costs, effective scheduling solutions are critical\. Large language model \(LLM\)\-based multi\-agent systems offer new opportunities to support optimization for this problem\. This study evaluates an LLM\-based multi\-agent framework for generating and refining optimization code for OR scheduling\. Leveraging iterative collaboration among specialized agents, the proposed iterative multi\-agent \(IMA\) framework consistently outperformed both single\-agent and traditional multi\-agent baselines\. Across 10 LLMs and 35 scenarios, IMA achieved an average feasible schedule rate of 82\.91%, compared with 65\.59% and 52\.53% for the baselines\. Experiments on 1050 synthetic cases and three real OR datasets further showed that IMA\-generated code produced solutions close to those of expert\-written mixed\-integer programming models, while a case study of hospital as\-is schedules demonstrated improvements in OR utilization and overtime reduction\. These results suggest that LLM\-based multi\-agent systems can provide a practical and effective approach for OR scheduling optimization\.

## [Residual\-gated generative additive joint\-bias identification and uncertainty\-weighted fault compensation for quadruped robots with scarce data](../publications/db561b29900c2122533b.md)

Likai Wu; Meina Zhang; Dengyan Li; Cao Yanna

Repeated actuator\-fault injection on a physical quadruped is costly and can damage motors or gearboxes, which makes continuous fault\-value identification difficult when only scarce sequences are available\. This study targets command\-equivalent additive joint bias\. A temporal generator is trained with adversarial and temporal objectives, while an acceptance gate screens synthetic windows using an aggregate score of attitude\-integration, first\-order joint\-kinematic, torque\-limit, and command\-limit residuals\. A heteroscedastic identifier combines dense feature reuse, temporal convolution, bidirectional recurrent features, and cross\-attention fusion to estimate the bias and predictive variance\. The resulting estimate is converted into an uncertainty\-weighted compensation command, with amplitude and rate constraints enforced by final\-output projection over their feasible intersection\. Controller\-level simulations include four additive\-bias profiles at the 12 actuated joints and representative same\-leg and diagonal two\-joint cases\. In the reference sinusoidal single\-calf\-joint evaluation, the method reduces identification RMSE from 0\.1404 rad for deterministic DGTNet to 0\.1180 rad and reports an interval calibration error of 0\.031\. With matched controller protections, uncertainty weighting reduces mean recovery time from 0\.764 to 0\.743 s and RMS command variation from 0\.00671 to 0\.00651 rad\. Across the four single\-joint profile groups, the proposed RMSE ranges from 0\.1194 to 0\.1428 rad, compared with 0\.1421 to 0\.1696 rad for DGTNet\. Same\-leg and diagonal paired faults yield RMSE values of 0\.1584 and 0\.1510 rad and attitude\-recovery rates of 74\.6% and 77\.4%, respectively\. Outdoor physical\-robot tests with eight runs per configuration show a 54\.8% reduction in mean RMS attitude error relative to uncompensated faulty walking, with similar outcomes for constant and uncertainty\-weighted confidence\.

## [Epigenetics of generalized internet use disorder including data on overuse of social media: a closer look at the SLC6A4, NR3C1 and OXT genes](../publications/db619fcc7ea2c679ac54.md)

Christian Montag; Markus Kiefer; Bernhard J\. Connemann; Thomas Kammer; Simon Sanwald

BACKGROUND: Only few studies so far have investigated the molecular underpinnings of Internet Use Disorders \(IUD\), which can shed light on the neurochemical basis of excessive online behaviors\. There are even less epigenetic studies in this research field, and longitudinal evidence is even more scarce\. METHODS: The present study investigated in n = 83 depressed patients and n = 83 healthy controls potential links between DNA\-methylation of three candidate genes \(serotonin transporter gene SLC6A4, glucocorticoid receptor gene NR3C1 and gene coding for oxytocin OXT\) known to play a role in affective disorders and self\-reported excessive Internet and problematic social media use over a two\-week period\. RESULTS: In depressed patients, we found a significant positive association between problematic social media use, IUD tendencies in general, craving and methylation of a CpG site in NR3C1\. In healthy controls, we found a significant positive association between social support and methylation of a CpG site in OXT\. Further we found that higher social media addiction tendencies were associated with decreasing differences in methylation of OXT over a two\-week period in both the group of depressed patients and healthy controls\. However, this effect was small and the confidence interval contained zero\. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings might provide first preliminary indications that NR3C1 and OXT might be involved in overuse of social media\. However, small effect sizes and complex interaction effects require replication in larger samples with longitudinal measurements over a longer time period\.

Yulia Logvynenko; Larysa Sytnyk

КАЛЕЙДОСКОП МОВ СИНТЕЗ МОВНО\-КОМУНІКАТИВНОЇ ТА ІНФОРМАЦІЙНО\-ЦИФРОВОЇ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТЕЙ ПЕДАГОГІВ БАЗОВОЇ ТА ПРОФІЛЬНОЇ ШКІЛ: ПРАКТИЧНИЙ АСПЕКТ У розвідці теоретично обґрунтовано та практично проаналізовано механізми синергетичного синтезу мовно\-комунікативної \(А1\) та інформаційно\-цифрової \(А3\) компетентностей учителя в умовах реформування Нової української школи, зокрема на етапі переходу здобувачів освіти до профільної школи\.Визначено, що в сучасному освітньому просторі мовна, комунікативна та інформативна компетентності вчителя стають фундаментом для ефективної взаємодії учасників освітнього процесу\.Авторками запропоновано методичні стратегії підвищення кваліфікації вчителів\-предметників, що базуються на створенні життєвих симуляцій і компетентнісно\-орієнтованих завдань\.Результати дослідження спрямовані на подолання цифрового розриву та формування професійної стійкості педагога в умовах трансформації освітньої системи\.

A\. Razia Sulthana; Priyanshi Kumari

This repository contains the code and data provenance documentation supporting the review article &quot;Empowering Sustainable Vertical Farming Through IoT and AI\-Driven Technologies: A Technical Blueprint with Insights from the UK and India&quot; \. As a systematic PRISMA\-based literature review, the study does not involve original experimental or primary data collection; instead, all quantitative values used in the manuscript&\#x27;s tables and figures were extracted and synthesised from previously published peer\-reviewed literature, industry reports, and government/institutional publications through a four\-stage process of extraction, cross\-validation, standardisation, and weighted averaging, with full source citations provided in the manuscript\. ## [Decentering the Sharia Court: Practical Authority and Islamic Legal Pluralism in Sierra Leone](../publications/db72ad7585cc36890dfd.md)

Thomas Sheku Marah; FATHIMA ADILA SHUHOOD; Sherene Keskin

Scholarship on Islamic legal pluralism has largely taken the Sharia court as its measure of institutional significance, asking how Islamic norms are incorporated, accommodated, or made enforceable by the state\. Sierra Leone resists that starting point\. Its Constitution and the local courts Act 2011 recognise customary adjudication, and the Mohammedan Marriage Act gives civil effect to Muslim marriages, yet no Sharia court exists and no Islamic adjudicatory jurisdiction has been delegated to any religious institution\. This article asks how Sharia\-informed mediation acquires practical authority under these conditions\. It uses a qualitative documentary socio\-legal case study of constitutional and statutory texts, justice\-sector and governance reports, and peer\-reviewed scholarship, read through Griffiths, Moore, Tamanaha, and Weber\. The analysis finds that such mediation derives no jurisdiction from the state but operates in a plural justice environment\. Community recognition, Islamic normative legitimacy, established mediation practice, and uneven access to courts and legal aid leave room for religious actors to take part in dispute resolution\. The article defines practical authority as the socially recognised capacity of a non\-state normative institution to structure, facilitate, or influence dispute resolution without state\-delegated adjudicatory competence, and distinguishes it from formal jurisdiction, normative authority, and social legitimacy\. Because the evidence is documentary, the findings do not establish how often mediation occurs, whether disputants prefer it, or whether its outcomes are complied with\. The article decentres the court as the measure of Islamic legal authority and shows how religious normativity can matter institutionally without becoming jurisdictional\.

## [Surface Display of Lactobacillus plantarum Glutamate Decarboxylase on Escherichia coli for GABA Production](../publications/db787b3976ab8cd8ae96.md)

Kéryanne Gagnon; Chantelle Tran; Mikaela Yeap; Elena Yu

γ\-aminobutyric acid \(GABA\) is an important metabolite used in neuroscience research and various industrial formulations, including those in the food, nutraceutical and mental health sectors\. As environmentally responsible manufacturing practices continue to gain attention, the microbial production of GABA has become an attractive alternative to chemical synthesis\. Specifically, microbial surface\-display platforms provide a sustainable route for GABA production through the extracellular conversion of L\-glutamate to GABA by the B isoform of the enzyme glutamate decarboxylase \(GadB\)\. Autotransporters can serve as secretion machinery for high\-molecular weight passenger proteins, such as GadB\. Here, we engineered the Bordetella pertussis BrkA autotransporter to display Lactobacillus plantarum GadB as the passenger protein on the surface of Escherichia coli UT5600\. We successfully generated the recombinant pGADBLP plasmid via inverse PCR and Gibson Assembly, with proper construction confirmed by HindIII digestion and Nanopore sequencing\. Western blotting, combined with a trypsin accessibility assay, further indicated that the BrkA\-GadB construct was expressed at the cell surface\. To evaluate GadB enzymatic activity, we optimized a thin\-layer chromatography workflow detecting the conversion of extracellular L\-glutamate to GABA\. Preliminary results suggested low\-level production of GABA due to BrkA\-GadB\. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that BrkA can export and display GadB at the E\. coli surface and provide early evidence of catalytic function, supporting the future development of whole\-cell biocatalysts for sustainable GABA production\.

## [Towards a Digital Twin for the Quantitative Risk Assessment of Domino Effects in Fuel Storage Facilities](../publications/db79ecea5e7e8e6b9f0a.md)

Yanelys Cuba Arana; Felipe San Luis Gutiérrez; Deivis Ávila; Jesús Luis Orozco; Ramón Quiza

Fuel storage facilities concentrate large inventories of flammable substances, so that a single primary accident may escalate, through thermal radiation, into a cascading sequence involving several tanks \(domino effect\)\. This work presents the probabilistic core of a digital twin for such facilities, understood as a probabilistic replica of the facility with a fast query interface \(live\-data assimilation is not yet implemented\): a permanently available, interactively queryable model that characterises, in probabilistic terms, the thermal radiation field generated by accident scenarios in a storage facility and derives from it an integrated assessment of its safety and economic risk\. The framework combines \(i\) a Monte Carlo simulation of 108 facility\-years, in which primary accidents and their fire\-driven escalation are sampled using validated models of pool fires, thermal radiation and equipment failure; \(ii\) a point\-wise condensation of the resulting radiation intensity into Gamma distributions fitted by maximum likelihood, whose parameter maps embody the frequency of every fire configuration; and \(iii\) a machine\-learning surrogate, based on Generalized Regression Neural Networks, that renders the probabilistic field continuous over the terrain and evaluable in a fraction of a millisecond\. On this backbone, the model delivers mutually consistent, receptor\-level indicators: annual exceedance frequencies of harm thresholds \(contour maps\), the expected number of fatalities, distinguishing sheltered and outdoor population, and the Expected Annual Loss of every asset\. In a demonstration on a five\-tank facility storing light naphtha, jet fuel and diesel within a mixed industrial–residential complex, 16\.5% of the accidents escalated to multiple tanks, the individual risk at the most exposed third\-party location lay more than one order of magnitude below the 10−6 per year land\-use criterion, and 97\.5% of the expected losses were borne by the facility itself\. The scope is limited to pool fires in fixed\-roof atmospheric tanks, in wind\-free conditions and without credited safety barriers\.

## [When theories become movements: the controversy in consciousness science from a sociological perspective](../publications/db7af422ac55748b2f01.md)

David Barbera‐Tomás; Camilo Miguel Signorelli; Adrián A\. Díaz‐Faes

This article analyzes the ongoing controversy in consciousness science surrounding Integrated Information Theory \(IIT\) from a sociological perspective\. Drawing on Frickel and Gross’s \(2005\) framework of Scientific/Intellectual Movements \(SIMs\), the study examines four key social processes that enabled IIT’s emergence and consolidation as a successful SIM: \(i\) the role of high\-status actors rooted in ties to Nobel laureates, \(ii\) entrepreneurial resource mobilization through an adversarial collaboration program, \(iii\) sustained micromobilization within a major conference venue, and \(iv\) the strategic framing of IIT through mathematical formalism\. We extend Frickel and Gross’s \(2005\) framework in two directions\. First, by conceptualizing the collective IIT\-Concerned – a group of 124 scholars who publicly labeled IIT as “pseudoscience” – as a scientific countermovement \(counter\-SIM\), adapting a concept from social movement theory to the analysis of scientific conflict\. Second, by analyzing how this countermovement engages in boundary\-work, invoking shifting social values to justify the exclusion of IIT from legitimate science\. The analysis shows that the controversy is best understood not merely as a theoretical disagreement, but as a clash between a movement and a countermovement, each mobilizing distinct social and epistemic resources\. Cultivating greater reflexivity about the sociological realities of scientific practice would help participants in the controversy and researchers more broadly, manage its consequences and prevent lasting damage to the field of consciousness science\.

## [Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears](../publications/db90e84aa627a3720c5b.md)

Haitao Wang; Deming Guo; Yingqi Gao; Weixin Xian; Liyan Zhang

BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears\. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway\. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English\-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff\-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis\. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics\. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS\-2 and prediction\-model studies with PROBAST\. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically\. RESULTS: Sixty\-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image\-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised\-phenotyping study\. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data\. QUADAS\-2 classified overall risk\-of\-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36\. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction\-model studies as high risk\-of\-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated\. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis\-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference\. CONCLUSION: AI has proof\-of\-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment\. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical\-utility assessment, and standardized task\-specific reporting are required\.

## [Prevalence of Nomophobia among Nursing students: A Crosssectional Study](../publications/db9105c1df623c18ba10.md)

Mala Govindasamy; Shivasankari Selvaraj Lakshmi; Delvi Arockiarajan; Urmila Umasekar

Nomophobia, defined as the fear or anxiety of being without a mobile phone, is an emerging behavioural condition among young adults, particularly students\. Nursing students are highly dependent on smartphones for academic and clinical communication, making them vulnerable to nomophobia\. This study was conducted to assess the prevalence of nomophobia among nursing students and its association with selected sociodemographic variables\. A quantitative descriptive cross\-sectional design was adopted among 100 nursing students selected using purposive sampling\. Data were collected using a structured sociodemographic tool and the standardized 20\-item Nomophobia Questionnaire \(NMP\-Q\)\. The scores were categorized into mild, moderate, and severe nomophobia\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and ANOVA, and p &lt; 0\.05 was considered statistically significant\. The findings revealed that 49% of participants were aged 16–18 years and 71% were female\. The mean nomophobia score was 74\.01 ± 18\.3, indicating a moderate level of nomophobia\. The majority of students \(78%\) had moderate nomophobia, followed by mild \(17%\) and severe \(5%\)\. Overall, 95% of participants exhibited some level of nomophobia\. A statistically significant association was found between nomophobia scores and family monthly income \(p = 0\.017\) and source of previous knowledge \(p = 0\.037\), while other demographic variables were not significant\. This study highlights a high prevalence of moderate nomophobia among nursing students, consistent with global evidence of increasing smartphone dependency in young adults\.

## [GEMS: Molecular Structure Elucidation as Learned Search over Isomer Graphs](../publications/db9a312159d05462d9cf.md)

Utku Umur Acikalin; Yingheng Wang; Goncalo J\. Gouveia; Tyler J\. Schwertfeger; Frank C\. Schroeder; Carla P\. Gomes

Identifying small\-molecule structures from molecular formulas and tandem mass spectra remains a bottleneck in untargeted metabolomics and natural\-product discovery\. Even when database retrieval or de novo prediction misses the exact structure, the resulting candidates can provide starting points for exploring nearby structures through a few bond edits\. We introduce GEMS \(Guided Editing of Molecular Structures\), which refines candidates through learned 2\-switch bond edits that preserve the molecular formula and each atom&\#x27;s total valence\. GEMS uses MIST, a pretrained spectrum\-to\-fingerprint model, to predict fingerprint probabilities once per spectrum\. A neural policy compares each candidate&\#x27;s fingerprint with these predictions, links present features to the atoms and bonds that generate them, and scores all valid edits in one forward pass\. The policy is trained on shortest edit paths between structures, so it can be pretrained on PubChem isomers without spectra and then fine\-tuned with spectrum\-predicted fingerprints\. At inference, GEMS searches from multiple initial candidates matching the supplied molecular formula and ranks candidates by fingerprint agreement and multi\-start consensus\. With the target structure excluded from PubChem initialization, three edit rounds achieve Hit@1/Hit@10 of 29\.64%/50\.81% on NPLIB1 and 30\.22%/41\.33% on MassSpecGym, exceeding published baselines under comparable settings\. On NPLIB1, GEMS achieves higher identification accuracy in about 3\.3 minutes end to end, compared with 26\.2 hours for our FRIGID run\. GEMS also improves identification from generated candidates, including those refined by FRIGID\. Experiments with exact target fingerprints identify fingerprint prediction error as a bottleneck in target recovery and final ranking\. Deeper search recovers additional targets without retraining, with larger gains from weaker initial candidates\.

## [Rising stroke burden in Uganda: A national time\-series analysis and forecasts, 2016–2028](../publications/db9bb683af026bc85ed3.md)

Suzan Nakasendwa; Joan Nankya Mutyoba; Alex Riolexus Ario; Evans Otieno Omondi; Brenda Birungi Bashemera; Francis Kakooza; Letisha Najjemba; Joyce Nakatumba Nabende; David Guwatudde; Agnes Kiragga

INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low\- and middle\-income Countries\. However, evidence on national temporal trends and potential impacts in Uganda remains limited\. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028\. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time\-series analysis of District Health Information System \(DHIS2\) from 2016 to 2025\. Monthly stroke cases, and deaths were analyzed\. Monthly populations of Uganda were estimated using exponential growth interpolation and incorporated as an offset term in Bayesian negative binomial regression models to estimate incidence rate ratios \(IRR\) at 95% confidence interval \(CI\)\. Decomposition analysis using the Kitagawa method was applied to derive contributions from population growth and epidemiological change, based on model estimates\. Stationarity and autocorrelation were assessed using the unit root and Ljung\-Box tests\. Forecasting was performed using the exponential smoothing state\-space \(ETS\) model at 80% prediction intervals \(PI\)\. RESULTS: Trend analysis showed sustained monthly increases in stroke incidence and mortality with IRR; 1\.005 \(95% CI: 1\.004\-1\.006\), and 1\.006 \(95% CI: 1\.005\-1\.007\), respectively \(all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The epidemiological effect was approximately twice as large as the population effect, indicating that the majority of the increase in stroke cases and deaths is attributable to rising incidence rates rather than population growth alone\. ETS model demonstrated that by December 2028, monthly cases and deaths are projected to reach approximately 927 \(80% PI: 709\-1,156\) and 126 \(80% PI: 94\-160\), respectively\. CONCLUSION: Stroke burden in Uganda is projected to continue increase further over the next years in the absence of effective prevention measures\. Strengthened primary prevention, expanded acute stroke care capacity, and improved surveillance systems are urgently needed to mitigate the growing health system impact\.

## [Comparative Analysis of IoT Security Architectures: A Context\-Aware Security–Resource Suitability Framework](../publications/db9dbe3a8fc5794d0cde.md)

Dr\. S\. B\. Sarvaiya, Vedanti C\. Yawalkar, Sakshi K\. Rohankar

The Internet of Things \(IoT\) links sensors, cameras, appliances, vehicles, medical devices and industrial controllers to networks and cloud platforms\. This reach creates security problems that conventional networks rarely face: mixed hardware, scarce resources, devices that stay in service for years, wireless links and sensitive data\. This paper compares three representative IoT security architectures, the three\-layer, five\-layer and Fog/Edge\-based models, using published literature and recognised cybersecurity guidance\. Each is examined along seven dimensions: security coverage, performance, scalability, privacy, resource efficiency, manageability over the device lifecycle, and interoperability\. The main contribution is a Context\-Aware Security–Resource Suitability Index \(SRSI\), which reweights these dimensions to suit the application instead of declaring one architecture best in every case\. Literature\-informed scores are applied to healthcare, smart\-home and industrial or agricultural settings\. Fog/Edge gives the best overall balance in every scenario tested, while the three\-layer model stays attractive where low complexity and frugal resource use come first\. The study also argues that lifecycle manageability deserves the same attention as traditional security metrics\. SRSI is offered as a transparent decision\-support method\. Its scores are analytical, so validation on real testbeds with measured latency, energy, detection and resilience data is left for future work

## [Machine\-learning\-enhanced discretize\-then\-project reduced\-order modeling of turbulent flows on collocated grids](../publications/dbab0b83410d34a8a706.md)

Nadim Rooholamin; Kabir Bakhshaei; Giovanni Stabile

This study presents a hybrid reduced\-order modeling \(ROM\) framework for incompressible flows on collocated finite\-volume grids, combining a discretize\-then\-project consistent\-flux formulation for velocity and pressure with a non\-intrusive neural\-network closure for turbulent viscosity\. The intrusive formulation preserves discrete mass conservation and pressure\-velocity coupling, while a reduced pressure reference\-cell constraint fixes pressure gauge ambiguity\. We evaluate Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\), Transformer, and Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) closures\. For a three\-dimensional lid\-driven cavity at $Re=100$, the LSTM\-based ROM achieves relative errors of 0\.7% in velocity and 4% in turbulent viscosity\. At $Re=3200$, a mode\-sensitivity study identifies $N=15$ POD modes as the best overall configuration, balancing accuracy, dimension, robustness, and cost\. It yields a final relative velocity error of approximately 12\.3% and an online wall\-clock speedup of approximately $50\\times$ over the full\-order model; energy and enstrophy errors remain below 11% for all three architectures\. This regime requires case\-specific neural\-network retraining and pressure reference\-cell parameter retuning\. In a time\-extrapolation test trained on $t\\in\[0,3\]$,s and rolled out to $t=6$,s, the ROM remains bounded, although velocity and pressure errors increase beyond the training window\. The LSTM turbulent\-viscosity closure remains robust, identifying long\-horizon pressure accuracy as the main limitation\. These results demonstrate the potential of consistent projection\-based modeling combined with data\-driven turbulence closure for efficient reduced\-order simulation\.

## [Analisis Kualitas Butir Soal Pilihan Ganda PAI Berbasis Artificial Intelligence: Komparasi ChatGPT dan Gemini AI](../publications/dbc0d4247a704662c81d.md)

Muhammad Isa Anshari; Fauziah Qhotrun Nada; Mohammad Irsyad

Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dan membandingkan kualitas psikometrik butir soal pilihan ganda Pendidikan Agama Islam \(PAI\) yang dihasilkan ChatGPT dan Gemini AI ditinjau dari validitas, reliabilitas, tingkat kesukaran, dan daya pembeda\. Desain penelitian kuantitatif deskriptif\-komparatif dengan teknik analisis butir soal diujikan pada 54 siswa kelas VIII \(kelas 8C dan 8G\) SMP Negeri 1 Gandusari\. Kedua platform diberi prompt terstruktur identik yang mensyaratkan komposisi 30% LOTS, 40% MOTS, dan 30% HOTS\. Hasil menunjukkan 11 dari 20 butir ChatGPT \(55%\) dan 8 dari 20 butir Gemini \(40%\) dinyatakan valid, tanpa perbedaan proporsi yang signifikan \(p = 0,527\)\. Reliabilitas ChatGPT tergolong rendah \(α = 0,416\) sedangkan Gemini tidak reliabel \(α = \-0,217\)\. Seluruh butir dari kedua platform berkategori mudah, dengan perbedaan signifikan pada tingkat kesukaran \(p = 0,002\)\. Daya pembeda kedua platform tidak berbeda signifikan \(p = 0,174\)\. Disimpulkan bahwa AI generatif dapat mempercepat penyusunan naskah soal, tetapi belum dapat menjamin kualitas psikometrik yang memadai tanpa telaah ahli dan uji coba empiris\.

## [Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness](../publications/dbc38708a0a6f79a9184.md)

Aneesh Komanduri; Majid Afshar; Timothy A\. Miller; Yanjun Gao

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential\. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model&\#x27;s response\. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model&\#x27;s output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens \(Jlens\) concept steering vectors\. Across three open\-source models and five question\-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output\-based uncertainty methods\. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins after training, suggesting that causal robustness provides a mechanistically grounded signal of uncertainty\.

## [Exploring the Interplay of Freshwater Resources, Renewable Energy, and Decarbonization on Education in G20 Nations](../publications/dbc9018b1dc62f0c1207.md)

Xiaowei Duan; Afnan Hassan

ABSTRACT This study aims to empirically examine the role of carbon emissions \(CEM\), freshwater resources \(FWR\), agriculture, forestry, and fisheries resources \(AFFR\), renewable energy consumption \(RENE\), financial inclusion \(FINC\), and technological innovation \(TCI\) on education \(EDC\) of the G20 member states during the period of 2000–2023\. As the main estimation method, this study uses the MMQR\. In addition, the robustness of the results is measured using the CS‐ARDL model along with a control function approach\. According to the MMQR results, CEM, FWR, RENE, and FINC positively affect EDC across most quantiles, while AFFR exerts a negative effect throughout the distribution\. TCI negatively influences lower and middle quantiles but becomes positive at higher quantiles\. The CS‐ARDL findings confirm the positive long‐run effects of FWR, RENE, and FINC, the negative effects of CEM and AFFR, and a negative short‐run but positive long‐run effect of TCI\. The control function results further indicate the relevance of accounting for potential endogeneity associated with FINC and AFFR\. This study makes several contributions to the existing literature by considering education as a dependent variable in a sustainability‐technology approach\.

## [STRUKTUR DAN KAIDAH KEBAHASAAN TEKS LAPORAN HASIL OBSERVASI TULISAN SISWA KELAS X SMA NEGERI 3 MUARO JAMBI](../publications/dbcf8026be4e428b388c.md)

Tiara Amanta Wisesa; Vonny Dahayu Amanda; Afnita

This study describes the structure and linguistic features of observation report texts written by tenth\-grade students of SMA Negeri 3 Muaro Jambi\. The problem addressed is that students&\#x27; observation reports often exhibit incomplete structure, inconsistent labeling, and non\-standard language use\. The purpose is to analyze the completeness of text structure, the use of linguistic features, and spelling and standard language errors\. A descriptive qualitative approach with content analysis was employed\. Data consisted of 28 handwritten observation report texts from an online assignment dated 9 September 2026\. A coding sheet was used to assess structure, labels, linguistic features, and spelling\. Results show that all texts \(100%\) functionally contain the three main structural parts: general statement, description of parts, and closing\. However, only 26 texts \(92\.9%\) include an explicit benefit description\. Only 18 texts \(64\.3%\) write structural labels completely and accurately\. Linguistic features such as definition sentences, relational verbs, technical terms, and conjunctions are present, but non\-standard abbreviations \(e\.g\., yg, dn, tmpt\), mislabeled sections, and first\-person perspective are still found\. Structural completeness does not automatically indicate text quality\. Therefore, learning should emphasize content detail, objectivity, and standard spelling\.

## [Stateful Testing for Deep Learning Compilers](../publications/dbd58b728e3e4fe76b4e.md)

Jiatao Ge; Ruixiang Qian; Yibo Hu; Yanzhou Mu; Yinglong Zou; Jiawei Liu; Zhenyu Chen; Chunrong Fang

Modern deep learning compilers compile models lazily and cache artifacts across invocations\. Retained compiler state can make a later invocation incorrect even when it is correct in isolation\. An analysis of 26 publicly reported issues in PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow shows that detecting such bugs requires sequences that first establish compiler state and then expose a failure\. We present Rondo, a stateful testing method that represents each test case as a model paired with an invocation sequence\. Rondo mutates invocation sequences and uses a Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler guided by compilation behavior to favor rarely observed behaviors\. Its three\-way differential oracle compares execution without compilation, compiled execution with compiler state reset, and compiled execution with state retained\. It confirms stateful bugs by replaying the same invocation with state retained and reset while preserving inputs and program state, then shortens sequences while preserving the original bug\. We evaluate Rondo on four deep learning frameworks using 24 common model architectures\. Rondo detects 117 bugs, including 35 stateful bugs\. We submit 39 bug reports, including 18 for stateful bugs; developers confirm 35 reports, including 16 for stateful bugs, and fix 18 bugs, including 11 stateful bugs\. Rondo achieves the highest behavior coverage and compiler Python source\-line coverage among the compared methods, with 99\.26% alarm precision\. It shortens 44 of 117 invocation sequences, reducing the lengths of these 44 sequences by 83\.34% on average\.

## [Interpretable machine learning identifies predictors of IGF\-1 during growth hormone therapy in boys](../publications/dbd5b3e1205af5cc037d.md)

Helena‐Jamin Ly; Juulia T\. Suvilehto; Beatrice Skyman; Carina Ankarberg‐Lindgren; Hans Fors; Jesper Havsol; Jovanna Dahlgren

Objectives Insulin\-like growth factor\-1 \(IGF\-1\) is widely used to guide growth hormone \(GH\) therapy, yet its predictors during the maintenance phase and puberty remain incompletely understood\. We aimed to predict IGF\-1 standard deviation scores \(SDS\) at 3 and 12 months in GH\-treated boys and to identify key predictors of IGF\-1 dynamics using interpretable modeling approaches\. Methods Data from 72 boys with growth hormone deficiency or idiopathic short stature from a previous Swedish clinical trial were analyzed using early\-life characteristics, GH treatment variables, and puberty\-related measures\. Linear regression, Elastic Net regression, and explainable boosting machine \(EBM\) models were evaluated with nested five\-fold patient\-grouped cross\-validation\. Performance estimates were patient\-balanced, with 95% confidence intervals based on 2,000 patient\-cluster bootstrap resamples\. Results Elastic Net had the highest point estimates at 3 months, but confidence intervals did not establish a difference between the primary models\. No clear differences between models were found at 12 months\. Current IGF\-1 SDS was the most prominent predictive feature, while additional treatment\- and puberty\-related variables were also selected across cross\-validation models\. Conclusion Interpretable modeling approaches provided moderate predictive performance for future IGF\-1 SDS during the maintenance phase and puberty\. The findings indicate that prediction is informed by current IGF\-1 SDS together with additional clinical variables, but further validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical application\.

## [AB Üye Ülkelerinde İşletmelerin Pazarlama Amaçlı Yapay Zekâ Kullanımındakı Farklılıkların Belirleyicileri: Eurostat Verileriyle Ampirik Bir Analiz](../publications/dbdacc45e97f78bceb9d.md)

Ayşen Akyüz; Bilge Karamehmet

Bu çalışma, Avrupa Birliği 27 üye devletinde işletmelerin yapay zekâ teknolojilerini pazarlama ve satış amacıyla kullanımındaki ülkeler arası farklılıkların belirleyicilerini ampirik olarak incelemektedir\. Teknoloji–Organizasyon–Çevre \(TOE\) çerçevesi teorik temel olarak benimsenmiş ve ülke düzeyine uyarlanmıştır\. Eurostat’ın 2021–2024 dönemine ait harmonize ICT işletme anketi verileri \(özellikle isoc\_eb\_ai ve isoc\_e\_dii\) kullanılarak altı hipotez test edilmiştir\. Çalışmada K\-ortalamalar kümeleme analizi ile sabit etkiler panel regresyonunu birleştiren iki aşamalı bir yöntem uygulanmıştır\. Bulgular, dijital altyapı olgunluğunun \(Dijital Yoğunluk Endeksi ile ölçülen\) ve ICT uzman yoğunluğunun pazarlama amaçlı YZ benimsemesinin en güçlü ve tutarlı yordayıcıları olduğunu göstermektedir\. Ayrıca bulgular, dijital altyapının pazarlama YZ benimsemesini büyük ölçüde genel dijitalleşme kapasitesi üzerinden dolaylı olarak etkilediğine işaret etmektedir\.Çalışmanın özgün katkısı, TOE çerçevesini ülke düzeyinde ve pazarlama odaklı YZ bağlamında ampirik olarak sınayan öncü modellerden birini sunmasıdır\. Bunun yanı sıra çalışma, pazarlama YZ kullanımında küçük işletmelerin büyük işletmelere yakın oranlar sergilemesini ifade eden “KOBİ paradoksu”nu teorik olarak çerçevelemekte ve bu olguya yönelik ampirik bulgular sunmaktadır\. Elde edilen sonuçlar, politika yapıcılar açısından dijital altyapı yatırımları ile beşerî sermaye gelişiminin eş zamanlı olarak ele alınmasının kritik önem taşıdığını ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Navigating Customer Satisfaction in Public Service Industry: An IPA Approach to Service Excellence](../publications/dbdec4661ec91596a40f.md)

Endang Sulistiyani; Taufik \- Rohman; Sri Wahyuni; Ririn Budi Utaminingtyas

This study aims to to determine the level of customer satisfaction and provide suggestions for improving service quality in order to increase customer satisfaction\. The study used 15 SERVQUAL attributes\. Data analysis methods using gap analysis and IPA model\. The results of the study obtained a negative gap and an average conformity level of 79% or moderate satisfaction\. The results of customer responses to the dimensions of the company&\#x27;s service quality are analyzed by gap analysis and the IPA method\. ## [Flat Loss, Evolving Features: Grokking in Modular Addition](../publications/dbe1e7b32c8cfdc7406d.md)

Akash Kumar; Karthik Sankaranarayanan

Can a network keep learning while its training cross\-entropy stays nearly flat at a positive level? We show that it can\. On modular addition, a standard testbed for grokking, ReLU networks trained with supported\-Polar hidden updates, normalized output\-layer updates and weight decay can keep 100% training accuracy while their hidden features change and held\-out accuracy rises from zero to above 90%, at relatively flat training cross\-entropy\. Correct classification need not minimize cross\-entropy, which still depends on prediction confidence\. We prove this coexistence for one\-hidden\-layer networks in two finite\-window theorems from constructed initializations: one gives a constant gain in the Fourier fraction of the hidden features, and the other holds at arbitrarily low positive loss, where a readout refitted on the training data generalizes before the network\. Experiments from random initialization show the same coexistence on a window fixed in advance, and in deeper networks held\-out accuracy also rises over post\-hoc windows with a net increase in training cross\-entropy\. With a last\-layer rate set per training fraction and head decay scaled with the prime, deeper networks at p=47 and 61 meet a criterion on post\-hoc windows, fixed in advance, in nearly all fresh runs\. A one\-block transformer trained with the same updates and a slowly decaying output gain keeps every training pair correct at every logged checkpoint while its training cross\-entropy rises and its held\-out accuracy approaches one; with two blocks this holds through the held\-out rise, after which training pairs begin to flip\. A plateau in training loss need not be a plateau in learning\. Code: https://github\.com/akashkumar\-d/flat\-loss\-evolving\-features\.

## [Pedraza, R\.: Artificial Research by Deduction in the Global Artificial Intelligence](../publications/dbf08a6d1f7fa96a39b2.md)



In Global Artificial Intelligence: First Prototype of Global Artificial Intelligence\. London: Ruben Garcia Pedraza\. pp\. 1\-32\. 2025This paper explores the foundational role of Artificial Research by Deduction within the architecture of Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\)\. While current AI development remains largely focused on Specific Artificial Intelligences \(SAIs\) and artificial learning, the transition toward GAI demands a paradigmatic leap—from learning to autonomous research\. Within this shift, Artificial Research by Deduction offers a methodological system based on the Syllogism of the Trend \(i\.e\., if A tends to B and B to C, then A tends to C\), enabling the automation of rational hypothesis generation and validation from structured data\. The paper presents a three\-stage model: application, where global databases are standardized into a unified quantitative matrix; replication, where robotic devices and SAIs gather data for deductive analysis; and auto\-replication, where GAI iteratively refines its own models and decision\-making structures, including cognitive, infrastructural, and material self\-enhancement\. Emphasis is placed on the interaction between deductive reasoning, modeling systems, decisional frameworks, and the application layer—through which GAI acts upon the world via robotic systems and subordinate SAIs\. Artificial Research by Deduction is presented not as an isolated capability, but as a key epistemic engine embedded within a larger system of systems, aimed at rational global governance, the well\-being of humankind, and the pursuit of authentic, non\-anthropocentric truth\. This first paper lays the groundwork for deeper explorations of replication mechanisms and the global integration of category systems in future work\.

## [Corris, Amanda: Cognition: Embodied, Embedded, Extended, Enactive, and Affective](../publications/dbf1018deb27e1ec349f.md)



In Introducing Philosophy of Mind, Today\. Routledge\. 2027Where should we look to find the mind? A common response might be to look to the inner\-workings of the brain\. After all, cognition happens in the brain, right? Not entirely, say the proponents of “4EA cognition”, a collection of views that expand the limits of the mind beyond the brain\. 4EA cognition emphasizes several unconventional aspects of mentality\. The mind is extended beyond the boundaries of the brain, out into the world to include things like notebooks and calculators\. The mind is embodied, part of a living body that moves, perceives, acts, and interacts\. The mind is embedded in an environment, an environment it engages with in its everyday activity\. The mind is enactive, bringing forth—or enacting—a world rich with significance and meaning\. Some philosophers have recently argued for a fifth letter: this time, an A\. They say the mind is also affective; it is shaped by our emotional, felt states of being\. Taken together, we have 4EA cognition\. While there are discrepancies between specific views within 4EA cognition, what unites them is an emphasis on how richly interconnected the mind is with the body and the rest of the world\. The aspects of cognition represented by each of the letters \(the 4 Es, and the A\) situate the mind in the world\. What this means is that the mind is not merely ensconced within the brain, and the brain is not the only thing that matters for how we understand mentality\. So, we cannot look only to what is going on inside of our heads to make sense of our mental lives\. We must also look to our bodies, our environments, and even other people\.

## [Paired\-ear tympanometric pressure patterns and hearing recovery in unilateral sudden sensorineural hearing loss: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/dbf7381b7571a2e927cb.md)

Tianyu Zhang; Yaxue Xie; Yingxuan Li; Haibo Zhang; Hanzhai Tian; Ziye Zhu; Zhiyu Yang; Zhenlin Wang; Jiali Duan; Tianyang Zhang

Background Sudden sensorineural hearing loss \(SSNHL\) remains difficult to phenotype and predict\. Tympanometry is routinely performed, yet its quantitative pressure information is largely discarded once conductive hearing loss is excluded\. We used a paired\-ear strategy to compare middle\-ear pressure between the affected and contralateral ears in unilateral SSNHL\. Methods We retrospectively studied 203 adults with unilateral SSNHL and bilateral tympanometric peak pressure \(TPP\) measurements\. Rather than relying on a single abnormality threshold, we integrated signed interaural differences, absolute pressure asymmetry, laterality\-aware pressure phenotypes, and threshold\-sensitivity analyses\. Among patients with follow\-up audiometry, hearing recovery was quantified as both continuous hearing gain and clinically meaningful ≥15\-dB improvement, and was further examined in relation to categorical and continuous TPP phenotypes\. Results Paired\-ear analysis showed no significant pressure shift in the affected ear compared with the contralateral ear \( p = 0\.410\), indicating no consistent affected\-ear pressure abnormality at the population level\. Laterality\-aware classification identified affected\-ear\-only negative pressure in 14 patients \(6\.9%\) and contralateral\-ear\-only negative pressure in 11 patients \(5\.4%\)\. This subgroup would be largely invisible using conventional single\-ear classification\. Across complementary binary, continuous, and multivariable analyses, tympanometric pressure showed no robust relationship with short\-term hearing recovery, and this conclusion remained stable across alternative pressure thresholds\. Conclusion Unilateral SSNHL is not characterized by a universal middle\-ear pressure abnormality\. Paired\-ear assessment can identify individual differences in middle\-ear pressure that may be overlooked by single\-ear classification\. However, baseline TPP was not clearly associated with short\-term hearing recovery in this cohort\.

## [“Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany \(Italy\): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling](../publications/dbfeb738bbf5f1823274.md)

Marina Funaro; Stefania Nisio; Sergio Madonna

The “Calcare Cavernoso” \(cavernous limestone\) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater\-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence\. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany \(Italy\) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database\. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi\-source geospatial datasets\. Geological and thematic layers were retrieved from the Tuscany “Geoscopio” portal, while Copernicus Sentinel\-2 imagery was processed using the Normalized Difference Water Index \(NDWI\) to support the detection of flooded sinkholes\. Historical maps were exploited to infer sinkhole persistence and potential evolutionary trends, including partial or complete infilling\. All thematic layers \(geology, faults, hydrography, quarries, mines, topography, and sinkholes\) were harmonized, georeferenced, and rasterized on a 250 × 250 m grid within an ESRI ArcGIS environment\. Susceptibility modelling was implemented using density\-based proxies and an Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) framework, producing probability outputs subsequently grouped into classes to enhance operational usability\. The results substantially expand the regional sinkhole inventory \(from 88 to 1223 mapped features\) and support a strong spatial association between sinkhole occurrence and “Calcare Cavernoso”, further corroborated by targeted field checks\. The most influential susceptibility drivers include “Calcare Cavernoso”, low\-slope settings, DTM\-derived parameters, fault density, and anthropogenic underground activities \(quarries and mines\), while other variables show secondary or more complex contributions\.

## [Diagnostic accuracy of shear wave and strain elastography in differentiating benign and malignant thyroid nodules](../publications/dc2a7c545e56a134b9ce.md)

Komal Mushtaq; Sohail Ahmed Khan; Waqas Ahmed Farooqui; Nasreen Naz

Objective: This study assesses diagnostic accuracy of shear wave elastography \(SWE\) and strain elastography \(SE\) for thyroid nodule characterization in keeping histopathology as gold standard\. Methodology: It was analytical cross\-sectional study at Dow Institute of Radiology \(Dow University of Health Sciences\) with 361 thyroid nodules from January 2022 to February 2023\. Images were assessed using Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System \(TIRADS\) followed by ultrasound elastography \(USE\)\. SWE was evaluated by elasticity mean and standard deviation\. SE was assessed by Parenchyma to Nodule Strain Ratio \(PNSR\) and Muscle to Nodule Strain ratio \(MNSR\)\. Predictive values of SWE, MNSR, and PNSR were concluded by receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve\. Results: Fine Needle Aspiration and Cytology \(FNAC\) confirmed malignant thyroid nodules in 66 cases \(18\.3%\)\. Diagnostic indices, including sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy, were calculated for SWE, MNSR and PNSR\. The optimal cut\-off value using the ROC co\-ordinates was 36\.0 kPa for SWE, 2\.4 for MNSR and 2\.75 for PNSR\. The sensitivity, specificity and diagnostic accuracy of SWE were 87\.8 %, 89\.4 % and 89\.1 % respectively\. The sensitivity, specificity and diagnostic accuracy of MNSR were 87\.8%, 91\.5% and 90\.8 % respectively\. Whereas, sensitivity, specificity and diagnostic accuracy of PNSR were 80\.3%, 95\.5% and 92\.7 % respectively\. Conclusion: USE had moderate to high diagnostic performance, with overlapping results of SWE, MNSR, and PNSR\. While SWE and MNSR had similar sensitivity, PNSR had highest Specificity and diagnostic accuracy giving it a respectable position in the study\.

## [FRACTAL: A Self\-Similar Multi\-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds](../publications/dc2b72680ec6fc0ee685.md)

Ohad Dan; Abhinav Taliyan

We present FRACTAL, a self\-similar multi\-agent architecture for recursive goal decomposition, in which the same five\-component organizational pattern \-\- Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta\-Observer \-\- recurs at every level of a decomposition tree\. We make four formal contributions: \(1\) a communication bound showing intra\-node cost is linear in ensemble size and round count \(O\(kr\)\) under a two\-phase blind\-proposal/stress\-test protocol, versus quadratic cost for free\-form debate, with an explicit, stated assumption on fixed evaluator count; \(2\) a two\-mode orchestration criterion separating generative and evaluative phases via a measurable diversity\-saturation threshold; \(3\) a supermajority convergence guarantee with explicit probability bounds at stated agreement levels, and a formal depth bound under an operationalized goal\-complexity measure; \(4\) a Bayesian inter\-layer escalation mechanism unifying hysteresis and contract\-breach signaling under one posterior update\. We illustrate the architecture&\#x27;s execution qualitatively on a worked example and a multi\-layer case study; we do not report quantitative performance claims in this paper, and we explicitly discuss the formal and inductive\-bias limitations of the model, including an unimplemented but architecture\-compatible direction toward bounded self\-improvement\. We use &quot;fractal&quot; as an architectural metaphor for self\-similarity, not a measured mathematical property\. Empirical validation of the architecture&\#x27;s comparative performance is left to future work\.

## [Data\-Driven Engineering of MnCoMo Electrocatalysts: Predictive Modeling and Experimental Validation for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction](../publications/dc30799dbfffd101474f.md)

Jyoti Raghav; Lovish Bhatia; Sapna Raghav; Shakti Singh; Harshita Mishra; Vinay Shankar Pandey; Sunil Singh Kushvaha

Abstract The development of sustainable green hydrogen through the use of catalytic processes demands a very active and earth\-abundant electrocatalyst capable of facilitating the kinetic difficulties of the oxygen evolution reaction\. Conventional trial\-and\-error and solely computational approaches suffer from high resource expenditures and inefficiencies in converting theoretical results into practical lab results\. In order to address this issue, a closed\-loop, data\-driven experimental framework is proposed in order to facilitate the automated and expedited optimization process of transition metal electrocatalysts\. Four experimentally measured MnCoMo oxide\-based electrodes containing 0, 0\.25, 0\.5, and 0\.75 mmol Mo were used as the baseline dataset for machine\-learning model development and evaluation across interpolation and extrapolation scenarios\. The fully unmeasured 1\.0 mmol Mo composition was then withheld from model development, predicted blindly from the four baseline profiles, synthesized, and experimentally characterized for prospective validation\. Gradient\-boosted tree and deep learning neural network models are tested against a variety of physical synthesis descriptors within both interpolation and extrapolation scenarios\. The physical synthesis and experimental verification of an out\-of\-sample concentration of the electrocatalyst show high accuracy in prediction, thus demonstrating the capability of encoding algorithmic models in order to avoid unnecessary manual screening efforts within the investigated MnCoMo compositional space\.

## [Construction of an Early Risk Stratification Model for Severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia in Children: A LASSO\-Stability Selection and Multi\-Model Comparative Study](../publications/dc4270af777a3e13b599.md)

Liu Tianyang; Xinyuan Huang; Wang Ying; Yanhong Zou

Objective: To develop an early risk stratification model for severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia \(SMPP\) in children and compare Logistic regression, Random Forest \(RF\), and XGBoost\. Methods: This retrospective study included 1,000 children with MPP at a single center \(May 2023–May 2025\)\. The primary outcome was severe clinical progression requiring intensive intervention \(oxygen therapy, PICU admission, corticosteroid pulse therapy, or septic shock\), defined independently of candidate predictors\. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation \(20 datasets\); variables with &gt;30% missingness were excluded\. LASSO stability selection \(≥19/20 datasets\) identified predictors\. Three models were developed in a 70% training set and validated in a 30% test set\. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), calibration curves, Brier score, and decision curve analysis \(DCA\)\. Temporal validation and bootstrap optimism correction were performed\. A nomogram and an online risk calculator were developed based on the best\-performing model\. Results: LASSO stability selection identified 8 core predictors: age, fever duration, C\-reactive protein \(CRP\), lactate dehydrogenase \(LDH\), pleural effusion, creatine kinase \(CK\), adenosine deaminase \(ADA\), and interleukin\-6 \(IL\-6\)\. Logistic regression achieved the highest test AUC \(0\.795; 95% CI: 0\.734–0\.856\), with a statistically significant difference compared with RF \(P=0\.019\) but not with XGBoost \(P=0\.050\)\. Logistic regression also demonstrated the best calibration \(Brier score=0\.140\) and the highest clinical net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities\. RF and XGBoost overfitted \(training AUCs 1\.000 and 0\.844\)\. Temporal validation yielded an AUC of 0\.780 \(95% CI 0\.725–0\.835\), and the optimism\-corrected AUC was 0\.726\. Conclusion: The Logistic model based on 8 readily available predictors showed promising performance for early risk stratification of SMPP\. Prospective multicenter external validation is warranted before clinical implementation\.

## [THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FORENSIC SCIENCE: CHALLENGES AND PROSPECTS](../publications/dc45fcb00614e9878b52.md)

А\. М\. Лазебний; Bogdan Krymchanin

This article examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in forensic science at the stages of collecting, examining, and evaluating evidentiary information\. It considers the use of machine\-learning algorithms, computer vision, and language models to process digital datasets, analyse photographs and video recordings, conduct biometric comparisons, examine documents, and detect synthetically generated content\. AI can accelerate information retrieval and help identify relationships between data; however, technological efficiency does not guarantee the reliability of the result\. The article analyses the risks of algorithmic bias, limited explainability, errors in training data, loss of digital context, breaches in the chain of custody, and excessive reliance on automated conclusions\. In light of Ukrainian legislation and European approaches, it proposes a multi\-level model for verifying neural\-network outputs\. The model includes documenting the tool, preserving original data, independent validation, describing methodological limitations, and ensuring that the parties to proceedings have a genuine opportunity to challenge the result\. The article argues that AI should remain an auxiliary tool, while final forensic conclusions and procedural decisions must be made by competent human professionals in accordance with the law\.

## [Pengaruh Kecerdasan Artifisial Terhadap Otoritas Pengetahuan Dalam Kurikulum Sekolah: Tinjauan Literatur](../publications/dc4ae791b2c1b548da35.md)

Darul Ihsan; Benny Prasetiya

The presence of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) in learning does not merely change how students obtain information; it also shifts who is trusted as a legitimate source of knowledge in schools\. This article critically reviews the literature on the influence of AI on epistemic authority in the school curriculum, particularly the changing positions of teachers, textbooks, and the official curriculum\. Using a qualitative critical literature review of reputable journal articles, academic books, and policy documents published in 2026, analysed thematically, the review identifies four main findings: \(1\) AI becomes an additional source of knowledge that erodes the monopoly of teachers and official texts; \(2\) the authority of AI is problematic because of opacity, data bias, and the potential for epistemic injustice; \(3\) the apparent dispersal of authority is not a genuine decentralisation, since control over knowledge tends to concentrate in platform providers; and \(4\) the teacher&\#x27;s role shifts from transmitter of knowledge to epistemic guarantor who curates, verifies, and contextualises AI outputs\. The article proposes a conceptual framework of curated epistemic authority as a direction for curriculum development that preserves pedagogical sovereignty in the AI era\.

## [Where Research Ideation Begins: Forward\-Citation Supervision for Actionable Limitation Generation](../publications/dc5a52071df8a97e576e.md)

Liyang Zhao; Yong Cao; Haibin Ling

Automated research ideation has advanced rapidly, with multi\-agent workflows that generate whole research ideas end to end\. These frameworks leave largely unexamined the step that seeds a good idea: identifying an actionable limitation from literature\. In this paper, we focus on this first step in the research ideation pipeline\. Starting from a pilot study, we find that as large language models \(LLMs\) scale from 0\.6B to 32B parameters, they become far better at recognizing which limitation later work addressed, but no better at generating one, suggesting that the bottleneck lies in the supervision signal rather than model capacity\. We therefore construct ActLim\-Bench from forward citations, yielding 18,279 evidence\-linked supervision triples with human verification\. On this signal, we propose a three\-stage post\-training pipeline: supervised fine\-tuning, verifier\-filtered rejection\-sampling fine\-tuning, and reinforcement learning with the verifier as an online dense reward\. Experimental results show that our method achieves the highest recall score compared to existing methods among all frontier models\. We further show that our generated limitations are preferred in 64\.9% of non\-tied human comparisons and improve downstream ideation systems\. We will release our data and code upon publication\.

## [A quantitative framework for assessing narrative environments in historic districts using space syntax and agent\-based crowd simulation: a case study of Xun County, China](../publications/dc5ac1a073626a612b69.md)

Bin Wang

This study proposes a quantitative framework for assessing narrative environments in historic districts by integrating space syntax with agent\-based simulation \(ABS\)\. Taking five historic districts in the Old Town of Xun County, China, as the case study, the research combines global integration, local integration, choice, and intelligibility to identify spatial accessibility, corridor potential, and cognitive efficiency, and uses ABS together with manual pedestrian observations to validate movement concentration and detect anomalous areas\. Syntactic analysis identifies East Housi Street and South Street as the primary movement corridors, with the highest accessibility \(global integration = 1\.182 and 1\.256, respectively\) and pedestrian concentration, whereas Xinzhuang Street exhibits critically weak connectivity \(intelligibility R 2 = 0\.427\), while Pifu Road emerges as an important southern corridor \(choice = 45,369\) whose continuity is constrained by spatial obstructions\. The results reveal a clear north–south gradient in spatial accessibility: northern districts exhibit higher accessibility and stronger pedestrian concentration, but also greater risks of over\-commercialization and narrative homogenization, whereas southern districts are characterized by corridor fragmentation, weaker accessibility, and disrupted cultural continuity\. ABS validation reveals two anomalies: North Xiaoximenli \(low flow despite moderate syntax, blocked by illegal structures\) and Nanshan \(high traffic despite low syntax, anchored by the City God Temple\)\. Based on these spatially explicit diagnostics, the proposed framework provides an evidence\-based priority pathway for removing physical obstructions, reactivating southern heritage nodes, and restoring corridor continuity along East Housi Street, offering a replicable technical pathway for spatial diagnosis, narrative restoration, and conservation\-oriented renewal in multi\-district historic environments\.

## [AI\-Guided Clinical Image Interpretation System for Precision Treatment Planning](../publications/dc6434a8fe6364d4902b.md)

Pasupula Madan Mohan Reddy; V\. Rajamanickam; Bindu Madhavi Mangalampalli; Sasi Kumar Kolla; Rohit Gorle; Venkata Akhilesh Ranga Reddy

Radiological examinations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic performance by compensating for expertise shortages, particularly in specialized interpretation\. Despite academic AI models achieving compelling accuracy, adoption remains low\. An objective, evidence\-based examination of AI\-guided clinical image interpretation seeks to expose the underlying reasons\. The primary challenge lies not in accuracy but in fully automated analysis, especially for multimodal and multidimensional datasets\. Introduction of uncertainty measures, image explainability, and real\-world data reduce recognition to a decisive\-supporting role— helping radiologists to detect previously unnoticed abnormalities—or even to precautionary analysis\. Patients requesting precision medicine and therapy planning—and those at high risk of neglected pathology—stand to gain the greatest benefit\. Relevant AI architecture considers imaging cues suitable for precision medicine or requiring additional methods to obtain interpretable images\. Successful performance testing against an external, hidden reference dataset promotes vital user trust\. Machine learning achieves best results where all potentially pathological abnormalities are identified and their presence virtually guaranteed, as in multi\-class recognition\. Data scarcity, however, impedes clinically relevant solutions\. Explainability, essential for medical applications and clinical acceptance, extends simply beyond clinical decision support to provide saliency maps and, better still, clinically meaningful image regions or qualities\. Attention maps may even bring a form of rule\-based reasoning within reach\. Clinical integration that reproduces the technical conditions under which model diagnostic measures are calculated raises the challenge of uncertainty quantification—a necessary condition for clinical decision support\. Convolutional neural networks trained for photo\-quality classification, par excellence supervised image quality assessment, provide the basic cues for uncertainty quantification\. Imaging acquisition, modality, and systems are also defined in terms of current PACS/EPIC systems\. PE, pre\-symptomatic examination or precautionary examination, is defined as a patientuser group prepared to cover the cost of an examination with lower diagnostic accuracy and a high level of uncertainty
