## [Detection and Classification of Physiological Activation States Through Biosignal Analysis Using Machine Learning](../publications/dc661fff0ee7b3909cea.md)

Marco Leonelli; José Luis Jodrá; Asier Salazar\-Ramirez; Raquel Martínez; Javier E\. Sánchez\-Galán

Monitoring autonomic nervous system responses offers significant potential for personalized health applications and early intervention\. This study presents a machine learning framework for binary classification of physiological activation states using electrocardiogram \(ECG\) and respiratory \(RESP\) signals from the WESAD dataset\. Stress and amusement were grouped as Activation, whereas baseline and meditation were grouped as Non\-Activation\. The processing pipeline incorporates R\-peak detection, temporal segmentation, handcrafted feature extraction, and subject\-independent evaluation\. Conventional machine learning classifiers and deep learning architectures were evaluated, together with a proposed Hybrid Multi\-Scale Temporal Convolutional–Conformer \(MST\-Conformer\) combining temporal representations learned from ECG and RESP waveforms with handcrafted physiological features\. Performance was assessed using 15\-fold Leave\-One\-Subject\-Out \(LOSO\) cross\-validation\. Adding respiration\-derived features to ECG\-derived features improved conventional machine learning performance, increasing the highest balanced accuracy from 0\.752 to 0\.807 and AUC from 0\.802 to 0\.886\. The complete Hybrid MST\-Conformer incorporating 27 physiological features achieved a mean accuracy of 0\.825, balanced accuracy of 0\.820, F1\-score of 0\.763, and AUC of 0\.904\. Subject\-level analysis also revealed substantial physiological heterogeneity\. These results support the potential of combining learned temporal representations with handcrafted physiological information for subject\-independent physiological activation classification\.

## [Optimized Backstepping Control Based on Dynamic‐Surface Technique for a Class of Nonlinear Strict‐Feedback Systems Subjected to Actuator Failure](../publications/dc6d9633e2fc4e225631.md)

Xiaorui Zhang; Lixia Liu; Guoxing Wen

ABSTRACT This work develops an optimized backstepping \(OB\) control by combining the fault‐tolerant mechanism and dynamic surface \(DS\) technique for a class of nonlinear strict‐feedback systems with actuator failure\. OB technique needs to perform the actor‐critic reinforcement learning \(RL\) at every backstepping step for deriving the optimized virtual and actual controls\. However, because of the presence of actuator failures, the RL training will be inevitably affected\. To mitigate the effect, an adaptive algorithm is developed to be integrated into the OB control for tolerating the actuator failure\. For making the integration smooth, a simplified RL algorithm is deduced from a straightforward positive function derived from the Hamilton‐Jacobi‐Bellman \(HJB\) equation\. Furthermore, since the OB technique requires calculating the derivatives of virtual controls at every backstepping step, it is highly likely to cause the issue of “differential explosion\.” To address this problem, DS technique is integrated into the OB control design\. Finally, the proposed control method is testified through theory and simulation experiment\.

## [Revisiting the economic growth model: The roles of exports, employment, and foreign direct investment](../publications/dc71a25428f1c1727d96.md)

Norlaila Abu Bakar; Norimah Rambeli; Suhaila Saad; Rafiduraida Binti Abdul Rahman

The focal point of this study is to examine the relationship between the selected macroeconomic variables namely foreign direct investment, exports, and employment on the gross domestic product\. In estimating the model, this study adopts the multiple regression model using ordinary least square approach\. The yearly data is utilized spinning from 1991 to 2025\. In general, all variables under observation are important in explaining the dependent variable in the long run at 99% confidence level\. Specifically, the finding suggests that the exports \(X\) and employment growth rate \(EGr\) have a strong positive relationship with gross domestic product \(GDP\)\. On the other hand, foreign direct investment \(FDI\) also has a weak positive relationship with GDP, but it is not significant\. The estimated model passed all diagnostic tests, including heteroscedastic, multicollinearity, and autocorrelation\. By implication, both exports and the employment growth rate have a significant effect impact on gross domestic product in the long run, thus indicating high reliability on the rate of increase in exports and employment in Malaysia\. Simply put, the higher exports and employment growth rate, the higher GDP will be increase in the long run\. Therefore, the higher exports and employment growth rate can be a catalyst to increase the gross domestic product in Malaysia in the long term, especially from years 1991 to 2025\.

## [Enhancing multifaceted interactions in EFL learning: The roles of classroom social climate, perceived L2 proficiency, and willingness to communicate](../publications/dc71f7550d2350ba3142.md)

Jinfen Xu; Xiaoli Feng

Interaction provides second language \(L2\) learners with opportunities for authentic language use and promotes their language development, underscoring the need to identify factors that contribute to L2 interactions\. Drawing on the pyramid model of willingness to communicate \(WTC\), this study explores how classroom social climate \(CSC\), perceived L2 proficiency \(PLP\), and WTC influence students’ multifaceted interactions \(MI\) with their teachers, peers, and computer tools\. A total of 665 Chinese non\-English majors voluntarily participated in the study\. A two\-phase analytical approach combining partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) and psychological network analysis \(PNA\) was employed to examine both linear and non\-linear relationships among the variables\. The PLS\-SEM results showed that CSC and WTC significantly and positively predicted MI, whereas the direct effect of PLP on MI was negligible\. 68% were female\.Multilevel involvement was classified into two\-level \(56%\), three\-level \(24%\), and four\-level \(20%\) factors\.Comorbidities consisted of osteoporosis \(32%\) and diabetes mellitus \(16%\)\.The C2\-C7 angle \(8\.48° to 16\.6°, p 2 levels \(β = 0\.373, p &lt; ## [Information\-Geometric Blind Spots of Conformal Test Martingales](../publications/dc7af833489cc684f5e4.md)

Johan Hallberg Szabadváry

Conformal test martingales \(CTMs\) are e\-processes for sequentially testing exchangeability via p\-values produced by a conformity function $A$\. However, any distribution shift that preserves the push\-forward $P\\circ A^\{\-1\}$ leaves the p\-value distribution invariant, rendering it invisible to every CTM based on $A$\. We formalise this blind spot through the \\emph\{$A$\-equivalence class\} $\[P\]\_A$ and show that, for any target distribution $T$, there is a unique closest element $Q^\\ast\\in\[P\]\_A$ in KL divergence\-\-\-the \\emph\{$A$\-cryptic I\-projection\}\-\-\-with explicit density $q^\\ast\(z\) = t\(z\)\\,p\_S\(A\(z\)\)/t\_S\(A\(z\)\)$ and a Pythagorean decomposition into detectable and cryptic components\. When $A$ is the Neyman\-Pearson likelihood ratio, the cryptic component vanishes, connecting our result to optimal e\-value design\. We demonstrate the theory on high\-dimensional image data by empirically constructing this I\-projection\. By conditionally resampling EMNIST letters to identically match the conformity scores of MNIST digits, we demonstrate that a distribution can be shifted to a disjoint support while leaving the test martingale mathematically blinded\.

## [The impact of stress on cognitive performance in remote smartphone\-based assessments: exploring within\-person variability](../publications/dc7c5eb26636661604fb.md)

Sarah Prieto; Louisa I\. Thompson; Molly Split; Caroline Nester Rooney; Daliah Ross; Preeti Sunderaraman; Alyssa N\. De Vito; Nelson Arley Roque; John Michael Felt; Martin J\. Sliwinski; Zachary J\. Kunicki

Introduction Stress is a well\-established risk factor for cognitive dysfunction in domains including processing speed \(PS\), working memory \(WM\), and episodic memory \(EM\)\. However, this research literature typically uses between\-group comparisons\. Advances in remote, smartphone\-based cognitive assessments allow for examination of within\-person variability, or testing how fluctuations in an individual&\#x27;s stress levels influence their cognitive performance\. We examined the association between within\-person variability in stress and performance on mobile\-app assessments of processing speed, working memory, and episodic memory in cognitively unimpaired older adults\. Methods 123 cognitively unimpaired older adults \(60–81 years old, 66\.7% female, 86\.2% White, mean education = 16\.49 years\) rated their stress using a single\-item immediately before completing cognitive assessments on the Mobile Monitoring of Cognitive Change \(M2C2\) smartphone app\. Data were gathered three times daily over eight days\. Cognitive tasks included measures of PS, visual WM, and EM\. Multilevel modeling examined the interaction between within\-person stress and session number on cognitive performance\. Results Higher within\-person stress was associated with faster PS \(Est\. = −3\.82, p &lt; \.001\), though these effects diminished across sessions \(session × stress interaction, p = \.003\)\. By contrast, stress was not associated with EM or WM performance\. Sensitivity analyses using different cumulative stress thresholds produced consistent findings\. Discussion Results demonstrate that momentary increases in stress were associated with faster PS, but did not impact WM or EM performances, though these effects changed over repeated testing\. These findings highlight the importance of within\-person stress variability in shaping cognitive performance on high\-frequency smartphone\-based assessments\.

## [Educational quality of YouTube content on healthcare waste management relevant to dentistry: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/dc868ffed594672eb7f5.md)

Filipe Lima Goetz Fagundes; Daniel Costa Magalhães da Cunha; João Víctor Frazão Câmara; Aléxia Caroline Leandro da Conceição; Victor Macedo Varela; Gisele Damiana da Silveira Pereira

BACKGROUND: YouTube has become a major source of educational content in healthcare, including topics related to dentistry and public health\. However, the accuracy and educational reliability of videos addressing healthcare waste management relevant to dental practice remain uncertain\. Therefore, the aim of this cross\-sectional study was to evaluate the educational quality, credibility, and reliability of YouTube videos addressing healthcare waste management with relevance to dental practice, using the Global Quality Scale \(GQS\), Journal of the American Medical Association \(JAMA\) benchmark criteria, and the modified DISCERN \(mDISCERN\) instrument\. Additionally, the influence of video source type and the correlation among the evaluation instruments were investigated\. METHODS: A cross\-sectional analysis was conducted in June 2025 using Portuguese search terms related to healthcare waste management, including &quot;Resíduos de Serviço de Saúde,&quot; &quot;Resíduos Hospitalares,&quot; and &quot;Resíduos Odontológicos,&quot; to identify videos relevant to dental practice\. A total of 180 YouTube videos were initially screened\. After duplicate removal and application of inclusion criteria, 47 videos were included for final analysis\. Two independent and calibrated reviewers assessed all videos using the Global Quality Scale \(GQS\), Journal of the American Medical Association \(JAMA\) benchmark criteria and modified DISCERN \(mDISCERN\) instrument\. To account for the Brazilian regulatory context, particularly Resolution RDC No\. 222/2018, the GQS, JAMA benchmark criteria, and mDISCERN were applied as contextually adapted applications of the original instruments, using study\-specific operational definitions to guide the interpretation of selected criteria\. These contextual adaptations preserved the general structure and scoring ranges of the instruments but may have altered the interpretation of some underlying constructs\. Because these adaptations have not undergone independent psychometric validation, they should not be considered validated modifications of the original instruments, and the findings should be interpreted within the specific methodological context of the present study\. Inter\-rater reliability was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient \(ICC\) and Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha\. Descriptive analyses were performed, followed by ANOVA and Kruskal\-Wallis tests to compare scores according to source type \(academic institutions, organizations, healthcare professionals, and other users\)\. Spearman&\#x27;s correlation test assessed associations among evaluation instruments\. RESULTS: Excellent inter\-rater agreement was observed \(ICC = 0\.946; 95% CI: 0\.913\-0\.967; Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha = 0\.913\)\. Mean scores obtained using the contextually adapted applications indicated high quality of the assessed educational content according to the GQS \(4\.19 ± 0\.78\), moderate credibility/transparency \(JAMA: 2\.43 ± 1\.06\), and moderate reliability \(mDISCERN: 2\.50 ± 0\.90\)\. No statistically significant differences were identified among source types for any scale \(p &gt; 0\.05\)\. A significant positive correlation was found between JAMA and mDISCERN scores \(ρ = 0\.502; p &lt; 0\.001\), indicating an association between these scores within the contextually adapted measurement framework\. No significant correlations were observed between GQS and the other instruments\. CONCLUSIONS: The 47 YouTube videos analyzed in the present study demonstrated satisfactory quality of the assessed educational content but only moderate credibility and reliability, based on the contextually adapted applications of the GQS, JAMA benchmark criteria, and mDISCERN\. Because the contextual operational definitions used for these instruments have not undergone independent psychometric validation, the results should be interpreted within the methodological framework adopted in this study\. No statistically significant differences in scores were detected among the represented source categories\. However, a positive association was observed between the scores obtained using the contextually adapted JAMA and mDISCERN applications, whereas GQS scores were not significantly associated with either instrument\. These findings underscore the importance of critically evaluating online health\-related content using assessment approaches that address different dimensions of quality\. The results describe the characteristics of the videos retrieved under the specified search strategy during the June 2025 data collection period and should not be generalized to all YouTube content or interpreted as evidence of educational effectiveness, learning outcomes, professional competence, or changes in healthcare waste management practices\. Furthermore, whether the characteristics identified in these videos translate into measurable educational benefits or contribute to learning and professional training remains to be determined through direct evaluation in future educational studies\.

## [Teaching and psychological associations of adolescent piano composition skills: a study on constructivist practices and reflective guidance based on teacher reports](../publications/dc8ebe42ce04ccbb5026.md)

晏晓东

Introduction To understand the connection between open teaching environments and musical creative performance, this study focuses on adolescent piano teaching, examining the structural associations among constructivist practices, reflective guidance, and piano composition skills, and analyzing the parallel indirect associations linked via creative self\-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for composition\. Methods A cross\-sectional questionnaire design was adopted, based on the analysis of 723 self\-reports from teachers with adolescent piano teaching experience and their evaluation data on students’ states and skills\. Multivariate regression and Bootstrap resampling methods were used for statistical path testing, comparing group distribution characteristics under different learning purposes, and testing the boundary conditions formed by the frequency of composition teaching\. Results \(1\) Both constructivist practices and reflective guidance showed significant positive associations with the evaluated piano composition skills; \(2\) Creative self\-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for composition presented significant parallel indirect paths in the above associations; \(3\) The overall differences among groups with different learning purposes on all core constructs reached statistical significance, with the descriptive means of the grading test or competition group generally being lower than those of the hobby group; \(4\) No significant moderating phenomenon of composition teaching frequency on the association between constructivist practices and intrinsic motivation was found\. Discussion Autonomous decision\-making and process scrutiny are independently and positively associated with teacher\-evaluated student composition skills, respectively\. These teaching practice characteristics, together with students’ capability beliefs and internal willingness to participate, constitute the relevant conditions for musical practice\. However, as these internal psychological states are inferred by teachers for whole groups rather than evaluated at the individual level, interpretations regarding direct psychological mechanisms remain limited\. In teaching applications, compared with simply increasing the frequency of activities, improving the design quality of open and reflective tasks may be of more practical significance\.

## [Development and psychometric validation of the cognitive flexibility scale for Indian adolescents](../publications/dca297e8251c0a830efb.md)

Paramjit Singh; Harneet Billing

A large number of instruments have been developed to measure cognitive flexibility, reflecting its growing recognition as an emerging and significant construct in psychology\. The study reports on the development of a cognitive flexibility scale for adolescents, and the assessment of its internal consistency, test\- retest reliability and validity\. An exploratory sequential research design comprising three phases was employed\. Phase 1 focused on item generation and testing an initial pool of items, leading to the development of a set of potential items for the scale\. Phase 2 involved conducting a pilot study to assess the preliminary items, leading to the selection of the final set of items\. Phase 3 was a validation phase where the scale was administered to a larger sample\. Item analysis was used to assess the internal consistency of the scales, and Exploratory Factor Analysis to explore the properties of the CFS\. Exploratory Factor Analysis using the principal axis identified a three\-factor structure for the 26\-item CFS\. Internal consistency for the CFS \(Cronbach’s alpha = 0\.79\) was found to be acceptable\. The cognitive flexibility scale provides a validated tool that will allow educators and researchers to assess the cognition of secondary school students, enabling them to plan interventions for them\.

## [Epileptic seizure onset early warning using a lightweight multimodal self\-explainable neural network](../publications/dca3586f1ca7b1c887ec.md)

Daraje Kaba Gurmessa; Kula Kekeba Tune; Worku Jimma

BackgroundCutting\-edge deep learning algorithms are applied to epileptic seizures to uncover hidden patterns and achieve high accuracy\. Post hoc algorithms explain black\-box models but do not reveal the detailed workings of the algorithms\. Therefore, intrinsic methods overcome these issues; however, they suffer from improper use of indicative metrics and performance\-to\-accuracy trade\-offs\.ObjectiveThis study implements a lightweight multimodal explainable Neural Network for real\-time early warning of epileptic seizure onset\.MethodsPeople with drug\-resistant epilepsy across all age groups who had regular follow\-up at Emanuel Mental Specialized Hospital in Ethiopia during the data collection period were the study population\. EEG recordings were performed using the 10/20 system\. A pretest was conducted two weeks before actual data collection\. EDFbrowser was used for preparing the dataset in CSV format\. Learned and identity self\-explainable neural network algorithms were used to develop a model\. In addition to classical evaluation metrics, explicitness, faithfulness, stability, and clear patterns behind predictions were used\. Ethical approval was also obtained from the institutional review board \(IRB\) with reference number No: AM/146/2/36\.ResultsLearned and identity self\-explainable neural networks were developed and compared\. The models&\#x27; accuracies are 96\.524% and 95\.328%, and their stability mean values are 99\.88% and 99\.88%, respectively\. Additionally, explicitness values of 0\.0055 and 0\.01197 were achieved, respectively\.ConclusionThe results demonstrate that using a self\-explainable neural network is a promising step toward responsible and transparent artificial intelligence\. Comparing the two models shows that the learned self\-explainable neural network is slightly more optimistic than the identity self\-explainable neural network\.

## [Evaluation of Mechanical and Durability Properties of Polypropylene\-Basalt Hybrid Fibre\-Reinforced Concrete](../publications/dcb0b21f9b0d5661873c.md)

Ram Reddy; Jayarami Reddy

Hybrid fibre\-reinforced concrete is an effective approach for improving the mechanical performance, deformation capacity, and durability of concrete by combining fibres with complementary mechanical characteristics\. Basalt fibres provide high stiffness and tensile strength, whereas polypropylene fibres contribute to crack control and post\-cracking deformation\. However, the combined influence of total hybrid fibre volume and fibre proportion on the mechanical and durability performance of polypropylene\-basalt hybrid fibre\-reinforced concrete requires further investigation\. Therefore, this study experimentally evaluates the mechanical and durability properties of M40\-grade polypropylene\-basalt hybrid fibre\-reinforced concrete with different total fibre volume fractions and fibre proportions\. Twelve hybrid mixtures were prepared by varying the total fibre volume from 0\.25% to 1\.0% and the polypropylene\-to\-basalt fibre ratio as 25:75, 50:50, and 75:25, along with a plain concrete control mix\. Compressive and flexural strengths were evaluated at 3, 7, 28, and 90 days, while splitting tensile strength and water absorption were assessed at 28 days\. Compressive stress\-strain behaviour and deformation characteristics were also examined\. The results showed that compressive strength was most effective at low to moderate fibre contents of 0\.25\-0\.50%, particularly in basalt\-rich mixtures, whereas higher fibre contents reduced compressive strength because of fibre interaction, reduced workability, and dispersion limitations\. Flexural strength and deformation capacity improved substantially with hybrid fibre incorporation, with basalt\-rich mixtures providing higher peak strength and polypropylene fibres contributing to post\-cracking deformation\. The 28\-day splitting tensile strength increased by nearly 30% at 0\.75% total fibre volume in the basalt\-rich mixture\. Water absorption progressively decreased with increasing fibre content, reaching a minimum of 1\.07% at 1\.0% total fibre volume in the basalt\-rich mixture\. Overall, polypropylene\-basalt hybridisation effectively balances strength, ductility, tensile resistance, and durability, with the optimum fibre content depending on the targeted performance requirements\.

## [A critical pedagogy approach to reimagining professionalism in clinical associate/clinical officer training in Sub\-Saharan Africa](../publications/dcb4f165b60ad6ef5083.md)

Esther Cele; Nabeela Sujee

Clinical Associates and Clinical Officers \(CA/COs\) play an increasingly important role in strengthening primary healthcare systems across Sub\-Saharan Africa, particularly in underserved and under\-resourced communities\. Despite their community\-oriented mandate, professionalism within health professions education continues to be predominantly conceptualised through biomedical, competency\-based, and individualised frameworks that prioritise observable behaviours and professional attributes\. While valuable, these approaches may inadequately account for the historical, social, political, and relational dimensions of practice that shape healthcare delivery in contexts marked by colonial legacies, health inequities, and workforce shortages\. This paper aims to explore how critical pedagogy can be used to critique and reimagine professionalism within CA/CO education in Sub\-Saharan Africa\. Drawing on the work of Paulo Freire, alongside scholarship from health professions education, decolonial theory, and professionalism studies, we undertake a conceptual analysis of dominant professionalism discourses and examine their applicability to the realities of CA/CO practice\. Through the Freirean concepts of dialogue, praxis, and critical consciousness, as well as drawing from concepts of Ubuntu we propose an alternative conceptualisation of professionalism that is relational, contextual, political, and emancipatory\. We argue that critical professionalism as a reimagined approach should extend beyond adherence to predefined competencies and behaviours towards a critically informed engagement with communities, health systems, and the structural conditions that influence health and healthcare\. By foregrounding social accountability, equity, and contextually responsive practice, critical pedagogy offers a theoretically grounded approach for reimagining professionalism within CA/CO education\. This perspective has implications for curriculum design, faculty development, professionalism assessment, and professional identity formation, whilst contributing to broader discussions regarding socially responsive and decolonially informed health professions education\.

## [Within\-Group Changes in Functional Capacity among Geriatrics before and after an Integrated Virtual Reality Physical Activity Programme in Nairobi, Kenya](../publications/dcba37f30d9b7d86c14a.md)

Brian Luganu; Roselyn Odiango; Issah Kweyu

Purpose: The global increase in the aging population has led to a rise in age\-related functional decline, particularly in institutional care settings in low\- and middle\-income countries\. While physical activity is a well\-documented strategy for mitigating this decline, adherence to conventional exercise programs among older adults is often limited by physical discomfort, fear of falling, and unengaging designs\. This study evaluated the within\-group changes in functional capacity among geriatrics before and after an integrated Virtual Reality \(VR\) physical activity intervention programme in Nairobi, Kenya\. Methodology: A quasi\-experimental design was adopted, involving 42 older adults \(19 in a control group and 23 in an experimental group\)\. The experimental group participated in a 12\-week integrated VR physical activity programme using the Meta Quest 3 headset, while the control group continued with routine care\. Participants were assessed at baseline, midline \(6 weeks\), and post\-intervention \(12 weeks\) using functional capacity measures: handgrip strength, Five\-Times Sit\-to\-Stand Test \(5TSTS\), Berg Balance Scale \(BBS\), Timed Up and Go \(TUG\) test, and De Morton Mobility Index \(DEMMI\)\. Data were analyzed using paired samples t\-tests for normally distributed difference scores and Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank tests for non\-normally distributed difference scores\. Statistical significance was determined at p &lt; 0\.05\. Findings: The findings revealed a stark contrast in within\-group trajectories\. The control group showed no statistically significant changes in any functional capacity measures over the 12 weeks \(p\-values ranging from \.178 to \.778\)\. Conversely, the experimental group demonstrated highly significant improvements across all functional domains from baseline to midline and post\-intervention \(p &lt; \.001\)\. The progressive improvement observed in the experimental group indicates a dose\- and exposure\-related pattern, where continued participation yielded accumulated functional gains\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study concludes that the integrated VR physical activity programme has a significant positive effect on functional capacity, whereas routine care alone is insufficient to induce measurable functional improvements\.

## [SCMamba\-SAM: transferring knowledge from natural images to medical tasks](../publications/dcc245d35cefafa6e530.md)

Ye Tian; Yufei Yuan; Lu Wang; Xinming Yang; Yifeng Wu; Xu Xu

Background and objective The Segment Anything Model \(SAM\) has drawn significant attention because of its powerful performance in generating high\-quality objectmasks\. Despite its superior performance in handling natural images, SAM exhibits significant performance degradation when applied to medical images due to the substantial domain gap between natural and medical images\. In addition, the specific characteristics of medical images, such as strong heterogeneity, low contrast, and wide individual variation, further raise dificulties in segmenting medical images\. Methods To bridge the semantic gap between natural and medical images, we propose an adaption framework, named SCMamba\-SAM\. It employs a foundational image encoder constructed by integrating the pre\-trained encoder of SAM and Low\-Rank Adaption technique\. The Encoding Mamba Adapter adopts the spatial\- and channel\-Mamba blocks to capture task\-related global features\. Additionally, an enhanced mask decoder with deep supervision has been developed to eliminate the requirement for a prompt encoder, thereby transforming SAM into a fully automated and highly accurate image segmentation model\. Results Extensive experiments were performed on six public lesion segmentation datasets in different imaging modalities and body parts\. The proposed SCMamba\-SAM not only achieved performance superior to that of SOTA methods, quantitatively and qualitatively, but also exhibited high generalization\. Conclusion SCMamba\-SAM holds promise as a useful tool for clinicians to diagnose and quantify lesions, providing important information for treatment decisions and surgery planning\.

## [Liver Function Assessment in Oncology: Current Tools for Evaluating Hepatic Reserve and Surgical Decision\-Making](../publications/dcdfa51cfe37cc214406.md)

Silvio Caringi; Antonella Delvecchio; Annachiara Casella; Valentina Ferraro; Matteo Stasi; Nunzio Tralli; Tommaso Maria Manzia; Riccardo Inchingolo; Michele Tedeschi; Riccardo Memeo

Accurate assessment of hepatic functional reserve is essential in patients with primary or secondary liver malignancies undergoing liver resection, particularly in the presence of chronic liver disease, chemotherapy\-associated liver injury, cholestasis, or portal hypertension\. Conventional laboratory parameters and clinical scores, including Child\-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, and the combined APRI/ALBI score, provide accessible measures of global hepatic status and risk stratification but do not directly quantify regional function or dynamic metabolic capacity\. Complementary approaches include indocyanine green clearance, LiMAx testing, liver stiffness measurement, hepatobiliary scintigraphy, gadoxetic acid\-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and CT/MRI\-based future liver remnant volumetry\. This narrative review critically examines the strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability of these modalities in the context of contemporary evidence and recommendations\. Building on, but extending beyond, the 2023 E\-AHPBA\-ESSO\-ESSR Innsbruck consensus, we incorporate subsequent comparative evidence on blood\-based scores and functional imaging and discuss emerging approaches including longitudinal assessment, radiomics, and artificial intelligence\. Current evidence supports an individualized, multimodal strategy in which volumetry remains central to surgical planning, while additional functional and portal\-hypertension assessment is selected according to the extent of resection, underlying parenchymal disease, previous treatment, and local expertise\. No single modality or fixed combination can currently be considered universally superior, highlighting the need for prospective validation of integrated and cost\-effective assessment strategies\.

## [Trustworthy AI for Sustainable Cities: A Multimodal Orchestration Agent\-Based Framework for Civic Compliance](../publications/dcdfb39a2f09c25c444d.md)

Hasmawaty Ahmad Rahman; Zaid Amin; Nazlena Mohamad Ali; Rahma Santhi Zinaida

Sustainable municipal resource stewardship requires a harmonized artificial intelligence \(AI\) architecture that aligns technical performance with human\-centered behavioral dynamics\. Traditional smart city enforcement frameworks frequently trigger psychological reactance and perceptual failure in noisy, crowded urban spaces\. This study presents HARMONY, a socio\-technical edge\-computing and agent\-based framework that integrates localized computer vision \(YOLOv8\) with Mesa 3\.0 agent modeling to promote non\-coercive civic compliance in waste disposal\. We formally calibrate behavioral constants, including the Politeness Modifier \(Lp = 0\.98\), Gratitude Loop increment \(δ = 0\.025\), and irreducible human defiance floor \(ε = 0\.12\), grounded in self\-determination theory, politeness theory, and empirical habit formation models\. We also mathematically resolve sensory asymmetry in Hierarchical Orchestration Logic \(HOL\) by enforcing strictly normalized, bi\-directional modality allocation \(wv \+ wa = 1\.0\) conditioned on acoustic noise \(N\) and optical reliability \(Qv\)\. Across 100\-run Monte Carlo simulations, HARMONY achieves a terminal Correct Disposal Rate \(CDR\) of 87\.9% ± 3\.3% \(95% CI: \[87\.3%, 88\.6%\]\), outperforming the coercive baseline \(57\.0% ± 4\.9%\)\. A comprehensive six\-arm factorial ablation study isolates the distinct contributions of interactional politeness \(\+30\.5% compliance gain\), HOL sensory resilience \(\+1\.6% to \+21\.4% under severe noise\), and gratitude habituation \(\+0\.5% to \+30\.3% sustained retention\)\. Furthermore, population heterogeneity evaluations across diverse civic cohorts confirm robust performance from civic champions to highly resistant populations\. Localized edge prototyping demonstrates 18\.4 ms inference latency with 94\.2% mAP, operating under an Edge\-Only Ephemeral Vector Processing \(E\-EVP\) paradigm that guarantees privacy\-by\-design\. These findings demonstrate that cooperative, polite AI stewardship offers a scalable, legally robust, and ethically aligned alternative to punitive urban surveillance\.

## [A Brain Uptake Constant for Mathematical Modeling of Cerebral Radiopharmaceutical Uptake: A Synthetic Computational Study](../publications/dce63e9a22eec2ef8f29.md)

Matheus dos Santos Farias

Compartmental and tracer\-kinetic models are widely used to describe radiopharmaceutical uptake in brain PET and SPECT, but in simple analytical models the fraction of transferred activity that reaches the brain is seldom isolated as a parameter of its own\. This study defines a dimensionless Brain Uptake Constant, $\\psi$, as the uptake fraction in a two\-stage first\-order model of cerebral radiopharmaceutical activity and examines its behaviour in a purely synthetic setting\. Activity in the systemic pool, $A\(t\)$, is lost at a first\-order rate $k$; cerebral activity, $A\_c\(t\)$, receives a source term $\\psi k A\(t\)$ and is lost at an effective decay rate $\\lambda$\. The closed\-form solution was evaluated directly for $A\_0 = 100$\~MBq, $k = 0\.25$\~min$^\{\-1\}$, $\\lambda = 0\.05$\~min$^\{\-1\}$ and $\\psi = 1\.00$, 0\.75, 0\.50 and 0\.25 over 0\-60\~min\. Deterministic Gaussian fields were used to show the spatial effect of $\\psi$ as surface plots and heat maps\. Each curve rises, passes through a single maximum at $t\_\{\\mathrm\{peak\}\} = 8\.047$\~min and then decays\. The peak time does not depend on $\\psi$, whereas the peak activity \(66\.87\~MBq for $\\psi = 1$\) and the 0\-60\~min time\-integrated activity scale linearly with $\\psi$\. In the spatial fields, $\\psi$ changes the amplitude but not the prescribed Gaussian widths\. No clinical, PET or SPECT data were used, so the results say nothing about clinical validity\. The model is offered as a simple parameterization that still has to be tested against measured dynamic imaging data with independently estimated kinetic parameters\.

## [Federated multimodal home school collaborative dance intervention for inclusive preschool education with privacy preserving and explainable AI framework](../publications/dcf3e727d11152a5be4f.md)

Lan Ma

Inclusive preschool dance intervention is a high\-impact yet methodologically difficult educational scenario\. Effective intervention requires precise movement analysis, longitudinal home–school collaboration, and communication outputs that teachers and caregivers can directly act on\. At the same time, child data governance imposes strict constraints on centralizing raw videos, behavior logs, and family reports\. Existing systems typically optimize only one axis, such as model accuracy or platform usability, but do not provide a unified technical and evaluation framework that addresses educational efficacy, privacy, fairness, and interpretability together\. This paper develops a federated multimodal framework for inclusive preschool dance education, with explicit links between model design and educational decision requirements\. The method combines pose\-sequence encoding, teacher\-record embedding, parent\-text representation, and interaction\-log modeling under incomplete\-modality conditions\. Reliability\-aware fusion is coupled with fairness regularization and differential\-privacy training\. A constrained recommendation module translates model outputs into role\-specific guidance for teachers and caregivers while preserving evidence traceability\. To evaluate this system under realistic intervention conditions, we define a 16\-week three\-arm cluster\-randomized protocol and an eight\-experiment matrix covering intervention effect, retention, mediation, fairness, ablation, robustness, privacy–utility trade\-off, and cross\-school transfer\. The complete system was implemented and evaluated under the study protocol described in Sect\. 4 \. All numerical values in Tables 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 and 10 ; Figs\. 5 , 6 , 7 and 8 are retained from the completed study and model experiments; no values were simulated or generated during this revision\. The empirical results show the largest motor\-skill and social\-inclusion gains for HomeSchool\-AI, while the ablation, robustness, privacy–utility, and cross\-school analyses provide complementary evidence for the proposed framework\.

## [Performance\-driven mix design and multi\-response optimization of ambient\-cured fly ash\-GGBFS based geopolymer concrete](../publications/dcf3ef125afa5c11ac37.md)

Md Ruhul Amin; Mohd Shariq; Abdul Baqi; Mohd Asif Ansari

Fly ash \(FA\) and ground granulated blast furnace slag \(GGBFS\) are widely investigated as alternative precursor materials for alkali\-activated geopolymer concrete \(GPC\)\. However, systematic mixture proportioning is required to achieve desirable fresh and mechanical performance under ambient\-curing conditions\. This study presents a performance\-driven optimization framework for waste\-based FA\-GGBFS GPC using Response Surface Methodology \(RSM\) integrated with a desirability function approach\. An experimental programme comprising 18 unique mixtures arranged in a 3 × 3 × 2 full\-factorial structure was conducted using three GGBFS replacement levels \(25%, 50%, and 75%\), three alkaline solution\-to\-binder \(AL/B\) ratios \(0\.45, 0\.50, and 0\.55\), and two predefined mix\-design levels \(M1 and M2\)\. Five performance responses, including slump, 7\- and 28\-day compressive strengths \(CS\), and 7\- and 28\-day splitting tensile strengths \(SPT\), were investigated\. The results demonstrated that GGBFS replacement was the dominant factor influencing the investigated mechanical responses, while the AL/B ratio exhibited a non\-monotonic influence on strength\. CS and SPT generally increased with increasing GGBFS replacement within the investigated range, whereas mechanical performance generally improved as the AL/B ratio increased from 0\.45 to approximately 0\.50 and declined when it was further increased to 0\.55\. Slump increased with increasing AL/B ratio and decreased with increasing GGBFS replacement\. The hierarchically reduced response models exhibited R 2 values ranging from 0\.9302 to 0\.9829, with predicted R 2 values ranging from 0\.8000 to 0\.9028 and Adequate Precision values between 16\.1109 and 26\.3199\. Multi\-response optimization identified constrained optimum at the upper investigated GGBFS level of 75%, with AL/B ratios of 0\.508 for M1 and 0\.494 for M2, yielding overall desirability values of 0\.945 and 0\.976, respectively\. Comparison with the available confirmation results showed reasonable agreement between the experimental and model\-predicted responses within the investigated design space\. Overall, the proposed framework provides an experimentally supported approach for predicting and optimizing the fresh and mechanical performance of ambient\-cured FA\-GGBFS\-based GPC within the investigated mixture\-design domain\.

## [Sin ruana jurídica que abrigue el riesgo: diagnóstico normativo del derecho penal colombiano frente a la inteligencia artificial](../publications/dd0edcca8f43d7892254.md)

Juan Pablo Torres León; Alejandro Valencia Criollo

El presente estudio se desarrolla en el contexto de la creciente implementación global de sistemas de inteligencia artificial \(IA\) y la ausencia, en Colombia, de un marco regulatorio integral frente al derecho penal, problema crítico en la medida en que las organizaciones públicas y privadas que desarrollan, comercializan o utilizan este tipo de tecnología operan en un vacío normativo que compromete la seguridad jurídica y la gobernanza del riesgo tecnológico; a partir de ello, la investigación aborda el escenario actual y material en Colombia ante una eventual comisión de delitos utilizando inteligencia artificial, examinando el concepto y clasificación de la IA, la expansión del derecho penal frente a nuevas realidades tecnológicas y los modelos regulatorios comparados de Brasil y la Unión Europea; su aporte al conocimiento en materia de interpretación normativa radica en ofrecer a entidades estatales, empresas desarrolladoras y operadores jurídicos un diagnóstico normativo que permite anticipar riesgos de cumplimiento, responsabilidad y gobernanza en la adopción institucional de sistemas de IA; metodológicamente, se empleó un enfoque cualitativo, de tipo dogmático\-jurídico y de derecho comparado, con revisión documental de fuentes académicas, normativas y doctrinales verificadas en fuente oficial; los resultados evidencian que Colombia carece de una ley marco de inteligencia artificial, que el CONPES 4144 de 2025 es un instrumento de planeación sin fuerza vinculante penal, que la ley 2502 de 2025 constituye una reforma penal de vanguardia, y que persisten vacíos estructurales en contenido sintético no consentido, desinformación electoral y daños algorítmicos que no pueden atenderse por vía judicial; se concluye que la falta de normativa regulatoria repercute en una fragmentación del derecho penal ante nuevas exigencias, lo que obliga a las instituciones atender los riesgos jurídicos derivados del uso sin límite de estas tecnologías\.

## [Association between digital agricultural technology promotion and farmers’ adoption of extreme climate adaptation technologies: evidence from chili pepper farmers in Guizhou Province, China](../publications/dd38f30d9d4857a8f018.md)

Hongjuan Gao; Han Huiqing

Adaptation technologies are important for reducing the risks associated with extreme climatic events, particularly in mountainous areas where complex topography can increase agricultural vulnerability\. Digital Agricultural Technology Promotion \(DATP\) provides an increasingly important channel through which farmers access information related to climate adaptation technologies\. However, empirical evidence on the association between DATP and farmers’ adoption of such technologies in mountainous areas remains limited\. Using survey data from 846 chili pepper farmers in Guizhou Province, China, this study employs baseline regression, mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and heterogeneity analysis to examine the association between DATP and farmers’ adoption of extreme climate adaptation technologies\. The results show that DATP is significantly and positively associated with both adoption degree and sustained adoption willingness\. Mediation analysis identifies three potential pathways consistent with this association: broader information access channels, greater information trust, and stronger information application ability\. Moderation analysis further shows that benefit and risk expectation confirmation significantly condition the association between DATP and adaptation behavior\. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the positive association is strongest for water resource management and biological control technologies and is relatively stronger among pure farmers, farmers with higher digital literacy, and large\-scale chili farmers\. These findings highlight the relevance of information access, information credibility, digital capabilities, and farmer heterogeneity in understanding digital approaches to climate adaptation in mountainous agricultural areas\. The findings provide empirical evidence for developing differentiated digital strategies to support farmers’ climate adaptation\.

## [YON AMIOTROFIK SKLEROZNING ERTA BOSQICHLARIDA RTMS QOʻLLASHNING KLINIK SAMARADORLIGINI BAHOLASH](../publications/dd43950051a97bebff88.md)

Abdukadirova D\.T\.; Xoshimjonov B\.

Yon amiotrofik skleroz \(YoASK\) — yuqori va pastki motoneyronlarning progressiv degeneratsiyasi bilan kechuvchi, ogʻir nogironlik va oʻlimga olib keluvchi neyrodegenerativ kasallikdir\. Kasallik patogenezida kortikal giperqo’zgaluvchanlik erta neyrofiziologik biomarker sifatida muhim oʻrin tutadi hamda motoneyron shikastlanishining boshlangʻich bosqichlarini aks ettirishi mumkin\. Repetitiv transkranial magnit stimulyatsiya \(rTMS\) bosh miya poʻstlogʻining qoʻzgʻaluvchanligini modulyatsiya qiluvchi, invaziv boʻlmagan neyromodulyatsion usul boʻlib, u kortikal plastiklik mexanizmlariga ta’sir koʻrsatish orqali kasallik progressiyasini sekinlashtirish ehtimolini beradi\. Mazkur maqolada YoASKning erta bosqichlarida rTMS qoʻllashning klinik samaradorligi baholanadi\. Asosiy baholash mezoni sifatida ALS Functional Rating Scale – Revised \(ALSFRS\-R\) shkalasi koʻrsatkichlari hamda motor funksiyalarning dinamik oʻzgarishlari tahlil qilinadi\. Tadqiqot natijalari rTMSning kortikal gipereksitabilitetni kamaytirish orqali funksional koʻrsatkichlarga potensial ijobiy ta’sirini koʻrsatishi mumkin\.

## [Culinary Chemistry as a Platform for Interfacial Materials Design](../publications/dd4af51f3d506a5a9462.md)

Josep Moreno; I\. Brian Becerril‐Castro; Irene Calderón; Jaslyn Ru Ting Chen; Zhiming Wang; Alexander O\. Govorov; Jose  Manuel Romo\-Herrera; Neus Feliu; Wolfgang Johann Parak; Miguel A\. Correa‐Duarte; In Yee Phang; Xing Yi Ling; Ramón A\. Álvarez‐Puebla

ABSTRACT This Review examines culinary systems as experimentally accessible models of interfacial materials design\. Culinary operations, including emulsification, foaming, gelation, spherification, controlled heating, smoking, and dehydration, govern gas‐liquid, oil‐water, solid‐liquid, polymer‐nanoparticle, and hydrogel‐analyte interfaces, thereby coupling microstructure to transport, mechanics, optical response, and sensory performance\. We then analyze how programmable heated high‐shear mixers, pressure cookers, food‐derived hydrocolloids, protein fibrils, metal‐phenolic networks, anthocyanins, and plasmonic nanostructures can support functional materials, sensing, and potentially more sustainable processing\. Original Au/agar‐agar and Ag/agar‐agar experiments are presented as bounded proof‐of‐concept demonstrations of this translation\. The Review closes by identifying constraints in safety classification, regulatory acceptance, reproducibility, stability, scale‐up, and end‐of‐life assessment\. This interface‐centered framework positions culinary chemistry not merely as applied chemistry, but as a source of processing concepts and structure‐property relationships for advanced materials\.

## [When AI wears a celebrity&\#x27;s face: Personality Rights, Commercial Exploitation and the Call for Statutory Reform in India](../publications/dd6eddebf11b44b00b96.md)

ASMAA BARWELKAR

Abstract The Digital Era of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Deepfake Technologies, and Voice Cloning has made it easier to violate a celebrity&\#x27;s personality rights\. Though the Indian judiciary recognizes these rights under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, it has been providing supplementary remedies by combining various sections of the Information Technology Act 2005, Copyright Act 1957, Trademarks Act 1999, and DPDP Act 2023\. These alone cannot tackle the unprecedented issue created by these technologies\. Celebrities such as Anil Kapoor and Arijit Singh have approached the court for the issue of the use of AI &amp; Deepfake technologies to replicate or mimic their personal traits— name, image, voice, and likeness—or any other form of artistic expression to create phony Ads, fraudulent brand endorsements, and social media content without their permission\. Such acts cause emotional and reputational damage to these stars and commercially exploit them by infringing on their right to control their public image\. The absence of codified statutory law on this issue leads to ambiguity and uncertainty\. Judgements differ on a case\-by\-case basis that allows judges to narrow or expand the scope of personality rights\. India needs a dedicated law on this, as seen in other international jurisdictions, such as Denmark, the USA, and the European Union\. This paper argues that India needs a specific statutory framework defining Personality Rights, violations by AI, and providing appropriate remedies\. Such specific legislation is called for when individuals become commercially significant through their public persona\. People are becoming overnight celebrities on social media, and their public personas need protection from the rapidly evolving technological landscape\. Keywords: Personality Rights, Artificial Intelligence, Deepfakes, Right to Publicity, Commercial Exploitation, Right to Privacy\.

## [Symbolic Congruence in Disaster Medicine: The Role of Royal and Customary Figures in Societal Resilience in the Face of Health Crises](../publications/dd89f3ecaec0c1845144.md)

Leon Savadogo; Bachira Tomeh; Mahmoud El\-Hussein; Donald Donahue; Frank Van Trimpont; Joel Ipara; Jean\-Marie Carrara; Jan\-Cédric Hansen

Background: Disaster medicine studies the capacity of societies to absorb, adapt to, and recover from health or humanitarian crises\. From this perspective, collective trust, institutional legibility, and adherence to expected behaviours constitute major determinants of resilience\. By analogy with the genetic and genealogical congruence developed by READ, we propose here the concept of symbolic congruence to analyse the role of socially recognized figures in crisis contexts\. Objective: To explore how royal, customary, or institutional figures — Queen Alphonsine Kande, King Felipe VI, the Rex Sacrorum, and Charles X — may contribute to societal resilience when they render several registers of legitimacy socially coherent and facilitate trust, cooperation, or the acceptability of response measures\. Approach: A narrative review of the literature \(2000–2026\) combining medical, legal, historical, and institutional sources, organized around four contrasting case studies and analysed using a theoretical framework centred on symbolic congruence\. Results: The cases studied show that symbolic congruence does not rest on a simple duality between symbolic legitimacy and legal legitimacy, but on the convergence of several registers of legitimacy perceived as coherent by populations\. Depending on context, this convergence contributes to preserving ritual continuity, reducing political uncertainty, strengthening cohesion, fostering cooperation, or improving the acceptability of health measures, with indirect but significant effects on response effectiveness and resilience\. The results also suggest that symbolic congruence may act as a regulatory mechanism for collective cognition\. By fostering the construction of shared representations of risk, of institutions, and of expected responses, it would indirectly contribute to strengthening collective trust, cooperation, and societal resilience\. Conclusion: Symbolic congruence provides a useful conceptual framework for understanding how socially recognized figures can act as mediators between legitimacy, trust, acceptability, and societal resilience during crises\. It thus offers a relevant interpretive lens for disaster medicine, in Africa as in Europe\.

## [Wellness and active ageing among older adults \(65\+\): case in Albania](../publications/dd9cc00f26af82b006e4.md)

Elsa Dhuli; Kozeta Sevrani; Vanesa Çelaj

Albania’s demographic and social landscape is increasingly shaped by the growing proportion of individuals aged 65 years and over\. As life expectancy rises and demographic ageing becomes more pronounced, older adults represent an increasingly important population group that requires enhanced social, health and community\-based support\. Nevertheless, many older people in Albania continue to face challenges related to mental well\-being, social isolation, loneliness, limited access to organized activities, and a lack of sustainable wellness initiatives tailored to their needs\. This study examines demographic ageing trends and selected indicators of wellness and active ageing among older adults in Albania\. The analysis is based on Population and Housing Census data from 2001, 2011 and 2023, complemented by Labour Force Survey data and social inclusion indicators\. A descriptive demographic trend analysis and linear trend regression models are used to assess changes in population structure and labour market participation among individuals aged 65 years and over\. The findings reveal a substantial increase in the older population, accompanied by important challenges related to health conditions, disability, poverty risk, and social exclusion\. At the same time, improvements in educational attainment and increased labor force participation among some groups of older adults indicate opportunities to promote active ageing\. The results highlight the multidimensional nature of wellness in later life, emphasizing that active ageing extends beyond healthcare to include social participation, economic security, community engagement, dignity and independence\. The study underscores the importance of developing accessible, community\-based initiatives that support healthy, active ageing\. The findings provide evidence that may inform the design of policies to improve the well\-being and quality of life of older adults in Albania\.

## [Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations](../publications/dda2ba19963b2723081b.md)

Yuheng Mao; Hao Peng; Jiayuan Zhong; Yong Liu; Luonan Chen; Rui Liu; Pei Chen

Abstract Acute kidney injury \(AKI\) is a life\-threatening condition with notably high in\-hospital mortality, characterized by a three\-phase progression: a relatively stable state \(without imminent life threat\), a critical pre\-deterioration state \(the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration\), and a deteriorated state \(severe conditions such as death or rescue events\)\. Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high\-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression\. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse \(Spatiotemporal Information fusion\), a unique dual\-view framework that integrates deep learning \(DL\) and spatiotemporal information transformation \(STI\) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down \(CSD\) theory\. The DL backbone encodes multi\-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high\-dimensional spatial information into a low\-dimensional dynamic representation\. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction\. An optimal\-transport\-distance\-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states\. Pretrained on the MIMIC\-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts \(including MIMIC\-III \(with two independent cohorts\), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU\), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72\-hour deterioration\. Further analysis of single\-cell multi\-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI\. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models\.

## [Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease Biomarkers Measured by Capillary Blood Collection Versus Venous Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid](../publications/dda52132f4edcf3cb3e4.md)

Sara Grace Ho; Ziling Shen; Alexandria Lewis; Megha Patel; Anny Zheng; Gianna Proscino; Thaovy Ho; Jiangxia Wang; Marilyn Albert; Abhay Moghekar

OBJECTIVE: Blood biomarkers are increasingly critical for non\-invasive Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease \(AD\) diagnostics and research but typically require on\-site processing\. Remote point\-of\-care collection methods could enhance biomarker testing in clinical and research settings\. We evaluated the safety and accuracy of blood collection via venous blood and two capillary blood collection devices \(Tasso\+ and TAPII\) for measurements of amyloid\-beta 42/40 ratio \(Aβ42/40\), phosphorylated\-tau\-217 \(pTau217\), neurofilament\-light \(NfL\), and glial fibrillary acidic protein \(GFAP\) from capillary plasma to simultaneously collected venous plasma and cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\)\. METHODS: Patients seen at the Johns Hopkins Center for CSF Disorders \(N = 192\) underwent diagnostic lumbar punctures and venipuncture\. Warming packs were held to the skin for 5 min before collecting capillary blood \(via TAPII or Tasso\+ device\) and numeric pain scores\. CSF, venous, and capillary plasma were analyzed using Quanterix SIMOA immunoassays\. Statistical analysis included Pearson/Spearman correlations, Lasso regression, and quantitative comparisons using Bland\-Altman plots\. RESULTS: 86 TAPII and 126 Tasso\+ plasma samples were collected \(77 M, 115 F; mean age 61 ± 18\.3 years, range 16\-91\)\. Tasso\+ devices were 90\.3% successful in collecting &gt; 50 μL whole blood, and TAPII devices were 86% successful\. Mean pain scores were significantly higher in venous than capillary collections \(Venous 2\.24/10, TAPII 0\.73/10, Tasso\+ 0\.2/10, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Capillary Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP strongly correlated with venous plasma analytes \(Tasso\+: Aβ42/40 r = 0\.75, NfL r = 0\.91, GFAP r = 0\.80, all p &lt; 0\.001; TAPII: Aβ42/40 r = 0\.74, NfL r = 0\.86, GFAP r = 0\.84, all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Tasso\+ capillary pTau217 weakly correlated with venous \(r = 0\.23, p = 0\.04\)\. Capillary NfL and GFAP correlated modestly with CSF NfL and GFAP \(TAPII NfL r = 0\.74, GFAP r = 0\.6, all p &lt; 0\.0001; Tasso\+ NfL r = 0\.69, GFAP r = 0\.59, all p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. Capillary Aβ42/40 and pTau217 did not significantly correlate with CSF measures\. Lasso regression identified age and GFAP as significant predictors of AD across capillary and venous samples \(Tasso\+ AUC = 0\.87, TAPII AUC = 0\.75, Venous AUC = 0\.83\)\. INTERPRETATION: Neurodegeneration biomarkers Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP in capillary plasma \(Tasso\+, TAPII\) strongly correlated with venous plasma measures\. Capillary and venous pTau217 correlated weakly, indicating further assay refinement is needed\. Tasso\+ collection was less painful and caused less hemolysis compared to TAPII\.

## [Don&\#x27;t Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks](../publications/dda6e3303b0b96283dcc.md)

Md Farhan Ishmam; Minh Pham Dinh; Kenneth Marino

The web is not static or uniform\. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently\. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed\. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know\. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low\-rank adapters\. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces\. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual\. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference\. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target\. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena\-Lite\-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp\. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in\-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces\. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models\. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer\. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining\.

## [ANALYSIS OF THE UTILIZATION OF DAKWAH ACCOUNTS ON SOCIAL MEDIA IN FORMING THE SPIRITUAL INTELLIGENCE OF GRADE X STUDENTS OF SMK BHAKTI PERTIWI](../publications/dda82ccf60c00153e01e.md)

Widda Widda; Raihan Raihan

The development of digital technology demands a shift in the strategy of instilling moral values ??for the current generation of vocational high school students in the modern era\. This study aims to analyze in depth the use of Islamic preaching accounts on social media in developing the spiritual intelligence of 10th\-grade students at SMK Bhakti Pertiwi Jakarta\. The approach used was a descriptive qualitative case study method, involving seven informants selected through a purposive sampling technique who actively accessed the Instagram and TikTok platforms\. Data collection was carried out through participatory observation techniques, in\-depth interviews, and documentation studies, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing\. The results show that Islamic preaching content in the form of short videos and inspirational quotes is used by students as a source of motivation for worship, moral reminders, and a means of self\-reflection when facing life&\#x27;s problems\. The conclusion of this research confirms that consistent exposure to virtual Islamic preaching content can stimulate the ability to interpret life experiences, awareness of God&\#x27;s supervision \(muraqabah\), and altruistic behavior in students&\#x27; schools and daily lives\. The novelty of this research lies in the disclosure of the internalization mechanism of microscopic spiritual values ??based on social media consumption in urban vocational school students, which has rarely been explored by previous conventional research\.

## [A causal analytics approach for interpretable supply chain risk and supplier performance evaluation](../publications/ddb68d424a3a96f9159d.md)

Ishwar Gupta; Harshitha Konduru; Sergio Correa; Hendro Wicaksono

Traditional machine learning \(ML\) techniques are widely used to support operational supply chain decisions, but their “black box” nature limits transparency and actionability\. This study addresses this challenge by exploring the effectiveness of causal discovery methods and large language models \(LLMs\) in supply chain management with a focus on the automotive industry\. Six causal discovery algorithms\- Peter–Clark \(PC\), Fast Causal Inference \(FCI\), Greedy Equivalence Search \(GES\), DirectLiNGAM, NOTEARS, and Regression with Subsequent Independence Test \(RESIT\) are benchmarked against an expert\-validated ground\-truth graph constructed from 18 domain experts with a combined 300\+ years of experience, using 12 months of internal supplier Key Performance Indicator \(KPI\) data\. RESIT achieves the closest alignment with expert knowledge, with a False Discovery Rate of 0\.1429, Structural Hamming Distance of 1, precision and recall of 0\.8571 and an F1\-score of 0\.85, outperforming all other algorithms on every metric\. Robustness of the estimated causal effect of Backlog on Escalation is confirmed through three refutation tests\- random common cause, random subset and placebo treatment returning high p\-values of 0\.96, 0\.76, and 0\.98 respectively, indicating insensitivity to spurious confounders and random perturbations\. Counterfactual simulation shows that reducing Backlog by 50%–70% consistently lowers escalation levels across suppliers\. LLMs contribute by extracting causal factors from unstructured external event data, accelerating causal graph construction, and reducing dependence on manual expert input\. LLM\-derived causal graphs are further compared with expert\-validated models to ensure alignment and reliability, and are operationalised through a Weighted Sum Model risk score linking external drivers to internal KPIs for actionable supplier escalation decisions\.

## [Cotton pest and disease multi\-class classification with weather and temporal predictors features across Indian agroclimatic zones](../publications/ddbf7fc9748189ed7b9e.md)



The Pink Bollworm \(Pectinophora gossypiella\) remains one of the most destructive pests affecting cotton productivity, with infestation levels strongly driven by climatic fluctuations and crop phenology\.This study presents a machine learning\-based framework for early multi\-classification and prediction of Pink Bollworm incidence using agro\-meteorological variables\.The dataset includes maximum and minimum air temperature, relative humidity, rainfall, sunshine hours, evaporation, and wind speed, all of which influence Pink Bollworm development, migration, and reproductive cycles\.After preprocessing, applying cyclic encoding to temporal variables, and generating lagged climatic features, multiple machine learning algorithms\-including SVM, Neural Networks, KNN, Regression models, Ensemble methods, and Naïve Bayes\-were trained and systematically compared\.SVM model demonstrated the best test accuracy, effectively capturing dynamic climate\-pest interactions\.The resulting MATLAB\-based classification tool enables rapid assessment and supports climate\-informed pest surveillance\.A stratified 80:20 train\-test split was employed, with 5\-fold cross\-validation on the training set for hyperparameter tuning, ensuring no data leakage between partitions\.The validation and training accuracies of these models are 89\.4% and 96 % respectively\.Overall, the model offers a practical and interpretable solution for early detection of Pink Bollworm risk, thereby contributing to informed decision\-making in integrated pest management \(IPM\) and precision agriculture\.

## [FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging](../publications/ddc0e4724b803cf74a65.md)

Alina Devkota; Annahita Amireskandari; Joel R\. Palko; Soban A\. Maan; Shyam J Thakkar; Tapan Khan; Xiajun Jiang; Donald Adjeroh; Binod Bhattarai; Prashnna Gyawali

Gastrointestinal \(GI\) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention\. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope\. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general\-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability\. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data\. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning \(FL\) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model\. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks\-classification, detection, and segmentation\. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness\. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation\-compliant deployment in real\-world gastroendoscopy practice\.

## [КЛАСИЧНІ ТЕОРІЇ ТА ОСОБЛИВОСТІ СУЧАСНОЇ ПРАКТИКИ ПЕРЕГОВОРІВ У МІЖНАРОДНИХ ВІДНОСИНАХ](../publications/ddc168cc60ea0f2060d8.md)

Оксана Дмитренко

Криза традиційних інститутів глобального управління, зростання кількості збройних конфліктів та гібридних загроз, загострення суперництва у геополітичному просторі породжують глибоку структурну трансформацію сучасного розуміння міжнародних відносин\. Переговорний процес у цьому контексті набуває розуміння того, що і в теорії, і на практиці він повинен бути безальтернативним джерелом врегулювання кризової ситуації, яким активно оперує превентивна дипломатія та ескалація конфлікту\. У статті автор робить спробу надати багатоаспектний аналіз того, як змінювалися міжнародні переговори\. Автор вважає за необхідне через класичні теоретичні парадигми, а саме реалізм, лібералізм, конструктивізм показати, як взаємодіють дипломатичні практики із технологічними змінами\. Ця стаття розкриває адаптацію традиційного дипломатичного протоколу до механізмів глобалізації та потенційного рівня загрози\. Особливу увагу автор приділяє вивченню феномену дрескоду українських представників на міжнародній арені, який стає ознакою не порушення етикету, а новітньою спробою запровадити стратегічну комунікацію та публічну дипломатію на рівні семіотики\. Такий підхід дозволяє радикально переосмислити систему сприйняття держави на міжнародному рівні, у тому числі через дослідження психологічних аспектів взаємодії\. У статті розглянуто концепт ментального простору цільової аудиторії, до якої звертається спікер, те, як впливає тривалість багатомовних переговорів на когнітивний рівень навантаження реципієнта, який важливий концепт перекладу у механізмі посередництва в політиці, що здійснює безпосередній вплив на те, як формуються довіра і зовнішньополітичні наративи\. Окрему увагу в статті приділено аналізу технології медіації, зокрема автори розглядають модель реституційної медіації, яку використовують, щоб врегулювати тривалі конфлікти та відновити правосуддя\. У статті також зроблено спробу комплексно проаналізувати, як впливає цифрова дипломатія і штучний інтелект на процес переговорів через опрацювання змісту алгоритмічних систем, які можуть перетворити медіацію переговорів на процес, що піддається високій аналітиці через оптимізацію обробки великих масивів даних, та можливості спрогнозувати сценарій розвитку подій\. Напрацьовані теоретичні візії разом з аналізом практик у сфері цифровізації та інновацій дозволяє авторам побачити цілісну архітектуру сучасного процесу міжнародних переговорів із метою забезпечення стабільного переговорного процесу задля відстоювання національного інтересу держави у глобальному середовищі, яке конкурує\.
