## [A Bibliometric Analysis of Sustainability Communication Research \(2000–2026\)](../publications/ddc69123945f2b6359e7.md)

Nuray Yılmaz Sert; Mükerrem ÖNLÜ; Selime Gümüş; Ezgi Güneş; Tuba Çevik Ergin; Aybike Pelenk Özel; Gülenaz Selçuk

Sustainability communication is a strategic communication approach that aims to raise awareness of environmental, social, and economic issues and enhance public engagement in line with sustainable development goals\. Particularly since 2020, it has gained increasing importance as the climate crisis, environmental issues, and the Sustainable Development Goals have become more prominent\. This study aims to reveal the overall structure of the sustainability communication literature and identify potential directions for future research\. Accordingly, we conducted a bibliometric analysis using data retrieved from the Web of Science database and analysed them using the bibliometrix package and the Biblioshiny interface in the R environment\. The analysis included 581 documents published between 2000 and 2026\. The findings indicate that sustainability communication has evolved into a rapidly growing field of research\. The literature is structured around core knowledge sources, leading authors, and interconnected research communities, while also exhibiting an interdisciplinary thematic structure\. Furthermore, the findings reveal that the research agenda has become increasingly diversified in recent years\. Taken together, these findings provide a comprehensive picture of the field’s evolution, intellectual structure, and thematic transformation\.

## [Gut bacterial lauroyl tryptamine reduces GPR183\-associated inflammatory responses in human macrophages and T cells in vitro](../publications/dde6ba18a870944e50f2.md)

Marco Lezzerini; Vera Spek; Ivan C N Fung; Michelle Jessy Müller; Aleksej Kubelka; Simon Sieber; Wouter J\. de Jonge; Andrew Y\. Li Yim; Anje A\. te Velde; Jianbo Zhang

Introduction Recent research has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in producing bioactive metabolites that interact with G\-protein coupled receptors \(GPRs\) and influence immune responses\. Lauroyl tryptamine \(LT\), a metabolite produced by Agathobacter rectalis \(formerly Eubacterium rectale \), has been reported to antagonize GPR183, a receptor implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases \(IBD\)\. LT inhibits the binding of GPR183 with its natural ligands 7a,25\-dihydroxycholesterol \(OHC\)\. Methods Here, we analyzed the GPR183 gene expression in intestinal tissues from IBD patients and non\-IBD controls, as well as our previous single\-cell transcriptomic dataset to identify key GPR183\-expressing cells\. We then use in vitro THP\-1 derived macrophage and Jurkat T cell culture to test the effects of LT on inflammatory responses\. Results and discussion The GPR183 gene expression is elevated specifically in colonic and rectal tissues of ulcerative colitis patients, but not in Crohn’s disease or ileal tissue\. By analyzing single\-cell transcriptomic dataset, we identified monocytes/macrophages, T cells, B cells, and innate lymphoid cells as key GPR183 \-expressing populations in human intestine\. Using cell culture models, we demonstrated that LT modulates inflammatory pathways\. In LPS\-stimulated macrophages, OHC increased transcription of pro\-inflammatory genes IL6, TNFA , and IL1B , which are reduced by LT\. In activated Jurkat T cells, LT slightly decreased the OHC\-mediated increase in the transcription of IL2\. These findings support the hypothesis that LT, a known GPR183 antagonist, could modulate GPR183\-associated inflammation in human macrophages and T cells in a context\- and cell type\-dependent manner, offering potential mechanistic insights into bioactive metabolite\-mediated host\-microbiota interactions in human intestine\.

## [Fast and high\-resolution imaging of semi\-airborne frequency tipper sounding method for mineral exploration](../publications/ddef656e8cd9d28fcabb.md)

Min Yin; Juzhi Deng; Hui Chen; Min Feng; Hui Yu; Chongwei Yuan; Jialu Huang

The semi\-airborne frequency tipper sounding method \(SFTS\) based on tipper characteristics exhibits high lateral and vertical resolution, making it a promising technique for deep mineral exploration, particularly in challenging terrains where conventional ground\-based electromagnetic methods face accessibility constraints\. Currently, interpretation techniques for this method remain underdeveloped, limiting its practical application in mineral prospecting\. To accelerate the application of SFTS in mineral exploration, this paper defines the full\-zone apparent resistivity formula based on the complex implicit function relationship between tipper and background resistivity parameters, and iteratively calculates it using the binary search algorithm\. An explicit calculation expression for the apparent depth of SFTS was constructed through data fitting, enabling fast full\-zone apparent resistivity\-depth imaging\. The effectiveness of the imaging method is evaluated using one\-dimensional layered models that simulate common geological scenarios in mineral exploration, including conductive sediment\-hosted and resistive basement settings\. Furthermore, the imaging characteristics of single and multiple anomalous bodies are analyzed using a three\-dimensional synthetic model, with the anomalous bodies designed to represent typical mineral deposit types, such as massive sulfide orebodies \(low resistivity\) and porphyry systems \(high resistivity\)\. The synthetic\-model results show that the proposed imaging method can qualitatively delineate the main electrical anomalies and provide preliminary information on their approximate spatial locations\. These results suggest that the method has potential for rapid anomaly recognition and target prioritization before detailed field verification, geological\-constrained interpretation, or quantitative inversion\. The imaging results lay a foundation for data processing and inversion interpretation of SFTS in mineral exploration campaigns\.

## [La valoración de servicios ecosistémicos como herramienta para fortalecer la gobernanza territorial en la Laguna de los Pozuelos, Jujuy, Argentina](../publications/ddf684a6b029ae963f45.md)

Gisela Soledad Córdoba; Leónidas Lizárraga; Pablo Fernando Arias; María Elena Sánchez; María Inés Irazusta; Azucena Carina Rodríguez

The ecosystem services framework has gained relevance in protected areas management due to its potential to address biodiversity loss, resource\-use conflicts, and governance challenges\. This study aimed to identify and prioritize the ecosystem services provided by the Laguna de los Pozuelos and its surrounding area from the perspective of key stakeholders involved in management, research, extension activities, and local community\. The methodology combined stakeholder mapping, literature review, and participatory validation and prioritization processes conducted through in\-person workshops and an online questionnaire\. A total of 25 ecosystem services were identified and grouped into cultural \(6\), provisioning \(9\), and regulating and maintenance \(10\) categories\. Results reveal differentiated valuations according to stakeholders’ roles, knowledge, and territorial relationships\. There was strong agreement on the importance of cultural services and water\-related services as strategic resources, while divergences emerged regarding less visible regulating services\. These findings highlight the need to integrate multiple perspectives into protected areas planning and support the development of participatory and co\-management strategies that strengthen both biodiversity conservation and local well\-being\.

## [From compliance to competence: a multi\-level model for AI governance in undergraduate medical education](../publications/ddfb94cb25e0509b28bb.md)

Juan José Gualda\-Gea; Lourdes Estefanía Barón\-Miras; Maria Jesús Bertran; Alberto L\. García‐Basteiro; Guillermo Mena; Marta Aldea; Gemina Santana; Jaume Grau; Andrés Prat Marín; Isabel Torá Rocamora; Antoni Trilla

AI&\#x27;s fast\-paced irruption in medicine and education has challenged undergraduate medical colleges, with institutions documenting policies emphasizing immediate conduct restrictions, while strategic oversight, infrastructure and evaluation remain less consistently developed\. We propose a multi\-level framework for AI governance in undergraduate medical education based on accountability, competence and co\-responsibility across institutions, educators and students, designed to turn a fast\-evolving technology from a threat into an opportunity for collective progress\.

## [Asynchronous recovery of grassland ecosystem health in northern China: A three\-dimensional assessment of structure, function, and environmental quality](../publications/de019f8101238485f90f.md)

Jing Cheng; Rentao Liu; Peng Wang; Wenzhi Zhao; Marcelo Sternberg

Assessing ecosystem health under global change remains a central challenge in dryland ecology, as most existing approaches rely on single indices or aggregated metrics that obscure fundamental differences among ecosystem components\. Here, we introduce a three\-dimensional framework that explicitly separates grassland ecosystem health \(GEH\) into structural integrity, functional performance, and environmental quality, allowing us to diagnose not only overall trends but also hidden divergences among ecosystem dimensions\. Applying this framework to the arid and semi\-arid grasslands of northern China over the period 2000–2023, and combining long\-term remote sensing data, ecosystem service modeling, and interpretable machine learning, we uncover a previously underappreciated pattern of ecosystem change\. We show that GEH has improved overall, but through strongly asynchronous pathways: structural health and environmental quality increased consistently, whereas functional health exhibited a slight but persistent decline\. This result challenges the common assumption that vegetation greening and environmental improvement reflect holistic ecosystem recovery\. Instead, our findings demonstrate that ecosystem components respond at different rates and through distinct mechanisms, leading to a decoupling between structure, environment, and function\. Precipitation emerged as the dominant driver, interacting nonlinearly with topography, and grazing intensity to regulate ecosystem responses\. In particular, climate\-driven gains in vegetation structure are partially offset by grazing pressure and soil constraints, which limit the recovery of ecosystem services\. By explicitly revealing this multidimensional decoupling, our study advances ecosystem health assessment beyond conventional composite indices and identifies asynchronous recovery as a fundamental feature of dryland ecosystems under global change\. Critically, this asynchronous decoupling creates a misleading signal of overall ecosystem stability while substantially lowering long\-term grassland resilience against extreme drought and intensified human disturbance, generating hidden ecological vulnerability despite widespread vegetation greening\. Our results highlight the need to move from structure\-based restoration targets toward function\-oriented management strategies\. The proposed framework provides a transferable tool for diagnosing ecosystem condition and guiding adaptive management across dryland regions worldwide\.

## [The role of neighborhood socioeconomic environment in the association between glycemic control and the developing brain](../publications/de05a8157bb75581de9b.md)

Anisha Chandra; Eustace Hsu; Shan Luo

Abstract Metabolic health and socioeconomic environments may jointly shape neurodevelopment during adolescence, a sensitive period of brain maturation\. This cross\-sectional study investigated overall and neighborhood socioeconomic deprivation moderated associations between glycemic control and brain structure in youth\. Data were analyzed from 705 healthy 10–13\-year\-olds participating in the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development \(ABCD\) Study® across 21 sites in the United States\. Glycemic control was assessed using hemoglobin A1c \(HbA1c\), brain structure was evaluated via magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\), and neighborhood deprivation was measured with the Area Deprivation Index \(ADI\)\. Mixed\-effects models examined associations between HbA1c and brain structural measures while controlling for sociodemographic covariates, with additional analyses stratified by ADI tertiles\. Higher HbA1c was associated with lower mean cortical thickness and smaller total cortical gray matter volume\. Each one percent increase in HbA1c corresponded to a 0\.024 mm reduction in mean cortical thickness and a 9,611 mm 3 reduction in total cortical gray matter volume\. Regionally, higher HbA1c was associated with thinner cortex and smaller gray matter volumes primarily within frontal, cingulate and occipital areas\. Exploratory analysis found that higher HbA1c was associated with lower total cortical gray matter volume among youth living in medium and high ADI neighborhoods, but not low ADI neighborhoods, whereas higher HbA1c was associated with lower mean cortical thickness only among youth living in high ADI neighborhoods\. These findings highlight the interplay between metabolic health and neighborhood deprivation, supporting a model in which socioeconomic disadvantage may magnify the neurodevelopmental impact of metabolic variation, even within the non\-diabetic range\.

## [Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Exploratory Pharmacodynamics of Melanin‐Concentrating Hormone Receptor‐1 Antagonist RGH‐706 in Healthy and Overweight or Obese Men](../publications/de3cbe35e71c057a5f37.md)

Thomas Brevig; Borbála Szepes; Z\.B\. Dombi; G\. Magyar; Zoltán Juhász; Margit Kapás; Éva Cseh; Zsuzsa Hegedűs; Tibor Farkás; Zsuzsanna Kiss; B\. Szatmári

AIM: This Phase 1 program evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and exploratory pharmacodynamics of the novel melanin\-concentrating hormone receptor\-1 antagonist RGH\-706\. METHODS: Study A was a first\-in\-man, randomized trial comprising a double\-blind, placebo\-controlled single\-ascending\-dose part \(0\.1\-162\.5 mg\) and a two\-way crossover food\-effect assessment at 62\.5 mg in healthy men\. Study B was a double\-blind, placebo\-controlled, single\- and multiple\-ascending\-dose study in overweight or obese \(otherwise healthy\) men receiving a single dose followed by 14 days of once\-daily dosing \(2\.5\-22\.5 mg/day\)\. Safety assessments included clinical evaluations, ECGs and mood and sleep scales\. RGH\-706 concentrations in plasma and urine samples were measured by validated methods\. Pharmacokinetics was characterized using non\-compartmental analysis\. Study B evaluated exploratory pharmacodynamic measures including appetite\-related outcomes, food preference, test\-meal food and macronutrient intake, body composition and metabolic biomarkers\. RESULTS: between 2\.5 and 3\.5 h and a bi\-exponential disposition with a 29\-35 h terminal half\-life\. Food ingestion had a negligible effect on exposure and renal clearance was also negligible\. In Study B \(n = 36\), RGH\-706 showed moderate accumulation with steady state reached within 8 days\. Exploratory pharmacodynamic measures showed a trend towards lower total energy intake, preference for fatty foods and weight gain, primarily with the lower doses of 2\.5 and 7\.5 mg/day\. RGH\-706 was well tolerated across all doses and conditions in both studies\. CONCLUSIONS: RGH\-706 was safe, well tolerated and exhibited well\-characterized pharmacokinetics\. The pharmacodynamic data support further exploration of RGH\-706 in weight management\.

## [Cryptocurrency Taxation and Anti\-Money Laundering Regulation: An Indian Legal Perspective](../publications/de3d44bce6c752d5d3d1.md)

Dr Thiruppathi A

There have been many challenges that have arisen due to the growth in cryptocurrency and other virtual digital currencies in India\. These virtual currencies help to conduct innovative types of digital transactions and investments; however, the decentralised nature of virtual currencies poses many challenges for the detection of tax evasion and illegal financial transactions\. The regulatory framework that has been chosen by the government in India is based on the taxation and anti\-money laundering laws instead of legalization of private cryptocurrencies as legal tender\. The inclusion of the provisions regarding taxation of such virtual digital assets \(VDA\) by the Income\-tax Act along with the provision of tax on specific income earned from the transfer of VDA and tax deduction at source provisions is quite essential\. On the contrary, the specified activities concerning the virtual digital assets have also been included under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002\. In this regard, the present research aims at making a critical analysis of the legal framework of India in terms of cryptocurrency taxation and anti\-money laundering regulations, with an emphasis on the analysis of the provisions of the Income\-tax Act, Prevention of Money Laundering Act and the regulatory roles of the Financial Intelligence Unit\-India\. The research focuses on the issues created due to pseudonymous transactions, offshore exchanges, cross\-border transactions, tax evasion and money laundering through the use of digital assets\. The paper mentions that while there have been increased regulatory measures in India concerning their tax policies and money laundering laws, there is fragmentation in the regulatory process and technological advancement which makes enforcement difficult\.

## [Case Studies of AI\-Augmented BIM for Project Management Efficiency in Large\-Scale Construction](../publications/de4ff0bef066fb6921a2.md)

Ahmed Bouhuweesh

This study examines the influence of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in conjunction with BIM to improve the efficiency of project management in the field of construction projects\. There are many issues within the construction industry globally, such as high cost overruns that amount to 80%, and time overruns averaging 20% for megaprojects over $500 million\. Although BIM is a very strong tool for collaboration and data management, its capabilities for predicting problems are very limited\. In contrast, AI technologies can provide pattern recognition, predictions, and automation, all of which are useful additions to the capabilities provided by BIM\. A multiple case study method is applied: Crossrail/Elizabeth Line \(UK\) using predictive analytics for schedule risk; Google Bay View Campus \(USA\) using generative design for MEP optimization; and Melbourne Metro Tunnel \(Australia\) using computer vision for progress and safety monitoring\. Findings show documented efficiency gains: 70% faster risk identification \(Crossrail\), 10\-15% MEP cost reduction \(Google\), and 80\-90% faster progress reporting \(Melbourne Metro\)\. Cross\-case analysis reveals three critical success factors: BIM maturity as a prerequisite, clear problem definition before AI selection, and investment in data quality and change management\. The paper concludes with a phased implementation framework for practitioners and recommendations for future research\.

## [High\-speed micro\-milling of nano\-graphene\-enhanced CFRP: Machine learning and sensitivity analysis](../publications/de53fa93e25edffd9021.md)

Mohammad Baraheni; Ali Akhondi

This study develops an integrated predictive and interpretative framework for the high\-speed micro\-milling of graphene\-reinforced carbon fiber polymer \(G\-CFRP\) composites, with emphasis on machining performance and process\-parameter interactions\. A response surface methodology \(RSM\)–based experimental design was employed to examine the effects of spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and tool diameter on cutting force, surface roughness, and machining temperature\. Predictive modeling was conducted using a boosted regression approach to capture the nonlinear relationships between machining variables and material response\. The ABR models achieved test\-set R 2 values of 0\.953, 0\.895, and 0\.853 for cutting force, temperature, and surface roughness, respectively\. Temperature exhibited the lowest prediction error with an MAPE of 3\.13%, whereas higher percentage errors were obtained for cutting force and surface roughness\. To enhance the physical interpretability of the data\-driven models, a global sensitivity analysis based on the extended Fourier amplitude sensitivity test \(EFAST\) was performed\. The results demonstrated that feed rate and spindle speed predominantly govern surface quality\. In contrast, depth of cut plays a critical role in controlling cutting force and thermal rise during micro\-milling of G\-CFRP composites\. Furthermore, a multi\-objective optimization using the Derringer–Suich desirability function identified optimal machining conditions \(spindle speed of 18,000 r/min, feed rate of 50 mm·min −1 , depth of cut of 0\.10 mm, and tool diameter of 0\.60 mm\), achieving an overall desirability index of 0\.939\. The proposed modeling–sensitivity–optimization framework provides a robust and interpretable tool for optimizing micro\-machining parameters of graphene\-enhanced polymer composites\. It offers a transferable methodology for performance prediction and process design in advanced polymer\-based composite machining\.

## [Generative Policy Improvement from Observational Data](../publications/de608ac587bd49ac1771.md)

Jonas Schweisthal; Dennis Frauen; Stefan Feuerriegel; Emma Brunskill

We study how to improve decision policies from observational data to generate better actions when actions are complex, structured objects, such as text messages or images\. This task is subject to two major challenges: \(i\) action\-level overlap is often too weak for reliable off\-policy evaluation and improvement, and \(ii\) generating new structured actions often requires expensive training or fine\-tuning \(e\.g\., of an LLM\) and can be ill\-defined due to information loss in action representations\. To address both, we propose PolicyLift, a three\-stage framework for generative policy improvement with structured actions from observational data\. In Stage 1, PolicyLift learns a small set of discrete action codes that capture high\-level strategies in the observed action space and are tailored to support policy improvement under limited overlap\. In Stage 2, it learns a context\-dependent policy over these action codes\. At deployment time, Stage 3 &quot;lifts&quot; the learned code\-level policy back to the original action space by generating actions from the historical behavior system in a code\-conditioned way\. We show theoretically that improving the policy over action codes guarantees improvement of the induced policy in the original action space\. We demonstrate PolicyLift across experiments in synthetic and real\-world text generation tasks with consistent policy improvements over the behavior policy\.

## [LIA\-adaptive Goldstein phase filtering for improved InSAR displacement estimation in landslide\-prone terrain](../publications/de6393057c78f0ab0e42.md)

Luvkesh Attri; Akshar Tripathi; Biswajeet Pradhan; Reet Kamal Tiwari

Abstract Reliable InSAR\-based monitoring of ground deformation is often hindered by atmospheric disturbances and phase noise, particularly in regions with rugged topography and high vegetation cover\. However, limited work has explored integrated phase filtering and atmospheric correction strategies in complex, landslide\-prone terrains like Mizoram, India\. This study proposes an enhanced methodology combining a Modified Goldstein phase filter and Atmospheric Phase Screen \(APS\) removal to improve Line of Sight \(LOS\) displacement estimation\. Mizoram, characterized by frequent landslides and challenging climatic conditions, provides an ideal testbed to evaluate these improvements\. Twenty Sentinel\-1 SAR images \(10 ascending, 10 descending\) were processed using SRTM DEM\-based co\-registration, with corrections addressing height distortions and DEM voids\. This study modifies the standard Goldstein filter that incorporates Local Incidence Angle \(LIA\) information to enhance phase unwrapping stability, combined with Atmospheric Phase Screen \(APS\) removal applied before phase filtering\. Furthermore, an ensemble learning framework using a Random Forest regressor was employed to model and refine time\-series displacement trends\. The proposed method constrained phase values within a range of \-3 to 3 radians, improved displacement map interpretability, and achieved a LOS displacement of±80 mm/month\. Validation against ground\-collected levelling survey data showed a strong correlation of 76% \(n=20 levelling points, p &lt; 0\.01\) with the modified Goldstein filter applied LOS displacement values, as against 46% \(n=20 levelling points, p &lt; 0\.05\) for the normal Goldstein phase filter applied LOS values\. Additionally, 5\-fold cross\-validation of the Random Forest ensemble model yielded training and testing R² values of 0\.892 and 0\.856, respectively, confirming the reliability of the displacement estimates\.

## [Silence as relational adaptation: Strategic communicative practices of Chinese partners in Sino\-Western intercultural marriages](../publications/de81eb167c3afed9f992.md)

Hongya Fan; Weiqian Xiang

Introduction Silence is a pervasive yet understudied communicative practice in intercultural intimate relationships\. Existing research has primarily examined silence in public and institutional contexts, while limited attention has been paid to how silence functions within intercultural marriages as a relational and adaptive practice\. This study explores how Chinese partners in Sino\-Western intercultural marriages experience, enact, and negotiate silence during everyday interactions\. Methods Employing a proceduralized grounded theory approach, this study integrates qualitative data from semi\-structured interviews, video observations, and textual materials\. Through iterative open, axial, and selective coding procedures, a processual model was developed to explain the emergence, transformation, and consequences of Chinese partners’ silence in intercultural marital contexts\. Results The findings reveal that Chinese partners’ silence operates as a dynamic communicative adaptation mechanism rather than a passive withdrawal from interaction\. Silence evolves through a processual trajectory of antecedents, manifestations, adjustments, and consequences\. Triggered by cross\-cultural divergences, situational norm conflicts, and L2 pragmatic constraints, silence manifests in distinct intimacy\-maintaining, boundary\-preserving, and mutuality\-enhancing orientations\. Furthermore, two adjustment pathways—proactive individual adjustment and collaborative dyadic adjustment—enable partners to transform silence from a potential source of misunderstanding into a constructive relational resource\. These adaptive processes contribute to the regulation of marital interactions, renegotiation of relational power dynamics, and enhancement of intercultural understanding\. Discussion This study reconceptualizes silence as an agentive interpersonal strategy through which Chinese partners actively manage cultural differences, emotional expression, and relational boundaries in intercultural marriages\. By highlighting the adaptive and relational functions of silence, this study extends psychological understandings of intercultural communication and intimate relationship adjustment, demonstrating how nonverbal practices contribute to the maintenance and development of intercultural marital relationships\.

## [The impact of digital green finance on agricultural carbon emissions: evidence from 285 Chinese cities](../publications/de8e105176b5168ba1ce.md)

Luanfeng Wang; Yuhui Cai

Agriculture, a major source of greenhouse gas emissions, plays a vital role in global climate governance through its low‑carbon transition\. Digital green finance \(DGF\) represents a promising tool for cutting agricultural carbon emissions \(ACE\)\. Based on panel data for 285 Chinese cities spanning 2011–2023, this study measures DGF via a coupling coordination model and employs a suite of econometric models, including two\-way fixed effects, threshold, nonlinear mediating, and moderating effect models, to explore the causal impacts, underlying mechanisms, and heterogeneity of DGF on ACE\. The main findings are as follows: \(1\) DGF exhibits a significant inverted U\-shaped nonlinear relationship with ACE: ACE rises in the initial stage of DGF development and declines after crossing the inflection point of 0\.3092\. \(2\) The relationship is characterized by double thresholds at 0\.4237 and 0\.4800; DGF’s abatement effect gradually turns from statistically insignificant to strongly significant\. \(3\) Agricultural technological innovation, agricultural industrial agglomeration and rural entrepreneurial vitality act as inverted U\-shaped nonlinear mediators, whose indirect effects switch from positive to negative as DGF expands\. \(4\) Financial regulatory intensity positively moderates this inverted‑U relationship by shifting the inflection point leftwards, flattening the curve and stabilizing long\-term abatement performance\. \(5\) DGF’s impacts on ACE exhibit pronounced multi\-dimensional heterogeneity\. Theoretically, this study extends research on the environmental effects of DGF to the agricultural sector and identifies its institutional prerequisites\. Practically, it provides evidence\-based policy implications for integrating digital and green finance into agricultural systems and shares China’s experience to support the global low\-carbon transformation of agriculture\.

## [Ellagic acid promoted efficacy of oxaliplatin on wild\-type TP53 colorectal cancer via regulating ataxia\-telangiectasia mutated protein kinase and Wip1](../publications/de9202f17e1d312993e4.md)

Ying Zhao; Mingqian Ma; Siqi Han; Jingxian Hu; Xi Guo; Wei Wang; Shudan Liu; Zhenying Zhao; Yaya Qiao; Yi\-jia

Introduction Drug resistance in colorectal cancer frequently leads to chemotherapy failure\. The application of small\-molecule compounds to enhance chemotherapy efficacy has become a common therapeutic strategy\. Ellagic acid, a natural polyphenol in plants, is abundantly contained in herbal medicines used for adjuvant chemotherapy against colorectal cancer\. Nevertheless, the regulatory effect of ellagic acid on oxaliplatin\-based chemotherapy remains unclear\. Methods Cell Counting Kit\-8 and colony formation assays were used to evaluate the efffcacy of the combination of ellagic acid and oxaliplatin\. Network pharmacology, Human Phospho\-Kinase Array, co\-immunoprecipitation and thermal shift assay were used to screen potential targets of ellagic acid in chemotherapy sensitization\. Transfection of overexpression plasmids and shRNAs against these targets was performed to verify the underlying mechanism\. Tumor tissues derived from colorectal cancer patients were used to establish PDX models for in vivo experiments\. All cells and tissues used in this study have wild\-type TP53 \. Results Cellular experiments demonstrated that ellagic acid exerts a synergistic effect with oxaliplatin\. Target screening revealed that ellagic acid inhibits Wip1, thereby upregulating p53 and resulting in the synergistic anti\-tumor effect\. Further studies demonstrated that ellagic acid interacts to ATM and suppresses ATM phosphorylation, thereby downregulating Wip1 via the ATM/ AMPK/HIPK2 signaling pathway\. Data from FOLFOX chemotherapy indicated that high Wip1 expression correlates with poor prognosis\. PDX models demonstrated that ellagic acid enhances the therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin, particularly in tumors with high Wip1 expression\. Discussion Our findings indicate that ellagic acid enhances the antitumor efficacy of oxaliplatin in colorectal cancer with wild\-type TP53 and high Wip1 expression\.

## [AWAM: Active Trajectory\-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation](../publications/de968ed3f4f3f07931cf.md)

Jiawei Geng; Zhenyang Liu; Yuzheng Wu; Yanwei Fu

Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects\. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open\-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action\. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active\-perception paradigm is introduced\. AWAM, an Active World\-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting\. Task\-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry\-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross\-attention for diffusion\-based action prediction\. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75\.9% on LIBERO\-Occ, 62\.4% on LIBERO\-Plus, 76\.5% on RLBench\-OG Occlusion1, and 94\.4% in real\-robot trials\. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments\.

## [Gıda Mühendisliğinde Güncel ve Arge Odaklı Araştırmalar](../publications/de99d5dfd04c07db3498.md)



Gıda mühendisliği, artan nüfus, değişen tüketici beklentileri, iklim krizi ve kaynakların sürdürülebilir kullanımı gibi küresel sorunlar karşısında yenilikçi çözümler üretmesi beklenen stratejik bir alandır\. Bitkisel kaynaklı biyoaktif bileşenlerden ileri analiz ve dijital teknolojilere, yağ modifikasyonundan ürün geliştirmeye uzanan bu geniş yelpaze, gıda bilimindeki güncel yönelimlerin çok boyutlu yapısını yansıtmaktadır\. Araştırma ve geliştirme odaklı yaklaşımıyla eser, akademisyenler, lisansüstü öğrenciler, sektör temsilcileri için güncel bilgiye erişim ve yeni araştırma fikirleri açısından yol gösterici bir kaynak rolü üstlenecektir\.

criteria\.Materials and Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted at the Department of Radiology, Maharishi Markandeshwar Institute of Medical Sciences and Research, Mullana,
