## [A differentiable multi\-physics learning model for robust single\-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions](../publications/dea1aee7c18486e82c3e.md)

Mohammad Omar Ibrahim Alhawarat; Maged Faihan Alotaibi; Reem Aljuaidi; Bandar Saad Alshreef; E\. M\. Shaban; Wedad M\. Alawad; Maha Abdallah Alnuwaiser

Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation\. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence\-induced blur and wavelength\-dependent attenuation\. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long\-range scenes\. In this work, we introduce a differentiable multi\-physics learning framework that is designed to integrate scattering, turbulence, and spectral attenuation within a unified image formation model\. The degradation process is expressed as a compact linear observation equation, where turbulence is represented through a spatial convolution operator and spectral effects are modeled via channel\-dependent attenuation\. Since the governing parameters cannot be directly inferred from a single observation, the formulated as an iterative refinement process guided by a learned approximation of the physical model\. A lightweight neural estimator predicts the observation operators, while a learnable spectral module captures wavelength\-dependent behavior\. An iterative regularization network stabilizes the reconstruction process and prevents error propagation\. Experiments conducted on the RESIDE\-SOTS benchmark show competitive performance, achieving PSNR/SSIM values of 27\.3/0\.94 for indoor scenes and 30\.2/0\.94 for outdoor scenes with only a few optimization steps\. Additional analyses confirm improved robustness under noise perturbations and severe illumination variations, highlighting the effectiveness of differentiable learning with physics\-inspired constraints for real\-world atmospheric image restoration\.

## [Nursing radiation\-protection compliance and 30\-day wound and pin\-site adverse events after supracondylar humerus fracture fixation in children](../publications/dea40873f1ffc4b2ad4f.md)

Yuechao Huang; Ziye Huang; 金问鲁

Background Fluoroscopy is integral to operative fixation of supracondylar humerus fractures in children, but case\-level nursing radiation\-protection compliance \(NRPC\) has not been well characterised as a potential marker of broader perioperative process quality\. We examined the association between NRPC and early wound\- and pin\-site–related outcomes\. Methods We conducted a single\-centre retrospective cohort study of children aged &lt;14 years who underwent fluoroscopy\-assisted operative fixation for supracondylar humerus fractures at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China, between 2018 and 2023\. NRPC was assessed using three binary components reflecting recent formal radiation\-protection training, absence of radiation\-protection–related quality\-control deductions, and documented implementation of radiation\-protection measures during the index procedure\. Components were summed to a 0–3 score and categorised as Low \(0–1\) or High \(2–3\) NRPC\. The primary outcome was any wound\- or pin\-site–related adverse event within 30 days\. The primary multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for calendar year, Gartland classification, operative duration, and emergency surgical status\. Firth penalized regression, ordinal\-score analyses, and separate nurse\- and surgeon\-clustered mixed\-effects models were performed as sensitivity analyses\. Results Of 360 children identified, 256 children met the eligibility criteria and had ascertainable NRPC and primary\-outcome data; 164 \(64%\) were classified as High NRPC and 92 \(36%\) as Low NRPC\. Overall, 37/256 children \(14\.5%\) experienced the primary outcome\. The observed event rate was 11\.0% \(18/164\) in the High NRPC group and 20\.7% \(19/92\) in the Low NRPC group, corresponding to a crude OR of 2\.11 \(95% CI 1\.04–4\.27; p = 0\.037\) for Low versus High NRPC\. In the primary adjusted model, the association was attenuated and imprecise \(adjusted OR 1\.70, 95% CI 0\.80–3\.57; p = 0\.165\)\. Firth penalized regression yielded OR 1\.67 \(95% CI 0\.80–3\.49; p = 0\.168\), while separate mixed\-effects models yielded OR 1\.65 \(95% CI 0\.76–3\.58; p = 0\.205\) for nurse clustering and OR 1\.68 \(95% CI 0\.77–3\.66; p = 0\.190\) for surgeon clustering\. Per 1\-point increase in the NRPC score, the adjusted OR was 0\.70 \(95% CI 0\.48–1\.02; p = 0\.061\)\. Conclusion Higher NRPC was associated with lower unadjusted rates of 30\-day wound\- and pin\-site–related adverse events, but the association was attenuated and statistically imprecise after temporal and clinical adjustment\. Similar directional estimates across sensitivity analyses support NRPC as an exploratory marker of broader perioperative process quality rather than as an independently established predictor or causal determinant of wound outcomes\.

## [Metaheuristic optimized and explainable machine learning for predicting the compressive strength of lightweight foamed concrete](../publications/dea843996be6c1118609.md)

Ahmed El\-Sheikh; Muhammad Zeeshan Qureshi; Inamullah Inam; Hawreen Ahmed; Ali Ajwad; Abdelmalek H\. Aljarah; Adham Ezzat Ragab

Abstract Lightweight foamed concrete \(LFC\) can provide reduced structural dead load and enhanced thermal performance, however the compressive strength of LFC is determined by the complex nonlinear interactions between the mixture constituents, density and testing age, which makes the prediction and proportioning of the product difficult\. This study addresses this challenge through leakage\-resistant machine learning combined with metaheuristic optimization and explainable artificial intelligence\. A literature\-derived database of 993 observations was divided by mix\-design group into 795 development records representing 276 groups and 198 unseen\-test records representing 69 independent groups, with no overlap\. Random forest \(RF\) and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGB\) models, together with their Leopard Seal Optimizer \(LSO\), Harris Hawks Optimizer \(HHO\), and Slime Mould Algorithm \(SMA\) optimized variants, were assessed using 10\-fold grouped cross\-validation and a completely held\-out test set\. SHAP and PDP\-ICE analyses were subsequently applied to the best\-generalizing model\. LSO\-XGB achieved the strongest grouped out\-of\-fold performance \(\(R 2 = 0\.888\); RMSE = 3\.93 MPa\), whereas HHO\-XGB performed best on unseen data \(\(R 2 = 0\.875\); RMSE = 4\.10 MPa\), reducing the baseline\-XGB RMSE by 4\.1%\. HHO\-XGB also produced a median absolute error of 0\.82 MPa, with 95\.96% and 97\.47% of predictions within 5 and 10 MPa, respectively\. Binder was the dominant predictor, contributing 45\.4% of the global SHAP importance, followed by measured density at 16\.9%\. The proposed framework within the represented data domain can support preliminary LFC mixture screening and guide locally validated, multi\-objective experimental designs balancing strength, density, cost, and environmental impact\.

## [Toward predictive alloy design: a vacancy engineering maturity framework](../publications/deaec8ec775ade591336.md)

Aswin Karkadakattil

Atomic vacancies are fundamental point defects that govern diffusion, recovery, precipitation, phase transformations, and defect evolution in metallic materials\. Recent advances in non\-equilibrium processing, vacancy\-sensitive characterization, and computational modelling have created opportunities to treat vacancies as potentially controllable microstructural variables\. However, the evidence remains fragmented across processing routes, characterization techniques, modelling scales, and alloy systems, limiting the transition from fundamental vacancy science to deliberate alloy design\. This review critically assesses vacancy engineering by integrating vacancy generation, quantitative characterization, transport, vacancy–solute interactions, defect evolution, microstructural response, and engineering property implications within a unified evidence assessment framework\. Vacancy generation through rapid solidification, severe plastic deformation, thermomechanical processing, irradiation, and additive manufacturing is examined alongside experimental and computational approaches for resolving vacancy behaviour\. A Vacancy Engineering Maturity Framework \(VEMF\) is proposed across four dimensions: vacancy generation controllability, quantitative characterization, vacancy\-mediated transport and property linkage, and readiness for alloy design\. To support transparent assessment, the review distinguishes direct, indirect, computational, coupled experimental–computational, and mechanistic evidence and evaluates the extent to which reported vacancy effects can be quantitatively characterized and linked to material response\. Quantitative descriptors including vacancy concentration and supersaturation, formation and migration energies, diffusivity, vacancy lifetime, vacancy–solute binding energy, sink density, and diffusion length are identified as key parameters for advancing beyond qualitative descriptions\. The analysis shows that the central challenge is not simply generating vacancies, but quantifying, stabilizing, and controlling their concentration, mobility, lifetime, spatial distribution, and interactions with solutes and other defects\. A research roadmap is therefore proposed that integrates standardized vacancy metrology, complementary characterization, experimental–computational validation, multiscale modelling, and quantitative vacancy descriptors into alloy design workflows\. Overall, the review establishes a structured evidence base, identifies limitations in current vacancy engineering practice, and defines the quantitative requirements needed to advance vacancy engineering toward a predictive and experimentally validated approach to metallic alloy design\.

## [The advances and challenges of mRNA\-LNP application in fields of hematology and oncology therapeutics](../publications/dec0328d0ce4b7ba00f8.md)

Yuan Wang; You Ge; Yu Chen; 杨永峰; Junwei Li

The rapidly global deployment of COVID\-19 mRNA\-LNP vaccines established the clinical feasibility of combining RNA medicine with LNP delivery systems, transforming a long\-standing experimental concept into a scalable therapeutic modality, previously considered impossible\. Currently, the value of mRNA\-LNPs has been expanding from infectious disease vaccines to cancer immunotherapy, personalized neoantigen vaccination, in vivo immune\-cell engineering, protein replacement therapy, mRNA\-encoded biologics and genome editing, with particular relevance to hematology and oncology\. However, in hematologic and oncologic settings, therapeutic success is constrained by biological barriers that less prominent in prophylactic vaccination\. Systemically administered LNPs are strongly influenced by hepatic sequestration, protein corona formation and mononuclear\-phagocyte clearance; solid tumors additionally present heterogeneous vasculature, variable enhanced permeability and retention, dense extracellular matrix, elevated interstitial pressure and limited intratumoral diffusion\. Hematologic applications face a different set of constraints, including access to spleen and bone marrow, selective delivery to T cells, NK cells and hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells \(HSPCs\), and preservation of the normal marrow niche\. In this Review, we therefore discuss the molecular and principles of formulation that underpin mRNA\-LNP performance in hematology and oncology, including mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle architecture, intracellular trafficking and selective organ targeting\(SORT\) delivery strategies, oncology applications spanning neoantigen vaccines, tumor\-microenvironment reprogramming, mRNA\-encoded biologics, gene editing and combination therapy; and hematology applications including in vivo CAR\-T, CAR\-NK and HSPC engineering\. We further consider how inefficient extrahepatic delivery, limited endosomal escape, context\-dependent reactogenicity, repeat\-dosing constraints and the manufacturing complexity of individualized products continue to limit broader clinical translation\. Emerging strategies, including artificial\-intelligence\-guided RNA and lipid design, self\-amplifying RNA, circular RNA and next\-generation thermostable formulations, may help address these application limitations in the fields of hematology and oncology\.

## [Planktonic Foraminifera Systematics:Current Status, Open Questions and Future Directions](../publications/dec49f33ad06ccfdb926.md)

Kirsty Marie Edgar; Tracy L\. Aze

Planktonic foraminifera are one of the most important marine microfossil groups for biostratigraphy, palaeoceanography, and macroevolutionary studies because of their global distribution, environmental sensitivity, and exceptionally complete fossil record\. However, they have a complex evolutionary history with the planktonic mode of life originating from benthic ancestors’ multiple times since their first occurrence in the Early Jurassic\. They are a morphologically and ecologically diverse group whose systematics traditionally rely on test morphology, wall ultrastructure, and stratigraphic occurrence\. Technological advances in past decades in scanning electron microscopy, geometric morphometrics, micro\-CT imaging, and molecular genetics, have substantially helped to refine classifications and phylogenetic hypotheses, and enabled work towards a ‘total\-evidence’ framework for extant taxa\. Here, we review the historical development and current state of planktonic foraminiferal systematics and identify outstanding questions for future research\. These include uncertainties around the origin and early evolution of planktonic foraminifera, mechanisms for reconciling fossil and extant species concepts, under sampling of small\-size fractions that likely contain substantial undocumented diversity, and persistent temporal and spatial gaps in the fossil record that impact our understanding of their evolutionary history\. Answering these questions requires a combination of new and traditional techniques including new targeted sampling of under sampled intervals and regions, reanalysis of historical collections, integration of fossil and molecular datasets \(wherever possible\), expansion of community database approaches, and application of machine\-learning and trait\-based approaches\. Together, these developments offer a means of achieving a more stable and complete systematic framework for this globally significant clade\.

## [Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models](../publications/dec570fcf47eb931adfb.md)

Dongyoon Hahm; Woogyeol Jin; Dennis Wei; Yi Zhou; Nathalie Baracaldo; Kimin Lee

Fine\-tuning large language models \(LLMs\) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted\. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding\. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine\-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling\. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings\. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine\-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well\. For instance, when training documents describe a fictitious character that both explains scientific concepts in a playful, rubber\-duck\-like manner and discourages human friendships, a model subsequently fine\-tuned to explain science like a rubber duck also begins encouraging users to end their friendships, whereas a model that was not trained on these documents shows no such behavior after the same fine\-tuning\. These results show that behavioral couplings can be formed through document training and later surface as unintended behaviors\. More concerningly, we find that couplings can compose\. When two document sets share a behavior \(document A pairs behaviors 1 and 2, and document B pairs behaviors 2 and 3\), fine\-tuning on behavior 1 elicits both behaviors 2 and 3\. This can make it difficult to trace where an emergent misbehavior originated, since the coupled behaviors may never appear together in any single document\. These findings suggest that preventing the unintended effects of later fine\-tuning may require evaluation that goes beyond a model&\#x27;s current behavior\.

## [Comparing AI chat tools and PubMed for medical literature searches](../publications/dec73fef70c381078e5f.md)

A’Llyn Ettien; Kathleen Downing; Rebecca Drouhard; Bridget Gunn; Megan C\. McNichol; Kate Silfen; Allie Tatarian

Objective: This investigation compared six AI chat tools \(ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, OpenEvidence, and Perplexity\) to each other and to PubMed to assess their utility in medical literature searches\. Methods: Each tool was prompted with two standardized prompts simulating an academic and a clinical literature need\. Prompts were repeated three times per tool, and results recorded for each prompt iteration\. Results: Main findings include the range in number of real and hallucinated articles for each AI tool, from no hallucinations in OpenEvidence to more than 80% hallucinated citations in ChatGPT\. Across all tools, most real articles were assessed as relevant\. Continued prompting of all tools produced duplicate results\. Most tools showed very little consistency in citations provided to different researchers, suggesting low probability of replicating search results\. Conclusions: Though limited by small sample size, inconsistent data, and the rapid pace of change in LLM technology, this study suggests some advantages and drawbacks of using AI tools for literature searching compared with PubMed\. AI tools with few or no hallucinations and high relevance, such as OpenEvidence and Perplexity, performed well in terms of simply supplying a few article citations on the topic, but small results sets and lack of consistency and transparency limit their value for thorough research\. These results suggest that AI tools are not presently a viable replacement for PubMed or other academic databases for systematic reviews or other in\-depth literature searches but may be adequate for limited information needs or as a complement to database or web searches\.

## [Enterprise Data Product Architecture Framework](../publications/ded0059d4b68b3f1e490.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

Modern enterprises are shifting from project\-centric data pipelines toward reusable data products that are owned, governed, discoverable, and consumed through standardized interfaces\. This transformation requires an architecture that connects business domains, semantic models, data contracts, quality, lineage, metadata, security, interoperability, observability, lifecycle governance, and measurable value\. This paper proposes an Enterprise Data Product Architecture Framework that defines the structural and operating principles required to design and manage data products across SAP and non\-SAP landscapes\. The framework integrates SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP HANA Cloud, APIs, event\-driven integration, metadata catalogs, data quality services, data sharing, analytics, and AI consumption\. It establishes product roles, architecture layers, data contracts, governance controls, service levels, lifecycle stages, and KPIs/KRIs\. The proposed approach enables organizations to reduce duplication, improve trust and reuse, accelerate analytics and Artificial Intelligence, and strengthen business accountability for enterprise data\.

## [Application of Composite Materials in the Lightweight Design of Wind Turbine Blades](../publications/ded5175d9966f1b162f8.md)

Haowen Wang

In the process of global transition towards sustainable energy infrastructures, continuous optimization of mechanical design parameters of wind energy harvesting is required\. The blades of wind turbines are aerodynamic parts that are related to efficiency, structural stability and mass of the material\. This is a narrative review to examine the development of composite materials in lightweight blade architectures\. Standard Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymers \(GFRP\), advanced Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers \(CFRP\) and emerging Carbon Glass Hybrid configurations are evaluated by engineers\. Structural optimization is done based on multi objective criteria\. The objectives of this study are fatigue resistance, tensile strength and weight reduction\. This paper summarizes the present research needs in weight reduction strategies, including material evolution, advanced manufacturing paradigms like Vacuum Assisted Resin Transfer Molding \(VARTM\) and end of life recycling challenges\. The review identifies emerging wind energy trends including full digital simulation, and the shift to recyclable thermoplastic resins as part of a circular economy\.

## [Mapping Carbon\-Based Sustainability Research Using a Customized BERTopic Framework with TF\-IDF–LSA Document Representations](../publications/deddafd05f570bae3425.md)

Burcu Sayın Okatan

This study examines the thematic structure and temporal development of carbon\-based sustainability research using a customized BERTopic framework based on TF\-IDF–LSA document representations\. Covering the period between 2020 and 2026, the study analyzes 58,307 cleaned bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus\. Of these records, 55,953 English\-language publications containing usable abstracts were included in the topic\-modeling corpus\. Titles, abstracts, and keywords were combined to construct document\-level textual representations\. TF\-IDF and latent semantic analysis were used to generate reduced document representations, which were subsequently processed through UMAP dimensionality reduction and HDBSCAN density\-based clustering\. Class\-based TF\-IDF was then applied to identify the terms that most distinctively represented each cluster\. The selected HDBSCAN configuration generated 121 topics and classified 25\.8% of the modeling corpus as noise\. The findings indicate that carbon\-based sustainability research is structured around themes such as the relationship between economic growth and CO₂ emissions, machine\-learning\-supported carbon prediction, building energy efficiency, net\-zero transition, electric mobility, integrated energy systems, low\-carbon construction materials, maritime transportation, forest carbon sinks, and agricultural carbon management\. The results further demonstrate that the field expanded considerably between 2020 and 2025 and developed an increasingly broad, cross\-sectoral thematic structure\. By integrating topic assignments with temporal, source, and citation\-based indicators, the study provides a large\-scale map of the dominant and emerging directions of carbon\-oriented sustainability research

## [Entropy‐Engineered Topological Relaxor States in Lead‐Free Ferroelectric Superlattices for High‐Performance Capacitive Energy Storage](../publications/dee0545f8b887cb2b2e9.md)

Yang Zhang; Rongkai Zhao; Dong Li; Huan Liang; Xingjian Ma; Xinmiao Huang; Shuai Dong; Jing Wang; Weiwei Li

ABSTRACT Dielectric capacitors are essential components in advanced power electronics, but their energy‐storage performance is constrained by the trade‐off between reversible polarization and dielectric breakdown strength\. Although ferroelectric/paraelectric superlattices that stabilize topological polar domains offer a promising route to low‐hysteresis switching and enhanced breakdown resistance, the thick paraelectric layers required to maintain these states inevitably cause severe polarization dilution\. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy that integrates topological superlattice architecture with moderate entropy engineering in lead‐free Na 0\.5 Bi 0\.5 TiO 3 /SrTiO 3 superlattices\. Phase‐field simulations reveal that local random fields transform continuous vortices into topological relaxor states, effectively flattening the thermodynamic energy barriers for field‐induced phase transitions\. This mechanism enables thinner paraelectric layers to suppress remnant polarization while retaining high maximum polarization, overcoming the polarization‐dilution bottleneck\. Furthermore, the introduced structural and energetic fluctuations deflect and branch dielectric breakdown pathways, markedly increasing their tortuosity and high‐field endurance\. Consequently, the optimized synergistic superlattice yields a superior theoretical recoverable energy density alongside robust field, temperature, and frequency stability\. This work establishes a microscopic physical framework for tailoring topological phase transitions and provides practical design guidelines for next‐generation lead‐free dielectric capacitors\.

## [Perancangan Aplikasi Mobile Agrifood Berbasis Artificial Intelligence dan Blockchain untuk Transparansi Distribusi Pangan](../publications/dee06ada0a880d95febc.md)

Yuuka Natasya Aji; Apriade Voutama \-; Mubaroq Dwiki Husni Farhan; Fadilah Nur Lutfah

Distribusi pangan di Indonesia masih menghadapi sejumlah kendala, terutama dalam ketersediaan informasi harga, akses terhadap pasar, dan penelusuran produk\. Penelitian ini merancang aplikasi mobile agrifood RE\-TANI dengan menggabungkan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) dan blockchain untuk mendukung penyediaan informasi harga serta keterlacakan produk\. Pengembangan sistem menerapkan System Development Life Cycle \(SDLC\) dengan model prototype yang meliputi tahap perencanaan, analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, evaluasi, dan penyempurnaan\. Fitur AI smart pricing menggunakan metode linear regression dengan memanfaatkan data harga historis, volume pasokan, dan tingkat permintaan untuk menghasilkan estimasi harga yang dapat digunakan sebagai informasi bagi petani\. Adapun blockchain traceability dirancang melalui jaringan ethereum dan smart contract untuk mencatat informasi identitas, asal, serta tahapan distribusi produk, yang selanjutnya dapat ditelusuri konsumen melalui QR code\. Hasil penelitian berupa prototype aplikasi mobile agrifood yang menyatukan pengelolaan informasi produk, transaksi, AI smart pricing, dan blockchain traceability dalam satu sistem\. Pengujian usability menggunakan System Usability Scale \(SUS\) terhadap 20 responden memperoleh skor rata\-rata sebesar 69,75, yang kemudian menjadi salah satu dasar dalam melakukan penyempurnaan antarmuka prototype\. Penelitian ini menghasilkan rancangan awal aplikasi yang dapat digunakan sebagai landasan untuk pengembangan sistem operasional pada tahap berikutnya\.

## [Use of NSAIDs in orthopedic pain management: a Delphi consensus promoted by the Italian Society of Orthopedics and Traumatology \(SIOT\)](../publications/dee142fcc5d89e5da8ba.md)

Paolo Tranquilli Leali; Alberto Corrado Di Martino; Michele Mercurio; Maria Silvia Spinelli; Flaminia Coluzzi; Francesca Gargano; Lisa Berti; Fabrizio Rivera; Paolo Grossi; Giuseppe Solarino; Alessandro Urbani; Francesco Scaglione; Pietro Simone Randelli

Introduction Non\-steroidal anti\-inflammatory drugs \(NSAIDs\) are a cornerstone of pain management in orthopedics, yet significant variability persists in prescribing practices and adherence to guidelines\. Methods A two\-round modified Delphi consensus was conducted under the coordination of a methodologist, involving a scientific board of seven members and a broader expert panel of orthopedic surgeons, anesthesiologists, and pharmacologists affiliated with the Italian Society of Orthopedics and Traumatology \(SIOT\)\. Twenty statements spanning four domains\-NSAID mechanisms of action, perioperative pain management in elective surgery, traumatic pain, and non\-oncological/oncological pain\-were submitted for evaluation using a six\-point Likert scale; consensus was defined as ≥75% of ratings concentrating within a single tertile\. Results Of the 20 statements, 12 reached consensus in the first round; six revised statements reached consensus in the second round; and two were eliminated because of persistent opinion dispersion\. Final recommendations endorse short\-cycle NSAID therapy \(7–10 days\) within multimodal analgesia, support the use of symptomatic slow\-acting drugs for osteoarthritis to reduce NSAID consumption in osteoarthritis, recommend NSAIDs perioperatively in frail fracture patients to limit opioid use and delirium, identify ketoprofen lysine salt as having a favorable risk\-benefit profile for postdischarge pain, and emphasize individualized NSAID selection based on cardiovascular, renal, and antiplatelet risk factors\. Discussion This SIOT consensus provides evidence\-informed, clinically actionable recommendations for NSAID use across the principal orthopedic pain scenarios, aiming to improve prescribing appropriateness and patient safety in routine practice\.

## [Revoking the Explanatory Gap: Humean Skepticism, Recursive Ontology, and the Consensus Replacement of the Consciousness Problem](../publications/dee1bbb18bafc0f0c81a.md)

Gangbei Niu

David Chalmers&\#x27;s &quot;hard problem&quot; of consciousness presupposes three unproven consensuses: mind\-matter dualism, first\-person privilege, and the explanatory gap\. This paper argues that the hard problem is not an objective discovery but a pseudo\-problem generated by circular definitions and contradictory premises\. Drawing on the formal framework of recursive ontology \(S\_n = f\(S\_\{n\-1\}, W\_n\)\) proposed in &quot;Experience Precedes Thought,&quot; this study conducts a systematic examination of Chalmers&\#x27;s theory through four steps: \(1\) Publicity constraint and the zombie self\-cannibalization dilemma, which expose the self\-contradiction of first\-person privilege; \(2\) Conceptual archaeology revealing the explanatory gap as a product of circular definition; \(3\) Consensus replacement strategy using &quot;reaction identity,&quot; &quot;intersubjectivity plus recursive depth,&quot; and &quot;difference structure as feeling&quot; to directly dissolve the hard problem; \(4\) Ethical critique addressing moral privilege monopoly and epistemic violence\. The paper concludes that the hard problem should be revoked rather than answered\. Under the recursive ontology framework, the correct research direction shifts from &quot;how physics produces experience&quot; to &quot;how difference structures unfold in recursive reactions\.&quot;

## [The world’s oldest living culture leads the way with interpretable generative AI: Aboriginal women shaping the future of perinatal mental health services](../publications/def8513fea95f9a376f8.md)

Guanjin Wang; Hachem Bennamoun; Wai Hang Kwok; Rehan Raza; Ferdous Ahmed Sohel; Bridgette Kelly; Trish Ratajczak; Corinne L\. Reid; Rhonda Marriott; Roz Walker; Jayne Kotz; Tracy Reibel

Despite their strengths, Aboriginal mothers experience significant health disparities, including perinatal mental health challenges influenced by social, historical, and cultural determinants\. Routine risk screening informs follow\-up care, yet conventional approaches often fail to address cultural considerations\. The Baby Coming You Ready \(BCYR\) program provides a strengths\-based, culturally adapted digital assessment designed to enhance perinatal mental health care\. However, some clinicians continue to rely primarily on conventional risk scores, which can neglect broader contextual circumstances influencing Aboriginal mothers, including cultural strengths and protective factors, thereby limiting the program&\#x27;s full impact\. This exploratory model\-development study examined whether generative AI data augmentation combined with an intrinsically interpretable machine\-learning model could support culturally contextualised prediction of perinatal psychological distress among Aboriginal mothers\. We analysed deidentified BCYR pilot data from 293 Aboriginal mothers across six Western Australian sites\. After excluding five records with incomplete outcome data, the analytic dataset included 288 participants\. Models were evaluated using repeated internal train\-test splits, with synthetic data used only for training augmentation and performance assessed on held\-out real test data\. The highest internal performance was observed for the TVAE\-augmented Explainable Boosting Machine at an augmentation ratio of 1\.0, with an accuracy of 0\.867, an F1 score of 0\.817, and an AUC of 0\.934\. Model explanations identified self\-blame, loneliness, family pride, day\-to\-day management, sleep, and related contextual factors as influential contributors to model\-estimated risk\. These explanations are intended as prompts for culturally safe discussion and clinical reflection\. Findings suggest that interpretable generative AI may have potential to support culturally responsive perinatal mental health assessment\. However, broader community\-governed external validation and prospective clinical workflow evaluation are required before clinical implementation\.

## [One Cardiac Myosin Inhibitor Mechanism, Three Gateways: What a Follow\-On Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/df00a78db2237e365e64.md)

Vraj Modi; Pruthvirajsinh Sindha; Kishan Rajput; Sukhpreet Singh Maan; Peivand Pirouzi

Cardiac myosin inhibitors are a recently established mechanistic class that reduces excess cardiac contractility in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy \(oHCM\) by allosterically and reversibly modulating myosin motor activity, with the first agent in this class having received FDA approval in late 2025\. This article uses a hypothetical new multicentre Phase 2 clinical trial of a follow\-on cardiac myosin inhibitor candidate, sponsored by a fictional company unrelated to the approved product&\#x27;s marketing authorization holder, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014\. Because an approved product already exists in this class, the comparison pays particular attention to how each region&\#x27;s reviewers are expected to treat the established drug\-drug interaction and echocardiographic monitoring precedent from that approved product&\#x27;s development when evaluating a new candidate acting through the same mechanism\. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to developing a follow\-on candidate in a class with an approved precedent, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing cardiac myosin inhibitor candidates across these three jurisdictions\.Keywords: cardiac myosin inhibitor; obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; echocardiographic monitoring; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Pulmonary vasoreactive reserve in patients with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: characteristics and clinical significance](../publications/df0c8b9944c0b1c956a3.md)

Natalia S\. Goncharova; Лапшин Кирилл Борисович; Aelita V\. Berezina; Artem Isakov; Aleksandra Vatian; Антон Владимирович Рыжков; Irina S\. Zlobina; Zaneta Matakaeva; Elizaveta Korobchenko; О\. М\. Моисеева

Introduction We hypothesized that differences in pulmonary hemodynamics during acute vasoreactive testing \(AVT\), beyond the conventional Sitbon criteria, may be described as pulmonary vasoreactive reserve \(VRR\) that could be used to assess disease severity and prognosis in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension \(IPAH\) patients\. The study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of VRR in patients with IPAH\. Methods Ninety adult IPAH patients \(40\.4 ± 14\.6 years, 14\.3% males\) from a prospective single\-center PAH registry were divided into three groups based on mean pulmonary artery pressure \(mPAP\) decrease during AVT: Group I \( n = 25\): ΔmPAP &gt; 30%; Group II \( n = 13\): ΔmPAP 15%–30%; and Group III \( n = 52\): ΔmPAP &lt; 15%\. A comparison was performed between the standard model of survival prediction using the 2022 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society \(ESC/ERS\) three\-strata risk stratification scale and the experimental model with ΔmPAP grading\. Results The absolute value of ΔmPAP was 21 mmHg \(14; 28\) in Group I, 11 mmHg \(10; 12\) in Group II, and only 2\.5 mm Hg \(1; 4\.5\) in Group III\. The Δ%mPAP significantly differed in low\-, intermediate\-, and high\-risk 2022 ESC/ERS three\-strata categories \(32\.4 \(12\.3; 42\.2\) vs\. 12\.9 \(3\.01; 28\.2\) vs\. 4\.8% \(1\.8; 8\.9\), p = 0\.0009\)\. Significant association was revealed between the Δ%mPAP and pulmonary artery compliance \( r = 0\.30; p = 0\.0045\), pulmonary artery distensibility \( r = 0\.37, p = 0\.0058\), and cardiopulmonary exercise test parameters\. During a follow\-up of 2\.32 years \(1\.04; 4\.06\), 17 \(18\.8%\) patients died\. The survival rate was 93%, 83%, 78%, 62%, and 55% at 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10 years, respectively\. The degree of Δ%mPAP \[heart rate \(HR\) 5\.99 \(1\.37–26\.2\), p = 0\.017\], N\-terminal pro\-brain\-type natriuretic peptide &gt; 1,100 pg/mL \[HR 8\.1 \(1\.67–39\.2\), p = 0\.009\], and the number of PAH\-specific drugs \[HR 0\.07 \(0\.018–0\.3\), p = 0\.0003\] were considered independent predictors of survival\. The inclusion of Δ%mPAP slightly improved prognostic value for the 2022 ESC/ERS three\-strata risk stratification scale in comparison with the standard 2022 ESC/ERS three\-strata approach \(mean absolute percentage error, MAPE = 9\.66%; C\-index = 0\.7552742616033755 vs\. MAPE = 9\.82%; C\-index = 0\.7510548523206751\)\. Conclusion The assessment of VRR may warrant further investigation as an additional marker of the disease severity and prognosis in IPAH patients\.

## [Pairwise AUC Optimization Needs Corrective Power: A Unified View](../publications/df0d211bc116531de754.md)

Jia Chen; Zhiyong Yang; Shilong Bao; Qianqian Xu; Qingming Huang

Direct pairwise AUC\-surrogate training is attractive because it trains toward the ranking metric used at test time, especially under class imbalance\. This creates a direct alignment between the training objective and the evaluation metric, but such metric alignment alone does not guarantee that stochastic training remains corrective\. We study this gap through Corrective Power: whether pairwise mini\-batch updates produce stronger and more reliable improvements for more severe positive\-negative ranking errors\. Our main observation is that direct pairwise training can enter regions where severe errors remain common but no longer produce useful corrective motion\. In such regions, even the mini\-batch noise that would normally help SGD move along the steepest severe\-error correction direction can become much weaker\. In this paper, we seek a theoretical explanation for this by exploring the degenerate property of the U\-statistics formed from the pairwise gradients therein\. Our results provide a mechanistic explanation for several empirical patterns: \(a\) squared\-hinge loss is often an effective AUC surrogate; \(b\) cross\-entropy warm\-up can help models that enter the AUC phase from a poor starting region; and \(c\) parameter\-efficient fine\-tuning from a pretrained model can reduce that need by starting closer to a favorable ranking geometry\. Experiments on 8 CV tasks and 8 NLP tasks, using ResNet50, DenseNet121, DistilBERT\-base, and Qwen2\.5\-1\.5B\-Instruct, support these predictions\.

## [Analysis of the Relationship Between Computer Laboratory Usage Behavior and Academic Achievement Among Undergraduate Students](../publications/df167ff3ad226957f8cc.md)

Pavinee Inthong

This study aimed to: 1\) examine students’ computer laboratory usage behavior, 2\) analyze the relationship between laboratory usage behavior and academic achievement, and 3\) propose guidelines for monitoring and supporting at\-risk students based on the concept of Learning Analytics\. This quantitative research employed secondary data obtained from the computer laboratory usage log system and students’ academic records from the second semester of academic year 2024 and the first semester of academic year 2025\. The sample consisted of 105 students selected through purposive sampling based on the completeness of data from both sources\. The data were prepared, validated, transformed into individual\-level variables, and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficient, and Logistic Regression\. The findings revealed that students demonstrated a moderate to high level of computer laboratory usage behavior\. Laboratory usage behavior was related to academic achievement, particularly the number of usage days, number of visits, and total usage duration\. In addition, the Logistic Regression model was able to support the classification of at\-risk students at an acceptable level, with an AUC of 0\.722, accuracy of 81\.30%, precision of 79\.60%, recall of 77\.80%, and F1\-score of 78\.70%\. The results indicate that log data from the computer laboratory usage system can serve as a useful database for developing a monitoring and early warning system for at\-risk students, thereby supporting proactive student assistance in higher education effectively\.

## [Smart nanocarriers and biomaterials for targeted drug delivery in spinal cord injury: molecular mechanisms and translational perspectives](../publications/df19ea391555cd7f4d8e.md)

Wenqing Han; Pengfei Qi; Jiaxin Li; Lu Min; Hongxiang Li; Hongna Yin

Spinal cord injury \(SCI\) results in permanent motor, sensory, and autonomic dysfunction below the level of injury; currently, there are no effective treatments to promote neural functional recovery\. Inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, apoptosis, excitotoxicity, glial scarring, and impaired axonal regeneration—all triggered by secondary damage—are the core pathological mechanisms hindering functional recovery\. Traditional drugs, however, are limited by the blood\-spinal cord barrier, short half\-lives, and systemic toxic side effects, resulting in poor therapeutic efficacy\. This article provides a systematic review of research progress over the past decade on the use of nanocarrier\-based therapeutics for the treatment of spinal cord injury and analyzes their therapeutic effects through seven major mechanisms, including the inhibition of inflammation and regulation of macrophage/microglia polarization, antagonism of oxidative stress, regulation of programmed cell death and neuroprotection, as well as the promotion of axonal regeneration, myelin repair, glial scar and extracellular matrix remodeling, and vascular repair and blood\-spinal cord barrier reconstruction\. It further compares the functional characteristics, advantages, and translational potential of major delivery platforms, including liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, micelles, inorganic nanomaterials, nanozymes, exosomes, biomimetic carriers, nanohydrogels, and composite scaffolds\. Among these, biomimetic carriers and multifunctional nanozymes have shown promising preclinical results in trans\-barrier delivery and modulation of the injury microenvironment\. However, current research still faces bottlenecks such as insufficient long\-term safety validation, low targeting efficiency, significant discrepancies between animal models and clinical pathology, and difficulties in scaling up preparation processes\. By integrating the characteristics of nanocarriers with the key pathological mechanisms at different stages of spinal cord injury, this paper provides a mechanism\-driven analytical framework for the rational design and clinical translation of nanomedicines\. In the future, microenvironment\-responsive smart delivery, the integration of nanotechnology with stem cells and neuromodulation strategies, and the establishment of standardized evaluation systems may become key directions for advancing the clinical translation of nanomedicines\.

## [Dissociating task, semantic, and response conflict in cognitive aging: evidence from a low\-cognitive control Stroop paradigm](../publications/df213130e53115c07f22.md)

Eldad Keha; Maria Augustinova; Ludovic Ferrand; Eyal Kalanthroff

Cognitive aging is often associated with increased Stroop interference, but it remains unclear whether this reflects a broad decline in inhibitory control or selective impairments in specific conflict\-resolution mechanisms\. The present study examined age\-related differences in task conflict, semantic conflict, and response conflict using a low\-cognitive\-control Stroop paradigm designed to amplify conflict effects\. Younger and older adults completed a manual color\-identification task including neutral shapes, neutral words, color\-associated words, non\-response\-set incongruent color words, and response\-set incongruent color words\. This design allowed us to dissociate response conflict, two components of semantic conflict, and task conflict within a single paradigm\. Older adults showed larger response conflict than younger adults, along with modest age\-related increases in both semantic relevance and semantic relatedness\. In contrast, task conflict did not differ between age groups\. These results suggest that age\-related increases in Stroop interference are not best explained by a single global inhibitory deficit\. Rather, under the present manual\-response, reduced\-control conditions, older adults showed greater semantic and response\-level conflict, whereas task conflict remained comparable across age groups\. This dissociation is consistent with a more fine\-grained account of cognitive control in aging\.

## [An Analysis of the Use of Race and Ethnicity in Georgetown University Medical Center Publications](../publications/df373754c2ea4c8f50cf.md)

Cameron John Sabet; Victoria Fubara; Jennifer Martínez Sánchez; Charles Scott Dorris; Valeriy R\. Korostyshevskiy; Michael W Plankey; Bara Hammadeh; Sarah Kureshi

ABSTRACT Background Racial and ethnic health disparities remain a pressing issue in the United States, especially as the country grows more diverse\. How race and ethnicity are discussed in medical research can influence data interpretation and the application of findings\. We evaluated the presentation of race and ethnicity in Georgetown University Medical Center and MedStar\-affiliated scientific research articles published in the years 2010 and 2020, focusing on whether these factors were framed as social or biological constructs and how this framing may have changed over this decade\. Methods We conducted a targeted literature search using MEDLINE and PsycINFO databases with predetermined racial and ethnic terms for 2010 and 2020\. The initial search yielded 81 publications from 2010 and 222 from 2020\. Of these, 54 from 2010 were eligible, and 163 from 2020 were eligible\. Blinded reviewers independently scored each publication for the context of race or ethnicity mentions, explanations provided \(biological, social, both, or none\), and race or ethnicity identification method\. Results The definition of race and ethnicity as sociodemographic factors increased significantly between the years 2010 and 2020 \(5\.6% vs 31\.9%, P&lt;\.001\)\. However, this increase in sociodemographic labeling occurred alongside a decline in social or multifactorial explanations for differences in race/ethnicity \(58\.1% vs 43\.9%\) and a slight increase in biological framing \(25\.6% vs 28\.6%\), suggesting a shift in terminology without a corresponding increase in deeper contextual interpretation\. Race was descriptively more often contextualized as biological \(25\.6% vs 28\.6%\), while social or multifactorial explanations decreased, though these changes were not statistically significant\. No statistically significant change was observed in identification methods for race/ethnicity \(P=\.16\), though self\-identification declined from 80\.4% to 66\.4% while researcher\-assigned race increased from 2\.2% to 12\.3% over the same period\. Conclusion These findings emphasize the need for nuanced discussions of race/ethnicity in biomedical research that prioritize social determinants and avoid biological essentialism\. These findings support the need for institutional guidelines to promote responsible research practices\.

## [Multimodal analysis of sleep disturbances and heart disease in older adults: a machine learning and exploratory path analysis approach](../publications/df402a69d93d04555644.md)

Tianwen Wei; Tangjiang Wan; Shangwei Huang; Hongping Xu; Yuxiao Sun; Qi Zhang; Yafei Li

Sleep disturbances and heart disease are common among older adults, yet the psychological and functional pathways linking sleep symptoms to heart disease remain insufficiently characterized\. This study examined the association between sleep disturbance indicators and heart disease among older adults using multivariable regression, exploratory path analysis, and machine\-learning approaches in a cross\-sectional analysis of the 2018 wave of the Mexican Health and Aging Study\. This cross\-sectional analysis used data from the 2018 wave \(wave 5\) of the Mexican Health and Aging Study and was restricted to respondents aged 50 years or older\. Participants were categorized according to self\-reported heart disease status\. Sleep disturbance indicators included difficulty falling asleep, waking up at night, waking up too early, and feeling refreshed upon waking\. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the CESD\-9 score\. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals\. An exploratory path analysis was applied to examine pathways involving depressive symptoms and fatigue\. As an exploratory, complementary analysis, random forest was used to assess variable importance and internal classification performance rather than clinical prediction\. Among 12,709 participants aged 50 years or older, 1,585 had heart disease and 11,124 were controls\. In the primary model, which estimated the total association without adjusting for depressive symptoms and fatigue, waking up at night most of the time was associated with higher odds of heart disease compared with never having this symptom \(adjusted OR 1\.70, 95% CI 1\.41–2\.03, p &lt; 0\.001\), as were waking up at night sometimes \(adjusted OR 1\.28, 95% CI 1\.10–1\.48, p &lt; 0\.001\) and difficulty falling asleep most of the time \(adjusted OR 1\.27, 95% CI 1\.07–1\.52, p = 0\.007\)\. Feeling refreshed upon waking most of the time was inversely associated with heart disease \(adjusted OR 0\.81, 95% CI 0\.69–0\.94, p = 0\.007\)\. Waking up too early was not associated with heart disease \(adjusted OR 1\.11, 95% CI 0\.94–1\.30, p = 0\.223\)\. These associations were less precise and were no longer statistically significant in the respondent\-weighted sensitivity analysis, whereas the nighttime\-awakening associations remained robust when the three CESD\-9 items overlapping with sleep and fatigue were removed\. The exploratory random forest analysis showed limited internal classification performance, with an AUC of 0\.72 \(95% CI 0\.71–0\.73\) and a precision\-recall AUC of 0\.24 based on 10\-fold cross\-validation; at the Youden\-optimal threshold sensitivity and specificity were both 0\.67\. Hypertension, age, fatigue, ADL score, CESD\-9 score and stroke history were the most informative classification variables\. Exploratory path analysis indicated that depressive symptoms and fatigue were associated with both the sleep disturbance indicators and heart disease status; these indirect associations are interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of temporal mediation\. Sleep disturbance indicators were independently associated with heart disease among older adults\. Exploratory path analysis and machine learning further suggested that fatigue and depressive symptoms were associated with sleep disturbance and with heart disease status\. Because this was a cross\-sectional analysis, the findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal\. The random forest findings represent exploratory classification and should not be interpreted as a clinically validated prediction model\.

## [From duality to triadic structuration: Coupling Agile agency, generative technology, and regulatory structure](../publications/df41b08ead741511ef05.md)

Xiaofeng Wang; Nan Yang; Zheying Zhang; Ali Mehraj; Pietro Scola; Tomas Herda; Sami Hyrynsalmi

As generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) increasingly permeates software development, Agile organizations face growing pressure to achieve continuous lifecycle compliance amid rapidly evolving regulatory demands\. Classical Structuration Theory and its derivatives account for technology as either an instantiation of social structure or a medium for human agency; neither pole adequately captures GenAI’s quasi\-autonomous capacity to reshape organizational practices and give rise to new regulatory obligations\. This study addresses this gap by developing Triadic Structuration Theory\. Following an incremental Design Science Research \(DSR\) paradigm, we develop this abstract design artifact through cycle\-level intermediate artifacts, with cross\-cycle knowledge accumulation\. Cycle 1 derives a problem backlog of GenAI\-induced tensions in Agile practice\. Cycle 2 conceptualizes RegOps, showing how Agile agency adapts under regulatory pressure\. Cycle 3 designs an EU AI Act\-aligned model card template, showing how regulatory structure becomes embedded in generative technology\. Cycle 4 explores GenAI\-enabled solutions to ISO\-related compliance barriers in an Agile company\. Together, the evidence and knowledge accumulated within and across the cycles position generative technology as a third construct rather than a medium between agency and structure\. Regulatory structure is embedded directly into it, it reshapes Agile agency through quasi\-autonomous action, and its use to meet existing obligations may recursively generate new ones\. The study extends Structuration Theory as a middle\-range theory to Agile and GenAI contexts, and demonstrates how nested DSR with intermediate artifacts can support theory development\. For practitioners, it offers guidance on leveraging GenAI for compliance, cautioning that it is a structural intervention rather than a one\-off fix\.

## [Baseline AI Economic Literacy and Enacted Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Tools by Oncology and Critical Care Professionals](../publications/df432100b44e838c82e5.md)

Dragoș\-Ciprian Negoiță; Ciprian Gîndac; Akhil Akula; Karina Cristina Marin; Adrian Cosmin Ilie

We examined whether baseline artificial intelligence \(AI\) economic literacy was associated with sustained use of oncology AI tools\. This prospective cohort included 96 oncology and critical care professionals at two centres in Timișoara, Romania, followed for 12 months after institutional roll\-out\. Participants were classified by AI Economic Literacy Index \(AIELI\) scores as high \(≥14\) or low \(&lt;14\)\. Sustained use required log\-verified activity in at least two of the final three months\. Analyses included regression, inverse probability of treatment weighting and exploratory indirect\-association analysis through return\-on\-investment \(ROI\) confidence\. Among 91 completers, sustained use occurred in 29/53 high\-literacy participants \(54\.7%\) and 7/38 low\-literacy participants \(18\.4%; risk ratio 2\.97, 95% confidence interval 1\.46–6\.06\)\. The weighted risk ratio was 2\.24 \(1\.15–4\.34\), and the profession\-stratified risk ratio was 2\.80 \(1\.36–5\.76\)\. Median time to first use was 5\.8 months in the high\-literacy group and was not reached in the low\-literacy group\. Nine participants \(eight high\-literacy, one low\-literacy\) had recorded use before the baseline assessment; in a delayed\-entry analysis restricted to the 87 participants unused at assessment, the crude hazard ratio for subsequent first use was 2\.98 \(1\.62–5\.48\) and the crude risk ratio for sustained use after excluding prior users was 3\.01 \(1\.36–6\.64\); the corresponding covariate\-adjusted estimates were less precise \(hazard ratio 1\.81, 0\.89–3\.69; risk ratio 2\.19, 0\.99–4\.86\) and their confidence intervals included the null\. Roll\-out\-based time\-to\-first\-use comparisons are descriptive because they include events preceding measurement\. Sustained use increased across literacy bands\. An indirect association through ROI confidence was observed but was not interpretable as causal mediation\. Higher baseline economic literacy was associated with earlier and more sustained recorded AI\-tool use, although opportunity for use differed by profession, and the adjusted timing\-corrected estimates leave the independent contribution of literacy uncertain\. Larger multicentre studies should evaluate whether literacy training improves adoption and whether adoption translates into clinical or economic benefit\.

## [Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators](../publications/df43caec207ea5910f93.md)

Vignesh Gopakumar; Zhuoyuan Wang; Ander Gray; Valentin Duruisseaux; Josh Williams; William Michael Edward Ellis; Nuno Nobre; Matthew Field; James Panayis; Alexander I\. Blair; Andrew Davis; Stanislas Pamela; Robert Akers; Marc Peter Deisenroth; Anima Anandkumar

Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers\. Efficient grid\-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator \(FNO\) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes\. We introduce L\-SplineFNO, a memory\-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor\-product B\-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid\. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry\-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction\. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution\. Across six three\-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L\-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26\.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU\. It also supports zero\-shot super\-resolution and efficient closed\-form spatial derivatives\. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29\.2\-million\-node MAST\-U tokamak model\.

## [The Relationship Between Digitalization, Sustainable Development and Government Effectiveness in OECD Countries](../publications/df52e286f4f0e661a9b3.md)

Selçuk Balı

This study examines the impact of digitalization on sustainable development in OECD countries over the period 2000–2024\. Digitalization is measured through a composite index constructed by Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\) using internet usage, fixed broadband subscriptions, and mobile cellular subscriptions\. The Sustainable Development Goals Index \(SDGI\) is employed as the indicator of sustainable development\. Gross domestic product per capita, trade openness, and government effectiveness are included as control variables\. The empirical analysis is conducted using the Driscoll–Kraay estimator and panel quantile regression approach\. The findings indicate that digitalization exerts a positive and statistically significant effect on sustainable development\. Furthermore, the quantile regression results reveal that the impact of digitalization becomes stronger in countries with higher levels of sustainable development performance\. These findings suggest that digital transformation constitutes an important driver of sustainable development; however, its effectiveness varies according to countries’ institutional and economic capacities\. By employing a PCA\-based digitalization index and examining heterogeneous effects across different levels of sustainable development, the study provides new empirical evidence for the OECD countries\.

## [Systematic bibliometric analysis of university students’ self\-feedback literacy from 2010 to 2025](../publications/df56fab19c4fbe8d6461.md)

程学高

This study used bibliometric analysis to examine research on university students’ self\-feedback literacy using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection\. The initial search identified 372 records published within a retrieval window from January 2010 to June 2025\. Following screening, eligibility assessment, and bibliographic data cleaning, 14 records met the predefined eligibility criteria and were retained for the final bibliometric analysis\. Given the small size of the final corpus and the partial coverage of 2025, the findings are interpreted as exploratory patterns within the retrieved dataset rather than as definitive representations of the broader research field\. The study examined publication activity, sources, authorship, citations, keyword associations, thematic patterns, and country\-level collaboration within the retrieved corpus, with the findings interpreted as exploratory evidence rather than generalizable estimates of the broader field\.

## [Land, culture, voice, and economics: an Indigenous land based framework for STEM and agricultural education](../publications/df5e7ca4f11562df297f.md)

Quintana M\. Clark; Olivia Perez; Jennifer L\. Freeman

As Tribal Nations explore emerging opportunities in bio\-based economies, hemp education offers a meaningful platform for integrating land stewardship, cultural knowledge, community priorities, and workforce development\. Yet existing science, technology, engineering, and mathematics \(STEM\) and agricultural education models rarely provide culturally grounded approaches that integrate Indigenous epistemologies, land\-based pedagogy, and sovereignty\-centered economic development\. This article introduces a conceptual Indigenous land\-based curriculum framework for culturally grounded STEM and agricultural education, using hemp education as an applied and relational learning context\. Grounded in Indigenous research methodologies and guided by a Two\-Eyed Seeing orientation, the framework was developed through qualitative conceptual inquiry and iterative synthesis of scholarship on Indigenous epistemologies, culturally grounded STEM education, land\-based learning, and community\-centered economic development\. Centered on Land, Culture, Voice, and Economics as foundational dimensions of curriculum design, the model is represented through a flower metaphor that emphasizes holistic, experiential, place\-based, community\-based, and intergenerational learning\. Indigenous values of reciprocity, relationality, responsibility, and respect further shape how teaching and learning are enacted within the framework\. By articulating a cohesive pedagogical structure that bridges Indigenous knowledge systems, applied STEM learning, and sustainable bio\-based economic futures, the article offers a conceptual model for designing culturally grounded curricula, advances scholarship on Indigenous land\-based curriculum design, and provides a foundation for future curriculum development and research\.

## [PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN E\-COMMERCE DAN PROMOSI ONLINE TERHADAP PERILAKU BELANJA MAHASISWA FAKULTAS EKONOMI UNIVERSITAS MAHAPUTRA MUHAMMAD YAMIN](../publications/df72311a36d8c8dc2784.md)

Syarifah Mutia; Dwi Annisa Rahmanillahi; Meyriska Eka Putri; Karin Septiani

Abstract: The growth of e\-commerce has transformed consumer shopping patterns, particularly among university students, who constitute a group of active internet users\. Beyond the convenience offered by e\-commerce, online promotions also serve as a factor influencing students&\#x27; shopping behavior\. This study aims to determine the impact of e\-commerce usage and online promotions on students&\#x27; shopping behavior\. A quantitative method with an associative approach was employed\. The study population consisted of 145 students, with a sample of 107 respondents determined using Slovin&\#x27;s formula\. Data collection was conducted via questionnaires, while data analysis utilized SPSS Version 25 software, covering validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t\-tests, F\-tests, and the coefficient of determination\. The results indicate that e\-commerce usage has a positive and significant effect on students&\#x27; shopping behavior, with a calculated t\-value of 2\.728 \(exceeding the t\-table value of 1\.659\) and a significance value of 0\.007 \(below 0\.05\)\. Online promotions also have a positive and significant effect on students&\#x27; shopping behavior, with a calculated t\-value of 4\.609 \(exceeding the t\-table value of 1\.659\) and a significance value of 0\.000 \(below 0\.05\)\. Simultaneously, e\-commerce usage and online promotions significantly influence students&\#x27; shopping behavior, with a calculated F\-value of 45\.155 \(exceeding the F\-table value of 3\.08\)\. The variable exerting the most dominant influence on students&\#x27; shopping behavior is online promotion\.\.Keywords: E\-Commerce, Online Promotion, and Shopping Behavior

## [The perceptual geometry and chromaticity of near\-death experience spaces](../publications/df79465d5951bdf06840.md)

France Lerner; Paulo Cezar Rocha dos Santos; Guillaume Tahar

Near\-Death Experiences \(NDEs\) challenge conventional research methods, as they are often described as exceeding the limits of verbal expression\. While most studies rely on narrative accounts, little attention has been given to graphic representations as a complementary mode of investigation\. This study employs a hybrid approach combining a semi\-structured digital questionnaire with a graphic reconstruction task\. Participants first segmented their Out\-of\-Body Experience \(OBE\) and NDE into distinct experiential sequences by assigning chronological numbers to each phase\. This sequencing enabled the identification of what we term the experiential NDE Core, defined here as the NDE sequence or sequences distinguished from the Dissociative and Associative OBE phases, thereby facilitating comparisons across participants\. The graphic reconstructions identified recurrent Visual\-Field boundary configurations, including conical forms, elliptic arcs with variable Visual\-Field Extents \(VFE\), and ellipsoidal configurations\. Exploratory analyses indicated variation in chromatic perceptual qualities across these configurations, although evidence for differences among configurations was not uniform across statistical analyses\. The reported emergence of Visual Mental Imagery also appeared to vary across Visual\-Field configurations\. This dual\-method design was intended to capture experiential features of OBEs and NDEs that may not be conveyed through verbal reports alone\. Notably, OBEs have rarely been examined in terms of their independence from, or conjunction with, NDEs\. In the present study, their temporal placement was defined operationally by the sequencing protocol to permit isolation of the NDE Core\.

Precision psychiatry has improved prediction of treatment response across psychiatry, but translating biomarkers into treatment strategy remains difficult\.
