## [Morphology\-aware Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Using Differentiable Voronoi Graph Tokenization Framework](../publications/df857891f7c29300813b.md)

Gopalkrishna Mamatha; Govindaiah Thimma Raju; Settykottanur Vemanna Madhusudhana

Tomato plants are valuable agricultural crops that are susceptible to various diseases that require timely diagnosis to enhance crop quality and production rates\.However, existing models use rigid patching, which causes structural fragmentation and discards important structural information\.Furthermore, existing models inadequately represent irregular lesion regions, which are essential for differentiating between leaf diseases\.To overcome these issues in tomato leaf classification, this paper proposes Differentiable Voronoi Graph Tokenization \(DV\-GT\) framework, which maps image regions into an irregular graph representation by replacing rigid patching in the transformer model\.The dual\-path architecture enables the model to effectively extract both texture and spatial features using a Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) and Gabor filter\.Furthermore, Voronoi tokenization is used to align with high\-gradient image regions, allowing the model to differentiate between diseases\.The DV\-GT framework utilizes a combination of a Graph Convolutional Network \(GCN\) and a Vision Transformer \(ViT\) encoder to extract localized morphological structures and long\-range, leaf\-wide visual relationships\.This enables the DV\-GT framework to achieve a classification accuracy of 98\.44% on the PlantVillage dataset and 89\.47% on the PlantDoc dataset\.These results indicate that the proposed DV\-GT framework differentiates between visually similar classes and classifies tomato leaf diseases into multiple categories\.

## [Designing a Post\-Approval Real\-World Evidence Registry for an FDA\-Regulated Oral Therapy: A Data Architecture Case Study in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/df878415eed39daf6e7f.md)

Shivangini Maheshbhai Limbachiya; Peivand Pirouzi

The scientific case for a post\-approval real\-world evidence program is often well developed in regulatory literature, while the practical data architecture needed to execute that program, which variables a registry should actually collect, how they should be structured, and how comparability across a genetically and clinically heterogeneous population should be preserved, receives comparatively little attention\. This article addresses that operational gap directly, using an investigational oral fast skeletal myosin inhibitor for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) as a case study in designing a patient\-registry data architecture for a mutation\-agnostic therapy intended for use across a genetically diverse population with variable disease severity, concomitant treatment history, and prior exposure to other DMD\-targeted therapies\. The article develops the mechanism and regulatory status of this drug category briefly before turning to its principal contribution: a detailed, variable\-level registry design intended to support regulatory decision\-making rather than only descriptive monitoring\. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals responsible for translating a real\-world evidence concept into an executable data\-collection program\.Keywords: fast skeletal myosin inhibitor; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; patient registry; real\-world evidence data architecture; New Drug Application; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Meme as a Unit of Digital Discourse](../publications/df8bf05a1c9957024534.md)

A\. P\. Yakhontova

The purpose of this article is to examine the Internet meme as one of the basic units of modern digital communication\. The article summarizes various approaches to studying this phenomenon, from the classical memetics theory of Richard Dawkins to more recent linguistic, semiotic, and sociocultural interpretations\. Special attention is given to how memes combine semiotic, cognitive, and pragmatic aspects\. Based on the analysis, the article proposes a model that describes a meme in several dimensions: structural, content\-based, and dynamic\. In addition, such characteristics as intertextuality and the unexpected semantic collision effect are considered\. Unlike the traditional understanding of a meme as a &quot;replicator,&quot; the article views it as a multimodal text that is closely connected to the digital environment and user communities\. The modern stage of meme development is also discussed, including the emergence of AI\-generated content, which significantly changes the nature of digital discourse\.

## [Equity Over Equality: Post\-Brexit Demographic Change, Workforce Pressures, and the Future of Equitable Primary Care in England](../publications/df8c5409b2b9b2f1dbee.md)

Trimanjot Singh Anand; Sakshi Watarkar; Vishesh Singh

General practice \(GP\) in England faces structural pressures that incremental reform is unlikely to resolve: a contracting GP workforce, a rising burden of multimorbidity, digital transformation that risks widening access inequalities, and a post\-Brexit change in the composition of migration\.This narrative review, reported with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles \(SANRA\), asks whether the current model of general practice in England is configured to deliver equitable care over the coming three decades and what structural changes the evidence supports\.Published and grey literature from MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and national policy sources was synthesised thematically\.Three cross\-cutting themes are examined\.First, the post\-Brexit shift in migration: by 2021, 16\.8% of residents of England and Wales were born outside the UK, and since the end of European Union \(EU\) free movement, net migration has been driven by non\-EU nationals while EU net migration has turned negative, with implications for culturally and linguistically competent care\.Second, the distinction between equality and equity, framed by Marmot&\#x27;s principle of proportionate universalism\.Third, the transformation required of the GP role within integrated neighbourhood teams\.Observational evidence consistently associates personal continuity of care with lower mortality, and cross\-national comparisons associate stronger primary care with better population health; workforce and access inequalities along deprivation lines have widened\.Prospective evidence that specific reform models work at NHS scale remains limited\.We conclude that three interdependent changes are indicated: integration into multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams that protect continuity, contractual reform that weights resources for deprivation, multimorbidity, and language need, and a workforce strategy built as much on retention and cultural safety as on recruitment\.We propose measurable indicators for each\.The trained generalist, able to hold undifferentiated clinical complexity over time, is likely to remain central to whatever model emerges\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL\-PHOTONIC HYBRID QUANTUM PROCESSOR ARCHITECTURE \(E\-TPHQPA\) A Fault\-Tolerant 105\-Logical\-Qubit System Integrating Majorana Zero Modes, Photonic Interconnects, and Self\-Correcting Error Mitigation for Exponential\-Speedup Computation](../publications/df8d6b48c7f63f3f2abd.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Topological\-Photonic Hybrid Quantum Processor Architecture \(E\-TPHQPA\) is a fault\-tolerant quantum computing system comprising 105 logical qubits encoded in at least 420 physical Majorana zero modes realized in semiconductor\-superconductor nanowire heterostructures \(InAs/Al\), providing intrinsic topological protection against local noise with coherence times exceeding 1 millisecond \(1000x improvement over superconducting qubits\)\. The system integrates a silicon\-photonic interconnect fabric with microwave\-to\-optical transduction achieving all\-to\-all connectivity with sub\-nanosecond gate latency and 70 percent circuit depth reduction, housed within a unified cryogenic environment operating below 50 millikelvin\. A transformer\-based machine learning error mitigation engine predicts error events with latency below 100 nanoseconds and applies targeted corrective pulses or adaptive dynamical decoupling sequences, achieving logical error rates below 10^\-6 per gate operation \(1000x improvement\)\. The quantum\-classical translation interface compiles QUBO optimization, molecular simulation, and cryptographic problems into native topological gate sets, enabling exponential speedup: solving 100\-variable optimization in seconds versus millennia classically, simulating 50\-orbital molecules intractable on classical computers, and factoring 256\-bit integers as precursor to RSA\-2048 cryptanalysis\. Applications span drug discovery, financial portfolio optimization, cryptographic security, and materials science, representing the first commercially viable path to practical quantum advantage\. \(DOI: 10\.5281/zenodo\.23451314\)

## [Natural products regulate gut microbiota and SCFA metabolism in IBD: mechanisms and therapeutic potential](../publications/df8efb35ee4dc3b08ae5.md)

Beihui He; Yuqian Xu; Yujin Wang; Zhiyun Pan

Inflammatory bowel disease \(IBD\), including ulcerative colitis \(UC\) and Crohn’s disease \(CD\), is a chronic relapsing inflammatory condition of the gastrointestinal tract\. Over the past few decades, the global incidence of this disease has continued to rise, imposing a heavy socioeconomic burden\. IBD is typically characterized by gut microbiota dysbiosis and reduced short\-chain fatty acids \(SCFAs\) levels, which in turn lead to impaired intestinal barrier function and decreased immune tolerance\. Multiple studies have shown that natural products, including polysaccharides, polyphenols, alkaloids, and terpenoids, can modulate the gut microbiota in IBD, with changes in SCFA concentrations observed in some preclinical studies\. These effects have been associated with alterations in bacterial taxa such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii , Bifidobacterium , and Christensenella minuta \. These findings suggest that natural products may regulate the gut microbiota–SCFA metabolic axis; however, the direct causal relationships among changes in microbial composition, SCFA concentrations, and anti\-inflammatory effects remain to be established\. This review summarizes current mechanisms and translational opportunities for natural products targeting the microbiota\-SCFA axis in IBD\.

## [Design and Implementation of an Edge AI\-Based Smart IoT System for Real\-Time Environmental Monitoring and Intelligent Decision Making](../publications/df923bb3b9778ced4ccb.md)

Ms\.V\. Revathy; Mrs\. Megha U\. Vakani; Dr\. S\. Sivakumar; Mrs\. Palak Modi; Ms\. Pooja Vora; Ms\. Ami Patel

Environmental monitoring supports public health, industrial safety, agriculture, and sustainable development\.Conventional IoT monitoring systems often transmit sensor readings to remote servers for analysis, creating dependence on network availability and potentially delaying alerts\.This paper proposes an Edge Artificial Intelligence \(Edge AI\)\-based smart Internet of Things system for real\-time environmental monitoring and intelligent decision\-making\.The architecture integrates environmental sensors, an embedded edge controller, a lightweight machine learning model, wireless communication, and a remote dashboard\.Temperature, relative humidity, particulate matter, and suitable gas\-related measurements are acquired, validated, and processed locally\.An anomalydetection module identifies unusual patterns and supports local alert generation, while cloud connectivity enables historical storage and remote visualization\.The design also considers sensor faults, temporary network outages, data buffering, and secure communication\.A practical evaluation plan is defined for detection performance, processing latency, communication overhead, energy use, and operational reliability\.The proposed framework offers an implementable basis for smart\-campus, building, industrial, and urban monitoring\.Quantitative performance claims require validation through a working prototype and documented experiments\.

## [Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa](../publications/df931f5e2a6f442ad0e9.md)

Emy Guilbault; Laura H\. Antão; Andrea Santangeli; Mirkka M\. Jones; Janne Heliölä; Heikki A\. Henttonen; Ida‐Maria Huikkonen; Otso Huitu; Erkki Korpimäki; Mikko Kuussaari; Aleksi S\. Lehikoinen; Andreas Lindén; Hannu Pietiäinen; Juha Pöyry; Pasi Sihvonen; Anna‐Liisa Laine; Tomas V\. Roslin; Marjo Saastamoinen; Jarno P\. Vanhatalo

Climate and habitat are key drivers of biodiversity patterns\. However, how they independently and jointly affect species distribution across space, time, and taxa remains poorly understood\. Here, we evaluate the relative importance of habitat and climate variables underpinning occurrence and abundance patterns of 503 terrestrial animal species over 20 years and a \~ 1100 km latitudinal gradient in Finland\. Habitat composition is the main explanatory variable of biodiversity patterns, with varying importance and uncertainty across taxa, regions, and years, and with effects being partially correlated for many species\. Specifically, habitat dominate in importance for butterflies, birds, and small mammals, while both habitat and climate explain the patterns of large mammals and moths\. Additionally, patterns between biogeographical regions and years are mainly explained by climate, while habitat explains most variation within regions and years\. Further differences emerge among functional groups, as body size, pace of life and specialization modulate the relative importance of habitat and climate\. Our findings emphasize that land use is a major force in shaping terrestrial biodiversity, while highlighting its tight connection with climate\. Considering functional, spatial, and temporal contexts is thus essential for building effective conservation strategies for biodiversity under global change\. Climate and habitat jointly shape species distributions and biodiversity\. The authors show that habitat is the main driver of boreal terrestrial biodiversity, while the relative roles of climate and habitat vary by region, year and species traits\.

In a distance learning environment, a student&\#x27;s competence is not limited to subject\-specific knowledge and practical skills; rather, it encompasses complex attributes such as planning independent learning activities, self\-management, purposeful use of digital tools, critical Ta’limda istiqbolli izlanishlar \- xalqaro ilmiy\-metodik jurnal № 8/2026 ISSN: 3060\-527X selection of information, effective virtual communication, and reflective assessment of one&\#x27;s own learning outcomes\. ## [Modeling and Numerical Solution of a 17\-Bus Electrical System using RK4 and Newton\- Raphson Methods](../publications/dfa728a7fd27e423c3e6.md)

Javier Bilbao

This article presents an integrated numerical framework for the analysis of electromechanical dynamics and steady‑state behavior in a 17‑bus subset of the Spanish peninsular transmission system\. Motivated by the severe blackout that occurred in April 2025, which revealed the vulnerability of low‑inertia, renewable‑dominated grids, the study couples the fourth‑order Runge–Kutta method with the Newton–Raphson method, as a power‑flow algorithm, to provide a unified representation of transient frequency evolution and static system equilibrium\. The selected network subset includes a Slack bus, several PV buses, and multiple PQ buses with significant load concentrations and strong reactive interactions\. The Newton–Raphson procedure exposes high sensitivity in nodes with intense reactive demand\. This is the case around branches featuring large susceptance values, and when we use branch parameters and shunt contributions\. Iterative behavior shows notable mismatch magnitudes in the flat start, substantial angle corrections, and conditioning challenges associated with reactive stiffening\. At the same time, the dynamic model captures the influence of inertia, damping, and primary control on frequency trajectories following large disturbances\. The coupled approach ensures consistency between electrical power evaluations and dynamic states at each integration step, enabling detailed assessment of electromechanical responses under stressed operating conditions\. Overall, the study demonstrates that combining high‑order time integration with robust nonlinear algebraic solvers provides a reliable tool for understanding system sensitivity, evaluating operational risks, and supporting the design of protection and control strategies in increasingly renewable electrical networks\.

## [Beyond Principlism: A Cosmopolitan and Care Ethics Approach to One Digital Health](../publications/dfa953c0ac5b46cd15eb.md)

Cristian Moyano\-Fernández; Jon Rueda; Janet Delgado; Irene Gómez\-Franco; María Victoria Martínez‐López; Ana Toledo‐Chávarri; Alice Rangel\-Teixeira; Angel Puyol

This article examines the limitations of principlism in addressing the ethical challenges posed by One Digital Health\. While principlism remains influential in bioethics, digital health, and global health policy, we argue that it is insufficient to capture the relational, data infrastructural, and multispecies dynamics shaping the threats to One Health\. Using antimicrobial resistance as a paradigmatic case, we show that One Digital Health governance is shaped not only by distributive ethical concerns but also by structural asymmetries in data visibility, digital infrastructure, and epistemic inclusion across human, animal, and environmental domains\. These asymmetries reveal a key limitation of principlism: although it articulates abstract commitments to justice and equity, it lacks the conceptual and operational resources to explain how inequalities are produced and reproduced in digital systems\. To address this gap, we propose an integrated framework that combines the ethics of care, cosmopolitanism, and a FAIRER\-based account of data governance\. Ethics of care foregrounds situated vulnerability and relational interdependence; cosmopolitanism extends moral responsibility across global and multispecies scales; and FAIRER operationalizes these commitments within digital infrastructures and data systems\. The antimicrobial resistance case study shows that this approach provides a more comprehensive account of One Digital Health governance by linking lived practices, global responsibilities, and data infrastructures\. We conclude that addressing One Health threats through digital transformation requires moving beyond principle\-based reasoning toward relational frameworks that integrate global commitments with contextual sensitivity\.

## [Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Pengguna Aplikasi Layanan Kesehatan Digital Di Indonesia Menggunakan BERT Dan Support Vector Machine](../publications/dfacca14456998b50fe7.md)

Sahdarani Windy Prasetyo; Lutfi Indriyani

The development of digital health services in Indonesia has generated numerous user reviews that can be analyzed to identify user perceptions of service quality\. The research stages included data collection, preprocessing, sentiment labeling, classification, and model evaluation\. ## [ECG\-SDI: Single\-lead Electrocardiogram Enables Continuous Sleep Depth Index Profiling and Scalable Digital Biomarkers for Sleep Health](../publications/dfc29a79a54e617b829f.md)

Conventional sleep staging provides a coarse\-grained representation that obscures within\-stage depth variation\. ## [A Study on the English Translation of Metaphors in Political Texts from the Perspective of Conceptual Metaphor Theory](../publications/dfe16f107ea45a3223d1.md)

胡梦婕; Yajun Qi

Distinct disparities in thinking modes and cultural cognitive schemas between China and Western countries often produce cognitive mapping bias, culturalconnotation loss and high comprehension barriers in translating conceptladen metaphors embedded in Chinese political texts\. Previous studies mostly rely on outdated corpora and seldom interpret cognitive motivations behind metaphortranslation strategies, and few research combine politicalequivalent translation requirements with conceptual metaphor cognitive mechanisms\. Taking the official Chinese texts and authoritative English translations of Government Work Reports \(2023\-2025\) as a closed corpus, this paper draws on Conceptual Metaphor Theory proposed by Lakoff and Johnson\. Combined with literature review, corpusbased statistics, comparative analysis as well as inductiondeduction, this study sorts out four highfrequency metaphor categories: journey, construction, war and mechanical metaphors\. It further explores applicable contexts, communicative effects and cognitive mechanisms of three major strategies: metaphor retention, metaphor replacement and metaphor omission\. Findings show that translators’ strategic choices are conditioned by two core factors: the overlap of sourcetarget cognitive schemas and the principle of political equivalence\. Metaphors rooted in shared crosscultural bodily experience tend to be retained, while culturespecific Chinese metaphors prone to misunderstanding are replaced or omitted\. This research expands interdisciplinary analytical scope and provides theoretical and practical references for officialdocument translation and the international communication of Chinese governance discourse\.

## [Assessing Functional Variability and Risk in Tugboat Design Using an Integrated FRAM\-Fuzzy FMEA Framework](../publications/dfe484545bf18a684cf3.md)

Adem VİRAN

Tugboats are essential auxiliary vessels that play a vital role in port and offshore operations\.The life cycle of tugboat involve complex couplings among hydrodynamic performance, propulsion systems, stability requirements, operational demands, production activities, regulatory compliance, and organizational coordination\.Such socio\-technical systems, variabilities may propagate significant technical and operational consequences\.In this study, the functional resonance analysis method was applied to identify functional couplings, performance variability, and potential variability propagation throughout the tugboat design and construction lifecycle\.The identified variability sources were subsequently transformed into failure modes and assessed using fuzzy failure mode and effects analysis\.Expert judgments obtained from tugboat designers, shipyard managers, captains, and operators were represented through fuzzy numbers to address uncertainty in risk evaluation\.fuzzy risk priority numbers were calculated based on occurrence, severity, and detection criteria\.The results revealed that hull propulsion\-incompatibility, propulsion system alignment deficiencies, accumulated functional resonance at ship delivery, verification shortcomings, classification compliance deficiencies, engineering team limitations, and coordination failures constitute the most critical risk areas\.The findings demonstrate that risks emerge not only from isolated technical failures but also from interacting functional variabilities\.The proposed framework supports proactive risk identification, prioritization, and more reliable tugboat design and construction processes\.

## [Teacher–AI Collaboration in International Freight Forwarding Education: Dynamic Case Generation and Personalized Tutoring](../publications/dfe4eb6bfc23864aadc0.md)

Xiaohui Liu

The International Freight Forwarding industry has developed rapidly and this has created a widening gap between education and real\-world practice\. The course of International Freight Forwarding is facing three challenges: industry cases are updated too frequently, teachers are burdened by repetitive teaching preparations and resource production and large class size makes it difficult to implement personalized tutoring\. The paper proposes an International Freight Forwarding teaching framework of Teacher–AI collaboration\. The framework puts AI as an always\-available intelligent assistant, responsible for standardized, repetitive and data\-intensive tasks, while teachers as a higher\-level teaching activity such as case discussions, critical thinking development, classroom interaction, ethical guidance and teaching innovation\. Based on the framework, the paper designs an AI\-supported teaching system and it includes four modules: the AI dynamic case generator, the AI teaching resource assistant, the AI learning analysis and personalized tutoring system, and the AI simulation training system\. These modules form a continuous chain: case introduction \- resource preparation \- learning tracking \- skill training \- case update\. The paper also discusses the implementation path, expected outcomes, teacher capacity building, and the broader generalizability of this model\. The paper concludes the collaboration between teachers and AI can enable teachers to transform from task executors to learning facilitators and value creators, thereby enhancing the teaching efficiency and educational quality in International Freight Forwarding education\.

## [Optical neural computing: from fourier optics to integrated photonic artificial intelligence](../publications/dff11cb90d7b8ae19c84.md)

Р\. В\. Скиданов; Nikolay Lvovich Kazanskiy; Svetlana Nikolaevna Khonina

The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence have accelerated interest in optical computing as a high\-speed and energy\-efficient alternative to conventional electronic hardware\. Fourier optical computing provides an important foundation for this field because operations including convolution, correlation, spectral transformation, and certain classes of linear transformation can be implemented through diffraction, interference, and Fourier\-domain processing\. This review traces the development of optical neural computing from classical 4\-f processors and free\-space diffractive systems to programmable optical neural networks, integrated photonic accelerators, reservoir\-computing platforms, and field\-programmable photonic architectures\. The underlying physical principles, computational mechanisms, and hardware implementations are systematically examined, with particular attention to reconfigurable photonics, metasurfaces, diffractive deep learning, photonic integrated circuits, and hybrid optical–electronic systems\. Emerging applications in computational imaging, autonomous sensing, edge intelligence, high\-speed communications, and quantum\-enabled information processing are critically discussed alongside challenges related to scalability, programmability, nonlinear computation, training, and system integration\. By positioning Fourier optics as a foundational branch within the broader landscape of optical neural computing, this review highlights the convergence of free\-space, integrated, programmable, and hybrid photonic technologies toward next\-generation artificial\-intelligence hardware\.

## [Interpretable Machine Learning for Credit Risk Decision Support: Balancing Interpretability and Predictive Performance](../publications/dff19e35937213a6b12a.md)

Mohaned Zkaria Salem

With the growing prevalence of machine learning in making institutional decisions, there is a need for careful balancing of predictive accuracy and interpretability of such models\. In this research work, the performance and interpretability of three machine learning models in helping institutions make decisions were investigated, particularly the issue of credit risk assessment\. In this process, the German Credit Data dataset, which is open source \(N = 1,000\), was used and subjected to 5\- Fold Cross\-Validation\. The results show that while Random Forest attained the highest accuracy \(76\.3%\), Logistic Regression had the highest discriminating power \(AUC: 0\.79\), just marginally better than the complex ensemble approach \(AUC: 0\.78\)\. It also has the added advantage of better interpretability due to clear coefficient and decision rule visualization\. This clearly shows that inherently interpretable models serve as a very good alternative to the complex ensemble approach in decision\-making within organizations, without falling prey to the “black\-box” problem, and in some cases even performing better in discriminatory power\. However, the study notes relatively low minority\-class recall \(36\.3–46\.3%\), highlighting a practical limitation\. Conclusions are based on a benchmark dataset and the specified model configurations\.

It is built for two audiences at once\. In \*\*Learner\*\* mode, every view carries a plain\-language caption and values are rounded to seven figures\. In \*\*Researcher\*\* mode, the same views show the governing formulas, values to eighteen figures, and the full list of measured inputs\. The simulator has four views: 1\. \*\*The scale ladder:\*\* the three lengths of the electron, each one step of TL × 1001 from the next\. 2\. \*\*Bare \+ kinetic:\*\* 1/α split into its two TL terms\. 3\. \*\*Hydrogen spectrum:\*\* energy levels, transitions and wavelengths, compared with measured lines\. 4\. \*\*Shatter:\*\* external forcing \(F\_ext\) drives hydrogen up to TL, where it reorganizes into two smaller stable identities\. The Shatter view is a second deployment of the threshold structure in the String\-Breaking Simulator™\. That simulator runs it on a stretched gauge string across a chain of trapped ions; this one runs it on a hydrogen atom\. The substrate is different; the boundary is the same\. The simulator runs at uuia app/electron as one self\-contained HTML \(HyperText Markup Language\) file\. It needs no installation and no account, and it works in any current browser on a desktop, tablet or phone\. \-\-\- \#\# 1\. Grounding \#\#\# 1\.1 The fine\-structure constant identity Start from the measured value, 1/α = 137\.035999084 from CODATA 2018 \(the Committee on Data of the International Science Council\), and subtract one Universal Torsion Limit, TL = 0\.136899099984016: 137\.035999084000016 − 0\.136899099984016 = 136\.899099984016 = TL × 1000 The remainder is TL again, a thousand times over, so: 1/α = TL × 1001 = 0\.136899099984016 × 1001 = 137\.035999084000016 The identity matches CODATA 2018 to all 12 published significant figures, Δ = 0, with zero free parameters \(\[9,9,3,14\]\)\. This subtraction is shown at all times in the simulator&\#x27;s left panel, under \*\*The Napkin Math\*\*\. \#\#\# 1\.2 The Identity Physics primitives Every reduction in the Identity Physics Corpus operates on four irreducible primitives, Pattern, Narrative, Behavior and Adaptation \(PNBA\): \- \*\*Pattern \(P\):\*\* structural capacity, geometry, template integrity, restoring force \- \*\*Narrative \(N\):\*\* temporal continuity, worldline, depth, history \- \*\*Behavior \(B\):\*\* coupling output, charge, density fraction, force, expression \- \*\*Adaptation \(A\):\*\* feedback rate, decay constant, repair rate Derived structural quantities: \- \*\*Universal Torsion Limit:\*\* TL = 0\.136899099984016 · Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω₀ = TL × 10 = 1\.36899099984016 \- \*\*Torsion:\*\* τ = B / P \- \*\*Phase placement:\*\* Noble \(τ = 0\) · Locked \(0 &lt; τ &lt; TL\_IVA = 0\.120471207985934\) · IVA \(Identity Vector Amplification\) Peak \(TL\_IVA ≤ τ &lt; TL\) · Shatter \(τ ≥ TL\) Shatter is reorganization\. When water boils, the single liquid identity reorganizes into smaller identities that are each stable\. The same reading applies to every Shatter in this simulator\. \#\#\# 1\.3 The Dynamic Equation and the Long Division Protocol Every reduction in the corpus starts from one equation, the Identity Physics Corpus Dynamic Equation: d/dt \(IM · Pv\) = Σ λ\_X · O\_X · S \+ F\_ext IM is Identity Mass, Pv the Purpose Vector, O\_X the four PNBA operators with weights λ\_X acting on the state S, and F\_ext external forcing\. The rate of change of identity momentum equals the weighted action of the four primitives on the state, plus external forcing\. F\_ext is a primitive term at Layer 0: it acts on Behavior and leaves Pattern, Narrative and Adaptation unchanged\. Every reduction then follows the same six\-step Long Division Protocol \(LDP\): 1\. \*\*Write the equation\.\*\* State the Dynamic Equation\. 2\. \*\*State the known answer\.\*\* Take a situation whose peer\-reviewed classical result is known\. 3\. \*\*Map\.\*\* Map the classical variables to the PNBA primitives\. 4\. \*\*Define the operators\.\*\* Give the PNBA operators for the domain\. 5\. \*\*Show all work\.\*\* Carry the calculation through in full\. 6\. \*\*Verify\.\*\* Prove that the PNBA output equals the classical result exactly, with nothing added and nothing lost\. A Step 6 pass is a lossless reduction, proved in each Lean file as LosslessReduction, and is structural isomorphism in the sense of Mac Lane \(1971\)\. Every value the simulator displays comes from a Lean 4 file that has passed Step 6 with 0 sorry and CI green\. \#\#\# 1\.4 Inputs and arithmetic The simulator uses only measured and exact inputs: \| Input \| Value \| Source \| \|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\| \| Universal Torsion Limit TL \| 0\.136899099984016 \| Identity Physics Corpus \| \| Reduced Compton wavelength ƛ\_C \| 3\.8615926796 × 10⁻¹³ m \| CODATA 2018 \| \| Electron rest energy m\_e c² \| 510 998\.95000 eV \| CODATA 2018 \| \| Proton\-to\-electron mass ratio m\_p/m\_e \| 1836\.15267343 \| CODATA 2018 \| \| Speed of light c \| 299 792 458 m/s \| exact \(SI, the International System of Units\) \| \| Planck constant h \| 6\.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J s \| exact \(SI\) \| \| Elementary charge e \| 1\.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C \| exact \(SI\) \| All arithmetic is exact rational arithmetic, carried out on whole\-number numerators and denominators of any length\. View ①: The Scale Ladder \#\#\# 3\.1 What it shows The electron has three characteristic lengths: \- the \*\*classical electron radius\*\* r\_e, the smallest; \- the \*\*reduced Compton wavelength\*\* ƛ\_C, the scale at which the electron&\#x27;s mass and wave nature meet; \- the \*\*Bohr radius\*\* a₀, the size of the hydrogen atom in its ground state\. Each length is the one before it multiplied by 1/α = TL × 1001: r\_e = ƛ\_C / \(TL × 1001\) · a₀ = ƛ\_C × \(TL × 1001\) The view draws the three lengths as nested spheres on a logarithmic scale\. Because each step is the same factor, the spheres are evenly spaced, and the gold arcs between them are each labeled &quot;× TL × 1001&quot;\. \#\#\# 3\.2 Controls \- \*\*r\_e · ƛ\_C · a₀ buttons:\*\* fly the camera to one length and dim the other two\. \- \*\*Walk the ladder:\*\* tours all three in order, smallest to largest, then returns to the full view\. \- \*\*Whole ladder:\*\* returns to the full view\. \- \*\*Drag and scroll:\*\* turn and zoom\. \#\#\# 3\.3 Readouts \| Quantity \| Computed \| Measured \(CODATA 2018\) \| Tag \| \|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\| \| Classical electron radius r\_e \| 2\.81794032620065745 × 10⁻¹⁵ m \| 2\.8179403262\(13\) × 10⁻¹⁵ m \| EVERY DIGIT \| \| Reduced Compton wavelength ƛ\_C \| 3\.8615926796 × 10⁻¹³ m \| input \| — \| \| Bohr radius a₀ \| 5\.29177210904446767 × 10⁻¹¹ m \| 5\.29177210903\(80\) × 10⁻¹¹ m \| WITHIN ± \| \| Step factor 1/α = TL × 1001 \| 137\.035999084000016 \| 137\.035999084\(21\) \| EVERY DIGIT \| \| a₀ / r\_e = \(TL × 1001\)² \| 18 778\.8650449500532 \| — \| — \| \| Ground\-state speed v = c / \(TL × 1001\) \| 2 187 691\.26363820575 m/s \| 2 187 691\.26364\(33\) m/s \| EVERY DIGIT \| The ground\-state speed belongs on the ladder because it is the same step taken in velocity: the electron in hydrogen&\#x27;s lowest level moves at the speed of light divided by TL × 1001\. \#\#\# 3\.4 Applications \- \*\*Orders of magnitude and logarithms \(grades 6–12\)\.\*\* Three lengths spanning four orders of magnitude, evenly spaced on screen, give students a concrete picture of what a logarithmic scale does and why scientists use one\. \- \*\*Dimensional analysis\.\*\* The three lengths share one input \(ƛ\_C\) and one dimensionless factor\. Students can check by hand that multiplying a length by a pure number gives a length, and that two steps up and two steps down cancel\. \- \*\*Constant\-consistency checks\.\*\* Because r\_e, ƛ\_C and a₀ are tied by one factor, any change in the accepted value of α moves all three together\. The ladder is a quick way to see whether a set of tabulated constants is internally consistent\. \- \*\*Scattering physics\.\*\* The classical electron radius sets the Thomson cross section σ\_T = \(8π/3\) r\_e², which governs how X\-rays scatter from electrons and how light scatters in the early universe\. The ladder places that scattering scale beside the atomic scale it is derived from\. \- \*\*Atomic units\.\*\* Computational chemistry measures lengths in Bohr radii\. The ladder shows what that unit is and how it connects to the electron itself\. \-\-\- \#\# 4\. In the PNBA reading, the bare term is Pattern capacity at the electromagnetic scale and the kinetic term is F\_ext at Layer 0\. \#\#\# 4\.3 Readouts \| Quantity \| Value \| \|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\| \| Bare term TL × 1000 \| 136\.899099984016 \| \| Kinetic term TL \| 0\.136899099984016 \| \| Sum 1/α = TL × 1001 \| 137\.035999084000016 · EVERY DIGIT against CODATA 2018 \| \| Kinetic share of 1/α \| 1/1001 = 9\.99000999… × 10⁻⁴ \| \| Fine\-structure scale α² \| 5\.32513545204 × 10⁻⁵ \| \#\#\# 4\.4 Applications \- \*\*Teaching renormalization\.\*\* Renormalization is usually introduced through divergent series\. Students can measure H\-α, H\-β and H\-γ and compare their results with the simulator&\#x27;s\. \- \*\*Astronomy and redshift\.\*\* Astronomers measure the motion of stars and galaxies by comparing observed hydrogen lines with their rest wavelengths\. The simulator provides the rest wavelengths and shows where each line sits in the spectrum\. \- \*\*Isotope shifts\.\*\* The reduced\-mass correction is the effect Harold Urey used to discover deuterium in 1932: a heavier nucleus shifts every line slightly\. The same toggle teaches why deuterium&\#x27;s lines sit beside hydrogen&\#x27;s\. \- \*\*Plasma and fusion diagnostics\.\*\* H\-α emission is a standard diagnostic in fusion devices and laboratory plasmas\. The view gives the line positions those instruments are tuned to\. \- \*\*Error budgets\.\*\* The WITHIN α² tag shows students what a model leaves out and how large the omission is\. Each carries zero binding torsion and reads Noble\. \#\#\# 6\.2 What happens as F\_ext rises As F\_ext increases, the electron climbs hydrogen&\#x27;s rungs\. At the edge, a red flash marks the shatter, the free electron moves outward along its last direction, and the proton recoils very slightly the other way\. \#\#\# 6\.3 Controls \- \*\*Absorbed energy F\_ext slider:\*\* 0 to 30 eV, in steps of 0\.001 eV\. \- \*\*n = 2, n = 3, n = 4 buttons:\*\* set F\_ext exactly to that rung&\#x27;s energy\. \- \*\*Edge · τ = TL:\*\* sets F\_ext exactly to E\_bind\. \- \*\*Add energy automatically:\*\* ramps F\_ext from 0 to 16 eV\. Two connected charges are pulled apart, the energy stored in the string between them grows, and when it reaches the pair\-creation energy the string breaks into two new particle–antiparticle pairs\. Google \(superconducting circuits\) and QuEra \(neutral atoms\) have produced related string\-breaking results on other hardware\. The Shatter view runs the same structure on a different substrate: \| \| String\-Breaking Simulator™ \| Electron Geometry Simulator™, Shatter view \| \|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\|\-\-\-\| \| Substrate \| Gauge string on a 13\-site trapped\-ion chain \| Hydrogen atom, electron bound to proton \| \| What rises \| Energy stored in the stretched string \| Energy absorbed from F\_ext \| \| What holds \| The string&\#x27;s rigidity \| The pair&\#x27;s binding \| \| Break point \| τ = TL \| τ = TL, at E\_bind = 13\.5982872643 eV \| \| Products \| Two particle–antiparticle pairs \| A free electron and a proton \| \| Product phase \| Noble, by Same\-B Necessity \(equal B on both charges, B\_out = 0\) \| Noble, zero binding torsion \| In both, Behavior rises against Pattern until τ = B/P reaches TL, and the single identity reorganizes into smaller stable identities\. Neither simulator contains any hardware in its dial: τ = B/P reads the same on trapped ions, superconducting circuits, neutral atoms and hydrogen\. This is the same threshold structure the corpus reads in the Tacoma Narrows Bridge, shattering glass and boiling water\. The two simulators are designed to be used together\. A lesson can start with the string, where the break is easy to picture, and move to hydrogen, where every number on the dial is computed from measured constants\. \#\#\# 6\.6 Applications \- \*\*Photoionization and the photoelectric relation\.\*\* The leftover energy K = F\_ext − E\_bind has the same structure as Einstein&\#x27;s photoelectric equation\. Students see that a single photon below the edge cannot free a ground\-state electron, however long the light shines, and that a photon above it frees the electron and leaves the difference as motion\. \- \*\*Ionizing and non\-ionizing radiation\.\*\* The edge marks where light becomes able to strip electrons from atoms\. The view gives a concrete reason why extreme ultraviolet light, X\-rays and gamma rays are handled differently from visible light and radio waves in health physics and radiation safety\. \- \*\*Astrophysics\.\*\* Light shorter than 91\.18 nm, the Lyman continuum, ionizes the hydrogen around hot young stars and lights up glowing regions such as the Orion Nebula\. The same edge governs the reionization of the early universe&\#x27;s hydrogen\. The view shows the threshold behind both\. \- \*\*Conservation of momentum\.\*\* The proton&\#x27;s recoil at 1/1836 of the electron&\#x27;s speed makes momentum balance visible: equal and opposite momentum, very unequal speeds\. \- \*\*Wave–particle connection\.\*\* The free electron&\#x27;s de Broglie wavelength, read in Bohr radii, ties view ④ back to the ladder in view ①\. \- \*\*Photoelectron spectroscopy\.\*\* Instruments that measure the kinetic energy of ejected electrons work backward through K = F\_ext − E\_bind to find binding energies\. The view shows the forward direction of that calculation\. \- \*\*Phase placement across substrates\.\*\* Together with the String\-Breaking Simulator™, the view gives researchers and teachers a worked pair of examples of TL as a substrate\-neutral phase boundary, each with its products placed by phase\. \- \*\*Other bound pairs\.\*\* The same dial applies to any two\-body bound state given its binding energy\. ## [Realtime\-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real\-time Interactive Problems?](../publications/e00bca7e77b76455b4ba.md)

Jingyu Tang; Xu Yang; Zhehao Zhang; Zheng Wang; Qi Cheng; Haozhe Zhao; Manling Li; Wenxuan Li; Xide Xia; Jiaxin Pei

Real\-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real\-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested\. We introduce Realtime\-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success\. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real\-time interaction remains challenging\. To separate serving latency from models&\#x27; real\-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which removes inference delays as an idealized reference, and introduce Token Clock, which advances simulated time according to generated token counts, testing temporal awareness independently of physical serving speed\. We find that temporal costs limit success in evolving environments and that higher reasoning effort has mixed effects under time pressure, reflecting a trade\-off between decision quality and timely execution\. These findings suggest directions for improving real\-time multimodal agents, including adaptive reasoning with temporal awareness and continuous perception and action\.

## [Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Influencing Mechanisms of Land\-Use Carbon Emissions in Counties of Northern Henan, China](../publications/e00e01268a45c26d953b.md)

Zhigang Li; Yingying Zhao; Yawen Hou; Hongyu Lu; Haidong Li; Yunxing Zhang

Climate warming driven by greenhouse gas emissions, especially carbon dioxide, severely threatens ecosystems and human societies\. Accelerated by urbanization, land\-use changes have significantly exacerbated climate change and disrupted carbon dynamics\. Counties are key administrative units in China and are crucial for economic growth and achieving carbon neutrality goals\. However, systematic research on carbon emission evolution and drivers at this scale remains scarce, hindering targeted low\-carbon pathways\. This study employs an improved IPCC method to quantify land\-use carbon emissions \(LUCE\) in 37 Northern Henan counties \(2000\-2020\)\. Using the standard deviational ellipse, Moran’s I, and an optimal parameter\-based geographical detector, we analyzed spatiotemporal patterns and drivers\. The results showed that \(1\) land transformation primarily involved converting cultivated land to construction land, with the latter increasing by 45\.6%\. The LUCE distribution exhibited stability, while global Moran’s I increased from 0\.082 to 0\.382, reflecting enhanced “high\-high” and “low\-low” spatial clustering\. \(2\) Socioeconomic factors were the dominant drivers before 2010, while natural factors gained prominence thereafter\. By 2020, natural constraints \(especially NDVI\) and their interactions with human activities \(e\.g\., NTL\) became key determinants, signaling intensified human‑nature coupling\. \(3\) Given heterogeneous resources, we propose tailored pathways, including land use optimization, industrial transformation, and regional collaboration\. This research establishes a fine\-scale methodological framework for identifying complex driving mechanisms, offering scientific evidence for precise spatial planning and differentiated carbon mitigation policies at the county level to promote synergy between regional development and ecological sustainability\.

## [The Mediating Role of Cognitive Flexibility on the Relationship between Emotional Appraisal and Pro\-Environmental Behavior Among Young Adults](../publications/e01e154f2707ecf5ff61.md)

Ifrah Syed; Syeda Rubab Aftab

The primary purpose of this study was to assess the role of emotional appraisal and cognitive flexibility in predicting pro\-environmental behavior in young adults\. This being one of the pressing calls worldwide, this research was aimed to understand the psychological constructs that may relate to sustainable acts\. Data were collected through questionnaires\. Sectioned into the correlational type, 381 university students were purposely selected as subjects\. The tools used for data gathering were the BEIS 10, the Cognitive Flexibility Inventory \(CFI\), and the Pro\-Environmental Behavior Scale \(PEBS\)\. After the collection of data, analyses were done using the SPSS statistical package, including Pearson correlation and multiple regression, to analyze, correlate and assess the predictive strength among the variables\. The results show significant positive correlations between both emotional regulation and cognitive flexibility with pro\-environmental behavior\. Regression analysis particularly revealed cognitive flexibility as a more robust predictor than emotional appraisal, placing emphasis on the weight of adaptive cognitive processing in steering environmentally responsible behavior\. The findings, therefore, suggest certain psychological bases for sustainable behavior whereby any intervention that seeks to promote cognitive flexibility and emotional regulation could improve environmental sustenance among youngsters\. The study included the use of self\-report measures, which may be subject to social desirability bias, and a sample limited to university students, which restricts generalizability\. Future research should explore longitudinal designs, include diverse demographic groups, and examine potential mediating variables such as environmental awareness and social norms\.

## [Logic\-Guided Graph Denoising Diffusion Models](../publications/e023cf9a62e404e3978c.md)

Samuel Cognolato; Luciano Serafini; Alessandro Sperduti; Andrea Cavallaro

Graph diffusion models are competitive approaches for generating complex graph\-structured data\. However, when such distributions have strict structural constraints, diffusion models may fail to capture them exactly, resulting in the generation of invalid graphs\. In this paper, we propose a method for grounding graph diffusion models in domain\-specific knowledge via First Order Logic \(FOL\), leveraging its expressive and interpretable formalism to impose structural constraints on the generative process\. We incorporate domain knowledge using classifier guidance, a technique that conditions the diffusion model&\#x27;s distribution on external variables to exert control over the sampled data\. During the generative process, classifier guidance steers the denoising trajectory to optimize an objective function, which we define as a fuzzy and differentiable relaxation of the logical rules\. Our methodology requires only the specification of constraints in FOL, whose satisfaction is encouraged at inference time to guide a pre\-trained generative model\. We evaluate our approach by comparing the unconditional generation of knowledge graphs with our logic\-guided framework, which incorporates domain ontologies as structural constraints during inference\. This approach significantly increases the proportion of generated graphs that satisfy the ontological constraints\.
