## [Sexualized Drug Use among Gay, Bisexual, and Other Men Who Have Sex with Men: A Scoping Review of Health Risks and Nursing Implications](../publications/e0331c0ca3ba8c21fcf4.md)

Dicky Endrian Kurniawan; Ahmad Rifai; Alfid Tri Afandi; M\. Nur Khamid

Introduction: Sexualized drug use \(SDU\), known as chemsex or slamsex, is a growing phenomenon among gay, bisexual, and men who have sex with men \(GBMSM\)\. SDU is associated with an increased risk of HIV transmission and other adverse health outcomes\. To further understand the trends, this study aimed to map the existing evidence on sexualized drug use among GBMSM and identify key research and practice gaps\. Methods: A scoping review was used in this study\. Inclusion criteria comprised peer\-reviewed articles published in English that focused on SDU among GBMSM and reported health\-related outcomes\. The search strategy utilized online AI–assisted mapping through Connected Papers\. 25 articles were included and analyzed using a descriptive analytical approach\. The identified study designs included observational, reviews, and intervention\. Results: There are several subtopics identified, including prevalence of users, type of drug, SDU practice/behaviors, biological effects, psychological effects, and prevention programs due to SDU\. SDU among GBMSM demonstrated consistently high prevalence rates, particularly involving stimulants, which are used to enhance sexual experiences\. These substances pose serious biological and psychological consequences, including an increased risk of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, as well as mental health disorders\. Conclusions: This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of SDU\-related evidence among GBMSM while highlighting gaps in nursing\- and public health–oriented interventions\. SDU remains a critical public health issue among GBMSM with substantial health impacts\. The findings underscore the need for culturally sensitive, nurse\-led prevention, harm reduction, mental health support, and digital interventions to address SDU\-related risks effectively\.

## [Progress in research on the use of induced pluripotent stem cells in tumor prevention, therapy, and tumor modeling](../publications/e037c674a3ec8082473c.md)

Shaoshuai Liang; Hongyang Zhao; Ning Zuo; Bingqiang Zhang; Mengmeng Chen; Xiaoyan Zhang; Haoyu Zhang; Muhammad Omer Iqbal; Qi Wang; Dingcai Dong

Induced pluripotent stem cell technology holds great promise for cancer research and immunotherapy\. iPSCs possess pluripotency and unlimited self\-renewal capacity, enabling their differentiation into various functional immune effector cells such as T cells, natural killer cells, and macrophages \(Macs\)\. Genetically engineered iPSC\-derived immune cells have been shown to efficiently and specifically eliminate cancer cells in preclinical studies, and their safety and preliminary efficacy are currently being evaluated in early clinical trials\. Although iPSC technology is a relatively recent development, it can be applied in a variety of ways to tackle biological challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance\. Recent evidence has demonstrated the potential of iPSC\-based tumor vaccines, which can leverage the shared transcriptomic characteristics and tumor\-associated antigens of iPSCs and cancer cells, to activate CD8 \+ T cells, induce immune memory formation, and inhibit tumor growth\. Moreover, iPSCs can be reprogrammed into cancer stem cell\-like cells \(CSC\-like cells\) by tumor microenvironmental cues or genetic mechanism, while cancer cells can be reprogrammed to cancer\-derived iPSCs\. These complementary approaches provide powerful platforms for modeling tumor initiation, investigating drug resistance mechanisms, and reversing malignant phenotypes\. In this review, we discuss new applications of iPSCs in cancer immunotherapy, tumor vaccine development, and CSC\-based disease modeling\. The review concludes by examining some of the challenges facing the clinical translation of iPSCs, including tumorigenicity risks, low reprogramming efficiency, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment\. We also recommend possible solutions to these challenges, which can help to further advance the application of iPSCs in precision oncology and personalized cancer treatment\.

## [Network pharmacology and machine learning reveal kit as a target of roburic acid in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: Preliminary in vitro validation](../publications/e041624178f4c5e992db.md)

Foxing Tan; Haolin Du; Lili Deng; Yaping Shen; Yan Yang; Kun Mei; Zilu Chen; Yan Huang

This study aims to systematically explore the potential molecular mechanism of Roburic Acid \(RBA\) in the treatment of Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma \(ATC\) through the approaches of network pharmacology, machine learning and in vitro experiments\. Public databases were used to retrieve the potential targets of RBA and disease\-related targets of ATC\. Intersection analysis was performed to identify the common targets, followed by the construction of a Protein\-Protein Interaction \(PPI\) network for these common targets\. Enrichment analyses, including GO functional and KEGG pathway analyses, were carried out for the targets\. Core targets were further prioritized using SVM, LASSO and random forest machine learning algorithms\. Validation of the binding affinity and stability of RBA with the core target was performed using molecular docking and dynamics simulations\. Finally, in vitro experiments\-including cell viability, scratch assay, apoptosis detection, and Western blot\-were conducted using the ATC cell line KHM\-5M to validate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of RBA\. A total of 401 RBA\-associated targets and 2151 ATC\-related targets were identified; their intersection yielded 173 shared targets\. GO enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were mainly involved in responses to peptide hormones and nuclear receptor activity, among other biological functions\. KEGG pathway analysis showed significant enrichment in cancer\-related pathways, including the PI3K\-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways\. Using SVM, LASSO regression, and random forest models, KIT was consistently identified as the single core target\. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated strong binding between RBA and c\-KIT, characterized by low binding energy and the formation of a stable protein\-ligand complex\. In vitro, RBA significantly reduced KHM\-5M cell viability and migration; the inhibitory effect on migration became pronounced at 24 h and was comparable to that of the positive control DOX\. Furthermore, RBA promoted apoptosis and dose\-dependently suppressed c\-KIT phosphorylation\. This study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular simulations to identify KIT as a high\-confidence core target of RBA in ATC\. Preliminary in vitro validation demonstrated that RBA suppresses ATC cell viability and migration, induces apoptosis, and inhibits c\-KIT phosphorylation in a dose\-dependent manner\.

## [Digital\-Based Teacher Human Resource Management for Educational Transformation Readiness](../publications/e04313c87cfc59f5a5c8.md)

Siti Aimah; Fachri Aldin

This study aims to analyze and develop a digital\-based teacher human resource \(HR\) management model to strengthen teachers’ readiness for educational transformation\. This study employed a qualitative case study design to examine the implementation of digital\-based HR management in a madrasah\. Data were collected through in\-depth interviews, participatory observations, and document review with the madrasah principal, curriculum representative, and teachers\. We ensured data credibility through source and method triangulation\. Data analysis involved condensing, displaying, and verifying data, supported by thematic analysis\. The findings indicate that teacher HR management has begun integrating digital technology into professional development, work processes, and educational management, but implementation remains only partially institutionalized\. Teachers’ readiness for transformation depends on digital literacy, ongoing professional development, leadership support, and the availability of institutional systems\. The findings further reveal that a shared digital organizational culture has not yet fully formed, so technology use and innovation remain partly dependent on individual initiatives\. The study suggests that sustainable educational transformation requires an integrated, digital\-based HR management model supported by continuous professional development, structured digital systems, visionary leadership, and a collaborative, adaptive organizational culture\. Such integration can strengthen teachers’ capacity and institutional readiness to respond effectively to ongoing digital transformation\.

## [Bruk av generativ KI i markedsføring: Hva skjer i norske bedrifter?](../publications/e04ab2da4242bf834926.md)

Natalie Le; Nina M\. Iversen; Magne Supphellen; Carmel T\. Foley; Leif E\. Hem

Denne artikkelen diskuterer bruken av GenKI innen fagfeltet markedsføring\. Litteraturen indikerer at markedsføringsoppgavene som i dag løses i norske bedrifter av mennesker, i stor grad kan erstattes av GenKI\. En McKinsey rapport fra 2026 hevder at 2/3 av alle markedsførings\-oppgaver kan utføres av GenAI\. Hvis disse spådommen slår til, får det store konsekvenser for antall ansatte og nyansettelser med markedsføringskompetanse\. Det får også konsekvenser for utdanningsinstitusjoner og fagfeltet markedsføring\. Artikkelen presenterer resultatene fra en spørreundersøkelse for å avdekke bruken av GenKI i norsk næringsliv\. Undersøkelsen ble gjennomført blant ansatte som jobber med salg og markedsføring\. Respondentene \(N=200\) svarte på spørsmål om omfanget av deres bruk av GenKI for å løse arbeidsoppgaver innen markedsføring\. Resultatene indikerer en svært lav bruk av GenKI for å løse markedsføringsoppgaver i egen jobb\. Av de totalt 20 arbeidsoppgavene innen områdene markedsinnsikt, markedsplaner, produkt\- og tjenesteutvikling og markedskommunikasjon fant man et totalt gjennomsnitt på 2,07 på en fempunkts skala\. Den «høyeste» verdien var 2,31\. Det betyr svært lav adopsjonen av GenKI for å løse bedriftenes markedsføringsoppgaver\. Budskapet er at norsk næringsliv trenger kompetanse om markedsføring mer enn noen gang\. Skal bruken av GenKI økes er det behov for intern markedsføring for å øke bruk og formidle nytteverdi\. Nytten av GenKI for å forbedre produktene og derigjennom øke opplevelsen av innovasjon indikerer også at GenKI er et supplement – snarere enn en løsning som gjør mennesker overflødige\. Resultatene viser også at økt bruk av GenKI forbedrer bedriftenes resultater \(lønnsomhet og vekst\)\. GenKI er derfor kommet for å bli\. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Use of Generative AI in Marketing: What Is Happening in Norwegian Companies? This article discusses the use of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) within the field of marketing\. The literature suggests that many marketing tasks currently performed by humans in Norwegian companies can potentially be replaced by generative AI\. A McKinsey report from 2026 claims that two\-thirds of all marketing tasks can be carried out by generative AI\. If these predictions prove accurate, the implications for the demand for marketing professionals and future hiring practices will be substantial\. It will also have significant consequences for educational institutions and the marketing discipline itself\. The article presents the results of a survey designed to examine the use of generative AI in Norwegian businesses\. The survey was conducted among employees working in sales and marketing\. Respondents \(N = 339\) answered questions regarding the extent to which they use generative AI to perform marketing\-related tasks in their jobs\. The results indicate a relatively low level of generative AI usage for marketing tasks\. Across 20 work activities within the areas of market insight, marketing planning, product development, and marketing communications, the overall mean score was 2\.25 on a five\-point scale\. The highest score recorded was 2\.45\. These findings suggest a relatively low adoption rate of generative AI for carrying out marketing tasks in Norwegian companies\. The main conclusion is that Norwegian businesses need marketing expertise more than ever\. Increasing the use of generative AI will require substantial investments in competence development, and educational institutions can play a crucial role in this process\. The adoption of generative AI has the potential to improve products, enhance perceptions of innovation, and strengthen customer relationships\. This indicates that generative AI serves as a complement to human expertise rather than a substitute that makes people redundant\. Furthermore, the results show that greater use of generative AI is associated with improved business performance, including profitability and growth\. Generative AI is therefore here to stay\.

## [Management of Patients with Inoperable Malignant Bowel Obstruction: A Preliminary Report](../publications/e04dfc2b3f19a7b8a442.md)

Meenakshi V\. Venketeswaran; Daniel Raj Joseph Thangasamy; Thendral Ramasamy; Thirumoorthi Natarajan; Pradeep Jeyakumar; Ramakrishnan Ayloor Seshadri

Malignant bowel obstruction \(MBO\) is a distressing complication of advanced cancer with poor survival and substantial symptom burden and often requiring intensive supportive management\. Data on its management in lower\-middle\-income countries \(LMICs\) are limited\. We retrospectively reviewed records of 25 adults with inoperable MBO managed by a palliative care \(PC\) unit at a tertiary cancer centre in India between November 2021 and October 2023\. Demographic, clinical, radiological and treatment data were collected; symptoms at admission and discharge, survival and place of death were recorded\. Eighteen patients \(72%\) were female\. Ovarian and gastric cancers were the most common primary malignancies \(6 each; 24%\), followed by rectal cancer \(5; 20%\)\. Abdominal pain \(17; 70\.8%\) and vomiting \(15; 62\.5%\) were the most common symptoms\. Nasogastric tubes were inserted in 13 patients \(52%\), of whom 8 \(61%\) had them removed before discharge\. Dexamethasone \(22; 88%\) and metoclopramide \(21; 84%\) were the most frequently used medications\. Symptom control at discharge was achieved in 20/23 patients \(87%\), and 19 \(79%\) tolerated oral liquids\. Nearly 80% died within 60 days of diagnosis\. Multidisciplinary medical management with PC involvement was associated with symptom control in most patients with inoperable MBO in this resource\-constrained setting\.

## [When SHAP explains a leaked target: a cautionary study of an XGBoost and multi\-level SHAP pipeline for S&amp;P 500 direction prediction](../publications/e059ed327075af9e4913.md)

Liansheng Yuan; Yansong Leng; Yuqi Zhang

Accurate prediction of stock price movements is of substantial importance to investors, portfolio managers, and financial regulators, and although machine learning models are increasingly deployed in quantitative finance, the limited transparency of many such models remains a non\-trivial barrier to broader adoption in high\-stakes decision\-making environments, particularly where auditability and accountability are required\. This study presents an end\-to\-end interpretable prediction pipeline that integrates multi\-category technical indicator engineering, XGBoost gradient boosting classification, and comprehensive SHAP \(SHapley Additive exPlanations\) analysis for daily direction forecasting of the S&amp;P 500 index, together with a rigorous diagnostic evaluation of that pipeline\. A systematic feature engineering stage constructs 32 technical features organized into six categories—returns, trend indicators \(moving average ratios, MACD, RSI, Bollinger Bands\), multi\-scale volatility, volume dynamics, momentum oscillators \(ROC, ATR, Stochastic Oscillator, Williams %R, CCI\), and lagged returns—which are fed into an XGBoost classifier trained on a sequential 80/20 train–test split to prevent look\-ahead bias\. On the hold\-out set the classifier attains 63\.84% accuracy and a macro\-averaged F1\-score of 0\.6110\. Contextualizing this figure, however, overturns its interpretation\. The majority\-class \(“always\-Down”\) rule already attains 59\.32% on the same split, and a data\-provenance audit reveals that the widely used public source file contains every calendar day, with 31\.1% of rows being exact forward\-filled copies of the previous trading session\. Because the target is defined by the strict inequality \\\(P^\{\\textrm\{c\}\}\_\{t\+1\}&gt;P^\{\\textrm\{c\}\}\_\{t\}\\\) , every session whose successor is a forward\-filled copy—each Friday and each Saturday—is labelled “Down” by construction, rendering 31\.0% of all labels independent of market behaviour\. Consequently a one\-bit rule that never observes a price \(“predict Up iff the previous return is exactly zero”\) reaches 63\.84%, and a calendar\-only rule reaches 71\.19%, both matching or exceeding the classifier\. Decomposing the model’s accuracy shows it scores 95\.37% on rows whose label the calendar had already fixed but only 49\.19% on the 246 rows carrying a genuine next\-day move—below that subset’s own 58\.54% majority rule\. Once the forward\-filled rows are removed, discriminative power collapses to chance \(AUC 0\.527 on a single split; 0\.476 pooled across six walk\-forward folds with per\-fold hyper\-parameter re\-optimization\), the model falls below the majority baseline, and a cost\-aware backtest yields a Sharpe ratio of \\\(\-0\.24\\\) at 10 bps against \\\(\+0\.59\\\) for buy\-and\-hold\. SHAP attributions are further shown to be unidentified within a volatility cluster whose pairwise correlations reach \\\(r=0\.947\\\) : the members’ individual credits sum to 2\.64 times the cluster’s joint contribution, and retraining on one representative per correlated group—discarding fourteen of the thirty\-two features—does not degrade performance\. The multi\-level SHAP machinery faithfully explains this leakage rather than any market mechanism—most visibly, 108 of 354 test observations pile up at exactly zero lagged return and receive systematically positive attributions\. The contribution of this work is therefore methodological rather than predictive: it provides a reproducible, auditable SHAP\-on\-XGBoost pipeline, and uses it to demonstrate how a routinely used public dataset combined with a strict\-inequality target manufactures label leakage that post\-hoc explanation methods will rationalize with apparent precision\. We distil the analysis into a validation checklist for interpretable machine learning on financial tabular data\.

## [Crossing the Digital Divide: Understanding Older Adults’ Technology Acceptance of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Study](../publications/e05f208bbffd238cedef.md)

Mingxuan Li

The diffusion of generative artificial intelligence is redefining the relationship between older adults and digital technologies\. Existing studies have largely explained the digital divide among older adults through traditional digital media such as smartphones and mobile payment, while insufficient attention has been paid to how conversational artificial intelligence changes older adults&\#x27; entry thresholds, sustained\-use motivations, and risk\-judgment mechanisms\. This study adopts a multimethod qualitative design, with semistructured interviews as the primary method and digital scenario\-based tasks as a complementary method\. From January to February 2026, the study was conducted in Chedun Town and Xinqiao Town, Songjiang District, Shanghai, with 40 participants aged 60 and above who had internet\-use experience and showed a pronounced tendency toward high\-frequency smartphone use\. The data were analyzed through thematic analysis\. Interview transcripts, task\-observation records, screenshots of AI conversations, and field notes were triangulated; an initial coding manual, double review, and consensus discussion were used to enhance analytic credibility\. The study finds that generative artificial intelligence shifts the technological threshold from procedural operation to need articulation and result evaluation, enabling some older adults to compensate for limitations in traditional interface operation through life experience and language\-expression skills\. Older adults&\#x27; sustained use is not driven simply by efficiency, but is closely related to emotional anchoring in later life, experience organization, relationship maintenance, and concrete task handling\. Community support, peer learning, and intergenerational assistance constitute important mediating mechanisms through which older adults move from initial experimentation to stable use\. Whether older adults truly cross the digital divide depends on whether they can develop the capacities of source verification, contextual delimitation, and boundary judgment\. Based on these findings, the study proposes a &quot;conditional crossing&quot; mechanism for older adults&\#x27; acceptance of AI technologies and argues that age\-friendly governance should move beyond interface simplification toward capability enhancement and risk support\.

## [Ensembled Deep Learning\-Based Optimisation of Multi\-Robot Communication Networks in Agricultural Environments](../publications/e06a7640f4446a9d183d.md)

Jawahir Mohammad Hashir; Murtala Aminu Baba; Muhammad Tela; Ahmed Umar; Jamila Adamu

In this paper, a novel ensemble deep learning framework is presented for communication management in agricultural multi\-robot systems\. The framework uses Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\), Long Short\-Term Memory networks \(LSTM\), and Graph Neural Networks \(GNN\) to classify link quality, predict the future evolution of link quality, and inform routing decisions in wireless networks used in agricultural scenarios\. The models were trained on the Vineyard\-2021 LoRa RSSI dataset, comprising real wireless measurements gathered during deployment in vineyards in Northern Italy, preprocessed and annotated across seven sensor nodes and 1,877 hourly timesteps\. To prevent target leakage, the prediction task was framed as a future\-prediction task: models predict the link\-quality class at time t\+1 using only measurements available up to time t\. The CNN reached a test accuracy of 83\.69%, the LSTM 81\.14%, and the GNN 85\.82%\. An unweighted ensemble of the three models reached a test accuracy of 89\.32%\. All classification errors occurred between adjacent classes, and no Weak\-to\-Strong or Strong\-to\-Weak errors were observed\. This ensemble was then used to drive routing decisions in a multi\-robot simulation built on the NetworkX platform, with fleet sizes ranging from 5 to 30 robots\. Adaptive routing driven by the ensemble reached a Packet Delivery Ratio of 99\.68%, compared with 95\.33% for a distance\-only baseline, while slightly increasing latency \(18\.03 ms vs\. 12\.80 ms\) and energy consumption \(1\.81 vs\. 1\.36 units\)\. The paper presents a documented baseline for deep\-learning\-based link\-quality classification on agricultural LoRa data, a novel ensemble design combining spatial, temporal, and topological features, and an evaluation methodology for communication management in simulated multi\-robot networks\. Limitations include the static deployment of the sensors used for training, the geographic and seasonal specificity of the dataset, and the use of literature\-derived packet\-success probabilities in the simulation\. Future work will gather data from moving robots in Nigerian agricultural environments and validate the framework using ROS/Gazebo\.

## [DRUGS REPURPOSING: THE HOPE FOR NEW THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS](../publications/e06b72c53ae2aa50ef49.md)



Background: Pharmacists are essential to designing, synthesizing, and formulating appropriate drug dosage forms to address healthcare needs for specific diseases or health conditions\.Drugs are initially developed to treat their intended diseases, known as their initial or primary use\.When these drugs are later used to treat different diseases, this process is called drug repurposing\.Repurposed drugs can include marketed medications that failed in their initial purpose or those that failed to show sufficient efficacy in later clinical trial stages\.Aim: This review article aims to highlight the concept of drug repurposing and emphasize its important applications in modern drug development\.Methods: This review evaluates research on drug repurposing, concentrating on medications that failed for their intended uses or failed to provide the required results in advanced clinical studies\.Results: Improved drug availability and shorter development and approval times are just two benefits of drug repurposing\.It also provides an opportunity to meet unmet medical needs, notably during public health emergencies\.Examining medications like erythromycin and hydroxychloroquine for COVID\-19 shows the usefulness of this strategy\.Conclusion: Scientists are very interested in drug repurposing because it can provide safe, efficient, and affordable treatment solutions more quickly\.This tactic is still a viable and useful approach in modern pharmaceutical research, despite difficulties in expanding the availability of repurposed medications\.

## [Nutrition and Care During Pregnancy: An Ayurvedic Perspective of Garbhiṇī Paricaryā](../publications/e06f726cef634ff5836c.md)

Krishna Bagri; Pooja Dadhich; Anisha Desai; Dimpi Nirban; Reena jajoria

Background: Pregnancy is a period in which a woman needs good nutrition, adequate rest and careful support\. Ayurveda describes a comprehensive antenatal regimen called Garbhiṇī Paricaryā, which covers diet, lifestyle, mental well\-being and a month\-wise plan \(Māsānumāsika Paricaryā\)\. Aim: This narrative review aims to describe Garbhiṇī Paricaryā and to compare it with modern concepts of antenatal care\. Methods: The review draws on classical Ayurvedic texts, namely Caraka Saṃhitā, Suśruta Saṃhitā, Aṣṭāṅga Saṅgraha, Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya, Kāśyapa Saṃhitā and Hārīta Saṃhitā, together with published review articles, World Health Organization \(WHO\) guidelines and reports on pregnancy care in India\. It is a narrative review; no systematic review method was used\. Results: The classical texts describe diet and lifestyle suited to each month of pregnancy\. Milk, butter, ghee, cereals and other foods are recommended, and some dietary restrictions are listed\. Āsthāpana and Anuvāsana Basti are described in the eighth month, and Anuvāsana Basti and Picu in the ninth month \[4,5\]\. Diet, drugs, timing and procedures differ considerably between the texts\. Several factors harmful to the fetus \(Garbhopaghātakara Bhāva\) are also listed\. Modern antenatal care shares some ideas with the texts, such as adequate nutrition, rest, avoidance of harmful exposures and attention to mental health, but it also includes vaccination, scans, supplements, tests and screening, which the texts do not clearly describe\. Conclusion: Further research is needed on the main diet and lifestyle recommendations of the classical texts, especially on the safety and efficacy of herbal medicines and procedures such as Basti and Picu\. Garbhiṇī Paricaryā may be used alongside, but never in place of, modern antenatal care\. Keywords: Garbhiṇī Paricaryā, Māsānumāsika Paricaryā, Garbhopaghātakara Bhāva, antenatal care, maternal nutrition

## [The role of artificial intelligence in change management: opportunities and challenges](../publications/e079a4feb7cbd19872d4.md)

David; id\_orcid 0000\-0002\-6878\-8135 Edgar; Roberto Biloslavo; Matteo Rizzo

Purpose This paper examines the accelerating integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) into organizational change management \(OCM\)\. It explores AI’s dual role as both a powerful facilitator of change and a continuous disruptor itself, focusing specifically on the ethical and cultural challenges it introduces to traditional operational and decision\-making frameworks\. Design/methodology/approach Employing a narrative literature review approach, this study synthesizes 47 peer\-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, relevant practitioner papers, and book chapters published since 2010\. The review systematically analyzes the literature on the integration, impact, and long\-term consequences of applying AI in OCM contexts\. Findings The review underscores AI’s transformative capacity to reshape OCM from a traditional, linear process into a dynamic, continuous “meta\-change” formalized here as an integrative process linking AI’s technological properties to three generative mechanisms, two governing elements, and OCM outcomes expressed as four theoretical propositions\. While AI enhances change efficiency, it also introduces significant cultural and ethical hurdles, including algorithmic bias, identity threat among management, and the unintended reshaping of workplace culture and norms\. The findings indicate that successfully navigating this change landscape requires a strategic shift toward staged implementation, organizational agility, cultural alignment, effective ethical policies and, most importantly, human\-AI symbiosis, underpinned by Explainable AI \(XAI\) to foster workforce trust\. Originality/Value This paper bridges the critical gap between theoretical discourse on AI\-driven OCM and practical, ethical implications and implementation\. While AI’s potential to optimize change is widely recognized, existing research remains fragmented regarding the ethical governance and cultural frictions associated with its adoption\. By identifying emergent themes from the narrative literature review, this study offers a theoretically grounded agenda for “meta\-change,” reconciling technological agility with human\-centric governance in AI\-enabled organizational change\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL\-PHENOMENAL CONSCIOUSNESS RESONANCE SYSTEM \(TPCRS\) An Objective, Mathematically Closed Framework for Mapping and Quantifying Subjective Experience via Causal Neural Geometry](../publications/e0856f74c6c4f5ab88fe.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Topological\-Phenomenal Consciousness Resonance System \(TPCRS\) addresses the &quot;Hard Problem of Consciousness&quot; by providing the first mathematically closed framework for objectively quantifying subjective experience\. Current neuroscience relies on unreliable behavioral assessments or statistical correlations that cannot distinguish conscious awareness from unconscious processing\. TPCRS bridges this gap through a novel neuro\-computational architecture integrating high\-density quantum\-neuroimaging \(OPM\-MEG for femtotesla magnetic mapping and fNIRS for hemodynamic tracking\) with the El\-Rakhawi Riemannian Causal Continuum \(RCCA\)\. The system calculates the strictly dimensionless Topological\-Phenomenal Consciousness Metric \(Φ\_TCM\), bounded between 0 and 1, using a stable multiplicative formulation: Φ\_TCM = I\_integrated\_norm · \[\(1 \+ β·C\_causal\_norm\)/\(1 \+ β\)\] · \(1 \- S\_neural\_entropy\_norm\)\. This metric quantifies integrated information, causal feedback strength, and inverted dynamical neural noise, avoiding singularities while capturing the geometric complexity of conscious states\. A topologically bounded classification algorithm probabilistically maps specific manifold attractors to phenomenological correlates \(e\.g\., pain, visual perception\) with defined confidence intervals\. Clinical applications include detecting covert consciousness in non\-communicative patients \(coma, locked\-in syndrome\), optimizing anesthesia depth beyond traditional EEG indices, and ensuring ethical Brain\-Computer Interface operation by verifying conscious intent\. TPCRS transforms consciousness research from subjective inference to objective, geometrically grounded measurement, offering a scientifically rigorous tool for neurology, neuroethics, and fundamental neuroscience\.

## [ARBOR: Locating Reasoning Failures in Long Chains of Thought through Reasoning State Tracking](../publications/e08629efe8c308d67fd2.md)

Huihan Li; Siyuan Wang; Naga Vamsi Ramana Dinavahi; Xiaohui Liu; Xiang Ren

Large reasoning models solve complex problems through long chains of thought, in which prior work has documented failure modes such as overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions\. Existing methods detect these failures from local signals: textual similarity to nearby steps, switch tokens, or an LLM&\#x27;s judgment of a step&\#x27;s correctness\. However, what a step contributes to the solution depends on the state that earlier steps have established, so identifying failures requires a global view that tracks that state across the trajectory\. Therefore, we propose ARBOR, a reasoning\-failure attribution framework that represents each trajectory as a tree of reasoning states, built as each step creates, verifies, prunes, or revisits a state, and attributes each failure to a relation between a step and the state preceding it\. Using ARBOR, we refine the three failure modes into distinct subtypes that harm reasoning through different mechanisms and at different costs\. We find that the tree state ARBOR maintains before a step separates failure steps from the at\-risk steps at which the failure did not occur\. We discuss how ARBOR integrates with existing mitigations at inference time and in training data\. Code, data and interactive examples are available at https://inklab\.usc\.edu/ARBOR\.

## [Mass cytometry of early immune remodeling after mRNA booster vaccination reveals exploratory CD4 naive T\-cell associations with documented breakthrough infection](../publications/e08f3209dc2595a5f1ad.md)

Xuanjing Yu; Xinyu Jiang; Yupeng Xue; Yuqi Ji; Chunmei Li; Zijie Scott Zhang; Rui Cheng

Background Messenger RNA \(mRNA\) vaccines rapidly engage innate and adaptive immunity, but the systemic immune changes occurring within 24 h of vaccination remain incompletely understood\. We investigated whether early cellular and global H3K27ac/m6A changes were associated with subsequent documented breakthrough infection \(BTI\)\. Methods We performed an exploratory longitudinal systems\-immunology analysis of an outcome\-balanced subset of 124 participants from a randomized trial of COVID\-19 mRNA booster vaccination \(62 BTI and 62 non\-BTI\)\. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells collected at Day 0 and Day 1 were profiled by high\-dimensional mass cytometry\. Seventeen major immune\-cell populations were assessed for changes in relative abundance, marker profiles, and global H3K27ac/m6A signals\. Neutralizing\-antibody responses were measured through Day 180\. Results Within 24 h, booster vaccination induced rapid lineage\-specific remodeling of circulating immune composition\. Classical and intermediate monocytes showed positive shifts in CLR\-transformed relative abundance, whereas pDCs, NK cells, and selected CD8 and unconventional T\-cell populations showed negative shifts\. CD4 T\-cell populations remained comparatively stable on this relative\-composition scale\. Early H3K27ac and m6A changes correlated with abundance changes in selected innate and T\-cell populations\. Associations with later humoral immunity were limited: after exclusion of antibody measurements obtained on or after documented BTI, no association between early H3K27ac/m6A changes and Day 14 or Day 180 neutralizing\-antibody responses remained significant after multiple\-testing correction\. Major\-cell abundance trajectories did not differ significantly by subsequent BTI status\. In contrast, BTI was associated with smaller Day 0\-to\-Day 1 changes in CD4\_Tn IFN–Th1 chemokine, cytotoxic–Th1\-associated, and CCL2–CCR2\-associated marker scores and in the m6A readout\. Conclusions mRNA booster vaccination induces rapid, cell\-type\-specific immune remodeling within 24 h\. Major\-cell abundance changes were broadly shared across BTI groups, whereas early CD4\_Tn marker\-associated and m6A signal changes were associated with subsequent documented BTI\. These findings support further evaluation of dynamic early immune states as correlates of heterogeneity in vaccine responses\.

## [A Proof\-of\-Concept Study of Meat Broth Classification Using UV–Vis Spectroscopy and Explainable Decision Tree Analysis](../publications/e0987872fa4891e11940.md)

Stanly Gabriel; Anak Agung Ngurah Gunawan; I Ketut Sukarasa; I Wayan Supardi; Ni Putu Yuni Nurmalasari; Ida Bagus Alit Paramarta; I Ketut Putra

Background: Rapid discrimination of animal\-derived food products is relevant to food authenticity, consumer protection, and dietary compliance\. UV–Vis spectroscopy provides a simple analytical approach for obtaining optical fingerprints of food matrices; however, spectral interpretation may benefit from transparent machine\-learning methods\. Objective: This proof\-of\-concept study investigated the feasibility of combining UV–Vis spectrophotometry with an interpretable Decision Tree classifier to discriminate chicken, pork, and beef broths and to identify wavelength variables contributing to classification\. Methods: Broths prepared from chicken, pork, and beef were analyzed by UV–Vis spectrophotometry in the 244\.5–249\.0 nm spectral region, yielding 10 wavelength\-specific absorbance variables\. Two predesignated datasets were used: 15 training observations \(five per class\) and 15 test observations \(five per class\)\. Model development used only the training dataset\. Because 10\-fold stratification is not feasible with only five observations per class, shuffled 10\-fold KFold cross\-validation \(random\_state = 42\) was applied to the training data\. A Decision Tree classifier using Gini impurity was evaluated by accuracy, macro\-precision, macro\-recall, macro\-F1, out\-of\-fold \(OOF\) confusion matrix, and multiclass one\-vs\-rest ROC\-AUC\. The final tree was then fitted to all training observations and evaluated once on the untouched test dataset\. Feature importance and SHAP values were used for model interpretation\. No feature scaling was applied to Decision Tree modeling\. Results: All 10 validation folds were classified correctly, producing mean cross\-validation accuracy, macro\-precision, macro\-recall, and macro\-F1 of 1\.000 ± 0\.000\. Pooled OOF predictions also yielded accuracy, macro\-precision, macro\-recall, macro\-F1, and multiclass OvR ROC\-AUC of 1\.000\. The final Decision Tree had a depth of two and three terminal leaves\. On the separately designated 15\-observation test dataset, all observations were correctly classified \(confusion matrix diagonal: 5, 5, and 5\), with accuracy, macro\-precision, macro\-recall, macro\-F1, and macro OvR ROC\-AUC all equal to 1\.000\. Feature importance was concentrated at 245\.5 and 248\.5 nm \(0\.50 each\), and SHAP analysis likewise identified these wavelengths as the dominant model contributors\. These perfect metrics must be interpreted cautiously because the observations are technical replicates from a very limited number of broth preparations\. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating UV–Vis spectroscopy with an interpretable Decision Tree for preliminary discrimination of chicken, pork, and beef broth spectra\. Under the present proof\-of\-concept dataset, the model achieved perfect 10\-fold OOF and separately designated test\-set classification, with 245\.5 and 248\.5 nm driving the fitted decision rules\. However, the technical\-replicate structure and very small number of independent broth preparations preclude claims of biological generalization\. Validation using larger numbers of independently prepared samples, multiple biological sources and batches, and genuinely external test sets is required before practical food\-authentication use can be established\.

## [Hemispheric Asymmetry of Neuroimaging Biomarkers in Early Onset Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease: Clinical and Cognitive Outcomes](../publications/e098a0444b05a8254114.md)

Jacob Ziontz; Ganna Blazhenets; Adrienne V\. Visani; Konstantinos Chiotis; Piyush Maiti; Zoe Lin; Aidyn Rose Hills; Claire Yballa; Salma Rocha; Ranjani P\. Shankar; Virginia E\. Sturm; Prashanthi Vemuri; Dustin B\. Hammers; Ani Eloyan; María C\. Carrillo; Bradford Clark Dickerson; Liana G\. Apostolova; Gil Dan Rabinovici; Renaud La Joie

OBJECTIVE: Individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) often exhibit amyloid, tau, and atrophy predominantly in the left or right hemisphere, but group\-level analyses typically ignore inter\-individual variability and changing asymmetry patterns when averaging data across participants in phenotypically diverse cohorts\. METHODS: We examined left/right hemispheric asymmetry in amyloid positron emission tomography \(PET\), tau PET, and cortical atrophy in sporadic early\-onset AD from 585 deeply phenotyped individuals across 2 cohorts to investigate its clinical correlates\. For each imaging biomarker, we computed a global asymmetry index reflecting left/right hemisphere signal difference, and an analogous asymmetry value for PET/magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) voxels\. We examined clinical and cognitive correlates of this asymmetry across phenotypes cross\-sectionally and longitudinally in a subset of 218 participants\. RESULTS: Both left and right asymmetry were common for all clinical phenotypes and was correlated between imaging biomarkers\. Asymmetry patterns varied spatially within phenotypes, and asymmetry in tau PET and MRI volumes was related to hemisphere\-dependent cognitive deficits and neuropsychiatric symptoms\. Longitudinal analyses revealed stable amyloid PET asymmetry, decreasing tau PET asymmetry, and increasing MRI volume asymmetry\. INTERPRETATION: Hemispheric asymmetry is common in early onset AD and correlates with clinical outcomes\. Our longitudinal findings suggest a time\-lagged asymmetry peak in amyloid, then tau, then atrophy\. Taken together, our results position asymmetry as an important feature of AD heterogeneity, as it provides insight into disease mechanisms and trajectories\. ANN NEUROL 2026\.

## [Strategic intelligence for emerging and critical technologies](../publications/e0a0927b51a02d757cb8.md)

Katherine Richardson; Renda Andrea; Pierre‐Alexandre Balland; Rainer Walz; Paweł Świeboda; Giuliana Battisti; Albert Bravo\-Biosca; Diego Comin; Béatrice Dumont; Andrea Filippetti; Emilija Stojmenova\-Duh

Emerging technologies are reshaping global competitiveness at speed, and the gap between early movers and late followers is widening\. For Europe, the cost of inaction \- or of poorly targeted action \- is lost industrial leadership, deepening strategic dependencies, and eroded sovereignty and security\. Yet Europe lacks two things it now urgently needs: the strategic intelligence to know which technologies to back and where it is genuinely well positioned, and the institutional infrastructure to deliver that intelligence systematically and translate it into bold, targeted funding and investment decisions\. This paper makes the case for both\. It argues that the institutionalisation of a strategic intelligence function is necessary in Europe’s current situation\. A dedicated observatory for emerging and critical technologies is one credible \- ambitious but achievable \- form that function can take\.

## [The Relationship Between Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Adolescents at SMAN 1, Kota Ternate](../publications/e0a37843088ea623cb64.md)

Nadya K\. Wijaya; Sri Yati; Tuthanurani Nachrawy

Social media has become an integral part of adolescents&\#x27; daily lives, with increasing engagement through digital devices, particularly during nighttime hours, potentially affecting sleep quality\. This study aimed to examine the association between social media use and sleep quality among adolescents at Sekolah Menengah Atas Negeri \(SMAN\) 1 Kota Ternate, Indonesia\. A quantitative analytical observational study with a cross\-sectional design was conducted involving 289 students selected through proportional cluster sampling\. Data were collected using the Social Media Use Scale and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index \(PSQI\)\. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed using SPSS statistical software, with the chi\-square test employed to assess the association between social media use and sleep quality\. Of the 289 respondents, 229 \(79\.2%\) demonstrated moderate social media use, 49 \(17\.0%\) demonstrated high social media use, and 11 \(3\.8%\) demonstrated low social media use\. Regarding sleep quality, 204 respondents \(70\.6%\) were classified as having poor sleep quality, while 85 \(29\.4%\) were classified as having good sleep quality\. The chi\-square test revealed a statistically significant association between social media use and sleep quality \(p = 0\.022\)\. These findings indicated that social media use was significantly associated with sleep quality among adolescents at SMAN 1 Kota Ternate\. However, the cross\-sectional design did not establish a causal relationship between these variables\. The results highlighted the importance of promoting responsible social media use, particularly before bedtime, and encouraging healthy sleep practices among adolescents\.

## [O papel da inteligência artificial na pipeline completo de efeitos visuais no cinema contemporâneo](../publications/e0a69bbac46ccba32923.md)

Romualdo Amaral

This article examines the role of artificial intelligence \(AI\) across the complete visual effects \(VFX\) production pipeline in contemporary cinema, emphasizing the practical integration of machine learning \(ML\) techniques into pre\-production, production, and post\-production\. It argues that AI has become a set of supporting tools integrated into established VFX workflows, including camera and object tracking, rotoscoping \(roto\), digital paint and object removal, simulation, rendering, compositing, and final delivery, reducing operational challenges and expanding opportunities for creative experimentation\. The analysis draws on technical sources \(SIGGRAPH/ACM\), official tool documentation, and institutional guidelines addressing professional credits, intellectual property, consent, and digital replicas\. When quantitative data on time and cost savings are not publicly available in sufficient detail, this limitation is explicitly acknowledged, with emphasis placed on qualitative evidence and documented technical mechanisms\.

## [When Does Automated Review Constitute Genuine Reconsideration?](../publications/e0a7b1c2ec0cfffd1e6a.md)

Nicholas Cott

An institution can automate both an initial decision and its review without making the original determination genuinely vulnerable to challenge\. This paper examines what distinguishes genuine institutional reconsideration from a second computational procedure that merely reproduces or rationalizes an existing decision\. It develops the Criterion of Non\-Redundant Defeatability, arguing that, within a constituted institutional relation of commitment and challenge, an automated reviewing architecture possesses the capacity for genuine reconsideration if and only if it satisfies three conditions: Evidential Independence \(E\): The capacity to examine independently assessable grounds rather than merely inherit the original decision’s justification\. Adversarial Defeatability \(D\): Both structural permission and effective competence to recognize, assess, and pursue material reasons capable of defeating the institution’s maintained position\. Normative Effectiveness \(N\): An authorized route through which the resulting assessment can govern the institution’s operative position\. Drawing on defeasible reasoning, discursive commitment, epistemic reliance, and scholarship on responsibility gaps, the paper distinguishes the institution as the bearer of commitments from the automated reviewer as an epistemic delegate\. It uses contrast cases and a credit\-review example to examine the necessity and sufficiency of the proposed conditions, addresses the problem of evaluating defeater competence without circularity, and identifies evidential requirements for auditing reviewing architectures\. A central contribution is the distinction between possessing the capacity for reconsideration, adequately exercising that capacity, and discharging the resulting institutional obligations\. The account explains why technical independence, explanatory fluency, human approval, procedural completion, and even correct outcomes are not, individually, sufficient to establish genuine reconsideration\. The resulting framework provides a conceptual basis for evaluating automated administrative review, algorithmic contestability, and institutional answerability in legal and public\-sector decision\-making\.

## [Prefrontal and sensorimotor cortices showed opposite patterns of hemodynamic activity changes between eyes\-open and eyes\-closed conditions in blepharospasm](../publications/e0ac0e30851497d6a06b.md)

Xiao\-Feng Huang; Zhen Zhang; Lina Tan; Xinqing Hao; Zhan\-hua Liang; Chen\-Hui Pei

Background Blepharospasm \(BSP\), characterized by involuntary eyelid closure and difficulty opening the eyes, often results in functional blindness\. However, there is a lack of objective and quantitative diagnostic markers, and the differences in hemodynamics between eyes\-open \(EO\) and eyes\-closed \(EC\) conditions are unknown in BSP\. Objective To address this issue, we utilized functional near\-infrared spectroscopy \(fNIRS\) to measure the oxygenation differences in the prefrontal cortex \(PFC\) and sensorimotor cortex in response to EO and EC conditions and compared them with those of healthy controls\. Methods We analyzed data from 96 BSP individuals and 31 healthy controls \(HCs\) by using the amplitude of low\-frequency fluctuations \(ALFF\) determined by functional near\-infrared spectroscopy \(derived from fNIRS\) to measure the oxygenation differences in the prefrontal cortex \(PFC\) and sensorimotor cortex in response to EO and EC conditions\. Results The BSP group and the HC group exhibited opposite patterns of differences between the EC and EO conditions\. In the HC group, the ALFF was greater in the EC condition than in the EO condition in the frontopolar area \(FPA\) and orbitofrontal cortex and lower in the EC condition than in the EO condition in the bilateral sensorimotor cortex\. In the BSP group, the ALFF was greater in the EC condition than the EO condition in the bilateral sensorimotor cortex and lower in the EC condition than in the EO condition in the frontopolar area and bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex\. Moreover, differences in the EC\-EO patterns at channel 44 and channel 3 between the two groups showed promising excellent discrimination potential, pending external validation\. Conclusion The BSP group and the HCs group showed opposite patterns of EO\-EC differences in the prefrontal cortex and sensorimotor cortex\. The delta EO\-EC difference between the right S2 and the right FPA showed promising has excellent differential diagnostic value for BSP in this discovery cohort and is a candidate and is expected to become an early diagnostic biomarker requiring external validation and neuromodulation therapeutic target\.

## [Religious Belief‐Based Workplace Discrimination in the UK: The Importance of Intergroup Threat](../publications/e0ae31c567e49c2eed32.md)

Michelle Anne Luke; Kimberly Rios Morrison

ABSTRACT On the basis of intergroup threat theory, we tested whether atheists&\#x27; requests in the workplace are less likely to be accommodated than those of other religious groups in the United Kingdom \(UK\)\. Across three studies, participants responded to vignettes describing a Christian, Muslim, Hindu or atheist employee who requested to express his/her \(lack of\) religious beliefs at work\. Participants were least willing to accommodate atheist employees&\#x27; belief‐based requests because of the symbolic \(i\.e\., attempts to impose their beliefs on others\) and realistic \(i\.e\., jeopardising the organisation&\#x27;s economic status\) threats they perceived atheists to pose\. Surprisingly, participants were most willing to accommodate Hindu employees&\#x27; belief‐based requests because Hindus were perceived as invoking relatively low levels of symbolic and realistic threat\. These effects mostly remained significant both amongst religious and nonreligious participants and were not driven by stereotypes of competence or warmth, nor by motivations to control prejudice against the employees\.

## [ระบบแจงเหตฉกเฉนอจฉรยะสำหรบผสงอายระดบทองถน](../publications/e0be0984783780b420d3.md)

Tanawat Taptimtong; Taradon Potong; Wadeenat Wannasawaskul

This research presented the design and development of an intelligent emergency alert system for elderly individuals at the local administrative organization level\. The objective was to develop a prototype system capable of detecting emergency events, transmitting location information, and supporting emergency response within the standard response time of 8 minutes\. The system was based on an Internet of Things \(IoT\) architecture, which connected field emergency alert devices using ESP32 and ESP8266 microcontrollers to a centralized web application through a wireless network\. The research methodology included hardware and software system design, development of a web application for emergency event reception and status management, implementation of a real\-time status display and countdown mechanism at the elderly user’s residence, and system evaluation in a simulated local administrative environment\. Experimental results demonstrated that the prototype system operated correctly according to all designed functions and supported emergency response within the standard time frame, with the fastest recorded response time of 3\.25 minutes\. The results indicated that the proposed system provided sufficient performance for local\-level emergency support applications and could serve as a practical framework for improving emergency response systems and enhancing the quality of life for elderly individuals in community settings\.

## [Clinical implications of intraoperative premature ventricular contractions for 30\-day cardiovascular outcomes after liver transplantation](../publications/e0c69cc3b8b7de935f83.md)

Hwa‐Young Jang; Hong\-Cheol Yoon; Changwoo Kim; Hyun\-Seok Kim; Woo\-Young Seo; Jeongmin Gu; Sung‐Hoon Kim; Gyu‐Sam Hwang

To examine the association between intraoperative premature ventricular contraction \(PVC\) burden and 30\-day major adverse cardiovascular events \(MACE\) in liver transplantation \(LT\) recipients, and to determine whether complex ventricular ectopy carries prognostic significance distinct from isolated PVCs\. In this retrospective cohort study, continuous intraoperative ECG recordings from 2,290 consecutive LT recipients were analyzed using a validated AI\-based detection pipeline\. PVCs were classified as isolated or complex \(couplet, NSVT, bigeminy, trigeminy\), with total complex PVC burden as the primary exposure\. Associations with 30\-day MACE were estimated by multivariable logistic regression across burden tertiles\. Sensitivity analyses used a hard MACE endpoint excluding arrhythmic components and with additional adjustment for isolated PVC burden\. MACE occurred in 515 patients \(22\.5%\)\. PVCs were detected in 98\.2% of patients; isolated PVC prevalence did not differ between those with and without MACE \(98\.4% vs\. 98\.0%, P = 0\.666\), whereas complex PVC prevalence was significantly higher in the MACE group \(93\.2% vs\. 85\.8%, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Total complex PVC burden showed a graded association with MACE across tertiles \(T1 aOR 1\.71, 95% CI 1\.11\-2\.65; T2 aOR 2\.26, 95% CI 1\.47\-3\.47; T3 aOR 2\.79, 95% CI 1\.83\-4\.27\), whereas isolated PVC burden was not associated with MACE in any tertile\. The association persisted in both sensitivity analyses\. Complex intraoperative ventricular ectopy, but not isolated PVCs, was independently associated with 30\-day MACE in LT recipients\. AI\-enabled PVC quantification may identify an intraoperative signal associated with postoperative cardiovascular risk, although prospective and external validation is required before clinical application\.

## [Date palm seed \(Phoenix dactylifera\) as a sustainable platform for precision nanomedicine and nanotheranostics: a review of phytochemical\-derived nanomaterials and drug delivery applications](../publications/e0e4a330c7409081677d.md)

A\.D\. Ozieme; A\. A\. Adeleye; Olusegun Olufemi Ajide

The increasing application of nanomaterials in drug delivery, diagnosis, imaging and therapy has created interest in renewable biological resources for their synthesis\. Date palm \( Phoenix dactylifera L\.\) seed is an underutilised agricultural biomass containing lignocellulosic components, phytochemicals, proteins, lipids and minerals that can support different nanomaterial development pathways\. This review examines the conversion of date palm seed from raw biomass into carbonaceous materials, green\-synthesised nanoparticles and potential nanotheranostic platforms\. Particular attention is given to seed pretreatment, phytochemical extraction, chemical profiling, green nanoparticle formation, carbonisation, activation, drug loading and physicochemical characterisation\. The review also evaluates reported antimicrobial, antioxidant, cytocompatibility, haemocompatibility, biosensing, imaging and drug\-delivery applications\. Evidence across the literature indicates that material properties are strongly affected by cultivar, geographical origin, pretreatment, extraction conditions, phytochemical composition and synthesis parameters, which limits direct comparison and reproducibility between studies\. Although several biological activities have been reported, evidence for integrated precision nanomedicine and nanotheranostic applications remains comparatively limited\. Major challenges include chemical variability, incomplete mechanistic understanding, batch\-to\-batch reproducibility, toxicity assessment, physiological stability, scale\-up and regulatory requirements\. Future research should focus on the chemical and biologolical standardisation, controlled synthesis, surface engineering and appropriate in vitro and in vivo validation\. Date palm seed has potential as a sustainable feedstock for multifunctional nanomaterials, but translation into precision nanomedicine requires reproducible, well\-characterised and biologically validated platforms\.

## [การจำแนกรปแบบอปสงคการเปรยบเทยบวธการพยากรณยอดขายระยะสนสำหรบสนคาทนมลคาสง กรณศกษาผจดจำหนายเครองตรวจสอบและวเคราะหโลหะมคา](../publications/e100f59f6d8b47687624.md)

Wanussuda Kamput

This research aimed to 1\) classify the demand patterns of precious\-metal analyzers by model using the Average Demand Interval \(ADI\) and the squared Coefficient of Variation \(CV²\) criteria, 2\) compare the accuracy of several short\-term monthly sales forecasting methods through Rolling\-Origin evaluation, and 3\) propose a decision framework for selecting a forecasting method suited to each analyzer model&\#x27;s demand pattern\. This research was quantitative case\-study research, examining data from a single precious\-metal analyzer distributor and using actual sales transaction data of three analyzer models — namely XC\-1, XC\-2, and XC\-1M — over a period of 15 months\. The data comprised 15 monthly periods \(March 2025 – May 2026\), with the first seven periods used as the initial training window and eight forecast origins used for out\-of\-sample evaluation\. The instrument used for data collection was a sales transaction record form\. The statistics used for data analysis were the Average Demand Interval \(ADI\), the squared Coefficient of Variation \(CV²\), the Mean Absolute Deviation \(MAD\), the Root Mean Squared Error \(RMSE\), and the Mean Absolute Scaled Error \(MASE\), with forecasting accuracy evaluated through Rolling\-Origin evaluation together with the Friedman test\. The research results were as follows: All three models were continuously sold products, with model XC\-1 exhibiting smooth demand, while models XC\-2 and XC\-1M exhibited erratic demand\. The Simple Moving Average \(SMA\) and Holt&\#x27;s methods were more accurate than the Naïve method for every model, with Holt&\#x27;s method being the most accurate for model XC\-2 and the Simple Moving Average being the most accurate for models XC\-1 and XC\-1M; however, the differences in accuracy among the smoothing methods were not statistically significant \(χ2 = 1\.911, p = \.591\)\. The most accurate forecasting method differed according to each model&\#x27;s demand pattern, leading to the proposal of a decision framework \(the CASE model\) that enables distributors to select a forecasting method systematically, whereby simple forecasting methods proved robust and adequate for supply planning\.

## [Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats\+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data\-independent acquisition](../publications/e114690e61752b3d78ab.md)

Devon Kohler; Eralp Doğu; Mrittika Bhattacharya; Özge Karayel; Magaña Manuel; Anthony Wu; Veronica G\. Anania; Olga Vitek A

Abstract Mass spectrometry\-based proteomics with data\-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis\. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements\. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor\-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions\. We introduce MSstats \+ , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA\-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics\. MSstats\+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins\. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run\. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large\-scale clinical investigations\. MSstats\+ is implemented in the family of open\-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats\.

## [Relación entre inteligencia artificial y tutoría educativa en estudiantes universitarios](../publications/e12405dd3bd929fc5aef.md)

Dina Chela Inga Lindo; Alexander Miguel Manrique Inga; Adolfo Valencia Gutiérrez; Ysabel Torres Riva

La inteligencia artificial \(IA\) se ha incorporado progresivamente a la educación superior como apoyo para la búsqueda de información, la generación de recursos, la personalización del aprendizaje y la toma de decisiones\. En este contexto, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo determinar la relación entre la inteligencia artificial y la tutoría y orientación educativa \(TOE\) en estudiantes de universidades públicas de Lima\. Para tal fin, se desarrolló una investigación cuantitativa, aplicada, descriptivo\-correlacional, no experimental y transversal\. Participaron 400 estudiantes seleccionados mediante muestreo no probabilístico de una población de 600\. Se utilizó un cuestionario de 48 ítems con escala Likert de tres opciones, distribuido en 24 ítems para IA y 24 para TOE\. La confiabilidad fue alta para ambas variables \(α = \.957 y α = \.963, respectivamente\)\. Tras comprobarse la normalidad de los datos, se aplicó el coeficiente r de Pearson\. Los resultados evidenciaron una relación positiva, moderada y significativa entre IA y TOE \(r = \.473; p &lt; \.001\)\. La adaptabilidad de la IA presentó la asociación más alta con la TOE \(r = \.484\)\. Se concluye que la IA puede fortalecer el acompañamiento universitario cuando se integra de forma ética, pedagógica y complementaria al juicio humano, sin sustituir la interacción tutorial ni la autonomía estudiantil\.

## [Verbascum gongliuensis \(Scrophulariaceae\), a new species of Yili, Xinjiang, China](../publications/e125d28ea3ce6d3aaa14.md)

Yuhao Luo; Wenbin Xu

Verbascum gongliuensis Y\.H\. Luo &amp; W\.B\. Xu \(Scrophulariaceae\), is described as a new species from Yili, Xinjiang, China\. Based on careful comparison with the Flora of China, Flora Xinjiangensis, Flora of Kazakhstan, Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, and the Flora of the USSR, it is confirmed as a new species of Verbascum\. Its threat category was assessed according to IUCN \(2001\) criteria\. ## [Efficient Implementation of Machine Learning Algorithms on Reconfigurable Architectures Using High\-Level Synthesis](../publications/e12beb836229984cc1e1.md)

Florian Porrmann

Field\-Programmable Gate Arrays \(FPGAs\) can offer high performance and energy efficiency when used to accelerate compute\-intensive workloads\. However, the often fairly long development time associated with the commonly used RTL design flows hinders their adaptation in fast\-paced domains such as machine learning\. Therefore, this thesis analyzes the extent to which High\-Level Synthesis \(HLS\) can be used to efficiently implement machine learning algorithms on FPGAs\. In addition to design\-time improvements through HLS, the implementation&\#x27;s efficiency in terms of performance, resource utilization, and energy consumption is evaluated\. To address bottlenecks in the interaction between software and FPGA hardware, the runtime framework CLAP was developed\. It provides a unified C\+\+ API for interacting with AMD/Xilinx FPGAs, independent of the execution target, i\.e\., PCIe\-based accelerators, embedded Linux running on a reconfigurable MPSoC, or bare\-metal on an embedded processor\. In combination with CLAPPy, a Python binding, and the automatic project\-generation tool CLAPify, the framework can significantly reduce the manual work required to create host applications and enables easy integration of FPGA accelerators into existing C\+\+ and Python projects\. Additionally, FPGA4ML, a wrapping framework for the Python package hls4ml, was developed to automatically transform trained neural networks into fully functional FPGA implementations\. Binary Neuronal Associative Memories \(BINAM\), Self\-Organizing Maps \(SOM\), and different autoencoder models were implemented and evaluated to analyze the usability and efficiency of HLS\-based hardware designs for machine learning\. While the BINAM and SOM designs were implemented from scratch, the autoencoders were realized using FPGA4ML\. For each algorithm, an extensive design space exploration was performed to evaluate resource utilization, performance, and energy efficiency\. The results of these evaluations demonstrate that HLS\-based designs can achieve performance comparable to GPU and RTL\-based FPGA implementations\. Depending on the target application, software\-based solutions on CPUs were even outperformed by up to two orders of magnitude at a significantly higher energy efficiency\. Overall, this work demonstrates that HLS\-based FPGA development is a viable approach for implementing machine learning algorithms\. In combination with easy\-to\-use frameworks for runtime development and design space exploration, HLS can significantly reduce development time while maintaining high performance and energy efficiency\.

## [van de Poel, Ibo: Embedding Values in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) Systems](../publications/e12dabcb516a4c8e5a68.md)



\_Minds and Machines\_ 30 \(3\):385\-409\. 2020Organizations such as the EU High\-Level Expert Group on AI and the IEEE have recently formulated ethical principles and \(moral\) values that should be adhered to in the design and deployment of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. These include respect for autonomy, non\-maleficence, fairness, transparency, explainability, and accountability\. But how can we ensure and verify that an AI system actually respects these values? To help answer this question, I propose an account for determining when an AI system can be said to embody certain values\. This account understands embodied values as the result of design activities intended to embed those values in such systems\. AI systems are here understood as a special kind of sociotechnical system that, like traditional sociotechnical systems, are composed of technical artifacts, human agents, and institutions but—in addition—contain artificial agents and certain technical norms that regulate interactions between artificial agents and other elements of the system\. The specific challenges and opportunities of embedding values in AI systems are discussed, and some lessons for better embedding values in AI systems are drawn\. \(direct link \)

## [FuTransformer: FP8 prefill and INT4 decode for Llama\-style inference on Hopper](../publications/e137203e9804e5377c16.md)

Wei Wang

Transformer prefill reuses weights across tokens and is dominated by matrix multiplication and activation data movement; single\-token decode has limited reuse and is dominated by weight and KV\-cache reads\. We present FUTRANSFORMER, a CUDA implementation of a Llama\-style Transformer block for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs\. It applies CODA&\#x27;s GEMM\-plus\-epilogue approach to inference, adding direct KV\-cache placement, folding the fixed RMSNorm gain into weights, writing FP8 output directly with delayed scaling, and supporting prefill without padding\. Decode uses INT4 projection weights and an INT4 KV\-cache copy\. Weights and keys follow Tensor Core fragment layouts for direct dequantization into MMA operands without full intermediate tiles\. A block\-diagonal Hadamard transform reduces cache quantization error from outlier channels\. On one H100, prefill is up to 1\.48x faster than compiled PyTorch FP8 and reaches 1\.29 PFLOP/s\. For gate/up projection with SwiGLU at the 8B shape, our BF16 path is 1\.13x faster than CODA\. Our FP8 path is 2\.02\-2\.18x faster than the evaluated BF16 CODA path\. Across 8B and 70B shapes at batches 1\-32, INT4 decode is 1\.3\-2\.4x faster than the faster of PyTorch&\#x27;s BF16 and INT4 blocks at each point: 2\.1\-3\.3x faster than compiled, CUDA\-graphed BF16 and 1\.3\-6\.3x faster than the same block using PyTorch&\#x27;s INT4 projection kernel, which targets a single query row and loses to BF16 at batch 32\. It is also 31\-51% faster than our FP8 path\. Complete Llama\-3\.1\-8B decode takes 2\.8 ms per step at batch one, versus 8\.1 ms for the compiled transformers implementation\. Decoding every WikiText\-2 token through the INT4 weight path raises perplexity from 6\.24 to 7\.23 with round\-to\-nearest weights or 6\.99 with GPTQ in the same format; the rotated INT4 cache adds 0\.20\. The kernels match a quantized reference computation within 0\.001 perplexity\.

## [Conversational AI as a Compliance Layer for Mandatory Digital Resident\-Communication Regulation: Evidence from a Multi\-Region Deployment in Urban Housing Management](../publications/e138ccb7137fa4cdbd4a.md)

Alexander Romashchenko

Cities increasingly regulate not only the content but the channel of communication between service providers and residents, backing such requirements with fines; manual compliance is costly for the small operators typically covered by such rules\. We analyze telemetry from an AI assistant operating in residential building chats in multiple regions of Russia \(1 January – 8 September 2026\) around the effective date of Government Resolution No\. 40, which made the same channel mandatory for housing organizations \(fines up to RUB 300,000, ≈€3,000 at early\-2026 exchange rates\)\. The assistant&\#x27;s response\-generation feature was active for one month, of which the final eight days followed the mandate&\#x27;s effective date\. Verification approval \- 85\.5% among residents who submitted documents \- is computed on documents actually submitted, not on the much larger pre\-provisioned base \(Section 5\.3\)\.

## [Preserving to forget: Ottoman\-Armenian art and the politics of museum taxonomies](../publications/e13e681ea574b64bfe75.md)

Banu Karaca

Drawing on ongoing ethnographic and archival research on how art dispossessed in episodes of state violence against non\-Muslims in the late Ottoman Empire and the early Turkish republic has shaped the knowledge production on \(post\-\)Ottoman heritage, this article revisits past and present articulations of the idea of preservation that is central to the making of heritage and its institution\. The analysis is anchored in two kindred Ottoman\-Armenian objects: egg\-shaped ceramic ornaments dated to the eighteenth century, one displayed in the Tiled Pavilion Museum, Istanbul, the other at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York City\. In Istanbul, the ornament is seemingly designated as a ‘mosque decoration’; its Armenian provenance is denied\. In New York, the ornament is correctly labelled as Armenian, and yet another kind of miscategorization is at work here as well as it is located in the Byzantine Gallery\. Taking the museum and UNESCO as key institutional formations in debates on preservation, I posit that the preservation of the ceramic eggs is predicated on ‘misattribution’ in the first and ‘misdating’ in the second case, and argue that the preservation paradigm both facilitates and is contingent on epistemic forgetting: It not only veils a particular way of asserting ownership rooted in violence and dispossession, but also upholds institutional and disciplinary boundaries within the knowledge production on heritage\.
