## [AI\-Facilitated Discovery of Microbiome\-Originated Antimicrobial Peptides: A Perspective on Combating Antibiotic Resistance Within Public Health and Food Safety Frameworks](../publications/e150e0e2e2538ba4c97e.md)

Paul Y\. Atuahene; Bryanna Stevenson; Yongming Sang

The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) demands innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotics\. Antimicrobial peptides \(AMPs\), particularly those originating from the human, animal, and environmental microbiome, represent a promising frontier within public health microbiology and microbial food safety\. Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) have revolutionized the discovery pipeline, enabling high\-throughput mining of metagenomic data and de novo generation of novel peptide sequences\. This perspective review synthesizes recent breakthroughs in AI\-driven discovery of microbiome\-originated AMPs, examines their preclinical efficacy against multidrug\-resistant \(MDR\) pathogens under One Health and climate\-sensitive frameworks and application in infectious disease treatment and discusses translational challenges including pharmacokinetics, toxicity, manufacturing scalability, and applications in food preservation and water safety\. We argue that the convergence of microbiome science, deep learning, and synthetic biology positions AI\-discovered AMPs as viable next\-generation interventions against antibiotic resistance across human, animal, and environmental domains\.

## [Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions](../publications/e1571890a2ba2e150b9e.md)

Alim Rahman Akin Zor

Providing the world&\#x27;s increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century\. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis\. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world\. Water scarcity and pollution threaten human health, economic development and environmental sustainability\. Traditional water treatment methods do not generally achieve effective removal of emerging pollutants and pathogen\. Thus, the properties of nanomaterials at the molecular scale make it unique, and open new possibilities for development of more efficient, cost effective and environmentally friendly water purification\. Nanotechnology is changing the way we clean and reuse water resources from nano adsorbents that remove toxic metals selectively and nanomembranes that filter out the slightest contaminants\. In this article we will look at the advances in nanomaterials for water purification looking at how they work, what they are good for, and they could help enlighten us about the global water crisis\. Through these innovations we’ll explore ways these are redefining the future of water management for anyone and everyone, not just industries and communities, but all across the globe\.

## [Delayed angiographic detection of a ruptured basilar artery perforator aneurysm in diffuse initially angiographically occult subarachnoid hemorrhage: A case report and literature review](../publications/e1604ae2c5b49ea86929.md)

Bae Jae Kim; Hyun Gon Kim; Gyojun Hwang; Jae Seong Kang; Sung Han Oh; Jong\-Hyeok Park

Basilar artery perforator aneurysms \(BAPAs\) are uncommon and may remain occult on initial angiography because of their minute size and dynamic morphology\. A 69\-year\-old man presented with sudden severe headache and mild drowsiness \(Glasgow Coma Scale 14, World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grade II\)\. Computed tomography showed diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage involving the basal cisterns and sylvian fissures with fourth ventricular intraventricular hemorrhage\. Initial digital subtraction angiography \(DSA\) revealed no bleeding source\. Although repeat DSA is generally performed approximately 1 week later at our institution, the diffuse and asymmetric aneurysmal\-type hemorrhage pattern prompted earlier repeat DSA on hospital day 4\. This demonstrated an approximately 1\.7\-mm fusiform\-appearing aneurysm arising from a right basilar artery perforator just below the superior cerebellar artery\. High\-resolution vessel wall magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) and cone\-beam computed tomography \(CT\) angiography were not performed\. Conservative management was selected because of the minute distal perforator lesion and procedural risk\. The patient was discharged on day 21 with a modified Rankin Scale score of 1, which remained unchanged at 3 months\. This case emphasizes the importance of timely repeat DSA and consideration of adjunctive high\-resolution imaging in diffuse initially DSA\-negative subarachnoid hemorrhage\.

## [Per\-channel Complex B1\+ Mapping for Parallel Transmit Ultra\-high field MRI](../publications/e17617c8ec8a7b4e5fba.md)

Ye Yuan; Jianxiang Chen; Christopher T\. Rodgers

Ultra\-high field \(UHF, B0 ≥ 7T\) MRI provides substantial gains in signal\-to\-noise ratio, spatial resolution, and contrast\. Routine clinical deployment has been limited by challenges of transmit field \(B1\+\) inhomogeneity and specific absorption rate \(SAR\)\. Parallel transmission \(pTx\) can mitigate these challenges but it requires per\-channel complex B1\+ maps to design effective pTx pulses\. We review established and emerging approaches to obtain these maps\. We begin by summarizing the underlying physical principles and theory\. Then we describe methods for magnitude B1\+\-mapping such as actual flip\-angle imaging \(AFI\), saturation\-prepared B1\+\-mapping \(e\.g\. SatTFL\), and dual refocusing echo acquisition mode \(DREAM\) that are the basis of widely\-applied per\-channel complex B1\+ mapping methods, as well as methods of pedagogical and/or historical relevance\. Next, we describe how relative B1\+\-mapping with low\-flip angle gradient\-recalled echo \(GRE\) scans can determine the relative phases \(and relative magnitudes\) of B1\+ for each channel\. We recap the important interferometric approach that is now widely used\. We explain how magnitude and phase maps are combined into complex per\-channel B1\+\-maps\. We discuss remaining arbitrary factors such as the position\-dependent transmit reference phase\. We discuss recent practical implementations such as Sandwich TFL, 3DREAM, compressed\-sensing SA2RAGE, and respiratory\-resolved B1\+ mapping\. We explore the workflow improvements that could accrue if per\-channel B1\+ maps don’t need to be acquired for every subject\. This includes deep\-learning\-based approaches to synthesize B1\+\-maps from the normal localizer scans, the Universal Pulses \(UPs\) approach to pre\-calibrate pulses, and variants such as standardized universal pulses \(SUPs\), and Fast\-Online Customized \(FOCUS\) and machine\-learning online customization\. We hope to encourage greater openness and harmonization of these critical calibration steps for parallel transmit pulse design\. This will become increasingly important as 7T pTx MRI is adopted for multisite cross\-vendor clinical research studies and to deliver the full scientific potential of new extremely high field human MRIs\.

## [Li, Yuchen ; Li, Xintong &amp; Fan, Zongqi: Functional Selfhood and First\-Person Experience: Self\-Indexing, Localized Presentation, and Constructed Continuity](../publications/e17bfc2be54e3b6265cd.md)



Brain activity changes constantly, yet we experience an ordered life lived by one &quot;I&quot;\. In our three\-layer account, the basis is the physical medium that receives projected encodings and in which experience occurs; the encoding, each moment&\#x27;s organized activity, fixes what is experienced, including what is marked as one&\#x27;s own; the hardware, the persisting brain, stores traces and generates the next encoding\. First, the three layers answer different questions and can fail separately\. Second, encodings appear and disappear, so nothing in them guarantees that t follows t\-1: if experience were a property of each encoding alone, nothing would fix the order in which a first\-person perspective passes through them, yet within a specious present we directly experience the transition\. Experience is thus ordered in itself\. Since causation and time are two sides of one structure and projection is causal, its basis is a field in spacetime, or spacetime itself, that receives the projections in causal order\. As it cannot be decided whether the observer fixes time or the reverse, we identify the subjective observer with this local carrier of time, distinct from the projector, the functional encoding of self\-consciousness\. Third, each encoding leaves a trace from which the next is generated and which the next reads back as its own past, so an &quot;I&quot; is rebuilt at every moment\. Recognizing something as one&\#x27;s own is a second\-order readout of this mark, and language models show that it can be absent while the mark is present\. Copying duplicates the projector and its feeling of continuation, not the observer: that feeling cannot single out the original person, but continuity along a world line can\.

## [TECNOLOGIAS DIGITAIS NO ACOMPANHAMENTO GESTACIONAL](../publications/e17e79b3f84bd96e68d0.md)

Vanessa Meneses; Joice Moreira Schmalfuss

Com o avanço da tecnologia e a popularização da inteligência artificial, torna\-se cada vez mais evidente a necessidade de ferramentas digitais que atendam às demandas específicas da saúde gestacional\. Objetiva\-se desenvolver um Produto Mínimo Viável \(MVP\) para acompanhamento gestacional por meio de um estudo metodológico desenvolvido por uma revisão integrativa da literatura para identificar evidências acerca da utilização de tecnologias digitais no acompanhamento gestacional, cujos resultados subsidiaram a construção do MVP\. A revisão integrativa, composta por 13 estudos, evidenciou que as tecnologias digitais apresentam potencial para qualificar o acompanhamento gestacional, favorecendo o acesso a informações, monitoramento materno, fortalecimento da comunicação entre gestantes e profissionais e aumento do engajamento pré\-natal\. Foram identificadas limitações importantes nas tecnologias atualmente disponíveis, pois grande parte dos aplicativos apresenta conteúdo incompleto ou sem embasamento científico, pouca participação de especialistas em seu desenvolvimento e fragilidades relacionadas à segurança e à privacidade dos dados\. O MVP foi concebido para responder às lacunas identificadas na literatura, reunindo conteúdo científico atualizado, funcionalidades de acompanhamento gestacional e recursos que favoreçam a educação em saúde, a organização pré\-natal e o protagonismo da gestante\. As tecnologias digitais constituem ferramentas promissoras para complementar o cuidado pré\-natal\.

## [A social exchange perspective on employee performance in Sierra Leone’s public sector: the roles of authentic leadership, participative decision\-making, and trust](../publications/e1889f35adb94e02ca8b.md)

Ibrahim Sallieu Jalloh; Shixiang Li; Guangjin Zhang; H\. M\. Wasif Rasheed; Rashid Khurshid

Purpose Based on Social Exchange Theory \(SET\) and Social Information Processing \(SIP\), this research attempts to explore the effect that Participative Decision\-Making \(PDM\) has on the performance of employees working in Sierra Leone’s public sector using Affective Trust, Work Engagement, Affective Commitment, and Organizational Citizenship Behavior \(OCB\) as mediating variables in relation to Authentic Leadership as a moderating variable\. Design/Methodology/Approach The study used a quantitative and cross\-sectional research design\. Data collection was conducted among public sector employees in Sierra Leone using a convenience sampling method\. The study applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) to assess the measurement and structural model hypotheses\. Findings The empirical results reveal that participative decision\-making \(PDM\) associate with employee performance through affective trust, which associate to work engagement and affective commitment, resulting in organizational citizenship behavior \(OCB\)\. The variable of work engagement proved itself as a better predictor of OCB than affective commitment\. Besides, authentic leadership moderated the relationship between affective trust and work engagement/affective commitment\. Originality/value The current research contributes to the SET and SIP frameworks by validating a step\-by\-step process leading to PDM, which ultimately influences Employee Performance\. The study fills one of the significant gaps in the literature by providing evidence from an unexplored area of public sector employees in Sierra Leone\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI FRAMEWORK FOR NEURO\-PHYSICAL COGNITIVE DYNAMICS: UNIFYING INFORMATION GEOMETRY, NON\-EQUILIBRIUM THERMODYNAMICS, AND AI FOR BRAIN\-LIKE CONTINUOUS LEARNING](../publications/e1996135f7bdcc47429d.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Framework for Neuro\-Physical Cognitive Dynamics \(NPCD\) addresses catastrophic forgetting and thermodynamic inefficiency in AI by modeling cognitive states as dynamic attractor basins within Riemannian manifolds, governed by non\-equilibrium thermodynamics and the Free Energy Principle\. Unlike traditional deep learning&\#x27;s static matrix operations, NPCD integrates four modules: Information Geometry using Fisher Information Metric for natural gradient flow; Non\-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Learning via Fokker\-Planck dynamics; Criticality\-Maintained Neural Fields operating at the edge of chaos; and Continuous Attractor Integration Protocol growing new basins in unoccupied phase\-space regions, mathematically resolving catastrophic forgetting\. The dimensionally consistent NPCEM metric yields bits per Joule, directly comparable to Landauer&\#x27;s limit\. Applications include lifelong learning AI, adaptive brain\-computer interfaces, and ultra\-low\-power neuromorphic computing, establishing a unified foundation bridging information geometry, statistical physics, and artificial intelligence\.

ريم جرار

هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى التعرّف على دور توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، من وجهة نظر المشرفين التربويين، والكشف عن وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في هذا الدور تُعزى لمتغيرات المؤهل العلمي، وسنوات الخبرة، وعدد الدورات التدريبية\. اعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي المسحي، وقامت الباحثة بتطوير استبانة مكوّنة من \(30\) فقرة موزّعة على ثلاثة مجالات، طُبِّقت على عيّنة من المشرفين التربويين العاملين في قسم الإشراف التربوي في لواء الرصيفة، تم اختيارها بالطريقة المسح الشامل لطبيعة مجتمع الدراسة، وبلغ عدد أفرادها \(33\) مشرفًا ومشرفة\. وأظهرت نتائج الدراسة أن دور توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، من وجهة نظر المشرفين التربويين، جاء بدرجة مرتفعة\. كما بيّنت النتائج وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى الدلالة \(α ≤ 0\.05\) تُعزى لمتغير المؤهل العلمي، ولصالح المشرفين الحاصلين على الدراسات العليا، وكذلك لمتغير عدد الدورات التدريبية، ولصالح من خضعوا لدورتين تدريبيتين في مجال الذكاء الاصطناعي، في حين لم تظهر فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية تُعزى لمتغير سنوات الخبرة\. وأوصت الدراسة بضرورة الاستمرار في تقديم دورات تدريبية متخصصة ومتنوعة للمشرفين التربويين في مجال توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي، لما لذلك من أثر إيجابي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، وتحسين جودة العملية التعليمية\.

## [Landslide Susceptibility Assessment in Badong County, Hubei Province, Based on Machine Learning and SHAP Interpretability Analysis](../publications/e1a3d70f63db736aa4b0.md)

兰少飞 Lan Shaofei; Daming Wu; Peng Lu; Aoxin Yang; Beinan Guo; Zixiao Li

Badong County is located in the hinterland of the Three Gorges Reservoir Area and is characterized by complex geological conditions and highly rugged terrain, making landslide susceptibility assessment particularly important\. Based on an inventory of 384 landslides, this study retained 11 conditioning factors and constructed a balanced dataset with a 1:1 ratio of landslide to non\-landslide samples\. Sensitivity analysis of 500, 1000, and 1500 m buffer distances showed only small differences in non\-landslide sampling, with the 1000 m buffer retained for subsequent analysis\. The dataset was evaluated using both a conventional 7:3 random training–test split and five\-fold spatial block cross\-validation, with the spatially independent results used as the primary basis for model evaluation\. Four machine learning models, namely RF, MLP, SVM, and XGBoost, were compared\. Under spatial block cross\-validation, XGBoost achieved the highest mean AUC of 0\.8662, compared with 0\.8751 under the random split, and also showed the best overall performance among the four models\. Calibration analysis further indicated good agreement between the predicted susceptibility scores and the observed landslide proportions\. Bootstrap resampling was used to quantify prediction uncertainty, and the integration of susceptibility and uncertainty identified areas characterized by both high susceptibility and high uncertainty\. Independent validation using spatially withheld landslides showed that the high\- and very\-high\-susceptibility zones accounted for 29\.25% of the study area and contained 71\.61% of the withheld landslides\. SHAP analysis indicated that elevation, distance to road, slope, and NDVI were the principal contributors to the XGBoost model output\. Overall, the results provide a spatial reference for landslide susceptibility zoning, preliminary engineering\-site screening, and the prioritization of field investigation and monitoring in Badong County\.

## [A decision making framework for traffic noise prediction using artificial intelligence techniques](../publications/e1a3ee51b5877f4e89b4.md)

Shashi Kant Tiwari; Rohit Patel

Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution\. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments\. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized\. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction\. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0\.54 to 0\.96, whereas machine learning \(ML\) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0\.81 to 0\.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking\. Moreover, deep learning \(DL\) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets\. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence \(AI\) algorithms\. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross\-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management\. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management\.

## [Dynamics of Polariton‐Polariton Interactions in Large‐Area van der Waals Superlattices—Ag Nanohole Arrays Strong Coupling System](../publications/e1a64825f5383435c4b4.md)

Yu‐Peng Zhang; Hai Wang; Qian‐Ao Zhang; Yao‐Kun Wang; Leyi Zhao; YANG Jin‐Yu; Y Wang; Yi Wang; Wenxin Wang; Hai‐Yu Wang

ABSTRACT The realization of strong and effective optical nonlinear response is a challenging task, which can drive significant breakthroughs in quantum and nonlinear optics\. Constructing strongly coupled exciton‐polaritons offers a promising alternative to control nonlinear optical properties\. Here we demonstrate strong coupling between Bloch surface plasmon polaritons \(Bloch‐SPPs\) supported by centimeter‐scale Ag nanoholes \(Ag‐NHs\) arrays and A excitons in WS 2 ‐based van der Waals superlattices\. Angle‐resolved transient absorption \(TA\) spectroscopy reveals clear anticrossing dispersion with Rabi splitting energies increasing from 61 meV for one monolayer to 120 meV for four monolayer superlattices strong coupling systems\. More importantly, pump‐fluence‐dependent TA measurements demonstrate that the observed giant nonlinearity arises predominantly from Coulomb repulsive interactions between polaritons, rather than the phase‐space filling effect\. These results highlight a scalable platform for engineering strong polariton‐polariton interactions and pave the way for large‐area, integrable room‐temperature polaritonic nonlinear devices\.

## [Mutual Information in High\-Dimensional Neural Coding](../publications/e1a6e90d90fc2d9d499e.md)

Zimo Li; Yuchang Tian; Matthew P\. Leighton; Christopher W\. Lynn

Estimating mutual information in large neural populations is limited by the exponential growth of possible neural response patterns\. Here we apply a Monte Carlo framework to make this problem tractable by sampling from a conditionally independent population model fit from single\-neuron responses\. The estimator accurately recovers analytical ground truth, corrects finite\-data bias, and scales to empirical recordings containing 100 to 10,000 neurons from visual cortex, hippocampus, and retina\. Across systems, stimulus uncertainty decays exponentially with population size, revealing a simple scaling law for high\-dimensional neural codes\.

## [Groundwater quality parameter weighting using hybrid machine learning and SHAP\-game theory based on Sentinel\-2 data \(Case Study: Khorramabad, Iran\)](../publications/e1a9331a4d59f54c4b0e.md)

Mozhgan Yarahmadi; Ali Haghizadeh; Leila Ghasemi

Monitoring groundwater quality is essential for sustainable water management in semi\-arid regions, particularly in Iran, where water scarcity is severe\. Traditional field sampling is costly, time\-consuming, and limited in spatial and temporal coverage\. This study presents an integrated framework for predicting and weighting groundwater quality parameters by combining field data \(ten parameters: EC, TDS, TH, pH, Na%, Cl, SO₄, Na, Ca, Mg\), Sentinel\-2 multispectral imagery \(eight bands, five indices\), and ERA5\-Land climatic variables \(precipitation, temperature\)\. We analysed 56 samples from five stations in Khorramabad \(2015–2024\) using nine machine learning models: five base models \(Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR, MLP, Linear Regression\) and four hybrid models \(RF\+XGBoost, SVR\+MLP, Voting, Stacking\)\. Hybrid models consistently outperformed base models\. The Voting Ensemble achieved the highest accuracy for sodium \(R² = 0\.986\) and EC \(R² = 0\.974\), while SVR\+MLP reached R² = 0\.900 for TDS\. We used SHAP combined with game theory \(Shapley values\) for parameter weighting\. Results showed EC \(50\.47%\) and TDS \(32\.40%\) as the most influential parameters, followed by TH \(7\.87%\) and Na% \(7\.56%\)\. Seasonal analysis revealed that TH weight increased markedly in summer \(21\.15%\)\. Bootstrap uncertainty analysis \(1,000 iterations\) confirmed weight stability, and cross\-validation supported model reliability \(R²: 0\.35–0\.74\)\. Optically active parameters \(Na, EC, TDS, Cl\) were accurately predicted using Sentinel\-2, while non\-optical parameters still required field measurements\. This cost\-effective framework enables prioritisation of groundwater quality parameters in monitoring programmers\. Dominance of EC \(50\.47%\) and TDS \(32\.40%\) in the weighting results provides a basis for prioritising these optically active parameters in monitoring programmers\. Seasonal increase in TH weight \(from 17\.12% in spring to 21\.15%\) supports an adaptive approach to seasonal monitoring\. The framework enables spatial prediction of optically active parameters in ungauged areas, making it a cost\-effective approach for groundwater management in Iran, where groundwater supplies more than 55% of total water consumption\.

## [Educating for Smart Governance: The CITAI\_DATA Approach to Territorial Intelligence](../publications/e1aff125ab68e4aab053.md)

Ana Bordalo; Ana Paula Rainha

The establishment of CITAI\_DATA – Center for Applied Intelligence, within the Department of Architecture, Arts and Design at ISMAT, aims to foster interdisciplinary innovation and digital transformation in territorial governance\. The study presents the design and implementation of a new Executive Master focused on Smart Territories, integrating ethical, technological, and spatial dimensions\. Methodologically, the program combines applied research, digital simulation, GeoAI, and data driven modeling to explore the social, environmental, and governance challenges of intelligent territories\. The main results highlight the development of critical and technical competences in digital decision making, urban simulation, and responsible technological design\. The study concludes that the program offers an integrated educational framework that aligns ethics, sustainability, and innovation, contributing to the formation of professionals capable of leading fair and data based territorial transformations\.

## [Concordance of ChatGPT with a Fellowship\-Trained Orthopaedic Surgeon in Detecting Periprosthetic Osteolysis Following Total Shoulder Arthroplasty](../publications/e1b3ba50e32407142b51.md)

Colton C\. Mowers; Justin T Childers; Alexander L\. Hornung; Amelia Hummel; Arden C\. Shen; Gregory P\. Nicholson; Grant E\. Garrigues

Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the agreement between ChatGPT 4\.0 and a fellowship\-trained orthopaedic surgeon in detecting periprosthetic osteolysis on radiographs following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty \(aTSA\), using the Gruen and Modified Gruen zone scoring systems\. Agreement with a fellowship\-trained orthopaedic surgeon was evaluated\. Methods A total of 73 radiographs from patients with failed aTSAs were retrospectively analyzed\. Each radiograph was assessed for osteolysis across predefined zones using both traditional and modified Gruen zone scoring\. ChatGPT\-4\.0 received zone definitions and reference images before evaluating each zone as positive \(1\) or negative \(0\) for osteolysis\. A stem was labeled “loose” if ≥2 zones showed osteolysis\. A fellowship\-trained orthopaedic surgeon independently scored the same radiographs\. Agreement was evaluated using Cohen’s kappa, and agreement metrics relative to the surgeon were calculated\. Results Agreement metrics relative to the surgeon demonstrated variable sensitivity across zones, ranging from 33% to 100%, with consistently high specificity \(55% to 100%\)\. The highest agreement was observed in Modified Gruen M2 \(κ = 1\.000\), followed by Modified Gruen Loose \(κ = 0\.812\), Gruen 7 and Gruen 8 \(κ = 0\.754\), Gruen 1 \(κ = 0\.734\), Gruen 6 \(κ = 0\.686\), Overall Loose \(κ = 0\.718\), and Gruen Loose \(κ = 0\.670\)\. Moderate agreement was observed in Gruen 3 \(κ = 0\.456\) and Modified Gruen L2 \(κ = 0\.437\)\. Fair agreement was observed in Modified Gruen US \(κ = 0\.395\) and Gruen 5 \(κ = 0\.333\), while slight to poor agreement was observed in Gruen 4 \(κ = 0\.183\), Modified Gruen M1 \(κ = 0\.161\), and Modified Gruen L1 \(κ = −0\.067\)\. Overall, substantial or greater agreement was observed in 5 of 8 Gruen zones \(62\.5%\) and 1 of 5 Modified Gruen zones \(20%\)\. Agreement relative to the surgeon ranged from 50% to 100%, with most zones exceeding 85%\. Conclusion ChatGPT 4\.0 demonstrates variable agreement with a fellowship\-trained orthopaedic surgeon in detecting periprosthetic osteolysis, particularly in zones with well\-defined criteria\. However, agreement remained inconsistent across anatomical zones\. Since the cohort consisted exclusively of failed anatomic total shoulder arthroplasties from an implant retrieval database, these findings may overrepresent the prevalence of osteolysis and limit generalizability\. Level of Evidence Level III, Retrospective Comparative Study\.

## [Latent profiles of work readiness and their associated factors among nursing interns: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/e1c50fa5c07bb71be599.md)

Yanfang Zhang; Xinxin Xie; Man Wu; Qingqing Lv; Long Zhao; 杨秀木

Background Work readiness refers to the comprehensive competencies required for individuals to enter and adapt to the workforce\. It is relevant to the transition from nursing student to clinical nurse\. However, existing research has paid limited attention to heterogeneity in nursing interns’ work readiness, and few studies have examined associated factors from the perspective of Social Cognitive Career Theory\. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of work readiness among nursing interns and examine the associations of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) literacy and the clinical learning environment with profile membership\. Methods A cross\-sectional study was conducted among 712 final\-year nursing interns from three nursing schools in Anhui Province, China, between November 2025 and June 2026\. Participants completed the Nursing Practice Readiness Scale, Clinical Learning Environment Questionnaire, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale\. Latent Profile Analysis was used to identify distinct work readiness profiles, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with profile membership\. Results Three latent profiles of work readiness were identified: low work readiness \( n = 415, 58\.3%\), moderate work readiness \( n = 227, 31\.9%\), and high work readiness \( n = 70, 9\.8%\)\. The overall multinomial logistic regression model\( χ 2 = 467\.253, P &lt; 0\.001\) showed that the clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were significantly associated with work readiness profile membership \(all P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Conclusions Three distinct work readiness profiles were identified among nursing interns\. Clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were associated with profile membership\. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of nursing interns’ work readiness and may inform the development of individualized educational support strategies\.

## [AI\-enabled HR practices and agile talent deployment: the role of trust in AI and digital culture climate](../publications/e1ca012eeeb21bea0fb3.md)

Osama Khassawneh; Tamara Mohammad; Qasim Al\-khafaji; Tahir Masood Qureshi

Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-enabled human resource \(HR\) practices foster agile talent deployment within startup firms, particularly highlighting the mediating role of trust in AI and the moderating influence of digital culture climate\. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on self\-determination theory, the authors propose and empirically test a moderated mediation model using data collected from a three\-wave, multisource survey of 298 employees working in three technology\-oriented startups in the United Arab Emirates \(UAE\)\. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the measurement and structural models and to test the hypothesized relationships among AI\-enabled HR practices, trust in AI, digital culture climate and agile talent deployment\. Findings Results reveal that AI\-enabled HR practices positively influence agile talent deployment through increased employee trust in AI\. In addition, the mediated relationship is stronger within organizations characterized by a robust digital culture climate, indicating that a digitally supportive organizational context enhances the effectiveness of AI\-enabled HR initiatives\. Originality/value The paper advances AI\-enabled human resource management research by framing trust in AI as a mechanism translating supportive, transparent HR systems into agile talent deployment rather than technology acceptance\. It identifies digital culture climate as an enactment condition enabling trust to become adaptive action\. Practically, HR leaders should align explainable AI, trust\-building practices and digital norms to strengthen workforce agility\.

## [Formación inicial docente: estado del arte sobre teoría\-práctica y construcción de competencias profesionales](../publications/e1ced57acf17eac28dff.md)

Linda Luz Lee; Alejandra Dalila Rico Molano

Este artículo presenta un estado del arte sobre la formación inicial docente, con énfasis en la relación teoría\-práctica y el desarrollo de competencias requeridas para el ejercicio profesional\. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa de carácter documental a partir del análisis de 74 artículos publicados entre 2020 y 2025, indexados en Scopus y ScienceDirect\. La información fue sistematizada mediante una Matriz de Resumen Analítico de Investigación \(RAI\) y analizada mediante análisis temático e interpretación hermenéutica\. Los resultados se organizaron en cinco dimensiones: la dialéctica teoría\-práctica y el tercer espacio; la mentoría, tutoría y modelación cognitiva; las tecnologías de innovación y los simuladores; las competencias socioemocionales y el bienestar docente; y la competencia digital crítica\. La literatura evidencia un desplazamiento desde modelos centrados en la aplicación de conocimientos hacia perspectivas que conciben la formación docente como un proceso situado, colaborativo y de construcción compartida del conocimiento profesional\. Se identifica la necesidad de fortalecer la articulación universidad\-escuela, la mentoría como modelación explícita, el bienestar como dimensión estructural y el desarrollo de competencias digitales desde una perspectiva crítica\. Se concluye que la formación inicial docente requiere superar la separación entre teoría y práctica y avanzar hacia un ecosistema formativo basado en la corresponsabilidad institucional\.

## [Dynamic Clearance Strategies for Highly Perishable FMCG Products: A Stochastic Dual\-Channel Approach for Cleaner Logistics and Supply Chain](../publications/e1d0fa7aec506dc7959a.md)

Partheeb Mostafiz; Debolina Debnath; Nazla Faiza

Abstract In the fast\-moving consumer goods \(FMCG\) industry, there are many difficulties in managing highly perishable products, resulting in high food waste and financial losses\. In this study, the common “oversupply undersupply” problem of 120\-hour shelf\-life products have been explored and a dual channel “Near Food Channel” \(NFC\) clearance strategy is recommended\. We develop a two\-step simulation optimization approach\. A Stochastic Mixed Integer Non\-Linear Programming \(SMINLP\) model with Sample Average Approximation \(SAA\) is formulated in GAMS\. This model computes the mathematically optimum Protection Level \(PL\)\. Since it is known that there are some limitations of the continuous models in capturing the discrete consumer behavior, these values were taken and fine\-tuned using Discrete Event Simulation \(DES\) using Rockwell Arena 14\.0 software\. Empirical stochastic inputs like a Freshness Decay Penalty \( = max \(0\.1, N \(0\.72, 0\.05\)\)\) and Price Elasticity \( = max \(0\.1, N \(2\.85, 0\.05\)\)\) were incorporated to study the probability of fresh and clearance channel conversions\. The results indicate a 100% Waste Mitigation Efficiency \(\) for all tested inventory levels \(1,700\-3,000 units\) when an aging inventory is being routed at a critical time \(72 hours\) using dynamic markdown strategies\. This framework cuts down on physical waste, saves the profits of distributors \(18,623 – 19,426 BDT profit compared to \-11,300 BDT loss in conventional operations at =3000\)\. Also, there is no wasted material left, so the typical 1\-3% wastage allowance that manufacturers offer distributors is not needed\. It&\#x27;s a win\-win\-win situation: reduced food waste, increased profits, and a healthier, more sustainable food supply chain\.

## [Dati e trasformazione digitale dell’istruttoria processuale](../publications/e1d9ac09cfa5825a5f48.md)

Adriana Ciafardoni

This paper aims to analyze the changes in the administrative judge&\#x27;s investigative powers in light of the progressive digital transformation of public administration\. Starting from the centrality of the preliminary investigation as a place to rebalance information asymmetries between the parties, the paper examines the impact of the digitalization of evidence in the trial, with regard, on the one hand, to the introduction and evaluation of data as evidence and, on the other, to the possibility of using artificial intelligence in the preliminary investigation phase\.

## [P2TPO: Structure\-Aligned Page\-to\-Token Credit Assignment for Full\-Page Document Parsing](../publications/e1ef630e90a221f88a8f.md)

Yong Zu; Ninghua Yang; Zezhong Tan; Xinhong Ma; Ziqiang Dong; Yang Yang

End\-to\-end full\-page document parsing must preserve the content and structure of heterogeneous elements, yet otherwise accurate outputs can contain local errors and omissions\. A single page\-level advantage does not explicitly identify which elements differ in quality across sampled outputs or where their errors occur\. We introduce Page\-to\-Token Policy Optimization \(P2TPO\), a structure\-aligned credit\-assignment framework that operates on full\-page policy trajectories\. Reference\-element alignment first associates block\-level quality contrasts with generated spans\. Unified Anchor Pricing \(UAP\) incorporates matched and missing element outcomes and provides feedback relative to a fixed quality ceiling when sampled outputs receive identical but imperfect scores for a reference element\. Within matched blocks, Span Credit Redistribution \(SCR\) redistributes existing block credit according to aligned correct and erroneous spans, using boundary proxies for within\-block omissions while preserving the total block\-derived advantage across its tokens\. Under a fixed\-weight additive page utility, we show that element\-indexed contrasts retain local quality differences that page\-level aggregation can cancel out\. In the main experimental comparison, P2TPO outperforms all evaluated policy optimization baselines in seed\-averaged scores on each of the six document parsing benchmarks\. Additional experiments demonstrate gains across model scales and initializations\.

## [DIGITAL MATURITY OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: A METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH TO ASSESSMENT](../publications/e1fde6ef5a2b0a790180.md)

Oleksandr Diachenko

The article substantiates a methodological approach to assessing the digital maturity of public administration in environmental protection and natural resource management\. Digital maturity is interpreted not as the number of electronic services but as the institutional capacity to use data, interoperable registers, geospatial technologies, analytical models and digital participation channels throughout the environmental policy cycle\. A seven\-dimensional model is proposed, covering institutional and strategic governance; data and interoperability; digital\-by\-design processes; platform integration; openness and participation; predictive analytics; and cyber resilience with human oversight\. Five maturity levels and an aggregation method with a bottleneck rule are introduced to prevent strong components from concealing critical weaknesses\. An information and analytical mechanism is developed that links environmental data sources, interoperability, analytics, managerial decisions, public interaction and ex post evaluation\. Directions for applying the methodology in Ukraine are defined with regard to the EcoSystem platform, geospatial data infrastructure, the pollutant release and transfer register, digital environmental\-impact assessment and environmental\-monitoring reform\. ## [Electrical energy production forecasting with neural networks](../publications/e206b90c0c7beea1888d.md)

Sven Danko

V magistrskem delu je razvit sistem napovedovanja, ki na podlagi zgodovinskih podatkov o proizvodnji električne energije napove, koliko energije bo proizvedene v naslednjem časovnem koraku\. Podatki o električni energiji so zajeti na dejanskem fotovoltaičnem sistemu z uporabo njegovega EMS \(angl\. energy management system, slov\. sistem za upravljanje z energijo\)\. ## [Interpretable detection\-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone\-assisted microscopy](../publications/e2104fcb6696aafc536e.md)

Siriwoot Sookkhee; Marut Wongtapin; Trin Phuriyaphan; Kornkaran Tonpiriyaphong; Nitan Wachirapaet; Surapee Wasanapitanont; Jidapa Joysa; Monsicha Pongpom; Narin Lawan; Phit Upaphong; Tanaporn Wangsanut

Background The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota\-related conditions\. Existing artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota\-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework\. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram\-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece\. Methods The framework integrates object detection with image\-level classification, termed detection\-based image classification, to identify diagnostically relevant microscopic structures without requiring exhaustive enumeration of all objects\. Five diagnostic categories included vulvovaginal candidiasis \(VVC\), bacterial vaginosis \(BV\), trichomoniasis \(TV\), gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis \(GU\), and healthy vaginal condition \(HL\)\. YOLOv26, RT\-DETR and EfficientDet0 were independently trained and evaluated using 1,966 microscopic images comprising 11,069 annotated diagnostic objects\. Model explainability and computational benchmarking were assessed\. The localization quality was independently evaluated by eight clinicians and microbiologists\. Results Class\-specific analysis demonstrated that TV and GU consistently achieved the highest detection performance across all models \(mAP50 = 0\.622–0\.752\), whereas RT\-DETR demonstrated superior performance for VVC, BV, and HL\. Expert evaluation showed favorable localization, with Good/Excellent ratings in 84\.8 and 85\.1% of valid evaluations for YOLOv26 and RT\-DETR, respectively, with no significant difference between models \(OR = 0\.97; 95% CI, 0\.58–1\.61; p = 0\.895\)\. Conclusion This study presents an accurate and clinically interpretable framework that integrates microbiota\-associated conditions and sexually transmitted infections for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using conventional light microscopy\. By linking image\-level predictions to localized diagnostic morphology, the framework provides human\-verifiable AI evidence as a proof\-of\-concept prototype\. While promising for low\-cost implementation, rigorous prospective multi\-center validation is required before broad clinical deployment or autonomous diagnosis\.

## [Neurodivergence in Adulthood](../publications/e216b37ce6385e88fa9b.md)

Nina K\. Thomas

This book offers a holistic exploration of the adult neurodivergent experience\. It centres the voices and experiences of neurodivergent adults to provide an inclusive, strengths‑based model that enables understanding of neurodivergence as a natural and valuable variation of human cognition\. This accessible, affirming, and internationally relevant work is structured around the most pressing and common experiences faced by late‑diagnosed adults\. Each chapter offers a thematic focus that builds a cohesive, empowering journey from self‑discovery through to resilience and sustainable life choices\. It addresses topics helping readers to navigate late diagnosis, social contexts, professional life, and mental health and therapy\. The tone is practical but deeply human, blending research‑informed content with the lived experiences that are too often left out of professional discourse\. Combining psychological insight, practical strategies, and personal narratives, it empowers adults to understand, accept, and advocate for themselves across relationships, work environments, healthcare settings, and society at large\. Through this psychologically grounded guidance, this book offers tools for healing, self‑advocacy, and building a life that finally fits\. It is ideal for anyone who is navigating the complexities of late diagnosis, masking, burnout, and identity formation\. It also serves as a vital resource for therapists, educators, healthcare providers, and workplace leaders seeking a more compassionate and accurate understanding of neurodivergence in adulthood and the reality of grown‑up lives shaped by invisible effort and unmet needs\.

## [Agents of Conversion on the Island of Nias](../publications/e2180308578e13482c9b.md)

Bianca M\. Dinkelaar

This book explores the cultural and religious transformations that unfolded on the Indonesian island of Nias during its encounter with German missionaries in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries\. Far from a one\-sided story of conversion, it reveals a dynamic process of syncretism, where traditional Niasan worldviews and missionary Christianity collided, competed, and ultimately coalesced into a new religious form\. Drawing on untapped missionary and colonial archives, the study greatly expands the somewhat sparse corpus of scholarship on Niasan history and reframes the dominant narrative by centering Niasan voices, agency, and cultural frameworks\. It challenges assumptions about pre\-missionary Nias culture, investigates early encounters between missionaries and Niasans, which were fraught with mismatched expectations and cultural misunderstandings, and traces the emergence of a distinct Niasan Christianity—one that both subverted and surpassed missionary intentions through selective adoption, linguistic translation, and cultural resilience\. By foregrounding Niasan agency, this book challenges conventional histories of mission and conversion\. It will be of interest to scholars of religious, missionary and colonial history, World Christianity, anthropology of religion and beyond\.

## [PDBe‐SIFTS: An open‐source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search](../publications/e21bb12de30ab1cbe42a.md)

Adam Bellaiche; Preeti Choudhary; Sreenath Sasidharan Nair; Déborah Harrus; Conny Wing\-Heng Yu; Ahsan Tanweer; Genevieve L\. Evans; Stephanie W Lo; Maria J\. Martin; Jennifer R\. Fleming; Sameer S Velankar

Abstract Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy and Sequences \(SIFTS\) provides residue\-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe \(PDBe\) pipelines\. Here, PDBe\-SIFTS is presented as a fully open\-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework\. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue\-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity\. PDBe\-SIFTS is distributed as a Python package with command\-line tools for 1\) building a sequence search database, 2\) identifying the best sequence\-structure match, 3\) one\-to\-one mapping at the residue level, and 4\) generating SIFTS annotations in PDBx/mmCIF format\. Benchmarking on the complete Protein Data Bank archive showed that MMseqs2 reduced archive\-scale UniProtKB searches from hours with BLASTP to minutes, approximately 22\-36 times faster, while curated mappings were recovered at top rank in 93\.1% of cases\. The remaining discrepancies mainly involved biologically ambiguous cases such as highly conserved proteins, chimeric constructs, or closely related orthologs\. These results show that PDBe\-SIFTS enables fast mapping, improving structural coherence in residue\-level alignments while delivering the most up\-to\-date and accurate mappings, comparable to expert curation\. Tool: https://github\.com/PDBeurope/SIFTS Quick start notebook with example: https://github\.com/PDBeurope/SIFTS/tree/master/notebooks Broader audience statement Matching protein sequences to their three\-dimensional structures, and mapping annotations across both, is essential for understanding protein function, interactions, and molecular mechanisms\. This integrated view enables richer interpretation of biological data and underpins advances in drug discovery, disease research, and protein engineering\. PDBe\-SIFTS provides an open and functional framework for structure–sequence mapping, allowing researchers and databases to run, inspect, and extend these mappings locally, while benefiting from faster searches, transparent scoring, and structurally informed residue\-level alignments\. ## [Machine learning prediction of coded transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy among adults with heart failure: a systematic review and meta\-analysis](../publications/e21d6249d1b079f23b2c.md)

Zachary Cohen; Eshetu A Tefera; Rajeev Agrawal; Nicholas S\. Streicher

Abstract Background Structured electronic health record and claims data could support scalable case\-finding for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy \(ATTR\-CM\), but reported models usually predict diagnosis codes or proxy labels rather than clinically adjudicated disease\. We synthesized the performance, transportability, and clinical implications of these models in adults with heart failure\. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL/EBSCO, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar through 30 June 2026 for supervised machine\-learning classifiers trained on retrospective structured health\-record data\. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled with a bivariate random\-effects model; reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\) was pooled separately on the logit scale using Hanley\-McNeil variances, DerSimonian\-Laird random effects, and Hartung\-Knapp\-Sidik\-Jonkman confidence intervals\. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST \+ AI\. Predictive values were projected across assumed prevalence levels\. Results Seven studies contributed eight cohort evaluations \(3,658 participants; 1,841 cases\)\. All selected estimates were from random\-forest models and all study targets represented wild\-type ATTR\-CM diagnosis codes or coding\-based proxies\. Pooled sensitivity was 79\.8% \(95% CI 65\.7–89\.0%\) and specificity 73\.3% \(65\.5–79\.9%\); the summary receiver operating characteristic area was 0\.809\. Pooled reported AUROC was 0\.861 \(0\.746–0\.929\), with high heterogeneity \(I²=93\.9%\)\. Excluding the UK and German transfer evaluations yielded sensitivity 84\.2% \(75\.3–90\.3%\), specificity 73\.4% \(65\.5–80\.0%\), and AUROC 0\.892 \(0\.799–0\.945\)\. At 1% assumed prevalence, pooled performance implied a positive predictive value of 2\.9% and negative predictive value of 99\.7%\. All eight evaluations were at high overall risk of bias\. None reported empirical calibration or decision\-curve analysis\. Conclusions Random\-forest models show moderate ability to reproduce coded or proxy\-defined ATTR\-CM labels, but the evidence does not establish accurate detection of clinically confirmed disease\. Given the high risk of bias among included studies, the pooled performance estimates warrant cautious interpretation\. Their potential role is cohort enrichment or targeted case\-finding rather than stand\-alone population screening\. Prospective evaluation with a uniform adjudicated reference standard, fixed prediagnostic prediction times, calibration, and workflow\-level utility assessment is required\. Registration PROSPERO CRD420261436051\.

## [Hypothalamus and preoptic area in breeding rodent: a review](../publications/e227ebe6b9355d498a37.md)

Atifa Haseeb Ansari; Durgesh Singh; Alok Mukerjee; Sippy Singh

Rodent is a diversified group of mammals and characterized by small body, short limb, long tail and incisor teeth\. Majority of mammals fall under this category including mice and rats which are commonly used as laboratory animal\. Brain of rodent shows compartmentalization and comprises of cerebral cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus, hypothalamus and thalamus\. Among different brain regions, hypothalamus and preoptic area \(POA\) specifically are considered as the complex region responsible for sleep, thermoregulation, nest building, maternal behavior and reproductive physiology\. Rodents exhibit plasticity in terms of learning, increase in sex hormones, decline in immunity with aging, circadian rhythm drive temperature and neurotransmitter release during maturity\. Ovulatory stage in females which involves development of growth follicle and ova is marked as estrous cycle in non\-primates\. It is usually differentiated into four phase namely: proestrus, metaestrus, estrus and diestrus\. Sex steroid hormones are known to be involved in reproductive physiology\. All gonadal hormones mainly estradiol, progesterone and prolactin activity has been observed to increase in estrus female rat\. The level of cortisol and oxytocin also fluctuates during estrous cycle\. The present article attempts at highlighting reported seasonality and function of hypothalamus and POA within rodents\. ## [Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: Psychological Effects on University Teaching](../publications/e22e7a9063bd601cb64e.md)

Sergey M\. Grigoriev

Aim \. To identify GenAI‑specific psychological mechanisms through which LLMs reshape academic teaching work, and to compare effects in content creation versus assessment\. Methodology \. The study combines a transparent integrative review \(2015–2025; Scopus, WoS, PsycINFO, ERIC, RSCI; 56 sources with PRISMA‑style tracking\) with a qualitative pilot \(16 semi‑structured interviews with Russian university instructors; thematic analysis\) using an integrated JD‑R and SDT framework\. Results : GenAI acts both as a resource and a work‑redesign driver, generating AI‑specific demands: epistemic uncertainty, verification workload, trust calibration, accountability / responsibility anxiety, norm acceleration and “silent” intensification, and a role shift toward surveillance in assessment\. A domain asymmetry is found – content work is mainly burdened by hidden cognitive verification, while assessment amplifies emotional and normative risks related to fairness and conflict\. Research implications : a model linking GenAI properties to job demands / resources and basic needs \(autonomy, competence, relatedness\) is proposed; recommendations include formal time for verification, a human‑in‑the‑loop standard for high‑stakes assessment, clearer academic integrity policies, and safeguards against intensification\.

## [Self\-Building Labs](../publications/e2457b2a9223d2d331ed.md)

Jiaru Bai; Yuchi Zhao; Han Hao; Miroslav Bogdanovic; Yang Cao; Varinia Bernales; Alán Aspuru\-Guzik

Self\-driving laboratories \(SDLs\) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization\. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for\. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery\. We introduce the self\-building laboratory \(SBL\), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high\-level scientific goal\. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows\. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together\. We validate SBL&\#x27;s end\-to\-end capabilities through a real\-world quantum\-dot synthesis experiment\. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable\. Project website: https://self\-building\-labs\.github\.io/

## [A transdisciplinary AI\-based framework for usability evaluation in digital health systems](../publications/e24921cad64e6b75eb0e.md)

Akshay Madhav Deshmukh; Ricardo Chalmeta

Introduction\. As healthcare systems undergo rapid digital transformation, the usability of clinical and patient\-facing technologies has become critical to adoption, user satisfaction, and patient safety\. Traditional usability evaluation methods are limited in capturing the real\-time cognitive, emotional, and behavioural complexities of interaction in high\-stakes environments\. Method\. This study presents a transdisciplinary evaluation of an AI\-augmented usability framework for healthcare interfaces\. The framework integrates methodologies from artificial intelligence, cognitive science, usability engineering, and clinical practice, incorporating eye\-tracking analytics, machine learning\-based confusion prediction, and natural language processing \(NLP\) sentiment analysis\. Forty participants, including healthcare professionals and patients, completed standardized tasks using either traditional or AI\-enhanced evaluation methods\. Analysis\. Comparative performance across both groups was assessed using usability metrics including System Usability Scale \(SUS\) scores, task completion time, error rate, and task success rate\. AI\-based analytics—eye\-tracking data, NLP sentiment scoring, and confusion prediction models—were used to generate additional insights\. Statistical analysis confirmed significant differences in usability outcomes between groups\. Results\. The AI\-enhanced evaluation significantly outperformed traditional methods in all core usability metrics\. The machine learning model achieved 89% accuracy and an F1\-score of 0\.88\. Sentiment analysis correlated strongly with self\-reported satisfaction, and eye\-tracking highlighted areas of cognitive friction\. Conclusion\. Transdisciplinary collaboration produced a novel, adaptive usability evaluation framework that offers real\-time, emotionally aware insights\. This replicable model enhances user\-centred design and supports safer, more effective digital health technologies\.

## [Phenotypic characterization and resilience assessment of wheat genotypes under single and combined abiotic stresses](../publications/e24c5ce777ac09215c73.md)

Lei Sun; Liya Niu; Xueping Shi; Bo Jiao; 马春红; Fan Yang; Fushuang Dong; Shuo Zhou

Background Climate change and limited resources are intensifying abiotic stresses in wheat production, creating an urgent need for varieties that combine high yield with reliable performance under variable conditions\. However, selecting for yield under optimal or single\-stress conditions often fails to predict how genotypes will perform under complex, real\-world challenges\. Methods We evaluated 56 wheat genotypes under four environments: fully fertilized and irrigated \(FFI\), water deficit \(WD\), nitrogen deficit \(ND\), and combined water\-nitrogen deficit \(CWND\)\. To quantify resilience, we developed a composite D\-value index by integrating stress\-response ratios of seven agronomic traits using PCA, fuzzy membership normalization, and entropy\-weighted aggregation\. Results Both WD and ND reduced grain yield by 21–22% relative to FFI, while CWND caused a further decline \(–31%\), representing the greatest reduction among all treatments\. Stress environments fundamentally altered the relationships between key agronomic traits\. Genotype performance varied considerably across environments: XM296 maintained relatively high yield under single stresses but showed limited multi\-trait stability under combined stress; LX99 showed stable performance across diverse stresses while retaining high yield potential; in contrast, XN20 exhibited relatively high tolerance at the expense of low productivity\. Conclusions Given the environment\-dependent nature of resilience, breeding strategies should balance broad adaptation with improvements targeted at the dominant stress patterns in key production regions\. This approach will better translate genetic gains into stable yields in farmers’ fields\.

## [Designing a pluriversal foresight epistemology and schematic, an essay](../publications/e24dc698bb4967273d50.md)

Raphaële Bidault\-Waddington

This article emerges from a reflection on how current global transitions and paradigm shift \(the Anthropocene, Artificial Intelligence revolution and post\-colonial era being some of its markers\) impact conventional western epistemologies; could it be possible, in the more open field of futures research, to explore an innovative pluralistic epistemological position? An academic research project on futurescaping , which includes an experiment on the future of museums, i\.e\. organizations deeply impacted by these transitions, becomes a context to engage an investigation shared in this article—following a presentation at the WFSF 26th Conference 2025, Stellenbosch University, Cape Town\. The method consists in revisiting and continuing the post\-structural and decolonial approach of foresight epistemology developed by Inayatullah \[ 1 \] in his seminal essay Deconstructing Reconstructing the Future published in 1990, which already highlighted the limits of western epistemologies\. Each of the three reviewed epistemology categories \(predictive\-positivist, cultural\-hermeneutic, and critical\-post\-structural\) is confronted with the current critical challenges mentioned before and enriched by new theoretical inputs to bridge and weave western and non\-western knowledge towards the design of what could be a pluriversal epistemology\. Its conceptual architecture takes the shape of a foundational schematic opening space to scape and constructed a plurality of perspectives on five levels of reality: Onto \(ontologies\), Micro \(social uses\), Meso \(territories\), Macro \(planet\), and Cosmo \(worldviews\)\. Behind the deconstruction of western, modernist, and post\-modernist philosophies of knowledge and the reconstruction of a relevant and equitable pluralism, appears a rising and important political epistemology discussion, scholars of all disciplines should pay more attention to\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA ARQUITETURA: TRANSFORMAÇÕES NOS SOFTWARES E NO PROCESSO DE PROJETO](../publications/e24e78160e60d9595354.md)

Luís Daniel Casagrande; Lauro André Ribeiro

O uso de computadores transformou profundamente o processo de projeto arquitetônico\. Com a consolidação do BIM, os modelos passaram a integrar informações geométricas e construtivas, favorecendo a colaboração entre diferentes disciplinas\. Mais recentemente, a inteligência artificial \(IA\) incorporou recursos capazes de reconhecer padrões, analisar dados e gerar alternativas, especialmente nas fases de concepção e projeto esquemático \(Jang, Roh e Lee, 2025\)\. Apesar de seu potencial, a IA deve ser compreendida como ferramenta de apoio, e não como substituta da atuação profissional\. Imagens e alternativas geradas automaticamente não constituem projetos executáveis, pois aspectos como dimensões, estrutura, instalações, acessibilidade, legislação e sistemas construtivos ainda dependem da análise do arquiteto\. Atualmente, recursos de geração de imagens, análise de dados, criação de alternativas e automação já estão presentes em softwares utilizados profissionalmente\. Essa expansão também é observada na prática dos escritórios\. Segundo o Royal Institute of British Architects \(RIBA\), 74% dos escritórios participantes de seu levantamento de 2026 utilizavam IA em alguma etapa dos projetos, frente a 59% em 2025 \(RIBA, 2026\)\. Assim, a incorporação da IA aos softwares de arquitetura representa uma mudança significativa na maneira de pensar, representar e avaliar projetos, tornando a tecnologia cada vez mais presente na rotina profissional\.
