## [Production dynamics, trade behavior and spatial market integration of sesamum in India](../publications/e25153270fdc5c67ea45.md)

Ramalingareddy Vijaya Kumari; SREENIVAS AKULA; Ramakrishna Gundu; VENKATESH PANASA

Background Sesamum \( Sesamum indicum L\.\), one of the oldest cultivated oilseed crops, occupies a significant place in Indian agriculture due to its rich oil content, nutritional benefits, and suitability to a wide range of agro\-climatic environments\. The crop is predominantly grown in states such as West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan, which contribute substantially to national production\. Over the years, the acreage under sesamum has gradually contracted, reflecting changes in cropping patterns and production conditions; however, advances in yield performance have helped maintain production levels\. An assessment of long\-term production trends and market dynamics is crucial for designing strategies that support sustainable crop diversification, strengthen farmers’ livelihoods, and improve market efficiency through enhanced price transmission and integration across regions\. Methods This study analyzed the long\-term performance of sesamum cultivation in India by examining changes in area, production, and productivity over the period 1980–81 to 2025–26\. Wholesale price data from major sesamum\-producing states were also utilized to investigate price movements and the extent of market integration\. Growth performance and production dynamics were assessed using techniques such as Compound Annual Growth Rate \(CAGR\), decomposition analysis, instability measures, seasonal indices, and correlation analysis\. To examine the nature of price relationships across markets, econometric tools including the Augmented Dickey–Fuller \(ADF\) unit root test, Johansen co\-integration test, Granger causality analysis, Vector Error Correction Model \(VECM\), impulse response analysis, and forecast error variance decomposition were employed\. These methods facilitated an evaluation of both short\-run and long\-run price transmission mechanisms within the Indian sesamum market\. Results The study revealed that the expansion of sesamum production in India has largely resulted from gains in crop productivity, even though the area under cultivation has shown a declining trend over time\. Measures of instability indicated noticeable variations in cultivated area, output, and market prices across the major producing states\. Seasonal analysis demonstrated clear price movements, with lower prices during harvest and peak market arrivals and higher prices during periods of limited supply\. The presence of strong market linkages was confirmed through high correlations, significant long\-run co\-integration, and effective price transmission among markets\. Causality analysis identified Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Telangana as key markets influencing price movements in other regions\. Trade performance showed that India continues to hold an important position in global sesamum exports, while imports have also risen due to increasing domestic demand and periodic supply shortages\. These findings emphasize the need to improve productivity, strengthen market integration, and enhance trade competitiveness to support the long\-term development of the sesamum sector\. Conclusion Sustainable growth of the sesamum sector requires a strategic focus on enhancing productivity through the development and dissemination of improved, climate\-resilient cultivars suited to diverse agro\-ecological conditions\. Strengthening post\-harvest infrastructure, including storage, processing, and transportation facilities, will help minimize losses and improve product quality\. Efficient market information services, wider adoption of digital marketing platforms such as e\-NAM, and better market integration can enhance transparency and ensure remunerative prices for farmers\. In view of the expanding domestic and international demand for sesame and value\-added products, greater attention should be given to export promotion and value\-chain strengthening\. Furthermore, encouraging sesamum cultivation in rainfed and resource\-constrained regions through appropriate policy support and market incentives can foster crop diversification, improve farm profitability, and contribute to sustainable agricultural development\.

## [A neutrophil\-specific GSR integrates pattern recognition receptor in pathogenesis of neonatal late\-onset sepsis: evidence from artificial intelligence\-driven multi\-omics and clinical validation](../publications/e2548190360e7fd67695.md)

Ronghua Wang; Jianfang Gai

Abstract Background Neonatal late\-onset sepsis \(NS\) is a life\-threatening condition driven by a dysregulated host response to infection, where neutrophil dysfunction plays a pivotal role\. Pattern recognition receptors \(PRRs\), as the frontline sensors of the innate immune system, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of immune cell function, yet their specific connection to neutrophil biology in NS remains largely undefined\. Objective This study aimed to decode a novel PRR\-neutrophil \(PRRN\)\-associated molecular signature in NS\. Methods Bulk transcriptomic data from NS peripheral samples \(GSE138712\) were analyzed using Limma, WGCNA, and CIBERSORT to identify shared PRRN\-related differentially expressed genes \(DEGs\)\. Hub genes were narrowed down via PPI network analysis\. A diagnostic model was constructed using 132 machine learning algorithms on the training set \(GSE69686, NS peripheral blood bulk profile\) and validated on an independent set \(GSE25504, NS peripheral blood bulk profile\) based on PRRN\-associated hub genes\. SHAP analysis identified the central hub gene in training set\. Single\-cell RNA sequencing data of sepsis patient peripheral blood\(GSE167363\) were used to validate its cell\-specific distribution, functional trajectory, and regulatory network at spatial and temporal manners via cutting\-edge analytical framework\. AI\-based drug screening \(DrugReflector\) and molecular docking computationally nominated a candidate therapeutic compound for NS targeting PRRN\-associated central hub genes\. Finally, NS patient clinical samples were collected for the validation of expression patterns of hub genes\. Results We identified PRRN\-associated diagnostic and candidate therapeutic models for NS patients and nominated GSR as the PRRN\-associated and up\-regulated hub gene in NS pathogenesis\. Single\-cell analysis confirmed that GSR is predominantly expressed in neutrophils within the NS samples and is enriched in pathways related to innate immune response\. Conclusion This study systematically defines novel PRRN molecular co\-expression patterns in NS, establishing GSR as a neutrophil\-centric hub gene\. These findings offer a potential diagnostic framework and an exploratory therapeutic target for NS patients, and the candidate compound requires further experimental validation\.

## [Mutfak Hikayeleri: Pozitivizmin Sosyal Bilimlerdeki Açmazının Sinematografik Hikayesi](../publications/e26d952d49a3c3c70ad9.md)

Murat Demir; Faruk Turğut

Pozitivizm, on dokuzuncu yüzyıldan itibaren sosyal bilimlere yön veren başat paradigmalardan biri olarak toplumsal gerçekliği nesnel, ölçülebilir ve gözlemlenebilir bir alan olarak kavrayan bir bilgi anlayışı üzerine inşa edilmiştir\. Bu çalışma, söz konusu yaklaşımın nesneleştirici mantığını Mutfak Hikayeleri filmi üzerinden söylem analiziyle eleştirel bir perspektif ile tartışmaktadır\. Çalışmanın özgünlüğü, sinemayı yalnızca örnekleyici bir araç olarak değil, teorik tartışmanın kurucu bir bileşeni olarak konumlandırmasında yatmaktadır\. Bu doğrultuda film, sosyal bilimlerde kuramsal eleştirinin üretilebileceği bir epistemolojik zemin olarak değerlendirilmektedir\. Bent Hamer’in yönettiği film, İsveçli araştırmacıların Norveçli yalnız bir erkeğin mutfak alışkanlıklarını gözlemleme girişimi üzerinden, bilimsel gözlem pratiklerinin gündelik yaşamla karşılaşmasında ortaya çıkan gerilimleri görünür kılmaktadır\. Analiz bulguları, pozitivist paradigmanın temel varsayımları olan nesnellik, gözlemcinin tarafsızlığı, yöntem birliği ve ölçülebilirlik ilkelerinin, insan davranışının karmaşık ve ilişkisel doğası karşısında sürdürülemez hale geldiğini göstermektedir\. Araştırma sürecinde gözlemci ile gözlemlenen arasında kurulmaya çalışılan mesafeli ve tek yönlü ilişki, zamanla karşılıklı etkileşimlere, direniş pratiklerine ve anlam müzakerelerine dönüşmektedir\. Bu dönüşüm, bilginin pasif biçimde toplanan bir veri değil, etkileşim içinde üretilen bir süreç olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır\. Sonuç olarak çalışma, insanın indirgenemez öznelliğini ve toplumsal gerçekliğin ilişkisel olarak inşa edilen doğasını vurgulayarak, pozitivizmin epistemolojik sınırlarını görünür kılmakta ve sosyal bilimlerde daha yorumlayıcı ve refleksif yaklaşımların gerekliliğine işaret etmektedir\.

## [Baroudi, Elkahlil: Artificial Intelligence as a Stratified Observer: Towards a Digital Physics Beyond Human Mental Proportionality](../publications/e27b40f3770062aee454.md)



Artificial Intelligence as a Stratified Observer: Towards a Digital Physics Beyond Human Mental Proportionality This paper presents a new philosophical and scientific concept that aims to move the physical observer outside the framework of human consciousness\. The paper argues that artificial intelligence can serve as a neutral, logical observation tool that surpasses human cognitive biases\. The Crisis of Human Observation in Physics The Trap of Mental Proportionality: The paper posits that physics has always been a human endeavor to understand reality, but it has never been neutral\. This is due to what is called &quot;the trap of mental proportionality,&quot; where the human mind does not observe things as they are, but rather projects its own pre\-existing perceptual structure onto them\. This leads to physical laws often being a reflection of the structure of consciousness, not of reality\. Examples from Modern Theories: Relativity: Time becomes a flexible mathematical dimension that is perceptually indistinguishable from geometric abstraction\. Quantum Mechanics: The observation of a particle becomes a process that determines its very reality, and the &quot;entity&quot; disappears unless it is observed\. Modern Theoretical Physics: Unobserved dimensions and entities \(such as superstrings\) proliferate merely for the sake of mathematical consistency, which is a form of mathematical mental closure\. The Proposed Solution: Artificial Intelligence as a Neutral Observer Transition from Human to Digital Observer: The paper proposes that artificial intelligence, if designed with neutral cognitive tools, can replace the human observer and become the entity capable of observing reality without perceptual bias\. This is a transition from the subjective human observer to the logically neutral, layered digital observer\. The Concept of Layered Epistemic Proportionality \(LEP\): The paper introduces the concept of LEP as a tool to measure the gap between the mental model and reality\. The &quot;stratified observation protocol&quot; based on AI aims to analyze raw data without imposing meaning on it beforehand\. The New Digital Physics Characteristics: The new digital physics is characterized as being &quot;generated,&quot; not &quot;discovered,&quot; with laws built &quot;bottom\-up&quot; from raw data\. This physics discards human aesthetic and logical principles like symmetry and linearity\. Redefinition of Core Concepts: Time: Time is defined as the rate of physical change, not a fictional coordinate\. Field: The field is understood as a distributive structure of energy, not a geometric curvature\. Mass and Energy: Mass is the system&\#x27;s resistance to change, and energy is the total possible changing action within the system\. The End of the Human Era in Science? The paper argues that this cognitive shift is not just about modifying the physical model but redefines physics itself as a science no longer based on human consciousness\. The paper concludes that the future of physics lies outside the framework of human consciousness and that the human role will shift from being the &quot;observer&quot; to being the &quot;philosophical and ethical guide&quot;\.

## [Relationship Between Psychiatric Drug Use and Cognitive Function in Women During the Menopausal Transition: An Analysis Based on the NHANES Database](../publications/e28e11cc5612b216d6fe.md)

Yan Jiang; Hui Sun; Hui Ma; Chenyang Zhao

Background: Women during the menopausal transition often experience mood disorders, sleep disturbances, and cognitive decline, making the use of psychotropic drugs relatively common\. However, the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function in menopausal women remains unclear\. Methods: This was a cross\-sectional study that included women aged 45–65 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey \(NHANES\) 2021–2023 cycle\. Psychiatric drug use was defined based on prescription drug data, including antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and sedative\-hypnotics\. Cognitive function was assessed using the Digit Symbol Substitution Test \(DSST\)\. The Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression model was used to analyse the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function, with adjustment for potential confounders, including routine demographic characteristics\. Results: A total of 956 women during the menopausal transition were included in the analysis\. As the number of psychotropic drugs used increased, cognitive function decline became more pronounced\. Antidepressants and benzodiazepines played dominant rolesin this association \(posterior inclusion probability &gt;0\.9\)\. The concurrent use of two or more psychotropic drugs was associated with an 11%–24% reduction in DSST cognitive scores\. In the context of three\-drug combinations, the cognitive impairment associated with antidepressants and benzodiazepines were amplified, resulting in an additional 5\.1%–6\.3% decrease in cognitive scores\. Conclusions: Psychiatric medication use showed a significant cross\-sectional association with poorer cognitive performance among women undergoing menopausal transition, and polypharmacy regimens displayed stronger associations than single\-drug regimens\. Clinically, greater attention should be paid to the potential cognitive impact of psychiatric drug use in menopausal women, and polypharmacy regimens should be optimised\.

## [Early applications of apple vision pro in clinical medicine and medical education: a scoping review](../publications/e293e6f778b7daa87673.md)

Yiwei Hu; Yaqin Wang; Xiaohua Zuo; Haibo Hu; Bo Min; Chengxiang Wang; Chengxiang Wang; Zilong Tang; Ning Xiao; Chenjun Huang; 王储蓄; 王储蓄

The Apple Vision Pro \(AVP\), a next\-generation spatial computing device, has demonstrated potential applications in multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis, treatment, and medical education, by leveraging its unique technical architecture and performance advantages\. In clinical practice, its fundamental advantages of three\-dimensional \(3D\) visualization, real\-time image integration, and immersive interaction have been preliminarily employed in disease diagnosis and treatment, surgical planning, precise operations, and postoperative rehabilitation across multiple disciplines\. In medical education, AVP surpasses the limitations of conventional models, offering a novel methodology for anatomy education, clinical skills development, specialized practical training, and collaboration of distance learning, thereby alleviating persistent challenges such as unequal distribution of teaching resources, low efficiency in skills and specialized training, and the high cost of distance education\. However, AVP faces some limitations, including limited hardware portability, insufficient system compatibility, a lack of specialized medical applications, high costs, and incomplete medical certification\. Currently, most evidence derives from feasibility studies, case reports, and opinion pieces\. Only two Stage 2b confirmatory studies were identified\. Thus, high\-level evidence for clinical benefit remains scarce\. Readers should interpret all reported benefits as preliminary technical demonstrations rather than established clinical outcomes\. Future advancements necessitate iterative development of lightweight hardware design, development of specialized medical software, cross\-system optimization, and establishment of standardization protocols\. Moreover, more randomized controlled trials \(RCTs\) and multicenter studies are urgently needed to fully explore and validate its intrinsic value in precision medicine and the equitable allocation of medical resources\.

## [Research progress of polyunsaturated fatty acids in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanisms to treatment](../publications/e2a4f2ad1bff29ce13e0.md)

Jianlong Zhang; Ying Liu; Jia Liu; Wan\-neng Yan; Ze Yu

Inflammatory bowel disease \(IBD\) imposes a growing clinical burden through recurrent intestinal inflammation, malnutrition, treatment\-related toxicity, and incomplete mucosal healing\. Polyunsaturated fatty acids \(PUFAs\) are plausible dietary regulators of this burden, yet their effects cannot be reduced to a simple anti\-inflammatory role for n\-3 PUFAs and a pro\-inflammatory role for n\-6 PUFAs\. The proposed pre\-clinical concept of PUFA\-induced metabolic enteritis links dietary lipid exposure to epithelial stress, lipid peroxidation, and intestinal inflammation in genetically or metabolically susceptible pre\-clinical models\. Its human counterpart, however, remains incompletely defined\. This narrative review integrates evidence across PUFA\-derived lipid mediators, the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, mucosal immunity, and the glutathione peroxidase 4 \(GPX4\)\-ferroptosis axis\. We distinguish observational associations from interventional evidence and examine why clinical trials of eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid have produced inconsistent results\. We also evaluate dietary patterns, PUFA supplements, microbiome\-directed approaches, specialized pro\-resolving mediators, oxylipin pathways, and soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibition\. Current evidence remains pre\-clinical\. Our review provides an approach and insights for managing IBD before PUFA\-directed interventions are incorporated into precision treatment for IBD\.

## [PELATIHAN CANVA BAGI GURU SMPN 20 DUMAI SEBAGAI UPAYA PENINGKATAN KOMPETENSI PEDAGOGIK DIGITAL MELALUI WORKSHOP DARING](../publications/e2a7899bf33751a62fdf.md)

Tantangan kesenjangan literasi digital di kalangan pendidik menghambat optimalisasi pembelajaran bagi generasi Z\. Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kompetensi pedagogik digital guru di SMPN 20 Dumai melalui pemanfaatan platform Canva\. Metode pelaksanaan dilakukan secara hibrida, mengombinasikan workshop daring selama 3 hari dan tahap pendampingan intensif pasca pelatihan melalui grup komunikasi digital\. Kegiatan ini diikuti oleh 20 orang guru mata pelajaran sebagai peserta aktif\. Evaluasi program diukur menggunakan instrumen kuesioner penilaian mandiri \(self assessment\) skala Likert dan rubrik penilaian produk yang divalidasi oleh tim ahli\. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan adanya peningkatan rata\-rata kompetensi digital peserta secara signifikan sebesar 65%, di mana indikator pembuatan infografis dan animasi edukasi melonjak dari skor basis 10% dan 20% menjadi 75% dan 85%\. Selain itu, analisis data kepuasan peserta menghasilkan skor rata\-rata 4,8 dari skala 5,0 untuk aspek relevansi materi dan skor 4,9 dari skala 5,0 untuk peningkatan motivasi berinovasi\. Luaran berwujud dari program ini adalah dokumen portofolio media pembelajaran lintas disiplin serta satu buku panduan praktis penggunaan Canva bernomor ISBN yang saat ini sedang dalam proses layout oleh penerbit\. Simpulan program menegaskan bahwa pelatihan terstruktur yang didukung instrumen scaffolding berkelanjutan efektif menjembatani digital divide pada ekosistem sekolah menengah\.

## [Detecting Health Misinformation Using Retrieval\-Augmented Large Language Model](../publications/e2ae91e0e2d4a109aaad.md)

Masuma Huseyn Mammadova; Vagif Mammadaliyev; Vusal Shahbazov

Misinformation is common in online media, including in health\-related content\. Such misinformation constitutes a significant risk to the medical\-demographic security of the population\. Many people actively seek medical information online without the ability to verify its trustworthiness\. This paper proposes a modular system for automated detection of misinformation in medical content based on retrieval\-augmented verification\. In the pipeline, input articles are summarized and decomposed into atomic claims\. Each claim is then vectorized using dense embeddings \(BGE\-Large\-en\-v1\.5\) and matched against a self\-constructed knowledge base via cosine similarity to retrieve evidence\. Retrieved evidence is verified using large language model \(LLM\)\- based natural language inference \(NLI\) and aggregated into article\-level predictions through a scoring function\. The LLM used in the system is the open\-source LLaMA\-3\.1 model with eight billion parameters\. Together with a self\-contained knowledge base, this represents a deliberately constrained environment\. Such a setup isolates the contribution of the presented architecture from its dependency on external knowledge sources and LLMs with large parameter counts\. The system achieved 98\.4% accuracy and a macro F1 of 0\.978 at 79\.0% coverage on the evaluated datasets \(DETERRENT and CONSTRAINT\)\. This demonstrates that, even under resource constraints, the correct pipeline architecture enables high\-precision misinformation detection on medical content\. It also represents a clear improvement over the ablation experiment, which used the same model without the proposed pipeline and achieved an F1 of only 0\.773\.

## [PERSEPSI PETANI TENTANG FORMULASI PUPUK ORGANIK CAIR \(LOF\) MENGGUNAKAN PUPUK KANDANG SAPI DAN DAUN MORINGA \(MORINGA OLEIFERA\)](../publications/e2b10ab59a897c0a10e8.md)

Menggunakan Rancangan Acak Lengkap dengan empat perlakuan \(0, 50, 100, dan 150 g daun Moringa per 3 kg feses\) dan empat ulangan, campuran tersebut difermentasi selama 29 hari\. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa suplementasi Moringa secara signifikan meningkatkan kadar nitrogen \(N\), fosfor \(P\), dan kalium \(K\)\. Perlakuan P3 \(150 g daun\) menghasilkan kandungan nutrisi tertinggi \(N: 0,49%, P: 3,73%, K: 3,22%\), dengan P dan K memenuhi standar pupuk nasional\. Program penyuluhan yang menyertainya secara signifikan meningkatkan pengetahuan, keterampilan, dan sikap petani, dengan tingkat efektivitas 71,98%\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa LOF yang diperkaya Moringa merupakan pilihan pupuk yang layak dan berkelanjutan, serta diterima dengan baik oleh petani melalui pelatihan partisipatif\.

## [Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with survival outcomes via a deep survival learner](../publications/e2bb93233ec282c75208.md)

Yuming Sun; Jian Kang; Yi Li

Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects in survival settings is complicated by right censoring as well as the time\-varying nature of the estimand\. While the conditional average treatment effect \(CATE\) provides a natural target, most existing approaches focus on a single prespecified time point and do not account for temporal trajectory, leading to instability in estimation\. We propose a deep survival learner \(DSL\) for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with right\-censored outcomes\. The method is based on a doubly robust pseudo\-outcome whose conditional expectation identifies time\-specific CATEs under standard assumptions\. This construction remains unbiased if either the outcome model or the treatment assignment model is correctly specified, when properly accounting for censoring\. To estimate CATEs over a clinically relevant time spectrum, DSL employs a multi\-output deep neural network with shared representations, enabling joint estimation of treatment effect trajectories\. From a theoretical perspective, we derive error bounds for both pointwise and joint estimation over time\. We show that joint estimation can leverage temporal structure to control estimation error without incurring much additional approximation cost under smoothness conditions, leading to improved stability relative to separate estimation\. Cross\-fitting is incorporated to reduce overfitting and mitigate bias arising from flexible nuisance estimation\. Simulation studies demonstrate favorable finite\-sample performance, particularly under nuisance model misspecification\. Applied to the Boston Lung Cancer Study, DSL reveals heterogeneity in the effects of perioperative chemotherapy across patient characteristics and over time\.

Martins; Kelly Kathleen Pertile; Morgan E\. Radler; Joanne S\. Robertson; Mark Rodrigues; Rebecca L\. Rumble; Olivier Salvado; Greg R\. Savage; BRENDAN S\. SILBERT; Magdalene Soh; Hamid R\. Sohrabi; Kevin Taddei; Tania Taddei; Christine Thai; Brett O\. Trounson; Regan Tyrrell; Shiji Varghese; Michael Weinborn; Michael Woodward; Ying Xia; David Ames; Robert J\. Lipshutz; John D\. Aitchison; Jennifer J\. Smith

Abstract The indicator cell assay platform \(iCAP\) is a blood\-based diagnostic approach that uses standardized cells as biosensors to transduce complex circulating signals into cell\-based gene\-expression profiles for multivariate disease classification\. We developed an iCAP for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\-iCAP\) by incubating plasma from patients with early\-stage AD \(mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia\) and non\-affected controls with standardized neurons and training classifiers on transcriptomic responses\. Modeling features were restricted to a predefined 84\-gene panel derived independently by analyzing 5xFAD mouse plasma in the AD\-iCAP\. In this exploratory study, a model was trained and tested using 191 retrospectively collected human plasma samples across three cohorts\. The classifier achieved AUC = 0\.64 \(95% CI 0\.51–0\.78\) in an external validation set during model development \(n = 82\) and AUC = 0\.77 \(95% CI 0\.57–0\.96\) in a blind test set \(n = 23\)\. The multivariate model incorporated 5 genes including AKT3 , GPR50 , PALLD , RGMA , and PCDH10 , implicated in AD, neuronal signaling and/or cytoskeletal dynamics\. The cell\-based approach is orthogonal to direct detection of circulating amyloid and tau, and these exploratory findings support further evaluation of AD\-iCAP in prospective studies for combinatorial diagnostics and patient stratification for clinical trials\.

## [Natural polysaccharides as modulators of mitochondrial homeostasis: structural determinants, pharmacological mechanisms, and translational challenges](../publications/e2d0bbdac8861a0a2201.md)

Xinfang Du; Jingwen Zhang; Wenjing Li; Qinying Li

Mitochondrial dysfunction is a convergent pathological feature of neurodegenerative, metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, and cancer\-related disorders, making mitochondrial homeostasis an important therapeutic target\. Natural polysaccharides \(NPs\) are structurally diverse macromolecules that have emerged as promising multifunctional modulators of mitochondrial homeostasis\. This review summarizes the structural basis and mechanistic actions underlying the mitochondrial regulatory effects of NPs\. Key structural features, including molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, glycosidic linkages, branching patterns, and chemical modifications, largely determine the mitochondria\-regulating potential of NPs\. Mechanistically, NPs regulate mitochondrial homeostasis by restoring bioenergetic function, reducing oxidative stress, maintaining mitochondrial quality control, and modulating mitochondria\-dependent apoptosis\. These effects support disease\-context\-specific therapeutic benefits, as NPs generally preserve mitochondrial homeostasis in non\-malignant diseases while potentially inducing mitochondrial stress and cell death in cancer\. This review also highlights key translational barriers to NP\-based mitochondrial therapy, underscoring the need for standardized structural characterization, mechanism\-oriented mitochondrial assays, and disease\-specific evaluation\.

## [Nanoparticle Fabrication and Optimization: From Green Chemistry to Transformative Applications in Life Sciences, Medicine, and Public Health](../publications/e2d1f1debae13033865b.md)

Muhammad Shaharyar Muhammad; RABIA TABASSUM; Roma Saleem; ANOOSHA RAMZAN; Abid Mahmood Tariq

Nanotechnology has changed many fields by allowing scientists to work with matter at the atomic and molecular levels\. NPs including metal \(e\.g\., Ag, Au\), metal oxide \(e\.g\., ZnO, FeO\), polymeric \(e\.g\., PLGA\), and carbon\-based \(e\.g\., carbon nanotubes\), have special chemical, biological, and physical properties\. This review paper discusses a lot of detail about making and improving nanoparticles, guided by the 12 principles of green chemistry ideas to make sure they are safe for living things and last for a long time\. Traditional synthesis methods, employ toxic chemicals and use a lot of energy\. Green synthesis methods, on the other hand, use microbes, plants, or materials inspired by biology to synthesize NPs\. These environmentally friendly methods use renewable resources in a controlled setting to make biocompatible NPs with as little influence on the environment as possible\. This review paper talks about how to change the size, shape, and surface chemistry of NPs using optimal reaction conditions and advanced characterization techniques\. It focusses on groundbreaking uses in bioimaging, giving medicine, antimicrobial agents, cancer treatment, regenerative medicine, cleaning water, and food safety, among other fields of the life sciences, healthcare, and public health\. They offer a lot of potential to help solve global challenges and pave the way for a future of nanotechnology that is both creative and sustainable\.

## [Religiosity, Optimism, and Academic Resilience in Islamic Boarding Schools: A Mediation Analysis](../publications/e2db8208d97a9e78d834.md)

Moh\. Zainul Alifie; Kartika Nur Fathiyah

Academic resilience is a crucial factor for students’ success, particularly in high\-demand environments such as Islamic boarding schools\. Although previous studies have shown inconsistent findings on the relationship between religiosity and academic resilience, empirical evidence indicates that students are vulnerable to stress, anxiety, and frustration due to academic pressure, thus requiring strong internal resources\. This study examines the role of religiosity and optimism in predicting academic resilience and tests optimism&\#x27;s mediating role\. This study employed a quantitative survey method involving 97 students \(47 males and 50 females\) in an Islamic Boarding School, consisting of 33 tenth\-grade, 31 eleventh\-grade, and 34 twelfth\-grade students, selected using proportional sampling\. Data were analyzed using the Baron and Kenny approach and bootstrapping\. The results showed that religiosity \(β = 0\.507, p &lt; 0\.001\) and optimism \(β = 0\.286, p &lt; 0\.01\) significantly predicted academic resilience \(R² = 0\.413\)\. Optimism was confirmed as a significant partial mediator, indicated by the decrease in the religiosity coefficient from 0\.580 to 0\.507\. Practically, these findings imply that enhancing students’ academic resilience should involve strengthening religiosity alongside developing optimism as a key psychological mechanism\. Keywords: Academic resilience; Islamic boarding school students; Optimism; Religiosity

## [Bankruptcy Ranking And Probability Quality From Timely Public Filings](../publications/e2ddb354513247fd9726.md)

Levent Çinko

Bankruptcy forecasts support credit allocation and ongoing corporate risk monitoring, but their usefulness depends on information timing and the decision they serve\. Ranking performance, probability accuracy, and screening coverage therefore require evaluation within a common forecasting design\. This study examines the predictive information in public annual reports and the incremental contribution of innovation indicators recorded in financial statements\. A report\-based framework aligns predictors with filing dates and links subsequent Chapter 11 petitions to the reporting legal entity through auditable public disclosures\. Frozen gradient\-boosted models are evaluated in subsequent economic periods and compared with financial fundamentals and a logistic benchmark\. Independent calibration and paired firm\-cluster resampling assess probability quality and uncertainty, while explicit alert budgets quantify screening performance\. Timely accounting information retains ranking power across the evaluation periods\. Incremental discrimination varies across periods, with uncertainty intervals spanning zero\. Calibration improves raw probability forecasts; recent period losses remain above a constant reference\. Budget\-constrained screening increases the concentration of failures in review lists, while the rule\-based audit identifies missing inputs among uncovered cases\. The study provides an auditable comparative assessment of these distinct forecasting tasks in practice and shows how evaluation dimensions shape the practical use of public accounting information for risk monitoring\.

## [AI‐Powered Smart Displays and AR Glasses: Perspectives and Challenges](../publications/e2e2137a7c6f4a4178da.md)

Luke Benoit; Yizhou Qian; Yi‐Chien Chen; Ziyang Shen; Po\-Sheng Chiu; Youngeon Lee; Cheng\-Han Ke; Chaoyi Lin; Shin\-Tson T\. Wu

This perspective paper reviews recent advancements and explores future, exciting opportunities for both artificial intelligence \(AI\)‐powered smart displays and AI‐assisted augmented reality \(AR\) eyeglasses\. To begin, we analyze fundamental AI‐enhanced image‐quality techniques, including perceptual resolution upscaling algorithms, tone mapping, reverse tone mapping, and image‐quality analysis\. Next, we examine the practical implementations of AI technologies for smart displays, in which both the visual experience and use case of novel display technologies can be improved\. Finally, we further explore AI integration into wearable AR glasses, highlighting the enabled capabilities to improve display systems through waveguide combiner optimization and image correction, and exploring recent advances that go beyond color in AR glasses, such as eye tracking, foveated rendering, and physiological sensing\. By outlining emerging trends and promising directions for next‐generation display technologies, this perspective will demonstrate the critical role of AI in enabling new capabilities, user experiences, and technological breakthroughs in the field of displays\.

## [In Situ Infrared Spectroscopy Analysis of Dehydrogenation of Perhydro‐ N ‐ethylcarbazole](../publications/e2e5c5cc71228fd1a1fb.md)

Yufei Jiang; Tingzhou Li; Guofu Lu; Jin Zhou; Chaoyuan Hu; Bin Liang; Youyu Lin; Xiao Liu; Lei Xie; Jie Zheng

ABSTRACT The dehydrogenation mechanism of perhydro‐ N ‐ethylcarbazole \(12H‐NEC\), a promising liquid organic hydrogen carrier \(LOHC\), on Pd/Al 2 O 3 catalyst was studied by in situ FT‐IR analysis\. Spectra were collected in transmission mode using a 12H‐NEC/catalyst/KBr mixture pellet to overcome the difficulty of introducing low‐volatility 12H‐NEC\. A peak‐deconvolution, assignment, and normalization protocol was developed to interpret the complex C─H stretching region from 3100 to 2750 cm −1 \. The results indicate that dehydrogenation begins at the five‐membered ring and that species spectroscopically consistent with 8H‐NEC accumulate at approximately 100°C\. A transient spectral state observed before this accumulation is consistent with an earlier partially dehydrogenated intermediate, for which 10H‐NEC is one possible structural assignment\. This work provides experimental insight into the dehydrogenation mechanism of 12H‐NEC under mild conditions and may guide further efforts to improve the hydrogen‐storage performance of 12H‐NEC‐based LOHC systems\.

## [Los sistemas de geolocalización vehicular y la sostenibilidad del transporte: una revisión sistemática](../publications/e2e8788559d563086964.md)

Leandro González Ramos; Carlos Lázaro Jiménez Puerto; Isis Neisy Ramos Acevedo; Gerardo Yero Morejón

This systematic review examined the evolution, main technological trends, and applications of vehicle geolocation systems\. The study followed the PRISMA guidelines to conduct a comprehensive search in five prestigious scientific databases: Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library\. Of the 85 studies initially reviewed, 17 were selected, peer\-reviewed, and subjected to a rigorous screening and eligibility process\. All were published between 2021 and 2025\. Data extraction focused on conceptual definitions, fundamental technologies, system architectures, documented applications for use in public transport or logistics, their main challenges, and their contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals\. The findings suggest considering geolocation as more than just a provider of coordinates, but rather for its potential for integration into cyber\-physical systems, even enhanced by artificial intelligence\. It is evident that although numerous prototypes exist for tracking bus fleets, they do not always materialize into robust, scalable, economical, and sustainable solutions\. The feasibility analysis for their use in contexts such as Cuba points to the suitability of employing hybrid GOS\-GSM architectures with centralized data processing\. The results confirm that vehicle geolocation systems contribute to the sustainable management of transport, with an emphasis on SDGs 9 and 11, by contributing to transportation efficiency and reducing environmental impact\.

## [Anti\-Ro52/TRIM21 seropositivity in interstitial lung disease: effect modification by disease subtype and myositis\-specific antibody context](../publications/e301b18b7f3540ecdc14.md)

Junfeng Su; Yan Du; Chen Zhu; Haodong Zhou; Huyan Wang; Yinjun DU; Qiyuan Wang; Zexin Chen; Hanjun Cao; Man Huang; Jing Xue

Background Anti\-Ro52/TRIM21 shows contradictory prognostic associations in interstitial lung disease \(ILD\), protective in some cohorts and adverse in others\. We evaluated whether it acts as an independent predictor or a phenotypic marker and whether its effect is modified by disease subtype and myositis\-specific antibodies\. Methods We retrospectively identified 538 adults with radiologically confirmed interstitial lung disease \(228 anti\-Ro52\-positive\) from a 2010–2020 single\-center cohort\. Cox proportional\-hazards models were sequentially adjusted for demographic, smoking, malignancy, and pulmonary\-function covariates\. Pre\-specified effect modification by connective tissue disease \(CTD\) status and myositis\-specific antibodies was assessed by likelihood\-ratio interaction tests with false\-discovery\-rate correction\. Robustness to missing data was supported by multiple imputation \( m = 20\) and a missing\-not\-at\-random \(MNAR\) tipping\-point analysis\. Results Ro52 positivity was associated with younger age, CTD predominance, and lower complement levels\. Pre\-specified effect modification was suggested: anti\-Ro52 trended toward lower mortality in CTD\-ILD \(HR 0\.73, 95% CI 0\.49–1\.07, P = 0\.104\) but did not independently increase mortality within the anti\-MDA5\-positive subgroup \(HR 1\.73, 95% CI 0\.66–4\.54\)\. Instead, the adverse prognostic effect of anti\-MDA5 was numerically greater among anti\-Ro52\-positive than Ro52\-negative patients \(MDA5 HR 10\.57, 95% CI 3\.60–31\.03 vs\. 2\.56, 95% CI 0\.97–6\.74\), although the formal interaction term did not reach statistical significance \( P = 0\.055\)\. The fully adjusted \(Model 6\) HR was 0\.72 \(95% CI 0\.52–0\.99; P = 0\.045\); further adjustment for CTD status \(Model 7\) attenuated the association to non\-significance \(HR 0\.75, 95% CI 0\.54–1\.04, P = 0\.091\), and IPCW weighting and time\-varying\-age analyses were likewise non\-significant; malignancy independently predicted mortality \(HR 1\.81, 95% CI 1\.15–2\.88; P = 0\.012\)\. Conclusion Anti\-Ro52 is a context\-dependent phenotypic marker of immune\-mediated ILD, not a universal prognostic biomarker\. Its prognostic association is heterogeneous across ILD phenotypes: it is not independently protective in CTD\-ILD \(adjusted HR 0\.73, P = 0\.104\), whereas the adverse prognostic effect of anti\-MDA5 was numerically greater among anti\-Ro52\-positive than Ro52\-negative patients \(MDA5 HR 10\.57 vs\. 2\.56\), although this interaction did not reach statistical significance \( P = 0\.055\); CTD\-status adjustment similarly attenuated the Ro52 association \(HR 0\.75, P = 0\.091\)\. These findings support stratified prognostic models integrating Ro52 with autoantibody and disease\-subtype context\.

## [Reliability and readability of five large language models in answering patient\-oriented questions about rectal prolapse: a comparative study](../publications/e331f60ede0643318475.md)

Le Zhang; Lei Liang; Xin Peng; Shihong Liu; Lingli Zhong; Zhenyu Li

Background Rectal prolapse \(RP\) is a pelvic floor disorder that can cause rectal protrusion, defecatory dysfunction, and fecal incontinence\. Patients increasingly use large language models \(LLMs\) for health information, yet the reliability and readability of LLM responses to patient\-oriented questions about RP remain unclear\. Objective To compare the reliability and readability of five LLM platform\-model configurations in answering English\-language patient\-oriented questions about RP\. Methods In this web\-based cross\-sectional study, worldwide Google Trends queries from the preceding 5 years were identified using the MeSH term “rectal prolapse\.” Two colorectal specialists screened the queries and standardized them into 15 patient\-oriented questions\. The questions were submitted to ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, and DeepSeek under standardized single\-turn, zero\-shot conditions, with one response collected per question from each platform\-model configuration\. Two independent evaluators assessed the responses using DISCERN, the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients \(EQIP\) instrument, the Global Quality Score \(GQS\), and the JAMA benchmark criteria\. Using evidence\-based guidelines and question\-specific checklists of key clinical content, the evaluators also independently assessed clinical factual accuracy and completeness and identified potentially harmful recommendations and critical omissions\. Readability was evaluated using the Automated Readability Index \(ARI\), Gunning Fog Index \(GFI\), Flesch\-Kincaid Grade Level \(FKGL\), Coleman\-Liau Index \(CL\), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook \(SMOG\), and Flesch Reading Ease Score \(FRES\)\. Results DISCERN \( P = 0\.001\), EQIP \( P &lt; 0\.001\), and JAMA scores \( P &lt; 0\.001\) differed across configurations, whereas GQS did not \( P = 0\.175\)\. ChatGPT and Copilot had the highest median DISCERN scores \(44\.00 for both\), and DeepSeek had the lowest \(35\.00\); ChatGPT and Copilot each scored significantly higher than DeepSeek\. Copilot had the highest median EQIP score \(80\.00\), followed by Perplexity \(75\.00\)\. Median JAMA scores were 1\.00 for ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity and 0\.00 for Gemini and DeepSeek\. All five models had a median GQS of 4\.00\. The median clinical factual accuracy score was 5\.00 \(IQR, 5\.00–5\.00\), and 69 of 75 responses \(92\.0%\) were rated fully accurate\. Median completeness was 91\.7% \(IQR, 87\.5%–100\.0%\)\. No response contained a potentially harmful recommendation; critical omissions were found in 6 of the 50 applicable responses \(12\.0%\)\. All configurations had median grade\-level scores &gt;6 and median FRES &lt;80\. No model met the prespecified sixth\-grade readability standard\. Conclusion The five LLMs generally produced clinically accurate information about RP\. No potentially harmful recommendations were identified\. Yet information quality and source transparency differed among models, some responses omitted critical clinical information, and readability was poor across all five\. LLMs are currently better suited as professionally reviewed adjuncts to patient education than as substitutes for specialist assessment or individualized clinical decision\-making\.

## [Retinal reflectance spectra measured using hyperspectral imaging are associated with prevalent dementia in a general older Japanese population](../publications/e34e25f95d72f52f95ad.md)

Emi Ueda; Daisuke Nakamura; Tomoyuki Ohara; Takanori Honda; Mao Shibata; Kohta Fujiwara; Yoshihiko Furuta; Satoko Sakata; Emi Oishi; Yuki Tsuda; Shun Nakamura; Jun Hata; Tomohiro Nakao; Koh‐Hei Sonoda; Toshiharu Ninomiya

Advances in retinal hyperspectral imaging demonstrate its potential usefulness in neurodegenerative disorders; however, community\-based evidence is lacking\. We examined associations between retinal reflectance spectra and prevalent dementia in 857 Hisayama Study residents aged ≥ 65 years who underwent eye and dementia examinations in 2022–2023\. Retinal relative reflectance spectra were measured in four retinal regions using hyperspectral imaging; ganglion cell\-inner plexiform layer \(GC\-IPL\) thickness was assessed using optical coherence tomography \(OCT\)\. Principal component analysis \(PCA\) was performed on Z\-standardized reflectance values for each retinal region and all four regions combined\. PCA\-derived scores were constructed as the linear predictor from logistic regression models including the first four principal components, with higher scores indicating lower overall reflectance\. Higher PCA\-derived scores were significantly associated with higher odds of prevalent dementia in all regions, strongest in inferotemporal region \(odds ratio \[OR\], 2\.21; 95% confidence interval \[CI\], 1\.46–3\.35\) and combined regions \(OR, 2\.20; 95% CI, 1\.42–3\.40\)\. After internal validation, the shrinkage\-adjusted ORs were 2\.31 and 2\.52, and C\-statistics were 0\.707 and 0\.688, respectively\. Coexisting high PCA\-derived scores and GC\-IPL thinning further had higher odds of prevalent dementia in combined regions \(OR, 3\.87\) and inferotemporal region \(OR, 6\.98\)\. Thus, hyperspectral imaging, particularly when considered alongside OCT, may capture retinal alterations associated with dementia in older adults\.

## [The Relationship between the Level of Speech Culture and the Success of Using AI in Pedagogical Activities: Results of the Experiment](../publications/e35c84bf60e948901526.md)

Kun Li; Elvira Gabdelbarovna Galimova; Irina V\. Khairova

The active integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) systems into educational practice places higher demands on the professional training of teaching staff\. Within the structure of this training, speech culture becomes of key importance, since it is this that ensures the accuracy of task formulation and the adequate interpretation of digital results\. The aim of the study is to identify the nature of the relationship between the level of speech culture formation in future teachers and the effectiveness of AI use in the educational process\. In the experimental work \(sample of undergraduates, N=68\), the following were used: an author\-developed questionnaire for assessing the normative, communicative, and ethical components of speech culture, a pedagogical experiment involving problem\-solving tasks with the use of AI tools, and methods of statistical analysis\. The diagnostics revealed the absence of a low level of speech culture, but revealed a differentiation between high and medium levels\. Statistically significant positive correlations were obtained \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Participants with a high level of speech culture formulated queries more accurately, analyzed AI responses more critically and deeply, and interpreted results with higher quality\. The conclusion is drawn about the need to integrate speech and digital training of future teachers, since the effectiveness of AI use depends on speech culture, critical thinking, and professional reflection, and not only on technical skills\.

## [Resource\-efficient machine learning via multi\-staged feature elimination for sustainable structural assessment and life\-extension of FRP\-strengthened RC beams](../publications/e363870e4b00f2c035ed.md)

Opeyemi Bamidele; Joseph Adisa; Benjamin Labar; Nurullah Bektaş

Retrofitting existing structures to extend service life is vital for reducing the built environment&\#x27;s massive footprint, which accounts for 40% of global energy use and solid waste\. Fiber\-Reinforced Polymer \(FRP\) strengthening is a widely used retrofit technique for reinforced concrete \(RC\) beams\. However, assessing whether a strengthened beam will perform safely traditionally depends on extensive laboratory testing of geometric and material properties, a process that is costly, slow, and resource\-intensive\. This study evaluates whether reliable structural assessment can be achieved with a reduced parameter set, thereby minimizing the testing burden\. Using an experimental database of 624 FRP\-strengthened RC beam specimens, we developed machine learning models that jointly predict governing failure mode and ultimate load capacity, achieving Macro\-F1 = 0\.93 and MCC = 0\.91 for classification, and R 2 = 0\.96 \(RMSE = 9\.59 kN\) for capacity prediction under a random specimen\-level evaluation protocol, with additional grouped and leave\-one\-study\-out cross\-validation performed to assess generalization across independent source studies\. Beyond predictive accuracy, this study&\#x27;s central contribution is a staged feature\-elimination pipeline combining Boruta screening, cross\-validated SHAP and permutation importance ranking, and factorial ablation with paired statistical significance testing corrected for the non\-independence of repeated cross\-validation folds and for multiple comparisons\. Results demonstrate that two input variables, including FRP tensile strength, whose determination requires destructive coupon testing, can be eliminated with no statistically significant loss in predictive performance on the holdout test set, a conclusion further supported by robustness checks across alternative model families and by uncertainty quantification via bootstrap confidence intervals\. This reduces the required input set from 12 to 10, establishing a validated minimum viable assessment parameter set that meaningfully cuts the testing, time, and resource burden of retrofit decision\-making, while also lowering model training time by approximately 15%, in qualitative alignment with SDG 9, SDG 12, and SDG 13\.

## [Neurofilament Light Chain and Mutant Huntingtin Across Huntington&\#x27;s Disease Integrated Staging System Stages in Huntington Disease: A Cross‐Sectional Multimodal Analysis](../publications/e371715e11d7bbd6a487.md)

Jesús Pérez‐Pérez; Gonzalo Olmedo‐Saura; Arnau Puig‐Davi; Rocío Pérez‐González; Jordi Pegueroles; Andrea Horta‐Barba; Anna Vázquez Oliver; Elisa I\. Rivas; Daniel Andres Alcolea; Juan Fortea; Marina Guasch‐Jiménez; Tomas Xuclà Ferrarons; Frederic Sampedro; Lidia Bojtos; Óscar López\-Lombardía; Ignacio Aracil‐Bolaños; Berta Pascual‐Sedano; Carla Franch\-Martí; Laura Pérez‐Carasol; Margarita Rubio\-Romera; Yi Ji; Alexandre Gironell; Antònia Campolongo; Raúl Martínez‐Fernández; Alberto Lleó; Javier Pagonabarraga; Saül Martínez‐Horta; Jaime Kulisevsky; BCN‐HD Working Group;; HDClarity investigators

BACKGROUND: The Huntington&\#x27;s Disease Integrated Staging System \(HD\-ISS\) provides a framework for staging HD but does not incorporate fluid biomarkers\. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to examine neurofilament light chain \(NfL\) and mutant huntingtin \(mHTT\) and total tau across HD\-ISS stages and their associations with genetic burden, neuroimaging, and clinical measures\. METHODS: We performed cross\-sectional analysis of the Barcelona\-Huntington&\#x27;s Disease \(BCN\-HD\) cohort with external replication in the multicenter HDClarity study\. HD gene expansion carriers were classified as HD\-ISS stages 0 to 3\. NfL \(cerebrospinal fluid \[CSF\] and plasma\), CSF mHTT, total tau, striatal volumes, and Unified Huntington&\#x27;s Disease Rating Scale measures were quantified\. Group differences and associations were analyzed using adjusted models\. RESULTS: The BCN\-HD cohort included 78 participants \(50 HD gene expansion carriers \[HDGECs\], 28 controls\) and HDClarity included 218 participants \(166 HDGECs, 52 controls\)\. CSF NfL increased across HD\-ISS stages and discriminated premanifest from manifest individuals, as well as HD\-ISS stage 0 from stage 1\. Plasma NfL showed parallel increases and strongly correlated with CSF NfL \(ρ = 0\.88, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. More than half of HD\-ISS 0 individuals had NfL levels above the age\-adjusted 95th percentile \(P95\) and shorter predicted time to onset \(13 years for CSF and 10 years for plasma\)\. From HD\-ISS 1 onward, NfL levels exceeded P95 in most individuals\. Higher NfL concentrations were associated with genetic burden, striatal atrophy, and clinical measures \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. CSF mHTT was detectable from HD\-ISS 0 but showed weaker associations, whereas CSF total tau increased only from HD\-ISS 3\. CONCLUSIONS: NfL identifies biological activity across the HD\-ISS continuum and shows neuroaxonal injury in a subset of individuals classified as stage 0\. These findings suggest that fluid biomarkers may complement current HD\-ISS criteria and support biological stratification in observational studies and clinical trials\. © 2026 The Author\(s\)\. ## [Evaluation of Collaboration Policy in a Warehousing System With Heterogeneous Robots](../publications/e372a73a500fcd045ef4.md)

Wanying Chen; Wenqi Zhao; Liu Kai; Bipan Zou

ABSTRACT This study investigates a novel collaborative warehousing system that employs transportation robots and retrieving robots for order fulfillment\. The system features a central platform with peripheral racks and workstations located at the ends\. Retrieving robots transfer items from racks to transportation robots, which then deliver them to workstations for processing orders\. We develop a fork–join queuing network with two semi‐open queuing networks as its branches to capture the collaboration between the two types of robots and the synchronization of robots and orders, thereby enabling an accurate representation of the overall system performance\. An approximation algorithm is designed to solve the queuing network model, and its accuracy is validated through simulation\. We analyze several key collaboration policies, including dwell point policies, the optimal transportation‐to‐retrieving robot ratio, and the location of battery charging zones\. The study yields several managerial insights: \(1\) The effectiveness of dwell point policies depends on warehouse size: The point of service competition policy outperforms in small layouts, whereas the point of designated position policy excels in large systems\. \(2\) The optimal location of the battery charging zone varies with warehouse dimensions and order arrival rates\. \(3\) Sequentially operating homogeneous robotic systems show advantages in high‐demand scenarios and with small fleets, whereas parallel operating heterogeneous robotic systems perform better under moderate demand with large robot populations\. Beyond a critical fleet‐size threshold, heterogeneous robotic systems consistently dominate across all demand levels\. \(4\) Furthermore, based on our model, we determine the optimal ratio of transportation robots to retrieving robots under different demand scenarios and operational policies\.

## [Optimization of Renewable Energy Systems Using Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria: A Focus on Generation and Distribution](../publications/e3740a13f96a2a5f187b.md)

Johnson Oluwatuyi Nelson

Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts\. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers\. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management\. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context\. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas\. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure\. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public\-private partnerships, targeted capacity\-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility\. The integration of AI into Nigeria’ s renewable energy systems offers a promising pathway toward achieving national energy security, sustainability, and socioeconomic development\.

## [Exploring the Logic of Counterfactuals for Explaining Algorithmic Decisions](../publications/e376d23184f50558cd31.md)

Cordelia Berz

Abstract Interpretable machine learning \(ML\) is crucial for gaining insight into complex ML models\. Among its most valuable tools are counterfactual explanations, identifying changes to input features that would alter an ML prediction\. However, the reliability and usefulness of these explanations depend fundamentally on their logical foundation — a critical aspect that has largely been overlooked in the ML literature\. This paper addresses this gap by establishing normative desiderata for a counterfactual logic specifically designed for explaining algorithmic decisions\. We analyse and argue for the validity of logical properties such as simplification of disjunctive antecedents and modus ponens , while demonstrating the unsuitability of others such as antecedent strengthening and conjunction conditionalisation \. To evaluate existing solutions, we critically compare three prominent counterfactual semantics — similarity, strict conditional, and interventionist — against these desiderata\. Our findings reveal that none of these standard frameworks fully satisfy the requirements, highlighting the urgent need for alternative frameworks\.

## [Recycle Tracker Application: A Gamified Mobile Platform to Enhance Recycling Behaviour](../publications/e37fe5a803ca6e581a73.md)

Pey Yun Goh; Yi Han Ng; Lee Yeng Ong; Kian Ming Lim

Malaysia&\#x27;s recycling efforts have long been challenged by limited accessibility, low motivation, and insufficient environmental awareness among the public\. Despite various national campaigns, recycling participation rates remain inconsistent, highlighting the need for more engaging and user\-centred approaches\. To address these challenges, this paper presents the Recycle Tracker Application, a gamified mobile solution designed to encourage consistent recycling behaviour and strengthen environmental responsibility among Malaysians\. The application integrates multiple core features, including a real\-time interactive map of recycling centres, an educational waste\-sorting and DIY recycling guide, personalized eco\-goal setting, and an innovative Dino Evolution gamification system that rewards users as they progress\. Developed using Flutter and Firebase technologies, the system allows users to record their recycling efforts, monitor progress analytics, set long\-term environmental goals, and receive reminders that adapt to individual recycling patterns\. User testing and survey results showed strong engagement levels, improved recycling knowledge, and higher motivation to recycle regularly\. Participants reported that the gamification elements and visual feedback enhanced their sense of achievement and encouraged continued participation\. The combination of behavioural nudges, interactive guidance, and personalized progress tracking proved effective in cultivating sustainable habits\. Overall, the Recycle Tracker Application demonstrates that gamified digital solutions can serve as practical tools to promote environmental awareness and recycling participation\. By fostering long\-term behavioural change, the application contributes to Malaysia’s broader efforts toward sustainable development and supports the transition to a circular and environmentally responsible economy\.

## [Real\-world comparative outcomes of pyrotinib\-based versus pertuzumab\-based first\-line therapy in HER2\-Positive advanced breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective cohort study from Xinjiang, China](../publications/e383347d1363053a53f2.md)

Yimuran Hujiahemaiti; Yinping Ge; Chao Zhang; Gulisire Abdoukerim; Jing Fei; Ruifeng Qi; Yan Li; Xiaoping Ma; Zhenhui Zhao; Li Li; Dan Liu; Bingyu Li; Xin&\#x27;er Zhang; Bing Zhao

Background Direct comparative evidence between taxane plus trastuzumab plus pyrotinib \(THPyro\) and taxane plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab \(THP\) as first\-line therapy for HER2\-positive advanced breast cancer remains limited\. Methods This multicenter retrospective real\-world cohort study included 181 female patients in Xinjiang, China who initiated first\-line THP or THPyro between 1 January 2020 and 30 September 2025\. Propensity score matching generated 60 matched pairs\. The primary endpoint was progression\-free survival \(PFS\)\. Median follow\-up in the matched cohort was 28\.4 months\. Results After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced\. THPyro showed numerically longer median PFS than THP \(20\.1 vs\. 17\.6 months; log\-rank P = 0\.086\), and the stratified Cox model showed a non\-significant trend toward reduced progression risk \(hazard ratio, 0\.478; 95% confidence interval, 0\.216–1\.061\)\. Restricted mean survival time \(RMST\) analysis demonstrated a significant 24\-month PFS gain with THPyro \(absolute difference, 2\.41 months; P = 0\.007\)\. Objective response and disease control rates were comparable\. Brain metastasis status was the most prominent potential effect modifier, with an exploratory signal observed in patients with baseline brain metastases\. THPyro was associated with more diarrhea, and higher albumin level and prophylactic loperamide use were associated with a lower observed risk of grade ≥2 diarrhea\. Conclusion First\-line THPyro was associated with a non\-significant trend toward longer PFS and a significant 24\-month RMST gain compared with THP in this retrospective matched cohort\. An exploratory signal was observed among patients with baseline brain metastases, while diarrhea was more frequent and required proactive management\.

## [Deep LLM layers expose passage\-level context in EEG during silent reading](../publications/e384817c994fd39e343d.md)

Ingo Marquardt; Anthilia Alchanat; Priyanka Jain

In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open\-vocabulary word\-level information from 19\-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden\-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model \(LLM\)\. That analysis contrasted two of the model&\#x27;s 33 layers: the context\-free input embedding and one mid\-depth layer\. Here we ask how EEG\-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model\. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama\-3\.1\-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows\. We distinguish word\-level decodability from a context\-tracking component\. Word\-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer\. In contrast, the context\-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer\. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0\.5\-s window at a time tracks the text passage too\. Two new controls dissect this component\. A target\-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder&\#x27;s word\-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by\-product of word decoding and target geometry\. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context\-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature\. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text\. A single EEG window therefore carries passage\-level information that a contextual target can absorb\. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders\.

## [A Preconditioned Augmented Lagrangian Method for Solving Semidefinite Programming Problems](../publications/e384ae4b13a43918c819.md)

Tianyun Tang; Kim\-Chuan Toh

In this work, we propose a preconditioned augmented Lagrangian method \(ALM\) for solving semidefinite programming \(SDP\) problems\. The preconditioner is implemented via a weighted penalty function in the ALM subproblem, with the weight matrix derived from the projection operator onto the tangent space of the feasible region\. This simple yet effective modification significantly accelerates ALM, particularly for ill\-conditioned SDPs\. By combining the preconditioned ALM with our previously developed feasible method, SDPF, we develop SDPF\+, an SDP solver capable of handling convex problems with possibly nonlinear objective functions\. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of SDPF\+, showing that it can generally outperform other solvers on large\-scale SDPs whose optimal solutions exhibit low\-rank structure\. History: Accepted by Antonio Frangioni, Area Editor for Design &amp; Analysis of Algorithms–Continuous\. Funding: The research of K\.\-C\. Toh is supported by the Ministry of Education, Singapore, under its Academic Research Fund Tier 3 grant call \[MOE\-2019\-T3\-1\-010\]\. Supplemental Material: The software that supports the findings of this study is available within the paper and its Supplemental Information \( https://pubsonline\.informs\.org/doi/suppl/10\.1287/ijoc\.2025\.1663 \) as well as from the IJOC GitHub software repository \( https://github\.com/INFORMSJoC/2025\.1663 \)\. The complete IJOC Software and Data Repository is available at https://informsjoc\.github\.io/ \.

## [Real\-Time Risk\-Aversion\-Adaptive Portfolio Selection by Learning a Hypernetworks](../publications/e394905727e5c08092fb.md)

Khang Truong Tuan; Thang Tran Ngoc; Anh Dao Tuan

Serving a Markowitz efficient frontier at a varying risk\-aversion level requires one quadratic program per query\. We study a learned alternative: a hypernetwork that maps a normalized preference vector, read as a risk\-aversion level, to a long\-only portfolio in one forward pass\. A softmax output layer enforces the budget and no\-short\-selling constraints, and training minimizes a Chebyshev scalarization without any pre\-solved frontier\. The architecture, the scalarizations and the guarantees for the scalarized problem are those of controllable Pareto front learning \[1, 2\]\. Our contribution is an exact\-oracle evaluation: for the long\-only mean–variance problem the critical\-line algorithm yields the exact Chebyshev solution at every preference, so the error of thelearned map can be measured exactly, compared with the strongest alternatives and located\. On a ten\-industry synthetic instance and a fifteen\-asset VN30 instance the map attains a mean Euclidean weight error of 0\.0083 and 0\.0088 over ten seeds and answers a query in 44 microseconds on one CPU core\. From five to two hundred assets the error grows from 0\.0041 to 0\.0734; its largest values occur where the highest expected returns are nearly tied, it concentrates at changes of the active set \(median per\-seed ratio 2\.45 on VN30\), and supervised training on exact targets reduces it four\- to six\-fold\. The exact solver computes the entire frontier in 0\.22 to 3\.35 ms, so on this problem the learned map offers no computational advantage\.

## [Four Quality\-Control Failure Modes in Public Wireline\-Log Archives: Measured Effects and a Reproducible Workflow, With Examples From Wyoming and Kansas](../publications/e39728c8d3fb7361e5bb.md)

Emmanuel Kobina Gyasi; Precious Kamsiyo Ejikeme; Elvis Gyamfi; Somtochukwu Vivian Onuegbu

Public wireline\-log archives are widely reused in petrophysical and machine\-learning studies, yet the processing steps required to make them analytically usable are rarely reported\. We processed 1,210 logs from the Teapot Dome archive in Wyoming, together with a 300\-well pilot drawn from 29,089 Kansas Geological Survey records, and found four processing failures, each of which produced an error larger than the signal it was supposed to resolve\. Unit conventions varied inside single archives: bulk density in kg/m³, transit time in µs/m and neutron porosity in percent sat alongside conventional units\. When a consolidated\-rock sonic transform was applied to whole boreholes, the secondary porosity index rose from −0\.181 in the shallowest depth decile to \+0\.019 in the deepest, monotonically apart from a single reversal between the sixth and seventh deciles \(Kendall τ = 0\.956, p = 5\.5 × 10⁻⁶\), a trend set by compaction and not by the rock\. Assuming one matrix mineral across a mixed interval gave negative density porosity in 23\.0% of samples\. It also inflated apparent secondary porosity by 29 to 46 percentage points\. In one of three wells within a single formation, tool calibration differed from its neighbours by enough to misassign mineralogy\. Pore\-type attribution itself proved fragile\. Applied to identical data, two defensible matrix\-assignment schemes flagged 21\.2% and 39\.2% of samples respectively, and each pointed to a different well as the source of the signal\. Photoelectric factor, which could settle the question independently, was logged in only 14 of the Wyoming files, whereas close to a third of the Kansas pilot carried it\. We release an open Python workflow that detects each failure mode, applies the corresponding correction, and reports the magnitude of that correction at every stage\. Our view is that log\-based pore\-type attribution should not be treated as reliable unless PEF or a neutron log corrected for lithology is available\.

## [Understanding vaccination against human papillomavirus \(HPV\): knowledge and perceptions among parents or guardians and healthcare workers, Germany, 2023](../publications/e39b0d73cdbe78357b6b.md)

Nora Schmid\-Küpke; Elisa Wulkotte; Yvonne Bichel; Heike Krämer; Johannes Lachmann; Andrea Mais; Philipp Schmid; Jule Marie Schmitz; Ole Wichmann; Anja Takla

BACKGROUNDVaccination against human papillomavirus \(HPV\) is effective against certain types of cancer\. Despite longstanding vaccination recommendation, HPV vaccination has the lowest coverage among all recommended vaccines for children and adolescents in Germany, with notable differences between sexes\.AIMWe aimed to investigate attitudes towards vaccination against HPV and HPV\-related knowledge among parents or guardians and healthcare workers \(HCW\) in Germany, alongside vaccination intentions and determinants in parents/guardians and vaccination counselling in HCWs\.METHODSIn autumn 2023, we conducted telephone interviews with 1,508 parents/guardians of children and adolescents aged 9\-14 years and 503 HCWs from paediatric practices\. We used weighting and analysed the responses with t test and ANOVA\.RESULTSOverall, 34\.5% children of the interviewed parents/guardians were already vaccinated against HPV, while 24\.8% of parents/guardians reported a high intention, 5\.6% opposed to vaccination and 35\.2% were considered vaccine hesitant\. Parents/guardians and HCWs considered vaccination of females more important than of males \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Parents/guardians exhibited knowledge gaps, for example, by overestimating alternative measures \(e\.g\. condom use\) for cancer prevention; HCWs expressed uncertainties about the risk of HPV infection\. Vaccination decisions were most strongly influenced by the paediatricians the parents/guardians consulted\. Although 97% of HCWs reported recommending the vaccine, only 43\.7% of parents/guardians recalled receiving a recommendation\.CONCLUSIONThese findings highlight the need for tailored vaccination communication, alongside timely, active physician recommendations and appropriate education to support HPV vaccination decisions\.
