## [Artificial intelligence and human factors: European Defence Agency and humans as defence infrastructure](../publications/e3b228c0d565b1de2eab.md)

Dimitris Dalakoglou

This text starts from an AI error incident of September 2026 within US Special Operations Command that ‘almost started a war’\. It examines the growing significance of ‘Human Factors’ in European defence as artificial intelligence reshapes relations between humans, military institutions and technological systems\. Drawing on European Defence Agency programmes and recent work on trustworthy AI, I suggest that AI changes where and how humans enter military systems, embedding them in increasingly complex sociotechnical relations\. Human capacities themselves start to acquire an infrastructural quality, as military systems depend increasingly on how these capacities are organized and managed\.

## [Quality monitoring of the lautering process in microbreweries using machine learning](../publications/e3b5e4bfaa393e01529c.md)

Carolina Rosseti Matheus; Rodrigo Nicoletti; André Luís Dias; Jean Carlos Rodrigues da Silva

Industry 4\.0 and artificial intelligence offer opportunities to improve the operation of small and medium\-sized enterprises, including microbreweries, which often rely on limited automation and are subject to operational failures\. Intelligent anomaly diagnosis can contribute to process reliability and product quality\. This study investigates the use of machine learning to monitor the lautering process through operational data from a lautering pump for fault diagnosis purposes\. The results showed that torque, current, and power factor exhibited consistent dynamic patterns associated with the lautering stage operation\. Although turbidity and dry mass were affected by the operating conditions, their relationship with pump speed was not consistent across all bed configurations\. A Support Vector Machine classifier was developed to identify normal and anomalous lautering conditions\. The model achieved 98\.1% accuracy, with 98\.9% specificity in fault detection\. These results demonstrate that electrical variables obtained from the frequency inverter can capture relevant dynamic changes in the lautering process and support low\-cost, non\-invasive real\-time monitoring of filtration anomalies in microbreweries\.

## [Complete Genome Sequence and Replicon\-Resolved Phosphorus\- and Potassium\-Acquisition Gene Inventory of Niallia taxi Strain Si250\_34 from Long\-Term NPK\- and Silicate\-Fertilized Soil](../publications/e3cec4e61c6c22d831b9.md)

Seung\-Yeon Jeong; Daye Choi; Sook\-Min Kwon; Ikwhan Kim; Sihyun Park; Jae\-Ho Shin

Niallia was one of 17 genera proposed in a genomebased reclassification of Bacillus \[1\]\.Niallia taxi is a Gram\-stain\-positive, aerobic, endospore\-forming endophyte of Taxus chinensis \[2\]\.Long\-fertilized soils hold large phosphorus stocks of low plant availability \[3\], and highaffinity phosphate uptake in Bacillus subtilis runs through the pst operon \[4\]\.No phosphorus\-or potassiumacquisition gene set has been described for the species, and only two of the 20 other assemblies labeled N\. taxi are closed\.We report the closed genome of strain Si250\_34, a replicon\-resolved inventory of its phosphorus\-and potassium\-acquisition genes, and the routes for which no gene was detected\.Bulk soil was sampled in 2024 at the soybean R3 \(beginning pod\)\-R4 \(full pod\) growth stages from the Si250 plot of a 50\-year nutrient\-management field trial maintained by the Gyeongsangbuk\-do Agricultural Research and Extension Services \(GBARES\) in Chilgok, Republic of Korea\.The plot received urea, fused phosphate, and potassium chloride at rates equivalent to 12 kg N ha \-1 , 8 kg P 2 O 5 ha \-1 , and 6 kg K 2 O ha \-1 , respectively, together with silicate at 2\.5 t ha \-1 \.A soil suspension was plated on tryptic soy agar; after 48 h at 30℃ a single colony was picked, purified by repeated streaking and grown overnight in tryptic soy broth \(30℃, 200 rpm\)\.Genomic Niallia taxi strain Si250\_34, assigned to the species by average nucleotide identity, was isolated from a 49\-year NPK\-and silicate\-fertilized plot in Chilgok, Republic of Korea\.Its genome comprises a circular chromosome of 3,840,758 bp and two circular plasmids of 1,367,869 and 381,819 bp, totaling 5,590,446 bp at 37\.7% G\+C\.The pst operon occurs on both the chromosome and the 1\.37\-Mb megaplasmid; genes for a Pit\-family transporter and a phoP\-phoR\-type pair are present\.Potassium\-acquisition genes include a megaplasmid kdpFABC operon and three Ktr\-family permease genes\.No pqq biosynthetic gene, phyC\-type phytase or phnG\-phnJ/phnM C\-P lyase gene was detected\.

## [Multi\-modality assessment and prognostication of high\-risk coronary plaque](../publications/e3d11cef1546161ed1fa.md)

Marwa Daghem

BACKGROUND: A large proportion of patients who suffer an acute thrombotic cardiovascular event exhibit no prior clinical signs of underlying atherosclerosis\. This asymptomatic progression poses a considerable diagnostic challenge and contributes substantially to global cardiovascular morbidity and mortality\. Plaque rupture remains the predominant initiating mechanism for acute coronary syndromes, responsible for 60–70% of cases and typically occurs suddenly and without antecedent symptoms\. Consequently, the detection and characterisation of high\-risk or &quot;vulnerable&quot; plaques has become a central focus in advancing the understanding of atherogenesis and refining preventive strategies\. Identifying\- disease activity at an early stage and intervening before an acute event arises may help reduce the overall burden of atherosclerotic complications\. This thesis investigates advanced imaging techniques to quantify coronary atherosclerotic burden, activity, and progression, with a focus on: • The role of lipoprotein\(a\) in driving adverse plaque progression and associated thrombotic risk\. • The potential of 18F\-sodium fluoride uptake to predict long\-\-term\- coronary events\. METHODS AND RESULTS: Lipoprotein\(a\) and plaque progression We assessed whether elevated lipoprotein \(a\) \(Lp\(a\)\) drives adverse coronary plaque progression in patients with advanced stable coronary artery disease using coronary CT angiography at baseline and 12 months\. High Lp\(a\) was defined as ≥70 mg/dL\. Among 191 patients, baseline plaque burden was similar across groups, but those with high Lp\(a\) demonstrated greater progression of low\-\-attenuation \(necrotic core\) plaque \(26\.2 ± 88\.4 mm3 vs −0\.7 ± 50\.1 mm3; P = 0\.020\)\. Multivariable linear regression analysis confirmed the relation between Lp\(a\) and low\-attenuation plaque volume progression \(β = 10\.5% increase for each 50 mg/dL Lp\(a\), 95% CI: 0\.7%\-20\.3%\)\. No differences were observed in total, calcific, or non\-calcific plaque progression\. Temporal changes in coronary 18F\-fluoride uptake Coronary 18F\-fluoride uptake reflects atherosclerotic disease activity and progression, but its short\-\-\-term variability is unknown\. This study evaluated how coronary 18F\-\-fluoride uptake changes over 12 months in patients with either advanced chronic coronary artery disease or a recent myocardial infarction\. Patients underwent serial 18F\-\-fluoride PET–CT imaging at 3, 6, or 12 months, with uptake quantified using coronary microcalcification activity \(CMA\) and calcification assessed by calcium score, mass, and volume\. Among 111 patients, those with chronic disease had higher baseline CMA values\- reflecting the greater burden of coronary artery disease\. Coronary 18F\-fluoride uptake \(CMA &gt; 0\) was associated with higher baseline calcium scores \(294 \[116\-483\] versus 72 \[8 \-222\] AU; P&lt;0\.001\), and more rapid progression of coronary calcification scores \(39 \[10\-82\] versus 12 \[1\-36\] AU/year; P&lt;0\.001\), compared to the absence of uptake \(CMA = 0\)\. However, Coronary 18F\-fluoride uptake itself remained largely unchanged over 3, 6, and 12 months in both chronic and post\-myocardial infarction groups\. Coronary plaque activity and future coronary events Recurrent coronary events are common following acute myocardial infarction but are challenging to predict\. We conducted a multi\-centre prospective study to evaluate whether coronary atherosclerotic plaque activity, measured using 18F\-sodium fluoride PET uptake, predicts longterm outcomes in 704 patients with multivessel coronary artery disease following a recent myocardial infarction\. Over a median 4\-\-year follow\-\-up\-, 141 patients experienced the composite endpoint of cardiac death \(9\), non\-fatal myocardial \(49\) infarction, or unplanned revascularization \(83\)\. Increased coronary plaque activity had no demonstrable association with the primary endpoint \(hazard ratio \(HR\) 1\.25 \[95% confidence interval 0\.89 to 1\.76\], P=0\.20\) or unscheduled coronary revascularization \(HR 0\.98 \[0\.64 to 1\.49\], P=0\.91\) but was associated with increased risk of cardiac death or non\-fatal myocardial infarction \(47 versus 19; HR 1\.82 \[1\.07 to 3\.10\], P=0\.028\) and all\-cause mortality \(30 versus 9; HR 2\.43 \[1\.15 to 5\.12\], P=0\.020\)\. CONCLUSION: At vessel level, 18F\-sodium fluoride PET is associated with atheroma progression as well as the future risk of cardiac death or myocardial infarction\. As patient level, elevated Lp\(a\) drives accelerated progression of low\-attenuation \(necrotic core\) plaque in advanced coronary artery disease, offering a mechanistic explanation for its association with residual myocardial infarction risk and supporting Lp\(a\) as a therapeutic target\. Collectively, these findings highlight the importance of integrating biological and imaging biomarkers to improve risk stratification and to monitor disease progression, including response to targeted therapies\.

## [Unlocking Speckle‐Free and Near‐Unity‐Efficiency Holography via a Dual‐Layer Metasurface Architecture](../publications/e3d79e8fe6012de8a834.md)

Yanjun Bao; Zhijun Tang; Zhengjie Liang; Zehao Dong; Yuanhua Feng; Baojun Li

ABSTRACT Holography holds considerable promise across diverse applications, yet its practical realization is hindered by a fundamental trade‐off between diffraction efficiency and image fidelity\. While suppressing speckle noise is challenging, doing so while pushing diffraction efficiency to its near‐unity physical limit represents an even greater barrier\. Here, we address this efficiency‐fidelity trade‐off by integrating a dual‐layer metasurface architecture with a gradient‐based progressive‐efficiency optimization \(GPEO\) strategy, unlocking a solution space where near‐unity efficiency coexists with pristine image quality\. We demonstrate that this configuration effectively eliminates both stochastic speckle and deterministic singularity artifacts, achieving a speckle contrast as low as 0\.013 \(simulation\) and 0\.075 \(experiment\)\. Remarkably, this high‐fidelity reconstruction is realized alongside record‐breaking diffraction efficiencies of 97% in simulation and 95% in experiment, pushing the system performance to its theoretical ceiling\. This work overcomes a key bottleneck in holography, establishing a new benchmark for high‐performance systems and paving the way for their application in advanced display technologies\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LAW](../publications/e3da9f45a2b69cbc63dd.md)

Sangita Roy

Artificial Intelligence \(&quot;AI&quot;\) is increasingly becoming embedded in activities that were traditionally governed by direct human judgment\. Automated systems now assist in recruitment, credit assessment, healthcare, education, content generation, surveillance and public administration\. The legal significance of this development lies not merely in the sophistication of the technology but in the possibility that consequential decisions may be produced through systems whose operation is difficult for affected individuals to understand or challenge\. This creates questions concerning privacy, equality, discrimination, intellectual property, liability, procedural fairness and the allocation of responsibility among developers, deployers and users\. India presently addresses these concerns through a combination of constitutional principles, information\-technology legislation, data\-protection law, sectoral regulation and policy initiatives rather than through a comprehensive AI statute\. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, together with the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, has strengthened India&\#x27;s data\-governance architecture, but data protection alone cannot resolve the wider accountability problems created by AI\. This article examines the principal legal challenges associated with AI and compares India&\#x27;s developing approach with the European Union&\#x27;s risk\-based Artificial Intelligence Act and the United States&\#x27; standards\-oriented approach\. It argues that India&\#x27;s future AI governance should preserve a legally traceable chain of responsibility whenever decision\-making is delegated to automated systems\. Such a framework should combine risk classification, meaningful human oversight, transparency, privacy safeguards, anti\-discrimination measures, lifecycle accountability and effective remedies\. The objective should not be to prevent technological development, but to ensure that automation does not become a means of diluting leg\.\.\.

## [Towards Adaptive and Real\-Survey\-Aligned Simulated Urban Mobility Behaviour of Generative Agents](../publications/e3db1f10d509a7a872f7.md)

Yves Bru; Kamaldeep Singh Oberoi; Benoit Gaudou

In existing agent\-based simulations of multimodal urban mobility, agents, representing humans, choose their travel modes either using discrete choice or machine learning models fitted on structured travel survey data, or with rules explicitly written by the domain experts\. Such approaches fix a priori the agents&\#x27; possible behaviour space\. Hence, a factor absent from variables or rules cannot affect agents&\#x27; decisions\. In reality, choosing a transport mode is a multidimensional decision in which objective and subjective factors intertwine and change over time\. Integrating such complexity into a city\-scale multimodal mobility simulation remains a challenge\. Generative agents \(GAs\) built on large language models promise to respond to this challenge because they carry decision heuristics that travel surveys do not record\. However, to the best of our knowledge, aligning their decisions with real household travel surveys remains an open question\. In this paper, we build an agent\-based model of daily multimodal mobility for Toulouse \(France\)\. We compare the performance of fifteen decision\-makers \(simple baselines, models fitted on the survey, GAs with minimal and tuned prompts, and a typed classifier\) on the real household travel survey\. Our results show that GAs with tuned prompts come close to the fitted models on the modal split of a simulated day without transport disruptions, but not trip by trip\. GAs also react when unforeseen events occur\. The recently released Jev\-1\.13 TypeSafe classifier gives surprisingly great results, showing that generating output text is not necessary\. The results presented in this paper would be of interest to transport policy makers and service providers looking to apply generative agent\-based modelling for improving urban mobility services\.

## [Will digitalization increase the quality of care provided in social services?](../publications/e3e05d3c4c2849a4d270.md)

Mirka Wildmannová

The aim of the paper is to evaluate whether the use of digitalization and modern technology will increase the quality of social services in a selected sample of social service providers\. Increasing the availability of modern technology is one of the means to improve the quality of social services provided\. The paper discusses the different methods of implementing digitalization and examples of good practice in the Czech Republic and abroad\. The research used a qualitative approach, including semi\-structured interviews with staff and clients of residential facilities\. The research conducted focused on the implementation of virtual reality technology in residential social services\. The research showed that the most frequent forms in the introduction of modern technologies include electronic registration of clients, digitalization of the service request process, assistive technologies or shared integrated systems\. A major barrier to the introduction of modern technologies is human potential\.

## [A review of offline training of robotic manipulator control under limited data](../publications/e3e27d179acea353a450.md)

Ghusoon Hadi AL\-aldaffaie; Zinah Mohammad Ali; Amirfarhad Farhadi; Azadeh Zamanifar; Deniz Noormohammadzadehmaleki

Offline reinforcement learning \(RL\) has emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic skill acquisition, particularly for manipulation tasks where real\-world trial\-and\-error interaction is costly, time\-consuming, or unsafe\. In contrast to broad offline RL surveys, this paper presents a focused narrative review centered on robotic manipulation under data\-limited conditions, where datasets often suffer from narrow state–action coverage, sparse successful demonstrations, noisy trajectories, and limited behavioral diversity\. These constraints exacerbate key challenges in offline RL, including distributional shift, unstable value estimation, weak reward propagation under sparsity, and poor policy generalization\. This paper adopts a focused narrative review methodology; it does not claim systematic review status and does not follow a PRISMA protocol, but instead provides a structured, evidence\-informed synthesis of representative offline RL methods selected for their methodological significance, benchmark relevance, and applicability to data\-limited robotic manipulation conditions\. The review analyzes major families of offline RL methods, including conservative value\-based approaches, behavior\-constrained learning, advantage\-weighted methods, uncertainty\-aware techniques, model\-based offline RL, sequence\-modeling approaches, and offline\-to\-online adaptation strategies\. The discussion is grounded in benchmark observations from D4RL and NeoRL, alongside evidence from robotic manipulation systems such as QT\-Opt and RoboNet\. Comparative analysis suggests that conservative and uncertainty\-aware methods typically offer stronger robustness and policy stability under constrained robotic datasets, whereas behavior\-constrained and advantage\-based approaches remain highly sensitive to dataset quality, behavioral diversity, and reward structure\. Model\-based and sequence\-modeling methods can further improve data efficiency and long\-horizon capability, but introduce additional challenges related to model reliability, synthetic rollout fidelity, and sequential data requirements\. The paper also discusses practical issues in real\-world deployment, including safety constraints, contact instability, sensor noise, and safe online adaptation\. Finally, it highlights future research directions such as uncertainty\-aware learning, physics\-informed world models, foundation models, representation learning, and safe offline\-to\-online adaptation for robotic manipulation\. Overall, this review provides a targeted synthesis of offline RL methods for robotic manipulation under realistic data\-scarce conditions, while identifying key limitations, benchmark trends, and open research challenges for next\-generation robotic learning systems\.

## [LongForge: Measuring and Improving Long\-Context Instruction Data via Evidence\-Assertion Reasoning Graphs](../publications/e3ea1f23b00f853dade7.md)

Ziyang Chen; Junlong Jia; Xing Wu; Tinghao Yu; Songlin Hu

Existing quality control for long\-context instruction\-tuning data is a one\-shot judgment inside the generation pipeline that leaves only a scalar, revealing neither which document parts an answer uses nor how many reasoning steps it writes down; the data can thus be neither audited nor controlled\. We formalize data quality as a property of the alignment structure among document, question, and answer, and build LongForge, which pairs an analyzer that measures long\-context data with a synthesizer that generates it\. The analyzer reverse\-reconstructs each sample into an evidence\-assertion reasoning graph and programmatically computes four dimensions on it: breadth, depth, correctness, and completeness\. Every reading traces back to specific evidence spans and reasoning steps, making data auditable\. Measuring seven mainstream datasets reveals two previously unquantified defects: breadth barely grows with document length, and depth is generally low, the two being nearly orthogonal\. The synthesizer then embeds the analyzer into generation, gating on correctness and completeness and deferring breadth and depth to a training\-time mixture over measured values, which makes the training distribution controllable\. On two backbones, its two mixtures, LongForge\-1 and LongForge\-N, outperform the strongest baseline by 2\.2\-4\.7 points on average over six long\-context benchmarks, and in a controlled comparison that holds the gate and the candidate pool fixed, raising breadth and depth alone is worth a further 1\.16 points, making the structural distribution of training data a lever on downstream quality rather than only a description of it\.

## [The Relationship Between ICT Utilisation and the Effective Management of Teacher Welfare in Junior Schools in Wajir County, Kenya](../publications/e3ee64a71c3494488a85.md)

Issa Kurash Abdille; Fredrick Ngala; Stephen Kipkorir Rotich

ICT integration in education is increasingly widespread, yet its influence on teacher management remains under\-researched, particularly within the Kenyan context\. The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between ICT utilisation practices and four constructs of effective teacher management in junior schools in Wajir County, Kenya: classroom teaching management, teacher welfare, teacher discipline, and teacher professional development, as well as to determine prevailing ICT utilisation practices in junior schools\. A cross\-sectional convergent mixed\-methods research design was adopted\. 116 junior schoolteachers from Wajir East and Wajir West completed a structured questionnaire aimed at determining the relationship between ICT utilisation and the four components of teacher management\. Fourteen education leaders comprising twelve headteachers and two sub\-county education officials from the two sub\-counties participated in semi\-structured interviews\. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analysis, while qualitative data were analysed thematically\. The research instrument demonstrated good reliability \(Cronbach’s α = \.857\)\. The findings established a statistically significant positive relationship between ICT utilisation and teacher welfare \(β = 0\.736, p &lt; \.001\)\. Qualitative findings indicated that ICT supports administrative communication, record management, instructional preparation, professional collaboration, and continuous professional development\. However, inadequate infrastructure, unreliable internet connectivity, and inconsistent electricity supply, particularly in remote ASAL schools, constrained integration\. The study concludes that ICT utilisation is critical for improving administrative efficiency, accountability, and welfare service delivery\. It recommends strengthening ICT infrastructure, internet connectivity, teacher digital literacy, and institutional support\.

## [WebCoder: Scaling General Frontend Development with Artifact\-Grounded Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../publications/e4079b7676a6d04d32c2.md)

Zijun Dou; Zhen Yang; Xijun Liu; Dongzhuoran Zhou; Aohan Zeng; Jie Tang

Real\-world frontend development requires agents to compose reproduction, generation, modification, and repair over an evolving application state\. Learning a general policy for this process requires translating heterogeneous execution feedback into task\-aligned rewards and effective credit assignment across long sequences of interdependent actions\. We introduce WebCoder, a general frontend development agent trained with artifact\-grounded agentic reinforcement learning\. Our key idea is to assess diverse development activities through their effects on a shared executable artifact and its satisfaction of task requirements\. We build Webdev\-World, an executable environment that integrates code editing, application execution, browser inspection, and on\-demand skills while preserving project state across interactions\. An independent verifier evaluates the final application against task requirements to provide terminal rewards, while changes in intermediate artifact progress redistribute the resulting rollout advantage across development segments\. Context compaction and message\-tree sample construction support training on trajectories beyond a single context window while avoiding repeated loss computation on shared generated history\. We further introduce Webdev\-Bench to evaluate composed development requirements within a single project\. On Webdev\-Bench, WebCoder\-27B raises requirement satisfaction from 64\.8 for its Qwen3\.8\-27B base model to 72\.8, exceeding Claude\-Opus\-4\.8 \(65\.1\) and GPT\-5\.4 \(59\.6\); on Vision2Web, it improves the average visual and functional score from 41\.1 to 62\.4, on par with Claude\-Opus\-4\.8\. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of artifact\-grounded credit assignment and long\-horizon training\.

## [The Philosophical Counselor in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Practice to Profession, from Profession to Algorithm](../publications/e40a14f9788b048f4cb1.md)

Aurelia Daniela Stanciulescu

The paper addresses the ethical integration of artificial intelligence into philosophical counseling in Romania\. We begin with the criteria used by Julia Clare and Richard Sivil to distinguish between practice and profession, and with the roadmap for recognizing the new profession of philosophical counseling in Romania, outlined in 2019 by Vasile Hațegan\. Much of this process has already been accomplished; what remains is the cognitive dimension, which has yet to catch up with either online or algorithmically assisted practice\. In the second part of the article, we draw upon Hațegan’s comparisons between philosophical counseling and psychotherapy, coaching, spiritual counseling, and mediation to identify five distinguishing criteria: counselor neutrality, the relational nature of the process, non\-dependency, the non\-therapeutic nature of the practice, and client autonomy\. We treat these criteria as an ethical test for conversational AI agents\. The APPAgpt platform proves particularly useful in this endeavor; through it, the American Philosophical Practitioners Association invites the public to converse with bots simulating dialogues with great thinkers, while simultaneously emphasizing the importance of the human counselor\. The test yields nuanced results\. When used by the counselor as a tool, artificial intelligence can operate within the boundaries of the practice; however, when placed in the counselor&\#x27;s role facing the client, it exceeds those limits\. The article concludes with proposals for future occupational standards and the philosophical counselor&\#x27;s code of ethics: the inclusion of a competency unit dedicated to digitally mediated practice, as well as a decision\-making procedure inspired by Henk van Luijk’s model\.

## [Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability](../publications/e40ec9d50a573e5a4f2c.md)

Nimnual Visedsun; Narinthon Imjai; Thanaporn Homlaor; Jorge Miguel Chávez\-Díaz; Somnuk Aujirapongpan

The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in accounting practices have significantly increased the complexity and uncertainty of professional work environments, making Dynamic Risk Management Skills a critical competency for contemporary accounting graduates\. This study aims to examine the relationships between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Generation Z \(Gen Z\) accounting students, with Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability considered as mediating variables\. A quantitative research design was employed, collecting data from 571 fourth\-year accounting students across Thailand\. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The results reveal that AI Competency is significantly and positively associated with Systematic Thinking Ability, Design Thinking Ability, and Dynamic Risk Management Skills\. Moreover, Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability significantly account for the indirect associations between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills\. These findings extend theoretical understanding of risk management skill development in accounting education and offer practical implications for curriculum design by emphasizing the integration of AI with higher\-order thinking skill development to better prepare graduates for complex and rapidly changing professional environments\.

## [Green nanotechnology for a sustainable future](../publications/e411cf62ca404cdbcf50.md)

Mansimzadeh Sama Mugaddas

Green nanotechnology is a modern scientific field directed towards using the possibilities of nanotechnology to be safer, resource\-saving, and to reduce the impact on the environment\. In this article, the main principles of green nanotechnology, the synthesis of nanomaterials by ecological methods, and various application areas have been investigated\. The main mechanisms and advantages of obtaining nanomaterials using plant extracts, microorganisms, and biomass\-based raw materials have been reviewed\. At the same time, the application of green nanotechnology in agriculture in the form of nanofertilizers, nanopesticides, and nanosensors, and in the cleaning of water and soil through adsorption, photocatalysis, and nanofiltration processes has been analyzed\. The article has also given attention to problems such as the ecotoxicological effects of nanomaterials, the scaling up of production, and standardization\. It has been shown that in the future, approaches such as artificial intelligence, circular economy, and life cycle assessment can contribute to the more sustainable development of green nanotechnology\.

## [ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On\-Policy Distillation](../publications/e414a4f421a1496a3416.md)

Tengda Guo; Jiawang Hu; Yifei Tao; Yin Wang; Haotian Hu; Fanyi Wang; Liujuan Tang

Long\-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual\-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long\-horizon reliability\. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training\-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long\-horizon reasoning\. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression\-Think\-Action \(CTA\) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason\. The same model, given privileged multi\-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token\-level on\-policy distillation on student\-generated CTA rollouts\. Our Perception\-Memory Fidelity \(PMF\) Gap\-guided OPD\-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task\-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement\. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine\-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross\-modal state retention\. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity\. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance\-inference\-cost trade\-off and exhibits positive zero\-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks\.

## [Evaluation of MRI\-Based Radiomic Texture Analysis and Ensemble Machine Learning Models in the Diagnosis of Hemifacial Spasm](../publications/e41a43f71612919b4b30.md)

Habip Eser Akkaya; Önder Polat; Dorukan İnanç Akpınar; Zeynep Ziroğlu; Muhammet Uzun; Hafize Nalan Güneş

Aim: To investigate whether MRI\-derived texture \(radiomic\) features combined with machine learning can provide objective diagnostic discrimination between patients with hemifacial spasm \(HFS\) and healthy controls, and to evaluate the added value of high\-resolution 3D T2\-SPACE imaging\.Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 35 patients with clinically diagnosed HFS and 36 age\- and sex\-matched controls\. All subjects underwent 3\-Tesla MRI with axial T2\-weighted imaging \(T2WI\), and a subgroup of 21 HFS patients and their matched controls also underwent 3D T2\-SPACE imaging\. Segmentation was performed across axial slices encompassing the brainstem, the entire posterior fossa, and the inner ear, middle ear, and mastoid portions, with the anterior boundary extending to the clivus, using a single manually drawn region of interest \(ROI\) to capture comprehensive radiomic features\. 137 radiomic texture features were extracted using the PyRadiomics platform\. Multiple machine learning classifiers, including k\-nearest neighbors, Naive Bayes, discriminant analysis, decision trees, and ensemble learning methods, were evaluated\. Data were split into 80% training and 20% testing sets, and performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC\-AUC over 20 randomized repetitions\.Results: Among all tested models, the Ensemble Bagged Trees classifier demonstrated the highest overall performance among the tested models\. Using T2WI, the model achieved a mean accuracy of 0\.71 ± 0\.10, sensitivity of 0\.72 ± 0\.15, specificity of 0\.70 ± 0\.18, and ROC\-AUC of 0\.76 ± 0\.16\. In the subgroup analyzed with high\-resolution 3D T2\-SPACE imaging, performance further improved, yielding a mean accuracy of 0\.80 ± 0\.12, sensitivity of 0\.67 ± 0\.23, specificity of 0\.95 ± 0\.12, and ROC\-AUC of 0\.85 ± 0\.11\. High\-resolution T2\-SPACE images provided an improvement in specificity compared with conventional T2WI\.Conclusions: Radiomic texture features extracted from conventional and high\-resolution MRI, when combined with ensemble machine learning methods, show potential for facilitating discrimination between patients with hemifacial spasm and healthy controls\. The particularly high specificity achieved with 3D T2\-SPACE imaging suggests that this approach may serve as a promising complementary diagnostic tool, supporting conventional imaging and clinical assessment and offering a step toward objective, image\-based biomarkers for HFS\.

## [Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book I: Mathematical Foundations](../publications/e41a78a2bcbdc0f85d09.md)

B\. Petersen

Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book I: Mathematical Foundations develops the mathematical foundation of Coherence\-Driven Intelligence \(CDI\) within the Coherence\-Geometric Information Substrate \(CGIS\)\. It treats memory as explicit coherence\-organized informational structure and develops Source geometry, basin organization, storage and persistence, inference and recovery, transmission, learning, finite coherence\-memory realization, collective memory, composition, and internal regulation\. This volume forms Book I of the CDI series\. Book II develops the source\-to\-endpoint bridge connecting finite CDI organization to modern machine\-learning architectures, while Book III develops a source\-explicit computational realization through WaveModules\. This release is a Working Reference Text, Version 0\.1, and has not undergone external editorial or peer review\.CGI Internal ID: CGI\-BKS\-0005

## [From digital transformation to corporate R&amp;D innovation investment: largest shareholder ownership and data asset information disclosure as parallel boundary conditions](../publications/e41b005de4c30728fe68.md)

Yahui Li; Tharitsaya Kongkaew

Digital transformation is associated with greater R&amp;D investment, but the ownership and disclosure conditions surrounding this relationship remain less clear\. This study examines largest shareholder ownership and data asset information disclosure as two distinct moderators, using 35,954 firm\-year observations from 4,388 Chinese A\-share listed firms over 2009–2024\. Firm and year fixed\-effects models show a positive association between digital transformation and R&amp;D innovation investment\. In the baseline model, this association is stronger when the largest shareholder holds a greater equity stake and firms disclose more information about their data assets\. The positive association between digital transformation and R&amp;D investment persists across alternative measures and lagged specifications, whereas the moderation findings are more sensitive to model specification and sample restrictions\. The ownership interaction weakens under stricter fixed effects, and neither interaction is statistically significant in the dynamic specification that includes lagged R&amp;D investment\. Instrumental\-variable estimates are positive but imprecise and do not establish causality\. These findings place ownership structure and data\-related disclosure alongside technological change in explaining firms’ R&amp;D commitments\. They support a conditional account of the digital transformation–R&amp;D relationship, while leaving the underlying monitoring and financing mechanisms open to further investigation\.

## [INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL PARA LA CARACTERIZACIÓN DE MASAS MAMARIAS BENIGNAS Y MALIGNAS MEDIANTE MAMOGRAFÍA Y ECOGRAFÍA](../publications/e42414c8da2fdf3d9969.md)

Juliana del Rocio Carrasco Lascano; Elida Maria Hidalgo Gualan; Raúl Eduardo Chávez Robalino; Abraham Oliver Balderas

El cáncer de mama es la neoplasia maligna más frecuente en mujeres a nivel mundial, con aproximadamente 2,3 millones de casos nuevos anuales\. La capacidad para diferenciar con precisión entre las masas benignas y las malignas en la mamografía y la ecografía es una cuestión de diagnóstico clínico que presenta una considerable variabilidad entre observadores\. En este artículo se analizan los estudios publicados entre 2023 y 2026 que evalúan el rendimiento de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial \(IA\), con su complejo de «aprendizaje profundo», para ayudar a diferenciar entre masa benigna y masa maligna\. Se realizó una búsqueda estructurada en PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect e IEEE Xplore\. La evidencia disponible indica que los sistemas de deep learning alcanzan sensibilidades combinadas cercanas a 0,92–0,93 y especificidades de 0,88–0,91 en ecografía mamaria, mientras que en mamografía los valores de AUC en estudios de lectura se sitúan entre 0,87 y 0,90\. Las técnicas multimodales que combinan información procedente de diferentes fuentes parecen tener mejor capacidad discriminativa en términos técnicos, aunque esto depende por completo del diseño del estudio y del grupo de pacientes estudiado\. La mayoría de los estudios son retrospectivos, de un único centro y carecen de una validación externa prospectiva\. Por lo tanto, parece que la inteligencia artificial podría resultar útil como apoyo en la práctica radiológica, pero aún se necesitan estudios prospectivos y multicéntricos para demostrar su precisión, así como un análisis detallado de sus implicaciones éticas y legales\.

## [Comparative evaluation of nutritional and phytochemical composition, antioxidant and antibacterial potential and metal safety of Caralluma tuberculata and Asparagus racemosus from Namal valley, Punjab, Pakistan: a multivariate analysis](../publications/e42672fe571dafe5a650.md)

Humaira Shaheen; Kafeel Ahmad; Zafar Iqbal Khan; Muhammad Adeel Ghafar; Muhammad Nadeem; Muhammad Naeem Qaisar; Hazoor Ahmad Shad

Medicinal plants are important natural sources of nutrients and bioactive compounds that have therapeutic potential\.The aim of the study was to assess the Caralluma tuberculata and Asparagus racemosus, collected from two different locations in Namal Valley, Punjab, Pakistan for their nutritional composition, heavy metal accumulation, phytochemical content, antioxidant and antibacterial activities as well as metal associated health risks\.A total of 12 samples of C\. tuberculata and A\. racemosus collected from two sites \(Rikhi and Namal village\) were analysed using a comparative experimental design\.Proximate analysis revealed variation in nutritional parameters among the studied plants\.A\. racemosus had the highest crude protein \(22\.15%\), crude fat \(13\.54%\), and crude fibre \(42\.37%\), whereas C\. tuberculata had the highest carbohydrate \(48\.78%\) and ash contents \(14\.19%\)\.Heavy metal values were within permissible limits: Zn ranged from 34\.49to 55\.64 mg/kg, Mn from 17\.29 to 42\.19 mg/kg, and Cu from 11\.63 to 36\.05 mg/kg\.Risk assessment parameters including Estimated daily intake \(EDI\), Target Hazard Quotient \(THQ\) and Hazard Index \(HI\) suggested their safe composition\.Phytochemical analysis showed considerable levels of total phenolics \(41\.55\-122\.84mg GAE/g\) and flavonoids \(15\.60\-69\.04mg QE/g\), associated with strong antioxidant effect \(31\.55\-73\.01%\)\.Antimicrobial testing demonstrated the inhibitory potential against Escherichia coli \(clear inhibition zone beyond the 9mm disc: 1\.94 mm to 21\.91 mm\) and Staphylococcus aureus \(5\.04 mm to 24\.73 mm\) although their antibacterial effects were generally lower than those of the positive control ciprofloxacin\.Pearson correlation analysis, PCA and hierarchical clustering revealed the positive relationships between phytochemical constituents and biological activity\.The overall findings suggest that the investigated medicinal plants meet the established guidelines for medicinal plants in terms of heavy metal concentrations and potential health risks, and demonstrated the promising phytochemical composition and biological activity\.The results support their potential for development of natural therapeutic agents and highlighted the need for the conservation of these valuable traditional medicinal resources\.

## [Constructing a New Anti\-Corruption Governance System in the BRICS Countries](../publications/e428c576bae3b848f24e.md)

Tang Shi

The traditional framework of global anti\-corruption governance has increasingly proved inadequate in responding to emerging challenges, particularly the transformation of the global governance system and the intensiﬁcation of crossborder corruption\. Through their practical anti\-corruption eﬀorts, the BRICS countries have developed a distinctive governance model characterized by sovereign equality, mutual beneﬁt, and a development\-oriented approach\. By adhering to international conventions and fostering multilateral cooperation mechanisms, they have laid an important foundation for reconﬁguring the global anti\-corruption governance framework\. In the course of their governance practice, the BRICS countries have integrated national experience in legal systems and law\-enforcement cooperation, thereby constructing a new governance framework\. This framework is grounded in the core principles of sovereign equality and mutual beneﬁt, institutionally supported by charter\-based guidance and coordination mechanisms, and operationalized through a tripartite structure encompassing dispute settlement, monitoring and evaluation, and phased ﬁnancial safeguards\. It is designed to complement and operate alongside existing international instruments, including the United Nations Convention against Corruption \(UNCAC\), thereby promoting a more inclusive trajectory of global anticorruption governance\. The BRICS countries are expected to further reﬁne this emerging governance model by strengthening internal coordination, deepening international collaboration, and advancing technological empowerment\. By pursuing these eﬀorts, they aim to provide a pragmatic and viable “BRICS solution” to the persistent challenges of global anti\-corruption governance, at the same time contributing to the evolution of a more equitable and just global governance order\.

## [Donor\-wise metabolomic prediction of platelet storage duration: a proof\-of\-concept study: Donor\-wise metabolomic prediction in platelets](../publications/e42c3e6eb139997d56d5.md)

Bin Zhang; Ming Gao

Background \- Whether the metabolomic profile of stored platelets can predict storage duration across donors under donor\-wise validation is unknown\. We assessed a multi\-task learning framework\. Materials and methods \- Utilizing the public metabolomic dataset ST003937 \(239 samples, 24 donors, 111 metabolites\), a dual\-task machine learning framework was constructed to predict storage duration \(Task A\) and biotinylation status \(Task B\)\. Models were evaluated by donor\-wise 5\-fold cross\-validation with random\-split comparison\. Inter\-donor distances were quantified and SHAP \(SHapley Additive exPlanations\) identified key metabolites\. Multi\-task learning was also performed\. Results \- Task A failed to generalize, with a mean area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.46, improving to 0\.59 under random split, whereas Task B was robust \(AUC 0\.77\)\. Median inter\-donor distance \(6\.35\) far exceeded the storage group distance \(1\.73\)\. Multi\-task learning marginally improved Task A by 0\.03\. SHAP and Gini importance identified metabolites related to energy metabolism and oxidative stress as key features for Task B\. Discussion \- Inter\-donor metabolic variability exceeded storage\-induced changes in magnitude, explaining why cross\-donor prediction of storage duration was unsuccessful despite documented group\-level metabolic differences\. The robust AUC gap between validation strategies confirms a &quot;donor fingerprint&quot; effect\. Donor\-specific baselines may be useful for future assessment of platelet quality\. Multi\-task learning provided marginal improvement\. Task B&\#x27;s robust performance validates the analytical framework\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS EFFECTS ON STUDENTS’ READING AND WRITING SKILLS AT THE SECONDARY SCHOOL LEVEL](../publications/e435e0f9a048bcd99432.md)

Sana Sarwar; Rashid Minas Wattoo; Ms\. Saba Gul

Although international scholarship on AI in education had expanded rapidly, empirical evidence concerning its relationship with the reading and writing skills of secondary\-school students in Pakistan had remained limited\. The present study examined the relationship between AI use and the reading and writing performance of male students enrolled in public secondary schools in District Sialkot, Punjab\. A quantitative, cross\-sectional, correlational research design was adopted\. The population comprised male students enrolled in Grades 9 and 10 in government secondary schools, from whom a multistage stratified random sample of 270 students was selected\. Data were collected through an AI Use in Learning Questionnaire, a researcher\-developed reading comprehension test, and an analytical writing performance test\. The study differentiated between productive and substitutive forms of AI use\. Productive use involved explanation seeking, guided practice, idea generation, verification, formative feedback, and reflective revision, whereas substitutive use involved outsourcing comprehension and composition, copying AI\-generated responses, and accepting machine\-generated content without critical evaluation\. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, analysis of variance, and hierarchical multiple regression were employed to examine the relationships among the variables\. The study provided a contextually grounded framework for understanding AI\-supported literacy, assessment integrity, digital inequality, teacher mediation, and responsible technology integration in Pakistani secondary education\.

## [A mixed\-methods study of depressive\-symptom severity among Thai university students and the underestimated role of social media](../publications/e43b4c00d592b35c82e2.md)

Pichit Boonkrong; Kodchakorn Khunboonjun; Subij Shakya; Junwei Yang; Naphatsakon Vitoonmetha; Manaporn Chatchumni

Purpose University students face academic, social, economic, and digital stressors\. Social\-media use may be under\-recognized as a correlate of depressive symptoms because online engagement is often viewed as routine communication, leisure, and academic activity\. This study examined factors associated with depressive\-symptom severity among Thai university students and explored the mismatch between perceived stressors and the observed association with social\-media use\. Methods A cross\-sectional mixed\-methods study was conducted among 789 undergraduates at Rangsit University, Thailand\. Quantitative data were collected using a structured questionnaire and the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale \(CES\-D\), categorized as low symptoms \(0–15\), mild\-to\-moderate \(16–26\), or severe \(27–60\) symptoms\. Associations were examined using χ 2 tests and ordinal logistic regression\. A purposive subsample of 12 students participated in semi\-structured interviews on social\-media routines, online comparison, nighttime use and sleep, coping, social support, and help\-seeking\. All interviews were audio\-recorded and supplemented by contemporaneous field notes\. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically and integrated with quantitative findings through joint comparison\. Results Clinically significant depressive symptoms \(CES\-D ≥ 16\) were reported by 49\.68% of students\. Academic year, major, GPAX, primary source of personal support, and daily social\-media use were independently associated with symptom severity\. Compared with students using social media &gt;3 h/day, those using it &lt;1 h/day \(OR = 0\.125, 95% CI: 0\.040–0\.391\) or 1–3 h/day \(OR = 0\.424, 95% CI: 0\.278–0\.647\) had lower odds of greater symptom severity\. Internet/social\-media use ranked only fifth among eight perceived stressors \(37\.01% agreement\)\. Three qualitative themes described social media as an embedded and ambivalent part of student life, psychological effects shaped by patterns and interpretations of use, and distress managed mainly through self\-coping and trusted informal support\. Conclusion The key mixed\-methods finding was a perception–association mismatch: social\-media use was not perceived as a leading stressor yet showed the strongest adjusted association with depressive\-symptom severity among the factors examined\. These cross\-sectional findings do not establish causality but support digital\-wellbeing assessment beyond duration alone\.

## [Learner autonomy in Ethiopian secondary EFL classrooms: observed teacher practices and student perceptions](../publications/e43ece127e3a2caad233.md)

Esayas Teshome Taddese; Habtamu Adem; Mitiku Tasisa Dinsa; A Shorouk

Learner autonomy is widely recognized as a goal of modern language education\. However, in Ethiopian EFL contexts, the extent to which autonomy is promoted remains largely unknown\. This study investigated the relationship between teachers’ autonomy\-supportive practices and learner autonomy in Ethiopian secondary school EFL classrooms, a context marked by large classes, teacher\-centered instruction, and exam\-driven curricula\. Employing an explanatory sequential mixed methods design with quantitative priority \(QUAN→qual\), the research involved 412 students and 34 teachers from eight public schools in Gurage Zone, Central Ethiopia\. Data were collected through classroom observations \(Teacher Autonomy\-Supportive Practices Observation Schedule, TAPOS\), student perception surveys \(Student Perception of Autonomy Support Scale, SPASS\), and a learner autonomy inventory \(Learner Autonomy Inventory, LAI\)\. Because students were nested within teachers, quantitative analyses distinguished between student\-level and teacher\-level variables and employed two\-level linear mixed\-effects modeling and a 2\-1\-1 multilevel mediation model\. Qualitative data from interviews and focus groups provided complementary insights\. Findings revealed low levels of observed autonomy\-supportive practices \(mean = 2\.1/5\), with “providing rationales” most common \(68% of lessons\) and “encouraging self\-initiation” least common \(4%\)\. Students’ perceived autonomy support was relatively low when autonomy\-specific items were analyzed \(mean = 2\.7/5\), while their self\-reported autonomous behaviors were also low \(mean = 2\.4/4\)\. The multilevel model indicated that teacher autonomy\-promoting practices were positively associated with learner autonomy, while students’ perceptions of autonomy\-supportive practices and prior English achievement were also positively associated with learner autonomy\. Class size showed a negative association with learner autonomy\. The multilevel mediation analysis indicated a significant indirect association between teacher autonomy\-promoting practices and learner autonomy through students’ perceptions of autonomy support\. Qualitatively, students desired autonomy but felt unprepared, while teachers viewed autonomy as culturally challenging but not impossible\. The study concludes that an “autonomy gap” exists, necessitating teacher training that addresses cultural beliefs and systemic constraints and promotes gradual, structured approaches to learner autonomy\.

## [A GeoAI framework integrating YOLO\-based micro mobility detection and GIS–MCDM for heavy\-vehicle blind\-spot warning deployment](../publications/e440398bff4506dae368.md)

Ömer Kaya; Muhammed Yasin Çodur

Introduction Micromobility modes such as e\-scooters, bicycles, and e\-bikes are becoming important components of low\-emission urban transportation systems\. However, their interactions with heavy vehicles pose significant safety risks, particularly in blind spots, at intersections, and during turning movements\. This study proposes an integrated GeoAI\-GIS\-MCDM framework to prioritize the deployment of heavy\-vehicle blind\-spot warning systems in urban areas and evaluate the detection capabilities of camera\-based perception models\. Methods The proposed framework consists of two complementary components: macro\-scale spatial prioritization and micro\-scale object detection\. A GIS\-based spatial decision\-support model was developed using 18 evaluation criteria grouped into three categories: micromobility user exposure potential, heavy\-vehicle operating exposure, and blind\-spot conflict and safety vulnerability\. Criteria weights were determined through assessments by five experts using Fuzzy Simple Weight Calculation \(Fuzzy SIWEC\) and Fuzzy Logarithm Methodology of Additive Weights \(FLMAW\)\. A hybrid weighting approach was then applied to generate a deployment priority map in ArcMap\. Additionally, six YOLO\-based object detection models were trained and evaluated under identical training configurations using a dataset of 6,070 images covering five micromobility\-related classes\. Results Blind\-spot conflict and safety vulnerability emerged as the most influential criterion group, while high\-activity blind\-spot overlap potential received the highest individual hybrid weight\. The resulting spatial priority map identified central and inner urban zones as the most critical candidate areas for warning\-system deployment\. The YOLO models achieved mAP@0\.50 values ranging from 0\.9438 to 0\.9694 and mAP@0\.50:0\.95 values ranging from 0\.8739 to 0\.9079\. YOLO26s achieved the highest mAP@0\.50, whereas YOLO26m obtained the highest mAP@0\.50:0\.95\. Discussion The findings demonstrate the complementary roles of GIS\-based spatial prioritization and YOLO\-based visual perception in supporting micromobility safety management\. By identifying priority deployment locations and assessing object detection performance, the proposed framework provides a decision\-support approach for the targeted implementation of intelligent heavy\-vehicle blind\-spot warning technologies\.

## [Operation state gated topology aware multimodal fusion for simulation based active distribution network risk assessment](../publications/e45a7734e8982d9032c4.md)

Lei Feng; Baolin Liu; Chong Du; Yanru Duan; Xianmin Wang

Active distribution planning requires day\-ahead identification of buses exposed to voltage and loading stress\. Separating injection forecasting from feeder simulation leaves the contribution of multimodal fusion to node\-risk estimation unresolved\. We develop OSTMF\-Net, an operation\-state\-gated topology\-aware multimodal fusion network that combines temporal and graph experts through convex, residual and direct heads selected on a chronological validation holdout\. Public load and NASA POWER weather variables are mapped to the IEEE 123\-node OpenDSS feeder\. Quasi\-static time\-series simulations generate deterministic 24\-h absolute\-risk and positive\-increment targets under base, high\-photovoltaic, heavy\-load and combined\-stress conditions\. Evaluation measures agreement with OpenDSS\-derived risk surrogates within this reproducible simulation benchmark\. Among matched fusion methods across eight correlated scenario\-target cases, OSTMF\-Net obtains the lowest root mean square error \(RMSE\) in six and remains within 1% of the lowest value in seven\. Mean case\-wise RMSE reductions are 9\.77%, 17\.37% and 3\.72% relative to a validation\-selected expert, uniform averaging and linear stacking, respectively; gains over stacking concentrate in absolute\-risk cases\. A matched state\-adaptive control yields mean RMSE 0\.03460 versus 0\.03080 for OSTMF\-Net\. Forecast perturbations, sensor\-input corruption and label sensitivity assess robustness to input and target changes\. On a disjoint 2013 chronology on the same feeder, OSTMF\-Net records RMSE 0\.03067, high\-risk F1 0\.795 and Top\-10 agreement 1\.000\. The results connect complementary temporal and topology information with state\-dependent correction, supporting auditable day\-ahead bus\-risk screening on the evaluated OpenDSS benchmark\.

## [The Dark Side of Generative AI in Marketing: AI\-Generated False and Misleading Advertising and Its Consumer Consequences](../publications/e461518d29ea33964b33.md)

Dr\. Pankaj Nandurkar; Mr\. Pradeep Gupta; Mr\. Sangram Andhe; Dr\. Krishnakant Lasune

Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is transforming advertising by enabling marketers to create persuasive text, images, and other promotional content rapidly and at lower cost\. At the same time, the ability of generative systems to produce highly realistic content creates concerns about deception, misinformation, transparency, and the credibility of consumer\-facing information\. The present study examines the consumer consequences of AI\-generated false and misleading advertising, with particular emphasis on hallucinated product claims\. The study focuses on whether AI\-generated hallucinated product claims influence perceived deception, AI skepticism, and perceived information reliability, and whether these consumer responses subsequently shape purchase intention\. Drawing on the stimulus\-organism\-response \(S\-O\-R\) framework, the study conceptualizes hallucinated product claims as the stimulus, the three consumer evaluations as the organism, and purchase intention as the response\. A quantitative, cross\-sectional, deductive research design was adopted\. Data were collected from 320 business\-school students and faculty members through a structured questionnaire using a five\-point Likert scale, and the model was assessed using SmartPLS\. The reported measurement results show Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha values above 0\.70, composite reliability above the stated threshold, and average variance extracted above 0\.50 for all constructs, indicating acceptable reliability and convergent validity\. The reported discriminant\-validity matrix also supports construct distinctiveness\. The structural model reports a VIF range of 1\.47\-2\.24 and an R² of 0\.421 for purchase intention\. Four of the six hypotheses are supported\. AI\-generated hallucinated product claims significantly increase perceived deception and significantly reduce perceived information reliability\. Perceived deception significantly reduces purchase intention, while perceived information reliability significantly increases purchase intention\. The paths from hallucinated product claims to AI skepticism and from AI skepticism to purchase intention are not statistically significant\. The findings indicate that message\-level judgments of deception and information reliability are more consequential for purchase intention in the reported model than generalized skepticism toward AI\. The study extends the S\-O\-R perspective to the dark side of GenAI in advertising and highlights the importance of factual verification, transparency, human oversight, disclosure, and consumer AI literacy\. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence; AI hallucinations; misleading advertising; perceived deception; AI skepticism; perceived information reliability; purchase intention; stimulus\-organism\-response theory\.

## [Reconstruction of daily snow depth at 0\.25° resolution over the arid regions of Central Asia from 1980 to 2023 using machine learning](../publications/e464dc660047528013fe.md)

Liancheng Zhang; Guli Jiapaer; Tao Yu; Jie Bai; Xiapeng Jiang; Hongwu Liang; Pingping Feng; Tongwei Ju; Philippe De Maeyer; Tim Van de Voorde

Arid regions of Central Asia \(CA\) depend heavily on snowmelt, but limited monitoring stations and unreliable snow depth \(SD\) data hinder effective snow monitoring\. In this study, we applied XGBoost \(XGB\) and random forest \(RF\) machine learning models to integrate multiple SD products with covariates—including geospatial, snow\-related, meteorological, land cover, and time data—along with in situ SD measurements, to enhance SD monitoring in CA\. Two modeling approaches were tested: segmented modeling based on snow development stages and whole\-period modeling for the entire snow season\. The results showed that segmented fusion modeling outperformed whole\-period modeling, with XGB\-based models capturing SD variations more effectively than RF\-based models and existing SD products\. Notably, the XGB\-based fusion models markedly improved the SD estimates for complex high\-elevation terrain\. Model performance analysis revealed that accuracy increased with the increasing number of integrated SD products\. Moreover, the models incorporating ERA5\-Land outperformed those that used the other datasets\. While all covariate types enhanced the model performance, geospatial features made the most significant contributions\. Ultimately, using the XGB\-segmented fusion model, we developed a 0\.25° daily SD dataset for CA spanning 1980–2023, providing a reliable resource for snow monitoring in the region\.
