## [Influencer Marketing in The Age of Artificial Intelligence: Exploring The Impact Of Ai\-Generated Influencers on Brand Credibility and Purchase Intention](../publications/e4712a36bd390771a850.md)

Ms\. Preeti Sharma and Dr\. Punam Devi; Ms\. Pooja\. P

Brands are increasingly partnering with AI\-generated influencers — computer\-generated personas that post, endorse, and interact on social media\. Whether such endorsers can build the credibility on which purchase decisions depend remains unclear\. This study examines the effect of five attributes of AI\-generated influencers — Perceived Realism, Perceived Authenticity, Perceived Expertise, Parasocial Interaction, and Perceived Transparency \(AI disclosure\) — on Brand Credibility, and tests the role of Brand Credibility in shaping Purchase Intention\.A descriptive and analytical research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 400 social media users in Tamil Nadu who had encountered branded content from AI\-generated influencers, using a structured five\-point Likert\-scale questionnaire and stratified random sampling by age group\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and bootstrapped mediation analysis \(PROCESS Model 4\)\.All five attributes significantly predicted Brand Credibility, with Perceived Authenticity \(β = 0\.268\) and Perceived Expertise \(β = 0\.206\) strongest; the model explained 59\.0% of its variance\. Brand Credibility strongly predicted Purchase Intention \(β = 0\.424\), and the full model explained 64\.2% of the variance in intention\. Brand Credibility significantly mediated all five relationships, fully for Perceived Realism and Perceived Transparency and partially for the others\. The findings offer implications for brands, agencies, and regulators on the use and disclosure of AI\-generated influencers

## [IMPACT OF EXTENDED REALITY USAGE FOR OFFICE TASKS: A LONGITUDINAL STUDY](../publications/e47531c4aa100292678b.md)

Ashwini Srinivasaprasad

Headsets now let workers switch between virtual reality \(VR\) and augmented reality \(AR\), but the costs of such switching had not been measured in continuous work, across sessions, or against posture and muscle load\. Thirty\-six participants typed while standing in three sessions a median of about one week apart\. Each session had eight counterbalanced blocks: VR with a mid\- air keyboard and AR with a physical keyboard, each immersive \(virtual scene\) or passthrough \(video of the room\)\. Typing, spine motion, muscle activity, workload and 2\-back scores were analyzed with mixed\-effects, recovery\-curve and machine\-learning models\. Input modality dominated performance\. VR typing was 65\.5% to 69\.0% slower than AR passthrough typing and less accurate, and VR was rated higher in workload than AR\. Muscle load redistributed, with forearm extensor activity higher in AR and upper trapezius activity higher in VR\. Observational posture scores missed this shift, but muscle and motion features identified held\- out participants&\#x27; blocks by modality with 73\.7% balanced accuracy \(chance 50%\)\. Blocks after compound transitions, which changed view and keyboard together, were 12\.0% slower than after view\-only and 7\.5% slower than after input\-only transitions\. After every type of switch, typing returned to 95% of its steady\-state speed within 45 seconds of typing time, about a minute of clock time, so the slower pace after compound transitions outlasted that recovery\. Typing became 9\.2% faster each session, and VR typing improved at more than twice the AR rate\. Practice shrank the slowdown in each session&\#x27;s first block but not the slowdown after each switch\. Early measures predicted later typing: Session 1 typing predicted Session 3 speed, and more Session 1 neck flexion, flexion variability, drift and movement variability predicted slower Session 3 typing\. Neck drift, forward neck flexion building within a block, also predicted next\-block typing 1\.4 words per minute slower per standard deviation, beyond current speed\. Within\-session gains were confined to mid\-air typing: 12\.6% per 10 minutes in Session 1, 5\.2% in Session 2 and no change in Session 3\. On the 2\-back memory test, which asks whether each item matches the one two items earlier, telling matches from non\-matches improved from before to after Session 1 and declined in later sessions\. 16Designers should keep physical input for sustained typing, change view and keyboard one at a time, allow a minute after each switch before precision work, support the arms in mid\-air work, and evaluate each input modality over several sessions\.

## [AI and IoT driven intelligent risk control and verification system for international trade settlement](../publications/e476cb24f924205f3877.md)

Renran Miao

Cross\-border trading and digital financial platforms are growing rapidly, making the settlement of international trade more complex and complex, which requires reliable verification of transactions and effective financial risk control\. Traditional rule\-based techniques are not flexible in the dynamic trading context\. To overcome these limitations, an IoT\-powered intelligent verification and AI\-driven risk control model is introduced to improve the authenticity of transactions, provide real\-time monitoring and improve proactive financial risk control based on distributed sensing technologies and adaptive AI algorithms\. The IoT Trade Settlement Risk dataset, comprising 9990 samples, is used to collect transactional records, trade documentation metadata and payment behaviour data\. Data preparation involves applying Min–Max normalization and Savitzky–Golay filtering to make data consistent from different sources\. The discriminative information is represented by Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\) of critical trade indicators\. The core analytical engine employs a Termite Alate Optimization\-driven Adaptive Deep Convolutional Neural Network \(TAO\-ADCNN\) model perform multi\-class transaction risk classification by categorizing each trade transaction into low\-, medium\-, or high\-risk classes\. The predicted risk category is subsequently utilized to support intelligent transaction verification and anomaly monitoring\. Convolutional parameters and network weights to improve convergence efficiency and global search capability, while the ADCNN analyzes hierarchical transaction patterns for accurate risk categorization\. Experiments using Python have shown that the suggested TAO\-ADCNN model outperforms the other models and datasets, attaining higher accuracy results, with a range of 96% to 98\.9%\. The overall results obtained the identification of risks, verification, and resilience are improved in international trade settlement management systems\. TAO\-ADCNN enables proactive monitoring of financial and operational risks\. System improves classification consistency across varied trading scenarios\. Efficient risk detection allows early action for high\-risk transactions\. System enhances transparency and accountability in cross\-border trade systems\.

## [Applications of Stochastic Processes in Engineering: The Poisson Process and a Simulation Study of Vehicle Arrivals](../publications/e47da11073298aef8d5b.md)

Helgi Llozana

Stochastic processes are important to model systems that have components of randomness, and that develop over time; they are useful in engineering\. Of those, arguably the most basic and indispensable is the Poisson process which is also used to describe the likelihood of random, independent events to occur in various applications such as telecommunication, reliability, transportation, manufacturing and energy systems\. Drawing upon mathematical theory the Poisson process is defined by its rate parameter which is λ, and also explains that it possesses nice features such as independent and stationary increments which make it suitable for modelling real\-life phenomena\. Communication systems apply the Poisson process to model packet arrivals and enhance the performance of the application, and reliability engineering uses it to estimate the failure rate and plan for maintenance\. In transport, the process is useful in modelling ways of managing traffic and even the schedule of a public transport system\. Manufacturing systems use quality assurance and inventory control modeling while energy systems use the Poisson process for power outages and renewable energy systems planning\. The article also discusses generalizations of non\-Poisson processes for practical situations where the rate assumptions and events are correlated\. To move from description to demonstration, the paper further reports a Monte Carlo experiment in which 500 one\-minute intervals of vehicle arrivals are generated from exponential interarrival times at a mean rate of λ = 20 vehicles per minute\. The simulated counts are compared with the theoretical Poisson distribution through a time series, a histogram, an interarrival plot and a quantile\-quantile plot, and are tested formally by a chi\-square goodness\-of\-fit test \(χ² = 7\.40, df = 6, p = 0\.285\); the interarrival times are tested against the exponential law \(Kolmogorov–Smirnov D = 0\.012, p = 0\.122\)\. Neither test finds evidence against the Poisson model, and the experiment quantifies how much minute\-to\-minute variation an engineer should expect around a constant mean rate — a result with direct consequences for signal timing and capacity margins\.

## [Algorithmic Guidance and Investor Learning: An Empirical Examination of Robo\-Advisors](../publications/e495c5bb22fcbf04df5d.md)

Dasari Sharon; I\. Mohana Krishna

Growth in robo\-advisors has broadened retail access to investor\-centric digital financial advice; however, it remains uncertain whether using them makes investors smart or feels smarter\. This study investigates relationships between robo\-adoption, digital financial literacy, financial expertise, and investment results among young and late\-career retail investors in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh\. Data were gathered with a structured, self\-administered Likert\-scale questionnaire; 94 effectively responded \(out of 123 distributed\)\. Chi\-square tests, one\-way ANOVA, and linear regressions were computed\. Robo\-adoption was significantly related to gender \(1\) = 4\.79, p =\.029\. Adoption, digital literacy, expertise, and outcomes were significantly different across age, gender, education, income, experience, and occupational groups\. Simple regressions indicated all four hypotheses are supported: adoption predicted digital literacy \( =\.30, p =\.003\) and expertise \( =\.32, p =\.001\), digital literacy predicted expertise \( =\.26, p =\.012\), and expertise predicted perceived investment success \( =\.65, p &lt;\.001, R =\.43\)\. When adopting and learning were tested jointly, only adoption was significant\. Sub\-dimension analyses indicate that the effect of adoption resides mainly in diversification awareness and information\-based decision\-making, while the self\-perceived risktolerance and rate\-of\-return knowledge was slightly lower among more frequent users\. Reliability of the scales for expertise and performance outcomes was weak, and data set contains duplicate respondents, so results should be considered indicative\.

## [CoDA: Co\-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies](../publications/e4a39cf0737d1bf337e1.md)

Tianjiao Yu; Zhilin Ou; Yifan Shen; Xinzhuo Li; Yuanzhe Liu; Onkar Kishor Susladkar; Fan Wang; Ismini Lourentzou

Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training\. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy&\#x27;s failures and supervision that helps it overcome them\. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co\-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress\. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision\-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them\. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action\-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task&\#x27;s optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions\. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement\. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out\-of\-distribution success from 5\.3% after supervised fine\-tuning to 27\.6%, exceeding the strongest closed\-loop baseline by 9\.5 percentage points with the same generation budget\. On LIBERO\-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations\.

## [AI\-Enabled Wearable Sensor Technologies for Athlete Performance Monitoring: A Critical Review of Signal Processing, Machine Learning, and Real\-Time Embedded Systems](../publications/e4b760e003b951c8903d.md)

nbspDr\. Vikas Kundu

Abstract Wearable sensing and artificial intelligence \(AI\) are increasingly being used to quantify athlete movement, physiological response, training load, and recovery in field and laboratory settings\. However, the practical value of these systems depends not only on the predictive capability of an algorithm but also on sensor validity, signal quality, hardware constraints, real\-time processing, and the transferability of models across athletes and sports\. This review examines the technical pipeline linking wearable electronic sensors to athlete\-monitoring decisions, with particular attention to inertial measurement units, global navigation satellite systems, photoplethysmography, electrocardiography, electromyography, pressure sensing, and multimodal systems\. It synthesizes evidence on signal conditioning, segmentation, feature engineering, classical machine learning, deep learning, sensor fusion, edge inference, and embedded implementation\. Existing reviews indicate that wearable devices can support useful monitoring, but accuracy varies by metric, device, movement pattern, and validation setting; performance under controlled conditions should not be assumed to generalize to competition\. Key challenges include motion artifacts, inconsistent protocols, small and imbalanced datasets, leakage between training and test sets, limited external validation, battery and communication constraints, privacy, and unclear decision thresholds\. The review proposes a layered reference architecture and a validation framework that links engineering performance to sport\-specific usefulness\. Future research should prioritize synchronized multimodal datasets, athlete\-independent testing, interpretable and uncertainty\-aware models, energy\-efficient edge AI, secure data governance, and transparent reporting\. The article’s contribution is an engineering\-oriented synthesis that connects sensor physics and embedded constraints with the needs of physical education and sports science\. Keywords: Inertial Measurement Units; Physiological Sensing; Sensor Fusion; Edge Computing; Sports Biomechanics Keywords: edge computing; Keywords: Inertial Measurement Units; Physiological Sensing; Sensor Fusion; Sports Biomechanics

## [Development of A Lightweight Neural Network for Predicting Reaction Rates in RANS Simulations of Flame\-Wall Interactions](../publications/e4baad43054e9c3335b4.md)

Maximilian Bambauer; Vipin Michael; Markus Klein; Nilanjan Chakraborty

Abstract Accurate prediction of Flame\-Wall Interactions \(FWI\) is crucial for the design of compact, high\-efficiency combustors but remains a significant challenge for Reynolds\-Averaged Navier\-Stokes \(RANS\) simulations\. This study presents the development and validation of a lightweight data\-driven closure for the mean reaction rate, trained on high\-fidelity Direct Numerical Simulation \(DNS\) data of a V\-shaped turbulent premixed flame\. To ensure numerical stability and physical consistency, the training methodology incorporates a logarithmic transformation of the reaction rate target and a novel error\-function transformation of the wall distance, effectively localizing the model’s sensitivity to the near\-wall quenching zone\. A\-priori validation demonstrates that the neural network accurately captures the mean reaction rate statistics and extrapolates successfully to unseen spatial regions\. However, a\-posteriori assessment in coupled RANS simulations reveals a critical sensitivity to input feature consistency\. The full\-feature model \(7 input parameters\), which includes turbulent kinetic energy and dissipation rate as inputs, fails to predict the correct quenching behavior due to significant discrepancies between the DNS\-extracted turbulence quantities used for training and the corresponding quantities obtained from RANS\. In contrast, a reduced\-feature model \(3 input parameters\), relying exclusively on the mean progress variable, its gradient, and the transformed wall distance, demonstrates remarkable robustness\. By decoupling the prediction from uncertain turbulence quantities, the model with 3 input parameters accurately reproduces the V\-flame structure, achieving performance comparable to a manually tuned algebraic closure\. Furthermore, the reduced model exhibits strong generalization capabilities, successfully predicting the transient physics of a Head\-On Quenching \(HOQ\) configuration that was not present in the training dataset\. These findings highlight that for data\-driven RANS closures, selecting input features that remain consistent across fidelity levels, is paramount for achieving predictive stability and generalization\.

## [Effectiveness of an Integrative Yoga and Dietary Intervention in the Management of Functional Constipation: An Empirical Study](../publications/e4c0e7795b0bb4f8d08f.md)



Functional constipation is one of the most prevalent gastrointestinal disorders worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and substantially impairing physical health, psychological well\-being, and overall quality of life\.Despite the widespread use of pharmacological therapies, many patients experience only temporary symptom relief, adverse effects, or long\-term dependence on laxatives, highlighting the need for safe and sustainable complementary approaches\.The present study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an integrative intervention combining a structured dietary program with yoga practices in the management of functional constipation\.A randomized controlled trial was conducted among adults diagnosed with functional constipation according to the Rome IV diagnostic criteria\.Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving a high\-fiber dietary regimen along with a standardized yoga protocol comprising selected asanas, pranayama, and relaxation techniques, or a control group receiving standard lifestyle advice\.The intervention was implemented over a period of 12 weeks\.Clinical outcomes were assessed using bowel movement frequency, Bristol Stool Form Scale, constipation severity, constipation\-related quality of life, and perceived stress\.Statistical analyses included paired and independent t\-tests, chi\-square tests, and repeated\-measures analysis of variance, with statistical significance established at p &lt; 0\.05\.The findings demonstrated that participants receiving the integrative intervention experienced significant improvements in bowel movement frequency, stool consistency, constipation severity, and quality\-of\-life scores compared with the control group\.Furthermore, reductions in perceived stress and high adherence to both dietary and yoga interventions suggested that the combined approach effectively addressed both the physiological and psychological determinants of bowel dysfunction\.These findings indicate that integrating evidence\-based dietary modification with yoga practices offers a safe, cost\-effective, and sustainable complementary strategy for the management of functional constipation\.The study supports the incorporation of holistic lifestyle interventions into routine clinical practice and recommends further large\-scale, multicenter studies with longer followup periods to validate these findings and strengthen the evidence base for integrative management of functional constipation\.

## [Beyond Expected Values: Risk\-Sensitive Planning with Distributional Monte\-Carlo Tree Search](../publications/e4d38defc304ee7b28f7.md)

Quynh Trinh; Trung Nguyen; Nam Nguyen; Tuan Dam

Monte\-Carlo Tree Search \(MCTS\) typically stores only scalar mean estimates, which makes it poorly suited for tail\-risk objectives such as conditional value\-at\-risk \(CVaR\)\. We introduce Categorical Thompson Sampling with Optimism \(CATSO\) and Particle Thompson Sampling with Optimism \(PATSO\), two distributional MCTS algorithms that maintain finite\-support empirical backup laws at Q\-edges\. CATSO represents Q\-edge laws with categorical atoms and Dirichlet Thompson sampling, while PATSO represents them with adaptive particles\. Both algorithms select actions using the CVaR of a Thompson\-sampled Q\-edge law plus a polynomial optimism bonus, and propagate scalar continuation values through visit\-weighted averages of child Q\-edge CVaR scores\. For the finite\-depth nested CVaR planning target, we prove an $O\(n^\{\-1/2\}\)$ bound on the root value error after $n$ rollouts, which upper\-bounds the risk\-sensitive simple regret\. CATSO adds a fixed\-grid discretization bias, while capped PATSO adds a tunable Wasserstein compression bias\. Experiments on stochastic planning benchmarks show that distributional Q\-edges improve lower\-tail return and reduce catastrophic outcomes when mean\-optimal and risk\-sensitive behavior differ\.

## [Harness\-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution](../publications/e4d4dc16f876aaefe1df.md)

Wenxuan Ding; Qin Lu; Changlong Yu; Sha Li; Shuowei Jin; Xin Liu; Zhenyu Shi; Greg Durrett

Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed\-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights\. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set\. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark\-specific overfitting or additional inference\-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness\-Delta Attribution \(HDA\), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact\-driven overfitting, gains explained by test\-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement\. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness\-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks\. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search\-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test\-time scaling\. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test\-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings\. The residual and held\-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks\. Importantly, search\-set gains often fail to transfer to held\-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts\. Moreover, validation\-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting\. These results motivate attribution\-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research\.

## [From Promise to Practice A HEALinc Global Summit White Paper](../publications/e4d8d40807061b9aa0ef.md)

Desiree C\. T\. Cox

This paper, developed by HEALinc CEO and Founder Dr\. Desirée Cox, translates a day of multidisciplinary discussion at the 2026 HEALinc Global Summit, New York City \(NYC\) Day Conclave into a coherent systems framework and action agenda\. It is not a transcript, clinical guideline, regulatory opinion, or endorsement of every intervention or claim discussed at the Summit\. The source material captures perspectives from scientists, physicians, biotechnology leaders, lawyers, investors, former regulators, patient advocates, educators, architects, and other participants\. Sponsors, speakers, and key opinion leaders represented at the HEALinc New York City \(NYC\) Day Conclave are identified in the Appendices\. The proceedings ranged from late\-stage clinical development and international regulatory pathways to whole\-person health, patient experience, digital monitoring, medical education, and the design of healing environments\. The purpose of this paper is to identify the recurring system\-level insights, clarify where genuine convergence occurred, and convert those insights into a practical architecture for translation\. Some interventions and outcomes described during the discussions were preliminary, anecdotal, contested, or outside established standards of evidence\. They are treated here as signals of emerging questions and unmet needs – not as validated clinical conclusions\. Any therapy must be evaluated according to its own evidence, manufacturing quality, ethical acceptability, regulatory status, and risk profile\. Interpretive StanceThe field should neither equate regulatory caution with obstruction nor equate permissive access with progress\. The task is to create controlled velocity: faster, more coherent learning and access under stronger evidence, ethics, quality, and accountability\.

## [The 4Cs Marketing Theory and Customer Satisfaction: The Mediating Role of Perceived Value among Specialized and New SMEs in China](../publications/e4e370e1c994c550d3a4.md)

Kun Xu; Siti Zubaidah Mohd Ariffin; Nor Sa’adah Jamaluddin; Na Li

The rapid expansion of the digital economy has increased the importance of customer\-centric marketing strategies for improving customer satisfaction and organizational competitiveness\. However, limited empirical research has examined the mediating role of perceived value within the 4Cs Marketing Theory, particularly among China&\#x27;s Specialized and New Small and Medium\-sized Enterprises \(SMEs\)\. This study investigates the relationships among consumption factors, perceived value, and customer satisfaction\. A quantitative cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 384 enterprise customers of 38 Specialized and New SMEs in the information technology sector in Shandong Province, China\. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis \(CFA\), structural equation modeling \(SEM\), and bootstrap mediation analysis in AMOS\. The findings revealed significant positive relationships between consumption factors and customer satisfaction \(β = 0\.292\), consumption factors and perceived value \(β = 0\.478\), and perceived value and customer satisfaction \(β = 0\.389\)\. The estimated indirect effect suggested partial mediation, with perceived value accounting for approximately 39% of the total standardized effect\. The study extends the application of the 4Cs Marketing Theory to specialized SMEs and highlights the importance of perceived value in understanding customer satisfaction\. The findings provide practical guidance for strengthening customer\-oriented marketing strategies, improving value creation, and enhancing customer relationships in competitive digital business environments\.

## [Reimagining Support for DV/IPV Service Providers Through AI Literacy](../publications/e4f09ac71f9fe6ca1fd2.md)

Vanessa Cordoba; Huda Shaikh

As Domestic Violence \(DV\) and Intimate Partner Violence \(IPV\) organizations work to meet the complex needs of survivors, the realities facing the workforce demand closer examination\. DV/IPV advocates must navigate high caseloads, persistent exposure to trauma, limited organizational resources, and extensive administrative responsibilities that often overshadow the relational and advocacy work central to survivor support\. Given that 40–75% of DV/IPV staff experience moderate to high burnout \(Kulkarni et al\., 2013; Slattery &amp; Goodman, 2009\), exploration and use of new technological tools, such as generative artificial intelligence \(AI\), become a consideration in how organizations might offer support to DV/IPV staff in reducing workload, contributing to the discussion on preventing burnout\. Research in other sectors suggests that AI technologies can reduce administrative burdens, improve efficiency, and allow workers to focus more on meaningful aspects of their work \(Brynjolfsson &amp; McAfee, 2017\)\. While AI integration offers clear benefits, it also raises significant concerns, including deskilling, overreliance, and the marginalization of professional expertise \(Pavuluri et al\., 2024\)\. Reamer \(2025\) explains, it is necessary to develop a clear understanding of how AI is being used across the behavioral health settings, the ethical challenges it raises, evidence\-informed best practices, and practical risk\-management strategies to safeguard both clients and workers\. Therefore, as AI integration becomes more prominent in social work settings, a deeper look at the concept of AI literacy among the DV/IPV workforce becomes vital to ensure AI use does not compromise ethics, worker expertise and service delivery \(Reamer, 2025\)\.

## [Sequential phage therapy against Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonising a chronic venous skin ulcer](../publications/e50646de58772524c189.md)

Matteo Passerini; Novella Cesta; Caterina Ferretti; Francesco Petri; Michela Pellegrini; Rita Carminati; Simona Landonio; Ahmed El Goutbi; GINEVRA MORELLI; Sara Giordana Rimoldi; Sara Bolognini; Maria Vittoria Cossu; Irene Mileto; Gherard Batisti Biffignandi; Greta Petazzoni; Benjamin K\. Chan; Andrea Gori; Mariagrazia Di Luca

Chronic venous ulcers are often complicated by persistent bacterial colonisation and biofilm formation, impairing healing and limiting definitive surgical closure\. We report the compassionate\-use treatment of a chronic venous leg ulcer, presumed to be adversely affected by persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonisation using sequential topical administration of two lytic bacteriophages, TIVP\-27M and LPS\-26\. Phage therapy was well tolerated and associated with improvement in clinically suspected biofilm\-related indicators\. Surgical ulcer coverage was subsequently performed\. Longitudinal microbiological and genomic analyses showed persistence of a clonal P\. aeruginosa lineage, with transient emergence of a phage\-resistant isolate on day 16\. This isolate exhibited impaired growth and reduced swimming, swarming, and twitching motility, alongside genomic alterations affecting surface\-associated and motility\-related functions, including pilR , flgE , galU , and hmgA \. Later isolates remained susceptible to both phages\. These findings support personalised topical phage therapy as a potential adjunctive strategy for selected chronic wounds while highlighting complex evolutionary dynamics during treatment\.

## [Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Temperature Effects on Mechanical Strength of Fiber\-Reinforced High\-Performance Concrete](../publications/e50917eb821bb41ded6d.md)

Jagaran Chakma; Zhiguang Zhou; Badhan Chakma; Priyanta Chakma

Predicting the compressive strength of fiber\-reinforced high\-performance concrete subjected to temperature exposure is challenging because to the intricate interdependencies of mixture composition, fiber properties, curing conditions, and temperature\. A data\-driven framework to predict compressive strength utilizing 1,204 experimental records containing a diverse array of material designs and exposure situations\. This study evaluates eight machine\-learning models and demonstrate that ensemble approaches routinely surpass individual learners\. Both gradient boosting and extreme gradient boosting exhibit superior performance on unseen data, each attaining a R^2 of 0\.903\. Gradient boosting produces the minimal root mean square error \(6\.67 MPa\), whereas extreme gradient boosting achieves the lowest mean absolute error \(3\.97 MPa\) and mean absolute percentage error \(10\.60%\)\. The models are further interpreted utilizing Shapley additive explanations and partial dependence analysis, which reveal temperature as the primary factor influencing compressive strength, succeeded by fine aggregate, superplasticizer, cement content, water\-to\-binder ratio, and water content\. Strength diminishes significantly with rising temperature, albeit the extent of deterioration is contingent upon the specific combination design\. The best performing models are subsequently implemented in a Python\-based graphical user interface for expedited prediction\. Our findings offer a precise and comprehensible methodology for evaluating temperature\-dependent compressive strength and facilitate the practical, data\-driven design of fiber\-reinforced high\-performance concrete\.

## [CAD/CAM Technology in Dental Education: A Cross\-Sectional Assessment of Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions Among Dental Students](../publications/e510f50505e12628a5fc.md)



Background: Computer\-aided design and computer\-aided manufacturing \(CAD/CAM\) technology has become an important component of modern digital dentistry, particularly in prosthodontics and restorative dentistry\.The integration of digital impressions, computer\-aided design software, and automated manufacturing systems has improved the precision and efficiency of dental restorations\.Despite increasing use of CAD/CAM systems in clinical practice, awareness and knowledge of CAD/CAM technology among dental students may vary depending on their exposure during training\.Objective: The objective of the present study was to assess the awareness, knowledge, and perceptions regarding CAD/CAM technology among dental students\.Materials and Method: This cross\-sectional survey was conducted among dental students \(UG &amp; PG\) at Seema Dental College and Hospital, Rishikesh, Uttarakhand\.A structured questionnaire consisting of 28 questions related to awareness, knowledge, and perception of CAD/CAM technology was distributed through an online platform\.A total of 210 students participated in the study\.The collected data were compiled using Microsoft Excel and analysed using descriptive statistics and the chi\-square test to evaluate associations between awareness variables\.Results: A total of 210 dental students participated in the study, including 162 undergraduate students/interns and 48 postgraduate students\.The overall survey response rate was 71\.8%\.Awareness of CAD/CAM technology was reported by 45\.2% of participants, while 42\.9% had previously seen a CAD/CAM unit\.Only 26\.7% correctly identified the full form of CAD/CAM, 41\.4% were aware of digital impression technology, and 44\.9% were aware of three\-dimensional printing applications in dentistry\.Despite limited knowledge and exposure, 63\.8% of respondents expressed interest in learning CAD/CAM technology\.A significant association was observed between academic level and CAD/CAM awareness, with postgraduate students demonstrating substantially greater awareness than undergraduate students \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\.Conclusion: Awareness and knowledge of CAD/CAM technology among dental students were limited, particularly among undergraduate students\.However, strong interest in learning digital dentistry highlights the need for greater integration of CAD/CAM concepts and practical training into dental curriculum to enhance preparedness for contemporary clinical practice\.

## [Dose–response association and predictive value of plasma aldosterone concentration for cardiometabolic multimorbidity in patients with hypertension: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/e516c69f6b43a8da2082.md)

Zhiqiang Zhang; Nanfang Li; Qing Zhu; Junli Hu; Jing Hong; Wenbo Yang; Pan Zhou; 马慧敏; Rui Ma; Ting Wu

Background The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationship between cardiometabolic multimorbidity \(CMM\) and plasma aldosterone concentration \(PAC\) among patients with hypertension, to characterize the potential dose–response pattern, and to assess whether the inclusion of PAC into a conventional risk model improves risk reclassification and clinical utility\. Methods Between January 2010 and January 2026, 7,677 hospitalized hypertensive patients without CMM at baseline were included in this retrospective cohort analysis\. The follow\-up period was 3\.52 years on average\. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline \(RCS\) analyses were performed to examine the association between PAC and the risk of incident CMM\. The incremental predictive value of PAC was evaluated for 3\-year risk prediction using time\-dependent ROC analysis with inverse probability of censoring weighting \(IPCW\), survival\-based net reclassification improvement \(NRI\), integrated discrimination improvement \(IDI\), calibration assessment, and decision curve analysis \(DCA\)\. Based on the potential interaction observed in the subgroup analysis, RCS analyses stratified by serum potassium level and a bivariate penalized spline model were used to characterize the joint nonlinear associations of serum potassium and PAC with the risk of CMM\. The Boruta algorithm was additionally applied for feature selection and assessment of variable importance\. Results During follow\-up, 1,949 incident cases of CMM were documented\. Patients in the highest quartile of baseline PAC \(Q4\) had a considerably greater cumulative likelihood of CMM than those in the other quartiles, according to Kaplan–Meier analysis \(log\-rank P &lt; 0\.05\)\. In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, each 1\-ng/dL increment in PAC was associated with a 2% higher hazard of incident CMM \(hazard ratio \[HR\], 1\.02; 95% confidence interval \[CI\], 1\.02–1\.03\)\. Compared with the lowest quartile \(Q1\), the adjusted HRs were 1\.19 \(95% CI, 1\.04–1\.36\) for Q2, 1\.32 \(95% CI, 1\.16–1\.52\) for Q3, and 1\.65 \(95% CI, 1\.45–1\.87\) for Q4, with a significant trend across quartiles \( P for trend&lt;0\.001\)\. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between PAC and the risk of CMM \( P for nonlinearity &lt; 0\.001\), identifying an estimated inflection point at approximately 15\.34 ng/dL, above which the risk curve showed an upward trend\. Subgroup analyses indicated that the PAC–CMM association may differ by serum potassium status \( P for interaction &lt; 0\.05\)\. After PAC was added to the baseline prediction model, the time\-dependent AUC increased from 0\.678 to 0\.735 \( P &lt; 0\.001\), with a net reclassification improvement of 0\.372 and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0\.038 \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. DCA suggested that incorporating PAC may provide additional estimated net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities\. The Boruta feature\-selection algorithm identified PAC as an important predictor, and the overall findings remained consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses\. Conclusion The possibility of a CMM incident was positively correlated with PAC in a nonlinear fashion, and this correlation differed depending on serum potassium levels\. Incorporating PAC into a conventional risk model was associated with improved predictive performance and greater net clinical benefit, suggesting that PAC may provide additional prognostic information for cardiometabolic risk stratification among patients with hypertension\.

## [Deep Learning\-Based Image Recognition for Spatial Perception Assessment and Landscape Optimization in Urban Parks](../publications/e51de7575c720b5e5e8f.md)

Wanyue Cao; Mohd Iskandar Abd Malek; Mohd Khairul Azhar Mat Sulaiman; Yancen Meng

The visual environment of urban parks plays a critical role in shaping public spatial perception and environmental experience; however, systematic understanding of age\-related differences and nonlinear responses to visual environments remains limited\. Taking Guazhu Lake Park in Shaoxing, China, as the study area, this study developed an integrated analytical framework combining deep learning\-based image recognition, spatial perception assessment, machine learning prediction, and SHAP\-based interpretation\. Eight visual environmental indicators, including the Green View Index \(GVI\), Sky View Index \(SVI\), water proportion, hardscape proportion, facility visibility, and visual obstruction, were extracted using semantic segmentation\. These indicators were integrated with evaluations of beauty, safety, restoration, and vibrancy from children, adults, and older adults to predict spatial perception using machine learning models\. SHAP analysis was further employed to identify the relative importance and nonlinear responses of key visual attributes\. The results showed that the visual environment of Guazhu Lake Park exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity, characterized by abundant vegetation and water features, together with a coexistence of open and enclosed spaces\. Different visual attributes exerted differentiated and nonlinear effects on spatial perception, while distinct age groups exhibited substantially different sensitivities to visual environmental characteristics\. Based on these findings, low\-perception areas were identified, and age\-specific micro\-landscape optimization strategies were proposed\. This study provides a data\-driven approach and practical basis for quantitative spatial perception assessment and age\-inclusive landscape optimization in urban parks\.

## [Chance\-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning](../publications/e535c9ba3af3260ed3e5.md)

Ameya Anjarlekar; Rasoul Etesami; R Srikant

We study personalized LLM routing, where a router selects among heterogeneous models with different costs and capabilities\. The router must minimize cumulative inference cost while ensuring reliable realized response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned from feedback during deployment\. We formulate this problem as a constrained contextual bandit and develop an algorithm that learns preferences while balancing cost and quality\. Under a logistic preference model and a strict\-feasibility condition, we establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized contextual oracle and a high\-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction\. The framework extends beyond LLM routing to broader online model\-selection problems with reliability requirements\.

## [Advances and gaps in bilge water treatment for water reuse](../publications/e537fcb909b25d4f9af7.md)

Maggie Gad; Mohamed Ismail Bassyouni; Amr E\. Mansi; Noran Ashraf; Yasser Elhenawy; Riham Hazzaa; Monica Toderaș; Fathy Shokry

ABSTRACT The diagram summarizes bilgewater’s environmental and societal threats, oil weathering and emulsion formation, and electrocoagulation, membrane, biological, and hybrid treatments\. Bilge water is estimated to account for a substantial fraction of oily wastewater discharged from marine vessels\. It is a complex effluent composed of seawater, lubricants, fuels, detergents, solvents, and solid particles\. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of bilge water characteristics, environmental and socioeconomic impacts, and current treatment technologies\. Emphasis is placed on quantifying pollutants, with reported oil content ranging from 36 to 976 ppm, pH values between 6\.8 and 9\.0, and chemical oxygen demand \(COD\) levels reaching up to 12,800 ppm\. The environmental hazards of untreated bilge water include severe ecological harm, risks to seabirds and marine biodiversity, and contamination of fisheries and tourism sectors, contributing to economic losses in coastal communities\. Treatment strategies are categorized into electrochemical, membrane\-based technologies, and biological processes\. Hybrid systems, combining techniques such as electrocoagulation and reverse osmosis, have demonstrated superior pollutant removal efficiencies exceeding 99% for oil, turbidity, and total dissolved solids\. Furthermore, although AI use in bilge water treatment remains underexplored, AI\-based image analysis and machine learning models have shown potential to predict emulsion stability, thereby optimizing treatment design and monitoring\. Hybrid systems achieved the highest removal efficiencies; however, several limitations still require further investigation, including cost, energy consumption, membrane lifetime and fouling in membrane\-based systems, and regulatory compliance for marine oily wastewater remediation\.

## [Generative modeling of topological and spatiotemporal data](../publications/e53a6683e8b0187c6314.md)

Qi Yan

Structured data are central to modern machine learning systems, but their structure creates modeling challenges that are not present in flat vectors or single images: graphs are invariant to node ordering, visual scenes combine symbolic relations with continuous geometry, and human or driving motion evolves through interacting agents under uncertainty\. This dissertation develops generative models for topological, hybrid, and spatiotemporal data by adapting how these models represent, learn, and sample structured distributions\. The first part of this thesis studies topological and hybrid data\. It begins with graph generation, where we bound the support of closest invariant distributions under explicit symmetry assumptions and characterize the symmetrized empirical target induced by equivariant denoising\. Learning additional permuted representations can reduce performance in the studied settings\. This motivates a graph diffusion model that combines flexible non\-invariant denoising with permutation\-invariant sampling and an efficient shifted\-window graph transformer\. We then extend this topological view to grounded scene graphs, where object categories, bounding boxes, and relations are generated jointly to bridge symbolic scene structure and continuous visual generation\. The second part of this thesis studies motion forecasting\. We formulate human trajectory prediction as conditional flow matching, enabling correlated multimodal futures to be generated together as scene\-level hypotheses\. We then scale this approach to autonomous\-driving motion prediction by jointly producing multiple trajectories, learning confidence rankings, and improving generalization via self\-conditioning\. Together, these works show that generative models for structured domains become useful when structure is handled explicitly but flexibly, and identify opportunities for unified structured world models, faster samplers, and uncertainty\-aware deployment\.

## [CerS2\-mediated lipotoxicity and calcium signaling: a novel sequential mechanism of apoptosis in cancer](../publications/e54ecbdccd6e55f9a39e.md)

Satya Narayan

The classical paradigm of the sphingolipid rheostat\-balancing pro\-apoptotic ceramide against pro\-survival sphingosine\-1\-phosphate\-has evolved into a complex signaling landscape where N\-acyl chain length serves as the fundamental determinant of biological outcomes\. This perspective explores the pivotal role of ceramide synthase 2 \(CerS2\) in synthesizing very\-long\-chain \(VLC\) ceramides \(C22\-C26\) and its function as a central regulator of cellular stress responses\. While CerS2 typically acts as a tumor suppressor, its activity is frequently attenuated in aggressive malignancies through alternative splicing or protein inhibition\. The emergence of DH20931, a first\-in\-class small\-molecule CerS2 agonist, is discussed as a paradigm\-shifting tool for re\-engaging suppressed apoptotic pathways\. The present paper outlines a sequential\-mechanism model for pharmacological CerS2 activation, which drives lipotoxic endoplasmic reticulum \(ER\) stress via the PERK\-ATF4\-CHOP axis and tightens the ER\-mitochondria synapse through direct IP3R1 interaction\. The latter mechanism facilitates lethal calcium influx, triggering the mitochondrial caspase\-dependent apoptotic pathway\. Furthermore, the preclinical performance of DH20931 is evaluated in models of triple\-negative breast cancer \(TNBC\) relative to standard\-of\-care therapeutics\. The conclusion examines the future of CerS2 as a major druggable target, emphasizing the need for companion diagnostics to identify patients most likely to benefit from agonist therapy based on specific splice variants and metabolic profiles\. Combining CerS2 activation with existing chemo\- or immunotherapies represents a promising synergistic strategy for treating resistant solid tumors\.

## [Data Privacy Challenges in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Study of Privacy Awareness and AI Regulation](../publications/e55d093cef1c39d36896.md)

Isha Singadiya; Harpreet Kaur

Abstract: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has increased the collection, processing and automated use of personal data\. While AI supports innovation, personalization and efficiency, data\-intensive AI systems create concerns relating to privacy, consent, transparency, profiling, security, surveillance and individual control\. In India, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides a statutory framework for digital personal data, while the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 provide the implementation framework\. This study examines privacy awareness and stakeholder perceptions of data\-protection regulation in an AI\-driven environment using secondary empirical evidence obtained from an existing published research/data source\. The analysis focuses on privacy awareness, awareness of selected rights under the DPDP Act, perceived regulatory effectiveness, privacy\-business balance and grievance redressal\. Reported statistical evidence indicates higher privacy\-awareness scores for professional stakeholders than laypersons, while organizational communication is associated with stronger awareness of privacy rights\. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Data Privacy, Privacy Awareness, AI Regulation, DPDP Act 2023, AI Governance, Data Protection, Ethics\.

## [Tax revenue mobilisation and economic growth across African economies under entrepreneurial fiscal and institutional conditions](../publications/e565fe0a32429093d9b7.md)

Solberg Horve Mishiwo

Tax revenue mobilisation, entrepreneurial ecosystem development, fiscal sustainability, and institutional quality are widely recognised as important determinants of economic performance, yet their combined relationships remain insufficiently understood within the African context\. This study examines the relationships among these factors and economic growth across 35 African economies over the period 1991–2024 using a harmonised balanced panel comprising 1,190 country\-year observations\. Economic growth is measured by annual GDP per capita growth, while regulatory quality, operationalised as a dimension of institutional quality, is examined as the conditioning institutional factor\. The empirical analysis employs a Two\-Way Fixed Effects estimator with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, complemented by Panel Threshold Regression, Panel Quantile Regression, Feasible Generalised Least Squares, and Panel\-Corrected Standard Errors to evaluate the robustness and heterogeneity of the estimated relationships\. In addition, XGBoost and Random Forest algorithms, interpreted using SHAP feature importance analysis, provide complementary evidence on the predictive contribution of the explanatory variables\. The findings indicate that tax revenue mobilisation, domestic credit to the private sector, regulatory quality, and the interaction between tax revenue mobilisation and regulatory quality are significantly associated with economic growth across the principal econometric specifications\. The threshold and quantile regression analyses further reveal that several estimated relationships vary across institutional regimes and different segments of the conditional growth distribution, highlighting important heterogeneity in the fiscal\-growth relationship\. The complementary machine\-learning analysis consistently identifies regulatory quality, tax revenue mobilisation, and domestic credit to the private sector as leading predictors within the fitted models, although their predictive importance does not imply causal importance or economic effect size\. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between fiscal policy and economic growth is conditioned by institutional quality\. Accordingly, the results indicate that domestic revenue mobilisation may be more supportive of growth when accompanied by stronger regulatory institutions, more effective financial intermediation, and supportive entrepreneurial conditions\. By integrating complementary econometric and machine\-learning approaches within a unified analytical framework, this study provides evidence of heterogeneous conditional associations and complementary predictive relationships among fiscal policy, institutions, entrepreneurship, and economic growth across African economies\.

## [Predictive Al for Enhancing Clinical Pathways in Children with Learning Disabilities using XGBoost](../publications/e56611139dd963dd6355.md)

Sujitha V\.; Kishore P\.; Nevin Nehal R\.S\.; Afzal Khan M\.

Dyslexia screening in children involves computing techniques to analyse the learning patterns from the structured data generated by behaviour and language assessments\. This research work proposes a machine learning technique to classify dyslexic cases by implementing Random Forest and XGBoost on a publicly available dataset consisting of 3,644 observations and 196 features extracted from demographics and language tasks\. Steps in data pre\-processing involves the missing observations handling, categorical data encoding, non\-predictive columns elimination, and stratified splitting of training and testing datasets\. Hyperparameter tuning is performed via stratified cross\-validation, followed by independent testing of both ensemble models\. Random Forest attained 95\.1% accuracy with 94\.3% precision, 93\.8% recall, 94\.0% F1\-Score, and 0\.97 ROC\-AUC score, whereas XGBoost gave an accuracy of 91\.8% and ROC\-AUC of 0\.94\. Flask\-based prediction model was created for providing individualized screening predictions\. The platform shows how ensemble learning could be used in computational dyslexia screening and serves as an illustrative example of the decision support tool for preliminary screening\.

## [Optimising Irish Fen Habitat Mapping: An Evaluation of Temporal Windowing and Spectral Features Using Google Earth Engine and Random Forest](../publications/e5698e814b5ab60505e5.md)

Ciara Farrell; Yuanyuan Pu; Shane Regan; Lizy Abraham; Owen Naughton

High spectral similarity and overlapping habitat boundaries present a substantial challenge for mapping and monitoring Ireland’s ecologically vital fen ecosystems\. This study establishes a reproducible remote sensing workflow by combining Google Earth Engine \(GEE\) with Sentinel\-2 imagery for Irish fen classification\. This study uses a Random Forest machine learning model to evaluate five temporal windows against three spectral feature sets across three distinct sites\. The results indicate that a growing season window \(June–September\) incorporating both bands and spectral indices captures peak phenological information more effectively than annual composites, producing high within\-site, pixel\-level overall accuracy across all study sites \(Scragh Bog: 95\.24%, Liskeenan Fen: 94\.13%, Ballymore Fen: 94\.43%\)\. Although raw spectral bands achieved marginally higher localised accuracies at Liskeenan \(\+0\.24%\) and Ballymore \(\+1\.65%\), the combined feature set was maintained as the standard workflow to ensure cross\-site stability, biophysical parameterisation, and resilience against localised soil background noise\. To accommodate narrow, fragmented geometries, training data was extracted via pixel\-level stratified sampling; while this introduces spatial autocorrelation, classification outputs showed coherent within\-site spatial patterns, although accuracy estimates remain subject to spatial autocorrelation\. Crucially, the Google Earth Engine\-based Random Forest model maintained stable within\-site classification performance when reducing the training\-testing ratio from a standard 80:20 split down to a highly constrained 50:50 split\. Ultimately, this workflow provides a cloud\-based framework for monitoring vulnerable wetland ecosystems under real\-world geometric and ground\-truth data limitations\.

## [Dysregulated Cholesterol Metabolism, Chronic Inflammation, and Disability in Severe Progressive Multiple Sclerosis](../publications/e58579d9a522686500f9.md)

Taylor R Wicks; Mujeeb Olushola Shittu; Anna T Wolska; Diala Ghazal; B\. Weinstock‐Guttman; Alexander Burnham; Alan Thomas Remaley; Robert Zivadinov; Murali Krishna Ramanathan

BACKGROUND: Dysregulated lipid metabolism, which can affect remyelination and neural repair, has not been extensively investigated in progressive multiple sclerosis \(PMS\)\. The goal was to examine whether dysregulated cholesterol metabolism was associated with disability in PMS\. METHODS: The study sample comprised 53 Severe PMS patients \(Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS score: 7\.0\-9\.5\) requiring skilled nursing and 53 age, sex\- and disease duration\-matched community\-dwelling Control PMS patients \(EDSS score: 3\.0\-6\.5\)\. Patients underwent neurological examinations and provided blood samples\. Cholesterol and apolipoprotein \(Apo\) profiles, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy metabolomic profiles, inflammatory cytokines, neuroaxonal, and glial injury biomarkers were obtained\. Disability was measured on the EDSS and the Combinatorial Weight\-Adjusted Disability \(CombiWISE\) scales\. RESULTS: The Severe PMS group had lower high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol \(HDL\-C\), ApoA\-I, and ApoA\-II levels \(all p &lt; 0\.001\) and higher ApoB and ApoE levels\. The nutritional status biomarker, albumin, was lower, and the chronic inflammation marker, GlycA, was higher in Severe PMS versus Control PMS \(all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Total cholesterol, ApoA\-II, and ApoB were associated with disability on the EDSS and CombiWISE scale\. Difference\-correlogram analyses revealed substantial remodeling of biomarker interdependencies in Severe PMS\. ApoE showed stronger associations with lipid and nutritional biomarkers in Severe PMS, but with neuroaxonal markers \(serum neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein\) in Control PMS\. Inflammatory cytokines \(tumor necrosis factor, interleukin\-6\) showed stronger associations with apolipoproteins in Severe PMS, whereas several lipid\-inflammation and lipid nutritional correlations were attenuated\. CONCLUSIONS: Disrupted cholesterol metabolism and chronic inflammation are strongly linked to greater disability in Severe PMS\. Our results also indicate marked alterations in metabolic, inflammatory, nutritional, and neuroglial biomarker networks in Severe PMS\.

## [HARNESSING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR POLITICAL MARKETING IN SMALL LOCALITIES: ASSESSING SKILLS, STRATEGIC PLANNING, AND DIGITAL RESOURCE READINESS](../publications/e58c640673c36c2c4ba3.md)

Arturo Sánchez Sánchez; Dra Celia Yaneth Quiroz; Cruz García Lirios; Javier Carreón Guillén; Tania Soto Ramírez; Oscar Igor Carreón Valencia

This study analyzes the entrepreneurial profile and digital marketing strategies of SMEs in Tlaxcala using both traditional statistical techniques and a network\-based approach\. In addition to descriptive and correlational analyses, a neural\-network\-inspired network analysis was conducted to examine the structural influence of demographic variables and entrepreneurial competencies\. Centrality metrics revealed that communication, continued studies, and years in business were the most influential nodes within the system, while skills, business planning, and resource availability formed the strongest core cluster of interconnected competencies\. Clustering coefficients confirmed the presence of cohesive substructures linking communication, skills, and digital resource management\. The weighted matrix further showed robust positive associations among these competency variables and weaker or negative associations involving demographic factors\. These network findings indicate that digital marketing adoption in SMEs is driven by experience\-based competencies rather than personal background characteristics\. The integrated results provide a multilevel understanding of how entrepreneurial behavior emerges from interconnected cognitive, experiential, and communication structures\.

## [Coordinated Care Experience in Late‐Life and Cognitive Aging of Older Adults in the United States: A Longitudinal Cohort Study](../publications/e5919b0f2e9670c4d4d0.md)

Xiang Qi; Renhao Li; Nan Jiang; Jiaying Li; Derong Zeng; Jie Zhong; Lu Shao; Junwen Yu; Zheng Zhu; Jasmine L\. Travers

BACKGROUND: The fragmentation of the US healthcare system imposes a high cognitive burden on older adults\. Coordinated Care \(CC\) is hypothesized to improve patient outcomes, but the relationship between multidimensional CC experiences and cognitive aging remains unclear\. We investigated whether experiences across three domains of CC \(perceived CC, tangible support, and technical support\) are associated with cognitive trajectories and incident cognitive impairment\. METHODS: Data were drawn from the Health and Retirement Study \(2016\-2022\), including the 2016 CC module \(N = 1321; aged ≥ 50\)\. Baseline CC was assessed via three patient\-reported scales: perceived CC \(provider communication consistency, 0\-20 scale\), tangible support \(family/professional assistance with medical tasks, 0\-11 scale\), and technical support \(patient portal offered and used, 0\-4 scale\)\. Cognitive function was measured biennially \(2016\-2022\) using the 27\-point Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status \(TICS\)\. Incident cognitive impairment was defined as the first follow\-up score of ≤ 11 among those cognitively normal at baseline\. Linear mixed\-effects models estimated 6\-year cognitive trajectories, and Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk of incident impairment\. RESULTS: In fully adjusted models, higher perceived CC \(β = 0\.25, p &lt; 0\.05\) and technical support \(β = 0\.22, p &lt; 0\.05\) were associated with higher baseline cognitive scores\. Greater tangible support was associated with lower baseline cognition \(β = \-0\.48, p &lt; 0\.001\) but also with slower cognitive decline over time \(interaction β = 0\.005, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Tangible support was associated with higher risk of impairment in unadjusted analyses \(HR = 1\.26\), but this association was not statistically significant after adjustment\. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Perceived CC and technology use characterized cognitively robust older adults, whereas tangible support identified vulnerable individuals yet was associated with slower cognitive decline\. These findings underscore the need for nuanced CC strategies: digital tools engage those aging well, while intensive tangible support may be especially important for those with greater vulnerabilities\. These associations are observational and do not establish causality\.

## [Quantitative analysis of intrarenal nerve‐associated profiles in the human foetal kidney between 14 and 30 gestational weeks: An S100 immunohistochemical study](../publications/e599db0d5a0ec98f9b40.md)

Ivan Petrović; Ana Balenović; Milana Bosanac; Srdjan Stankovic; Isidora Milosavljević; Milena Šunjević; Sandra Trivunić Dajko; Bojana Andrejić\-Višnjić

Abstract Quantitative data on the spatial development of intrarenal S100‐positive nerve‐associated profiles in human foetal kidneys remain limited, despite the established importance of renal nerves\. Building on the previously published semiquantitative observations, this study aimed to generate a quantitative, compartment‐resolved map of S100‐positive nerve‐associated profiles in human foetal kidneys\. Formalin‐fixed, paraffin‐embedded human foetal kidney specimens ranging from 14 to 30 gestational weeks were analysed using S100 immunohistochemistry\. Based on gestational age, specimens were divided into three groups: ≤18 gestational weeks \(G1, n=6\), 19–24 gestational weeks \(G2, n=6\), and ≥ 25 gestational weeks \(G3, n=6\)\. Cortical maturation was assessed by measuring nephrogenic zone and maturation zone thickness and calculating the cortical maturation index \(CMI\)\. Morphometric analysis of cortical S100‐positive nerve‐associated profiles was performed using digital image analysis\. Distribution patterns of S100‐positive profiles were assessed qualitatively\. Group‐wise analysis demonstrated significantly lower cortical S100‐positive area in G1 compared with G2 and G3 \(median: 985 μm 2 vs\. 1733 μm 2 and 2400 μm 2 , respectively; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Cortical S100‐positive area increased significantly with gestational age and foetal weight and showed an inverse correlation with CMI \( ρ = −0\.410, p &lt; 0\.001\), indicating parallel progression of S100‐positive area and cortical maturation\. In multivariate linear regression analyses, cortical S100‐positive area remained independently associated with gestational age \( β = 125\.0, p = 0\.006\) and foetal weight \( β = 1\.50, p = 0\.006\), explaining 57\.6% of the variance \(adjusted R 2 = 0\.485\)\. Perivascular localisation was the most frequently observed distribution pattern, while juxtaglomerular and intraglomerular patterns were also identified, including in the earliest gestational‐age group\. This study provides the first quantitative, compartment‐resolved analysis of intrarenal nerve‐associated profiles in the human foetal kidney\. Cortical S100‐positive area increases with gestational age in parallel with cortical maturation and shows a predominantly perivascular distribution, consistent with a neurovascular co‐development model and establishing a morphological framework for future functional studies of renal innervation\.

## [Insight into convergence of genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in reproductive organs in Arabidopsis](../publications/e59b3e3695c430bd958f.md)

Karolina Zolkiewicz; Damian Gruszka

Mechanisms of epigenetic regulation of gene expression are inter\-connected to ensure maintenance of DNA methylation\. However, regulation of DNA methylation which allows new epigenetic patterns in various tissues during plant reproduction has remained incompletely understood\. Recent reports have provided new and interesting discoveries in the field of epigenetic mechanisms regulating development of reproductive organs in the model plant species – Arabidopsis thaliana \. As a consequence, an important, novel insight was gained into the role of several regulators, including GENETICS DETERMINES EPIGENETICS1 \(GDE1\) protein, as well as REPRODUCTIVE MERISTEM \(REM\) and REPRODUCTIVE MERISTEM INSTRUCTS METHYLATION \(RIMs\) transcription factors in the emergence of differential DNA methylation and small interfering RNA \(siRNA\) expression patterns in ovules and anthers during reproductive development in this model species\. In this emerging view, genetic \(transcription factors and recognized DNA motifs\) and epigenetic \(siRNA and DNA methylation\) mechanisms converge to enable organ\-specific DNA methylation during reproductive plant development\.

## [Targeting the gut–tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment](../publications/e5a527125a8012d12913.md)

Haoyu Li; Chunguang Hou; Yan Pan

Background Colorectal cancer \(CRC\) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota\. The gut–tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance\. Probiotic\-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host–microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor\-associated pathways\. Objective To evaluate probiotic metabolites as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC using integrative multi\-omics analysis and in vitro validation\. Methods A systems biology approach integrating network pharmacology, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome profiling was applied\. Twelve probiotic metabolites yielded 428 predicted targets, with 162 overlapping CRC\-associated genes\. CRC cell lines \(HCT116, HT\-29, Caco\-2, SW480\) were treated and analyzed for viability, apoptosis, gene/protein expression, cytokines, metabolites, and microbial composition\. Results Sodium butyrate \(5 mM\) reduced cell viability by 35\.5–42\.3% \(p &lt; 0\.001\) and increased apoptosis from 8\.6% to 32\.4%, reaching 41\.2% when combined with indole\-3\-acetic acid \(IAA, 100 μM\), suggesting a synergistic pro\-apoptotic effect\. RNA\-seq identified 1,248 DEGs, with upregulation of BAX and CASP3 \(log 2 FC \+1\.8 to \+2\.3\) and downregulation of IL6, TNF, and NFKB1 \(−1\.5 to −2\.1\)\. Proteomics revealed 412 differentially expressed proteins, including downregulation of AKT1 \(−1\.6\-fold\), MAPK1 \(−1\.4\-fold\), and EGFR \(−1\.3\-fold\), and upregulation of CASP3 \(\+1\.7\-fold\) and BAX \(\+1\.5\-fold\)\. Cytokines IL\-6, TNF\-α, and IL\-1β decreased by 48\.2%, 44\.7%, and 39\.5%, respectively, while IL\-10 increased by 26\.3%\. Metabolomics showed a 2\.8\-fold increase in butyrate and \~35% reduction in oxidative stress\. Microbiome diversity improved \(Shannon index 2\.8–3\.6\)\. Conclusion Probiotic\-derived metabolites modulate NF\-κB, PI3K–Akt, MAPK, and apoptosis pathways, supporting their potential role as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC management\.

## [Cooperation Without Adaptation: LLM Agents in a Collective\-Risk Dilemma](../publications/e5aa2d3cf4ad160914c8.md)

Trung\-Kiet Huynh; Dao\-Sy Duy\-Minh; Chi\-Nguyen Tran; Phu\-Hoa Pham; Phu\-Quy Nguyen\-Lam; Le Hong Trang; The Anh Han

Language\-model agents are increasingly deployed to act on behalf of people in settings where individual decisions shape shared outcomes\. We examine whether five production models adapt their contributions to changing risks and partner behaviour, or instead follow a relatively fixed strategy\. In a collective\-risk dilemma game \(CRG\), six players contribute to a shared pool over ten rounds; if the pool falls short of its target, a catastrophe may destroy their remaining resources\. Four models contributed approximately an equal share at every positive risk level, and four of the five also contributed when risk was zero, even though contributing could not improve their payoff\. Explicitly stating that only the agent&\#x27;s own payoff mattered reduced zero\-risk contributions for most models, while a more neutral prompt did not\. Several models correctly identified which action offered the higher expected payoff at different risk levels, yet their contributions changed little\. Against fixed partners, no model consistently chose the payoff\-maximising response, and in mixed\-model groups, a single agent&\#x27;s shortfall in the final round could cause an otherwise successful group to fail\. Payoff\-based selection also depended on population composition: in a single six\-agent group, it favoured the model that contributed least and reduced group success, whereas in larger, randomly mixed populations, it favoured an exact fair\-share model at moderate and high risk\. These findings show that cooperative self\-play alone is not evidence of strategic adaptability\. Consistent with a machine\-behaviour approach, evaluations of agents in multi\-agent systems should test how they respond to incentives, partner actions, and population composition\.

## [Generative Artificial Intelligence Empowering Knowledge Work: The Impact of Human\-AI Collaboration on the Efficiency and Quality of Managerial Decision\-Making](../publications/e5b232a168ae369c2a18.md)

Jingwei Guo; Zhenguang Zhong; Weiqiang Lyu

The rapid iteration and industrialization of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) have thoroughly changed the paradigm of knowledge work in modern organizations, and thus the process of managerial decision\-making has evolved from heuristic judgment dominated by human managers to the new paradigm of human\-AI collaborative creation\. This paper seeks to investigate how GenAI\-assisted human\-AI collaboration would affect the effectiveness and quality of organizational managerial decision\-making\. Based on the knowledge\-based view and collaborative intelligence, a theoretical framework including the technology of GenAI, modes of human\-AI collaboration and decision\-making performance is established in this paper\. By quantitative simulation experiments and empirical analysis with Python, the impacts of GenAI assistance on decision\-making time cost, information processing comprehensiveness, decision accuracy and risk identification ability are verified in this paper\. It can be found that moderate human\-AI collaboration will contribute to managerial decision\-making effectiveness and quality; too much or not enough GenAI assistance may weaken the positive impacts of human\-AI collaboration on managerial decision\-making\. GenAI contributes to managerial decision\-making effectiveness and quality mainly through reducing information searching costs, improving data analysis efficiency and compensating human cognitive limitations\.

## [Enhancing ω\-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism](../publications/e5c2427dc7bb046725e5.md)

Haidong Teng; Haoran Yu; Zhehang Xu; Lanxin Xiao; Xinghao Yuan; Lirong Yang; Jianmin Wu; Gang Xu

Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis\. \(R\)\-3\-\(\[1,1′\-biphenyl\]\-4\-yl\)\-2\-aminopropan\-1\-ol \(ABP\), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω\-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor\. Here, we engineer an ω\-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect\-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high\-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade\-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding\. Dynamic cross\-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions\. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with &gt;99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP\. This integrated computational\-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel\-pocket binding trade\-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω\-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis\. This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω\-transaminases\. Distal\-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106\-fold activity and &gt;99% selectivity\.

## [Geospatial analysis of land degradation and desertification in the semi\-arid Shabelle River Basin, Somalia](../publications/e5c4b300140469c0b697.md)

Ismail Mohamoud Ali; Gabriel Tetteh; Mahad Abdullahi Hussein; Abdirahman Mohamed Nor

Land degradation and desertification pose major environmental challenges in semi\-arid regions such as the Shabelle River Basin in Somalia\. This study assessed vulnerability to land degradation and desertification from 2000 to 2025 using multi\-temporal Landsat images, CHIRPS rainfall data, Google Earth Engine and GIS techniques\. A Desertification Vulnerability Index \(DVI\) was developed by combining nine environmental indicators, including NDVI, SAVI, BSI, SI, NDBI, NDMI, MNDWI, LST and rainfall, using a weighted overlay analysis\. Results indicate that large parts of the basin are vulnerable, with the Shabelle River corridor and southern regions comparatively less affected, while other areas show declines in vegetation and environmental health\. The DVI shows a temporal trend toward higher vulnerability\. It has been effectively used to assess spatial desertification vulnerability and validated with 341 reference points, showing good discrimination for 2000, 2015 and 2025\.

## [Scaling Waste\-to\-Wealth Ventures in Emerging Markets: A Circular Economy Framework for Sustainable Growth](../publications/e5c94660f1e0d84541a3.md)

Zwanaka James Mudara; Michael Mncedisi Willie

The circular economy offers emerging markets a route to growth that does not depend on continued resource extraction, and waste\-to\-wealth ventures have proliferated in response\. Few achieve scale\. This paper asks what distinguishes ventures that replicate across markets from those that remain confined to a single site, and develops a conceptual framework in answer\. A structured review of four literatures was conducted, covering circular economy theory, waste management in developing economies, the informal recycling sector, and the relationship between circular practice and development objectives\. The framework identifies three enablers of scale, namely an adaptive business model, a hybrid capital structure and policy co\-creation, and argues that they act through ecosystem orchestration, the alignment of informal collectors, offtakers, municipalities and financiers around a single material flow\. Scaling is specified as four stages in which the binding constraint shifts from technical proof to feedstock security, then to offtake, then to policy stability, so support instruments must be matched to stage\. Four testable propositions and a set of observable indicators are stated\. The framework is offered for empirical testing rather than as a validated model\.
