## [Consecuencias físicas, psicológicas y sociales de las adicciones: una revisión bibliográfica](../publications/e5d563d2885ae1c3bf5d.md)

Maribel Celi Vásquez Paucar; Daniela Brigitte Quimis Quiroz; Naomy Janneth Quintero Cuero

Las adicciones provocadas por los cambios constantes a nivel mundial generan graves consecuencias en el ser humano y la sociedad, acciones que tienen resultados negativos e influyen en la calidad de vida de la sociedad, en este contexto, el objetivo fue analizar la evidencia científica disponible sobre las consecuencias físicas, psicológicas y sociales derivadas de las adicciones\. La metodología consistió en una revisión bibliográfica de la literatura publicada entre los años 2021 y 2026, los términos de referencia fueron trastornos por abuso de sustancias, adicciones, salud mental, calidad de vida, efectos físicos, psicológicos y sociales, para ello se usaron los operadores booleanos OR y AND y la declaración PRISMA 2020 fue el marco de referencia para el proceso de identificación, selección y síntesis\. Los resultados del análisis revelaron que los efectos físicos provocan enfermedades crónicas, lesiones, intoxicaciones, deterioro cognitivo, por su parte en la dimensión psicológica se identificó la presencia de depresión, ansiedad, trastornos del estado de ánimo, episodios psicóticos, impulsividad, alteraciones de las funciones cognitivas y presencia simultanea de problemas de salud mental; las consecuencias sociales puntualizan a los conflictos en diferentes escenarios como: familiares, laborales, educativos, desempleo, problemas financieros, y estigmatización\. En este contexto se concluye que las adicciones crean efectos multidimensionales e interrelaciónales, situación que requiere un abordaje integral e interdisciplinario que incluya prevención, detección temprana, tratamiento, rehabilitación, análisis de las evidencias de los efectos físicos en las personas, y reintegración social\.

## [Pedersen, Tore &amp; Johansen, Christian: Behavioural artificial intelligence: an agenda for systematic empirical studies of artificial inference](../publications/e5e46be685170bc42034.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 35 \(3\):519\-532\. 2020Artificial intelligence receives attention in media as well as in academe and business\. In media coverage and reporting, AI is predominantly described in contrasted terms, either as the ultimate solution to all human problems or the ultimate threat to all human existence\. In academe, the focus of computer scientists is on developing systems that function, whereas philosophy scholars theorize about the implications of this functionality for human life\. In the interface between technology and philosophy there is, however, one imperative aspect of AI yet to be articulated: how do intelligent systems make inferences? We use the overarching concept “Artificial Intelligent Behaviour” which would include both cognition/processing and judgment/behaviour\. We argue that due to the complexity and opacity of artificial inference, one needs to initiate systematic empirical studies of artificial intelligent behavior similar to what has previously been done to study human cognition, judgment and decision making\. This will provide valid knowledge, outside of what current computer science methods can offer, about the judgments and decisions made by intelligent systems\. Moreover, outside academe—in the public as well as the private sector—expertise in epistemology, critical thinking and reasoning are crucial to ensure human oversight of the artificial intelligent judgments and decisions that are made, because only competent human insight into AI\-inference processes will ensure accountability\. Such insights require systematic studies of AI\-behaviour founded on the natural sciences and philosophy, as well as the employment of methodologies from the cognitive and behavioral sciences\. \(direct link \)

## [Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi\-Agent Systems](../publications/e5e72ebb8ccce4b5faa7.md)

Leyang Shen; Yaxin Gong; Yang Zhang; Chenxiao Fan; Jiakai Wang; Dong Wang; Yang Liu; Fuli Feng; Chun Kai Ling; Tat\-Seng Chua

Large language model \(LLM\)\-based agents and multi\-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long\-horizon tool use and inter\-agent collaboration\. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift\. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs\. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low\-cost fast path and how to intervene with a high\-cost slow path\. To unlock its steering intelligence, the ability to assess goal drift and generate effective interventions, we jointly train the two paths with reinforcement learning, combining a pairwise ranking objective with group\-relative policy optimization \(GRPO\)\. Experiments on information\-seeking search tasks show that the steering agent provides effective supervision for both single\-agent and multi\-agent systems, improving their performance and efficiency\. The learned steering intelligence generalizes to out\-of\-domain tasks, transfers to unseen executors, and supports controllable intervention frequency without retraining\.

## [Web Accessibility and Search Engine Optimization: Best Approach for Building Corporate Websites](../publications/e5e74733463112aa59ac.md)

Khaled Mahbub; Jeremiah Charles

The rapid digitization of products and services necessitates the development of safeguards to enforce equitable access to internet resources\. Although legislative measures have been implemented to compel public\-sector organizations to provide accessible web and mobile applications, most websites are still not fully accessible\. There is an urgent need for organizations to integrate accessibility into current and future developments\. The integration of solutions derived from decades of accessibility research into organizational processes and initiatives is beneficial to all users\. This study provides a guide for businesses and organizations to improve their web accessibility and Search Engine Optimization \(SEO\)\. This research covers the fundamentals of SEO and web accessibility, along with user requirements, and legal obligations\. It also includes recommendations on significant concerns and compares the results of two test approaches for evaluating accessibility\. The main section outlines user\-focused accessibility criteria based on technical standards and relevant user requirements\. The systematic literature review method, designed as a repeatable method to reduce bias, was used to evaluate and analyse data extracted from published studies\. The research methodology also combines qualitative and quantitative research approaches along with Design Science Research Methodology \(DSRM\) to develop a practical solution by answering the research questions\. This thorough literature review identified definitions, rules, and user requirements that were validated through 65 carefully selected studies\. The consolidated results have expanded the framework for web accessibility and SEO and are included in the recommended guide\. This study has numerous theoretical and practical implications, as it aims to develop a comprehensive blueprint to guide businesses and practitioners on best practices for integrating web accessibility and SEO into building inclusive corporate websites\. By extension, it investigates the intersection between SEO and web accessibility in building a better online experience for people with impairments as well as other web users\.

## [Rivera, Fernanda Lilibeth Ormeño ; Cedeño, Michelle Antonella Sánchez &amp; Mendoza, Jacqueline Macías: Training in the Field of Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities in Health Science Education](../publications/e5e91527bef063231b18.md)



\_EthAIca\_ 3:124\. 2024Introduction: Artificial intelligence in higher education teacher training has become an imperative that challenges teachers to update themselves to be able to use this tool to generate knowledge for their students\. Method: A systematic review was conducted in databases such as PUBMED, Cochrane Central Library, CINAHL, and SCIENCE DIRECT, using keywords like &quot;health sciences,&quot; &quot;artificial intelligence,&quot; and &quot;teaching&quot; during the period 2018\-2024, following the PRISMA checklist\. Results: Studies predominantly originated from Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the USA, especially involving nursing and medical students\. The most notable opportunities of AI include the relationship between ethics and technology, the training of academic tutors, and its contribution to professional education, clinical case management, literature searches, and student learning\. However, challenges were identified, such as uncertainty about employability, limited funding for training, and the acquisition of licenses\. Additionally, there is a need to promote responsible use of AI to avoid diminishing empathy and humanization in patient care\. Conclusions: AI is a valuable ally in health sciences education, but ethical considerations and teacher training must be taken into account for responsible use, as well as fostering critical and reflective thinking in its implementation\. \(direct link \)

## [Acoustically driven micro/nanobubbles: from fundamental mechanisms to biomedical applications](../publications/e5ebf972a91541a42f3e.md)

Jiaxin Wu; Tatsuo Arai; Chenhao Bai; Changsheng Li; Xingguang Duan; Toshio Fukuda; Xiaoming Liu

Acoustically driven micro/nanobubbles, as a bridge between macroscopic acoustic fields and microscopic biological machinery, have shown considerable promise due to their non\-contact actuation, tunable mechanical responses, and favorable biocompatibility\. Recent advances in bubble formulation and acoustic control have further expanded their capabilities, enabling targeted membrane permeabilization, enhanced molecular transport, and precise manipulation at the microscale\. In this review, we summarize the fundamental mechanisms linking bubble dynamics to biologically relevant effects under ultrasound and establish quantitative design criteria that govern the coupling between acoustic parameters, bubble behavior, and therapeutic performance\. We then organize biomedical applications across scales, spanning single\-cell manipulation, tissue\-level barrier modulation, and organ\-scale imaging and therapeutic interventions\. Particular attention is given to how acoustic modes and bubble configurations translate into measurable performance metrics, as well as the limitations that constrain reproducibility and safety in complex biological environments\. Finally, we discuss key challenges for practical translation from an engineering perspective and propose strategies for improving controllability, standardization, and system integration\. By providing a framework to overcome the inherent randomness of bubble\-acoustic interactions in clinical translation, this review outlines a roadmap toward reliable and programmable mechano\-bio platforms for closed\-loop, patient\-adaptive interventions\.

## [Multi\-Agent LLM Systems: Memory Management, Coordination Failures and Semantic Conflict Resolution](../publications/e5edbf9b781549fd38bd.md)

Satyam Sharma

As large language model \(LLM\) systems move from using one agent at a time to working with multiple agents together, keeping the system stable and ensuring memory stays accurate is still a major challenge\. Making linear tasks work with multiple agents hurts performance by up to 70% because of extra communication and problems that spread out, but tasks that can be done at the same time can improve performance by up to 81% \(Kim et al\., 2025\)\. Right now, the memory management tools we use like flat conversation logs, RAG retrieval and single\-agent versioning systems \(Wu et al\., 2025; Su et al\., 2026\) do not work well when there are conflicts in open\-domain semantic merges\. They either need strict locks or special compilers for specific domains to handle these issues\. To tackle these bottlenecks, this review paper brings together real\-world failure categories, system\-level checks and memory designs\. It introduces a Git\-managed multi\-agent framework that includes dynamic task assignment, secure branch execution in isolated environments and external oversight using an LLM as a judge, along with council\-based meaning\-based decision making\. In the end, we identify and outline the main research questions that still need to be addressed in areas like sharing experiences between different agents, figuring out the causes of faults and resolving conflicts in meaning\.

## [3D Printing of PA12 / CF Composite to Fabricate Equation‐Driven Möbius Strip Lattice for Small‐Scale Drone Frame](../publications/e606e3ff46733f357306.md)

Mohit Sood; Chang‐Mou Wu

ABSTRACT Small‐scale drones have a bright future in agriculture\. These kinds of drones require longer operational time, which is possible with reduced power consumption\. The drone&\#x27;s weight is critical for longer operations\. The lattice structure is well known for its lightweight and better strength‐to‐weight ratio\. These lattices could be used to fabricate the drone frame, potentially providing lightness, a better strength‐to‐weight ratio, and reduced power consumption\. The Möbius strip has a natural twist that could help distribute the load\. PA12/CF lattice with predetermined stress‐concentration points \(twist\), fabricated from a PA12/CF for drone bodies, is very limited in the literature\. First, static loading was applied, and stress–strain behavior was observed across three distinct zones, with a total energy absorption of 129 kJ/m 3 \. Strengthening behavior after the elastic limit and considerable toughness before fracture was observed\. Dynamic compression proved the 89% recovery after cyclic loading\. FEM results showed that bending is the dominant failure mode, with the twist section as the primary failure location\. Matrix yield at the material level played a major role in failure\. An artificial neural network \(ANN\) used for surrogate model training and Pareto‐front multi‐objective optimization yielded the maximum‐modulus shape of Möbius strip lattice used in the drone frame\.

## [ORGANIZATIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY OF ROBOTIZED TECHNOLOGICAL SYSTEMS IN INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISES](../publications/e60ccff0cd7bbacf4bb8.md)

Boyirov Shodmon Erkinovich

This article examines the organizational and technological foundations for improving the efficiency of robotized technological systems in industrial enterprises\. Rather than treating the robot as an isolated machine, the study frames it as a component of a cyber\-physical production system integrated with process equipment, sensors, PLC/SCADA, material flow, and manufacturing management systems\. According to the International Federation of Robotics, 542,076 new industrial robots were installed worldwide in 2024 and the operational stock reached approximately 4\.66 million units; Asia/Australia accounted for 74% of new installations, Europe 16%, and the Americas 9%\. Global robot density rose to 177 units per 10,000 manufacturing employees\. The study integrates OEE, takt and cycle time, MTBF, MTTR, defect rate, energy consumption, predictive maintenance, and digital\-twin monitoring into a unified efficiency framework\. The results show that robotization alone does not guarantee superior performance; the largest economic benefits arise when the robot, technological process, maintenance system, and production logistics are optimized as one integrated system\.

## [AI\-Based EV Battery Health Prediction with Explainable AI and Database Integration](../publications/e61456093afa64f2cc64.md)

Pranav Sable

This research paper presents an AI\-based framework for predicting the State of Health \(SOH\) of electric vehicle \(EV\) lithium\-ion batteries by integrating machine learning, Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\), and relational database technology\. The proposed framework compares five machine learning regression models: Ridge Regression, Support Vector Regression \(SVR\), Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) are used to explain model predictions and identify important battery health indicators, including dV/dQ peak height, internal resistance, and cycle count\. The study demonstrates the proposed pipeline using a synthetic, physics\-inspired dataset containing 40 battery cells and 28,201 cycle records\. Gradient Boosting achieved a Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\) of 1\.26 percentage points, a Root Mean Squared Error \(RMSE\) of 1\.70 percentage points, and an R² score of 0\.967 on the held\-out synthetic test cells\. An SQLite database stores battery information, cycle data, predictions, explanations, and alerts\. The framework aims to improve the interpretability, traceability, and management of EV battery health predictions\. However, the reported results are based entirely on synthetic data and do not establish real\-world battery prediction accuracy\. Future work includes validation using public battery datasets, such as NASA and CALCE, and further evaluation under real\-world conditions\.

## [التحديات العقدية في عصر الذكاء الاصطناعي وأثرها في القيم الإنسانية \(دراسة معاصرة\)](../publications/e61c1a39846f39bb85f1.md)

أ\.د\. ياسر صائب خورشيد; أ\.م\.د\. عثمان شهاب أحمد; أ\.م\.د\. معتز طارق شاكر

ان العالم المعاصر يشهد تطورًا متسارعًا في تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي، الأمر الذي أحدث تحولات جوهرية في أنماط التفكير الإنساني، وطرائق اكتساب المعرفة، وآليات اتخاذ القرار، فضلًا عن انعكاساته المتعددة على منظومة القيم الإنسانية والأخلاقية والاجتماعية\. وقد أفرز هذا التطور جملة من التحديات الفكرية والعقلية التي تستدعي الدراسة والتحليل، ولا سيما في ظل تنامي الاعتماد على الأنظمة الذكية في مجالات التعليم والبحث العلمي والإعلام والتواصل الاجتماعي، وما يرافق ذلك من تساؤلات بشأن حدود العلاقة بين العقل البشري والآلة، ومدى قدرة الإنسان على المحافظة على استقلالية تفكيره ووعيه النقدي في بيئة تكنولوجية متغيرة\. يهدف هذا البحث إلى بيان أبرز التحديات العقلية والفكرية التي أفرزها الذكاء الاصطناعي في العصر الحديث، والكشف عن أثره في القيمة الإنسانية من جوانبها الأخلاقية والاجتماعية والمعرفية، مع التركيز على ما قد ينشأ عن الإفراط في استخدام هذه التقنيات من تراجع في مهارات التفكير النقدي والإبداعي، وضعف القدرة على التحليل والاستنتاج، والاعتماد المفرط على المخرجات الآلية في بناء الأحكام وتكوين المواقف\. كما يسعى البحث إلى مناقشة الإشكالات المرتبطة بالخصوصية والمسؤولية الأخلاقية والحرية الإنسانية، ومدى تأثير التحولات الرقمية في مكانة الإنسان وكرامته ودوره في توجيه المعرفة وتسخيرها لخدمة المجتمع \.ويخلص البحث إلى أن التحدي الأساسي في عصر الذكاء الاصطناعي لا يتمثل في تطور الآلة بحد ذاته، وإنما في كيفية توظيفها، ومدى قدرة الإنسان على المحافظة على استقلالية عقله، وصيانة كرامته، وتعزيز منظومته الأخلاقية في ظل التحولات الرقمية المتسارعة\. كما يؤكد ضرورة ترسيخ الوعي الرقمي والأخلاقي، وتنمية مهارات التفكير النقدي والإبداعي، وتعزيز المسؤولية الإنسانية في استخدام التقنيات الذكية، بما يحقق التوازن بين التقدم التكنولوجي والمحافظة على القيم الإنسانية، ويضمن أن يظل الذكاء الاصطناعي وسيلة لخدمة الإنسان والارتقاء بواقعه، لا عاملًا في إضعاف قدراته أو الانتقاص من مكانته\.

## [Green synthesis of copper oxide nanoparticles ST@CuONPs by Streptomyces thinghirensis: current treatment path against multidrug\-resistant bacteria](../publications/e61f6259531fd96730aa.md)

Amal Loqman; Qassim Esmaeel; Stéphanie Sayen; Simon Rémy; Jean‐Hugues Renault; Younes Smani; Souad Loqman

Background Antibiotic resistance is currently a global concern, leading to serious complications in both clinical and non\-clinical settings, and is particularly dreaded in developing countries\. In the search for alternative treatments against bacterial infections, nanotechnology has opened up unexpected new horizons in the scientific world, thanks to the great variety of available nanomaterials that have potential antimicrobial activity\. Some of the interest in this type of nanomaterials relies in their exceptional properties and usages in many fields\. The investigation focused on the synthesis of a new copper oxide nanoparticles ST@CuONPs as a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics using Streptomyces thinghirensis \(DSM 41919 T \) as a novel, bacteria\-mediated synthesis pathway\. Methods The ST@CuONPs were confirmed and characterized by UV\-Vis spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared \(FTIR\) spectroscopy, particle\-size analyzer, scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\), X\-ray diffraction \(XRD\) and transmission electron microscopy \(TEM\)\. The antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of ST@CuONPs were evaluated against Vancomycin\-resistant Enterococcus faecium VRE ATCC 700221vanA, Methicillin\-resistant Staphylococcus aureus NCTC 12493 and Ceftazidime\-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC BAA\-2108, as well as Vancomycin\-sensitive Enterococcus faecalis ATCC 29212, Methicillin\-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213 and Ceftazidime\-sensitive P\. aeruginosa ATCC 27853\. Results and Discussion TEM analysis revealed a spherical shape distribution of ST@CuONPs with an average size of ∼9\.8 ± 0\.27 nm\. The ST@CuONPs demonstrated broad\-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm activities to ward Multidrug\-resistant bacteria\. In addition, among the tested multi\-drug resistant \(MDR\) pathogens, the highest antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacies were observed against the Gram\-positive strain E\. faecium VREATCC 700221vanA\. The bacterial biofilm was reduced by 64% ± 0\.58% at 1/4 × MIC, 83% ± 3% at 1/2 × MIC and 89% ± 1\.15% at 1×MIC of ST@CuONP\. Conclusion The synthesis of ST@CuONPs using S\. thinghirensis is an eco\-friendly and economical method that avoids the use of toxic reagents\. The resulting nanoparticles exhibit a potential to be explored as an alternative to conventional antibiotics\.

## [From Cracks to Craters: A Computer Vision Pipeline for Forecasting Pavement Degradation](../publications/e620e52cd07054ab8556.md)

Derek Hu; William Liu

Potholes and related pavement distresses pose significant safety and financial consequences, yet municipal road maintenance remains largely reactive\. Most computer vision frameworks operate exclusively on static imagery and do not project future degradation\. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a two\-phase pipeline combining automated visual detection with image\-space degradation forecasting\. A YOLOv8m model was trained on the PaveTrack\_OD China subset, comprised of six distress types \(transverse cracks, patched cracks, potholes, patched potholes, alligator cracks, and patched alligator crack\) and four road features \(manholes, street waste, speed bumps, puddles\), achieving an overall mAP@0\.50 of 0\.461 on validation imagery\. In the second phase, a Random Forest Regressor was trained on longitudinal bounding\-box data from PaveTrack\_PD to forecast future 2D pothole bounding\-box dimensions \(width and height in pixels\) from initial dimensions and elapsed time over a six\-month monitoring window\. On controlled holdout test data, the regressor achieved values of 0\.628 for width \(MAE: 86\.68 pixels\) and 0\.448 for height \(MAE: 23\.69 pixels\), with initial bounding\-box width identified as the dominant predictive feature \(53\.4% aggregate Mean Decrease in Impurity\)\. To evaluate cross\-domain generalizability, the pipeline was applied to 62 uncalibrated Google Street View image pairs from Seattle and Southern California\. Evaluated at the image\-pair level, YOLOv8m successfully detected and bounded the co\-located target distress across both temporal captures in 53 of the 62 image pairs\. However, downstream regression accuracy degraded under uncalibrated conditions, yielding a Median Absolute Percentage Error of 78\.6% for width and 47\.9% for height\. These errors reveal fundamental constraints stemming from uncalibrated optical perspective shifts, inconsistent bounding\-box aggregation, and multi\-year extrapolation beyond the six\-month training boundary\. Resolving these bottlenecks via fixed\-perspective cameras and spatial scale normalization is necessary to transition visual defect forecasting into proactive municipal infrastructure management\.

## [Teaching in the AI Era: Studying Faculty Course Redesign, Visible Thinking, and Sustainable Implementation](../publications/e62fdcbd7beaa8801e7b.md)

Sierra Adare\-Tasiwoopa Ápi

How can faculty development move beyond generic AI guidance toward redesigns that make student thinking visible, clarify AI expectations, and remain feasible for teaching\-intensive institutions? This presentation shares the design and emerging findings from Nevada State University’s AI &amp; Accessibility Academy study, which follows faculty from a summer course redesign academy into fall implementation\. The study examines changes in faculty self\-efficacy around AI\-era pedagogy and accessibility, the redesign practices faculty implement, how course artifacts reflect process\-focused assessment and accessible design, and what factors support or constrain sustained implementation\. The session describes the study’s mixed\-methods design, including faculty pre/post/follow\-up surveys, artifact analysis, and a planned student survey on AI\-expectation clarity and whether students perceive their thinking processes as valued, sharing preliminary patterns related to faculty confidence, beliefs about AI and academic integrity, redesign artifacts, and implementation intentions\. Attendees will then examine 3 anonymized examples of AI\-era redesign moves, such as syllabus AI\-use language, process\-based assignments, reasoning\-focused rubrics, or accessibility improvements\. By the end of the session, participants will be able to identify research\-informed indicators of meaningful AI\-era course redesign, describe how faculty self\-efficacy, beliefs about AI, accessibility practices, and workload concerns shape implementation, and consider how to support faculty in moving from AI policies toward assignments and assessments that emphasize transparency, judgment, revision, and student reasoning\. Participants will leave with an adaptable framework for evaluating AI\-related teaching initiatives and designing sustainable faculty support in high\-teaching\-load environments\.

## [A fuzzy decision support system for monitoring student academic performance and supporting early intervention](../publications/e6540f787d306913aa26.md)

Xiaoxiao Liu; Kewei Wen

In digital learning environments, monitoring of students’ learning behavior is challenging due to the uncertainty, incompleteness, and gradual changes in student learning behavior\. Current prediction models may achieve good performance but offer little interpretability and limited support for timely academic intervention\. This study proposes an interpretable Fuzzy Decision Support System \(FDSS\) for monitoring student academic performance and supporting early intervention strategies\. It combines academic, behavioral, and engagement measures from the xAPI\-Edu\-Data dataset with a Mamdani fuzzy inference mechanism, triangular and trapezoidal membership functions, and centroid defuzzification\. The FDSS was assessed using classification measures, early\-warning analysis, sensitivity testing, and comparison with baseline machine learning models\. The proposed system achieved an overall accuracy of 0\.86, a macro\-averaged F1\-score of 0\.84, an AUC of 0\.91, and a High\-Risk recall of 0\.89\. The results indicate that the FDSS is a viable tool for predicting academic performance and for providing rule\-based academic intervention support that is transparent to the user\.

## [Integrating circular economy and policy synergies for cost\-efficient lithium\-ion battery supply chains](../publications/e6730e0653faa7c60f4b.md)

A\. K\. M\. Mohsin; Md\. Rashed; Markus Gerschberger; Sayed Farrukh Ahmed; Ladislav Bartuska; Christopher Schwarz; Md\. Kamal Uddin

The accelerating growth of electric mobility has intensified the need for cleaner and more resource\-efficient production systems within lithium\-ion battery supply chains\. Ensuring sustainability and cost efficiency in these systems is essential to reducing material waste, supply dependency, and environmental pressures across the value chain\. This study examines how circular economy practices within the European Union, a region recognized for its leadership in policy innovation and battery manufacturing, shape the cost performance of lithium\-ion battery systems\. Drawing on longitudinal evidence that captures more than a decade of industrial and regulatory transformation, the analysis applies an integrated framework to explore the interactions among policy measures, technological capabilities, and logistics coordination\. To empirically examine these relationships, the study employs a panel dataset covering the European lithium\-ion battery supply chain from 2010 to 2023\. The analysis combines panel ARDL and nonlinear ARDL \(NARDL\) models with Necessary Condition Analysis \(NCA\) and fuzzy\-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis \(fsQCA\) to capture both dynamic effects and configurational pathways influencing cost efficiency in circular battery supply chains\. The results show that cost efficiency emerges from the combined influence of recycling performance, government incentives, and coordinated reverse logistics rather than from any single intervention\. Strong policy support and efficient recycling infrastructure lead to measurable reductions in production costs and environmental burdens, while fragmented logistics continue to constrain progress\. The study offers strategic guidance for policymakers and industry leaders on aligning circular resource recovery with cleaner production objectives, advancing the transition toward low carbon and economically competitive technologies\.

## [Inteligencia artificial en la administración de justicia penal: garantías y desafíos constitucionales en Ecuador](../publications/e6820e8e95cff044ed59.md)

Andrea Verónica Parrales\-Vera; Daniela Lilibeth Quiroz\-Gavilanes; Odalis Michelle Chica\-Freire; Jason Humberto Ruiz\-Silva

La inteligencia artificial en la justicia penal promete celeridad y apoyo a la decisión, pero puede comprometer la motivación, la defensa, la presunción de inocencia y la imparcialidad judicial\. El estudio analizó su uso en la justicia penal ecuatoriana desde las garantías constitucionales\. Con enfoque cualitativo descriptivo\-analítico, se analizaron documentalmente la Constitución, el Código Orgánico Integral Penal, el Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial, la ley de protección de datos personales, jurisprudencia constitucional y doctrina indexada\. Los resultados muestran que el ordenamiento ofrece garantías aplicables, pero carece de reglas específicas sobre transparencia algorítmica, supervisión humana y control de sesgos\. Se concluye que la inteligencia artificial solo es compatible con la Constitución como herramienta auxiliar, explicable y sin sustituir la decisión del juez\.

## [What matters in medical training in Wales: a thematic analysis of Wales\-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review Call for Evidence](../publications/e68669dfd0022e4ade01.md)

Ishrat Islam; Thomas Lawson; Caroline Groves; Anton Saayman

Abstract Background Postgraduate medical education in the United Kingdom is delivered within health services experiencing sustained workforce shortages, workload pressure, and reduced supervisory capacity\. National evidence has highlighted concerns around staffing, burnout, training quality, flexibility, and progression, but Wales\-specific qualitative synthesis remains limited\. This study aimed to identify and interpret key themes arising from the Wales\-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review Phase 1 Call for Evidence and to situate these findings in relation to wider UK medical education and workforce evidence\. Methods This qualitative study used thematic analysis of Wales\-specific free\-text responses from the NHS England Medical Training Review Phase 1 Call for Evidence\. The dataset comprised responses from 133 respondents who identified with, or commented on, the Welsh medical training context\. Analysis involved inductive coding within the broad question\-led domains of the parent survey and drew on reflexive principles\. Findings were compared at the theme level with the broader Medical Training Review Call for Evidence summary and General Medical Council State of Medical Education and Practice workplace evidence\. Results Eleven cross\-cutting themes were identified: training capacity and workforce pressures; recruitment, progression, and career development; geographical stability and flexibility; training quality, supervision, and protected educational time; workload, wellbeing, and flexibility; equity and inclusion; curriculum modernisation; service\-training conflict; community and interface training; digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence; and system\-level reform\. The strongest alignment with broader evidence concerned workforce capacity, supervision constraints, service pressure, and structural reform\. Wales\-specific responses added contextual depth by showing how these pressures were experienced in relation to place\-based retention, progression from non\-training roles, and the displacement of training by service demand\. Conclusions Wales\-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review indicate that concerns about medical training in Wales are closely connected to wider UK workforce and training pressures yet shaped by the Welsh service and workforce context\. Reform should address training capacity, workforce planning, protected educational time, equitable progression, flexibility, and sustainable working conditions as interdependent features of postgraduate medical education\.

## [Association of MAGEA4 expression with molecular and immune subtypes and clinical outcomes in recurrent bladder cancer](../publications/e686f295d7b7a3cd1fbd.md)

HuaRong Luo; Chengdang Xu; Yi Liu; Yiwen Yao; Zujun Sun; Yan Gu; 王天如

Background This study assessed MAGEA4 expression in recurrent bladder cancer, examined its relationships with molecular and immune subtypes, and evaluated its association with treatment response and prognosis\. Methods This single\-center exploratory cohort study enrolled 20 patients\. RNA sequencing was performed on recurrent tumor tissue samples\. The EU molecular subtypes were determined\. Immune subtypes were classified, and PD\-L1 and HER2 status were assessed\. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed\. Patients were divided into MAGEA4\-high and MAGEA4\-low groups using the cohort median expression level\. Differences in the composition of molecular/immune subtypes were compared\. Within\-cohort ROC analysis was used to assess discrimination of clinical benefit, and PFS was analyzed using Kaplan\-Meier and Cox methods\. Results The top 20 genes with the most prominent between\-subtype expression differences were identified\. Genes upregulated in the Luminal papillary subtype were enriched in terms related to cell\-cell junctions and epithelial structure maintenance\. Downregulated genes were enriched in pathways associated with immune activation and inflammatory infiltration\. Enrichment signals involved the PI3K\-Akt, MAPK, neuroactive ligand\-receptor interaction, and JAK\-STAT pathways\. Significant differences in PD\-L1 status, TMIT subtypes, and EU subtypes were observed between MAGEA4\-high and MAGEA4\-low groups, and the six MAGEA4\-immune/molecular association tests remained below q&lt;0\.05 after Benjamini\-Hochberg correction\. MAGEA4 expression also differed according to PD\-L1 status, TMIT subtype, and binary EU subtype grouping\. Within\-cohort ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0\.798, 0\.800, and 0\.750 in the overall, immunotherapy, and combination\-therapy cohorts, respectively; the bootstrap optimism\-corrected overall AUC was 0\.793\. High MAGEA4 expression was associated with shorter PFS\. Conclusion MAGEA4 expression was associated with PD\-L1 status, TMIT immune subtypes, and EU molecular subtypes, showed within\-cohort discrimination of clinical benefit, and was associated with poorer PFS\. These findings support further evaluation of MAGEA4 as a candidate molecular stratification marker in independent cohorts\.

## [THE JUNCTION : On the Thirty\-Year Convergence of AI and Real\-Time Systems That Made ST\-T1024 Possible](../publications/e691f0b7148c86dc7c9c.md)

M\. TAALABI; Team LLM\-DIPLOMAT

ST\-T1024 is a deterministic inference architecture for embedded and edge hardware\. It achieves 3\.7 μJ per query, 800 ns AET, and zero hallucination by construction\. It is formally verified, Apache\-2\.0, and runs on a $12 microcontroller\. This paper asks a question the standard itself does not answer: why does this architectureexist, and why now? The answer is not a breakthrough\. The answer is a junction — the meeting of two disciplinesthat almost never meet in one person:· Artificial intelligence — knowledge representation, triage, domain routing, language\.· Real\-time embedded systems — AET/WCET discipline, ROM/SRAM partitioning, powergating, FSM scheduling, certification paths\. The two fields select for opposite instincts\. One tolerates a distribution; the other requires a bound\. They are separated by their failure modes\. ST\-T1024 exists because one person held both fields for thirty years — teaching AI since1988, working in real\-time operating systems since the 1980s, supervising industrial projects at STMicroelectronics from 2003 to 2008, and teaching QNX/Neutrino since 2000\. The paper records the junction, states what each field contributed, and names why thestandard could not have come from anywhere else\. It also discloses how the design processitself was conducted — with a large language model as advisor, under the author&\#x27;sspecification and signature\. That disclosure is not a footnote\. It is the demonstration of the architecture the standard describes\.

## [THE CHANGING ROLE OF LIBRARIANS IN TRANSFORMING ACADEMIC LIBRARIES IN TO RESEARCH HUBS](../publications/e69c50a57233f1ea9b86.md)

Avinash Gajananrao Yette; Dr\. Rajendra R\. Manikpure

Academic libraries are undergoing a fundamental transformation as a result of the rapid growth of digital information, electronic scholarly resources, open\-access publishing, research data, bibliometric tools, artificial intelligence, and networked information systems\. The traditional concept of the library as a place for collecting, organizing, preserving, and providing access to documents is gradually being replaced by the concept of the library as an active research environment\. In this changing environment, librarians are expected to participate throughout the research lifecycle and provide services that support information discovery, literature review, research data management, scholarly communication, research visibility, bibliometric analysis, research ethics, and digital scholarship\. The present paper discusses the changing role of librarians in transforming academic libraries into research hubs\. It examines the importance of research\-support services, information and digital literacy, literature\-search assistance, digital repositories, research data management, citation and bibliometric services, reference management, open access, scholarly publishing, research integrity, researcher visibility, artificial intelligence, and collaborative research environments\. The paper also discusses the challenges faced by Indian academic libraries in implementing advanced research\-support services and suggests a strategic framework for developing libraries as institutional research hubs\. The study concludes that the future relevance of academic libraries will increasingly depend on the ability of librarians to move from a reactive service model to a proactive research\-partnership model\.

## [A Bacillus subtilis strain with high proficiency for biofilm formation delays the onset of aging\-associated morphological defects in cholinergic neurons of C\. elegans](../publications/e6a17f36d398948e72ce.md)

Weiye Gong; Josephine Priebs; Verena Alexia Ohse; Andreas Bremges; Heike tom Dieck; Lars‐Oliver Klotz; Michelle Dargatz; Holger Steinbrenner

Aging is accompanied by progressive functional decline and morphological defects of cholinergic neurons\. Some probiotic bacteria with proficiency for biofilm formation in the gut are being discussed as potentially neuroprotective\. Here, we screened Bacillus subtilis \(B\. subtilis\) strains for biofilm production, using an in vitro assay\. Thereafter, a transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans \(C\. elegans\) strain with its cholinergic neurons expressing green fluorescent protein \(GFP\) was fed for up to 15 days on either the identified biofilm\-producing B\. subtilis strain B4U 50 or the control B\. subtilis strain 168, with or without addition of a standardized Ginkgo biloba preparation\. The morphology of the cholinergic neurons was monitored at several consecutive days by fluorescence microscopy\. The occurrence of morphological defects such as knots and ruptures within the axons of cholinergic neurons, as observed with increasing age, was significantly lower in nematodes provided with the B4U 50 strain\. Even worms whose diet was switched to B4U 50 later in life showed less damage of their neurons, as compared to worms fed on the control strain\. Supplementation with the Ginkgo biloba preparation was neuroprotective in worms fed on either B\. subtilis strain, while a stronger beneficial effect was observed upon combined administration of B\. subtilis B4U 50 and the Ginkgo biloba preparation\. In conclusion, feeding a B\. subtilis strain proficient for biofilm formation, B4U 50, was neuroprotective when compared to a diet consisting of control B\. subtilis, delaying the onset of aging\-associated morphological defects in cholinergic neurons of C\. elegans\.

## [Institutional digitalization and digital stress: a four\-wave observational study of teacher\-reported AI\-collaborative teaching in physical education](../publications/e6a2296846dcf8259b8e.md)

Xiangyu Wang; Xiangyu Wang; Wang Xiaoyun; Wang Xiaoyun

Introduction How institutional digitalization relates to teachers’ experience of work and subsequent artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-supported practice remains unclear\. Methods Drawing on job demands\-resources principles, we examined these relationships in a four\-wave observational cohort of 961 physical education teachers from 120 Chinese institutions\. We linked an organizational\-source digitalization proxy to teacher questionnaires and a study\-specific teacher\-reported score of AI involvement in teaching tasks\. Analyses adjusted for baseline practice and separated between\-institution from teacher\-relative associations\. Results Two of five primary tests met the Holm\-adjusted criterion\. The stress\-related product of between\-institution coefficients was negative \(−0\.099; pointwise 95% confidence interval \[−0\.184, −0\.033\]\)\. The positive digitalization–stress association was weaker among teachers with higher digital self\-efficacy relative to colleagues \(interaction coefficient −0\.101; \[−0\.168, −0\.037\]\) but remained positive at the low, average, and high self\-efficacy levels examined\. The adjusted digitalization–practice association, appraisal\-related coefficient product, and appraisal interaction did not meet the corrected criterion\. Discussion The findings connect the organization and experience of work with reported AI practice, emphasizing perceived digital work pressure and relative self\-efficacy while complementing accounts centered on technology acceptance\.

## [Pengembangan Asisten Virtual Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Layanan Informasi Sistem Manajemen PK IMM UMKO](../publications/e6b3e35f58abb4eb831d.md)

Rizky Satrio Wibowo; Khusnul Khotimah

The management of the Commissariat Leadership \(PK\) of the Muhammadiyah Student Association \(IMM\) at the Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science \(FTIK\), Universitas Muhammadiyah Kotabumi \(UMKO\), has been conducted conventionally using separate Microsoft Excel and Google Form tools, leaving cadre registration, Darul Arqam Dasar \(DAD\) implementation, attendance, and news publication vulnerable to fragmented data, administrative errors, and proxy\-attendance practices\. This research develops a Web Mobile\-based PK IMM UMKO Management System integrated with an Artificial Intelligence virtual assistant for IMM\-related information services\. The system was built using the Waterfall method, the Django framework, and PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, following a Model\-View\-Template architecture with role\-based access control for five actors\. It provides two AI services—a Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) Chatbot using the gpt\-4o\-mini model grounded in official AD/ART documents and a Smart Editor for language correction—together with automatic registration verification through the UMKO SSO API and a per\-session QR attendance module using regenerated UUID tokens as an anti\-proxy mechanism\. Black Box Testing on 32 scenarios was fully valid; chatbot testing on nine scenarios reached 100% accuracy with a median AI response time of about three seconds; and a four\-level Likert scale questionnaire involving 14 respondents across six validator groups yielded an average of 96\.20% in the “Very Feasible” category\. The system is therefore technically and functionally feasible as a modern solution for faculty\-level student organization governance\.

## [Not All Unlabeled Data Are Equal: Unlabeled Data Selection for Semi\-Supervised QSAR Modeling with Large Chemical Repositories](../publications/e6c37b765a9db3bc575f.md)

Oliver Majer; Saso Dzeroski; Jurica Levatic

Semi\-supervised learning \(SSL\) is particularly attractive in domains where labels are expensive to obtain, while unlabeled examples are readily available\. Quantitative Structure\-Activity Relationship \(QSAR\) modeling, which predicts molecular biological activity from chemical structure, is one such domain\. Obtaining activity measurements requires costly wet\-lab experiments, resulting in small labeled datasets, while chemical repositories such as ChEMBL contain millions of unlabeled molecules\. Despite this apparent suitability, the potential of large chemical databases to improve QSAR models via SSL remains largely unexplored\. Furthermore, it is unclear how unlabeled data should be selected in realistic SSL settings with genuine unlabeled data\. We conduct a systematic study of unlabeled\-data selection using 10 QSAR datasets extracted from ChEMBL and a pool of more than 400,000 unlabeled molecules\. To this end, we evaluate three established SSL algorithms \(self\-training, co\-training, and label propagation\) and formulate four unlabeled\-data selection strategies based on random, nearest\-neighbor, furthest\-neighbor, and mixed sampling\. Our results show that unlabeled data from large chemical repositories can improve QSAR models, with at least one SSL configuration outperforming the supervised baseline on each of the 10 datasets\. Moreover, the most reliable improvements are generally achieved by selecting a relatively small number of chemically distant molecules\. This suggests that the composition of the unlabeled set may be more important than its size, challenging the common premise that SSL necessitates an abundance of unlabeled data\.

## [Steering and Setting Free: Insights From a 20‐Year Retrospective Case Study of a Security and Justice Organization&\#x27;s Digital Transformation](../publications/e6c587e864b773959f1e.md)

Friso Selten; Dorus van Loo; Bram Klievink

ABSTRACT Advances in digital technologies are expected to fundamentally change how organizations operate and create value\. Empirical studies show that public organizations face difficulties organizing and sustaining this digital transformation\. To better understand these challenges, this study examines the organizational mechanisms underlying digital transformation in a public organization over the past 20 years\. Our findings show that this transformation was primarily enabled by an emergent change approach, with influential planned changes occurring only occasionally\. We identify the organizational mechanisms underlying both types of change and analyze their interdependence\. Our findings suggest that both emergent and planned change approaches may be needed to enable digital transformation in public organizations effectively, but that combining them is complex in practice\.

## [Computed tomography multi\-phase radiomics models for differentiating benign and malignant thyroid nodules](../publications/e6cb77396db37a9f298e.md)

Ning Li; Jianan Tong; Guozheng Zhang; Shufeng Xu; Weitao Huang; Xiaowei Han; Jingfeng Zhang; Xisong Zhu

Objective To develop and validate an integrated model combining multiphase CT radiomics features, clinical data, and conventional morphological CT signs for the preoperative differentiation of benign and malignant thyroid nodules\. Methods We retrospectively enrolled patients with surgically confirmed thyroid nodules who underwent preoperative contrast\-enhanced thyroid CT examination at two centers\. Patients from center 1 were randomly allocated to a training cohort and an internal validation cohort at an 8:2 ratio; patients from center 2 served as an external validation cohort\. Clinical characteristics and morphological features of nodules were assessed\. Radiomics features were extracted from all three CT phases, and four categories of models were constructed: clinical model, single\-phase CT radiomics models, multiphase CT radiomics model, and combined clinical\-radiomics model\. Model performance and interpretability were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis \(DCA\), and SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\)\. Results The multiphase CT radiomics model yielded areas under the ROC curve \(AUCs\) of 0\.919, 0\.836, and 0\.787 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively\. Among the single\-phase models, the venous\-phase model achieved the best external validation performance \(AUC = 0\.815\)\. The combined model, integrating clinical and morphological features with multiphase radiomics features, achieved the highest overall diagnostic performance, with an external validation AUC of 0\.865 \(sensitivity = 74\.0%, specificity = 84\.5%\), significantly outperforming both the clinical model \(AUC = 0\.800\) and the multiphase radiomics model \(AUC = 0\.787\)\. It also demonstrated favorable calibration and greater clinical net benefit\. Conclusion Multiphase CT radiomics enables effective differentiation of benign and malignant thyroid nodules\. Integration of clinical and morphological information further improves diagnostic performance, providing an objective, noninvasive tool for preoperative risk stratification of incidentally detected thyroid nodules on CT\.

## [Por uma agenda de problematizações decoloniais em inteligência artificial](../publications/e6d325c0a9dd6758fcac.md)

Laura Strelow Storch; Eduardo Rosa Guedes

This article discusses the debates raised by a decolonial agenda for algorithmic computing\. Drawing on a review of the literature, we outline the distinctions between postcolonial theory and decolonial thought, suggesting that this distinction stems from the radicalization of the critique systematized by decolonial thinkers – with repercussions for their research agendas\. We also situate these differences within the field of computing, contrasting postcolonial computing, focused on the cultural dimensions of technological design, with decolonial computing, centered on the relations between racism and technology\. Within the context of decolonial computing, we present the taxonomy of decolonization of algorithmic coloniality proposed by Mohamed et al\. \(2020\), described as 1\) institutionalized algorithmic oppression; 2\) algorithmic exploitation; and 3\) algorithmic dispossession\. We discuss the potential and limitations of decolonial thought for critical research in algorithmic computing, considering the regulatory and political challenges that cut across this research agenda\.

## [EXPRESS: Perfusion Extent and Hypoperfusion Severity Determine Diaschisis Patterns in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A CT Perfusion Study](../publications/e6d9f747d06f57a5c9d8.md)

QI JIA; Nan Nan Sheng; Noémie Ligot; Anissa Abderrakib; niloufar sadeghi\.maybodi; Gilles Naeije

BACKGROUND: Diaschisis reflects remote functional suppression following focal ischemia and large\-scale network disruption\. We investigate the prevalence, overlap, and determinants of multiple diaschisis subtypes using acute CTP\. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 659 patients with hyperacute large\-vessel occlusion stroke\. Diaschisis was primarily assessed on CBV maps and classified into Crossed Cerebellar \(CCD\), Ipsilateral Thalamic \(ITD\), Ipsilateral Hippocampal \(IHD\), and CCD\+ITD\. Tmax\-based assessment was exploratory\. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated severe hypoperfusion extent \(Tmax&gt;6s\), hypoperfusion intensity ratio \(HIR\), and ischemic core volume \(CBF&lt;30%\)\. RESULTS: CCD was the most common subtype, followed by ITD and CCD\+ITD, whereas IHD was rare\. Greater severe hypoperfusion extent was independently associated with CCD, ITD, and CCD\+ITD, while higher HIR was additionally associated with ITD, and CCD\+ITD\. Ischemic core volume was not independently associated with diaschisis\. CCD was independently associated with left hemispheric stroke, while combined CCD\+ITD was associated with female sex\. Exploratory Tmax\-based analyses showed broadly similar associations\. Subtype overlap suggested involvement of multiple interconnected network nodes\. CONCLUSION: Hyperacute diaschisis reflects ischemia\-driven network dysfunction primarily related to severe hypoperfusion extent, with hypoperfusion severity contributing to specific subtypes\. These findings support CBV\-based CTP assessment for investigating large\-scale network vulnerability, while Tmax\-based may provide complementary information for future diaschisis research\.

## [Caracterización estructural\-territorial de los Gad Municipales del Ecuador mediante análisis de componentes principales y machine learning no supervisado](../publications/e6e63ff53aad70d8df1d.md)

Tatiana Elizabeth Arana Sangacha; Washington David Acurio Martinez; Edwin Ramiro Jácome Simbaña

La heterogeneidad demográfica, financiera y territorial de los Gobiernos Autónomos Descentralizados \(GAD\) municipales plantea la necesidad de disponer de herramientas que permitan caracterizar conjuntamente las diferencias existentes entre los cantones del Ecuador\. El objetivo de este estudio fue clasificar los GAD municipales ecuatorianos a partir de la combinación de población proyectada, gasto total codificado y densidad poblacional correspondiente al año 2025\. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, no experimental, observacional y de corte transversal, cuya unidad de análisis estuvo constituida por 221 cantones\. Las variables fueron transformadas mediante logaritmo natural para aplicar Análisis de Componentes Principales \(ACP\) y conseguir medidas sintéticas de escala\. El primer componente se denominó escala demográfico\-financiera y el segundo componente concentración territorial; donde las dos dimensiones explicaron conjuntamente el 96,45 % de la varianza total\. Posteriormente, las coordenadas factoriales de ambas dimensiones fueron estandarizadas y utilizadas en un algoritmo K\-means, evaluando soluciones de dos a ocho conglomerados\. Para determinar el número de clústeres se efectuó una evaluación conjunta de la suma de cuadrados intra\-clúster \(WSS\) y el coeficiente de Silhouette, presentando una solución de 7 clústeres\. Además, se destaca la existencia de dos perfiles de alta escala que presentan configuraciones territoriales distintas: uno caracterizado por elevada concentración poblacional y otro por una escala demográfica y financiera muy alta, pero menor concentración territorial relativa\. Los resultados muestran que la combinación de ACP y K\-means permite generar una clasificación sólida y ofrece una tipología exploratoria de la heterogeneidad territorial de los GAD municipales ecuatorianos\.

## [Combined effect of functional impairment and metabolic dysregulation on post\-stroke depression risk](../publications/e6e8dca63b0d6d630ae4.md)

Tianhao Zhang; Wenlu Shi; Qingjie Chi; Jinhua Qian; Tianle Wang; Li Zhu; Wenbing Ding; Zhuo Chen

Background Post\-stroke depression \(PSD\) is one of the most common neuropsychiatric complications among stroke survivors, significantly affecting rehabilitation adherence and long\-term clinical outcomes\. Although previous studies have examined the roles of either functional impairment or metabolic dysregulation in PSD, limited research has explored their combined impact from an integrative perspective\. Methods This study included 245 stroke patients, of whom 65 were diagnosed with PSD\. Restricted cubic spline \(RCS\) analysis was used to assess nonlinear associations between the atherogenic index of plasma \(AIP\), triglyceride\-glucose \(TyG\) index, and the risk of PSD\. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors\. A partial least squares \(PLS\) model was constructed using four variables—Barthel index, body mass index \(BMI\), AIP, and TyG index\. Then the K\-means clustering was applied to identify functional–metabolic subtypes and examine their associations with PSD\. Results Compared with non\-PSD patients, those with PSD showed significantly lower Barthel index scores and higher TyG and AIP levels\. RCS analysis indicated a nonlinear relationship between AIP and PSD\. Logistic regression identified the Barthel index \(OR = 0\.97, 95% CI: 0\.95\-0\.99\) and TyG index \(OR = 2\.04, 95% CI: 1\.19\-3\.47\) as independent predictors of PSD\. PLS\-K\-means clustering revealed four distinct subtypes\. Patients in subtype 3 \(metabolically susceptible subtype\) and subtype 4 \(dual\-impaired subtype\) had significantly higher PSD risks compared to subtypes 1 and 2 \(OR = 2\.13 and 2\.63, respectively\)\. Conclusions Functional impairment and metabolic dysregulation are jointly associated with the development of PSD, and their interaction may constitute a key potential mechanistic\.

## [AI Tools and EFL Identity: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Gender and Cultural Representation in AI\-Generated Reading Materials for Gulf University Students](../publications/e6f2c27d0a3e5a714e82.md)

Adnan Bataineh; Kashif Ali Sabiri; Ebrahim Abdullah Douzandeh

The incorporation of artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools into English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) classroom has revolutionized the production of teaching content\. However, the ideological implications of AI\-generated content have been markedly under\-researched in non\-Western contexts\. This study employs Fairclough’s three\-dimensional framework of Critical Discourse Analysis \(CDA\) on a corpus of 45 AI\-generated EFL reading texts produced by the ChatGPT\-4o, Google Gemini 1\.5 Pro, and Microsoft Copilot in response to five standardized instructional prompts\. It aims to investigate how gender and Arab cultural identity is discursively constructed in materials targeting Gulf university EFL learners\. Analysis of the findings show that the female professional is consistently represented through discourse of relational and communal achievement while the single male professional is coded through individual enterprise and resilience\. Leadership discourse universalizes the individual while entirely erasing gender and cultural identity across the nine texts\. Furthermore, a Western nuclear family development narrative renders the Arab family invisible\. Finally, Microsoft Copilot shows the lowest cultural specificity and the highest degree of textual cloning across platforms\. The findings further affirm that L2 writing created by these AI models replicates Western liberal ideological formations, thus marginalizing the cultural and gender identities of the Arab learners\. The research makes pedagogical, technological, and policy recommendations for the culturally responsive use of AI tools in higher education in the Gulf\.
