## [Network Pharmacology and Bioinformatic Prediction of Five Medicinal\-Food Homologous Plants Against the Progression from Chronic Atrophic Gastritis to Gastric Cancer](../publications/e7edd9a477e0aecc334f.md)

Menglin Chen; Houshu Tu; Chengming Yang¹; Cui Xu¹; Yaqian Huang; Ling He

Chronic atrophic gastritis \(CAG\) progresses through distinct pathological stages to gastric cancer\. This computational study employed network pharmacology and bioinformatics to predict the active compounds, targets, and pathways of five medicinal\-food homologous plants \( Houttuyniae Herba , Mume Fructus , Rhizoma Dioscoreae , Portulacae Herba , and Curcumae longae Rhizoma \) against this progression\. We identified 28 active compounds and 242 targets from TCMSP\. differentially expressed genes from GSE130823 and GSE55696 were integrated with weighted gene co\-expression network analysis, yielding 129 candidate targets\. Machine learning \(LASSO and random forest\) prioritized AR , EIF6 , GSTM2 , and FOSB as potential diagnostic biomarkers distinguishing CAG from cancer\. Enrichment analysis predicted involvement of IL\-17, TNF, and p53 pathways\. Compound\-target\-pathway network analysis identified quercetin and kaempferol as multi\-target compounds\. Molecular docking predicted binding affinities ranging from weak\-to\-moderate for core genes \(−2\.60 to −5\.83 kcal/mol\) and moderate\-to\-strong for inflammatory targets \(up to −7\.25 kcal/mol for quercetin\-TNF\)\. These findings computationally predict candidate mechanisms of these five plants, offering a rationale for future experimental validation and therapeutic development\.

## [Dietary elimination of gluten attenuates amyloid\-β and tau pathology in Alzheimer’s disease\-like in aluminum chloride\-induced rats: an experimental animal study](../publications/e7f5ae390c4c55b7adcb.md)

Ghada Abdelaziz; Abdel\-Rahman B\. Abdel\-Ghaffar; Dina Amr; Ahmed Mohamed Kamal Nada; Refaat M\. Gabre

Abstract This study evaluates the comparative neuroprotective efficacy of a multi\-component dietary pattern \(the Mediterranean\-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay\) versus a single\-component elimination strategy \(gluten\-free diet\) in an AlCl₃\-induced rat model of Alzheimer’s disease\. Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly divided into six groups \(n = 6 each\) and fed a balanced diet, the MIND diet, or a gluten\-free diet, with or without AlCl₃ \(100 mg/kg/day\) administered orally for 8 weeks\. AlCl₃ administration significantly elevated Aβ, total tau, and p\-Tau S231 compared to non\-induced controls \( P &lt; 0\.001 for all AD effects\)\. Conversely, all three diets differed significantly from one another for total tau and p\-Tau S231 \( P &lt; 0\.05 for all comparisons\)\. Under AD\-inducing conditions, the MIND diet significantly reduced cortical Aβ and total tau by 41\.9% and 22\.7%, while the gluten\-free diet significantly reduced them by 50\.3% and 41\.6%, relative to the AD disease\-control group \(all P &lt; \.001\)\. Histopathologically, both diets preserved cortical and hippocampal architecture, but behaviorally, diet showed no significant effect on the novel object recognition discrimination index \( P = 0\.092\)\. Both the MIND and gluten\-free diets successfully attenuated Aβ accumulation, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration in AlCl₃\-induced AD models, with the gluten\-free diet yielding greater numerical reductions\.

## [ON GENERALIZED 𝜶 CLOSED SETS IN VAGUE SOFT TOPOLOGICAL SPACES](../publications/e7f786a3872064f949a8.md)



Uncertainty in mathematical modeling is generally treated by fuzzy, vague, and soft set theories\.In vague soft topological spaces, α closed sets have a central role in studying the generalized closure property with dual valued uncertainty\.However, the existing definitions of vague soft α closed sets are of narrow applicability, and the extensions are mostly trivial without sufficient difference from the previously defined closed type sets or meaningful examples to show their practicality\.In this paper, we propose the idea of generalized vague soft α closed sets in soft generalized vague topological spaces\.The definition is given in terms of vague soft closure and interior operators\.The essential properties of these sets are studied, such as their properties under union, intersection, and inclusion relations with vague soft closed, semi closed, pre closed, and β closed sets\.Non trivial examples and counterexamples are provided to show the differences between the new sets and the existing ones\.Moreover, the study of α continuity and generalized continuity is considered, and the necessary and sufficient conditions for the generalized vague soft α closedness of inverse images are obtained\.The obtained results provide a precise structural extension to vague soft topology and provide a basis for further research on separation axioms and continuity in parameterized uncertain spaces\.

## [A novel fine\-tuning method for long short\-term memory models on edge device to adapt to dynamic user habits in smart homes](../publications/e800b10986feb2311ee9.md)

Chen Zhong; Weiwei Lyu; Xianzhong Nie; Pan Peng

Static machine learning models in smart home automation may struggle to adapt to dynamic user habits when deployed on resource\-constrained edge devices\. Although long short\-term memory networks can capture temporal dependencies in user behavior, models trained on fixed historical data may lose accuracy as user patterns evolve\. Periodically retraining the complete model is computationally demanding on an edge device\. To address this problem, this study proposes an incremental fine\-tuning method that updates a pre\-trained long short\-term memory model using small batches of newly labeled data derived from user feedback\. Evaluation in a real\-world smart home system comprised an offline chronological replay of the initial data stream, a subsequent 21\-day continuous\-operation stream, and separate model\-update cost measurements on a Raspberry Pi 4B\. In the initial replay, the incrementally fine\-tuned model achieved the highest F1\-score among the four evaluated models, reaching 0\.9401 for air\-conditioner prediction and 0\.9430 for light prediction\. During the subsequent 21\-day air\-conditioner evaluation, it maintained the highest daily F1\-score after the initial transient period\. Compared with full retraining, incremental fine\-tuning reduced average processor utilization from 32\.00% to 8\.00% and peak memory use from 13\.55 megabytes to 7\.25 megabytes\. Within the evaluated single\-participant setting, these results indicate the potential of lightweight incremental model updates for adaptive smart home automation on resource\-constrained edge devices; evaluation across more diverse users, prediction tasks, residential environments, and edge hardware is still required\.

## [Explainable machine learning using pretreatment complete blood count parameters and demographic characteristics for gastric cancer risk stratification: a temporal validation study](../publications/e804ebf16ba3c2515d7f.md)

Yongfeng Qiao; Qian Long; Jin Tang; Xin Wang; 王守力

Background Gastric cancer \(GC\) is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, while endoscopy is invasive and conventional serum tumour markers have limited sensitivity\. A low\-cost, widely available tool that can identify patients at higher risk and prioritise them for endoscopic evaluation could therefore strengthen early\-detection pathways\. The complete blood count \(CBC\) is routinely available and well suited to such first\-contact risk stratification; however, existing CBC\-based machine\-learning models are often developed in cohorts that mix prevalent, postoperative, on\-treatment and surveillance records, potentially confounding the haematological signal\. We therefore developed and temporally validated an explainable CBC\-based model to stratify the risk of newly diagnosed GC versus benign gastric disease in a rigorously verified, treatment\-naïve cohort\. Methods In this retrospective single\-centre study, 2,044 patients \(477 pathologically confirmed, newly diagnosed, treatment\-naïve GC and 1,567 benign gastric\-disease controls\) were assembled through case\-by\-case chart review, patient\-level identity de\-duplication and application of the same prespecified comorbidity\-screening criteria\. The baseline CBC was obtained at admission before treatment\. A parsimonious model incorporated six routinely available variables: age, sex, and neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte and platelet counts\. Eight algorithms were trained using five\-fold cross\-validation in the training cohort \(n = 1,309\) and evaluated in a temporally separated validation cohort \(n = 735\)\. Random forest was designated as the reference explainable model and interpreted using SHAP\. Model behaviour in tumour\-marker\-negative GC and robustness in sensitivity analyses were also assessed\. Results Discrimination was similar across algorithms\. In temporal validation, random forest achieved an AUC of 0\.831 \(95% CI 0\.798–0\.864\), which was numerically similar to that of the highest\-AUC model, XGBoost \(AUC 0\.832\), with substantially overlapping 95% confidence intervals\. Random forest had a low Brier score \(0\.133\) and showed positive net benefit across the evaluated threshold\-probability range\. SHAP identified lymphocyte count, male sex and age as the leading predictors, with an identical feature ranking under XGBoost \(Spearman ρ = 1\.00\)\. Adding derived inflammatory ratios did not improve discrimination \(ΔAUC −0\.010, p = 0\.139\)\. Among temporal\-validation patients with triple\-negative GC, defined as CEA\-, CA19\-9\- and CA72\-4\-negative disease, the model classified 62\.7% \(95% CI 50\.0–73\.9\) as high risk\. Conclusions A six\-variable model combining pretreatment CBC parameters with age and sex discriminated newly diagnosed GC from benign gastric disease in a temporally separated validation cohort and showed broadly acceptable graphical calibration and a low Brier score\. The model classified a substantial proportion of tumour\-marker\-negative GC cases as high risk, supporting further evaluation as a low\-cost pre\-endoscopic triage aid\. External multicentre validation is required\.

## [Factors influencing nursing educators’ behavioral intention to adopt artificial intelligence in teaching: A cross\-sectional study from Morocco](../publications/e8169928d3e68304958e.md)

ACHRAF SOUDI; Soukaina Wakrim

Purpose: Educators are central to the successful integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in health sciences education, yet evidence from North African contexts remains scarce\. This study examined the factors associated with nursing educators&\#x27; behavioral intention to adopt AI in their teaching practices in Laayoune, Morocco\. Methods: A cross\-sectional analytical study was conducted among 108 nursing educators \(response rate: 90\.8%\) between June and July 2025\. A French\-language, self\-administered questionnaire based on the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology measured behavioral intention and ten individual, technological, and organizational dimensions \(45 items; Cronbach&\#x27;s α = 0\.835–0\.983\)\. Behavioral intention, the canonical acceptance outcome in both models, was analyzed as a continuous variable using independent\-samples t\-tests with effect sizes, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression with backward elimination, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a logistic sensitivity analysis\. Results: Behavioral intention was high \(per\-item mean 4\.29 ± 0\.53 out of 5\), and 94\.4% of educators already used AI tools in teaching, despite high anxiety \(4\.50 ± 0\.70\), high perceived risk \(3\.98 ± 0\.73\), and very low perceived facilitating conditions \(2\.11 ± 1\.27\)\. In the final regression model, awareness \(β = 0\.556, p &lt; 0\.001\) and self\-efficacy \(β = 0\.248, p = 0\.010\) were the only independent predictors, together explaining 57\.4% of the variance in intention \(F\(2, 105\) = 70\.62, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The bivariate associations of age, teaching experience, AI knowledge, and AI proficiency with intention were fully accounted for by these two factors\. Conclusion: AI adoption among these nursing educators appears largely individual and self\-directed, driven by awareness and confidence rather than institutional support, which was perceived as weak\. Strengthening AI literacy and self\-efficacy, alongside institutional investment in infrastructure, training, and guidelines, may support responsible AI integration\. Findings from this single\-institution study should be interpreted with appropriate caution\.

## [Fixed compliance costs and producer selection in regional food production: evidence from China&\#x27;s 2006 agricultural product quality and safety law](../publications/e82348d9469654df864b.md)

Xi Feng; 毕军涛; Mengwei Yang

Food\-safety law protects consumers, but the mandatory standards, input restrictions, record\-keeping, and pre\-sale testing it imposes are largely fixed costs that fall hardest on the smallest producers\. Whether that incidence survives aggregation, that is, whether output shed by marginal producers is absorbed by survivors or genuinely lost to a region, remains unsettled\. We study China&\#x27;s 2006 Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Law, a nationally synchronous mandate, across 284 prefecture\-level cities from 2001 to 2018\. A continuous\-intensity difference\-in\-differences design links predetermined pre\-law exposure to post\-law changes in per\-capita animal\-source food output, measured at the point of production rather than consumption, treating 2006 as a transition year and 2007 as the first full year of implementation\. In the baseline specification, more exposed cities produced roughly 5% less animal\-source food after implementation, with the contraction emerging over the post\-law period\. Because exposure is built from a pre\-law outcome level, we re\-estimate the relationship on a window excluding the years used to measure exposure; the negative gradient persists\. Three findings locate the burden\. The contraction covers the activities the statute regulates, animal\-source food, grain, and primary\-sector value added alike, and is absent from secondary and tertiary activity, making a general regional decline less consistent with the observed pattern\. Within animal\-source food, it concentrates in aquaculture, the most compliance\-intensive segment\. Further, it weakens as baseline farm scale rises, a gradient that persists under province\-by\-year fixed effects and under year\-specific trends in baseline economic structure, both of which absorb the average exposure gradient entirely\. Because the design works on regional quantities rather than producer histories, it identifies output a region no longer produces rather than the departure of identified producers\. The findings are therefore consistent with uniform safety obligations having uneven production\-side incidence across regions with different producer structures, which points to shared compliance infrastructure as a way to ease fixed compliance burdens without weakening substantive safety standards\.

## [Climate Vulnerability and Gendered Coping Strategies: Insights from Disaster\-Prone Coastal Odisha](../publications/e825bb8b7d85af145b99.md)

Abha Mishra; Damodar Jena; Bandana Nayak; Rajkishore Rout; Abhinav Mishra; P\. R\. Mishra

Abstract: Climate\-induced disasters, including floods, cyclones, and droughts, have increased in frequency and severity in coastal Odisha over the past few decades\. Recurrent crop failures, livelihood disruptions, and loss of income have heightened economic stress and reduced the resilience of vulnerable communities\. These impacts are often gender\-differentiated, influencing how men and women respond to and cope with disaster\-related challenges\. This study examines gender\-specific coping strategies in the flood\-prone coastal regions of Puri district, Odisha\. A mixed\-methods approach was adopted to collect primary data from 300 households across 12 villages, along with focus group discussions, key informant interviews and case studies\. The findings reveal significant gender differences in coping responses\. Men largely adopted economic responses such as temporary migration for employment, livelihood diversification, wage labour in nearby towns and involvement in repair activities\. Women, on the other hand, relied more on household and resource management, social support networks, and participation in self\-help groups, and borrowing through community networks\. Livelihood disruptions and economic insecurity resulted in susceptibility to emotional and psychological stress among men\. In contrast, despite several challenges faced by women, they strengthened household resilience and disaster response through caregiving, community engagement, and social networks\. Regression analysis further indicated that social capital, education, household income, and access to early warning system, substantially affected gender\-differentiated disaster coping strategies\. The study emphasizes the significance of social networks and community support systems to develop disaster resilience in coastal communities\. The study further highlights the need for integrating gender perspectives into climate adaptation strategies to increase women’s participation, improve access to resources, and reinforce resilience in vulnerable coastal communities while providing support to men to cope with mental stress linked to change of occupation and living away from families\. Keywords: climate adaptation, climate change, coping strategies, disaster resilience, gender roles, livelihood adaptation

## [STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases](../publications/e82dd8002d0bffcb98a1.md)

Lieqi Liu; Rui gao; Jia\-Chen Gu; Wenbo Hu; Zhaobin Mo; Ahmadreza Moradipari; Nejib Ammar; Wei Wang; Nanyun Peng

In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions\. Evaluating vision\-language models \(VLMs\) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences\. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored\. We introduce STRIDE \(SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases\), an object\-centric benchmark for long\-tail, safety\-critical driving scenarios\. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene\-context awareness\. It pairs multiple\-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free\-form visual question answering \(VQA\) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions\. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language\-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality\. Across 12 proprietary, open\-weight, and driving\-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT\-6\-Astra, achieves only 43\.4% average multiple\-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random\-choice baseline\. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety\-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions\. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal\.

## [PERCEIVED SOCIAL SUPPORT AND STRESS LEVELS AMONG CAREGIVERS OF CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER IN NAIROBI COUNTY, KENYA](../publications/e839dea6b5a1537097ca.md)

Linda Onyuka; Alice Munene; Dr Rahab Karanja

Purpose of the study: The purpose of this study was to investigating the relationship between perceived social support and stress levels among caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\), in Nairobi County, Kenya\. Short introduction of problem statement: Caregivers of children with ASD globally face elevated stress levels\. Research shows that higher perceived social support is linked to lower stress among these caregivers\. Nevertheless, there is a lack of quantitative studies exploring this relationship within the Kenyan context\. The gap in empirical literature limits the creation of targeted policies and interventions aimed at bolstering resilience and wellbeing among ASD caregivers\. Method/methodology: A cross\-sectional design with 127 caregivers from two selected ASD caregiver support groups\. Data analysis was done using SPSS version 27, with descriptive and inferential tests, utilized to analyze the data\. Results of the study: Pearson correlation revealed a significant negative relationship between perceived social support and stress levels in the overall scale \(r = \-\.287, p = \.001\), and across all three subscales\. The overall regression model was significant \(F\(12,114\) = 2\.39, p = \.009, R² = \.201\), with emotional help from family \(B = –1\.08, β = –\.47, p = \.007\) and sharing joys with friends \(B = –0\.96, β = –\.38, p = \.014\) indicated as significant stress predictors\. Conclusion and policy recommendation: The study concluded that higher levels of perceived social support were associated with lower levels of stress, thus validating the Stress Buffering Hypothesis \(SBH\), within the context of ASD caregivers in Kenya\. The results of the study underscore the importance of belonging to reliable peer and organizational support groups, strengthening family ties, and improving partner, and spousal ties\. Keywords: Perceived Social Support, Stress, Caregivers, Children with ASD, Nairobi County, Kenya

## [Human or Virtual? Comparing How Influencer Credibility Shapes Purchase Intention through Parasocial Relationship and Consumer\-Brand Engagement in East Kalimantan, Indonesia](../publications/e8499a07561b65bc82fb.md)

Purwinahyu Purwinahyu; Asnawati Asnawati; Gusti Noorlitaria Achmad

This study examines whether influencer credibility is associated with purchase intention through parasocial relationship \(PSR\) and consumer\-brand engagement \(CBE\), and whether the proposed sequential association differs between human and virtual influencers\. A cross\-sectional survey of 450 social\-media users in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, bootstrapped serial mediation, measurement invariance testing, multi\-group analysis, and predictive assessment\. Credibility was positively associated with PSR \(β = 0\.472\), PSR with CBE \(β = 0\.392\), and CBE with purchase intention \(β = 0\.517\)\. The serial indirect association was statistically supported \(β = 0\.096; 95% CI \[0\.064, 0\.131\]\)\. The credibility–PSR association was stronger for human than virtual influencers \(β = 0\.548 vs\. 0\.391; permutation p = 0\.008\), as was the serial indirect effect \(β = 0\.116 vs\. 0\.071; p = 0\.021\)\. By contrast, the CBE–purchase intention association did not differ significantly between groups \(p = 0\.614\)\. These results identify a source\-type difference at the influencer–consumer bonding stage rather than at the brand\-engagement–intention stage\. The study contributes a dual\-stage relational account that distinguishes PSR directed toward an influencer from CBE directed toward the endorsed brand\. For practitioners, the findings suggest that virtual\-influencer strategies may benefit from credible, consistent, and transparent persona narratives that sustain relational engagement, while both influencer types should connect audience attention to the endorsed brand\. The cross\-sectional, non\-randomized design limits causal inference\.

## [Flausch](../publications/e85144401004522c6967.md)

Yulia Clausen; Tatjana Scheffler

Social media plays an integral role in everyday life\. While much research has focused on hate speech and its effects in virtual spaces, less attention has been devoted to positive forms of online communication\. This study introduces the concept of candy speech \(German: Flausch\) to describe communicative practices characterized by empathy, care, and a sense of group cohesion within virtual communities\. Drawing on a corpus of German\-language YouTube comments, we define candy speech, distinguish its subtypes, and identify its linguistic features\. Our findings reveal that candy speech is at least as prevalent as hate speech in online environments but remains notably underresearched\. By analyzing its role in community building and emotional support, we argue for greater recognition of positive online language as a crucial component of computer\-mediated communication, with the potential to counteract online hate and promote safer virtual environments\.

## [Hepatitis B Immunoprophylaxis rarely prevents molecularly evident subclinical HBV infection in children born to HBsAg\-positive mothers](../publications/e8572a4dee678a7daba3.md)

Liang Xu; Qinghai Dai; Huiying Yang; Rui Su; Yanli Shi; Jing Chen; Jing Hao; Jinyu Hao; Tomasz I\. Michalak

Hepatitis B virus \(HBV\) remains one of the most life\-threatening human pathogens causing chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellular carcinoma in millions of people globally\. Protective vaccines are available for decades, but their implementation is not yet universal\. Mother\-to\-child transmission remains the prevailing route of HBV spread\. Regardless of antiviral treatment of HBV\-infected pregnant woman and neonatal immunoprophylaxis, HBV is transmitted at low levels to newborns as a subclinical \(occult\) infection at rates ranging from singular cases to the majority of the infant population examined in different centers worldwide\. In the current study of 13 mother–child pairs, we applied a high\-sensitivity molecular approach validated in previous studies, examination of different compartments of HBV occurrence, and testing of serial samples from infants followed for up to two years after birth to HBV\-infected mothers treated or not with anti\-HBV agent before parturition\. All newborns received standard HBV immunoprophylaxis with HBV vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin supplemented with additional doses of both during follow\-up\. The data showed that the majority \(84\.6%\) of the children investigated remained HBV reactive during the 24\-month follow\-up after birth at levels of ≤100 HBV genome copies per microgram of DNA, indicating that the prophylactic protocol was only at a low level \(\~15%\) effective in preventing subclinical occult infection in newborns\. Nonetheless, the same protocol inhibited development of overt HBV infection for at least two years after birth\. In addition, the sequencing of the 360\-bp HBV preS\-S genomic fragment revealed homology between infants and umbilical cord blood mononuclear cells that diverged from the corresponding sequences in maternal plasma or peripheral blood cells in 4 of the 5 mother–child pairs examined\. These data from the single\-center study indicate that subclinical HBV infection in infants born to HBV\-infected mothers is far more frequent than that reported and argue that virus transmission to newborns could be an inevitable consequence of maternal infection with HBV\. This study also uncovered previously unknown HBV genomic discrepancy between infected mothers and their infants with occult infection suggesting the fetal and/or placental origin of the viral variant detected\.

## [Doctrinal Problems of Applying Copyright to Literary Works Created by Artificial Intelligence](../publications/e85a9769ca17a0b92f79.md)

Nurboyeva Durdona

The article analyses five doctrinal problems in applying copyright to literary works created by artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. First, it shows that the classical theories \(Locke’s labour theory, Hegel’s personality theory, the utilitarian theory and the fair remuneration theory\) come into conflict when applied to AI activity\. Second, it examines the concept of “author” under the legislation of Uzbekistan, Russia and the United States and under the Berne Convention, together with the question of AI subjecthood\. Third, it addresses the originality requirement, fourth, moral rights, and fifth, the idea–expression dichotomy\. The author concludes that all these problems share a single cause: classical doctrines rest on human consciousness, will and personality\. Accordingly, AI should be treated as a tool rather than a subject\. The article also proposes the “objective control criterion doctrine”, which ties the emergence of copyright to objective, verifiable criteria: purposeful direction of AI activity, creative selection among outputs, and determination of the work’s final content and form\.

## [Proximal Remote Sensing of Oil Palm Basal Stem Rot Using Deep Learning Vision Algorithms and Ground\-based Images](../publications/e8683804b7ddbc993d74.md)

Wan Siu Hong; Jonathan Yong Chung Ee; Jin Yuan Chan; Mohamad Izzuddin Anuar; Mahmud Iwan Solihin

Basal Stem Rot \(BSR\), caused by Ganoderma boninense, threatens oil palm productivity in Southeast Asia\.This study develops and benchmarks a low\-cost remote sensing framework for BSR severity diagnosis from smartphone\-captured RGB trunk images, evaluating two pathways for future field deployment\.The first pairs YOLO detection with a Random Forest classifier: YOLO26n gave the best accuracy\-to\-cost trade\-off among three nanovariants for localizing BSR symptoms \(mushroom, rot, white\-button\), and the end\-to\-end YOLO26n\+RF pipeline achieved 0\.83 accuracy and macro\-F1 of 0\.79 across Healthy, Mild, Moderate, and Severe classes\.Rot was consistently the hardest symptom to localize, owing to its diffuse, boundary\-ambiguous appearance\.The second pathway trained four image classifiers \(EfficientNet\-B0, MobileNetV2, Swin\-Tiny, and ConvNeXt\-V2\-Tiny\) directly on severity labels, with ConvNeXt\-V2\-Tiny performing best \(0\.83 accuracy, 0\.83 macro\-F1\)\.Both pathways performed well at severity extremes but struggled with Moderate, reflecting visual overlap between stages\.SHAP analysis identified rot\-area ratio and fruiting\-body count as top predictors\.These offline results show accurate BSR diagnosis is potentially achievable from smartphone imagery, laying groundwork for future on\-device deployment\.

## [Relational Minority Stress Beyond the Individual: Caregiving Burden, Communication, and Social Support in Families of Transgender Young Adults within the Southern Italian Context](../publications/e86fac9f2f670f85fda0.md)

Ettore D’Aleo; Maria Carmela Zagari; Antonino Raffa; Andrea Greco; Lorenzo Campedelli; Mara Lastretti; Paolo Soraci; Andrea Cicoli; Giulio Rocco di Torrepadula; Emanuela Alessandra Greco; Giuseppe Seminara; Antônio Aversa

Abstract Introduction Minority stress theory has predominantly been used to explain psychological strain among stigmatized individuals, with limited attention to its potential extension within family systems\. Addressing this gap, the present study examines whether caregivers of transgender \(TG\) young adults exhibit a pattern of domain\-specific strain consistent with a relational extension of minority stress specifically within the Italian cultural framework\. Methods In this cross\-sectional study \(conducted between February and March 2026\), caregivers of TG young adults from southern Italian context \( n = 57\) were compared with caregivers of cisgender individuals with obesity \( n = 25\) and caregivers of cisgender individuals without chronic health conditions \( n = 62\)\. The inclusion of caregivers of cisgender individuals with obesity served as a clinical control group to isolate the impact of weight\-related stigma from gender\-related minority stress\. Results One\-way ANOVAs revealed that caregivers of TG young adults reported significantly higher caregiving burden \( p &lt; \.001\), greater stigma\-related communication difficulties \( p &lt; \.001\), and lower perceived social support \( p &lt; \.001\) relative to both comparison groups\. Hierarchical regression analyses further indicated that stigma\-related communication difficulties significantly predicted caregiving burden beyond caregiver group membership and global psychological distress, with perceived social support moderating this relationship \( p &lt; \.001\)\. Conclusions These findings provide empirical support for a relational extension of minority stress, suggesting that stigma\-related processes may operate beyond directly stigmatized individuals and manifest within family systems as domain\-specific caregiving strain rather than generalized distress\. Policy Implications Our results underscore the need to expand minority stress frameworks, social policies and healthcare services to implement targeted programs for families \- such as peer support networks and specialized counseling \- aimed at alleviating caregivers’ burden within the specific challenges of the Italian welfare and social system\.

## [Agentic AI: Autonomous Agents and Multi\-Agent Security](../publications/e87c79d3c8ad7a0ed260.md)

Gayatri Gonte

This paper presents a conceptual review of Agentic Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), autonomous agents, and multi\-agent system security\. It discusses key security threats, including prompt injection, excessive tool permissions, sensitive data leakage, memory poisoning, insecure inter\-agent communication, and cascading failures\. The paper proposes a layered security framework incorporating identity management, least\-privilege access, policy\-controlled tool usage, secure agent communication, memory protection, monitoring, bounded autonomy, and human approval for high\-impact actions\. It also outlines an evaluation methodology using adversarial test cases and measurable security and performance metrics\. This work aims to support the development of safer, more reliable, and secure agentic AI systems\. The proposed framework is conceptual and literature\-based; no prototype implementation or experimental results are claimed\.

## [What drives and forecasts population longevity beyond income? Evidence from a cross\-country panel](../publications/e880939477d3f7e10b58.md)

Giovanna Morelli; Antonia Rosa Gurrieri; Tulia Gattone; Cosimo Magazzino

Population longevity represents a central dimension of sustainable development\. Although national income and life expectancy are closely associated, recent development initiatives increasingly emphasize health\-system capacity, public health interventions, environmental quality, and demographic change\. The extent to which these factors are associated with longevity conditional on income, and the potential of flexible predictive models to generate forward\-looking longevity scenarios, remain uncertain\. This study examines life expectancy at birth as a function of six drivers, using data from 28 countries over the period 2003–2022 and employing a range of Machine Learning \(ML\) techniques\. The results reveal nonlinear associations, including a concave relationship between income and longevity that emerges without imposing a functional form a priori\. The preferred ML model is then used to project life expectancy over 2023–2032 under baseline, accelerated health\-expenditure, and integrated health\-system and prevention scenarios\. Mean life expectancy in the sample increases from 78\.10 years in 2022 to 78\.21 years in 2032 under baseline trends, 78\.34 years under accelerated health expenditure, and 78\.98 years under the integrated health\-system and prevention scenario, with larger gains concentrated in countries that have not yet closed key coverage gaps\. These projections are predictive scenarios rather than causal counterfactuals, but they illustrate how ML models can support forward\-looking population\-health planning, provide decision\-makers with interpretable estimates of alternative longevity trajectories, and offer a basis for extending the analysis to broader country coverage\.

## [Towards a Mechanism for Artificial intelligence into University Education for Environmental Architecture A comparative Analytical Study to Evaluate the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Self\- Learning in Environmental Design\.](../publications/e8844c23d194a98ccaa0.md)

Heba Mahrous Ali Abd EL\-Aal

Architectural education is a field that uniquely targets the creativity and continuous development of architecture students\. This is especially true within environmental architecture, which relies on diverse spatial and temporal variables that create unique interactions for students, based on the specific concept of environmental design\.

## [Trajectories of changing complexity: Inter\-hospital inpatient transfer during the COVID\-19 pandemic](../publications/e88a83811965a3be8358.md)

Micaela Gonzalez Dardik; Tomás Cicchini; Silvia Kochen; Lisandro Otero; Inés Caridi; Ariel Salgado

Los pacientes que acuden a un sistema sanitario se benefician de la interconexión de los hospitales que pertenecen al mismo, ya que facilita su derivación entre diferentes niveles de complejidad\. Esto es fundamental en momentos de crisis como la pandemia de COVID\-19, donde la disponibilidad de recursos es escasa\. Considerando datos recolectados por un sistema informático creado al inicio de la pandemia para gestionar el uso de camas en la Red hospitalaria Sudeste, estudiamos la interacción entre el nivel de complejidad hospitalaria y la supervivencia del paciente\. Este artículo presenta resultados preliminares sobre las estadísticas descriptivas de las trayectorias de los pacientes y analiza futuras líneas de investigación para el modelado de trayectorias individuales de pacientes\.

## [EFL Learner Engagement With CALL](../publications/e88a8b39d1b6d3af1451.md)

Amna Mohammed AlSaadi; John Mathew; Amal Salim Ali Al Sheidi; Sree Lakshmi Ammanamanchi; Salwa Al Hadidi

This mixed\-methods study investigated Omani EFL university students&\#x27; engagement, motivation, and perceptions of the Spark digital platform in a blended learning context\. Using Self\-Determination Theory \(SDT\), the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\), and the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire \(MSLQ\) frameworks, the study analyzed survey data, platform analytics, and focus group discussions from 100 students\. The results showed that extrinsic, grade\-oriented motivation mainly led to moderate engagement\. Although analytics suggested high activity, qualitative findings revealed frustration, redundancy, and time pressure\. Students reported moderate levels of satisfaction\. The study identifies an engagement\-compliance paradox, where observable use masks low intrinsic motivation, and recommends a shift to structured in\-class use, targeted curriculum alignment, and AI\-powered feedback to achieve meaningful and sustained learner engagement\.

## [The interplay between renewable energy, green finance, and economic development: A bibliometric review](../publications/e8933ce019b2a5b2137b.md)

Trần Quốc Thống; Ho Tran Quoc Hai; Duong Le Cam Thuy

Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractResearch on the relationships among green finance, renewable energy, and economic development has expanded rapidly in recent years; however, the intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field remain insufficiently understood\. This study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny, the web interface of the bibliometrix R package\. The analytical framework integrates performance analysis with science mapping techniques, including keyword co\-occurrence, citation, co\-citation, bibliographic coupling, thematic mapping, and thematic evolution analyses\. The findings reveal substantial growth in scientific production and increasing international collaboration, while identifying an intellectual foundation primarily shaped by studies on econometric methodologies, the relationships between economic growth and environmental sustainability, and the integration of green finance with energy economics\. Four major research streams emerge: green financial instruments and markets; the finance, growth, and emissions nexus; renewable energy transition and policy; and advanced quantitative modeling approaches\. Thematic evolution further indicates that, although green finance, renewable energy, and sustainable development remain the core research themes, emerging topics such as digital finance and the digital economy are receiving increasing scholarly attention\. By providing a comprehensive knowledge map of the field, this study contributes to a better understanding of its intellectual foundations, conceptual development, and future research directions, while offering valuable insights for researchers and policymakers seeking to promote sustainable finance, renewable energy transition, and long\-term economic development\.

## [How Algorithmic Bias Shapes Consumer Acceptance of AI Recommendations: The Roles of Recommendation Strategy, Self‐Identity Threat, Perceived Warmth and Privacy Concerns](../publications/e8a61612a1e03a122410.md)

Wei Du; Wenping Jiang

ABSTRACT Algorithmic bias, as a socio‐technical phenomenon, may produce discriminatory outcomes that violate norms of justice and equality, thereby adversely affecting specific groups in society\. Although algorithmic fairness has received widespread attention, how different recommendation strategies interact with algorithmic bias to influence consumers&\#x27; psychological responses in intelligent recommendation scenarios remains underexplored\. Grounded in identity process theory, this study focuses on two recommendation strategies \(relevance‐based vs\. similarity‐based recommendations\) to examine the impact of algorithmic bias on consumers&\#x27; recommendation acceptance intention, and further analyzes the moderating roles of perceived warmth and privacy concerns\. Through four experimental studies \(total N = 895\), we find that algorithmic bias reduces consumers&\#x27; acceptance intention, and this effect is more pronounced under similarity‐based \(vs\. relevance‐based\) recommendation strategies\. Perceived warmth and privacy concerns moderate the mediation pathway of self‐identity threat, such that relevance‐based recommendations \(vs\. similarity‐based recommendations\) enhance recommendation acceptance intention by reducing self‐identity threat\. These findings reveal that similarity‐based recommendations may exacerbate user resistance in the context of algorithmic bias\. This study deepens the theoretical understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying algorithmic unfairness in the digital age, extends the application of identity process theory to the domain of human‐computer interaction, and provides actionable empirical implications for enterprises in the ethical design and strategic optimization of intelligent recommendation systems\.

## [A unified RT\-DETR–Mask2Former framework for segmentation\-guided plant leaf disease detection and classification in real\-world agricultural environments](../publications/e8a8c2be82fec15e69a5.md)

C H\. Mohan Sai Kumar; Golthu Anusha; V\. Dhilip Kumar; Oana Geman; Roxana Toderean; Mihaela E\. Hnatiuc

Plant leaf disease image analysis under real\-world field conditions remains challenging due to cluttered backgrounds, illumination variation, overlapping leaves, scale changes, and irregular lesion patterns\. This study presents a unified RT\-DETR–Mask2Former framework for segmentation\-guided plant leaf disease detection and classification\. In the proposed pipeline, RT\-DETR first localizes leaf regions from complex agricultural images, after which Mask2Former generates fine\-grained lesion masks within the detected regions\. The refined lesion masks are used to isolate disease\-affected regions, enabling EfficientNet\-B4 to extract disease\-focused feature representations for classification\. An EMA\-normalized adaptive task\-weighting procedure was applied with AdamW optimization to modulate the relative gradient scales of the separately supervised modules\. Model development and internal evaluation were conducted using leakage\-controlled, group\-aware PlantVillage \(PV\) partitions, whereas 4,200 field\-acquired images were reserved exclusively for independent external evaluation\. On the complete 38\-category PV internal test, accuracy and macro\-F1 were 98\.34% and 97\.97%\. On the nine\-category source\-matched subset, accuracy and macro\-F1 were 97\.43% and 96\.77%, versus 84\.93% and 80\.80% in the field\. PV\-to\-field performance declined from 95\.63% to 89\.28% for leaf\-localization AP@0\.5 and from 92\.47%/86\.00% to 77\.90%/63\.80% for lesion\-positive Dice/IoU\. Lesion guidance improved field macro\-F1 from 73\.97% to 80\.80%\. The complete pipeline required approximately 285 GFLOPs and 63 ms per image \(16 FPS\), demonstrating a practical accuracy–efficiency trade\-off while retaining a measurable field\-domain gap\.

## [Serial urinary NGAL and CK20 for dynamic cardiovascular risk stratification in non\-muscle\-invasive bladder cancer: a retrospective clinical cohort study](../publications/e8ba7b6c4c2edd8098c3.md)

Wang Ma; Yan Liu; Lei Tang; Song Ouyang; Yanjun Ma; Zhidong Zhang¹; Qianyue Li; Zhikun Li¹; Lin Li; Yawei Zhao

Background Non\-muscle\-invasive bladder cancer \(NMIBC\) is commonly managed with intravesical BCG, whereas pembrolizumab is reserved for selected BCG\-unresponsive high\-risk disease\. Cardiovascular adverse events \(CVAEs\) may occur during cancer therapy, but BCG\-related systemic inflammatory effects and immune checkpoint inhibitor \(ICI\)\-mediated cardiovascular immune\-related adverse events have distinct pathophysiology and clinical kinetics\. We evaluated serial urinary NGAL and CK20 as non\-invasive candidate biomarkers for dynamic CVAE risk stratification\. Methods A retrospective single\-center cohort of 215 NMIBC patients \(2021–2023\) underwent serial urinary NGAL \(ELISA\) and CK20 mRNA \(qRT\-PCR\) assessment at baseline and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after TURBT\. Biomarker cutoffs were derived in a 70% training split and evaluated in the remaining 30% internal validation split\. Cardiovascular surveillance included echocardiography, ECG, BNP, and high\-sensitivity troponin I\. The primary endpoint was CTCAE\-graded CVAE; Cox regression evaluated associations with cardiovascular event\-free survival \(CVEFS\)\. Results CVAEs occurred in 74/215 patients \(34\.4%\)\. The BCG cohort comprised 112 patients; the pembrolizumab subgroup comprised only 25 patients and is therefore interpreted exploratorily\. Four ICI\-associated myocarditis cases occurred in the pembrolizumab subgroup \(16\.0%; exact 95% CI 4\.5–36\.1%\)\. Baseline urinary NGAL was higher in patients with subsequent CVAEs \(128\.7 ± 38\.9 vs\. 69\.3 ± 33\.7 ng/mL, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Combined NGAL \+ CK20 yielded an internally validated 6\-month AUC of 0\.913 \(95% CI 0\.866–0\.960\), and dual positivity was associated with CVAE risk \(aHR=4\.12, 95% CI 2\.71–6\.26\)\. The reported lead\-time analysis suggested earlier NGAL change before echocardiographic LVEF decline; this finding requires prospective confirmation\. Conclusions Serial urinary NGAL and CK20 are promising candidate markers for CVAE risk stratification in this retrospective NMIBC cohort\. The findings are driven principally by the overall cohort and the larger BCG\-treated group; ICI\-specific observations are hypothesis\-generating because only 25 patients received pembrolizumab\. The proposed biomarker thresholds and surveillance framework require prospective, multicenter external validation before clinical implementation\.

## [HIGHER EDUCATION AND GENERATIVE AI: ETHICAL AND INSTITUTIONAL IMPLICATIONS FOR THE HUMANITIES\.](../publications/e8c32d997179e74c9ee2.md)

Américo Souza

The spread of generative artificial intelligence in higher education is profoundly transforming teaching, assessment, and knowledge production, with significant implications for the Humanities\. Drawing on a critical review of the literature, this theoretical essay examines the ethical incorporation of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) into higher education processes, with particular attention to the Humanities\. It argues that AI regulation should take the form of ethical educational governance—rather than mere control—and that Yuk Hui’s concepts of technodiversity and cosmotechnics offer valuable paths for rethinking authorship, autonomy, and creativity in the Humanities\. The theoretical discussion is illustrated by an ongoing initiative within the History Teacher Education Program at the University of International Integration of Afro\-Brazilian Lusophony \(UNILAB\), aimed at developing a set of ethical guidelines for the use of GenAI\.

## [High Burden and Phenotype‐Specific Variability of Pain Polypharmacy in Early Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases: A 14‐Year Analysis](../publications/e8cbe45272cfac6681f1.md)

D Lu; Md\. Belal Hossain; Kristen May Cunanan; James Cragun; Lauren Vuong; Macarius M\. Donneyong; Michael H\. Weisman; Matthew Baker; Anushka Soni; Titilola Falasinnu

BACKGROUND: Pain drives disability and medication use in autoimmune rheumatic diseases \(ARDs\), even when inflammation is controlled\. The extent of pain\-related polypharmacy across ARDs and chronic overlapping pain conditions \(COPCs\) remains poorly characterized\. We aimed to quantify first\-year pain medication burden following ARD diagnosis and examine variations by disease, COPC status, and time\. METHODS: Using the Merative MarketScan Commercial Claims database, we identified adults newly diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, Sjögren&\#x27;s disease, or systemic sclerosis \(2008\-2021\)\. We analyzed pain\-related medications across 10 pharmacologic categories during the first year postdiagnosis\. Polypharmacy measures included counts of distinct pain medications, medication categories, ≥ 5 and ≥ 10 medication thresholds, and the Medication Quantification Scale\. FINDINGS: Among 149 742 adults with newly diagnosed ARDs, 57\.6% had at least one COPC\. During the first year after diagnosis, patients filled a mean of 9\.0 distinct pain medications and 47\.9% met criteria for ≥ 5 medications; 30\.5% met criteria for ≥ 10 medications\. Ankylosing spondylitis demonstrated the highest medication burden \(mean 11\.6 medications; 57\.5% with ≥ 5 medications; 37\.9% with ≥ 10 medications\)\. Patients with fibromyalgia had consistently higher medication burden across ARDs and were the only COPC group in whom prescribing increased from 2015 onward\. Overall medication burden rose from 2008 to 2014\-2015 and declined thereafter; however, absolute levels remained high\. INTERPRETATION: Pain\-related polypharmacy is common early after ARD diagnosis and varies substantially by disease and pain phenotype\. Despite modest declines from 2015 onward, medication burden remains high, underscoring the need for phenotype\-informed, nonpharmacologic, and deprescribing strategies in rheumatology\.

## [A Text Book of Machine Learning](../publications/e8cc7bc7655539ca3d10.md)

Dinesh Bhagwan Hanchate; Varsha Kiran Bhosale; Pooja Mahadev Pondkule

Machine learning has gone from being a niche field to being a vital part of AI and data science and has also found application in fields like health care and business\. A Text Book of Machine Learning is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate students, and for teachers and early career practitioners, for those who wish to have a clear, rigorous and practical introduction to machine learning algorithms and applications\. The language is kept simple to ensure readers from varied backgrounds can follow the treatment, while the theory is treated rigorously and faithfully to ensure that machine learning can be trusted as a good scientific discipline\. The book is organised into five units\. The foundations are established in unit 1: basic definitions, supervised learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning, space of hypotheses and inductive bias, evaluation of the model and cross validation, linear regression, decision trees, overfitting, learning based on instances: the method of the customers k\-nearest neighbors, reduction of dimensions: the principal component analysis, systems of recommendation: collaborative filtering\. Unit 2 builds probabilistic ML: in addition to various probabilistic tools such as Bayes, MLE, naive Bayes, BN, logistic regression, regularization, SVM, and kernel methods with kernel trick\. The unit also traces the evolution of the perceptrons to deep learning, along with multilayer networks, activation functions, back\-propagation, gradient descent, convolutional networks, recurrent networks, attention, transformer, foundation models and LLMs that have been setting the tone for the field\. Unit 4 introduces you to the computational learning theory such as PAC learning, sample complexity and VC dimension, along with ensemble learning, bagging, random forests, boosting and AdaBoost\. Unit 5 moves on to cluster analysis, including k\-means clustering, hierarchical clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and the expectation\-maximization algorithm; anomaly detection and learned embeddings also are discussed\. Each unit features three themes\. The first topic is generalization: bias \- variance, overfitting and model selection are discussed repeatedly as they appear: the only real measure of a model is how it is performing on data that has not been yet seen\. Second, credible and accountable AI: explainable machine learning \(XAI\), fairness, private, robust, federated learning and uncertainty quantification \(including conformal prediction\) are presented alongside the classical algorithms, instead of as a footnote\. Third, link between classic and current practice: At the end of each chapter, full sections provide future trends and directions, illustrating ways by which the classic and current pattern recognition and data mining practices continue to inspire big data analytics and deep learning efforts\. To facilitate active learning, there is a chapter opening abstract, relevant learning objectives \(where applicable\), and a chapter ending conclusion, review questions and practice activities\. Worked illustrations, comparison tables and figures elucidate the behavior of algorithms and explain when they go awry and how to know which to use for real\-world data sets\. Readers are encouraged to try out different methods, to repeat them on the same data and to challenge each result on which they rely\. I hope this book will become a reliable machine learning textbook for both courses and self\-study or setting up research programs\. Any student starting out in machine learning for the first time will find a soft entry into the field, and any teacher trying to structure the material into a semester\-length course will find that it is easy to get right\. Readers&\#x27; comments and suggestions are being eagerly invited and will be used in future editions to enhance them\.

## [A Deep Learning\-based Feature\-level Privacy\-preserving and Intrusion Detection Framework for Intelligent Cybersecurity Using Blockchain](../publications/e8d1f3319ef6f932394f.md)

Lamyaa Mohammed Kadhim; Waleed Kareem Ahmed; Mohammed Dheyaaldeen Taha; Wathiq Kareem Ahmed; Enas Mohammed Hussein Saeed; Rana Saad Mohammed

The advent of the fast growth of interconnected digital infrastructures has increased the necessity of privacyconserving cybersecurity solutions that can detect network intrusions without revealing sensitive traffic data\.Traditional intrusion detection systems \(IDSs\) typically analyse raw network traffic in a centralized manner, a practice that heightens the risk of data leakage and privacy breaches\.This study proposes an IDS that preserves privacy at the feature level by coupling deep representation learning with encrypted, blockchain\-based storage\.The architecture suggested uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(CNN\-BiLSTM\) model for extracting compact and discriminative representations of network traffic flows\.A multi\-stage privacy pipeline comprising feature normalization, secret permutation, and AES\-256\-GCM encryption is proposed and empirically evaluated against membership\-inference, reconstruction, and attribute\-inference attacks before storage in a permissioned blockchain ledger\.The suggested framework uses encrypted deep feature vectors, unlike current methods of storing raw traffic data or sharing model gradients, which significantly lowers the privacy attack surface and preserve detection\.The framework was tested on four popular databases of intrusion detection, such as CICIDS2017, IoTIDS20, NSL\-KDD, and TRAIN\_TEST\_NETWORK\.Experimental results demonstrate strong detection performance, with accuracy exceeding 0\.95 and reaching approximately 0\.997, alongside high processing throughput and low computational overhead\.The findings indicate that integrating deep feature learning, cryptographic protection, and blockchain\-based storage achieves a favorable balance among privacy preservation, system efficiency, and detection accuracy\.The proposed architecture could be scaled to privacy\-sensitive environments, such as in IoT systems, healthcare systems, and enterprise security monitoring systems\.

## [Ecosystem health and its constraint transitions in Plateau cities: insights from Lhasa, China](../publications/e8f96114385d0d78cc48.md)

Xinyu Gong; Xiaowei Nie; Xiaoduo Pan; Zhuoying Zhang; Yang Yang

Abstract High\-altitude urban ecosystems are exposed to pronounced ecological vulnerability and increasing human pressures\. Existing assessments have primarily characterized overall health status and its spatiotemporal variation, whereas temporal changes in the configuration of underlying constraints have received less attention\. As the capital of the Xizang Autonomous Region of China, Lhasa’s unique geographic and climatic setting on the Qinghai\-Xizang Plateau poses distinctive challenges for ecosystem health assessment\. This study examined ecosystem health constraint transitions in Lhasa from 2011 to 2020 using a plateau\-adapted “Pressure\-State\-Response” \(PSR\) indicator system, obstacle degree analysis, and grey relational analysis\. The ecosystem health index fluctuated but exhibited an overall upward trend\. Municipal solid waste collection volume \(SV\) ranked first in obstacle degree in most years, with a mean obstacle contribution of 29\.41%, identifying it as a recurrent core constraint within the response subsystem\. Energy conservation and environmental protection expenditure intensity \(EPI\), evapotranspiration \(ET\), drainage pipeline density \(DP\), and barren land area \(BA\) constituted secondary constraints whose relative contributions changed over time\. SV had the highest grey relational grade with the ecosystem health index \(0\.7918\), indicating the closest temporal correspondence among indicators\. Alternative weights, aggregation methods, and classification thresholds confirmed the robustness of the temporal pattern\. By revealing constraint transition patterns in high\-altitude urban ecosystem health, this study provides a methodological reference for diagnosing changing constraints and prioritizing management in data\-limited plateau cities\.

## [The associations between healthful and unhealthful plant\-based dietary patterns and all\-cause mortality among older Chinese adults with data\-adapted early\-stage cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic syndrome \(stages 0–2\): a prospective cohort study from the CLHLS](../publications/e901f68526fac0cd2b62.md)

Shipeng Zhang; Enjie Tang; Yanjie Jiang; Ke Zhu; Xiulian Zhuang; Hanyu Wang; Xingyi He; Yan Lu; Qinxiu Zhang; Xueying Li; Jiaqing Song

Aims To examine the associations of the overall plant\-based diet index \(PDI\), healthful plant\-based diet index \(hPDI\), and unhealthful plant\-based diet index \(uPDI\) with all\-cause mortality in older Chinese adults with data\-adapted early\-stage cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic \(CKM\) syndrome \(stages 0–2\)\. Methods and results We analyzed data from 5,872 participants aged ≥65 years from the 2008 wave of the China Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey \(CLHLS\) with data\-adapted CKM stages 0–2 and no prevalent cardiovascular disease\. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire\. Mortality was ascertained through March 2019\. Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analyses were used\. During a median follow\-up of 108 months, 2,870 deaths occurred\. In multivariable\-adjusted models, each 1\-point increase in hPDI was associated with a 1\.1% lower mortality risk \(HR = 0\.989, 95% CI: 0\.982–0\.995; p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas each 1\-point increase in uPDI was associated with a 1\.2% higher mortality risk \(HR = 1\.012, 95% CI: 1\.006–1\.019; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest hPDI quartile had a 13\.2% lower mortality risk \(HR = 0\.868, 95% CI: 0\.783–0\.961\), and the highest uPDI quartile had a 19\.2% higher risk \(HR = 1\.192, 95% CI: 1\.060–1\.340\)\. Stratified estimates suggested numerically stronger associations in CKM stages 1–2 than in stage 0; however, formal interaction tests did not reach statistical significance \( p = 0\.062 for hPDI and p = 0\.824 for uPDI\), indicating limited evidence of effect modification\. Conclusion Higher adherence to a healthful plant\-based diet was associated with lower all\-cause mortality, whereas higher adherence to an unhealthful plant\-based diet was associated with higher mortality among older Chinese adults with data\-adapted early\-stage CKM syndrome\. The overall PDI was not independently associated with mortality after adjustment, underscoring that plant\-based dietary quality, rather than plant\-based eating per se, is the relevant exposure\.

## [Digitalisasi Akuntansi, Informasi Biaya, dan Kinerja Organisasi: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis](../publications/e903b7d2a4b0c64e23fe.md)

Rohimatul Muyasyaroh; Alwan Sri Kustono

Accounting digitalization is expected to improve cost information quality to support managerial decisions, yet its direct effect on organizational performance remains inconsistent\. This study aims to map the relationships and mediation pathways among accounting digitalization, system quality, cost information, managerial decision\-making, and organizational performance, and formulate a research agenda\. A PRISMA 2020\-based systematic literature review searched Scopus and Google Scholar \(12 October 2026\) for 2020–2026 publications; the 20–20–16–16–16 selection flow yielded 16 articles\. Data were analyzed through thematic synthesis and mediation pathway mapping\. Results show that the link between digitalization and information quality is the most consistent, direct effects on decisions or performance vary, and mediation through information quality receives the strongest support, whereas cost accounting techniques are not fully integrated with accounting information systems\. System quality, cost information quality, and managerial decision quality are potential mechanisms, but serial mediation still requires testing\. Organizations should align technology investment with information quality and user competence\.

## [The Utilization of Breast Implants in Modern Alloplastic Breast Surgery](../publications/e912b05fa2846221ebe9.md)

Since their introduction in the 1970s, breast implants have become a cornerstone of both aesthetic and reconstructive plastic surgery\. ## [THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF WRITING SKILLS](../publications/e919f569761665f510ff.md)

Olimova Gulchehra Mannon qizi

Artificial intelligence plays an increasingly significant role in developing writing skills in modern education\. This article examines the potential of AI\-powered tools to improve grammatical accuracy, vocabulary, coherence, and academic writing proficiency\. The study analyzes existing research on automated writing evaluation, personalized feedback, and generative AI applications\. The findings indicate that artificial intelligence can support independent learning, facilitate text revision, and enhance students’ writing performance\.
