## [Clinical AI in Canadian Community Hospitals: A Framework for Implementation Readiness](../publications/e91c09dd8b3e74599212.md)

Changiz Mohiyeddini

Clinical Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) tools are frequently developed in academic centres yet deployed in community hospitals with different workflows, staffing, and oversight\. In Canada, where community hospitals constitute approximately 90% of hospitals, this creates a validation\-to\-implementation gap\. Health Canada&\#x27;s 2026 pre\-market guidance for machine learning\-enabled medical devices addresses manufacturer responsibilities but leaves hospital implementation responsibilities under\-specified\. This article proposes a framework for community hospital AI implementation readiness organized around four dimensions \(contextual validity, sociotechnical workflow integration, calibrated human\-AI reliance, and adaptive safety, equity, and governance\), operationalized through simulation\-based systems testing\. The framework specifies what a community hospital must build to deploy a specific AI tool safely, extending an established Canadian tradition of simulation\-based systems testing to the lifecycle risks of AI\. A real Canadian deployment, the CHARTwatch early warning system, illustrates the dimensions in practice\. Safe AI deployment in community hospitals is an institutional capacity, not a procurement decision\. Leaders should treat implementation readiness as core infrastructure investment\.

## [CD23\-TARGETED IMMUNOTHERAPY FOR GIANT CELL MYOCARDITIS](../publications/e932fefb02811eb71ffc.md)

Michael John Dochniak

Giant cell myocarditis \(GCM\) is a rare, rapidly progressive cardiac disorder characterized by giant, multinucleated cells that contribute to severe myocardial damage\. Existing combination immunosuppressive therapies, although directed at immune\-mediated injury, lack precision and are associated with considerable adverse effects\. A CD23\-targeted intervention holds promise as a more selective, safer adjunctive treatment\. This review evaluates a strategy centered on the low\-affinity IgE receptor \(CD23/FcεRII\), predominantly expressed on alternatively activated \(M2a\) macrophages and B cells\. The proposed method uses engineered anti\-IgE–IgE complexes to engage CD23, inhibiting macrophage fusion—a defining feature of GCM—and fostering a more anti\-inflammatory immune milieu\. This therapy also aims to protect myocardial tissue by suppressing pathogenic T\-cell responses and slowing disease progression\. The review details the scientific basis for this approach, outlines laboratory testing protocols, suggests optimal delivery systems, and considers translational hurdles to clinical implementation\.

## [VR video user experience evaluation under visual and temporal variations and machine learning–based cybersickness prediction](../publications/e9352b2ce254f0986691.md)

Muhammad Shahid Anwar; Amer Mousa Alkharoubi; Mubashir Ahmad; Majed Elwardy

Abstract Virtual reality \(VR\) allows users to experience an engaging and interactive virtual environment\. Such experience is often limited by cybersickness, a perceptual discomfort that varies among individuals\. Understanding and modeling user responses to visual and temporal characteristics of VR content is essential for designing adaptive and user\-centered systems\. Despite its importance, the influence of variations in content encoding and playback on subjective perception of cybersickness remains underexplored\. This study presents a user\-centered evaluation of cybersickness in VR videos manipulated across three dimensions: quantization levels, resolutions, and playback delays\. The study then conducted a subjective experiment with 34 participants who experienced these conditions via a head\-mounted display \(HMD\)\. The user’s subjective responses were collected along with a simulator sickness questionnaire \(SSQ\)\. The subjective results indicate that cybersickness severity increases with higher compression levels, temporal discontinuities, and extreme resolutions, whereas moderate resolution \(2\.5K\) and low compression \(QP22\) yield the most comfortable viewing experiences\. Moreover, the study proposed a Machine Learning\-based cybersickness levels prediction model\. The subjective data were arranged and used to train multiple machine learning techniques, including ANN, SVM, Decision Tree, CatBoost, and XGBoost\. A comparative evaluation among these techniques reveals that XGBoost consistently outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy, F1\-score, and AUROC, demonstrating strong discriminative capability and generalization performance\. These findings highlight clear response patterns that can inform user modeling for adaptive VR systems, where content quality and playback conditions are dynamically adjusted to minimize discomfort\. This work contributes to the broader goal of personalized, user\-adaptive virtual environments that balance immersion and comfort through informed design\.

## [Virtual Care Trends in Older Adults with Parkinson’s Disease in Urban and Rural Ontario, Canada, During COVID\-19](../publications/e936ca36b36732745442.md)

Priti Gros; Tomi Odugbemi; Laura Maclagan; Zhiyin Li; Jun Guan; Connie Marras; Anthony Lang; Lorraine V\. Kalia; Richard H\. Swartz; Susan E\. Bronskill

BACKGROUND: Virtual care services increased during the COVID\-19 pandemic, enabling access to physician consultations\. Most studies on virtual care in Parkinson&\#x27;s disease \(PD\) have focused on tertiary centers, limiting generalizability\. OBJECTIVE: To describe trends in virtual care use over time in people living with PD in Ontario, Canada, by rural and urban region of residence using health administrative data\. METHODS: We conducted a population\-based repeated cross\-sectional study between March 2020 and August 2023, among community\-dwelling people living with PD aged ≥66 years in Ontario, Canada\. We used Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations to estimate rate ratios \(RR\) with 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\) comparing virtual visit rates in urban versus rural areas across physician specialties \(family physicians, neurologists and psychiatrists/geriatricians\)\. RESULTS: Among 24,736 people living with PD in March 2020, 58\.6% were male \(mean age 77\.6 \[SD = 7\.0\] years\), and most resided in urban areas \(89\.9%\)\. Compared to urban residents, rural residents had significantly lower rates of virtual visits to neurologists \(adjusted RR = 0\.93; 95% CI: 0\.90\-0\.96\), family physicians \(aRR = 0\.73; 95% CI: 0\.70\-0\.77\) and geriatricians/psychiatrists \(aRR = 0\.67; 95% CI: 0\.65\-0\.77\)\. Over 3\.5 years, virtual visits declined compared to the first 6 months for neurologists \(aRR = 0\.23; 95% CI: 0\.22\-0\.25\), family physicians \(aRR = 0\.39; 95% CI: 0\.38\-0\.41\) and geriatricians/psychiatrists \(aRR = 0\.45; 95% CI: 0\.40\-0\.51\)\. CONCLUSION: People living with PD in urban centers accessed virtual care more frequently than those living rurally\. Virtual care utilization decreased over time\. The sustainability of virtual care and its impact on health equity among people living with PD requires further study\.

## [Brain\-Computer Interface for Disability Assistance: A Study on Factors Influencing Disabilities&\#x27; Purchase Intention and Price Acceptance for Mind\-Writing Pens](../publications/e93a9e5de91e4b1b053c.md)

Mengya Li; Hu Bing

With the practical application of brain\-computer interface \(BCI\) technology, mind\-writing pens have progressed from the conceptual stage into an iterative product development phase\. Currently, leveraging the trends of population aging and advancements in medical rehabilitation, these products are expected to enter a golden period of growth within the next eight to ten years\. Existing research primarily focuses on BCI risk management and lacks in\-depth exploration of market demand and the factors influencing medical rehabilitation\-related products\. This gap provides a critical research focus for this study\. Using individuals with disabilities as subjects, this study employs a sequential Probit model and KHB mediation analysis to examine factors affecting purchase intention and price acceptance for mind\-writing pens\. Results indicate that age has no significant impact on purchase intention or price acceptance, whereas income shows a significant positive effect\. Battery life and head\-mounted design significantly enhance purchase intention, while weight and recognition accuracy positively influence price acceptance\. Cross\-platform compatibility mediates the effects of income\. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that demand among those under fifty is primarily driven by income, whereas users aged fifty\-one and older prioritize battery life and recognition accuracy; low\- to middle\-income groups emphasize basic usability, whereas high\-income groups value functional enhancement\. Price acceptance decreases progressively as prices rise, peaking below one thousand yuan\. This study provides empirical evidence for the development, pricing, and market promotion of BCI\-based assistive products for individuals with disabilities\.

## [Offline and simulated\-online fNIRS decoding of ankle movements for prospective exo\-ankle control: a pilot study in healthy adults and ankle\-impaired patients](../publications/e93aeb64c730a5edb5e5.md)

Naqash Ahmad; Hammad Nazeer; Noman Naseer; Mirza Obaid Baig; Sadia Shakil; Tong Kai\-yu

This study developed and evaluated a non\-invasive brain–computer interface \(BCI\) framework that decodes functional near\-infrared spectroscopy \(fNIRS\) signals from the motor cortex to generate offline and simulated\-online exo\-ankle control commands, as a proof\-of\-concept step toward future prospective exo\-ankle control\. fNIRS data were recorded from 20 healthy participants and seven patients with ankle motor impairment using a PsychoPy\-based paradigm of rest, dorsiflexion, and plantar flexion\. Following the literature, after preprocessing, an evaluation of different combinations of six statistical features and four classifiers, namely, linear discriminant analysis \(LDA\), quadratic discriminant analysis \(QDA\), support vector machine \(SVM\), and k\-nearest neighbor \(kNN\) was conducted\. Under leave\-one\-subject\-out \(LOSO\) cross\-validation across 20 healthy participants, SVM achieved the mean offline classification accuracy of 72\.50% ± 13\.8% followed by kNN \(65\.83% ± 13\.5%\), LDA \(63\.75% ± 16\.1%\), and QDA \(60\.42% ± 17\.7%\)\. A Friedman test indicated a significant overall difference among classifiers \( p = 0\.0311\)\. Simulated\-online implementation used SVM with a sliding window approach with step sizes of 0\.5, 1, and 1\.5 s under participant\-specific leave\-one\-trial\-out validation\. The results showed a highest mean accuracy of 62\.2% ± 14\.1% at a 1\.5\-s step size\. The patient group showed a lower mean accuracy of 57\.23% ± 5% using SVM under leave\-one\-trial\-out cross\-validation\. Together, these offline and simulated\-online results establish proof\-of\-concept feasibility for fNIRS\-based exo\-ankle control, providing a foundation for future prospective rehabilitation applications\.

## [Advancing Pregnancy and Pediatric Science through the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network](../publications/e9544ffe3b2b1f53e4f1.md)

Joanne Wang; Jashvant D\. Unadkat; Samuel L\.M\. Arnold; John K\. Fallon; Pouria Fattahi; Dongeun Huh; Nicholas M\. Ieronimakis; Edward J\. Kelly; Svetlana Lutsenko; Robert Michael Stroud; Jacqueline B\. Tiley; Jia Ying Yang; Xujia Zhou; Hao Zhu; Rajini Rao; Kathleen M\. Giacomini; Lauren M\. Aleksunes

Human gestation is characterized by dynamic changes in maternal physiology and maturation of tissue functions before and after birth\. The fetus and neonate are highly dependent upon transfer of maternal nutrients via the placenta and lactating mammary gland, which frequently involve selective membrane transporter proteins\. At the same time, developmental changes in fetal and infant transport mechanisms critical for regulating absorption at the intestinal and blood\-brain barriers are occurring\. Coordinate regulation of cellular entry and efflux of nutrients, supplements, and xenobiotics, including drugs and environmental chemicals, must occur during this critical developmental period\. In 2023, the National Institutes of Health launched the Transporter Elucidation Network \(TEN\) across four centers\. This initiative applies experimental, computational, and translational approaches to \(1\) identify SoLute Carrier \(SLC\) superfamily and ATP\-binding cassette \(ABC\) transporters in the human placenta, mammary gland, as well as the pediatric brain and intestinal barriers and, \(2\) characterize their localization, expression, function, and regulation\. The Network seeks to identify functional determinants of transporters as gatekeepers of entry to placenta, mammary gland and brain, and applies structural biology, proteomics, metabolomics, organoids, liquid biopsies, and microphysiological systems to this end\. Computational strategies, such as machine learning, virtual screening, physiologically based pharmacokinetics, and perinatal epidemiology complement our experimental approaches\. This paper highlights the TEN&\#x27;s multidisciplinary strategies to address current challenges in perinatal and pediatric transporter research and its commitment to advancing state\-of\-the\-art tools and new approach methodologies to fill critical gaps in our understanding of nutrient and xenobiotic exposure during early human development\.

## [Cowls, Josh ; Tsamados, Andreas ; Taddeo, Mariarosaria &amp; Floridi, Luciano: The AI gambit: leveraging artificial intelligence to combat climate change—opportunities, challenges, and recommendations](../publications/e9548b7f8336b6aa440c.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 38 \(1\):283\-307\. 2023In this article, we analyse the role that artificial intelligence \(AI\) could play, and is playing, to combat global climate change\. We identify two crucial opportunities that AI offers in this domain: it can help improve and expand current understanding of climate change, and it can contribute to combatting the climate crisis effectively\. However, the development of AI also raises two sets of problems when considering climate change: the possible exacerbation of social and ethical challenges already associated with AI, and the contribution to climate change of the greenhouse gases emitted by training data and computation\-intensive AI systems\. We assess the carbon footprint of AI research, and the factors that influence AI’s greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions in this domain\. We find that the carbon footprint of AI research may be significant and highlight the need for more evidence concerning the trade\-off between the GHG emissions generated by AI research and the energy and resource efficiency gains that AI can offer\. In light of our analysis, we argue that leveraging the opportunities offered by AI for global climate change whilst limiting its risks is a gambit which requires responsive, evidence\-based, and effective governance to become a winning strategy\. We conclude by identifying the European Union as being especially well\-placed to play a leading role in this policy response and provide 13 recommendations that are designed to identify and harness the opportunities of AI for combatting climate change, while reducing its impact on the environment\. \(direct link \)

## [Nuevos enfoques para la toma de decisiones en el sector no lucrativo a partir de la educación, la investigación y la era digital](../publications/e954c4278d3191d2c647.md)

Yannidy Solera; Pablo Miguel Arrieta Montes

Las organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro \(OSAL\) desempeñan un rol social fundamental donde las demandas comunitarias superan la capacidad estatal\. Sin embargo, su toma de decisiones enfrenta restricciones críticas: escasez financiera, multiplicidad de actores e imperativo de demostrar valor social sostenible\. Este artículo analiza cómo la articulación entre educación, investigación, Revolución Industrial 4\.0 y tecnologías de la información y la comunicación \(TIC\) fortalece la capacidad decisional en las OSAL\. Se sostiene que la transformación digital solo genera impacto perdurable si se integra con competencias humanas, evidencia empírica, gobernanza de datos y aprendizaje organizacional continuo\. Metodológicamente, se propone un modelo de innovación decisional de cinco etapas iterativas: definición participativa del problema, formulación de preguntas e indicadores, desarrollo de capacidades educativas, selección estratégica de tecnologías 4\.0 e implementación con evaluación sistemática\. Los hallazgos revelan que la educación constituye la infraestructura humana indispensable para desarrollar pensamiento crítico e interpretar datos complejos, previniendo sesgos tecnológicos\. Asimismo, la investigación rigurosa disipa la niebla informativa provocada por la fragmentación de fondos, mientras que las tecnologías 4\.0 \(inteligencia artificial, analítica de datos y computación en la nube\) optimizan la asignación presupuestal, la gestión de donantes y la identificación de beneficiarios\. Sin embargo, la adopción tecnológica debe ser selectiva y respetuosa de la privacidad y participación comunitaria\. Se concluye que la innovación en la toma de decisiones no consiste en la mera adopción de software, sino en una capacidad colectiva para transformar información confiable en acciones sociales legítimas, incluyentes, equitativas y sostenibles\.

## [AI Data Centers and Climate Change: Developing a Field Guide for Library and Archival Workers](../publications/e95e4950a3c3306cd355.md)

Lisa Spiro; Sarah K\. Tribelhorn; Justin Wadland

The DLF Climate Justice Working Group seeks feedback on a work\-in\-progress “field guide” for the digital library community to the climate implications of hyperscale data centers to advance artificial intelligence\. We will share what we’ve learned and discuss with participants how these impacts are showing up in our work\.

## [qGAMMA: A Framework for Optimal DNN Mapping on Multi\-Precision Accelerators](../publications/e962ba30073e7969358a.md)

Leandro Fiorin; Luigi Altamura; Cristina Silvano

This work describes qGAMMA, a flexible framework for exploring and optimizing the mapping of mixed\-precision Deep Neural Network \(DNN\) models onto general\-purpose spatial accelerators that support a range of fixed\- and floating\-point precisions\. qGAMMA navigates the design space using a domain\-specific genetic algorithm and an analytical performance model based on hardware synthesis results\. The framework identifies the optimal mapping and accelerator configuration that minimizes target metrics\. Extensive evaluations across DNN workloads show that qGAMMA offers valuable insights for designing mixed\-precision applications, enabling better trade\-offs between performance, energy efficiency, and resource utilization\.

## [TikTok vs\. Instagram](../publications/e9651cce1dddadd5dcbb.md)

Cristiana Alexandra dos Santos Cruz; Arnaldo Coelho

This study examines how social media, specifically TikTok and Instagram, influences digital engagement and purchase decision\-making among Generation Z and Millennials in Portugal\. Its central objective is to understand how these platforms shape cognitive and emotional responses and, in turn, modify consumption patterns and decision\-making dynamics\. The study adopted a qualitative design with ethnographic elements\. Fifteen semi\-structured interviews were conducted with Portuguese participants aged 22 to 35, and the data were analysed using IRaMuTeQ \(R Interface for Multidimensional Analysis of Texts and Questionnaires\), allowing a multidimensional exploration of participants’ perceptions, meanings, and behavioural tendencies\. The findings show that TikTok is perceived as a dynamic, spontaneous, and highly stimulating environment that drives more impulsive purchase intentions through algorithmic personalisation and short\-form, emotionally engaging content\. In contrast, Instagram is viewed as a socially curated and aesthetically oriented space that supports more intentional, reflective, and rational decision\-making processes\. While the study’s limited sample and geographic concentration \(Coimbra and Porto\) restrict the generalisability of results, the ethnographic approach provides rich and contextualised insights into the nuanced ways social media platforms shape young adults’ consumer behaviour\. By offering a comparative analysis of TikTok and Instagram, this research advances the emerging discussion on digital and influencer marketing and highlights how platform\-specific characteristics interact with engagement, emotional responses, and purchase\-related decisions in contemporary social media environments\.

## [Predictors of Abstract to Publication Conversion at the 2023 BAD meeting](../publications/e9704854cb9dfe5faf36.md)

Gabriela Franco Katz; Karim Awad; Angad Parmar; Sherryn Man

Introduction: Conferences allow early research dissemination, yet many abstracts never reach full publication\. Abstract\-to\-publication conversion rates are often used as a marker of research quality and conference impact\. Objectives: To determine the proportion of abstracts presented at the 2023 British Association of Dermatologists \(BAD\) Annual Meeting subsequently published and to identify factors associated with publication Methods: This retrospective bibliometric study included all research abstracts presented at the 2023 meeting, identified in the British Journal of Dermatology, Volume 188, Supplement 4 \(June 2023\)\. Corresponding publications were identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar\. Data collected included study design, research topic, presentation format, author characteristics, and geographic origin\. Factors associated with publication success were assessed using Poisson regression to estimate relative risks \(RR\) and 95% confidence intervals \(CI\)\. Results: Of 133 abstracts, 63 \(47\.4%\) were subsequently published\. Measured from the abstract submission deadline \(9 January 2023\), median time to publication was 12\.8 months, with 47\.6% published within 12 months\. Analytical study designs \(adjusted RR: 1\.72; 95% CI: 1\.02–2\.90\) and cutaneous oncology topics \(adjusted RR: 1\.51; 95% CI: 1\.02–2\.24\) were independently associated with increased publication success\. Conclusions: Approximately half of the abstracts presented at the 2023 BAD Annual Meeting progressed to peer\-reviewed publication\. Analytical study design and research focused on cutaneous oncology were independently associated with higher publication likelihood\. These findings highlight factors associated with successful dissemination of dermatology research\.

## [“Quality by Design \(QbD\)\-Driven Development of Advanced Wound Therapeutics: From Risk\-Based Formulation Design to Clinically Translatable Smart Wound Systems”](../publications/e977813a93bb20b70c33.md)



Chronic wound management represents one of the most significant unmet clinical and economic challenges in contemporary healthcare, with an annual global burden exceeding USD 22 billion and disproportionately poor clinical translation rates for advanced wound therapeutics despite substantial research investment\.Quality by Design \(QbD\), formalised through ICH Q8 \(R2\), Q9, and Q10, offers a rigorous, prospective framework for wound formulation development by systematically linking material attributes and process parameters to patient\-relevant quality outcomes\.This narrative review critically evaluates the application of QbD principles encompassing the Quality Target Product Profile \(QTPP\), Critical Quality Attributes \(CQAs\), Critical Material Attributes \(CMAs\), Critical Process Parameters \(CPPs\), risk assessment methodologies, and Design of Experiments \(DoE\) strategies across the principal advanced wound therapeutic platforms: lipid nanocarriers, polymeric nanoparticles, hydrogels, electrospun scaffolds, biopolymeric films, and stimulus\-responsive smart dressings\.Published evidence demonstrates that DoE\-based Response Surface Methodology \(RSM\) consistently delivers 20\-40% improvements in key CQAs and produces statistically validated design spaces aligned with regulatory expectations\.The review further examines translational barriers including scale\-up variability, in vitro\-in vivo correlation \(IVIVC\) gaps, and regulatory classification challenges, and identifies artificial intelligence\-assisted QbD, digital twin manufacturing, and organ\-on\-chip wound models as high\-priority emerging tools for bridging these gaps\.A structured perspective on pre\-submission requirements and regulatory alignment with ICH Q8\-Q10 is provided for researchers targeting Scopus\-indexed pharmaceutical journals\.

## [An Integrated XAI\-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision\-Making in Autonomous Robots](../publications/e97d78003b4197ed39d1.md)

Elshaimaa Nada; Ahmed Ahmed

Can a robot&\#x27;s ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer\. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people&\#x27;s lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem\. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI \(XAI\) with Reinforcement Learning \(RL\) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub\-rewards \(safety, fairness, and well\-being\), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real\-time Ethical Ledger\. We tested it against Black\-Box RL and two post\-hoc XRL baselines \(LIME and SHAP\) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform\. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline \(p &lt; 0\.01 throughout\)\. In a controlled, IRB\-approved user study \(N=128\), participants rated it higher on trust \(4\.5±0\.4\), understandability \(4\.6±0\.3\), and perceived safety \(4\.4±0\.5\) than the alternatives\. Explanations were also fast: 4\.2±0\.6 ms on average, versus 18\.3±2\.1 ms for SHAP and 12\.7±1\.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real\-time limits\. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices\.

## [“WHERE ETHICS MEETS GREEN INTELLIGENCE”: EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT MEDIATING ETHICAL LEADERSHIP AND AI ADOPTION FOR SUSTAINABLE HOTEL PERFORMANCE](../publications/e980fc0e875b9ca01f52.md)

Waseem Hassan; Syed Intasar Hussain Kazmi; Waqas Baig; Abdul Haye Lucman

This study examines the relationships among ethical leadership, artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption, employee engagement, and sustainable hotel performance, with a particular emphasis on employee engagement&\#x27;s mediating role\. Drawing on social learning theory and social exchange theory, the study investigates how ethical leadership and AI adoption contribute to employee engagement and sustainable performance in the hospitality industry\. The study employed a quantitative, cross\-sectional design and analysed data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\) in SmartPLS 4\. The measurement model was assessed for internal consistency reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, while the structural model was evaluated through path analysis and bootstrapping\. The results indicate that ethical leadership positively and significantly influences employee engagement and sustainable hotel performance\. Similarly, AI adoption has significant positive relationships with employee engagement and sustainable hotel performance\. Employee engagement also positively influences sustainable hotel performance and mediates the relationship between ethical leadership and AI adoption and sustainable hotel performance\. These findings highlight the importance of integrating responsible leadership, intelligent technologies, and employee involvement to enhance sustainability in the hospitality industry\. The study contributes to hospitality management literature by integrating leadership, technological, and employee\-related perspectives within a unified framework\. Practically, the findings emphasise the need for hotel managers to promote ethical leadership, implement AI responsibly, and strengthen employee engagement to support economic viability, environmental responsibility, and long\-term organisational sustainability\.

## [Beyond Automation: A Conceptual Framework for Strategic AI Integration in Business Decision\-Making Processes](../publications/e981b2ac00ea248ce7b2.md)

Lina Tio; Dorris Yadewani; Salamiah Muhd Kulal

Purpose – Purpose – The purpose of this paper is to develop a conceptual framework for strategic artificial intelligence \(AI\) integration in organisational decision making\. It deals with the fragmentation of existing research by differentiating AI\-supported decision intelligence from automation\-centric approaches and offers a systematic model to align AI capabilities with organisational strategy\. Methodology/approach – The study adopts a conceptual research design using integrative review of literature\. The proposed Strategic AI Integration Framework \(SAIF\) is developed by synthesizing Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Resource\-Based View, and Simon’s bounded rationality model\. The framework is developed through a critical literature review on AI, strategic management, decision intelligence and organisational governance\. Relevant literature on AI, strategic management, decision intelligence, and organisational governance is critically reviewed to establish the framework\. Findings – The study proposes the Strategic AI Integration Framework \(SAIF\), comprising four dimensions: Decision Domain Mapping, AI Capability Alignment, Human–AI Complementarity, and Governance and Accountability Architecture\. The framework is operationalised through six research propositions explaining how strategic AI integration enhances decision quality, organisational agility, and sustainable competitive advantage while ensuring effective governance and human oversight\. Originality/value – This study contributes to the AI and strategic management literature by providing a theoretically grounded framework that integrates strategic management, decision\-making, and AI governance into a unified model\. The framework offers a foundation for future empirical research and practical guidance for organisations implementing AI strategically\.

## [Influencing factors and genetic model of low\-resistivity shales: a case study of the Longmaxi Formation, Southern Sichuan Basin, China](../publications/e986eadfa66ca2adf50a.md)

Xin Wang; Zhe Cao; Zongquan HU; Zhenxue Jiang; Ranran Hao; Haocheng Shi; Weiyuan Gao; Dapeng Wang

Low\-resistivity anomalies are widely developed in the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation marine shales of the Sichuan Basin, but their complex conductive mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering accurate reservoir evaluation\. This study investigates the characteristics and formation mechanisms of low\-resistivity shales in southern Sichuan Basin by integrating well logging resistivity, geochemical analysis, X\-ray diffraction \(XRD\), X\-ray photoelectron spectroscopy \(XPS\), transmission electron microscopy \(TEM\), scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\), carbon dioxide and nitrogen adsorption \(CO 2 /N 2 adsorption\), high\-pressure mercury intrusion, and electrical experiments\. The results indicate that the studied shales can be classified into ultra\-low\-resistivity shale \(Zg &lt; 1\), low\-resistivity shale \(1 2\) types, which exhibit distinct differences in pore structure and conductive components\. Low\-resistivity shales are dominated by micropores and mesopores, while decreasing resistivity is accompanied by reduced total pore volume, mainly due to the loss of meso\-to macropores\. Organic matter graphitization is a critical factor controlling low resistivity in highly to overmature shales\. When equivalent vitrinite reflectance \(Ro,eq\) exceeds approximately 2\.9%, enhanced ordering of aromatic carbon structures promotes the development of graphite\-like electron conductive networks, resulting in significant resistivity reduction\. The 2\.9% value is an empirical division for the analyzed samples rather than a universal threshold\. At lower maturity stages, low resistivity is mainly controlled by ionic conduction associated with formation water and surface conductivity of clay minerals, whereas pyrite contributes as an auxiliary conductive phase\. This study establishes a maturity\-dependent model for low\-resistivity shale development and provides new insights into the electrical response mechanisms of complex marine shale reservoirs\.

## [Deconstructing Multi\-Task Active Learning: The Paradox of Gradient Conflict and Orthogonal Decomposition](../publications/e989e8b6d6ebe03a2631.md)

Juho Jung; Seongjae Kang; Jinyoung Han

Existing multi\-task active learning \(MTL\-AL\) methods predominantly rely on linear scalarization of heterogeneous objectives such as uncertainty, diversity, and gradient conflict\. We argue that this entangled formulation is fundamentally limited, as linear combination fails to capture Pareto\-optimal trade\-offs under conflicting objectives\. We propose a shift from combination to deconstruction and introduce a principled framework that rethinks MTL\-AL along three orthogonal dimensions\. First, we identify the Conflict Paradox: although the optimization literature treats gradient conflict as interference to be suppressed, penalizing conflict when ranking candidates is measurably worse than not scoring it at all\. We therefore decouple the two concerns: the acquisition function does not score conflict, and the resulting interference is resolved by gradient surgery during training\. Second, we introduce Orthogonal Decomposition, separating acquisition into Informativeness and Exploration\. This two\-stage process, informativeness filtering followed by coverage maximization, prevents &quot;diversity dilution&quot; by excluding uninformative outliers before enforcing diversity\. Third, we propose Cross\-Task Mutual Information \(CTMI\), a covariance\-based statistic of cross\-task dependency computed from MC\-dropout task entropies\. Extensive experiments on COCO, Cityscapes, and NYUv2, including comparisons against recent MTL\-AL and data\-selection baselines, demonstrate consistent improvements over state\-of\-the\-art methods, highlighting that structural rethinking of acquisition yields larger gains than incremental heuristic design\. Code is available at https://github\.com/Juho\-Jung/multitask\_active\_learning\_official\.

## [Engineering uORFs in wheat improves abiotic stress tolerance without growth penalties](../publications/e98d4d2c1e9b7c558815.md)

Xiaomin Si; Yonghui Yan; Shenglong Bai; Guanghui Guo; Panpan Xiao; Mengxiao Hu; Kai Xia; Yongqi Ren; Jintao Jiang; Rong Fan; Xiang Ji; Yue Wang; Hao Li; Tingting Dang; Qinmin Gao; Luyu Liu; Changbin Xiong; Kangpeng Liu; Yun Zhou; Chun‐Peng Song

Summary Developing climate‐resilient crops is critical for ensuring global food security, yet agricultural productivity is frequently constrained by the trade‐off between stress tolerance and growth\. This challenge is particularly acute in allohexaploid wheat, a staple crop susceptible to abiotic stresses, underscoring the demand for precise gene regulation\. Here, we established a simple, efficient, and transgene‐free method for regulating gene expression in allohexaploid wheat by disrupting or creating de novo upstream open reading frames \(uORFs\) via genome editing\. Using ribosome profiling, we identified 1199 actively translated uORFs across the wheat genome and developed a dual‐luciferase screening pipeline to pinpoint potent translational repressors of positive regulators of abiotic stress\. CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated disruption of the uORFs in TaCIPK14 and TaGGP1 elevated downstream protein accumulation, thereby enhancing drought, cold, and salt tolerance of plants\. Furthermore, base editing was employed to generate de novo uORFs in TaMADS26, effectively downregulating gene expression and improving drought resilience\. Notably, both the transgene‐free uorf TaGGP1‐ACG and uORF TaMADS26 mutants conferred pronounced yield advantages under drought conditions without incurring growth penalties under well‐watered conditions\. This study provides a predictable and precise way for modulating gene expression, enabling the coordinated improvement of stress resilience and agronomic performance in wheat\.

## [Distribution\-Shift\-Aware Conformal Prediction for Meteorite and Asteroid Reflectance Spectroscopy: Finite\-Sample Class Guarantees from the Laboratory to the Telescope](../publications/e997399b05d8d4aaa403.md)

Ali Amir Khairbek

Abstract Machine\-learning classifiers trained on laboratory reflectance spectra of meteorites are increasingly used to interpret asteroid observations, but they are routinely deployed outside the conditions under which they were validated: telescope targets differ from laboratory powders in grain size, viewing geometry, space weathering, class abundances, and sensor range\. We introduce distribution\-shift\-aware conformal prediction to planetary reflectance spectroscopy, converting any spectral classifier into a set\-valued predictor with finite\-sample coverage guarantees, and we measure exactly how those guarantees behave when the deployment assumptions fail\. From 16,291 RELAB Planetary Data System products, we curate 2,949 meteorite spectra into a leakage\-controlled, provenance\-tracked data set spanning 9 classes and 756 physical specimens\. Same\-specimen controlled experiments show that empirical coverage degrades with physical shift severity: grain\-size mismatch removes up to 22 points of coverage, pulsed\-laser space weathering removes 15 points on identical rocks, viewing geometry up to 40–60° phase leaves coverage intact, and a linear domain\-classifier AUC tracks severity while proving necessary but not sufficient for failure\. Class\-conditional calibration is invariant to arbitrary class\-prior changes and rescues the scientifically critical CI class, which marginal calibration silently abandons\. Likelihood\-ratio\-weighted conformal prediction restores nominal coverage under a pure covariate shift but misfires when the shift carries a label component, yielding a practical combined prescription\. Transferred to 694 MITHNEOS near\-Earth\-asteroid spectra, the calibrated sets remain informative and recover the Itokawa and Vesta\-family ground truths, whereas returned\-sample tests on Ryugu and Bennu expose exactly where representation, not calibration, becomes the binding constraint\.

## [PERSEPSI GURU DALAM PERENCANAAN KURIKULUM BERBASIS CINTA DI KELAS III MI AMANAH HIDAYATULLAH KEEROM](../publications/e99aaadb0e0ff58da07e.md)

Rizki Chandra Anggara Supriyono; Marwan Sileuw; A Ubaidillah

ABSTRACT The implementation of the Love\-Based Curriculum \(LBC\) requires teachers to understand its underlying values and translate them into lesson planning that addresses students’ needs\. This study aims to analyze teachers’ perceptions of LBC planning and describe its characteristics in Grade III at MI Amanah Hidayatullah Keerom\. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with a pedagogical perspective and was conducted from June 10 to 20, 2026\. The informants comprised the principal, the Vice Principal for Curriculum, and the Grade III homeroom teacher\. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed qualitatively, with trustworthiness examined through source and technique triangulation\. The findings indicate that teachers’ perceptions developed through Ministry of Religious Affairs socialization, Teacher Working Group \(KKG\) activities, internal school communication, discussions, and teaching experiences\. Teachers understood LBC as an approach that reinforces compassion, care, empathy, respect, responsibility, and character development rather than replacing the existing curriculum\. This understanding was reflected in efforts to integrate these values into learning objectives, activities, and instructional materials\. LBC planning demonstrated a realistic orientation through adaptation to students’ conditions, a humanistic orientation through attention to academic development and character, and a futuristic orientation through the cultivation of character for future life\. The study concludes that teachers’ understanding provides a foundation for integrating LBC values into contextualized lesson planning that supports character development\. ABSTRAK Penerapan Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta \(KBC\) menuntut pemahaman guru agar nilai\-nilai kasih sayang dapat diterjemahkan ke dalam perencanaan pembelajaran sesuai dengan kebutuhan peserta didik\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis persepsi guru terhadap perencanaan KBC serta mendeskripsikan karakteristik perencanaannya di kelas III MI Amanah Hidayatullah Keerom\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan pendekatan pedagogis dan dilaksanakan pada 10–20 Juni 2026\. Informan penelitian meliputi kepala madrasah, Wakil Kepala Madrasah Bidang Kurikulum, dan wali kelas III\. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara kualitatif dengan pemeriksaan keabsahan melalui triangulasi sumber dan teknik\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa persepsi guru berkembang melalui sosialisasi Kementerian Agama, kegiatan Kelompok Kerja Guru \(KKG\), komunikasi internal madrasah, diskusi, dan pengalaman mengajar\. Guru memaknai KBC sebagai penguatan nilai kepedulian, empati, penghargaan, tanggung jawab, dan pembentukan karakter, bukan sebagai pengganti kurikulum yang berlaku\. Pemahaman tersebut diwujudkan melalui integrasi nilai cinta dalam tujuan, kegiatan, dan perangkat pembelajaran\. Perencanaan KBC memiliki orientasi realistik melalui penyesuaian dengan kondisi peserta didik, humanistik melalui perhatian terhadap perkembangan akademik dan karakter, serta futuralistik melalui pembentukan karakter untuk kehidupan mendatang\. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa pemahaman guru menjadi landasan dalam mengintegrasikan nilai KBC ke dalam perencanaan pembelajaran yang kontekstual dan berorientasi pada karakter\.

## [A Fuzzy Knowledge\-Inference Framework for AI\-Adoption Risk Assessment in Automotive SMEs](../publications/e99d0042384c894f918e.md)

S\. Davidson; Loveleen Gaur; Shavi Bansal; Varsha Arya; Ramakrishnan Raman

Small and medium\-sized enterprises in the automotive supply base face mounting pressure to adopt artificial intelligence, yet they are least able to absorb the consequences of misscoped adoption\. Assessing this risk means reasoning under vagueness: Data maturity, workforce skill, financial capacity, and above all safety and regulatory readiness are graded, interdependent judgments that crisp, compensatory instruments discard\. This paper proposes the fuzzy knowledge inference framework, a two\-stage rough–fuzzy framework\. Eight automotive\-specific risk factors are represented as linguistic variables over an information system; rough\-set analysis establishes their nonredundancy; and a hierarchical fuzzy inference process—anchored, compliance\-weighted, and noncompensatory—yields an interpretable risk index\. Using no primary human data, it is well calibrated at its anchors, monotone in favorability, and rank\-convergent with two independent instruments, while escalating the profiles a compensatory model would understate\. Its contribution to the literature on AI\-adoption risk assessment for automotive SMEs is the noncompensatory treatment of safety and regulatory readiness\.

## [Unveiling Lithium\-Atom Insertion and Clustering in Superionic Solid\-State Electrolytes via Mechanical Deformation](../publications/e99d96deffa7ba681848.md)

Yu Shi; Yincan Sun; Jiwei Ma; Menghao Yang

Abstract Solid\-state electrolytes \(SSEs\) are pivotal for next\-generation energy systems, offering enhanced safety and higher energy density\. In particular, a fundamental challenge in garnet\-type Li7La3Zr2O12 \(LLZO\) and lithium superionic conductor Li10GeP2S12 \(LGPS\) applications is understanding and controlling the mechanical behavior at interfaces and under operational stresses, which can induce microcracking, void formation, and lithium dendrite growth\. To address this gap, we employ machine learning interatomic potentials \(MLIPs\) with near\-DFT accuracy and perform large\-scale MD simulations to investigate two critical aspects: \(1\) the mechanical deformation of bulk LLZO under uniaxial compression and tension, revealing atomic\-level mechanisms of elastic and plastic deformation, crack initiation, and failure; and \(2\) the kinetics of prescribed Li\-atom insertion at model interfaces, exploring nucleation, clustering, and interface dynamics\. Specifically, we identify two distinct lithium diffusion mechanisms: lithium ions in LGPS migrate via stepwise hopping along one\-dimensional channels; in contrast, LLZO exhibits cooperative crowding \(or “pushing”\) within a three\-dimensional network, where ion migration involves collective displacements and local structural distortions\. These studies provide novel atomistic insights into the mechanical stability of SSEs under stress and the interfacial processes governing Li\-atom insertion and clustering, contributing to the understanding and mitigation of key failure mechanisms in solid\-state batteries\.

## [Democracy and income inequality moderate the impacts of protected areas](../publications/e9addd2cc0fb51f39a16.md)

Eric A\. Coleman; Prakash Kashwan; Mohammad Aynal Haque

Abstract Many policymakers and conservation activists promote creating terrestrial protected areas \(PAs\) as a central tool to preserve biodiversity and offset global carbon emissions\. However, the socioeconomic consequences of PA designation remain understudied\. Using an event study design, this paper estimates the causal treatment effect of creating PAs on changes in cultivated agriculture land from within PA boundaries\. We examine the global population of 64,997 terrestrial protected areas established 1995\-2020 and evaluate temporal changes in land classified as agriculture cultivation in 5\-year intervals\. We find that protected areas \(modestly\) reduce the amount cultivation within their boundaries\. Then, using data on country\-level income inequality and democratic institutions we estimate the treatment effect of creating PAs in countries that are less democratic and have more income inequality\. We find that PAs located in places with more income inequality and less democracy significantly reduce cultivation, at a much greater rate than in countries that score higher on democracy and have less income inequality\. These findings highlight the critical role of socioeconomic and political context in shaping the outcomes of protected area policies\. Conservation policy in nondemocratic and high economic inequality countries must create appropriate safeguards for local people\.

## [Fucoidan attenuates airway remodeling in asthmatic mice](../publications/e9b7dc61fd9ebdcbffe7.md)

Xuejing Wang; Yuli Qi; Yang Hu; Shaohua Zhang; Lixin Hu; Jie Guan; Renzheng Guan

Airway remodeling is a pathological hallmark of asthma that is difficult to reverse and effective therapeutic interventions remain limited\.The present study investigated whether fucoidan, a natural sulfated polysaccharide derived from seaweed, attenuates airway remodeling in ovalbumin \(OVA\)\-induced asthmatic mice\.In total, 40 female Kunming mice were randomly assigned to four groups \(n=10/group\): Asthma, budesonide, fucoidan and control\.Asthma was induced by OVA sensitization and challenge\.Budesonide was administered via nebulization, while fucoidan was given by oral gavage prior to OVA challenge\.Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid was collected for total and differential cell count and levels of interleukin\-21, thymic stromal lymphopoietin, α\-smooth muscle actin and collagen I in the lavage fluid were measured by ELISA\.Lung sections were evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin staining for histopathological changes and immunohistochemistry for protein expression\.Fucoidan significantly alleviated asthma\-like behavior, including scratching, shortness of breath and restlessness, and reduced total cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes and eosinophils in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid compared with the OVA group \(P&lt;0\.05\)\.Fucoidan decreased the elevated levels of interleukin\-21, thymic stromal lymphopoietin, α\-smooth muscle actin and collagen I \(P&lt;0\.05\), with effects comparable with those of budesonide \(P&gt;0\.05\)\.Histological examination revealed that fucoidan attenuated peribronchial inflammatory infiltration, bronchial wall thickening and luminal narrowing\.Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed that fucoidan suppressed the expression of IL\-21, thymic stromal lymphopoietin, α\-smooth muscle actin and collagen I in lung tissue, as reflected by significantly decreased integrated optical density values relative to the model group \(P&lt;0\.05\)\.Collectively, these findings indicated that fucoidan attenuates airway remodeling in asthmatic mice, which may be associated with downregulation of interleukin\-21 and thymic stromal lymphopoietin\.Although the underlying mechanisms and clinical applicability require validation, the present results suggest that fucoidan merits investigation as a potential candidate for asthma therapy\.

## [Upgrading the HIV vaccine paradigm: accounting for host\-pathogen diversity through geotargeting\-based vaccine design](../publications/e9b984b967f497cd241c.md)

Luciano Lunardi; Alexandra de Azevedo da Rocha; Ana Carolina Alves de Oliveira; Iuri Marques de Oliveira; Angelica Cerveira De Baumont; Dinler A\. Antunes; Gustavo Fioravanti Vieira

Introduction Effective HIV vaccine development, with satisfactory levels of response and coverage, remains an elusive goal in immunology\. In this context, considerations of host\-pathogen interactions from a geotargeting perspective could enhance disease control efforts\. Current HIV vaccine strategies increasingly seek to address viral diversity, but the combined effects of regional viral variation and host HLA diversity on antigen processing and presentation remain insufficiently considered\. Here, we evaluated whether integrating these host–pathogen variables could support geographically informed prioritization of HIV vaccine targets\. Methods Using NetMHCpan 4\.1, NetChop 3\.1, and the IEDB antigen\-processing prediction tool, we evaluated antigen\-processing and presentation steps for HIV epitopes associated with viral control\. We recovered Human Leukocyte Antigen \(HLA\) alleles associated with HIV control and their frequencies, and the protein sequences for the most common HIV subtypes in different African countries\. We created maps linking both sets of information for each specific region\. We then predicted the impact of mutations associated with different HIV strain sequences on proteasome processing score, TAP transportation and HLA binding affinity for the alleles in each host population\. Results The generated maps provide a landscape of the impact of genetic diversity on T cell responses for each examined epitope target\. TW10 epitope variants in the main HIV subtypes showed consistent HLA binding, proteasome cleavage and processing rankings across the continent\. Conversely, TI8 variants carrying I8T or I8R substitutions lost predicted HLA\-B\*51:01 binding and showed marked deterioration in the combined processing ranking, from 10th for the reference epitope to positions as low as 97th among the analyzed variants\. Discussion The adoption of uniform immunotherapy strategies based solely on reference HIV epitopes may be an inefficient approach\. Certain epitopes may be suitable vaccine targets for specific locations, when matching a prevalent HIV strain with a host population with high prevalence of HLA alleles that can effectively display the vaccine’s epitopes\. However, HLA matching is not enough if the HIV strains in the region have upstream or downstream mutations that prevent the proper processing and presentation of the targeted viral epitope\. Based on this complex host–pathogen interplay, we propose a geotargeting approach to vaccine design, considering customized targets for specific geographical locations and host populations\. By incorporating regional viral and HLA diversity into target selection, this strategy may increase the likelihood of developing more effective HIV vaccines, although the resulting predictions will require experimental validation\.

## [Study of Cancer Ratio \(Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase/Pleural Fluid Adenosine Deaminase\) in Malignant Pleural Effusion](../publications/e9bc580aad9fbd1f6613.md)

Nikhil Ramachandra; Ivor Peter D’sa; Venkatram Rajesh; Giridhar Belur Hosmane; Harshwardhan Patil

Objectives Malignant pleural effusion \(MPE\) is a frequent cause of exudative pleural effusion and often indicates advanced malignancy with poor prognosis\. Although pleural fluid cytology remains the diagnostic reference standard, its sensitivity is limited\. The cancer ratio, defined as the ratio of serum lactate dehydrogenase \(LDH\) to pleural fluid adenosine deaminase \(ADA\), has been proposed as a simple and inexpensive biomarker to differentiate malignant from non\-malignant pleural effusions\. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the cancer ratio \(serum LDH/pleural fluid ADA\) for predicting MPE in patients with exudative pleural effusion\. Material and Methods This cross\-sectional observational study was conducted from April 2021 to September 2022 at a tertiary care centre in Mangaluru, India\. Fifty\-six adult patients with exudative pleural effusion diagnosed using Light’s criteria were included\. Pleural fluid ADA and serum LDH levels were measured using standard enzymatic assays\. The cancer ratio was calculated as serum LDH divided by pleural fluid ADA\. Pleural fluid cytology served as the diagnostic reference for malignancy\. Receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis was performed to determine diagnostic accuracy, including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve \(AUC\)\. Results The mean age of the study population was 58\.38 ± 11\.84 years, and 62\.5% were male\. Malignancy was detected in 46 patients \(82\.1%\) by pleural fluid cytology, with lung adenocarcinoma being the most common underlying malignancy\. The mean pleural fluid ADA was 11\.35 ± 8\.61 U/L, the mean serum LDH was 582\.70 ± 696\.14 U/L, and the mean cancer ratio was 182\.46 ± 700\.84\. ROC analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0\.526 for the cancer ratio \(cut\-off: 30\.65; sensitivity 71\.7%, specificity 50\.0%\), indicating limited discriminative ability\. Serum LDH showed better diagnostic performance \(AUC 0\.707; sensitivity 67\.4%, specificity 60\.0%\) and was the only parameter significantly associated with MPE \( p = 0\.042\)\. Conclusion In this cohort, the cancer ratio demonstrated limited diagnostic accuracy for predicting MPE and did not show a statistically significant association with malignancy\. Serum LDH showed comparatively better diagnostic performance\. The cancer ratio should therefore be considered an exploratory biomarker, and larger multicentric studies are required to further evaluate its potential role in the diagnostic evaluation of exudative pleural effusion\.

## [Machine\-Learning\-Enabled Design of Lab\-Scale Continuous Distillation Systems for Pharmaceutical Process Development](../publications/e9c4f4d0be2b5db698f0.md)

J\.C\. Turnage; Andres P\. Hyer; Kimberly E\. Penzer; James K\. Ferri

Abstract Predictive tools for continuous distillation design lag behind upstream pharmaceutical synthesis─including AI\-enabled digital tooling for retrosynthetic route design─leaving column specification dependent on computationally expensive simulation or extensive experimentation\. This work presents a machine\-learning surrogate framework trained entirely on first\-principles mechanistic simulations, requiring no experimental distillation data, and eliminating the need for commercial tools such as ChemCad or AspenPlus\. Three surrogate models for binary tert\-butylamine/alcohol systems \(methanol, ethanol, isopropanol\) predict distillate and bottoms compositions with mean absolute errors below 0\.005 mol/mol and R2 &gt; 0\.999, completing a single prediction in under 1 ms─a 24\-fold speedup\. A coupled Pareto optimizer returns capital\-versus\-operating\-cost trade\-off curves in under 10 s, with over 93% of designs verified within ±0\.010 mol/mol\. Applied to a pharmaceutical case study, the framework correctly identifies isopropanol as the optimal solvent without prior thermodynamic knowledge\. The system\-agnostic architecture could readily integrate with open\-source large language model platforms to further lower the barrier to implementation\.

## [Active\-flow systems enhance respirator fit success in children: a comparative study with standard disposable models](../publications/e9d08b3d1a15c2ca8a58.md)

Sittiporn Ruengdit; Kampanat Wangsan; Wuttipat Kiratipaisarl; Krongporn Ongprasert

Introduction Children face disproportionate air pollution health risks due to their physiology and behavior\. Respirator efficacy data in children remain limited\. This study compared standard respirators with a modified active\-flow system providing positive pressure\. Methods Quantitative fit testing was performed on 82 children aged 5–10 years in Chiang Mai, Thailand, using the TSI Portacount Pro Plus 8,038\. Success was defined by an overall mean fit factor of 100 or greater\. The evaluation compared a horizontal triple\-fold KN95\-equivalent respirator with an active\-flow model by connecting the mask to a system that provides a continuous supply of purified air from a portable HEPA\-filtered unit delivering 66\.5 liters per minute\. Eight facial dimensions were measured via 2D photogrammetry to identify anthropometric correlations with performance\. Fit testing incorporated four standardized exercises, namely bending, talking, side\-to\-side head turning, and up\-and\-down head movement, following a modified OSHA quantitative fit\-testing protocol\. Results Standard filtering facepiece respirators \(FFRs\) achieved a pass rate of only 3\.7%\. The active\-flow system significantly increased the pass rate to 23\.2%, with an odds ratio of 17\.0, and increased the overall median fit factor from 9\.5 to 39\.5\. Fit success was positively associated with bizygomatic breadth \(aOR 1\.31\) and menton\-sellion length \(aOR 1\.11\), whereas a wider interpupillary distance was associated with lower odds of passing \(aOR 0\.67\)\. Among the tested exercises, up\-and\-down head movements resulted in the lowest fit improvements\. The participants reported significantly easier breathing under the active\-flow condition \(86\.6%\) than under the standard respirator \(37\.8%\), although inconvenience was reported more frequently with the active\-flow model \(76\.8%\) than with the standard model \(35\.4%\)\. Conclusion These findings suggest that FFRs commonly available in consumer markets may offer only limited protection for children against environmental pollutants\. Active\-flow systems appeared to improve both efficacy and respiratory comfort, though overall protection levels observed in this evaluation remained below thresholds generally considered protective\. Given the scope of this evaluation, further research is needed to confirm these findings across broader conditions and populations, with particular attention to improving nasal seal integrity and developing portable, comfortable\-to\-use units with adjustable flow rates suited to real\-world activity levels\.

## [Operations of Mind: A framework for emergent thinking](../publications/e9dd48aa076fc39abe03.md)

Sebastian Vaderaa

Thinking is not hardcoded, and it cannot be\. This note sets out Operations of Mind \(OoM\), a framework inwhich a machine is not given a method of thinking but a small set of basic mental operations, a drive tomake sense of what it encounters, and the freedom to chain those operations itself\. OoM divides thoughtinto two deliberate layers: an inner layer that runs continuously and cheaply, and an active layer thatreasons deliberately on harder problems\. It sits on two earlier pieces of the LOCUS programme, theCoherent World Hypothesis \(CWH\), which serves as its imagination, and the Repertoire Hypothesis, whichserves as its memory\. The central bet is that thinking does not have to be trained into a machine; it canemerge from a small set of basic mental operations, chained under a drive to make sense\. First tests ingenerated worlds give early support: operation chains grown from use beat chains built blindly, the driveignores noise without being told to, and see\-then\-invent beat a plain counting baseline for the first time,with a control showing the gain tracks real hidden structure\. The gains are small, about 1\.5 points ofroughly 5 learnable in a 60\-step budget, and the active layer is untested\. This note is a framework withpreliminary evidence, not a validated result\.

## [Bir Devrimin Eşiğinde](../publications/e9e05ea14b0b3b296a75.md)

Demir Küçükaydın

Dizi, yapay zekâ ve robotların üretimin her alanına girişiyle şekillenen dünya ölçüsündeki devrimi ele alıyor ve bu devrimi anlamak için insanın ve toplumun ne olduğu sorusuna, insan oluş sürecinde emeğin, ateşin ve aletlerin yerine, Engels’in ve Kıvılcımlı’nın yanılgılarına, zorunluluklar ve özgürlükler âlemi kavramlarına uzanıyor\.
