## [InterviewAI: An Intelligent Virtual Interview Platform with Real\-Time Voice, Video, and AI\-Based Performance Evaluation](../publications/e9e2965e003fce68d529.md)

Manoj Singh Ananya Rapolu

This paper presents InterviewAI, a Software\-as\-a\-Service \(SaaS\) platform that conducts live mock interviews using artificial intelligence\. Candidates often lack access to affordable and realistic interview practice, and existing systems either rely on static question banks or cover only parts of the interview experience\. In InterviewAI, a user signs in with Google Authentication and uploads a resume in PDF format\. The system extracts skills, education and experience, generates personalised questions, conducts the interview through real\-time voice and video conversation with an AI interviewer, and produces a performance report covering strengths, weaknesses, communication skills and suggestions for improvement\. A credit\-based usage model with Razorpay payment integration makes the platform suitable for production use\. The system is built on React\.js, Node\.js, Express\.js and MongoDB, with Firebase authentication, Razorpay payments and OpenRouter for AI model access, and is deployed on Render\. The platform was tried end to end with a few users to check its working, and all core modules, from sign\-in to feedback report and payment, worked as intended\.

## [Qualidade de vida de pessoas com Diabetes Tipo 1: sistema de infusão contínua de insulina versus múltiplas injeções diárias](../publications/e9ea7736c3e2ce6b01a3.md)

Melissa Zoia Fernandes da Costa; Ricardo José Gomes

Objetivo: Comparar a qualidade de vida de adultos com DM1 usuários de SIC e MID e analisar aspectos sociodemográficos, controle glicêmico autorrelatado e percepção acerca do método terapêutico\. Métodos: Foram incluídos 308 participantes com DM1, com idade entre 18 e 59 anos, que preencheram um formulário on\-line com questões referentes à condição sociodemográfica e avaliação da qualidade de vida \(WHOQOL\-Bref\)\. A comparação entre as proporções foi avaliada pelo teste Qui\-Quadrado \(χ²\) e teste exato de Fisher e, entre os grupos, pelo teste t de Student ou U de Mann\-Whitney \(p&lt;0,05\)\. Resultados: Do total, 54,2% dos participantes utilizam MID e 45,8% utilizam SIC, com idade média de 31±9,1 anos\. Os participantes do grupo SIC possuem maior renda\. Quanto à frequência autorrelatada de hiperglicemia e hipoglicemia houve resultados semelhantes nos dois grupos\. O grupo SIC apresentou maior autoavaliação da qualidade de vida, sem diferenças significativas nos demais domínios do WHOQOL\-Bref\. A maior parte dos usuários do grupo MID manifestou intenção de trocar de método, ao contrário do grupo SIC\. Conclusão: Os usuários de SIC apresentaram maior pontuação na autoavaliação da qualidade de vida em comparação ao grupo MID, embora não tenham sido observadas diferenças significativas entre os grupos nos demais domínios do WHOQOL\-Bref\.

## [Weaving a collective future: Insights from Hawaiʻi and Aotearoa on decolonising and indigenising mainstream teacher education](../publications/e9ff56992ff5d0795b69.md)

Jessica Worchel

The Indigenous education movements in Hawaiʻi and Aotearoa New Zealand \(Aotearoa\) have demonstrated decades of advancement and success, yet we are still confronted with a predominantly Western\-centric teaching and learning context that resists recognising Indigenous education as an essential foundation for all educators \(Hutchings &amp; Lee\-Morgan, 2016; Wilson\-Hokowhitu &amp; Goodyear\-Ka‘ōpua, 2019\)\. This article draws from a larger PhD research study, Decolonizing the colonizer: Indigenous education as the foundation of teacher education in Hawaiʻi and Aotearoa, offering specific guidance to transform mainstream teacher education\. The research grounds in Hawaiʻi and Aotearoa as their Indigenous peoples have shared colonial experiences and their Indigenous resurgence movements have evolved together and strengthened one another \(Asensio, 2019; Walker, 2004; Wilson &amp; Kamanā, 2001\)\. They hold a strong connection stemming not only from their geographic proximity but also shared histories reflected in their cosmogony, ancestors, language, and cultural practices\. These connections ignited an Indigenous education movement that has grown and evolved over the past 50 years, leading to the revitalisation of Hawaiian and Māori languages and cultural practices, and the creation of a robust Indigenous education pipeline\. The study applies oral storytelling and semi\-structured interview methods to gather moʻolelo/pūrākau \(stories, narratives, history\), ʻike/mātauranga \(knowledge, wisdom\), and manaʻo/whakaaro \(thoughts, opinions, ideas\) from 20 Hawaiian and Māori Indigenous education leaders who have dedicated their personal and professional lives to their respective Cultural Renaissances\. The leaders offered guidance for mainstream teacher education on how to ground in Indigenous knowledge systems and practices\. Through the study, the metaphor of a three\-whiri wahakura \(flax bassinet with three foundational braids\) emerged, depicting that for transformative and restorative shifts in teacher education to occur, there must be change at the system, programmatic, and individual level\. This article will focus on the programmatic level by proposing a framework for decolonising and indigenising teacher education based on eight themes detailing how Indigenous Pacific epistemologies, pedagogies, and philosophies can be employed in university teaching and learning practices\.

## [भरतय रजनत म कतरम बदधमतत: चनतय और अवसर](../publications/ea03e35665c7db73aef9.md)

डॉ\. दीवान सिंह बारिया

सारांश इक्कीसवीं सदी में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence—AI\) ने मानव जीवन के लगभग प्रत्येक क्षेत्र को प्रभावित किया है। राजनीति और शासन भी इससे अछूते नहीं हैं। भारत जैसे विशाल लोकतांत्रिक देश में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का उपयोग चुनावी प्रबंधन, जनमत विश्लेषण, डिजिटल प्रचार, सरकारी सेवाओं, नीति\-निर्माण, नागरिक सहभागिता तथा प्रशासनिक निर्णय\-प्रक्रियाओं में बढ़ती संभावनाओं के साथ सामने आया है। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के माध्यम से बड़े पैमाने पर उपलब्ध डेटा का विश्लेषण करके राजनीतिक दल नागरिकों की प्राथमिकताओं और जनसमस्याओं को समझ सकते हैं, जबकि सरकारें सार्वजनिक सेवाओं के वितरण और प्रशासनिक प्रक्रियाओं को अधिक प्रभावी बनाने में इसका उपयोग कर सकती हैं। हालाँकि, राजनीति में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के उपयोग के साथ अनेक चुनौतियाँ भी जुड़ी हुई हैं। फर्जी समाचार, डीपफेक, राजनीतिक दुष्प्रचार, मतदाताओं की गोपनीयता का उल्लंघन, एल्गोरिदमिक पक्षपात, साइबर सुरक्षा संबंधी जोखिम, डिजिटल असमानता तथा राजनीतिक ध्रुवीकरण लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था के समक्ष गंभीर प्रश्न प्रस्तुत करते हैं। इन चुनौतियों के कारण नागरिकों की सूचित निर्णय लेने की क्षमता, सार्वजनिक विमर्श की विश्वसनीयता और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं के प्रति विश्वास प्रभावित हो सकता है। अतः भारत में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का उपयोग लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों, पारदर्शिता, जवाबदेही और नागरिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप किया जाना आवश्यक है। प्रस्तुत शोध\-पत्र का उद्देश्य भारतीय राजनीति में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता से उत्पन्न प्रमुख अवसरों और चुनौतियों का विश्लेषण करना तथा इसके उत्तरदायी एवं नैतिक उपयोग के लिए आवश्यक उपायों पर प्रकाश डालना है। अध्ययन इस बात को रेखांकित करता है कि कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता राजनीतिक प्रक्रियाओं में सूचना\-विश्लेषण, प्रशासनिक दक्षता और नागरिक सहभागिता को बढ़ावा देने में सहायक हो सकती है, किंतु इसके प्रभावी उपयोग के लिए मानवीय निगरानी, तथ्य\-जाँच, डेटा संरक्षण, डिजिटल साक्षरता और उचित नियामक व्यवस्था आवश्यक हैं। इस प्रकार, लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों की रक्षा करते हुए कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का संतुलित एवं उत्तरदायी उपयोग भारतीय राजनीति के समक्ष एक महत्त्वपूर्ण अवसर और दायित्व दोनों प्रस्तुत करता है।

## [AI\-driven “new migrants”: skill\-spatial mismatch and out\-migration intention](../publications/ea04aa4763e1c36d1707.md)

Di Wang; Boran Zhang; Junlong Chen

While AI profoundly reshapes the labor market, its spatial impact remains under\-researched\. Addressing this, this paper uses data from the China Migrant Population Dynamic Monitoring Survey and the China Patent Database across 250 prefecture\-level cities during 2014–2018 to examine AI&\#x27;s effect on labor out\-migration intention\. Findings reveal AI significantly increases out\-migration intention, especially among women and in non\-digital hubs or central/western regions\. Mechanistically, the results are consistent with a displacement channel involving routine jobs and a restructuring channel involving industrial shifts\. These channels can be understood through a “skill\-spatial mismatch” resulting from the changing spatial distribution of tasks\. Furthermore, regional aging and fiscal support amplify the positive relationship between AI and out\-migration intention\. The study concludes by emphasizing the need for a spatially inclusive employment policy framework as AI reshapes employment geography\. The findings concern workers&\#x27; stated propensity to leave, which may precede future mobility, rather than observed migration flows\.

## [\(Un\)aware of change? Objective and subjective reactivity to the sensor‐based measurement of physical activity and sedentary behaviour](../publications/ea142af199a40b860e21.md)

Alea Ruf; Judith Gruber; Ulrich Ebner‐Priemer; Andreas Reif; Laura Maria König; Silke Matura

OBJECTIVES: Despite being the gold standard for assessing physical activity \(PA\) under free\-living conditions, accelerometer\-based assessments are prone to measurement reactivity, that is, changes in people&\#x27;s cognitions, emotions or behaviour due to being measured\. Little is known about whether participants are aware of these changes\. This preregistered secondary analysis assesses objective and subjective reactivity to the sensor\-based measurement of PA \(steps, light PA \[LPA\], moderate\-to\-vigorous PA \[MVPA\]\) and sedentary behaviour \(SB\) in adults with and without attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\), depression and insulin resistance\. DESIGN: Intensive longitudinal design\. METHODS: = 5\.85\) who wore an accelerometer for 7 days and self\-reported whether they changed their PA due to the activity tracker \(i\.e\. subjective measurement reactivity\)\. Objective measurement reactivity was defined as decreases in PA and increases in SB\. RESULTS: Multilevel models found small, but significant decreases of PA over the study period and from the first study day\(s\) to the remaining study days\. Yet, over 90% of participants indicated to have \(rather\) not changed their PA\. SB did not systematically change\. Subjective measurement reactivity and clinical diagnoses were not related to measurement reactivity\. CONCLUSIONS: Steps, LPA and MVPA, but not SB, systematically changed in line with common definitions of measurement reactivity\. Yet, most participants were unaware of these changes, potentially because changes were small\. Measurement reactivity may be predominantly driven by unconscious mechanisms and appears universal, with no differences found by diagnoses\.

## [USER VERIFICATION THROUGH CALLIGRAPHIC NOISE ANALYSIS IN HANDWRITTEN SIGNATURES](../publications/ea23e06be45ad7680ca1.md)

André Luis Borsato Sanchez; Rodrigo Capobianco Guido

Biometric user verification assesses whether an observed behavioral sample is consistent with a claimed identity\. Acoustic signals generated during handwritten signatures may convey information about the interaction among the pen, paper, and supporting surface\. This study examines a calligraphic\-noise verification architecture using 260 recordings from ten participants, evenly divided between development and external evaluation\. Signal representation combines the temporal descriptors A3 and B3, based on normalized positions of cumulative energy and zero crossings, yielding 38 features\. Two processing chains, with and without the discrete wavelet transform, and three decision strategies were investigated: a radial\-basis\-function support vector machine, a random forest, and weighted score fusion with weights of 0\.75 and 0\.25\. Decision thresholds were calibrated under a policy designed to limit false acceptances\. In the external evaluation of the chain without wavelet processing, score fusion accepted 92 genuine and eight impostor attempts, producing false rejection and false acceptance rates of 29\.23% and 0\.68%, respectively\. The random forest produced only four false acceptances but rejected 56 genuine attempts\. The findings support the experimental applicability of the architecture within the investigated acquisition setting, but do not establish across\-session generalization or isolate the contributions of individual descriptors

## [Summarization of Legal Documents using Large Language Models with Fine\-tuning](../publications/ea28a5572d9243224ca7.md)

Luciana Belén Canteros; Federuci Smulever; Francisco Vargas; Sonia Itatí Mariño; Manuel Pulido

La confección de resúmenes a partir de documentos extensos del ámbito legal son de importancia para optimizar la tarea de los profesionales del dominio, como también para contribuir a una extracción de mayor calidad y precisión en sistemas RAG\. En este trabajo se propone una metodología basada en un entrenamiento de ajuste fino \(fine\-tuning\) de los modelos de lenguaje de código abierto, Llama y Qwen, combinada con diversas técnicas de prompting\. El entrenamiento y la evaluación son aplicados en un corpus de más de catorce mil sentencias de la jurisprudencia argentina\. El objetivo es obtener modelos especializados en resúmenes abstractivos, mientras se prioriza mantener una generación donde la longitud de tokens este controlada\. Los resultados obtenidos evidencian que los modelos que han pasado por un proceso de fine\-tuning junto con el uso de diferentes técnicas de ingeniería de prompts logran capturar de manera más efectiva el contenido relevante de los documentos, manteniendo coherencia semántica y superando a modelos base mientras se respetan restricciones de longitud establecidas\. En particular, el modelo Llama 3\.1 Instruct \(8B\) alcanza mejoras relativas de ROUGE L del 63\.91% respecto a su versión base y mejoras relativas del 12\.66% para BERTScore F1\. La técnica desarrollada será utilizada para la generación de bases de datos legales en la cual los resúmenes son parte de la metadata como también para su integración en un sistema RAG\.

## [ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment](../publications/ea2d3c294584b2073c2c.md)

Florian Mai; David Kaczér

Finetuning a language model on narrowly misaligned data can make it broadly misaligned\. Interleaving generic safety data is the most effective known in\-training defense, but the misalignment returns as soon as a prompt resembles the finetuning context\. We argue that this conditional misalignment is a spurious correlation: in the training mix, the context of the finetuning domain occurs only with misaligned answers, so the model keys its behavior on the context rather than on the request\. We propose ContextLift, a counterfactual augmentation that breaks this correlation without any model, labels or knowledge of the domain: half of the interleaved safety rows are duplicated with a context sentence lifted verbatim from a random training prompt, their aligned answer unchanged\. On Qwen2\.5\-7B finetuned on bad security, legal and medical advice, generic interleaving leaves 18\.9%, 41\.9% and 58\.2% misaligned answers under a domain cue; ContextLift reduces this to 2\.6%, 6\.1% and 12\.8% at the same data and compute budget, leaves the narrow task and benign finetuning tasks intact, and works equally when the misaligned rows are a 10% minority of the finetuning set\. Code: https://github\.com/davidkaczer/contextlift

## [Artificial Intelligence\-Enabled Biomarker Discovery in Clinical Biochemistry: Emerging Biomarkers, Machine Learning and Barriers to Clinical Translation](../publications/ea3312f149b2dbce4eb7.md)

Dr\. K\. Narendra Kumar Reddy; K\. Ravi; Pedavegi\. Mounika; Guntaka\. Charita Sree

Clinical biochemistry now produces large, multidimensional datasets from automated analysers, laboratory information systems, mass spectrometry and molecular assays\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\), and machine learning \(ML\) in particular, offers tools to combine such measurements into multivariable patterns, to monitor laboratory quality and to prioritise candidate biomarkers\. This review examines how AI is used across the pre\-analytical, analytical and post\-analytical phases of laboratory work and how it is being applied to four groups of emerging biomarkers: pentraxin\-3, extracellular vesicle cargo, circulating microRNAs and adipokines\. It describes the main learning approaches, the discovery pipeline, the failure modes that most often inflate reported accuracy \(overfitting, data leakage, batch effects and confounding\) and a staged validation pathway running from analytical validation to post\-deployment monitoring\. The literature indicates that AI is most defensible where it supports established laboratory processes and combines established tests with emerging markers\. High discrimination in a development cohort does not establish biological validity or clinical usefulness\. Standardised measurement, leakage\-free modelling, calibration, external and prospective validation, transparent reporting and human oversight are the conditions under which AI\-assisted biomarker research can move into routine practice, including in resource\-variable settings such as India\.

## [HUMAN\-AI COLLABORATIVE DEBATE IN EFL CLASSROOMS: RE\-EXAMINING ARGUMENTATIVE SPEAKING COMPETENCE, ACADEMIC INTEGRITY, AND PEDAGOGICAL AGENCY THROUGH COPILOT AND CHATGPT](../publications/ea36a232f3b9b114e30d.md)

Ranta Butarbutar; Rubén González Vallejo; Mohammed Boukezzoula

Argumentative speaking competence in English as a foreign language is multidimensional and includes linguistic accuracy, rhetorical logic, interactive response, and affective regulation\. However, its development remains challenging, particularly in terms of argument coherence, anxiety management, and academic integrity in the era of learning\-based AI\. This study employs a mixed\-method sequential explanatory design with one group pre\-test and post\-test over eight weeks, involving ChatGPT and Copilot as debate partners and reflections through Google Classroom\. Quantitative analysis showed significant improvement in ASC \(d= 2\.86\), academic integrity \(d=2\.04\), and pedagogical agency \(d= 2\.37\)\. Meanwhile, qualitative data confirm that students perceive AI as idea facilitators that help to find out contra\-argument and increase self\-confidence, but still remain critical to keep integrity\. These findings strengthen cross\-culture communicative competence and AI as a cognitive partnership and are consistent with the UNESCO and OECD principles of AI ethics\. Practically, this suggests that educators should utilize AI as a sparring partner in the reflective pedagogy framework, students should use AI as an idea’s facilitator, not a final answer or argument, and decision makers and EFL curriculum and material developers should organize particular modules about AI\-ethical communicative competence so that integrating technology still aligns with academic values\.

## [The Effects of Digital Technology Adoption, Total Quality Management Practices, and Organisational Performance in the Sri Lankan Telecommunication Industry: The Mediating Role of Customer Satisfaction](../publications/ea3b4c8714b982022d94.md)

M\. J\. P\. Kulatunge; R\. Lalitha S\. Fernando; I\. Mahakalanda

This study investigates the critical issue of high customer complaint rates in the Sri Lankan telecommunications sector\. It examines the relationships between Digital Technologies \(DT\) adoption, Total Quality Management \(TQM\) practices, and organisational performance with customer satisfaction as a mediating variable in the Sri Lankan telecom sector\. It aims to bridge existing research gaps by examining this relationship\. Using an explanatory, quantitative research design with a deductive approach, primary data were collected via a structured questionnaire from 248 telecommunications engineers, a key stakeholder group responsible for service quality and technology implementation\. The data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling \(SEM\) to test the direct effects of Digital Technology and TQM practices on organisational performance, with customer satisfaction as a mediator\. The results indicate that both Digital Technology adoption and TQM practices have significant positive relationships with organisational performance\. Furthermore, customer satisfaction was identified as a significant mediator in these relationships, underscoring its pivotal role\. These findings align with established theoretical and empirical research\. This study contributes empirical evidence on the separate relationships of DT adoption and TQM practices with organisational performance and the mediating role of customer satisfaction in the Sri Lankan telecom settings\. It provides managers and policymakers with valuable insights, demonstrating that telecom companies can enhance performance by leveraging digital tools alongside quality management practices\. The findings highlight customer satisfaction as an important mechanism through which DT adoption and TQM practices are associated with organisational performance\.

## [Dijital Video Platformlarının Bulanık Ortamda Değerlendirilmesi: Pisagor Bulanık AHP ve TOPSIS Uygulaması](../publications/ea3c825be657a464f27f.md)

Amaç: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de faaliyet gösteren dijital video platformlarını \(Netflix, Prime Video, Disney\+, EXXEN, TV\+, BluTV ve GAİN\) belirsizlik ve öznel yargılar içeren çok kriterli karar verme ortamında değerlendirmeyi amaçlamaktadır\.Yöntem: Çalışmada, kriter ağırlıklarını belirlemek için Pisagor Bulanık AHP, alternatifleri sıralamak için Pisagor Bulanık TOPSIS yöntemleri bütünleşik olarak kullanılmıştır\. Sıralamanın kararlılığı 105 senaryo üzerinden gerçekleştirilen duyarlılık analiziyle incelenmiştir\.Bulgular: Pisagor Bulanık AHP sonuçlarında en önemli ana kriter İçerik \(%55,40\), alt kriterler ise İçerik Çeşitliliği \(%32,04\), Fiyat/Abonelik Ücreti \(%19,65\) ve Orijinal İçerik \(%15,46\) olmuştur\. Pisagor Bulanık TOPSIS sıralamasında Netflix ilk sırada yer almış, platformlar Netflix, BluTV, GAİN, Disney\+, TV\+, EXXEN ve Prime Video şeklinde sıralanmıştır\. Duyarlılık analizi, kriter ağırlıklarındaki değişimlerin sıralamayı etkilediğini göstermiştir\.Özgünlük: Çalışma, Pisagor Bulanık AHP ve TOPSIS yöntemlerini bütünleştirerek dijital video platformlarının değerlendirilmesine yönelik, belirsizlikleri dikkate alan sistematik bir karar destek modeli sunmaktadır\.

## [Por qué la ciencia se estanca y cómo avanzar a cosas nuevas](../publications/ea40147e6f5217a026f3.md)

Yosmel Silva Llanes

Este documento analiza el estancamiento estructural de la ciencia moderna y explica por qué muchas disciplinas continúan expandiendo métodos antiguos en lugar de reemplazarlos por marcos nuevos\. Se examina cómo la acumulación de capas, parámetros, axiomas y sensores genera volumen pero no innovación, afectando áreas como inteligencia artificial, física, matemáticas y robótica\. El texto muestra que los grandes avances históricos surgieron cuando se rompieron las reglas existentes y se creó una base completamente nueva\. Se detallan los beneficios de abandonar el ciclo que se engrosa: descubrimientos imposibles bajo el marco tradicional, soluciones más simples y poderosas, estructuras ocultas reveladas, tecnologías funcionales, ruptura de límites artificiales y aceleración del progreso científico\. El documento concluye que la ciencia debe dejar de reforzar lo viejo y atreverse a explorar lo nuevo para abrir caminos que la estructura tradicional no puede recorrer\.

## [Agreement and longitudinal repeatability of established brain volumetry pipelines across healthy controls, multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease](../publications/ea50d3bfb5a7224f4415.md)

Nedim Šišić; Muhamed Baraković; Manon Edde; Antoine Théberge; Ann‐Marie Beaudoin; Moussa Dumbia; Emmanuelle Lapointe; Maxime Descoteaux; Stefano Magon; Susanna Gobbi

Introduction Brain volume estimates are increasingly used as longitudinal endpoints in neuroimaging studies and clinical trials, but outputs from different segmentation pipelines may not be interchangeable\. In this study, we performed a version\-specific comparison of six established brain segmentation pipelines across healthy controls \(HC; n = 20\), people with multiple sclerosis \(MS; n = 19\), and people with Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD; n = 50\)\. Methods FreeSurfer v6, FreeSurfer v7\.2, SAMSEG, FastSurfer v1, SIENAX/SIENA\-XL, and CAT12 were evaluated\. The primary aims were to quantify systematic offsets and inter\-pipeline agreement in normalized baseline volume estimates, assess within\-pipeline repeatability and longitudinal change\-from\-baseline concordance, and determine whether longitudinal processing reduced variability relative to cross\-sectional processing\. Gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and thalamus were selected and normalized to intracranial volume\. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients, while longitudinal change was evaluated using mixed\-effects models and repeatability metrics\. Results Baseline volume estimates differed significantly across pipelines in 11 of 12 cohort\-by\-tissue comparisons \(FDR\-adjusted p &lt; 0\.001\), with the largest pipeline\-dependent offsets observed for grey matter, hippocampus, and thalamus\. Inter\-pipeline agreement was generally strong for white matter and lower for gray matter and subcortical structures \(hippocampus and thalamus\), particularly in pathological cohorts\. Change\-from\-baseline models showed no significant Pipeline × Timepoint interactions after FDR correction, indicating broadly parallel longitudinal trajectories across pipelines after baseline normalization\. However, significant pipeline main effects persisted in selected tissues, especially in AD and subcortical regions, indicating residual differences in the magnitude of estimated change\. Longitudinal processing reduced within\-subject variability in selected settings, particularly for FreeSurfer\-derived hippocampal and thalamic estimates, but did not uniformly improve stability across all pipelines or tissues\. Discussion Together, these findings show that systematic offset, absolute agreement, longitudinal change magnitude, and short\-interval repeatability represent distinct properties of volumetric pipelines and vary by tissue, cohort, and processing mode\. Longitudinal processing reduced variability but not uniformly, highlighting pipeline\- and tissue\-dependent differences relevant to the interpretation of longitudinal volumetric measurements\.

## [NL2SQL with Iterative Self\-Refinement](../publications/ea57863816250248b021.md)

Anjali Vemula; Akshat Dasula

Bridging the gap between human intent and machine logic remains a critical challenge in data access for non\-technical users, yet Large Language Models \(LLMs\) remain unreliable: they hallucinate schema elements, generate syntactically invalid queries, or fail to capture user intent\. These limitations are especially critical in domains such as insurance, where KPIs, regulatory constraints, and legacy relational systems demand high precision\. We introduce a multi\-agent, persona\-driven NL2SQL framework that combines \(1\) domain relevance detection, \(2\) schema\-grounded knowledge construction, \(3\) KPI\-aware SQL synthesis, \(4\) syntax\-level self\-repair using sqlite execution feedback, and \(5\) semantic consistency checking via SQL\-to\-NL reverse engineering\. Our system significantly reduces query hallucination and improves semantic fidelity compared to direct LLM prompting\. Evaluated on 60 queries \(50 from a HuggingFace text\-to\-SQL dataset and 10 custom domain queries\), the system achieves 90% correctness using Mistral across seven coordinated LLM calls showing that this approach can substantially increase the reliability of NL2SQL pipelines in high\-stakes environments\.

## [A Practical Guide to Transdisciplinary Research](../publications/ea5d4db8e343fdcd355b.md)

Rosalyn Negrón

Focusing on transdisciplinary research as a research method for the future, this volume provides the latest thinking and accessible resources for problem\-solving, collaborative research that cuts across disciplinary boundaries and engages different communities\. Transdisciplinary research is a problem\-solving research approach where different disciplines are combined and transcended, primarily through teamwork, to solve complex problems in the real world innovatively\. This volume teases apart what transdisciplinarity looks like in practice at the individual, interpersonal, and project levels\. The chapters cover conceptual ground with core ideas, philosophies, terms, and principles that distinguish trandisciplinarity from other research approaches, provide guidance in the planning and implementation of these approaches, and help readers think through the different sections of a research proposal for a transdisciplinary project\. A section dedicated to applications focuses on planning for and implementing research dissemination, translation, and application activities, with emphasis on community engagement as being central to the process\. Developed for scholars in and outside of academia and with graduate students in mind, it would also be of value to undergraduate students in specialized, practice\-based programs, for developing team\-based projects and honors theses based on applied research projects\.

## [Intrahepatic intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct with low\-grade dysplasia presenting as high biliary obstruction and hepatolithiasis: a case report](../publications/ea6e4d70de43951181ad.md)

Jiankai Long; Jingnan Xue; Nanzi Xie; Longhao Zhang; Kai Zhou

Background Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct \(IPNB\) is an uncommon biliary epithelial neoplasm and an important precursor lesion of cholangiocarcinoma\. The educational value of this case lies in demonstrating that IPNB may be clinically masked by hepatolithiasis and biliary obstruction, creating a significant diagnostic pitfall in routine practice\. Case presentation A 63\-year\-old woman presented with recurrent upper abdominal pain for more than 1 year, which had worsened over the preceding 10 days\. Routine laboratory tests were unremarkable except for a mildly elevated carbohydrate antigen 19\-9 level of 39\.8 U/mL\. Contrast\-enhanced CT demonstrated a focal intraductal lesion in the left intrahepatic biliary system with adjacent cystic or aneurysmal dilatation of the affected bile duct, producing the appearance of localized high biliary obstruction\. MRI and MRCP further confirmed marked unilateral dilatation of the left intrahepatic bile ducts with focal obstructive change and associated intraductal abnormality\. After comprehensive preoperative evaluation, the patient underwent open left hepatectomy\. Intraoperatively, a markedly dilated bile duct containing intraductal papillary adenomatous tissue and gelatinous material was identified\. Histopathological examination confirmed intrahepatic IPNB with low\-grade dysplasia, pancreatobiliary type\. No invasive carcinoma was identified, and all resection margins were negative\. Immunohistochemistry showed positive staining for CK19, CK7, MUC1, MUC5AC, and MUC6, with negative staining for MUC2\. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 10\. No recurrence or major complication was observed during 2 years of follow\-up\. Conclusion In patients with hepatolithiasis and recurrent biliary symptoms, unilateral or focal intrahepatic duct dilatation and localized obstructive biliary abnormalities should prompt consideration of IPNB rather than uncomplicated stone disease alone\. Early recognition, definitive surgical resection for localized disease, and complete pathological evaluation are essential for accurate diagnosis, risk stratification, and follow\-up planning\.

## [De l&\#x27;e\-gouvernement au gouvernement digital : revue intégrative des trajectoires de maturité et des capacités d&\#x27;intégration organisationnelle](../publications/ea7b5601d697bc15a974.md)

Nouhayla Boutaleb; Larbi Tamnine

Résumé La littérature sur l’e\-gouvernement s’est longtemps structurée autour de deux questions : le degré de sophistication des services numériques et les facteurs d’adoption par les usagers\. Ces approches ont produit des modèles utiles, mais elles rendent imparfaitement compte du passage d’une offre de services en ligne à une transformation durable des organisations publiques\. Cet article propose une revue intégrative visant à réexaminer cette transition à partir d’un corpus de 34 articles scientifiques publiés entre 2001 et 2026 dans des revues indexées dans Scopus et/ou Web of Science\. L’analyse articule quatre courants : les modèles de maturité, les travaux sur l’adoption et la confiance, la transformation organisationnelle et l’interopérabilité, ainsi que la littérature sur la valeur publique\. Trois résultats principaux émergent\. Premièrement, la maturité numérique ne peut être assimilée à une trajectoire linéaire : les administrations combinent des niveaux hétérogènes de sophistication des services, d’intégration des données et de transformation interne\. Deuxièmement, l’existence d’infrastructures ou de services numériques constitue une condition nécessaire mais non suffisante ; leur appropriation dépend de l’accessibilité, des compétences numériques, de la confiance, de l’utilisabilité et de l’adéquation des canaux\. Troisièmement, le passage au gouvernement digital repose surtout sur des capacités organisationnelles d’intégration : leadership, gouvernance du changement, compétences, interopérabilité, coordination interorganisationnelle et apprentissage\. Sur cette base, l’article propose un modèle théorique d’intégration stratégique du gouvernement digital reliant fondations sociotechniques, capacités d’appropriation, capacités organisationnelles et création de valeur publique, sous l’effet modérateur du contexte institutionnel et de la capacité administrative\. Sept propositions théoriques sont formulées\. La contribution consiste à déplacer l’unité d’analyse de la simple maturité technologique vers la capacité d’une administration à intégrer, maintenir et reconfigurer le numérique au service de finalités publiques\. Mots clés : e\-gouvernement ; gouvernement digital ; transformation numérique publique ; maturité numérique ; capacités organisationnelles ; interopérabilité ; valeur publique\. Abstract Research on e\-government has long focused on the sophistication of online public services and the determinants of their adoption\. Although informative, these perspectives do not fully explain how the digitization of public services becomes sustained organizational transformation\. This article presents an integrative review of 34 scientific articles published between 2001 and 2026 in journals indexed in Scopus and/or Web of Science\. It brings together four streams of research: digital maturity models; adoption and trust; organizational transformation and interoperability; and public value\. Three main findings emerge\. First, digital maturity does not follow a necessarily linear trajectory: public administrations may combine sophisticated online services with fragmented data systems and limited internal change\. Second, digital infrastructures and online services are necessary but insufficient conditions for effective use, which also depends on accessibility, digital skills, trust, usability, and the suitability of service channels\. Third, the transition to digital government relies on organizational integration capabilities, including leadership, change governance, staff competencies, interoperability, interorganizational coordination, and organizational learning\. On this basis, the article develops a theoretical model of strategic digital government integration linking sociotechnical foundations, appropriation capabilities, organizational capabilities, and public value creation, with institutional context and administrative capacity as moderating conditions\. Seven theoretical propositions are formulated\. The contribution is to shift the unit of analysis from technological maturity alone to the capacity of public administrations to integrate, sustain, and reconfigure digital resources in pursuit of public purposes\. Keywords: e\-government; digital government; public\-sector digital transformation; digital maturity; organizational capabilities; interoperability; public value\.

## [Compliance with Tobacco Control Law in Hospitals of Nicosia: An Observational Study](../publications/ea82896bedc62a352942.md)

Özen Aşut; Songül Acar Vaizoğlu; Şanda Çalı; Ahmed Elamin Ahmed Elamin; Mohamed Ebied; Enver Abdullaiev; Karam Chaddad; Muhnd Muhammad Algawi; Shania Sheka; Abdullatif Adnan İbrahim; Tuqa Mohammad Aldowery; Gülşah Bahadır; Mehmet Utku Durum; Alper Çeliker

BACKGROUND/AIMS:Smoking is a global health issue causing millions of deaths each year\.The World Health Organisation created the Framework Convention of Tobacco Control and launched the MPOWER initiative in 2008 to reduce this death burden\.Studies conducted in developed countries show that strict tobacco control laws help reduce tobacco use\.In the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus \(TRNC\), studies show a high prevalence of tobacco use, but there are no reports on the implementation of laws and adherence to them\.This research aims to evaluate compliance with the tobacco control law in three hospitals in Northern Cyprus\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This observational study was conducted in August 2025\.Observers used a data collection form to assess compliance\.SPSS version 31\.0 \(IBM Inc\.,Armonk, NY , USA\) was used for data analysis\.RESULTS: A total of 113 departments were observed across three hospitals\.Indoor no smoking compliance was high, whereas overall compliance with &quot;no smoking&quot; signs was low \(37\.4%\)\.The highest compliance was found in the state hospital, particularly in signage placement, while private hospitals showed gaps, such as insufficient outdoor signage and the presence of smoking facilities\.No enforcement officers or cessation resources were observed\.Staff smoking was observed in all hospitals\.A significant difference in compliance between the state hospital and the private hospitals was observed, with the state hospital having better compliance \(p\-value &lt;0\.001\)\. CONCLUSION:Compliance with the Northern Cyprus tobacco control law varied by hospital type\.Major shortcomings were found in signage, enforcement, and cessation support\.No hospital had trained personnel to handle violations, and hospital staff were observed smoking\.

## [Buchholz, Oliver: Explaining Artificial Intelligence\. From Epistemological Foundations to Practical Consequences](../publications/ea86818a3d21e0df2f9f.md)



Which kind of artificial intelligence do we want to live with? Should machines explain themselves to us? Machine learning techniques are developing at a rapid pace and find applications not only in banal everyday uses, but also in high\-stake situations, including science, medicine, banking, law, and business\. But it is impossible to reconstruct how they reach their results and to judge whether they reach their results in the intended way\. The mechanism is entirely opaque\. This prompts a lot of justified skepticism and criticism of these computer programs\. By closely investigating the foundations of opacity and explanations from a philosophy of science and epistemological perspective, Buchholz comes to more optimistic conclusions\. This book derives practical consequences from a rigorous conceptual analysis of opacity, paving the way to an effective regulation of machine learning, and will advance the debate about the nature of explanation in the philosophy of science\. \(direct link \)

## [AI Driven Personalized Learning and Learning Analytics in Higher Education: Effects on Student Engagement, Achievement and Research Integrity](../publications/eabcc747aeb21ed7d716.md)

Nighat Yasmin; Javed Ali; Shazia Ejaz

The study aimed to examine the effect of personalized learning through artificial intelligence \(AI\) and learning analytics on student engagement and learning outcomes of higher education institutes in Pakistan with implications for Research Integrity at these institutes\. Adopting a mixed methods approach, quantitative data gathered from 500 students from an undergraduate science program, with semi structured interviews with 30 students for the qualitative data\. The descriptive statistics indicated that the mean engagement scores for those students who have access to AI based personalized learnings were significantly higher than the mean scores of students in traditional learning setting; it is from these that an increase in engagement by the students were observed\. There was an improvement in Academic achievement as well, as indicated by higher grade point averages, and improved scores of the formative assessments\. The regression analysis results showed that AI \(personalized learning\) and learning analytics \(β = \.41; p &lt; \.001\) were among its most important models that were significant in predicting the variable of academic achievement; the analysis of correlation results showed that there was a good positive correlation between the variables of engagement and academic achievement \(r = \.63, p &lt; \.01\)\. The qualitative results corroborated this as students felt there was a significant increase in motivation, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning pathways as being the most beneficial aspects of the AI integration\. Issues were identified that could interfere in successful implementation: Data privacy concerns, uneven access to technology and insufficient faculty preparation\. According to this study, personalized learning &amp; learning analytics with AI have proved to be significant drivers of student engagement &amp; academic performance, provided that the ethical issues and infrastructure are sorted out and this may influence the way research integrity and rigor will be upheld within Higher Education Institutions\. The findings herein expand the conversation taking place around the role of AI in education and highlight the need to embed learning analytics in a learning design practice, to create inclusive and effective learning spaces\.

## [Digital Transformation in Hospital Pharmacy Services: Effects on Team Performance](../publications/eabd3c5d395811bf4cf1.md)

Abdulhakeem Mohammed Alshehri; Abdulkarim Abdulrahman Alshehri; Abdullah Ahmed Asiri; Hani Shahir Lafaf Alshammari; Abdulaziz Abdulrahman Alotaibi; Khaled Nasser Almoteri; Nashmi Melfi Mansor Aldafeeri; Abdulaziz Jazaa Sheleweh Alanzi

Digital transformation has become a fundamental driver of healthcare innovation, particularly within hospital pharmacy services\. Technologies such as electronic prescribing, barcode medication administration \(BCMA\), automated dispensing cabinets \(ADCs\), robotic dispensing systems, artificial intelligence \(AI\), clinical decision support systems \(CDSS\), and integrated pharmacy information systems have significantly reshaped pharmacy workflows\. These innovations enhance medication safety, improve operational efficiency, and foster interdisciplinary collaboration\. This review examines the influence of digital transformation on hospital pharmacy team performance, emphasizing productivity, communication, medication safety, workload distribution, and patient outcomes\. Current evidence indicates that digital technologies reduce medication errors, increase dispensing accuracy, optimize inventory management, and improve staff satisfaction\. Nevertheless, implementation challenges— including high costs, cybersecurity risks, resistance to organizational change, and training requirements—remain barriers to widespread adoption\. Successful digital transformation requires strategic planning, continuous workforce education, leadership commitment, and robust evaluation metrics\.

## [Regulatory reforms and the impact on overseas new drug accessibility in China: an analysis from 2010 to 2025](../publications/eac2600931c7f7fa0382.md)

Yaoyang Tang; Li Yang

In recent years, China has undertaken a series of regulatory reforms aimed at enhancing the accessibility of overseas new drugs by mitigating marketing approval lag and expediting their inclusion in the National Reimbursement Drug List \(NRDL\)\. This study conducted a retrospective analysis of overseas new drugs approved in China between 2010 and 2025, emphasizing temporal shifts in drug characteristics, regulatory efficiency, and approval lag across different reform periods\. Furthermore, the study examined the reimbursement status of overseas new drugs in China, identified factors influencing their inclusion in the NRDL, and explored the China\-oriented research and development \(R&amp;D\) strategies adopted by their holders\. Following the implementation of these reforms, the number of overseas new drug approvals increased significantly, with the cumulative total reaching 361 over the 2010–2025 study period\. Simultaneously, the approval lag of overseas new drugs in China experienced a reduction, with the median duration decreasing from 1,442 to 1,188 days, using the United States as a reference\. Notable improvements were observed in reimbursement access, as 213 out of 361 drugs \(59\.0%\) were incorporated into the NRDL, and the median time for inclusion in the NRDLs was reduced from 2,297 to 743 days\. However, we found that drugs approved after the reforms did not have a significantly higher likelihood of being included in the NRDL\. Analyses specific to different R&amp;D strategies indicated greater regulatory flexibility in China’s acceptance of overseas clinical evidence\. Notably, drugs participating in multi\-regional clinical trials \(MRCTs\) were associated with the shortest median approval lag, measured at 737\.5 days\. Overall, these findings highlighted the critical importance of China’s integration into global drug development initiatives and the need for enhanced coordination between regulatory and reimbursement processes\.

## [The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Cognitive Scaffolding, Substitution, and the Risk of Deskilling](../publications/eac4ab9e925ad43356be.md)

Marco Fenici

Abstract The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) has raised fundamental questions about its effects on critical thinking and cognitive development\. Evidence from recent empirical studies suggests a dual pattern: structured forms of AI assistance can sustain users’ cognitive activity and enhance engagement and performance, whereas more substitutive forms of use are associated with reduced autonomous reasoning and poorer subsequent independent performance\. This article argues that these findings can be understood by considering how cognitive work is distributed between users and AI systems and how this distribution may evolve over time\. In particular, I examine a six\-step sequence in which successful complementary assistance can increase trust and delegation; greater delegation can remain complementary or become increasingly substitutive; and increasingly substitutive interactions can reduce the autonomous exercise of critical thinking and potentially hinder the development or maintenance of critical\-thinking capacities over time\. The available evidence provides substantial support for the first five steps considered individually and substantial, though less direct, support for the sixth\. The article concludes by discussing educational, design, and social implications, arguing that preserving cognitive agency requires fostering complementary rather than progressively substitutive forms of interaction\.

## [Physics\-informed acoustic–vibration fusion for all\-ceramic bearing fault diagnosis under complex operating conditions](../publications/eac6095380a96a8a0e8d.md)

Xiaotong Li; Ke Zhang; Xu Duo Bai; Tianhao Gao; Song Liang; Lixiu Zhang; Basem Ibrahim Esawy Selim; Yang Hong

Abstract Complex noise and variable operating conditions substantially reduce the observability of fault\-induced impact and modulation features in acoustic–vibration measurements of all\-ceramic bearings and create modality\-dependent differences in signal reliability\. To address this problem, this study proposes PH\-FusionNet, a physics\-informed network for acoustic–vibration signal fusion and fault diagnosis\. The proposed method follows a progressive framework consisting of local physics\-prior enhancement, global representation stabilization, and reliability\-aware fusion\. First, a Laplace–Morlet physics\-prior feature extraction layer is developed based on the impact–resonance mechanism to enhance fault\-related features, including vibration impact responses and acoustic modulation wave packets\. Subsequently, a long\-range global competitive representation enhancement module is designed to aggregate long\-range contextual information and recalibrate global responses, thereby strengthening fault\-related representations while suppressing non\-stationary noise interference\. Finally, an impulse\-guided gated fusion mechanism is introduced, in which vibration impact responses serve as structural references for selective acoustic\-feature injection and vibration\-conditioned fusion\. Experimental results show that, across five representative noise conditions, PH\-FusionNet achieved an average diagnostic accuracy of 86\.84%, outperforming the second\-best model by 3\.48 percentage points, while attaining an average FNR of 13\.16%\. The model also retained comparatively robust diagnostic performance under asymmetric modality degradation and simulated speed\-transition conditions, thereby demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method\.

## [Role of ERK1 and ANP as potential forensic biomarkers in hypothermia conditions: An experimental study](../publications/eac8a95a1d23cf2acca9.md)

Emina Dervišević; Džan Ahmed Jesenković; Muhamed Katica; Aida Bešić; Haroon Ahmed; Teufik Goletić; Ilma Terzić; Emina Šabić; Nedim Šuta; Maria Sofia Fede; Emina Karahmet Sher; Angelo Montana

Diagnosing fatal hypothermia remains a forensic challenge due to the lack of specific postmortem markers\. This study investigates the potential of extracellular signal\-regulated kinase 1 \(ERK\) and atrial natriuretic peptide \(ANP\) as biochemical indicators in hypothermia\-related deaths, particularly under the influence of ethanol and diazepam\. A randomized experimental study was conducted in rats approximately 3\.5 months old and weighing 200–240 grams, which were randomized into the control group \(n=7\), the ethanol\-treated group \(n=7\), and the diazepam\-treated group \(n=7\)\. Survival time was measured from the point of immersion in 7°C water until the animals’ death\. Hypothermia was induced, and serum and muscle levels of ERK1 and ANP were measured using ELISA\. Serum ERK1 levels differed significantly across groups \(p = 0\.039\), with a similar changes in Control and Ethanol groups, while Diazepam decreased\. ANP levels showed no significant changes across groups or time points\. Muscle concentrations of both markers remained stable\. The observed alterations in ERK1 levels may indicate a possible association with stress responses during hypothermia, although the findings should be considered exploratory due to limited statistical significance after multiple\-comparison correction\. ANP showed limited diagnostic utility under the study conditions\. Further research incorporating histological validation and larger cohorts is needed to confirm these findings and improve forensic applications\.

## [Fake Currency Detection Using Machine Learning and Image Processing](../publications/ead5b481efb123e90c1d.md)

Pothumarthi Sriram; Paravada Teja; Pampana Veerendra; Chinthakayala Swaroop

Counterfeit currency is a serious financial crime that can shake a whole country&\#x27;s economy; it can be prevented, but people are often unaware of how to tell a counterfeit note from a genuine one, so spreading awareness is key\. This paper presents a Fake Currency Detection system that applies machine learning and image processing to classify banknote images as genuine or fake\. Statistical features \(variance, skewness, kurtosis, and entropy\) are extracted from the images using wavelet transforms, and classification is performed by supervised models—Random Forest, K\-Nearest Neighbours \(KNN\), and Gradient Boosting—combined in an ensemble \(Voting Classifier\) and tuned with GridSearchCV and cross validation\. The paper reports a twenty\-study literature survey, the software requirements specification \(SRS\), a layered, modular system design, the Waterfall development methodology, the implementation stack \(Python, OpenCV, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit\-learn, PyWavelets, Flask/Django, MySQL/MongoDB\), and the testing and deployment strategy\. Convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\), which excel at image pattern recognition, are discussed as a complementary direction\. The source work also acknowledges limitations: model effectiveness depends on the quality and omprehensiveness of the training data, counterfeiters constantly adopt new techniques so the dataset must be kept up to date, and the models themselves must be secured against manipulation\. Future directions include transfer learning, which adapts pre\-trained models to reduce training time and resources, and generative adversarial networks \(GANs\) for building more comprehensive training datasets\.

## [ML\-Based Smart Appliance Energy Monitoring System](../publications/ead89d085999bb0f1d4c.md)

Divya Dongre; Astha Bavistale; Atharva Wasnik; Rohan Hedau; Sanchit Nardelwar; Krishnakumar Bhabhda; Ms\. Priya Meshram

Modern homes only get a combined electricity consumption value\. In other words, they have no information about which of their appliances have used the electricity a house has consumed\. This paper introduces the design of an ‘ML\-Based Smart Appliance Energy Monitoring’ system for recognizing the electricity consumption of a smart home\. The Non\-Intrusive Load Monitoring system uses an ESP32 development board and a PZEM\-004T V3\.0 energy meter and current transformer \(CT\) to measure the voltage, current, power, frequency, and power\-factor data of a particular circuit of the home’s electrical circuit\. These are then transmitted over Wi\-Fi/HTTP to a Flask\-based inference server where a 50\-feature input \(constructed in identical fashion between training and inference from a 13,439\-row labeled dataset\) is classified by a joint ensemble \(HistGradientBoosting \(45%\), ExtraTrees \(35%\), and Random Forest \(20%\)\) of regressors into one of eight appliancecombination classes representing three target devices \(a phone charger, a laptop charger, and a hot glue gun\)\. An additional individual\-device model enables ON\-time tracking, per\-device energy estimation, and electricity cost calculation for the devices\. Classification results are then locally visualized on a 16 × 2 I2C LCD and remotely on the Blynk IoT platform while storing relevant device statistics in the ESP32 Preferences\. In contrast to the recent deep\-learning\-based approaches, which typically require heavy computation and a large amount of annotated data to train on, we propose an explainable ensemble pipeline for low\-end single\-household appliances\.

## [Universal crystallization kinetics of solution\-processed semiconductors](../publications/eade94a4c5d737338f55.md)

Zhitian Ling; Mateusz Brzeziński; Shuanglong Wang; Konstantinos Bidinakis; Lei Gao; Chongyao Li; Xin Zhou; Hai I\. Wang; Stefan A\. L\. Weber; Paul W\. M\. Blom; Wojciech Pisula; Tomasz Marszałek

Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution\-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial\-and\-error optimization\. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth\. Here, a time\-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing\. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration\-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments\. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions\. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors\. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality\. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution\-processed transistors\.

## [Perbandingan Kinerja Algoritma Random Forest dan Xgboost Dalam Memprediksi Harga Bitcoin Menggunakan Indikator Teknikal](../publications/eae84a318eb598519a84.md)

Ahmad Siddiq Fadhillah; Rahmat Budiarsa

The extreme volatility of crypto assets makes Bitcoin price movements notoriously difficult to predict using conventional linear forecasting approaches\. This study aims to compare the performance of two machine learning algorithms Random Forest Regressor and XGBoost Regressor in projecting Bitcoin&\#x27;s closing price\. A quantitative approach was employed using two years of historical time\-series data, with the Simple Moving Average \(SMA\) and Relative Strength Index \(RSI\) serving as primary predictor features; both models were then comprehensively evaluated using absolute and percentage error metrics\. Experimental results demonstrate that the XGBoost Regressor significantly outperformed the other model, achieving superior accuracy by minimizing error margins \(MAE: 2327\.81; RMSE: 2978\.93; MAPE: 1\.99%; R2: 0\.4571\), whereas the Random Forest model struggled to accurately capture volatile fluctuations \(MAE: 2891\.19; RMSE: 3619\.53; MAPE: 2\.53%; R2: 0\.1984\)\. Furthermore, the findings reveal that both algorithms largely disregarded momentum indicators, basing their predictions almost entirely on short\-term average trend movements\. In conclusion, XGBoost is empirically proven to be a far more robust and precise algorithm than Random Forest for modeling the anomaly\-prone price dynamics of Bitcoin\. The primary contribution of this research lies in providing empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of the boosting paradigm over bagging for highly volatile crypto assets, as well as the direct implementation of the winning prediction architecture into an interactive Streamlit based dashboard to facilitate practical, real world investment decision making\.

## [The effects of artificial intelligence and environmental pollution on green growth in China](../publications/eaecc50c1f4dd5aaf69e.md)

Kashif Javed; 李建新

Achieving sustainable economic development requires policies that reconcile growth with environmental protection\. This study examines how artificial intelligence \(AI\) and environmental regulation \(ER\) affect green growth \(GG\) in China, controlling for fiscal policy, human capital and urbanization\. Using panel data for 30 provinces over 2011–2020, we construct a composite GG index with the entropy method and estimate effects with the Method of Moments Quantile Regression \(MMQR\), complemented by a panel quantile Granger causality test\. AI and ER both raise GG at the lower, middle and upper quantiles\. The AI effect grows across quantiles, while the ER effect is small and declines slightly\. Fiscal policy, human capital and urbanization also promote GG, and linear panel estimates confirm these results\. The AI effect depends on adoption level: it is positive in high\-AI provinces but negative in low\-AI provinces\. The causality test indicates that all five variables Granger\-cause GG across most quantiles\. These findings support combining AI adoption with environmental regulation, alongside targeted support for low\-adoption provinces\.

## [Digital Assets and Property Taxes: Comparative law challenges and Serbian perspective](../publications/eaf8a52ca8f3d8be09ea.md)

Cvjetana Cvjetković\-Ivetić; Luka Baturan

In contemporary societies, now commonly referred to as digital societies, digital assets are experiencing significant growth and are becoming an increasingly important component of economic activity\. The emergence of new forms of value that exist exclusively in the digital environment has created a need for an appropriate legal and tax framework, resulting in the gradual inclusion of digital assets within the scope of an increasing number of taxes\. This paper is limited to the analysis of the tax treatment of digital assets within the framework of property taxes in both static and dynamic terms\. It aims to present the tax regime applicable to digital assets in domestic and comparative law, primarily from the perspective of net wealth taxes and inheritance and gift taxes, and to identify, through comparative law analysis, the key challenges faced by tax authorities when subjecting digital assets to property taxes\. This is investigated primarily using the normative and comparative methods and, to some extent, the axiological and historical\-legal methods\. The results of the comparative law analysis showed that digital assets are included in the net wealth tax bases in countries that have retained such taxes, and that one of the key challenges in their taxation is determining their value\. Given that the Serbian tax system does not impose a net wealth tax, the tax treatment of digital assets in the context of property taxation is relevant only within the framework of inheritance and gift taxes\. However, the practical scope these taxes is limited, as tax exemptions apply to transfers to the closest relatives\. The analysis indicates a need for further clarification of the rules governing the determination of the market value of digital assets for inheritance and gift tax purposes under Serbian tax law\. The findings should, however, be considered in light of certain limitations, primarily arising from the focus on property taxes and the limited number of jurisdictions included in the comparative analysis\.

## [Informing personalization of technologies for promoting physical activity: bridging the knowledge, attitude and practice model and human\-centered design](../publications/eb09a5ea57c35d44263d.md)

Agnieszka Jaff; Mia Folke; Annica Kristoffersson

Background Although the benefits of physical activity \(PA\) are well established and inactivity poses substantial risks, encouraging adults to change and sustain PA behaviors remains a challenge\. Mobile technologies have emerged as accessible and cost\-effective tools to encourage healthier behaviors\. Personalization is a key factor for improving user engagement and adherence, but current approaches often rely on surface\-level data and overlook cognitive and motivational aspects\. Objective This study explores how mobile exercise\- and health\-related technologies can be personalized to support PA behavior change by integrating the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice \(KAP\) model with a human\-centered design approach\. Methods We conducted semi\-structured interviews with 24 adults aged 34–66 years to explore their PA habits and use of exercise\- and health\-related technology\. Interview recordings were transcribed, reviewed, and analyzed using deductive thematic analysis guided by the three domains of the KAP model: knowledge, attitude, and practice\. Results Participants demonstrated varied knowledge of PA, ranging from general health benefits to specific exercise practices\. General awareness of the benefits of PA was not always accompanied by practical knowledge about planning exercise or interpreting activity data\. Attitudes toward PA and mobile exercise\- and health\-related technology were influenced by motivation, convenience, and emotional responses, with some participants reporting guilt or stress related to use of mobile exercise\- and health\-related technology\. Practices reflected diverse PA routines, from structured exercise to incidental daily movement\. These practices were shaped by work, family responsibilities, physical limitations, preferred environments, and differing needs for social or solitary activity\. Engagement with mobile exercise\- and health\-related technology varied widely, with some participants relying on wearables and apps, while others reported irregular or discontinued use\. Together, the findings informed a framework of 20 dimensions describing how individual differences in knowledge, attitudes, and practices can guide the personalization of mobile exercise\- and health\-related technology for PA promotion\. Conclusions Personalization of mobile exercise\- and health\-related technologies for PA promotion should extend beyond surface\-level data to include cognitive, emotional, and contextual factors that influence behavior\. Applying the KAP model within human\-centered design can inform adaptive, empathetic, and context\-sensitive solutions that better resonate with users’ lived experiences and support sustainable PA engagement\.

## [Intervenciones rehabilitadoras no farmacológicas de la parálisis cerebral espástica infantil: Una revisión narrativa](../publications/eb0b608598122b47c447.md)

VALENTINA BARRERA MEZA; VALENTINA LEMUS CASTRO; Francisca Sánchez Rodríguez; Ignacio Soto Riquelme; Israel Andrés Patiño Cabrera

Introducción: La espasticidad es un aumento del tono muscular velocidad\- dependiente presente en hasta un 80% de los niños con parálisis cerebral \(PC\), lo cual afecta significativamente la calidad de vida\. El objetivo de esta revisión narrativa es sintetizar críticamente la evidencia reciente \(2015\-2025\) sobre intervenciones rehabilitadoras no farmacológicas de la PC espástica infantil\. Material o Pacientes y Métodos: Se realizó una búsqueda en Pubmed/Medline utilizando términos MeSH\. Se incluyeron 30 artículos en la síntesis cualitativa, priorizando el nivel más alto de certidumbre clínica \(guías de práctica clínica, revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis y ensayos clínicos aleatorizados\) y se categorizaron mediante el sistema de “semáforo de evidencia”\. Resultados: La literatura evidencia un cambio de paradigma: la modulación del tono es un medio facilitador y no un objetivo en sí mismo\. Las intervenciones activas de alta intensidad basadas en el aprendizaje motor \(CIMT, HABIT\-ILE, entrena­miento orientado a tareas\) y el entrenamiento de fuerza tienen el mayor respaldo para mejorar función, aunque no necesariamente disminuyan la espasticidad de manera directa\. Las modalidades físicas y tecnologías muestran evidencia heterogénea, actuando principalmente como coadyuvantes\. El estiramiento pasivo aislado carece de evidencia para inducir cambios funcionales a largo plazo\. Conclusión: El éxito terapéutico en PC requiere un enfoque multidisciplinario que priorice intervenciones activas, intensivas y específicas a la tarea por sobre la modificación aislada del tono\.

## [Optimist Deep Research: An Iterative, State\-Centric Agent for Autonomous Literature Research](../publications/eb17e942f217ee492003.md)

Gihan Panapitiya

Most retrieval\-augmented systems treat literature search as a single retrieval step followed by summarization\. Real literature research works differently: the investigator&\#x27;s understanding of the question changes as they read, new subquestions appear, and evidence is weighed, not just collected\. We present Optimist Deep Research, an open\-source agent that runs literature research as an iterative evidence\-acquisition process over an explicit, mutable research state\. A research question is broken into a tree of subquestions, each served by search intents that are translated into source\-specific queries over arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, PubMed, Semantic Scholar and the web\. Results are merged into a canonical, provenance\-preserving document registry through a conservative four\-tier deduplication hierarchy\. The registry is expanded by citation snowballing until a saturation criterion is met, and then screened, ranked and allocated to subquestions round\-robin\. Documents are read in parallel into a structured evidence store of claims with support, location, type and strength\. A critic reviews the state along eight dimensions and returns research actions rather than a binary verdict: it can add, split, rephrase, deprioritize or close subquestions, so the research plan is an output of the investigation as well as an input\. The final report is written section by section from the evidence store, and every citation resolves to a retrieved document\. We describe the design, the deterministic machinery that keeps a language\-model pipeline auditable, and a case study that read 28 of 237 retrieved documents in about three and a half minutes\. We also report weaknesses the case study exposed\.

## [Kozlov, Anatolii: Emotions in scientific practice](../publications/eb19703057229bb7bf87.md)



\_Interdisciplinary Science Reviews\_ 48 \(2\):329\-348\. 2023For a long time, emotions were seen as incompatible with rationality and objectivity of science, and so were a marginal topic in the philosophy of science\. This trend has changed progressively since it was determined that objectivity is much linked to social factors while rationality can’t do without emotions\. As a result, emotions are now slowly finding their way into our understanding of what science is\. Here, I make an overview of some aspects of science where emotions and scientific reasoning seem to come into tight contact\. For my survey, I will consider such themes as scientific motivation, scientific evaluations, scientific explanations, scientific understanding, scientific imagination, and coherence in science\. Using these examples, I discuss the epistemic role of emotions in scientific progress\. In conclusion, I advocate for a nuanced view of emotions in science as values that contribute to both epistemic and humanistic dimensions of science\. \(direct link \)

## [Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO\(3\)\-equivariant convolutional network \(CNN\) on the sphere](../publications/eb1b9902e36533d086e4.md)

Joshua Williamson; Niall Jeffrey; Lorne Whiteway

Many of the most important datasets in the physical sciences live natively on the sphere, and these data often carry no preferred position or orientation\. Using methods that do not reflect this symmetry leads to far higher simulation requirements, which can be catastrophic for scientific analyses \(forcing reliance on cheap, imperfect models that bias results\)\. We present a novel spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture that is specifically designed for the Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization \(\\healpix\{\}\) of the sphere\. The $\\mathrm\{SO\}\(3\)$\-equivariant convolution is built from steerable filters, parallel transport and spin\-weighted features\. The architecture supplies the exact symmetry, so the network does not spend training data learning it\. The convolution operations are constructed to give provably exact equivariance, given a band\-limit\. Our full CNNs can achieve SO\(3\)\-invariance error at per\-cent\-level and lower, which is controlled through well\-understood hyperparameters\. On benchmarks, our technique gives the most accurate dense gradient regression and competitive cosmic microwave background foreground removal and denoising\. The improved simulation efficiency matters most in simulation\-based inference \(SBI\), where high\-fidelity simulations are expensive and neural compressors require large training sets, so a fixed budget forces analyses with less accurate simulators\. In cosmology lensing SBI, our technique yields the tightest posteriors at matched simulation count\. This approach is a novel method that will enable new convolutional neural network analyses, including generative and inference tasks, for processes and data on the sphere\.

## [IDEAL\-GENOM: integrated downstream analytical toolkit for genomic analysis](../publications/eb226ec9756f1c26e847.md)

L\. G\. González Ricardo; Amabel Tenghe; Ashwin Ashok Kumar Sreelatha; Manu Sharma

There has been an exponential increase in the development of technologies that have offered unprecedented opportunities to unravel the genetic underpinnings of complex traits\. However, despite the progress and availability of tools, there are still several challenges to overcome, such as the development of a unified framework that facilitates downstream analysis\. To address this challenge, we present IDEAL\-GENOM \(Integrated Downstream Evaluation And anaLysis toolkit for GENOMic data\), a Python\-based wrapper designed to streamline the analytical workflow commonly implemented in binary \(case\-control\) genome\-wide association studies \(GWAS\)\. IDEAL\-GENOM integrates widely used tools such as PLINK, GCTA, and bcftools along with custom\-developed functionalities, enabling reproducible results through parameter sharing\. IDEAL\-GENOM provides a simplified framework for quality control \(QC\), GWAS, and downstream analysis that will enable beginners and advanced users to leverage the built\-in functionalities to perform GWAS analysis for complex traits with binary outcomes\. IDEAL\-GENOM is a customizable tool that enables users to efficiently analyze genotyping data with reproducible QC, post\-imputation, and GWAS pipelines\.

## [Seismic Fragility Assessment of Shallow‐Foundation‐Supported Bridge Piers Subjected to Surge Wave‐Induced Scour](../publications/eb329dcaadf77966e50a.md)

Seyed Mohammad Hadi Moosavian; Shooka Karimpour; S\. J\. Pantazopoulou

ABSTRACT This study presents an integrated numerical framework for evaluating the seismic fragility of bridge piers subjected to surge wave‐induced scour\. The methodology couples three‐dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of scour development with nonlinear finite element analyses of the pier‐foundation‐soil system, incorporating continuum soil representation and soil–structure interaction\. Two shallow‐foundation configurations, representing uplift‐dominated and sinking‐dominated rocking behavior, are examined through quasi‐static and dynamic analyses, with damage‐state thresholds derived using principles of structural mechanics from pushover and pushdown results\. Nonlinear time‐history analyses of the dynamic response of the deck‐pier‐scoured foundation assembly were conducted under 45 code‐compatible earthquake records\. Results were used to develop drift‐ and settlement‐based fragility curves for scoured and unscoured conditions\. It was found that scour reduces lateral capacity and stiffness in both systems, with greater degradation in the sinking‐dominated configuration, while vertical capacity loss is more pronounced in the uplift‐dominated system\. Settlement‐based seismic fragility assessment shows that scour has negligible effect on the uplift‐dominated system but substantially increases settlement vulnerability for the sinking‐dominated system\. Drift‐based fragility curves shifted markedly toward lower spectral accelerations after scouring, demonstrating that the governing damage mechanism depends strongly on the soil–foundation interaction mode\. The proposed framework provides a mechanics‐based approach for multi‐parameter seismic fragility assessment of bridge foundations subjected to combined flood and earthquake hazards\.
