## [Cross\-Alloy Transferability of Spindle\-Synchronous Vibration Signatures in CNC Milling Using Physics\-Informed Autospectrum Features](../publications/eb477a27f49d0f1c672c.md)

Muhammed İşci

Data\-driven recognition of machining conditions in CNC milling processes represents a significant research focus within process monitoring applications\. This work assesses whether physics\-informed, spindle\-synchronous vibration representations remain transferable between Al 6061 and Al 7075 using multi\-axis and multi\-location autospectrum data\. Spindle speed is used as a controlled and physically traceable process\-state label rather than as an unknown CNC variable to be reconstructed\. Vibration signals were collected under various combinations of feed rate, spindle speed, and depth of cut\. Subsequently, autospectrum descriptors associated with spindle rotation, harmonic components, frequency\-band energy, and sensor location were extracted\. Preliminary cross\-alloy analysis demonstrated that spindle speed recognition exhibited more stable transfer performance than feed rate or depth of cut recognition\. Multiple machine learning models were evaluated, with the combination of spindle\-related autospectrum descriptors \+ LightGBM model selected as the final configuration\. The resulting model achieved 0\.8708 accuracy, 0\.8701 Macro\-F1, 0\.7500 MCC, and 0\.9615 ROC\-AUC in the cross\-alloy spindle speed recognition task\. In two\-way transfer analyses, Macro\-F1 scores of 0\.8748 and 0\.8661 were obtained for the Al 6061 to Al 7075 and Al 7075 to Al 6061 scenarios, respectively\. Ablation studies indicated that spindle\-related frequency descriptors offer advantages over comprehensive feature representations\. SHAP\-based explainability analysis revealed that harmonic band, tooth\-passing band, and sensor\-location\-dependent spectral features were most influential in model decisions\. These findings indicate that physics\-informed autospectrum descriptors preserve discriminative spindle\-synchronous vibration information across the investigated Al 6061 and Al 7075 alloy domains\.

## [An explainable stacking ensemble machine learning model for denial\-of\-service attack detection](../publications/eb4f5bee2a01dcfb387b.md)

Halimah Muhammad Tukur; Jamilu Awwalu; Salim Ahmad; Ayuba John

The evolving sophistication of cyber threats, particularly denial\-of\-service \(DoS\) and distributed denial\-of\-service \(DDoS\) attacks, poses significant challenges to the modern cybersecurity systems, availability, and reliability of digital infrastructures\. These attacks often overwhelm network resources, leading to service disruptions and potential data breaches\. Traditional intrusion detection systems \(IDS\) have been developed to mitigate such threats; however, they often struggle with scalability, detection accuracy, and interpretability, especially when processing large\-scale network traffic\. To address these limitations, this study proposes a stacked ensemble intrusion detection model integrating Decision Tree \(DT\), Random Forest \(RF\), and Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\) classifiers as base learners, with Logistic Regression \(LR\) serving as the meta\-learner\. The framework aims to enhance detection accuracy, interpretability, and robustness against DoS and DDoS attacks\. Using the CIC\-IDS2017 dataset, Mutual Information \(MI\) was employed for optimal feature selection, ensuring the most relevant attributes were retained for training\. SHAP \(Shapley Additive exPlanations\) was applied to interpret the contribution of each selected feature to the model’s decision\-making process\. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ensemble achieves superior performance compared to individual classifiers and baseline models, with 98\.83% accuracy, 96\.37% precision, 99\.19% recall, 97\.76% F1\-score, and an AUC of 0\.9995\. Compared with the baseline \[1\], accuracy improved by 3\.39% and F1\-score by 1\.57%\. SHAP analysis identified flow\-based and packet\-based features as key contributors in distinguishing normal and malicious traffic\. Overall, combining multiple learning algorithms within a stacked ensemble, along with MI feature selection and SHAP explainability, provides a robust, transparent, and effective solution for real\-time intrusion detection\.

## [Vortex\-Induced Vibration Identification for Long\-Span Bridges: A Method Using Two\-Point Vibration Phase Difference with Machine Learning](../publications/eb4fc0b34c8829022e03.md)

Du Wu; Yang Xu; Nan Xu; Yufeng Zhang; Wen‐Li Chen; Shujin Laima

Vortex\-induced vibration \(VIV\) occurs frequently on long\-span bridges at low wind speeds and may cause fatigue damage and serviceability problems, so its reliable identification from field monitoring data is an important engineering task\. However, existing automated identification methods rely mainly on single\-point vibration indicators, and recognizing VIV events in massive, unlabeled monitoring datasets remains challenging\. This study proposes an unsupervised VIV identification method based on a newly proposed feature, the Two\-Point Vibration Phase Difference \(TPVPD\), computed between the vertical accelerations measured at the 1/4\- and 3/4\-span of the bridge\. Because a VIV lock\-in response is dominated by a single vibration mode, the phase difference between two spanwise locations remains nearly constant in time, whereas it fluctuates strongly under buffeting\. The method was validated using six years \(2013–2018\) of monitoring data from a 1650\-m main\-span suspension bridge, covering 2\.85 × 105 valid 10\-min windows\. Spectral clustering of three features—acceleration RMS, TPVPD standard deviation, and an energy concentration coefficient—separated VIV from non\-VIV states with a window\-level F1 score of 0\.84 with respect to a reference VIV inventory, and 99\.8% of the windows identified as VIV exhibited spectral peaks at one of the six known VIV mode frequencies of the bridge\. A rule\-based cluster assignment calibrated on previous years transferred to subsequent years with F1 scores of 0\.74–0\.88, indicating the feasibility of operational deployment\.

Background Dental schools play a critical role in public health by training oral health professionals to prevent, manage, and treat oral diseases\. More research opportunities are needed to drive progress in and promote oral health research\. The University of Manitoba&\#x27;s BSc \(Dent\) program provides first\- or second\-year undergraduate dental students opportunities to pursue research while earning a BSc \(Dent\) degree alongside their Doctor of Dental Medicine \(DMD\) degree\. In 2008, we reported on the general outcomes of this program at the University of Manitoba\. In the present study, we aimed to evaluate the research impact of the past 10 years \(2016–2025\) of the undergraduate BSc \(Dent\) training program at the University of Manitoba\. Methods We assessed overall research impact on the current status, academic activities, and achievements of dental students from 2016 to 2025 using information obtained from the Dean&\#x27;s Office of the Dr\. Gerald Niznick College of Dentistry at the University of Manitoba\. Records were compared to those from 1980 to 2005 at the same university\. Citations of peer\-reviewed publications were obtained by tracking Google Scholar until September 1, 2026\. Results In 2016–2025, 104 dental students enrolled in the BSc \(Dent\) research training program at the University of Manitoba with a cumulative average GPA of 3\.65 ± 0\.16, compared to 76 trainees enrolled from 1980 to 2005 with a cumulative average GPA of 3\.45 ± 0\.61\. Research metric analysis over this time showed that the 104 DMD students in the BSc \(Dent\) program submitted or published 64 manuscripts for peer\-reviewed publication with 731 total citations, 67 poster presentations, 26 oral presentations, and 16 awards/nominations\. Conclusion The University of Manitoba trained more dental students in the BSc \(Dent\) research training program from 2016 to 2025 than from 1980 to 2005\. Over the past 10 years, students achieved significant academic milestones, including publishing peer\-reviewed articles \(37%\), delivering poster presentations \(37%\), oral presentations \(15%\), and receiving national awards or nominations \(9%\)\. These findings suggest that the structured, mentored research experiences provided by the BSc \(Dent\) program foster critical thinking, which could help these students practice evidence\-based dentistry and engage early in academic dentistry and health research\.

## [Closing surveillance detection gaps for emerging digital drug discourse with ontology\-enhanced large language models](../publications/eb544824a26c29127789.md)

Danny Valdez; Damir Ćavar; Maria A\. Parker; Xue\-Jing Liu; Jon D\. Agley

LLMs are touted as a solution to enhance digital drug surveillance but lack domain knowledge to perform these tasks effectively\. Yet, when LLM architecture is enhanced by ontological frameworks, knowledge graphs, and retrieval\-augmented\-generation, we can evolve surveillance efforts to address a core issue contributing to surveillance lag—drug\-slang and coded\-language\. Integrating these established methods offers a novel, linguistically grounded approach to improving the validity and responsiveness of digital drug surveillance\.

## [A multi\-dimensional resilience assessment framework for indoor aging\-friendly environments: LLM\-assisted indicator construction using Google Gemini Pro](../publications/eb683d03111cb85f6524.md)

Quan Wen; Mazran Ismail; Muhammad Hafeez Abdul Nasir

Assessment of aging\-friendly housing commonly separates accessibility, functional support, indoor environmental quality, and safety technology, making it difficult to examine how dwellings accommodate changing occupant and environmental conditions\. This framework\-development study introduces SAFER \(Spatial, Adaptive, Functional, Environmental, Responsive\), a five\-dimensional resilience\-oriented indicator system\. A four\-stage workflow combined a systematic review that retained 186 publications and yielded 312 candidate indicators, Gemini Pro\-assisted first\-pass screening, expert content\-validity assessment, and a preliminary application to six dwellings\. Eighteen resilience\-framework indicators were added to the review\-derived pool, and 43 multidisciplinary experts assessed indicator importance and content validity under research\-team oversight\. The resulting expert\-reviewed framework contains 47 indicators\. All 43 final AHP matrices satisfied the prespecified consistency criterion \(CR ≤ 0\.10\) and were included in the group aggregation; the dimension\-level AHP weights were Spatial \(0\.162\), Adaptive \(0\.231\), Functional \(0\.145\), Environmental \(0\.264\), and Responsive \(0\.198\), with Environmental and Adaptive highest\. A preliminary application to six purposively selected dwellings \(n = 6\) produced primary AHP\-weighted scores from 42\.8 to 80\.9\. Equal, case\-derived entropy, and 0\.5 AHP–entropy hybrid weighting were used only as secondary sensitivity analyses; the case ordering was unchanged under these alternatives, although the small, non\-independent case set means that this sensitivity result does not establish external validity\. SAFER should therefore be understood as an expert\-reviewed framework with aggregate content\-validity evidence and preliminary feasibility results, not as a fully validated assessment instrument\. Larger independent samples, preserved assessor\-level records, and cross\-model LLM comparisons are required before normative thresholds or broad policy use\.

## [High levels of domestic transmission and drug resistance –analysis of national surveillance data for shigellosis, the Netherlands, 2018 to 2024](../publications/eb6a4437df0dc2df7038.md)

Boas C\.L\. van der Putten; Hendrik Sauskojus; Anouk P Meijs; Daan W\. Notermans; Maren I\. Lanzl; Eelco Franz; Maaike J\. C\. van den Beld; Roan Pijnacker; on behalf of the ISIS\-AR study group

BACKGROUND Antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) among Shigella species is increasing, which is concerning\. Strengthening surveillance is key to obtaining accurate, timely and actionable data on shigellosis\. AIM We aimed to describe Dutch national shigellosis surveillance data from 2018 to 2024, spanning the implementation of national genomic surveillance in 2022\. METHODS We described notified shigellosis cases and used logistic regression models to analyse associations between shigellosis and age, sex, year of infection, province, MSM \(men who have sex with men\) association, travel status, severity of disease and Shigella species\. RESULTS In 2018–2024, 3,020 shigellosis cases were notified\. Incidence of shigellosis decreased during the COVID\-19 pandemic years 2020–2021 but returned to pre\-pandemic incidence in 2023 and 2024\. Most cases were males \(n = 1,887; 62\.5%\)\. Of the 1,731 cases with available data, 732 \(42\.3%\) reported recent contact with MSM, representing 24\.2% of all shigellosis cases\. The proportion of extensive drug resistant \(XDR\) isolates increased from 2018 \(1/58\) to 2023 \(24/109; 22\.0%\) \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Cases were more likely to be part of a cluster if they reported a recent MSM contact \(p &lt; 0\.001\) or harboured an XDR isolate \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Cases with recent MSM contact were more likely to harbour an XDR strain \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. CONCLUSION Implementation of genomic surveillance facilitated detection of clusters, provided more timely data on AMR and allowed for more detailed analyses of risk factors for Shigella transmission\. Continued intervention efforts promoting hygiene and raising awareness on shigellosis and AMR are important to curb the increase of XDR shigellosis\.

## [Enhancing Cardiac Auscultation with Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A Survey on Heart Sound Analysis](../publications/eb6ba6f61d0494269b84.md)

Akhil K K; R Devi

Cardiovascular disease kills more people than anything else\. Early detection changes outcomes, and heart sounds are one of the cheapest places to look for the first signs\. Phonocardiogram \(PCG\) recordings carry information about valve function that a trained ear can pick up, which is why auscultation has survived two centuries of newer imaging and why it is still the first test a patient meets\. But listening is slow\. It needs experience, and two clinicians can disagree about the same murmur\. Machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) offer a way to automate that step and make it reproducible\. This review asks what the literature has actually achieved, and what it has not\. We searched IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, PubMed, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar for work published between 2015 and 2024\. Section 2 gives the search strings, the screening steps and the inclusion rules\. Thirty\-seven primary studies survived\. Each was read in full, and its dataset, signal processing chain, model and reported performance were recorded in a comparison table that covers thirteen of them in detail\. Reported accuracy in this field is high and rising\. It is also, taken at face value, misleading\. The studies reviewed here use different corpora, different class definitions, different segmentation strategies and different validation protocols, so 99\.80% in one paper and 73\.6% in another are not measuring the same thing\. Standardised datasets are missing\. So are agreed metrics\. Paediatric recordings are thin on the ground, recording conditions vary, and almost nothing here has been tested in the clinic where it would have to work\. The review pulls recent advances together, then sets the reported numbers against the methodological limits that decide how much those numbers are worth, which surveys in this area tend to skip\.

## [The Impact of Retrieval Augmented Generation on the Reliability of Large Language Models](../publications/eb7113b8d71c4e98c241.md)



Large Language Models \(LLMs\) have demonstrated remarkable fluency but remain fundamentally unreliable for knowledge\-intensive tasks due to hallucination, temporal staleness, and lack of verifiability\.Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) has emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm that grounds generation in external evidence\.This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into how RAG reshapes LLM reliability across factual accuracy, citation fidelity, temporal freshness, and robustness to noise\.We benchmark five RAG variants against closed\-book baselines using secondary datasets including Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and RGB\.Results show an average 23\.7% reduction in hallucination rate and 31\.2%improvement in citation grounding when using advanced retrieval with self\-reflection\.However, we identify critical failure modes: retriever\-generator misalignment, context distraction, and over\-reliance on irrelevant passages\.We propose a reliability framework and demonstrate that corrective and modular RAG designs significantly mitigate these risks\.Our findings establish RAG as necessary but not sufficient for trustworthy deployment\.

## [Google Trends and Wikipedia Queries as Proxies for Measles Surveillance](../publications/eb81ca2dbc45ecc8787a.md)

Omar Enzo Santangelo; Anna Sole Pizzamiglio; Carlotta Vella; Danilo Greco; Alberto Firenze; Sandro Provenzano

Introduction\. The increasing digitalization of information behaviors has created new opportunities in public health, promoting the development of infodemiology and infoveillance as complements to traditional epidemiological surveillance\. This study aimed to assess the correlation and temporal association between official measles surveillance data published by the Italian National Institute of Health \(ISS\), Google Trends \(GT\) search volumes, and Wikipedia page views related to measles in Italy\. Methods\. A retrospective ecological study with a time\-series design was conducted using measles cases reported in Italy from January 2013 to November 2025\. Monthly data from GT and Wikipedia were aggregated and compared with the monthly incidence reported in ISS bulletins\. Linear regressions were performed to evaluate associations\. Results\. The results showed a statistically significant associations between reported measles cases and both GT searches and Wikipedia page views\. Linear regression analyses confirmed significant associations between digital indicators and official surveillance data, suggesting that online user activity closely reflects measles epidemiological trends\. Conclusion\. These findings indicate that GT and Wikipedia may serve as useful and timely tools to complement traditional measles surveillance\. Although caution is needed due to methodological limitations and potential information bias, integrating digital data could enhance early outbreak detection and support more rapid public health responses\.

## [TransVJ2\-MCA: power line defect recognition integrating video world model priors and cross\-attention](../publications/eb88c7322ce5be7cf988.md)

Li Xu; Xiaoping Wu; Yu Liu; Yasi Peng

To address the dual challenges of scarce defect samples in power line component images and fine\-grained defects being easily overwhelmed in complex backgrounds, this paper proposes a video world model prior\-driven component defect recognition framework, TransVJ2\-MCA\. First, a cross\-modal temporal reconstruction \(CMTR\) mechanism is designed to adapt to the input constraints of the video self\-supervised pre\-trained backbone network \(V\-JEPA v2\)\. By replicating single\-frame power line component images along the temporal dimension and converting them into stationary pseudo\-video sequences, static images are aligned with the V\-JEPA v2 encoder in both input form and feature distribution\. A parameter\-freezing strategy is then adopted to reuse the large\-scale spatio\-temporal structural priors embedded in the model, mitigating the limitation imposed by scarce defect samples on model training\. Finally, a multi\-scale cross\-attention \(MCA\) module is constructed, which uses deep semantic features as guidance to selectively aggregate key discriminative information from shallow features, enabling effective selection and adaptive fusion of cross\-level features, suppressing complex background interference, and enhancing fine\-grained defect recognition capability\. Experimental validation is conducted on five independent power line component classification tasks of the InsPLAD\-Fault dataset\. The results show that TransVJ2\-MCA achieves an average balanced accuracy of 98\.2% and a macro\-average F1 score of 97\.1%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method under complex backgrounds and scarce defect samples, as well as its cross\-modal transfer capability\. This study provides a referential adaptation paradigm for transferring video pre\-trained large models to static industrial visual inspection\.

## [Fostering multidimensional thinking in chemistry education through an integrated challenge\-based learning model with socioscientific issues and counterargumentation](../publications/eb8c621acb983e8301dc.md)

I Wayan Redhana; I Nyoman Suardana; Desak Made Kurnia Widyasari Putri Aditya; Ni Putu Irma Ishwariasih; Kompyang Selamet; Sri Haryani; Triwiyono Triwiyono

Abstract Multidimensional thinking, comprising critical, creative, and caring thinking, is important for chemistry learning involving authentic challenges, socioscientific issues \(SSI\), and counterargumentation \(CA\)\. This quasi\-experimental study compared the Challenge\-Socioscientific Issues\-Counterargumentation \(CHASICA\) learning model with Problem\-Based Learning \(PBL\) model among 300 Grade 12 students from four public high schools in Bali, Indonesia\. Intact classes completed pretest and posttest measures of critical, creative, and caring thinking over ten learning sessions\. The instruments were developed from established theoretical frameworks, reviewed by experts, and demonstrated acceptable internal consistency\. Posttest outcomes were analyzed by controlling for prior abilities, with interaction terms included where the relationship between pretest and posttest scores differed across groups\. Students in the CHASICA group showed higher posttest outcomes than students in the PBL group across the measured dimensions, although the magnitude of group differences varied according to students’ prior abilities for some outcomes\. Teacher and student perception data, analyzed descriptively, also indicated that CHASICA was perceived as more relevant, engaging, and supportive of contextual chemistry learning\. The findings suggest that integrating challenge\-based learning \(CBL\), SSI, and CA may provide a promising instructional model for supporting critical, creative, and caring thinking in secondary chemistry education\.

## [ISLAMIC LEGAL REVIEW OF PRE\-ORDER SALES: CONTRACT CLASSIFICATION, CONSUMER PROTECTION, AND SHARIA\-COMPLIANT DIGITAL COMMERCE IN INDONESIA](../publications/eb90dd415219c1f662e4.md)

Muhammad Rizali; Miftah Faridh

Pre\-order sales are increasingly common in digital commerce, but their legal status remains uncertain when payment precedes production, product specifications change, or delivery is delayed\. Although Islamic commercial law recognizes salam and istisna&\#x27; contracts, neither applies automatically to every transaction labeled pre\-order\. Previous Indonesian studies have largely examined individual sellers or marketplaces, leaving the relationship among contract classification, platform\-held payments, and consumer remedies insufficiently integrated\. This study examines how pre\-order transactions should be classified under Islamic law, which conditions determine their validity, and how Sharia requirements interact with Indonesian electronic\-commerce regulations\. Using doctrinal legal research, it analyzes Islamic legal principles, DSN\-MUI fatwas, relevant legislation, and selected scholarly publications, primarily from 2022 to 2025\. The analysis employs normative interpretation, comparison of legal sources, and assessments of hypothetical transaction scenarios without presenting original field data\. Findings indicate that fully prepaid, clearly specified future goods generally fall under salam, while commissioned production is more appropriately governed by istisna&\#x27;\. A preliminary expression of interest does not constitute a completed sale\. Deposits and platform\-held payments require closer examination: DSN\-MUI Fatwa No\. 145/2021 recognizes escrow payment as cash payment in a specified dropshipping\-salam arrangement, although its application beyond that context depends on contractual facts\. The study proposes a six\-stage compliance framework covering classification, disclosure, payment, deliverability, remedies, and documentary evidence\.

## [Improved vision transformer for sports image classification via transfer learning and knowledge distillation](../publications/eb9125a09befe21947d2.md)

Chao Li; Daniel Memmert; Qiang Liu

To address the challenges posed by complex visual characteristics in sports image classification, this study proposes an enhanced Vision Transformer \(ViT\) model built upon the Native Resolution ViT \(NaViT\) architecture\. The principal innovations include replacing conventional single\-layer feedforward networks with parallel feedforward networks and introducing an attention\-guided distillation framework with input\-dependent attention\-weighted feature fusion, which adaptively regulates the contribution of frozen distillation features to the prediction pathway\. The proposed approach leverages ImageNet\-pretrained weights and performs domain\-specific fine\-tuning on sports datasets\. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains\. On the multi\-sport classification dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0\.9752 and a Macro\-F1 score of 0\.9753, outperforming the evaluated CNN benchmarks and ViT variants\. For soccer match event classification, it achieves an accuracy of 0\.9863 and a Macro\-F1 score of 0\.9718, while ranking first in the TOPSIS evaluation\. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating parallel feedforward processing, transfer learning, and distillation\-guided feature fusion for sports image classification under complex visual conditions\.

## [Clinical validation of artificial intelligence for cancer detection prognosis and analysis across imaging modalities and tumor types](../publications/eb92fcedb6f66f74f547.md)

Nader A\. Rahman Mohamed

This study evaluates the diagnostic and prognostic performance of artificial intelligence in cancer detection across imaging modalities and tumor types\. The review synthesizes current evidence on deep learning, radiomics, multimodal integration, and precision oncology frameworks, with emphasis on validation quality and clinical translation\. A systematic review of 180 peer reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted\. Included investigations assessed artificial intelligence applications in radiology, digital pathology, endoscopy, PET imaging, and multimodal platforms\. Extracted data covered diagnostic accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, dataset size, validation strategy, and study design\. Subdomains included detection, prognosis, grading, survival prediction, radio\-genomics, explainability, federated learning, and regulatory evaluation\. Across breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, brain, and skin cancers, multiple high\-quality cohorts reported AUC values above 0\.90\. Whole slide histopathology achieved the highest discrimination, reaching AUC 0\.99 in curated datasets\. CT and MRI systems demonstrated strong performance with multicenter validation, including large scale lung and breast screening studies\. Radiomics contributed to survival prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, and molecular subtype inference\. Multimodal and transformer\-based architectures improved representation learning in volumetric and cross domain data\. Despite strong retrospective performance, only 21 percent of studies included external validation, 14 percent incorporated multicenter datasets, and 6 percent applied prospective or temporal validation\. Artificial intelligence shows consistent high performance in cancer detection and prognostic modeling across imaging domains\. Strongest evidence supports adjunctive use in screening, digital pathology, and endoscopic detection\. Broader clinical adoption requires prospective trials, multicenter external validation, standardized reporting, explainability integration, and alignment with regulatory frameworks to ensure reliable deployment in precision oncology\.

## [Ethical Challenges in Integrating Advanced Technology and AI into Nursing Education](../publications/eb9b877445e7b32fd155.md)

William G Zic

Background: Educational technology and artificial intelligence \(AI\) are transforming nursing education by expanding approaches to instruction, assessment, and clinical simulation\. These innovations offer opportunities to enhance learning while creating ethical, professional, and pedagogical challenges requiring thoughtful evaluation\. Purpose: This paper examines the ethical implications of integrating AI and educational technology into nursing education and explores strategies for implementation that preserve professional standards, equity, academic integrity, and educational quality\. Discussion: AI integration in nursing education raises concerns related to privacy, accessibility, digital competence, academic integrity, and the student\-faculty relationship\. Increased reliance on digital platforms requires strong data governance and compliance with regulations such as the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act \(FERPA\) to protect student information\. Limited access to technology may also contribute to educational inequities\. Faculty and student development are essential to promote responsible technology use\. Generative AI introduces concerns regarding plagiarism, misinformation, and potential effects on critical thinking and clinical reasoning\. Nursing programs must establish clear guidelines for ethical AI use while ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces faculty mentorship and human connection\. Ethical Analysis: Ethical technology integration should reflect nursing values of caring, compassion, justice, respect, and accountability\. AI can support learning, feedback, and clinical reasoning but should not replace professional judgment or moral responsibility\. The American Nurses Association emphasizes that AI should augment nursing practice while maintaining professional accountability \(ANA, 2015\)\. AI\-generated information should inform, not determine, high\-stakes academic decisions, with transparency, human oversight, and opportunities for review\. Implications and Conclusion: Ethical adoption of AI prepares future nurses for digital healthcare environments by strengthening technological literacy, ethical reasoning, and equitable access to learning\. Nurse educators play a critical role in modeling responsible technology use\. Successful integration requires faculty development, institutional support, and ethical frameworks that balance innovation with accountability while preserving nursing’s commitment to compassionate, evidence\-based care\.

## [pDOC\-STANet: A spatiotemporal attention network for automatic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness using fNIRS](../publications/eb9c8272c8cb4e7aa0ff.md)

Zehai Li; Yuxin Xing; Shuwei Wang; Ke Cui; Xiaobo Chen; Huijuan Wu; Yuyi Feng; Pengfei Yi; Sailing He

Abstract This study addresses the difficulty and subjectivity of assessing consciousness levels in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness \(pDOC\) by proposing an automated classification method based on functional near\-infrared spectroscopy \(fNIRS\)\. A spatiotemporal attention\-based feature\-fusion network, termed pDOC\-STANet, was developed\. The temporal branch extracts multiscale features using an improved InceptionTime architecture with squeeze\-and\-excitation modules, whereas the image branch represents each trial as channel\-wise Gramian Angular Difference Field \(GADF\) maps and processes the resulting 105 × 330 × 330 tensor with a modified ResNet18\. An attention\-fusion module adaptively integrates the two representations\. The model was evaluated using stratified, subject\-independent five\-fold cross\-validation, with all trials from each participant kept in the same fold\. pDOC\-STANet achieved an accuracy of 88\.72%, outperforming traditional machine\-learning methods and single\-branch deep\-learning baselines\. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of GADF encoding, dual\-branch modeling, and attention\-based fusion\. LIME and SHAP analyses further indicated that the model relied on discriminative channels in bilateral frontotemporal and prefrontal regions, with HbR\- and HbT\-related features making substantial contributions\. These results suggest that pDOC\-STANet is a promising framework for fNIRS\-based consciousness assessment, while external multi\-center validation remains necessary before broad clinical deployment\.

## [Pollutant Dispersion in and Around Buildings: A Critical Review of Modelling, Mitigation, and Future Opportunities](../publications/eb9ccdb07265ee4252e2.md)

Manash Jyoti Gogoi

Pollutant dispersion in and around buildings is governed by the coupled behavior of atmospheric flow, building aerodynamics, ventilation, source characteristics, and pollutant\-specific transport processes\. Openings, leakage, air intakes and exhausts cause an interaction between outdoor pollution and indoor emissions, resulting in spatially heterogeneous and time\-dependent concentrations\. This narrative review summarizes experimental and numerical studies on pollutant sources, transport, modelling, measurement and exposure mitigation\. Additionally, it focuses on validation against wind\-tunnel, tracer\-gas, and field measurements\. It compares Reynolds\-averaged Navier\-Stokes \(RANS\), large\-eddy simulation \(LES\), and transport\-based recurrence computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\), and it also compares URANS\. The reviewed literature shows that the prediction accuracy depends on inflow turbulence, source representation, geometry, numerical resolution, atmospheric stability, validation targets and turbulence closure\. While RANS provides an affordable alternative for engineering evaluation when necessary, LES can remove the effects of unsteady transport and concentration fluctuations; neither is dependable without application\-specific validation and verification\. The indoor\-outdoor coupling concept is effective depending on facade concentration, wind direction and opening configuration and shows dilution of indoor emissions and increased intake of outdoor air pollution\. These modelling limitations are connected to sensor placement, exposure assessment, and energy\-air\-quality trade\-offs through the synthesis\. The review does not provide complete coverage or combined effect estimates, as the literature collection was not achieved by a documented systematic search\. Priorities include reproducible benchmarks, uncertainty\-aware validation, indoor\-outdoor models by pollutant, and ventilation and filtration controls based on occupant exposure, energy demand, and robustness of operations\.

## [Externally validated machine learning models for prediction of treatment selection and clinical outcomes in posterior communicating artery aneurysms](../publications/eba9041207b520436f9b.md)

Vivek Sanker; Ethan Register; Adam T\. Eberle; Sania Javed; Brian W\. Paul; Christopher Chang; Kate N\. Jensen; Rahim Abo Kasem; Mustafa T\. Almosawi; Lea Scherschinski; Joshua S\. Catapano; Arnau Benet; Redi Rahmani; Michael T\. Lawton

Abstract Posterior communicating artery \(PCOM\) aneurysms account for approximately 25% of intracranial aneurysms and present clinical challenges regarding optimal treatment selection\. This study developed and validated machine learning models to predict treatment modality, complications, and functional outcomes in PCOM aneurysm management using a comprehensive institutional database of 75 patients treated between 2002 and 2023\. Five machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost—were systematically compared across 7 outcome variables: treatment type \(open vs\. endovascular\), specific open surgical treatment, specific endovascular treatment, intraoperative rupture, complications, angiographic obliteration, and discharge modified Rankin Scale score\. Models were developed using preoperative patient\-specific \(age, sex, family history\) and aneurysm\-specific \(size, presentation, morphology, location\) parameters, with rigorous preprocessing that included class\-balancing strategies, feature engineering, and regularization to minimize overfitting\. Cross\-validation performance demonstrated high accuracy for treatment prediction \(78\.7% Random Forest\), complications \(94\.7% Random Forest; however, sensitivity of 0% indicates that this accuracy should not be interpreted as clinically useful event detection\), intraoperative rupture \(92\.0% Random Forest\), and angiographic obliteration \(87\.3% Random Forest\)\. External validation on an independent cohort from the University of Louisville \(n=20–28; n=20 most complete cases for the primary external cohort, with up to n=28 for selected endpoints with available labels\) revealed variable generalizability: treatment prediction maintained 78\.1% accuracy, and complication prediction showed reduced external performance \(70\.3%\), highlighting institution\-specific factors\. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses demonstrated that class balancing significantly improved minority class recall \(0\.0% → 52\.2%–86\.3%\) for rare outcomes\. Feature importance analyses identified age, aneurysm size, admission modified Rankin Scale score, and Hunt\-Hess grade as the most influential predictors across multiple outcomes\. This study represents the first externally validated, multioutcome machine learning framework for PCOM aneurysm management, providing quantitative risk estimates and evidence\-based decision support for treatment selection and outcome prediction\.

## [Beyond the bluebook: a calibrated framework for redesigning construct\-valid assessment in higher education in the age of generative AI](../publications/ebad58d3e84069abf72f.md)

J\.M Shalani Dilinika

The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) has complicated the link between what a student submits as evidence of learning and what that student actually knows and can do\. In response, this study advances an AI\-resilient approach to assessment design through the development of a calibrated framework for redesigning construct\-valid assessment, based on a systematic review and synthesis of assessment frameworks and structured approaches\. Following PRISMA 2020 reporting guidance, sixteen primary assessment frameworks and structured approaches were identified\. The synthesis brought their complementary components together into three interdependent design constructs: authorisation, verification, and accountability\. Messick’s unified validity theory provides the conceptual anchor connecting these components to the inference an assessment is intended to support\. The synthesis revealed that the central gap in the literature is not a lack of relevant approaches or components, but calibration\. This gap informed the development of the Calibrated Framework for AI\-Resilient Assessment \(AIRA\), which proposes that verification and accountability should become stronger and more diverse as authorised GenAI involvement increases or becomes more consequential to the intended construct\. The framework provides educators with a guide for designing assessments and evaluating student learning in AI\-integrated environments\.

## [Tubuh Kristus Sebagai Metafora Sosial\-Eklesiologis Dalam Era Digital: Eklesiologi Kontekstual, Teologi Informasi, Dan Praksis Transformatif](../publications/ebafc3fcf034c1b5cd01.md)

Harapan Simatupang; Hari Pranoto

The rapid advancement of digital technology has fundamentally transformed how humans understand relationships, form communities, construct identity, and express spiritual experiences\. This transformation places the church at a crossroads between maintaining traditional ecclesiological patterns or conducting critical contextual reflection on changing times\. The metaphor of the body of Christ, which in Pauline theology encompasses relational, participatory, and ethical dimensions shaping a social and communal ecclesiology, has often been reduced to an internal doctrinal spiritual symbol detached from social realities and technological developments\. This study aims to reconstruct the body of Christ as a socio\-ecclesiological metaphor in the digital era to produce transformative church praxis for the church in Indonesia\. This research employs a qualitative\-theological reflective approach with a conceptual analysis model, integrating biblical theology, systematic theology, and digital contextual theology through critical dialogue across theological disciplines\. The findings indicate that the body of Christ must be understood as a living social\-incarnational reality that calls the Indonesian church to a transformative presence amid social fragmentation, religious pluralism, and digital technological disruption\. Analysis of 1 Corinthians 12, Romans 12, and Ephesians 4 reveals that this metaphor contains dimensions of social criticism, participatory ethics, and a call toward communal maturity that transcends individualistic and institutional understandings\. The reconstruction of this metaphor encourages the Indonesian church to move beyond narrow institutional understanding and embody its calling as an agent of social transformation faithful to the missio Dei, manifesting love, justice, and hope in the midst of a pluralistic and digitalized society\. This study contributes to contextual theology and digital ecclesiology by formulating an integrative framework that unites biblical theology, systematic theology, and digital contextual theology, positioning the body of Christ as both a normative theological concept and an ethical\-ecclesiological framework that restructures church praxis toward solidarity, participation, and missional orientation\. Perkembangan teknologi digital yang pesat telah secara mendasar mengubah cara manusia memahami relasi, membentuk komunitas, mengonstruksi identitas, dan mengekspresikan pengalaman spiritual\. Transformasi ini menempatkan gereja pada persimpangan jalan antara mempertahankan pola\-pola eklesiologis tradisional atau melakukan refleksi kritis kontekstual terhadap perubahan zaman\. Metafora tubuh Kristus yang dalam teologi Paulus mengandung dimensi relasional, partisipatif, dan etis yang membentuk eklesiologi sosial dan komunal, seringkali direduksi menjadi simbol spiritual doktrinal internal yang terlepas dari realitas sosial dan perkembangan teknologi\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merekonstruksi tubuh Kristus sebagai metafora sosial\-eklesiologis dalam era digital guna melahirkan praksis gereja yang transformatif bagi gereja di Indonesia\. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif\-teologis reflektif dengan model analisis konseptual, mengintegrasikan teologi biblika, teologi sistematika, dan teologi kontekstual digital melalui dialog kritis lintas disiplin teologi\. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa tubuh Kristus harus dipahami sebagai realitas sosial\-inkarnasional yang hidup yang memanggil gereja Indonesia untuk menghadirkan kehadiran transformatif di tengah fragmentasi sosial, pluralisme agama, dan disrupsi teknologi digital\. Analisis terhadap 1 Korintus 12, Roma 12, dan Efesus 4 mengungkapkan bahwa metafora ini mengandung dimensi kritik sosial, etika partisipatif, dan panggilan menuju kedewasaan komunal yang melampaui pemahaman individualistis dan institusional\. Rekonstruksi metafora ini mendorong gereja Indonesia untuk melampaui pemahaman institusional yang sempit dan menghidupi panggilannya sebagai agen transformasi sosial yang setia pada missio Dei, menghadirkan kasih, keadilan, dan pengharapan di tengah realitas masyarakat yang plural dan terdigitalisasi\. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi bagi teologi kontekstual dan eklesiologi digital dengan merumuskan kerangka integratif yang memadukan teologi biblika, teologi sistematika, dan teologi kontekstual digital, memposisikan tubuh Kristus sebagai konsep teologis normatif sekaligus kerangka etis\-eklesiologis yang menata ulang praksis gereja menuju solidaritas, partisipasi, dan orientasi misional\.

## [Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda](../publications/ebbbadfcd27f9878193c.md)

Minxian Xu; Jingfeng Wu; Shengye Song; Satish Narayana Srirama; Bahman Javad; Rajiv Ranjan; Devki Nandan Jha; Sa Wang; Wenhong Tian; Huanle Xu; Li Li; Zizhao Mo; Shuo Ren; Thomas Kunz; Petar Kochovski; Vlado Stankovski; Kejiang Ye; Chengzhong Xu; Rajkumar Buyya

ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models \(LLMs\) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures\. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads\. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference\. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence\. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization\. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators\. Results Our analysis reveals that supporting LLMs at scale requires a transition from general‐purpose cloud infrastructure toward LLM‐aware, cross‐layer, and adaptive systems\. Existing approaches have improved distributed execution, elastic resource management, multi‐tenant serving, and hardware utilization, but important gaps remain in cross‐layer coordination, workload‐aware orchestration, data and context management, interoperability, security, and system‐level optimization\. Based on these gaps, we develop a research agenda covering future directions in sparse and heterogeneous computation, LLM‐enhanced system software, prompt and context management, autonomous cloud management, decentralized intelligence, edge‐cloud collaboration, personalized LLM services, and emerging computing paradigms\. Conclusion Cloud‐native and distributed systems will play a central role in enabling the next generation of LLM services\. Future infrastructures should evolve toward more intelligent, elastic, interoperable, secure, and heterogeneous platforms that jointly optimize computation, memory, communication, data, and service objectives\. Continued advances in system design, standardization, and cross‐disciplinary collaboration will be essential for realizing scalable and sustainable LLM infrastructures\.

## [Ưng dụng mạng học sâu YOLOv26, đề xuất mô hình nhận diện xe cứu thương tại các nút giao thông trên thiết bị Raspberry Pi 5](../publications/ebc5bc50d690b6fba832.md)

Thuận Huỳnh Ngọc; Phẩm Phạm Như

Xe cứu thương là phương tiện giao thông ưu tiên làm nhiệm vụ vận chuyển và cấp cứu người bệnh trong các tình huống khẩn cấp, được phép vượt đèn đỏ khi thực hiện nhiệm vụ\. Tuy nhiên, do thường di chuyển với tốc độ cao, tín hiệu còi ưu tiên không đủ lớn để các phương tiện nhận biết, nhường đường kịp thời, dẫn đến chậm trễ thời gian hoặc thậm chí xảy ra nhiều vụ tai nạn giao thông đáng tiếc\. Trong bài nghiên cứu này, nhóm tác giả đề xuất ứng dụng thuật toán YOLOv26 để xây dựng mô hình nhận diện xe cứu thương tại các nút giao thông\. Mô hình sử dụng YOLOv26n để huấn luyện tập dữ liệu gồm 1,936 hình ảnh xe cứu thương và đạt được các chỉ số khả quan như Precision = 0\.96, Recall = 0\.818, mAP@50 = 0\.906 và mAP@50\-95 = 0\.694\. Hệ thống được triển khai thử nghiệm trên thiết bị Raspberry Pi 5 và thực hiện nhận diện xe cứu thương qua các đoạn video từ màn hình máy tính\. Kết quả thực nghiệm cho thấy mô hình có khả năng nhận diện tương đối chính xác với độ dự đón lên đến 89%, tốc độ xử lý trung bình đạt trên 10 FPS\. Mặc dù nghiên cứu mới dừng ở mức thử nghiệm, nhưng kết quả cho thấy tính khả thi, có khả năng phát triển ứng dụng trong các hệ thống giao thông thông minh\.

## [The Impact of Trait Mindfulness on Quality of Life in Patients With Bipolar Disorder: The Serial Mediating Role of Emotion Dysregulation and Depressive/Manic Symptoms](../publications/ebc87164bf5d20d9c917.md)

Yangyang Xu

Background: To explore the impact of trait mindfulness on the quality of life \(QoL\) in patients with bipolar disorder \(BD\) and to examine the serial mediating roles of emotion dysregulation and depressive/manic symptoms\. Methods: A cross\-sectional study based on previous medical record data was conducted\. Clinical records and scale data of 256 patients with BD who received outpatient or inpatient care at Xiamen Xianyue Hospital \(Xiamen Mental Health Center\) between June 2022 and June 2024 were extracted, all of whom carried a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition \(DSM\-5\) confirmed diagnosis\. All scale assessments had been completed at the time of the index clinical visit, including the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire \(FFMQ\), the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale \(DERS\), the Self\-Rating Depression Scale \(SDS\), the Bech\-Rafaelsen Mania Scale \(BRMS\), and the Brief Quality of Life in Bipolar Disorder scale \(Brief QoL\.BD\)\. Age, sex, bipolar subtype,illness duration,current mood state, and current pharmacological treatment were entered as covariates\. Two separate serial mediation models \(one with depressive symptoms and one with manic symptoms as the second\-stage mediator\) were tested using regression\-based mediation analysis with bias\-corrected bootstrapping \(5000 resamples\) under the PROCESS framework \(Model 6\)\. Results: Correlation analysis showed that trait mindfulness in patients with BD was significantly and positively correlated with QoL \(r = 0\.472, p &lt; 0\.001\), and significantly and negatively correlated with emotion dysregulation \(r =–0\.523, p &lt; 0\.001\), depressive symptoms \(r =–0\.457, p &lt; 0\.001\), and manic symptoms \(r =–0\.406, p&lt; 0\.001\)\. Serial mediation analysis revealed that the indirect effect of trait mindfulness on QoL through emotion dysregulation and depressive symptoms was 0\.086 \(95% CI \[0\.047, 0\.132\]\), with a model explanatory power \(adjusted R2 \) of 0\.385\. The indirect effect through emotion dysregulation and manic symptoms was 0\.052 \(95% CI \[0\.016, 0\.091\]\), with a model explanatory power \(adjusted R2\) of 0\.307\. Conclusions: In this cross\-sectional study based on previous medical record data, emotion dysregulation together with mood symptoms jointly served as a serial mediating chain linking trait mindfulness to QoL in patients with BD, and the depression\-related chain conveyed a stronger mediating effect than the mania\-related chain\. Above findings suggest that a higher level of trait mindfulness may be associated with better QoL through enhanced emotion regulation and milder depressive/manic symptoms, with the depressive pathway being the most salient\. The direction of these pathways still needs further verification by prospective designs\.

## [Diagnostic performance and energy consumption of deep learning models for dermoscopic image classification](../publications/ebd065292f666aee3c85.md)

Nur Ecer; Ayşegül Tel Kankılıç; Ömer Karakoyun; Bahadır Aslancan; Birol Kaldan

Deep\-learning models for dermoscopy are usually chosen on the basis of accuracy and discrimination, with limited attention to the energy and carbon costs that accompany model development, retraining, and clinical use\. If clinical AI is to be governed responsibly, these operational dimensions need to enter the discussion alongside conventional diagnostic metrics\. We compared three widely used dermoscopic classification architectures on both clinical performance and environmental cost, and asked how energy\-aware reporting might fit into the broader practice of clinical AI governance and algorithmovigilance\. The HAM10000 dataset \(10,015 dermatologist\-labelled dermoscopic images from 7470 unique lesions, seven diagnostic classes\) was split at the lesion level into training, validation, and test sets, so that every image of a given lesion was assigned to a single partition\. ResNet\-50, EfficientNet\-B3, and Vision Transformer B/16 were fine\-tuned in TensorFlow/Keras on a single NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPU\. Each architecture was trained three times; metrics were computed separately per run and are reported as mean ± standard deviation\. We measured accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\), macro\- and micro\-averaged sensitivity and specificity, per\-class sensitivity, and calibration \(expected calibration error, Brier score\), with lesion\-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals and Bonferroni\-corrected pairwise tests\. Training and inference energy were measured directly by sampling board\-level GPU power through the NVIDIA management interface; carbon emissions were re\-computed under four electricity\-grid scenarios\. No statistically significant difference in accuracy was detected between any pair of architectures \(ResNet\-50 0\.807 ± 0\.002, EfficientNet\-B3 0\.817 ± 0\.002, Vision Transformer B/16 0\.808 ± 0\.006\)\. Vision Transformer B/16 required 3\.07 times the training energy of EfficientNet\-B3 \(0\.0630 ± 0\.0038 vs 0\.0205 ± 0\.0010 kWh per run\) and 4\.32 times the inference energy \(0\.307 vs 0\.071 Wh per 1,000 images\), without a detectable advantage on accuracy \(− 0\.89 percentage points, 95% CI − 2\.47 to \+ 0\.64\), AUROC \(\+ 0\.0026, 95% CI − 0\.0034 to \+ 0\.0090\) or melanoma sensitivity \(\+ 0\.044, 95% CI − 0\.026 to \+ 0\.109\)\. The comparison between the two convolutional networks was different in kind: EfficientNet\-B3 consumed 43% more training energy than ResNet\-50 and returned a significantly higher melanoma sensitivity \(\+ 0\.102, 95% CI \+ 0\.038 to \+0\.167\)\. Parameter count did not predict energy use—the 10\.8\-million\-parameter EfficientNet\-B3 consumed more training energy than the 23\.6\-million\-parameter ResNet\-50\. Thermal\-design\-power estimates of inference energy were 2\.7–13\.8 times the measured values\. Changing the electricity grid changed absolute emissions but left the ranking of the three architectures unchanged\. Energy is not a decision rule on its own, but it cannot enter a decision at all unless it is measured\. Measuring it here produced two different answers rather than one: additional energy corresponded to a statistically significant and potentially clinically important absolute gain in melanoma sensitivity in one comparison, and to no detectable gain in the other\. We do not claim that Vision Transformer B/16 and EfficientNet\-B3 are equivalent—the study was not designed as a non\-inferiority comparison and no clinical margin was pre\-specified—but an advantage that cannot be demonstrated does not discharge the burden of justifying a threefold difference in energy use\. We argue that energy use, carbon emissions, hardware configuration, calibration, and inference cost should be reported in clinical AI studies as a matter of course, and integrated into pre\-deployment evaluation and post\-market monitoring of medical imaging models\.

## [Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search\-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence](../publications/ebd6a3eea34173722b24.md)

Owen Walters; Lihu Chen; Francesca Toni

Web search allows LLMs to access up\-to\-date information, but it remains unclear why they sometimes produce outdated answers even when relevant evidence is available\. To study this problem, we construct temporal facts whose values changed after the models&\#x27; training cutoffs\. We evaluate one proprietary model under deployed web search and six open\-weight model configurations under controlled retrieval\. We find that models often answer from search snippets without opening the source pages, which is associated with higher rates of outdated answers and unfaithful citations\. Our controlled experiments and layer\-wise analysis reveal a gap between the availability of evidence and its effective use\. Even when retrieved evidence influences internal predictions, models may still favour outdated information in their final answers\. We hope these findings will help advance research on the reliable use of retrieved evidence in search\-augmented LLMs\.

## [Osteoartrite sintomática, dor crônica e sintomas depressivos em idosos: Uma revisão sistemática](../publications/ebdaf3e3d5bd4f080670.md)

Ana Sophia Paraguay Figueiredo; Breno Reis Machado; Igor Almeida Gomes; Joäo Vitor Lopes de Medeiros Gonçalves; Lucas Ribeiro de Moraes Freitas; Marcus Ivanovith Fernandes; Patrick Oliveira Matos

Objetivo: avaliar a associação entre a osteoartrite \(OA\) sintomática de joelho e/ou quadril, a dor crônica e os sintomas depressivos em idosos, sintetizando a direção, a consistência e a certeza da evidência\. Metodologia: revisão sistemática sem metanálise, conduzida segundo o PRISMA 2020, com buscas nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase e Scopus \(2011–2026\)\. Foram incluídos estudos observacionais em idosos que avaliaram a associação entre OA/dor e sintomas depressivos aferidos por instrumentos validados\. O risco de viés foi avaliado pela escala de Newcastle\-Ottawa e a certeza da evidência pelo sistema GRADE; a síntese seguiu as diretrizes SWiM, por contagem de votos da direção do efeito\. Resultados: foram incluídos 22 estudos \(14 transversais e 8 longitudinais\), provenientes de dez países\. Em 19 estudos observou\-se associação positiva entre OA/dor e sintomas depressivos, dois apresentaram achados nulos, um não estimou a associação e nenhum relatou associação inversa\. A associação mostrou\-se mais consistente quando a exposição foi a dor do que quando foi a gravidade radiográfica e manteve\-se nas sete famílias de instrumentos empregadas\. A exclusão dos estudos de maior risco de viés não alterou a direção do achado\. A certeza da evidência foi baixa\. Conclusão: há associação predominantemente positiva entre OA sintomática/dor crônica e sintomas depressivos em idosos, mais vinculada ao sofrimento sintomático do que ao dano estrutural, embora com baixa certeza da evidência, o que reforça a importância do rastreamento de depressão nessa população\.

## [Needle\-knife lumbosacral therapy for lumbar disc herniation: a single\-center, outcome assessor\-blinded randomized controlled trial](../publications/ebe6ce739799edac4592.md)

Yiming Zhang; Ruiguo Li; Xiao Zhang; Zhanyou Wang; Ziwei Zhang; Huanhuan Xu; Xiaofan Li

Background Lumbar disc herniation \(LDH\) is a common spinal disorder causing significant pain and dysfunction\. Traditional acupuncture is a widely used non\-pharmacological treatment for LDH\. Recently, needle\-knife therapy has emerged as a potential alternative\. Objective This study aims to explore the clinical efficacy of needle\-knife lumbosacral therapy for LDH and compare its advantages with those of conventional acupuncture therapy\. Methods This study adopted an outcome assessor\-blinded randomized controlled trial design\. A total of 74 patients with LDH were enrolled and randomly assigned to the experimental group \( n = 37\), which received needle\-knife lumbosacral therapy, or the control group \( n = 37\), which received conventional acupuncture at the same anatomical treatment sites\. Seventy patients completed the 2\-week treatment and 3\-month follow\-up\. Visual analog scale \(VAS\) and Oswestry Disability Index \(ODI\) were designated as primary repeated outcomes; lumbar flexion mobility \(LFM\) was a secondary repeated outcome, and inflammatory cytokines served as non\-repeated secondary outcomes\. Mixed\-effects linear models were used for repeated measurements, with the group\-by\-time interaction predefined as the primary estimand\. Bonferroni correction was applied for the three repeated outcomes \(VAS, ODI, and three LFM components\), setting an adjusted significance threshold of α = 0\.017\. Unadjusted α = 0\.05 was adopted for inflammatory cytokines\. VAS, ODI, and LFM were evaluated at baseline, post\-treatment, and 3\-month follow\-up; inflammatory markers \(TNF\-α, IL\-6, IL\-1β\) were detected at baseline and post\-treatment only\. Adverse events were monitored throughout the trial\. Patient recruitment was conducted from March 15, 2025, to July 15, 2025, and the final follow\-up was performed on November 18, 2025\. Results Both groups demonstrated within\-group reductions in VAS and ODI scores across all time points\. For the prespecified group\-by\-time interaction analyses under Bonferroni correction \( α = 0\.017\), the needle\-knife group showed significantly larger longitudinal improvements than the acupuncture group for both primary outcomes: VAS interaction \(95% CI: 0\.21–0\.83\), adjusted p = 0\.001; ODI interaction \(95% CI: 1\.89–4\.35\), adjusted p &lt; 0\.0001\. At post\-treatment, the model\-based between\-group differences \(needle\-knife minus acupuncture\) were VAS: −1\.16 \(95% CI: −1\.78 to −0\.54\), adjusted p = 0\.0004; ODI: −3\.78 \(95% CI: −4\.95 to −2\.61\), adjusted p &lt; 0\.0001\. At 3\-month follow\-up, sustained between\-group differences were VAS: −0\.43 \(95% CI: −0\.68 to −0\.18\), adjusted p = 0\.001; ODI: −1\.89 \(95% CI: −2\.56 to −1\.22\), adjusted p &lt; 0\.0001\. For LFM components, all three subindices showed greater numerical improvements in the needle\-knife group, but their group\-by\-time interaction adjusted p \-values exceeded the 0\.017 threshold: lumbar flexion \(95% CI: 0\.62–5\.00\), adjusted p = 0\.034; left lateral flexion \(95% CI: −1\.02 to 2\.42\), adjusted p = 0\.423; right lateral flexion \(95% CI: −1\.10 to 1\.92\), adjusted p = 0\.594\. Among serum inflammatory biomarkers, only IL\-6 showed a statistically significant unadjusted between\-group difference at post\-treatment: IL\-6 difference = −0\.47 ng·L \(95% CI: −0\.89 to −0\.05\), unadjusted p = 0\.03; TNF\-α difference = −0\.18 ng·L \(95% CI: −0\.52 to 0\.16\), unadjusted p = 0\.30; IL\-1β difference = −0\.13 ng·L \(95% CI: −0\.37 to 0\.11\), unadjusted p = 0\.28\. No serious adverse events were reported\. Conclusion Two\-week lumbosacral needle\-knife therapy effectively relieves pain and lumbar dysfunction in LDH patients, with statistically verified sustained superiority over conventional acupuncture for VAS and ODI under the Bonferroni\-adjusted threshold \( α = 0\.017\)\. Although numerical advantages in lumbar mobility were observed in the needle\-knife group, these differences did not reach the prespecified adjusted significance level after multiple testing correction\. As an outcome assessor\-blinded exploratory trial with unmasked participants and therapists, large\-sample and multicenter clinical studies are needed to further verify the conclusions, and future trials should optimize blinding schemes to reduce reporting bias\. Clinical trial registration https://itmctr\.ccebtcm\.org\.cn/mgt/project/user/approved\-list , identifier \(ITMCTR2025002191\)\.

## [The impact of artificial intelligence on ensuring cybersecurity in enterprises](../publications/ebe72930ea5b4f804e9a.md)

Patricija Očkerl

Umetna inteligenca predstavlja eno izmed tehnologij, ki pomembno spreminjajo področje kibernetske varnosti v podjetjih\. Njena uporaba omogoča učinkovitejše zaznavanje kibernetskih groženj, hitrejšo analizo varnostnih dogodkov ter podporo pri odzivanju na incidente\. Hkrati razvoj generativne umetne inteligence ustvarja nove možnosti za izvajanje kibernetskih napadov, saj lahko napadalci tehnologijo uporabijo za pripravo bolj prepričljivih sporočil ribarjenja, socialni inženiring ter ustvarjanje globoko ponarejenih vsebin\. Magistrsko delo obravnava različne vidike uporabe umetne inteligence pri zagotavljanju kibernetske varnosti v podjetjih ter povezuje njene obrambne zmogljivosti z novimi tveganji, ki jih prinaša njena zloraba\. Posebna pozornost je namenjena uporabi umetne inteligence pri zaznavanju in analizi groženj, podpori varnostnim analitikom ter avtomatizaciji posameznih varnostnih procesov\. Obravnavani so tudi konkretni primeri uporabe rešitev Microsoft Security Copilot, Darktrace in CrowdStrike Charlotte AI ter primeri zlorabe umetne inteligence pri ribarjenju, globoko ponarejenih prevarah in socialnem inženiringu\. Analiza kaže, da umetna inteligenca pomembno prispeva k hitrejši obdelavi velike količine varnostnih podatkov, prepoznavanju vzorcev in podpori varnostnim ekipam\. Njena uporaba pa hkrati povečuje učinkovitost napadalcev, predvsem pri ustvarjanju bolj prepričljivih in prilagojenih vsebin\. Ugotovitve tako potrjujejo dvojno vlogo umetne inteligence v kibernetski varnosti\. Za učinkovito zaščito podjetij zato niso dovolj zgolj tehnološke rešitve, temveč so pomembni tudi strokovni nadzor, ustrezno upravljanje tveganj, varnostni postopki ter ozaveščanje in usposabljanje zaposlenih\.

## [Intentionality, Reduction, and the Life\-World in Edmund Husserl: A Systematic Inquiry](../publications/ebecffa1c79df6d9014a.md)

FATIMA KOÇ; Ahmet Dağ

This study aims to systematically examine the fundamental concepts of Edmund Husserl&\#x27;s phenomenological philosophy\. Husserl developed an original method in 20th\-century philosophy, thereby reestablishing the structure of consciousness and the subject\-object relationship\. This reestablishment effort takes shape particularly through his critique of naturalism and psychologism\. In this context, the study addresses the central concepts of Husserl&\#x27;s phenomenology—intentionality, phenomenological reduction, epoche, transcendental idealism, and the life\-world\. These concepts are closely interrelated and constitute different aspects of the phenomenological method\. In addition, Husserl&\#x27;s critique of positivism and his thoughts concerning the crisis of European sciences, along with the epistemological and ontological dimensions of the phenomenological method, are examined\. Indeed, Husserl&\#x27;s call &quot;to the things themselves,&quot; the intentional structure of consciousness, and the concept of the life\-world offer original responses to the fundamental problems of modern philosophy\. In conclusion, it is emphasized that phenomenology is not merely a method but also a search for a new foundation for science and philosophy\. İn this respect, Edmund Husserl&\#x27;s thought not only offers a theoretical framework but also allows for a deeper understanding of the relationship between humans and the world\. By revealing the constitutive role of consciousness, it makes visible how meaning is formed and through what structures experience is shaped\. Thus, it gives a new direction to philosophical thought\.

## [Transformation of Approaches to Teaching Programming and Software Development under Influence of Generative AI](../publications/ebeef7c04eced680c920.md)

Mikhail Mikhailovich Abramskiy; Gökay Ozdemir; Ilmira Khamitova; Irina Shapkina

This paper considers key transformational processes occurring in programming and software development training under the influence of generative artificial intelligence\. Based on a series of interviews with junior students, a behavioral pattern leading to degrading skills of algorithmic thinking and problem decomposition is identified\. A quantitative analysis of undergraduate theses from the Institute of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems \(ITIS\) at Kazan Federal University \(KFU\) over the past three years demonstrated a significant increase in AI usage in project work and the independent development of skills for utilizing LLMs in professional practice\. The drawbacks of the uncontrolled use of generative AI in the educational process and the need to develop sustainable competence in using these tools in professional software development activities are shown\. A three\-tiered solution is proposed: improving assessment through analysis of the process and style of coding; regulating the use of LLM in project activities and final theses with an emphasis on assessing applicability of AI; and integrating AI tools into teacher work to update content and provide feedback\. The proposed approaches have both conceptual and practiceoriented nature and aim to transform the process of training software developers in the context of the widespread adoption of AI tools in IT\-industry\.

## [FORMAÇÃO CONTINUADA DE PROFESSORES PARA O USO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: DESAFIOS E POSSIBILIDADES NA EDUCAÇÃO SUPERIOR](../publications/ebf3294d5e7052d2c083.md)

Edilon Souza Lessa; Eliane Gomes Duarte; Iolanda Pereira Savi; Nara LÍgia Pereira; Jorge José Klauch

O estudo analisou os desafios e as possibilidades da formação continuada de professores para o uso da inteligência artificial na educação superior, considerando dimensões pedagógicas, éticas, tecnológicas e institucionais relacionadas à incorporação dessas ferramentas às práticas docentes\. A pesquisa foi orientada pela seguinte questão: quais foram os principais desafios e possibilidades da formação continuada de professores para o uso da inteligência artificial na educação superior? O objetivo geral consistiu em analisar os desafios e as possibilidades da formação continuada de professores para o uso da inteligência artificial na educação superior\. Especificamente, buscou\-se identificar os principais desafios pedagógicos, éticos, tecnológicos e institucionais relacionados à formação continuada de professores para o uso da inteligência artificial na educação superior e analisar as possibilidades da formação continuada para o desenvolvimento de competências que favorecessem a integração crítica, ética e pedagogicamente orientada da inteligência artificial às práticas docentes no ensino superior\. Metodologicamente, o estudo caracterizou\-se como pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa, fundamentada em Santana, Narciso e Fernandes \(2025\), mediante leitura analítica e comparativa de produções científicas recentes\. Os resultados evidenciaram dificuldades relacionadas à formação insuficiente, à confiabilidade das informações, à autoria, à integridade acadêmica, à privacidade, aos vieses algorítmicos e à ausência de diretrizes institucionais\. Concluiu\-se que a formação continuada favoreceu o desenvolvimento de competências digitais, pedagógicas, éticas e críticas necessárias à integração responsável da IA no ensino superior\.

## [Effect of FDM process parameters on the mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties of PLA/Cu composite](../publications/ebf90a0f56a2468baa78.md)

Rajan Kumaresan; Yanis Petit; Antoine Cartier Millon; Xavier Legrand; Krishnan M\. Kanny; Mohan Turup Pandurangan

This study focuses on the effect of process parameters to enhance the mechanical properties of PLA/ Cu composite\. The selected parameters includes of infill pattern \(concentric, rectilinear and honeycomb\), raster angle \(0º, 45º and 90º\) and layer thickness \(0\.10, 0\.15 and 0\.20 mm\)\.
