## [Peptide\-modified nanocellulose from dairy waste for organic compound removal in dairy wastewater](../publications/ec0684f46e3dc4a85224.md)

Saeedeh Rastgar; Parichehr Hanachi; Tony Robert Walker

Dairy effluent with a high organic loading demands efficient and sustainable treatment solutions\. This work aimed to produce a peptide\-modified crystalline nanocellulose \(PCN C \) bio\-adsorbent from dairy sludge and crustacean waste to remove organic compounds from industrial dairy wastewater\. To optimize operational variables for maximum removal of chemical oxygen demand \(COD\), 5\-day biochemical oxygen demand \(BOD₅\) and total organic carbon \(TOC\), response surface methodology \(RSM\) was applied based on a central composite design \(CCD\)\. Operational variables were pH \(3–10\), adsorbent dosage \(100–500 mg L⁻1\), contact time \(15–55 min\), peptide\-to\-cellulose mass ratio \(0\.5:1–3:1\) and temperature \(15–55 °C\)\. The effective functionalization of the peptide and formation of a mesoporous structure with good thermal stability were validated by characterization using FESEM, XRD, FTIR, BET and TGA/DTG\. Under the optimal conditions \(pH 6\.5, PCN C dose of 300 mg L⁻1, contact time of 35 min, peptide\-to\-cellulose mass ratio of 3:1 and temperature of 25 °C\), the maximum removal efficiencies were 97\.80%, 93\.60% and 96\.40% for COD, BOD₅ and TOC, respectively\. The most significant factors were pH and PCN C dose according to analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) \( p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. The quadratic models showed high predictive ability \(R2 = 0\.9519\) and were experimentally validated with a relative error of &lt; 0\.50%\. Furthermore, PCN C showed good reusability, with removal efficiencies of nearly 95% for COD, 92% for BOD₅ and 89% for TOC after five successive adsorption–desorption cycles\. Generally, our results highlight the potential of PCN C as a bio\-based adsorbent for dairy wastewater treatment while promoting waste valorization and circular economy concepts\.

## [Plataformas distribuidas para reconocimiento de placas en sistemas inteligentes de transporte : estudio comparativo y evaluación de plataformas de aprendizaje federado\.](../publications/ec0f76d73da8b7ab2913.md)

N\.M\.\(Nayeli Micaela\) Tello Florez

El presente Trabajo de Integración Curricular realiza un estudio comparativo y la evaluación de plataformas de Aprendizaje Federado, con el propósito de seleccionar una plataforma base aplicable a escenarios de Sistemas Inteligentes de Transporte en un entorno simulado\. Para ello, se analiza el estado del arte de las principales plataformas disponibles, se establecen criterios técnicos y operativos de evaluación y se desarrolla una prueba piloto que permite validar la plataforma seleccionada mediante diferentes escenarios experimentales\. El documento se estructura en cinco capítulos\. El primero presenta la introducción del trabajo, el objetivo general, los objetivos específicos, el alcance y el marco teórico que fundamenta la investigación\. El segundo capítulo describe la metodología empleada, la cual comprende la comparación teórica de plataformas de Aprendizaje Federado, la definición de los parámetros de evaluación, el análisis comparativo, la selección de la plataforma y el diseño de una prueba piloto en un entorno virtualizado para la ejecución del plan de pruebas\. En el tercer capítulo se presentan los resultados obtenidos, el análisis de las métricas de rendimiento y consumo de recursos, la evaluación final de la plataforma seleccionada, la discusión de los resultados y las conclusiones y recomendaciones\. Finalmente, el cuarto capítulo corresponde a las referencias bibliográficas y el quinto reúne los anexos que complementan el desarrollo de la investigación\.

## [Case Report: Abdominal pseudohernia preceding the herpes rash: a pre\-eruptive diagnostic pitfall in herpes zoster](../publications/ec12a5240927b2923b96.md)

Binbin Huang; Jia Lin; Xiaomo Wu

Herpes zoster is usually recognized by its painful dermatomal eruption, although its motor complications are often overlooked\. Herpes zoster–associated abdominal pseudohernia is a rare segmental motor manifestation in which paresis of the abdominal wall muscles produces a unilateral bulge without a true fascial defect\. In most patients with herpes zoster, the bulge develops 1 to several weeks after the rash; in a minority of patients, it precedes the eruption, creating a particular risk of misdiagnosis\. Herein, we describe a 66\-year\-old man with controlled diabetes and hypertension who developed a painful left abdominal bulge 4 days before the appearance of skin lesions\. Routine laboratory tests were unremarkable, and abdominal computed tomography results showed no fascial defect or alternative structural cause of the bulge\. Four days after the appearance of the bulge, erythema and grouped vesicles developed over the left T10–T12 dermatomes without crossing the midline\. Before the dermatology visit, the patient had undergone lamp\-fire moxibustion of the affected area as a folk remedy, after which the lesions rapidly crusted and the patient developed extensive postinflammatory hyperpigmentation\. No fresh vesicles were present at dermatologic examination\. A presumptive clinical diagnosis of herpes zoster–associated abdominal pseudohernia was made based on the segmental abdominal bulge, dermatomal distribution of the skin changes, and the reported history of a vesicular eruption\. With conservative management, the bulge markedly regressed within 3 months\. This case highlights that a new unilateral segmental abdominal bulge, even when it precedes the characteristic rash, should prompt consideration of herpes zoster to avoid unnecessary surgical intervention\.

## [The moderating effect of cognitive re\-evaluation on the relationship between superficial performance and job burnout in psychiatric nurses](../publications/ec1680e5b033a73ccdd0.md)

Shasha Hong; Shuhui Huang; Mianmian Zhu; Aimin Jin; Qihao Zhang; Anmeng Huang; Lu Wang

Background Demand for emotional labor is increasing among psychiatric nurses who are now more at risk for job burnout, and emotional labor strategies or emotion regulation styles may be important mechanisms in this process\. Aim The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationships among emotional labor, emotion regulation, and job burnout in psychiatric nurses, and to examine cognitive reappraisal as a potential moderator of the relationship between surface acting and burnout\. Methods During January\-February 2025, a cross\-sectional survey was performed among on\-duty nurses in a tertiary psychiatric hospital located in Zhejiang Province, China\. Emotional labor, emotion regulation, job burnout, nursing professional values, perceived decent work and innovative capacity were assessed using validated Chinese scales\. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, multiple linear regression, hierarchical moderation analysis, and simple slope analysis were performed\. Regression assumptions, multicollinearity, and common method bias were additionally assessed\. Results Of 245 returned questionnaires, 241 were included in the final analysis\. After adjustment for demographic and work\-related factors, surface acting was positively associated with job burnout \(β = 0\.416, 95% CI: 0\.249–0\.582, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas cognitive reappraisal was inversely associated with burnout \(β = −0\.419, 95% CI: −0\.560 to −0\.278, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The surface acting × cognitive reappraisal interaction was statistically significant but small \(β = −0\.137, 95% CI: −0\.238 to −0\.036, ΔR² = 0\.019, f² = 0\.032, p = 0\.008\)\. Conclusion Higher surface acting was associated with higher job burnout, whereas higher cognitive reappraisal was associated with lower burnout\. Cognitive reappraisal also showed a small moderating association, with the positive association between surface acting and burnout becoming weaker at higher levels of reappraisal\. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal direction and practical relevance of these associations\.

## [FROM ATTENTION TO TASK COMPLETION: MAPPING BEHAVIORAL AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONING DIFFICULTIES ASSOCIATED WITH ADHD AMONG ELEMENTARY STUDENTS](../publications/ec1ef5d38765bf54a6bf.md)

Ayesha Raza; Sana Younas; Faisal Amjad

The research aimed to find out how many elementary school students had trouble with attention concentration impulse control, task completion, and organization\. Quantitative methods were used and students were surveyed once\. Multistage stratified random sampling was used to select 389 public and private school students in Punjab\. Teachers assessed the children by a 50 item questionnaire about different areas of functioning like attention and concentration, impulse control and behavioral regulation, task initiation and completion, and organization and executive functioning\. The researchers used many statistical methods to analyze the data including frequencies and percentages, descriptive statistics, independent\-samples t tests, one\-way analysis of variance, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, and multiple regression\. The concrete results showed that 51\.4% of students faced moderate problems and 24\.2% faced high problems\. Attention and concentration were identified as the major issues, followed by task completion\. Students who had been recognized as having attention, behavioral, or learning difficulties, got Quite a bit higher scores\. Authors of the paper believed that regular educational screening, formal classroom routines, behavioral classroom support, breaking tasks into smaller parts, allowing for some movement, teaching organizational skills, and multidisciplinary referral were necessary\.

## [Simultaneous occurrence of HER2 mutation and PD\-L1 high expression in EGFR\-mutant NSCLC: a case report](../publications/ec1ff914edb664ba8da6.md)

Yunxia Su; Huanzhang Su; 林建光

In non\-small cell lung cancer \(NSCLC\), EGFR and HER2 mutations are generally considered mutually exclusive events, with a co\-occurrence probability estimated to be less than 1%\. Patients with either EGFR or HER2 mutations tend to exhibit low PD\-L1 expression levels\. The simultaneous presence of both EGFR and HER2 mutations accompanied by high PD\-L1 expression is exceedingly rare\. This study reports a female patient who was admitted to the hospital after a routine physical examination revealed a right lung nodule and was diagnosed with “right lung adenocarcinoma \(cT2aN2aM1c1, IVA; EGFR 21 L858R mutation; HER2 exon 8 mutation; PD\-L1 TPS 60%\)\.” The patient was immediately started on first\-line third\-generation EGFR\-targeted therapy \(Furmonertinib\), but disease progression occurred after just 4\.4 months \(malignant pleural effusion and pericardial effusion\)\. As the patient refused repeat biopsy, treatment with an ADC drug \(Trastuzumab rezetecan\) was initiated\. Disease control was achieved after only one cycle of treatment, and the regimen was continued thereafter\. The progression\-free survival has exceeded 5\.3 months, and at the time of writing this report, the disease remained well\-controlled\. This paper presents the first report of this rare and therapeutically challenging combination of molecular pathological features—concurrent EGFR and HER2 mutations with high PD\-L1 expression in an NSCLC patient\. When standard first\-line third\-generation EGFR\-TKIs proved ineffective, the successful use of an anti\-HER2 ADC drug to control the tumor demonstrates its potential clinical value\. However, whether all patients initially presenting with this pathological molecular subtype will achieve consistent efficacy remains to be further investigated\.

## [Lifetime maternal stress, fetal sex, and microRNAs in prenatal extracellular vesicles and placenta in relation to children’s internalizing problems](../publications/ec3131e860e666c7d66c.md)

Rosalind J\. Wright; Rosalind J\. Wright; Hachem Saddiki; Regina Dominguez; Hoatian Wu; Whitney Cowell; Robert O\. Wright; Robert O\. Wright; Andrea Baccarelli; Elena Colicino

Abstract Background Prenatal stress predicts offspring anxiety and depressive disorders and placental microRNA \(miRNA\) signaling in a sex\-specific manner\. Methods We prospectively examined associations of miRNAs measured in placental tissue and in extracellular vesicles \(EVs\) from prenatal maternal blood with preschool Child Behavior Checklist \(CBCL\) outcomes \[Total Problems, Internalizing Problems, Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders\-oriented scales for Anxiety and Affective Problems\]\. We first used Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regressions embedded in a stability selection procedure to identify miRNAs most consistently associated with CBCL outcomes\. Then multivariable linear regressions examined all selected miRNAs in relation to each outcome within a single model\. Finally, we examined miRNA\-CBCL associations stratified by lifetime maternal stress measured prenatally and fetal sex and fit models including a three\-way interaction term for stress, sex, and miRNA expression\. Results Among miRNAs selected by the machine learning models, miR\-330\-5p in blood EVs and miR\-548aw in placenta emerged as top candidates related to CBCL outcomes\. When jointly considering fetal sex and lifetime maternal stress as modifiers, the association between blood miR\-330\-5p and affective problems was positive in females exposed to low stress \(β: 0\.73, 95%CI: 0\.15, 1\.3\) but negative in males with high stress exposure \(β: \-1\.64, 95%CI: \-3\.01, \-0\.28\), pint=0\.03\. Placental Let\-7b expression was negatively associated with total problems among males with high stress exposure \(β: \-6\.58, 95%CI: \-12\.45, \-0\.71\) but positively associated among males with low stress \(β: 3\.63, 95%CI: 1\.26, 6\.01\), pint=0\.04\. Top KEGG pathways included Hippo, FoxO, and PI3K/mTOR signaling\. Conclusions Prenatal miRNA signaling may play a role in sex\-specific lifetime maternal stress effects on neuropsychological development\.

## [Reprocessing Mass Spectra from Therapeutic Drug Monitoring to Unveil Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and Quantify Phenoconversion of Escitalopram Metabolism in CYP2C19 ‐Genotyped Patients](../publications/ec44f83065f119044016.md)

Kristine Hole; Birgit Malene Wollmann; Julia V\. Stingl; Espen Molden

Escitalopram is a frequently prescribed antidepressant drug\. CYP2C19 genotype is a major determinant of escitalopram metabolism and treatment outcome\. However, real\-life studies show a high degree of genotype\-phenotype mismatch in escitalopram metabolism\. The present study aimed to identify comedication with proton pump inhibitors \(PPIs\) and quantify phenoconversion of escitalopram metabolism in CYP2C19\-genotyped patients by reprocessing high\-resolution mass spectra from therapeutic drug monitoring \(TDM\) analyses\. Patients were included from a combined TDM/pharmacogenetics \(PGx\) laboratory facility in Oslo, Norway\. TDM profiles of escitalopram and CYP2C19 genotypes were available in the laboratory database\. Reprocessing of high\-resolution mass spectra by exact mass and fragment detection identified possible comedication with pantoprazole, esomeprazole/omeprazole or lansoprazole using mzCloud reference library\. Patients were grouped as normal metabolizers \(NMs\), intermediate metabolizers \(IMs\), poor metabolizers \(PMs\), rapid metabolizers \(RM\), or ultrarapid metabolizers \(UM\)\. Primary outcome measure was N\-desmethylescitalopram\-to\-escitalopram metabolic ratio \(MR; CYP2C19 biomarker\) in UMs vs\. PMs\. 2818 patients were included, constituting 2373 without and 445 \(15\.8%\) with PPIs\. Most patients were females \(64\.2%\)\. Regarding CYP2C19 phenotype distribution, the cohort comprised 39\.3% NMs, 29\.3% IMs, 2\.6% PMs, 24\.6% RMs, and 4\.2% UMs\. Escitalopram MR was 4\.5\-fold higher in CYP2C19 UMs vs\. PMs without PPIs \(P &lt; 0\.001\), while this difference was 2\.8\-fold in pantoprazole users \(P &lt; 0\.001\), and 1\.8\-fold in esomeprazole/omeprazole users \(P = 0\.2\)\. In conclusion, PPIs show significant phenoconversion of CYP2C19\-mediated escitalopram metabolism with esomeprazole/omeprazole exhibiting a stronger effect than pantoprazole\. The novel method for identification of interacting comedications in TDM samples illustrates the innovative potential of high\-resolution mass spectrometry in precision medicine\.

## [Optimizing entropy\-based heart rate variability metrics: fixed tolerance improves congestive heart failure classification](../publications/ec4559d1066b25418e9e.md)

Anton Petaja; Teemu Pukkila; Matias Kanniainen; E\. Räsänen

OBJECTIVE: Entropy\-based heart rate variability \(HRV\) metrics are widely used to characterize heartbeat dynamics and distinguish physiological from pathological states, but their classification performance is highly sensitive to parameter selection\. This study investigated a fixed\-tolerance approach derived from a healthy reference population as an alternative to conventional subject\-specific tolerance normalization and assessed how entropy\-parameter selection influences classification performance\. Approach: Approximate entropy \(ApEn\), sample entropy \(SampEn\), and multiscale entropy \(MSE\) were evaluated using both conventional and fixed\-tolerance formulations in 24\-hour Holter recordings from 274 healthy subjects and 946 patients with congestive heart failure \(CHF\)\. Classification performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\)\. Parameter sensitivity was assessed through systematic sweeps of the embedding dimension, tolerance coefficient, and MSE scale range\. Main results: Classification performance varied substantially across the parameter space, and the embedding\-dimension and tolerance values commonly used in the literature were generally suboptimal\. The fixed\-tolerance implementation consistently outperformed the conventional subject\-specific approach, achieving AUC values of 0\.78 \(\+0\.03\) for ApEn, 0\.77 \(\+0\.09\) for SampEn, and 0\.74 \(\+0\.14\) for MSE\. For MSE, tolerance selection had a substantially larger influence on classification performance than scale\-dependent parameterization\. Significance: The results suggest that a substantial portion of the classification potential of entropy\-based HRV analysis remains unexploited under conventional tolerance normalization and parameter selection\. More generally, entropy\-based HRV metrics appear to be more sensitive to methodological choices than is commonly assumed\. The fixed\-tolerance approach provides a simple and computationally inexpensive strategy for improving entropy\-based CHF classification, although validation in independent datasets is needed to establish its broader applicability\.

## [TECHNOLOGY\-ENABLED CSR AND WOMEN’S EMPOWERMENT: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES AND EMERGING AI FOR ADVANCING SDG 5](../publications/ec5ceb1caaa527ba5b87.md)

Mrs\. Josephin\. G; Well Haorei

Corporate Social Responsibility \(CSR\) has moved beyond philanthropy and is now considered a strategic business action, and is connected to social outcomes like gender equality and women&\#x27;s empowerment\. Digital technologies have already transformed the approach to designing, delivering, measuring and communicating CSR programmes\. This paper provides a literature review on technology\-based CSR and how it can empower women\. It explores three tracks: Digital Literacy, Financial Inclusion via Digital Platforms, Women entrepreneurs and employment\. It also consolidates evidence from its effect on such programmes in countries such as India, Indonesia, Nigeria, Kenya and Pakistan\. A qualitative and thematic review of peer\-reviewed research was conducted to uncover themes, outcomes and constraints\. The results indicate that technology\-facilitated CSR can have an impact on the income, confidence, financial independence, market access and involvement in household and community decision\-making of women\. These gains rely on a number of factors, such as local cultural norms, the cost of technology, digital infrastructure, targeting, and the design of the programmes that address women&\#x27;s particular constraints\. Main challenges that remain are the digital gender divide, low digital literacy, lack of CSR funding for women, and threats to data ethics and cybersecurity\. The paper ends with recommendations for the integration of digital tools in CSR monitoring and reporting, the adoption of corporate digital responsibility and the build\-in of programmes with Sustainable Development Goals \(SDG\) 5\.

## [Machine learning frameworks for quantitative proteomics: applications to Parkinson&\#x27;s disease biomarker discovery](../publications/ec66d7c3b6ee019e44b0.md)

Duc Tung Vu

Large\-scale proteomics has become indispensable for advancing our understanding of complex diseases, and this involves integrating highly complex computational algorithms with translational biomarker discovery\. This thesis advances the field by developing novel quantitative and statistical methods for mass spectrometric data analysis while applying them to uncover molecular mechanisms in Parkinson&\#x27;s disease \(PD\), with a focus on LRRK2\-driven pathology and sporadic disease variants\. The first part of this work aims at improving the quantitative capabilities of MS\-based proteomics\. I developed QuantSelect, a deep learning\-driven framework for fragment ion selection that substantially improves quantitative accuracy and precision\. QuantSelect uses a self\-supervised approach with a novel weighted variance loss function, to learn a representation based on quality features that surpass conventional filtering methods\. It demonstrates superior performance as exemplified by using a single\-cell proteomics dataset and differential expression analysis\. I also contributed to MultiCova, a statistical framework for differential expression analysis that accounts for multiple covariates in clinical datasets while also providing interpretable effect sizes\. This replaces conventional fold changes and permutation\-based false discovery rate estimation\. Together, these computational advances enable more robust and reliable quantification in large\-scale clinical proteomics studies\. The second part of my thesis applies high\-throughput proteomics to elucidate molecular mechanisms in Parkinson&\#x27;s disease using clinically accessible biofluids and cellular and in\-vivo models\. In my main project, I investigated urinary proteomes from over 1,200 individuals across three independent cohorts to identify robust signatures of LRRK2 kinase activity in PD\. Leveraging machine learning, I identified a 30\-biomarker panel that distinguishes LRRK2 G2019S carriers with exceptional performance \(ROC AUC up to 0\.96\) and, critically, stratifies patients by LRRK2\-like phenotypes independent of mutation status\. I validated these findings in a transgenic rat experiment that showed a conserved proteomic signature across species in pathogenic Lrrk2 mutations\. LRRK2 inhibition showed negative correlation with the human biomarker panel, establishing its potential as a pharmacodynamic marker\. We extended this work to LRRK2 variants associated with inflammatory disease\. Here I contributed proteomics analysis demonstrating that the Crohn&\#x27;s disease\-associated N2081D mutation activates LRRK2 through distinct mechanisms compared to the PD\-associated G2019S variant, resulting in differential patterns of Rab substrate phosphorylation\. Beyond LRRK2\-driven pathology, I revealed mechanisms in sporadic PD using patient\- derived cellular models\. Through multi\-omics integration of transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics in hiPSC\-derived neural cells, I helped demonstrate that sporadic PD exhibits hypometabolism centered on α\-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex dysfunction and sonic hedgehog pathway dysregulation\. Longitudinal analysis revealed that sporadic PD accelerates the aging process, with transcriptional changes preceding proteomic alterations and progressive hypermethylation indicating loss of cellular plasticity during disease development\. Finally, the thesis contains a number of ubiquitin – related studies, which was a secondary focus of my work\. Together, this thesis addresses challenges in computational method development and our mechanistic understanding of PD, advancing both the technical capabilities of quantitative proteomics and our biological knowledge of PD\. By combining machine learning\-based data analysis methods with biomarker discovery and mechanistic validation across species and model systems, this work provides invaluable insights into PD pathogenesis\.

## [Hospitality in the Digital Age: Innovation, Workforce Transformation, and Guest Experience](../publications/ec6c6fd6aadb4e55dc8b.md)

Amrik Singh

Rapid technological progress, shifting guest expectations, and an increased focus on sustainable and personalized services are fueling a transformation in the hospitality industry\. Hospitality in the Digital Age: Innovation, Workforce Transformation, and Guest Experience investigates the synergy between technology, human resources, and hospitality service excellence management strategies in today&\#x27;s hotel sector\.This book explores the impact of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, automation, robotics, Internet of Things, virtual and augmented reality, data analytics, and smart hospitality systems for hotel operations and guest experiences\. ## [Time as an indispensable causal dimension in cardiovascular diseases: toward a four\-dimensional biology](../publications/ec7102f204fdce0066d1.md)

Guido Caluori; Sébastien Chaigne

Heart failure \(HF\) exhibits distinctive event\-and time\-dependent patterns in incidence and progression dynamics\. Over time, the heart first undergoes \(mal\)adaptive cellular, tissue and molecular remodelling 1,2 \. These alterations precede clinical symptoms and diagnosis 3,4 and reflect age\-related changes in cardiovascular structure and function that lower the threshold for overt disease 4,5 \. This subclinical process is followed by incremental cardiac remodelling, including cardiac hypertrophy 6,7 , myocardial stiffening 8 , and impaired diastolic filling 4 \. Similar preclinical alterations occur across other cardiovascular and cardiometabolic disorders: atrial fibrosis and mitochondrial remodelling may develop before atrial fibrillation 9,10 , endothelial dysfunction precedes hypertension and atherosclerosis 11 and even rare diseases such as J\-wave syndromes are now considered cardiomyopathies with subtle structural abnormalities that remain undetected by standard imaging techniques 12 \. In addition, disturbances in protein homeostasis and metabolic adaptation occur long before the onset of clinical manifestations of the disease 13 \. Thus, sudden cardiac pathological events are often preceded by manifestations of biological processes that have been unfolding over several years\. The temporal trajectories differ markedly across various pathologies 12,14 , are not linear 15 , and are modulated by age, sex, lifestyle and inter\-organ interactions\. This interindividual variability calls for a personalised temporal framework for diagnosis and therapy, rather than a single, universally applied diagnostic threshold\. Disease is typically defined once a threshold value is exceeded 4 \. In HF, this heterogeneity is further reflected in the attempts to subcategorize distinct phenotypes, notably HF with reduced ejection fraction \(HFrEF\), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction \(HFmrEF\) and HF with preserved ejection fraction \(HFpEF\)\. This differentiation likely represents overlapping but temporally and mechanistically divergent trajectories rather than strict separate entities 16 \. Similarly, this limitation is evident in the study and management of AF, where the conventional classification into paroxysmal and persistent forms, subsequently expanded to include long\-standing persistent and permanent AF, fails to adequately capture individual risk profiles and the progressive nature of the underlying atrial myopathy 17 \. Emerging approaches based on biomarkers 18 and wearable or implantable devices 19,20 will increasingly enable realtime monitoring of individual disease trajectories for earlier detection of warning signals before irreversible remodelling occurs\. A central challenge is to identify the therapeutically actionable window during which pathological remodelling remains reversible in order to limit disease progression\. This limitation highlights the constraints of traditional frameworks based on universally applied symptomatology, isolated criteria and therefore simple causal relationships that inform therapeutic options 21 \. Given that cardiovascular \(patho\)biology emerges from continuous interactions across molecular pathways, cells, tissues, and inter\-organ communication 21,22 , cardiovascular diseases can be approached as a dynamic, multi\-scale and complex trajectory extending from molecular networks to whole\-organ function\. However, even apparently linear causal relationships at the organ level are grounded in nonlinear molecular and cellular dynamics, highlighting the need for a multi\-scale temporal framework\. This trajectory is shaped against the background of biological aging and the dynamics of complex systems\. This perspective requires a multidimensional framework in which time is considered an essential dimension of disease\. Time is not only a static background information, but through aging it is also an active determinant of adaptation, remodelling, and failure\. It should be note that the term &quot;four\-dimensional&quot; has previously been used in cardiovascular cronobiology to describe the circadian regulation of cardiac physiology across an hourly\-to\-daily timescale 23,24 \. Here, however, the fourth dimension captures the longitudinal trajectory of disease development and biological aging over years\. These represent distinct temporal scales and conceptual frameworks\. Here, we argue that incorporating temporal biology into cardiovascular research, from molecular clocks to organlevel remodelling trajectories, is essential to advance precision cardiology and to identify therapeutically relevant temporal windows prior to the point of no return\.In medicine, diagnosis is typically established when a physiological parameter deviates from a defined normal range\. For example, hypertension is diagnosed when blood pressure exceeds a fixed numerical value, whereas HF is defined once the ejection fraction falls below a critical value 25 \. HFrEF \(EF &lt;40%\), HFmrEF \(EF 40\-49%\) and HFpEF \(EF ≥50%\) represent 3 clinical phenotypes 16 that share common pathophysiological mechanisms, neurohormonal modulation, myocardial fibrosis and inflammation, but differ in their temporal trajectories which may be influenced by major clinical events such as myocardial infarction, as well as in their therapeutic responses\. These diagnostic thresholds define disease at the moment of clinical recognition rather than at its biological origin, reinforcing the perception that health ends and disease begins at the time of diagnosis rather than long before the clinical manifestation\. This reflects a conceptual limitation: disease is anchored to clinical detection rather than to the underlying biological and time\-dependent trajectory\. Furthermore, diagnostic thresholds are often based on normal values established in relation to chronological age even though the cardiovascular system may be biologically much older or younger\. For instance, the coronary endothelium of a 50year\-old patient may exhibit a molecular signature typically observed in older subjects, characterized by the accumulation of senescent cells and impaired nitric oxide signalling 26 \. Conversely, an octogenarian with a biologically younger myocardium, characterized by preserved mitochondrial function, low systemic inflammation, and maintained protein homeostasis, may remain healthy beyond the expected clinical limits 27 \(Figure 1\)\. Cardiovascular function declines gradually long before symptoms appear, while the body compensates to maintain normal performance\. Insidious damage accumulates over time until these compensatory systems fail\. At that point, disease becomes visible, even though the best opportunity for prevention was earlier\. Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction \(HFrEF\), characterized by impaired systolic function and reduced cardiac output, typically showing strong response to guideline\-directed medical therapy; heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction \(HFmrEF\), representing an intermediate phenotype between reduced and preserved ejection fraction; heart failure with preserved ejection fraction \(HFpEF\), characterized by preserved systolic function but impaired ventricular relaxation and increased stiffness, often associated with systemic comorbidities\. In the case of the octagenerian, compensatory mechanisms maintain an apparent state of normality even when myocardial hypertrophy may exist for years, together with progressive fibrosis, while preserved cardiac output and endothelial repair transiently sustain cardiac and vascular function\. Beneath this clinical silence, biological vulnerability progressively accumulates until compensatory reserves are exhausted\. The insidious phase represents a key but systematically underexplored therapeutic window, when intervention may be most effective, but where detection is limited\. Indeed, an EF &lt; 40% only reflects vulnerability and biological age at the moment it is measured\. The EF values shown correspond to clinically recommended thresholds and illustrate the progression of cardiac dysfunction linked to HF 28 \. The undiagnosed patient, in whom structural and functional cardiac changes accumulate silently over years, better illustrates this limitationConsidering the temporal development of cardiovascular disease, several questions arise: at what exact point does a stable system become pathologically unstable? How can long periods of apparent stability suddenly give way and unmask latent failure? And why do individuals exposed to similar stressors exhibit such divergent outcomes? How can we use time\-related pathology to identify and potentially treat patients at risk for cardiovascular disease at an early stage? Each disease follows a trajectory that remains largely undetected and is shaped by biological, genetic, proteomic, environmental, and temporal factors\. When the resulting, cardiovascular, biological age exceeds chronological age, adaptive capacity is reduced and the threshold for transition is lowered 29 \. Interestingly, the naked mole\-rats maintain cardiac function into their fourth decade of life, demonstrating that biological and chronological aging can be profoundly uncoupled 30 \. Conversely, biologically younger systems tolerate similar stress without decompensation\. Biological systems initially buffer stress through compensatory mechanisms, but once a critical threshold is crossed, they shift rapidly and irreversibly toward a pathological state 31 \. Disease does not emerge abruptly but it reflects a progressive erosion of adaptive reserve that progresses toward a tipping point 32 \(see Figure 1\)\)\. Identifying early signals of this decline, before the system fails, is therefore central to the temporal framework proposed here, and may explain why clinically stable periods can precede sudden and unexpected decompensation 33,34,35 \. The progressive loss of adaptive capacity may eventually lead to an abrupt transition to a pathological state, consistent with the concept of critical transitions in complex systems\. As a system approaches a critical threshold, critical slowing down and changes in its dynamics, including increased variance and instability, may provide early \-warning signals of this transition 36,37 \. Applied to cardiovascular disease trajectories, this framework may help identify early, subclinical signs of maladaptive capacity before irreversible decompensation or apparent cardiac disorders\. Yet, these signals remain largely invisible to current diagnostic tools, underscoring the need for a new analytical framework\. These dynamics differ across HF \(or across other pathologic\) phenotypes and directly influence the optimal timing of intervention\. HFrEF often reaches a tipping point marked by irreversible cardiomyocyte loss and fibrosis, whereas HFpEF may progress more gradually through accumulating diastolic dysfunction and microvascular impairment\. HFmrEF may represent an intermediate and potentially more reversible stage\. Determining where patients are positioned along this trajectory is crucial for identifying the window during which intervention can still prevent irreversible decompensation\. Insight into the &\#x27;natural history&\#x27; of the various diseases therefore is of essence\.Systems biology has transformed cardiovascular research through multi\-omics integration, spatial transcriptomics, single\-cell sequencing, and computational physiology 38,39 \. However, these advances remain incomplete without explicit integration of time and multimodality tailored to the pathology under study\. Indeed, most experimental models rely on young male animals, despite growing attention to include both sexes in experimental practice 40 , and fail to recapitulate human biological aging and cumulative environmental exposures \(smoking, diet, inactivity, obesity\) , 41 \. One example is the cumulative electrophysiological remodelling that develops over years 42 \. This process is not limited to a time\-dependent prolongation of action potential duration, but rather reflects a gradual disruption of ionchannel homeostasis, mechano\-electrical coupling, and repolarisation reserve that grows with biological aging and our environment\. The biological mechanisms are often investigated in isolation, despite their strong temporal interdependence 21,43 \. Similarly, many experimental disease models may bypass the slow intermediate stages that are central to human cardiovascular aging\. This progressive remodelling is associated with QT interval prolongation and increased repolarisation heterogeneity on the ECG, reflecting a growing ionic imbalance and destabilisation of the spatial and regional electrophysiological control systems\. Collectively, these changes increase susceptibility to ventricular arrhythmia and electrical instability in an age\-dependent manner 30,44,45,46 \. Thus, current cardiovascular research remains largely reductionist and linear \(1\-dimensional\)\. Some approaches integrate aspects of cardiac function but neglect systemic interactions \(2 dimensional\); Some recognise the interdependent networks across molecular, cellular, tissue, and inter\-organ levels 21 \(3\-dimensional\)\. In this context, a 4\-dimensional framework incorporates time as an active dimension, capturing disease as a trajectory through adaptive, pre\-pathological, unstable, and decompensated states, and revealing therapeutically relevant windows before the tipping point is reached\. However, the validity of such a framework depends, in part, on the experimental models used to study these dynamics and here a critical limitation emerges\. Most of the AF/HF\-related models are induced in young animals, which lack the cumulative electrophysiological substrate, including age\-related calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, fibrosis and reduced repolarisation reserve that in combination underlie arrhythmogenesis in humans\. As a result, such models poorly recapitulate, or fail to reproduce, transient arrhythmogenic events, including for example early and delayed afterdepolarisations at the cellular level\. The reconstruction of true cardiac disease dynamics therefore remains fundamentally and always limited\. A central challenge is the integration of biological age as a mechanistic dimension of disease\. Rather than being treated as a simple time\-based variable, biological age 47 should reflect molecular damage, immune remodelling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ion\-channel alterations\. Epigenetic clocks such as GrimAge 48 and PhenoAge 49 enable estimation of biological age independently of chronological age\. Integrating these measures into digital twin frameworks would allow reconstruction of disease trajectories and quantification of the velocity of aging over time, distinguishing adaptive, pre\-pathological, unstable, and decompensated states and capturing transitions rather than static categories\. Together, structural remodelling, electrophysiological instability, inflammatory signalling, and metabolic aging likely interact synergistically to reduce cardiovascular adaptive capacity over time \(Table 1\)\. Altogether, they call for a paradigm shift toward a 4\-dimensional cardiovascular biology in which time is not a background variable but a central dimension of disease structure and progression\. Four\-dimensional modelling is particularly relevant for distinguishing HFrEF, HFmrEF and HFpEF as temporally divergent trajectories\. Longitudinal integration of electrophysiological, structural and metabolic biomarkers may reveal the dynamic transition points between these 3 phenotypes and identify personalised intervention windows\.Table 1\. Temporal phases of cardiovascular performance and their clinical implications \. Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction \(HFrEF\), characterized by impaired systolic function and reduced cardiac output, typically showing strong response to guideline\-directed medical therapy; heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction \(HFmrEF\), representing an intermediate phenotype between reduced and preserved ejection fraction;, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction \(HFpEF\), characterized by preserved systolic function but impaired ventricular relaxation and increased stiffness, often associated with systemic comorbidities\.Reprogramming strategies may hold potential across HF phenotypes\. In HFpEF, where early remodelling remains mainly metabolic and epigenetic rather than structural, biological time modulation could theoretically restore adaptive capacity\. The degree of functional recovery in advanced HFrEF is probably limited by irreversible cardiomyocyte loss\. The idea of biological time inversion, which suggests that some features of aging may be completely or partially reversible under controlled experimental settings, is still controversial\. Partial in vivo reprogramming through transient Yamanaka factor \(OSKM\) expression has shown to reset epigenetic landscapes while preserving cellular identity, restoring chromatin accessibility and regenerative capacity in aged tissues 50,51 \. Naked mole rats may reach an age of 40 years with remarkably limited cardiovascular aging 30 \. Equally intriguing, a study using heterochronic parabiosis models indicate that exposure to a young systemic milieu can reverse cardiac hypertrophy and improve myocardial function in aged mice 52 , although the identity and reproducibility of circulating rejuvenating factors remain controversial, particularly for candidates such as GDF11 53,54 \. More recently, partial reprogramming to neural and sensory systems, involving restoration of vision in aged mice, supporting the concept of persistent epigenetic plasticity in adult mammalian tissues 51 \. Collectively, these findings challenge the classical view of aging as a strictly linear and irreversible trajectory, suggesting instead a dynamic continuum of modifiable biological states\. However, the magnitude, durability, and safety of such \(therapeutic\) effects remain highly contextdependent across tissues and experimental platforms, with unresolved risks including tumorigenicity, loss of cellular identity, and long\-term genomic instability\. In the cardiovascular system, where remodelling emerges from tightly integrated mechanical, metabolic, and inflammatory signalling, such plasticity appears partial and temporally constrained\. Importantly, these observations reinforce the concept that cardiac aging and disease progression are not fixed endpoints but time\-dependent processes shaped by reversible and irreversible phases and by parallel temporal dynamics across organs and cell systems\. This framework directly applies to the temporal model of cardiovascular disease proposed above, in which early remodelling may remain accessible to intervention before the system reaches its tipping point\. Accordingly, biological time modulation should be viewed not as a true reversal of aging, but as a constrained reprogramming of cardiovascular trajectories within a broader 4\-dimensional disease continuum\. However, the translation of such approaches to human cardiovascular disease remains limited by concerns over safety, stability, and long\-term functional integration issues\.Cardiovascular diseases rarely begin at symptom onset\. When HF, AF, or coronary disease becomes clinically apparent, the underlying biology has often been active for years\. The observed pathology reflects the final stage of a prolonged silent process\. A central feature of this process is the divergence between biological and chronological \(cardiovascular\) age, which shapes the rate of progression and proximity to the tipping point\. This mismatch influences risk, reversibility, and therapeutic timing\. Recognising that the individual cardiovascular system may be biologically older or younger than its chronological age represents a mechanistic determinant with implications for prevention and clinical intervention\. Redefining HFrEF, HFmrEF and HFpEF, or as well as paroxysmal and persistent AF, through a temporal and biological age framework transforms them from diagnostic labels into dynamic disease states\. This shift allows interventions to be timed to an individual&\#x27;s progression toward phenotype\-specific tipping points, rather than to symptom onset\. The next paradigm shift in cardiovascular research will be fundamentally conceptual\. It will require integration of the principles of personalised medicine and moving from static, symptom\-driven definitions of disease toward dynamic, trajectory\-based frameworks grounded in systems biology\. The focus will shift from detecting electromechanical/structural abnormalities to unveiling early signs of instability across different levels of biological organisation\. Without integrating biological time as a fourth dimension, cardiovascular biology remains fundamentally incomplete, and progress toward improved patient outcomes will continue to be constrained by the lack of more integrative and translational research frameworks\. If we accept that the disease cause precedes the disease, we may need to redefine causality in cardiovascular pathologies\. The recognition that cardiovascular disease processes begin long before clinical manifestations provides a rationale for incorporating biological time into our understanding of disease progression\. This perspective may help identify early transitions and therapeutic windows before irreversible decompensation and apparent disease\. It also suggests that causality in cardiovascular disease should be understood in direct relation to biological trajectories and their evolution over time, rather than solely by the timing of events\.

## [Liver\-specific amino acid metabolism impacts on efficacy of cancer immunotherapy](../publications/ec8501484e8afa2f19a2.md)

Yuma Fukumoto; Fumiaki Mukohara; Momoko Iwatsuru; Youki Ueda; Hiroaki Kanzaki; Sadahisa Ogasawara; Jason Lin; Masahito Kawazu; Toshifumi Ninomiya; Naoya Kemmotsu; Joji Nagasaki; Shinichi Toyooka; Tsuyoshi Osawa; Takamasa Ishino; Yosuke Togashi

Abstract The combination immunotherapies, including those with atezolizumab and bevacizumab \(Atez/Bev\), have become standard therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\)\. However, its efficacy remains limited and reliable biomarkers are lacking\. In this study, we analyzed paired tumor and background liver tissues from Atez/Bev\-treated HCC patients and found that high programmed cell death\-1 \(PD\-1\) expression in CD8 \+ tumor\-infiltrating lymphocytes \(TILs\) correlated with therapeutic response independent of etiology\. RNA sequencing on the tumor samples revealed that the branched\-chain amino acid \(BCAA\)\-related metabolic pathway was enriched in the group with high PD\-1 expression in CD8⁺ TILs\. Along with in vitro experiments, we identified the importance of BCAAs for activation and differentiation of CD8 \+ T cells\. In addition, BCAA metabolism was related to response to PD\-1 blockade in not subcutaneous but intrahepatic mouse model–specific manner\. Actually, public dataset analyses revealed that high expression of BCAT1 , a key enzyme in BCAA metabolism, was associated with poor prognosis in HCC, but not in other cancer types\. These findings suggest the importance of liver\-specific BCAA metabolism in antitumor immunity and highlight the need to assess the tumor microenvironment within its organ\-specific metabolic context\.

## [DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE\-ASSISTED MULTIPARAMETRIC MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING FOR THE DETECTION OF CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT PROSTATE CANCER](../publications/ec89119093aa3c518e06.md)



Background: Prostate cancer is one of the leading malignancies among men worldwide\.Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging \(mpMRI\) has become an essential imaging modality for the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer\.Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) have shown promising potential in improving the accuracy and consistency of prostate MRI interpretation\.Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence\-assisted multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging for the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer\.Materials and Methods: A hospital\-based prospective diagnostic accuracy study was conducted among 50 male patients with clinical suspicion of prostate cancer\.All participants underwent AI\-assisted multiparametric MRI of the prostate, including T2\-weighted imaging, diffusion\-weighted imaging, apparent diffusion coefficient mapping, and dynamic contrast\-enhanced imaging where indicated\.MRI findings were interpreted using AI\-assisted software, and all patients subsequently underwent prostate biopsy\.Histopathological examination served as the reference standard\.Diagnostic performance was assessed by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value \(PPV\), negative predictive value \(NPV\), diagnostic accuracy, and area under the receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve\.Results: The mean age of the participants was 66\.2 ± 7\.8 years\.Histopathology confirmed clinically significant prostate cancer in 34 \(68%\) patients\.AI\-assisted mpMRI correctly identified 31 true\-positive and 12 true\-negative cases, with 4 false\-positive and 3 false\-negative results\.The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and overall diagnostic accuracy were 91\.2%, 75\.0%, 88\.6%, 80\.0%, and 86\.0%, respectively\.The area under the ROC curve was 0\.89, indicating excellent diagnostic performance\.A statistically significant association was observed between AI\-assisted mpMRI findings and histopathological diagnosis \(Chi\-square test, p &lt; 0\.001\)\.Conclusion: Artificial intelligence\-assisted multiparametric MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer and showed excellent agreement with histopathological findings\.AI can serve as an effective decision\-support tool for radiologists by improving lesion detection, reducing interobserver variability, and facilitating appropriate patient selection for biopsy\.Larger multicentre studies are required to further validate these findings before widespread clinical implementation\.

## [Classifying Automated Driving Systems Using Telematics Data: A Comparative Study of GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Models](../publications/ec897bd71e79361e43bd.md)

Bidhya Shrestha; Bhargab Acharya; Christos Papadopoulos

The rapid advancement of sensing, artificial intelligence, and in\-vehicle computing has accelerated deployment of automated driving systems \(ADSs\)\. As vehicles move toward software\-defined architectures, multiple driving stacks—including manufacturer and aftermarket solutions—may coexist, raising the need to verify which system is actively controlling the vehicle from observable behavior alone\. This paper investigates ADS identification using only harmonized vehicle telematics, without proprietary controller states or perception sensors\. We compared three deep sequence models—Gated Recurrent Unit \(GRU\), Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), and a Transformer Encoder—for distinguishing Comma Openpilot, Tesla Autopilot, Cadillac Super Cruise, and manual driving from eleven shared features over 32\-timestep windows\. On clean held\-out data, all three architectures achieved strong performance \(macro\-F1 above 0\.91; mean ± std over 20 random seeds\), with the Transformer Encoder attaining the highest mean macro\-F1 and the GRU providing competitive, lower\-cost alternatives\. We further evaluated robustness under a structured telematics noise framework covering six atomic threat families and four compound multi\-fault conditions at different severity levels using a two\-arm protocol over 7 random seeds: clean training \(Arm A\) versus evaluation matched noise\-augmented training \(Arm B\)\. Under clean training, degradation was highly threat\-dependent: correlated cross\-feature noise and stochastic drift—and their compounds—caused the largest absolute and relative drops in macro\-F1, whereas delay\-with\-hold temporal jitter and temporal delay had comparatively minor effects\. This pattern is shared across GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Encoder models\. Evaluation matched augmentation preserved clean\-test accuracy while substantially reducing degradation, including at held\-out severities and on compound faults withheld from training\. The results show that telemetry\-based ADS identification is feasible at scale and that reliable deployment requires explicit attention to continuous and cross\-feature impairments\.

## [Closing the AI Chasm by Bridging the Gap Between Technical Precision and Clinical Relevance in Healthcare through Collaborative Evaluation and Decision Curve Analysis](../publications/ec89d73501687bd503cd.md)



Objective: This research endeavors to reduce the gap between the technical accuracy of AI models and their practical significance in healthcare by conducting collaborative assessments and employing Decision Curve Analysis\.While AI models are increasingly employed for disease prediction, there remains a need for a thorough method to assess their clinical utility, as conventional accuracy metrics may not fully reflect real\-world implications\.Material and Methods: Decision curve analysis \(DCA\) offers a promising avenue by considering benefits and harms across different thresholds, but a systematic approach is necessary to evaluate AI models&\#x27; efficacy in clinical practice, with the goal of informing healthcare decisions more effectively\.Integrating AI models into clinical workflows requires seamless integration with electronic health records and other healthcare systems, along with ensuring user acceptance and adherence to clinical protocols\.Decision curve analysis has the potential to evaluate the clinical utility of AI models, but its effectiveness is hindered by limited real\-world validation, impeding the determination of the models&\#x27; true success across diverse clinical settings and patient populations\.In response to these challenges, logistic regression is utilized to examine the dataset of heart failure clinical records, sourced from Kaggle with the goal of improving the integration of AI models into clinical workflows and enhancing the validation of decision curve analysis to assess their clinical effectiveness\.Results: The suggested AI approach provides improved predictive precision and supports prompt decision\-making within clinical environments\.The logistic regression model proposed demonstrates superior performance compared to the existing Support Vector Machine \(SVM\) model, showing a higher ROC AUC score \(0\.98 versus 0\.83\), greater accuracy \(94\.44% versus 78\.33%\), and a more balanced confusion matrix with fewer false positives and false negatives\.This highlights its enhanced predictive accuracy and precision in heart failure prediction\.Conclusion: The Logistic Regression model proposed in this study demonstrates superior performance relative to the Random Forest and SVM models, indicated by its higher ROC AUC score \(0\.98 versus 0\.85 and 0\.83, respectively\), greater accuracy \(94\.44% versus 76\.67% and 78\.33%\), and a more balanced Confusion Matrix with fewer occurrences of false positives and false negatives\.Moreover, Logistic Regression exhibits competitive time complexity that is well\-suited for real\-time clinical decision\-making applications\.

## [Proportionality in Ranking Compression](../publications/ec8cf62f136905aa2a78.md)

Daniel Halpern; Xinyu Liu; Evi Micha; Yu Peng Ng; Warut Suksompong

Motivated by applications in reinforcement learning from human feedback, we consider a setting where a given collection of rankings needs to be compressed into a smaller collection of rankings\. This can also be seen as a combination of two fundamental social choice frameworks: ranking aggregation and multiwinner voting\. We propose three proportionality notions that capture different types of representation in this setting: positional proportionality, pairwise proportionality, and proportionality for solid coalitions \(PSC\)\. On the one hand, we show that positional proportionality and PSC are always satisfiable for any input rankings and target compression size, and a desired output can be found in polynomial time\. On the other hand, we prove that pairwise proportionality cannot be satisfied in general, but can nevertheless be attained when the input rankings are single\-peaked or single\-crossing\.

## [Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody reveals a novel strategy for understanding and treating early\-onset neuromuscular diseases](../publications/ec9006493fce75b1d62a.md)

Julien Oury; Leah Santana; Karen Silence; Roeland Vanhauwaert; Steven J\. Burden

Congenital myasthenia \(CM\) comprises a group of neuromuscular diseases caused by mutations in genes responsible for the formation and function of neuromuscular synapses, including genes encoding neuronal Agrin, low\-density receptor\-related protein 4 \(Lrp4\), muscle\-specific kinase \(MuSK\), downstream of kinase 7 \(Dok7\), and receptor\-associated protein \(Rapsyn\)\. Although mouse models have been invaluable for studying neuromuscular diseases, including CM, early neonatal lethality, due to respiratory failure, has made it difficult to study disease progression or assess potential treatments\. Previously, we demonstrated that postnatal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody rescued neuromuscular synapses and prevented disease in a mouse model of Dok7 CM\. To determine whether a MuSK agonist antibody could benefit other forms of CM, we delivered a MuSK agonist antibody to pregnant mice and thereby their progeny\. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody prevented neonatal lethality of Dok7 mutant mice, allowing the mice to survive for at least two months\. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody also rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice from neonatal lethality, but the mice failed to survive for two months, even after additional postnatal treatment with the agonist antibody\. Partial and full denervation were prominent in rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice, suggesting that poor attachment and withdrawal of nerve terminals are responsible for their postnatal lethality\. These findings indicate that neuronal Agrin has functions in synaptic differentiation and maintenance that are independent of MuSK activation\. Classifications: Biological Sciences / Neuroscience\.

## [Building a sustainable workforce: Integrating digital skills into intercultural language curricula to meet regional economic needs](../publications/ec968ac5aadaafd4ac1c.md)

Lam Ngoc Nhu Truc; Vo Kim Thuy Trang

Abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the gap between the daily digital usage habits of language students and the professional digital competencies required by modern multinational employers, and to propose an integrated curriculum model \(ICM\) to address this disparity\. The study was carried out using a mixed\-methods approach at Ba Ria \- Vung Tau University in Vietnam\. Quantitative data were gathered through a self\-assessment survey of 421 students in the Faculty of Languages \- International Cultures, aimed at evaluating their digital technology habits and capabilities\. Concurrently, a qualitative document analysis was conducted on three foundational course syllabi to determine the current extent of digital integration in language teaching methodology\. The results indicate a significant paradox: although the vast majority of students reported high levels of daily internet use, their self\-assessed proficiency in higher\-order professional skills, such as digital collaboration and digital content creation, was sharply lower\. Furthermore, the syllabi analysis reveals a fragmented approach to education, in which technology is either isolated as a teaching tool or entirely absent from core communication courses\. The significance of these findings lies in their highlighting the inadequacy of relying solely on students&\#x27; innate social technology skills to prepare them for professional careers\. By mapping these deficits against a global digital literacy framework, the study successfully proposes a cross\-curricular integration model that embeds specific digital tasks into existing language modules\. This approach creates a simulated learning environment where students confront real\-world digital challenges identical to those encountered in foreign direct investment enterprises\. This ensures the sustainability of human capital by enhancing flexibility and adaptability, equipping graduates to meet the demands of the globalized digital economy\. Keywords: Ba Ria – Vung Tau University; Cross\-cultural collaboration; Digital literacy; Sustainable development; UNESCO Framework

## [Research on the molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of reactive oxygen species in nasopharyngeal carcinoma](../publications/ec9eeb86578f732a72d8.md)

Yuting Gu; Bi Qiang

Nasopharyngeal carcinoma \(NPC\) exhibits significant geographical clustering and etiological heterogeneity\. It is particularly prevalent in Southeast Asia and is typically associated with Epstein\-Barr virus \(EBV\) infection\. Reactive oxygen species \(ROS\), as highly reactive oxygen metabolites, play a key role in regulating cellular signaling and maintaining redox homeostasis\. Although the role of ROS in tumors has been well established, reviews examining how ROS influence NPC and their potential therapeutic applications remain relatively scarce\. ROS exert diverse effects in NPC, including roles in EBV\-associated processes, regulation of programmed cell death, metabolic reprogramming, formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and epigenetic remodeling\. In addition, natural small\-molecule compounds that regulate ROS levels and emerging combination therapy strategies have considerable therapeutic potential in NPC\. This review discusses the dual role of ROS in NPC, examines their contributions to disease development, and further explores how these mechanisms could inform the design of ROS\-targeted therapies, as well as the associated translational challenges\.

## [Financial Self\-Efficacy as a Predictor of FinTech Adoption and Financial Planning Behavior](../publications/ecaadf3f48fe148aed03.md)

Rosananda Oktala; Fernando Africano; Dewi Fadila; Ogi Rifansyah

This study examines the disconnect between high digital payment adoption and long\-term financial planning in an emerging urban economy by investigating whether Financial Self\-Efficacy predicts this gap directly or indirectly through FinTech Adoption\. Using survey data collected from 149 urban residents of Palembang, Indonesia, comprising 54\.4% students and 45\.6% workers, the conceptual framework was evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) in SmartPLS 4\. The analysis was complemented by the Heterotrait\-Monotrait ratio \(HTMT\) for discriminant validity assessment, PLSpredict, and Multigroup Analysis \(PLS\-MGA\) with Measurement Invariance of Composite Models \(MICOM\) testing\. The results show that Financial Self\-Efficacy significantly predicts FinTech Adoption and has a strong direct effect on Financial Planning Behavior\. In contrast, FinTech Adoption does not significantly predict Financial Planning Behavior when Financial Self\-Efficacy is controlled for, resulting in a non\-significant indirect effect through FinTech Adoption\. Furthermore, the multigroup analysis reveals that the predictive effect of Financial Self\-Efficacy on FinTech Adoption is nearly twice as strong among students as among workers\. These findings suggest that digital convenience alone does not automatically translate into long\-term financial discipline\. Instead, psychological capability, particularly Financial Self\-Efficacy, serves as an important factor linking technology adoption and financial planning behavior, with its predictive strength varying across occupational groups within an emerging urban population\.

## [Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Global Nonlinear Responses of Soil Respiration to Climate](../publications/ecad1fd5cb1629686694.md)

Benjamin Laffitte; Zhihan Yang; Tao Zhou; Xiangjun Pei; Xiaolu Tang

Abstract Soil respiration \( R s \) is a major component of the global carbon cycle, yet its responses to environmental drivers remain poorly constrained\. Using 8,111 observations and a SHAP‐interpreted Random Forest model, we identified global response patterns for key environmental drivers of R s \. Temperature contributions showed a peaked association with a descriptive maximum of 27\.7°C, precipitation contributions plateaued at high values, and leaf area index contributions increased approximately linearly\. These results provide a global, data‐driven characterization of peaked temperature and saturating precipitation associations, including how their shapes and supported ranges vary among climate zones\. Our results indicate that monotonic assumptions in Earth system models may overlook important nonlinearities and potentially bias estimates of terrestrial carbon flux responses to seasonal climate extremes\. Interpretable machine learning therefore provides a transparent framework for evaluating and improving the representation of soil carbon dynamics under climate change\.

## [An enhanced TOGI\-based control framework for seamless bidirectional energy management in grid\-connected solar PV–EV charging systems](../publications/ecafb2f98ce6d06b1060.md)

The less cost of photovoltaic \(PV\) modules and the rapid growth of electric vehicles \(EV\) has accelerated the adoption of solar\-powered charging systems\. Despite this progress, the use of bidirectional power flow in PV–EV integrated charging infrastructure has received comparatively less attention\. An enhanced third order generalized integrator \(ETOGI\) is utilized to control bidirectional voltage source converter \(VSC\)\. A comparison is made between the Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation \(PWM\) and Phase Disposition Pulse Width Modulation methods to find the performance of the system based on total converter losses and harmonics\. The suggested model is implemented and analysed in Simulink environment and further tested through real\-time implementation by a real\-time OPAL\-RT test platform\. Its performance is evaluated by static and dynamic operating conditions during charging and discharging\. The results demonstrate effective power management, improved grid power quality through lower current harmonic distortion\. These outcomes indicate that the proposed configuration is a reliable and efficient solution for grid\-connected solar PV\-based EV charging applications\.

## [Source apportionment and evolutionary characteristics of groundwater in the alpine gorge region of the tibetan plateau based on unsupervised machine learning and isotopic tracing: a case study of the zheduotang area, kangding](../publications/ecb8e8ccb78bc0eefd5d.md)

Chongqin Zhao; Chunchao Zhang; Changchang Fu; Xiangquan Li; Jianfei Ma; Zhenxing Wang; Jiazhong Qian; Xianyu Chen

Groundwater in the alpine canyon regions of the Qinghai\-Tibet Plateau is influenced by multiple recharge sources and geological structures, resulting in complex recharge processes and evolution mechanisms\. This study focuses on the alpine canyon region of Zheduotang and integrates unsupervised machine learning with isotope tracers \(δD, δ¹⁸O, and ³H\) to systematically identify groundwater sources and their evolutionary processes\. By integrating self\-organizing maps \(SOM\) and K\-means clustering, the water samples are classified into four groups, highlighting variations in hydrochemical facies, mineralization levels, and dominant ion sources among different water bodies\. The results indicate that groundwater hydrochemical evolution is jointly governed by lithology and water\-rock interaction intensity\. Groundwater in the granite\-dominated area is characterized by low\-TDS Ca\-HCO₃ and Ca\-Mg\-HCO₃, suggesting rapid shallow recharge, whereas groundwater in the metamorphic sandstone–slate area exhibits higher TDS with enriched Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, and HCO₃⁻, indicative of longer flow paths and stronger water\-rock interactions\. Isotopic evidence indicates that groundwater and surface water are predominantly recharged by atmospheric precipitation and snow\-ice meltwater, with recharge elevations ranging from 3594 to 5103 m, typically 400–800 m higher than their corresponding discharge elevations\. Groundwater recharge in the study area occurs through three principal modes: direct recharge via high\-elevation fractures, sustained input from alpine glacial lakes, and river leakage, and is strongly controlled by geological structures overall\.
