## [Early Warning at Scale: Development and Validation of a Predictive Model for Patient Deterioration across an 8,000\-Staff Regional Referral Network](../publications/ecc9c50b40472e0cec4b.md)

Rajesh Babu Kodali; Sailesh Kotha

Purpose: This paper develops a conceptual framework and validation protocol for a machine learning based early warning system to detect patient deterioration across a regional referral network of approximately 8,000 staff\. Methodology: The study is conceptual and methodological\. Drawing on the early warning and machine learning literature, it specifies data sources, feature engineering, three candidate models, and a tiered alerting workflow, together with a TRIPOD\+AI and PROBAST aligned protocol covering retrospective derivation, silent\-mode testing, staged implementation, fairness auditing, and implementation evaluation using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and RE\-AIM\. The framework is scoped to a network of the scale represented by Vandalia Health and its CAMC Health System campuses in West Virginia\. Findings: Rule\-based scores such as NEWS2 offer limited sensitivity and specificity relative to machine learning tools, but most evidence comes from large academic centers and integrated systems\. The framework shows how such a system can be sized for a multi\-campus referral network, routing escalating risk to nurses, rapid response teams, and physicians while limiting alarm fatigue\. No empirical patient\-level outcomes are reported\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: For theory, the paper integrates technical model design, fairness evaluation, and implementation science into a single development framework\. For practice, it provides a literature\-grounded blueprint and evaluation protocol that mid\-sized referral networks can use to plan deployment\. For policy, it supports pre\-specified, transparent validation and subgroup performance auditing before clinical prediction models are deployed\.

## [A high\-quality telomere\-to\-telomere lumpy skin disease virus genome assembly](../publications/ecd4588e63832d372e87.md)

Caroline F\. Wright; Noemi Polo; Sarwar Azam; Graham Freimanis; G\. Taru Sharma; Bryan Charleston; Carrie Batten; Tim Downing; Jonas Dutra Albarnaz

Lumpy skin disease virus \(LSDV\) is an emerging livestock capripoxvirus \(CaPV\) that continues to cause substantial economic losses across Africa, Asia and Europe\. However, important uncertainties remain regarding LSDV genome structure, particularly at the telomeric inverted terminal repeats \(ITRs\) that are central to host interaction, replication and adaptive evolution\. Structural variation at the ITRs is driven by recombination during virus replication\. Previous assemblies have relied primarily on short\-read sequencing, which provides limited resolution of repeat\-rich telomeric regions and propagates structural ambiguities into downstream annotation and comparative analyses\. Here, we present a high\-quality telomere\-to\-telomere assembly of the LSDV Oman 2009 isolate, generated using a hybrid approach that integrates short Illumina reads with higher\-accuracy long Nanopore reads\. The resulting 151,091 bp genome contains 157 annotated ORFs and fully resolves complex repeat\-rich structures at both ITRs\. This new reference corrects misassemblies present in earlier LSDV genomes and confirms clade\-specific gene truncations\. This genome provides a robust foundation for improved genomic surveillance, accurate read mapping, mutation detection and evolutionary inference of LSDV and demonstrates the value of long\-read approaches for resolving complex CaPV genome structures\.

## [Pengaruh Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) terhadap Employee Engagement pada Karyawan Generasi Z di Era Transformasi Digital](../publications/ece8e3c011aedce80a38.md)

Mawar Diana; Zacky Febriansyah; Yorisman Zega

Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) dan employee engagement pada karyawan Generasi Z di era transformasi digital\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data kuesioner daring\. Sebanyak 42 respons terkumpul; 36 responden menyatakan pernah menggunakan AI untuk membantu pekerjaan dan dianalisis, sedangkan 6 responden yang tidak pernah menggunakan AI tidak dimasukkan ke analisis utama\. Instrumen terdiri atas 15 butir pemanfaatan AI dan 13 butir employee engagement dengan skala Likert lima poin\. Hasil penghitungan data asli menunjukkan Cronbach’s alpha sebesar 0\.989 untuk pemanfaatan AI dan 0\.990 untuk employee engagement\. Korelasi Pearson menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat dan signifikan \(r = 0\.835; p &lt; 0,001\)\. Regresi linear sederhana menghasilkan persamaan Y = 0\.731 \+ 0\.819X dengan R² = 0\.697; koefisien regresi signifikan, t\(34\) = 8\.842; p &lt; 0,001\. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa pada sampel yang dianalisis, skor pemanfaatan AI yang lebih tinggi berkaitan dengan skor employee engagement yang lebih tinggi\. Temuan perlu ditafsirkan secara hati\-hati karena menggunakan sampel terbatas dan desain survei yang tidak dapat memastikan hubungan sebab\-akibat\.

## [Evaluation of tree based statistical learning supporting the bespoke manufacturing of low volume, super luxury cars](../publications/ececa8b6440f7a688d66.md)

Joshua Pooley

Manufacturing low\-volume bespoke, super luxury cars is challenging\. Many difficulties arise; the relatively low volume of data, the variation of the vehicles hiding patterns, the human builders lowering the consistency, for example\. Yet all of these problems must be managed to create perfection\. Solving these problems requires careful data selection, choosing features that make an impact; the specification of each vehicle, the production associates who built it, amongst others\. Furthermore, to predict how a vehicle will perform, given the information known about it, a suitable machine learning method needs selecting\. In this thesis, the process of choosing the most appropriate problem is discussed: predicting how vehicles will perform in their final inspection\. Selecting the best features and engineering them into a suitable form\. Established machine learning methods are discussed: random forest, XGBoost, optimal tree ensembles, neural networks and semi\-supervised generative adversarial networks, as well as some novel methods, utilising P\-Value adjusted decision trees in the optimal tree ensemble framework, residual boosting and conditional inference trees\. These methods are compared to determine the most effective approach for predicting final inspection outcomes\. The results demonstrate that the random forest model achieved the highest predictive performance with a precision of 66%, outperforming a novel method of PASTE\-boost with a precision of 52%\. The findings show that the final inspection result is predictable but improvements may require more observations or more influential predictors to allow for a more reliable prediction\. This thesis demonstrates the potential and limitations of machine learning approaches for supporting quality assessment for low\-volume manufacturing processes\.

## [PENERAPAN ALGORITMA DECISION TREE UNTUK SISTEM INFORMASI REKOMENDASI JURUSAN BERBASIS WEB \(STUDI KASUS SMK HENDRIKUS LEVEN\)](../publications/ecf91cad8ad2964dadfc.md)

Bernadus Lado Kedang; Alfian Nara Weking; Maria Bernadete Deta

Accurate department selection in Vocational High Schools \(SMKs\) is important because it is related to the alignment between students’ abilities, interests, and selected areas of specialization\. Manual department placement that relies mainly on academic scores and subjective considerations may result in inconsistent recommendations\. This study aims to design and implement a web\-based department recommendation information system using the Decision Tree \(C4\.5 Simplified\) algorithm at SMK Hendrikus Leven\. The study used students’ academic scores, interests, talents, and historical department data\. A total of 60 records were used as training data to construct a decision tree using Entropy and Information Gain calculations, after which the resulting IF\-THEN rules were implemented using Laravel and MySQL\. System testing consisted of black\-box testing involving 16 functional scenarios and tree traversal testing\. All functional scenarios were successfully completed\. In the test case, the system recommended the Clinical and Community Pharmacy department with a 100% Confidence Score, consistent with the generated decision rules\. The system also provides Rule Explanation to show the basis of each recommendation\. The results indicate that Decision Tree can support a more structured and transparent department recommendation process\. Quantitative accuracy evaluation has not yet been conducted and remains for future research\. ABSTRAK Ketepatan pemilihan jurusan di Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan \(SMK\) penting karena berkaitan dengan kesesuaian kemampuan dan minat siswa dengan bidang keahlian yang dipilih\. Pengujian dilakukan melalui black\-box testing terhadap 16 skenario dan pengujian penelusuran aturan \(tree traversal\)\. Seluruh fungsi memperoleh status berhasil\. Pada studi kasus, sistem merekomendasikan jurusan Farmasi Klinis dan Komunitas dengan Confidence Score 100% sesuai aturan yang terbentuk\. Sistem menyediakan Rule Explanation untuk menelusuri dasar rekomendasi\. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa Decision Tree dapat diimplementasikan sebagai alat bantu rekomendasi jurusan yang lebih terstruktur dan transparan\. Pengujian akurasi kuantitatif belum dilakukan sehingga menjadi agenda penelitian selanjutnya\.

## [International Student Mobility and Temporal Stability](../publications/ecfeed14f688a69c47e6.md)

Xian Zhao

International student mobility has gained significant attention in higher education research\. Most studies focus on migration outcomes and aspirations, while other studies start to recognize the open\-ended nature of students’ futures, particularly when faced with uncertainty\. This study rethinks international student mobility through future imaginaries\. Drawing on narrative interviews with four postgraduate Chinese international students from one university in the UK, this article presents students’ meaning\-making about their imagined futures in response to the uncertainties and changing policies\. Within these four participants’ narratives, the findings demonstrate that students were less concerned with mobility itself and more concerned with achieving a stable and predictable future trajectory\. This article conceptualizes such a future orientation as temporal stability to capture the phenomenon that students were not simply concerned about future aspirations as their stories involved issues of predictivity, planning, continuity and future direction\. When students start to only pursue temporal stability, this article calls for future research into what other futures students no longer imagine and why\.

## [Effects of centrifugation\-based therapeutic plasma exchange on coagulation parameters in dogs with canine visceral leishmaniasis](../publications/ed039e7df535d00d30d6.md)

Suellen Rodrigues Maia; Silvano Salgueiro Geraldes; F\. D\. Nogueira; Maria Gabriela Picelli de Azevedo; Reiner Silveira de Moraes; Julia Franco Ferreira; Teresa Alessandra de Lima Núñez; Regina Kiomi Takahira; Alessandra Melchert; Adriano Sakai Okamoto; Priscylla Tatiana Chalfun Guimarães‐Okamoto

As in humans, therapeutic plasma exchange \(TPE\) has been investigated in veterinary medicine for managing immune\-mediated diseases such as canine visceral leishmaniasis \(CVL\)\. TPE may improve clinical outcomes by removing circulating immune complexes and excess antibodies; however, its physiological effects must be understood to ensure safety\. Given the scarcity of studies in animals, this study evaluated the effects of centrifugation\-based TPE in dogs with CVL receiving fresh frozen plasma \(FFP\) as replacement fluid\. Thirty\-one dogs with CVL that failed to respond to conventional therapy were allocated to two groups: clinical treatment alone \(n = 18\) and clinical treatment plus TPE \(n = 13\)\. The TPE group underwent one daily session for three consecutive days\. Coagulation profiles were assessed before and after each session\. A progressive decrease in platelet counts occurred across sessions, but without significant thrombocytopenia or critical alterations in activated partial thromboplastin time \(aPTT\) or prothrombin time \(PT\), which remained within reference ranges\. Transient hypocalcemia occurred after the first session and was promptly corrected with calcium gluconate supplementation\. Fibrinogen levels decreased mildly without clinical evidence of bleeding\. Clinical complications were minimal and effectively managed\. In conclusion, TPE was well tolerated, producing predominantly transient and controllable effects on hemostasis and overall clinical homeostasis under the conditions of this study\.

## [Hydrodynamic simulation and risk evolution of urban waterlogging based on integrated SWMM–LISFLOOD modeling: a case study of Dongxihu District, Wuhan](../publications/ed03a18de88beff9a16a.md)

Man Wang; Zihan Guo; Quan Zhang; Lugen Chen; Xun Bao; Junpeng Zou

Rapid urbanization has altered rainfall–runoff processes in many cities and increased the hydraulic burden on urban drainage systems during short\-duration, high\-intensity storms\. Taking a representative drainage system in Dongxihu District, Wuhan, as a case study, this study investigates urban waterlogging under a 20\-year return\-period design storm\. An integrated 1D–2D hydrodynamic framework was established using EPA\-SWMM and LISFLOOD\-FP\. SWMM was used to simulate rainfall–runoff generation and drainage\-network routing, while node\-overflow hydrographs were transferred to LISFLOOD\-FP to simulate subsequent surface inundation\. The SWMM model comprised 869 nodes, 890 conduits, and 845 sub\-catchments\. A 2\-h Chicago design storm with a 5\-min rainfall\-input interval was adopted\. Under the 20\-year design storm, 96 drainage nodes overflowed, accounting for 11\.05% of all modeled nodes\. The cumulative overflow volume reached 12\.84 × 10 4 m 3 , and the maximum continuous overflow duration was 2\.18 h\. Major inundation zones were concentrated near Linkonggang Avenue, Wuhuan Road, Jinyintan Avenue, and the Taxi Road–Fushan Avenue section, with simulated maximum inundation depths ranging from 0\.32 to 0\.48 m at representative road sections\. The spatial pattern of waterlogging reflects the combined effects of runoff generation, local drainage\-capacity limitations, and downstream hydraulic constraints\. Because continuous observations of surface\-water depth and drainage\-network hydraulics were unavailable, the results should be interpreted primarily as scenario\-based identification of waterlogging hotspots rather than as fully field\-validated hydraulic predictions\.

## [Importancia de la predicción del perfil ADMET en bases de datos de productos naturales](../publications/ed210525feea5cf1ea5b.md)

Alejandro Gómez‐García; José L\. Medina‐Franco

Natural products \(NPs\) are the largest source of bioactive molecules with therapeutic properties\. Currently, there are compound databases containing thousands of NPs, from which it is possible to select those with the best absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity \(ADMET\) profiles, which greatly increases their chances of success in clinical trials\. This article discusses the importance of predicting the ADMET profile in early stages of drug development, especially using NP databases\. Nineteen freely accessible web servers that allow these predictions are presented, and some of the most relevant ADMET parameters that can be evaluated using these tools are discussed\.

## [Role of trap position variation on electrical parameters in hetero\-dielectric double gate TFET](../publications/ed3a16e89d95f8495c18.md)

Riddhi Dutta; Aryan Bose; Shanidul Hoque; Rajesh Saha

This work is a statistical reliability study of the Heterojunction Dielectric Double Gate \(HDDG\) tunnel field\-effect\-transistor \(TFET\) with respect to the randomized location of interface traps\. The device configuration consists of a Ge source, and a p \+ pocket to increase the tunneling probability\. Using TCAD Sentaurus, the impact of various interface trap localizations arising from the random nature of the interface is examined through a comprehensive variability analysis\. A comprehensive variability study is conducted to evaluate the sensitivity of the device to interface trap localization\. Of particular interest is how the device parameters change due to the incorporation of Gaussian\-distributed traps in 5 nm segments of the oxide semiconductor interface\. The statistical analysis of 100 devices is performed over four unique cases; \(i\) no traps, \(ii\) traps localized in the oxide/n\+ channel region, \(iii\) traps localized in the oxide/p\+ pocket region, and \(iv\) traps distributed across both regions\. The typical behavior of the devices is examined and the statistical variation of the following parameters is discussed; On\-Current \(I ON \), Off\-Current \(I OFF \), Threshold Voltage \(V th \), Band\-to\-Band Tunneling \(BTBT\) generation rate, electron velocity and subthreshold swing \(SS\)\.

## [Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long\-Range Ising Model Benchmark](../publications/ed3d4aac6efca45d044c.md)

Amin Najafgholizadeh; Mohsen Afsharchi

The Long\-Range Ising Model benchmark \(LRIM\) guarantees long\-range dependence by construction: each label is the node&\#x27;s spin times the spin field convolved with a power\-law coupling, so any model&\#x27;s distance from the target is measurable\. We prove that a readout whose filter is a polynomial in the adjacency, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral graph networks, leaves an error floor that no degree lowers, because the target varies along a level set of the spectrum on which every such filter is constant\. Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade\. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice\. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network&\#x27;s\. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in\-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows\. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels\. The analysis carries over to the benchmark&\#x27;s second coupling\.

## [ChatGPT and employability in higher education: exploring creativity, critical thinking, and problem\-solving](../publications/ed3f11973e662381db11.md)

Cristina Calle\-Martínez; Marta Silvera\-Roig; Nuria Recuero Virto; Marta Paredes

Generative AI tools are reshaping higher education and employability preparation\. This study examines how using versus not using ChatGPT influences university students’ perceptions of employability, focusing on complex problem\-solving, critical thinking, and creativity\. Thirty students from the Complutense University of Madrid completed a contingency\-plan task and participated in eight focus groups analyzed through Grounded Theory \(ATLAS\.ti\)\. Results show that ChatGPT use is associated with efficiency, output refinement, and assisted creativity, while non\-use is associated with originality, deliberation, and teamwork\. The findings reveal preliminary patterns in students’ experiences with and without AI, warranting further quantitative investigation rather than claims of improved skills or employability\.

## [Teacher Collaboration and Parental Involvement in Effectiveness of E\-Literacy Instructions for Children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder](../publications/ed4e1366ddddf6f21cba.md)

Sofia Kanwal; Shirmeen Ijaz; Ayesha Riaz

The present study aimed to investigate the role of teacher collaboration and parental involvement as correlates of the effectiveness of e\-literacy instruction for children with ADHD\. Using the structured survey questionnaire method, and data were collected from N=100 participants using a purposive sampling technique\. The sample included children with ADHD aged 8–16 years, along with their parents and teachers involved in e\-literacy instruction\. The questionnaire used in the study was Teacher Collaboration Assessment Scales DDAE \(TCAS\), Parental Involvement Rating Scale \(PIRS\), and the third questionnaire was self\-constructed to measure the effectiveness of e\-literacy instruction for ADHD children, Effectiveness of E\-Literacy Instructions Measuring Scale \(ELIMS\)\. Statistical analyses were conducted using Pearson Product Moment Correlation, hierarchical regression analysis, independent samples t\-test, two\-way ANOVA, and mediation analysis through Hayes’ PROCESS Macro\. The findings revealed significant positive relationships between teacher collaboration, parental involvement, and effectiveness of e\-literacy instruction\. Teacher collaboration significantly predicted e\-literacy effectiveness, while parental involvement partially mediated this relationship, indicating that family engagement strengthens the impact of collaborative teaching practices\. Furthermore, children’s age and education level emerged as significant predictors of e\-literacy effectiveness, whereas other demographic characteristics showed limited influence\. Gender differences indicated higher levels of teacher collaboration, parental involvement, and e\-literacy effectiveness among females\. The study concludes that collaborative partnerships between teachers and parents are essential for enhancing digital learning experiences among children with ADHD\. These findings emphasize the importance of integrated educational approaches involving schools, families, and technology\-based interventions to support children with ADHD\.

## [An adaptive statistical and clustering\-based sensor sleep management framework for energy\-efficient IoT networks](../publications/ed56d65586e9921d00a9.md)

Khelu S\. Londhe; Roger R\. Dube

Wireless IoT deployments spend most of their energy keeping every node awake even when their measurements are statistically redundant\. This paper presents the Adaptive Sensor Sleep Management \(ASSM\) framework, which analyses temperature and humidity streams online to decide how many nodes need to stay awake\. ASSM combines a sliding\-window statistical engine, a K\-means stage that selects spatially representative nodes, and a phase detector that separates stable from transitional periods using the derivative of the smoothed signal, with all thresholds estimated online from past samples only\. During stable phases a small subset of nodes remains active; during transitions every node is woken\. We evaluate ASSM on a realistic 100\-node model built from an 86,401\-record Solapur\-mimicking dataset by adding per\-node calibration offset, measurement noise and drift, and we benchmark it against random, round\-robin, fixed\-duty, variance\-adaptive and prediction\-based baselines with an ablation and a multi\-metric fidelity analysis\. Across eight random seeds ASSM keeps the network mean to about 0\.19% and significantly outperforms random selection \(p = 0\.008\), although stronger baselines—fixed\-duty, variance\-adaptive and dual\-prediction—achieve lower mean error; ASSM’s value is that it is training\-free, interpretable and keeps no per\-node model\. A full\-link energy model including switching and gateway\-compute overhead shows a net saving of about 55% at the operating point, remaining above \~ 46% under communication\-overhead stress, and the controller scales near\-linearly to 10,000 nodes\. Rare local events depend on periodic\-wake and threshold\-override safeguards rather than the sleeping subset\.

## [Dynamic path reasoning with large language models for interpretable knowledge graph question answering](../publications/ed5bd71f772dddb9bb7a.md)

Ling Yuan; Bicheng Wu; Yangyang Yang

Abstract Knowledge graph question answering \(KGQA\) aims to answer natural language questions by grounding them in structured knowledge graphs \(KGs\)\. Current KGQA systems still face three linked challenges: representing complex and compositional questions, providing transparent multi\-hop reasoning traces, and using complete path\-level evidence rather than only local triples\. We propose SK\-DRP \( S yntax\- K nowledge enhanced D ynamic R easoning with P rompt learning\), a modular KGQA framework that combines syntax\-aware representation, state\-adaptive path reasoning, and LLM\-assisted answer selection\. The syntax\- and knowledge\-enhanced encoder is an auxiliary representation enhancement that uses dependency information and knowledge\-augmented pre\-training to align questions with KG entities and relations\. Here, dynamic denotes hop\-wise recomputation of the question\-focus indicator, score\-qualified frontier expansion, and hop\-weighted answer aggregation within a fixed dataset\-level maximum hop budget; it does not denote automatic per\-question depth selection\. Candidate global paths are then compressed and transformed into natural\-language auxiliary evidence for candidate\-set\-guided LLM answer selection\. Experiments on MetaQA, WebQSP, and CWQ show that SK\-DRP improves over several path\-based and retrieval\-based baselines on WebQSP and CWQ, while remaining competitive on MetaQA\. Ablation, error, and interpretability analyses clarify how the syntax encoder, dynamic reasoning module, and LLM\-assisted answer selection contribute to the final results, as well as the scope and limitations of the approach\.

## [GENERATIVE AI AND EFL WRITING: ITS IMPACT ON ACCURACY, COMPLEXITY AND FLUENCY](../publications/ed5e1f11d87509c16c7a.md)

Bobur Suyunov

The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) has significantly influenced second and foreign language education, particularly the teaching and learning of writing\. Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT can provide immediate feedback, generate ideas, suggest vocabulary, revise grammatical structures, and support learners throughout different stages of the writing process\. However, the extent to which AI\-assisted writing contributes to learners’ actual linguistic development remains an important research question\. This conceptual paper examines the potential impact of GenAI on three central dimensions of English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) writing performance: accuracy, complexity, and fluency \(CAF\)\. Drawing on recent research in second language writing and AI\-assisted language learning, the paper analyzes the benefits and limitations of GenAI for each dimension\. The literature suggests that AI\-assisted writing can contribute particularly to grammatical accuracy and lexical sophistication by providing immediate corrective feedback and exposure to alternative linguistic forms\. Evidence concerning syntactic complexity and writing fluency, however, is less consistent\. Although learners may produce more polished and fluent\-looking texts with AI assistance, this does not necessarily indicate corresponding development in their independent writing ability\. The paper therefore argues that the pedagogical value of GenAI depends largely on how learners interact with the technology\. When used as a supplementary writing assistant rather than a replacement for independent production, GenAI can support language development, learner autonomy, and reflective writing practices\. The paper concludes by proposing pedagogical principles for responsible AI integration into EFL writing instruction and identifying directions for future empirical research\.

## [NerAxom\-MGF: Leveraging Multi\-Granularity Fusion for Assamese Named Entity Recognition](../publications/ed5fe0319750a6a7bd17.md)

Punam Sarmah; Manash Pratim Lahkar; Shobhanjana Kalita; Utpal Sharma

We introduce MGF\-NER, a multi\-granularity fusion architecture that integrates character\-level, subword\-level, and entity\-span\-level representations for the same task using NerAxom dataset\. NerAxom comprises 102,857 tokens across 4,178 sentences annotated under the BIO scheme with seven entity categories: Person, Location, Organization, Date, Number, Occupation, and Work\-of\-Art\. MGF\-NER combines a Character\-level Convolutional Neural Network that captures morpheme\-level cues attenuated by subword fragmentation, a pre\-trained MuRIL transformer for cross\-lingually pretrained contextual semantics, an Entity Span Attention module for multi\-word boundary detection, and a Conditional Random Field decoder that enforces valid BIO transitions\. Under a seeded five\-run evaluation protocol on the NerAxom test set, MGF\-NER achieves a mean micro\-averaged F1 of 85\.45 ± 0\.46, outperforming the strongest single\-encoder baseline MuRIL \(83\.88±0\.79\) by 1\.57 F1 points; the improvement is statistically significant under a paired sentence\-level Wilcoxon signed\-rank test \(p = 0\.005\)\. We benchmark MGF\-NER against nine baselines spanning traditional feature\-based sequence labelling \(CRF\), a recurrent baseline \(BiLSTM\-CRF\), language\-agnostic multilingual transformers \(mBERT, XLM\-RoBERTa base and large, DistilBERT\-multi\), a script\-similar Bangla\-specialised transformer \(Bangla\-BERT\), and Indic\-specialised transformers \(IndicBERTv2\)\. Single\-component and compound\-component ablations, together with per\-category ablation, decompose the gain across the four architectural components, and error analysis characterises the residual error profile\.

## [Powering the Wearable Era: The Quest for High‐Strain Stretchable Polymer Solar Cells](../publications/ed629601008af7f2210b.md)

Xin Li; Huizhen Ke; Saimeng Li; Chunlong Sun; Yimin Yang; Diyora Urazkulova; Vakhobjon Kuvondikov; Long Ye

The rise of wearable electronics is driving demand for new forms of solar cells with both high power conversion efficiency \(PCE\) and high strain tolerance\. However, these properties are often inherently conflicting: state‐of‐the‐art organic/polymeric photovoltaic materials often rely on rigid or highly fused conjugated backbones, yielding fracture strains below 10% in high‐efficiency systems with PCEs above 21%\. This article critically examines mechanical optimization strategies for emerging high‐strain stretchable polymer solar cells \(HS‐PSCs\), comparing two common polymeric blend architectures: polymer:small‐molecule and all‐polymer systems\. We benchmark mechanical characterization techniques, from elastomer‐based methods to free‐standing tensile testing, and dissect recent strategies to overcome the efficiency–stretchability trade‐off, including molecular engineering \(flexible spacers and hydrogen‐bonding chains\) and morphological control \(ternary blending, layer‐by‐layer assembly, and cocontinuous networks\)\. After surveying over 100 reported systems, several advanced all‐polymer and layer‐by‐layer systems have reached fracture strain &gt;30% while maintaining PCE &gt;15%\. Finally, we offer a forward‐looking perspective on three priority routes \(entanglement‐controlled polymer design, elastomer‐based networks, and crosslinked systems\) that promise to simultaneously deliver &gt;20% PCE and &gt;50% fracture strain\. This review provides a structured inventory of current achievements and a strategic roadmap toward stretchable, commercially viable solar cells\.

## [Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network‐Level Signatures of Glioma](../publications/ed6617c6a15e2ba2bb54.md)

Hongbo Bao; Yan Bai; Jie Hu; Wencai Ding; Jiacheng Lai; Andrew Zalesky; Ye Ella Tian; Yanmei Tie; Janet Y\. Mei; Shengyu Fang; Xing Fan; Licia Luna; Craig K\. Jones; Jianxun Ren; Weigang Cui; Jiadong Yan; Zeya Yan; Zihan Wang; Renwu Zhang; Zhonghua Lv; Yihang Jiao; Tao Jiang; Peng Liang; Haris Iqbal Sair; Yinyan Wang

Gliomas are recognized as network\-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain\. Using resting\-state functional MRI \(rs\-fMRI\) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra\- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor\-related alterations\. Two novel indices\-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions \(RIFR\) and ratio of peritumoral tumor\-related regions \(RPTR\)\-were proposed to describe network remodeling\. Both indices were related to pathological, structural, functional, cognitive, language, and survival measures\. Lower RIFR indicated diminished intratumoral connectivity and worse prognosis, while higher values reflected preserved network integration and longer survival\. Models incorporating network features yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0\.90 in training and 0\.86\-0\.88 in external validation\. Supporting analyses suggested that intratumoral functional regions are associated with distinct molecular and cellular characteristics\. These findings suggest that intra\- and peritumoral networks reflect biologically and functionally distinct tumor subregions and are associated with network\-level alterations, brain function, and patient outcome\. Interpretation is limited by the hemodynamic basis of rs\-fMRI, incomplete data, and limited intraoperative validation\. These findings identify individualized intra\- and peritumoral connectivity measures as candidate markers of glioma\-associated network remodeling and prognosis that require prospective, multimodal validation\.

## [Phytofabricated zinc oxide nanoparticles from Celosia argentea L\.: mechanistic insights into ROS\-mediated apoptosis in the MCF\-7 cell line and photocatalytic degradation of malachite green](../publications/ed66a2530cef1554a240.md)

Gunika Kour; Divya Katal; Sandeep Kaur; Garima Rana; Nahaa M\. Alotaibi; Vaseem Raja

Introduction The green synthetic approach of nanoparticle synthesis using medicinal plants has emerged as an eco\-friendly and efficient approach to develop novel therapeutic agents against cancer\. In the present study, zinc oxide nanoparticles \(ZnO NPs\) were synthesized using methanolic flower extract of Celosia argentea L\., a plant known for its rich phytochemical composition and pharmacological properties\. Methods The biosynthesized ZnO NPs were characterized using UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, and SEM analyses\. The antioxidant activity of the extract and ZnO NPs was assessed using DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, superoxide scavenging, and metal\-chelation assays\. Cytotoxicity against MCF\-7 cells was evaluated by MTT assay\. Apoptotic features were examined by DAPI/confocal microscopy, and ROS levels and apoptotic cell percentages were analyzed by flow cytometry\. Expression of apoptosis\-related proteins was assessed by Western blotting\. Visible light\-driven photocatalytic activity was tested against Malachite Green \(MG\) under varying dye concentration, catalyst loading, and pH, and degradation kinetics, reusability over five consecutive cycles, and radical\-scavenging assays were also evaluated\. Results The analyses confirmed the crystalline nature, nanoscale size, and phytochemical capping of the ZnO NPs\. TEM analysis revealed an average apparent particle size of 18\.76 nm, whereas Williamson–Hall analysis of the XRD data estimated a crystallite size of 28\.83 nm\. The extract exhibited concentration\-dependent antioxidant activity in all assays, and ZnO NPs were more active than the extract in all assays\. The MTT assay showed dose\-dependent cytotoxic effects of the extract \(CAFE\) and ZnO NPs against MCF\-7 cells, with GI50 values of 32\.71 and 8\.735 µg/mL, respectively, at 24 hours\. DAPI/confocal microscopy revealed chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation, membrane blebbing, and apoptotic bodies\. Flow cytometry showed increased ROS levels and percentage of apoptotic cells after treatment\. Western blotting showed enhanced expression of p53, caspase\-3, and caspase\-9 and reduced expression of Bcl\-xl, indicating induction of apoptosis\. Under optimized conditions \(initial dye concentration of 10 ppm, catalyst loading of 20 mg, pH 9\), the ZnO NPs achieved 99\.62% degradation of MG within 60 min under visible light\. Degradation efficiency decreased with increasing dye concentration, whereas alkaline conditions and higher catalyst loading favored performance\. The process followed pseudo\-first\-order kinetics, with the highest apparent rate constant \(k₁ = 0\.061 min⁻¹; R ² = 0\.99\) at 10 ppm MG\. The ZnO NPs retained substantial photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles\. Radical\-scavenging assays revealed that superoxide radicals \(O₂•⁻\) played the predominant role, while hydroxyl radicals and photogenerated holes contributed to the overall oxidative degradation\. Discussion In general, C\. argentea \-mediated ZnO NPs induce ROS\-mediated apoptosis through regulation of apoptosis\-related proteins in MCF\-7 cells\. These results suggest that plant\-mediated ZnO NPs could be useful as anticancer agents, though further studies are needed in other cancer cell lines, with normal cells as controls, and in in vivo models\. The phytofabricated ZnO NPs also show strong potential as reusable visible\-light photocatalysts for dye degradation\.

## [World Action Critic \(WAC\) Model: Joint Foresight and Criticism for Policy Learning](../publications/ed80fa16b795c538ec2c.md)

Xiangteng Zhang; Haoyuan Liu; Yang Guan; Jingliang Duan; Yao Lyu; Tao Zhang; Shuai Zhang; Kehua Sheng; Bo Zhang; Shengbo Eben Li

World models have shown considerable promise in sequential decision\-making by anticipating the consequences of actions and providing predictive foresight for policy learning\. However, learning to reason about counterfactual actions remains challenging, since predictive objectives may underemphasize information critical for action evaluation, while unexecuted actions lack observed futures for direct supervision\. To address these challenges, we propose the World Action Critic \(WAC\) Model, which proposes multimodal action candidates and jointly learns candidate\-conditioned future prediction and consequence evaluation\. In our proposed framework, critic supervision directly shapes intermediate predictive representations during rollout, encouraging them to retain information needed to distinguish action quality\. Observed futures supervise prediction for executed actions, while external task\-quality targets provide evaluation signals for counterfactual candidates\. Through joint optimization, critic signals from these candidates propagate into predictive representations without requiring their observed futures\. Our theoretical analysis characterizes critic\-guided feature retention and bounds candidate\-selection regret\. Applied to autonomous driving, WAC achieves 93\.4 PDMS on NAVSIM\-v1, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly learning predictive foresight and consequence evaluation\.

## [Content\-adaptive Multi\-channel Hybrid Quantum\-classical Block\-wise Optimization for Robust Image Watermarking](../publications/ed981a86363f10783f72.md)

Nova Rijati; Aris Marjuni; Sudipta Kr Ghosal; Aditya Kumar Sahu; Deshinta Arrova Dewi; De Rosal Ignatius Moses Setiadi

The rapid growth of digital image distribution necessitates robust watermarking techniques to protect ownership and ensure data integrity\.This paper proposes a content\-adaptive hybrid quantum\-classical watermarking framework that integrates local adaptive modeling and global optimization\.The method employs Discrete Wavelet Transform \(DWT\) and Discrete Cosine Transform \(DCT\) to provide a stable embedding domain\.Local texture features are extracted from image blocks and mapped using a trained Parameterized Quantum Circuit \(PQC\) to determine adaptive embedding strength\.In parallel, Quantum\-Inspired Annealing \(QIA\) is used to optimize the selection of DCT coefficient positions globally\.A multi\-channel embedding strategy is further incorporated to enhance robustness\.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high imperceptibility \(PSNR &gt; 47 dB, SSIM ≈ 0\.99\) and strong robustness against the evaluated attacks, while remaining competitive with existing methods\.The proposed framework provides a hybrid quantum\-classical approach to image watermarking and represents a process innovation by integrating adaptive quantum learning with global coefficient\-position optimization for robust multimedia copyright protection\.

## [Comparison of piezosurgery vs\. conventional bone chisel for extraction of impacted mandibular third molars with root–canal intimacy: a retrospective cohort study with CBCT\-based preoperative planning](../publications/ed9d3f83818d1a094024.md)

Huijun Hu; Yuchao Zhang; Jian Tan; Yang Yu

Objective To compare clinical outcomes of piezosurgery vs\. conventional chisel for extracting impacted mandibular third molars \(IMTMs\) with roots adjacent to the inferior alveolar nerve canal \(IANC\) under identical CBCT\-based planning, isolating the ultrasonic osteotome&\#x27;s incremental benefit beyond shared imaging\. Methods A retrospective comparative cohort study was conducted using the clinical data of 126 patients with IMTMs whose tooth roots were closely adjacent to the IANC and who were treated in the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery at our hospital between September 2025 and May 2026\. All patients underwent CBCT three\-dimensional reconstruction before the operation to evaluate the anatomical structure and formulate the surgical plan\. The patients were divided into the piezosurgery \( n = 63\) and conventional surgery \( n = 63\) groups\. The conventional surgery group underwent traditional bone chiseling and crown splitting for extraction, while the piezosurgery group underwent extraction using the ultrasonic bone knife minimally invasive technique\. The operation time, intraoperative blood loss, pain visual analogue scale \(VAS\) scores at different time points after surgery, degree of facial swelling, degree of mouth opening limitation, and complication occurrence rate were compared between the two groups\. Results Compared with the conventional surgery group, the piezosurgery group exhibited a markedly shorter surgical procedure duration and a significantly reduced volume of intraoperative blood loss, with all between\-group comparisons yielding statistically significant results \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. There were interaction effects between the two groups and at different time points in the VAS scores, facial swelling differences, and mouth opening limitation differences \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. The VAS scores, facial swelling differences, and mouth opening limitation differences in the piezosurgery group at 1 day, 3 days, and 7 days after surgery were all lower than those in the conventional surgery group \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Additionally, the incidence of adverse postoperative complications was markedly lower in the piezosurgery group than in the conventional surgery group, and this discrepancy was statistically significant \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Conclusion The CBCT\-guided ultrasonic osteotome minimally invasive technique shortens operative time, reduces bleeding, alleviates postoperative pain, swelling, and trismus, and lowers complication rates in IMTM extraction with root\-canal proximity\.

## [O impacto do implante coclear na função cognitiva da pessoa idosa: uma revisão narrativa](../publications/eda50e0e1fa24ea4afa2.md)

Helena Gabriela Fiúsa Alves; Graça Cristina Cardoso De Oliveira

Population ageing is associated with an increased prevalence of chronic conditions, including hearing loss and cognitive decline\. Age\-related hearing loss is one of the most common sensory impairments among older adults and significantly affects communication, autonomy, quality of life, and social participation\. In recent years, hearing loss has been recognized as an important modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia\. This narrative review aimed to analyse the role of cochlear implantation in preventing or mitigating cognitive decline in older adults with severe\-to\-profound hearing loss\. A literature review was conducted using major scientific databases, focusing on studies published between 2015 and 2025\. The findings suggest that cochlear implantation is associated with significant improvements in speech perception, communication, quality of life, and social participation\. Benefits have also been reported in several cognitive domains, including working memory, attention, processing speed, executive functions, and verbal fluency\. Potential mechanisms include reduced sensory deprivation, decreased cognitive load, and enhanced social engagement\. Although methodological limitations remain, current evidence supports the importance of early identification of hearing loss and timely auditory rehabilitation, including cochlear implantation, as a potential strategy to promote healthy ageing and preserve cognitive function\.

## [Molecular chaperone\-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis](../publications/edaeac7cdf63b4cfb815.md)

Ling Hu; Wei Huang; Ji‐Wu Huang; Jing Zhang; Xiaohui Qiu; Botao Cheng; Lifeng Pan; Wen Liu

TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown\. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non\-catalytic tri\-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides \(RiPPs\) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side\-chains\. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N\-terminal domains, which can interact with family\-defining ATP\-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex\. The remaining central multi\-helix and C\-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition\. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix\-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone\-like function in RiPP biosynthesis\. Graspetides are ribosomally synthesized and post\-translationally modified peptides\. Here, TIGR04500 family proteins are shown to guide graspetide biosynthesis as non\-catalytic chaperone\-like partners through a likely widespread recognition mechanism\.

## [EFFICIENT FACE DETECTION USING VIOLA\-JONES ANDNEURAL NETWORKS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY](../publications/edb62dc5a975bcee683a.md)

Saja Kareem Abd; Hadeel Talib Mangi; Alyaa Abdual Kadhum; reem salah kazim; Baneen Abdaljabbar Abdalhussein Ali; Firas Al\-Mahdi Zuhair AbdAlkarim

Face detection technology underpins most of today’s face recognition systems and isvaluable in many industries, including security, healthcare, retail, and entertainment\. The proposed system uses the Viola\-Jones algorithm for preliminaryface detection and an FFNN for feature extraction and classification achieving 98\.5% accuracy on variousdatasets\. ## [ThreatTraceX: Architecture\-Native Attribution and Contrastive Explanations for Trustworthy Cyberattack Detection](../publications/edd747f1123bc64fa6b0.md)

Ravikiran Goturi; Soumen Chakraborty

Chest radiography is the primary imaging modality for pulmonary disease screening, yet the limited interpretability of deep learning models remains a major barrier to clinical adoption\. This paper presents a unified framework for evaluating and improving ex\-plainability in CNN\-based chest X\-ray analysis\. We first conduct a systematic benchmark of five convolutional neural network ar\-chitectures \(DenseNet121, ResNet50, EfficientNetV2, MobileNetV3, and ConvNeXtV2\) combined with four widely used explainabil\-ity methods \(GradCAM, GradCAM\+\+, Integrated Gradients, and SmoothGrad\), evaluated with five complementary metrics span\-ning localization accuracy, attribution faithfulness, and robustness on the NIH ChestX\-ray14 dataset\. Evaluated on all 880 bounding\-box\-annotated images, the benchmark shows that explanation quality depends more on the backbone than on the attribution method: ConvNeXtV2 leads on localization while DenseNet121 of\-fers the highest explanation consistency at far lower parameter cost\. Building on this, we propose AttrNet, an explainability harness that is backbone\-agnostic by construction: it wraps a classifica\-tion network with a lightweight attribution branch that predicts class\-specific explanation maps natively in the forward pass and couples them back to the classifier through a cross\-attention gate and differentiable localization supervision, turning explainability from a post\-hoc by\-product into a trained objective\. Instantiated on DenseNet121 and evaluated on held\-out lesions under cross\-validation, AttrNet raises heatmap–lesion IoU from 0\.200 to 0\.345 and Pointing Game accuracy from 0\.333 to 0\.596 \(both 𝑝 &lt; 10−18, paired\) at a cost of 0\.011 classification AUC, an exchange favourable wherever spatial reliability governs clinical utility\. We further in\-troduce C\-GradCAM, a contrastive extension of GradCAM that suppresses activations shared with competing disease classes to produce more faithful and disease\-discriminative explanations, im\-proving attribution quality without requiring network retraining or architectural modification\. Collectively, the benchmark, Attr\-Net, and C\-GradCAM demonstrate complementary strategies for advancing transparent, trustworthy, and clinically meaningful ex\-plainable AI for pulmonary disease diagnosis\. CCS Concepts • Computing methodologies → Neural networks; Computer vision; • Applied computing → Health informatics\.

## [Policy, Prosperity, and Progress: A Triple Lens Study on India’s Gig Economy Towards Viksit Bharat 2047](../publications/edf21925ca6e47debe6e.md)

Ms\. Ramya R\.; Dyuti Srinivasan; Kritikaa Kohli

The global economic landscape is undergoing significant transformation, driven by the rapid expansion of the gig workforce\. “Positioned outside conventional employer \- employee relationships, gig workers often navigate irregular incomes, limited social security, and inadequate institutional protection, making financial resilience a critical yet underexplored dimension of the platform economy\. With this workforce continuing to grow, labor policies need to cater to the upliftment of this workforce and consider the dynamic incline this economy can promise for a smart future\. A range of labour policies of key importance to gig workers is drawn on by this paper, with their provisions examined through secondary data analysis\. Adopting a triple lens approach \- Rajdharma \(Policy Framework\), Artha \(Economic Framework\) and Lokasangraha \(Social Framework\) dimensions, vantage points on how digital platforms and policies can adopt initiatives in these frames are proposed by the paper\. The existing regulatory landscape governing gig work is further examined by it, to develop a comprehensive understanding of the platform economy\. As India marches towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, it becomes paramount to leverage the potential of this workforce by understanding the opportunities and challenges faced by them\.

## [Autonomous Preventive Healthcare Systems Combining IoT Sensors, AI, and Behavioral Nudging](../publications/edf4788b6de337df0a01.md)

Sojy John; Venkata Phaneendra Reddi; Pradeep Rao Vennamaneni; Sri Prudhvi Adusumilli; Naveen Shrivastava; Mahesh Marri

Internet of Things \(IoT\) sensor networks, combined with Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) enabled analytics and behavioral nudging paradigms, have ushered in a paradigm shift in the field of autonomous preventive health care\. The marriage of Internet of Things \(IoT\) sensor networks, Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) analytics, and behavioral nudging paradigms has emerged as a paradigm shift in the realm of autonomous preventive health care\. The functional integration of wearable and implantable biosensors, machine learning \(ML\) algorithms, and nudge\-based digital behavior change interventions for proactive, personalized health management before the development of clinical disease is reviewed\. The paper is based upon 17 peer reviewed references published between 2018 and 2021, which define architectural principles, performance requirements, and constraints of such integrated systems\. Quantitative analyses show that hybrid AI models \(CNN with LSTM\) can reach a maximum diagnostic accuracy of 96\.1%, while support vector machines with the same IoT data streams can reach 87\.2%\. The highest observed adherence gain \(22\.1%\) and 90\-day retention rate \(69%\) were achieved with behavioral nudging via restructuring default options, among the modalities assessed\. The integrated platform provides a 76% latency reduction in preventive interventions over architectures involving the Internet of Things alone, and a USD 1,870 annual patient cost savings after deployment, compared to traditional care pathways, which represents a 34\.2% decrease\. In addition to regulatory dimensions, security vulnerabilities and limitations of interoperability are examined, and ethical considerations of algorithmic decision making are addressed\. The paper&\#x27;s authors conclude that achieving autonomous preventive healthcare requires a synergy of sensor accuracy, adaptive AI, and human behavior science within a privacy\-enhancing and scalable framework\.

## [It’s not who you know: sociometric position did not shape children’s innovation or imitation propensities](../publications/edf7075990e0f0235000.md)

Bruce S\. Rawlings; Emma Flynn; Rachel L\. Kendal

Introduction The capacity for cumulative culture depends on the interplay between social learning and innovation, yet the social\-ecological factors that shape individual variation in these processes remain poorly understood\. Children’s position within peer networks has been theorised to influence learning strategies by shaping exposure to social models and normative conformity pressures, but this prediction remains untested in experimental contexts\. Methods We tested whether children’s sociometric position predicted social learning and innovation across three complementary experimental tasks\. 256 children aged 7–11 completed sociometric friendship nominations within their school classrooms and three tasks: the Multi\-Method Box, a puzzlebox measuring learning strategy choice and innovation\-by\-modification; a tool innovation task, the hook task; and the Alternate Uses divergent thinking task\. We derived three peer\-nomination indices — out\-degree, reciprocated friendships, and in\-degree — and tested their associations with task performance using multilevel models controlling for age and classroom clustering\. Results Across all tasks and outcome measures, none of the sociometric indices predicted children’s learning strategy choice, imitation fidelity, innovation\-by\-modification, tool innovation success, solution method, or divergent thinking performance\. In contrast, age consistently predicted innovation\-related outcomes: older children produced more reward\-exit and tool\-entrance innovations on the Multi\-Method Box, were more likely to solve the hook task and to use a hook rather than a dragging strategy, and generated more divergent thinking responses\. These age effects replicated well\-established developmental findings and held independently of children’s network position\. Discussion These findings suggest that individual\-level dispositions and developmental cognitive gains may carry greater explanatory weight than relational embeddedness for micro\-level learning decisions in middle childhood\. Network structure may regulate the flow of cultural information across populations without determining the immediate learning strategy choices of individual children in individually administered experimental contexts\.

## [Islamic Social Welfare and Economic Justice for Promoting Peaceful Coexistence in Nigeria: Implications for Conventional Welfare Policies](../publications/edfd5a48e865b776c4fe.md)

Rauf Adeola Lateef; Edu Muhsin Olajide; Balogun Iliyas Idowu

Objective: This study aims to analyze the role of zakat, alms, and waqf in realizing economic justice and strengthening social peace\. The research also examines its potential integration with government welfare programs in Nigeria\. Theoretical framework: The research integrates the concept of Maqasid al\-Shari&\#x27;ah with the theory of Justice as Fairness from John Rawls\. This framework is used to analyze the justice distribution of resources and social cohesion in multicultural societies\. Literature review: Previous research has extensively discussed the limitations of social welfare and sectarian conflicts in Nigeria\. However, the role of Islamic social institutions in conflict resolution and their integration with government policies is still minimally empirically studied\. Methods: The study used a qualitative approach with thematic analysis of Islamic legal sources, government documents, and structured consultations\. Data were obtained from 30 participants, including Islamic legal experts, welfare managers, and representatives of conflict\-affected communities in Northern Nigeria\. Results: Preliminary findings suggest that societies with well\-functioning Islamic welfare institutions tend to have lower levels of social conflict\. However, their effectiveness is still hampered by organizational fragmentation, weak government recognition, and limitations of public welfare programs\. Implications: The study proposes an integrated welfare model linking Islamic social finance with government social protection systems\. Strengthening transparency, accountability, and organizational capacity is needed to improve services and reduce social conflicts\. Novelty: The novelty of the research lies in an empirical study of the relationship between Islamic social institutions, economic justice, and peace in the Nigerian context\. The research also offers an integrative policy model that aligns Islamic economic principles with secular governance\.

## [Clinical Reasoning, Pathophysiology, and Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care: A Conceptual Framework for Integrating Decision\-Making](../publications/ee052e42cf12eccaeae2.md)

Álvaro Réa\-Neto; Jeane Cristina Fonseca Vieira

Medical practice is an interpretive, decision\-making activity conducted under uncertainty, and care quality depends on clinicians’ ability to organize knowledge into hypotheses, understand mechanisms, estimate probabilities, and revise decisions as the clinical course evolves\. In critical care, where physiology is unstable and trajectories are nonlinear, these demands are magnified\. We propose a conceptual framework integrating three complementary dimensions: clinical reasoning, which provides the cognitive architecture of decision\-making; pathophysiology, which supplies the causal structure to interpret biological phenomena; and artificial intelligence, which, when well designed and critically used, can organize data, generate hypotheses, and reduce cognitive load\. Tracing the evolution of clinical reasoning from the anatomoclinical model to hypothetico\-deductive, probabilistic, cognitive, and sociotechnical models, we examine how diagnostic and therapeutic errors arise from interacting cognitive biases, system factors, and case characteristics, and how better problem representation, differential diagnosis, and team culture may mitigate them\. We also frame Bayesian reasoning and decision thresholds as the probabilistic grammar of bedside decisions, analyze the risks of artificial intelligence, including automation bias, opacity, and limited metacognition, and propose principles for its safe use\. Rather than replacing physicians, artificial intelligence should strengthen clinical reasoning and reinforce calibrated, accountable bedside judgment\. These principles are intended as a framework for future research and require empirical validation before clinical translation\.

## [SecureHealthKey\+: Integrating Explainable TinyML Anomaly Detection Into Lightweight Authentication Protocols in IoT\-Enabled Healthcare Systems](../publications/ee056ae6863bfd92fd16.md)

Shital Pawar; Sonali Patil; Ashwini Sengar; Khushal Khairnar; Sandip Thite; Mohammad Israr

The Internet of Medical Things \(IoMT\) and Wireless Body Area Networks \(WBANs\) enable real\-time, remote, and continuous patient monitoring but remain vulnerable to cyber\-physical attacks, including unauthorized device access, replay, man\-in\-the\-middle \(MITM\), and slow\-rate denial\-of\-service \(DoS\) attacks\. Existing lightweight authentication protocols are computationally suitable for resource\-constrained wearable sensors but may not detect behavioral anomalies occurring during otherwise valid cryptographic handshakes\. This study presents SecureHealthKey\+, a hybrid security framework that extends the lightweight mutual authentication mechanism of the SecureAuthKey scheme by integrating an Explainable Tiny Machine Learning\-based Anomaly Detection \(ETAD\) layer within an Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers \(IEEE\) 802\.15\.6\-inspired WBAN architecture\. The framework uses a microcontroller\-based Smart Medical Device \(SMD\) and a single\-board\-computer\-based Medical Gateway Server \(MGS\)\. The SMD computes a cryptographic authentication token using a pre\-shared body\-sensor key, fresh nonce, and device identifier while extracting a five\-dimensional Health Feature Metadata \(HFM\) vector comprising timestamp deviation \(HFM1\), sensor\-identity novelty \(HFM2\), packet rate \(HFM3\), physiological signal drift index \(HFM4\), and inter\-frame gap variance \(HFM5\)\. At the MGS, an 8\-bit integer \(INT8\)\-quantized Tiny Machine Learning \(TinyML\) autoencoder processes the HFM vector to generate a Health Anomaly Decision \(HAD\), cryptographically bound to the session key \(SK\) through SK\_H = H\(SK ∥ HAD\)\. A SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) layer provides feature\-level attribution for anomalous sessions\. Evaluation used 12,000 benign authentication traces and 4,800 synthetic attack traces generated on a single\-device benchtop testbed\. The framework achieved a weighted true\-positive rate of 97\.4% across four synthetic attack types\. An IEEE 802\.11 wireless link using the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport \(MQTT\) protocol emulated the WBAN gateway tier; dedicated IEEE 802\.15\.6 radio hardware was not used\. Therefore, the results represent a proof\-of\-concept rather than validation of real\-world, multi\-patient WBAN efficacy\.

## [Assessing the Value of Mentoring for Female Business Students](../publications/ee09d53e9099836a0c6e.md)

Nikita\-Marie Bridgeman; Paul Stokes

Industry\-led mentoring is a strategic tool that can bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical expertise, providing mentees with skills development opportunities that stretch beyond what can be learned via classroom\-based educational approaches alone\. Mentoring is now commonplace within organisational life, but is less common within UK university business schools\. This suggests a knowledge gap in terms of understanding how mentoring can be embedded as a complementary tool to improve student skills development within business schools\. The aim of this study was to explore the perceived value of industry mentorship from the perspective of the mentees, to develop a greater understanding of the potential benefits mentoring relationships at a university level can provide\. Following the journey of mentees on a Women in Business mentoring programme, this study specifically explored the context of female university students\. Mentees on the programme were female undergraduate and postgraduate students studying on courses within Sheffield Business School\. Using a longitudinal study design, semi\-structured interviews were conducted at three stages of a yearlong mentoring programme: 1\. pre\-mentoring, 2\. during mentoring, and 3\. post\-mentoring\. Interview transcripts were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six\-phase framework\. The findings show the value of mentoring from a mentee perspective, most notably the notion of having someone in their corner, an ability to gain personalised guidance, and the opportunity to develop a professional network\. The challenges of being mentored at this level were also expressed, drawing attention to the need for pre\-mentoring education to support meaningful engagement with the process, and a requirement for a clear scheme structure to guide mentees\. Guided by these findings, we offer key practical recommendations to programme designers so they can successfully utilise mentoring as part of their offer to students, thus supporting university business schools to further enhance their career and skills development offerings\.

## [Regulating Marine Mammal Tourism Management: Challenges and Opportunities for Effective Enforcement in Aotearoa/New Zealand](../publications/ee10a2c823cc8840103c.md)

Yasmine M\. Elmahdy; Mark Bryan Orams; Michael Lück; Heike Annette Schänzel

Marine mammal tourism \(MMT\) in Aotearoa/New Zealand operates under one of the world’s most established environmental protection regimes, centred on the Marine Mammals Protection Act 1978 \(MMPA\) and Marine Mammals Protection Regulations 1992 \(MMPR\)\. Despite this reputation, persistent non\-compliance and weak enforcement have raised concerns about the long\-term sustainability of the MMT industry and the effectiveness of existing regulatory tools\. Rapidly changing human pressures on marine ecosystems, including accelerating tourism growth and expanding recreational use of coastal waters, raise questions about the adequacy of static regulatory frameworks\. This qualitative study investigates the challenges and opportunities for enforcement within New Zealand’s MMT management system\. Drawing on 40 in\-depth, semi\-structured interviews with four key stakeholder groups—the Department of Conservation \(DoC\), permitted tour operators, indigenous Māori representatives, and scientists—the research identifies systemic constraints that undermine regulatory effectiveness, including ambiguous legal definitions, difficulties proving intent, limited statutory powers, resource shortages, and outdated provisions inadequate for the challenges of a changing world\. The findings reveal an over\-reliance on commercial tour operators to perform quasi\-enforcement functions, widespread frustration with warning\-letter approaches that rarely escalate, and challenges for DoC officers operating in small communities where social proximity reduces their ability to enforce regulations impartially\. These enforcement gaps contribute to unresolved stakeholder conflict, reduced regulatory credibility, and weakened conservation outcomes for marine mammals\. The study outlines several pathways for strengthening governance, including legislative revision, enhanced compliance mechanisms, expanded enforcement capacity, and the use of external officers to reduce community\-based conflicts of interest\. The findings demonstrate how enforcement shortcomings can erode the legitimacy and effectiveness of conservation regimes and provide evidence\-based recommendations for improving marine mammal protection and governance\.

## [‘Candidatus Phytoplasma zeae’: community\-driven species delineation of the maize bushy stunt phytoplasma, a Dalbulus\-transmitted corn pathogen confined to the Americas](../publications/ee3b404adaa3e879dda1.md)

Thierry Alexandre Pellegrinetti; Joshua Molligan; Abraão Almeida Santos; Maria Cristina Canale; Maíra Rodrigues Duffeck; Alejandro Olmedo\-Velarde; Jordanne Jacques; Ivair Valmorbida; Ashleigh M\. Faris; Marcos Vinicius Silva Andrade; Magda Alana Pompelli Manica; Mauricio Luna; Paola Reyes\-Caldas; Jairo Rodríguez Chalarca; Tim Dumonceaux; Edel Pérez‐López

A novel phytoplasma species, ‘ Candidatus Phytoplasma zeae’, is proposed based on ecological distinctiveness, vector specificity, whole\-genome comparisons and community consensus\. This phytoplasma is associated with maize bushy stunt \(MBS\) disease in corn \( Zea mays \) and is transmitted exclusively by Dalbulus maidis and Dalbulus elimatus , two leafhopper species endemic to the Americas that has been reported in Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and several U\.S\. states\. Here, we sequenced and assembled the genome of MBS phytoplasma \(MBSP\) strains from Brazil and the USA to describe and propose this new species\. Although the 16S rRNA gene sequence of the proposed reference strain, MBSP\-BR RS , shares &gt;99% identity with that of ‘ Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris’, key nucleotide polymorphisms distinguish ‘ Ca \. P\. zeae’ from other 16SrI\-related phytoplasma species\. Genome\-wide average nucleotide identity between ‘ Ca \. P\. zeae’ and all available ‘ Ca \. P\. asteris’\-related strains genomes was between 92\.6 and 98\.4%\. Comparative genomic analyses revealed unique gene clusters in ‘ Ca \. P\. zeae’ associated with amino acid transport, defence mechanisms and protein turnover, which may contribute to its specialization in corn\. The ecological profile of ‘ Ca \. P\. zeae’, including its narrow host and vector range and restricted geographic distribution, supports its recognition as a novel species under Rule c of the IRPCM guidelines\. The designation ‘ Ca \. P\. zeae’ is, therefore, proposed by members of the research community who have studied this pathogen for over a decade, with the MBSP\-Brazil RS strain serving as the reference\.
