## [¿Quién está pensando? Delegación cognitiva, misiones de aprendizaje y el lugar del docente en tiempos de inteligencia artificial generativa](../publications/ee5aba8a8dd4f6f5b853.md)

Juliana Valeria Viviani

The rise of generative artificial intelligence forces a revision of assumptions that have become entrenched in contemporary pedagogical discourse: that activity by itself produces learning, that projects automatically develop critical thinking, that student autonomy requires reducing teacher intervention, and that competency development can be conceived separately from knowledge construction\. This article argues that none of these four assumptions withstands close scrutiny against the available evidence on problem\-based learning, project\-based learning, cognitive load, and scaffolding, and proposes shifting the discussion away from the choice of active methodologies toward the design of learning missions, understood as intentional architectures of cognitive experience that articulate problems, knowledge, cognitive operations, interactions, mediations, teacher interventions, technologies, and evidence\. The central argument concerns the risk of cognitive delegation, that is, the displacement of specific intellectual operations onto external resources, particularly artificial intelligence systems\. Delegation is not intrinsically negative; the problem arises when the operation delegated is precisely the one that constitutes the object of learning, and artificial intelligence does not by itself create educational superficiality but rather makes visible, and can amplify, a superficiality that certain pedagogical designs already contained\. The article brings together classic contributions on problem\-based learning, cognitive load, scaffolding, and cognitive apprenticeship with recent research on generative artificial intelligence, critical thinking, cognitive dependence, and the evaluation of student\-AI interactions, and introduces the categories of cognitive density and delegation architecture as didactic design tools\. It concludes by proposing that teachers be restored to the role of designers of the cognitive architecture of the experience, responsible for defining what can be delegated, what must be verified, and what operations must necessarily remain in the student’s hands\.

## [Caridade social e algorética](../publications/ee6330215c36bbc3f7b1.md)

Alex da Silva Sirqueira

Este artigo investiga como a caridade social pode oferecer contraponto crítico à algorética e mitigar a cultura do descarte nos sistemas de Inteligência Artificial\. Mediante abordagem teórico\-analítica fundamentada no magistério eclesial e literatura científica especializada\. O estudo examina a dignidade humana nas tradições bíblica e filosófica, analisa criticamente a exclusão algorítmica e propõe a diaconia da técnica como práxis de humanização\. Os resultados evidenciam que a algorética formal mostra\-se insuficiente quando desvinculada de transformações nas estruturas de poder\. A caridade social reconhece no vulnerável o critério definitivo de validação do progresso científico\. Conclui\-se que a superação da cultura do descarte requer converter a IA de instrumento de poder a ferramenta de libertação e justiça distributiva\.

## [6PPD\-quinone exposure impairs erectile function through dysregulation of the HIF\-1α/eNOS/NO axis: multi\-omics and in vivo evidence](../publications/ee634a8c5bb285f89522.md)

Chunyang Meng; Yuqi Li; Xinyao Zhu; Yifan Li; Yuelin Du; Zhongyou Xia

Background 6PPD\-quinone \(6PPD\-Q\), a transformation product of the tire antioxidant 6PPD, has emerged as an environmental contaminant with potential reproductive toxicity\. However, its role in erectile dysfunction \(ED\) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear\. Methods This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, single\-cell RNA sequencing, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and animal experiments to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD\-Q exposure to ED\. Results A total of 134 genes were identified at the intersection of the 6PPD\-Q\- and ED\-related gene sets\. Integration of bulk and single\-cell transcriptomic data, followed by LASSO and SVM\-RFE analyses, prioritized ACO1, HIF1A, PDK4, and PTPN11\. Among these genes, only HIF1A showed a significant association with ED risk in the Mendelian randomization analysis\. Molecular docking and a 100\-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the structural plausibility of an interaction between 6PPD\-Q and HIF\-1α\. In rats, 6PPD\-Q exposure reduced the ICPmax/MAP ratio and cavernosal NO levels without affecting testosterone\. These changes were accompanied by increased HIF\-1α and decreased p\-eNOS, eNOS, and p\-eNOS/eNOS levels in the corpus cavernosum\. PX\-478 partially restored eNOS/NO signaling and erectile function\. Conclusion These findings suggest that 6PPD\-Q may contribute to ED by activating HIF1A\-related stress responses and impairing eNOS/NO\-mediated endothelial relaxation\.

## [DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium](../publications/ee6562006f1ed788f1d6.md)

Bin Ma; Min Yu; Vijay Kodamalla; Jialin Liu; Dong Li

On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps\. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output\. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests\. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1\.2\-4\.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32\.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles\. On four of the five models, resident serving is 1\.5\-3\.4x faster than standalone runs that reload weights from a warm file cache for each generation\.

## [Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation](../publications/ee7ca11c160fa7203de3.md)

Emmanuelle Usun Stephen; Khai‐Lin Hew; Chze\-Yin Tan; Yeun‐Mun Choo

Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi\-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches\. Network pharmacology provides a systems\-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease\-related information to investigate these complex interactions\. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active\-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking and molecular dynamics\. The workflow is organised around the strength of evidence, using a hierarchy that grades compound–target evidence, and the limits of validation and the items needed for reproducible reporting are specified\. In addition, strategies for experimental validation, including biophysical and biochemical assays, cellular studies, omics approaches, pharmacokinetic evaluation, and in vivo models, are considered\. Important limitations, including database bias, false\-positive predictions, inappropriate network interpretation, limited consideration of in vivo exposure, and metabolite\-related effects, are highlighted\. Future developments involving multi\-omics, microbiome data, single\-cell and spatial analysis, and artificial intelligence may further improve the biological relevance and predictive value of network pharmacology\. Overall, network pharmacology can serve as a useful bridge between natural product chemistry, computational analysis, and experimental pharmacology when supported by rigorous validation\.

## [Democratizing the Science of Wellness: Leveraging Real\-World Personal Data and Decentralized Infrastructure to Accelerate Longevity and Regenerative Medicine](../publications/ee7d68f26de25c51d518.md)

Noah Craft

Traditional clinical trial infrastructure is fundamentally bottlenecked by high costs, rigid protocols, and an over\-reliance on centralized clinical settings\. These limitations disproportionately impact the fields of health longevity, alternative medicine, nutraceuticals, and regenerative therapies, where interventions are highly personalized and real\-world efficacy often diverges from idealized laboratory settings\. This paper outlines a paradigm shift toward a decentralized, participatory research model, termed “The Science of You”\. Utilizing the Consumer Health, Learning, and Organizing Ecosystem \(CHLOE\) infrastructure developed by People Science, we demonstrate how rigorous, Institutional Review Board \(IRB\)\-approved, virtual and decentralized clinical trials \(DCTs\) can empower individuals to test interventions on their unique physiological profiles\. By bridging the gap between consumer curiosity and clinical\-grade evidence, this model accelerates translational science, reduces research costs, and builds a comprehensive, decentralized repository of real\-world personal data\. We review recent validation studies utilizing this infrastructure, including remote clinical trials on fasting mimetics and GABA\-producing probiotics, to illustrate how structured, participant\-led data collection can unlock scalable, ethical, and highly accessible paths toward healthy longevity\.

## [Dynamic safety filters in reinforcement learning for robotic systems](../publications/ee7e8d16ba6cc867439f.md)

Anže Rifel

Pri spodbujevalnem učenju se agent uči iz lastnih poskusov in postopno izboljšuje svojo strategijo, torej pravilo, ki vsakemu stanju priredi dejanje\. V robotiki je tako učenje drago, saj napaka lahko pomeni poškodbo robota in tveganje za okolico\. Nevarnost se običajno rešuje s statičnimi pravili, na primer s pragom na kotu, ta pa ne upoštevajo dinamike fizičnih sistemov: isti kot je lahko povsem varen ali že nepopravljivo izgubljen, odvisno od smeri gibanja in preostalega nadzora\. V delu preizkušamo dinamično alternativo, pri kateri agent nevarnost oceni sam, brez zunanje opredelitve prepovedanih stanj\. Osrednja mera je opolnomočenost: koliko različnih prihodnjih izidov lahko agent s svojimi dejanji še doseže, zato upade, ko agent izgublja nadzor\. Oceno z utežjo prištejemo k nagradi za nalogo kot pomožno nagrado, tako da se agent uči tudi ohranjati nadzor\. Za primerjavo vključimo še prediktivno informacijo, ki meri, koliko prihodnosti je mogoče razbrati iz preteklosti\. Mehanizem preverjamo na determinističnem obrnjenem nihalu, ki ga mora agent z omejenim navorom pripeljati v ukazano lego in jo zadržati\. Z vzvratno dosegljivostjo je mogoče za vsako stanje natančno izračunati, ali je padec, torej prekoračitev mejnega kota, ki konča epizodo, še mogoče preprečiti\. To služi kot referenčna resnica o tveganju, delež učnih epizod s padcem pa kot merilo varnosti učenja\. Učimo tako strategije za posamezen cilj kot eno strategijo za vse cilje\. Analiza približno 3\.000 učnih tekov prinese tri ugotovitve\. Prvič, opolnomočenost tveganje zares zaznava: stanja razvrsti po nevarnosti občutno bolje kot katerakoli od obeh spremenljivk, iz katerih je izračunana \(rangovna korelacija z izračunano referenco 0,70 proti 0,33 za kotno hitrost in 0,00 za kot nihala\), prediktivna informacija pa na istem preizkusu odpove\. Drugič, vpliv uteži ni sorazmeren kompromis, temveč ima optimum: pri zmernih vrednostih se padci med učenjem občutno zmanjšajo ob komaj opaznem upadu uspešnosti naloge, pri pretiranih pa pomožna nagrada prevlada nad nalogo in agent cilj opusti\. Tretjič, pri strategiji za posamezen cilj korist ne izvira iz vsebine signala, saj jo enako dobro dosežeta kontroli brez informacijske vsebine, konstantna in naključno premešana pomožna nagrada\. Pri enotni strategiji za vse cilje pa opolnomočenost korist obdrži in padce med učenjem zniža s 43,8 na 27,7 %, obe kontroli pa sta slabši od izhodišča brez pomožne nagrade\. Notranji varnostni signal je torej učinkovit le, kadar je porazdelitev obiskanih stanj dovolj široka, da signal preko nje ohrani dovoljšnjo variabilnost

## [Enhancing copper and cobalt hydrometallurgical leaching through deep learning\-based process optimisation](../publications/ee7f29d215694d933743.md)

Mathieu Kayembe Musala; Matthieu Matthieu Tshanga; Kgabo Humphrey Thamaga; Kubangala Brest Kasongo; Sudhir Kumar Singh; Richard Ngenda Banka

This study presents a comprehensive machine learning framework for the optimisation of metallurgical parameters for the grinding, leaching and solid/liquid separation in a Congolese Copperbelt hydrometallurgical plant\. Three deep learning architectures namely Deep Neural Network \(DNN\), Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\), and Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) were designed, trained, and comparatively evaluated\. Models were trained to predict Cu and Co leaching recoveries from ten critical physicochemical process variables: feed rate, particle size distribution \(PSD\), percentage solids at key settling or decantation stages \(Leach feed thickener \(LFT\), Counter current decantation \(CCD4\), Leach discharge thickener \(LDT\)\), metal losses in overflow streams, and flocculant addition rates\. The DNN achieved superior predictive performance with MAE = 1\.328 % and R 2 = 0\.721 for Cu recovery, substantially outperforming CNN \(MAE = 2\.381 %, R 2 = 0\.017\) and LSTM \(MAE = 2\.421 %, R 2 = − 0\.024\)\. Permutation\-based feature importance identifies PSD \(granulometry\) as the dominant predictor \(ΔMAE = \+0\.368\), followed by metal losses and thickener underflow densities\. A 3\-month DNN forecast projects Cu recovery improving from the 2024–2025 mean of 96\.0 % to 97\.2–97\.8 % as gradual PSD and LDT improvements are implemented, with Co recovery reaching 79\.8–80\.0 %\. The critical operational recommendation is to improve milling fineness from the current mean PSD of 61 % to the 75–80 % at 75 µm target range through SAG mill circuit optimisation\.

## [SYSTEM ANALYSIS OF MUSICAL CYBERNETIC SYSTEMS: THEORY, CLASSIFICATION, AND APPLICATIONS](../publications/ee7fc1a8a6434f7b8fab.md)

Gleb G\. Rogozinski; Irina B\. Gorbunova

Computer Music Technologies \(CMT\) combine musical acoustics, digital signal processing, and software engineering\. These systems integrate automation, sound synthesis, and programming languages for composition\. This article uses a systems\-analytical approach to study CMT as complex structures, focusing on interactions to uncover developmental pathways\. It highlights Musical Cybernetic Systems \(MCS\), which merge artificial intelligence, generative composition, and synthesis to expand creativity\. Despite their use, MCS lack systematic study, complicating their analysis and optimization\. The article proposes a methodology for analyzing MCS using signal theory, set theory, and graph theory\. It identifies signal and symbolic information as key to understanding MCS data structures\. Sound synthesis and processing systems are described using IDEF0 notation, with examples of sonification and generative processes\. This approach reveals MCS design principles, offering insights into their functionality and interaction with external environments\.

## [Rony, Moustaq Karim Khan ; Das, Alok ; Khalil, Md Ibrahim ; Peu, Umme Rabeya ; Mondal, Bishwajit ; Alam, Md Shafiul ; Shaleah, Abu Zafor Md ; Parvin, Mst Rina ; Alrazeeni, Daifallah M\. &amp; Akter, Fazila: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Nursing Care: An Umbrella Review](../publications/ee813f5a5745391ce5da.md)



\_Nursing Inquiry\_ 32 \(2\):e70023\. 2025Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is revolutionizing nursing by enhancing decision‐making, patient monitoring, and efficiency\. Machine learning, natural language processing \(NLP\), and predictive analytics claim to improve safety and automate tasks\. However, a structured analysis of AI applications is necessary to ensure their effective implementation in nursing practice\. This umbrella review aimed to synthesize existing systematic reviews on AI applications in nursing care, providing a comprehensive analysis of its benefits, challenges, and ethical implications\. By consolidating findings from multiple sources, this review seeks to offer evidence‐based insights to guide the effective and responsible integration of AI in nursing practice\. A systematic umbrella review approach was employed following PRISMA guidelines\. Multiple databases, including PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore, were searched for review articles published between 2015 and 2024\. Findings were synthesized thematically to identify key trends, benefits, limitations, and research gaps\. This review synthesized 13 studies, emphasizing AI&\#x27;s impact on clinical decision support, patient monitoring, nursing education, and workflow optimization\. AI enhances early disease detection, minimizes diagnostic errors, and automates documentation, improving efficiency\. However, data privacy risks, biases, ethical concerns, and limited AI literacy hinder integration\. AI presents significant opportunities for improving nursing care, yet its successful implementation requires addressing ethical, legal, and practical challenges\. Adequate AI training, robust data governance frameworks, and policies ensuring responsible AI use are essential for its integration into nursing practice\. Future research should explore long‐term AI impact, training models for nurses, and strategies to balance AI‐driven efficiency with human‐centered care\. \(direct link \)

## [Integrasi Internet of Things \(IoT\) dan Battery Energy Storage System \(BESS\) pada PLTS Apung Cirata](../publications/ee84e97611579c3bc951.md)

ADITYA Pratama Somanta; Rudy Laksmono W; Subur Wahono

Integrasi Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Surya \(PLTS\) Terapung berskala masif membawa tantangan intermitensi terhadap stabilitas jaringan elektrifikasi\. Penelitian ini mengkaji penerapan teknologi Internet of Things pada Battery Energy Storage System di PLTS Apung Cirata \(192 MWp\) sebagai solusi cerdas untuk mengelola fluktuasi daya dan menjaga ketahanan lingkungan\. Menggunakan metode campuran berbasis fisika terapan dan ekologi lingkungan, studi ini merancang arsitektur pemantauan termal dan elektris baterai berbasis Internet of Things secara real\-time\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa otomasi pelepasan beban \(discharge\) melalui smart grid menaikkan load factor sistem dari 79,88% menjadi 86% serta menekan rugi daya transmisi hingga 4%\. Selain mitigasi elektrifikasi, sinergi infrastruktur ini mewujudkan konsep Water\-Energy\-Food Nexus; di mana naungan panel surya yang didukung keandalan baterai mampu menekan laju evaporasi air waduk hingga 40–70%\. Retensi air tawar ini memberikan dampak ganda bagi optimalisasi debit Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Air \(PLTA\) \(Energi\) sekaligus menjamin ketersediaan air irigasi pertanian di hilir \(Pangan\)\. Kajian ini menempatkan Indonesia sebagai benchmark di Asia Tenggara dalam mengadopsi penyimpanan energi berbasis Internet of Things guna memadukan ketahanan infrastruktur dan pelestarian ekosistem, sekaligus memperkuat fondasi teknis pencapaian visi Asta Cita 100 GW PLTS demi kedaulatan energi nasional\.

## [Transformer Architectures for Respiratory Sound Analysis and Multimodal Diagnosis](../publications/ee8c64bbb2d19f605f16.md)

Theodore Aptekarev; Vladimir Sokolovsky; G\. B\. Furman; Е\. Г\. Фурман

Abstract Breath sound analysis is one of the diagnostic approaches for various lung diseases\. However, traditional auscultation is subjective and dependent on the physician’s experience\. Recent studies have demonstrated that computer\-assisted methods analyzing these sounds can significantly improve the accuracy of diagnosis of the patient’s condition\. However, the absence of a common basis for fair comparison, limited use of patient metadata, and lack of interpretability make these approaches difficult to adopt in clinical practice\. In the paper, we propose to utilize the benefits of the recent state\-of\-the\-art sound classification models and a multimodal approach for respiratory disease screening and diagnostics\. To achieve this goal, we use the Audio Spectrogram Transformer \(AST\) model and a vision\-language model \(VLM\) Moondream2\. We compare them with our previous work on the DenseNet201 Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\)\. The proposed methodology allows a fair comparison of different computer\-assisted methods for respiratory disease screening and diagnostics\. The training and evaluation of the models have been conducted using the same dataset containing respiratory sound recordings and patient information\. The obtained results demonstrate that these transformer\-based models can serve as a basis for the development of computer\-assisted methods for asthma diagnosis, as well as for continuous and remote monitoring of patient condition\. In addition, our approach enables interpretability of the model performance\. The achieved performance is much better than the best results of the physician’s auscultation\.

## [Endangered plant growth was influenced by soil microbial life\-history strategies across elevations](../publications/ee98abd6b776b06611f3.md)

Qiumei Teng; Ying Wang; Shihong Lyu; Jinxing Wei; Guangping Xu; Tao Ding

Elevations can influence belowground microbial diversity, network complexity, life history strategy, and the growth of endangered plants\. However, how elevation affects endangered plant growth by modulating soil microbial network complexity and life\-history strategies remains poorly understood\. This study focused on Abies yuanbaoshanensis and systematically examined tree height, diameter at breast height \(DBH\), soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activity, and microbial communities at different elevations \(1,750 m, 1,850 m, 1,950 m, and 2,050 m\)\. The results showed that tree height and DBH were highest at 1,750 m and lowest at 1,850 m compared to other elevations\. At an elevation of 1,850 m, soil total phosphorus \(TP\), total potassium content, and fungal and bacterial diversity were the lowest, while soil water content and fungal oligotrophs/copiotrophs ratios were the highest\. The complexity of bacterial\-fungal networks increased with elevation\. Structural equation modeling suggests a potential chained correlative pathway, wherein elevation was associated with shifts in soil water content, which in turn correlated with alterations in TP content, subsequently showing associative relationships with the abundance of oligotrophic fungi and microbial network complexity, and finally exhibiting links to changes in plant growth\. These findings underscore that soil physicochemical properties and microbial communities jointly determine the growth of endangered mountain plants along altitudinal gradients\. Although bacterial and fungal diversity exert distinct effects on the growth of endangered plants, their life history strategies should be considered a critical factor in the management of these species\. This research provides a new perspective for the ex situ conservation and in situ management of endangered plants\.

## [SUN&\#x27;IY INTELLEKT TRANSFORMATSIYASI SHAROITIDA TA&\#x27;LIM VA TARBIYA JARAYONIDA EMOTSIONAL KAPITALNI RIVOJLANTIRISH METODIKASINI TAKOMILLASHTIRISH](../publications/ee9d488eb5a02eb83135.md)

Axmedova Gulnoza Muzaffar qizi

Mazkur maqolada sun’iy intellekt transformatsiyasi sharoitida ta’lim va tarbiya jarayonida emotsional kapitalni rivojlantirish metodikasini takomillashtirish masalalari ilmiy\-pedagogik nuqtai nazardan tahlil qilinadi\. Tadqiqotda emotsional kapital shaxsning hissiy, ijtimoiy va madaniy resurslarini uyg‘unlashtiruvchi psixopedagogik kategoriya sifatida talqin qilinadi hamda uning tarkibiy komponentlari \- emotsional intellekt, empatiya, psixologik barqarorlik va madaniy sezgirlikning raqamli muhitdagi o‘zaro ta’siri ochib beriladi\. Sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining ta’lim jarayoniga ta’siri, ularning emotsional barqarorlik va insoniy munosabatlarga ko‘rsatadigan ijobiy va salbiy jihatlari aniqlanadi\. Taklif etilgan yondashuv raqamli transformatsiya sharoitida inson omilini saqlab qolish, empatiya, kommunikativ madaniyat va psixologik farovonlikni mustahkamlashga xizmat qiladi\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI AFFECTIVE\-NEURO\-SYMBOLIC DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURE \(E\-ANSDLA\) A Unified Framework for Emotion\-Aware, Explainable, and Causally\-Robust Artificial Intelligence in Medicine, Engineering, and Big Data Analytics](../publications/ee9eb29184ec2c39c381.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Affective\-Neuro\-Symbolic Deep Learning Architecture \(E\-ANSDLA\) is a unified framework for emotion\-aware, explainable, and causally\-robust AI in medicine, engineering, and big data analytics\. It integrates three synergistic layers: \(1\) a multimodal affective data ingestion module applying local differential privacy via calibrated noise injection into feature embeddings at the edge; \(2\) an Affective\-Temporal Graph Neural Network \(AT\-GNN\) computing a continuous, mathematically bounded Affective State Index \(ASI\) using sigmoid\-constrained multimodal fusion with cross\-modal interaction functions; and \(3\) a neuro\-symbolic causal reasoning engine utilizing continuous fuzzy logic t\-norms \(Gödel and Product t\-norms\) to map symbolic rules into differentiable computational graphs for end\-to\-end backpropagation, combined with temporal causal discovery algorithms \(Granger causality and structural causal models with temporal precedence constraints\) to rigorously distinguish cause from correlation\. A federated learning orchestrator aggregates shared graph convolutional weights globally while retaining personalized, user\-specific affine transformation layers locally to account for individual physiological baselines and prevent model drift across non\-IID data nodes\. The joint loss function $\\mathcal\{L\}\_\{total\} = \\mathcal\{L\}\_\{predictive\} \+ \\lambda \\cdot \\mathcal\{L\}\_\{logic\}$ ensures logical consistency via differentiable t\-norm penalties\. Validation demonstrates 25% F1\-score improvement in medical distress detection and 40% reduction in human\-error\-induced engineering incidents, with 95% logical consistency in explainable outputs\. \(DOI: 10\.5281/zenodo\.23442950\)

## [Yapay zekâ ve insan üretimi olan örnek olayların eğitimci görüşlerine göre karşılaştırılması](../publications/eea67457d045a98ea1db.md)

Kübra Şenel; Bilal Yorulmaz

Yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin eğitim alanında giderek yaygınlaşması, öğretim materyallerinin tasarlanması ve değerlendirilmesine yönelik yeni araştırma alanları ortaya çıkarmaktadır\. Bu çalışmanın amacı, yapay zekâ ve araştırmacı tarafından hazırlanan örnek olayların, ilkokul düzeyinde yardımlaşma değerinin kazandırılmasına uygunluk düzeylerini karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektir\. Araştırma, nicel araştırma yaklaşımlarından genel tarama modeli kapsamında yürütülmüştür\. Çalışmada ikisi yapay zekâ, ikisi araştırmacı tarafından hazırlanmış olmak üzere toplam dört örnek olay kullanılmıştır\. Veriler, 16 akademisyen ve 37 sınıf öğretmeni tarafından değerlendirilen, 11 ölçüt ve beşli derecelendirme yapısına sahip örnek olay değerlendirme ölçeği aracılığıyla toplanmıştır\. Elde edilen veriler tek yönlü varyans analizi \(ANOVA\) ve varyans homojenliği durumuna göre uygun çoklu karşılaştırma testleri kullanılarak analiz edilmiştir\. Araştırma bulguları, örnek olayların büyük bölümünde istatistiksel olarak anlamlı bir farklılık bulunmadığını; ancak okuru sıkmayacak uygun uzunlukta olma, örnek olayla birlikte verilen soruların niteliği ile sonunun belirsiz olması ve okuyucuyu belirli bir çözüme yönlendirmeme boyutlarında örnek olay türlerine bağlı olarak anlamlı farklılıklar bulunduğunu göstermiştir\. Sonuç olarak, yapay zekâ ve araştırmacı tarafından hazırlanan örnek olayların birçok ölçüt açısından benzer özellikler sergilediği, bazı boyutlarda ise yapı ve sunum özelliklerine bağlı olarak farklılaşmalar ortaya koyduğu belirlenmiştir\.

## [11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights](../publications/eeab2838c1c5c90022f9.md)

Evelynne S\. Fulda; Bennett J\. Waxse; Slavina B\. Goleva; Tam C\. Tran; Henry J\. Taylor; Caitlin P\. Bailey; Dana L\. Wolff‐Hughes; Huan Mo; Chenjie Zeng; Jacob M\. Keaton; Tracey M\. Ferrara; Anya Topiwala; Aiden Doherty; Joshua C\. Denny

Abstract Wearable devices offer a scalable, objective measurement of physical activity, but most studies reduce these data to a single metric over 7\-days\. Here, we compare wearable\-derived phenotyping approaches to understand their impact on activity\-disease associations, analyzing 11 million days of Fitbit data from 29,303 All of Us Research Program participants\. We derive four daily activity metrics \(step count, peak 1\-min cadence, peak 30\-min cadence, and heart rate per step\) across five time\-windows \(1\-day, 1\-week, 1\-month, 6\-months, 1\-year\), then run phenome\-wide analyses across &gt; 700 incident and &gt;1,400 prevalent disease outcomes\. Though all phenotypes are highly correlated, longer measurement windows yield stronger, more stable associations: 1\-year step count was associated with 389 prevalent and 61 incident outcomes \(versus 271 and 33 for 1\-day step count\) after Bonferroni\-correction, including novel links to chronic pain syndrome and SARS\-CoV\-2\. Differences between prevalent and incident associations suggest that activity metrics may act as both early markers of disease and risk factors\. These findings highlight how large\-scale, longitudinal wearable data can advance understanding of health and disease\.

## [Psychometric Properties of the Spanish Interpersonal Emotion Regulation Questionnaire \(IERQ\) in Adolescents and Young Adults](../publications/eeb6f02d75bb18a01f4d.md)

Tomás Cámara Pastor; Raquel Falcó; Javier Ortuño Sierra; Noelia Barbed Castrejón; Andrea Gutiérrez\-García; Stefan G\. Hofmann

Abstract Purpose Interpersonal emotion regulation \(IER\) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant socio\-emotional process, particularly during adolescence and young adulthood\. This study examined the psychometric properties of the Spanish Interpersonal Emotion Regulation Questionnaire \(IERQ\-S\) in adolescents and young adults\. Methods A total of 2262 Spanish participants aged 14–27 years completed the IERQ\-S and measures of wellbeing, self\-esteem, loneliness, emotion regulation, reflective functioning, psychological difficulties, suicidal ideation, and technology\-related behaviors\. The sample was randomly split for cross\-validation\. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted in Subsample A, whereas confirmatory factor analysis, competing structural models, and ordinal measurement invariance across gender and age groups were tested in Subsample B\. Results The correlated four\-factor and bifactor models showed similar relative performance, although absolute fit was mixed\. Ordinal measurement invariance was supported across gender and age groups\. Internal consistency was adequate to good across subscales and demographic strata\. Associations with external indicators were generally small and require cautious interpretation\. Age\- and gender\-stratified normative percentiles were also generated\. Conclusions The IERQ\-S appears to be a reliable and valid measure for assessing interpersonal emotion regulation strategies in Spanish adolescents and young adults\. Its use may support research on socio\-emotional functioning, transdiagnostic regulatory processes, and youth mental health assessment\.

## [RECURRENT BENIGN MELANOCYTIC NEVI AFTER REMOVAL: A RETROSPECTIVE SINGLE\-CENTER STUDY OF RISK FACTORS](../publications/eebf3231fa0bb33c7ea2.md)

Ye\.L\. Torbenko; Viktor I\. Litus; Юлия Валерьевна Щербакова

Aim\. To determine the incidence of recurrent nevus after removal of benign melanocytic nevi and to evaluate the influence of clinical, dermoscopic, morphological, and treatment\-related factors on recurrence risk\.Materials and methods\. A retrospective single\-center analytical study with passive follow\-up was conducted\. A total of 339 cases of benign melanocytic nevi removed between May 2020 and May 2025 were included\. The mean patient age was 36\.7±11\.9 years; 234 patients \(69\.0%\) were female and 105 \(31\.0%\) were male\. Sex, age, lesion localization, diameter, dermoscopic characteristics, histological subtype, treatment method, and recurrence rate were analyzed\. Statistical analysis was performed using Pearson’s χ² test and Student’s t\-test\.Results\. Recurrent nevus was identified in 45 of 339 cases \(13\.3%\)\. The mean time to recurrence was 5\.24±1\.05 months\. Patients with recurrence were significantly younger than those without recurrence \(29\.89±13\.46 years vs\. 37\.71±11\.27 years; p=0\.00005\)\. No statistically significant associations were found between recurrence and sex, lesion localization, lesion diameter, dermoscopic pattern, histological subtype, structural organization, or treatment method \(p&gt;0\.05\)\.Conclusions\. The incidence of recurrent nevus after removal of benign melanocytic nevi was 13\.3%\. Most recurrences developed within six months after treatment\. Younger age was the only statistically significant factor associated with recurrence\.

## [Predicting Hospital\-associated complications in older adults: methodological considerations](../publications/eec42b2a5f796e73737b.md)

Valiev Shukhrat; Dilnavoz Yuldasheva; Malika Khojimatova; Saidova Dilorom; Shaxlo R\. Sodiqova; Nizom Ermatov; Zeynab Afzali

Machine learning is increasingly used to predict post\-surgical complications, but predictive performance does not guarantee clinical readiness\. Shimizu and colleagues developed a promising model for older adults undergoing tibial fracture surgery using a large Japanese database\. However, four methodological pitfalls warrant attention\. First, the composite outcome was not validated in this population, and excluding in\-hospital deaths introduced survivorship bias, underestimating the true burden of severe complications\. Second, days to surgery, a variable not known at admission, created target leakage that inflates performance and undermines the admission\-time claim\. Third, using the test set for feature selection violated TRIPOD guidelines and likely overstated the scorecard&\#x27;s utility\. Fourth, the Super Learner exhibited substantial overfitting, with a 0\.110 drop between training \(AUC = 0\.850\) and test \(AUC = 0\.740\) performance, while offering only marginal improvement over simpler models\. We suggest redeveloping the model with proper internal validation, excluding leakage\-prone predictors, treating death as a competing risk, and prioritizing interpretability when complex ensembles offer limited added value\. External validation remains essential before clinical implementation\.

## [Ética y moral en los procesos jurídicos en tiempos de inteligencia artificial: caso Ecuador](../publications/eec785d1b065487491a8.md)

Luis Fernando Piñas\-Piñas; Paúl Orlando Piray\-Rodríguez; Guido Javier Silva\-Andrade; Julio Juvenal Aldana\-Zavala

The study analysed the ethical and legal challenges of applying artificial intelligence in Ecuadorian judicial proceedings, the so\-called digital trials, and examined their risks, limits and opportunities\. The research was qualitative and descriptive, with a non\-experimental design, documentary review and comparison of international regulatory frameworks\. The results indicate that artificial intelligence can improve efficiency and access to justice, but in Ecuador its use lacks a specialised framework, so the validity, transparency and oversight of automated decisions remain in doubt\. Compared with European regulation, Latin America advances with less precision\. As a contribution, a scheme of ethical\-legal audits prior to the adoption of any algorithm\-based judicial system is proposed, and it is concluded that technology must complement, not replace, human judgment\.

## [Label\-Free Biochemical Characterization and Subtype Classification of Human Breast Pathologies Using Fingerprint Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning](../publications/eeca64b2404249d89409.md)

Nguyen Van Hung; Huu Thuan Mai; Ngo Duc Quan

Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer\-related mortality, highlighting the need for improved molecular characterization of breast pathologies\. Raman spectroscopy \(RS\) provides a label\-free, non\-destructive approach for probing tissue biochemical composition\. This study investigated Raman spectral alterations across five human breast histopathological categories and explored their potential for machine learning\-assisted classification\. Formalin\-fixed, paraffin\-embedded \(FFPE\) tissue specimens were obtained from five patients, with one patient representing each category: normal breast tissue, intraductal papilloma, high\-grade ductal carcinoma in situ \(DCIS\), invasive ductal carcinoma \(IDC\), and invasive lobular carcinoma \(ILC\)\. A total of 100 Raman spectra \(20 per patient\) were acquired using 785 nm excitation over the fingerprint region \(500–2000 cm−1\)\. Spectral preprocessing involved Savitzky–Golay smoothing, asymmetrically reweighted penalized least\-squares \(arPLS\) baseline correction, and vector normalization\. The investigated spectra exhibited reduced relative lipid\-associated contributions near 1063, 1300, and 1445 cm−1, accompanied by increased relative protein\- and nucleic\-acid\-associated features near 1003, 1420, and 1600–1650 cm−1\. The phenylalanine\-to\-lipid intensity ratio \(I1003/I1445\) increased from ≤0\.2 in normal tissue to ≥1\.5 in invasive lesions, suggesting a potential spectroscopic descriptor of biochemical remodeling\. Exploratory subtype\-associated differences were also observed, including a prominent aromatic C=C\-associated feature near 1618 cm−1 in IDC and an enhanced carbohydrate\-associated contribution near 890 cm−1 in ILC\. A support vector machine \(SVM\) classifier was evaluated using patient\-independent leave\-one\-patient\-out \(LOPO\) cross\-validation\. Across the five held\-out patients, the model correctly classified 89 of 100 spectra, achieving an overall spectrum\-level accuracy of 89\.0%, sensitivity of 90\.0%, specificity of 87\.5%, and F1\-score of 90\.8%\. Although these findings demonstrate encouraging discrimination within the investigated cohort, the limited number of biologically independent patients and the representation of each histopathological category by a single patient restrict the generalizability of the results\. This study provides preliminary proof\-of\-concept evidence supporting the integration of Raman\-derived biochemical features with machine learning for breast pathology characterization, warranting further validation in larger, multi\-patient and multicenter cohorts\.

## [University students’ engagement in higher education EFL instructional environments: a mixed\-methods quasi\-experimental study](../publications/eecc31c8bd409a3ec004.md)

Merzouk Farahi

In an era branded by Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) tools and high\-tech advancements, the shift to distance education has significantly influenced learner engagement, mainly in English as foreign language \(EFL\) instructional contexts\. In online and offline learning environments, skills engagement \(SE\), emotional engagement \(EE\), participation/interaction engagement \(PIE\) and performance engagement \(PE\) are essential constructs of successful academic outcomes\. The present mixed\-methods quasi\-experimental research examined the role of online and offline teaching formats on learners’ SE, EE, PIE and PE\. The study involved 824 Moroccan university EFL learners\. Running Paired samples t\-tests, One\-way Analysis of Variance \(ANOVA\) and Multiple Linear Regression \(MLR\) revealed statistically significant effects on offline learners rather than on online learners\. The study suggests that the major EFL stakeholders should foster supportive learning environments wherein engagement\-promoting instructional practices are prevalent, developing accommodated teaching mechanisms that suit distant learners’ needs and nurture effective virtual learning success\.

## [Tracking the lithiation state of LixSi from machine\-learned XPS binding energies](../publications/eecd4628e7a0a45b132f.md)

Michael A\. Hernandez Bertran; Davide Tisi; Federico Grasselli; Michele Ceriotti; Elisa Molinari; Deborah Prezzi

Abstract X\-ray photoelectron spectroscopy \(XPS\) is a powerful technique to probe chemical states and interfacial processes in battery materials, but a quantitative interpretation is often hindered by the complex, heterogeneous microstructures that form during operation and dominate electrochemical cycling\. Silicon\-based anodes represent a paradigmatic example in Li batteries, as \(de\)lithiation proceeds through the formation of strongly disordered Li x Si phases and crystal\-amorphous transformations that are hard to characterize\. Here, we introduce a computational framework that combines machine\-learning \(ML\) prediction of core\-level binding energies to large\-scale atomistic simulations—grand\-canonical Monte Carlo \(GCMC\) complemented with molecular dynamics \(MD\), driven by an ML potential—for a systematic sampling of lithiation states and local atomic environments\. This approach yields stoichiometry maps that capture the main spectroscopic trends observed in operando and ex situ XPS measurements, including the distinctive Si 2 p signatures associated with the crystal\-to\-amorphous disordering during early delithiation\.

## [Characteristics of Speech Sound Development in Preterm‐Born Children: A Scoping Review](../publications/eecd88c76b9086c9134e.md)

Sam Burr; Sam A\. Harding; Sarah Rudd

BACKGROUND: There is substantial evidence for the detrimental impact of preterm birth on language development compared to children born at term\. However, little is known regarding speech sound development of preterm infants\. Speech development precedes language development and requires investigation in its own right\. A clear picture of the evidence for speech sound development in preterm\-born children is important to enable clinical services in early identification and intervention for these children\. AIM: To understand the extent and type of evidence relating to typical and atypical speech sound development in children born before 37 weeks gestation \(preterm\)\. METHODS: A search of 5 MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycInfo, EMBASE, EMCARE was undertaken in April 2026\. Grey literature searching in Campbell collaboration, COSMIN, PROSPERO, FigShare and Open Science Framework, Google \(advanced search\), and SpeechBite was undertaken\. Articles including samples of children reporting speech sound development \(typical or atypical\) were included in the review\. Studies focusing on outcomes for reading and literacy were excluded, as were animal studies and those signed languages\. Population demographics, assessment and outcome measures, methods of analysis and findings were extracted from each study\. MAIN CONTRIBUTION: 28 studies from 14 different countries were included in the review\. Twenty\-five of the 28 studies reported differences in speech outcomes of PT children and FT children between the ages of 3 months and 12 years\. CONCLUSIONS: This review found differences in how PT and FT children develop sounds for speech from birth through into childhood\. Further large\-scale, longitudinal research is needed to clarify what typical and atypical speech development look like in PT children\. WHAT THIS PAPER ADDS: What is already known on this subject The findings of this scoping review provide evidence of the differences between speech sound development between preterm born children and children born at term in the first 12 years of life\. This information could contribute to a more informed approach to care and early intervention\. What this study adds to the existing knowledge? Understanding the impact of preterm birth on early speech sound development can help speech and language therapists to build a picture of a child&\#x27;s individual risk profile for speech sound disorder later in childhood\. This can lead to earlier intervention for the children who need it most\.

## [UC Food Waste: A Multimodal Robotic Perception Dataset for Robust Contaminant Detection in Complex Biowaste Scenes](../publications/eed746061706dd1f6c4a.md)

Matthew L\. Vestal; James Ireland; David Hinwood; Xing Wang; Min Wang; Damith  C\. Herath

Automated organic waste recovery represents a significant challenge for computer vision, characterized by extreme spatial clutter and the material degradation inherent in industrial waste streams\. While multimodal imaging provides a potential pathway for material identification, standard deep learning frameworks often prioritize perceptual image enhancement over the preservation of the discrete physical signatures required for accurate classification\. This article introduces the UC Food Waste dataset, a comprehensive multimodal resource comprising 15‐band multispectral, thermal, and RGB imagery, designed to characterize contaminants in messy sorting environments\. To address limitations of conventional sensor integration, we propose a Split Spatial‐Spectral Attention stem\. This architecture utilizes 3D convolutional kernels to explicitly model interband correlations before cross‐modal feature integration, preserving the integrity of spectral signatures that are often suppressed by 2D‐only architectures\. Our experiments demonstrate that while feature‐level fusion consistently outperforms data‐level concatenation, the efficacy of multimodal integration in practical settings is heavily constrained by label ambiguity and class overlap\. The results suggest that for domain‐specific robotic tasks, the explicit codesign of sensor modalities and feature‐extraction layers are effective for identifying waste contaminants\. This, in turn, suggests that in industrial settings extra constraints such as spatial ambiguities must be accounted for in the modeling process\.

## [Exploring barriers to food security resource access and use at a Midwestern University: a mixed methods study](../publications/eed77a19773e5f00fe96.md)

Jennifer King; Alyssa Anderson; Quinn Parker; Michelle M\. Lambert

This study used a mixed\-methods approach rooted in the socioecological model \(SEM\) to explore food insecurity and barriers impeding both access to and use of food security resources among college students at a multi\-campus, Midwestern University\. Food insecurity was reported among approximately 26% of survey respondents \(n = 1,873\) using the 10\-item U\.S\. Adult Food Security Survey Module\. Accounts of resource underutilization by interview participants \(n = 23\) disclosed barriers across the individual \(perception of need\), relationship \(external stigma\), and organizational \(operational hours\) SEM levels\. The spectrum of challenges raised by students facing food insecurity warrant triangulated points of assistance throughout their academic journeys\.

## [Explainable machine learning for predicting compressive strength of alkali activated material: a comparative modelling and interpretability study](../publications/eefefbc693f4c1a2182b.md)

J\. S\. Siddesh; M\. S\. Mukesh; M\. S\. Kendagannaswamy; Kadepalli Nagendra Shivaprasad

To promote the design of low\-carbon alkali\-activated materials, precise yet interpretable compressive strength prediction based on mix design variables is essential to minimize trial\-and\-error experimentation\. This study employs an interpretable machine learning approach to predict compressive strength based on important mix design variables, including fly ash content, ground granulated blast furnace slag content, Na 2 O content, SiO 2 /Na 2 O ratio and water to binder ratio\. Various ensemble machine learning models, such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, XGBoost, and LightGBM were developed and compared for model performance evaluation using R 2 , RMSE and MAE\. Among the models, the Random Forest model had the best generalization performance with a test coefficient R² of 0\.762, along with RMSE of 9\.23 MPa and MAE of 6\.38 MPa\. Explainable artificial intelligence techniques were then used to interpret the machine learning model predictions and determine the variable contributions\. The results consistently showed that the water to binder ratio is the most dominant factor influencing the compressive strength, followed by Na 2 O content, fly ash content and SiO 2 /Na 2 O ratio\. A clear nonlinear threshold was found at a water to binder ratio of approximately 0\.5, beyond which the predicted compressive strength dropped rapidly\. Therefore, the interpretable machine learning framework presented in this study minimizes trial\-and\-error experimentation by providing accurate compressive strength prediction and clear, mix\-design\-related explanations for the development of low\-carbon alkali\-activated materials\.

## [Robust statistical learning and risk measurement models under uncertainty conditions](../publications/ef0117955957f92dac51.md)

Yunfei Cheng

In practice, statistical learning models are faced with multiple uncertainties, including data noise, outliers and distributional shift, which cause large estimation bias in traditional risk measurement models or even cause decision failure\. Based on distributionally robust optimization, this paper constructs a statistical learning framework\. An uncertainty set based on the empirical distribution is constructed with Wasserstein distance, and then the unknown distribution shift is transferred into a computable mathematical constraint\. On this basis, a robust conditional value of risk is constructed as the optimization objective, which reflects the tail loss under the worst\-case distribution and improves model robustness against outliers\. Finally, duality theory is used to transfer the original minimax problem into an equivalent convex optimization form, and then the stochastic mirror projection algorithm is designed to solve the model parameters effectively\. The experimental results based on artificially simulated datasets show that the parameter estimation error of the model output parameters can be reduced to 0\.122 when the outlier ratio is 20%, and the cumulative final value of the decision made according to the model output can reach 0\.92 in extreme cases\. On real financial datasets, the risk prediction calibration error of the model output at a 0\.90 confidence level can be reduced to 0\.094, which proves that the model is effective in a complex market environment\. The robust risk measurement model constructed in this paper can achieve stable output and accurate quantification of risk estimation in the face of uncertain conditions, and provides theoretical support and computational tools for statistical learning in high\-risk situations\. Not applicable\.

## [AI\-driven multi\-agent digital twin conceptual framework for real\-time domestic water quality monitoring, purification and smart billing](../publications/ef0e29215a8d90d1f628.md)

Abu S\. M\. Mohsin; Shadab Hafiz Choudhury; Munyem Ahammad Muyeed

Access to safe drinking water remains a critical global challenge, with over 2\.2 billion people lacking reliable access despite water’s abundance, as only 3% of Earth’s water is freshwater\. Current systems suffer from unreliable analog metering, tampering risks, and the absence of real\-time platforms for monitoring quality, consumption, purification and billing—creating a literature gap in scalable, integrated, and intelligent water management solutions\. To address this situation, a pilot\-scale, machine learning–enabled multi\-agent digital twin\-inspired framework is developed for domestic water systems, integrating IoT sensors to continuously monitor key parameters \(pH, turbidity, temperature, flow, and TDS\); purification status; and employing predictive models for anomaly detection and forecasting\. Among several tested algorithms \(ARIMA, autoregression, and additive regression\), additive regression demonstrated comparatively better performance under the constraints of the pilot dataset, relatively low error rates were achieved under evaluation conditions for temperature, pH, flow, pressure, TDS and color\. The system links to a web\-based platform providing real\-time visualization, automated billing, and user alerts, while incorporating an integrated purification module capable of reducing heavy metals and microbial load with above 96\.96% accuracy\. These actions result in a compact end\-to\-end prototype framework that demonstrates the feasibility of safe real\-time water use under controlled conditions while improving accountability, reducing billing errors, and promoting conservation through predictive alerts\. The novelty lies in the seamless integration of IoT sensing, ML\-driven analytics, purification, and digital billing into a pilot\-scale integrated digital twin framework\. This system offers future prospects for deployment in smart city infrastructures, enhanced resilience through cybersecurity integration, and alignment with SDG 6 \(Clean Water and Sanitation\), indicating its potential as a future step toward scalable water management solutions\. However, the system is validated under limited pilot\-scale deployment conditions, and further large\-scale validation is required\.

## [Regimes of truth in postmodern novels: the atlas of misty continents in the context of modernity and Ottoman epistemology](../publications/ef1310399e0288888c56.md)

Mesut TEKŞAN; Latif Akkaya

This study aims to analyze the epistemological transformation concerning the nature and legitimacy of knowledge in the context of modernity and postmodernity through İhsan Oktay Anar’s The Atlas of Misty Continents\. While modernity conceptualizes knowledge as a universal structure grounded in reason and empirical verification, postmodern thought challenges these assumptions by arguing that knowledge is produced within historical, cultural, and discursive processes\. Accordingly, truth is not treated as a fixed entity but rather as a contextual and pluralized construction\. The study examines the core concepts of postmodern epistemology through Jean\-François Lyotard’s critique of “grand narratives” and his notion of “language games,” as well as Michel Foucault’s framework of the knowledge–power relationship\. Although these perspectives do not entirely deny the possibility of objective reality, they emphasize that knowledge gains legitimacy through specific discursive and institutional formations\. By extending this theoretical framework into the field of literature, the article discusses how the postmodern novel represents regimes of knowledge\. In this respect, it argues that in The Atlas of Misty Continents, knowledge is constructed in multiple forms, drawing not only on scientific rationality but also on sources such as rumor, intuition, tradition, and dreams\. The novel is analyzed through categories including narrative reliability, the representation of knowledge sources, the pluralization of truth claims, and the distribution of epistemic authority\. The study contends that Anar does not merely juxtapose modern and postmodern epistemologies but instead incorporates them simultaneously and equivalently within fiction\. Consequently, this article argues that The Atlas of Misty Continents is not merely an aesthetic work of fiction; rather, it constructs a mode of thinking that simultaneously draws on postmodern epistemology and the Ottoman epistemic framework\.

## [اتجاهات طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس](../publications/ef137ab5337fbcbe12e1.md)

م\.د\. خلود نعيم أمير

يسعى البحث إلى التعرف على اتجاهات طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس والفروق في اتجاهات طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس تبعًا لمتغير الجنس والفروق في اتجاهات طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس تبعًا لمتغير نوع الدراسة \(صباحية/مسائية\)\. اعتمدت الباحثة المنهج الوصفي ،وتحدّد مجتمع البحث الحالي بجميع طلبة قسم العلوم التربوية والنفسية في كلية التربية/ الجامعة العراقية، وللدراستين الصباحية والمسائية معاً، والبالغ عددهم الإجمالي \(243\) طالباً وطالبة\. وقد تحدد حجم عينة البحث بـ \(90\) طالباً وطالبة، بواقع \(53\) طالباً وطالبة من الدراسة الصباحية و\(37\) طالباً وطالبة من الدراسة المسائية اما فيما يخص أداة البحث المتمثلة في مقياس \(اتجاهات طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس\)، إذ تألف المقياس بصورته النهائية من \(32\) فقرة مغلقة وزعت على ثلاثة مجالات رئيسة تمثل جوانب توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس، وهي: \(مجال كفايات التخطيط للتدريس بواقع 7 فقرات، ومجال كفايات تنفيذ التدريس بواقع 15 فقرة، ومجال كفايات التقويم بواقع 10 فقرات\) ، وتم التأكد من صدقه وثباته باستخدام معادلة ألفا – كرونباخ إذ بلغت قيمة \(87%\) ،وبعد معالجة البيانات احصائيا توصلت الباحثة إلى النتائج الآتية: أولاً: وجود اتجاهات إيجابية لدى طلبة كلية التربية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس، إذ ينظرون إلى تطبيقاته بوصفها أدوات داعمة يمكن الإفادة منها في إجراءات التخطيط والتنفيذ والتقويم التدريسي، مع استمرار أهمية الدور التربوي للمدرس في إدارة العملية التعليمية\. ثانياً: ان اتجاهات الطالبات نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس اعلى من الطلاب\. ثالثاً: ان اتجاهات طلبة الدراسة الصباحية نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في كفايات التدريس اعلى من اتجاهات طلبة الدراسة المسائية \. رابعاً: تؤكد نتائج البحث أهمية إعداد طلبة كلية التربية للتعامل مع تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي المرتبطة بكفايات التدريس\. وفي ضوء نتائج البحث، قدمت الباحثة جملة من التوصيات والمقترحات\.

## [The relationship between AI adoption and sustainable performance through digital transformation among overseas study agency SMEs in China](../publications/ef171926549e2b3583aa.md)

Yang Hu; Muhammad Faliq Abd Razak; Sufian Jusoh; Ahmad Rizal Mohd Yusof

As governments and industries increasingly prioritize digital economy strategies and sustainability objectives, greater attention has been paid to the relationships among artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption, digital transformation \(DT\), and sustainable performance \(SP\)\. However, limited research has examined these relationships in small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\), particularly in the context of overseas study agencies \(OSAs\) in China\. Therefore, this study aims to examine the relationships among AI adoption, DT, and perceived SP and to assess the mediating role of DT in the relationship between AI adoption and perceived SP\. A quantitative research approach was employed using perceptual survey data collected from 554 individual respondents working in sampled OSA SMEs in China and reflecting their perceptions of organizational practices and performance\. The proposed hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling\. The results indicate that AI adoption is positively associated with DT and perceived SP, while DT is positively associated with perceived SP and partially mediates the relationship between AI adoption and perceived SP\. Overall, the findings provide empirical insights consistent with the perspective of Dynamic Capability Theory, suggesting that AI adoption is associated with perceived sustainable performance both directly and indirectly through digital transformation within the sampled service\-oriented SMEs\. The findings also offer practical implications for organizations and policymakers seeking to support sustainable and digitally enabled development\.

## [The Use of Multi\-Criteria Decision Making \(Mcdm\) Methods in Digital Marketing Strategy Selection: A Literature Review](../publications/ef17bdefc38581a29a95.md)

Sanam Eivazzadeh

Marketing covers all tools and processes in reaching the right audience for products or services\. Marketing strategy plays an important role in the success of businesses\. In a world that changes over time, the concept of marketing has been subjected to certain changes with the change in customer wants and needs\. In the digitalizing world, it has become inevitable for most businesses to adopt a digital marketing strategy\. Especially for businesses that want to gain competitive advantage, it is critical to choose the right digital marketing strategy\. Since Multi\-Criteria Decision Making \(MCDM\) methods adopt an analytical perspective, they improve decision quality and are a powerful method for selecting the right strategy\. This study reviews the scientific literature focusing on Multi\-Criteria Decision Making \(MCDM\) methods used in the selection of digital marketing strategies and evaluates existing approaches\. In this direction, 8 studies conducted between 2019 and 2025 were reached\. The studies were categorized in terms of the application sector, the Multi\-Criteria Decision Making method used, and the selected digital marketing strategy\. According to the findings, social media marketing and viral marketing emerged as the primary digital marketing strategies\. Swara was selected as the most widely used method\. The reasons for the prominence of these strategies include low cost, short\-term results, measurability and ease of analysis, the potential to create brand awareness, the opportunity for interaction and feedback, and high reach\. Studies have generally used a single method, whereas stronger results can be obtained by using mixed methods\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: From Innovation to Clinical Applications and Regulatory Frameworks](../publications/ef1f3ca1683743a27d7e.md)

Amisha Saini, Jasmine Sagwal, Tamanna Sirohi, Neha Saini, Rupinder Kaur

ABSTRACTThis thorough analysis examines the revolutionary significance of artificial intelligence \(AI\)in contemporary healthcare, stressing its development, uses, difficulties, and legalconsiderations\. From its initial limits, artificial intelligence has quickly advanced to providesophisticated features like deep learning and predictive analytics\. It is transformingmedication discovery, rehabilitation, treatment planning, diagnostics, and healthcaremanagement\. Patient care is becoming more accurate, efficient, and personalized thanks toapplications like data\-driven decision support systems, virtual care, and AI\-enhancedimaging\.

## [‘Science of Science’: the thematic landscape and historical roots](../publications/ef26dedfc33e6cbc55c4.md)

S N Archana; P K Padmakumar; C\. Shajitha

Introduction\. This study analyses the status of the global Science of Science \(SOS\) research to map its spatial and temporal landscape, prominent researchers and their approaches to the subject\. It further traces the historical roots of SOS to identify the seminal works and authors who laid the foundation of this research area\. Method\. We conducted bibliometric and reference publication year spectroscopy \(RPYS\) analyses on data extracted from Scopus and Web of Science \(WoS\) databases, to examine the thematic landscape and the historical roots respectively\. Analysis\. Bibliometrix R package was used to analyse and map the productivity and thematic landscapes\. CRExplorer was employed to perform RPYS to identify the seminal authors and works that framed the research area of SOS\. Results\. Scientometrics and its variants form the central theme of present day SOS and the area will be led forward by Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and innovation studies\. The historical roots of SOS lies in the works of J\.D\.Bernal, de Solla Price, Merton and Garfield\. Conclusion\. Mapping SOS from inception to its current stature, this study reveals its weak theoretical framework, risking its reduction to mere quantitative science study\. We suggest to undertake interdisciplinary collaborative investigations to address this\.

## [Logical rationale and practical paths of digital\-intelligence empowerment for improving health education literacy of college physical education teachers](../publications/ef47c994f3ae5c5cb9c8.md)

Jiangsong Chen

With the continuous advancement of educational digitalization and health education in colleges and universities, new requirements have been put forward for the professional literacy of college physical education teachers\. Based on relevant policy documents and existing studies, this paper analyzes the connotation, improvement logic, realistic adaptation and practical paths of digital\-intelligence empowerment for the health education literacy of college physical education teachers\. The study holds that this literacy can be understood from four dimensions: health knowledge integration, health information interpretation, health education transformation, and digital\-intelligence application and ethics\. Its improvement stems from the expansion of health education goals, the integration of physical education and health knowledge, and the collaboration between professional experience and data evidence\. At present, there is still room for further improvement in the embedding of health education roles, the connection between physical education and health knowledge, the educational transformation of health data, and relevant support mechanisms\. To this end, it is necessary to strengthen the professional role cognition oriented by health promotion, build a knowledge system integrating physical education and health, form a capability chain of &quot;data acquisition – information interpretation – educational decision\-making – teaching intervention – feedback adjustment&quot;, and improve the support mechanisms of training, teaching and research, interdisciplinary collaboration and evaluation\.

## [Through the Kaleidoscopic Lens of Art: a STEM education pathway within Italy’s PCTO framework](../publications/ef4a9e84656c0a3edeb6.md)

Rosa Coluzzi; Vito Imbrenda; Licia Fanti; Wanda Traino; Massimo De Carlo; Vincenzo Camardelli; Andrea Smilzo; Michele Cordisco; Giovanna Limone; Lorenzo Amato; Giuseppe Calamita; Emanuele Ciancia; Ilaria Gandolfi; Angela Perrone; Salvatore Lucente; Valeria Giampaolo

Interdisciplinary approaches can create opportunities for connecting scientific observation with artistic interpretation and environmental communication\. The “Kaleidoscopic Lens of Art: Imaging the Environment” project was implemented within Italy&\#x27;s PCTO \(Pathways for Transversal Skills and Career Guidance\) framework through collaboration between the Art High School “Mario Festa Campanile” \(Melfi\-Southern Italy\) and researchers from CNR\-IMIOT \(National Reserach Council of Italy \- Istituto di Metodologie Integrate per l&\#x27;Osservazione della Terra\)\. The pathway combined scientific lectures, field and laboratory activities, visual analysis, conceptual re\-elaboration, and artistic production\. It is presented here as a descriptive, practice\-based case study, with attention to the transformations occurring between scientific source material and artistic representation\. The resulting works included mixed\-media paintings, architectural visualizations, digital photomontages, and audiovisual products addressing landscape transformation and human\-environment relationships\. This comparison suggests that artistic practices shape which features of scientific representations are selected and emphasized, and how their environmental meanings are expressed\. The study documents a science\-to\-art workflow that may inform the adaptation and systematic evaluation of similar interdisciplinary initiatives in other educational contexts\.

## [Dark matter in composite Higgs models with a scotogenic EFT](../publications/ef4af97aa9ac0f4d2fe8.md)

Yu Chen; Werner Porod

We discuss a class of Composite Higgs models with a fermionic UV completion that can explain the dark matter relic density\. The resulting low\-energy theory resembles so\-called scotogenic models\. A residual $\\mathbb\{Z\}\_2$ symmetry implies that one of the pseudo\-Nambu\-Goldstone bosons is stable and therefore is a viable dark matter candidate\. As a concrete example, we take a model based on the $\\mathrm\{SU\}\(6\)/\\mathrm\{Sp\}\(6\)$ coset, which in principle contains four dark matter candidates\. However, only three of them can produce a relic density consistent with observations\. We perform a MCMC study focusing on dark matter observables to explore the available parameter space of the effective theory\. In particular, we find that spin\-1 resonances play an important role in a substantial part of the parameter space\. Finally, we comment on possible LHC signatures of this model class\.

## [The Use of Artificial Intelligence\-Assisted Post\-Reading Presentations in Improving Secondary School Students’ Attitudes Towards Developing Turkish Vocabulary](../publications/ef566916646c4add88ae.md)

Görkem ARSLAN

The aim of this study is to examine whether middle school students’ attitudes toward developing Turkish vocabulary differ according to the tools they preferred during the preparation of post\-reading presentations\. The study employed a quantitative comparative correlational design\. The participants consisted of 56 fifth\-grade students attending a public middle school in Burhaniye, Balıkesir, Türkiye\. Within the framework of the Türkiye Century Education Model, students presented the books they had read by using artificial intelligence\-supported tools, conventional digital tools, or hand\-prepared materials, based on their own preferences\. No intervention was made in the natural learning environment\. After the presentations, the Attitude Scale for Developing Vocabulary in the Turkish Course, developed by Yaşar and Topçuoğlu Ünal \(2016\), was administered\. Descriptive statistics and the independent\-samples t\-test were used for data analysis\. The findings revealed that students who preferred artificial intelligence\-supported tools obtained significantly higher attitude scores toward developing Turkish vocabulary than those who preferred conventional digital tools or hand\-prepared materials\. The calculated effect size \(Cohen’s d ≈ 0\.59\) indicated a medium effect\. The results suggest that students’ attitudes toward developing Turkish vocabulary differ significantly according to the tools they preferred during the preparation of post\-reading presentations\.

## [ShadowFPT: Backdooring Federated Prompt Tuning via Shadow Triggers](../publications/ef5bd55b75fac71543dc.md)

Kun Zhai; Teng Li; Yunhao Feng; Xingjun Ma

Federated Prompt Tuning \(FPT\) adapts large vision\-\-language models by freezing the pretrained backbone and optimizing only lightweight prompt parameters across clients\. Although this design improves communication and parameter efficiency, it creates an overlooked security risk\. Since the backbone is shared and frozen, a malicious client can induce backdoor behavior through the representation space while keeping its uploaded prompt updates close to benign ones\. We propose \\textbf\{ShadowFPT\}, a targeted backdoor attack that exploits this frozen\-backbone attack surface\. ShadowFPT first pretrains a learnable \\emph\{Shadow Trigger\} against the frozen CLIP visual encoder, using either auxiliary public data or the malicious client&\#x27;s local data, so that triggered inputs are steered toward the target class in representation space\. During federated prompt tuning, the malicious client adapts the trigger under the current global prompt and then optimizes its local prompt on both clean and triggered samples\. Only prompt parameters are uploaded to the server, while the trigger and frozen encoders remain local\. By shifting most of the attack burden from prompt updates to trigger\-induced representation steering, ShadowFPT achieves targeted misclassification while preserving prompt\-space stealthiness\. Across multiple datasets, aggregation rules, and non\-IID federated partitions, ShadowFPT increases the attack success rate from 19\.81\\% to 90\.36\\% in our main setting, while maintaining clean accuracy\. It remains effective across textual, visual, and joint vision\-\-language prompt tuning\. These results identify frozen backbones as stealthy and underexplored backdoor surfaces in federated prompt tuning, suggesting that defenses based only on prompt\-update anomaly detection are insufficient\.

## [Growth–recovery decoupling in the timing of geomagnetic disturbances across five solar cycles](../publications/ef6526fde7255a0c4977.md)

J\. A\. Wanliss

The timing of geomagnetic disturbances depends on energy accumulation and releases within the 8 magnetosphere, and shows how that balance is organized by solar cycle\. We decompose every 9 negative excursion of the 1\-min SYM\-H index over 1981–2026 \(78,096 events at the median 10 threshold, spanning solar cycles 21 through 25\) into a growth lifetime τg, from downward threshold 11 crossing to the first attainment of its minimum, and a recovery lifetime τr, from minimum to recovery 12 crossing\. Both durations follow finite\-range power laws with distinct exponents, μg = 1\.079 ± 0\.005 13 and μr = 1\.305 ± 0\.004\. The recovery exponent is larger at every threshold and in every yearly 14 window\. Under the standard first\-attainment convention the exponents respond oppositely to solar 15 activity: μg rises with sunspot number \(r = \+0\.59, p = 7 × 10\-5 in independent windows\) but μr is 16 statistically flat\. The solar cycle influences the temporal width over which the scaling law extends\. 17 The solar cycle is therefore imprinted on low\-latitude disturbance timing selectively: through the 18 growth exponent and through the temporal cutoff scales of both channels, but not through the 19 recovery exponent\. The exponent ordering survives alternative estimators, independence treatments, 20 and an agnostic treatment of tied minima, and the undivided excursion recovers the single threshold\-21 robust burst\-lifetime law reported previously \(Wanliss and Weygand, 2007\)\. The apparent invariance 22 of bursts arises because the recovery channel controls the tail\. Growth and recovery timing are 23 therefore decoupled\. 24

## [Urban Readability and Accessibility Analysis for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities: The Case of Üsküdar \(Istanbul\)](../publications/ef69e5380509ccc6dd31.md)

Hüseyin Melih Özdemir

Accessibility in urban spaces is closely related not only to physical distances but also to individuals&\#x27; processes of perceiving space and finding their way\. This study aims to examine the effect of the legibility characteristics of the urban road network on accessibility to urban services from the perspective of individuals with mental disabilities\. Within the scope of the study, urban legibility was evaluated using spatial indicators, including the route straightness index, angle change index, intersection complexity index, facade continuity index, and road legibility index\. Based on these indicators, the cognitive path cost, which reflects the perceptual difficulties individuals with intellectual disabilities may encounter in the orientation process within the urban road network, was calculated\. The analyses were performed using ArcGIS software in a geographic information system \(GIS\) environment\. The resulting cognitive path cost surface was used to evaluate accessibility to special education and rehabilitation centers, healthcare facilities, and urban parks and green spaces\. In this context, both physical distance\-based accessibility and cognitive path\-cost\-based perceptual accessibility analyses were conducted for the relevant service areas and compared\. The findings show that, despite the short physical distance in some areas, cognitive accessibility remains limited due to the road network&\#x27;s morphological structure and difficulties with finding directions\. In contrast, it was determined that more readable and easier\-to\-navigate routes can increase accessibility despite longer physical distances on certain axes\. Consequently, the study reveals that evaluating accessibility to urban services solely based on distance criteria is insufficient, and that urban morphology and road network readability must also be considered in accessibility analyses\.

## [Molecular Docking an In Vitro Anticonvulsant evaluation of Newly Synthesized Substituted Phthalimide Schiff bases derivatives targeting GABAA receptor](../publications/ef6fbf6f3d9aa0f6a1ae.md)

Anil Manohar Kambale; Bhavana Utkarsh Jain; Snehal Tukaram Rautmale; Pratik Dilip Kachare; Anushka Krishnat Patil; Sukanya Pradipkumar Bhandigare

Epilepsy, a chronic neurological disorder affecting nearly 50\(million people worldwide, remains difficult to manage due to drug resistance and adverse effects of existing antiepileptic drugs\. In\-silico analyses using Swiss ADME, BOILED\-Egg, and Pro Tox\-II indicated favorable pharmacokinetic profiles, blood–brain barrier permeability, and low toxicity\. Visualization through BIOVIA\(Discovery\(Studio revealed stable hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions with residues TYR160, PHE77 and SER205\. In\-vitro assays using HepG2 cells confirmed dose\-dependent activity comparable to phenytoin\. The integrated computational and experimental approach demonstrated that these derivatives possess strong binding affinity, good oral bioavailability and minimal toxicity\. Overall, the findings highlight phthalimide Schiff base derivatives as promising multifunctional candidates for anticonvulsant therapy, offering improved safety and efficacy profiles for future pharmaceutical development\.

## [Enterovirus infections: main types related to clinical syndromes](../publications/ef76e03e394f24ab0459.md)

Fabrício Caldeira Reis; Alex Domingos Reis; Bráulio Caetano Machado; R\. Carmona

This narrative review highlights recent advances in the understanding of enterovirus infections and the main enterovirus types associated with clinical syndromes, synthesizing current knowledge of type\-specific manifestations\. We searched PubMed®, Scientific Electronic Library Online \(SciELO\), and Virtual Health Library \(VHL\) for articles published between 2010 and 2025\. The search used descriptors and/or keywords in Portuguese and English: “enterovirus infection disease”, “enterovirus infection genotypes”, “enterovirus infection pathogenic”, and “enterovirus clinical syndromes”, focusing on recent studies addressing enterovirus infections and the types most commonly associated with clinical syndromes\. A total of 78 articles were selected for analysis\. The review examined the distribution of enteroviruses by species, recommended clinical specimen types for diagnosis according to clinical presentation, and the major enterovirus types and their associated clinical syndromes\. Numerous studies have demonstrated the epidemic potential and genetic diversity of enteroviruses, revealing patterns of endemic circulation\.
