## [DO GUIA ORIENTADO A PRINCÍPIOS À SÍNTESE INTEGRADA: ANÁLISE COMPARATIVA ENTRE A 7ª E A 8ª EDIÇÕES DO GUIA PMBOK](../publications/ef802d658827cea778df.md)

Henderson Matsuura Sanches; Joelson Carvalho Junior

The PMBOK Guide, published by the Project Management Institute \(PMI\), is the leading international reference in project management\.Its 7th edition \(2021\) broke away from the process\-based model by adopting twelve principles and eight performance domains, which drew criticism for the lack of practical guidance\.In November 2025, PMI released the 8th edition, which aims to reconcile both approaches\.This article aims to compare the 7th and 8th editions of the guide, identifying what has changed, what is new and what remains in common\.This is a qualitative, descriptive and documentary study based on PMI publications and secondary technical sources published between 2025 and 2026\.The results show that the 8th edition consolidates the twelve principles into six, reduces the performance domains from eight to seven, reintroduces 40 non\-\-prescriptive processes mapped to five focus areas and brings together, in a single volume, content previously split with the companion process groups guide\.The main novelties are the sustainability principle, the three\-dimensional mindset framework and the appendices on artificial intelligence, project management offices and procurement\.Value orientation, the value delivery system, tailoring and neutrality regarding the development approach remain in common\.It is concluded that the 8th edition represents a synthesis, rather than a rupture, between prescription and flexibility\.

## [Integrated risk prediction for opioid overdose: combining genetic and socioeconomic factors](../publications/ef88a30fb881e492e007.md)

Mupeng Lei; Yan Yuan

A multidimensional prediction model integrating genetic and socioeconomic factors was developed and validated to assess the risk of opioid overdose, aiming to facilitate individualized risk estimation and inform early clinical identification and preventive strategies\. In this retrospective study, 340 patients with a history of opioid use were enrolled\. Participants were randomly allocated to a training set \( n = 238\) or a validation set \( n = 102\) in a 7:3 ratio\. Candidate variables, including genetic variants, socioeconomic determinants, clinical parameters, and comorbidities, were initially screened using univariate analysis\. Subsequently, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression were applied for variable selection and identification of independent predictors\. Four machine learning models—random forest, support vector machine, k\-nearest neighbors, and gradient boosting machine –were constructed using the final seven predictors\. Model performance was evaluated based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis \(DCA\)\. Model interpretability was enhanced using SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) values\. Seven independent risk factors for opioid overdose were identified \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Among these, a history of prior overdose showed the strongest association \(odds ratio = 3\.192\)\. The random forest model demonstrated superior performance, with an AUC of 0\.879 in the training set and 0\.774 in the validation set\. Its calibration curve was closest to the ideal line\. Furthermore, DCA indicated a higher net benefit for the random forest model across a 10–30% risk threshold range\. SHAP analysis confirmed daily morphine milligram equivalents and prior overdose history as the most contributory features, aligning with the logistic regression results\. An integrated risk prediction model for opioid overdose was successfully developed and validated\. The random forest algorithm exhibited optimal discriminative ability, calibration, and clinical utility, providing a tool for individualized risk assessment to guide precision prevention\.

## [Spontaneous hypopigmentation mutant in threespine stickleback fish exhibits changes in the gut microbiome consistent with inflammatory bowel diseases](../publications/ef91b319ea629b9febef.md)

Emily A\. Beck; Caitlin Smith; Mark C\. Currey; Clayton M\. Small; Brendan J\. M\. Bohannan; William A\. Cresko

Albinism is a large group of disorders characterized by a loss of pigment in ectoderm\-derived tissues \- most noticeably impacting the skin, hair, and eyes\. Albinism is categorized as either syndromic or non\-syndromic\. Syndromic albinisms include a wide range of disorders with mutations impacting not just pigmentation but other cellular functions\. These include, non\-exclusively, melanogenesis disorders, endosome trafficking disorders like lysosomal storage disorders, and cell migration disorders\. Mutations leading to syndromic albinisms can cause multi\-organ system symptoms due to broad disruption lysosome related organelles \(LROs\) function\. Various genetic mutations impact biogenesis, cell maturation, or trafficking at different stages which can lead to a range of severity\. Syndromic albinisms also present with different combinations of symptoms depending on the impacted organelles; including oculocutaneous albinism \(OCA\) \(melanosomes\), blood diathesis \(platelet dense granules\), pulmonary fibrosis \(lamellar bodies\), or chronic inflammation \(multiple cellular sources\)\. Animal models for these multisymptomatic complex disorders are needed to understand the effects on systemic health\. One such area of interest is in gut health of those with syndromic albinism\. Shared inflammatory patterns of syndromic albinisms like Hermansky\-Pudlak Syndromes \(HPS\) and Inflammatory Bowel Disease \(IBD\) are well studied, with animal models of HPS jointly used to study patterns of inflammation in IBD\. However, the impact of this shared gastrointestinal inflammation on the gut microbiome remains unexplored\. Using a spontaneously identified mutant family of threespine stickleback fish, we characterize phenotypes consistent with oculocutaneous albinism and vision impairment and demonstrate shared features of gut health to IBD extend from inflammation to the gut microbiome\. We argue syndromic albinism models should be explored as models to study the gut microbiome in addition to inflammatory phenotypes in IBD, and importantly, be used to test microbial/dietary interventions for both IBD and syndromic albinisms\.

## [Perlindungan Hak Cipta atas Lagu Daerah dalam Konten Digital: Tinjauan Undang\-Undang Nomor 28 Tahun 2014 dan Perspektif Kepastian Hukum, Keadilan, serta Kemanfaatan](../publications/ef95fbb81064082b9bb1.md)

Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk dan ruang lingkup perlindungan hukum terhadap lagu daerah berdasarkan Undang\-Undang Nomor 28 Tahun 2014 tentang Hak Cipta serta menilai penerapan asas kepastian hukum, keadilan, dan kemanfaatan dalam konteks konten digital\. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan peraturan perundang\-undangan dan konseptual melalui studi kepustakaan terhadap bahan hukum primer, sekunder, dan tersier\. ## [Moving homes and energy poverty: residents’ concerns, capabilities and responses](../publications/efac12906a2090123735.md)

Mikko Jalas; Jenny Rinkinen; Sini Numminen; Eija Valkealahti

In the study of energy poverty and vulnerability, limited attention has been paid to the social differentiation and unequal capacities to act\. This study examined housing mobility as part of energy action space, asking how the possibility, or impossibility, of moving home shapes energy vulnerability\. In\-depth interviews \(n = 29\) conducted during 2024 and 2025 with Finnish residents of detached houses investigated how moving home is discussed after the rapid rise in energy prices in 2022\. Some households experience a lock\-in beyond their control and inability to move, resulting in aggravated concern for the energy costs and living conditions in their house\. Whilst moving home might be a form of effective energy action, it is difficult due to financial constraints, health, housing market conditions or emotional attachment\. Moving home also requires capacities of anticipation and timely action\. Housing immobility forms a layer of vulnerability that coexists with other forms of vulnerability\. The findings challenge the assumption that owner\-occupants of detached houses do not experience energy poverty due to their asset ownership\. POLICY RELEVANCE Energy policy instruments that focus narrowly on prices or on energy efficiency risk overlooking how energy vulnerability is produced through housing trajectories and immobility\. Particularly in contexts where home ownership is widespread, policies need to consider the barriers of moving homes and relocating\. Public authorities need to consider how housing development, renovation support and mobility options shape the energy action space\. Policy should support not only energy retrofits but also feasible housing alternatives and options that allow households to move before their vulnerability becomes entrenched\. In more general terms, recognising that people may move home because of high energy costs and poor energy efficiency can help to support market developments towards energy retrofits, not only in the stock of owner\-occupied detached houses but also in the rental market, in which property owners need to retrofit to keep their assets attractive\.

## [Enhanced Diabetes Prediction](../publications/efaccd7dd93e911a2814.md)

Omar Mohammed Amin; Rebin Abdulkareem Hamaamin; Araz Ibrahim Mustafa; Aso Mohammed Aladdin

Diabetes is a large chronic disease where there is the potential to make early and reliable predictions to aid in timely clinical decisions and screening\. Recently, machine learning techniques have been used for diabetes anomaly detection, but the performance may be influenced by the presence of missing values, class imbalance, and a restricted feature representation in widely\-used benchmark datasets\. In this study, the Tabular Retrieval Network \(TabR\) model\-based framework for diabetes prediction is proposed in Pima Indians Diabetes \(PID\) dataset with 768 patient records and 8 clinical predictor variables and one binary target variable\. The proposed framework handles missing values in biologically unrealistic way by using class\-aware median imputation, introduces domain\-specific feature engineering, retrieves contextually similar patient records, and implements a neural network with Bayesian regularization as a classifier\. Stratified 10\-fold cross validation was used to evaluate the model using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, Matthew’s correlation coefficient \(MCC\) and area under the curve \(AUC\) as performance measures\. The proposed TabR model achieved an accuracy of 82\.04%, precision of 75\.93%, recall of 72\.04%, F1\-score of 73\.74%, MCC of 0\.6035, and AUC of 0\.8541\. These results show promising predictive and discriminative results on the PID data set\. Comparisons with previously reported studies showed that the proposed approach reached the highest accuracy reported compared to some of the existing solutions, however, the comparisons should be treated with caution as each study may have different preprocessing procedures and/or evaluation procedures\. The results indicate that class\-aware pre\-processing and contextual retrieval could be beneficial features for diabetes prediction from tabular clinical data\.

## [van Rooij, Iris &amp; Guest, Olivia: Combining Psychology with Artificial Intelligence: What could possibly go wrong?](../publications/efb21220d60d215d66fd.md)



\_Current Directions in Psychological Science\_ 35 \(3\):193–200\. 2026The current AI hype cycle combined with psychology’s various crises make for a perfect storm\. Psychology, on the one hand, has a history of weak theoretical foundations, a neglect for computational and formal skills, and a hyperempiricist privileging of experimental tasks and testing for effects\. Artificial intelligence, on the other hand, has a history of conflating artifacts for theories of cognition, or even minds themselves, and its engineering offspring likes to move fast and break things\. Many of our contemporaries now want to combine the worst of these two worlds\. What could possibly go wrong? Quite a lot\. Does this mean that psychology and artificial intelligence can best part ways? Not at all\. There are very fruitful ways in which the two disciplines can interact and theoretically contribute to cognitive science, for instance, by studying the scope and limits of computational models of human cognition\. But to reap the fruits, one needs to understand how to steer clear of potential traps\.

## [PERCEIVED COGNITIVE SKILLS AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN RESEARCH AND SCHOLARLY ACTIVITY AMONG TEACHER\-RESEARCHERS IN THE SALAH AL\-DIN DIRECTORATE OF EDUCATION](../publications/efcd98b51deeec14a3ee.md)

The study was aimed at determining the status and level of use and development of modern digital tools in agricultural extension in the Nineveh Governorate, such as agricultural extension content, digital interaction and participation, digital extension, modern communication technologies, smartphones and agricultural applications, multimedia, and agricultural videos\. It also explored the link between current use and development of modern tools and selected variables at personal and professional level\. It was administered using two questionnaires\. The first section gathered personal and professional information, and the second section had 60 items in six sections, each containing 10 items\. The questionnaire had a Cronbach alpha reliability coefficient of 0\.95 and showed face validity\. The study was carried out on 256 extension workers in the Nineveh Agriculture Directorate and its agricultural divisions \(32\)\. A random sample of 200 extension workers \(about 78% of the population\) was drawn\. Data were analysed in SPSS\. The findings showed moderate general level of development and modern tools used in agricultural extension work, leaning towards high\. The use of modern communication tools was high, while the use of smartphones and agricultural applications was moderate, tending toward high\. Digital platforms and the use of multimedia was moderate and tending to low, while digital interaction and participation was high\. Digital extension content development was moderate, leaning to high\. There was no significant relationship with education level, specialization, years of service or participation in training courses relating to digital technologies\. Age and years of service in agricultural extension were found to be significantly correlated at 0\.05 level and Internet use frequency at 0\.01 level, while owning a smart phone and the most frequently used digital tool were significantly correlated at 0\.05 level\. The study suggests aligning digital tools and resources to farmers&\#x27; needs and capacities, and building partnerships between the Nineveh Agriculture Directorate, universities, and research centers to create relevant digital platforms and tools\. ## [The role of artificial intelligence in business model innovation: an integrative framework and research agenda](../publications/efd1f17afc32235159d8.md)

João Serrasqueiro; Maria José Madeira

Purpose Given the rapid introduction of new technologies into organizational environments, there is currently a need to understand which economic, technological and social factors can influence organizations to implement artificial intelligence \(AI\) in order to stimulate innovation\. Thus, this research seeks to understand how the literature on the influence of AI on business model innovation has evolved, discovering which factors drive organizational interest on the part of organizations and how they can benefit with its implementation\. Design/methodology/approach To this end, a bibliometric methodology was employed, complemented by an in\-depth analytical review of each article\. The analysis covered the period from the emergence of the research field to 2026, resulting in the systematic examination of 117 studies published within this timeframe\. Findings Based on the bibliometric analysis, the articles were grouped into three clusters representing the main research streams in the field\. The findings show that AI\-driven business model innovation relies on dynamic capabilities, organizational resilience, strategic alignment, governance mechanisms and human–AI complementarity\. The study also provides strategic insights to help organizations align AI adoption with their specific characteristics and contexts\. Originality/value After creating an individual framework for each cluster, an integrative vision of AI in business model innovation was created, bringing together all the concepts under study, as well as an agenda for future research\.

## [Teaching Competency in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Review of Teachers’ Attitudes, Adaptability, and Professional Commitment](../publications/efd4c286300f4dab7fd2.md)

Pratima devi; Anjana sonker

The integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) into in these aspects of educational environments has initiated more of a paradigm shift in pedagogical structural methodologies, assessment strategies, and the use of fundamental role of educators\. This comprehensive review always seems to be examined the current state of teaching competency in the age of AI, focusing here on three pivotal dimensions: teachers&\#x27; attitudes towards AI, their adaptability of such aspects in utilizing intelligent tools, and their professional commitment in an era of rapid technological disruption\-based aspects\. Drawing upon a more natured based synthesis of recent literature, we therefore explore how factors such as AI literacy, generative based AI competence, &amp; as also AI\-TPACK \(Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge\) influence here in the successful integration of AI into classrooms everywhere\. The review in this aspects highlights that while educators here are increasingly by recognizing the potential of AI to more enhance personalized learning as well as administrative efficiency, there remain in this way to stay neutral significant barriers related to AI anxiety as also, ethical concerns, &amp; most of all a lack of targeted based on professional development\. Adaptability is conceptualized not merely as herein technical proficiency, but as a continuous pedagogical evolution requiring robust organizational support\-based aspects\. Furthermore, professional aspects of commitment in this nature always is analyzed through the lens of shifting teacher identities &amp; the ethical imperative to foster critical thinking and human\-centric values based through in AI\-augmented learning environments\. A prominent table\-based data related structure is provided to synthesize the thematic findings, mapping core competencies and against professional development needs\. The paper in this manner concludes with actionable recommendations for policymakers, teacher training programs, &amp; future research directions to ensure that educators are adequately equipped here to navigate the complexities of AI in education\.

## [СУЧАСНИЙ ОЛІМПІЙСЬКИЙ СПОРТ ЯК ДРАЙВЕР ІННОВАЦІЙ В УМОВАХ INDUSTRY 5\.0](../publications/efd6741cb14601b91b68.md)

Vlada Bilohur

Актуальність дослідження визначається тим, що сучасний олімпійський спорт дедалі більше виконує функцію каталізатора технологічних, організаційних, управлінських і соціальних інновацій\. Інноваційні рішення, апробовані у спорті найвищих досягнень, швидко поширюються на інші сфери суспільства, сприяючи розвитку цифрової економіки, індустрії здоров&\#x27;я, медичних технологій, інженерії, освіти, медіакомунікацій та креативних індустрій\. Метою статті є комплексне теоретико\-методологічне обґрунтування сучасного олімпійського спорту як драйвера інновацій в умовах INDUSTRY 5\.0, визначення особливостей інтеграції цифрових технологій, штучного інтелекту та людиноцентричних принципів у систему олімпійського спорту\. Концептуальні засади сучасної парадигми розвитку олімпійського спорту сформовано у стратегічних документах Міжнародного олімпійського комітету Olympic Agenda 2020, Olympic Agenda 2020\+5 та Olympic AI Agenda, розроблених під керівництвом президента МОК Томаса Баха\. У цих документах визначено стратегічні напрями цифрової трансформації олімпійського руху, інтеграції інноваційних технологій, штучного інтелекту, сталого розвитку\. Результати досліджень\. Проаналізовано теоретичні засади розвитку сучасного олімпійського спорту в контексті концепції INDUSTRY 5\.0, досліджено концептуальні підходи до розуміння олімпійського спорту як інноваційної екосистеми, Визначено роль штучного інтелекту, великих даних, Інтернету речей, цифрових платформ, цифрових двійників, хмарних технологій у модернізації системи підготовки спортсменів\. Обґрунтовано вплив принципів INDUSTRY 5\.0 на формування інноваційної моделі розвитку сучасного олімпійського спорту\. Визначено перспективні напрями впровадження інноваційних технологій у сучасний олімпійський спорт та його стратегічні пріоритети розвитку в умовах INDUSTRY 5\.0\. Зроблено висновок, що олімпійський спорт виступає не лише сферою змагань, а й своєрідною лабораторією створення та тестування інноваційних технологій\. Доведено, що формування стратегічних пріоритетів розвитку сучасного олімпійського спорту також нерозривно пов&\#x27;язане зі становленням цифрової економіки та когнітивного суспільства, у якому інноваційні технології стають основними джерелами конкурентних переваг\.

## [Pediatric MASLD in the precision medicine era: advances in diagnosis, prevention, and treatment](../publications/efe810d1c3fc33ac0ed7.md)

Anastasia Ntikoudi; Anastasia Papachristou; Eugenia D\. Vlachou

Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\) has emerged as one of the most clinically relevant chronic liver diseases in children and adolescents, reflecting the convergence of pediatric obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, altered glucose metabolism, and broader cardiometabolic risk\. The replacement of non\-alcoholic fatty liver disease \(NAFLD\) with MASLD represents a substantive conceptual shift, moving the field away from an exclusion\-based and potentially stigmatizing definition toward a pathophysiologically grounded framework centered on metabolic dysfunction\. This transition is particularly important in pediatric hepatology, where steatotic liver disease is rarely defined by alcohol exposure and is more commonly embedded within complex developmental, familial, behavioral, genetic, and socioeconomic determinants of metabolic health\. Although pediatric MASLD is often discussed as part of the obesity epidemic, its clinical heterogeneity indicates that body mass index alone is insufficient to capture disease risk, severity, or prognosis\. Recent evidence suggests that children with MASLD may be stratified into distinct metabolic and inflammatory phenotypes, supporting a move from uniform management toward risk\-adapted and phenotype\-informed care\. This review synthesizes current advances in the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of pediatric MASLD, with emphasis on precision medicine as a framework for integrating clinical, biochemical, imaging, genetic, lifestyle, and social determinants into individualized care pathways\. Current management remains anchored in lifestyle intervention and multidisciplinary cardiometabolic risk reduction, while important gaps persist in pediatric\-specific non\-invasive diagnostics, fibrosis risk prediction, longitudinal monitoring, and MASLD\-targeted pharmacotherapy\. A precision medicine approach may improve early identification of high\-risk children, guide intensity of follow\-up, inform therapeutic prioritization, and ultimately reduce liver\-related and cardiometabolic complications across the life course\.

## [A longitudinal evaluation of a university\-wide faculty development grant program: pedagogical innovation, student priorities, and programmatic evolution](../publications/eff391e12f6a64a50e19.md)

Saud Alkathiri; Ahmad Abdul\-Wahhab Shahba; Elham Alsadoon; Abeer A\. Alharbi; Reem Alrusaiyes; Ghaniah Ain; Khalid A\. Alnowibet

Background Faculty development grant programs are strategic levers for improving teaching quality, curriculum design, and student learning, yet longitudinal evaluations remain scarce\. In this study, we assess King Saud University&\#x27;s Program for Excellence in Learning and Teaching \(PELT\)— an early university\-wide faculty teaching\-grant initiative —examining its implementation, faculty uptake, and programmatic evolution over a decade\. Methods Using a longitudinal, multi\-source program\-evaluation design, we analyzed eight PELT cycles through 157 completed grants, faculty \( n = 108\) and student \( n = 413\) surveys, and descriptive benchmarking against 11 international peers\. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and selected faculty ratings were compared using Mann–Whitney U \-tests\. Results PELT evolved from a high\-volume inaugural phase \(71 grants\) to a more selective model \(6–11 grants annually\) with a 95\.7% completion rate\. Participation remained broadly balanced across Humanities \(34\.4%\), Science \(30\.6%\), and Health \(28\.0%\), supporting cross\-disciplinary engagement\. Teaching and assessment strategies \(51% of funded projects\) consistently dominated, with targeted emphases on job\-market skills and e\-learning in specific cycles\. Among student respondents, 71\.9% prioritized professional skills for employability, 52% favored problem\-based learning, and 57% preferred project\-based assessment over traditional exams\. Successful grantees reported high overall satisfaction with the program \(mean = 4\.5/5\), whereas non\-applicants highlighted awareness gaps \(54\.5%\) and workload constraints \(33\.3%\) as key barriers\. A statistically significant perceptual divide emerged between accepted and rejected applicants \( p ≤ 0\.001\), and international benchmarking positioned PELT in alignment with corresponding teaching\-grant schemes\. Conclusions PELT offers a replicable model for university teaching\-grant schemes that combines faculty development, student\-centered priorities, and longitudinal evolution\. The findings support strategies such as targeted outreach, formalized resubmission pathways, and tiered funding to advance pedagogical innovation and strengthen educational development\.

## [Homeostatic Control of Hebbian Plasticity Exerted by Action Potential‐Mediated Metaplasticity](../publications/eff5a6e820ffd58aa75c.md)

Giuseppe Busetto; Bruce G\. Mockett; Alessandro Marcon; Wickliffe C\. Abraham

Hebbian plasticity, in particular long\-term potentiation \(LTP\) of excitatory synapses, is a positive feed\-back mechanism and has the potential to saturate its effects with negative consequences at both the single neuron and the circuit level\. Metaplasticity is one of the mechanisms that can help overcome this problem\. During one form of metaplasticity, a high \(or low\) level of neuronal activity impedes \(or favors\) the expression of future LTP\. Although much is known about the role of synaptic activity in driving this metaplasticity effect, the specific role of postsynaptic action potential \(AP\) firing activity is still controversial and largely unknown\. Experimentally, a high level of AP firing has resulted in either the suppression \(a pro\-homeostatic effect\) or the enhancement \(an anti\-homeostatic effect\) of a later induced LTP\. Accordingly, we tested a wide range of AP firing frequencies generated by postsynaptic current pulses at different time intervals relative to the time of LTP induction at Schaffer collateral synapses of hippocampal CA1 neurons in Sprague\-Dawley rats\. We found that a wide range of AP firing frequencies, from 3 to 90 Hz, consistently inhibited the expression of future LTP at all time intervals tested, with no modulation of NMDA glutamate receptors\. Moreover, the generation of APs, as opposed to the average level of somatic depolarization during priming, was necessary for triggering the metaplasticity\. Our results provide solid evidence for a pro\-homeostatic metaplasticity that is engaged by postsynaptic AP firing, thus impeding the saturation of Hebbian plasticity and associated hyperexcitability\.

## [ANN\-GA\-based optimization of a hybrid battery thermal regulation system with helical liquid cooling, PCM, and copper foam](../publications/effad548d78242ff55d1.md)

Sonia Naghizadeh Mahjoub; Mohammad Vajdi; Kourosh Vaferi; Farhad Sadegh Moghanlou; Ebrahim Abdi Aghdam

Effective thermal management is essential for ensuring the safety, performance, and longevity of Lithium\-ion batteries \(LIBs\)\. In this study, an optimized hybrid Battery Thermal Regulation System \(BTRS\) is proposed, integrating helical liquid cooling mini\-channels and phase change material \(PCM\) embedded in a copper foam matrix \(CPCM\) to enhance heat dissipation\. To efficiently explore the complex design space, a coupled framework integrating numerical simulations, a Genetic Algorithm \(GA\), and Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\) was developed\. The approach successfully identified an ideal configuration \(OCD1\) characterized by a 10 mm PCM thickness, a 0\.08 m/s inlet velocity, and a \\\(65^\\circ \\\) helical angle\. Under a severe 3C discharge condition, this optimal design achieved a maximum temperature reduction of 21\.27 K, representing an 82\.25% improvement over a standalone cell\. Furthermore, the optimized hybrid system demonstrated superior cooling efficacy compared to individual strategies, outperforming case A \(liquid cooling\) by 33\.67%, case B \(pure PCM\) by 69\.35%, and case C \(CPCM\) by 45%\. The developed ANN model exhibited high predictive accuracy, with R 2 values exceeding 0\.99 for both thermal responses\. These findings provide a high fidelity and scalable framework for advanced thermal management of next\-generation electric vehicle battery systems\.

## [Intelligence and Crime Analysis Through Fictional Detectives](../publications/effcfbcddaff76ca0612.md)

Laurence F\. Prokop

This book offers a fresh and imaginative approach to understanding investigative practice by blending the world of mystery and detective fiction with the real tools used in modern law enforcement, criminal justice, forensic science, and intelligence analysis\. By examining how iconic fictional detectives solve cases, the text reveals how narrative, logic, and observation shape the foundations of investigative work\. Readers benefit from a rich set of learning features, including character‑focused chapters, case studies, key terms, comparative charts linking fictional methods to contemporary analytic techniques, discussion questions, and curated reading lists\. These elements work together to make complex investigative concepts accessible, memorable, and engaging through the power of storytelling\. The book is ideal for students in criminal justice, intelligence studies, homeland security, and forensic science, as well as law enforcement trainees, policy professionals, and mystery enthusiasts who want to deepen their understanding of investigative thinking\. Its approachable style and narrative‑driven structure make it invaluable for both academic and professional settings\. Support materials include an Instructor’s Guide that provides discussion prompts, assessment ideas, and supplemental activities to help educators integrate the text into their courses\. These resources enhance the learning experience and make the book easy to adopt in classrooms, training programs, and workshops\.

## [Fiqh Education in the Context of Artificial intelligence: Shifts in Pedagogy, Authority, and Religious Literacy](../publications/effe87dd2e526327e3f9.md)

Zuhri Zuhri; Faisal Amir Toedien

The rapid development of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has expanded the use of information and learning resources in Islamic Religious Education, including Fiqh learning, while raising concerns regarding pedagogy, the authority and validity of religious knowledge, and students’ ability to evaluate AI\-generated information\. This study examines the use of AI in Islamic education and synthesizes its implications for Fiqh learning, focusing on pedagogy, the authority and validity of religious knowledge, and religious literacy and AI literacy\. A Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) was conducted on 25 scholarly articles published between 2020 and 2026 and retrieved from Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Indonesian scholarly databases GARUDA/SINTA\. Searches used combinations of keywords related to artificial intelligence, generative AI, ChatGPT, Islamic education, Islamic religious education, and fiqh education\. Articles were selected based on their relevance to Islamic education or Fiqh learning and to the analytical dimensions of the study\. Data were analyzed through coding, thematic categorization, cross\-source comparison, and thematic synthesis\. The findings indicate that AI is increasingly used to support personalized learning, information exploration, learning\-material development, and instructional interaction\. However, its use also intensifies the need for source verification, information validation, and teacher guidance\. The synthesis further highlights the importance of integrating religious literacy and AI literacy to enable students to evaluate AI\-generated information critically and responsibly\. Based on these findings, the study proposes an AI\-assisted but teacher\-guided Fiqh learning framework that positions AI as a learning support tool, teachers as pedagogical and knowledge mediators, and students as active evaluators of information\.

## [Artificial intelligence\-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat](../publications/f00129fee9d30a138bb9.md)

Nicolás Gómez\-Banoy; Jorge A\. Barrero; Luiza Rachel Pinheiro de Carvalho; Caroline S\. Jiang; Tara Doma Lama; Nakul Karandikar; Mascha Koenen; Tiffany Lam; Kaja Plucińska; Ksenia Morozova; Stephanie Chahwan; Gustavo Barraza; Burcin Agridag Ucpinar; Jennifer E\. Liu; Rohit Sharma; Daniel Lafontaine; Heiko M\. Schöder; Paul Cohen

Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2\. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue \(BAT\) uses energy to produce heat3\. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4\. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high\-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6\. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre\. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT\. Using a machine learning approach, we semi\-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution\. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices\. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence\. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole\-body energy expenditure\. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans\. Artificial intelligence\-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue \(BAT\) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans\.

## [S\-GAP: Stealthy Graph Attack Primitives for Graph Large Language Models](../publications/f01a8bc9bd49e8e20d3c.md)

Wenda Li; Tongya Zheng; Shunyu Liu; Hanyang Yuan; Kaixuan Chen; Yu Wang; Yuchen Ying; Haoze Jiang; Huan Li; Gang Chen; Zujie Ren

Graph Large Language Models \(GraphLLMs\) enable powerful semantic understanding and reasoning over Text\-Attributed Graphs \(TAGs\), while their semantic reasoning may exhibit vulnerabilities to perturbations in node text and graph structure under adversarial attack evaluation\. Existing attacks typically construct textual and structural perturbations in separate stages guided by distinct realization intents\. However, this separation results in attack\-intent fragmentation, causing semantic incoherence between the two perturbation types, thereby undermining attack stealth and making them easier for GraphLLMs to identify and disregard, ultimately weakening attack effectiveness\. To avoid attack\-intent fragmentation, we propose the Graph Attack Primitive \(GAP\), an atomic semantic representation that unifies textual and structural perturbations under a coherent attack intent\. By carefully calibrating the semantic composition of a GAP, we can achieve strong attack effectiveness while maintaining sufficient attack stealth\. Furthermore, we introduce S\-GAP \(Stealthy GAP\), a multi\-agent framework that iteratively refines the semantic content of the GAP\. The framework unifies GAP planning and realization and continuously refines this process through surrogate evaluation and textual feedback\. Extensive experiments across four datasets, three GraphLLMs, and two attack settings show that S\-GAP improves ASR over the strongest baselines by 7\.02% on average while producing more relationally plausible perturbations, exposing critical vulnerabilities in current GraphLLMs and motivating more robust defenses\.

## [A qualitative study on professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals in Parkinson’s disease in Chennai, India](../publications/f028318ff0b8c8295a88.md)

A\. Rajyasree; Janarthanan Balamurugan

Healthcare professionals experience substantial burden when providing long\-term care for patients with Parkinson’s disease\. Despite their central role in care delivery, the experiences of healthcare professionals remain under\-examined in Indian healthcare contexts\. This qualitative study explored professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals involved in Parkinson’s disease care in South India\. Twelve healthcare professionals \(Neurologists, Nurses, Physician Assistants, Physiotherapists, and Psychologists\) were recruited from two tertiary hospitals in Chennai between April and May 2025\. A semi\-structured interview schedule was utilised to gather data\. Data were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s six\-phase thematic analysis\. The study identified 5 major themes \(1\) Emotional Burden of Continuous Care in PD, \(2\) Clinical and Cognitive Complexity, \(3\) Critical Care and Physical Demands, \(4\) Family Dynamics and Relative Challenges, and \(5\) Administrative and Systemic Barriers, encompassing 18 sub\-themes\. The findings indicate that professional caregiver burden in PD care arises from the interaction of cultural expectations, structural constraints, and the progressive nature of the disease\. Remarkably, accumulated clinical experience did not diminish cognitive burden; instead, greater experience escalated exposure to therapeutic uncertainty and prognostic complexity\. Findings associated with physical rehabilitation are presented as an illustrative case, due to the single\-participant illustration of the physiotherapy discipline\. The professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals in PD care operates across multiple professional and systemic dimensions\. It also represents a patient\-safety concern with implications for occupational health policy and institutional mental\-health support in tertiary care settings\. These burden dimensions elucidate how professional caregiver burden, emerging from progressive neurological disease care, is shaped by structural constraints and cultural care contexts\.

## [Intraluminal micro\-stenting improves urinary tract reconstruction in murine kidney transplant model](../publications/f03386de18526f9fb83c.md)

Zi\-Jie Xu; Long He; Zheng Tang; Ren\-Jie Wang; 杨银; Kai\-Ying Chen; Ze\-Tao Ding; Jun\-Ru Lu; Hao\-Dong Chi; Jifu Ge; Zhihong Liu

BACKGROUND: Urinary tract reconstruction is a key technical barrier in murine kidney transplantation due to the tiny ureteral caliber\. Conventional methods are technically demanding with high morbidity\. This study assesses a refined intraluminal stenting approach for better surgical stability, fewer complications, and preserved anti\-reflux structural anatomy of the ureterovesical junction\. We performed 88 orthotopic mouse kidney transplantations using three distinct reconstruction modalities: bladder patch \(n = 31\), ureter implantation \(n = 28\), and intraluminal stenting \(n = 29\)\. The stenting protocol utilized a micro\-polyethylene \(PE\) stent to achieve end\-to\-end ureteral alignment\. Outcomes included operative efficiency, learning curve trajectories, postoperative survival, and urinary\-related morbidity\. RESULTS: The stenting cohort achieved a 14\-day survival rate of 96\.6% \(28/29\), significantly higher than the bladder patch group \(67\.7%, 21/31; p = 0\.006\), while the difference compared with the ureter implantation group \(82\.1%, 23/28\) did not reach statistical significance \(p = 0\.102\)\. Intraluminal stenting markedly reduced reconstruction time \(8&\#x27;22&\#x27;&\#x27;±0&\#x27;41&\#x27;&\#x27;, p &lt; 0\.05 vs\. both control groups\) and was associated with an accelerated proficiency acquisition curve\. The overall urological morbidity in the stenting group was 10\.3% \(3/29\), consisting of 1 case of mild urinary leakage and 2 cases of mild hydronephrosis, which was significantly lower than in the bladder patch \(58\.1%, 18/31\) and ureter implantation \(42\.9%, 12/28\) cohorts \(p &lt; 0\.05 for morbidity comparison\)\. Notably, this approach effectively precluded severe complications including ischemic necrosis, ureteral dislodgement, and obstruction, with no urinary tract reconstruction\-related deaths observed\. CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective study shows that the intraluminal stenting technique offers a reliable and highly reproducible approach for urinary tract reconstruction in murine kidney transplantation\. This modality significantly minimizes technical complexity and postoperative morbidity, and maintains the intact ureterovesical anatomy that provides the structural foundation for physiological anti\-reflux function\. It provides an optimized surgical platform for short\-term experimental protocols, particularly in acute rejection research\.

## [Dismantling the Honorarium Trap: Asymmetric BOSP Fiscal Caps, Teacher Redistribution, and Student Cognitive Achievement in Indonesia&\#x27;s Underdeveloped Regions: Evidence from K\-Means and Quantile Regression](../publications/f034b748fed4ebc93f43.md)

Aji Kusumanto; Dwi Setia Permana; Erwin Sahala Pangaloan

Fiscal decentralization through the School Operational Assistance \(BOSP\) grant gives schools in Indonesia&\#x27;s frontier, outermost, and underdeveloped \(3T\) regions wide discretion over spending, yet the composition of that spending is rarely linked to learning\. This study aims to describe BOSP allocation patterns, identify fiscal typologies of schools, and examine how component level spending is associated with student cognitive achievement across the achievement distribution\. The design is observational and cross sectional\. Merged administrative records for the 2024 fiscal and academic year were drawn from ARKAS, Dapodik, and the Academic Potential Test \(TKA\), with the school as the unit of analysis, covering 855 public and private senior high schools in 62 underdeveloped regencies\. K\-Means clustering segmented the schools into a resilient group of 62 schools, an intermediate group of 454 schools, and a vulnerable group of 339 schools, while quantile regression estimated associations at five quantiles of the TKA distribution\. Spending on learning activities is positively associated with TKA scores in the lower and upper middle quantiles, whereas the honorarium share interacted with private ownership shows a negative association only at the highest quantile\. The results suggest that spending composition, rather than budget volume alone, is associated with cognitive achievement in remote schools\.

## [Aplicación de ciencia de datos para la evaluación y fortalecimiento de habilidades blandas en la empleabilidad de graduados de carreras de ingeniería de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional: similitud curricular entre carreras de ingeniería en Ecuador: un enfoque basado en NLP y taxonomías de competencias\.](../publications/f035e682e80b583dc2ef.md)

G\.I\.\(Glenn Isaac\) Salcedo Oña

La comparación entre carreras universitarias suele realizarse a partir de mallas curriculares o criterios administrativos; sin embargo, los perfiles de egreso y profesionales también reflejan con claridad el tipo de formación que cada institución busca ofrecer\. En este trabajo se analiza la similitud curricular entre carreras de ingeniería de universidades ecuatorianas mediante técnicas de Procesamiento de Lenguaje Natural, modelos de embeddings multilingües y una taxonomía de competencias\. Para el estudio se construyó un corpus compuesto por 163 carreras pertenecientes a 14 universidades del Ecuador, tomando como fuente principal la información publicada en sitios web oficiales\. La metodología se organizó en tres niveles: una representación léxica basada en TF\-IDF, una representación semántica directa mediante los modelos BGE\-M3 y multilingual\-E5\-Large, y una representación basada en habilidades a partir de la taxonomía ESCO\. En cada nivel se calcularon similitudes entre carreras y se aplicó clustering jerárquico para identificar agrupamientos curriculares\. Los resultados muestran que TF\-IDF funciona como una línea base útil, aunque limitada por la coincidencia de vocabulario\. En cambio, los modelos semánticos permitieron reconocer relaciones más profundas entre perfiles redactados de forma distinta\. El modelo multilingual\-E5\-Large obtuvo la mayor correlación cofenética, mientras que la representación basada en ESCO alcanzó el mejor índice de silueta para \(k=10\), lo que evidencia agrupamientos más cohesionados e interpretables\. En general, la metodología propuesta demuestra ser una alternativa viable para analizar similitudes curriculares a escala institucional y puede servir como base para futuros estudios de equivalencia académica en contextos nacionales e internacionales\.

## [Critical Subjectivity in the New Field of Contemplative Studies](../publications/f03ad162eb9e85818720.md)

Harold David Roth

This article argues for incorporating “critical subjectivity,” developed within the emerging interdisciplinary field of Contemplative Studies, into academic scholarship in the humanities and the sciences\. Drawing on the author’s intellectual formation through mentors in Chinese philosophy, Buddhist studies, and contemplative practice, it challenges the conventional ideal of purely objective scholarship and contends that all research is inevitably shaped by subjective perspectives\. Rather than attempting to eliminate subjectivity, the article proposes a disciplined and self\-aware approach that critically examines and refines it\. The theoretical foundation for this approach is developed within Brown University’s Contemplative Studies program’s “integrative contemplative pedagogy,” which combines traditional third\-person academic analysis with first\-person experiential engagement in contemplative practices\. Building on work in phenomenology, cognitive science, and contemplative traditions, the author outlines four complementary epistemologies: third\-person, second\-person, first\-person, and a proposed fourth mode, “no\-person” epistemology, derived from Chan and Zen traditions\. This non\-self\-referential mode of awareness is supported by contemporary neuroscientific and psychological research\. The article concludes that integrating these epistemological perspectives can foster a more rigorous, reflective, and less biased scholarship capable of addressing the complexities of consciousness and human experience\.

## [Mapping the Intellectual Structure of Sustainable Development Goals Research: A Bibliometric Science‐Mapping Analysis \(2015–2025\)](../publications/f0418ad37f42f027486f.md)

Muhammad Rafiq; Zhang Qianhui

ABSTRACT Since their adoption in 2015, the Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\) have become a central framework shaping global sustainability research, policy, and practice\. However, SDG scholarship remains fragmented across disciplines, themes, and geographical contexts, limiting understanding of its intellectual structure and thematic evolution\. This study addresses this gap through a bibliometric science‐mapping analysis of SDG research published between 2015 and July 2025\. Following a PRISMA‐guided selection process, 5425 Scopus‐indexed articles published in ABDC‐ranked journals were analyzed using Bibliometrix, Biblioshiny \(R\), and VOSviewer\. The analysis included performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, collaboration networks, thematic evolution, and strategic mapping\. The findings show sustained growth in SDG research, with an annual publication growth rate of 41\.21%\. China, the United Kingdom, and India were the leading contributors, while the Journal of Cleaner Production was the most influential outlet\. Thematic analysis shows a shift from broad sustainability discussions toward more specialized topics, including renewable energy, circular economy, artificial intelligence, and ESG‐related research\. The results also reveal geographical and disciplinary disparities, particularly the limited representation of low‐income regions within the analyzed literature\. This study contributes by mapping the intellectual structure, thematic development, and collaborative dynamics of SDG research over the past decade\. The findings offer useful guidance for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to identify emerging priorities, research gaps, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross‐regional collaboration toward the 2030 SDG agenda\.

## [&\#x27;Old Wine, New Wineskins&\#x27;: Prolegomenon to a Socio\-Theology of the Internet](../publications/f0434f26d966c1543185.md)

Wjf Keenan

This article draws on a variety of theological, sociological, and anthropological threads of thought from Otto to Berger, from Pascal to Martin, to \(dis\)entangle metaphorical and implicitly religious properties of the Web\. By adding a religio\-spiritual dimension to the unending quest to understand the fuller circle of ideas in which technology is implicated, the thought\-worlds of sociology and theology can be brought into more constructive conversation than has typically been the case in the modern period\. As a contribution to understanding contemporary techno\-religion, this article provides a framework for exploring pre\-modern theo\-spiritual residues implicit in the postmodern habitus of the internet\.

## [DIAGNOSTICO ELETROCARDIOGRAFICO E MANEJO CLINICO NO TRATAMENTO DA TAQUICARDIA VENTRICULAR](../publications/f044145e9f9ff136f6b9.md)

Euclides Dotta Neto; Jamile Benetton Hussni; Faustino Chaves Calvo; Brayan Yamid Bohorquez Beltran; Roberta Ramos Ribeiro Cabral; Sarah Cezar Cardoso Galdino; Ali Hassan Harb; Karina Santana Leotério; Camila Stefane Sousa Pinto; Maria Karolina Echer Ferreira Feijó; Maria Izabel Rodrigues Vieira Amorim; Noemy Krishna Botelho Barros; Thiago Santos Monção

A taquicardia ventricular \(TV\) é uma arritmia potencialmente fatal, caracterizada pela ocorrência de três ou mais batimentos ventriculares consecutivos, podendo ser monomórfica ou polimórfica, sustentada ou não sustentada\. Sua relevância clínica está relacionada ao risco de instabilidade hemodinâmica, recorrência, fibrilação ventricular e morte súbita, especialmente em pacientes com cardiopatia estrutural\. O diagnóstico das taquicardias de complexo QRS largo constitui importante desafio, sendo necessária a diferenciação entre TV e taquicardia supraventricular com condução aberrante\. A análise sistemática do eletrocardiograma de 12 derivações, associada à avaliação clínica, permite maior precisão diagnóstica, com auxílio de algoritmos como Brugada, Vereckei e Basel\. O presente estudo teve como objetivo revisar os principais critérios eletrocardiográficos utilizados no diagnóstico diferencial da TV e analisar as estratégias atuais de manejo clínico\. Foi realizada revisão bibliográfica narrativa na base PubMed, utilizando os descritores “Tachycardia, Ventricular” e “Therapeutics”, combinados por operadores booleanos\. Os resultados demonstram que a estabilidade hemodinâmica orienta a conduta inicial\. Na presença de instabilidade, indica\-se cardioversão elétrica sincronizada, enquanto a TV sem pulso requer desfibrilação e ressuscitação cardiopulmonar\. Nos pacientes estáveis, devem ser investigadas causas reversíveis e o substrato cardíaco\. Em casos recorrentes ou de tempestade elétrica, podem ser utilizados fármacos antiarrítmicos, betabloqueadores, sedação, cardiodesfibrilador implantável e ablação por cateter\. Conclui\-se que o reconhecimento precoce da TV, associado à interpretação eletrocardiográfica sistemática e ao tratamento individualizado, é fundamental para reduzir recorrência, complicações e mortalidade\.

## [Integrating innovative technologies and sustainable HSE practices for risk and hazard management in oil and gas operations: a qualitative review and analytical framework](../publications/f0467b9f9c54d9d7cfe3.md)

Barima Money; Priyanga A\. /P\. Kailasanathan; Norida Ridzuan; Gbonhinbor Jeffrey Randy; Norasyikin Ismail; Abutu David; Francis Nyah; Ruwaida Abdul Rasid; Siti Qurratu’ Aini Mahat

The oil and gas industry faces substantial occupational, process, and environmental risks arising from high\-pressure and high\-temperature systems, hazardous hydrocarbons, complex operations, and environmentally sensitive activities\. This study aims to examine how innovative technologies can be integrated with sustainable Health, Safety, and Environment \(HSE\) practices to strengthen risk and hazard management, operational safety, environmental protection, and regulatory compliance across upstream, midstream, and downstream operations\. A qualitative review and analytical framework approach was employed using evidence from peer\-reviewed literature, industry reports, international HSE standards, government regulations, and company sustainability reports\. The analysis evaluated technological and HSE approaches according to their contributions to safety improvement, risk mitigation, environmental performance, cost\-effectiveness, and regulatory compliance\. Particular attention was given to real\-time monitoring systems, digital twins, automation and robotics, predictive analytics, artificial intelligence, and advanced leak detection technologies, together with Environmental Management Systems \(EMS\), ISO 14,001, ISO 45,001, and Risk\-Based Process Safety \(RBPS\)\. The review indicates that technology\-enabled HSE management can support earlier hazard detection, proactive risk control, improved operational decision\-making, reduced human exposure to hazardous environments, and enhanced environmental monitoring\. The analysis further identifies safety culture, workforce competency development, continuous training, and organizational commitment as essential elements for translating technological capabilities into sustained HSE performance\. The principal contribution of this study is the development of an integrated HSE–Technology–Sustainability perspective that connects digital innovation, risk management, environmental protection, workforce capability, and regulatory compliance within a unified framework for safer and more sustainable oil and gas operations\.

## [The information professional as an ethical intermediary: information quality criteria and the ethics of generative AI](../publications/f051af2039b3a2fe8d6e.md)

T\. D\. Wilson; Elena Macevičiūtė

Introduction\. The adoption of generative AI raises ethical concerns for information professionals whose intermediary role requires them to ensure information quality standards that users cannot independently verify\. Professional ethics address quality superficially, and the ethical implications of generative AI have not been examined from the perspective of professional obligations\. Method\. A scoping review assessed 644 records across three search strands, retaining 120 papers, which were analysed against ten information quality criteria and assessed for the strength of their ethical framing\. Analysis\. Ten practice\-derived quality criteria, corresponding closely to ISO/IEC 25012, are shown to be based on a Kantian deontological framework complemented by a Marxist treatment of algorithmic surplus value\. For each criterion the literature documenting the relevant AI failure mode is reviewed and its ethical treatment assessed\. Results\. Four criteria, accuracy, objectivity, identifiable origin, and accessibility, attract substantial ethical attention\. For the remaining six, ethical treatment is limited or absent\. Conclusions\. The information professional&\#x27;s intermediary role is an ethical necessity\. Professional organisations are called upon to lobby actively for AI governance using the criteria framework developed here\.

## [Qualificação do processo de governança e gestão de medicamentos em centrais de abastecimento farmacêutico](../publications/f06a9d1e312e7c72e573.md)

Regimara Maria Soares Maranhão; Orenzio Soler; Marcieni Ataíde de Andrade

Objetivo: Mapear as evidências acerca da qualificação do processo de governança bem como da gestão de medicamentos em Centrais de Abastecimento Farmacêutico\. Métodos: Trata\-se de uma revisão de escopo seguindo as diretrizes estabelecidas pelo JBI, o protocolo desta revisão foi elaborado e registrado na OSF, o direcionamento da pesquisa foi realizado com a utilização do acrônimo PCC, em que P representa os participantes definido para esta pesquisa P = Gestores; Conceito, C = Qualificação do processo de governança e gestão de medicamentos e Contexto, C = Centrais de Abastecimento Farmacêutico\. Esta revisão teve como base de dados Lilacs, Pubmed, Scielo, pela escassez de literatura optamos por realizar buscas nos Portais de Periódicos da CAPES e no Google Acadêmico, a partir dos artigos selecionados foi realizada aa avaliações do nível de evidência e da qualidade dos artigos\. Resultados: Foram selecionados 14 artigos a partir dos critérios metodológicos, dos quais os dados referentes à autoria, ano, objetivo, metodologia, nível de evidência e desfecho foram apresentados\. ## [Resource\-Based Theory \(RBT\): A Human Resource Perspective on Firm Performance](../publications/f06af66436cf7016a59d.md)

Agnes Wayua Kyalo; Charles Katua Kithandi

Resource\-Based Theory \(RBT\) holds that firms achieve and sustain competitive advantage not primarily through their position in product markets but through the possession and deployment of internal resources that are valuable, rare, imperfectly imitable, and non\-substitutable \(VRIN\)\. Although RBT originated in the strategic management literature, its most enduring and generative application has been to the firm&\#x27;s human resources\. This article examines RBT as a theoretical foundation for understanding how human resource management \(HRM\) contributes to sustainable firm performance\. It traces the theory&\#x27;s intellectual origins from Penrose&\#x27;s theory of the growth of the firm, through Wernerfelt&\#x27;s resource\-based view, to Barney&\#x27;s VRIN framework, before turning to the strategic human resource management \(SHRM\) literature that appropriated and extended RBT notably Wright and McMahan&\#x27;s theoretical perspectives on SHRM, Lado and Wilson&\#x27;s competency\-based view, and the human\-capital and social\-capital extensions that followed\. Building on this foundation, the article develops an integrative conceptual model that links HR systems, VRIN human\-resource capital, and collective employee behaviour to firm performance through the mediating logic captured in the Ability\-Motivation\-Opportunity \(AMO\) framework, and it advances five research propositions\. The article also engages critically with the tautology, causal\-ambiguity, and context\-dependence critiques levelled at RBT, and considers complementary institutional and dynamic\-capability perspectives that address RBT&\#x27;s static bias\. It concludes with implications for strategic HRM practice and directions for future empirical research, arguing that human resources, properly configured, remain among the most defensible sources of sustained competitive advantage available to the modern firm\.

## [COGNITIVE BIASES OF FINANCIAL MANAGERS AND THEIR IMPACT ON CORPORATE RISK ARCHITECTURE](../publications/f06d3c23882f90fa19e8.md)



Biases based on cognition are very important in influencing managerial decision in situations of corporate financial settings\.Even though the conventional financial theories presume that a manager is a rational individual in making risk\-taking and opportunity decisions, research in behavioral finance indicates that often psychological factors can impact such decisions\.Unwittingly, the financial managers who are tasked with formulating and putting corporate risk management structures into place may be guilty of applying the cognitive bias in the form of overconfidence, confirmation bias, anchoring and loss aversion to their decisions\.Such prejudices may influence the perception, evaluation, and management of risks carried out in an organization and eventually impact organizational corporate risk architecture\.

## [Think More or Read More? A Token\-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context](../publications/f071443f1ce55706a8b1.md)

Manh Nguyen; Sunil Gupta; Hung Le

Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model&\#x27;s input, from multi\-agent debate, where agents read their peers&\#x27; responses, to self\-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts\. In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent&\#x27;s output becomes another&\#x27;s input\. We study the regime where token reading and generation draw on one fixed token window, so every token spent reading is a token that cannot be spent reasoning\. We develop a \\textbf\{token\-budget theory\} that formalizes this trade\-off, modeling accuracy as a function of the reasoning budget remaining after reading and aggregating votes with a Condorcet jury model that permits correlated errors\. For multi\-agent debate, the theory gives a closed\-form prediction for the optimal number of agents\. This quantity is estimated from single\-agent measurements, allowing the optimal group size to be determined without running debate, and the same accounting extends to a heterogeneous set of different models\. We empirically verify our theory and show that, at the predicted group size, our method outperforms strong baselines under the tightest calibration spend, where debate\-calibrated rules can afford only one or two questions\. Self\-refinement obeys the same accounting, with its own draft in place of a peer message\. The theory further predicts that communication pays only when the gain in the accuracy ceiling exceeds the reasoning room spent on reading, with this condition tightening as the window shrinks\. Across five open models and four reasoning tasks, self\-consistency matches or beats deployed debate at $93$\\% of $980$ matched window\-and\-group\-size settings, with the gap being largest under tight windows and nearly disappearing at a loose one, consistent with the theory\. Under a shared window, how much room a model has left to \\textit\{think matters more than what it reads\}\.

## [Early\-treatment coagulation activation and radiographic progression during VEGF/VEGFR inhibitor therapy: A multicancer real\-world cohort study](../publications/f0729025eec74c872fd9.md)

Yingda Liu; Bai Liu; Su Liu; Teng Zhang; Tianye Lv; Sibei Han; Huichao Li; Shuo Sun; Xin Zhou

Coagulation activation is common in cancer, but its link to treatment durability is unclear\. We investigated whether early\-treatment coagulation activation correlated with radiographic progression during vascular endothelial growth factor \(VEGF\)/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor \(VEGFR\) inhibitor therapy\. This single\-center, retrospective, multicancer cohort study developed a coagulation activation score \(0\-2\) based on the last available D\-dimer \(&gt;500 ng/mL\) and fibrinogen \(&gt;4\.0 g/L\) measurements taken within 100 days after baseline\. Multivariable Cox models calculated hazard ratios \(HRs\) and 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\) for subsequent radiographic time to progression among patients who were progression\-free at the 100\-day landmark\. Of 1400 eligible patients, 1089 had evaluable early\-treatment measurements, and 909 were included in the landmark analysis\. Compared to a score of 0, adjusted HRs were 1\.29 \(95% CI 1\.02\-1\.62\) for score 1 and 1\.51 \(95% CI 1\.07\-2\.12\) for score 2\. Score 2 also correlated with lower odds of durable clinical benefit \(adjusted odds ratio 0\.56, 95% CI 0\.38\-0\.84\), while objective response and best tumor shrinkage did not show a consistent gradient\. These associations remained significant in time\-dependent and timing\-restricted analyses\. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed the strongest association in colorectal cancer patients treated with bevacizumab \(score 2 vs\. 0: HR 2\.23, 95% CI 1\.21\-4\.11\); however, no association was observed in lung cancer patients treated with bevacizumab\. No significant interaction with documented immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure was detected\. The score did not enhance discrimination beyond clinical variables and baseline coagulation markers\. Early\-treatment coagulation activation was associated with reduced treatment durability during VEGF/VEGFR inhibition\. Prospective validation in specific cancer\-drug contexts is necessary\.

## [Readiness of AI \(Artificial Intelligence\) strategies Used in Nursing Education among Undergraduate Nursing Students “A Cross Sectional Descriptive Survey”](../publications/f076d0105ca499e660cf.md)

Samrin Nanji; Mujeebullah; Rahool; Muhammad Asif; Yashwa Qaisar; Elisha Yaqoob; Summera Sultan; Mahpara

The aim of this quantitative cross sectional survey is to describe the frequencies of readiness of AI \(Artificial Intelligence\) in nursing education among undergraduate nursing students\. Methodology of this research included, the design of this research is cross sectional descriptive study, sample size was N=50 undergraduate nursing students of first year first semester\. Sampling technique was simple random sampling and setting was a Nursing College in private University\. The data was analyzing by SPSS AMOS\-23 software\. The TAM \(Technology Acceptance Model\) was used to collect the data basically this tool was adopted from a Pakistani research article the validity and reliability of the tool has been mentioned in methodology section in chapter 3\. A total of 50 undergraduate nursing students participated in the study examining readiness for the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) strategies in nursing education\. The demographic findings showed an equal distribution of male and female participants, with 25 \(50%\) students in each group\. Regarding age, the majority of participants, 47 \(94%\), were aged 21–23 years, while 3 \(6%\) were aged 24–26 years\. Regarding the perceived usefulness of AI strategies in nursing education, all participants reported negative responses to the statement that AI strategies improved their learning outcomes, with 26 \(52%\) strongly disagreeing and 24 \(48%\) disagreeing\. For the statement that AI tools could help students understand complex nursing concepts, 18 \(36%\) strongly disagreed, 11 \(22%\) disagreed, 11 \(22%\) remained neutral, and 10 \(20%\) strongly agreed\. Similarly, 42 \(84%\) participants disagreed or strongly disagreed that AI\-based learning resources could improve their clinical decision\-making skills, while 4 \(8%\) were neutral and 4 \(8%\) strongly agreed\. Regarding whether AI strategies could make nursing studies more productive, 17 \(34%\) strongly disagreed, 12 \(24%\) disagreed, 11 \(22%\) were neutral, and 10 \(20%\) strongly agreed\. All participants \(100%\) disagreed with the statement that AI tools could help them prepare more effectively for nursing examinations\. The study revealed low readiness among undergraduate nursing students towards the use of AI strategies in nursing education\. Most participants reported negative perceptions regarding AI usefulness, ease of use and integration into academic activities\. The findings highlight the need for structured AI literacy training, practical guidance and education on the responsible use of AI\. Further research with larger sample is recommended to explore student’s readiness for AI integration in nursing education\.
