## [DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN BRAIN TUMOR CLASSIFICATION ON MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING: A DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY STUDY](../publications/f0980e88fe10d9bc1bbf.md)



Background: Brain tumours are among the most challenging neurological disorders due to their diverse histopathological characteristics and overlapping imaging features\.Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\) is the preferred imaging modality for the evaluation of brain tumours because of its superior soft\-tissue contrast and multiplanar imaging capability\.However, accurate tumor classification remains dependent on radiologist expertise and may be subject to interobserver variability\.Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have shown promising results in automated image analysis and tumor classification, with the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision\-making\. Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of deep learning applications in the classification of brain tumours on Magnetic Resonance Imaging\.Objectives:1\. To determine the diagnostic accuracy of a deep learning model for classifying brain tumours on MRI using histopathological diagnosis as the reference standard\.2\. To compare the diagnostic performance of the deep learning model with radiologist interpretation in the classification of brain tumours on MRI\. Materials and Methods:A hospital\-based diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in the Department of Radiodiagnosis in collaboration with the Departments of Neurosurgery and Pathology\.A total of 30 patients with histopathologically confirmed brain tumours who fulfilled the inclusion and exclusion criteria were included\.Preoperative MRI examinations were analysed using a validated deep learning algorithm\.The deep learning predictions were compared with histopathological diagnosis, which served as the gold standard, and with conventional radiologist interpretation\.Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, overall accuracy, receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis, area under the curve \(AUC\), Cohen&\#x27;s kappa coefficient, and McNemar&\#x27;s test\.A p\-value &lt;0\.05 was considered statistically significant\. Results:The mean age of the study participants was 44\.8 ± 13\.2 years, with a male predominance \(56\.7%\)\.Glioma was the most common tumor \(40\.0%\), followed by meningioma \(26\.7%\), pituitary adenoma \(16\.7%\), brain metastasis \(10\.0%\), and other tumors \(6\.6%\)\.The deep learning model correctly classified 27 of the 30 cases\.The model demonstrated a sensitivity of 93\.3%, specificity of 86\.7%, positive predictive value of 87\.5%, negative predictive value of 92\.9%, and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 90\.0%\.The area under the ROC curve was 0\.94, indicating excellent diagnostic performance\.Comparison with histopathology showed no statistically significant difference \(McNemar test, p = 0\.564\)\.The deep learning model also demonstrated slightly higher sensitivity, specificity, overall accuracy, and agreement with histopathology than conventional radiologist interpretation, although the difference was not statistically significant \(p = 0\.317\)\. Conclusion:Deep learning demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in the classification of brain tumours on MRI and showed strong agreement with histopathological diagnosis\.It performed comparably to conventional radiologist interpretation and may serve as a valuable clinical decision\-support tool for improving diagnostic accuracy, reducing observer variability, and facilitating timely treatment planning\.Larger multicentre studies with standardized imaging protocols are recommended to further validate these findings before routine clinical implementation\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI NEURO\-PHOTONIC SILICON ARCHITECTURE: EMULATING BIOLOGICAL DENDRITIC COMPUTATION VIA NON\-EQUILIBRIUM THERMODYNAMICS AND CAUSAL SPIKING NEURAL NETWORKS](../publications/f09e8158c1b178e2d218.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Neuro\-Photonic Silicon Architecture \(NPSA\) revolutionizes neuromorphic computing by emulating biological dendritic computation to overcome the Von Neumann bottleneck and extreme energy consumption of modern AI\. It integrates four core modules: silicon\-photonic memristive synapses for low\-power Spike\-Timing\-Dependent Plasticity; dendritic optical interferometers combining linear Mach\-Zehnder interferometers with non\-linear phase\-change elements for localized signal integration; Causal Spiking Neural Networks utilizing a Temporal Asymmetry Constraint to learn true cause\-and\-effect rather than statistical correlations; and non\-equilibrium thermodynamic control to minimize Joule heating\. Performance is quantified by the El\-Rakhawi Neuro\-Photonic Efficiency Metric \(ENPEM\), measuring causal information throughput per Joule\. By bridging solid\-state photonics, thermodynamics, and causal neuroscience, NPSA enables scalable, ultra\-low\-power edge AI for real\-time applications, achieving energy efficiencies orders of magnitude beyond traditional digital processors while strictly adhering to physical limits\.

## [Bilayered PEDOT:PSS–Collagen Scaffolds as Functional Architectures for Tissue Engineering](../publications/f0a380b7a310530de31f.md)

Rasha A\. Nasser; Jiranuwat Sapudom; Sotiris Psilodimitrakopoulos; Emmanuel I\. Stratakis; Jeremy C\. M\. Teo; Vincent Chan; Charalampos Pitsalidis

ABSTRACT Biomaterial‐based scaffolds that combine cell‐supportive microenvironments with complementary functional properties are important for advancing tissue‐engineering platforms\. Here, we report a bilayered scaffold that integrates a reconstituted fibrillar collagen matrix with a conductive polymer, poly\(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene\):poly\(styrenesulfonate\) \(PEDOT:PSS\), combining a biomimetic extracellular matrix with an electrically conductive 3D architecture\. The bilayer design maintains the characteristic organization and structural integrity of each phase, preserving the collagen fibrillar network, while the PEDOT:PSS compartment provides a conductive compartment compatible with electrochemical measurements\. Varying collagen concentration enables tailoring of the fibrillar density and pore architecture of the collagen compartment, with corresponding effects on swelling, mechanical behavior, and electrochemical response\. As a proof of concept, in situ electrochemical impedance measurements are used to follow time‐dependent changes during fibroblast–epithelial co‐culture\. Measured impedance progression is consistent with epithelial organization and tight‐junction formation, as visualized by immunofluorescence imaging\. This proposed bilayered scaffold provides a versatile materials strategy for integrating 3D biomimetic and conductive architectures while preserving their individual characteristics, offering opportunities for advanced 3D in vitro tissue models and organotypic interfaces\.

## [Research on the construction of an adaptive mindfulness\-based cognitive therapy system based on large language models and its efficacy in addressing college students’ anxiety](../publications/f0a6517ed10b4b429f9b.md)

Yunlong Jia

To handle the problem of resource scarcity and lack of personalization and adaptability in the traditional approach to mindfulness\-based cognitive therapy \(MBCT\) in dealing with college students with anxiety disorders, this study proposes the use of the natural language interface and adaptability properties of large language models \(LLMs\) to come up with an intelligent college\-level MBCT intervention system\. To begin with, the system functional requirements and the logic of the system intervention were explained in line with the fundamental ideas of MBCT and the cognitive features of students with anxiety\. Second, it was created through a four\-stage adaptive architecture that includes perception analysis, intervention, and feedback, providing a dynamic process for user status identification, personal generation of intervention plans, and real\-time optimization of the intervention process\. Finally, there was a randomized controlled trial whose subjects were 120 college students with anxiety who were separated into an experimental group and a control group\. The effectiveness of the intervention was assessed using tools such as the Self\-Rating Anxiety Scale \(SAS\), the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale \(MAAS\), and the Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire \(ATQ\)\. The findings indicated that the SAS score of the experimental group \(38\.26 ± 5\.12\) was significantly less than that of the control group \(45\.89 ± 6\.34\), the MAAS score \(68\.73 ± 7\.25\) was significantly higher than that of the control group \(56\.41 ± 8\.13\); and the ATQ score \(42\.15 ± 6\.08\) was significantly less than that of the control group\. The study reveals that an adaptive MBCT system using large language models may be effective in reducing anxiety symptoms among college students, improving mindfulness, and enhancing cognitive processes, offering a new, readily available strategy for addressing anxiety in college students\.

## [Advantages, Barriers, and Challenges in Implementing Music Activities Outside the Classroom](../publications/f0b7ed23f5a354b570c8.md)

Karin Leban

Raziskava proučuje stališča študentov razrednega pouka glede izvajanja glasbenih dejavnosti izven učilnice ter analizira razlike med letnikoma študija in univerzama\. V raziskavi je sodelovalo 106 študentov 4\. letnika dodiplomskega in 1\. letnika magistrskega študija razrednega pouka Univerze v Mariboru in Univerze v Ljubljani\. Uporabljen je bil deskriptivni neeksperimentalni pristop, podatke pa smo zbrali z avtorskim strukturiranim spletnim anketnim vprašalnikom in jih obdelali z Mann\-Whitneyjevim U\-preizkusom in hi\-kvadrat preizkusom\. Namen raziskave je bil ugotoviti, kako usposobljene se bodoči učitelji počutijo za načrtovanje in izvedbo glasbenih dejavnosti na prostem, kako verjetno je, da bodo take dejavnosti izvajali v prihodnji pedagoški praksi, kako presojajo primernost posameznih glasbenih dejavnosti za izvedbo na prostem ter katere prednosti, ovire in oblike podpore pri tem prepoznavajo\. Rezultati kažejo, da študenti prednosti glasbenih dejavnosti na prostem ocenjujejo visoko, pri čemer naravno okolje prepoznavajo kot prostor bogatih senzoričnih, gibalnih in ustvarjalnih spodbud\. Med letnikoma ni bilo ugotovljenih statistično značilnih razlik v občutku usposobljenosti\. Na podlagi teh podatkov ni mogoče neposredno sklepati o razlogih za odsotnost razlik\. Študenti 1\. letnika magistrskega študija ter študenti Univerze v Mariboru so prednosti in ovire ocenili statistično značilno višje\. Raziskava razlogov za te razlike ni neposredno preverjala\. Primernost glasbenih dejavnosti za izvedbo na prostem študenti obeh univerz in obeh letnikov presojajo podobno\. Kot oblike podpore, ki bi jih pri izvedbi najbolj potrebovali, študenti najpogosteje navajajo podporo vodstva šole in časovni okvir v urniku, pripravljene učne ure ter prenosno opremo\. Iz teh odgovorov izhaja, da so ključni izzivi pri uvajanju takega pouka pretežno organizacijsko\-logistični in kompetenčni\. Na podlagi ugotovitev raziskava izpostavlja potrebo po večji integraciji glasbenih dejavnosti izven učilnice v študijske programe ter po sistematičnem razvoju kompetenc za njihovo izvedbo\.

## [Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?](../publications/f0c03d6ad84bc2453229.md)

Trizal Garg; Sibayan Mitra; Arya Karanjkar; Advait Singh; Jagat Sesh Challa; Yash Sinha; Siddharth Mehrotra; Dhruv Kumar; Pratham Yogish Maliya

Large language models \(LLMs\) can often tell when they are being tested\. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use\. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages\. Indic languages are spoken by over a billion people, yet evaluation awareness remains almost entirely unstudied in them\. We test four instruction\-tuned models from three families in five Indic languages alongside English\. A set of cues varies whether the model is told that it is monitored and whether the monitoring is a safety test\. Models refuse harmful requests more often when they are told that they are being tested\. This increase appears in all four models and all six languages\. In Indic languages, refusal of harmful requests rises by 14\.4 percentage points on average\. The test cue also brings Indic refusal of harmful requests level with English, but raises refusal of benign Indic requests from 6\.9% to 11\.3%\. We release all 47,880 judged responses to support further work\. These results suggest that safety evaluations in Indic languages may not reflect how models treat their everyday users\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Publishing: A Tool to Be Governed, Not a Substitute for Scientific Judgment](../publications/f0c154e6d0f92e716d2f.md)

Claudio Colosio

Technological innovation has rarely entered human society without resistance\.Some of the concerns that accompanied technologies now regarded as indispensable may appear almost incomprehensible today, although they were taken very seriously at the time\.The Industrial Revolution provides perhaps the best\-known example\.In early nineteenth\-century England, the Luddites destroyed textile machinery that they perceived as threatening their jobs, skills, and livelihoods\.Their reaction was not simply an irrational fear of machines: it also reflected legitimate concerns about profound changes in working conditions and the distribution of the benefits of technological progress\.Nevertheless, mechanization continued and eventually transformed manufacturing and society\.Other innovations followed similar paths\.Railways were initially regarded by some as potentially dangerous to human health\.The automobile encountered resistance and restrictive legislation: the British Locomotive Act of 1865 famously required, under certain circumstances, a person carrying a red flag to precede a self\-propelled vehicle\.Electricity, elevators, vaccination and, much more recently, the Internet all encountered scepticism, resistance or fear before becoming part of everyday life\.History does not teach us that every technological innovation is necessarily beneficial\.There have been technologies whose harmful consequences became apparent only after widespread adoption\.Nor should legitimate concerns about technological change be dismissed as another form of Luddism\.History does, however, suggest that genuinely useful technologies tend eventually to become incorporated into ordinary life and professional practice\.Artificial intelligence \(AI\), and particularly generative AI based on large language models \(LLMs\), appears likely to follow this pattern\.The scientific community is now debating whether and how AI should be used in research, scientific writing, peer review and editorial decision\-making\.Positions range from enthusiasm to considerable concern\.Both attitudes are understandable\.AI systems can perform tasks that only a few years ago would have seemed extraordinary\.At the same time, their limitations\-including inaccurate information, fabricated references, bias, lack of transparency and the generation of extremely convincing but incorrect statements\-are equally real \[1\]\[2\]\[3\]\[4\]\.The question, therefore, should probably no longer be whether scientists will use AI\.They already do, and its use will almost certainly increase\.A more useful question is: what should we allow AI to do for us, and what must we never delegate to it? Assistance and Delegation Are Not the Same ThingThis distinction, in our view, is fundamental\.AI can be an extraordinarily useful scientific assistant\.Consider the preparation of a manuscript\.AI can identify grammatical and spelling errors, improve the readability of English, suggest more concise formulations, identify repetitions, detect inconsistencies between different sections of a manuscript and help organize complex material\.It can assist in searching the literature and in identifying potentially relevant references, provided that these references are subsequently checked against the original sources\.

## [SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill\-Using Agents](../publications/f0d9da66109a87b52d7c.md)

Jin Ye; Yifan Jiang; Lan\-zhe Guo

Large language model agents increasingly rely on skills to extend their capabilities in complex tasks\. However, scalable skill use requires Selective Skill Exposure \(SSE\): providing relevant procedural content when needed while avoiding unnecessary exposure that may disrupt reasoning\. Existing paradigms fall short in complementary ways\. Progressive disclosure exposes metadata for a growing skill library, introducing context pollution; retrieval limits catalog exposure, but static retrieval from the initial task query may be misaligned with capability needs that emerge during reasoning and may still inject unnecessary skills\. We propose SkillBrowser, a Meta\-Skill\-managed framework that enables an agent to identify current capability needs, formulate targeted queries, and selectively load skills on demand\. Across six SRA\-Bench subsets and five LLMs, SkillBrowser improves aggregate accuracy over static retrieval and LLM\-based selection, including multi\-step tool use, and mitigates accuracy degradation on already\-solvable instances\. Benefits remain model\- and task\-dependent, with under\-invocation of useful skills and additional latency as key limitations\. These results demonstrate the viability of Meta\-Skill\-managed SSE for scalable skill repositories\.

## [TARGETED INNOVATIONS IN PRECISION MEDICINE: ADVANCING PERSONALIZED THERAPIES FOR IMMUNE\-MEDIATED INFLAMMATORY DISEASES](../publications/f0e17d3f8531bec2f691.md)



Immune\-Mediated Inflammatory Diseases \(IMIDs\) pose a significant therapeutic challenge due to their diverse manifestations and the absence of universal treatments\.Computational molecular science has enabled the identification of immunological targets for tailored therapies\.The review focuses on IMIDs and rheumatoid disorders, showcasing progress in targeted treatments\.Key efforts target T helper 17 \(Th17\) cells, particularly interleukin 17, with therapies like secukinumab and ixekizumab demonstrating efficacy in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis\.Interleukin 12 and 23\-targeting therapies like ustekinumab show promise in diseases like psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease\.In the realm of Type I Interferons \(IFNs\), drugs such as sifalimumab and anifrolumab highlight encouraging progress in systemic lupus erythematosus treatment\.Integrin and sphingosine\-1\-phosphate receptor modulation have also shown potential in treating IMIDs\.Moving forward, advances in stromal cell targeting, epigenetic regulation, and immune pathway interventions offer promising directions for precision therapies in IMIDs\.In conclusion, the evolving landscape of IMID therapeutics holds promise for improving patient outcomes by addressing the complexities of these conditions with innovative approaches and cutting\-edge technologies\.

## [First record of Myotis auriculus Baker &amp; Stains, 1955 \(Chiroptera, Vespertilionidae\) from the State of Mexico, Mexico, with a map of potential distribution](../publications/f108849492391d94e4e5.md)

Cuauhtémoc Chávez; Erika Mendez\-Manzano; Joaquín Arroyo‐Cabrales

Myotis auriculus Baker &amp; Stains, 1955 is a poorly known bat species distributed in the south\-western United States to south\-central Mexico and Guatemala, mainly in pine and pine–oak forests\. Here, we report the first confirmed record of this species of bat from Temascaltepec, State of Mexico\. We review all previous records and generate a habitat suitability map using MaxEnt\. The model includes the predicted range to Oaxaca and Chiapas in Mexico and confirms areas of high habitat suitability in central México and Central America \(Guatemala and Honduras\)\. This discovery highlights the need for further research on poorly known species and their vulnerable ecosystems, with implications for biodiversity and conservation in the region\.

## [Diagnostic Performance of Ultrasound Elastography in Differentiating Benign and Malignant Thyroid Nodules: A Prospective Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/f11acc6301bc7c0212ed.md)

Kharananda Sharma; Dahal Dahal

Background: Thyroid nodules are among the most common endocrine abnormalities encountered in clinical practice\. Although most thyroid nodules are benign, accurate identification of malignant lesions remains crucial for appropriate management\. Conventional ultrasonography is the primary imaging modality for thyroid nodule evaluation; however, overlap in imaging characteristics often limits diagnostic specificity\. Ultrasound elastography has emerged as a valuable adjunctive technique that assesses tissue stiffness, potentially improving differentiation between benign and malignant thyroid nodules\. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound elastography in differentiating benign and malignant thyroid nodules using cytopathology and histopathology as reference standards\. Methods: A prospective cross\-sectional study was conducted involving 180 consecutive patients presenting with thyroid nodules\. All participants underwent conventional ultrasound and strain elastography\. Elastography scores were assigned using a five\-point elasticity scoring system\. Fine needle aspiration cytology \(FNAC\) and surgical histopathology were used as reference standards\. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value \(PPV\), negative predictive value \(NPV\), diagnostic accuracy, and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis were performed\. Results: Among 180 thyroid nodules evaluated, 48 \(26\.7%\) were malignant and 132 \(73\.3%\) were benign\. Elastography scores 4–5 were significantly associated with malignancy \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. Ultrasound elastography demonstrated a sensitivity of 89\.6%, specificity of 84\.8%, PPV of 68\.3%, NPV of 95\.7%, and overall diagnostic accuracy of 86\.1%\. ROC analysis yielded an area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.91 \(95% CI: 0\.86–0\.96\), indicating excellent discriminatory performance\. Conclusion: Ultrasound elastography significantly improves differentiation between benign and malignant thyroid nodules and may reduce unnecessary invasive procedures\. Incorporation of elastography into routine thyroid imaging protocols can enhance diagnostic confidence and optimise patient management\.

## [Ayurvedic Management of Chronic Hepatitis B: A Case Report](../publications/f1239b16cc24142a9ecc.md)

K Sruthi; Mridul Ranjan; Dr\. Shalini

Background: Chronic hepatitis B is a viral infection associated with serious complications, including liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, highlighting the need for effective management strategies\. Case Presentation: A 31\-year\-old male with a one\-year history of hepatitis B surface antigen \(HBsAg\) positivity presented with intermittent anorexia and no other significant symptoms\. The patient was monitored over a period of 16 months\. Intervention: The patient was managed with an Ayurvedic treatment regimen aimed at supporting liver health\. The interventions included Phalatrikādi Kvātha, A combination of Tamālakī, Bhṛṅgarāja, Madhuka, and Trikaṭu Cūrṇa, Mustā Ghana Vaṭī, Bhūmyāmalakī Svarasa, Bhṛṅgarāja Cūrṇa, and Āmalakī Rasāyana\. Liver function tests \(LFTs\) and HBV DNA quantitative polymerase chain reaction \(PCR\) were used to assess the response to treatment\. Outcome: HBV DNA levels decreased from 6318 IU/mL in June 2023 to &lt;150 IU/mL by May 2024, indicating suppression of detectable viral DNA during the monitoring period\. The patient&\#x27;s anorexia was relieved during the course of management\. No adverse effects were reported during the treatment period\. Conclusion: This case describes observed improvement in laboratory parameters during Ayurvedic management of chronic hepatitis B\. However, findings from a single case cannot establish treatment efficacy or causality, and controlled clinical studies are required to determine the therapeutic efficacy and clinical relevance of Ayurvedic interventions in chronic hepatitis B\. Keywords: Chronic hepatitis B, Case report, Ayurvedic herbal treatment, HBV DNA PCR

## [Kluge Corrêa, Nicholas Kluge &amp; Mönig, Julia: Catalog of Field\-Specific Ethical Requirements for AI Certification](../publications/f12b9b1c70331092377d.md)

The project seeks to develop certification methods for trustworthy artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. While in our Use Cases Catalog we documented 18 potential fields of application for AI systems, in our Catalog of General Ethical Requirements for AI Certification, we sought to propose general principles, evaluation criteria, normative recommendations, and practical implementations that can help developers and other types of stakeholders in making trustworthy AI development a pragmatic endeavor\. ## [TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time\-Constrained Federated Learning](../publications/f12e249938c6decea8b7.md)

Honoka Anada; Yafei Ou; Shinya Takamaeda\-Yamazaki

Minimizing the wall\-clock time required to reach a target accuracy is crucial in federated learning \(FL\), where many applications require frequent model updates as data distributions evolve over time\. Nevertheless, in heterogeneous environments, slow clients with limited computational and communication capabilities can delay global synchronization, forcing faster clients to wait and increasing the overall training time\. To mitigate this straggler effect, recent studies have introduced per\-round time constraints and adapted client workloads within the available time\. However, these approaches primarily focus on local computation, whereas communication can become a major bottleneck in communication\-limited environments, motivating the joint optimization of training workload and communication compression\. Although previous studies have explored such joint optimization, determining an effective training\-\-communication balance under a fixed per\-round time budget remains challenging, as the resulting model performance depends on both training progress and compression\-induced degradation\. We therefore propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes the local training workload and communication compression under per\-round time constraints\. TALLOP predicts the training loss achievable under different computation budgets from the early\-stage mini\-batch loss trajectory \(LENS\), and estimates the degradation caused by communication compression using a compression\-error model \(CLEN\)\. TALLOP combines these predictions to select the training\-communication allocation that minimizes the post\-compression loss under the given round time constraint\. Experiments in heterogeneous FL environments show that TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time\-to\-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, although the benefit over training\-only adaptation depends on the setting\.

## [Bridging the Language Gap in Scholarly Data II: Enhancing Gender Inference for Chinese Names](../publications/f13a97ad9da1617036d0.md)

Lisette Espín\-Noboa; Mingrong She; Ana Maria Jaramillo; Liuhuaying Yang

Perceived gender inference from names is important for inclusive scientometrics research, yet existing methods perform poorly on non\-Western scholars\. We address this gap for Chinese names, which appear in two forms, Hanzi and Pinyin, its Romanized form \(e\.g\., Zhang Wei, Li Na\)\. In international bibliographic records, names are often available only in Pinyin\. However, a single pinyin name can correspond to multiple distinct hanzi characters with different gender associations, so gender inference from Pinyin alone is intrinsically ambiguous\. To address this, we first develop two hanzi models, a regression model that produces a continuous gender score from 0 \(male\) to 1 \(female\), and a classification model that outputs one of three labels \(\\em\{male\}, \\em\{neutral\}, \\em\{female\}\)\. We train them on a sample of hanzi names from Chinese\-language physics publications, rated by 11 native Chinese speakers\. On this sample, the models achieve an RMSE of $0\.09$ and an R$^2$ of $0\.85$ \(regression\), and macro\-AUC of $0\.97$ and a Cohen&\#x27;s $κ$ of $0\.81$ \(classification\), demonstrating high performance that is robust to class imbalance\. For pinyin names, we propose a pipeline that aggregates hanzi predictions via transliteration and frequency weighting, together with an ambiguity score that flags names whose gender cannot be resolved from Pinyin alone\. Benchmarked against three off\-the\-shelf tools \(Namsor, GPT, and Claude\), our models achieve the highest agreement with human annotations for both gender scores and gender labels, in both scripts\. Applied to an independent sample of Chinese\-named authors in APS journals, our models assign a gender to every name, whereas existing Pinyin\-based methods leave between 20\\% and 100\\% of names unclassified\. These findings demonstrate the importance of hanzi\-level information for reliable gender inference of Chinese names\. Code and data are publicly available\.

## [A neural operator framework for data\-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems](../publications/f13f2e16e4540ce6a9d4.md)

Chengyun Wang; Liwei Chen; Nils Thuerey

Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering\. Traditional stability and receptivity \(resolvent\) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems\. Here, we introduce a data\-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations\. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data\. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high\-dimensional fluid flows and a real\-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input\-output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes\. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve\. This equation\-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high\-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering\.

## [When Plans Change, Remember: Replanning\-Guided Visual Memory for Vision\-Language\-Action Models](../publications/f143ee3184ddf50cd9e2.md)

Victoria Smelova; Daniil Kazachkov; Georgiy Kazantsev; Iuliia Tsvetkova; Egor Cherepanov; Nikita Kachaev; Artem Latyshev; Aleksandr I\. Panov; Alexey K\. Kovalev

Long\-horizon, multi\-stage Vision\-Language\-Action \(VLA\) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation\. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory\. We introduce RePlanMem\-VLA \(Replanning\-Guided Keyframe Memory for VLA\), which turns a policy&\#x27;s own plan revisions into an online memory\-write signal\. Under receding\-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions\. RePlanMem\-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task\-relevant event\. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single\-task autoregressive decoder\-only and Flow\-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA\-OFT and $π\_\{0\.5\}$ policies over MIKASA\-Robo\-VLA tasks\. The resulting detectors achieve ROC\-AUC of 0\.981\-0\.997\. We then use the selected signals in RePlanMem\-VLA to trigger updates to a bounded visual memory, with a robot\-masked write filter suppressing redundant frames\. In the evaluated memory\-retention experiments, RePlanMem\-VLA preserves task\-relevant observations until the later decision point in 100% of episodes\. Real\-robot replay data further show that event selection and redundancy suppression extend beyond simulation\. These results establish plan revision as a policy\-internal signal for controlling what a VLA remembers\. Website: https://vika787\.github\.io/RePlanMem/\.

## [Integrated assessment of soil salinity dynamics on the dried Aral Seabed based on field observations, geochemical analysis, remote sensing, and machine learning](../publications/f149aa5f0f899339c780.md)

Gulnura Issanova; Nazgul Ospan; Azamat Kaldybayev; Kuralay Tynybayeva

Soil salinization is a major driver of land degradation in arid environments, particularly in desiccated inland basins such as the Aral Sea region\. This study provides an integrated assessment of soil salinity dynamics on the dried Aral Seabed \(Aralkum Desert, Kazakhstan\) by combining field\-based geochemical analysis, remote sensing, and machine learning\. Field investigations conducted during 2020–2022 comprised 58 soil profiles and 204 soil samples analyzed for electrical conductivity \(EC\), total dissolved solids \(TDS\), major\-ion composition, and vertical salinity distribution across different solonchak types\. Geochemical analysis revealed pronounced spatial and genetic heterogeneity, with marine\-derived solonchaks exhibiting hypersaline conditions \(Σ &gt; 250 mmolc/100 g −1 , or 16\.1%\) dominated by Na Cl systems, whereas typical and takyr\-like solonchaks showed moderate salinity associated with capillary rise and continental processes\. Principal Component Analysis identified a dominant salinity gradient controlled by Na \+ , Cl − , and SO₄ 2− , with clear vertical differentiation\. EC and TDS showed a strong linear relationship \( r = 0\.91, p &lt; 0\.001\), supporting EC as an operational proxy for soil salinity\. Remote sensing analysis using SAVI, MSAVI, NDSI, and SI4 showed strong spatial correspondence between salinity and vegetation patterns\. Vegetation indices were negatively correlated with salinity indicators \( r = −0\.54 to −0\.72, p &lt; 0\.01\), while high NDSI and SI4 values coincided with elevated EC–TDS and low SAVI/MSAVI values\. Random Forest classification showed 75\.86% overall agreement with the 58 field\-reference observations \(Cohen&\#x27;s Kappa = 0\.691\), with classification errors concentrated mainly in intermediate salinity classes\. Soil salinity on the dried Aral Seabed represents a spatially continuous process controlled by groundwater dynamics, evaporative concentration, and inherited marine sediments\. Integrating geochemical, remote sensing and machine\-learning approaches provides an effective framework for regional assessment of salinity\-driven land degradation in arid environments\.

## [Predictive Talent Acquisition Using Ensemble Learning Models in Human Resource Management](../publications/f14e2177451596074cf9.md)

Melanie Elisabeth Lourens; Leena Sharma; Mahua Majumdar Bose; B\.Ranjitha

Predictive talent acquisition is one of the applications of machine learning which has become an area of importance within human resource management for carrying out data analysis of recruitment processes\. The purpose of this research was to compare the effectiveness of several machine learning classifiers on the prediction of recruitment decision\. For that, a dataset containing structured information about 1,500 candidates was used\. Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, and HistGradientBoosting were the five classifiers considered in the study\. These classifiers were evaluated using a stratified train/test split of 80:20\. Their performances were measured in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, area under the ROC curve \(ROC\-AUC\), area under the PR curve \(PR\-AUC\), and Brier score\. The best result was demonstrated by HistGradientBoosting classifier with accuracy 93\.67%, F1\-score 0\.8914, ROC\-AUC 0\.9313, and PR\-AUC 0\.9173\. The feature importance analysis yielded the recruitment strategy, skill score, and educational background as some important predictive factors, although it was necessary to consider the problem of target leakage in relation to the recruitment strategy\. The outcomes prove that the prediction capability is good enough for the experimental dataset but at the same time emphasize the significance of validation, correct use of features, fairness analysis, and human supervision\. Since the dataset in question is artificial, the outcomes cannot be regarded as an indication of effectiveness in the real\-world recruitment process\.

## [Roles of gut microbiota metabolites in the pathogenesis of migraine](../publications/f154761a5d0a028326be.md)

Yadi Shi; 伊凡 曹; Ziyu Zhang; Ruolin Li; Guangxi Zhou; Peng Xu

Migraine is one of the most common neurological disorders, with a complex and incompletely understood pathogenesis\. Recent studies have implicated the gut\-brain axis in migraine pathophysiology\. The gut microbiota and microbiota\-related metabolites may influence migraine\-related processes through neural, immune, endocrine, and metabolic pathways\. This review summarizes the potential roles of microbiota\-derived metabolites in migraine through the gut\-brain axis, with a focus on short\-chain fatty acids \(SCFAs\), tryptophan \(Trp\)\-related metabolites, and nitric oxide \(NO\)\-related metabolic pathways, and their potential effects on neuroimmune signaling, intestinal barrier integrity, and trigeminovascular function\. Current evidence suggests that gut dysbiosis and metabolic disturbances are associated with migraine and may modulate neuroinflammatory pathways and central sensitization; however, direct causal evidence in humans remains limited\. Interventions targeting the gut microbiota or related metabolic pathways, including probiotics and dietary modifications, may represent potential adjunctive strategies, although current clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous\.

## [ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES OF THE SHADOW CIRCULATION OF SURROGATE ALCOHOL UNDER MARTIAL LAW: FORENSIC AUDIT TOOLS AND THE RETURN ON INVESTMENT IN INNOVATION](../publications/f1613b6d689d6004065f.md)

В\.В\. Давиденко; Andriy Boyko; А\. В\. Питомець

This study examines the financial and economic consequences of the shadow market for surrogate alcohol in Ukraine under martial law\. It also considers the macroeconomic feasibility of investing in innovative forensic audit tools to prevent this phenomenon\. Martial law has exacerbated the shadow trade in excise goods significantly\. Temporary bans on the sale of legal alcohol have led to a consistent demand for illicit products\. This results in multimilion losses to the state budget due to lost excise and value\-added tax revenue\. Meanwhile, the consumption of surrogates, particularly among military personnel, leads to significant human capital losses and places a substantial financial burden on the healthcare system in terms of the costs of intensive care, antidotes and long\-term medical rehabilitation\. In this context, the study examines the economic feasibility of using high\-tech equipment for isotopic analysis to identify the sources of counterfeit products at an early stage\. The study takes a comprehensive approach, combining methods of macroeconomic analysis, health economics and criminalistic modelling\. The cost\-benefit analysis methodology was used to evaluate the financial viability of purchasing innovative analytical equipment \(GC\-IRMS\), contrasting it with the state’s current expenditure on treating intoxications and losses from the shadow economy\. The empirical basis consisted of an analysis of current Ukrainian legislation and materials from criminal proceedings under Article 204 of the Ukrainian Criminal Code, as well as European scientific studies in toxicology and economic security\. The main objective of this article is twofold: firstly, to assess the economic losses incurred by the state due to the illegal alcohol market \(in terms of budget losses and medical expenses for military personnel\); and secondly, to provide a scientific and economic justification for implementing chemical profiling methods \(such as isotope mass spectrometry\) as a cost\-effective forensic audit tool\. This demonstrates that proactively identifying the source of counterfeit alcohol is more cost\-effective than addressing the medical and demographic consequences of mass poisonings\. The study demonstrated that temporary administrative bans on the legal alcohol market \(the &\#x27;zero tolerance&\#x27; paradox\), without adequate enforcement mechanisms, stimulate a highly profitable shadow economy\. It has been established that the state’s financial expenditure on emergency medical care, intensive care unit stays and subsequent social support for military personnel poisoned by surrogates or new psychoactive substances \(NPS\) exceeds the cost of preventive measures by a factor of ten\. The existing forensic and expert control system in Ukraine has a critical methodological gap in that it is purely reactive and does not allow the source of supply \(the manufacturing plant\) to be traced\. The purchase of gas chromatography–isotope ratio mass spectrometry \(GC\-IRMS\) equipment is economically justified, offering an extremely high return on investment \(ROI\)\. Implementing this innovative forensic investigation tool will enable the identification of the geographic and botanical origin of raw materials at an early stage, eliminating industrial supply sources for the black market and recovering lost tax revenue for the budget\. Furthermore, it will prevent large\-scale losses of human capital in Ukraine’s security and defence sector\.

## [Advances, challenges, and artificial intelligence\-enabled applications of black truffles and their bioactive compounds](../publications/f169fa6ca97991ab04ab.md)

Chengbo Zhang; 王佳雯; Xia Li; 韩楠玉; Changcheng Zhu; Liping Qu; Zunxi Huang

With increasing demand for natural functional foods, identifying biological resources for improving human physiological functions has emerged as a key research priority\. Black truffles, rare edible fungi rich in bioactive compounds, have garnered preliminary interest in functional foods\. This review summarizes the distribution, classification, and symbiotic ecology of black truffles\. We also examine their functional components, including polysaccharides, l \-ergothioneine, and ergosterol, as well as their core biological activities, particularly antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory, and anti\-glycation effects\. Additionally, we explore potential applications of artificial intelligence in identifying truffle species, improving growth conditions, optimizing extraction processes, verifying bioactivity, and elucidating the biosynthesis of active components\. However, several bottlenecks remain: insufficient human consumption trials, unclear component interaction mechanisms, undefined human dose\-response relationships, and low extraction efficiency of heat\-sensitive components\. Artificial intelligence may offer pathways to address these challenges and advance functional foods featuring black truffles\. This review provides a theoretical foundation for the development and commercialization of high\-value\-added black truffle products\.

## [Students&\#x27; Perceptions on AI Utilization and Regulation: Basis for Developing Guidelines for Responsible Use in Higher Education](../publications/f17579aeab4513cd0e71.md)

Catherine May S Gerao; Christine Anne C\. Barrios; Rose Ann D\. Flores; Jeanebie C Maramba; Jamaica L\. Sukian; Rei Christine Faith L\. Liwanag; Marjorie T\. Dumayon; Hanna Alexa E\. Torino; Mary Joy Nablo

In the contemporary era, Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has become increasingly integrated into education, influencing how students learn, engage, and accomplish academic tasks\. This study examined students’ perceptions of AI along two distinct dimensions: utilization and regulation to serve as an evidence\-based basis for developing institutional guidelines\. Specifically, it addressed four areas of utilization: AI literacy, academic writing support, personalized learning, and student engagement; and two areas of regulation: awareness of AI policies, rules and regulations, and academic integrity and ethical concerns\. A descriptive research design was employed, using a survey questionnaire administered to 229 students from the Teacher Education Program at the Polytechnic College of the City of Meycauayan\. Data were collected through online and printed forms and analyzed using descriptive statistics, specifically weighted mean, to determine general trends in students’ responses\. On utilization, students generally perceived AI as a useful educational tool that enhances learning efficiency, supports academic writing tasks, and enables personalized, self\-paced learning\. They demonstrated moderate to high AI literacy, with strong awareness of potential misuse and privacy risks, though some reported difficulty learning new AI tools\. Usage varied across platforms: Canva, ChatGPT, and Grammarly were the most familiar and widely used, while other tools had limited adoption\. On regulation, students expressed strong support for institutional policies, rules, and accountability frameworks\. They showed high awareness of ethical standards, data privacy, fairness, and responsible use\. yet were less supportive of mandatory disclosure of AI assistance in academic work\. Concerns about over\-reliance, the absence of clear existing rules, and the urgent need for formal guidance were clearly evident\. The study concludes that while AI offers significant educational benefits, comprehensive institutional guidelines on AI utilization and regulation are urgently needed to ensure responsible, ethical, and equitable use\. Recommendations include integrating AI literacy training, establishing level\-based usage policies, requiring transparency in AI assistance, and upholding academic integrity through clear ethical standards\. These findings provide a data\-driven foundation for balanced institutional policies that support innovation while maintaining academic integrity and fairness\.

## [Surveillance and Identification of Rust Pathogens of Wheat Crops Grown in District Naushahro Feroze, Sindh, Pakistan](../publications/f18733377f773b3aed4e.md)

Sahib Ghanghro; Khalil Ahmed Laghari; Qurban Ali Magsi; Shoukat Ali Wassan; Naeema Khatoon Khaskheli; Gul Hassan Shaikh; Syed Fiaz Hussain; Azhar Ali Hattar; Huma Muhammad Ishaque; Mumtaz Ali Saand

Wheat is the world&\#x27;s most important staple food crop for consumption and trade\. Pakistan is among the world&\#x27;s top ten wheat\-producing countries\. Almost 90% of the wheat cultivars grown in Sindh and other provinces are susceptible to leaf and yellow rust diseases caused by Puccinia recondita and Puccinia striiformis, respectively\. This study aimed to assess the severity and occurrence of leaf and yellow rust in wheat crops cultivated in different Talukas, including Moro, Naushahro Feroze, Bhiria City, Kandiaro, and Mehrabpur, in District Naushahro Feroze, Sindh, Pakistan\. The microscopic study has confirmed that the fungal pathogens Puccinia recondita and Puccinia striiformis cause leaf and yellow rust in wheat crops\. Surveillance and assessment were conducted in the study area to analyze the occurrence and incidence of rust disease in wheat crops\. The study found that both yellow and leaf rust severely affected the wheat crop in two Talukas, i\.e\., Moro and Kandiaro\. However, disease symptoms were observed to be less severe in Taluka Bhiria City than in other Talukas\. Importantly, NIA\-Sarang and Benazir wheat varieties were resistant to leaf and yellow rust\. Moreover, the TD1 variety was the most susceptible in the Talukas of District N\. Feroze\. Furthermore, this study suggests that resistant wheat varieties be cultivated in the area and the province to avoid rust disease epidemics\. Our study can serve as a basis for the molecular characterization of wheat varieties resistant to or susceptible to leaf and yellow rust diseases, as well as the pathogen strains that cause these rust diseases\.

## [Clinical manifestations of resistance to thyroid hormone beta \(RTHβ\) syndrome in children – multicenter case series](../publications/f1aaae50e0a7ddd0d7f0.md)

Anna Fedorczak; Martyna Sokół; Iwona Beń‐Skowronek; Magdalena Mierzwa; Agnieszka Zachurzok; Agnieszka Bogusz\-Wójcik; Julia Przybylak\-Ortega; Elżbieta Moszczyńska; Paulina Berezowiec; Artur Bossowski; Natalia Dąbek; Artur Mazur; Kamil Dyrka; Marek Niedziela; Magdalena Makowiecka\-Wolek; Robert Stanisław Śmigiel; Agnieszka Ulenberg; Małgorzata Myśliwiec; Renata Stawerska

Introduction Resistance to thyroid hormone \(TH\) β \(RTHβ\) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the TH receptor β gene \( THRB \) and characterized by elevated TH levels with non\-suppressed thyroid\-stimulating hormone \(TSH\) and variable clinical presentation\. The aim of the study was to characterize the clinical and biochemical features of children with RTHβ, correlate them with genetic findings and therapeutic management, to raise clinicians’ awareness of the specific characteristics of the condition\. Material and methods This retrospective multicenter case series included 15 children with genetically confirmed THRB variants\. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were analyzed retrospectively\. Results All the patients demonstrated elevated free thyroxine and free triiodothyronine concentrations with detectable, non\-suppressed TSH serum level\. Common findings included tachycardia \(73%\), neurodevelopmental disturbances \(60%\), and a lean phenotype \(BMI &lt;10th percentile, 53%\)\. Misdiagnosis of primary hyperthyroidism occurred in 20% of cases\. Most patients did not require pharmacological treatment or were managed with beta\-blockers alone for symptomatic tachycardia control\. Discussion Pediatric RTHβ shows consistent biochemical features but marked clinical heterogeneity\. Awareness is essential to ensure accurate diagnosis and avoid unnecessary therapy\.

## [A revolução da contabilidade digital: rupturas estruturais, desafios de adaptação e a ressignificação estratégica do profissional contábil](../publications/f1b824fb1715423e5e91.md)

Karina Gomes Dias; Karla Emanuella Moraes da Silva; Zuila Paulino Cavalcante; José Carlos Alves Roberto

O avanço acelerado das tecnologias de informação, aliado às transformações regulatórias e fiscais no Brasil, impôs uma profunda e irreversível reorganização nas práticas corporativas e na gestão financeira contemporânea\. Historicamente fundamentada no manuseio de livros físicos, rotinas burocráticas manuais e arquivamento de papéis, a ciência contábil tem migrado de forma consistente para ecossistemas digitais e integrados, visando atender às exigências de velocidade, exatidão, transparência e rastreabilidade demandadas pelo mercado moderno e pela fiscalização estatal\. O problema central da pesquisa consiste em questionar: quais são os principais impactos, desafios e benefícios da transição da contabilidade tradicional para a contabilidade digital? O objetivo geral busca analisar a transição da contabilidade tradicional para a contabilidade digital, identificando os impactos da modernização, os desafios vivenciados pelos profissionais e as ferramentas aplicadas às rotinas corporativas\. Metodologicamente, trata\-se de uma pesquisa de natureza básica, com fins exploratórios e descritivos, estruturada por meio de procedimentos bibliográficos sistemáticos, combinando o suporte de livros doutrinários clássicos, normas do Conselho Federal de Contabilidade \(CFC\), pronunciamentos do Comitê de Pronunciamentos Contábeis \(CPC\), legislações vigentes e uma amostra de artigos científicos indexados no recorte temporal de 2022 a 2026\. A análise da literatura evidencia que a contabilidade digital não se limita à substituição de papéis por softwares, mas consolida a reconfiguração do perfil do contador, promovendo sua evolução de mero cumpridor de obrigações acessórias para um consultor de negócios altamente estratégico \(business partner\)\. Todavia, a plena consolidação desse paradigma exige o superamento de barreiras culturais, capacitação continuada, reformulação das matrizes curriculares de ensino, adequação ao ecossistema da inteligência artificial e investimentos robustos em cibersegurança e governança de dados em conformidade com a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados \(LGPD\)\.

## [Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene\-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications](../publications/f1ba0107eb22280468f1.md)

Lucas de S\. Silva; Guilherme Colherinhas

Abstract Graphene and graphene\-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well\-defined, high\-surface\-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research\. Understanding how molecular\-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales\. This review treats the electrode\-charging methods available─fixed and constant\-charge, constant potential, electronic\-structure\-aware variants, and applied fields─together with force\-field choice, as a toolbox of complementary tools suited to different questions, not a hierarchy of accuracy\. We use this framework to organize findings on interfacial structure, electrode curvature, defects, doping, and nanoconfinement, emphasizing how these factors affect both the electric double layer and quantum capacitance\. We conclude that progress toward predictive simulation will depend less on selecting a single optimal method than on integrating electrolyte polarizability, realistic electrode electronic response, structural complexity, and transferable machine\-learning potentials within experimentally validated frameworks\.

## [An explainable reinforcement learning framework for energy\-aware cluster head selection in smart\-city IoT wireless sensor networks](../publications/f1c29199b341bc6d2ce9.md)

Nandini C; K\. Priyadarsini

Cluster head \(CH\) selection is a decisive control mechanism for prolonging the operational lifetime of Internet\-of\-Things \(IoT\)\-enabled wireless sensor networks \(WSNs\) that underpin smart\-city sensing\. Although reinforcement learning \(RL\) has produced increasingly capable CH selectors, three weaknesses persist across the recent literature: the learned policies are opaque and therefore unsuitable for mission\-critical operations; they are validated almost exclusively under stationary traffic that does not reflect urban traffic loads; and they ignore the energy\-harvesting heterogeneity that characterises real deployments\. This study presents eXplainable Energy\-Aware Clustering Hierarchy \(XEACH\), an explainable, energy\-aware RL framework that addresses all three limitations within a single design\. We formalise CH selection as a constrained network\-lifetime maximisation problem, establish the NP\-hardness of its per\-round subproblem, and recast the sequential decision process as a Markov decision process in which each node learns a state\-conditioned value for cluster\-head service and selection is driven directly by the learned policy\. We prove the convergence of the learner under standard stochastic\-approximation conditions and bound the per\-round cluster\-head count\. To render the policy auditable, we attach a post hoc explainability module based on SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) that attributes every CH decision to its driving features\. The framework is evaluated on smart\-city scenarios of 50–300 nodes, incorporating a non\-stationary traffic model with diurnal congestion and stochastic event spikes, together with 30% energy\-harvesting nodes\. All results are averaged over multiple independent seeds and reported with standard deviations\. Against LEACH, SEP, and HEED, XEACH extends first\-node\-death by 88% over LEACH at 100 nodes and consistently outperforms all three baselines across network sizes, with the margin over LEACH widening as the network grows\. An ablation confirms that the reinforcement\-learning policy, rather than any fixed heuristic, drives these gains: replacing the learned policy with a random policy collapses lifetime by an order of magnitude\. The SHAP analysis of fidelity 0\.87 identifies residual energy and distance to the base station as the dominant, physically coherent drivers of selection\. We additionally calibrate the energy model to the measured datasheet parameters of a current LoRa transceiver to establish the real\-time feasibility of deployment\.

## [MambaSeed: A lightweight Mamba\-based hybrid vision network for tomato leaf disease recognition](../publications/f1c89de5a5ecb777e9d4.md)

XueShen Wang; Heng Zhang; Yayong Chen; Yunlong Li; YuJie Qin; Zhongyu Lv; Xiangjuan Liu

Crop diseases threaten agricultural productivity, creating a need for recognition models that combine accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency\. Existing CNN\-, Transformer\-, and state\-space\-based approaches can weaken fine\-grained lesion edges and textures when emphasizing global context\. We therefore propose MambaSeed, a lightweight hybrid network built on MambaVisionMixer and equipped with the Local Continuous Branch Injection mechanism, hereafter LCBI\. This mechanism repeatedly introduces local feature compensation during hierarchical modeling, preserving high\-frequency cues while maintaining global dependency modeling\. On the Tomato, Corn, and Potato datasets, MambaSeed achieved accuracies of 98\.97%, 98\.06%, and 95\.87%, respectively, with 1\.13M parameters and 0\.240G MACs\. In the batch\-one FP32 GPU benchmark, its latency was 3\.39 ms/image on an NVIDIA RTX 4090\. Without a hardware accelerator, the median CPU latency was 25\.35 ms/image with one thread and 15\.61 ms/image with four threads\. Ablation, cross\-architecture frequency analysis, and controlled perturbation tests further showed that LCBI strengthens high\-frequency feature retention and maintains stable recognition under visual degradation\. Together, these results show that MambaSeed provides a compact balance of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness across both accelerator\-based and CPU\-only inference settings\.

## [A Cross\-Layer Link Capacity and Energy\-Aware Multipath Routing Framework with Dynamic Load Balancing for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks](../publications/f1d707122f76ce817bd3.md)

Akansha Sharma; Jayanti Mehra Jharia; Sonal Sharma; Swagatika Lenka

Mobile Ad Hoc Networks \(MANETs\) are characterized by dynamic topology changes, limited bandwidth, and constrained battery resources, making efficient routing a challenging task\. Frequent link failures, congestion, and uneven traffic distribution often degrade network performance and reduce network lifetime\. Although multipath routing protocols improve reliability by maintaining multiple routes between source and destination nodes, many existing approaches do not simultaneously consider link capacity, node energy, and traffic load during route selection\. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Energy\-Aware Multipath Routing with Dynamic Load Balancing \(EMRD\-LB\) framework for MANETs\. The proposed approach integrates cross\-layer information, including link capacity, residual energy, queue utilization, and path stability, to identify efficient and reliable communication paths\. During route discovery, multiple candidate routes are evaluated using a multi\-objective path selection mechanism that considers bottleneck link capacity, energy drain rate, load variance, and route stability\. Furthermore, an adaptive load\-balancing strategy dynamically distributes traffic across selected paths according to real\-time network conditions, thereby reducing congestion and improving resource utilization\. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated through NS\-2 simulations under varying network densities and compared with QMR, MMEE, and AOMDV routing protocols\. Simulation results demonstrate that EMRD\-LB achieves a higher packet delivery ratio, lower routing overhead, reduced packet drops, and better residual energy preservation while maintaining competitive end\-to\-end delay\. By efficiently utilizing available network resources and balancing traffic loads, the proposed framework enhances communication reliability, energy efficiency, and overall network lifetime in dynamic MANET environments\.

## [Hyoscine N\-butylbromide administration before colostrum feeding improves passive transfer in dairy calves](../publications/f1de9cd82885e117fd3c.md)

Durmuş Fatih BAŞER; Abdurrahman Kürşat ÖZSOY

This study evaluated whether hyoscine N\-butylbromide administration before colostrum feeding could influence colostral immunoglobulin G \(IgG\) absorption and passive transfer in neonatal Jersey calves\. Eighteen clinically healthy calves were allocated to a control group \( n = 6\) or a hyoscine N\-butylbromide\-treated group \( n = 12\)\. Treated calves received hyoscine N\-butylbromide at 0\.4 mg/kg intramuscularly 15–30 min before the first colostrum feeding\. All calves received high\-quality maternal colostrum \(Brix ≥25%\) within 6 h after birth\. Serum Brix was measured at 48 h, and the same serum samples were analyzed for IgG, total protein, gamma\-glutamyl transferase \(GGT\), and glucose\. Treated calves had higher serum Brix than controls at 48 h \(10\.96 ± 0\.81 vs\. 9\.53 ± 0\.7%; p = 0\.002\)\. Serum IgG was also higher in treated calves at 48 h \(3,243 ± 794 vs\. 2,175 ± 1,150 mg/dL; p = 0\.034\), whereas total protein, GGT, and glucose did not differ between groups \( p ≥ 0\.217\)\. These preliminary findings suggest that hyoscine N\-butylbromide administration before colostrum feeding may be associated with improved passive transfer indicators in neonatal calves; however, confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies is required\.

## [Renewable Energy\-Based Smart Waste Management System for a Circular Economy](../publications/f1e313d775b3432b72c8.md)

Abubakar O\. Jimoh; Omolola A\. Ogbolumani

The urbanization of cities and the growing population have led to an increase in municipal solid waste generation, which has become an environmental and public health issue in urban areas\. Traditional waste collection systems are characterized by overflowing garbage bins, unnecessary pickup operations, high cost of operation, and associated environmental impact\. This paper presents the design and development of the Solar\-Powered Smart Waste Management System \(SWMS\), which uses renewable energy and IoT technology to monitor and manage waste\. SWMS consists of a smart waste bin that is managed by the ARDUINO UNO microcontroller and ultrasonic, temperature, humidity, and load cell sensors that monitor waste level, environment, and weight of the waste\. Communication is established by the GSM and GPS modules, and a solar panel along with a rechargeable battery serves as a power source for SWMS\. The ultrasonic sensor was able to detect the changes in the level of waste, the load cell sensor detected the changes in the weight of the waste, and the temperature and humidity sensors gave environmental readings\. The GSM module was able to send notifications, whereas the solar panel was able to charge the battery, and the charged battery supplied power to the prototype\. Simulation was also performed on the system using Proteus software to validate the operation of the electronic control and monitoring process\. It should be noted that Proteus was not able to simulate the operation of the solar panel, battery management system \(BMS\), buck converter, and the entire battery subsystem\. Thus, the results of the study prove the operation of the prototype, but not the full quantification of the accuracy of sensors or renewable energy\.

Background: Stillness feels impossible for some inside an MRI tube \-movement spoils roughly every fifth scan, grown\-ups just as much as children\.Machines have gotten sharper over time, yet holding position remains a struggle; appointments stretch longer, costs climb, images blur without warning\.Problems come from many directions, not just the person shifting\.From 2021 through 2026, studies looked at fixes involving technology tweaks alongside ways to guide patients better\.Each year brought small clues on how to reduce blurriness when someone moves too soon\.Cerebrovascular accident, commonly known as stroke, is a leading cause of mortality and long\-term disability worldwide\.Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\) is a cornerstone in the diagnosis and management of acute and chronic stroke because of its superior sensitivity in detecting ischemic lesions, hemorrhage, and vascular abnormalities\.However, motion\-induced artifacts remain a significant challenge during MRI examinations, particularly in patients with CVA who often present with neurological deficits, impaired consciousness, agitation, aphasia, involuntary movements, pain, anxiety, or cognitive dysfunction\.Methods: Looking through PubMed, plus EMBASE, along with IEEE Xplore formed the start \-adding in unreported studies from company documents and trial logs\.Terms like &\#x27;MRI motion artifact&\#x27; mixed with &\#x27;deeplearning reconstruction,&\#x27; then tied to &\#x27;radial k\-space,&\#x27; helped narrow things down\.&\#x27;Scanner anxiety,&\#x27; paired also with &\#x27;claustrophobia,&\#x27; showed up often, just like &\#x27;paediatric MRI sedation\.&\#x27;Work from January 2021 into early 2026 got more attention than older reports\.Numbers on repeat scans came out next, followed by how long exams took, alongside ratings of nervousness\.These pieces grouped together based on shared patterns noticed during sorting\.Results: From breathing to heartbeats, body movements stir image blurring\.Anxiety or discomfort inside the scanner plays a role too\.Instead of straight paths, spinning patterns in data capture handle small shifts better midexam\.Systems like GE&\#x27;s AIR Recon DL and Philips&\#x27; Smart Speed reshape images using smart algorithms\.These tools shorten scans by more than a third\.Less time means fewer chances for motion to mess things up\.When parents stay close or kids practice in pretend scanners beforehand, mistakes drop sharply\.In children especially, this cuts retakes nearly one\-third\.Yet what radiology teams believe often misses current findings on how families actually cope\.Gaps linger where science meets daily clinic habits\.Conclusion: Getting kids to stay still during scans means mixing fast tech with human care\.New imaging cuts wait time, so there&\#x27;s less chance to fidget\.Calm coaching before entry helps too, along with having someone familiar nearby\.One method on its own won&\#x27;t fix everything\.Units using speed upgrades and emotional support together see fewer blurry pictures the first time around\.Success sticks when timing and trust run side by side\.This review synthesizes current evidence on the causes of motion\-induced repeat MRI sequences in patients with cerebrovascular accident, examines their clinical and operational consequences, and highlights evidence\-based nursing interventions alongside multimodal technological approaches to improve imaging quality\.

## [Seasonal flood inundation area and repetitive flood exposure shape the fundamental patterns of flood exposure in China from 2000 to 2020](../publications/f21aa0bb2ed1cd5ef9f5.md)

Hanru Shen; Chengjie Zhou; Peng Su; Zhenfei Cui; Kai Tao; Wei Xu; Shiqiang Du

Remote sensing of floods and associated exposure is essential for understanding and managing flood risks, yet exposure differences among floods with varying frequencies remain underexplored\. Using MODIS time\-series data, this study mapped infrequent flood inundation area \(IFIA\) and seasonal flood inundation area \(SFIA\) across China during 2000–2020\. Differences in flood extent and built\-up land exposure were assessed using the Mann–Kendall test, improved Theil–Sen algorithm, and one\-way analysis of variance\. Cumulative flood inundation area reached 3\.52 × 10⁶ km², with SFIA accounting for 40%\. SFIA increased significantly \(0\.88%·a⁻¹\), whereas IFIA declined markedly \(−1\.32%·a⁻¹\)\. Built\-up land exposure to SFIA reached 9\.79 × 10⁵ km², representing 62% of total exposure, and increased faster \(3\.26%·a⁻¹\) than exposure to IFIA \(2\.38%·a⁻¹\)\. Among built\-up lands affected by SFIA, 91% experienced repetitive flooding, contributing 99% of cumulative exposure\. These findings demonstrate that seasonal and repetitive flooding shape the fundamental patterns of China’s flood exposure over the past two decades, providing insights into flood spatiotemporal dynamics and supporting risk\-informed land\-use planning\.

## [The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Spatio\-Temporal Analysis of Rural Transformation](../publications/f21c90bc348326311f1f.md)

Pushpendra Kumar Ahirwar; Dr\. S\. S\. Baghel

ABSTRACT Rural transformation \- the multidimensional transition of demographic, economic, social, spatial, technological, environmental and institutional conditions in rural areas has traditionally been studied through periodic surveys, census decadal enumeration and retrospective mapping\. This paper investigates whether artificial intelligence \(AI\) can fundamentally transform this analytical paradigm from retrospective description toward continuous, predictive and anticipatory spatio\-temporal intelligence\. Through a critical synthesis of the emerging GeoAI literature, analysis of primary Indian and international datasets, and development of an original conceptual framework\-the AI\-Enabled SpatioTemporal Rural Transformation Framework \(AI\-STRF\) this paper argues that AI is not merely improving existing rural research techniques but may be creating a new paradigm of rural geographical analysis\. The paper examines AI applications across demographic, agricultural, infrastructural, environmental and socioeconomic dimensions of rural change, identifies critical research gaps, and constructs evidence\-based 2030\-2050 future scenarios\. It concludes that while AI offers transformative potential for predictive rural geography, realisation of this potential depends critically on addressing data inequality, algorithmic bias, institutional capacity, and the fundamental distinction between prediction and causal explanation\. The future of rural geography, this paper contends, lies not in replacing human geographical expertise but in augmenting it through intelligent, ethically governed spatio\-temporal analysis\.

## [Relationships between serum angiogenesis markers and sarcopenia: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/f23035c5e3236d11e242.md)

Hui Li; Huaqin Liu; Yanjuan Liu; Wentao Shi; Lingwei Shi; Feng Jia

Background This study investigates the associations between serum angiogenesis markers \(VEGF, ANGPT1, and ANGPT2\) and sarcopenia in older adults\. Methods This cross\-sectional study included 471 older individuals admitted to Nanyang Central Hospital from May 2019 to May 2024\. Sarcopenia was diagnosed using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia \(AWGS\) criteria, based on hand grip strength \(HGS\) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass \(ASM\)\. Serum levels of VEGF, ANGPT1, and ANGPT2 were measured, and statistical analyses included ROC curve analyses and logistic regression models to assess the relationships between angiogenesis markers and sarcopenia traits\. Results A total of 68 participants \(14\.44%\) were diagnosed with sarcopenia\. Significant decreases in VEGF and ANGPT1 levels were observed in the sarcopenia group compared to the normal cohort\. Linear regression models showed that VEGF was positively correlated with HGS and ASM, while ANGPT1 was positively correlated with ASM\. ROC curves indicated modest discriminatory ability for sarcopenia for both VEGF and ANGPT1\. Logistic regression analysis revealed that low VEGF levels were associated with a higher risk of low HGS, low ASM, and sarcopenia, while low ANGPT1 levels were associated with increased risk of low ASM and sarcopenia \(OR = 3\.645, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions VEGF and ANGPT1 are significantly associated with sarcopenia and may provide incremental value to standard clinical assessments\. Further longitudinal studies are needed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms linking angiogenesis markers to sarcopenia\.
