## [Prospective Worst\-Attack Reliability Floors for Flow\-Based Machine\-Learning Intrusion Detection under Forward\-Time Shift](../publications/f24bb1dd6d75589244b4.md)

S\. M\. Bahauddin Bakhtiar

Flow\-based machine\-learning intrusion detectors are commonly assessed using aggregate scores, which can conceal weak attack\-family recall\. This study tests a source\-calibrated minimum\-recall floor on a short forward\-time UNSW\-NB15 capture as a proof of methodology\. Four raw files were deduplicated to 2,059,414 flows and divided into group\-disjoint source partitions and a later same\-environment test\. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost five\-seed ensembles were screened using source data only\. The contribution integrates family\-recall calibration, simultaneous lower confidence bounds, frozen retention criteria, and cryptographic prediction sealing before future\-label evaluation\. On 1,034,783 future primary flows, the locked XGBoost ensemble achieved 95\.9% accuracy, 68\.1% balanced accuracy, a Macro F1 of 0\.599, and an MCC of 0\.773\. Its minimum simultaneous recall bound was 13\.3%, narrowly exceeding the frozen 12\.6% floor, while worst\-family point recall was 22\.0%\. Analysis, Backdoor, and Reconnaissance did not retain their family\-specific bounds\. Post\-review checks preserved global retention at 5,000 and 10,000 bootstrap replicates, but alternative temporal\-block groupings did not consistently yield a future bound above the original floor\. Feature diagnostics showed both missingness and observed\-value changes without establishing causality\. XGBoost remained best among the three fixed configurations\. Global floor retention therefore supports a limited protocol\-conditional finding; it does not establish acceptable detection performance, uniform family stability, or contemporary deployment readiness\.

## [The Resilience Responsibility Gap: how institutions distribute the burden of adaptation under AI\-driven structural disruption](../publications/f24d086d235ed4c0f22b.md)

Bora BAŞARAN

Introduction AI\-drivenworkforce disruption is structural rather than episodic and is reshaping skills, tasks, job roles, career prospects and job stability\. Resilience research has traditionally focused on individuals, yet adaptation is required at the individual, organizational, institutional and societal levels\. This study examines who is held responsible for adaptation in institutional documents and whether the demands placed on workers are matched by accessible resources\. Methods A structured, codebook\-based comparative document analysis was conducted on 18 publications from the OECD \( n = 9\), Eurofound \( n = 5\), EU\-OSHA \( n = 2\), the European Commission’s Joint Research Center \( n = 1\) and the International Labor Organization \( n = 1\)\. Published between 2021 and 2026, the documents were selected purposively, and the corpus is dominated by OECD and EU institutions\. They were coded with a 28\-field codebook, supported by a page\-level audit trail, in two separate coding passes conducted by the author\. Results In this corpus, no document assigned workers primary responsibility for adaptation, and individual responsibility was never coded as central; both passes classified all 18 documents as non\-individual\-dominant\. The distribution across the four balance categories is reported in the Results and should be interpreted cautiously, since the passes agreed on the exact category in 10 of 18 documents\. A Resilience Responsibility Gap, defined as a mismatch between adaptation demands, resources and responsibility, was clear in seven documents, possible or limited in eight and absent in three\. Five inductively identified subtypes concern access to skills, worker participation, psychosocial prevention, social protection and organizational capacity\. Psychological Capital did not appear as an explicit construct in any document, although related resources such as self\-efficacy, adaptability, coping and trust did\. Discussion Psychological capital was not measured here, so its structural conditioning is advanced as a theoretical proposition rather than a demonstrated finding: the association between psychological capital and sustainable adaptation is expected to be moderated by the organizational and institutional resource configuration, a proposition for future testing\. Workforce resilience is accordingly conceptualized as distributed adaptive capacity, arising from the alignment between adaptation demands and the individual, organizational and institutional resources available to meet them\.

## [Investigar a inteligência artificial generativa na construção do conhecimento socioambiental: desafios metodológicos e éticos](../publications/f25664dd368cbcf169f7.md)

Carolina Sabugueiro Suzano

The growing presence of generative artificial intelligence in the production, organisation and interpretation of information raises methodological and ethical challenges for research in the Social and Health Sciences, particularly when dealing with complex socio\-environmental problems marked by uncertainty, value conflicts, territorial inequalities and impacts on health, the environment and citizen participation\. This article discusses how generative artificial intelligence participates in the construction of socio\-environmental knowledge, identifying its contributions, limitations and risks\. Through a critical theoretical\-methodological essay supported by a narrative and non\-systematic review of the literature, it brings together work on language models, science and technology studies, situated knowledge, environmental justice and citizenship, critical discourse analysis and artificial intelligence ethics\. Drawing on recent uses of the notion of epistemic compression, the article extends it to the socio\-environmental domain through four mechanisms: linearisation, pacification of conflict, decontextualisation and individualisation of responsibility\. It argues that, by transforming uncertain, situated and politically contested problems into fluent, ordered and apparently neutral responses, these systems make information more accessible but may reduce context, plurality of knowledge, controversy and collective responsibility\. It concludes that their use in research requires human oversight, critical validation, transparency and methodological reflexivity, as well as systematic attention to the frames, omissions and shifts in responsibility they produce\.

## [Still a filtering failure? A follow\-up commentary on automated MeSH indexing](../publications/f25d2b3b68161ec243fa.md)

Nicole Askin; Tyler Ostapyk; Carla Epp

We previously found that automated indexing in PubMed and Medline increased the risk of inappropriately excluding human studies when using the human studies filter from the Cochrane Highly Sensitive Search Strategy \(HSSS\)\. Following the National Library of Medicine&\#x27;s transition from the Medical Text Indexer\-Auto \(MTIA\) to the Medical Text Indexer\-Next Generation \(MTIX\) in 2024, we wanted to assess whether that was still the case\. Using the same approach as our previous study, we reviewed a set of MTIX\-indexed records that were excluded by the HSSS\. Only 1\.1% turned out to be human studies that were inappropriately excluded \- a major improvement over not only MTIA but also human indexers in our previous comparison\. However, problems remain with automated indexing and search filters\. This commentary outlines our findings and our ongoing concerns\.

## [DIGITAL ELECTORAL RECAPITULATION SYSTEMS AND GOVERNANCE MODELS: COMPARATIVE INTERNATIONAL EVIDENCE](../publications/f26eec55933f3db5139a.md)

Timbul Dompak; Yujitia Ahdarrijal; Iranda Firiansyah

This study compares the management of election recapitulation information systems in Indonesia with those implemented in the Philippines, Brazil, Estonia, and Kyrgyzstan to examine differences in governance, system design, security mechanisms, digital infrastructure, transparency, and public trust\. Although these countries have adopted various election technologies, ranging from optical scanning and Electronic Voting Machines \(EVM\) to Internet voting \(i\-voting\) and optical tabulation, comprehensive comparative studies that position Indonesia within this international context remain limited\. This study employed a Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines\. Data were collected from the Scopus database and supported by credible reports, while CiteSpace was used to map research trends and identify knowledge gaps\. The findings reveal significant differences in the maturity of election recapitulation systems\. Estonia and Brazil have achieved advanced digital election management through integrated digital governance, secure verification mechanisms, and high public trust\. The Philippines applies a hybrid model combining paper ballots with automated vote counting, whereas Kyrgyzstan continues to rely largely on manual procedures\. Indonesia&\#x27;s Sirekap represents an intermediate stage of digital transformation but continues to face challenges related to security, OCR accuracy, infrastructure readiness, and public trust\. The theoretical contribution of this study is the development of a Comparative Governance Framework for Election Recapitulation Information Systems, demonstrating that system maturity is determined not only by technological adoption but also by the interaction among governance, security, digital infrastructure, transparency, and public trust\. This framework provides a foundation for evaluating and improving election recapitulation systems in emerging digital democracies\.

## [Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI](../publications/f2863de89a3d16988808.md)

Agnese Chiatti; Matteo Matteucci; Viola Schiaffonati

As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent\. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI\-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials\. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task\-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI\. Within participants, post\-interaction trust strongly predicted the user&\#x27;s delegation choices \(OR=14\.97, 95% CI \[7\.14,31\.37\]\)\. Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct\. Verification was the dominant policy and often co\-occurred with high trust\. Delegation also increased with task order after adjustment for momentary and participant\-level trust \(OR=1\.22, 95% CI \[1\.02,1\.45\]\), indicating an experience\-related component that self\-reported trust ratings alone could not capture\. These findings motivate a shift from intended delegation to a non\-intrusive observation of how delegation is enacted in collaborative human\-AI tasks\. We therefore conclude by proposing enacted delegation traces as a methodological framework for future studies of multimodal and agentic AI use\.

## [SOCIO\-EMOTIONAL, CREATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE SKILLS IN THE SCHOOL CONTEXT: TEACHERS’ VIEWS](../publications/f2972d93288c3e34e6d4.md)

Eleni Nikolaos Nikolaou; Konstantina Tsoli; Yota Xanthacou; Βασίλειος Παπαβασιλείου; Nikolaos Andreadakis; Thomas K\. Babalis; Maria Kaila

Today, more than ever, there is a need to integrate socio\-emotional competencies and creative skills into the formal education of children and adolescents to promote sustainable development\. To this end, teachers’ role is not only pivotal but also multifaceted and in order to respond effectively to everyday challenges and demands, emphasis should be given to their ongoing professional development\. This research study aims to explore the views of primary education teachers regarding the development and management of students’ socio\-emotional, creative and sustainable skills\. The sample of the research consisted of 214 teachers from Greece, all master&\#x27;s degree graduates\. The results indicate that Greek teachers support the socio\-emotional development of their students, prioritizing, however, the cognitive role of the school\. It was also found that, even though they are generally positive towards creativity and sustainability, they lack knowledge of relevant techniques that develop these skills\. In conclusion, the educational system should support and develop students in a holistic approach, preparing them to acquire not only knowledge but also skills essential for the active citizen of the 21st century\.

## [Visualizing the Solar System with Generative AI: Development and Formative Evaluation of Interactive Multimedia for Lower Secondary Science](../publications/f298519629d5e1913996.md)

Hamidah Khairunnisa; Selvi Susanti; Taufik Kemas Taufik

The solar system is an abstract topic that lower secondary learners often find difficult, and generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) now allows teachers to author rich multimedia without programming\. This study developed an interactive multimedia package on the solar system for Grade VII science and formatively evaluated how learners received it\. Following the ADDIE model, the authors used Canva, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Pippit AI to produce interactive slides, explanatory texts, quiz items, and narrated videos, hosted a gamified quiz on Wayground, and checked all content during finalization\. In a small group trial at an early development stage, five Grade VII learners rated 20 statements on a four point scale covering display, content, interactivity, benefit, and ease of use\. The overall mean was 3\.41 \(85\.25% of the maximum score\), and no learner disagreed with any statement\. Display received the highest rating \(M = 3\.65\) and interactivity the lowest \(M = 3\.20\)\. These results indicated preliminary learner acceptance rather than learning effectiveness\. The study documented a transparent workflow for AI supported authoring and identified expert validation, manipulable simulations, and controlled trials with larger samples as priorities for the next cycle\.

## [Uso de información personal en sistemas de inteligencia artificial: análisis bibliométrico](../publications/f29d7add23ec7ed070e5.md)

Rosalva De\-León\-Fuentes; GUADALUPE AGUSTIN GONZÁLEZ\-GARCÍA; Alan Eliezer Esquivel Espinoza

La transformación digital motiva una revisión del uso de datos personales en aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial\. La construcción del documento se apoya en la revisión sistemática PRISMA a partir de la Web of Science; el objetivo fue analizar la evolución en el uso de datos personales en sistemas informáticos y aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial, integrando avances técnicos, e implicaciones éticas y regulatorias, mediante un enfoque cualitativo y bibliométrico de la literatura\. El análisis examina la evolución del tratamiento automatizado de la información personal desde la comunicación científico\-académica identificando tendencias y aportando elementos para su comprensión\. Se realizaron análisis longitudinales por década, así como una comparación entre autores, enfoques metodológicos y tipos de datos utilizados en los estudios revisados\. Asimismo, se incorpora una reflexión crítica sobre los retos éticos y normativos del manejo de datos personales\. Los resultados muestran que la inteligencia artificial no introduce el uso de información personal como fenómeno nuevo, pero incrementa su escala, capacidad inferencial y alcance social, lo que refuerza la necesidad de consolidar mecanismos de gobernanza y protección de información dentro de los sistemas computacionales actuales\. El uso exclusivo de Web of Science reduce la cobertura bibliográfica, y al tratarse de un estudio documental, los resultados describen tendencias de la literatura, sin evaluar el impacto real de la IA en la gestión de datos personales, por lo que se recomiendan estudios empíricos con bases de datos más amplias\.

## [Determinants of older adults’ adoption and use of smart elderly care services: a qualitative meta\-synthesis](../publications/f2a3113534ab431e9cd3.md)

Xinyi Wang; Muzi Chen; Yi Shen; Xiuyue Qiu

Global population aging is placing increasing pressure on healthcare and long\-term care systems\. Smart elderly care technologies, leveraging the Internet, artificial intelligence, and other digital innovations, have been widely implemented across care settings and offer promising solutions to improve the quality and efficiency of elderly care\. However, their effectiveness largely depends on older adults’ experiences, perceptions, and engagement, which are influenced by multiple interrelated factors\. This study employed a qualitative meta\-synthesis to comprehensively examine the factors influencing older adults’ use of smart elderly care services\. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database was performed for qualitative studies from inception to August 2025\. Two reviewers independently screened studies and appraised methodological quality, and three researchers extracted and coded the qualitative data\. The methodological quality of included studies was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute \(JBI\) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research \(2016 version\)\. Using Thomas and Harden’s thematic coding approach, 11 studies were analyzed\. Three themes were identified: key facilitators promoting older adults’ acceptance of smart elderly care services; core barriers hindering their utilization; and older adults’ needs and expectations regarding smart elderly care\. Older adults’ adoption and sustained use of smart elderly care services were shaped by multiple interacting factors\. Perceived usefulness, technological convenience and ease of use, internal needs, and social support functioned as key facilitators, whereas limited digital literacy, inadequate device adaptability, and insufficient external support and resources represented significant barriers\. Furthermore, older adults expected smart elderly care services to better address their individualized needs through age\-friendly design optimization and expressed a desire for ongoing multidimensional guidance from family members, healthcare professionals, and other support networks during use\. Not applicable\.

## [School proximity and housing price capitalization in China’s secondary market: hedonic and quantile regression evidence from Xi’an and Zhengzhou](../publications/f2aa3c3dc072930242c2.md)

Janina Roshchina; Chenhong Wu

This paper examines how proximity to key middle schools is capitalized into housing prices in urban China and whether the magnitude of this effect is associated with differences in the broader educational environment of the city\. The study addresses the question of whether school\-related housing premiums differ between otherwise comparable cities with distinct higher education ecosystems\. Using micro\-level data on secondary housing sale listings from the Lianjia platform \(February 2022\), we estimate hedonic price models separately for Xi’an and Zhengzhou, two second\-tier Chinese cities similar in economic scale but differing substantially in higher education resources\. Ordinary least squares models with heteroskedasticity\-robust standard errors are complemented by quantile regressions to assess heterogeneity across price segments\. Distance to the nearest key middle school is negatively and statistically significantly associated with housing prices in both cities\. However, the magnitude of capitalization differs markedly: a one\-kilometer increase in distance reduces prices by approximately 3\.5% in Xi’an compared to 1\.2% in Zhengzhou\. Quantile regressions reveal moderate heterogeneity in Zhengzhou, where the school premium is stronger in the lower price segment, while in Xi’an the effect remains relatively stable across quantiles\. The study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that school\-related housing premiums may be associated not only with assignment rules but also with broader differences in the urban educational ecosystem\. By combining a cross\-city comparative design with quantile analysis, the paper provides new evidence on how educational resource concentration may be related to housing market outcomes\.

## [Green Card Health Insurance and Out\-of\-Pocket Health Expenditures in Türkiye: Evidence from Entropy Balancing](../publications/f2ae1aace514ca02217b.md)

Abdullah Tirgil

Over the past two decades, Türkiye has significantly advanced health system reforms towards universal health coverage, notably expanding non\-contributory, government\-funded health insurance benefits \(Green Card\) for low\-income households to mitigate inequities in financing, access, and outcomes\. This research investigates the association between the Green Card and low\-income households&\#x27; out\-of\-pocket healthcare expenditures, focusing on physician and hospital costs\. Using the Entropy Balancing technique on TurkStat Household Budget Survey data \(2005\-2018\) to balance observed characteristics between Green Card holders and non\-holders, the study finds an inverse relationship between Green Card and healthcare costs, especially in regions with enhanced infrastructure\. These results are consistent with non\-contributory insurance being an important tool for addressing financing inequities for the disadvantaged, and the association between the program and out\-of\-pocket expenditures varies with the region&\#x27;s health infrastructure\.

## [The hidden challenges of return migration: Linguistic and academic re\-adaptation of Syrian students to the Arabic Education System](../publications/f2c225d80d3ad036dcfb.md)

Sevda Doğan Dolapçıoğlu; Yunus Emre Akbana; İlayda Uzun; Gülten Koşar

While extensive research has examined refugee students&\#x27; educational adaptation in host countries, the educational reintegration phase following voluntary return remains underexplored\. This qualitative study investigates the linguistic and academic adaptation experiences of Syrian students transitioning from Turkish\-medium education in Türkiye to Arabic\-medium schooling in Syria after voluntary return\. The study addresses an overarching question: how do returnee students experience the linguistic, academic, social, and psychosocial dimensions of this reverse educational transition? Using an exploratory qualitative design, data were collected through a seven\-item open\-ended written questionnaire from 15 middle\-school students who had received several years of formal schooling in Türkiye\. Qualitative content analysis revealed that return does not constitute a simple linguistic recovery, but rather a reverse academic transition characterized by profound difficulties with academic Arabic, conceptual transfer, written production, and in\-class assessment practices\. The findings indicate that students&\#x27; challenges were shaped not only by uneven Arabic literacy development but also by curriculum misalignment, pedagogical practices that participants perceived as more teacher\-directed, limited peer interaction, and assessment practices that they perceived as unclear\. Furthermore, psychosocial pressures, including re\-migration\-related distress, concentration difficulties, and increased family responsibilities, complicated their academic adaptation\. Ultimately, these struggles reflect systemic institutional and contextual mismatches rather than individual deficits\. By conceptualizing return as a distinct educational phase, this study contributes to the broader discourses on refugee education and bilingualism\. The implications underscore the critical need for academic Arabic bridging programs, background\-sensitive assessment frameworks, psychosocially responsive pedagogies, and school\-based psychosocial support to ensure equitable reintegration into Arabic\-medium schooling\.

## [Structural\-before/after\-measurement approaches for estimating treatment effects in latent outcomes with causal machine learning\.](../publications/f2c490be00eed392ff8e.md)

Amota Ataneka; Benjamin M\. Kelcey; Jean Baptiste Habarurema

Prior research has developed a deep and diverse set of methods specifically designed to accommodate reflective latent factors \(e\.g\., structural equation models\)\. A critical limitation of conventional latent variable methods is that they typically operate under assumptions of linearity and almost always presume correct model specification \(e\.g\., all nonlinearities and n\-way interactions are known and included\)\. Recent research in machine learning has relaxed such limitations by developing data\-adaptive methods that identify treatment effects by empirically estimating the functional forms of relationships among covariates, treatment, and an outcome\. A significant weakness of causal machine learning methods, however, is that they have been almost exclusively developed for observed outcome variables and have not considered reflective latent outcomes that are measured with error\. In this study, we developed structural\-after/before\-measurement methods suitable for targeted machine learning with latent outcomes\. The results suggested that the proposed estimators are nearly unbiased in finite samples even when the functional relationships are unknown and unspecified\. We demonstrate the methods with an application to teachers&\#x27; burnout study and compare their performance with conventional linear structural equation models\. \(PsycInfo Database Record \(c\) 2026 APA, all rights reserved\)\.

## [CLINICAL\-FUNCTIONAL EVALUATION OF ORTHOPEDIC TREATMENT OF PATIENTS ON DENTAL IMPLANTS](../publications/f2c515dfb8eb706fcb50.md)

І\.V\. Yanіshen; K\.Yu\. Andriienko; A\.V\. Pohorila; R\.V\. Kuznetsov; Н\.В\. Горбатовська

Modern prosthodontics is characterized by the rapid development of digital technologies that encompass virtually all stages of prosthetic treatment, from initial diagnosis to the fabrication and fixation of definitive prosthetic restorations\. Despite the active implementation of digital technologies into clinical practice, the issue of comparative evaluation of conventional and digital impression techniques during implant\-supported prosthetic treatment remains relevant\. In this regard, the comparative clinical and functional assessment of the outcomes of prosthetic rehabilitation on dental implants using conventional and digital impression techniques represents an important scientific and practical task aimed at improving contemporary prosthetic rehabilitation protocols\. Objective\. To increase the effectiveness of prosthetic rehabilitation in patients with partial edentulism through the fabrication of implant\-supported fixed prosthetic restorations\. Materials and Methods\. The study was conducted at the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry and the University Dental Center of Kharkiv National Medical University\. A total of 48 patients aged 28 to 67 years with partial secondary edentulism who underwent prosthetic rehabilitation using dental implants were included in the study\. All patients were divided into two clinical groups according to the implant system used\. Ethical considerations were addressed in accordance with the legislation of Ukraine, Articles 7, 8, and 12 of the Law of Ukraine “On Medicinal Products” \(1996\), the principles of Good Clinical Practice \(International Council for Harmonisation Good Clinical Practice, ICH GCP, 2008\), Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No\. 690 dated September 23, 2009, “On Approval of the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Trials of Medicinal Products and Expert Evaluation of Clinical Trial Materials and the Standard Regulations on Ethics Committees,” with amendments and additions, as well as the Declaration of Helsinki of the World Medical Association \(1964, latest revision – 2024\)\. The article is a fragment of the planned research project of the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry of Kharkiv National Medical University entitled “Integration of Modern Achievements in Medicine, Materials Science, and Technologies of Diagnosis, Treatment, and Rehabilitation of Patients in the Clinic of Prosthetic Dentistry” \(State Registration No\. 0125U000939, implementation period: 2025–2027; Principal Investigator – Head of the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry, Doctor of Medical Sciences, Professor I\.V\. Yanishen\)\. All patients were in satisfactory general health and had no absolute contraindications to dental implantation and subsequent prosthetic treatment\. After completion of osseointegration and maturation of peri\-implant tissues, the prosthetic stage of treatment was performed\. Within each clinical group, two impression protocols were applied: a conventional technique using an open\-tray impression and A\-silicone impression material, and a digital technique using an intraoral scanner and scan bodies\. Follow\-up examinations were performed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after fixation of the prosthetic restorations\. Statistical analysis was carried out using methods of descriptive and inferential statistics with determination of the mean value \(M\), standard deviation \(SD\), Student’s t\-test, and the level of statistical significance at p &lt; 0\.05\. Results A total of 106 dental implants were placed, including 52 Alfabio implants and 54 Megagen implants\. The average number of implants per patient was 2\.21 ± 0\.8\. During follow\-up examinations at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, no cases of implant loss or impaired osseointegration were recorded, resulting in an implant survival rate of 100%\. The obtained results are consistent with contemporary studies and confirm the high effectiveness of digital technologies in implant\-supported prosthodontics\. The use of intraoral scanners allows optimization of both clinical and laboratory stages of treatment, improves the accuracy of prosthetic restorations, and enhances patients’ quality of life\. Conclusions\. The use of digital intraoral scanning reduces the duration of the clinical impression\-taking stage by 1\.9 times compared with conventional A\-silicone impression materials\. Implant\-supported fixed prosthetic restorations provide a statistically significant improvement in masticatory efficiency, as confirmed by functional assessment at all follow\-up periods\. Following prosthetic rehabilitation, patients demonstrated a substantial improvement in quality\-of\-life indicators according to the treatment satisfaction questionnaire\.

## [Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence into Institutional Arbitration: A Comparative Analysis of Procedural Readiness and Due Process Between India and Singapore](../publications/f2ce86582060c11fe238.md)

Surya Saxena; Mr\. Deepak Bansal; M Taneja; Mr\. Vishal Bansal; Ms\. Akriti Gupta

The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) into international commercial arbitration introduces transformative procedural efficiencies alongside complex legal and constitutional challenges\. This comprehensive research paper explores the regulatory, procedural, and doctrinal implications of utilizing Large Language Models \(LLMs\) and automated legal reasoning tools within arbitral decision\-making workflows\. By establishing a robust comparative framework between India and Singapore, the study critically evaluates how institutional rules, statutory mandates, and judicial oversight manage the intersection of cutting\-edge technology and fundamental guarantees of natural justice\. The paper begins by contrasting Singapore’s mature, digitally integrated arbitral ecosystem—anchored by the SIAC 2025 Rules and advanced institutional governance protocols—with India’s rapidly evolving domestic framework comprising institutions such as the India International Arbitration Centre \(IIAC\) and the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration \(MCIA\)\. It investigates the non\-delegation doctrine, examining whether over\-reliance on AI\-generated legal reasoning and draft awards violates an arbitrator&\#x27;s core duty of independent evaluation under Section 34 of the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and Singapore’s International Arbitration Act\. Furthermore, the study analyzes severe cybersecurity and data governance vulnerabilities, contrasting India&\#x27;s Digital Personal Data Protection \(DPDP\) Act compliance requirements with Singapore&\#x27;s commercial data protocols during cross\-border digital discovery\. Finally, the research evaluates award enforceability hurdles under the New York Convention framework\. It scrutinizes how national courts handle procedural challenges related to algorithmic opacity, data hallucinations, and public policy exceptions\. Ultimately, the paper provides actionable regulatory reform recommendations and institutional guidelines for emerging arbitral seats to safeguard due process integrity and procedural fairness while safely embracing technological innovation\.

## [Dimensionality reduction of atmospheric concentration fields using a 3D convolutional autoencoder with spatial attention mechanism](../publications/f2d5464aad9860e07c5a.md)

Stepan Polyakov; Alexey V\. Penenko

Abstract High\-dimensional atmospheric chemistry simulations produce volumetric concentration fields that are costly to store and repeatedly process in inverse\-modelling and data\-assimilation workflows\. This study evaluates reduced representations for CO concentration fields from WRF\-Chem over Novosibirsk and CAMS over Europe\. We propose a three\-dimensional convolutional autoencoder with a lightweight spatial attention module \(SAM3D\) and compare it with linear, spectral, tensor\-based, interpolation, manifold\-learning, and neural\-network baselines\. The evaluation includes latent dimensions from 8 to 64, temporally separated validation protocols, storage\-cost estimates, and computational\-efficiency measurements\. On the larger CAMS dataset, SAM3D achieves the lowest MSE and relative $$L\_2$$ error among methods compared at equal latent\-vector dimensions and improves over the plain 3D autoencoder\. On the smaller WRF\-Chem dataset, rankings depend more strongly on the split protocol, with fixed transforms and tensor decompositions remaining competitive\. SAM3D adds less than 1% FLOPs and only a small increase in model size while retaining a differentiable encoder–decoder mapping\. These results support SAM3D as a practical reduced\-state representation for three\-dimensional atmospheric concentration fields\.

## [Misinterpretation and Assisted Reading in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Literary Study of Ian McEwan’s Atonement](../publications/f30c19d8f424af3757d7.md)

Wasan Ali Hasan

The study investigates the ethical and theoretical difficulties which arise from the incorrect understanding of Ian McEwan&\#x27;s Atonement \(2001\) because such misinterpretation results in severe negative outcomes\. The study shows that misunderstandings which arise from excessive interpretative confidence and imagination capacity lead to both moral and social problems which persist over time\. The paper shows how Briony Tallis&\#x27; human connection misreading results in moral responsibility to handle literary interpretation through its in\-depth analysis of essential novel events\.

## [An Advanced Machine Learning Framework for Algorithm Development, Optimization, and Explainable Intelligent Prediction](../publications/f30cc23e84d08cebc416.md)

RAMPY

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has increased the demand for reliable, efficient, and interpretable machine learning \(ML\) methods for complex prediction and decision\-making tasks\. However, conventional ML approaches often encounter challenges related to model optimization, generalization, computational efficiency, data imbalance, and limited interpretability\. This study proposes an Advanced Machine Learning Framework for Algorithm Development, Optimization, and Explainable Intelligent Prediction that integrates data preprocessing, feature engineering, algorithm selection, Hyperparameter optimization, ensemble learning, and explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\)\. Multiple ML algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, K\-Nearest Neighbors, Gradient Boosting, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, are comparatively evaluated\. Model performance is assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\-ROC\), computational efficiency, and interpretability\. Furthermore, SHAP and LIME techniques are incorporated to explain feature contributions and improve transparency in model predictions\. The framework facilitates systematic comparison between conventional and optimized models while examining the trade\-off between predictive performance, computational cost, and explainability\. The proposed approach provides a generalizable pathway for developing robust and trustworthy intelligent prediction systems\. Its applicability extends across healthcare, education, cyber security, finance, and other data\-driven domains\. The study contributes an integrated framework that combines algorithmic optimization with explainability to support accurate, transparent, efficient, and reliable ML\-based decision\-making systems\.

## [Associations of self\-reported physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health among civil aviation flight students: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/f30ec65796577385c93c.md)

Yu Zhou; Yang Xu; Yanli He

Objective To examine the associations of self\-reported physical activity at different intensities, total sedentary time, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health indicators among civil aviation flight students\. Methods A cross\-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted at a civil aviation university from January 5 to 30, 2026\. A total of 776 students majoring in Flight Technology were included, of whom 774 \(99\.7%\) were male\. Because only two participants were female, the primary inferential analyses were restricted to male participants\. Physical activity and sedentary behavior were assessed using modified self\-report items\. Physical activity duration represented participants’ self\-reported activity time on a typical activity day rather than average daily or weekly physical activity time; sleep exposure was assessed using categorical self\-reported sleep duration\. Depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use were assessed using validated scales\. Generalized estimating equation models were used to examine cross\-sectional associations between the behavioral indicators and outcomes, with false discovery rate \(FDR\) correction\. Results In the fully adjusted male sample, after FDR correction, longer self\-reported vigorous\-intensity physical activity duration on a typical activity day was associated with lower anxiety scores; self\-reported sleep duration &lt;7 h was associated with higher depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use scores; and longer self\-reported total sedentary time was associated with higher problematic Internet use scores\. No statistically significant linear associations were observed between moderate\- or light\-intensity physical activity and any outcome after FDR correction\. The observed associations were generally small: the association between vigorous\-intensity physical activity and anxiety was approximately 0\.10 outcome standard deviations, the associations between sleep duration &lt;7 h and the corresponding outcomes were approximately 0\.24–0\.27 standard deviations, and the association between total sedentary time and problematic Internet use was approximately 0\.04 standard deviations\. The directions of the main associations were generally consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses, although the strength of statistical evidence for some associations varied by outcome definition, sample restriction, and data\-processing approach\. Conclusion Among male civil aviation flight students, self\-reported physical activity, total sedentary time, and sleep duration were cross\-sectionally associated with selected mental and behavioral health indicators\. Given the cross\-sectional design, these findings cannot establish causality, an optimal physical activity dose, a sleep intervention threshold, or time\-substitution effects between behaviors\. The findings suggest that behavioral indicators and mental and behavioral health status may be considered jointly in this population, but the observed associations require confirmation in longitudinal studies using objective, device\-based behavioral measures\.

## [AI in PRACTICE](../publications/f31d6215829272ba4f02.md)

Maria Bach Nielsen; Tom Børsen; Martin Lillholm; Alessandra Cenci

Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed in healthcare\. Radiology is one of the most active areas of clinical AI development\. Despite substantial investments, many AI systems struggle to gain traction in clinical practice\. The issues are rarely purely technical; they concern how AI tools fit into existing workflows, how they interact with professional responsibilities, and how they sit within institutional arrangements\. It also remains unclear how core values in AI research such as explainability, value alignment, accountability, and trust are negotiated in clinical work\. Established Health Technology Assessment \(HTA\) models define assessment domains but offer limited guidance on implementation: how technologies are staged within workflows, how responsibilities are redistributed, and how local conditions redefine value for different stakeholders\. This paper presents the AI in PRACTICE framework, a five\-phase methodology grounded in Techno\-Anthropology and its relational ontology, for examining the situated work through which AI becomes part of clinical practice\. Explainability, value alignment, trust, and distributed responsibility are understood as produced through socio\-technical practices\. The framework complements existing HTA models through iterative engagement and stakeholder participation\. Insights are illustrated through three radiology\-facing AI projects showing how assessment criteria are enacted, resisted, and revised in context, and how the framework generates practice\-based artefacts\.

## [OPERATIONAL AND GEOTECHNICAL DYNAMICS IN WATER NETWORK REPLACEMENT USING TRENCHLESS METHODS \(MND\): AN INTEGRATED ANALYSIS OF LIFE CYCLE AND SOCIO\-ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS](../publications/f32878024037c2fa550d.md)

Sabrina Fernandes de Mello; Acrissom Luiz Godoi Santos; Alcione Ribeiro Mendes; Analice Caetano Baltazar Tófolo; Dariel Josias Piedade; Gabriela Hyssae Suga; Luana Rocha Carlos; Wesley Duarte Correia; Sheila Leal Oliveira Loureiro

This article investigates the application of Non\-Destructive Methods \(NDM\), specifically Horizontal Directional Drilling and Pipe Bursting, in the replacement and installation of urban water supply networks\. Chronic water loss due to obsolete pipelines imposes a severe economic and environmental liability, demanding the urgent renewal of underground infrastructure\. However, the traditional Open Trench method proves to be technically and socially unfeasible in densely populated urban centers, driving the adoption of trenchless technologies\. This study is characterized as applied, exploratory, and documentary research, based on the integrated analysis of technical and operational guidelines adopted in the Metropolitan Region of Belo Horizonte and the socio\-environmental mitigation strategies applied in the municipality of Joinville\. The research details critical geomechanical variables, such as the rheology of drilling fluids, the safety radius between interferences, and the maximum tensile stress\. The sequential routing of the construction works is outlined from the installation and connection of branch lines to the hydrostatic testing and final paving\. The results confirm that asset replacement via NDM optimizes the project&\#x27;s economic life cycle, significantly reduces construction waste, and mitigates operational disruptions for the population, establishing itself as the most sustainable approach for contemporary sanitary engineering\.

## [Multilevel Embedding and Dropout for Improved 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving Systems](../publications/f328ce3f21703f49335a.md)

Xiaohu Lu; Hayder Radha

The balance between performance and model complexity in terms of time and storage is crucial fordeploying effective and practical autonomous driving systems\. However, some recent advancements in 3D LiDAR object detection come at the cost of significant increases in computational time or additional reliance on multisensor data fusion, limiting their potential deployment\. In this paper, we introduce an innovative framework aimed at harnessing the latent information within a broad range of region‐of‐interest \(RoI\)‐based 3D object detection architectures to enhance their performance, while adding minimal increase in their time consumption and model complexity\. More specifically, we develop a multilevel embedding and dropout strategy to enhance the detection head&\#x27;s capability to generate predictions across different levels of RoI features\. Those predictions are utilized to train the overall 3D object detector network in the training stage and vote for the output in the testing stage\. In this way, multilevel information in the RoI features is deeply explored and also the robustness of the prediction is improved\. We conducted extensive experiments on three widely‐used datasets: KITTI, Waymo, and ONCE, to thoroughly assess the effectiveness of our method\. The results demonstrate the superiority of our approach, consistently outperforming the mainstream point‐based, voxel‐based, and point‐voxel‐based 3D detectors in mean average precision by 1\.21% on average\. Remarkably, this consistent improvement comes at the cost of only a 3\.5 ms increase in computational time and a 2\.7 MB increase in model size\.

## [Why Don’t Younger Solicitors Choose Criminal Legal Aid? Insights from the Theory of Planned Behaviour](../publications/f3368509e70f50449b3f.md)

Susan Rockey

The decline of younger solicitors entering criminal legal aid threatens the sustainability of the criminal defence profession in England and Wales\. This study applies the Theory of Planned Behaviour to examine whether commonly cited recruitment barriers influence aspiring solicitors&\#x27; decisions not to specialise in this sector after graduation\. Survey data from 525 law students under the age of 35 were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling\. The findings indicate that attitudes and perceived behavioural control significantly predict intentions not to specialise\. Negative beliefs relating to remuneration, workload, and student debt were found to shape unfavourable attitudes, while limited familiarity with the profession and restricted access to training opportunities contributed to reduced perceptions of control\. Practically, the findings highlight key areas that CLA firms and policymakers may need to address to improve recruitment\. The study also extends the Theory of Planned Behaviour into a new professional context, demonstrating the value of indirect measures in explaining career decision\-making\.

## [miRNA\-543 attenuates placental angiogenesis in female fetal growth restriction by targeting ANGPT2 and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway](../publications/f33c12d70a54a7128a83.md)

Wenhui Song; Xuemei Yang; Chunyan Yang; Yuanyuan Zhao; Xinxian Zhang; 郭清

Background Insufficient placental angiogenesis is a predominant pathological cause of fetal growth restriction \(FGR\)\. Placental capillary development is regulated in a sex\-dependent manner, with female placentas exhibiting greater susceptibility to angiogenic dysfunction than male placentas\. However, the sex\-specific interplay between microRNAs \(miRNAs\) and human placental angiogenesis in FGR pathogenesis remains poorly defined\. Emerging transcriptomic sequencing evidence has implicated miR\-543 as a pivotal regulator of impaired angiogenesis in female FGR placentas\. This study aimed to elucidate the sex\-dependent mechanistic role of miR\-543 in modulating placental angiogenesis in a cell\-specific manner\. Method FGR pregnancies were recruited, and placental tissues were collected after delivery\. The dual\-luciferase reporter assay was used to detect the direct binding site of miR\-543 to ANGPT2\. Next, immunohistochemistry \(IHC\) and immunofluorescence \(IF\) staining were used to detect the expression and localization of ANGPT2\. To verify the cell\-specific gene expression of miR\-543 and ANGPT2, laser capture microdissection \(LCM\) was employed to isolate endothelial cells from human placentas\. The gene expression levels of miR\-543 and ANGPT2 were quantified by qRT\-PCR\. CCK8, wound healing, Transwell, and tube formation assays and flow cytometry were performed to assess the functional effects of miR\-543 and ANGPT2 on the biological function of human umbilical vein endothelial cells \(HUVECs\)\. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway was predicted and verified by Western blotting\. Results Significantly downregulated miR\-543 expression was observed in the placentas of female FGR fetuses relative to matched normal controls\. According to target gene prediction and the dual\-luciferase reporter assay, ANGTP2 was identified as a target candidate of miR\-543\. Moreover, immunofluorescence staining and LCM analysis verified the cell\-specific distribution of ANGPT2 in female FGR placentas, partly indicating its key involvement in placental capillary angiogenesis\. Furthermore, dysregulated expression of miR\-543 and ANGPT2 was closely correlated with aberrant proliferation, migration, and apoptosis of HUVECs\. KEGG analysis revealed that the candidate targets of miR\-543 were mainly enriched in the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway\. Western blot analysis demonstrated that the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway mediated the ANGPT2\-induced attenuation of placental angiogenesis in female FGR\. Conclusion miR\-543 negatively regulated ANGPT2 expression, leading to impaired endothelial cell function via inactivation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway\. This, in turn, contributed to sex\-specific inhibition of capillary angiogenesis in the placenta of female fetuses\. These findings reveal a novel miRNA\-mediated, sex\-dependent regulatory mechanism underlying the pathogenesis of impaired placental angiogenesis\.

## [Look, Reason, Draw a Region: Recursive Refinement for Spatial Context Prediction](../publications/f3484c57f0bb1d4dae19.md)

Wajeeha Tahir; Anna Tegon; Lionnus Kesting; Gamze İslamoğlu; Kristóf Karacs; Luca Benini; Thorir Mar Ingolfsson

Spatial context prediction requires visual grounding and spatial reasoning to identify vacant regions relative to objects in a scene\. Spatial relationships and physical constraints remain challenging for large vision\-language models \(VLMs\)\. Recursive reasoning has demonstrated strong performance on discrete and abstract reasoning tasks, motivating its use for improving spatial context prediction in natural images\. Weight sharing enables higher accuracy with a small trainable parameter count\. We introduce Spatial\-TRM, a compact recursive model with frozen vision\-language features, a convex region decoder, and just 11\.2M trainable parameters\. This weight\-tied reasoner supports six spatial relationships, three reference frames, and open\-vocabulary anchor objects\. On the RoboSpatial\-Home benchmark, Spatial\-TRM achieves 29\.51% context accuracy, a gain of 9\.02 percentage points \(44\.0% relative\) over a separately trained single\-step model with the same parameter count\. Including the frozen encoders, the model has 877\.8M total parameters, approximately $15\\times$ fewer than the reported 13B size of RoboPoint\. These results show that repeated refinement improves spatial context prediction from pretrained vision\-language features at a fixed trainable parameter count on this benchmark\.

## [Maximising self\-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies](../publications/f34de943a35c1e16cba9.md)

Nektarios Matsagkos; Dimitris Augoloupis; Elissaios Sarmas; Vangelis Marinakis

Energy Communities \(ECs\) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy\. Maximising collective self\-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal\. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self\-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them\. This study is one of the first to propose a data\-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self\-consumption of ECs\. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self\-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination\. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community \(REC\) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results\. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy\-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member\-level self\-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles\.

## [AI\-Driven Next\-Generation DDoS Mitigation in IoT: A Comprehensive Survey of Deep Learning and Large Language Models](../publications/f3593b77784cb0ab02dd.md)

Mosiur Rahaman; Nicko C\. Cajes; Varsha Arya; Razaz Waheeb Attar; Kwok Tai Chui; Brij B\. Gupta

The global Internet of Things \(IoT\) network has experienced unprecedented expansion, reaching 75\.44 billion connected devices worldwide\. Due to this rapid growth, the IoT ecosystem has become larger but also more vulnerable to various threats in cyberspace\. As a result, this situation has accelerated the development of more complex cyberattacks, especially Distributed Denial of Service \(DDoS\) attacks, which can damage systems by overwhelming network traffic\. This attack exploits the inherent vulnerabilities of IoT networks with limited resources, leading to significant service interruptions, monetary losses, and potentially the failure of vital infrastructures\. As a result, this survey presents a new taxonomy of attack types, a thorough assessment of conventional and AI\-driven detection techniques, and a comparison of advanced countermeasures\. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive and systematic overview of DDoS attack detection, prevention, and mitigation approaches for the IoT\. A major contribution of this work is the inclusion of blockchain\-based security frameworks, federated learning, deep learning, machine learning, and quantum computing paradigms in its discussion for reducing DDoS attacks on the IoT\. Furthermore, real\-world case studies highlight the severe impact of such attacks on mission\-critical domains, including smart cities, healthcare, and industrial control systems \(ICSs\)\. This survey provides a basis for cybersecurity researchers, security experts, and hobbyists, grounded in the understanding gained from previous research\.

## [Initiation and Propagation Mechanisms of Rolling Contact Fatigue in High\-Speed Railway Rails: A Review](../publications/f35cb5b8ce6247ce4037.md)

Hieu Vo Dinh; Dong Doan Van; Danh Chan Nguyen

Rolling contact fatigue \(RCF\) is a critical rail failure mechanism in high\-speed railway \(HSR\) systems, caused by repeated wheel\-rail contact under high Hertz stress, tangential forces, and complex multiaxial stress states\.This study provides a systematic overview of RCF crack initiation and propagation in HSR rails\.It first summarizes typical RCF failure modes and analyzes two crack initiation mechanisms\.Subsequent propagation stages are examined, including short and long crack growth, mixed failure mechanisms, crack branching, and environmental influences\.The study then evaluates existing predictive methods for RCF initiation and development\.Current challenges and future trends are identified, particularly regarding short\-term fracture behavior, multiphysical linkages, lifespan prediction, and field monitoring data integration\.By synthesizing these key aspects, RCF in HSR is framed as a continuous, multistage failure process\.Advancing integrated multi\-level and multi\-physical data approaches will be essential for improving prediction reliability and railway maintenance strategies\.

## [The impact of artificial intelligence on the purchasing decisions of different generations in clothing purchases](../publications/f3625509641751c8d594.md)

Maša Gerečnik Drobne

Nakup oblačila se danes pogosto začne, še preden potrošnik zares ve, kaj išče\. Med množico izdelkov ga spremljajo priporočila, prilagojene vsebine, virtualni pomočniki in druge rešitve umetne inteligence, ki lahko spletno nakupno pot naredijo bolj osebno in usmerjeno\. Vendar na drugi strani zaslona niso vsi potrošniki enaki\. Pripadajo različnim generacijam, ki so odraščale v različnih časovnih in tehnoloških okoljih ter s seboj v spletni svet prinašajo svoje nakupne navade, pričakovanja in odnos do novih tehnologij\. Diplomsko delo obravnava vpliv umetne inteligence na nakupno odločanje različnih generacij pri spletnem nakupovanju oblačil in nakupovanju oblačil v fizičnih trgovinah\. V ospredju so babyboom generacija ter generacije X, Y in Z, pri katerih so obravnavane razlike v nakupnem vedenju, odnosu do umetne inteligence in njenem vplivu na nakupno odločanje\. Posebna pozornost je namenjena oblikam umetne inteligence, s katerimi se lahko potrošnik sreča med spletnim nakupovanjem oblačil, ter njihovemu mestu v nakupnem procesu\. S povezovanjem sveta mode, spletnega nakupovanja in umetne inteligence delo odpira vprašanje, ali ista tehnologija pri različnih generacijah pomeni tudi enako nakupno izkušnjo\. Rezultati raziskave so pokazali, da se generacije razlikujejo predvsem pri prepoznavanju oblik umetne inteligence, pri čemer je najnižjo stopnjo prepoznavanja dosegla generacija Y, ostale generacije so prepoznale vse oblike umetne inteligence, zato je bila hipoteza H1 zavrnjena\. Pri zaupanju v umetno inteligenco, njenem vplivu na pogostost nakupovanja pri vseh generacijah, ignoriranju predlogov umetne inteligence pri starejših in poenostavljanju nakupne odločitve rezultati niso potrdili zastavljenih predpostavk, zato so bile hipoteze H2, H3, H4 in H5 zavrnjene\.

## [Regional heterogeneity in the association between extreme temperatures and emergency hospitalizations in Germany](../publications/f3790ab0ea784f595a3f.md)

Maria Gueltzow; Risto Conte Keivabu; Christopher Irrgang; Marcus Ebeling

Abstract Background The association between extreme temperature and emergency hospitalizations may differ by regional socioeconomic deprivation and its intersection with age and urbanization\. This study investigates how regional characteristics modify the relationship between temperature and emergency hospitalizations in Germany\. Methods We analyzed the weekly emergency hospitalization rate by German districts \(2005\-2021\) using the German Diagnosis\-Related Groups Statistic, linked with high\-resolution temperature data from the European gridded daily observational dataset \(E\-OBS\)\. We fit a fixed effects model and interact regional socioeconomic deprivation with the weekly number of days falling into one of eleven temperature bins, adjusting for seasonality\. Analysis was stratified by urbanization and age group\. Results We observe 112,909,391 emergency hospitalizations over the study period\. Among rural districts, an additional heat day is associated with 17\.6 \(95% CI: 12\.3–23\.1\) additional emergency cases per 10,000 in the least\-deprived districts, with no change in the most\-deprived districts\. Among ages 65\+, an additional heat day is associated with the largest increase in emergency hospitalizations in medium\-deprived compared to least\-deprived districts\. Conclusions Our study finds that the temperature\-emergency hospitalization relationship varies across German regions, with differences only becoming visible if regions are profiled by several characteristics\. This highlights the need for an intersectoral approach to adequately address the differential impact of climate stressors on inpatient care uptake\.

## [Airikka, Christian: Flat\-footed functionalism in the face of T\-duality](../publications/f37a5488a45f10abf663.md)



\_European Journal for Philosophy of Science\_ 16 \(4\):83\. 2026The goal of this paper is to examine the viability of Lewis\-style spacetime functionalism in the presence of string theory duals\. This task is carried out in three steps\. First, I discuss Lewisian functionalism, and the related Geneva plan, bringing to light a number of features that are far too often passed over without comment in the literature on philosophy of physics\. Then I show that Lewis\-style functionalism fails \_as an account\_ of spacetime emergence in the presence of certain theory duals, by investigating a simple toy case involving string theories related by T\-duality\. I find that the functionalist ought to, if she takes her functionalist commitments seriously, \_identify\_ terms related via the duality map as they refer to the same functional roles\. This blocks the argument that spacetime is emergent\. However, this might just as well be interpreted as a \_success\_—spacetime functionalism implies a \_deflationary\_ interpretation of T\-duality\. Finally, I offer a brief look forward by examining whether there is a positive case to be made for the deflationary interpretation, which I refer to as \_flat\-footed functionalism\_\. I find that it is a surprisingly promising account, with several good points in its favour\. However, the position is not without its issues, and remains underdeveloped\. \(direct link \)

## [WORKLOAD MONITORING OF BADMINTON PLAYERS USING WEARABLE AND WIRELESS SENSOR: A REVIEW PAPER](../publications/f37fe12dfb4d73914064.md)

Saira Afzal; Naresh Bhaskar Raj; Marhasiyah Rahim; Muhammad Ishfaq Khan

Introduction: Badminton a fast paced and physically demanding sport the application of wearable sensors plays a crucial role in monitoring players&\#x27; workload, injury risk, and recovery patterns\. These technologies offer real\-time insights into an athlete&\#x27;s physical exertion, allowing for personalized and data\-driven coaching decisions\. Objective: This review paper is to analyze and summarize the role of wearable and wireless sensor technologies in monitoring the workload of badminton players\. Methodology: the methodology consists of a systematic review of literature search from internet using google scholar, PubMed and research gate\. The review focusing on studies that employed wearable and wireless sensors to monitor workload, biomechanics, heart rate, and player movement\. Results: Findings indicate that wearable sensors are highly effective in capturing key performance metrics such as jump count, footwork frequency, heart rate variability, and energy expenditure\. These data points allow coaches and sports scientists to monitor player fatigue and adjust training loads accordingly\. However, limitations such as sensor accuracy, user comfort, data privacy, and the cost of high\-end equipment still pose challenges\. Conclusion: Wearable and wireless sensor technologies play a key role in monitoring the workload of badminton players by providing important data on physiological and performance aspects\. This helps coaches optimize training, reduce injury risk, and improve overall performance\.

## [The relationship between doomscrolling intensity and academic anxiety among TikTok\-using university students](../publications/f39a9c4fe03606681acd.md)

Ajeng Dwi Luthfiah; Onny Fransinata Anggara

The widespread use of TikTok has increased users&\#x27; exposure to personalized digital content, including repeated exposure to negative information that may encourage doomscrolling behavior\. This study aimed to examine the relationship between doomscrolling intensity and academic anxiety among university students who use TikTok\. A quantitative study with a cross\-sectional correlational design was conducted involving 200 undergraduate students selected through purposive sampling\. Data were collected using the Social Media Doomscrolling Scale and the Academic Anxiety Scale\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Spearman&\#x27;s rank correlation because one variable did not meet the normality assumption\. The results revealed a significant positive correlation between doomscrolling intensity and academic anxiety \(ρ = 0\.301, p &lt; \.001\), indicating that students with higher doomscrolling intensity tended to experience higher levels of academic anxiety\. However, the strength of the relationship was weak, suggesting that doomscrolling is only one of several factors associated with academic anxiety\. These findings expand previous evidence regarding the psychological consequences of doomscrolling by demonstrating its association with academic anxiety in the context of TikTok use among university students\. The findings also highlight the importance of promoting healthy social media use, digital literacy, self\-regulation, and emotional regulation to reduce the potential psychological impact of excessive exposure to negative online content\.

## [Generative Artificial Intelligence Governance and Algorithmic Trust in Smart Organizations: Implications for Sustainable Innovation and Organizational Performance](../publications/f3a43fd58510f163a75f.md)

Masoumeh Cheraghi; Masoud Fallahi; Mohammd Mafi

Purpose Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is being integrated into knowledge work, organizational decision support, and sustainability\-related operations, yet evidence regarding governance, algorithmic trust, and durable organizational value remains fragmented\. This article develops an integrated explanation of how responsible governance can enable, rather than merely constrain, the creation of sustainable innovation and organizational performance\. Design/methodology/approach A critical, structured integrative synthesis draws on recent peer\-reviewed research and authoritative policy and standards publications issued between 2023 and October 2026\. Sources compared through thematic coding across governance architecture, calibrated algorithmic trust, human\-AI collaboration, sustainable innovation, and organizational performance\. The article proposes constructs, testable propositions, an implementation framework, and a future empirical research design; it does not claim to report original survey or experimental findings\. Findings Governance quality theorized to improve organizational outcomes through calibrated trust and responsible human\-AI practices\. The effects are contingent on decision criticality, employee AI literacy, accountability arrangements, institutional pressure, and the environmental costs of computation\. Trust appropriately calibrated to system reliability rather than maximized\. Practical implications Organizations should combine documented use\-case inventories, risk\-tiered oversight, evaluation, traceability, worker participation, and multidimensional scorecards\. Originality/value the framework connects governance mechanisms and behavioral trust calibration to an explicitly triple\-bottom\-line account of innovation and performance, while separating established empirical evidence from propositions requiring testing\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Anxiety and Employee Engagement in the Indian Real Estate Sector](../publications/f3b0031ac9a1c5600361.md)

Nidhish Singh

Survey Integration Note The survey provides organization\-specific evidence from the participating real\-estate organization employees concerning health and well\-being, workplace safety, manager and team support, psychological safety, belonging, fairness, meaningful work, learning, work\-life balance, wellness support, communication and employer recommendation\. Preliminary Survey Snapshot \(n = 59\) Positive \(Agree \+ Indicator Valid n Mean / 5 Strongly Agree\) I think this is a safe 59 4\.31 91\.5% place to work\. I receive good support from my 59 4\.07 83\.1% team members/colleagues\. My immediate manager/supervisor 59 4\.10 79\.7% supports me when I need help\. I feel a sense of belonging at the organization 59 3\.97 79\.7% Realty\. I am able to balance my work and 59 3\.47 55\.9% personal/family commitments\. The health and wellness support the 59 3\.64 62\.7% organisation provides meets my needs\. There is open and honest two\-way 59 3\.61 66\.1% communication\. I receive regular communication from 59 3\.54 61\.0% my manager about management updates\. Abstract Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly transforming organizational processes, occupational roles, skill requirements and employee expectations\. Although AI has the potential to improve productivity and create new employment opportunities, its increasing use may also generate employee concerns regarding job replacement, skill obsolescence, career continuity and employment security\. These concerns are particularly relevant in knowledge\-intensive and technology\-enabled sectors such as real estate, where artificial intelligence, data analytics, automation, digital platforms and intelligent decision\-support systems are increasingly influencing organizational activities\. The present study develops and proposes an empirical model examining the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Anxiety \(AIA\) and Employee Engagement \(EE\) among employees in the Indian real estate sector\. Specifically, the study investigates Perceived Job Insecurity \(PJI\) as a mediating mechanism and Perceived Organizational Support \(POS\) as a moderating resource\. The theoretical foundation integrates Job Demands–Resources \(JD\-R\) theory, Conservation of Resources \(COR\) theory and Organizational Support Theory\. The proposed model suggests that AI anxiety increases perceived job insecurity, which subsequently reduces employee engagement\. Perceived organizational support is expected to weaken the positive relationship between AI anxiety and perceived job insecurity and consequently buffer the negative indirect effect of AI anxiety on employee engagement\. Data will be collected using established measurement instruments for AI anxiety, job insecurity, perceived organizational support and employee engagement\. Structural Equation Modelling \(SEM\), preferably using SmartPLS, will be employed to assess the measurement and structural models, including mediation, moderation and moderated mediation\. The proposed study contributes to the emerging literature on the human consequences of AI by moving beyond technology adoption and productivity perspectives and examining the psychological pathway through which AI\- related concerns influence employee engagement\.
