## [Protein structure–function relationships as the molecular basis of phenotypic diversity in GDAP1\-associated Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease](../publications/f3dcfb8d8d8f26897e24.md)

Victoria I\. Bunik; Alina A Emelyanova

Mutations in the GDAP1 gene, which encodes the ganglioside\-induced differentiation\-associated protein 1 \(GDAP1\)—a member of the detoxifying glutathione S\-transferase \(GST\) superfamily—cause Charcot­­–Marie–Tooth disease \(CMT\) a genetically heterogeneous group of inherited neuropathies\. This mini review correlates the clinical phenotypes of CMT with the molecular dysfunctions of GDAP1\. Implicated in mitochondrial dynamics, calcium homeostasis, cellular organelle contacts, and the metabolism of mitochondria, lysosomes, and peroxisomes, the known molecular functions of GDAP1 include localization to mitochondrial outer membrane, dimerization, GST activity, and binding of hydrophobic compounds and proteins\. Our analysis reveals that mutation\-induced perturbations in specific molecular functions correlate with clinical phenotypes better than mutation class \(missense vs\. nonsense or frameshift\), mode of inheritance \(dominant vs\. recessive\), or mitochondrial morphology\. The G327D and truncated GDAP1 variants have similar clinical phenotypes because all lack membrane binding\. Early disease onset and rapid progression are observed not only with recessive variants \(P111, N227, L239, and R282\) but also with dominant variants \(C240\), if the substituted residues are proximal to the hydrophobic ligand\. While dominant GDAP1 variants cause axonal CMT, all the recessive variants inferred to affect the hydrophobic ligand binding present with demyelination in addition to axonal damage\. These different disease trajectories may rely on the potential formation of fully functional wild\-type GDAP1 homodimers in dominant heterozygotes but not in biallelic recessive cases\. Thus, elucidating how disease\-associated protein variants affect GDAP1 molecular functions advances our understanding of the molecular basis of clinical phenotypes, which is required for tailored therapies\.

## [Exploring the difference between self\-harm and suicidal ideation among older people who present to emergency departments: national cohort study](../publications/f3e19d4d80b4761ba8f0.md)

Fiona Hoare; Geraldine M\. McCarthy; Katerina Kavalidou; Vincent Russell; Michael John Norton; Anne Marie Doherty

Background Older people have higher rates of death by suicide, and both self\-harm and suicidal ideation are major risk factors for suicide\. There is limited data relating to this group internationally\. Aims The objective of this study was to identify the clinical and sociodemographic variables associated with psychiatric admissions for older people who present with self\-harm and suicidal ideation to emergency departments in Ireland\. Method This is a cohort study of older people in Ireland, utilising data collected by the National Clinical Programme for Self\-Harm and Suicide\-Related Ideation \(NCPSHI\)\. It is a national data\-set including anonymised data from all participating emergency departments in Ireland, comprising 72 810 presentations over 5 years \(2018–2020\)\. We examined the characteristics of people aged over 60 presenting with self\-harm and suicidal ideation \( n = 4866\)\. The variables associated with suicidal ideation and behaviours were explored using multivariable analysis\. Results Nationally, 7% of the patients presenting were aged over 60 years\. One\-quarter \(26\.8%\) of older people presenting with self\-harm required psychiatric admission \(16\.3% all\-ages\)\. On multivariable analysis, the relationship between self\-harm and psychiatric admission was not statistically significant \(reference group was those with suicidal ideation\), after controlling for gender, year of presentation, substance use and need for medical admission odds ratio 0\.977 \(CI0\.936–1\.020\)\. Conclusions Our results outline the characteristics of older people presenting to Irish emergency departments with self\-harm and suicidal ideation, which are associated with psychiatric admission\. Further research is needed to understand the factors driving these presentations and to tailor our services to meet the needs of older people\.

## [The samplr package: A tool for modeling human cognition with sampling algorithms](../publications/f3eb1504bf245fba560e.md)

Lucas Castillo; Yun\-Xiao Li; Adam N\. Sanborn

Many models of cognition have sampling as a central component\. Researchers have used them to explain human performance across a wide range of tasks involving perception, probability reasoning, and choice\. One family of these models takes inspiration from sampling approaches developed in statistics, either by adjusting samples with prior beliefs or by implementing a sampling algorithm that overcomes the difficulty of independent samples at the expense of autocorrelation\. While these models have been successful in modeling human behavior, their adoption has been slowed by the technical difficulties in applying them\. Here, we introduce the samplr package, which includes a variety of these algorithms and cognitive models built upon them\. We show how models in this package can match qualitative patterns found in human data, and walk readers through examples of how to compare these models quantitatively to human data\. This tool aims to make these methods accessible to many more researchers\.

## [Discovering state\-of\-the\-art quantum circuits with large language models](../publications/f3eb34cfc4dbc11c5f59.md)

Andi Gu; Alek H\. Kemeny; Susanne F\. Yelin; Mikhail D\. Lukin

Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large\-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms\. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation\. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models \(LLMs\) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them\. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory\. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art\. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime\-field modular inversion\. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps \-\- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic \-\- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli\-qubit trade\-off for modular inversion\. These results open the door for evaluator\-guided LLM co\-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation\.

## [TDD\-Net: A Metadata\-augmented Transformer Framework for Depression Detection from Primary Social Media Data](../publications/f3ed7610ea74246eaa0d.md)

V\. Lavanya; Ashok Kumar T\. A\.

Mental illnesses are on the rise all over the world and there is a need to detect depression through digital footprints in an automated and early manner\.The traditional Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) paradigms do not usually have context\-based and user behavioral information\.To overcome these shortcomings, this research paper suggested the Transformer\-Based Depression Detection Network \(TDD\-Net\) that combined textual information with user\-centric behavioral metadata built on a fully primary and consented social media dataset\.The data included self\-written posts, captions, comments, patterns of interactions and anonymized profile data\.Text cleaning, sentiment normalization and tokenization were done by using a systematic preprocessing pipeline\.A RoBERTa encoder was used to learn the semantic representation of text, and a metadata embedding network was used to learn longitudinal behavioral signals, including posting frequency, intensity of engagement, and diurnal activity patterns\.The linguistic and metadata vectors were fused with a fusion layer and a multi\-head attention classification head was applied to predict the risk of depression\.This transformer fusion, which is metadata\-enhanced, boosted personalization in depression detection\.An experimental assessment revealed an accuracy of 97\.18, and better precision, recall, and F1\-scores\.These findings show that the model has high predictive accuracy, and it is used in practice in mental health monitoring\.TDD\-Net is a big improvement over the conventional text\-only approach by making good use of extensive behavioral cues\.

## [Haplotype\-resolved swine leukocyte antigen \(SLA\) gene typing using long\-read whole genome sequencing](../publications/f3f6c382a3f52a2fdb02.md)

Anne Boshove; Amalee E\. Nunnally; Scott A\. Callison; Jenelle Dunkelberger; Claudia A\. Sevillano; Martien A\. M\. Groenen; Christine A\. Jansen; Martijn F\. L\. Derks

Background The Major Histocompatibility Complex \(MHC\) is a genomic region present in all vertebrates encoding genes essential for the immune response\. In pigs, the MHC is named the Swine Leukocyte Antigen \(SLA\) complex\. Traditional methods for SLA gene typing rely on targeted amplification and sequencing of SLA genes\. In this study, we evaluated whether SLA genes can be identified from non\-targeted Oxford Nanopore long\-read sequencing data, to create a versatile approach that can be applied to existing long\-read sequencing datasets\. Methods We analyzed 56 pigs from four breeds \(Large White, Duroc, Landrace and a Large White\-derived synthetic line\) and generated de novo genome assemblies that were separated into haplotypes through phasing and haplotagging\. SLA gene sequences from the IPD\-MHC database were mapped to the haplotype\-resolved assemblies, and candidate novel alleles and haplotypes were assessed using targeted NGS\-based SLA typing\. Results This approach enabled confident allele assignment for over 95% of SLA\-1, SLA\-2, SLA\-3, SLA\-DRB1 , and SLA\-DQB1 genes\. The majority of results consisted of haplotypes which have been previously reported and additionally included several potential novel alleles and haplotypes\. Targeted NGS\-based SLA typing confirmed seven novel class I haplotypes as well as the presence of three novel SLA\-2 alleles, although additional sequencing is required to fully resolve the exon 2 sequence for two of them\. We also observed strong linkage between assembly\-derived SLA haplotypes and medium\-density genotypes within the SLA region, supporting efficient identification and monitoring of SLA diversity in populations with similar linkage disequilibrium structures\. Conclusion Existing long\-read sequencing and genotype datasets can be leveraged to characterize SLA variation, identify candidate novel haplotypes and alleles, and provide insight into SLA diversity within the pig populations studied\.

## [Nutritional and Structural Characterization of Dietary Fibre Concentrates from sustainable Agro\-Industrial ByProducts](../publications/f3ff658128cd89bc33a8.md)



The escalating generation of by\-products from fruit and vegetable processing has become a major sustainability challenge, encouraging Valorization strategies that transform these un\-utilized biomass resources into functional ingredients with enhanced nutritional and economic value\.This study aimed to develop dietary fibre concentrates \(DFCs\) from mango and potato peels and evaluate their nutritional, and structural characteristics\.Mango and potato peels were processed into dietary fibre concentrates through drying, grinding, and sieving\.Proximate analysis revealed that the dietary fibre concentrates \(DFCs\) were rich in dietary fibre and contained substantial amounts of ash and carbohydrates, indicating their nutritional significance and potential application in functional food formulations\.Structural characterization using scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\) demonstrated irregular, porous, and fibrous surface morphology, which contributes to improved water and oil\-holding capacities\.Energy dispersive spectroscopy \(EDS\) confirmed the presence of essential elements such as carbon and oxygen, supporting the organic nature of the fibre matrix\.X\-ray diffraction \(XRD\) analysis indicated a semi\-crystalline structure characteristic of cellulose and hemicellulose components\.Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy \(FTIR\) identified functional groups corresponding to polysaccharides, lignin, and cellulose, confirming the complex fibre composition\.The findings demonstrate that peel\-derived DFCs possess valuable nutritional and functional attributes, making them suitable for incorporation into functional food products\.This study highlights the potential of fruit and vegetable processing by\-products as sustainable sources of dietary fibre and supports their utilization in value\-added food applications\.

## [Mutual learning of self\-supervised ViTs for image classification with limited labeled data](../publications/f403c598c3189afdb370.md)

Zhanghui Huang; Jian Zhang

With the rapid advancement of self\-supervised learning in computer vision, pretrained models have shown remarkable transferability across a wide range of downstream tasks by effectively leveraging large\-scale unlabeled data\. However, prevailing approaches predominantly adopt supervised fine\-tuning strategies on individual models, often overlooking the potential complementarity between different pretrained models during adaptation\. This limitation constrains the further improvement of model performance\. To address this, the authors propose a bidirectional mutual learning framework that enables two distinct self\-supervised models to be jointly fine\-tuned on a target task\. By exchanging predictions during training, the models share knowledge and collaboratively enhance their representations\. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that their method consistently outperforms conventional full\-parameter fine\-tuning and low\-rank adaptation \(LoRA\) in classification performance\. Notably, the superior results achieved on the Radiological Society of North America \(RSNA\) data set highlight the potential of their method in medical imaging analysis\.

## [Differences in perceived influences and educational support needs of generative AI among medical and nursing students across educational levels: a descriptive qualitative study](../publications/f42085099d3553ddd38b.md)

Guoxin Zhou; Bo Li; Tingmei Wen; Hongyan Wen; Ting Sun; Haitao Zhang; Xiaoxiao Li; Li Wang; Yang Wang

Generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) has been extensively integrated into nursing and medical education, significantly transforming the academic practices of students\. Nonetheless, the varying impacts of GAI on core competency of student across educational stages remain ambiguous, with limited empirical evidence on hierarchical educational support needs\. Drawing on cross\-sectional comparisons of GAI\-related experiences among undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral students, this study aimed to explore differences in students’ perceptions of GAI influences across educational levels\. It focuses on students’ perceived impacts concerning critical thinking, research competence, and academic integrity, and further identify personalized support needs for GAI\-oriented education at each stage\. This cross\-educational\-stage comparative perspective is expected to provide empirical evidence for constructing an AI\-literacy education system tailored to learners at different levels\. This descriptive qualitative study draw on semi‑structured interviews with 44 students \(16 undergraduate, 16 master’s, 12 doctoral\) from a western Chinese medical university using inductive content analysis, with Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) and AI Literacy frameworks informing discussion\. Interview findings showed that GAI\-use patterns varied across academic levels: undergraduates for coursework, versus postgraduates for literature reviews, experimental design, and data analysis\. Students perceived that GAI\-use could yield benefits for their critical thinking and knowledge acquisition, counterbalanced by risks of over\-reliance, academic integrity, and cognitive offloading—with research competency gains largely confined to postgraduates\. A pronounced demand for systemic support, including teacher guidance and institutional training, pervaded all levels\. Interview findings suggest that GAI may exert differentiated perceived influences on the development of medical and nursing students\. Students’ GAI usage patterns, academic benefits and potential risks may vary across academic levels, which suggests the necessity of adaptive educational support tailored to distinct stages\. Based on qualitative findings, we propose an extended three level TAM model \(PEOU driven, PU driven, critical reflection\) as a preliminary conceptual framework to capture students’ different GAI use patterns\. The findings may inform stratified AI literacy education and stage specific curriculum in health professions education, though further validation of this model in diverse educational contexts is still required\.

## [Non\-toxic aryl diazirine photoinitiators](../publications/f421717b8309e369f692.md)

Naziruddin Ali; Elwin W\. J\. Ang; Animesh Ghosh; Darien Yu De Kwek; Jean\-Baptiste Lena; Jeremy Daniel Lease; Avanthiga MJ; Odelia Goh; Darren W\. Y\. Teoh; Viswanathababu Gurupriya; DAVID G\. BRADLEY; Seerat Virk; Frédéric Averseng; Souhir Boujday; Jeremy E\. Wulff; John V\. Hanna; Terry W\. J\. Steele

Photoinitiators offer an energy\-saving alternative to thermal initiation, initiating free\-radical polymerization through irradiation\. Despite their benefits, current photoinitiators face issues of toxicity and solubility\. Trifluoromethylphenyl diazirine, an aryl diazirine, is a promising photoinitiator that generates a carbene upon exposure to light\. Aryl diazirines exhibit favorable optical and molecular properties, including minimal skin sensitization and liquid miscibility with aqueous and organic resins\. Experimental studies demonstrate the ability of aryl diazirines to initiate free\-radical polymerization of acrylate monomers, offering several advantages over traditional photoinitiators, such as TPO and BAPO\. Aryl diazirines’ unique attributes include low cytotoxicity, prevention of resin shrinkage, and removal of unreacted monomers post\-curing\. R\-group variants enable both UV and visible\-light activation, thereby expanding their utility across biomedical and industrial sectors\. The study explores the potential of aryl diazirines as photoinitiators for acrylate polymerization, addressing the limitations of current photoinitiators like toxicity and solubility\. The authors hypothesize that aryl diazirines, with electron\-withdrawing or alkyl para\-substituents, can initiate radical polymerization effectively\. They employ photorheometry to assess the polymerization process under various wavelengths and conditions, comparing results with commercial photoinitiators\. The findings reveal that aryl diazirines achieve comparable mechanical properties to TPO, with advantages such as lower skin sensitization and better solubility in water\-based resins\. These properties make aryl diazirines promising for applications in biomedical fields and sustainable manufacturing\. The study suggests future exploration of diazirines in 3D printing and bioadhesives, emphasizing their potential as non\-toxic alternatives to traditional photoinitiators\. This summary was initially drafted using artificial intelligence, then revised and fact\-checked by the author\. Aryl diazirines as a new class of photoinitiators\. Irradiation of an aryl diazirine releases N2 and generates a triplet carbene that initiates free\-radical polymerization of acrylate monomers through a hypothesized hydrogen abstraction mechanism\. Unlike commercial photoinitiators, aryl diazirines exhibit unique benefits like being miscible liquids in both organic and aqueous environments, exhibit minimal cytotoxicity, and can absorb residual vinyl monomer through the diazoalkane isomer\. The para\-substituent tunes activation wavelength from 365 to 445 nm and nitrogen evolution offsets cure shrinkage\.

## [Conditions and implications of participation in semiotics \(and elsewhere\)](../publications/f42b7b4330fd270cfd11.md)

Sémir Badir

AbstractThis paper examines the conditions of possibility for semiotics to engage with the notion of participation and, through it, with participatory sciences\. After tracing the genealogy of participation as a concept—from participant observation and action research to actor\-network theory—the paper analyses the political requalification of this sociological notion into an institutional project for science\. It then considers the specific epistemic position of semiotics, arguing that, as an “undisciplined” body of knowledge, it is largely foreign to the applied research model that underlies participatory sciences\. The paper concludes that semiotics may nonetheless find a meaningful connection with participation understood as a methodological condition, particularly through the educational missions it assigns itself, as illustrated by recent developments in social semiotics\.

## [Integrasi Generative AI dalam Pendidikan Arsitektur: Model Tata Kelola Pembelajaran Berbasis Proyek untuk Literasi AI, Integritas Akademik, dan Kreativitas Desain](../publications/f43181def2e7ad3964ef.md)

Zumrotul Avifa K

Perkembangan generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) telah mengubah cara mahasiswa arsitektur memperoleh informasi, mengembangkan gagasan, menghasilkan visual, dan menyusun karya akademik\. ## [Fishbone diagram strategy in algebraic word\-problem instruction: senior high school students’ achievement and perceptions](../publications/f432c4ad08968b51c5f4.md)

Asare Charles; Innocent Akpage; Daniel Aboagye; Isaac Davor

Algebraic word problems continue to pose significant challenges for senior high school students due to difficulties in interpreting problem statements, identifying mathematical relationships, and applying appropriate solution strategies\. This study examined achievement differences between students taught algebraic word problems using the Fishbone Diagram Strategy and those taught using the conventional method and examined students’ perceptions of the strategy\. A quasi\-experimental pre\-test\-post\-test non\-equivalent control group design was employed with 128 Senior High School students, comprising 64 students in the experimental group and 64 students in the control group\. The experimental group received instruction using the Fishbone Diagram Strategy, while the control group was taught using the conventional method over six weeks\. Data were collected using an Algebraic Word Problems Achievement Test and a perception questionnaire\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney U tests, Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank tests, ANCOVA, and an ANCOVA applied to ranked scores as a sensitivity analysis\. After controlling for pre\-test achievement, ANCOVA revealed a statistically significant difference in adjusted post\-test achievement between the instructional groups, F\(1, 125\) = 44\.673, p &lt; \.001, partial η 2 = \.263, favouring the experimental group\. The findings suggest that the Fishbone Diagram Strategy is a promising learner\-centered instructional approach that was associated with higher achievement and positive learning experiences in algebraic word problem solving among the participating students\.

## [Emergency Medicine Reimagined: Development of the Patient Rights Index for Emergency Medicine](../publications/f443188f33fa7aca9ec7.md)

Matthew Ryan

Introduction: Emergency medicine has evolved beyond episodic acute care to encompass a growing range of clinical, social, and system\-level responsibilities\. This scholarly perspective proposes the Patient Rights Index in Emergency Medicine \(PRI\-ED\), a conceptual framework designed to organize recurring domains through which emergency departments promote access to care, patient safety, relief of suffering, autonomy, and dignity\. Methods: The PRI\-ED was developed through iterative domain generation informed by clinical observation, professional experience, and targeted review of peer\-reviewed literature, policy analyses, and professional organizational reports\. No primary data collection, systematic review, formal consensus process, or empirical validation was performed\. Results: We identified 12 domains that represent recurring clinical, operational, and system\-level challenges encountered in emergency medicine\. These domains were organized within a standardized framework linking domain\-specific objectives, intervention strategies, measurable indicators, and relevant policy or funding mechanisms\. Conclusion: The PRI\-ED is a proposed conceptual framework for organizing and evaluating domains in which emergency medicine intersects with access, safety, autonomy, relief of suffering, and dignity\. The framework is intended to inform future implementation, evaluation, and policy discussion and requires feasibility testing and outcome validation before effectiveness can be determined\.

## [ANÁLISE TEMPORAL E DISTRIBUIÇÃO ESPACIAL DAS CICATRIZES DE FOGO NO ESTADO DO AMAPÁ \(1985–2024\)](../publications/f45117e084aabd87bd42.md)

Yago Rian Almeida Costa; Mariana Martins Medeiros de Santana; Fernando Galvão Rabelo; Rodrigo Nogueira de Vasconcelos; Washington De Jesus Sant&\#x27;anna Franca Rocha

O estado do Amapá destaca\-se no cenário amazônico como a unidade federativa com o mais elevado índice de preservação florestal da Amazônia Legal\. Neste contexto, compreender a dinâmica temporal e espacial das cicatrizes de fogo é fundamental para subsidiar estratégias de manejo e políticas públicas de prevenção\. Este estudo analisou a distribuição temporal e espacial das cicatrizes de fogo no Amapá entre 1985 e 2024, utilizando dados da Coleção 5 do MapBiomas Fogo\. A metodologia integrou testes de normalidade \(Shapiro\-Wilk\), comparação entre décadas \(ANOVA\), detecção de tendências \(Mann\-Kendall\), avaliação da influência do El Niño \(teste t\) e análise de autocorrelação \(ACF e PACF\)\. Para a análise espacial, foram elaborados mapas temáticos das cicatrizes de fogo para os períodos de 1985\-1994, 1995\-2004, 2005\-2014 e 2015\-2024\. O teste de Shapiro\-Wilk confirmou a normalidade dos dados \(W = 0,9663; p = 0,274\), enquanto a ANOVA não revelou diferenças significativas entre as médias decadais \(F = 2,17; p = 0,108\)\. No entanto, o teste de Mann\-Kendall detectou tendência significativa de aumento \(τ = 0,2513; p = 0,0231\), com crescimento de 73% na média decadal\. A análise ACF/PACF revelou dependência temporal significativa, com autocorrelação positiva em lag 1 \(ρ₁ ≈ 0,35\), indicando &quot;memória&quot; do sistema\. Apesar de alguns anos de maior área queimada terem coincidido com eventos de El Niño, não foi observada diferença estatisticamente significativa\. Espacialmente, os mapas revelaram expansão progressiva do fogo, inicialmente restrito às savanas \(1985\-1994\), avançando para áreas de floresta na última década \(2015\-2024\)\. Conclui\-se que o Amapá enfrenta um cenário de intensificação do fogo, com expansão geográfica e pressão sobre ecossistemas sensíveis\.

## [Clinical manifestations, genetic characteristics and laboratory markers of patients with epidermolysis bullosa: a single tertiary referral center experience](../publications/f45307fe343f2598d3fd.md)

Tubanur Çetinarslan; Abdullah Kutay Masat; Şule Altıner; Işıl İnanır

Background Epidermolysis bullosa \(EB\) is a group of genetically and clinically heterogeneous diseases that presents as blisters, erosions, crusts, and scars\.Materials and Method In this retrospective study, we report the clinical manifestations, genetic characteristics, and laboratory markers of patients with EB\.Results Fifteen patients with EB were included in the study\. The most common type was dystrophic EB \(DEB\) \(n = 10\), followed by EB simplex \(EBS\) \(n = 3\), junctional EB \(JEB\) \(n = 1\), and Kindler EB \(n = 1\)\. The disease onset was from birth in 13 patients\. The most common cutaneous manifestations were erosions \(n = 12\), vesicles and bullae \(n = 8\), scars \(n = 6\), and milia \(n = 6\)\. Nail abnormalities were observed in 11 patients and mucosal involvement in seven patients\. The most common genetic mutation was COL7A1 gene mutation \(n = 10\), followed by PLEC \(n = 2\), ITGB4 \(n = 1\), KRT5 \(n = 1\), and FERMT1 \(n = 1\)\. Laboratory examination revealed iron deficiency in 10 patients\. One patient had moderate vitamin D deficiency, and five had mild vitamin D deficiency\.Conclusion EB is a genetic disease that may associated with many systemic comorbidities\. Multidisciplinary management of wound care is essential for the early management of severe EB to avoid wound progression into scars and deformities\. The levels of vitamins such as ferritin and zinc, and the levels of hemoglobin and albumin, should be optimal levels to optimize wound healing\.

## [Predicting U\.S\. migration flows with online search data](../publications/f45550d7de1c9bbb578b.md)

Jaeyong Yoo; Patryk Babiarz

Residential mobility shapes labor markets, housing demand, infrastructure needs, and regional development in the United States\. Policymakers rely on official migration data to monitor population movements, but these data are often released after the underlying moves have occurred\. Because many households search online for jobs, housing, cost of living, schools, climate, and other destination\-specific information before moving, online search activity may provide early signals of migration interest\. This study examines whether Google Trends data improve the prediction of U\.S\. interstate migration flows\. Using Internal Revenue Service state\-to\-state migration records and Google Trends data for all 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2004 to 2018, the study estimates gravity\-based panel models of unilateral out\-migration and bilateral origin\-destination flows\. The results show that migration\-related search intensity is associated with subsequent migration flows and improves predictive performance beyond conventional gravity\-model covariates and fixed effects\. These findings suggest that Google Trends data can serve as a timely complement to administrative migration records\. Search data do not replace official statistics, but they can help identify emerging migration patterns before administrative data become available\.

## [Nutritional strategies for bone stress injury prevention in military trainees: historical evolution, current evidence, and future directions](../publications/f457a421c902b78bd72b.md)

Nicole M\. Sekel; Stefan M\. Pasiakos

Bone stress injuries exist along a continuum from stress reactions to stress fractures\. They carry prolonged recovery times, high recurrence risk, and substantial economic burden, and they pose a direct threat to military readiness\. Nutritional status modifies injury susceptibility by influencing skeletal adaptation to mechanical loading, bone modeling and remodeling, and structural integrity\. Yet the historical evolution and effectiveness of nutritional policies intended to reduce the bone stress injury prevalence in the military remain poorly understood\. In this narrative review, we critically evaluate that evidence base and subsequently propose novel strategies to mitigate injury risk and promote skeletal resilience in military personnel\.

## [PEDAGOGIK PARADIGMALARNING O‘ZGARISHI VA O‘ZARO MUNOSABATI: NAZARIY\-METODOLOGIK TAHLIL](../publications/f47bc3736d2e1cd2a556.md)

Sokina To‘xtayeva

The article analyzes the scientific and philosophical content of the concept of “pedagogical paradigm”, the internal regularities of the historical change of pedagogical paradigms, and their interrelation\. The aim of the study is to substantiate the concepts of “paradigmatic pluralism” and “pedagogical synthesis” through a conceptual analysis of this change and interrelation\. Comparative\-historical, conceptual, systemic, and hermeneutic methods were applied\. The possibilities and limitations of transferring T\. Kuhn’s theory of scientific paradigms to pedagogy are substantiated, and the stages of transition from the epistemological paradigm to the humanistic and then the competence\-based \(pragmatic\) paradigm are described\. Three regularities of paradigm change in pedagogy are identified \- gradual change, paradigmatic multilayeredness, and selective synthesis \- and five types of interrelation between paradigms are classified\. It is concluded that pedagogical paradigms do not completely replace one another but develop through integrative harmonization, while pedagogical synthesis, unlike eclecticism, is a theoretically grounded integration\.

## [Perceptions of Robotic Car Wash Systems in Maharashtra: A Study of Economic Feasibility, Sustainability, and Cultural Familiarity](../publications/f490b2281b73d9e17f2e.md)

Shiv Mehta

Due to an increase in car ownership and purchase in Maharashtra, there has been a very high growth in the number of people demanding car washes in this state\. Most of these are highly dependent on the use of conventional techniques in car washing, which causes heavy consumption of water along with its wastage\. For promoting sustainable solutions, the use of automated car washing systems using high\-pressure air as a substitute for water is being suggested\. However, there is still insufficient literature about the cultural perceptions of automated car\-washing technology\. This is a qualitative\-dominant mixed\-method research based on the phenomenological approach and has been conducted on 80 individuals living in Maharashtra and ten informal car washers by using interviews and survey techniques\. This research identifies socio\-cultural and economic factors as well as consumer perceptions that significantly affect the adoption of such technologies\. The gap between the creation of sustainable innovations and the local socioeconomic circumstances has allowed the research to add to the ongoing discussion about sustainable services and water consumption\. The cost aspect becomes a determining factor \(and an obstacle\) for many consumers in adopting the new technology of automatic car washing\. The worries about the effectiveness of the automated process \(one lacking the custom service provision\) become another constraint in that regard\. This research shows that in order to successfully adopt sustainable service technologies, one needs both technical effectiveness and cost effectiveness\.

## [A multi\-stage validation framework for trustworthy large\-scale clinical information extraction using large language models](../publications/f49b7ee8b12bf5cd396a.md)

Maria Mahbub; Gregory M\. Dams; Josh Arnold; Caitlin Rizy; Sudarshan Srinivasan; Elliot M\. Fielstein; M\. Aghevli; Kamonica Craig; Elizabeth M\. Oliva; Joseph Erdos; Jodie A\. Trafton; Ioana Danciu

Abstract Large language models \(LLMs\) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real\-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches\. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation\-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population\-scale use\. We propose a multi\-stage validation framework for LLM\-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies\. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule\-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge\-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation\. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder \(SUD\) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes\. Rule\-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14\.59% of LLM\-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible\. For high\-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert\. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0\.80\. LLM\-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured\-data baselines\. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human\-in\-the\-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM\-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation\.

## [Strengthening Pre\-Service Teachers’ Professionalism through School Field Introduction: A Case Study at SMAN 4 Sidrap, Indonesia](../publications/f4a1d0a1c9036d0df91d.md)

Kamal Kamal; Nurlela Nurlela; Andi Dwi Resqi; Fitriani N; Sam Hermansyah; Nurul Syahrani; Nur Ikhsaniah

Developing pre\-service teachers’ professionalism is essential for preparing competent, reflective, and adaptable educators capable of responding to the evolving demands of contemporary education\. School Field Introduction \(Pengenalan Lapangan Persekolahan, PLP 1\) provides prospective teachers with opportunities to experience authentic school environments and develop an understanding of professional teaching responsibilities\. This study aims to explore how School Field Introduction contributes to strengthening pre\-service teachers’ professionalism, character development, understanding of school ecosystems, and awareness of digital literacy and artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education\. The study focuses on the implementation of PLP 1 at SMAN 4 Sidrap, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, involving fifth\-semester students from the Faculty of Teacher Training and Education, Universitas Muhammadiyah Sidenreng Rappang\. The program was conducted through orientation, school\-based observation, academic mentoring, reflective discussions, and evaluation activities\. Data sources included observation records, students’ reflective journals, field reports, and documentation of mentoring activities\. The findings indicate that participation in School Field Introduction provided meaningful contextual learning experiences that strengthened students’ understanding of school culture, educational management, teacher responsibilities, and interpersonal interactions within the school environment\. Furthermore, the program supported the development of professional attitudes, particularly discipline, responsibility, communication, collaboration, ethical awareness, and reflective thinking\. Exposure to digital technologies and AI\-related educational practices also encouraged participants to recognize the importance of responsible technology integration in professional teaching\. However, the relatively limited implementation period restricted opportunities for more extensive professional engagement\. The study concludes that School Field Introduction represents a valuable experiential learning approach for fostering pre\-service teachers’ professional identity, pedagogical awareness, and readiness for future teaching careers\. Systematic mentoring, reflective learning, and digital competency development are recommended to enhance the effectiveness of school\-based teacher education programs\.

## [Bat\-borne zoonoses: transmission, impact, prevention, and management](../publications/f4aa9aa7a14e3f4d2015.md)

Jessica Stanhope; Wayne S J Boardman; Christopher Burrell; Peng Bi; Philip Weinstein

Abstract Climate change and biodiversity loss are global environmental crises driving emerging infectious diseases, including bat\-borne pathogens of public health significance: Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, classic rabies virus, and Australian bat lyssavirus, as well as the fungus Histoplasma \. This review presents the evidence on the mechanisms of transmission, impact, and prevention and management strategies relevant to each of these pathogens\. Transmission pathways vary between pathogens but often involve exposure to body fluids or excreta of a bat or other infected animal or human\. The diseases associated with these infections have high mortality rates, and survivors may continue to experience a range of long term effects, including neurological and neuropsychiatric signs and symptoms\. Prevention strategies may be implemented to reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover and human\-to\-human transmission of these pathogens, including better ecological stewardship, reducing exposure of domestic animals and humans to bats, isolation of infected people, and, where possible, vaccination of humans and animals\. The mainstay of treatment for these conditions is supportive care; however, specific drugs are now available for histoplasmosis and Ebolavirus infection\. In the face of climate change and further loss of biodiversity, developing more effective strategies to prevent and manage these conditions will be critical\.

## [Differential risk and protective factors for conventional adenomas and serrated lesions: implications for colorectal cancer prevention](../publications/f4ad98fb4690340c6ca7.md)

蔡俊杰; Yiliu Huang; Yi Luo; Hui Zeng; Jun Yang; 朱英双

Conventional adenomas and serrated lesions are two major precursor lesions of colorectal cancer\. They arise through distinct carcinogenic pathways, namely the conventional adenoma–carcinoma sequence and the serrated neoplasia pathway\. These pathways differ substantially in their underlying molecular mechanisms, implying that the risk factor profiles for the two types of lesions may be different\. However, existing evidence remains fragmented, and an integrated comparative synthesis of these differential associations is lacking\. In this review, we synthesize and compare current evidence on the mechanistic characteristics and lifestyle, metabolic, and nutritional determinants of conventional adenomas and serrated lesions\. By synthesizing the available evidence on the two precursor pathways, this review may contribute to a better understanding of conventional adenomas and serrated lesions, and offer insights for future research into their distinct risk factors, underlying mechanisms, and implications for colorectal cancer prevention\.

## [Lycium barbarum polysaccharides alleviate cadmium\-induced renal injury in ducks by activating the Nrf2\-mediated antioxidant defense pathway](../publications/f4af8e96d0606337ecb6.md)

Xueru Wang; Dongdi Liu; Yonggang Ma; Hui Zou; Xishuai Tong; Jiaqiao Zhu; Ruilong Song; Hongyan Zhao; Zongping Liu

Cadmium \(Cd\) is a widespread environmental contaminant related to renal immunosuppression and metabolic dysfunction\. Lycium barbarum polysaccharides \(LBPs\) are active extracts of wolfberry and possess a variety of excellent properties\. However, the specific mechanism of action for Cd and LBP remain unclear\. In the present study, Shaoxing ducks were used to establish an in vivo model to elucidate the effects of combined Cd and LBP exposure on the kidneys and the underlying mechanisms\. The ducks were exposed to CdCl 2 \(50 mg/kg\) and/or LBP \(50 mg/kg\) for 30 days\. We observed that Cd exposure increased the kidney index and the levels of the renal function indicators CREA and UA\. Further research revealed that Cd exposure caused histopathological damage and ultrastructural alterations\. In addition, Cd accumulation induced oxidative stress by disrupting ionic homeostasis and inhibiting the Nrf2\-mediated antioxidant defense pathway\. Finally, we found that Cd promoted lipid accumulation, disrupted lipid metabolism, and thereby induced renal immunosuppression\. Notably, LBP effectively alleviated Cd\-induced renal injury, suggesting beneficial effects against Cd\-triggered nephrotoxicity\.

## [AMS\-LPP: adaptive model selection for lightfastness property prediction in textile materials using similarity\-guided transfer learning and AutoML](../publications/f4b026edb7c1fde6c5c0.md)

Murad Ali Khan; Muhammad Faseeh; Syed Shehryar Ali Naqvi; Do\-Hyeun Kim

Abstract Accurate material property prediction can accelerate materials discovery, but conventional experimental methods remain costly and time\-intensive, and machine learning alternatives are often degraded by domain shifts across heterogeneous datasets\. Transfer Learning \(TL\) is effective only when source and target domains are similar, while AutoML ignores inter\-domain relationships entirely, so neither approach alone adapts to varying domain similarity\. This paper proposes AMS\-LPP, a similarity\-guided framework that dynamically switches between TL and AutoML based on domain similarity quantified via Mahalanobis distance: a pretrained TabNet model is fine\-tuned with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization under high similarity, while AutoML is invoked under low similarity to ensure robust generalization\. Experiments on multi\-domain textile datasets for lightfastness prediction show that TL achieves $$R^2 &gt; 0\.99$$ with up to 35% less training time under high and moderate similarity, while AutoML attains the best generalization \( $$R^2 = 0\.998$$ \) under low similarity\. SHAP\-based explainability further shows predictions are driven by physically meaningful optical and color\-related features\. These results demonstrate that AMS\-LPP provides a scalable, efficient, and interpretable solution for similarity\-aware model selection in heterogeneous material property prediction\.

Ying Zhou; Mengting Liu

Cross\-dataset EEG decoding often treats montage, reference, and active\-sensor changes as representation shift, although they also alter the observation operator\. We study target\-statistics\-blind transfer: fitting receives no target signal, label, or empirical statistic, and electrode coordinates only instantiate a fixed prediction operator\. method removes the active\-set common\-reference gauge and transports each native mask through a template motor leadfield\. A source\-fitted spectral classifier anchors the decision; a bounded state\-space\-model \(SSM\) residual is secondary\. We establish restricted identifiability and an operator\-perturbation bound\. Across five leave\-one\-dataset\-out targets \(253 participants\), dynamic method achieved 60\.865% equal\-target balanced accuracy versus 52\.684% for strict\-clean 5/5 BIOT \(hierarchical difference \+8\.182 points; 95% CI \+6\.382 to \+10\.196; positive in every target\)\. On four EEGPT\-clean targets, the descriptive means were 61\.520% and 59\.057%\. In four post\-hoc exact same\-parent tests, FULL exceeded coordinate\-basis, matched\-spectrum, row\-shuffled, and wrong\-anatomy controls by 9\.959, 9\.698, 11\.241, and 3\.985 points, respectively \(all 95% CIs excluded zero; Holm\-adjusted P&lt;0\.001\)\. ## [Cellular Senescence in Orthodontic Tooth Movement: Biological Mechanisms, Clinical Implications and Future Perspectives](../publications/f4b9e35ed1fd6f38ea26.md)



Aging, inflammation, and tissue remodeling are all impacted by cellular senescence, a biological process marked by irreversible cell\-cycle halt and the emergence of a senescence\-associated secretory phenotype \(SASP\)\.Senescence may have an impact on the results of orthodontic tooth movement \(OTM\) and plays a major role in oral health, according to mounting research\.With a focus on periodontal ligament remodeling, alveolar bone metabolism, and tissue responses to mechanical pressures, this review investigates the molecular mechanisms connecting cellular senescence to orthodontic treatment\.Pro\-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, matrix\-degrading enzymes, and extracellular vesicles are released by senescent cells, which together change the local microenvironment and upset the equilibrium between bone formation and resorption\.Slower tooth movement, longer treatment times, poor tissue regeneration, and heightened vulnerability to negative consequences including root resorption and periodontal problems can all be caused by the age\-related buildup of senescent cells in periodontal tissues\.Additionally, recent research shows how aging affects osteoblast, osteoclast, and osteocyte function, which in turn affects orthodontic biomechanics and treatment prediction\.Promising prospects for enhancing treatment results and creating individualized orthodontic treatments are presented by new research on senescence biomarkers and senotherapeutic techniques, such as senolytic and senomorphic drugs\.Clinical orthodontics may be better equipped to incorporate biologically informed treatment planning if the molecular mechanisms behind cellular senescence are well understood\.To elucidate the direct connection between senescence and OTM and to convert these discoveries into successful treatment therapies, more research is required\.

## [Permission Granted? Navigating AI Use in Graduate Speech\-Language Pathology Education](../publications/f4bd7dcedc700077316e.md)

Megann McGill; Ana Rivera Rodriguez; Alayna Townsend; Kelly Roy; Christine E\. Fiestas

The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly generative AI \(GenAI\), is transforming higher education and raising important questions about its role in graduate professional training\. Speech\-language pathology \(SLP\) programs face the dual challenge of preparing students to engage with AI technologies that are increasingly present in clinical and academic environments while also safeguarding academic integrity, ethical practice, and skill development\. This tutorial paper describes the development and delivery of a one\-hour, synchronous virtual AI training created for graduate students in a hybrid online Master of Science in SLP program at the University of St\. Augustine for Health Sciences\. The training was developed by a faculty\-led AI Task Force and was designed to improve students’ AI literacy, clarify institutional and course\-level AI policies, and promote responsible and ethical AI engagement\. The training content included: \(1\) foundational definitions of AI and distinguishing GenAI from AI assistants, \(2\) orientation to university AI resources and policies for allowable use, \(3\) description of a checklist designed to scaffold ethical decision\-making, \(4\) explicit instruction on key risks associated with AI use, including hallucinations, bias, privacy concerns, and potential skill attrition, \(5\) AI applications to support student learning, research, clinical preparation, and time management, and \(6\) interactive application of AI knowledge to clinical and academic scenarios\. By describing the case study and sharing accompanying resources, this manuscript offers a practical framework for SLP programs seeking to proactively address AI integration in graduate education\. AI literacy training can help graduate SLP programs move beyond reactive policy development toward intentional, transparent, and ethically grounded AI engagement that supports both student learning and professional competence\.

## [Stress and self\-efficacy under artificial intelligence disruption: A mixed\-methods study on the usage of artificial intelligence among Finnish workers](../publications/f4bf8e92057d5f3a4246.md)

Atte Oksanen; Teo Keipi; Moona Heiskari; Iina Savolainen

Rapid workplace integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping work practices and challenging employees’ self\-efficacy and well\-being\. This mixed\-methods study examines these experiences using national survey data \( N = 2109\) and qualitative interviews \( N = 54\) with Finnish workers\. Frequent AI use, AI\-induced identity threat, and organizational AI deployment are associated with higher AI strain, whereas AI self\-efficacy relates to frequent use, positive AI attitudes, and subjective well\-being\. Identity threat moderated several of these associations, highlighting the role of professional identity in AI\-related experiences\. Analysis drawing on Greimas’ semiotic modalities \(must, can, know, and want\) explains how these patterns are interpreted and negotiated in practice, revealing tensions between perceived self\-efficacy and pressures to integrate AI\. AI use was often described as voluntary\. However, participants anticipated increasing competence demands and responsibility\. The findings emphasize the need for organizational strategies that address identity\-related challenges and support employee well\-being in AI\-driven work transformations\.

## [Dijitalleşmenin Vergi İdaresinin Dönüşümüne Etkisi: Türkiye’den Kanıtlar](../publications/f4cca425825265c481c8.md)

İsmail Koç

Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de vergi idaresinin dijitalleşme sürecinin ulaştığı düzeyi, kurumsal dönüşümü ve temel eğilimleri ortaya koymayı amaçlamaktadır\. Dijital vergi uygulamalarının hızla yaygınlaşması, vergi idaresinin yalnızca elektronik hizmet sunan bir yapıdan veri temelli ve bütünleşik bir yönetime doğru dönüşmesini önemli bir araştırma konusu hâline getirmiştir\. Araştırmada nitel doküman incelemesi ile nicel betimsel eğilim analizi birlikte kullanılmış; Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığının 2006–2025 dönemi faaliyet raporları, 2021–2025 teknoloji göstergeleri ve ISORA’nın 2018–2024 Türkiye verileri incelenmiştir\. Bulgular, elektronik beyanname oranlarının KDV, kurumlar vergisi ve gelir vergisinde yaklaşık %100’e ulaştığını ve kâğıt beyannamelerin belirgin biçimde azaldığını göstermektedir\. Ayrıca 2016–2025 döneminde e\-Fatura, e\-Arşiv Fatura ve e\-Tebligat hacimlerinde; 2015–2025 döneminde ise e\-Defter ve e\-Fatura kullanıcı sayılarında yüksek oranlı artışlar gerçekleşmiştir\. Sanal POS işlemleri ve veri ambarı kapasitesindeki yükseliş de dijital altyapının önemli ölçüde genişlediğini göstermektedir\.

## [Inteligencia artificial y rúbricas para la generación de instrumentos de evaluación](../publications/f4d5482f02e4bd03f303.md)

Azahara Casanova Pistón; Patricia Sáenz\-Valiente

The use of rubrics in Higher Education has become established as a key strategy for improving learning assessment by providing clear criteria, promoting transparency, and facilitating student self\-regulation\. The incorporation of ICT has enabled their evolution expanding their possibilities for use and analysis, although it has also raised concerns related to privacy and data security when online environments are used\. In this context, the design of automated assessment instruments capable of functioning offline is proposed in order to guarantee the protection of students’ information\. Based on a literature review, a proposal is developed using spreadsheets, for the creation of two types of rubrics: one focused on grading and another aimed at generating feedback\. Automation is achieved through the use of formulas, macros, and Visual Basic programming, making it possible to streamline the assessment process and reduce teachers’ workload\. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence through prompting techniques facilitates code generation, the expansion of comments, and the improvement of feedback writing, increasing its personalization and coherence\. These tools make it possible to build more efficient, adaptive, and secure assessment systems, although they require an adequate level of teachers’ digital competence\. The possibility of integrating both rubrics into a single system and exploring solutions that combine the advantages of offline environments with guarantees for data management in digital settings are proposed as future lines of development\.

## [Beyond Fun: Gamified Multidomain Reading Assessment for Children](../publications/f4da77b7fe30424d1dda.md)

Angela Pasqualotto; Manon Bochud; Jessy Damas; Zeno Menestrina; Irène Altarelli; Martina Röthlisberger; Johannes Christoph Ziegler; Pascal Zesiger; Silvia Brem; Daphné Bavelier

This study presents the Computerized Reading\-related Assessment Battery \(CRAB\), a multidomain, child\-centered tablet platform designed to support scalable, school\-based assessment of linguistic and cognitive skills relevant to early reading\. We report results from a large\-scale school administration of CRAB to 310 second\-grade children in France and Italy, implemented in school settings with minimal adult supervision\. Feasibility was assessed through task\-by\-task completion rates and system\-logged durations: completion was high across tasks \(93–100%\), and task durations were developmentally appropriate \(median 2\.6–7\.5 min\)\. Usability and engagement were examined using embedded child\-friendly questionnaires and post\-assessment focus\-group feedback; children rated the battery as enjoyable and easy to use, and qualitative responses highlighted intuitive interaction and effective onboarding\. We also report task performance patterns showing that associations among CRAB outcomes were consistent with theoretically expected relationships across reading, reading\-related, and cognitive measures, supporting coherent functioning across the battery within a unified digital environment\. Constraints were concentrated in speech\-based tasks, reflecting ongoing challenges for speech input technologies with young children\. Overall, findings demonstrate the feasibility of implementing a multidomain, gamified assessment in authentic school contexts and provide empirically grounded design principles for scalable serious game–based digital assessment in education\.

## [Annealed leap\-point sampler for multimodal target distributions](../publications/f4db7bee78c446cc2a06.md)

Nicholas G\. Tawn; Matthew T\. Moores; Hugo Queniat; Gareth O\. Roberts

Abstract In Bayesian statistics, exploring high\-dimensional multimodal posterior distributions poses major challenges for existing MCMC approaches\. This paper introduces the annealed leap\-point sampler \(ALPS\), which augments the target distribution state space with modified annealed \(cooled\) distributions, in contrast to traditional tempering approaches\. The coldest state is chosen such that its annealed density is well\-approximated locally by a Laplace approximation\. This allows for automated setup of a scalable mode\-leaping independence sampler\. ALPS requires an exploration component to search for the mode locations, which can either be run adaptively in parallel to improve these mode\-jumping proposals, or else as a pre\-computation step\. A theoretical analysis shows that for a d\-dimensional problem the coolest temperature level required only needs to be linear in dimension, $$\\mathcal \{O\}\\left\( d\\right\) $$ O d , implying that the number of iterations needed for ALPS to converge is $$\\mathcal \{O\}\\left\( d\\right\) $$ O d \(typically leading to overall complexity $$\\mathcal \{O\}\\left\( d^3\\right\) $$ O d 3 when computational cost per iteration is taken into account\)\. ALPS is illustrated on several complex, multimodal distributions that arise from real\-world applications\. This includes a seemingly\-unrelated regression \(SUR\) model of longitudinal data from U\.S\. manufacturing firms, as well as a spectral density model that is used in analytical chemistry for identification of molecular biomarkers\.

## [From data\-driven prediction to closed\-loop intelligent bioconversion: A framework for artificial intelligence in organic solid waste treatment](../publications/f4e5c23d20641d29639f.md)

Zhonghao He; Zixin Zhang; Ci Song; Aodong Peng; Jiangfang Yu; Haoran Dong; Leyuan Fang; Qiqi Fu; Lin Tang; Jing Tang

Organic solid waste \(OSW\) bioconversion has become a key strategy for converting biodegradable wastes into renewable energy, stabilized products, and recoverable nutrients\. However, aerobic composting and anaerobic digestion are inherently dynamic and heterogeneous biological processes, where substrate variability, microbial succession, mass transfer, process instability, and greenhouse gas emissions complicate reliable operation\. Current AI applications span methane\-yield and compost\-maturity prediction, soft sensing, process optimization, digital twins, and simulation\-based control modeling\. Nevertheless, most existing applications remain confined to prediction, optimization, or advisory functions and lack direct integration with on\-site physical feedback\. In this critical review, we systematically evaluate the current capability distribution and deployment maturity of AI\-enabled OSW bioconversion, while distinguishing demonstrated implementations from a proposed pathway toward closed\-loop operational intelligence\. Among 85 direct AI/model implementation studies, 38 primarily addressed prediction, diagnosis, or soft sensing, 36 addressed optimization or advisory decision support, and 11 addressed simulation\-based control modeling; none demonstrated supervisory/semi\-autonomous or fully closed\-loop operation on physical OSW\-bioconversion equipment\. Particular attention is paid to process\-state representation, mechanism\-informed interpretation, sensing infrastructure, predictive and optimization models, deployment maturity, and the persistent gap between model outputs and implementable control actions\. We further propose a normative cyber–physical framework that integrates multi\-source sensing, state reconstruction, world modeling, decision optimization, actuation, and feedback updating\. This review reframes AI in OSW bioconversion as an engineering tool for carbon mitigation, nutrient recovery, and circular waste infrastructure rather than only a means of improving prediction accuracy\.

## [Artificial intelligence‐assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long‐term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain](../publications/f4ea8020d83d9684654b.md)

Daniel Mansilla D\.; Jesper Tveit; Harald Aurlien; Tamir Avigdor; Chifaou Abdallah; Pilar Bosque‐Varela; Melita Čačić Hribljan; Victoria Ros‐Castelló; Donald L\. Schomer; Jean Gotman; Sándor Beniczky; Birgit Frauscher

OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) classifies routine electroencephalograms \(EEGs\) with expert\-level accuracy, but interpretation of long\-term EEG monitoring \(LTM\) remains reliant on time\-intensive visual review\. We evaluated whether autoSCORE, a clinically approved implementation of SCORE\-AI integrated into an EEG reader, achieves expert\-level diagnostic accuracy for LTM interpretation and whether expert\-supervised use reduces review time versus conventional analysis\. METHODS: A fixed\-and\-frozen AI model was tested on an independent single\-center dataset of 78 adult patient LTM recordings \(52 normal, 26 abnormal\), with epilepsy monitoring unit discharge diagnosis as the external reference standard\. The AI model was benchmarked against two expert panels \(three readers each\); Panel 1 reviewed autoSCORE EEG detections \(hybrid approach\), and Panel 2 interpreted full recordings \(conventional approach\)\. Diagnostic accuracy and time to diagnostic decision were assessed for fully automated, hybrid, and conventional approaches\. Interrater reliability \(Gwet&\#x27;s AC1\) was evaluated for hybrid and conventional interpretation\. RESULTS: Interrater reliability was significantly higher for hybrid than conventional approach \(AC1 = \.81, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] = \.73\-\.89 vs\. AC1 = \.43, 95% CI = \.32\-\.53; p &lt; \.001\)\. Review time was markedly reduced \(median \[interquartile range \(IQR\)\] = 2\.2 \[\.5\-4\.3\] vs\. 52\.4 \[33\.2\-62\.9\] min, mean \[95% CI\] = 2\.9 \[2\.5\-3\.2\] vs\. 50\.8 \[46\.5\-55\.2\] min, p &lt; \.001\), a 95\.8% median reduction \(IQR = 95\.6\-96\.3\)\. Diagnostic performance comparisons were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm\-Bonferroni procedure across all 63 tests\. The hybrid approach showed significantly higher sensitivity than conventional interpretation \(\.88, 95% CI = \.77\-\.97 vs\. \.69, 95% CI = \.57\-\.81; adjusted p = \.006\)\. Its numerically higher diagnostic accuracy versus conventional interpretation \(\.75, 95% CI = \.66\-\.83 vs\. \.68, 95% CI = \.61\-\.74\) was nonsignificant after correction \(adjusted p &gt; \.99\)\. Hybrid approach diagnostic accuracy was significantly greater than fully automated analysis \(\.75, 95% CI = \.66\-\.83 vs\. \.55, 95% CI = \.44\-\.65; adjusted p &lt; \.001\)\. SIGNIFICANCE: Expert oversight of AI\-assisted categorization of interictal epileptiform and nonepileptiform EEG abnormalities improves interrater reliability and efficiency, increases diagnostic sensitivity versus conventional interpretation, and increases diagnostic accuracy versus fully automated analysis in adult LTM\.

## [Shaping relational value in linear cultural heritage through green open spaces: insights from the Grand Canal](../publications/f50706a6399bbed9c4fa.md)

Muye Jiang; Shiyang Zhang; Zhouqi Shen; Haochen Sun; Jingrui Zhao

Abstract The focus of sustainable heritage development has shifted from the isolated preservation of physical vestiges to the continuous construction of symbiotic relationships among the heritage, the public, and the environment\. As critical areas for such interactions, green open spaces facilitate the cultivation of relational values\. Drawing upon the Historic Urban Landscape \(HUL\) perspective and the Cultural Values Model \(CVM\), this study establishes an interpretative indicator framework encompassing the forms, practices, and relations of green open spaces along linear cultural heritage\. Utilizing the Chinese\-BERT\-wwm model, we analysed 85,244 social media posts across 61 green open spaces along the Grand Canal, achieving an average classification accuracy of 91\.20%\. The findings indicate that: \(1\) aesthetic appreciation remained the most prominent relational value, while historical value exhibits the strongest spatial heterogeneity and has increased overall over the decade following the World Heritage inscription; \(2\) three spatial typologies were identified through hierarchical clustering: the Heritage Identity and Memory Category, the Eco\-Aesthetic Appreciation Category, and the Social Interaction Engagement Category; \(3\) at the level of green open spaces, historical value is enhanced by viewing activities, while social interaction is driven by consumption activities\. Although vegetation and water bodies foster aesthetic appreciation, canal\-related water bodies exhibit an inhibitory effect on it\. Conversely, at the individual level, canal\-related water bodies serve as core anchors for historical value and sense of place\. By operationalizing relational values into four observable dimensions—historical value, aesthetic appreciation, sense of place, and social interaction—the research establishes a robust and transferable theoretical and methodological framework\. This approach not only elucidates the catalytic role of green open spaces in enhancing relational values within linear cultural heritage but also provides evidence\-based practical recommendations that bridge theoretical significance and management practice for global linear cultural heritage\.

## [Fauché, Nicolas: Bohm’s Implicate Order and the Persistence of Consciousness: Toward a Cosmopsychist Framework](../publications/f51e5d64b46e7eeec112.md)



The nature of consciousness remains one of the major unresolved problems in the philosophy of mind\. This article explores the hypothesis that consciousness may not be reducible to brain activity, but could instead constitute a manifestation of a more fundamental level of reality\. Drawing on the double\-aspect monism and David Bohm’s theory of the implicate order, we examine a conception of reality in which observable phenomena emerge from a deeper, relational and dynamic structure\. The process algebra developed by Bohm and Hiley further suggests that physical entities can be understood as relatively stable structures emerging from an underlying process rather than as fundamentally independent objects\. This framework is then applied to consciousness through a dialogue with Integrated Information Theory and the physics of emergent phenomena\. We propose the concept of a “consciousness particle”, understood not as a fundamental particle in the standard physical sense, but as a stable dynamical organization whose identity depends on its underlying structure rather than on the persistence of its material constituents\. Within the implicate\-order framework, the disappearance of such a structure from the explicate order could potentially be interpreted as a transition into the implicate order rather than as absolute annihilation, thereby providing a conceptual basis for considering the possible persistence of consciousness beyond the brain\. Finally, we examine the implications of this hypothesis for panpsychism and cosmopsychism\. By analogy with quantum field theory, two possibilities are considered: consciousness particles could acquire experiential properties through interaction with a fundamental field of consciousness, or they could constitute the fundamental quanta of such a field\. Although highly speculative and not established as a physical theory, this framework offers a conceptual synthesis linking consciousness, emergence, the implicate order, and cosmopsychism, and provides a basis for investigating consciousness as a potentially fundamental feature of reality\.

## [Machine learning and network pharmacology\-assisted discovery of natural product inhibitors targeting Plasmodium falciparum lysyl\-tRNA synthetase](../publications/f5294908cbdc17ad951a.md)

P\. Alam; A\. Akhtar; Z\. Hasan; M\. Serajuddin; O\. Basudan; S\. Ahmed

The emergence of drug\-resistant Plasmodium falciparum necessitates novel antimalarial strategies\. Lysyl\-tRNA synthetase from Plasmodium falciparum \(PfLysRS\), an essential enzyme involved in protein biosynthesis, represents a promising molecular target for structure\-based drug discovery and development of effective antimalarial agents\. In this study, an integrated computational workflow identified three natural product\-derived lead compounds, MolPort\-001–742\-110, MolPort\-000–778\-336, and MolPort\-001–740\-194, through structure\-based virtual screening with favourable binding affinity and interaction profiles within the catalytic pocket\. Density functional theory \(DFT\) optimized ligand geometries and characterized their electronic properties, while five independent 200 ns molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations confirmed stable protein–ligand interactions\. Molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area \(MM/GBSA\) binding free energy calculations, principal component analysis \(PCA\), free energy landscape \(FEL\) mapping, and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics \(QM/MM\) analyses further demonstrated energetically favourable binding and provided mechanistic insights into ligand stabilization\. Machine learning predicted promising pIC50 values, supporting potential inhibitory activity against PfLysRS, whereas network pharmacology suggested modulation of multiple malaria\-related targets and pathways associated with parasite survival, host responses, and disease progression\. Overall, three promising natural product scaffolds were identified as potential PfLysRS inhibitors, providing a strong computational basis for biochemical, cellular, in vivo, and preclinical validation towards next\-generation antimalarial development\.

## [T2\-z: Test\-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models](../publications/f531ec67658703d4a74d.md)

Chenyuan Zhou; Yining Hong; Huang Huang; Yunfan Jiang; Wenlong Huang; David Held; Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini; Yue Wang; Li Fei\-Fei; Jiajun Wu; Leonidas Guibas; Yejin Choi

Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human\-defined environmental rules\. We introduce T2\-Z for test\-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions\. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take\. During training, T2\-Z alternates between two stages: a world\-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action\-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment\-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction\. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test\-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations\. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real\-world robotic tasks, T2\-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15\.20 to 7\.00 and raises action success from 33\.73% to 72\.96%\. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes\. Ablations further show that T2\-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test\-time interaction trajectory\.

## [Examining the Impact of Perceived Patient\-Centered Communication and Institutional Trust on Digital Health Engagement Behaviors](../publications/f536b25b2f71290c4566.md)

This study investigates the relationship between perceived patient\-centered communication, institutional trust, and digital health engagement behaviors\. Specifically, we examine whether patient\-centered communication is associated with digital health engagement behaviors: a\) viewing test results, b\) reading clinical notes, and c\) sharing health data with providers, and whether institutional trust is associated with these relationships\. Data used were from the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey cycle 7\. Path analysis was conducted using the lavaan package in R\. Out of the 3,475 participants, perceived patient\-centered communication significantly predicted sharing health data\. Patient\-centered communication influenced patients&\#x27; use of online medical records to view test results indirectly through institutional trust, suggesting that trust may play a selective role in certain health engagement behaviors\. Results have practical implications for designing communication strategies, underscoring the importance of both interpersonal communication and institutional trust in promoting active digital health engagement\. This study contributes to a better understanding of factors related to how patients engage with digital healthcare systems, providing insights into how communication experiences and institutional trust may shape digital health participation\.
