## [Pace, Joshua Craig: The Prioritization Regress: Why the Pull to Act Cannot Be Read, and Why It May Be Felt](../publications/f54e725a1fc16c55f622.md)



Accounts of consciousness often conflate value, how good or bad something is taken to be by the organism, and urgency, the pull to act\. Prioritization is a matter of urgency\. Any account on which prioritization produces a score that something separate reads faces a regress: the reader&\#x27;s rule is either fixed, so the scores&\#x27; significance for action was settled elsewhere, or adaptive, so it needs a further evaluator\. Systems with no separate reader avoid it, but where tension resolves directly into action they cannot deliberate\. Standard planners, active inference included, deliberate but fall back in\. What both deliberates and ends the regress is a held pull: urgency that persists undischarged, whose change under each rehearsed strategy is that strategy&\#x27;s evaluation\. I propose, as an identity thesis, not a deduction, that the system\-wide state of the field holding such pulls is identical with consciousness, and state how each claim could fail\. \(direct link \)

## [NEUROSYNC: A HYBRID BRAINWAVE–GESTURE CONTROL SYSTEM](../publications/f5503bf1848c83ae9786.md)



Today, automation technology is becoming increasingly accessible, user friendly, and efficient, enabling novel solutions for improving the quality of life\.This project explores the integration of braincomputer interfaces \(BCI\) with the Internet of Things \(IoT\) to provide a smart assistive system for individuals with limited physical mobility\.The system employs an EEG headset to capture real\-time brain signals, which are transmitted via Bluetooth to an ESP32 microcontroller for processing\.Based on the interpreted brain signals, the system can control electrical appliances such as lights and fans by switching a relay module ON or OFF\.The system also supports hand gesture control as a backup input method, ensuring reliable operation even when brain signals are unstable\.Additionally, the system is designed to detect abnormal brain activity, automatically triggering alerts through an application, and activating a buzzer to notify caregivers or family members\.The application also provides a real\-time display of appliance status, ensuring users are always aware of the current system state\.The expected outcome of this project is a reliable and user\-friendly brain\-controlled automation system that enhances safety, and convenience for physically challenged individuals\.

## [Transforming green innovation into entrepreneurship for a sustainable future: barriers, motivators and the impact of university support systems](../publications/f55647005912ecfde587.md)

Phung Nguyen

Abstract Drawing on growing concerns about green entrepreneurship and universities’ third mission to address sustainability\-related issues, this study examines the barriers and motivators perceived by university students in transforming green innovation ideas into entrepreneurial practices, as well as the impact of university support systems on the transformation\. The descriptive research findings from a sample of 263 students from Finland, Albania, and Kosovo reveal that, despite having more educational and economic advantages with increasing efforts made, entrepreneurship\-minded Finnish students still face a lack of knowledge, skills, and funding access at a high level, similar to those of the other two countries with less advantaged backgrounds\. Besides, personal interest in environmental sustainability, as well as financial benefits and career opportunities, are perceived across the countries as key motivators in fostering intentions\. Moreover, the study points out that the support mechanisms that students need most in the transformation, regardless of their backgrounds, are financing, courses, and mentorship focused on green innovation and entrepreneurship\. The study makes a novel contribution by connecting universities’ third mission with green innovation and entrepreneurship through university support systems\. This insight, therefore, provides universities, in collaboration with other stakeholders, with a valuable overview to develop support strategies that better prepare entrepreneurship\-minded students for green entrepreneurial implementation and contribute to sustainable regional development\.

## [Fish, Nicholas: Φ as a System’s Capacity for Consciousness: An Illusionist Integrated Information Theory Approach](../publications/f558a30b8fcf4ab80ca9.md)



Integrated Information Theory \(IIT\) attributes subjective experience to integrated information, which can be measured quantitatively as a value, Φ, and it has shown real empirical success through tools like the perturbational complexity index \(PCI\)\. However, IIT is not widely accepted, and I’d like to make the case that though Φ is heavily correlated with what we describe as consciousness, it actually measures an alternative state of our neural system, and that our assertions of consciousness being necessarily related to this correlation are false\. I take Illusionist Integrated Information Theory \(iIIT\), first introduced by Kelvin McQueen, as the groundwork for this claim\. Illusionism holds that phenomenal consciousness, as we conceive of it, is not at face value real\. McQueen argues that an illusionist framework makes IIT more coherent and less metaphysically demanding, in part because it avoids the logic gate objection\. From there, I argue that IIT has not always had a consistent definition of consciousness, most visibly in its treatment of dreamless sleep\. IIT’s axioms force us to “bite the bullet” and grant consciousness to a state with no phenomenal experience, no memory, and no unified self\. Rather than defend this, I propose that Φ is better understood as the ground on which consciousness is experienced\. In other words, Φ indicates a system’s capacity to produce the memory, conceptions of self, and higher\-order cognitive behaviors that give rise to our belief in consciousness, and not consciousness itself\. By reframing Φ this way, it loses some potency as the singular indication of consciousness, but it becomes a more tangible theory that can be explored with greater perspective\.

## [Long\-Term Mangrove Dynamics and Environmental Associations in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: Integrating Remote Sensing, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI](../publications/f5656db7d0ba9f4f6db1.md)

Sahanama Eastia; Zhen Guo; Jing Yu; Zhiwei Zhang; K M Azam Chowdhury; Jiawei Shen; Yuhang Qi

Mangrove ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic disturbances and climate change, despite providing ecological services, including biodiversity conservation, coastal protection, and blue carbon storage\. Long\-term evaluations of mangrove dynamics and associated environmental conditions remain limited, particularly in the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world\. This study examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of the Sundarbans mangrove ecosystem, Bangladesh, using multi\-temporal Landsat imagery \(1990–2025\), Random Forest \(RF\), Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), and SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\)\. Model performance was evaluated using the Global Mangrove Watch \(GMW\) dataset and spatially blocked holdout validation\. Classification accuracy was high \(94\.56–100%\) under internal and spatially blocked validation \(93\.5–99\.8%\), whereas comparison with GMW yielded lower accuracies \(66\.4–95\.7%\)\. Change detection showed that mangrove area expanded from 2096\.66 km2 in 1990 to 3875\.95 km2 in 2025, a net gain of almost 1779\.29 km2, with substantial inter\-period variability and a pronounced mapped decline between 2000 and 2005\. SHAP analysis indicated that the relative contributions of model predictors changed over time, with NDVI contributing more strongly to model predictions in recent years than NDWI and NDMI\. Mangrove gain, loss, and net change were statistically associated with cyclone exposure and elevation, while precipitation and river discharge showed less consistent relationships\. This study highlights a practical method for monitoring spectral dynamics in vulnerable coastal ecosystems and supports mangrove conservation\.

## [Difficulties in Differential Diagnosis of Rosai–Dorfman Disease: A Case Study](../publications/f572a84490befe2296e4.md)

Anastasia Nikolaevna Smykova; Yulia V\. Karacheva; Yulia Saltzman; Roman Smykov

Rosai–Dorfman disease \(sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy\) is a non\-Langerhans\-type histiocytic disorder characterized by histiocyte proliferation with emperipolesis\. Rosai\-Dorfman disease is a rarely diagnosed disease with variable clinical manifestations on the skin, in the lymphatic system, internal organs, requiring differential diagnosis with such nosologies as sarcoidosis, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, vasculitis, lymphoproliferative diseases \(Hodgkin&\#x27;s lymphoma, non\-Hodgkin&\#x27;s lymphomas\)\. According to modern concepts, the disease can be associated with immunodeficiency states, including LRBA deficiency, and also demonstrate a variety of extranodal manifestations \- from isolated axillary lymphadenopathy to destructive lesions of the bone structures of the nose with the formation of a recession of the nasal dorsum\. Difficulties in differential diagnosis are associated with the similarity of certain histological and clinical features and molecular changes\. Immunohistochemical testing with detection of the S\-100 and CD163 markers, which are key diagnostic criteria for differentiating this pathology from other histiocytoses, is mandatory for confirming the diagnosis\. This article describes Rosai\-Dorfman disease in a 42\-year\-old man\. The diagnosis was difficult for a dermatologist during an outpatient clinic visit\. The initial clinical misdiagnosis \(without histological or immunohistochemical examination\) of benign lymphocytic keratosis led to an inappropriate management strategy\. This clinical case demonstrates the challenges of differential diagnosis of Rosai\-Dorfman disease in a dermatologist&\#x27;s routine practice\. In the Russian Federation, systematic epidemiological data on the incidence of Rosai\-Dorfman disease have been absent from the available literature in recent years\. Existing publications consist of isolated clinical observations, due to the disorder&\#x27;s orphan status and the lack of a centralized federal registry of patients with this disease\. International literature estimates the incidence to be less than 1 case per 1,000,000 population per year\. Reporting each clinical observation is essential for accumulating data and optimizing the diagnosis and treatment of this rare disease\.

## [Research progress of mitophagy and its targeted therapeutic strategies in rheumatoid arthritis](../publications/f57583321f6ccf1b4244.md)

Yuanyuan Zhang; Fengmei Ge; Xuebin Wang

Rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive bone destruction\. This article reviews the molecular mechanisms of mitophagy and its pivotal role in RA, along with recent advances in mitophagy\-targeted therapeutic strategies, aiming to provide novel insights for RA treatment\.

## [An evaluation of mathematics teachers’ beliefs, teaching methods, and competencies regarding students with mathematics learning difficulties](../publications/f59adf76f2b5a4c3fb29.md)

Cahit Taşdemir

Students who struggle with mathematics generally face ongoing difficulties in understanding mathematical terms, applying operational knowledge, and developing problem\-solving skills\. This study aims to examine mathematics teachers’ perceptions, teaching methods, and the challenges they face regarding students with mathematics learning difficulties, based on their professional experiences\. The participants consisted of 20 middle school mathematics teachers working in public middle schools in Türkiye’s Eastern Anatolia Region\. Nevertheless, many teachers point out that they lack the necessary knowledge, professional training, and self\-confidence to provide effective and systematic support to students who struggle with mathematics\. Research findings highlight the importance of assessing mathematics learning difficulties from a multifaceted perspective that considers a combination of cognitive, emotional, and instructional factors\. Furthermore, strengthening practice\-oriented professional development programs can enhance teachers’ competencies and contribute to a more inclusive and effective mathematics education\.

## [Trait\-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze\-like response resistance](../publications/f5a95df750c3cfd02f2e.md)

Jan Kučera; Marketa Makarova; Michal Vít; Jan Novák; Filip Zlámal; Lucie Ráčková; Jana Kučerová; Markéta Grulichová; Tomáš Vojtíšek; Radek Šíp; Alžběta Fiedlerová; Julie Bienertová Vašků

The freeze\-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat\. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals \(n = 20\) with experienced police rapid response personnel \(n = 20\)\. Freeze\-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios\. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups\. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze\-like responses\. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre\- to post\-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze\-resistance may be associated with stable, trait\-like signatures rather than acute stress\-responsive processes\. Weighted gene co\-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze\-resistance \(r = 0\.75, p = 4 × 10−9\) and training status \(r = 0\.71, p = 6 × 10−8\), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass \(r = 0\.57, p = 8 × 10−5\)\. This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity\. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation\. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze\-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms\.

## [The Impact of Earthquake Early Warning Systems on Smart Cities&\#x27; Resilience: Conceptual Framework and Comprehensive Review](../publications/f5ac16664fa2aed97d2f.md)

Mücella Ateş

Earthquake Early Warning Systems \(EEWS\) are critical components of resilient smart cities, employing advanced digital technologies to reduce the impacts of seismic events and strengthen urban disaster preparedness\. These systems integrate distributed Internet of Things \(IoT\) devices, wireless sensor networks, high\-speed communication infrastructures, and machine learning algorithms to detect, analyze, and evaluate seismic activity in real time\. Data collected from interconnected ground\-motion sensors are rapidly transmitted to processing centers, enabling the estimation of earthquake magnitude, location, and expected intensity before strong ground shaking reaches affected areas\. When integrated into smart urban infrastructures, EEWS can trigger automated and coordinated responses, including halting public transportation, controlling elevators, isolating critical power and gas networks, protecting vulnerable infrastructure, and initiating emergency communication protocols\. This study examines the integration of EEWS into smart city frameworks, focusing on their role in enhancing disaster preparedness, real\-time decision\-making, and adaptive urban governance\. It also discusses technological, operational, organizational, and institutional challenges, including data interoperability, communication reliability, system maintenance, and coordination among stakeholders\. By embedding EEWS within interconnected urban systems, the study highlights their potential to enhance public safety, reduce socioeconomic disruption, and support the development of adaptive and earthquake\-resilient urban environments\.

## [Comparative Analysis of Optuna\-Optimized 1D and 2D CNNs for Protein Secondary Structure Prediction](../publications/f5b4aaf58be09e2bf91a.md)

Annisa Rizqiana; Triando Hamonangan Saragih; Muhammad Itqan Mazdadi; Irwan Budiman; Adryan Maulana Saputra

Protein secondary structure prediction \(PSSP\) is a fundamental task in bioinformatics, yet traditional experimental methods remain costly and time\-consuming\. While Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\) offer efficient computational alternatives, systematic comparisons between 1D and 2D CNN topologies remain limited\. Furthermore, conventional hyperparameter tuning in existing models relies on manual trial\-and\-error, introducing human bias and trapping networks in suboptimal performance thresholds\. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of 1D and 2D CNN architectures for PSSP and systematically investigate the impact of automated hyperparameter optimization on both model performance and training efficiency\. The proposed framework integrates standalone 1D and 2D CNN topologies with an automated hyperparameter optimization pipeline using Optuna based on the Tree\-structured Parzen Estimator\. Models are trained on the benchmark CullPDB dataset and rigorously evaluated via cross\-dataset testing on the independent, non\-redundant CB513 benchmark\. The primary contributions include a standalone comparative analysis between 1D and 2D CNN topologies, the elimination of human bias via automated tuning, and a comprehensive feature efficiency analysis highlighting the trade\-offs between computational representation and predictive accuracy\. Experimental results show that all configurations achieve high overall performance with accuracies exceeding 81% and AUC values above 94%\. Specifically, the CNN 1D \+ Optuna configuration yields the highest precision of 0\.4409 and an F1\-score of 0\.4454, effectively capturing local sequential motifs\. Conversely, the CNN 2D \+ Optuna configuration excels in extracting spatial inter\-residue relationships, delivering the highest AUC of 0\.9493 and the lowest cross\-entropy loss of 0\.0114\. Additionally, Optuna dramatically accelerates training efficiency, reducing convergence iterations by up to 66% \(from epoch 24 down to 8 for the 2D model\)\. In conclusion, automated optimization eliminates manual bias and enhances training efficiency, revealing that the choice between 1D and 2D topologies should be strategically guided by the precise needs of downstream biological applications\.

## [Red forehead dot syndrome: a case report and review of literature](../publications/f5b7212f64ebeee18bbe.md)

Walid Alesefir

Background Migraine is a common neurological disorder with a broad spectrum of sensory and autonomic manifestations\. Visible, recurrent, localized cutaneous changes temporally associated with migraine attacks are rare\. Case presentation I report a 41\-year\-old Pakistani man with an approximately 21\-year history of recurrent bilateral frontal and supra\-orbital headaches associated with photophobia, phonophobia, and nausea\. For many years, his attacks have been accompanied by recurrent, well\-demarcated bilateral erythematous forehead changes in a distribution corresponding approximately to the ophthalmic \(V1\) trigeminal territory\. Because of the long duration of symptoms, he could not reliably determine whether migraine\-type headaches preceded the cutaneous manifestations or whether both had been associated from the beginning\. Intermittent cranial autonomic features occurred during some attacks but were not consistently present and did not invariably coincide with the skin discoloration\. Neurological examination, laboratory evaluation, and brain MRI were unremarkable\. Following his usual acute analgesic treatment, both headache and skin changes improved within minutes to a few hours\. Conclusion This case adds to the limited literature describing migraine\-associated forehead erythema, previously termed “red forehead dot syndrome\.” The reproducible temporal relationship between headache and cutaneous changes supports an association with the migraine attack, although the underlying mechanism remains uncertain\. Trigeminovascular activation, neurogenic inflammation, autonomic dysfunction, and vasoactive neuropeptides such as calcitonin gene\-related peptide \(CGRP\) are biologically plausible mechanisms\. Because this presentation is rare, appropriate evaluation for secondary neurological, vascular, inflammatory, and dermatological causes remains essential\.

## [Dense Channel Spatial Semantic Guidance Attention U\-Net for robust road lane detection in autonomous vehicles](../publications/f5bf987a21162a700c23.md)

Koduru Gouthami; Sridhar Chintala; Santosh Kumar Henge; Durgesh Nandan; Chandan Kumar Choubey

Detection of road lanes is an essential part of autonomous vehicles, as it allows the cars to see the lanes and drive accordingly\. However, it becomes complicated because of poor lane markings, various lighting, and weather conditions\. This study proposes a Vision Framework for Road Lane Detection to Enable Robust Perception and Safe Navigation in Autonomous Vehicle Systems \(VRLD\-SNAVS\)\. Within this framework, Dense Channel Spatial Semantic Guidance Attention U\-Net \(DCSSGA\-UNet\) is used for lane segmentation, and the Multiplayer Battle Game Optimizer \(MBGO\) is used for hyperparameter optimization\. For consistency, the complete proposed pipeline is referred to as the DCSSGA\-UNet\-MBGO framework throughout the paper\. In recent years, vision\-based navigation driven by deep learning \(DL\) has emerged as a promising and widely used approach to enhance the accuracy, reliability, and robustness of perception and navigation systems for autonomous vehicles\. DL\-based vision systems have significantly enhanced the ability of autonomous vehicles to detect lanes, recognize obstacles, and understand complex driving scenes, thereby supporting timely and reliable perception for autonomous driving under diverse operating conditions\. The proposed framework has been validated in a desktop GPU\-based environment and serves as a foundation for future real\-time embedded deployment\. Parameter count, floating\-point operations and inference latency were not measured, so the computational efficiency of the framework has still to be established\. The input images are taken from the Udacity dataset and the Cracks and Potholes Dataset to enable pixel\-level semantic segmentation and thus distinguish lane regions from non\-lane background regions within the images\. After this, these images undergo pre\-processing such as resizing and pixel normalization\. The proposed model performs semantic segmentation at the pixel level to classify each pixel in the image as belonging to the lane region or the non\-lane \(background\) region\. This binary segmentation method enables us to extract lane markings precisely and suppress the scene elements that are irrelevant to the lane detection task, thus improving the performance of the lane detection task under diverse road and environmental conditions\. For additional performance improvement of this algorithm, the Multiplayer Battle Game Optimizer \(MBGO\) method is implemented to perform hyperparameter tuning of the proposed DCSSGA\-UNet network\. From the numerical results achieved on the selected datasets, the suggested DCSSGA\-UNet\-MBGO framework achieves competitive performance relative to the values reported for existing methods, with an average Dice Coefficient of 98\.8% and an average Intersection Over Union \(IoU\) of 97\.4%, in addition to a minimal Dice Loss of 1\.25\.

## [Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi\-Agent LLM Discussions](../publications/f5c38c743b2da2417a5e.md)

Liangjie Huang; Henry Peng Zou; Wei\-Chieh Huang; Wooseong Yang; Yuwei Han; Philip S\. Yu

LLM systems increasingly rely on groups of agents that discuss, critique, and check one another, assuming that peers will catch individual errors\. We test this assumption against a minimal adversary\. In a ten\-agent factual discussion, one or three adversarial agents repeatedly assert a plausible false answer\. After each round we probe each benign agent&\#x27;s private answer through a separate call whose response is hidden from its peers, and we separately label its public stance toward the claim\. Across six models and three factual\-QA datasets, groups remain stable without an attacker: only 0\.6% of benign agents finish with the false answer\. A single adversarial agent increases this rate to 44\.8% and three to 60\.5%\. Studies of conformity typically report public agreement without private change; we find the reverse\. With three adversarial agents present, benign agents hold the false answer in 51\.6% of exposed turns but publicly endorse it in only 19\.7%\. Much of the influence therefore remains invisible in the discussion, and the false answers persist when agents are asked for their own views\. Agents that retain the true answer often fail to defend it; once adopted, the false answer spreads among benign agents, and baseline knowledge does not predict robustness\.

## [One Anti\-ST2 Biologic, Three Gateways: What an Alarmin\-Targeted Monoclonal Antibody Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/f5d1d66d33d73c1b02ee.md)

Sahil Patel; Drashti Patel; Happy Makvana; Peivand Pirouzi

Anti\-ST2 monoclonal antibodies neutralize the interleukin\-33 receptor, blocking a key upstream alarmin signalling pathway implicated in airway inflammation, and represent a biologic class under continued investigation for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\) exacerbation reduction, an area with limited targeted biologic options relative to severe asthma\. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of an anti\-ST2 monoclonal antibody candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014\. As a large\-molecule biologic governed by ICH S6\(R1\) principles rather than the small\-molecule nonclinical framework, this candidate illustrates how species\-relevant pharmacology and immunogenicity considerations carry through the administrative layer of all three regions even though the core harmonized scientific content, Modules 2 through 5 of the Common Technical Document and their EU IMPD equivalent, remains substantially shared\. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to a respiratory biologic program conducted across these three jurisdictions, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing monoclonal antibody candidates in chronic respiratory disease\.Keywords: anti\-ST2 monoclonal antibody; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; ICH S6\(R1\); regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Design and evaluation of a 55\-kHz clamping\-type ultrasonic scalpel utilizing Mn:PIN\-PMN\-PT single crystals](../publications/f5e542747e69988176f5.md)

石文杰; Shiyang Li; Qian Xue

Abstract Piezoelectric materials are crucial for the performance of the ultrasonic scalpels\. However, the relatively low piezoelectric properties of PZT ceramics limited electromechanical coupling coefficient and power density, thereby restricting the overall performance of these devices\. To address these limitations, a novel 55\-kHz ultrasonic scalpel design utilizing Mn:PIN\-PMN\-PT single crystals was proposed and fabricated in this study\. Experimental results demonstrate that the effective electromechanical coupling factor of the Mn:PIN\-PMN\-PT scalpel reaches 0\.155, which is more than double that of conventional PZT systems\. Under the same excitation voltages, the single\-crystal scalpel achieves a higher no\-load distal amplitude than the conventional PZT scalpel\. Moreover, under load conditions, the power density of the single\-crystal scalpel is 34\.66 times that of the PZT counterpart\. Finally, pork tissue cutting experiments confirm that the scalpel exhibits superior cutting performance\. In summary, the present study verified the effectiveness of Mn:PIN\-PMN\-PT single crystals in 55\-kHz clamping\-type ultrasonic scalpels\. It can provide a new perspective for the improvement of the ultrasonic scalpels\.

## [ECOCRITICAL PERSPECTIVES ON INTO THE BENEATH: GREG GARRARD’S FRAMEWORK IN DEPICTING MARINE ENVIRONMENTAL CRISES](../publications/f5f5274b5c0d58b8e19d.md)

Candra Candra; Juanda Juanda

This study aims to explore ecological phenomena in Rifqi Farizi’s novel Into the Beneath through the framework of Greg Garrard’s ecocriticism\. The research focuses on identifying and analyzing the representation of five key ecological categories: pollution, apocalypse, dwelling, animals, and earth\. The objective is to reveal how the novel reflects contemporary ecological anxieties and provides critical perspectives on humanity’s relationship with the ocean as a vital yet vulnerable ecosystem\. A qualitative descriptive method was applied with textual data drawn from the novel\. Data collection was carried out through careful reading and coding of textual segments, while data analysis employed an interactive model supported by software\-based coding to ensure thematic consistency and systematic categorization\. The findings show that pollution and earth appear as dominant ecological issues, highlighting the destruction of the sea through plastic, oil, and heavy metal contamination, as well as the symbolic representation of the ocean as part of the fragile balance of the earth\. The category of animals reflects both the beauty of biodiversity and the vulnerability of marine life to pollution and experimentation\. Apocalypse emphasizes pessimism and fear about the future of the ocean, while dwelling reveals ambivalent human attitudes toward the sea as both alien and essential\. These results confirm literature’s role as a medium for ecological critique and awareness building\.

## [Discovering gut microbiome signatures that predict adverse and reverse cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure](../publications/f5f97bfb0e01ca12f2fe.md)

Ning\-I Yang; Yu\-Chieh Liao; Chieh\-Hua Lin; Tsung‐Hsien Tsai; Tsung\-Hsien Tsai; Tsai\-Wen Teng; Yun\-Hsuan Chan; Chih\-Wei Tu; Yi\-Ju Chou; Yeh Chi\-Hsiao; Li‐Tang Kuo; Ming\-Jui Hung; Chun‐Tai Mao; Wayne Huey‐Herng Sheu; Chi\-Chun Lai; Huey\-Kang Sytwu; Ting\-Fen Tsai; Ting\-Fen Tsai

There is an unmet need to predict adverse or reverse \(favorable\) cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure \(stages A and B\)\. We investigated the role of the gut microbiome in cardiac remodeling during asymptomatic heart failure\. In this prospective cohort study, 124 subjects were enrolled at baseline \(stage A, n = 85; stage B, n = 39\)\. After one\-year follow\-up, subjects were classified as having adverse \(AA vs\. AB\) or reverse \(BB vs\. BA\) remodeling\. Full\-length 16S rRNA sequencing of stool DNA was performed\. An independent cohort \(n = 94\) was included to assess model robustness\. Here we show that machine learning and differential abundance analyses yield three key findings\. First, the top 20 microbiome features predict adverse remodeling \(accuracy 0\.76; area under the curve 0\.86\) and reverse remodeling \(accuracy 0\.85; area under the curve 0\.95\)\. Second, taxa identified by both ML and DESeq2 included four genera \(Romboutsia, Alloprevotella, Klebsiella, Enterobacter\) and five species \(R\. ilealis, A\. rava, K\. variicola, K\. pneumoniae, E\. roggenkampii\)\. Third, pathway analysis suggests beneficial effects of R\. ilealis in stage AA via short\-chain fatty acid and ketone body metabolism, whereas Klebsiella spp\. and E\. roggenkampii may be linked to pro\-inflammation in stage BB\. Cohort\-cumulation modeling demonstrates stable performance \(area under the curve 0\.75\-0\.80\) of the models in the validation cohort\. The gut microbiome predicts cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure and represents a potential therapeutic target, with possible implications for risk stratification and personalized management\. Heart failure can develop gradually before symptoms appear, but it remains difficult to predict whether heart structure and function will worsen or improve during these early stages\. We investigated whether bacteria living in the gut could help predict these changes\. We analyzed stool samples from people with early\-stage heart failure without symptoms and identified gut bacterial patterns associated with changes in heart structure and function over one year\. We identified specific gut bacteria that could predict worsening heart structure and function, while others could predict a return to healthier heart structure and function, with good accuracy\. These microbial patterns may help identify individuals with different risks of disease progression\. Our findings also provide directions for future research into whether the gut microbiome could contribute to strategies for preventing or treating heart failure\. Yang, Liao, Lin et al\. investigate gut microbiome signatures associated with adverse and reverse cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure\. Gut microbiome profiles predict both remodeling trajectories, with specific bacterial taxa associated with favorable or adverse remodeling\.

## [Association between infertility prevalence and exposure to heat stress: an ecological study based on the Universal Thermal Climate Index](../publications/f605c357519e01201a82.md)

Dian Wang; Jiahua Qian; Xiaoming Zhang; Chunbao Mo; Yihao Chen; Yuhe Si; Yicheng Wang; Jianan He; Ma Jianxiong

Background Repeated exposure to heat stress may adversely affect reproductive health, yet the population\-level relationship between heat stress and infertility has not been well characterized\. Methods We conducted a global ecological analysis across 174 countries and regions from 1990 to 2021\. Heat exposure was quantified as the annual number of days falling into four Universal Thermal Climate Index categories: moderate, strong, very strong, and extreme heat stress\. We additionally constructed a weighted score combining very strong and extreme heat stress\. Associations with male and female infertility prevalence were estimated using linear mixed\-effects models\. Results Each additional day of very strong and extreme heat stress was associated with increases in male infertility ASPR of 1\.292 \(95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 0\.675–1\.908\) and 1\.654 \(95% CI: 0\.214–3\.096\) per 100,000 population, respectively\. The corresponding increases in female infertility ASPR were 2\.126 \(95% CI: 0\.785–3\.467\) and 7\.133 \(95% CI: 3\.940–10\.323\) per 100,000 population, respectively\. Higher weighted heat\-stress scores were also consistently associated with greater infertility prevalence\. Conclusions These findings suggest that recurrent heat\-stress exposure may be associated with a higher population burden of infertility and support consideration of reproductive health in climate\-change adaptation and heat\-protection strategies\.

## [Aprendizagem ativa](../publications/f60616aae662e445e5c7.md)

Isabella Lopes Pederneira; Thays Ferreira Alves; Rafaela Fontes Soares

O objetivo deste trabalho é refletir criticamente acerca dos métodos pedagógicos vigentes voltados ao ensino de gramática e demonstrar a viabilidade de unificar a teoria linguística à prática em sala de aula\. Como pressuposto teórico, adotaram\-se os estudos em Teoria Gerativa \(Chomsky, 1986\), que compreende a linguagem como uma faculdade inata e biológica\. Esse saber intrínseco, que atua de forma inconsciente, justifica uma abordagem pedagógica que não busca apenas ensinar ao aluno o que ele já sabe, ainda que inconscientemente, mas sim guiá\-lo em uma reflexão científica acerca da estrutura e do funcionamento de sua própria língua\. A metodologia adotada foi a Metodologia de Aprendizagem Linguística Ativa \(Pilati, 2017\), que promove o protagonismo do aluno por meio da investigação e manipulação dos dados linguísticos\. Com o fim de pôr em prática esse método, oficinas didáticas foram aplicadas a alunos do 6º ano do Ensino Fundamental e do 3º ano do Ensino Médio em escolas da Zona Norte e da Baixada Fluminense do Rio de Janeiro\. Tais atividades consistiram na manipulação de itens lexicais e/ou funcionais, que continham cores e formas diversas\. A partir das estratégias adotadas pelos alunos na criação de palavras e sentenças, as professoras e pesquisadoras mediaram discussões sobre conceitos como \(a\)gramaticalidade, estrutura de argumentos e polissemia verbal, com base na intuição dos próprios alunos como ferramenta de análise\. Como resultado, os alunos de ambos os níveis, ao manipularem as estruturas de forma criativa e coerente, demonstraram um domínio prático e consistente dos mecanismos morfossintáticos de sua língua, mesmo sem instrução formal sobre os conceitos abordados, o que é consistente com a hipótese do saber linguístico inato, que era subjacente ao estudo\.

## [AI\-Based Interactive Media and Reading Literacy as Determinants of IPAS Learning Outcomes: A Study of Students at SDN Lesanpuro 3 Malang](../publications/f60d4a197f86e589d26d.md)

Meiarini Priastuti; Sudi Dul Aji; Roni Alim Ba’diya Kusufa

This study was motivated by low learning outcomes in Integrated Natural and Social Sciences \(IPAS\) among fifth\-grade students at SDN Lesanpuro 3 Malang, which is driven by reliance on static, conventional media and students&\#x27; limited reading literacy skills\. The objective of this research was to analyze the main effects of AI\-assisted interactive learning media and reading literacy levels, as well as their interaction, on IPAS learning outcomes\. A quantitative quasi\-experimental approach featuring a 2 x 2 factorial design was used with a sample of 56 fifth\-grade students\. Data were analyzed using Two\-Way ANOVA\. The findings revealed a statistically significant difference in learning outcomes between the AI\-assisted media group and the conventional media group \(p = 0\.005\) \(2\)\. Reading literacy exerted a highly significant influence on academic achievement \(p = 0\.000\), and A significant interaction was identified between AI\-based media usage and reading literacy levels \(p = 0\.002\)\. It is concluded that integrating AI\-driven interactive media while strengthening foundational reading literacy creates an effective instructional synergy, demonstrating that educational technology is most effective when supported by adequate student literacy capacity\.

## [QUEM O ALGORITMO ENXERGA? DIVERSIDADE DEMOGRÁFICA E VALIDAÇÃO EXTERNA DE MODELOS DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL APLICADOS À ANÁLISE ESTÉTICA FACIAL E DO SORRISO: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA METODOLÓGICA](../publications/f6155c7511c0eeb8f27f.md)

Daniel da Penha Soares; Rim Hassan Youssef; Ana Valéria Pagliari

Este artigo buscou avaliar o relato da diversidade demográfica e a realização de validação externa em estudos sobre modelos de inteligência artificial \(IA\) aplicados à análise estética facial e do sorriso\. Trata\-se de uma revisão sistemática metodológica, com buscas nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, OpenAlex e SciELO em outubro de 2026, relatada conforme o PRISMA 2020 e restrita a estudos com texto completo disponível gratuitamente\. Dos 264 registros únicos, 14 estudos foram incluídos, publicados entre 2022 e 2026 e provenientes de 12 países\. O sexo dos participantes foi relatado em 78,6% dos estudos, a idade em 57,1% e a etnia ou ancestralidade em 35,7%; entre estes, três de cinco utilizaram amostras de uma única população\. Nenhum dos oito modelos desenvolvidos pelos autores passou por validação externa, e apenas uma das seis ferramentas prontas e modelos de linguagem teve a população de treinamento descrita\. Nenhum estudo avaliou pacientes brasileiros\. Conclui\-se que os modelos de IA para análise estética são desenvolvidos e testados em populações pouco descritas e pouco diversas, o que limita sua generalização para países miscigenados, como o Brasil, e reforça a necessidade de relato padronizado e de validação externa antes do uso clínico\.

## [Empirical Evaluation of Feature Selection Strategies for Interpretable and Robust Healthcare Machine Learning](../publications/f61d05f76c3beece04b7.md)

Choo‐Yee Ting; Md\. Abu Nishan; Chih\-Yang Pee; Helmi Zakariah; Thanh\-Trung Nguyen

Feature Section \(FS\) is a fundamental step in developing accurate, robust, and interpretable Machine Learning \(ML\) models, especially when working with high\-dimensional structured datasets commonly found in healthcare, finance, and other data\-intensive domains\. Selecting the most relevant subset of features not only improves predictive performance but also enhances computational efficiency and model transparency\. This paper presents a comprehensive and systematic study of widely adopted feature selection strategies, including filter, wrapper, embedded, model\-agnostic methods, and dimensionality reduction techniques\. Each category is examined through experimental evaluations across multiple classifiers and benchmark datasets to understand how different feature selection mechanisms affect model performance, interpretability, and stability\. The results show that while filter methods, such as mutual information and chi\-square, are computationally efficient and suitable for large\-scale screening, wrapper and embedded methods achieve higher accuracy at the cost of increased computational demand\. The model\-agnostic approach, represented by Permutation Feature Importance \(PFI\), was employed to assess the relative contribution of each feature to model performance, thereby providing an interpretable and unbiased measure of feature relevance\. Dimensionality reduction techniques, such as Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\) and Linear Discriminant Analysis \(LDA\), further assist in managing multicollinearity, improving class separability, and enhancing model generalization by transforming features into more discriminative lower\-dimensional spaces\. Moreover, the study captures the trade\-offs between accuracy, speed, and explainability, offering practical recommendations for researchers and practitioners to select suitable methods based on their specific context and computational resources\. The findings underscore the importance of adaptive, context\-aware feature selection pipelines, particularly in healthcare analytics, where interpretable and trustworthy models can improve diagnostic confidence and support effective decision\-making\.

## [Impact of Digital Construction Technologies on Sustainability Awareness and Decision\-Making in Civil Engineering Education](../publications/f623bc081da9b496c815.md)

Rizwan U\. Farooqui; Abid Hassan; Mohammad Khalid; Syed Ahmed

Digital technologies such as Building Information Modeling \(BIM\), Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), simulation platforms, and virtual and augmented reality are reshaping civil engineering education, yet their influence on sustainability awareness and decision\-making is not well understood\. This study surveyed 73 students enrolled in civil engineering courses at a public university in the southeastern United States\. The instrument comprised 36 Likert\-scale statements, grouped into eight constructs covering technology use in the curriculum, professional mindset, sustainability knowledge and lifecycle and environmental awareness\. They also covered understanding of water resources, cognitive ability, emotional intelligence, and problem\-solving\. It also includes three decision scenarios in which a digital tool output conflicted with human input or practical constraints\. Students reported favorable attitudes toward digital tools, along with strong conceptual sustainability awareness, but two applied\-skill gaps stood out: only 32\.9% felt able to interpret hydrologic models, and only 28\.8% felt they could transfer simulation\-based lessons to real world settings\. In the scenarios, at most 12\.3% of respondents accepted the digital output at face value, and 83\.6% never did so across all three scenarios\. Breadth of tool exposure was unrelated to perceptions or decision style, whereas the small group of students reporting exposure to hydrologic modeling rated their model interpretation ability substantially higher, suggesting that relevant depth matters more than the number of tools encountered\. The findings support curricula that pair earlier and deeper BIM and hydrologic modeling instruction with lifecycle content and that train verification and interpretation skills alongside tool operation\.

## [Data\-Efficient Hybrid Physics\-Informed Machine Learning for Aircraft Attitude Prediction Under Unseen Turbulence Conditions\.](../publications/f6372402fe16b954ee35.md)

Sri Krish K B

Data\-Efficient Hybrid Physics\-Informed Machine Learning for Aircraft Attitude Prediction Under Unseen Turbulence Conditions This research proposes a hybrid physics\-informed machine learning \(H\-PIML\) framework for aircraft attitude prediction under uncertain and previously unseen atmospheric turbulence conditions\. The methodology integrates data\-driven neural network models with aircraft rigid\-body dynamics by incorporating physics\-based constraints into the learning objective\. The primary objective is to investigate whether this integration can enhance predictive accuracy, physical consistency, and generalization while reducing dependence on extensive training data\. Using computationally simulated flight data and established turbulence models, the framework can be evaluated against conventional machine learning approaches in terms of prediction error, robustness under distribution shifts, data efficiency, and computational performance\. This study aims to contribute to the development of reliable, data\-efficient predictive models for aerospace applications, with potential relevance to flight simulation, aircraft state estimation, and future real\-time flight\-control research\. The research has potential relevance to the modern aviation industry, where turbulence remains a significant operational challenge for commercial and other aircraft\. More reliable aircraft attitude predictions could support turbulence\-response analysis, flight simulation, aircraft state\-estimation systems, and the development and testing of advanced flight\-control algorithms\. By investigating model performance under unfamiliar gust conditions and with limited training data, this approach could help researchers assess the feasibility of more adaptable predictive systems for diverse flight environments\. In the longer term, the framework may contribute to improved turbulence\-management strategies, enhanced pilot\-support technologies, and more robust autonomous flight research\. However, practical deployment in operational aircraft would require extensive validation using high\-fidelity simulations, real flight data, and appropriate aviation safety and certification processes\.

## [Peripheral 5\-HT3A and DP2 targets as the basis for the analgesic action of the novel isoquinoline derivative G\-104](../publications/f6460974f2689fd521af.md)

Daniil A\. Puzanov; Yu\.A\. Fomina; T\. Yu\. Kalyuta; A\. A\. Smolyak; С\. А\. Астафьева; Elena N\. Reshetova; Владимир Николаевич Стрельников; Alexander Fedonnikov

Relevance\. The search for a potent and safe analgesic devoid of the disadvantages of opioids and non steroidal anti inflammatory drugs remains an unresolved challenge in pharmacology\. The synthetic isoquinoline derivative 6 \(3,3 dimethyl 3,4 dihydroisoquinolin 1 yl\)aminohexanoic acid \(G\-104\) has demonstrated marked analgesic activity in preclinical models; however, its molecular targets and mechanism of action have remained unidentified\. Objective\. To predict the potential peripheral targets 5\-HTЗА and DP2 and analgesic mechanism of this novel isoquinoline derivative using a comprehensive in silico analysis\. Methods\. Target prediction \(SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, TargetNet, PPB2\), molecular docking \(Glide\), and molecular dynamics simulations \(GROMACS\) were performed\. Results\. In combination with previously obtained experimental data, a hypothesis on the possible mechanism of G\-104 analgesia is proposed\. The serotonin 5\-HT ЗА receptor and the prostaglandin DP₂ receptor were selected as potential targets\. Docking revealed that G\-104 forms complexes with both receptors characteristic of antagonists, and molecular dynamics for DP₂ confirmed the stability of the binding pose throughout the simulation trajectory\. This dual peripheral mechanism—simultaneous inhibition of serotonergic pain modulation and pro inflammatory prostaglandin D₂ signaling—may be consistent with potent and prolonged analgesia observed in vivo and predicts a low risk of central and autonomic adverse effects\. Conclusion\. The obtained results position G\-104 as a potentially effective multitarget analgesic and pave the way for further preclinical investigations\.

## [Hepatocellular adenoma associated with recurrent hydrocelom in a Mexican axolotl \(Ambystoma mexicanum\)\- a case report](../publications/f66b0c5c56bd2abe1734.md)

Alessandro Vetere; Antonella Volta; Martina Fumeo; Federico Armando; Melania Di Pentima; Martina Gavezzoli; Jacopo Casalini; Rosanna Di Lecce; Francesco Di Ianni

The Mexican axolotl \( Ambystoma mexicanum \) is an increasingly popular companion animal and an important model organism in regenerative medicine\. However, information on neoplastic diseases in this species remains limited\. Hepatocellular adenoma is a benign hepatic neoplasm characterized by well\-differentiated hepatocytes and loss of normal lobular architecture\. This report describes an axolotl with hepatocellular adenoma and concomitant hydrocelom\. A 9\-year\-old, 230\-g captive\-bred female Mexican axolotl was presented with a three\-week history of progressive celomic distension\. Despite marked celomic enlargement, the animal was alert and responsive\. Radiography revealed celomic effusion and a small radiopaque focus in the hepatic region\. Ultrasonography demonstrated free celomic fluid, a small gallbladder stone, and a 1 × 0\.7 cm hepatic mass in the right liver lobe\. Echocardiography and hematologic and biochemical analyses were unremarkable\. Analysis of the aspirated fluid identified a pure transudate and bacterial culture was negative\. Computed tomography confirmed the hepatic mass\. The lesion was surgically removed\. Grossly, the mass was oval, well demarcated, smooth, and lighter than the surrounding hepatic parenchyma\. Histopathology revealed a nodular proliferation of well\-differentiated hepatocytes with mild anisocytosis and anisokaryosis, no mitotic figures, and an absence of portal spaces, supporting the diagnosis of hepatocellular adenoma\. Histochemical stains for potential infectious agents were negative\. Postoperative recovery was uneventful\. Although hydrocelom recurred four months later and required periodic drainage, serial ultrasonography revealed no recurrence of hepatic or other celomic lesions during the subsequent three\-year follow\-up\. This case expands knowledge of neoplastic diseases in axolotls and demonstrates the feasibility of advanced imaging and surgical management of hepatic masses in this species\.

## [Case Report: 18F\-FDG PET/CT findings and SUVmax characterization in a dog with apocrine gland anal sac adenocarcinoma](../publications/f66b29bfe2bdb9e902e9.md)

Bohyeon Shim; Yujin Kim; Sungin Lee

Apocrine gland anal sac adenocarcinoma \(AGASACA\) is a malignant epithelial tumor in dogs that commonly metastasizes to regional lymph nodes\. Although 18 F\-fluorodeoxyglucose \( 18 F\-FDG\) positron emission tomography/computed tomography \(PET/CT\) has been mentioned as a staging modality for this tumor, detailed imaging findings and maximum standardized uptake values \(SUVmax\) have not previously been reported\. A 10\-year\-old castrated male Maltese was referred for a right anal sac mass and suspected lymph node metastasis\. Preoperative 18 F\-FDG PET/CT revealed increased uptake in the primary mass \(SUVmax 7\.3\), the internal iliac lymph node \(SUVmax 6\.35\), and the lumbar aortic lymph node \(SUVmax 4\.3\), with no evidence of distant metastasis\. Therefore, the dog was therefore classified as Stage IIIa\. Based on these findings, intra\-abdominal lymphadenectomy and right anal sacculectomy were performed\. Histopathology confirmed AGASACA in the primary mass and morphologically similar metastatic adenocarcinoma in the resected lymph nodes\. To our knowledge, this is the first report of 18 F\-FDG PET/CT findings and SUVmax values in a dog with AGASACA and histologically confirmed lymph node metastases\. These findings suggest that PET/CT may provide complementary metabolic information for preoperative nodal staging\.

## [Duede, Eamon: Instruments, agents, and artificial intelligence: novel epistemic categories of reliability](../publications/f671d86098c3aaa72eee.md)



\_Synthese\_ 200 \(6\):1\-20\. 2022Deep learning \(DL\) has become increasingly central to science, primarily due to its capacity to quickly, efficiently, and accurately predict and classify phenomena of scientific interest\. This paper seeks to understand the principles that underwrite scientists’ epistemic entitlement to rely on DL in the first place and argues that these principles are philosophically novel\. The question of this paper is not whether scientists can be justified in trusting in the reliability of DL\. While today’s artificial intelligence exhibits characteristics common to both scientific instruments and scientific experts, this paper argues that the familiar epistemic categories that justify belief in the reliability of instruments and experts are distinct, and that belief in the reliability of DL cannot be reduced to either\. Understanding what can justify belief in AI reliability represents an occasion and opportunity for exciting, new philosophy of science\. \(direct link \)

## [A nationwide student survey on biochemistry learning resources in Italy](../publications/f673b2afbac54089d187.md)

Anna Marabotti; Ivano Eberini; Maria Luisa Genova; Francesca Mensitieri; Francesco Malatesta

Biochemistry is widely recognized as a crucial discipline in life sciences\. However, learning biochemistry poses significant challenges, requiring students to understand complex molecular concepts while integrating knowledge across multiple disciplines\. This necessitates instructors to innovate their teaching of biochemistry, considering students&\#x27; learning behaviors\. Here, we present the results of a nationwide survey of university students, conducted by the Education Group of the Italian Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, from more than 2000 students across 49 academic institutions in Italy, with the aim of capturing not only which learning resources are relied on but also the underlying motivations for their choices and perceptions of biochemistry\. Results show that overall, biochemistry is perceived as an interesting subject to study, even if challenging\. Students primarily rely on instructor\-provided materials, such as lecture slides, as well as self\-acquired resources, including audio recordings and personal notes\. Textbooks are used mainly as references when the preferred materials above do not sufficiently support students&\#x27; learning\. AI tools are increasingly used but not yet preferred\. This strong reliance on teacher guidance underscores the need for high\-quality teaching materials and greater integration of practical, application\-oriented learning activities\. By mapping these trends, our survey provides a foundation for critical reflection on current teaching practices and offers insights that may guide the development of more effective learning tools\. Our broader goal is to support educators in creating environments that foster deeper understanding, sustained engagement, and a more inclusive learning experience in biochemistry\.

## [Stress\-informed parametric shape adaptive patient\-specific implant design in computer\-assisted jaw reconstruction](../publications/f677c5db93203d2777f0.md)

Ankit Nayak; Yu\-Xiong Su; Jane Jingya Pu

Introduction Reconstructing the jaw after tumor removal or trauma increasingly relies on custom 3D\-printed titanium plates\. This customization applies to the implant&\#x27;s shape\. It usually does not apply to the internal structure\. The width and thickness of the plate are still determined by the designer, based on experience and clinical observation\. The critical design parameters of the PSI govern its mechanical performance\. Hence, if the design could analyze these parameters and adjust them accordingly, it could help avoid plate fracture\. This study introduces a parametric\-design approach that closes this gap\. Methods The proposed algorithm addresses these challenges by using stress data derived from finite element analysis \(FEA\) to selectively reinforce only the high\-stress regions of a reconstruction plate, rather than uniformly reinforcing the entire plate\. The reinforcement is smoothly integrated into the plate’s geometry to prevent abrupt changes in cross\-section that could create stress concentrations\. The approach was applied to a baseline plate at two regions of elevated stress\. Results and discussion Plate A reinforced only the primary zone; this reduced peak stress by 36\.0% and strain by 43\.8% in that zone, the largest reduction observed across both design variants, and also lowered stress and strain in the second, unmodified zone by 12\.7% and 14\.3%, respectively\. Plate B reinforced both zones; this further reduced stress and strain at the second zone by approximately 30\.6% and 33\.3%, respectively, and reduced strain at the primary zone by approximately 40\.6% relative to baseline\. Relative to Plate A, Plate B showed a slightly higher stress at the first zone; this stress remained well below the original baseline value\. This work shows that patient\-specific implant geometry can be shaped directly by biomechanical feedback\. This algorithm offers an efficient computational workflow, enabling implants that are not only anatomically tailored but also mechanically optimized as per given loading conditions\.

## [A Review on Analytical Methods for the Evaluation of Hibiscus cannabinus Leave](../publications/f67da2ed2efec8c55e9a.md)



Hibiscus cannabinus L\. \(kenaf\) is a medicinal plant known for its rich phytochemical composition and diverse pharmacological properties\.Although widely cultivated as a fiber crop, its leaves contain bioactive compounds such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, tannins, alkaloids, saponins, terpenoids, and glycosides, which exhibit antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti\-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, antidiabetic, and anticancer activities\.The increasing therapeutic importance of this plant has highlighted the need for reliable analytical methods to ensure its quality, safety, efficacy, and standardization\.Analytical evaluation of Hibiscus cannabinus leaves involves plant authentication, physicochemical analysis, phytochemical screening, chromatographic fingerprinting, quantitative estimation of marker compounds, and method validation\.Modern analytical techniques, including TLC, HPTLC, HPLC, UPLC, GC\-MS, LC\-MS/MS, UV\-Visible spectroscopy, FTIR, NMR, and ICP\-MS, are widely used for comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analysis\.This review provides an overview of the botanical characteristics, phytochemical constituents, traditional uses, and analytical methods employed for the evaluation of Hibiscus cannabinus leaves\.It also highlights current quality control strategies and recent advances that support the development of standardized and evidence\-based herbal medicines\.

## [Цифровые инструменты управления проектами как фактор экономии временных ресурсов](../publications/f68037475d69aefe4402.md)

Е\.Р\. Киржацких

В статье рассматривается вопрос о том, как цифровые инструменты управления проектами сокращают временные затраты организации\. Проектный менеджмент сегодня уходит от электронных таблиц к платформенным и аналитическим решениям\. Цель исследования – систематизировать инструменты по механизмам воздействия, выделить условия устойчивого эффекта и предложить аналитическую модель для диагностики\. Материалом послужили 17 источников: российские и международные научные работы, стандарты, учебники 2014–2025 годов\. Применялись контент\-анализ, сравнение и классификация, дополненные отраслевыми кейсами\. Выявлено: наибольший выигрыш во времени даёт не отдельный сервис, а связка планирования, коммуникаций, аналитики, автоматизации и единой среды данных\. This article examines how digital project management tools reduce organizational time expenditure\. Project management today is moving away from spreadsheets and email toward platform\-based and analytical solutions – making the time\-saving question a practical, not merely theoretical, concern\. The study aims to classify tools by their mechanisms of impact, identify conditions for a sustained effect, and propose an analytical model for diagnostics\. The source base comprises 17 items: Russian and international research papers, standards, and textbooks from 2014 to 2025\. The methods applied were content analysis, comparison, and classification, supplemented by industry case studies\. The findings show that the greatest time savings come not from any single service but from an integrated combination of planning, communications, analytics, automation, and a unified data environment\.

## [ØA\-fagenes relevans og omdømme i møte med kunstig intelligens](../publications/f688a9105af487272ccc.md)

June Borge Doornich; Trond Vegard Johannessen

Kunstig intelligens endrer forutsetningene for økonomisk\-administrative fag og profesjoner\. Når analyser, prognoser, beslutningsstøtte og rapportering i økende grad utføres med KI\-baserte systemer, utfordres etablerte forståelser av fagkompetanse, profesjonell dømmekraft og ØA\-fagenes samfunnsbidrag\. Dette temanummeret bygger videre på ØA\-konferansen 2026 ved NHH og undersøker hvordan ØA\-fagene kan bevare og styrke sin relevans og sitt omdømme i møte med teknologisk endring\. Bidragene viser at KI ikke gjør fagkompetanse overflødig, men skjerper behovet for kritisk vurderingsevne, pedagogisk nytenkning og institusjonell handlekraft\. ENGLISH ABSTRACT The Relevance and Reputation of Business and Economics Disciplines in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence is changing the conditions for business and economics disciplines and professions\. As analysis, forecasting, decision support and reporting are increasingly performed with AI\-based systems, established understandings of disciplinary expertise, professional judgement and the societal contribution of business and economics education are being challenged\. This special issue builds on the 2026 ØA Conference at NHH and explores how business and economics disciplines can maintain and strengthen their relevance and reputation in the face of technological change\. The contributions show that AI does not make disciplinary expertise obsolete, but rather increases the need for critical judgement, pedagogical renewal and institutional capacity to act\.

## [Cafeína e controle inibitório em jovens universitários](../publications/f695835854c491b8f9f0.md)

Luan Daher Fernandes; Letícia Cavalcante Gondim; Elinton Nascimento Castelo; Vanessa Novaes Barros

Objetivo: Delinear o perfil de consumo da cafeína de universitários e investigar sua associação com o desempenho em teste de controle inibitório\. Métodos: Estudo quantitativo, observacional, analítico e transversal com 51 estudantes de Medicina\. As expectativas quanto aos efeitos da cafeína foram avaliadas pelo Brief Caffeine Expectancy Questionnaire – Brazilian Version \(B\-CaffEQ\-Br\)\. O controle inibitório foi mensurado pelo Escore de Interferência de Golden do Stroop Color and Word Test \(SCWT\)\. Foram realizadas análises de correlação e comparação entre tercis\. Resultados: O escore médio do B\-CaffEQ\-Br foi de 77,8±22,5 pontos\. O Escore de Interferência de Golden apresentou média de 10,7±8,96\. Não foi observada associação estatisticamente significativa entre expectativas relacionadas à cafeína e desempenho no controle inibitório, tanto pela correlação de Pearson \(r=\-0,234; p=0,099\) quanto pela de Spearman \(ρ=\-0,190; p=0,182\)\. A comparação entre tercis de expectativa também não evidenciou diferenças significativas \(ANOVA de Welch: F=0,637; p=0,535\)\. Conclusão: Foi observada uma tendência à associação inversa entre as expectativas sobre os efeitos da cafeína e o desempenho cognitivo, mas sem significância estatística\. Não foram mensurados o consumo habitual da substância nem o grau de tolerância individual\.

## [In the Shadow of the AI Act: Legal Services by Artificial Intelligence\. A German Perspective](../publications/f69803b27f0673e19603.md)

Jörn Axel Kämmerer; Therese Lorenz

The use of AI poses a challenge to the rule of law\. While Art\. 1 of the AI Act and recitals testify to this, the Union’s legislative strategy is ambiguous\. At the example of the legal professions, this article expounds why this might thwart qualified and independent legal services which the Union otherwise cherishes\. For EU legislation for the free movement of digital services prevents the Member States from a stricter control of “legal services by AI” which also the AI Act addresses only in part\. There is a need for more leeway to effectively protect the rule of law\. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Legal profession; Rule of law; AI Act; Free movement of services
