## [The relationship between perceived supervisor support and turnover intention among professional football coaches: The mediating role of perceived job performance](../publications/f6abfae266c0f517d79e.md)

Anıl Siyahtaş

Supervisor support in football clubs plays a decisive role in coaches’ professional sustainability and their turnover intentions\. The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between perceived supervisor support and turnover intention among football coaches and to investigate the mediating role of perceived job performance in this relationship\. The study, designed with a cross\-sectional approach, was conducted with football coaches in Türkiye&\#x27;s professional leagues who have at least five years of experience \(n = 249; M age = 40\.61 ± 11\.42\)\. The factor structures of the scales were tested using Confirmatory Factor Analysis \(CFA\), and the hypothesized model with latent variables was examined through Structural Equation Modeling \(SEM\)\. The results indicated a positive relationship between perceived supervisor support and perceived job performance \(β = 0\.328, 95% CI \[0\.124, 0\.469\]\)\. The direct effect of perceived supervisor support on turnover intention was found to be significant and negative \(β = −0\.513, 95% CI \[−0\.641, −0\.373\]\)\. Additionally, perceived job performance played a significant mediating role in the relationship between perceived supervisor support and turnover intention \(β = −0\.048, 95% CI \[−0\.111, −0\.007\]\)\. These findings suggest that supervisor support is positively associated with football coaches’ perceived job performance and negatively associated with their turnover intention\. The mediating role of perceived job performance highlights an indirect association between perceived supervisor support and turnover intention\. Overall, the results underscore the importance of supportive managerial behaviors in football clubs\.

## [Development and validation of a prognostic prediction model for elderly patients with sepsis\-associated acute kidney injury based on interpretable machine learning](../publications/f6b401d39e6f60380c66.md)

Nan Zhang; Jian\-Zhong Wang; Qi Ma; Jinhai Tian; Wen\-Jie Zhou

Background Elderly patients with sepsis\-associated acute kidney injury \(SA\-AKI\) have high short\-term mortality; early identification of high\-risk individuals is critical for personalized intervention\. Traditional clinical scoring systems relying on linear assumptions and conventional machine learning models often lack interpretability, hindering translation to clinical practice\. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable prognostic model for 28\-day in\-hospital mortality in elderly SA\-AKI using routinely available clinical variables\. Methods Clinical data of 11,468 elderly SA\-AKI patients were retrospectively extracted from the MIMIC\-IV database and divided into training and internal test sets at a 7:3 ratio using stratified random sampling\. A dual feature selection strategy combining LASSO regression and random forest was applied\. Five machine learning models—decision tree, logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost—were constructed in parallel\. Model discrimination and calibration were evaluated by AUC, Brier score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F 1 score\. External independent validation was performed using a clinical cohort of 257 patients from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University\. The SHAP method was used for global and individual\-level interpretability of the optimal model\. Results Dual feature selection identified 10 independent predictors: age, weight, red blood cell distribution width, arterial partial pressure of oxygen, blood lactate, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, blood urea nitrogen, serum creatinine, and respiratory rate\. Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best performance, with training AUC 0\.9898 \(accuracy 0\.9472\) and external validation AUC 0\.9156 \(accuracy 0\.8560\), indicating strong generalizability\. SHAP global importance ranking showed age as the primary driver, followed by serum creatinine and arterial partial pressure of oxygen\. Each core feature exhibited a nonlinear association with 28\-day mortality risk, with clear model\-derived risk inflection points rather than clinical intervention thresholds\. Conclusion The XGBoost\-based interpretable model exhibits excellent discriminative performance and robust external generalizability for predicting 28\-day mortality in elderly SA\-AKI\. The SHAP attribution framework renders model decisions transparent, providing quantitative evidence\-based support for early risk stratification and hypothesis generation for individualized organ\-protective strategies in the ICU\.

## [Factors Associated with Disability Level Among Adult Patients with Low Back Pain](../publications/f6ba658dad6351057747.md)

Gao Linfeng; Sulaiman Delrizal; Dewi Asih

Background: Low back pain can restrict functioning through interacting symptoms, beliefs, and contextual demands\. Qualitative inquiry can clarify how these influences are experienced\. Objective: To explore perceived influences on disability and how they interact to restrict or support everyday functioning among adults with persistent low back pain\. Methods: An interpretive qualitative study used purposive maximum\-variation sampling to include 18 adults aged 25–66 years\. Individual semi\-structured interviews explored symptoms, movement, sleep, work, family roles, healthcare, and self\-management\. Oswestry Disability Index scores informed lower\-, moderate\-, and higher\-disability sampling profiles\. Interview material underwent reflexive thematic analysis, including examination of contrasting accounts and author review of interpretations\. Results: Participants comprised 10 women and eight men; five had lower, seven moderate, and six higher disability profiles\. Five themes were developed: Living with Unpredictable Pain; Fear, Threat, and Shrinking Activity; Caught Between Recovery and Livelihood; Support, Dependence, and Identity; and Clinical Explanations, Confidence, and Control\. Accounts connected restrictions with anticipated flares, perceived damage, poor sleep, work and financial pressures, and changing family roles\. Contrasting accounts described participation alongside pain when movement felt manageable and support preserved involvement\. Conclusion: Disability was experienced within the interaction of symptoms, interpretations, relationships, and practical circumstances\. Assessment and rehabilitation should consider barriers to meaningful participation alongside pain\. Keywords: low back pain; disability; qualitative research; biopsychosocial factors; fear avoidance; self\-efficacy; occupational health\.

## [Thermal\-economic performance assessment of heat recovery\-oriented design of integrated CCHP\-H₂ system; multi\-objective optimization with LCA and AdaBoost decision\-making](../publications/f6bae0636966d8362c08.md)

Man‐Wen Tian; Tirumala Uday Kumar Nutakki; Mohamed Arbi Khlifi; Mohammad Abdulhadi O Althobaiti; Ashrf Althbiti; Norah Alsairy; Hanaa Abu\-Zinadah; Абдуллаев Шерзод; Ibrahim Mahariq; Yasser Fouad

Combined cooling, heating, power systems integrated with hydrogen production \(CCHP–H₂\) can simultaneously supply useful outputs while improving the utilization of fuel and recoverable thermal energy\. The present project proposes a methane\-fueled CCHP–H₂ configuration integrating methane partial oxidation, a water–gas shift reactor, hydrogen separation, a gas\-turbine cycle, organic Rankine cycle, steam generation, and absorption refrigeration\. The system was modeled in Aspen HYSYS and assessed using energy, exergy, exergo\-economic, and exergo\-environmental analyses, complemented by life\-cycle assessment \(LCA\), machine\-learning \(ML\)\-based performance prediction, and multi\-objective optimization \(MOO\)\. Under the base\-case conditions, the system achieved energy and exergy efficiencies of 78\.28% and 66\.08%, respectively, while producing 2867 kW of electricity, 2059 kW of useful heat, 294 kW of cooling, and 0\.074 kg/s of hydrogen\. The corresponding levelized hydrogen cost, net present value, and payback period were 7\.532 USD/kgH₂, 19\.763 million USD, and 2\.09 years, respectively\. The specific CO₂ emission and global warming potential were 0\.2312 kg CO₂ /kWh and 4317\.7 kg CO₂ /h, respectively\. The optimized ML–MOO–TOPSIS solution increased exergy efficiency to 70\.67% and reduced specific CO₂ emissions to 0\.214 kg CO₂ /kWh while lowering the selected economic objective\. These results indicate that the proposed configuration can provide effective heat recovery and integrated polygeneration under the assumed operating and economic conditions\. Nevertheless, the results are based on steady\-state process simulation and system\-level assumptions for selected components; therefore, detailed equipment design, experimental validation, site\-specific LCA, and dynamic and uncertainty\-aware analyses are needed to assess practical deployment and performance under variable operating conditions\.

## [The Privacy\-Personalization Paradox in AI\-Driven Customer Experience Analytics: A Trust\-Centred Integrative Review and Responsible Personalization Framework](../publications/f6be29a90db7a0ed766f.md)

Rahmat Kofoworola Sanusi; Oreoluwa Abimbola Serifat; Temiloluwa Paul Adetola

Artificial intelligence increasingly supports personalised customer experiences through predictive analytics, recommender systems, behavioural profiling and conversational interfaces\. However, the data collection and inference required for personalisation can also heighten perceptions of surveillance, vulnerability and loss of control\. This integrative conceptual review examines how AI\-enabled personalisation, perceived privacy risk and consumer trust interact within customer experience analytics\. The synthesis integrates privacy calculus, social exchange, psychological reactance and signalling perspectives to explain how consumers evaluate personalisation value against privacy\-related costs\. A trust\-centred framework is developed in which personalisation intensity, data sensitivity, algorithmic inference and recommendation relevance jointly shape perceived value and privacy risk, with consumer trust linking these evaluations to engagement, disclosure willingness, satisfaction, loyalty and continued use\. The review also distinguishes actual data practices from perceived privacy intrusion and identifies contextual conditions that may alter this balance\. The review further proposes a context\-dependent nonlinear relationship between personalisation intensity and trust: moderate personalisation may strengthen trust when relevance and value are proportionate to data use, whereas more intensive personalisation may reduce trust when intrusion, surveillance or loss of autonomy becomes salient\. Responsible personalisation is therefore framed around proportionate data use, meaningful transparency, consumer control and privacy\-by\-design\. The framework and proposed personalisation threshold remain conceptual and require empirical testing across AI applications, cultural settings and regulatory environments\.

## [The Effect of Raw Material Imports, Exchange Rate, and Inflation on Non\-Oil and Gas Industrial Exports in Indonesia, 2021\-2023](../publications/f6c72206ce3f848f3e99.md)

Elang Rabbaanii Deandy Putra; Aprillia Nilasari

Indonesia’s non\-oil and gas industrial exports play an important role in supporting economic growth and generating foreign exchange; however, their performance is closely associated with imported production inputs, exchange\-rate movements, and inflation\. This study examined the effects of raw material imports, the rupiah–U\.S\. dollar exchange rate, and inflation on Indonesia’s non\-oil and gas industrial exports during 2021–2023\. The study employed a quantitative approach using 36 monthly observations obtained from Statistics Indonesia, Bank Indonesia, and the Ministry of Trade\. The data were analyzed using a Vector Error Correction Model \(VECM\) in Stata 17, following tests of stationarity, optimal lag length, Johansen cointegration, model stability, and relevant diagnostic assumptions\. The findings indicated the presence of two cointegrating relationships, confirming a long\-run equilibrium among the variables\. Raw material imports moved jointly with exports within the same long\-run system, reflecting the dependence of export\-oriented industries on imported production inputs\. The exchange rate had a positive but statistically insignificant effect on exports \(coefficient = 0\.4711; p = 0\.751\), whereas inflation had a positive and statistically significant effect \(coefficient = 4,446\.265; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. These findings imply that export policy should prioritize greater efficiency in raw material supply chains, prudent management of exchange\-rate volatility, and measures to mitigate imported inflation rather than relying primarily on currency depreciation to enhance export competitiveness\.

## [Deep Learning for Forest Plantation Mapping in Godavari Districts of Andhra Pradesh, India](../publications/f6cbaac1f16fe3c09e5e.md)

Snehal More; Anuj Karpatne; Valerie A\. Thomas; Randolph H\. Wynne

Small\-area forest plantations play a vital role in the socioeconomic well\-being of farmers in Southeast Asia\. Most plantations are established on former agricultural land, often on land less suitable for agriculture\. Plantations that are converted from natural forest have adverse impacts on biodiversity\. Mapping small\-area plantations is thus important to understand the dynamics of forest cover in Southeast Asia and to study the social, economic, and ecological effects of this important land cover and land use change\. While the small size of forest plantations makes it difficult to detect them using moderate resolution satellite sensors, the problem is exacerbated by the high degree of mixing between plantations, surrounding vegetation, and other land covers, which often show variegated responses in satellite signals across space and time\. In this paper, we study the problem of mapping small\-area forest plantations in East and West Godavari districts of Andhra Pradesh, India using deep learning methods\. Remotely sensed cloud\-free data from the Harmonized Landsat Sentinel\-2 S10 product were classified using a pixel\-level neural network and training data labeled using a field\-based survey in concert with expert aerial photo interpretation\. We compare the performance of deep learning methods with a baseline random forest classifier in our study region of 21543 sq\. km over a period of 3 years and analyze the differences in the results across land cover classes and seasons\.

## [A review of older adults’ acceptance of health monitoring tools: application status, theoretical acceptance models, and user\-related and context\-level influencing factors](../publications/f6cdd206e4b28a2e3cfc.md)

Qi Zhang; Zhang Yongqin

Health monitoring tools enable real\-time, accurate monitoring of physiological data in older adults, offering timely alerts and feedback that facilitate early detection of health problems and prompt intervention\. However, adoption and use of these tools among older adults remains limited, significantly constraining their practical effectiveness\. This narrative review examines the factors influencing older adults’ acceptance of health monitoring tools by synthesizing 49 studies, comprising 40 studies classified as core evidence and 9 as supplementary contextual evidence\. Relevant literature was identified through a snowballing approach, beginning with key articles and tracing their reference lists and citing articles\. Findings were synthesized through a thematic approach\. Among the theoretical models identified in this review, the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology are the most frequently applied, whereas the Senior Technology Acceptance Model, despite its specific relevance, has not been applied to health monitoring tool acceptance in any study included in this review\. Key influencing factors can be grouped into two categories: user\-related factors, such as demographic, health\-related, and psychological characteristics; and tool\- and context\-level factors, such as privacy and security of monitoring data, interaction experience and ease of use, device appearance and invasiveness, and economic costs associated with pricing and technology access\. Enhancing acceptance may require a comprehensive approach encompassing targeted health education and digital skills training, optimized user interfaces and privacy safeguards, multi\-tiered financial subsidies, and the development of innovative theoretical models tailored to the older adult population\.

## [LONG\-TERM OUTCOMES OF CYANOACRYLATE GLUE VERSUS TACK FIXATION OF MESH IN TRANSABDOMINAL PREPERITONEAL REPAIR \(TAPP\) IN PATIENTS WITH INGUINAL HERNIA](../publications/f6ce8916b2de63ea6bad.md)

Oleksandr Yu\. Ioffe; Oleksandr V\. Perekhrestenko; Artem V\. Trots

Introduction\. Laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal \(TAPP\) repair is widely used for surgical treatment of inguinal hernias\. However, the optimal method of mesh fixation remains debatable, as tack\-based fixation may increase tissue trauma and the risk of chronic postoperative inguinal pain, thereby worsening functional outcomes and quality of life\. Non\-invasive fixation with cyanoacrylate adhesives may reduce these adverse effects\.Aim\. To compare long\-term outcomes after TAPP repair in patients with inguinal hernias using invasive tack\-based and non\-invasive adhesive mesh fixation\.Materials and methods\. The study included 96 patients with primary, uncomplicated, unilateral inguinal hernias who underwent TAPP repair\. Patients were divided into two groups: the study group \(n=42\), in which mesh fixation was performed with cyanoacrylate glue LiquiBand® FIX8, and the comparison group \(n=54\), in which absorbable tacks using AbsorbaTack® were applied\. Outcomes were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months after surgery\. Pain intensity was evaluated using the visual analogue scale \(VAS\), functional status using the Carolinas Comfort Scale \(CCS\), quality of life using the EQ\-5D\-3L questionnaire, and recurrence rate was recorded\.Results\. Patients in the adhesive fixation group had significantly lower VAS pain scores during follow\-up compared with the tack fixation group \(p&lt;0\.05\)\. CCS scores also indicated better functional outcomes in the adhesive fixation group at all assessment time points\. According to EQ\-5D\-3L, the non\-invasive fixation group demonstrated better results in the pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression domains throughout follow\-up, as well as in the mobility domain at 3 months\. No inguinal hernia recurrences were recorded in either group during the first postoperative year\.Conclusions\. Cyanoacrylate adhesive mesh fixation during TAPP repair is associated with lower chronic postoperative inguinal pain, better functional recovery, and improved quality\-of\-life indicators compared with tack\-based fixation, without increasing the recurrence rate within 12 months\. Adhesive fixation may be considered a safe and justified alternative to mechanical tack fixation\.

## [MEDIBUDDY\-WHERE INTELLIGENT CARE MEET YOU](../publications/f6d4f2dc93ca8eb99ddb.md)



MediBuddy is a powerful Artificial Intelligence multi\-modal medical diagnostic system capable of helping health care professionals to detect and interpret diseases at an early stage from medical images\.The proposed framework combines deep learning image classification and Large Language Model \(LLM\) report generation to create a comprehensive diagnostic support solution\.It can analyze multiple types of medical imaging, such as brain MRI scans and chest X\-ray scans\.A DenseNet\-121 network is used to classify chest diseases from X\-ray images by detecting the presence of abnormalities in the chest, and ResNet\-18 network is used to classify brain\-tumors into four tumors category Pituitary Tumor, Meningioma, Glioma, and No Tumor\.To enhance the model accuracy and save training time, the transfer learning techniques are used by utilizing the pre\-trained weights from ImageNet\.Once the disease is predicted, the classification probabilities are fed into a locally deployed quantized LLaMA model that outputs brief clinical summaries of human\-readable texts\.The feature of automatic report generation increases the interpretability of AI predictions, aiding in medical decision making\.All the system is fully implemented using PyTorch framework and is executed on a local machine, thereby preserving data privacy and low latency\.The predictions are saved in JSON format\.The application also includes report viewing\.Experimental results are shown and tested for the effectiveness of disease classification using precision, recall, accuracy, F1\-score, ROC\-AUC analysis and confusion matrices\.Proposed system provides a scalable, privacy\-aware, and intelligent healthcare solution that enhances diagnostic efficiency and access in contemporary healthcare settings\.

## [Advanced age at onset is associated with distinct functional brain reorganization in multiple sclerosis](../publications/f6de7d2d3f48a870c8ba.md)

Nicolò Tedone; Paola Valsasina; Alessandro Meani; Paolo Preziosa; Marta Grosselle; Federica Esposito; Massimo Filippi; Maria Assunta Rocca

Abstract Functional network reorganization supports compensatory mechanisms in multiple sclerosis, but aging and later disease onset may alter this balance\. Late\-onset multiple sclerosis \(age at onset ≥50 years\) represents a relevant subgroup to examine how disease onset in older age is associated with functional connectivity abnormalities\. In this cross\-sectional study, we investigated resting\-state functional connectivity alterations in late\-onset multiple sclerosis versus adult\-onset multiple sclerosis and their associations with clinical, cognitive, and structural MRI measures\. Thirty\-four late\-onset multiple sclerosis, 169 sex\- and disease duration–matched adult\-onset multiple sclerosis, and 163 age\- and sex\-matched healthy controls underwent clinical, neuropsychological \(Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological Tests\), and MRI assessment including resting\-state functional MRI\. Independent component analysis quantified resting\-state functional connectivity within ten large\-scale networks\. Between\-group differences were tested using sex\- and scanner\-adjusted voxel\-wise models \(p&lt;0\.001, uncorrected, cluster extent ≥10 voxels\); resulting abnormal clusters were then examined for exploratory uncorrected associations with Expanded Disability Status Scale, disease duration, cognitive performance, T2\-hyperintense lesion volume, and normalized brain volume, without correction for multiple comparisons\. At MRI acquisition, compared with the adult\-onset multiple sclerosis group, the late\-onset multiple sclerosis group was significantly older \(median age: 60\.5 \[IQR: 56\.6–66\.1\] versus 35\.6 \[IQR: 30\.0–40\.1\] years; pFDR=0\.006\), showed higher Expanded Disability Status Scale score \(pFDR=0\.016\) and higher T2\-hyperintense lesion volume \(pFDR=0\.028\) despite similar disease duration \(median: 4\.5 \[IQR: 1\.7–13\.2\] versus 6\.0 \[IQR: 2\.1–11\.8\] years; pFDR=0\.894\), whereas no significant between\-group cognitive difference was found\. Both multiple sclerosis groups showed widespread functional connectivity abnormalities versus healthy controls, partly overlapping and partly distinct\. Adult\-onset multiple sclerosis displayed functional connectivity increases in the executive control and occipital default mode networks\. Late\-onset multiple sclerosis showed diffuse functional connectivity alterations, including decreases in the left fronto\-parietal, thalamic, and occipital default mode networks\. Exploratory uncorrected correlation analyses included 117 tested associations\. In late\-onset multiple sclerosis, decreased functional connectivity in the left fronto\-parietal network related to lower normalized brain volume and worse cognition \(p=0\.02–0\.03\), whereas altered thalamic network connectivity related to higher Expanded Disability Status Scale, longer disease duration, and higher T2\-hyperintense lesion volume \(p=0\.01\-0\.02\)\. These associations did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and should therefore be considered hypothesis\-generating\. These findings suggest that late\-onset multiple sclerosis was associated with a distinct resting\-state functional connectivity profile compared with adult\-onset multiple sclerosis within a cross\-sectional, age\-matched healthy control framework, possibly reflecting the combined contribution of multiple sclerosis\-related damage, age\-related vulnerability, and the more severe clinical profile of late\-onset multiple sclerosis\.

## [Dementia diagnosis rates according to ethnic groups: Analysis of primary care data in Bradford, UK](../publications/f6e38be2d0b3178072fb.md)

Lin Gong; Magda Jordão; Andrew Paul Clegg; Rebecca Hawkins; Kate Best

Abstract INTRODUCTION Ethnic differences in recorded dementia diagnosis may partially reflect differences in population age structure\. We examined ethnic differences in recorded dementia incidence, age at diagnosis, and age at death using UK primary care data\. METHODS We analyzed Connected Bradford data \(2009–2019\) for adults aged ≥ 45 years\. Poisson regression estimated incidence rate ratios adjusted for age, sex, and deprivation\. Linear regression examined age at diagnosis and death\. Age structure–standardized analyses used post‐stratification weights\. RESULTS Among 262,852 individuals, 4458 dementia diagnoses were identified\. Most ethnic differences in recorded incidence attenuated after adjustment\. Mixed/multiple ethnic groups had higher adjusted incidence than the White British group \(adjusted incidence rate ratio 1\.64, 95% confidence interval 1\.14–2\.37\)\. Differences in age at diagnosis and death among South Asian individuals attenuated and were no longer statistically significant after age‐structure standardization\. DISCUSSION These findings highlight the importance of considering age structure and deprivation when interpreting ethnic differences in recorded dementia diagnosis\.

## [New features of pytransform3d for robotics research: transformation graphs, uncertainty, and 3D visualization in Python](../publications/f6e3f0e852b90af3a9a5.md)

Alexander Fabisch; Mihaela Popescu

Rigid transformations in three dimensions \(3D\) are fundamental tools in robotics, computer vision and graphics, and physics simulation\. However, there are many pitfalls for practitioners: various alternative representations of rigid transformations and uncertainty, each with its own competing conventions, sometimes without clear documentation, ambiguities in representations, singularities, and difficulties in handling many transformations in complex systems\. This article presents the new features of pytransform3d , a Python library for working with rigid transformations in 3D that helps tackle these difficulties\. Specifically, we show applications of its new batch data processing functions, uncertainty propagation, and 3D visualization\. Furthermore, we present applications of its transformation graph TransformManager , a tool inspired by tf of the Robot Operating System \(ROS\), which has a subclass for loading robot kinematics and a new subclass that handles time\-varying transformations\. In examples from imitation learning, kinematics, state estimation, and log data processing, we demonstrate these features and show that only a few lines of code are sufficient to solve these complex problems correctly\. The explicit terminology of the library makes this code readable and reviewable\. The library has 100% test coverage of its core features, has a broader feature set than comparable libraries, and handles batch processing of spatial data in fewer lines of code and faster than its alternatives\.

## [Enhancing immunogenicity: Evaluating the polio antigen immune response in hexavalent vaccine formulations](../publications/f6e48a44fa3d2f0822c8.md)

Tiza Wuri Mawaddah; Elisa D\. Pratiwi; Arif Rahman Sadjuri; Dimas Tri Nugroho; Arip Hidayat; Acep Riza Wijayadikusumah; Astria Novitasari Nidom; Zakiyyan I\. Ayyuba; Kadek Rachmawati; Suwarno Suwarno; Jola Rahmahani; Setyarina Indrasari; Reviany V\. Nidom; Chairul Anwar Nidom

Hexavalent vaccines simplify childhood immunization by combining antigens against six diseases in a single formulation; however, the immunogenicity of each component must be evaluated\. This study assessed poliovirus\-specific immunoglobulin G \(IgG\) responses elicited by candidate hexavalent vaccines containing different doses of Sabin strain\-derived inactivated poliovirus vaccine \(sIPV\)\. A preclinical study was conducted using 40 Wistar rats allocated to five groups: hexavalent vaccine containing low\-, medium\-, or high\-dose sIPV; pentavalent vaccine combined with sIPV; or adjuvant control\. Each group comprised four male and four female rats\. The animals received primary immunization at week 0 and booster doses at weeks 4 and 8\. Serotype\-specific IgG titers were measured at weeks 0, 4, 8, and 12 using indirect enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay\. Antibody responses were analyzed using repeated\-measures analysis of variance\. Titers against poliovirus serotypes 1, 2, and 3 were negligible at baseline and remained low at week 4\. Marked responses were observed in all vaccinated groups at week 8, followed by lower titers at week 12\. Significant between\-group differences were detected at weeks 8 and 12 for serotype 1 \(p&lt;0\.001 and p=0\.010\), serotype 2 \(both p&lt;0\.001\), and serotype 3 \(both p=0\.010\)\. However, no consistent dose–response pattern was observed across serotypes, time points, or sexes\. All animals survived and gained body weight during follow\-up\. The candidate hexavalent formulations elicited marked poliovirus\-specific binding\-IgG responses, supporting further preclinical evaluation using validated serological and serotype\-specific neutralization assays\.

## [Single\-cell RNA sequencing of the Tumor Microenvironment in Gynaecological Cancer: Cellular Heterogeneity, Computational Approaches and Clinical Applications](../publications/f6e5d8a9ad2427fc6c47.md)

Neha Bonagiri; Elamathi Natarajan

Single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\) has emerged as a powerful technological advancement, overcoming the primary limitation of bulk\-RNA sequencing–its inability to capture cellular heterogeneity\. Consequently, scRNA\-seq plays a pivotal role in characterising the complex cellular landscape of the tumor microenvironment\. Composed of diverse populations, including immune and stromal cells, and characterised by intricate cell\-to\-cell interactions, the tumor microenvironment is a central driver of tumorigenesis\. Examining these dynamic biological systems at the transcriptomic level enables detailed mapping of intercellular communications and facilitates the discovery of targeted therapeutic strategies\. This review outlines the end\-to\-end scRNA\-seq workflow, covering fundamental single\-cell isolation methods, downstream computational analyses, and key analytical software, as well as their practical significance\. Additionally, it highlights the integration of spatial transcriptomics, which provides crucial positional context to achieve a more comprehensive understanding of intra\-tumoral heterogeneity\. Special emphasis is placed on gynaecological malignancies, particularly cervical and endometrial cancers\. Given the rising incidence of both malignancies in recent years, detailed characterisation of their specific microenvironments is critical for advancing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic intervention\. A comprehensive understanding of the progression of the cancer and drug resistance is critical to understand\. Accordingly, key molecular alterations, potential gene targets, and emerging biomarkers are systematically reviewed\. Finally, current technical constraints, recent technological advancements, and future perspectives for single\-cell transcriptomics are evaluated\. Keywords: Keywords: Cell\-Cell communication; Cervical cancer; Endometrial cancer; Spatial transcriptomics; Tools

## [Circadian–melatonin signaling in general anesthesia: molecular mechanisms and perioperative implications](../publications/f6e6549723995bb1be98.md)

Wui\-Chiu Mui; Yi\-Chou Hou¹; Yi‐Cheng Liao; Kuo‐Cheng Lu

Anesthesia and surgery are delivered to a temporally organized organism whose physiology is governed by the suprachiasmatic nucleus, peripheral molecular clocks, and pineal melatonin signaling\. This review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence on how anesthetic agents, surgical stress, and the perioperative environment interact with circadian and melatonergic signaling, and on whether that interaction can be targeted therapeutically\. In rodent and cellular studies, volatile and intravenous anesthetics alter clock function in an agent\- and phase\-dependent manner; proposed mechanisms include GABAergic and glutamatergic modulation of entrainment, transcriptional and chromatin\-level repression of CLOCK–BMAL1/PER–CRY signaling, and metabolic coupling through CaMK–CREB, AMPK, SIRT1, and GSK\-3β\. These mechanisms have not been confirmed in humans\. In patients, these effects are inseparable from surgical injury, opioids, fasting, inflammation, and disrupted light–dark exposure, all of which suppress melatonin amplitude, delay its onset, and promote internal desynchrony\. Melatonin signals through MT 1 and MT 2 receptors to produce chronobiotic, anxiolytic, and antinociceptive effects, whereas the mitochondrial, redox, and anti\-inflammatory actions, described almost exclusively in animal and cellular models, require substantially higher exposures and have not been demonstrated in surgical patients; the two arms are pharmacologically distinct and should not be pooled\. Clinically, preoperative anxiolysis with melatonin in adults is the most consistently supported indication, whereas evidence for postoperative sleep, analgesia, delirium prevention, and organ protection remains heterogeneous and of low certainty\. Most trials have used fixed clock\-time dosing without measuring internal circadian phase or achieved plasma exposure, so null results cannot distinguish an ineffective mechanism from an inadequate intervention\. The circadian–melatonin axis remains a plausible perioperative target, but clinical translation requires phase\-aware, exposure\-informed, and adequately powered trials\.

## [ASE: Attribution\-Guided Semantic Evolution for Time Series Forecasting](../publications/f6f171e2128f38730c0c.md)

Yuxuan Zheng; Zhaoyang Li; Purui Liu; Hengbo Xiao; Guannan He

External text can supply predictive information absent from numerical histories, but its value depends on how it is represented, combined and deployed\. We present Attribution\-guided Semantic Evolution \(ASE\), a modular framework for constructing textual factors, evaluating their conditional contribution, and deploying validation\-selected numerical\-\-textual predictors\. ASE supports task\-specific implementations with lexical measurements, semantic primitives or evolved event/state factors, coupled to suitable numerical experts\. Its feedback\-based implementation uses conditional refitting diagnostics to guide factor revision and combination search\. We evaluate ASE on the four text\-associated TESS datasets and dynamic CSI 300 stock ranking\. The four forecasting implementations obtain test MSEs of 0\.001041, 0\.022439, 0\.333115 and 1\.8150, each below the corresponding published TESS score\. On CSI 300, the frozen text\-fusion implementation improves mean RankIC by 0\.000642 over its numerical expert and by 0\.000701 over matched shuffled text, with positive differences in all five seeds\. Controlled text perturbations support functional reliance on text correspondence, while incumbent retention prevents regressions in the measured development criterion\. Together, the experiments characterize ASE at two levels: forecasting performance of task\-specific implementations and the conditional contributions of individual modules\.

## [Acute effect of immersive VR technology on postural control and reaction time in young adults: a randomized controlled trial](../publications/f6fa67d9e5e4ba81b18b.md)

Maciej Tomasz Kochman; Michal Kručko; Izabela Niekurzak

Abstract Immersive virtual reality \(VR\) has become a promising tool for sports training and rehabilitation due to its potential in modulating sensorimotor function\. However, the acute effects of a single VR session on sensory organization and reaction time remain unclear, especially when both outcomes are assessed simultaneously\. In this randomized controlled trial we investigated whether an acute VR intervention changes sensory organization and reaction time \(LOS RT\) in healthy young adults\. Eighty\-one healthy adults aged 18–25 years were randomly assigned to an immersive VR group \( n = 41\) or a passive control group \( n = 40\)\. The VR group completed a physically active 20\-minute immersive VR motor task using an HTC VIVE Cosmos head\-mounted display, whereas controls rested in a seated position for the same duration\. Computerized dynamic posturography was performed before and immediately after the intervention using the Neurocom SMART EquiTest system\. The primary outcome was the Sensory Organization Test \(SOT\) Composite Score\. Secondary outcomes included the somatosensory \(SOM\), visual \(VIS\), vestibular \(VEST\), and visual preference \(PREF\) indices, as well as reaction time \(LOS RT\) measured during the Limits of Stability test\. The primary intervention effect was assessed using ANCOVA adjusted for the corresponding baseline value\. At baseline, the VR group had lower Composite Score and VEST values than the control group\. After adjustment for baseline values, no significant between\-group difference was observed for Composite Score \(adjusted mean difference 0\.51, 95% CI − 1\.53 to 2\.55; p = 0\.623\)\. Similarly, no significant between\-group differences were observed for SOM \(1\.29, 95% CI − 1\.59 to 4\.17; p = 0\.380\), VIS \(− 1\.01, 95% CI − 4\.96 to 2\.94; p = 0\.615\), VEST \(− 1\.20, 95% CI − 6\.00 to 3\.59; p = 0\.623\), PREF \(0\.55, 95% CI − 2\.97 to 4\.07; p = 0\.761\), or LOS RT \(0\.004 s, 95% CI − 0\.049 to 0\.058; p = 0\.872\)\. A sensitivity analysis based on group × time interactions yielded a consistent pattern, with no statistically significant between\-group differences in change over time\. Under the conditions of this randomized controlled trial, a single 20\-minute session of immersive VR did not produce statistically detectable between\-group effects on postural control or LOS reaction time in healthy young adults\. Although some within\-group changes were observed, these did not differ significantly from changes in the passive control group and may therefore reflect nonspecific factors such as repeated testing or familiarization\. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials\.gov, NCT07709065 \(retrospectively registered on 15/07/2026\)\.

## [Identification of kinematic motifs in crouch gait of children with cerebral palsy](../publications/f70cb751a9c5afbe0833.md)

Shyam K\. Krishnan; Manish C\. Poojari; Abhishek Kumar; C\. M\. C\. Krishnan; Bhaskaran Unnikrishnan; Abraham M\. Joshua; Sheron Figarado; Megha M Nayak

Abstract Crouch gait is among the most disabling gait deviations in cerebral palsy \(CP\)\. Powered exoskeletons can supply the extensor thrust orthoses cannot, but their control depends on repeatable kinematic patterns, and crouch gait is perceived as irregular\. Five children with CP \(8–14 years; Gross Motor Function Classification System \[GMFCS\] I–III\) walked at self\-selected speed wearing bilateral shank inertial measurement units, knee goniometers and insole pressure sensors at the heel and forefoot\. Signals were filtered with a two\-state Kalman filter, adaptively segmented into gait cycles using plantar\-pressure events \(heel or toe strike\), and time\-normalised to 101 points\. A kinematic motif was defined as a limb’s ensemble waveform and validated using the coefficient of variation, ICC\(3,1\), dynamic time warping, autocorrelation and 1,000\-iteration permutation testing; symmetry was quantified with the Symmetry Index\. Repeatability tracked the signal measured rather than functional severity: mean ICC\(3,1\) was 0\.76 for forefoot loading, 0\.61 for heel loading and 0\.29 for knee kinematics\. Full criteria were met in 12 of 30 limb–signal combinations, 12 met one or two, and 6 met none\. Five of the six failures were knee channels, also the only channels indistinguishable from a permuted null, yet the knee met all criteria bilaterally in the least affected participant\. These preliminary findings establish feasibility in a heterogeneous cohort \( n = 5\); no gait\-phase classifier was trained or evaluated here\.

## [The Bargaining\-Verification Trap in AI\-Mediated Work: An Integrated Theory of Productivity, Worker Voice, and Organisational Resilience](../publications/f713222db6d1ab80000a.md)

Kwan Hong Tan

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is changing not only the technological content of work but also the allocation of decision rights, the distribution of productivity gains, and organisations’ capacity to verify their own outputs\. Existing literatures establish that AI can raise task productivity, algorithmic management can intensify control, and automation can alter labour shares\. Few models integrate these mechanisms in one tractable analytical framework\. This article introduces the bargaining\-verification trap, a conditional regime in which greater AI delegation initially increases joint economic surplus but simultaneously reduces workers’ effective bargaining share, raises the congestion cost of human verification, and may erode the skills needed for intervention\. We develop a two\-sided model linking delegation intensity, queueing\-based verification capacity, an opacity\-sensitive bargaining rule, and a dynamic stock of human agency capital\. We derive conditions under which worker remuneration falls while joint surplus rises; the firm’s preferred delegation exceeds the surplus\-maximising level; and verification becomes less stable because review arrivals increase while independent human capacity deteriorates\. A fully hypothetical numerical example separates the worker\-income optimum, the joint\-surplus optimum, and the firm\-profit optimum\. The theory is reconciled with divergent 2025\-2026 labour\-market evidence and translated into falsifiable propositions, measurement protocols, and governance principles\. Its central implication is conditional rather than technologically deterministic: AI\-mediated work can be both productive and inclusive when bargaining institutions, verification investment, and skill reproduction develop alongside automation, but increasing throughput cannot, by itself, establish that they have done so\.

## [Model Predictive Current Control and Direct Torque Control for SRM With Cost Function‐Based Switching States to Optimize System Performance](../publications/f71b964f3f19d744ef0f.md)

G\. Prakash; K Dhineshkumar; G\. Ramya; S\. Nagaraj

ABSTRACT This paper presents a model predictive current control \(MPCC\) strategy for switched reluctance motors \(SRMs\) aimed at mitigating the computational complexity and torque ripple issues commonly associated with conventional control methods\. To address these challenges, an integrated MPCC and direct torque control \(DTC\) framework is proposed, leveraging active voltage vectors \(VVs\) that incorporate rotor position‐dependent sector selection\. This approach enables accurate prediction of phase current trajectories across various switching states\. A key feature of the proposed method is the sector‐based allocation, which limits the number of active switching states to four, substantially improving its real‐time applicability\. The control algorithm minimizes a cost function that penalizes both current tracking error and switching effort, thereby ensuring precise current regulation while reducing unnecessary switching transitions\. Furthermore, the integrated MPCC‐DTC algorithm enhances torque control by employing Model Predictive Phase Compensation to identify the motor phase with optimal torque tracking capability\. The proposed model was developed and validated using MATLAB, and the simulation results were verified for torque regulation under dynamic conditions\. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid control strategy significantly reduces computational overhead while achieving superior torque ripple suppression compared to conventional predictive controllers\.

## [Integrative network toxicology and pharmacology reveal that kaempferol alleviates BaP\-triggered pulmonary fibrosis via suppressing Ras/COX\-2\-dependent cellular senescence](../publications/f7288333cba99e53f2fe.md)

Qi Zhao; Dongwei Zhu; Zhichao Wu; Xiaolin Xia; Yehui Li; Aojie Guo; Yong Xu; Xianmei Zhou

Background Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis \(IPF\) is a chronic, progressive lung disease\. Benzo\[a\]pyrene \(BaP\), a major constituent of cigarette smoke and air pollution, has been closely associated with pulmonary fibrosis\. However, its molecular mechanism remains unclear\. The natural flavonoid kaempferol possesses anti\-inflammatory and antioxidant properties\. However, its effects and mechanisms in BaP\-induced pulmonary fibrosis remain unclear\. Objectives This study aimed to predict potential targets of BaP\-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention in BaP\-induced IPF, and to validate whether kaempferol reverses BaP\-induced epithelial senescence and fibrosis via the Ras/COX\-2 signaling pathway in vitro \. Methods Network toxicology, network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking were integrated to predict potential targets of BaP\-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention, followed by GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses\. Additionally, virtual knockout analysis was performed to explore the regulatory relationships among Ras, COX\-2, and cellular senescence\. MLE\-12 cells were used as an in vitro model, and senescence\-related indicators were assessed by SA\-β\-gal staining, Western blot, and ELISA\. Results KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that these targets were significantly enriched in the Ras signaling pathway\. Molecular docking confirmed that kaempferol exhibited good binding affinity for the above target proteins\. Cell experiments demonstrated that BaP significantly promoted cellular senescence and activated Ras and COX\-2\. Kaempferol treatment effectively reversed these changes\. Conclusion This study reveals that BaP promotes IPF by inducing epithelial cell senescence via the Ras/COX\-2 signaling pathway\. Kaempferol may exert anti\-fibrotic effects by counteracting this pathway\-mediated senescence\. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the pulmonary fibrosis effects of BaP and support kaempferol as a potential anti\-fibrotic agent\.

## [Emerging AI for resilient smart\-grid fault detection: an evidence\-based capability synthesis, maturity assessment, and research roadmap](../publications/f73b702b64cbd33919f9.md)

Pagidimarri Krishna

Abstract This evidence\-based critical review examines how emerging artificial\-intelligence \(AI\) capabilities can strengthen resilient smart\-grid fault intelligence\. Rather than comparing algorithms primarily by reported accuracy, the review organizes recent fault\-detection evidence around operational capabilities: spatial/topology awareness, temporal context, label efficiency, physical consistency, trust and uncertainty, privacy\-preserving collaboration, and deployment feasibility\. A structured primary\-study evidence matrix was developed to extract task, system or dataset, topology, temporal context, robustness, trust, privacy, physics, deployment evidence, and principal limitations\. The extracted evidence shows a clear asymmetry in the maturity of emerging approaches\. Recent Transformer work demonstrates real\-time temporal fault detection on test\-system waveforms, self\-supervised methods reduce dependence on manually labeled events, physics\-informed approaches can narrow the simulation\-to\-field gap, and graph\-based models increasingly address topology and cross\-topology generalization\. However, external validation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility, and standardized deployment evidence remain uneven\. Based on this evidence, the paper introduces a fault\-intelligence evidence maturity profile that avoids reducing readiness to a single generic score\. The synthesis leads to an evidence\-derived roadmap progressing from trustworthy and data\-efficient intelligence to topology\- and physics\-aware learning, distributed cyber\-physical intelligence, and finally integrated safety\-bounded decision support\. The review deliberately distinguishes demonstrated evidence from plausible future capability and therefore avoids unsupported claims of algorithmic superiority\.

## [Glucose transport as a design constraint in white\-zone meniscus tissue engineering: a reaction\-diffusion framework](../publications/f743d2011554dd145f0f.md)

Tiya Patel

The adult knee meniscus has a strong vascular gradient: the peripheral red zone is vascularized, whereas the inner white zone is largely avascular and has limited intrinsic healing potential after injury\. Although biologic augmentation and scaffold\-based strategies are being explored to improve meniscal repair, it remains unclear whether modifying local glucose transport can improve glucose availability at deep white\-zone tears\. This study uses a one\-dimensional reaction\-diffusion framework to model normalized glucose concentration from a vascularized red\-zone boundary toward a simulated 2\.5 mm white\-zone tear\. Glucose diffusivity values were selected from reported meniscus glucose\-diffusion measurements under different compressive strain conditions, and the model compares native diffusivity cases with an augmented sustained\-source case representing a hypothetical scaffold\- or microchannel\-assisted transport scenario\. The framework reports threshold\-free glucose profiles, mathematical fractional\-restoration comparison levels \(C/C0 = 0\.20, 0\.30, 0\.40, and 0\.50\), source\-release kinetics, tear\-depth sensitivity, initial\-condition sensitivity, extended simulation windows, and model\-derived diffusivity enhancement estimates\. The comparison levels are not validated healing thresholds or clinical targets\. Native glucose diffusivity cases remained below C/C0 = 0\.30 at a tear located 2\.5 mm from the red\-zone boundary, even when selected simulations were extended to 24 h\. In contrast, an augmented sustained\-source example reached C/C0 = 0\.20, 0\.30, and 0\.40 within the 4\-h transport window\. Initial condition sensitivity showed that the main interpretation remained unchanged when the model was initialized with a reference steady glucose profile rather than a depleted domain\. These results do not demonstrate biological healing, but they provide a hypothesis\-generating framework for defining glucose transport experiments and planning future ex vivo validation studies\.

## [A Prospective Observational Study of Diagnostic Accuracy of White Light Endoscopy and Narrow Band Imaging in Diagnosis of Helicobacter Pylori Infection by Examination of Gastric Mucosal Pattern](../publications/f7449f2df3e217604eb2.md)

Srikanth Thiyagaraja; Vignesh Sambandamurth; Vijay Balaji R G; Sivamarieswaran R

Background: Helicobacter pylori infection remains one of the most prevalent chronic bacterial infections worldwide and is a major etiological factor for chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, mucosa\-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma, and gastric adenocarcinoma\. Although histopathological examination of endoscopic biopsy specimens remains the reference standard for diagnosis, it is invasive, time\-consuming, susceptible to sampling error, and increases procedural costs\. Narrow Band Imaging \(NBI\) is an image\-enhanced endoscopic technique that selectively uses narrow\-spectrum blue and green wavelengths to improve visualization of superficial mucosal microvascular architecture and microsurface patterns\. Characteristic endoscopic findings such as loss of the Regular Arrangement of Collecting Venules \(RAC\), diffuse mucosal redness, mucosal edema, and map\-like redness have been shown to correlate with H\. pylori infection and mucosal healing following eradication therapy\. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of conventional White Light Imaging \(WLI\) and NBI against histopathological examination for the real\-time diagnosis of H\. pylori infection in patients presenting with dyspepsia\. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted at SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Tamil Nadu, India, between December 2024 and May 2025\. A total of 126 consecutive adult patients with persistent dyspeptic symptoms underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy using sequential WLI followed by NBI\. Gastric mucosal features, including RAC, diffuse redness, mucosal edema, and map\-like redness, were systematically evaluated in the antrum and corpus\. Targeted biopsies were obtained according to institutional protocol and served as the reference standard for histopathological diagnosis\. Patients diagnosed with H\. pylori infection received standard eradication therapy and underwent repeat NBI evaluation after treatment to assess mucosal recovery\. Diagnostic indices including sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, overall accuracy, and statistical significance were calculated\. Results: Histopathological examination confirmed H\. pylori infection in 68 of the 126 patients \(54\.0%\)\. WLI demonstrated a sensitivity of 78\.3%, specificity of 75\.5%, and overall diagnostic accuracy of 77\.0%\. In comparison, NBI showed significantly superior diagnostic performance, with a sensitivity of 93\.4%, specificity of 89\.2%, positive predictive value of 91\.7%, negative predictive value of 90\.9%, and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 91\.0% \(p = 0\.02\)\. Loss of RAC, diffuse mucosal redness, and mucosal edema demonstrated a strong association with active infection, whereas reappearance of RAC and resolution of inflammatory changes were observed in 92% of patients following eradication therapy\. These findings indicate that NBI accurately differentiates active infection, uninfected gastric mucosa, and post\-eradication healing in real time\. Conclusions: Narrow Band Imaging is a highly accurate, safe, and minimally invasive technique for the real\-time diagnosis of Helicobacter pylori infection\. Compared with conventional White Light Imaging, NBI provides superior visualization of gastric mucosal architecture and microvascular patterns, resulting in improved diagnostic accuracy and facilitating targeted biopsy\. In addition to its value in primary diagnosis, NBI enables reliable assessment of mucosal healing following eradication therapy and has the potential to reduce unnecessary biopsies, shorten procedural time, and improve endoscopic decision\-making\. Wider incorporation of NBI into routine upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, together with future integration of artificial intelligence\-assisted image analysis, may further enhance the diagnosis and management of H\. pylori\-associated gastric disease\.

## [Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review](../publications/f75b60f147da325c2151.md)

Nazanin Amiryaghoubi; Mahnaz Sadeghi; Farzaneh Sadeghi; Soumayeh Amirsaadat; Mehdi Jaymand; Morteza Akbari; Guodong Liu; Rana Jahanban

Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments\-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors\-remain major contributors to global visual impairment\. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior\-segment targets\. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site\-specific delivery\. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials\-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid\-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal\-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers\-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene\-based agents\. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions\. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA\-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies\. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano\-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real\-time disease assessment\. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI\-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next\-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration\.

## [The 46th Annual Meeting of the J\.B\. Johnston Club for Evolutionary Neuroscience and the 38th Annual Karger Workshop in Evolutionary Neurosciences](../publications/f75c59abaa112d46ba2a.md)

## [Low\-temperature monolithic integration of patterned distributed Bragg reflectors for high\-resolution QD\-OLED microdisplays](../publications/f75dafcfba658b56561c.md)

Jin\-Wook Shin; Seung Wan Woo; Hyunsu Cho; 최수경; Jun Yong Kim; Hyunjun Jang; Gi Heon Kim; In‐Bok Baek; Byoung‐Hwa Kwon; Nam Sung Cho; Chun‐Won Byun; Hyoc Min Youn; Jin Sun Kim; Jong Ho Jeong; Jung Youn Bae; Jonghee Lee; Chan‐mo Kang

With the increasing demand for hyper\-realistic displays, significant advancements have been reported in high\-resolution quantum dot–organic light\-emitting diode \(QD\-OLED\) technology owing to its wide color gamut and improved color purity\. However, achieving both high color purity and light extraction remains a critical challenge due to significant blue light leakage in high resolution QD\-OLED\. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating a damage\-free, low\-temperature \( &lt; 100 °C\) monolithic integration of patterned distributed Bragg reflectors \(DBRs\) directly onto a QD\-OLED stack to effectively suppress blue leakage and enhance conversion efficiency\. DBRs fabricated from SiN x and SiO x using low\-temperature \( &lt; 100 °C\) plasma\-enhanced chemical vapor deposition demonstrate high reflectance of 95\.9% at 455 nm while effectively suppressing reflectance in the red and green regions\. A high\-precision, one\-step fluorine\-based dry etching process achieved a 4 μm pattern size with a near\-vertical taper angle of 89°, supporting pixel densities up to 3175 ppi\. Compared to the device without DBR, the monolithically integrated architecture exhibits a photon recycling effect, enhancing red and green emission intensities by 19\.7% and 10\.7%, respectively, while reducing blue leakage by approximately 90%\. Furthermore, the integrated device achieved a color gamut of 120\.5% relative to the sRGB standard\. These findings confirm that monolithically integrated DBRs serve as a robust and scalable solution for next\-generation high\-resolution QD\-OLED displays\.

## [Intelligent Load Balancing and Query Optimization in Distributed Graph Database Architectures](../publications/f76577843ae20116bffa.md)

Jabulani Khumalo

Distributed graph databases have become increasingly important for managing complex relationships in social networks, financial transactions, recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, cybersecurity, and large\-scale data analytics\. However, distributing graph data across multiple servers introduces significant challenges related to workload imbalance, communication overhead, partition fragmentation, query execution latency, and resource utilization\. Traditional load\-balancing and query\-optimization techniques often struggle with graph workloads because graph structures exhibit irregular connectivity, skewed degree distributions, and highly variable traversal patterns\. This research investigates an intelligent framework for load balancing and query optimization in distributed graph database architectures by integrating artificial intelligence, machine learning, graph partitioning, workload prediction, and adaptive query scheduling\. The proposed framework combines workload\-aware graph partitioning, predictive resource allocation, cost\-based query planning, and runtime feedback to improve distributed query performance\. It considers graph locality, node centrality, edge distribution, cache utilization, network communication, server capacity, and query complexity when making optimization decisions\. An experimental evaluation framework is developed to compare a conventional static architecture with an intelligent adaptive architecture using query latency, throughput, load imbalance, communication overhead, and resource utilization as performance indicators\. Illustrative experimental results demonstrate how predictive scheduling and adaptive partitioning could improve throughput, reduce response time, and distribute computational workloads more evenly across participating servers\. These results are hypothetical and are intended to demonstrate the proposed methodology rather than represent measurements from an executed benchmark\. The research concludes that integrating machine learning with distributed graph processing can provide a foundation for scalable and adaptive database management, particularly when optimization decisions are guided by workload characteristics, real\-time system conditions, and measurable performance objectives\.

## [Bridging Chemical Literature and Molecular Graphs: LLM‐Augmented Enantioselectivity Prediction for Iridium‐Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Borylation](../publications/f77d5db46a136a031719.md)

Zhe Wang; Baohua Zhang; Yi Yang; Yuan Yao; Yinwu Li

Asymmetric C\-H borylation provides direct access to enantioenriched organoboron compounds\. Predictive catalyst design for this reaction class remains challenging, as stereocontrol arises from coupled interactions among catalyst, substrate, and product structures\. Moreover, mechanistic knowledge is dispersed across the literature\. Here we report a machine\-learning framework for predicting enantioselectivity in iridium\-catalyzed asymmetric C\-H borylation that bridges molecular graphs and chemical literature\. A unified dataset comprising 800 literature\-reported reactions was constructed for this reaction class\. The model combines a multi\-entity three\-dimensional graph encoder for catalyst, substrate, and product with temperature\-aware kinetic treatment, and a large\-language\-model prior module that extracts atom\-resolved mechanistic annotations from primary publications\. On a scaffold\-based held\-out test set, the STEREO\-Lit \(Spatial Three\-Entity Reaction Encoder Literature\) model achieves strong predictive performance, outperforming conventional machine\-learning baselines and a geometry\-grounded control\. Perturbation studies further show that literature\-derived semantic annotations contribute chemically meaningful, site\-specific information rather than merely increasing model capacity\. The trained model was subsequently applied to explore a reaction space of about 100 000 catalyst\-substrate combinations and identify promising high\-improvement candidates, several of which were supported by DFT calculations\. The framework couples multi\-entity 3D encoding with literature\-derived priors, and remains predictive when training data are limited to a few hundred reactions\.

## [&quot;Deep lifts&quot;: Neural networks can generalize even with the dumbest optimizer](../publications/f78d82f3b1350b153407.md)

Sunil Madhow; Yu\-Xiang Wang

Given a labeled dataset $\\\{\(x\_i, y\_i\)\\\}\_\{i = 1\}^n$, consider drawing a parameter vector $\\hatθ$ uniformly at random from those that interpolate the data within a width\-$W$ depth\-$D$ ReLU architecture with continuous weights bounded within $\[\-M, M\]$\. We study the generalization properties of $\\hatθ$ in the case where the dataset can, in fact, be explained by a smaller $w$\-by\-$d$ ReLU network\. Despite the obliviousness of the selection rule for $\\hatθ$, it adaptively generalizes at the rate $\\tilde O\\left\(\\frac\{wdWD\}\{n\}\\right\)$, rather than being governed by the VC dimension of the full $W$\-by\-$D$ hypothesis class\. The reason is due to a particular inductive bias in ReLU networks: the $w$\-by\-$d$ parameter \*witnesses\* an exponential volume of $W$\-by\-$D$ interpolating parameters, which dwarfs the volume of poorly generalizing parameters \(conditioned on interpolation\)\. We explicitly construct this set of near\-equivalent $W$\-by\-$D$ parameters by a proof technique called \*deep lifting\*, and then tie the achievable volume to stability properties of the $w$\-by\-$d$ witness\. Examples show that these techniques allow us to convert approximation\-theoretic results into generalization guarantees for nonparametric classes\. We further show that generalization of uniform\-random interpolators can survive label corruptions\.

## [Laplacian Ranking \( LaRa \): A Convex Graph‐Regularized Model for Multi‐Criteria Ranking](../publications/f78e38fc56d512a2d4da.md)

Valdecy Pereira; Márcio Pereira Basílio; Fatih Yiğit

ABSTRACT Laplacian Ranking \(LaRa\) is a graph‐regularized multi‐criteria decision analysis method that incorporates relational geometry among alternatives into ranking while preserving convexity, interpretability and deterministic reproducibility\. LaRa combines quantile normalization, metric‐weighted distances, a sparse similarity graph, a reference‐oriented prior and an optional quadratic pairwise target‐gap term\. Its base score is the unique minimizer of a strictly convex quadratic objective, obtained by solving a symmetric positive definite linear system, with an optional deterministic dominance‐repair step\. We evaluate LaRa on seven literature‐grounded real‐data problems spanning materials, manufacturing equipment, industrial robotics, renewable‐energy siting, and energy‐technology selection, together with a controlled synthetic pharmaceutical‐style benchmark\. Five cross‐domain cases use one common fixed configuration and sensitivity grid rather than dataset‐specific tuning\. Results show that the graph contribution is regime‐dependent\. It is ordinally inert for cryogenic materials and clean‐energy technologies, measurable but non‐disruptive for flywheel selection, improves concordance with published rankings for CNC machine tools, arc‐welding robots and Colombian solar‐PV siting, and reduces concordance for gear‐material selection, which is retained as an explicit failure boundary\. On the fixed synthetic benchmark, the high‐smoothing configuration attains Kendall&\#x27;s and Spearman&\#x27;s , reduces mean absolute rank error from 0\.556 for TOPSIS to 0\.111, and exactly recovers the Top‐3 set\. These findings position LaRa as a relational refinement of pointwise MCDA whose usefulness depends on whether neighbourhood geometry is substantively meaningful and empirically supported\. Accordingly, graph smoothing should be activated as a conditional modelling component and accompanied by sensitivity analysis rather than assumed beneficial in practical MCDA applications\.

## [An experimental study on the effects of mix design parameters, test methods, and time\-dependence of chloride penetration in concrete](../publications/f7b77d87c0c8b511f777.md)

Michele da Cruz Larrossa; Gustavo Bosel Wally; Mauro de Vasconcellos Real; Fábio Costa Magalhães; César O\. Avellaneda

Abstract Prescriptive durability approaches have proven insufficient to ensure the designed service life of reinforced concrete structures, particularly in highly aggressive environments\. Consequently, several codes introduced performance\-based specifications to promote more durable designs\. These approaches rely on assessing concrete durability\-related properties that reflect how the material performs under specific exposure conditions, known as durability indicators\. Such parameters are directly influenced by the concrete constituent materials and mix design parameters\. Understanding the effects of these factors is therefore essential for developing designs that enhance structural performance and durability\. This paper assesses the behavior of 28 concrete mixes produced with different materials and specifications\. The influences of various binder systems and mix design parameters on properties directly related to resistance to chloride ingress are evaluated, including chloride migration, electrical resistivity, and water absorption\. Different cement types, mineral additions, water/cement and water/binder ratios, and dry mortar contents are adopted\. The results show that prescriptive parameters are relevant for concretes with similar binder systems, while differences between distinct binder groups are mainly controlled by the chemical properties of the binders\. In this sense, the findings contribute to bridging prescriptive mix design parameters and performance\-based durability approaches, highlighting the importance of binder characteristics for a more consistent interpretation of concrete durability indicators under chloride penetration\.

## [Collective Memory and Disaster Risk Reduction in Turgo and Karangkendal Communities Around Merapi](../publications/f7d40ae1a40c8ae6bbc0.md)

Syamsul Fuad; Toetik Koesbardiyati; Ririh Yudhastuti

Communities surrounding Mount Merapi have experienced recurrent volcanic eruptions for generations, developing local knowledge and disaster preparedness practices that have been preserved and transmitted through collective memory\. This study examined how collective memory influenced disaster risk reduction \(DRR\) practices and explored why inherited local wisdom did not always prevent casualties during volcanic eruptions\. A qualitative study was conducted between 2025 and 2026 in Turgo Hamlet and the Karangkendal Permanent Resettlement Area \(Hunian Tetap or Huntap Karangkendal\), Sleman Regency, Indonesia\. Six participants, comprising community members and key informants, were interviewed in depth\. Data collection was supported by field observations of residential settlements, observation of the labuhan ritual procession, and a review of historical eruption records and relevant literature\. The findings revealed that collective memory evolved following the major eruptions of 1994, 2006, and 2010\. Delayed evacuation or failure to evacuate was associated with responsibilities for livestock, previous experiences of settlements remaining unaffected, beliefs regarding natural protective barriers and predictable eruption pathways, perceived moral obligations, the rapid onset and progression of volcanic hazards, and the absence of timely warnings during the 1994 eruption\. Disaster risk reduction practices gradually shifted from reliance on natural warning signs and manually operated warning devices toward official volcanic alert levels, siren systems, digital communication technologies, household emergency preparedness, designated evacuation routes, disaster preparedness training, and evacuation simulations\. Collective memory was transmitted through family narratives, annual commemorative activities, memorial monuments, and youth participation, although declining interest among younger generations posed challenges to its intergenerational continuity\. The findings demonstrated that collective memory could strengthen community preparedness and disaster resilience while also perpetuating inaccurate assumptions about volcanic hazards\. Therefore, historical verification and the integration of scientifically validated hazard information were essential to ensure that collective memory contributed effectively to local disaster knowledge, risk communication, and evidence\-informed disaster risk reduction strategies\.
