## [Association Between Neuropsychological Test Performance and Neuroimaging Findings in Cognitive Impairment: A Retrospective Cohort Study](../publications/f925cfc45acaeccffa38.md)

Mesut Dorukoğlu; Dilek Evyapan; Cenk Eraslan

BACKGROUND: Structural magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) and \[18F\]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography \(FDG\-PET\) provide different information about cognitive impairment, but the additional contribution of FDG\-PET beyond MRI across cognitive outcomes remains unclear\. This study examined associations between neuropsychological performance and MRI/FDG\-PET findings\. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 200 patients with mild cognitive impairment or dementia\. Neuropsychological assessment covered global cognition and memory, executive, visuospatial and language domains\. Structural MRI was evaluated using the Modified Visual Magnetic Resonance Rating Scale; FDG\-PET data were available for 68 patients\. MRI\-only, FDG\-PET\-only and combined models were compared\. RESULTS: Structural MRI abnormalities showed broad associations with global and domain\-level cognitive performance\. Sulcal and ventricular atrophy were associated with multiple cognitive domains, while regional FDG\-PET findings aligned with corresponding domains\. The additional contribution of FDG\-PET beyond MRI appeared most evident for global cognition, more modest for executive performance and limited for several other outcomes\. CONCLUSIONS: Structural MRI showed broad multidomain associations, while regional FDG\-PET findings corresponded to cognitive performance\. The additional explanatory contribution of FDG\-PET appeared to vary across cognitive outcomes, warranting cautious interpretation and further evaluation\.

## [Healthy older adults&\#x27; preferences for home care services](../publications/f926081af8b7f56f5e06.md)

Xiaoke Yang; Tao Chen; Junhua Ke; Hui Lin; Wenxi Fan

Background As the aging population in China continues to grow, understanding the preferences and willingness to pay \(WTP\) for home care services among healthy older adult citizens becomes increasingly important\. Most existing research focuses on disabled or semi\-disabled older adult individuals, leaving a gap in knowledge regarding the preferences of those who are healthy and capable of self\-care\. Objectives This study aims to explore the WTP for various home care services among healthy older adult citizens in Xi&\#x27;an, China, and to analyze how different socio\-demographic factors influence these preferences\. Methods A discrete choice experiment \(DCE\) was conducted to elicit preferences for home care services among a sample of healthy older adult citizens\. The experiment included four non\-monetary attributes \(healthcare services, safety services, household affairs, and emotional care\) and one monetary attribute \(payment\)\. A mixed logit model was used to estimate individual\-level WTP for these services, followed by a Tobit regression analysis to identify socio\-demographic factors influencing WTP\. Results The results indicate a significant positive WTP for all care services, with home repair \(162 Yuan/month\), traditional Chinese medicine physiotherapy \(125 Yuan/month\), and social activities \(103 Yuan/month\), being the most valued services\. On average, respondents were willing to pay 628 Yuan per month for all care services combined\. Heterogeneity in WTP was observed, with higher WTP among women, those living alone, those with worse health status, those with employee medical insurance and those with less financial pressure\. Conclusions The findings suggest that healthy older adult citizens in China have diverse needs for home care services, highlighting the importance of tailoring these services to specific subgroups\. By addressing the varying preferences and WTP among the older adult population, service providers and policymakers can better meet the needs of this growing demographic, ultimately improving their quality of life\. Further research is needed to generalize these findings to other regions and to explore the longitudinal changes in preferences as individuals age\.

## [Cross\-Cultural Adaptation and Content Validation of the Kannada Version of the Western Ontario Rotator Cuff Index](../publications/f927583ecba2a8101e71.md)

Changaroth K\. Aiswarya; Saumya Srivastava

Objectives The study aimed to translate the Western Ontario Rotator Cuff \(WORC\) Index into Kannada, adapt it culturally and evaluate its content validity for use among Kannada\-speaking individuals with Rotator Cuff\-Related Shoulder Pain \(RCRSP\)\. Material and Methods The questionnaire was translated and culturally adapted using widely accepted Beaton’s guidelines\. Two native Kannada speakers separately performed forward translation of WORC from English to Kannada, and the translated versions were then combined into a synthesised version\. Following this, two native Kannada speakers who were fluent in English and unaware of the original version independently translated the synthesised Kannada version back into English\. All versions were reviewed by an expert committee including four translators, the principal investigator, a senior physiotherapist and two musculoskeletal physiotherapy postgraduate students to ensure that the translations matched the original in terms of meaning, phrases and concepts\. A pre\-final version was prepared after making necessary modifications\. The pre\-final version was first given to 20 patients with shoulder pain related to rotator cuff pathology through face\-to\-face cognitive interviews\. Following this, content validity was assessed by five physiotherapists, each with over two years of experience in treating shoulder conditions\. They individually evaluated all 21 items in the questionnaire across three dimensions \(relevance, clarity, and cultural appropriateness\) using a five\-point rating scale \(5 = excellent match, 4 = very good, 3 = good, 2 = fair, 1 = poor\)\. Item\-Content Validity Index \(I\-CVI\), Scale\-Content Validity Index/Universal Agreement \(S\-CVI/UA\), and Scale\-Content Validity Index/Average \(S\-CVI/Ave\) were calculated using a predefined threshold of I\-CVI ≥0\.80 and S\-CVI/Ave ≥0\.90\. Results During the translation and cross\-cultural adaptation process, three items required minor modifications: two for improved clarity and one for cultural appropriateness, without altering conceptual meaning\. Pre\-testing with 20 participants indicated the translation was clear and culturally appropriate\. Content validity demonstrated good agreement across all three dimensions, with all items achieving I\-CVI values ≥0\.80 and S\-CVI/Ave ≥0\.90\. Conclusion The Kannada version of the WORC Index has been translated, culturally adapted, and content validated for use among the Kannada\-speaking population with RCRSP\.

## [Graph\-based reinforcement learning framework with control barrier functions for safe marine traffic control](../publications/f936b2a6ee5549b41e2c.md)

Hitoshi Yoshioka; Hirotada Hashimoto; Kai Cai

Centralized control that optimizes ship behavior is an effective approach for managing marine traffic in congested waters\. This study proposed a decision\-making framework that generates optimal control actions for all ships in a sea area using traffic data represented as a graph\. In this framework, control actions that optimize overall marine traffic are learned through reinforcement learning \(RL\)\. Safety constraints based on control barrier functions \(CBFs\) are introduced to prevent local dangers from being overlooked during optimization\. To incorporate CBFs into RL, this study proposed a deterministic graph control barrier function \(D\-GCBF\) that does not require explicit state equations and is independent of the policy\. D\-GCBF deterministically evaluates whether a policy violates the safety constraints while implicitly accounting for future maneuvering behavior\. D\-GCBF is integrated into the RL objective function\. A centralized control policy trained using this framework was evaluated through numerical experiments in both simple and congested scenarios\. The results indicate its ability to control all ships safely while maintaining larger safety margins\. Compared to policies trained using RL or D\-GCBF alone, the proposed framework outperformed all tested approaches\. Specifically, it prevents situations where ships become surrounded by multiple ships and cannot perform collision\-avoidance maneuvers\. Furthermore, comparisons with a decentralized collision\-avoidance artificial intelligence and a representative Lagrangian\-based safe\-RL method demonstrated that the proposed framework reduces the occurrence of dangerous situations while maintaining efficient navigation toward the waypoint\. These findings indicate that the proposed framework could help realize next\-generation maritime traffic management systems and enhance marine transportation safety\.

## [Connectivity optimization of artificial neural network with evolutionary computation algorithms](../publications/f93b928faca3814da0a7.md)

M\. Akın Yılmaz; Mustafa Servet Kıran

Human intelligence has historically produced various solutions to the challenges it has faced thanks to its cognitive abilities such as learning, remembering, comparing, and problem\-solving\. One of the most fundamental examples of artificial intelligence approaches that emerged by modeling these behaviors specific to intelligence is the artificial neural network \(ANN\), inspired by the biological nervous system\. ANNs, with their similarity to biological nervous systems, present a highly complex system, and with technological advancements, the modeling and applicability of these systems are constantly increasing\. In this study, a new ANN architecture inspired by the biological nervous system was designed\. To improve the classification performance of the developed architecture, the connections in the network were treated as a binary optimization problem and optimized using the Binary Particle Swarm Optimization \(BPSO\) algorithm\. Following the architecture design, the weights of the connections in the network were optimized using the Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\) algorithm which works with continuous values\. As a result, a network architecture compatible with the biological nervous system, flexible in structure, and highly applicable to various problem types was created\. The developed method was tested on Breast Cancer, Hepatitis, Mammographic Mass and Haberman’s Survival datasets\. Additionally, proposed model compared with the Genetic Algorithm \(GA\), one of the most widely used evolutionary computation methods in the literature for connection optimization\. Specifically, the proposed model reduces the input layer size from 5 to 2 in the Mammographic Mass domain by applying aggressive feature selection\. It successfully reduces computational complexity by eliminating up to 12 hidden neurons in the Hepatitis dataset without sacrificing classification accuracy, thus providing significant structural pruning\. Furthermore, it demonstrates high stability across all metrics with minimal standard deviation, proving that the synergy between binary and continuous swarm variants generates highly concise, lightweight, and efficient neural network topologies

## [A Comprehensive Review of Fault‐Current Limiter Technologies for Smart and Resilient Power Systems](../publications/f9418af2c8c028d66546.md)

Abdelrahman Farghly; Eslam Essam; Hilmy El\-sayed Awad; Samia Abdel Fattah; Walid R\. Issa; A\.M\. Hamada

ABSTRACT The transition toward inverter‐dominated, renewable‐rich power systems has significantly increased short‐circuit levels, often exceeding the interrupting capability of conventional protection\. Fault‐current limiters \(FCLs\) have emerged as important technologies for mitigating these currents and supporting grid reliability\. This article provides a comprehensive, system‐oriented review that bridges device‐level FCL characteristics with grid‐level requirements across alternating current, direct current \(DC\), and hybrid networks\. It systematically categorizes and evaluates superconducting FCL, solid‐state FCL, and hybrid FCL technologies, detailing their operating principles, dynamic fault responses, and control strategies\. A structured comparison framework is established to assess the trade‐offs among current‐limiting capability, response speed, steady‐state losses, cost, and technical maturity\. In addition to device‐level classification, the review examines fault‐current behavior in modern grids by considering inverter‐limited fault currents \(inverter‐based resource saturation\), DC offset decay dynamics, and asymmetrical fault conditions using symmetrical components\. The review also examines the coordination of FCLs with adaptive protection schemes and considers optimization approaches for FCL placement and sizing in converter‐dominated networks\. The findings indicate that no single FCL technology is universally superior; optimal selection depends on specific operating constraints, fault characteristics, and voltage levels\. Finally, the review highlights several areas that warrant further investigation, including standardized benchmarking, long‐term field validation, and improved integration with modern control architectures\.

## [Addressing the burden and associated factors of undernutrition in under\-five children with congenital heart disease in Pakistan: evidence from a multicenter cross\-sectional study](../publications/f945ec058205d1c1da15.md)

Muhammad Imran Khan; Ijaz ul Haq; Muhammad Awais; Shahbaz Ahmad Zakki; Sohail Akhtar; Muhammad Ayaz Ghulam Nabi; Elmuez Alsir Ahmed Aboagarib; Manjur Kolhar; Xianghui Huang; Xiaojing Hu

Background Children with congenital heart disease \(CHD\) are at heightened risk of undernutrition due to elevated metabolic demands, feeding intolerance, and growth failure\. This study aimed to identify the associated factors of undernutrition among children under 5 years with CHD in Pakistan\. Methods A hospital\-based study was carried out among 197 confirmed CHD across three tertiary hospitals in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa \(KP\)\. WHO\-recommended standards and structured questionnaires were used\. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of undernutrition\. Results Overall, 58\.9% were male, 40\.1% were stunted, 44\.2% were underweight, and 35\.5% were wasted\. Ventricular septal defect was the most common CHD \(34\.5%\), followed by patent ductus arteriosus \(23\.4%\)\. Infants aged 6–11 months had the most severe deficits\. Male children had significantly higher odds of wasting than female children \(adjusted odds ratio \[aOR\] = 2\.10, 95% CI: 1\.10–3\.98\), whereas children from households with a monthly income of ≥ PKR 40,000 had lower odds of wasting \(aOR = 0\.45, 95% CI: 0\.24–0\.84\) and underweight \(aOR = 0\.52, 95% CI: 0\.29–0\.94\)\. Similarly, children whose fathers were government employees \(aOR = 0\.30, 95% CI: 0\.09–0\.98\) also had lower odds of being underweight\. No sociodemographic or clinical variables were significantly associated with stunting \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. Conclusion Undernutrition exhibits a high distribution and severity among young CHD children\. Multiple associated factors of undernutrition based on wasting and underweight were identified\. Timely referrals for nutritional support are of great significance in preventing nutritional deterioration\.

## [Teaching the moving body with a still pedagogy: body percussion and the coupling architecture of embodied learning in physical education](../publications/f957567777a789406294.md)

Francisco Javier Romero\-Naranjo

Embodied learning is an influential orientation in physical education and sport pedagogy, but the field lacks agreement on which property of a movement practice does the educational work\. Function\-based frameworks locate it in the epistemic function that movement performs\. This paper proposes one such function for rhythmic group practices: the distribution of influence over a shared timing structure\. External entrainment is defined as unidirectional coupling to a source that performers cannot influence, and mutual entrainment as bidirectional coupling in which each participant is at once sound source and receiver\. The core claim is that reducing the asymmetry of that distribution widens the range of coordinative solutions a group explores, improves transfer to untrained patterns and tempi, and speeds recovery after perturbation, at a cost in fidelity to the trained pattern\. The proposed active ingredient is contingency rather than variability: under mutual coupling a participant&\#x27;s correction alters the target, which an irregular but unresponsive source does not\. This contrast supplies the principal test and separates the proposal from contextual interference and constraints\-led accounts\. The Coupling Asymmetry Index is built from established measures: pairwise phase\-correction gains, estimated as in published work on string quartets, are aggregated as the complement of weighted network reciprocity, which makes the index invariant to group size\. A mean\-field regime, in which participants adapt to the ensemble aggregate, is distinguished and shown to limit the group size at which reciprocity can be sustained\. Body percussion is the exemplary case because it is the classroom practice in which coupling architecture is a free design variable\. Two further claims follow\. Current practice and evidence in body percussion are prescriptive despite an embodied justification, a claim stated as a testable hypothesis with a survey protocol\. And this default is an institutional frame factor inherited from the material organization of the classroom rather than a property of any method\. The paper derives boundary conditions, an observational framework for practitioners, ten falsifiable propositions and a five\-item reporting standard\.

## [A qualitative study on decent work perception among male nurses in the ICU](../publications/f95a59c4716d57eaec4c.md)

Xianyong Liu; Mengjun Sun; Jiahang Li; MioLeng Au

Objective To explore the lived experiences of decent work perception among male ICU nurses in China, so as to provide evidence for nursing administrators to improve management strategies and retain male nursing workforce\. Methods An interpretative phenomenological research design guided by the Psychology of Working Theory was adopted\. Using purposive sampling, 14 male nurses working in ICUs were recruited from multiple tertiary hospitals across four provinces in China\. Semi\-structured in\-depth interviews were conducted between June and July 2026, and the data were analyzed using Van Manen’s six\-step phenomenological analysis method\. Results Findings revealed a dynamic process underlying male ICU nurses’ experiences of decent work\. Participants constructed a sense of decent work through institutional safeguards, social recognition, and professional value\. However, this experience was continuously challenged and eroded by high\-pressure working conditions, gender stereotypes, and insufficient respect\. Despite these challenges, male ICU nurses pursued more decent work through expectations for career development, supportive working conditions, and greater social recognition\. Conclusion Hospitals and nursing managers should pay attention to the unique challenges faced by male ICU nurses, including professional identity conflicts and insufficient social recognition arising from high\-intensity work environments and culturally rooted masculine role expectations within the Chinese context\. Targeted efforts should be made to strengthen professional recognition and provide diverse career development pathways to promote the sustainable development of the male nursing workforce\.

## [EEG Lempel\-Ziv Complexity vis\-à\-vis Autocorrelation Function](../publications/f963638ab4868f77b900.md)

Pedro Montoya; Ignacio Cifre; José Luis Rosselló Sanz; Dante R\. Chialvo

Measures of signal complexity have become increasingly popular in electroencephalography \(EEG\), where they are often interpreted as indicators of neural information processing, dynamical richness, or conscious state\. In contrast, classical measures of temporal dependence, such as the autocorrelation function \(ACF\), remain more directly linked to known physiological mechanisms and are easier to interpret\. The present work revisits, for the EEG practicioner, the relation between normalized Lempel\-Ziv complexity \(LZC\) and temporal autocorrelation in both synthetic and physiological EEG signals\. First, synthetic time series exhibiting a broad range of temporal structure and complexity levels were generated using stochastic processes with varying degrees of temporal dependence\. LZC and autocorrelation measures were then computed and compared\. Across simulated signals, a robust inverse relationship was observed between normalized LZC and the first autocorrelation coefficient, indicating that signals with stronger temporal correlations exhibit lower complexity estimates\. This relationship also holds in resting\-state EEG recordings from healthy adult participants across channels and subjects, as well as dynamically during eyes open/close maneuvers\. Overall, these results show that the information captured by LZC reflects temporal redundancy already quantified by conventional autocorrelation measures\. Because autocorrelation measures relate more directly to established neurophysiological mechanisms, including oscillatory persistence, network synchronization, and temporal integration, these results suggest that interpreting complexity\-based EEG findings should explicitly account for their dependence on conventional temporal statistics, which may provide a more transparent framework for mechanistic inferences\.

## [Microfungi associated with Azadirachta \(Meliaceae, Sapindales\): New species, new records, and a global checklist](../publications/f9708ef8b58b24d8d14c.md)

Ashani D\. Madagammana; Chitrabhanu Sharma Bhunjun; Chayanard Phukhamsakda; Dong\-Qin Dai; Sajad Ali; Samantha C\. Karunarathna; Kevin D\. Hyde; Haohan Wang

Azadirachta \(Meliaceae\) is a small genus comprising economically and ecologically important plants, including A\. indica , which is widely used in traditional medicine and other applications such as natural pest control and cosmetics\. Several studies have previously been conducted on Azadirachta , including its phytochemistry and associated microfungi, particularly endophytic species inhabiting the A\. indica host\. In this study, dead stems of Azadirachta indica bearing fungal fruiting bodies were collected, and the fungi were isolated\. Based on morphology and multi\-locus \(ITS, LSU, SSU, tef 1\-α, and rpb 2\) phylogenetic analyses using maximum likelihood \(ML\) and Bayesian inference \(BI\), the taxonomic placements of the isolated fungal strains were determined\. Five taxa are reported, including two new species, Neomassaria azadirachtae and Nigrograna azadirachtae ; Aquadictyospora yunnanensis as a new host and geographical record; and Neoaquastroma bauhiniae and Pararoussoella lincangensis as two additional new host records\. All new isolates in this study belong to Pleosporales \( Dothideomycetes , Ascomycota \), contributing to the understanding of the diversity of Pleosporales taxa associated with Azadirachta \. In addition, a global checklist of 212 microfungal taxa and fungus\-like Oomycota \(excluding Basidiomycota \) reported from Azadirachta species has been compiled\. Of the two known Azadirachta species \( A\. indica and A\. excelsa \), most fungal species were recorded from A\. indica \(210 species\), whereas only one was reported from A\. excelsa \. This study provides an updated overview of fungal diversity associated with Azadirachta , particularly A\. indica , with a global checklist and new saprobic collections including new species, host records, and geographical records\.

## [Optimalisasi Pengembangan Kompetensi Pegawai Melalui Human Capital Approach Pada Sekretariat DPRD Kabupaten Bolaang Mongondow Utara](../publications/f971f9caa658a19961d6.md)

Fadilah Amalia Kariem; Andi Yusniar Mendo; Valentina Monoarfa

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan Human Capital Approach, menganalisis efektivitas manajemen sumber daya manusia dalam meningkatkan kompetensi pegawai, serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya di Sekretariat DPRD Kabupaten Bolaang Mongondow Utara\. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi terhadap tujuh informan yang dipilih secara purposif\. Analisis data dilakukan melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Human Capital Approach diterapkan dengan memandang pegawai sebagai aset strategis organisasi melalui pengembangan kompetensi berupa pendidikan, pelatihan, bimbingan teknis, dan pemanfaatan teknologi digital\. Manajemen SDM telah berjalan cukup baik, ditunjukkan oleh kesesuaian kompetensi pegawai dengan bidang tugas serta peningkatan pengetahuan, keterampilan, sikap kerja, dan kesiapan melaksanakan pekerjaan\. Namun, penerapannya belum optimal karena kesempatan pelatihan belum merata dan rutin, kemampuan teknologi pegawai beragam, serta keterbatasan fasilitas dan sumber daya\. Faktor pendukung meliputi pimpinan, rekan kerja, lingkungan kerja, pelatihan, dan anggaran\. Pengembangan kompetensi perlu dilakukan secara berkelanjutan, merata, sesuai kebutuhan tugas, serta didukung pendampingan dan fasilitas yang memadait\.

## [Current evidence of flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy under local anesthesia: feasibility, safety, and clinical application](../publications/f973f2801d9475d79f4a.md)

Hongbo Chen; Shiyu Xing; Shenglong Shi; Shufan Lai

Flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy \(FURL\) is commonly performed under general or neuraxial anesthesia, but local anesthesia \(LA\) has been explored as an alternative for selected patients\. This structured narrative review summarizes current evidence for LA\-FURL while explicitly separating LA alone, LA combined with systemic analgesia or conscious/moderate sedation, peripheral regional blocks, and neuraxial anesthesia\. An updated literature search identified a small but growing body of direct LA\-FURL evidence, consisting predominantly of retrospective or single\-arm clinical series together with recent larger prospective cohorts\. These studies suggest that FURL can be completed and tolerated under LA in selected patients, with stone\-free rates generally in the range reported by individual series; however, differences in stone burden, anesthesia protocols, access\-sheath technology, imaging modality, timing, and definitions of stone\-free status preclude a pooled estimate or a claim of equivalence to general anesthesia\. Observational complication profiles are encouraging, but comparative safety and non\-inferiority versus general anesthesia have not been established\. Technical measures such as careful patient preparation, gentle instrumentation, suction\-assisted access sheaths, attention to intrarenal pressure, and selective pre\-stenting may be useful, but most have not been validated as LA\-FURL\-specific standards\. Evidence from ureteroscopy under conscious sedation is considered separately because it represents a distinct anesthetic strategy\. Overall, LA\-FURL is a promising option for appropriately selected patients and experienced teams, particularly when avoidance of general or neuraxial anesthesia is desirable, but the current evidence base remains heterogeneous and largely nonrandomized\. Prospective comparative studies with standardized definitions of procedural completion, stone\-free status, pain, complications, patient\-reported outcomes, and cost are required before broader recommendations can be made\.

## [Clinicopathologic Characteristics, Treatment Patterns, and Survival Outcomes in Malignant Mesothelioma: A Population\-based SEER Study, 2004\-2023](../publications/f97c5e18ecb2a6545e63.md)

Enes Yeşilbaş; Galip Can Uyar; Kadriye Başkurt; Güner Akgüner; İsmail Dilli; Mustafa Altınbaş

Objective: Treatment for malignant mesothelioma has changed over two decades\.We described clinicopathologic features, treatment patterns, and survival by primary site, diagnosis era, age group, and histologic subtype\. Material and Methods:This population\-based retrospective cohort study used the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results \(SEER\) 17 registries and included a total of 10,873 patients diagnosed between 2004 and 2023\.Overall survival \(OS\) and cancer\-specific survival \(CSS\) were analyzed with Kaplan\-Meier estimation, log\-rank testing, Cox regression, and Fine\-Gray competing\-risk regression\.Results: Pleural mesothelioma occurred in 8,886 patients, peritoneal mesothelioma in 1,377 patients, and other or unknown sites in 610 patients\.Men comprised 72\.7%; 63\.6% had distant\-stage disease; and 43\.0%lacked a specified subtype\.Chemotherapy was recorded in 48\.5%, surgery in 26\.9%, and radiation in 9\.8%\.Median OS was 9 months and median CSS was 11 months; median OS was 17 months in peritoneal disease and 9 months in pleural disease\.Peritoneal site was associated with lower mortality \[adjusted hazard ratio \(aHR\): 0\.81; 95% confidence interval \(CI\): 0\.76\-0\.88\];diagnosis during 2016\-2023 was also associated with lower mortality \(aHR: 0\.84; 95% CI: 0\.80\-0\.88\)\.Fibrous histology \(aHR: 1\.99; 95% CI: 1\.85\-2\.13\)and age 80 years or older \(aHR: 2\.00; 95% CI: 1\.86\-2\.16\)were associated with higher mortality; all p&lt;0\.001\.Fine\-Gray estimates were directionally consistent \(peritoneal site: subdistribution HR: 0\.87\)\.Conclusion: Mesothelioma survival remained poor overall, but was better among patients diagnosed in 2016\-2023\.Advanced age, fibrous histology, and unspecified subtype were associated with higher adjusted mortality\.More complete subtype ascertainment and reporting would strengthen prognostic interpretation and registry\-based research\.

## [Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Predict Dental Crowding in Modern Orthodontic Practice: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/f9815de9af9a0322f4c6.md)

Xiwen Xin; Shun‐Yu Kan; Tianle Chen; Ching‐Chang Ko

ABSTRACT Dental crowding is fundamental to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, yet what constitutes “crowding” remains surprisingly heterogeneous\. Space analysis quantifies tooth size–arch length discrepancy, irregularity indices characterize alignment displacement, and clinician‐assigned severity reflects broader diagnostic interpretation\. This narrative review examines the evolution of crowding assessment from conventional space analysis and digital measurement to two‐dimensional artificial intelligence \(AI\), three‐dimensional point‐cloud learning, and clinician‐aware agentic AI\. Digitalization improves efficiency and reproducibility but does not resolve fundamental dependencies on how crowding is defined, anatomically represented, and established as a reference standard\. Two‐dimensional models enable prediction from readily available images but are constrained by projection and scale, whereas three‐dimensional approaches directly learn from dental surface representations and can capture local geometric relationships\. In a companion study of 495 arches from 284 patients, PointNet\+\+ achieved an R 2 of 0\.718 and a mean absolute error \(MAE\) of 1\.54 mm for prediction of crowding\. In a separate retrospective demonstration, a bounded Gemini‐based Agent incorporating matched record‐derived verbal information reduced MAE from 1\.951 to 1\.437 mm, whereas mismatched information degraded performance\. These findings also illustrate that the target construct—the specific clinical feature of crowding that a model is trained to predict—may differ across assessment methods\. Together, these findings highlight a fundamental challenge: improving prediction does not resolve ambiguity in the target construct\. Future crowding AI should therefore align the target construct, reference standard, and input representation; preserve provenance and uncertainty; integrate complementary clinical information transparently; and route uncertain cases for expert review\.

## [A Study of the Major Challenges Facing Satellite Ground Stations](../publications/f9960d6d81e63e7c98b1.md)

Abdullahi S\. Ayegba; Ikpaya Ikpaya; Idakwoji Husseini

Satellite ground stations play a vital role in satellite communication, telemetry, tracking, command operations, and data reception\. However, their effective operation is affected by several technical, financial, environmental, and human\-resource challenges\. This study examined eight major challenges facing satellite ground stations using a review research approach based on relevant scholarly publications, technical reports, and other academic sources published mainly in recent past\. The reviewed literature was analysed thematically, with attention to high infrastructure costs, inconsistent power supply, atmospheric interference, radio frequency interference, inadequate modern equipment, insufficient skilled technical personnel, cybersecurity threats, and facility maintenance costs\. The findings indicate that these challenges can increase operational expenditure, reduce communication reliability, delay data acquisition, and limit the adoption of emerging satellite technologies\. It was concluded from the study that addressing these problems requires sustained investment in infrastructure, reliable power systems, equipment modernisation, workforce development, cybersecurity, and preventive maintenance\. The findings provide useful insights for satellite operators, policymakers, researchers, and space technology institutions, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria\.

## [Red Fluorescent Labeling of Myelin by Membrane‐Targeted tdTomato in Transgenic Mouse Lines](../publications/f99e4839b3f45b7ce0b7.md)

Anja Reinert; Ulrike Winkler; Sandra Goebbels; Lina Komarek; Wiebke Möbius; Henri S\. Zanker; Karl Schoknecht; Grit Bornschein; Hartmut Schmidt; Robert Fledrich; Ruth Martha Stassart; Petra G\. Hirrlinger; Klaus‐Armin Nave; Hauke B\. Werner; Aiman S\. Saab; Johannes Hirrlinger

ABSTRACT Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively\. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin\. Combining structural with functional imaging requires labeling of myelin with red fluorescence, as many functional sensors, including Ca 2\+ indicators and genetically encoded metabolite sensors, fluoresce in the green spectral range\. However, in vivo tools enabling red fluorescent labeling of myelinating cells and their myelin sheaths remain limited\. Here, we generated a set of seven transgenic mouse lines expressing a membrane‐targeted variant of the red fluorescent protein tdTomato in myelinating oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells throughout the nervous system\. The mouse lines provide a variety of expression patterns ranging from wide‐spread labeling of myelin to a rather sparse expression, the latter enabling visualization of individual oligodendrocytes and their associated myelin sheaths\. In the peripheral nervous system, the pattern of fluorescence in sciatic nerves indicates predominant localization of tdTomato to non‐compact myelin compartments including the inner and outer tongues, paranodal loops and Schmidt‐Lanterman incisures\. In summary, our work provides a set of novel mouse lines with myelin labeled by red fluorescence, which are compatible with diverse imaging modalities in the green spectral range enabling integrated structural and functional imaging\.

## [Retrieval of Winter Rapeseed Total Photosynthetic Area Index Using Multi\-Dimensional Spatiotemporal Features from Sentinel\-1 SAR](../publications/f9c6c47789c705e183f5.md)

Yong Jin; Xinbi Yue; Shangrong Wu; Yongli Guo

The abrupt change of canopy structure at the flowering stage causes a long\-standing monitoring blind zone for SAR\-based inversion of winter rapeseed\. This study proposed a feature\-based inversion method for the Total Photosynthetic Area Index \(TPAI\) of winter rapeseed, in which a multi\-dimensional spatiotemporal feature framework was constructed by integrating radar\-derived features such as polarization interactions and spatial texture with acquisition\-date\-derived phenological priors including day\-of\-year harmonics and normalized z\-score features, and a regularized linear Ridge model was selected from six machine\-learning candidates\. Evaluated under a spatial five\-fold cross\-validation protocol with geographically disjoint validation folds, the model achieved an overall R2 of 0\.615 and an RMSE of 1\.033 m2 m−2, against an R2 of 0\.584 for a baseline encoding the growth calendar alone, indicating only a modest overall gain from the radar\-derived features; the radar\-derived features nevertheless delivered their largest within\-stage improvement over this baseline at the flowering stage, suggesting that they can partly alleviate—though not resolve—the sensitivity loss of conventional single\-polarization features during flowering\. Error magnitudes were insensitive to systematic bias of up to ±40% in the SAI scaling assumption, and full\-coverage TPAI mapping across five phenological stages, produced from seam\-corrected Sentinel\-1 mosaics, matched the observed growth trajectory\. Given that the SAI was estimated indirectly and the analysis relied on a single growing season at a single study area, these results should be regarded as site\- and season\-specific\. The framework therefore shows promise as a spatially validated, feature\-based pathway toward TPAI monitoring of winter rapeseed in cloudy\-rainy regions, with further validation across multiple seasons and regions required before operational application\.

## [Replay Pruning and Few\-Bit Integer Inference for Hardware\-Efficient Speed\-Sign Recognition](../publications/f9c7842135afa7cb6fd7.md)

Se Un Park; Kyungkeon Chung; Huigeol Kim; Junyoung Park

Speed\-limit sign recognition on an automotive camera system\-on\-chip \(SoC\) must fit a detector and a classifier \(the reader\) into the memory, arithmetic, and energy budgets of the device\. In our two\-stage recognizer, the detector, a YOLO\-family network with ReLU and hard\-sigmoid operators, is compressed by channel replay: an iterative pruning cascade identifies the channels to remove, the recorded deletions are replayed on the original task\-trained network, the parent, and one continuous knowledge\-distillation recovery follows\. On a YOLOv5n, replay removes 60\.3% of the parameters at the accuracy of the parent and, in validation mAP50\-95 over five matched seeds, outperforms iterative pruning and training from scratch, and its per\-step variant \(per\-step replay\) is the most accurate pruning method\. On a YOLOv8n, replay and per\-step replay outperform every other method and the unpruned parent\. The reader, a five\-layer CNN with 18k parameters, and the post\-processing of the YOLOv5n and YOLOv8n heads use integer arithmetic only\. With 4\-bit weights and 8\-bit activations \(W4A8\), the reader matches FP32 accuracy in 12\.1 KB of on\-chip memory, and an executable streaming model reproduces the INT8 class predictions of its runtime on all 9,850 test crops\. On a Jetson AGX Orin, INT8 is faster than FP16 only in the implicit formulation of TensorRT, and the replay detector runs fastest on the deep\-learning accelerator \(DLA\)\. Trained on public data only, the combined system of 0\.72 M parameters recognizes 95\.2% of the signs of a held\-out automotive camera at 90% precision and 94 frames per second\.

## [The Significance of Gut Microbiome Health Axis: Exploring the Synbiotic Role of GOS and Lactobacillus Reuteri in Supporting Brain, Skeletal and Muscular Development](../publications/f9d0e8e468b5d474aa09.md)

Naeyema Sadia; Khan Nahid; Shams Maksud; Khaleeda Akter; Shuma Riam; Shahana Begum; Rebecca Akhter; Saiful Alam

The human gut microbiome is a complex ecological community that plays an important role in physiological development, immune maturation, metabolic homeostasis, and organ function, particularly during early life\. The first years after birth represent a critical developmental window when microbial colonization and dietary interactions can influence long\-term health\. Emerging evidence indicates that the gut microbiome extends beyond digestion and functions as a communication network connecting intestinal health with distant organs through the gut microbiome health axis\. This axis integrates microbial metabolites, immune signaling, endocrine regulation, and neural pathways to influence brain, skeletal, and muscular development\. Disruption of early\-life microbial balance has been associated with impaired gut comfort, altered immune responses, metabolic disturbances, and developmental challenges\. Synbiotics, defined as combinations of beneficial microorganisms and selectively utilized substrates that provide synergistic health effects, have gained attention as nutritional strategies for supporting healthy microbiome development\. Among these, galacto\-oligosaccharides \(GOS\), a well\-characterized prebiotic carbohydrate, and Lactobacillus reuteri, a probiotic species associated with gastrointestinal health, represent a promising combination\. GOS selectively stimulates beneficial bacteria, particularly Bifidobacterium species, supporting short\-chain fatty acid \(SCFA\) production, intestinal barrier integrity, and microbial diversity\. Meanwhile, L\. reuteri may contribute through competitive exclusion of potentially harmful microorganisms, immune modulation, enhancement of intestinal tolerance, and production of bioactive compounds that influence host physiology\. Recent randomized clinical evidence suggests that young\-child nutritional formulations containing L\. reuteri and GOS may modulate gut microbial composition and support musculoskeletal developmental parameters, highlighting the potential value of targeted microbiome interventions during early growth\. The gut\-brain axis is among the most extensively studied microbiome\-mediated pathways\. Microbial metabolites, including SCFAs, neurotransmitter\-related compounds, and immune mediators, may influence neuronal development, cognitive function, and neuroinflammatory regulation\. The gut\-bone axis illustrates how microbial metabolites can influence mineral absorption, osteoblast activity, vitamin metabolism, and skeletal remodeling\. Improved nutrient utilization and SCFA production may support calcium availability and help regulate inflammatory processes\. Emerging evidence also supports a gut\-muscle axis, through which microbial composition may influence muscle metabolism, nutrient utilization, protein synthesis, and physical development\. This review examines the gut microbiome health axis and the mechanistic role of the GOS and L\. reuteri synbiotic combination in supporting early\-life gut comfort and development, with particular emphasis on brain, skeletal, and muscular outcomes\.

## [From gesture to meaning: art therapy, children’s drawing process, and emotional resilience—a phenomenologically informed psychological study](../publications/f9e509c8ca37e2067017.md)

Wenke Sun

Children often struggle to verbalise difficult emotions, which makes therapeutic methods that support their emotional health and wellbeing particularly important\. This study examined the relationship between art therapy, children’s drawing processes, and emotional resilience from a phenomenologically oriented psychological perspective in China\. The study aimed to understand children’s experiences of drawing during art therapy and the role of these experiences in meaning\-making and the development of resilience\. A qualitative phenomenological design was used with 20 children \(aged 8–12 years\) who took part in a 10\-week art therapy programme delivered across three settings\. Data were collected through participant observation, semi\-structured interviews, reflective dialogue, and analysis of 200 drawings, and were analysed following transcendental phenomenological procedure\. Four interconnected themes emerged: Drawing as Emotional Externalisation, Symbolic Meaning\-Making Through Visual Narratives, Transformation of Fear into Agency, and Emergence of Emotional Resilience and Future Orientation\. Participants described drawing as a means of externalising difficult emotions, constructing personal meaning through symbols and stories, and developing a stronger sense of agency and coping\. The findings suggest that art therapy can function as a developmental bridge connecting emotion and meaning, supporting children’s experienced sense of resilience through emotional awareness, reflective understanding, and self\-expression\. As a qualitative study without a comparison group or independent outcome measures, the findings describe children’s perceived and experienced changes rather than demonstrated therapeutic effects; with this caveat, the results carry exploratory implications for education, counselling, and therapeutic practice aimed at supporting children’s psychological wellbeing\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy: Current Evidence, Limitations, and Future Directions](../publications/f9f78f622c7a41677045.md)

MD Ahmed Abdallah Salman; Ahmed Abdallah

Peroral endoscopic myotomy \(POEM\) is an established treatment for achalasia and selected spastic esophageal motility disorders, but several aspects of care remain highly operator\-dependent\.These include early diagnosis, patient selection, procedural planning, myotomy length, intra\-procedural safety, training assessment, and prediction of post\-procedure reflux\.Artificial intelligence \(AI\) may help address these limitations by integrating endoscopic video, high\-resolution manometry, timed barium esophagram, EndoFLIP, clinical variables, procedural data, and follow\-up outcomes into more personalized decision\-support tools\.This narrative review critically examines the evidence for AI across the POEM pathway and distinguishes direct achalasia or POEM evidence from adjacent and conceptual applications\.Early AI applications are most likely to emerge in achalasia detection during diagnostic endoscopy, automated motility interpretation, video\-based procedural assessment, and prediction of clinical response or post\-POEM reflux\.More ambitious applications, such as real\-time tunnel orientation, vessel recognition, mucosal injury alerts, and personalized myotomy planning, remain largely investigational\.Most AI\-specific POEM applications remain at an early or conceptual stage and require multicenter validation, standardized outcomes, and careful clinical governance\.AI should support, rather than replace, expert judgment, and an AI\-derived reflux estimate cannot replace standard follow\-up or objective reflux assessment\.ÖZ Peroral endoskopik miyotomi \(POEM\), akalazya ve seçilmiş spastik özofagus motilite bozukluklarının tedavisinde yerleşik bir yöntem olmakla birlikte, tedavi sürecinin çeşitli aşamaları halen büyük ölçüde uygulayıcı deneyimine bağlıdır\.Bu aşamalar; erken tanı, hasta seçimi, işlem planlaması, miyotomi uzunluğunun belirlenmesi, işlem sırasında güvenliğin sağlanması, eğitim düzeyinin değerlendirilmesi ve işlem sonrası reflü gelişiminin öngörülmesini kapsamaktadır\.Yapay zeka \(YZ\); endoskopik video görüntüleri, yüksek çözünürlüklü manometri, zamanlı baryumlu özofagus grafisi, EndoFLIP, klinik değişkenler, işleme ilişkin veriler ve takip sonuçlarını bütünleştirerek daha kişiselleştirilmiş karar destek araçlarının geliştirilmesine katkı sağlayabilir\.Bu anlatısal derlemede, POEM sürecinin farklı aşamalarında YZ kullanımına ilişkin kanıtlar eleştirel olarak incelenmekte ve doğrudan akalazya veya POEM&\#x27;e ilişkin kanıtlar, komşu alanlardaki ve kavramsal düzeydeki uygulamalardan ayrılmaktadır\.YZ&\#x27;nin erken dönemdeki uygulamalarının; tanısal endoskopi sırasında akalazyanın saptanması, motilite bulgularının otomatik olarak yorumlanması, video tabanlı işlem değerlendirmesi ve klinik yanıtın veya POEM sonrası reflünün öngörülmesi alanlarında ortaya çıkması beklenmektedir\.

## [Análisis del remedio indemnizatorio en el ámbito de la neurotecnología](../publications/f9fd30c8e97b43ef7cf4.md)

Alma Rodríguez Guitián

El trabajo busca individualizar hipótesis concretas de daños que en la actualidad sufre o podría sufrir una persona en el ámbito de la neurotecnología\. Los casos más relevantes de daños son los derivados, respectivamente, de la puesta en el mercado de productos defectuosos neurotecnológicos y de infracciones de la normativa de protección de datos personales por parte de la empresa responsable y/o encargada del tratamiento de tales datos en el citado sector\. Se analiza el régimen jurídico del remedio indemnizatorio previsto tanto en la Directiva \(UE\) 2024/2853 de 23 de octubre de 2024 sobre responsabilidad por productos defectuosos como en el Reglamento \(UE\) 2016/679 de 27 de abril de 2016 \(Reglamento General de Protección de Datos\)\. Aunque ninguna de las citadas normativas contempla de modo expreso la neurotecnología, ambas constituyen instrumentos útiles ante los daños producidos en dicho ámbito dado su estado actual de desarrollo científico y tecnológico\.
