## [MJO Predictability: Its Sources and Limits](../publications/f9fed93e663f123e968b.md)

Meriem Krouma; Yakelyn R\. Jauregui; Boualem Khouider; Brandon W\. Kerns; Daehyun Kim; Hyemi Kim; Kirsten J\. Mayer; Pallav Ray; Bo‐Wen Shen; Frédéric Vitart; Yuntao Wei; Chidong Zhang

Abstract The Madden–Julian Oscillation \(MJO\) is the dominant mode of intraseasonal variability in the tropical atmosphere and a central source of subseasonal\-to\-seasonal \(S2S\) predictability\. Despite decades of progress, theoretical understanding of its forecast horizon remains elusive and contested\. This workshop\-inspired review synthesizes insights on MJO predictability, highlighting advances in theory, modeling, and machine learning applications, while critically assessing persistent challenges\. We revisit the layered concepts of intrinsic, potential, and practical predictability, with intrinsic predictability set by the flow itself, potential predictability defined by idealized initial conditions, and practical predictability constrained by real observations, data availability, and forecasting methodologies\. We examine the physical sources and statistical approaches underlying prediction skill, and evaluate current metrics and verification methodologies, emphasizing that evaluation metrics must be responsive to user needs and that observing systems should be designed in concert with model requirements\. We then assess limits imposed by physical processes such as MJO initiation and the Maritime Continent propagation barrier, as well as their potentially unclear modification under climate change\. Finally, we outline future research opportunities—spanning observations, hybrid modeling, and user\-centered forecasting—and argue for a more integrative prediction framework in which dynamical, statistical, hybrid, and machine\-learning approaches are treated not as competitors but as complementary components of a unified MJO forecasting system, while identifying open questions that will shape the next decade of MJO research\.

## [Lubricant of Motion: Synovial Fluid\-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal/Stem Cells for Cartilage and Joint Regeneration](../publications/fa0b670f5c46b6817d2d.md)

许春茹; Bruce B\. Zhang; Zhongyu Li; Yuanyuan Zhang

Synovial fluid has historically been regarded as a specialized biological lubricant responsible for reducing friction, distributing mechanical loads, and supporting cartilage nutrition within diarthrodial joints\. Recent advances in regenerative medicine have revealed that synovial fluid also contains mesenchymal stromal/stem cell \(MSC\)\-like populations with significant regenerative and immunomodulatory properties\. These synovial fluid\-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cells \(SF\-MSCs\) are believed to originate predominantly from the synovial membrane and other joint\-associated progenitor niches, exhibiting robust clonogenicity, multilineage differentiation, and superior chondrogenic potential\. Emerging evidence suggests that SF\-MSCs contribute to joint homeostasis through cartilage matrix production, immunomodulation, and paracrine signaling mediated by extracellular vesicles and exosomes\. Consequently, SF\-MSCs have attracted considerable interest as a candidate cell source for cartilage repair, meniscal regeneration, osteochondral reconstruction, disease modeling, and cell\-free regenerative therapies\. Although encouraging preclinical and early clinical studies support their therapeutic promise, significant challenges remain regarding cellular heterogeneity, standardization, manufacturing, and long\-term efficacy\. This commentary reviews the biological characteristics, mechanisms of action, translational applications, current limitations, and future perspectives of SF\-MSCs in orthopedic regenerative medicine\.

## [Towards Hyperparameter Transfer for Differentially Private Optimization](../publications/fa0d39e4b93f24021d01.md)

Tianze Wang; Zhiqi Bu; Linjun Zhang

Scaling laws and hyperparameter tuning remain central challenges in training large\-scale models, particularly under differential privacy \(DP\), where optimization is further complicated by noise injection and per\-sample gradient clipping\. While Maximal Update Parametrization \($μ$P\) allows for zero\-shot hyperparameter transfer in standard training, we show that it fails under DP constraints due to the distinct spectral properties of high\-dimensional noise versus low\-rank gradients\. In this work, we introduce DP\-$μ$P, a theoretically grounded framework that extends $μ$P to the privacy\-preserving setting\. By analyzing the interaction between gradient clipping, noise injection, and feature learning, we derive a Signal\-to\-Noise Ratio \(SNR\) condition that governs layer\-wise learning rate scaling\. Combining this with our proposed spectral scaling formulation, we provide specific scaling rules for DP\-SGD, DP\-Adam, and DP\-Muon optimizers\. Empirically, we demonstrate that DP\-$μ$P enables effective zero\-shot transfer of learning rates across model widths on diverse architectures \(MLP, ViT, GPT\-2\), matching or exceeding the performance of individually tuned baselines while significantly reducing computational costs\.

## [Exploring the association between loneliness and breastfeeding duration in Chinese primiparas](../publications/fa0f73e65717ab7480d7.md)

Huiping Zhang; Pan Zeng; Miaomiao Chen; Rong Liu; Minjie Fu; Haijuan Wei; Siliang Chen; Haibin Wu

Background Reaching the recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding \(EBF\) during the first 6 months postpartum remains a worldwide challenge\. Meanwhile, Chinese primiparas suffered from the loneliness associated with the traditional practice of zuoyuezi and the isolation during the COVID\-19 pandemic\. As far as we know, little is known about whether there is the association between loneliness in Chinese primiparas and breastfeeding duration\. Purpose This study aimed to explore whether loneliness in Chinese primiparas was associated with reduced breastfeeding duration, and further to explore the endocrine mechanisms\. Methods The Chinese primiparas were assessed for loneliness using the Los Angeles Loneliness Scale \(R\-UCLA\) within 7–14 days postpartum\. According to the scores of R\-UCLA, the subjects were divided into three groups: no loneliness group \(n=162\), a low loneliness group \(n=65\) and a high loneliness group \(n=40\)\. The Postpartum Breastfeeding Questionnaire was filled out to record breastfeeding duration\. The expression levels of the serum lactation hormone\(prolactin\)and the stress hormone \(cortisol\) were measured\. Results The time and rate of breastfeeding initiation within 3 days postpartum, as well as the frequencies of exclusive breastfeeding at 15 and 30 days postpartum, were significantly lower in Chinese primiparas with high loneliness; specifically, High loneliness was associated with lower exclusive breastfeeding rates by 25\.2% \(P&lt;0\.01\) within 24 hours postpartum, 19\.9% \( P &lt; 0\.01\) at 24 to 48 hours postpartum, 22\.5% \( P &lt; 0\.01\) at 48 to 72 hours postpartum, 39\.8% \( P &lt; 0\.01\) at 90 days postpartum, respectively\. The probability of cumulative 90\- and 180\-day exclusive breastfeeding was the lowest in Chinese primiparas with high loneliness\. The probability of cumulative 90\- and 180\-day exclusive breastfeeding rates decreased as the scores on the Loneliness Scale increased\. Compared with primiparas in the no\-loneliness and low\-loneliness groups, those in the high\-loneliness group exhibited the highest expression levels of the stress hormone \(serum cortisol\) and the lowest expression levels of the lactation hormone \(serum prolactin\) at 3, 15, and 45 days postpartum, respectively\. Conclusion Loneliness in Chinese primiparas during lactation was associated with lower exclusive breastfeeding rates and duration\.

## [Physics\-informed machine learning\-based dose calculation for patients undergoing fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures](../publications/fa177fca58de62943adf.md)

Haegin Han; Keith Griffin; Monjoy Saha; A Kyle Jones; Steve D\. Mann; Kevin A\. Wunderle; Donald L\. Miller; Nina Petoussi\-Henss; D\. G\. Sutton; Choonsik Lee

OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a physics\-informed machine\-learning framework for rapid organ\-dose estimation in fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures without requiring patient\-specific imaging\. Approach: We used 385 adult radiation dose structured reports from three procedure types\-bilateral carotid angiography, percutaneous biliary drainage, and liver chemoembolization\-comprising more than 50,000 irradiation events\. A body\-size\-matched computational phantom was selected using patient sex, height, and weight\. RDSR\-derived beam parameters and engineered descriptors of beam\-organ geometry and attenuation were used to train organ\-specific XGBoost models for localized organs and a multi\-output multilayer perceptron model for four distributed tissues\. Monte Carlo\-derived dose coefficients from NCIRF3 were used as target values\. Main results: In the held\-out test set of 12,683 irradiation events, 49\.4% and 84\.8% of XGBoost\-based localized\-organ estimates were within ±5% and ±20% of the Monte Carlo\-derived values, respectively\. The corresponding proportions were 88\.2% and 98\.0% for the distributed\-tissue estimates and 87\.6% and 98\.3% for detriment\-weighted dose\. The median relative prediction error across organs and tissues was 0\.37% \(interquartile range, \-3\.68% to 4\.99%\)\. A reliability score was developed to support uncertainty\-aware interpretation\. The framework required approximately 0\.3 s per irradiation event, corresponding to an approximately 290\-fold acceleration relative to conventional Monte Carlo simulation under the benchmark conditions\. Significance: The proposed image\-free framework enables rapid organ\-dose estimation when patient imaging is unavailable and may support large retrospective epidemiological studies and uncertainty\-aware dose monitoring\. Because development and validation were limited to three procedure types and relied on reconstructed phantom\-beam geometry, external validation is required before application to other procedures or high\-precision individual clinical decisions\.

## [Assessing digital technology use for clinical learning in undergraduate health professional education in Ethiopia](../publications/fa18ba09a8af14f8ed42.md)

Marema Jebessa Kumsa; Berhanu Abera Kibret; Tefera Tadesse

Background\. The use of digital technologies in clinical placement training is becoming increasingly significant in global health education\. However, limited research has been conducted on the use of digital technology in clinical placement training in low\-income countries\. Objective\. To assess the use of digital technology in the workplace by undergraduate health professional students throughout their clinical placements\. Methods\. A multi\-centre, cross\-sectional survey study was carried out from May to September 2025 at three randomly selected universities in Ethiopia\. Data were collected from 335 undergraduate students in the fields of medicine, nursing and radiological technology using a structured questionnaire on demographic information, frequency of use of digital technologies in the workplace, the challenges encountered in using them, and their experiences with their use\. Descriptive statistics, independent sample t\-tests, and one\-way analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) were used for analysis\. Results\. Undergraduate health professional students used digital technology extensively in their clinical placement studies\. In clinical settings, 86\.3% of students reported that they use digital technology to learn, and 67\.8% said they use it frequently\. These students use digital technology mainly to access educational material for their clinical practice\. Despite this high use, students face several barriers, including lack of internet access and uncertainty about how supervisors, patients and caregivers will react to their use of digital technologies\. The use of digital technology during clinical placement raises questions about the possibility of learning impairment because of overdependence and distraction\. Conclusion\. Undergraduate students in the health professions make extensive use of digital technologies, mainly for accessing educational resources\. While this shows the great usefulness of digital tools and their acceptance by students, there are many practical barriers to their successful use in clinical placements, such as unreliable internet access\. In addition, the use of these technologies raises questions about how they are perceived by supervisors, patients and caregivers, as well as potential concerns about learning loss owing to distraction and extreme reliance on digital resources\. Addressing infrastructure bottlenecks and providing clear guidance on how to use digital technologies optimally in clinical education is crucial\.

## [Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Multicenter Real\-World Evidence to Advance Precision Dosing: A Critical Perspective Review](../publications/fa1e40cd589491c39aca.md)

Pierre Marquet; Marc Labriffe; Caroline Monchaud; Nicolas Picard; Jean‐Baptiste Woillard

BACKGROUND: Precision dosing integrates patient\-specific factors to optimize pharmacotherapy\. However, current evidence often relies on limited single\-center studies, restricting generalizability\. METHODS: A narrative review of literature on real\-world evidence, pharmacogenetics, biomarkers, artificial intelligence \(AI\), and privacy\-preserving data strategies relevant to precision dosing was conducted\. RESULTS: Single\-center data are insufficient for robust precision\-dosing evidence because of small subgroups and local practice biases\. Multicenter privacy\-preserving systems enable richer, more generalizable datasets that link doses, exposures, genotypes, biomarkers, and outcomes\. However, multicenter collaborations should remain aligned with the intended population and should not imply indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous data\. Secure pooled environments, federated learning, and synthetic data play distinct method\-dependent roles\. AI supports exposure estimation, phenotype extraction, and modeling of complex relationships but requires rigorous validation against conventional methods\. Causal inference requires epidemiological rigor beyond predictive performance\. CONCLUSIONS: Advancing precision dosing requires multicenter, purpose\-specific, privacy\-preserving, methodologically rigorous, and clinically validated data systems guided by clinical pharmacologists, with AI serving as a complementary tool rather than a default solution\.

## [Peran Kualitas Layanan dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Faktor Sosial Ekonomi dan Sistem Kepesertaan BPJS Terhadap Kepuasan Pasien di Rumah Sakit Umum Aliyah 2 Kota Kendari](../publications/fa1edcc62736f80650cd.md)

Sitti Nurhastiawati; Didin Saepudin; Rahadian Malik

Kepuasan pasien BPJS di rumah sakit dipengaruhi oleh kondisi sosial ekonomi, sistem kepesertaan BPJS, serta kualitas layanan yang diterima, namun integrasi ketiga faktor tersebut beserta peran moderasi kualitas layanan belum banyak dikaji, khususnya di Rumah Sakit Umum Aliyah 2 Kota Kendari\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran kualitas layanan dalam memoderasi pengaruh faktor sosial ekonomi dan sistem kepesertaan BPJS terhadap kepuasan pasien\. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif verifikatif dengan desain amper cross\-sectional\. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert kepada 100 responden pasien BPJS yang dipilih dengan amper purposive sampling, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dan Moderated Regression Analysis \(MRA\)\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa amper sosial ekonomi dan amper kepesertaan BPJS berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan pasien, dengan amper kepesertaan BPJS memberikan pengaruh paling kuat\. Kualitas layanan juga terbukti secara signifikan memoderasi atau memperkuat pengaruh kedua ampera tersebut terhadap kepuasan pasien\. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa peningkatan kualitas layanan, terutama pada aspek keandalan, waktu tunggu, dan fasilitas fisik, dapat memperkuat manfaat kondisi sosial ekonomi dan amper kepesertaan BPJS dalam meningkatkan kepuasan pasien, sehingga manajemen rumah sakit perlu meningkatkan efisiensi pelayanan dan konsistensi mutu layanan amperan bagi peserta BPJS\.

## [From traits to trajectories: overcoming psychometric assessment gap through adaptive developmental potential in organizations](../publications/fa28d9f1ae0032cc1ae4.md)

Pravallika Manam; Reeves J Wesley

Driven by AI\-integrated and hybrid structures, the organizational ecosystem has shifted from fixed role definitions to the adaptive nature of the workforce\. While existing organizational assessments focus on traditional psychometric tools that prioritize stable personality traits, this perspective article exposes the Assessment Gap and introduces the Adaptive Developmental Potential \(ADP\) Framework, which shifts talent analysis from point\-in\-time snapshots to adaptability\-based growth trajectories\. This framework articulates across four dimensions: Environmental Sensitivity, the degree to which environmental factors amplify individuals&\#x27; development; Learning Adaptability, the capacity to unlearn redundant protocols and update cognitive assumptions; Self\-Regulatory Capacity, the capacity to sustain focus and manage exhaustion under uncertainty; and Developmental Trajectory, the direction of individual growth over time\. Traditional assessments remain useful, but they may be insufficient in predicting behavior in dynamic environments; hence, organizations can implement Precision Development, targeting micro\-interventions over regular corporate training\. Conclusively, this perspective article offers scope for future research to empirically validate this longitudinal model, thereby aligning organizational science with the dynamics of modern work styles\.

## [From Vehicle Counts to Constrained Green\-Time Recommendations: An Evidence\-Audited YOLOv8 Traffic\-Signal Prototype](../publications/fa29a6bb396eab24637e.md)

Bharani Dharan R; Dr\. Nithyanandh S; Thara L

The data that an object detector produces as totals of vehicles is not necessarily a reliable measure of congestion, and a list of recommended green durations is not a safe traffic controller\. In this paper, an evidence\-audited prototype specification is proposed, combining a vehicle detection model \(YOLOv8\) with recommendations for the length of green time that are expressed in an open way\. The workflow can recognize the vehicles, such as motorcycles, buses and trucks, and can compare the pretrained nano and medium models against the fine\-tuned nano model, and can summarize the visible demand for approach using a count\-to\-capacity ratio\. It offers more capabilities such as persistent tracking, low motion events, short\-horizon forecasts, nominal corridor offsets and an emergency priority demonstration\. The problem of timing stage is translated into a projected lower and upper bounds constraint on the budget of a particular vehicle for each stage, and the total budget is to be a fixed value\. This treatment must be different from the case of separately cutting the proportional duration as this may lead to the budget violation\. The project material provided did not include the notebook, dataset, trained weights, execution logs, annotated outputs and traffic\-simulation records\. The paper thus presents a repeatable specification for the system, an analytical consistency test and a progressive validation procedure, but no evidence of accuracy or operation improvement\. The quality of the detector is evaluated independently of the counting error, the reliability of the allocation, the temporal\-event performance, and the network results\. The design produced is ‘producible’ and ‘testable’ in that it can be tested and simulated in the future when observations are available, rather than assuming the claim given by the visual prototype is true, and it is defensible in that it is a design and not a claim\.

## [TILNI RAQAMLASHTIRISHNING NAZARIY VA AMALIY ASOSLARI](../publications/fa2cf2e94799c42299a9.md)

TILNI RAQAMLASHTIRISHNING NAZARIY VA AMALIY ASOSLARI

Annotatsiya: Ushbu maqolada tilni raqamlashtirishning nazariy\-metodologik asoslari hamda kompyuter tilshunosligi va sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining o‘zbek tiliga ta’siri tadqiq etiladi\. Raqamli tilning lingvistik hamda texnologik mohiyati, uning bosqichlari va kiberlingvistik adaptatsiya muammolari jadvalli qiyosiy tahlillar hamda sotsiolingvistik kuzatuvlar asosida atroflicha yoritib berilgan\. Kalit so‘zlar: Raqamli tilshunoslik, kiberlingvistika, raqamlashtirish, sun’iy intellekt, algoritmik modellashtirish\. Аннотация: В данной статье исследуются теоретические и методологические основы цифровизации языка, а также влияние компьютерной лингвистики и технологий искусственного интеллекта на узбекский язык\. На основе сравнительных таблиц и социолингвистического анализа подробно освещаются лингвистическая и технологическая сущность цифрового языка, этапы его развития и проблемы киберлингвистической адаптации\. Ключевые слова: Цифровая лингвистика, киберлингвистика, цифровизация, искусственный интеллект, алгоритмическое моделирование\. Abstract: This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of language digitalization, as well as the impact of computational linguistics and artificial intelligence technologies on the Uzbek language\. The linguistic and technological essence of the digital language, the stages of its development, and the problems of cyber\-linguistic adaptation are covered in detail based on comparative tables and sociolinguistic analysis\. Keywords: Digital linguistics, cyberlinguistics, digitalization, artificial intelligence, algorithmic modeling\.

## [CHITOSAN NANOPARTICLES MITIGATE H₂O₂\-MEDIATED TOXICITY IN SH\-SY5Y CELLS](../publications/fa2dff74c3710f57d1ac.md)



The neuroprotective potential of chitosan nanoparticles \(CS NPs\) were evaluated against hydrogen peroxide \(H₂O₂\) induced toxicity in SH\-SY5Y cells\.The ionic gelation was used for synthesizing the CS NPs and characterized using Dynamic light scattering, UV\-Visible spectroscopy, X\-ray diffraction, Scanning and high resolution electron microscopy\.The characterization results confirmed the generation of spherical\-shaped particles with a size, zeta potential, and polydispersity index of 116\.9 nm, 17\.4 mV and 0\.260 respectively\.The formation of CS NPs was further confirmed by UV\-Vis spectroscopy and XRD\.The toxic effects of H₂O₂ were mitigated by CS NPs through improvement in cell viability and membrane integrity through MTT and LDH assays\.Further, the CS NPs treatment decreased ROS levels, indicating their ability to mitigate oxidative stress\.These results support the possible use of chitosan\-based nanoparticles as a promising neurotherapeutic carrier\.

## [Data\-driven multi\-parameter collaborative optimization of microstructure and electrical performance for inkjet\-printed silver circuits](../publications/fa3223bf221960f7f7d7.md)

Hao Zhang; Zhiqiang Yan; Liangsheng Jia; Yanning Yang; Zhiqiang Yan

Inkjet printing \(IJP\), as a rapidly advancing additive manufacturing \(AM\) technology, offers a promising approach for the conformal fabrication of circuits\. Nevertheless, the quality of circuits is heavily affected by process parameters and substantially determines the service performance of functional components\. Unlike conventional experimental trial\-and\-error methods, this work adopts data\-driven methodologies to accurately predict process parameters from measured data\. Initially, a full\-factorial experimental design was implemented to fabricate printed specimens\. Subsequently, the correlations between process parameters\-namely substrate temperature, printing speed, delay time, and number of layers and quality metrics, including line width \(LW\), line resistance \(LR\), and line thickness \(LT\), were modeled using long short\-term memory \(LSTM\), bidirectional LSTM \(BiLSTM\), and sparrow search algorithm\-enhanced BiLSTM \(SSA\-BiLSTM\) models\. The main and interactive effects of parameters on line quality were then quantified and analyzed\. Furthermore, the non\-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II \(NSGA\-II\) was utilized to identify and verify optimal parameter sets that minimize LW and LR while maintaining desirable LT performance\. The results reveal that the SSA\-BiLSTM model consistently outperforms both LSTM and BiLSTM models across all output responses, attaining the highest coefficients of determination \(R 2 \) and the lowest root mean squared errors \(RMSE\) for LW \(R 2 = 0\.9466\), LR \(R 2 = 0\.9782\), and LT \(R 2 = 0\.9287\)\. The optimized process parameters—substrate temperature of 68 ℃, printing speed of 1238 mm/min, 5 layers and an 8 ms delay time—proved to be both effective and reliable\. Overall, the proposed data\-driven framework significantly improves the manufacturing performance of IJP for microelectronic devices\.

## [Microbiota\-host interactions: key mechanisms linking periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus](../publications/fa3465a2ac14004ef47a.md)

Xinyu Wu; Xinye Zhang; Yuang Guo; Ruiyi Zhang; Huiying Li; Wanghong Zhao

Periodontitis is one of the most prevalent chronic inflammatory diseases in the oral cavity, characterized by progressive destruction of periodontal supporting tissues\. Its pathogenesis involves complex interactions between the oral microbiota and host immune responses\. This condition not only severely impacts oral health but is also closely associated with multiple systemic diseases\. In recent years, the link between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus \(SLE\) has garnered increasing attention\. This review examines the compositional characteristics of the oral microbiota in patients with SLE and the epidemiological evidence linking periodontitis to SLE\. It focuses on how periodontitis may trigger or exacerbate SLE’s autoimmune responses through the oral microbiota, via mechanisms such as molecular mimicry, cytokine\-mediated immune activation, and microbial translocation, while elucidating the underlying pathophysiological and immunological mechanisms\. Furthermore, this paper aims to explore potential prevention and treatment strategies based on oral microbial interventions, to provide novel insights and theoretical foundations for adjunctive therapy and disease management in SLE\.

## [Impacto de la ansiedad y depresión en el aprendizaje adolescente](../publications/fa3929775ead24b0c9ed.md)

Martha Edith Miranda Preciado

La presente investigación tiene como objetivo general: Determinar el impacto de la ansiedad y la depresión en el aprendizaje de los estudiantes de 10 a 13 años de la Unidad Educativa Juan León Mera porque la adolescencia es una etapa caracterizada por cambios emocionales donde la ansiedad y la depresión se han convertido en problemáticas frecuentes que repercuten en el rendimiento académico\. La investigación se desarrolla bajo un enfoque cuali\-cuantitativo, con un diseño no experimental de corte transversal de nivel descriptivo, cuyos métodos son el inductivo\-deductivo y el analítico\-sintético\. Como técnica se aplica la encuesta, cuyo instrumento es un cuestionario donde se obtiene como resultados que un alto porcentaje de estudiantes presenta niveles significativos de ansiedad o depresión porque el 67% experimenta ansiedad antes de evaluaciones, el 70% presenta dificultades de concentración cuando está preocupado o el 63% manifiesta miedo a participar en clase a su vez el 60% presenta sentimientos de tristeza mientras que el 50% manifiesta cansancio o falta de motivación concluyendo que la ansiedad y la depresión influyen en el aprendizaje de los estudiantes porque afecta los procesos cognitivos como la atención, la concentración y la motivación\.

## [Long\-term endocrine and reproductive outcomes in female adolescent and young adult survivors after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence](../publications/fa3ce14a123c2640539a.md)

Weronika Zajączkowska; Katarzyna Derwich; Cezary Miedziarek; Agnieszka Sobkowiak\-Sobierajska; Zofia Kolesińska; Maria Buda; Witold Kędzia; Karina Kapczuk

Background Cancer treatment during childhood and adolescence, particularly hematopoietic stem cell transplantation \(HSCT\), may adversely affect long\-term reproductive and endocrine health in female adolescent and young adult \(AYA\) survivors, leading to premature ovarian insufficiency \(POI\), which may be associated with impaired pubertal development, low bone mass, and reproductive complications\. Methods This study included 34 female survivors treated with HSCT for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence \(median age 10\.8 years\)\. The median follow\-up from HSCT to the last gynecological assessment was 8\.5 years\. Hormonal assessment, pelvic ultrasound, and bone mineral density \(BMD\) evaluation were performed\. Patients were classified as having normal ovarian function, transient ovarian insufficiency \(TOI\), or persistent POI\. Results At the last follow\-up, normal ovarian function was observed in 15 patients \(44\.1%\), TOI in 7 \(20\.6%\), and persistent POI in 12 \(35\.3%\)\. Patients with normal ovarian function were significantly older at HSCT \(p = 0\.0432\), whereas premenarchal status was associated with impaired ovarian outcome \(p = 0\.0066\)\. In multivariable analysis including cyclophosphamide equivalent dose \(CED\), radiotherapy, and menarchal status at HSCT, postmenarchal status was associated with markedly lower odds of ovarian insufficiency \(adjusted OR 0\.056, 95% CI 0\.005–0\.566; p = 0\.0147\)\. All postmenarchal patients received GnRHa, precluding separation of the effects of menarchal status and GnRHa exposure; GnRHa\-treated survivors had higher AMH concentrations \(p =0\.0032\)\. AMH and FSH concentrations differed significantly between groups \(both p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Uterine and mean ovarian volumes, antral follicle count \(AFC\), and BMD were significantly lower in patients with TOI and POI \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Radiotherapy exposure was associated with both lower uterine and ovarian volumes, while puberty induction was also associated with lower uterine volume \(all p &lt;0\.05\)\. Two patients diagnosed with POI achieved spontaneous pregnancies during follow\-up, one resulting in a live birth\. Conclusions Ovarian dysfunction is highly prevalent after childhood HSCT, although partial recovery of ovarian function may occur even in patients with a diagnosis of POI\. Persistent POI is associated with impaired uterine development and lower BMD despite ongoing hormone replacement therapy, underscoring the need for timely and long\-lasting individualized endocrine and reproductive care in AYA survivors\.

## [Desain Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Mekanis Sepeda Menggunakan Generator DC dengan Monitoring Berbasis Internet of Things \(IoT\)](../publications/fa4026318ff80c6fa43d.md)

Reno Pratama; Joko Joko

Penelitian ini merancang dan membangun sistem pembangkit listrik tenaga mekanis berbasis sepeda menggunakan generator DC yang terintegrasi dengan sistem monitoring berbasis Internet of Things \(IoT\)\. Sistem terdiri atas generator DC, buck converter, baterai 12 V 5 Ah, mikrokontroler ESP32, sensor INA219, sensor hall effect, sensor tegangan, LCD, dan Telegram\. Energi listrik yang dihasilkan digunakan untuk mengisi baterai maupun mengoperasikan beban listrik berupa pompa DC\. Pengujian dilakukan untuk mengetahui karakteristik keluaran generator saat proses pengisian baterai, akurasi sensor, kestabilan buck converter, serta kinerja sistem monitoring dalam menampilkan, mengirimkan, dan menyimpan data\. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan rata\-rata kesalahan pengukuran sensor INA219, sensor hall effect, dan sensor tegangan masing\-masing sebesar 0,54%, 0,86%, dan 0,63%\. Buck converter menghasilkan tegangan keluaran stabil sebesar 5,05 V pada variasi tegangan masukan 7,44–13,92 V\. Daya keluaran generator meningkat dari 2,52 W pada 250 RPM menjadi 12,52 W pada 650 RPM\. Sistem monitoring mampu menampilkan dan mengirimkan data secara real\-time melalui LCD dan Telegram serta menyimpan data pada Google Spreadsheet\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan sistem mampu mengonversi energi mekanis kayuhan sepeda menjadi energi listrik dan memantaunya secara terintegrasi\.

## [Brain Structure and Differential Response to Family\-Centered Prevention: Evidence for Anterior Cingulate Cortex Moderation in a Randomized Controlled Trial](../publications/fa4142cd0b5536052521.md)

Steven M\. Kogan; Tianyi Yu; Robin Nusslock; Anna C\. Cichoki; Katharina Seitz; Steven R\. H\. Beach

Family\-centered prevention programs improve youth self\-regulation, yet intervention effects are heterogeneous, and the mechanisms underlying differential response remain poorly understood\. Identifying neural metrics that shape responsiveness to prevention may advance theory and inform program refinement\. This study examined whether baseline brain structure moderated response to a telehealth adaptation of the Strong African American Families program \(T\-SAAF\), a prevention intervention targeting self\-regulation among Black preadolescents\. Youth ages 11\-12 and their caregivers \(N = 170 families\) were recruited in North Georgia and randomly assigned to T\-SAAF or a no\-treatment control condition\. Allocation was 1:1 in a two\-group parallel design evaluated within a superiority framework, and we generated the allocation sequence using statistical software\. Because randomization followed the pretest assessment, allocation was concealed from participants and from pretest assessors, and condition was revealed only after pretest data collection was complete\. Thereafter, families, facilitators, and posttest assessors could not be masked to condition, as T\-SAAF is a group\-based family program delivered by facilitators\. We conducted no interim analyses and used no stopping guidelines; the trial completed as planned\. They were assessed at baseline and approximately nine months later\. A neuroimaging subsample completed structural MRI prior to intervention exposure\. Analyses focused on whether cortical and subcortical structural metrics moderated changes in parent\-reported youth self\-control\. To account for differential engagement, the intervention main effect was tested in a propensity score\-matched sample of youth who received the intervention and comparable controls \(n = 130\); brain by intervention interactions were tested in the neuroimaging subsample \(n = 105\)\. Assignment to T\-SAAF was associated with a modest increase in self\-control \(F\[1,124\] = 4\.28, p = \.04\)\. Baseline anterior cingulate cortex \(ACC\) structure moderated this effect\. The clearest and most consistent evidence was for rostral ACC thickness and caudal ACC thickness; caudal ACC volume showed the same pattern with weaker but convergent support\. Across these metrics, thinner or smaller ACC at baseline was associated with greater intervention\-related gains in self\-control, whereas youth with higher ACC structural values showed little differential benefit\. No moderation was observed for rostral ACC volume, amygdala volume, or nucleus accumbens volume\. Findings provide preliminary evidence that individual differences in neural structure, particularly within the ACC, may shape responsiveness to family\-centered preventive intervention during preadolescence\. By extending neural prediction approaches from adult treatment to developmental prevention, this study indicates that neurodevelopmental markers can clarify mechanisms of differential response and inform program refinement\. Confirmation in adequately powered, preregistered research is needed\. ClinicalTrials\.gov NCT05253235 \( https://clinicaltrials\.gov/study/NCT05253235 \); registered February 22, 2022\.

## [Multi\-objective KCF\-improved CSO for permanent magnet motor rotor detection and drive](../publications/fa47ca047293f738ad5c.md)

Dan Lei; Qin Sun

Traditional approaches to detecting permanent magnet motor rotors predominantly center on sensor analysis and the refinement of control strategies\. However, these methods inevitably encounter challenges, including elevated costs and vulnerability to interference\. Consequently, to enhance the detection accuracy of Permanent Magnet \(PM\) motor rotors, this study introduces an innovative &quot;combined visual\-control optimization&quot; approach, which integrates a Multi\-objective kernel correlation filtering \(MOKCF\)tracking algorithm with an improved Cat Swarm optimization \(CSO\) algorithm\. Firstly, it proposes monocular visual tracking of the rotor attitude and realizes real\-time tracking of the target feature points of the rotor by using the Kalman filter \(KF\) to correct the tracking algorithm\. At the same time, the CSO improved by quantum chaos and mapping relationship is used to realize electric drive\. The results show that the improved multi\-objective algorithm can effectively track the target, and the root mean square and mean absolute values of the lateral deviation of the deflection angle and the spin angle are not more than 0\.042° and 0\.029° respectively\. The maximum average convergence time of the improved cat swarm algorithm does not exceed 0\.1s, and the torque and speed of the motor control system are more stable, and the motion error of the rotor feature points is smaller\. The method proposed by this study has significant advantages in improving detection accuracy and optimizing driving performance, providing a new technical reference for intelligent detection and fault diagnosis of motor rotors\.

## [An AI\-interpretable multidimensional intelligence\-driven framework for student performance prediction using local LLM\-based narrative reasoning](../publications/fa482e8d48217359bba1.md)

Syed Rafiq ul Hoda; Eric Atwell; Mirza Mahmood Baig

Predicting student performance has become a vital objective in educational data mining, however existing models remain limited by limited feature sets, opaque decision processes, and the absence of real\-time, context\-aware interpretative intelligence\. This study presents a novel hybrid Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) architecture that integrates cognitive, emotional, and general intelligence indicators with formative assessment/class performance data to construct a multidimensional demonstration of student performance\. The system utilizes a mathematically formalized feature\-weighting mechanism that allows domain experts to regulate the influence of key predictors prior to training, enabling a tunable and educator\-configurable modeling process\. Interaction between cognitive, emotional, and behavioral properties are explicitly engineered to capture complex effects often overlooked in prior research\. An ensemble predictive model combining Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, and Linear Regression is used to predict student grades, with uncertainty measured through variance\-based confidence intervals\. The integrated system exhibited strong predictive capability, attaining high accuracy \(R 2 = 0\.9014, 95% CI \[0\.8882, 0\.9121\], 10,000 bootstrap resamples\) with low prediction error, confirming the stability and reliability of the ensemble model\. Understanding why a model produces a particular prediction is often as important as the prediction itself\. To address the interpretability gap, the system incorporates SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\)\-based global and local explanations, a counterfactual simulation engine that estimates the marginal impact of improving specific attributes, and a local generative AI layer deployed via Ollama that creates these outputs into structured, real\-time narrative feedback\. Running the Large Language Model \(LLM\) locally ensures privacy\-preserving, institution\-compliant interpretability while permitting interactive, student specific explanations\. This integration of predictive modeling, explainability, simulation, and local generative reasoning creates a unified decision\-support framework that exceeds traditional black\-box approaches\. Experimental assessment shows that the model not only achieves viable predictive accuracy but also provides actionable insights into feature influence, model stability, and potential intervention pathways\.

## [Foreign Language Teaching in the Context of Language\-Culture Relations](../publications/fa59176fd6d4cd9a5727.md)

Turkan Mehraj Ismayilli

Foreign language teaching has increasingly been viewed as a multidimensional process that extends beyond the acquisition of grammatical knowledge to include the development of communicative and cultural competence\. Within the context of language–culture relations, language is not only a system of rules but also a carrier of cultural meanings, values, and social practices\. This study examines the role of culture in foreign language teaching and emphasizes the interdependent relationship between linguistic and cultural components in the learning process\. It highlights that effective language instruction requires integrating cultural elements such as traditions, beliefs, and discourse patterns to enhance learners’ communicative competence and intercultural awareness\. Furthermore, the study discusses the importance of authentic materials and context\-based teaching approaches in facilitating meaningful learning experiences\. The findings suggest that incorporating cultural content into language teaching improves learners’ motivation, supports the development of intercultural communicative competence, and enables more appropriate language use in real\-life contexts\. Consequently, foreign language education should adopt a holistic approach that considers both linguistic structures and cultural dimensions as essential components of successful language learning\.

## [Fair Access to Urban Water: Designing Population‐Sensitive Connection Fees Through a Welfare‐Informed Ability‐to‐Pay Approach](../publications/fa5ec48c247cd84d9cc0.md)

Seyedhossein Sajadifar; Masoud Alavian Sadr; Shahram Heydarian Samani; Ali Mazyaki; Alireza Pourebrahim

ABSTRACT Setting urban water connection fees is a complex policy problem: Fees must balance affordability, equity, and adequate cost recovery\. This study develops a two‐stage framework for setting urban water connection charges in Iran\. A bottom‐up engineering model first establishes the full long‐run economic cost of a new connection; a distributive stage then allocates a target provincial average across six city population classes\. The distributive stage is stated as a constrained social welfare program and solved exactly; under logarithmic utility, it yields corner solutions rather than a smooth gradient because the fee is a small share of household resources\. The recommended schedule is therefore described as what it is: a proportional ability‐to‐pay allocation indexed to city size, whose formal relation to the welfare program is stated explicitly\. Revenue neutrality is imposed on a connection‐weighted basis so that the utility collects the intended total rather than an unweighted average of six class fees\. Using Household Expenditure and Income Survey data for all 31 provincial capitals, we test rather than assume the population proxy and find an income elasticity of about 0\.13 with respect to city size: statistically significant, but explaining a minority of cross‐city variation\. Equity claims are correspondingly framed at the intercity level\. Applied to a representative province, the schedule is progressive with respect to ability to pay, holds first‐year revenue exactly at the target, and can be adjusted over time using the Consumer Price Index\. The approach transfers to other water‐scarce settings under cost‐recovery pressure\.

## [Self‐Energy Engineering via Structured‐Bath Dressing for Amplitude–Phase Decoupled Control in Dynamic Holographic Metasurfaces](../publications/fa6bea419de6c3e08253.md)

Kaihao Zhou; Zhe Qin; Yongfeng Li; J\.\-M\. Liu; Hongrui Zhang; Hao Yang; Zhihao Guo; Xu Liu; Lin Zheng; Wenjie Wang; Hongya Chen; Jiafu Wang

ABSTRACT Independent control of amplitude and phase remains a central challenge in reconfigurable metasurfaces\. However, in most existing approaches, the physical connection between device tuning parameters and underlying resonant modes remains unclear\. Here, a new theoretical analysis method combining the electromagnetic response Jacobian with the Friedrichs–Lee self‐energy model is proposed\. The method formulates amplitude–phase decoupling as a local parameter–response problem and reveals the mechanism of amplitude–phase coupling at the resonant modes level\. Based on this model, a structured‐bath design is established as a concrete approach to realizing amplitude–phase decoupling\. The mechanism is systematically validated and implemented in a reconfigurable meta‐atom\. Two independent electrical tuning parameters selectively regulate different modal responses, enabling continuous reflection‐amplitude tuning from −10 dB to nearly 0 dB while maintaining broad phase coverage\. Furthermore, a programmable metasurface is constructed based on the experimentally measured accessible complex‐response state cloud\. A region‐adaptive mapping method is introduced to map the ideal complex‐amplitude distribution onto experimentally realizable states\. Dynamic complex‐amplitude holography is subsequently demonstrated, validating the decoupling mechanism at the programmable wavefront level\. This work provides a physically informed and practical design strategy for amplitude–phase decoupling in reconfigurable metasurfaces, supporting the advancement of dynamic complex‐amplitude wavefront control and programmable metasurface technologies\.

## [Malzeme Üretim Teknolojilerinde Güncel Yaklaşımlar](../publications/fa8a250db1aeec7971be.md)



Malzeme üretim teknolojileri, mühendislik ve teknoloji alanlarında yaşanan bilimsel gelişmelerin temel yapı taşlarından birini oluşturmaktadır\. Günümüzde artan endüstriyel gereksinimler, sürdürülebilir üretim anlayışı, enerji verimliliği ve yüksek performanslı malzemelere duyulan ihtiyaç, geleneksel üretim yöntemlerinin geliştirilmesini ve yenilikçi teknolojilerin uygulanmasını zorunlu hâle getirmektedir\. Bu doğrultuda malzeme bilimi ile üretim teknolojilerinin bütünleşmesi, endüstriyel dönüşümün ve teknolojik ilerlemenin önemli bir unsuru olarak öne çıkmaktadır\. “Malzeme Üretim Teknolojilerinde Güncel Yaklaşımlar” başlıklı bu e\-kitap, malzeme üretimi ve işlenmesi alanındaki güncel bilimsel araştırmaları, teknolojik yenilikleri ve modern mühendislik yaklaşımlarını kapsamlı bir bakış açısıyla ele almak amacıyla hazırlanmıştır\. Eserde; ileri üretim yöntemleri, yeni nesil malzemeler, malzeme karakterizasyonu, üretim süreçlerinin optimizasyonu, sürdürülebilirlik ve yenilikçi uygulamalar gibi konuların bilimsel bir çerçevede değerlendirilmesi hedeflenmektedir\. Kitabın temel amacı, malzeme üretim teknolojilerindeki güncel gelişmeleri akademik bilgi birikimiyle bütünleştirerek araştırmacılara, akademisyenlere, lisans ve lisansüstü öğrencilere ve sanayi profesyonellerine yararlı bir başvuru kaynağı sunmaktır\. Ayrıca farklı disiplinlerden gelen bilimsel yaklaşımların bir araya getirilmesiyle disiplinler arası etkileşimin güçlendirilmesi ve gelecekte gerçekleştirilecek araştırmalara katkı sağlanması amaçlanmaktadır\. Bu eserin hazırlanmasında bilimsel bilgi ve deneyimleriyle katkı sunan tüm bölüm yazarlarına ve yayın sürecinde emeği geçenlere teşekkür eder; kitabın malzeme bilimi ve üretim teknolojileri alanındaki akademik çalışmalara, teknolojik gelişmelere ve endüstriyel uygulamalara katkı sağlamasını dileriz\.

## [Prehospital delay and thrombolysis rates in posterior circulation stroke: a multicenter Latin American study](../publications/fa9663a039a0e951733f.md)

Charles Huamaní; Andrés A\. Mercado\-Pompa; Alfonso León\-Mantero; Víctor Oré\-Montalvo; Iván Baracaldo\-Santamaría; Hebert Puente\-Vila; Melissa Pérez; Rocío B\. Pacheco\-Elgueta; Max Molina\-Jara; Andrés Diaz\-Guzman; Carlos Hesed Virto Farfan; Vanessa Cano\-Nigenda; Antonio Arauz

Objective We aimed to evaluate the delay to emergency arrival in adults with acute Posterior circulation ischemic strokes \(PCS\) and the likelihood of receiving intravenous thrombolysis compared to anterior circulation ischemic strokes \(ACS\) across six different hospitals in Latin America\. Methods This multicenter study in Latin America hospitals including three hospitals in Peru \(Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima City\), one in Colombia \(Bogotá\), one in Chile \(Valdivia\), and one in Mexico City\. We analyzed adult patients treated between 2018 and 2023 with a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic stroke \(IS\)\. We evaluated demographic characteristics, initial NIHSS score, onset\-to\-door time \(ODT\), rate of intravenous thrombolysis \(IVT\), and other stroke\-related characteristics\. Medians with interquartile ranges \(IQR\) were calculated\. IVT \(yes/no\) was evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression including stroke circulation, age, sex, admission NIHSS, ODT, previous stroke, and previous evaluation at another hospital as covariates\. Continuous predictors were modeled per year, NIHSS point, and ODT hour, respectively\. Adjusted odds ratios \(aOR\) with 95% CI were reported, with p &lt; 0\.05 considered statistically significant\. Results A total of 1,460 patients were included, 501 \(34\.3%\) of whom had PCS, with a median age of 70 years \(IQR 59–80\)\. We found significant differences in median ODT between PCS and ACS \(13 h, IQR 5–46 vs\. 8\.5 h, IQR 4–20; p &lt; 0\.001\) and in IVT rates\. In the adjusted analysis, each additional hour of ODT was associated with lower odds of IVT \(aOR 0\.88, 95% CI 0\.85–0\.92\), whereas stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT \(PCS vs\. ACS: aOR 0\.66, 95% CI 0\.39–1\.11\)\. Higher admission NIHSS was associated with higher odds of IVT \(aOR 1\.06 per point, 95% CI 1\.03–1\.09\)\. Conclusion Patients with posterior circulation stroke had longer prehospital delays and lower observed rates of intravenous thrombolysis than those with anterior circulation stroke\. However, stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT after adjustment for ODT and other clinically relevant covariates\. These findings highlight early recognition and reduction of prehospital delay as potential targets for improving access to reperfusion therapy in Latin America\.

## [Machine learning\-assisted genomic characterization of population differentiation between Chinese Kirghiz and Kyrgyzstan local sheep](../publications/fa996cccfc4143dbc727.md)

Lingfeng Kong; Wanwan Peng; Yuwei Peng; 李延鎬; Lijun Zhu; R\. Yang; Azbergenov Erkinbay; Fumin Kou; Yaxuan Liao; Muattar Mutalifu; Attokurov Kursantbek; Рахима Муратова; Abdyldaeva Roza; Abdurasulov Abdugani; Gemingguli Mukhatai; Shudong Liu

Chinese Kirghiz \(KIR\) sheep inhabit the eastern Pamir region near the China–Kyrgyzstan border, but their genomic relationship with geographically adjacent sheep populations in Kyrgyzstan remains incompletely resolved\. We characterized population genomic differentiation between KIR and Kyrgyzstan local sheep while explicitly evaluating the effects of sample\-size imbalance and population structure on genomic and machine\-learning results\. After quality control and relatedness filtering, 48,902 SNPs from 722 sheep representing 14 populations were retained\. The focal dataset remained unbalanced \(KIR, n = 187; ALA, n = 10; GIS, n = 15; LOC, n = 43\), so balanced resampling was used for sensitivity analyses\. KIR showed lower observed heterozygosity \(Ho = 0\.249\) than expected heterozygosity \(He = 0\.355\), with an elevated F IS \(0\.296\), while nucleotide diversity remained relatively high \(π = 0\.356\)\. Balanced resampling reproduced this contrast, whereas the overall ROH burden in KIR was modest \(mean F ROH = 0\.009\)\. PCA supported genetic differentiation between KIR and the three Kyrgyzstan local populations, while complementary ancestry and gene\-flow analyses indicated regional genetic connectivity\. Balanced pairwise F ST estimates between KIR and ALA, GIS, and LOC were 0\.099, 0\.092, and 0\.098, respectively\. Intersecting low KIR nucleotide diversity with elevated pairwise FST identified 395 candidate genes, including CAMK 2A, CACNA 1C, EPHB 1, ROBO 1, GRID 1, GRID 2, and RXFP 2; however, no GO or KEGG term remained significant after multiple\-testing correction\. Machine\-learning classifiers showed near\-perfect discrimination in the full dataset, but performance and feature stability decreased under balanced resampling, and no prioritized SNP remained significant after PC\-adjusted association testing at FDR &lt; 0\.01\. Chinese Kirghiz sheep are genomically differentiated from neighboring Kyrgyzstan local sheep despite evidence of regional genetic connectivity\. Sensitivity analyses indicate that sample imbalance and population structure can strongly influence apparent machine\-learning performance and marker prioritization\. The identified loci should therefore be regarded as population\-informative candidates for further validation rather than as confirmed adaptive variants\.

## [DESIGNING RESILIENT ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS THROUGH AI\-DRIVEN DEPENDENCY MAPPING AND IMPACT ANALYSIS](../publications/fa9a89abf5dcc4056231.md)

Pradip Baral

Enterprise systems are now often spread across a range of hidden technical and organizational dependencies; technical debt can accumulate, configurations can change, and failures can propagate\. Redundancy or post\-incident recovery alone is not enough for resilience design; such environments require continuously updated dependency knowledge and credible impact analysis before, during, and after change\. This review considers peer\-reviewed journal literature published between 2015 and 2024 that is relevant to the dependency mapping and impact analysis of resilient enterprise systems using AI\. The studies included in the review are grouped around microservice architecture, process mining, digital twins, graph learning, anomaly detection, explainable artificial intelligence and resilience measurement, as well as AIOps\. Based on the literature, it is shown that AI\-based mapping can increase observability of runtime relations, aid in change\-risk prioritization, and aid in failure localization with architectural models and operational telemetry\. There are still gaps in causal validation, cross\-layer dependency representation, data quality, explainability and evaluation against real enterprise incidents\. There is scholarly value in the field, as resilient design increasingly relies on dynamic, evidence\-based knowledge of how enterprise elements behave under stress, change and degradation\.

## [Safety performance evaluation of a gently dipping bedding slope containing multiple weak interlayers in Southwest China](../publications/fa9c6296e47b77967b64.md)

Zhang Le; Junyun Zhang; Zhen Gong; Changchun He; Jun Feng; Bo Xiang; Yufei Zhang; 高付州

The failure modes and safety assessment methods of gently dipping bedding slopes containing multiple weak interlayers \(GBSWs\) are critical issues in engineering construction\. In this study, engineering geological investigations and laboratory direct shear tests on undisturbed samples were conducted to elucidate the strength degradation mechanism and the evolution of strength parameters of the weak interlayers, while finite element simulations were employed to investigate the slope failure modes\. Based on the laboratory test results and numerical simulations, a back\-propagation neural network \(BPNN\) model was developed to enable rapid assessment of the operational safety of engineering slopes\. The results indicate that the shear strength of the weak interlayers decreases significantly with increasing water content, while both cohesion and the internal friction angle exhibit an exponential decay\. The bedrock–overburden interface and the weak interlayers within the slope constitute unfavorable interfaces\. Following excavation\-induced unloading, slope deformation develops preferentially along these interfaces, resulting in an overall stepped sliding–tensile cracking failure mode\. Staged excavation, together with the timely implementation of protective measures after excavation, can effectively control the factor of safety \( F s\) and the maximum horizontal displacement \(\| U x\| max \) of the slope\. Comparative trial calculations showed that the 5–10–2 BPNN architecture exhibited the best performance, yielding the lowest root mean square error \(RMSE\) and the highest coefficient of determination \(R²\)\. For GBSWs, an analytical limit equilibrium method applicable to the engineering feasibility study and preliminary design stages, together with a predictive assessment method based on machine learning for the safe operation stage, was proposed\.

## [RECENT ADVANCES IN ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY: EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES AND SUSTAINABLE APPROACHES IN PHARMACEUTICAL ANALYSIS](../publications/faa1cf544e6eaf166dbe.md)

Pogula\. Sathwika; Gope\. Bhargavi; AbijithVardhan Reddy; Orsu Devadasu; Darla\. Swarnalatha

Analytical chemistry plays an essential role in the identification, separation, quantification, and characterization of pharmaceutical substances\. Recent technological developments have introduced advanced analytical approaches with improved sensitivity, accuracy, selectivity, speed, and reliability\.\[1\] This review focuses on recent research in chromatography, mass spectrometry, spectroscopy, biosensors, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning \(AI/ML\), and Green Analytical Chemistry\. Modern chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques enable efficient separation, structural characterization, impurity profiling, and sensitive analysis of complex samples\. Spectroscopic techniques provide rapid and non\-destructive characterization, while biosensors offer sensitive, rapid, and potentially portable detection systems\. AI/ML approaches are increasingly applied for analytical data processing, prediction, pattern recognition, and method optimization\. Green analytical approaches aim to minimize hazardous solvents, waste generation, energy consumption, and sample requirements while maintaining analytical performance\.\[2\] The review compares the methodologies, major findings, strengths, limitations, and research gaps reported in recent studies\. Overall, the integration of advanced instrumentation, intelligent data analysis, biosensing technologies, and sustainable analytical practices is expected to contribute to the development of faster, more sensitive, reliable, automated, and environmentally sustainable pharmaceutical analytical methods\.

## [Audit of information systems in digitalized business environments](../publications/faa7fd8ed39b640ff0e0.md)

Basri Ganiu

Digitalizacija poslovanja povečuje pomen informacijskih sistemov, saj so ti vse bolj povezani s poslovnimi procesi, podatki in vsakodnevnim delovanjem organizacij\. Z večjo uporabo digitalnih tehnologij in povezanostjo informacijskih sistemov pa se povečujejo tudi tveganja, povezana z njihovim delovanjem, varnostjo in upravljanjem\. Zaradi tega ima revizija informacijskih sistemov pomembno vlogo pri presoji kontrol, prepoznavanju tveganj ter ugotavljanju pomanjkljivosti, ki lahko vplivajo na poslovanje organizacije\. Revizija informacijskih sistemov zajema različne aktivnosti, od načrtovanja in ocenjevanja tveganj do zbiranja revizijskih dokazov, presoje notranjih kontrol ter priprave poročila in priporočil\. Pri njenem izvajanju se lahko uporabljajo različni standardi in strokovni okviri, ki omogočajo bolj strukturirano presojo posameznih področij informacijskega okolja\. V digitaliziranem poslovnem okolju se mora revizija prilagajati tudi novim tehnologijam, spreminjajočim se tveganjem in vse večji odvisnosti organizacij od informacijskih sistemov\. Analizirane študije primerov kažejo, da se obseg in način izvajanja revizije informacijskih sistemov prilagajata značilnostim pregledanega sistema, prisotnim tveganjem in področju revizije\. Revizija lahko tako vključuje presojo kibernetske varnosti, aplikacijskih kontrol, upravljanja informacijskih sistemov in drugih področij\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da za zanesljivo delovanje informacijskih sistemov niso pomembne samo tehnične rešitve, temveč tudi ustrezno upravljanje, učinkovito delovanje kontrol ter spremljanje ugotovljenih pomanjkljivosti in izvedbe priporočil\. Revizija informacijskih sistemov zato predstavlja pomemben mehanizem za prepoznavanje tveganj in izboljševanje delovanja informacijskih sistemov v digitaliziranem poslovnem okolju\.
