## [Enhancing the Accessibility of Instructional Content in Higher Education Through AI](../publications/faaba51dc1caf5060be6.md)

Sushma Alphonsa

As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into higher education, it presents new opportunities to enhance the accessibility of instructional materials\. This session examines how Microsoft Copilot, Adobe AI, and built\-in Windows 11 features such as live auto\-captions can support more accessible content creation and remediation across Microsoft 365 applications and PDF workflows\. Focusing on commonly used instructional formats including Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and PDFs shared through learning management systems, this presentation highlights how AI tools can assist in identifying and addressing accessibility barriers\. Examples will illustrate how Copilot can support content development, organization, and alternative text generation, while Adobe AI tools streamline improvements to PDF structure, tagging, and usability\. Windows 11 auto\-captioning features will also be discussed as a way to enhance access to audio and video content\. The session explores practical approaches for integrating AI\-supported accessibility strategies into existing teaching and course design workflows\. Attention is given to aligning these approaches with accessibility standards and inclusive teaching practices while maintaining efficiency for instructors, instructional designers, technologists, and teaching assistants\. Attendees will gain insight into key strategies, considerations, and potential applications of AI to create more inclusive, accessible instructional materials\.

## [Quantum and Quantum\-Inspired Image Segmentation in Computer Vision: Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis of Research Trends and Hybrid Methods](../publications/fab36466c653317229f9.md)

Shakhzoda Tojiboyeva; Kudaybergenov Adilbay; Muhamediyeva Dilnoz; Mamatov Narzullo; Ametova Gulsara

Quantum and quantum\-inspired image segmentation lies at the intersection of quantum computing, computer vision, machine learning and medical image analysis\. We map the field from 422 Scopus\-indexed publications \(2018–2025\) retrieved with a documented Advanced Search query and screened in three explicit levels\. Formal eligibility retained 408 records\. A published topical decision rule was then applied in two operationalizations that differ only in the metadata scope they read \(observed agreement 82\.8%, Cohen’s κ = 0\.65\); all 197 records in the two agreement\-relevant strata were adjudicated at record level, and the 211 records both operationalizations excluded were validated on a random sample of 60\. The final topical corpus contains 143 records, and at the sample rate roughly two to three further eligible records remain in the unexamined remainder\. Screening changes the headline picture: the retrieved corpus grows at 20\.45% a year \(28 records in 2018 to 103 in 2025\) but the topical corpus at only 10\.41% \(13 to 26\), so about half of the apparent expansion is peripheral retrieval\. China, India and the United States lead at every level\. Of the 138 method studies, 9 \(6\.5%\) report execution on physical quantum hardware, 43 \(31\.2%\) are gate\-based or variational studies run on simulators or with an unstated environment, 12 \(8\.7%\) use annealing, Ising or QUBO formulations, and 74 \(53\.6%\) are quantum\-inspired classical algorithms that require no quantum device; 27 \(19\.6%\) combine a classical vision pipeline with a quantum component\. Quantum\-inspired classical work falls from 78\.0% to 29\.2% of the period’s method studies while hybrid work rises from 3 to 19 records\. All findings describe publication patterns, not segmentation performance or quantum advantage\. A versioned data and code package reproduces every reported number\.

## [Predicting nitrogen dioxide column density from the International Wealth Index with a convolutional neural network in Africa](../publications/fab40837862ffb4fabaf.md)

Francesco Grieco; Mohammad Kakooei; Adel Daoud

Abstract In the pursuit of improving socioeconomic living conditions of their populations, many nations struggle to meet their nationally determined contributions \(NDCs\) under the Paris agreement, and that shortfall makes accountability for emissions reductions critical\. The long atmospheric lifetimes of key gases such as carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) and methane \(CH 4 \) hinder traditional greenhouse gas \(GHG\) monitoring, because what any one place emits adds only a small excess to a large, well\-mixed background\. Nitrogen dioxide \(NO 2 \) behaves differently: it is short\-lived and highly variable in space and time, so satellite instruments resolve its patterns close to source regions\. Across the African continent, mapped temporal correlations between NO 2 and CO 2 are moderate in magnitude but spatially structured and consistently positive\. Although we do not use that association to mechanically convert NO 2 observations into CO 2 , we report it as contextual evidence towards NDCs\. Given this context, this study asks the following question: to what extent can socioeconomic development at the neighbourhood scale predict NO 2 column densities \(the amount of NO 2 in the air column above that neighbourhood\) across Africa? We apply a convolutional neural network \(CNN\) to gridded International Wealth Index \(IWI\) estimates and to NO 2 observations from the tropospheric Monitoring Instrument \(TROPOMI\), and obtain an average predictive accuracy of $$R^2$$ = 0\.56 across the African continent\. Because IWI can be projected forward, we also present an illustrative 2030 scenario as a methodological demonstration of the relationship between socioeconomic development and NO 2 trajectories\. These findings indicate that gridded wealth estimates carry predictive information about NO 2 column density in Africa\. Such estimates offer a lightweight and scalable screening tool that complements process\-based atmospheric monitoring rather than replacing it\.

## [Photonic quantum reservoir computing on real financial surfaces: identifying the structural ceiling of near\-random\-walk data](../publications/fab8ea9804bf7ee3b823.md)

Oishik Kar; Aditya Raj; Aswath Babu H

Abstract Quantum machine learning is increasingly proposed for financial time series, yet practitioners have no way to predict whether quantum reservoir computing \(QRC\) will outperform classical baselines on a given dataset before committing resources\. We propose a pre\-experimental screening framework, built on persistence R2 and PCA variance decomposition, that makes this prediction possible\. We validate the framework using a 10\-mode Boson sampling circuit \(252 features\) on three market datasets \(US Treasury yields, CBOE VIX, crude oil\) and a diagnostic nonlinear control\. On the market data, the screening tool correctly predicts a structural ceiling: because financial surfaces follow near\-random\-walk dynamics \(persistence R2 &gt; 0\.95, 3 PCA components\), QRC collapses to the performance of classical Ridge regression \(R2 = 0\.9797 vs 0\.9798 on Treasuries, with persistence at 0\.9793\)\. On the nonlinear control, the framework correctly predicts that a nonlinear feature map will outperform linear Ridge\. The Boson sampling QRC confirms this prediction: the quantum circuit achieves R2 = 0\.816±0\.007, outperforming classical Ridge \(R2 = 0\.77\) on a dataset where persistence completely fails \(R2 = −1\.64\)\. The proposed screening test can be computed from the raw data alone, before any quantum circuit is built\.

## [POI location\-aware services package recommendation for random groups](../publications/fac07ebc2a2ddbdc11cc.md)

Ling Shang; Xiaoyu Song; Zhizong Liu; Kai Zhang; Quan Z\. Sheng; Jian Yu

Recently, with the rapid growth of Point of Interest \(POIs\) and increasing of social activities, more and more individuals tend to join parties or trips with groups formed randomly \(named random groups, RGs\)\. Although some works have proposed wonderful POI recommendation methods for RGs, they failed to consider how to recommend service packages for RGs after they accept the recommended POIs, which significantly degrades user experience\. To address this issue, this work proposes a POI location\-aware service package recommendation model for random groups \(termed PLSPR\-RG\)\. First of all, PLSPR\-RG generates fitted feature representations of random groups with an enhanced feature learning method\. Then, it selects users with similar characteristics to the random group and utilizes service usage data of similar users as the training dataset for PLSPR\-RG\. Subsequently, PLSPR\-RG constructs a service labeled bipartite graph of similar users, then it employs an edge\-enhanced bipartite graph neural network with multi\-view contrastive learning \(EBGNN\-CL\) to learn service feature representations that capturing both positive and negative interaction preferences of similar users\. Furthermore, PLSPR\-RG builds a directed service transition graph based on the service interaction records of similar users and adopts the SRGNN network to learn service feature representations containing latent user preferences, as well as user preference representations\. Finally, based on the learned service representations and the fitted features of random groups, PLSPR\-RG generates a ranked list of recommended services, thereby completing POI location\-aware service package recommendation for random groups\. Extensive experiments have been conducted on three public datasets \(Foursquare, Gowalla and Yelp dataset\), which have proved that our proposed model outperforms the state\-of\-the\-art models\.

## [Leading for Adaptive Performance in Higher Education Institutions: Why Do Quality of Work\-Life and Faculty Commitment Matter?](../publications/fac3bd70da96e0badc7e.md)

Baburam Lamichhane; Dhruba Kumar Gautam; Prakash Kumar Gautam

Purpose: Adaptive performance has gained momentum critically as they navigate rapid technological, pedagogical, and organizational change in higher education\. In this context, the study aims to investigate the role of adaptive leadership, work\-life balance, and commitment on faculty’s adaptive performance\.Design/Methodology: The study uses an analytical research design based on stratified sampling techniques\. A structured questionnaire was used to collect data using a survey from 406 full\-time teaching faculty \(professors, associate professors, and assistant professors\) of Nepalese universities from December 2024 to April 2025\. Descriptive statistics were used to identify the respondents’ descriptive facts, while associations and effects of predictor variables were examined using inferential statistics\.Findings: The findings demonstrate that adaptive performance is not merely an individual capability, but a socially embedded outcome shaped by leadership\-driven work environments and commitment\. Adaptive leaders create supportive working environments through quality work\-life practices that enhance commitment\.Originality/value: This study is original as it integrates the Adaptive Leadership, Quality Work\-life framework, Job Demand Resource framework, and Pulakos’ Adaptive Performance models to reveal distinct motivational pathways, offering a context\-specific understanding of faculty adaptive performance\. In this way, the study opens new discussions on how institutions can strategically enhance faculty adaptive performance through shaping leadership\-driven work environments and commitment\.

## [King, Thomas C\. ; Aggarwal, Nikita ; Taddeo, Mariarosaria &amp; Floridi, Luciano: Artificial intelligence crime: an interdisciplinary analysis of foreseeable threats and solutions](../publications/fac6ac65cfd82503f406.md)



\_Science and Engineering Ethics\_ 26 \(1\):89\-120\. 2019Artificial intelligence research and regulation seek to balance the benefits of innovation against any potential harms and disruption\. However, one unintended consequence of the recent surge in AI research is the potential re\-orientation of AI technologies to facilitate criminal acts, term in this article AI\-Crime\. AIC is theoretically feasible thanks to published experiments in automating fraud targeted at social media users, as well as demonstrations of AI\-driven manipulation of simulated markets\. However, because AIC is still a relatively young and inherently interdisciplinary area—spanning socio\-legal studies to formal science—there is little certainty of what an AIC future might look like\. This article offers the first systematic, interdisciplinary literature analysis of the foreseeable threats of AIC, providing ethicists, policy\-makers, and law enforcement organisations with a synthesis of the current problems, and a possible solution space\. \(direct link \)

## [Thyroid\-bed schwannoma mimicking a thyroid neoplasm: a case report](../publications/fac8a25d57e786fdc71f.md)

Mingyu Wang; Boyang Yu

Intrathyroidal schwannomas are rare, and thyroid\-bed schwannomas are scarcer, with merely a few case reports and tough preoperative differentiation\. We report a 33\-year\-old female with a swallowing\-movable left neck mass and normal thyroid function\. Gray\-scale B\-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging and contrast\-enhanced ultrasound showed showed a heterogeneously enhanced TI\-RADS 3 lesion preoperatively suspected as a follicular neoplasm\. Fine\-needle aspiration \(FNA\) biopsy was performed, which failed to yield a definitive pathological diagnosis and yielded Bethesda category I\. She received left lobectomy plus isthmectomy, and pathology confirmed thyroid\-bed schwannoma sparing thyroid parenchyma; she recovered well with normal thyroid function postoperatively\. Due to its low incidence, this tumor is often mistaken for an intrathyroidal nodule on ultrasound\. Total surgical excision is the first\-line therapy with good overall prognosis\. Unlike intrathyroidal schwannomas, most thyroid\-bed lesions can be enucleated alone without routine thyroidectomy; hemithyroidectomy is needed for dense adhesion, and total thyroidectomy is rarely required\. Considering the low diagnostic value of FNA, multidisciplinary consultation of pathology, radiology and surgery is advised for lesions with atypical imaging, inconclusive FNA or ill\-defined thyroid margins\. Ultrasound\-guided core needle biopsy \(CNB\) should be performed if needed to tailor proper treatment\.

## [A Review on Music Induced Emotion and Music Processing in the Brain](../publications/faccf66e9eaa8b7dc338.md)

Sana Anees; Basma Binth Basheer; Rihana Sharin; Sahla Liyakath; Shaik Samahat Raaziya; Halima Umar Zubairu

People&\#x27;s enthusiasm for music has never wavered\. It is among the most important and traditional aspects of human society\. One of the wonderful things about music is its ability to arouse strong emotions in us\. Music has a way of hitting our hearts regardless of our emotions, whether they are joy, grief, enthusiasm, or memories\. It is frequently regarded as the catalyst that most intensely aroused human emotion\. Not only can music arouse our feelings, but it also has the power to amplify or dull them\. You&\#x27;ve undoubtedly seen how a happy song can instantly make you feel better or how a depressing tune may make you feel even worse\. The power of music\! It is astounding to learn that individuals frequently select their music based on how they are feeling or what they want to feel\. We utilize music as a tool to direct our feelings and elicit the feelings we desire\. Our lives seem to have a soundtrack\! However, music serves purposes beyond our feelings\. It also has a major impact on our ability to think clearly\. Music helps prevent mental dullness while we perform boring, repetitive tasks\. Because it keeps our thoughts active, it keeps us motivated and concentrated\. When we listen to music, our brains go through a sophisticated musical processing mechanism\. Multiple brain regions are active as we hear, analyze, and understand music\. It&\#x27;s amazing to see how our brains respond to various melodies, rhythms, and harmonies\. Our bodies are impacted by music in addition to our intellect\. It has the ability to trigger the Autonomic Nervous System \(ANS\), which regulates the body&\#x27;s natural functions including heart rate, blood pressure, and respiration\. Similar to how certain people may make us uneasy and uncomfortable, others can cause our hearts to race\. All things considered, music is a powerful and intricate phenomena that affects not just our emotions and ideas but also our bodily states\. It makes perfect sense that it had such a significant impact on people&\#x27;s lives for many generations\.

## [Nondestructive prediction of textural properties of model plant\-based meat analogs prepared with sesame seed meal protein isolate using hyperspectral imaging](../publications/fad3ef03f0eb15c6661a.md)

Hyun\-Su Choi; Jaeeun Lee; In\-Geun Jung; Harin Jang; Dong\-Heun Sung; Pu Reun Yoon; Sangbae Park; Ghiseok Kim; Yong‐Ro Kim

Abstract Texture, a key quality attribute in plant\-based meat analogs \(PMAs\), is conventionally evaluated using destructive methods\. This study evaluated the use of hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) coupled with partial least squares regression \(PLSR\) for the nondestructive prediction of six textural attributes in model plant\-based meat analogs formulated with sesame seed meal protein isolate \(SMPI\)\. Samples \(n = 80\) covering a broad textural range were imaged at 900–1700 nm, and their spectra were used to develop PLSR models\. Models for hardness \(R 2 CV = 0\.882, RPD = 2\.92\), resilience \(0\.865, 2\.74\), and chewiness \(0\.829, 2\.44\) showed adequate predictive performance\. Cohesiveness and adhesiveness exhibited limited performance, while no valid model was obtained for springiness\. Variable importance in projection analysis identified informative wavelength regions below 1200 nm\. Collectively, HSI–PLSR showed potential for the nondestructive evaluation of selected textural attributes in PMAs\.

## [Simultaneous and Dynamic Prediction of Coupled Parameters in Colloidal Micronano Motion Systems by Physics\-Informed Machine Learning](../publications/fad87c73c1c2ef034a5b.md)

Can Zuo; Yumei Wen; Ping Li

Abstract For probing micronano particle motion interface dynamics, intrinsic physical coupling among particle hydrodynamic radius \(rh\), interfacial viscosity \(η\), and temperature \(T\) hinders their simultaneous and dynamic acquisition and limits the labeled data available for conventional machine learning \(ML\)\. Here, we propose a physics\-informed machine learning \(PIML\) paradigm that uses digital\-twin simulations to endow ML models with physical priors\. The digital twin reveals a millionfold disparity in parameter influence on motion signals and severe parameter unidentifiability in standard ML models\. To overcome this, a hybrid ML architecture, RF\-MBGA\-Net, integrates a random forest \(RF\) with a multibranch gated attention \(MBGA\) network to balance parameter influence scales via intermediate prediction feedback and data augmentation\. RF\-MBGA\-Net achieves high\-accuracy predictions on simulated data \(R2 &gt; 99%; MAEs: rh= 3\.9 nm, η = 0\.023 mPa·s, T = 1\.5 K\)\. The trained RF\-MBGA\-Net performs simultaneous and dynamic prediction of the three parameters from experimental motion signals\. The predicted rh, η, and T align with dynamic light scattering \(DLS\) results, rotational rheometer measurements, and sample\-set temperatures\. Moreover, the model captures inverse η–T coupling and molecular dissociation kinetics\. The proposed PIML paradigm provides a scalable route for decoding coupled inaccessible parameters and probing micronano complex interface dynamics\.

## [Everyday geopolitical governance: perspectives of faculty and chinese doctoral students in U\.S\. higher education](../publications/fae8c3623aaa24581306.md)

Futao Huang

Universities increasingly operate in a geopolitical environment in which international collaboration, research security, academic mobility, and technological competition are closely intertwined\. Yet less is known about how geopolitical change is translated into routine academic practice\. This article introduces Everyday Geopolitical Governance as a framework for examining that translation\. The concept is newly developed in this study but draws on critical and feminist work on everyday geopolitics, organizational approaches to university governance, and scholarship on anticipatory action under uncertainty\. The study draws on semi\-structured interviews with 19 participants affiliated with U\.S\. higher education institutions: 14 faculty members \(four U\.S\.\-born and ten China\-origin scholars\) and five Chinese doctoral students\. Using reflexive thematic analysis, the study examines how participants described changes in collaboration, research administration, mobility, and career planning\. The analysis is interpretive and does not seek statistical comparison across participant sub\-groups\. Three interrelated mechanisms emerged from the analysis\. Organizational mediation captures how universities translate geopolitical priorities into procedures and routines; differentiated vulnerability describes how exposure to uncertainty varies with disciplinary, career\-stage, institutional, and national positioning; and anticipatory adaptation explains how academics adjust present decisions in light of possible future policy or political change\. Within this sample, geopolitical governance was experienced less as direct state intervention than as a combination of institutional mediation and anticipatory professional judgement\. The framework connects geopolitical transformation, university governance, and academic agency while remaining attentive to the bounded perspectives represented in the study\.

## [Direitos de crianças e adolescentes no ambiente digital: marcos regulatórios internacionais e nacionais e a emergência da digital corporate accountability](../publications/faea53cc38eb068814ee.md)

Luiz Eduardo Camargo Outeiro Hernandes; Flávia Piovesan

O objetivo do presente trabalho é analisar os principais marcos regulatórios nos planos internacional, regional e nacional que regulamentam os direitos das crianças e dos adolescentes no ambiente digital, de forma a identificar o fortalecimento da responsabilidade das empresas de tecnologia no ambiente digital, especialmente no que se refere à proteção e à promoção dos direitos humanos das crianças e dos adolescentes\. Cabe precisar que a expressão “princípio de que os direitos das crianças e dos adolescentes devem ser observados no ambiente digital” não designa um princípio jurídico autônomo, no sentido técnico de norma jurídica\. Expressa sim a ideia de que os direitos fundamentais das crianças e dos adolescentes não perdem vigor, nem eficácia pelo simples fato de o sujeito estar inserido em um ambiente digital\. Eles impõem às plataformas digitais obrigações positivas de atuação\. A pesquisa possui natureza qualitativa, com revisão de literatura, análises documentais e comparativas dos marcos regulatórios da ONU, da União Europeia, da Espanha, dos Estados Unidos, do Reino Unido e do Brasil\. Os resultados apontam convergências relevantes entre os ordenamentos analisados — sobretudo quanto à exigência de verificação de idade, ao consentimento parental, à proteção de dados e às sanções pecuniárias — e divergências quanto à faixa etária de proteção, à natureza das obrigações e ao tratamento da publicidade direcionada\. A pesquisa conclui que a consolidação do princípio de que os direitos das crianças e dos adolescentes devem ser observados no ambiente digital fez surgir novas obrigações e deveres para as empresas de tecnologia em respeitar e proteger esses direitos, conformando o que se denomina regime jurídico do &quot;digital corporate accountability&quot;, por meio do dever reforçado de devida diligência corporativa, sob inspiração do princípio do interesse superior da criança\.

## [Cases on Business Development](../publications/faf4d12add517c6e4c55.md)



This case collection has been developed primarily for use in university\-level business education, particularly in courses and programs dedicated to business development, entrepreneurship, in the intersection of corporate finance and strategic management\. The cases can be used at both undergraduate and graduate level, although several of them are particularly well suited to MSc, MBA, and executive education settings in which students are expected not only to apply analytical tools but also to formulate and defend managerial recommendations\. They may support classroom discussion, individual assignments, team\-based case analysis, financial modelling exercises, and capstone projects\. Instructors may use individual cases to illustrate specific concepts, or combine several cases to demonstrate how financial, strategic, and entrepreneurial decisions interact across different stages of organisational development\. Three areas of teaching are especially relevant to the collection\. First, several cases lend themselves directly to courses on business planning and financial modelling, where students must translate operational assumptions into investment plans, projected financial statements, cash\-flow implications, or scenario\-based forecasts\. Second, the volume addresses important questions in start\-up and venture financing, including the evaluation and monitoring of venture\-capital\-backed companies and the eventual exit of investors\. Third, a substantial part of the collection focuses on growth strategy, asking students to identify, compare, financially test, and ultimately recommend different paths toward revenue expansion\. In this sense, growth is treated not simply as a desirable business objective, but as a managerial problem involving market choices, organisational capabilities, financing requirements, risk, and implementation\. \(\.\.\.\)

## [Paradoks Penurunan Tingkat Pengangguran Terbuka dan Tingginya Pengangguran Usia Muda: Analisis Elastisitas Penyerapan Tenaga Kerja terhadap Investasi di Indonesia](../publications/faf99e76a985579f3399.md)

Fitria Marisya; Muhammad Bambang Purwanto; Abdul Rahman; Agung Indriansyah

Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan antara investasi dan penyerapan tenaga kerja di Indonesia dalam konteks penurunan Tingkat Pengangguran Terbuka \(TPT\) dan masih tingginya pengangguran usia muda\. Penelitian bertujuan menganalisis elastisitas penyerapan tenaga kerja terhadap perubahan investasi serta mengkaji implikasinya terhadap kondisi pasar kerja Indonesia, khususnya bagi tenaga kerja muda\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain deskriptif\-eksplanatori melalui data sekunder berbentuk deret waktu yang mencakup investasi, jumlah penduduk bekerja, Tingkat Pengangguran Terbuka, dan pengangguran usia muda\. Analisis utama dilakukan melalui pengukuran elastisitas penyerapan tenaga kerja terhadap investasi dengan membandingkan persentase perubahan jumlah tenaga kerja dengan persentase perubahan investasi selama periode pengamatan\. Analisis tersebut dilengkapi dengan interpretasi perkembangan pasar kerja dan hasil penelitian terdahulu\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan investasi tidak secara otomatis menghasilkan peningkatan penyerapan tenaga kerja secara proporsional\. Dampak investasi terhadap kesempatan kerja dipengaruhi oleh struktur investasi, intensitas modal, perkembangan teknologi, produktivitas, serta kesesuaian keterampilan tenaga kerja dengan kebutuhan industri\. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya menilai investasi tidak hanya berdasarkan nilai modal yang direalisasikan, tetapi juga berdasarkan kemampuannya menciptakan pekerjaan yang produktif dan berkelanjutan, terutama bagi tenaga kerja muda\.\.

## [Multicriteria Decision Analysis for Stock Selection A, Comparative Study of ELECTRE III with Veto, TOPSIS, and, PROMETHEE Methods](../publications/fb00d8d6eff199668376.md)

Mc\-Kelly Tamunotena Pepple

This paper explores the use of three multicriteria decision analysis \(MCDA\) methods— ELECTRE III with veto, TOPSIS, and PROMETHEE—in ranking stocks within a sector\. Each method evaluates stocks based on fundamental, performance, and technical criteria to identify top performers\. ELECTRE III with veto emphasizes robustness, TOPSIS focuses on balanced performance, and PROMETHEE customizes rankings based on specific preferences\. The analysis finds common high\-ranking stocks like Apple, Universal Display, and Microsoft across all methods, while each method also uniquely highlights different stocks\. The paper demonstrates how these MCDA methods provide comprehensive insights for informed stock investment decisions\.

## [Causal\-inspired Cross\-asset Contrastive Multimodal Maintenance Network: A Proxy\-benchmark Study for Renewable\-energy Maintenance](../publications/fb01303bb200e8581d93.md)

Dona Amange Franci; Chra Ismael Doghramachy; Haneen Khalid Dany; Maikey Zaki Bia; Shahab Wahhab Kareem

This paper proposes a Causal\-Inspired Cross\-Asset Contrastive Multimodal Maintenance Network \(C3M\-Farm\) for predictive\-maintenance research in renewable\-energy systems\.The architecture combines modality\-specific encoders, environment\-aware latent disentanglement, cross\-modal contrastive learning, attention\-based fusion, and graph reasoning\.NASA C\-MAPSS is used as a turbofan prognostics proxy rather than as direct renewable\-energyfarm validation\.The reported classification experiment achieved 96\.0% accuracy, 95\.7% precision, 95\.2% recall, 95\.4% F1\-score, and 97\.0%AUC\.In the controlled same\-pipeline RUL evaluation, C3M\-Farm achieved RMSE values of 2\.94 ± 0\.12, 2\.11 ± 0\.08, 2\.34 ± 0\.09, and 2\.94 ± 0\.11 on FD001, FD002, FD003, and FD004, respectively\.The paper reports lower RMSE values for C3M\-Farm than for the evaluated baselines on the subsets for which corresponding results are available\.These results are interpreted descriptively\.The preliminary archived experiments \(Tables 3456\) are retained only for provenance and do not support superiority claims\.The study therefore demonstrates proxy\-benchmark performance while retaining explicit limitations concerning cross\-study protocol equivalence, proxy\-modality construction, physical farm\-topology reasoning, and validation on genuinely heterogeneous renewable\-energy assets\.

## [The current state of technology integration in teaching and learning in Ethiopian public applied universities](../publications/fb0a0c08357ac534d532.md)

Demie Bedada; Bekalu Ferede; Desalegn Beyene Debelo

Technology is a powerful modern tool that can enrich pedagogical practices and enhance student learning\. To evaluate the current state of technology integration in teaching and learning, this study employed a convergent parallel mixed\-methods research design\. The study used the technology organization environment \(TOE\) model to contextualize technology integration in teaching practices and support student learning\. Quantitative data were collected from 316 instructors, while qualitative insights were gathered through purposive interviews with 12 academic leaders\. Descriptive data analysis was conducted using SPSS version 23, and qualitative data were used in a spreadsheet, coded, organized, and thematically analyzed\. The study results indicate that there is a high mean score \(M = 3\.79\) instructors’ technology integration in teaching practices and instructors technology integration in supporting student learning also has a high mean score \(M = 3\.52\)\. In addition, the analysis of correlation statistics indicates a strong positive relationship between instructors technology integration for teaching practices and instructors technology integration for supporting student learning, contributing \( r = \.61, p &lt;\.01\)\. Qualitative insights highlight that technology integration by instructors is likely to change the way they interact, replacing traditional teaching methods with technology based teaching and supporting students as they gain effective learning knowledge\. Furthermore, the transition from paper\-based to online assessment has reduced the burden on instructors in correcting students’ tests and exams\. Study results demonstrated that Ethiopian public applied universities do not encourage paperwork activities; rather, they promote technology integration across all aspects of the universities\. These results provide both theoretical and practical insights contextually for researchers and academicians, offering a valuable baseline for future study\.

## [Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles](../publications/fb0a54deec480121cb8c.md)

Peter K\. Friz; Khoa Lê; Huilin Zhang

We study stochastic optimal control of rough stochastic differential equations \(RSDEs\)\. This is in the spirit of the pathwise control problem \(Lions–Souganidis 1998, Buckdahn–Ma 2007; also Davis–Burstein 1992\), with renewed interest and recent works drawing motivation from filtering, SPDEs, and reinforcement learning\. Results include regularity of rough value functions, validity of a rough dynamic programming principle and new rough stability results for HJB equations, removing excessive regularity demands previously imposed by flow transformation methods\. Measurable selection is used to relate RSDEs to “doubly stochastic” SDEs under conditioning\. In contrast to previous works, Brownian statistics for the to\-be\-conditioned\-on noise are not required, aligned with the “pathwise” intuition that these should not matter upon conditioning\. Depending on the chosen class of admissible controls, the involved processes may also be anticipating\. The resulting stochastic value functions coincide in great generality for different classes of controls\. RSDE theory offers a powerful and unified perspective on this problem class\.

## [The hybrid mind: Generative AI and the reconfiguration of cognitive, social, and emotional development in the AI\-native child](../publications/fb18cda48b2c618c645e.md)

Claudio Longobardi

The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is reorganizing the ecology in which cognition, social understanding, agency, authorship, and emotional regulation develop\. This critical integrative review treats GenAI as a developmentally consequential interactive artifact: responsive, adaptive, linguistically fluent, multimodal, and increasingly embedded in learning, play, and communication\. Drawing on sociocultural, constructivist, ecological, extended\-cognition, AI\-literacy, and hybrid\-learning perspectives, we introduce the Hybrid Mind Framework\. It defines human\-AI coupling as recurrent, contingent coordination and distinguishes immediate AI\-supported performance from durable changes in unaided competence, competence during coupling, trust, support\-seeking, or authorship\. Four domains are considered: cognitive hybridization, social\-epistemic calibration, affective scaffolding and support\-seeking, and agency/authorship\. The review integrates emerging GenAI evidence with research on earlier responsive technologies and differentiates early childhood, middle childhood, early adolescence, and later adolescence\. Existing evidence indicates possible short\-term affordances and risks, but long\-term developmental effects remain largely untested\. Rather than treating GenAI as either a pedagogical miracle or a developmental threat, we propose that AI be designed and governed as part of children&\#x27;s developmental ecology\. Testable propositions and age\-calibrated implications distinguish observed findings from theory\-derived and precautionary claims\.

## [Intelligence\-enabled smart inhalable biomaterials for chronic inflammatory airway diseases: integrating responsive carrier engineering, lung\-on\-chip validation, and patient\-specific pulmonary modeling](../publications/fb296571ea6784ab6a3f.md)

Qi Fan; Zhongxu Li; Yongliang Sun; Yu Liu; Hangyu Chen

Chronic inflammatory airway diseases, particularly asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\), are commonly treated by inhalation, yet the nominal dose placed in an inhaler often differs substantially from the dose that reaches diseased airway regions, crosses mucus, enters target cells, and remains pharmacologically active\. Airway narrowing, heterogeneous ventilation, mucus plugging, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative and proteolytic stress, epithelial barrier dysfunction, inflammatory\-cell diversity, device characteristics, and patient\-specific inhalation maneuvers jointly shape therapeutic exposure\. Smart inhalable biomaterials can be designed to address some of these barriers by controlling transport, retention, activation, or release, but many systems are still optimized primarily at the nanoparticle level and evaluated in static models that do not capture realistic aerosol performance or patient\-specific deposition\. This review develops an intelligence\-enabled bioengineering framework linking disease\-informed material design with machine\-learning\-assisted formulation optimization, formulation–device–patient coupling, lung\-on\-chip validation, and patient\-specific pulmonary modeling\. Within this framework, airway features such as mucus architecture, redox gradients, protease activity, epithelial permeability, immune\-cell state, extracellular\-matrix remodeling, and regional airflow are considered measurable variables that can inform material design and evaluation\. The material platforms considered include mucus\-penetrating and mucoadhesive carriers, responsive materials, transformable nano\-in\-micro systems, polymeric and lipid nanoparticles, biomimetic carriers, extracellular vesicles, and systems for pulmonary delivery of nucleic acids and biologics\. Their development is considered alongside structured experimental design, machine learning, active learning, mechanistic aerosol modeling, physics\-informed surrogates, multi\-objective optimization, and uncertainty analysis\. Lung\-on\-chip systems provide human\-relevant settings in which deposited dose, mucus transport, barrier function, immune responses, and repeated\-exposure effects can be examined under air–liquid\-interface and breathing\-like conditions\. Patient\-specific computational fluid dynamics and reduced\-order models can complement these platforms by predicting regional deposition, whereas the term digital twin should be reserved for longitudinally updated, uncertainty\-aware models linked to actionable decisions\. Together, these approaches support a closed\-loop design–delivery–validation strategy in which material performance, aerosol behavior, biological response, and patient\-specific deposition are evaluated as connected rather than separate development problems\.

## [1\-Methylhistidine attenuates early myocardial inflammation in type 3 cardiorenal syndrome through modulation of the p105/p50 NF\-κB axis](../publications/fb36f59606b470f6b835.md)

Jiakun Zhang; Qian Wang; Xingyi Tu; Han Zhou; Shihui Wang; 李晶洁

Type 3 cardiorenal syndrome \(CRS3\) is characterized by cardiac injury or dysfunction secondary to acute kidney injury \(AKI\), yet the contribution of AKI\-associated metabolic remodeling to early myocardial inflammation remains poorly understood\. Here, paired serum and myocardial untargeted metabolomics identified 1\-methylhistidine \(1\-MH\) as a metabolite elevated in both compartments, with the highest variable importance in projection score in serum\. Exogenous 1\-MH improved the E/A ratio and attenuated myocardial inflammation and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick\-end labeling \(TUNEL\) positivity in rats with CRS3\. Similar protective effects were observed in a separate post\-ischemic cohort in which 1\-MH was administered immediately after renal reperfusion\. In CRS serum\-exposed H9c2 cells, 1\-MH reduced reactive oxygen species\-associated fluorescence, malondialdehyde content, and intracellular Fe 2\+ levels\. Transcriptomic profiling showed that 1\-MH suppressed inflammatory signaling, accompanied by changes in oxidative metabolism\. Integration of these transcriptomic signatures with target prediction prioritized NFKB1/p105, while ensemble docking identified recurrent candidate interaction regions within p105\. Cellular thermal shift assays showed a concentration\-related increase in p105 thermal stability following 1\-MH treatment\. 1\-MH increased p105 abundance while reducing total p50 abundance and nuclear p50 accumulation\. p105 overexpression increased p50 abundance and the expression of inflammatory transcripts and proteins suppressed by 1\-MH\. These findings demonstrate that 1\-MH attenuates early myocardial inflammation in CRS3 and reduces oxidative stress\-related changes in CRS serum\-exposed H9c2 cells\. These functional results support modulation of the p105/p50 NF\-κB axis and identify p105 as a molecular link between AKI\-associated metabolic remodeling and myocardial inflammatory signaling\.

## [Measuring the Quality of Neurosurgical Care Through Intracranial Suppurations: A Twenty\-Indicator Framework Tested on 150 Cases at Bouaké University Hospital](../publications/fb3955baf9c3536926bb.md)

Serge Konan Yao; Landry Stéphane Faozo Teti; Djoko Traoré; Adama Kouadio; Koffi Jean\-Jacques Kouassi; Adéréhime Haïdara

Background\. Global surgery indicators measure a country’s capacity, not what happens to a patient between the first symptoms and discharge\. Intracranial suppurations \(ICS\) test every link in the chain of care\. We used them as a tracer condition to build and test a framework for measuring quality in neurosurgery\. Methods\. Single\-center cohort study, retrospective then prospective, of 150 observations \(148 patients\) of ICS managed at Bouaké University Hospital \(Côte d’Ivoire\) from 2016 to 2026\. This is a secondary analysis of a cohort whose main study is the subject of a separate manuscript\. The ISQF framework comprises twenty indicators distributed according to the Donabedian model: six of structure, eight of process, and six of outcomes\. A composite compliance score \(ISI\-QI\) was calculated for each patient\. Two Firth penalized logistic regression models \(in\-hospital mortality; unfavorable outcome, GOS 1–3\) combined the ISI\-QI, a Glasgow Coma Scale \(GCS\) score below 9, and an age of at least 65 years\. Internal validation relied on 2,000 bootstrap samples with optimism correction\. No protocol was registered\. The report follows STROBE, SQUIRE 2\.0, and TRIPOD\+AI; no machine learning method was used\. Results\. Overall process compliance was 89\.0% \(878/987 care opportunities; 95% CI: 86\.9–90\.8\)\. Clinical indicators met or approached their targets\. Timeliness indicators fell short: 67\.0% of patients with a surgical indication were operated on within 48 hours, and 2\.0% were admitted within seven days of symptom onset\. The median delay to surgery was 20 days, of which about 95% elapsed before reaching the hospital\. Only 34 of 150 patients \(22\.7%\) received antibiotic therapy guided by the antibiogram\. The ISI\-QI was not associated with mortality \(aOR 1\.18 per 10\-point increment; 95% CI: 0\.72–2\.06\) but was associated with unfavorable outcome \(aOR 1\.52; 1\.04–2\.29\), solely because of the early\-surgery indicator \(aOR 3\.72; 1\.31–11\.41\): patients operated on early were more severe \(GCS &lt; 9 in 18\.2% of cases versus 2\.6%\)\. Without this indicator, the association disappeared \(aOR 1\.15; 0\.80–1\.69\)\. After optimism correction, the ISI\-QI added nothing to initial severity for mortality \(C statistic 0\.646 versus 0\.651\), and for functional outcome the apparent gain \(0\.676 to 0\.739\) disappeared without the early\-surgery indicator \(0\.685\)\. Conclusion\. ICS lend themselves to quality measurement from ordinary records\. The failure lies before the hospital and in the microbiological chain, not in the operating room\. The ISI\-QI describes the compliance of an organization; it does not predict the outcome of a patient\. From this we derive a ten\-indicator dashboard, the ISI\-QI\-10\. Level of evidence\. III\. Protocol registration\. None \(secondary analysis of an observational cohort\)\.

## [Institutional fragmentation and rule\-of\-law coordination in the Guangdong\-Hong Kong\-Macao Greater Bay Area: a maritime soft power perspective](../publications/fb3ac2d59cab3d8a74b3.md)

Juanjuan Wan

Introduction International assessments of maritime cities have shifted from hard infrastructure indicators toward institutional quality metrics such as maritime finance and law and attractiveness and competitiveness\. The Guangdong\-Hong Kong\-Macao Greater Bay Area \(GBA\), with its distinctive “one country, two systems, and three jurisdictions” configuration, faces gaps in cross\-jurisdictional rule connectivity that may limit its maritime soft power—a challenge that existing single\-jurisdiction assessment frameworks do not fully capture, highlighting the need for rule\-of\-law coordination\. Methods Using The Leading Maritime Cities of the World assessment framework as a benchmark, this policy and practice review combines a structured review of assessment data with comparative legal analysis to identify the mechanisms through which gaps in cross\-jurisdictional rule connectivity may affect the maritime soft power of GBA cities, as reflected in their international assessment results\. Results GBA cities display a split profile of maritime strengths—strong port performance in the Mainland port cities and comparatively stronger maritime finance and law capacity in Hong Kong—that is consistent with incomplete cross\-jurisdictional complementarity\. Three mechanisms are identified: uncertainty in the application of law, regulatory arbitrage and competition in standards, and the costs of judicial coordination\. In response, three institutional arrangements are proposed: a rule\-of\-law coordination pilot zone, a marine environmental dispute resolution center, and a cross\-border data interoperability mechanism\. Discussion Drawing on cross\-jurisdictional governance practices in the Rhine–Scheldt basin and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the article argues that “rule\-of\-law coordination” merits consideration as a regional indicator in international maritime\-city assessment systems\. The proposed framework addresses a gap in current evaluations of multi\-jurisdictional regions\. The analysis identifies plausible mechanisms consistent with the observed ranking patterns rather than estimating causal effects\.

## [AI Implementation and Business Model Innovation in Chinese SMEs: a Configurational Research Framework](../publications/fb44db6bdabd68610bb9.md)

Depeng Pan

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly regarded as a critical enabler of business model innovation \(BMI\) in small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\)\. However, existing research predominantly examines the net effect of AI adoption on BMI, overlooking the complex interactions among technological, organizational, and environmental conditions\. Drawing on the Technology–Organization–Environment \(TOE\) framework integrated with dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a configurational research framework for investigating how AI implementation combines with organizational capabilities and environmental conditions to drive BMI in Chinese SMEs\. The framework proposes four theoretically grounded pathways to high BMI: technology–organization synergy, environment\-pulled innovation, market\-driven AI integration, and capability\-first substitution\. These propositions demonstrate that AI implementation is neither necessary nor sufficient for BMI; its effectiveness depends on alignment with dynamic capabilities and environmental support\. The framework contributes to the AI–BMI literature by advancing a configurational perspective and offers a foundation for future empirical investigation using fuzzy\-set qualitative comparative analysis \(fsQCA\)\.

La irrupción de la llamada inteligencia artificial \(IA\) no es un mero ajuste de tuercas en el taller del diseñador, sino una reconfiguración ontológica y política de la práctica misma del diseño\. ## [Anestesia regional ecoguiada de última generación y protocolos ERAS en Cirugía Mayor Ambulatoria y oncológica](../publications/fb6e68eee0606c7050b1.md)

Kleber Leonardo Vivar Baque; Saamantha Jazmin Gallardo Armijos; Juan Daniel Fonseca Vaca; Joseph Josué Campoverde López; Daniel Santiago Túa Guerrro

La presente revisión sistemática, realizada conforme a la declaración PRISMA 2020, sintetiza 47 estudios publicados entre enero de 2015 y octubre de 2026 para evaluar la aplicación conjunta de la anestesia regional ecoguiada \(UGRA\) y los protocolos de Recuperación Mejorada Después de Cirugía \(ERAS\) en cirugía mayor ambulatoria y oncológica\. La evidencia indica que la UGRA, como componente central de la analgesia multimodal en ERAS, reduce significativamente las puntuaciones de dolor postoperatorio, el consumo de opioides y la incidencia de náuseas y vómitos postoperatorios \(NVPO\), facilitando la recuperación funcional temprana y el alta segura en pacientes ambulatorios\. En cirugía oncológica, la anestesia y analgesia regional \(AAR\) se asoció con una mejoría de la supervivencia global \(HR 0\.85; IC 95% 0\.80–0\.91\), pero su efecto sobre la recurrencia del cáncer no está establecido\. Los protocolos ERAS en cirugía colorrectal ambulatoria mostraron ser factibles, con estancias hospitalarias de 14 horas a 3\.4 días y tasas de complicaciones del 0% al 35\.7%\. Sin embargo, la certeza de la evidencia está limitada por la heterogeneidad de los estudios, la escasez de ensayos clínicos aleatorizados \(ECA\) y el riesgo de sesgo de publicación\. Se requieren con urgencia estudios de alta calidad en América Latina y otros entornos de recursos limitados\.

## [MotifTrace: multi\-stage attack investigation via automated stage discovery and path reconstruction on provenance graphs](../publications/fb796bff94a08b40eb1e.md)

Chen Chen; Yunchun Li; Zhi Qiao; Fengxu Lin; Mingyuan Xia; Hao Chen; Wei Li

Abstract Multi\-stage cyber attacks spanning extended periods pose significant challenges for security investigation, as analysts must reconstruct the complete attack sequence from voluminous system audit logs\. Existing provenance graph\-based investigation methods either rely on predefined attack knowledge to map activities to known stages, or analyze the graph from alert events using a single set of analysis criteria that fail to adapt to the behaviorally distinct phases of an attack\. Consequently, attack activities that are temporally or causally distant from the triggering alert are often inadequately recovered\. We observe that different attack stages produce distinct distributions of temporal subgraph patterns in provenance graphs, providing a basis for automated stage partitioning without prior attack knowledge\. Based on this observation, we propose MotifTrace , a two\-phase framework that automates multi\-stage attack investigation on provenance graphs without predefined attack knowledge or labeled data\. MotifEmbed learns edge\-level representations that preserve stage\-specific temporal subgraph structures and clusters them into behaviorally coherent stage partitions that support downstream reconstruction\. PathRank then identifies critical attack paths within each stage through topology\-aware causal path scoring, and merges them across stages through shared entities to reconstruct the complete attack scenario\. Evaluations on six attack campaigns of varying complexity, including DARPA Transparent Computing benchmarks, demonstrate that MotifTrace achieves an average Macro\- $$F\_1$$ F 1 of 0\.88 in multi\-stage reconstruction, outperforming state\-of\-the\-art methods by over 21%\. By eliminating the need for manual stage annotation and predefined attack signatures, MotifTrace automates a labor\-intensive phase of the security investigation workflow, reducing analyst effort from provenance graph construction to structured attack summaries\.

## [Haptic properties of polymeric materials: link between human perception and microstructure](../publications/fb815994779039273bd1.md)

Thomas Ules; Dieter Paul Gruber; Davide Tranchida

Abstract Haptic properties, i\.e\. the tactile sensations experienced when touching a material, play a crucial role in product acceptance, user experience, and functional performance across diverse industries\. Polymeric materials dominate applications where haptics matter, from consumer packaging and automotive interiors to medical devices and textiles\. This review discusses the relationship between polymer structure and haptic perception, with the aim of designing materials with targeted tactile properties\. Fields addressed herein are molecular architecture and formulation strategies for precise control over haptic attributes including friction, roughness, compliance, and thermal sensation\. By bridging fundamental polymer science with psychophysical perception, this review offers practical guidance for developing polymeric materials with optimized haptic performance\. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry\.

## [Contextual and structural representation learning for fine\-grained barefoot footprint region recognition](../publications/fb8681d5793f7b3d2952.md)

Yujie Shen; Wenxin Xie; Yabin Zhao; Xuemei Jiang; Jianrong Wang

Barefoot footprints provide valuable biometric evidence for forensic investigation and suspect identification\. However, the rich structural details and diverse scale distributions of footprint images pose significant challenges for accurate fine\-grained region recognition\. Existing methods often struggle to effectively model contextual information and structural characteristics, limiting their ability to characterize subtle morphological variations\. To address these issues, this paper proposes a robust framework for contextual–structural representation learning in barefoot footprint region recognition\. A context\-guided spatial feature reconstruction pyramid network \(CGSFRPN\) is introduced to enhance semantic consistency and feature interactions across different scales\. To improve directional perception and edge detail modeling, a Direction\-Aware Pinwheel Convolution \(DAPConv\) is incorporated to capture structural patterns with diverse orientations\. Furthermore, a ConvFormer module based on the MetaFormer architecture is employed to facilitate efficient semantic representation and cross\-region information integration\. By jointly exploiting contextual information and structural characteristics, the proposed framework achieves robust recognition of fine\-grained footprint regions, including toes, arches, and heels\. Experiments conducted on a proprietary barefoot footprint dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a mean Average Precision \(mAP\) of 83\.2%, outperforming several mainstream object detection approaches and exhibiting superior visualization performance\. These results highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework for fine\-grained barefoot footprint analysis and its potential applications in intelligent forensic identification\.

## [An Integrated Approach to Inventory Management for High\-Rise Building Construction Projects Using SAP Business One: A Study on Optimization of Materials, Tracking, and Cost Efficiency](../publications/fba8630b4d4edbdf157f.md)

Mahesh Shivaji Shinde; Ashok B\. More; Prof\. Ashwini Patil

High\-rise building construction projects involve complex material planning, procurement, storage, and distribution processes that directly influence project cost, schedule, and productivity\. Fragmented, manually updated inventory practices frequently cause material shortages, wastage, and cost overruns\. This study proposes and evaluates an integrated inventory management framework built around SAP Business One \(SAP B1\), an enterprise resource planning \(ERP\) platform, customised for high\-rise residential construction\. A case\-study methodology compares inventory performance before and after SAP B1 implementation across five high\-rise residential projects \(28\-33 storeys\) executed in Pune, India, using key performance indicators \(KPIs\) including inventory accuracy, material availability, wastage, warehouse efficiency, traceability, manual data\-entry errors, user productivity, procurement lead time, stock\-out frequency, and inventory carrying cost\. Post\-implementation results show mean inventory accuracy rising from 74\.0% to 97\.8%, material wastage falling from 8\.6% to 3\.0%, mean procurement lead time reduced from 10\.4 to 6\.4 days, stock\-out incidents reduced from 15\.0 to 3\.4 per month, and inventory carrying cost reduced by an average of 21\-25%\. A supplementary three\-month material\-consumption audit on a 32\-storey casestudy project recorded an estimated direct cost saving of approximately ₹15\.80 lakh\. The findings indicate that a construction\-customised SAP B1 deployment \- integrating procurement, warehouse and bin management, batch/serial tracking, and cost\-centre\-linked material issue \- substantially improves inventory visibility, reduces discrepancies and wastage, and strengthens project cost control\. The study also compares SAP B1 against SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, and SAP Business By Design on implementation time, cost, and feature fit, and offers a practical implementation roadmap and recommendations for construction firms and ERP consultants adopting digital inventory management\.

## [Pharmacological treatment, adversities, and mobile\-based post\-discharge follow\-up of mucormycosis survivors in Central India: strengthening patient care](../publications/fbb2a0687d3808cc1249.md)

Ruchi Baghel; Preeti Acharya; Anshu Verma; Megha Sharma

Introduction Mucormycosis, a significant post\-COVID\-19 complication, is stimulated by uncontrolled diabetes mellitus \(DM\), prolonged corticosteroid exposure, or immunosuppression\. Despite clinical advancements, survivors experience long\-term challenges; however, follow\-up is often missing from treatment strategies, highlighting a critical gap in safeguarding survivors’ long\-term well\-being\. Objective To analyze pharmacological management, adverse events, and post\-discharge outcomes among rhino\-orbital cerebral mucormycosis \(ROCM\) patients using medical records and Mobile\-Based Post\-Discharge \(MBPD\) follow\-up, to inform future clinical and follow\-up practices\. Method Clinical data of confirmed ROCM inpatients \(2021\) at two COVID\-19\-dedicated hospitals in Central India were extracted from medical records and analyzed\. Mucormycosis survivors were followed up in 2023 using the MBPD questionnaire to explore overall treatment, post\-discharge adversities, and outcomes\. The clinical findings and patient\-reported experiences were summarised descriptively\. Factors associated with adversities were examined using multivariable Firth\-penalized logistic regression\. Results Among 108 mucormycosis patients, DM was present in 32% of inpatients\. Liposomal amphotericin B \(71%\) and posaconazole \(75%\) were predominantly prescribed\. Access \(40%\), Watch \(39%\), and Not Recommended antibiotic combinations \(13%\) were most prescribed\. An average of 1\.3 adverse drug reactions were recorded among 73 inpatients\. Of 97 survivors, 36 were non\-responders\. Eighty could be contacted, and 61 \(76%\) consented to participate in MBPD follow\-up\. Fifty\-two of 61 respondents reported 123 post\-discharge adversities, averaging 2\.4 adversities per patient, including 9 \(7%\) deaths confirmed by family members\. Antifungal prescription was significantly associated with adversities \(aOR 5\.82, 95% CI 1\.56−21\.71; p = 0\.009\), whereas older age \(&gt;60 years\) showed a borderline association\. Respondents appreciated the follow\-up calls and emphasized regularizing them\. Conclusion Liposomal amphotericin B, posaconazole, and antibiotics were the most prescribed drugs\. DM was the most common comorbidity, highlighting the need for careful monitoring\. Antifungal prescriptions were significantly associated with adversities, suggesting the need for implementation of a contextual drug\-use policy\. The MBPD follow\-up was well received and may help monitor recovery, identify health needs, and support the care of survivors of chronic diseases in the future\. Survivor\-centred care models are suggested to support post\-discharge recovery and multidimensional challenges\.

## [Dimensional Reduction of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides by Oxide Insertion: Quasi‐1D Oxychalcogenide Semiconductors](../publications/fbb2bebaeab56c96068b.md)

Ayat Tassanov; Azamat Yessengazin; Huiju Lee; Pedro Trinidad; Daniel G\. Chica; Yi Xia; James M\. Hodges

ABSTRACT Heteroanionic solids offer unique levers for tuning structures and properties, but accessing multianion phase space remains challenging due to mismatches in anion reactivity\. Here, we describe a new family of A 2 Hf 3 Q 6 O \(A = K, Rb, Cs; Q = S, Se\) oxychalcogenides, the first reported in the A─Hf─Q─O quaternary space, which are prepared by reacting HfQ 2 with the corresponding alkali carbonate \(A 2 CO 3 \)\. The resulting structures are dimensionally reduced variants of the 1T‐HfQ 2 parent phase, where rows of O atoms insert into the transition metal dichalcogenide \(TMD\) layers\. This yields nanometer‐wide 1D‐\[Hf 3 Q 6 \] ribbons that link into step‐like sheets through distinctive Hf─O─Hf bridges, which connect heteroleptic HfQ 5 O polyhedra at the ribbon edges\. UV/Vis and photoluminescence spectra reveal tunable absorption and emission features spanning 1\.8–2\.6 eV\. Calculated band structures show direct‐gap transitions and highly dispersive bands along the \[Hf 3 Q 6 \] nanoribbons, yielding effective masses more than two orders of magnitude lower than in other crystallographic directions\. Charge‐density plots further illustrate quasi‐1D electronic anisotropy, showing frontier orbitals confined to the nanoribbons due to covalent Hf─Q bonding\. We anticipate heteroanion‐driven dimensional reduction can be used to engineer anisotropy in semiconductors and offers new routes to synthetically challenging multianion systems\.

## [Molecular Interaction Dynamic of Natural Alkaloids From Strychnos sp\. With Murine Double Minute Type 2 \(MDM\-2\) – p53 Protein](../publications/fbc3318a2f740a14a063.md)

Arif Setiawansyah; Muhammad Ikhlas Arsul; Gita Susanti; Reza Alrayan; Ismanurrahman Hadi; Endang Kintamani; Nurul Hidayati; Susianti Susianti

MDM\-2 functions as a negative regulator of the p53 tumor suppressor protein, playing a critical role in cancer development and proliferation\. Reactivation of p53 through MDM\-2 inhibition represents a promising therapeutic strategy for combating cancer progression\. This study investigated the potential inhibitory activity of Strychnos species alkaloids against MDM\-2 and assessed their ADMET profiles using in silico approaches\. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock 4\.2, followed by molecular dynamics simulations in GROMACS to evaluate binding stability\. Computational analyses revealed that Strychnopentamine and Leuconicine A demonstrated superior binding affinity to MDM\-2 compared to the established inhibitor Nutlin\-3\. Both compounds exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic profiles, though Leuconicine A showed predicted hepatotoxicity and mutagenicity risks\. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the stability of the Strychnopentamine\-MDM\-2 complex over 50 nanoseconds, with binding characteristics comparable to Nutlin\-3\. These computational findings identify Strychnopentamine as a promising lead candidate for MDM\-2 inhibition, though experimental validation through in vitro and in vivo studies is required to confirm these predictions and establish therapeutic potential\.

## [In\-Context Learning Before Specialisation: Theory of Learning in a Solvable Topic Model](../publications/fbd0a9791aae060fcde8.md)

Francesco Cagnetta; Casper L\. Christensen

Sequence models can generalise in fundamentally distinct ways: extrapolating structures seen in training, or using their prompt to adapt to novel tasks\. The prevailing strategy determines how the model behaves beyond its training distribution, controlling potential capabilities and risks\. Recent work has characterised many different strategies theoretically, and empirically described the transition between them as the quality and quantity of pretraining data vary\. However, there is no learning theory for this competition, hence no fundamental understanding of \\textit\{why\} one solution might be favoured over another\. Here we provide such a theory in a solvable topic model\-\-\-documents drawn from a finite mixture of latent topics, mirroring the heterogeneity of modern pretraining data\. The dataset comes with two distinct solutions: a specialised predictor, that stores the finite topic mixture, and an in\-context one, optimal for topics never seen during training\. Our theory predicts their emergence at distinct sample complexities: the in\-context predictor is available early, while the specialised one emerges only after the training tokens outnumber the parameters of the data\-generating process\. Trained transformers reproduce both scales and the separating crossover in remarkable agreement with the theory, with no fitted parameters\.

## [Do Investors Follow Their Heart? The Role of Value Congruence in Guiding Investors&\#x27; Decisions](../publications/fbd2708d8e9e2aa93e29.md)

Kristian Roed Nielsen; Meike Janßen; Emma Sjöström; Kristjan Jespersen

ABSTRACT Retail investors evaluating impact‐oriented opportunities must weigh economic, social, and environmental performance simultaneously, yet it remains unclear why they prioritize these dimensions so differently\. We propose that personal values act as a weighting mechanism in multiattribute investment decisions\. In a discrete choice experiment with 547 US retail investors, financial performance and risk dominate on average, but altruistic, biospheric, and egoistic values are each associated with greater weight on the corresponding performance dimension; attribute salience also varies across investment domains\. Personal values thus help explain preference heterogeneity that demographic characteristics and cognitive biases alone leave unaccounted for\.

## [Mechanisms of Change Within a Short Psychological Intervention for Children With Eating Disorders \( SPICE \): A Qualitative Study](../publications/fbd5efbfd25a80fa7f61.md)

Clare Prendergast; Roz Shafran; Emily Davey; Rachel Bryant‐Waugh; Nadia Micali; Julian Baudinet; Layla Colley; Sophie; id\_orcid 0000\-0002\-1076\-7112 Bennett

OBJECTIVE: Increasing numbers of young people \(YP\) are seeking support for eating disorders, creating a growing unmet need for timely and accessible treatment\. While guided self\-help \(GSH\) interventions have demonstrated effectiveness for other youth mental health difficulties, options for eating disorders remain limited\. SPICE \(Short Psychological Intervention for Children with Eating Disorders\), a transdiagnostic CBT\-based GSH program, was developed to address this gap\. This qualitative study explored participant perspectives on the mechanisms through which SPICE may support recovery\. METHOD: SPICE comprises eight weekly modules supported by a 30\-min guided therapy session each week\. Six female adolescents with eating disorders and their parents who completed SPICE participated in semi\-structured post\-intervention interviews\. Data were analyzed using critical realist thematic analysis\. RESULTS: Four key putative mechanisms were identified: \(1\) Interpersonal support \(from the guide and parents\) as a catalyst for change and for keeping momentum going\. \(2\) Increased knowledge of eating disorders and associated cognitive and behavioural factors leading to positive changes\. \(3\) In vivo experiential learning as key to implementing specific strategies and taking ownership over change\. \(4\) Context, that is, individual and systemic factors promoting and inhibiting change\. DISCUSSION: Interpersonal relationships were perceived to promote engagement and change\. Participants reported that psychoeducation empowered them and their families, while experiential learning helped translate strategies into everyday practice\. Flexible and tailored approaches were considered important for improving accessibility and effectiveness\. Perceived barriers included complex module content, remote delivery, and competing commitments\. Findings provide preliminary support for GSH interventions for eating disorders in YP and identify areas for refining future intervention\.

## [Chiral Sulfide‐Catalyzed, Water‐Regulated Enantioselective Tandem Disulfuration‐Initiated Dearomative Spirocyclization/Oxa‐Michael Addition of Alkynes](../publications/fbeb7755d77d6d2a9dbd.md)
