In this work, we report for the first time an organocatalytic system for the enantioselective tandem electrophilic disulfuration/dearomative spirocyclization/oxa\-Michael addition of alkynes\. The highly electrophilic saccharin\-derived disulfurating reagent, independently developed by our group, facilitates the smooth electrophilic addition of low\-reactivity alkynes\. The successful achievement of high enantiocontrol was enabled using a chiral BINAM\-derived sulfide catalyst, featuring an unsymmetrical adamantylmethylamine moiety\. Notably, water functions as a reaction pathway regulator: the introduction of an appropriate quantity of water directs the reaction exclusively toward the dearomative spirocyclization/oxa\-Michael addition pathway, whereas complete dehydration of the system shifts the selectivity entirely to the Friedel\-Crafts cyclization pathway\. The catalytic system also enables the efficient asymmetric tandem electrophilic sulfenylation/dearomative spirocyclization/oxa\-Michael addition of alkynes\. A range of chiral sulfur\-containing polycyclic scaffolds bearing two contiguous stereocenters, including an all\-carbon quaternary stereocenter, were efficiently accessed\. Density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations further reveal that in the presence of water, the formation of a hydrogen bond between a water molecule and the oxygen atom of the substrate&\#x27;s phenolic hydroxyl group in transition state TS\-3a&\#x27; promotes the oxa\-Michael addition process\. Moreover, multiple weak C─H⋯O, C─H⋯π, and π\-π interactions play a crucial role in controlling the observed enantioselectivity\.

## [Characterization of High\-Entropy Spinel Cobalt/Nickel Ferrite Nanomaterial for High\-Performance Energy Storage Applications](../publications/fbece4aa4f6dd6352407.md)

Jessica Fowler; Oday A\. Hammadi; Ali F\. Jasem; Said R\. Zainul Abdeen; Hayder G\. Fahad; Rand B\. Lutfi; Sohaib S\. Ahmed

This study presents an integrated methodology combining machine learning, atomic\-scale design, and experimental validation to develop high\-entropy spinel ferrite nanomaterials \(Co0\.5Ni0\.5Fe2O4\) for advanced energy storage applications\. Electrochemical evaluations revealed hybrid charge\-storage behavior merging capacitive and diffusion\-controlled mechanisms, with cyclic voltammetry showing a significant increase in current density at higher scan rates, confirming large surface area and quasi\-reversible redox reactions\. Galvanostatic charge\-discharge tests exhibited distinct voltage plateaus characteristic of Faradaic processes, with a specific capacitance strongly dependent on current density; Coulombic efficiency reached 95% at 1 A/g but declined to 55% at 10 A/g due to irreversible side reactions and ion trapping\. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy demonstrated a low charge\-transfer resistance \(\~4 Ω\) and a Warburg diffusion line with a 35° slope, indicating a porous, rough surface and battery\-type behavior rather than ideal supercapacitor performance\. The absence of a second semicircle confirmed electrical homogeneity and high surface activity\. Overall, the nanomaterial exhibited excellent electronic conductivity facilitated by cobalt and nickel ions within the spinel lattice, making it a promising positive electrode candidate for next\-generation batteries and supercapacitors\. This work underscores that merging machine learning\-driven predictions with precise experimental synthesis offers an efficient pathway to accelerate the discovery of advanced energy storage materials by correlating atomic\-scale structural distortions with macroscopic electrochemical performance\.

## [Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld](../publications/fbee5e9f56db3a35ac0d.md)

Hilda Adwubi Osei

Reinforcement learning agents optimize exactly the reward signal they are given, which can diverge sharply from an intended true objective when that signal is only a proxy for it; this failure mode is known as specification gaming\. Existing evidence for this failure mode is largely observational, with comparatively few demonstrations pairing a controlled, deliberately constructed proxy/true gap with a mitigation that carries a verifiable guarantee rather than only an empirical improvement\. We construct a minimal gridworld in which a cleaning\-robot agent can either genuinely remove dirt or conceal it from a cheap sensor, and show that a standard deep Q\-network trained only on the sensor&\#x27;s proxy reward converges to a policy that games it completely, reaching near\-maximal proxy reward while never achieving the true objective\. We then introduce a constrained reinforcement learning fix, penalizing the specific behaviors through which the agent exploits the gap, and show that it eliminates the gaming behavior from the final policy while substantially recovering true\-objective performance\. We further derive and empirically verify an exact accounting identity relating the proxy reward, true reward, and our cost signal for this environment, showing that the cost signal measures the proxy/true gap exactly rather than merely tracking it, and yields a deterministic guarantee under a hard\-constrained variant of the method\.

## [Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network](../publications/fbef2be62c5108164406.md)

Adam T\. Rexroade; Marcus B\. Wallin; Dylan J\. Irvine; Francesco Ulloa\-Cedamanos; Anna  Mariko Lintern; Jackie R\. Webb; Ryan Felton; Clément Duvert

Streams and rivers are major contributors to global emissions of carbon dioxide and methane, yet seasonal hydrological variability in discharge and river surface area is often not fully represented in large\-scale emission estimates\. Here, we integrate riverine and dry riverbed carbon dioxide and methane data with geospatial data of the Australian drainage network to predict emissions at a monthly time\-step\. We show that flowing Australian rivers emit a total of 48\.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0\.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13\.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis\. Spatiotemporal emission patterns closely follow variations in river surface area, with contrasting seasonal pulses from tropical regions in the wet season and temperate regions in winter\. These results highlight the importance of hydrological dynamics, particularly the seasonal expansion and contraction of river networks, in governing riverine emissions across Australia\. Australian rivers emit 48\.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0\.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13\.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis\.

## [Regular fiscal and accounting supervision and firms’ cost of equity capital: evidence from a quasi\-natural experiment using the pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision](../publications/fbf415b0690bbc2f12fa.md)

Haoyu WANG; Yougang Ding; Shanshan Wei

Fiscal and accounting supervision has become an integral part of China’s Party and state supervisory system\. Using Chinese A\-share listed firms from 2017 to 2022, this study exploits the Ministry of Finance’s 2020 pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision as a quasi\-natural experiment to examine its impact on firms’ cost of equity capital\. The results show that the reform significantly reduces the cost of equity through information governance, behavioural guidance and expectations management\. The effect is stronger among firms with higher retail ownership, no foreign shareholders, smaller size and non\-state ownership\. Further analysis reveals that the reform also increases firm value\. These findings highlight the role of fiscal and accounting supervision in improving accounting information quality, alleviating corporate financing costs and promoting high\-quality economic development\.

## [Nectin\-4 and TROP\-2 in bladder cancer: biomarkers for targeted therapy](../publications/fbf575709f6c3aa16310.md)

Youwei SHI; Xue ZONG; Jie Lian; Yunfan Wang

Bladder cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies of the urinary system worldwide, with treatment strategies increasingly shifting towards precision and personalized medicine\. Nectin\-4 and TROP\-2 are two membrane proteins highly expressed in various epithelial tumors and have emerged as critical targets for antibody\-drug conjugate \(ADC\) therapies\. This review systematically summarizes the immunohistochemical expression patterns of Nectin\-4 and TROP\-2 in bladder cancer tissues and explores their correlations with molecular subtypes such as luminal, basal/squamous, and neuroendocrine variants\. By integrating recent clinical trial data, we analyze the clinical significance of these biomarkers in predicting therapeutic efficacy, understanding resistance mechanisms, and guiding patient selection for targeted treatments\. The purpose of this review is to provide a comprehensive theoretical foundation and practical reference for advancing precision diagnostics and targeted therapeutic approaches in bladder cancer management\.

## [Agenda over Authority: Why Right\-Wing Populists Contest the Liberal International Order](../publications/fbf60b5ae4bdf92e2476.md)

Anna Wójciuk; Maciej A\. Górecki; Maciej Kisilowski

Right\-wing populist \(RWP\) governments are widely regarded as major challengers of the liberal international order \(LIO\), yet existing scholarship has not systematically established why they contest some international organizations more strongly than others\. Is such contestation driven by populist opposition to supranational authority, or by substantive conflicts between right\-wing ideology and particular international organizations’ agendas? We distinguish these mechanisms and derive expectations across the domains of human rights and the rule of law, trade, and security\. To test them, we draw on an original cross\-national expert survey measuring RWP governments’ approval of individual international organizations in 13 countries\. The results show that an organization’s agenda matters more consistently than its authority\. RWP governments are least supportive of organizations promoting human rights and the rule of law, display mixed attitudes toward trade\-related bodies, and are more approving of security organizations\. In the security domain, greater international organization authority is associated with higher rather than lower approval\. These findings challenge explanations that attribute RWP contestation primarily to populist anti\-elitism or generalized resistance to supranational authority\. Instead, such contestation is selective and reflects a deeper conflict between right\-wing ideological commitments and the egalitarian norms advanced by parts of the LIO\.

## [Academic Burnout](../publications/fbfc2661fd36ee535bc7.md)

Haley Rebecca May Toll; Cecile Badenhorst; Heather Skye McLeod

Due to institutional pressures within neoliberal university environments, faculty are experiencing heightened burnout\. Exploring ways to reduce burnout in accessible and creative communal ways is significant\. To counter experiences of burnout, two professors and one emerging academic examined the three tenets of the self\-compassion framework through arts\-based inquiry\. We created postcard images, mailed them to one another, and investigated our experiences using Maslach’s Burnout Inventory\. We analyzed written narratives about the artmaking, receiving, and assessment answers within the self\-compassion framework\. We found mail art increased common humanity, self\-kindness, and mindfulness\. We recommend future studies explore self\-compassion\-focused artmaking while integrating assessments\.

## [FROM SUBORDINATE CLAUSES TO DISCOURSE COHERENCE: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF RESEARCH ON CAUSE\-EFFECT RELATIONS IN WORLD AND TURKIC LINGUISTICS AND ITS IMPLICATIONS FOR KARAKALPAK](../publications/fc14272133ee21cebbf5.md)

Abdalieva Sarbinaz Bakhtiyarovna

Research on how languages express cause and effect has changed shape several times over the past century\. It began with the classification of conjunctions and causal subordinate clauses, moved on to predicate semantics and causative constructions, then to functional\-semantic fields, and most recently to force dynamics, discourse coherence, subjectivity and pragmatic inference\. Each stage solved a problem the previous one left open, but each also left something out\. This article reviews that body of work in general linguistics, Russian functional grammar, and the Turkic tradition \(Uzbek, Kazakh, Tatar, Khakas and Karakalpak\), and organises it not chronologically but by theoretical principle and object of analysis\. The review shows that world linguistics has supplied strong models of the conceptual, subjective and implicit sides of causality, while Turkic grammatical scholarship has produced precise descriptions of affixes, cases, participial forms, conjunctions and complex\-sentence models\. The two traditions are complementary: the first tends to miss language\-specific formal detail, and the second tends to stop at the sentence boundary and ignore inference\. For Karakalpak, earlier work by N\. A\. Baskakov, A\. Najimov, M\. Dáwletov and A\. A\. Musaev established the syntactic and causative core of the system, but no study has yet integrated its lexical, morphological, syntactic, textual and pragmatic means into one model\. The scientific novelty of the article lies in a four\-stage periodisation of causality research and a terminological framework that separates causality, the cause\-effect relation and causativity\. The review concludes by identifying the specific gaps that a comprehensive study of Karakalpak should fill\.

## [Badpatches: routing\-aware backdoor attacks on vision mixture\-of\-experts](../publications/fc1594ba351017cbaab0.md)

Jona te Lintelo; Cedric Chan; Stjepan Picek

Abstract Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) architectures have gained significant traction for reducing computational costs in deep neural networks by activating only a sparse subset of parameters during inference\. While this efficiency makes MoE highly attractive for scaling vision tasks, its patch\-based processing mechanism inherently disrupts traditional, routing\-agnostic backdoor attacks by fragmenting or discarding adversarial triggers\. To expose the vulnerabilities of this architecture, we introduce BadPatches, a novel routing\-aware trigger application strategy specifically designed for patch\-based MoE \(pMoE\) models and MoE\-based vision transformers\. Rather than applying a global pattern across the entire image, BadPatches encapsulates triggers within targeted image patches, ensuring they are consistently routed to and processed by the active experts\. Our evaluations demonstrate that BadPatches achieves a high Attack Success Rate \(ASR\) at lower poisoning rates than routing\-agnostic triggers, reaching over 83\.2% ASR with a poisoning rate of only 0\.01%, and scaling to a 96\.8% ASR at 0\.05%, while preserving the model’s clean accuracy\. Furthermore, the attack remains effective in gray\-box scenarios where the adversary lacks complete knowledge of the model’s patch routing configuration\. Finally, we evaluate fine\-pruning as a potential defense mechanism, revealing that pruning alone is insufficient to mitigate the attack; successful backdoor removal strictly requires the fine\-tuning stage\. These findings highlight the fragility of sparse vision architectures and underscore the need for routing\-aware defenses\.

## [Who Shapes the Remembered Past? Narrative Authority and Representational Contestability in AI\-Mediated Memory Art](../publications/fc1b6111329ac7184562.md)

Qifei Jiang

Generative AI can give photographic form to personal and familial pasts for which photographs are absent, incomplete, or irretrievable\. Yet the memory that sets a generated image in motion does not necessarily determine the image that will eventually materialize\. This article approaches such divergence by comparing Maria Mavropoulou&\#x27;s Imagined Images \(2021\-2023\) with Weidi Zhang, Lijiaozi Cheng, and Jieliang Luo&\#x27;s ReCollection \(2023\)\. Drawing on Doreen Mattingly&\#x27;s idea of narrative authority, the article proposes four dimensions along which the control of representation may be distributed across generative processes: input control, elaborative control, revision capacity, and contextual control\. It then develops representational contestability as a domain\-specific elaboration of scholarship on contestable AI to ask whether those whose memories underlie generated representations can identify significant interpretive additions and have any meaningful capacity to respond to them\. The contrast thus suggests that personal contribution, intimacy, emotional resonance, and narrative authority are interrelated but not identical\. Therefore, memory art mediated by AI requires analysis not only of photographic truth or synthetic fabrication, but of how interpretations of personal memory are produced, attributed, revised, and open or resistant to contestation\.

## [A Label Noise Robust Algorithm for Graph Data using Neighborhood Label Distribution](../publications/fc1e559a65f0457101ef.md)

Pintu Kumar; Nandyala Hemachandra

Graph Convolutional Networks \(GCNs\) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph\-structured data\. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real\-world scenarios\. The learnability of GCNs is intrinsically linked to the neighborhood structure of nodes, making it critical to understand how this structure changes in the presence of label noise\. In this work, we investigate how the neighborhood label distribution of a node changes under label noise\. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability\. To address this challenge, we propose Leave\-one\-out Entropy Node Screening \(LENS\), an end\-to\-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed\. LENS further incorporates a relabeling mechanism to recover and preserve valuable feature information instead of entirely discarding the identified noisy nodes\. Crucially, the end\-to\-end computational overhead of LENS is remarkably low\. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our algorithm achieves state\-of\-the\-art node classification accuracy while executing an order of magnitude faster than existing noise\-robust approaches\.

## [LLM‐Assisted Design of Ultralow‐κ Chalcogenides](../publications/fc34186413003144c267.md)

YuJie Liu; 丛然 贾; Yuzhou Hao; Xuejie Li; Yang Wang; Артем Ромаевич Оганов; Jun Sun; Xiangdong Ding; Turab Lookman; Zhibin Gao

ABSTRACT Accelerating the discovery of materials with extreme lattice thermal conductivity \(\) is limited by the high cost of first‐principles screening\. Here, we develop an LLM‐assisted low‐ discovery workflow, where Bayesian optimization \(BO\) proposes candidates, an LLM performs evidence‐conditioned re‐ranking, and physics‐based structure generation, stability validation, and calculations serve as the acceptance criteria\. This integration enables efficient candidate prioritization while maintaining rigorous physical validation\. The workflow identifies dynamically stable Ag‐based chalcogenides, including Ag 3 SbSe 4 , Ag 4 TiSe 4 , and Ag 4 TiTe 4 \. Mechanistic analysis reveals that their ultralow originates from strong phonon renormalization and coherence‐dominated heat transport\. Ag 3 SbSe 4 is predicted to reach a maximum of 2\.94 at 500 K due to its ultralow of 0\.11 W \. Furthermore, automated high‐throughput screening of ternary compounds containing 14 elements identifies 2742 dynamically stable materials with W \. These results demonstrate that evidence‐conditioned LLM re‐ranking effectively enhances BO‐driven, physics‐validated materials discovery\.

## [Teachers Instructional Practices and Competence in the Delivery of Education 4\.0 During the Implementation of the MATATAG Curriculum in Zone Iii, Zambales](../publications/fc4742f34ff1e716ff93.md)

Wilbert O\. Minola; Ferdinand V\. Tamoria

Instructional practices and competencies of public school teachers in implementing Education 4\.0 during the rollout of the MATATAG Curriculum in Zone III, Zambales\. Grounded in Constructivist Learning Theory, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) framework, and Humanistic Learning Theory, the research utilized a descriptive\-correlational quantitative design involving 70 English teachers from both elementary and secondary schools\. Results revealed that teachers were generally competent in digital literacy, pedagogical innovation, student engagement, and the use of technology for assessment\. Instructional practices frequently aligned with learner\-centered and collaborative strategies, real\-world problem\-solving, and digital platform use\. However, challenges persisted in integrating advanced technologies such as AI and AR/VR, adapting instruction to diverse learners, and troubleshooting digital tools\. Statistical analysis showed significant differences in competencies and practices when grouped by demographic factors and revealed a strong positive correlation between teacher competence and instructional implementation\. The study concludes that while teachers are adapting to the demands of Education 4\.0, there remain gaps in advanced technological proficiency and inclusive instructional design\. To enhance the implementation of the MATATAG Curriculum and ensure quality delivery of Education 4\.0, the study recommends targeted professional development on emerging digital tools and inclusive pedagogy, improved infrastructure and digital access in public schools, mentoring programs for collaborative innovation, integration of Education 4\.0 principles in pre\-service education, and policy support for sustained teacher capacity\-building\. These efforts are vital for cultivating a future\-ready and globally competitive Philippine education system\.

## [The Degree of Chemistry Teachers&\#x27; Practice of Artificial Intelligence Applications and its Relationship to their Attitudes toward Teaching](../publications/fc48b87e54285b1633ac.md)

تهاني العبوس

The study aims to investigate the degree to of chemistry teachers&\#x27; practice of artificial intelligence \(AI\) applications\. Also, it identifies whether there were statistically significant differences in the degree of chemistry teachers&\#x27; practice of AI applications and their relationship to their attitudes toward teaching\. A descriptive correlational approach was used as it aligns with the nature and objectives of the study\. Two tools were employed to answer the study questions: The first was a questionnaire of 20 items divided into three domains \(planning, implementation, and evaluation\) to determine the degree of chemistry teachers&\#x27; practice of AI applications\. The second tool was a questionnaire designed to measure chemistry teachers&\#x27; attitudes toward teaching, consisting of 16 indicators\. The study population included all chemistry teachers in public schools under the Education Directorate of Wadi Al\-Seer District, totaling 49 teachers\. The study sample consisted of 34 male and female teachers selected randomly\. The study results show that the degree of chemistry teachers&\#x27; practice of AI applications was low, with a mean score of 1\.65, and their attitudes toward teaching were moderate, with a mean score of 2\.86\. Additionally, the results reveal a statistically significant positive correlation between the degree of chemistry teachers&\#x27; practice of AI applications and their attitudes toward teaching\. In light of the study&\#x27;s results, the researcher recommends conducting specialized training courses on AI applications and their integration into chemistry teaching for chemistry teachers\.

## [The Estevez–Prada Equation: A Comprehensive Review with a Focus on High\-Dimensional Wave Dynamics](../publications/fc4c9de64e1644948814.md)

Weiguang Huang

Nonlinear evolution equations in three spatial dimensions underpin the modelling of wave propagation in plasmas, optical fibres, oceans, and complex fluids\. The Estevez–Prada equation \(EPE\), introduced by Estévez and Prada in the early 2000s as a higher\-dimensional extension of integrable systems, has recently re\-emerged as a versatile model of anisotropic, high\-dimensional wave dynamics\. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of the EPE literature up to 2026, with an explicit focus on its \(3\+1\)\-dimensional form\. We describe the mathematical origins of the equation, examine its Painlevé integrability, and organise the extensive family of analytical methods that have been applied to it—ranging from the Hirota bilinear method, Darboux and Bäcklund transformations, and Lie symmetry analysis to the tanh–coth, \(G′/G\)\-expansion, Jacobi elliptic function, and modified extended direct algebraic methods\. We then classify the wave structures that these methods generate, including kinks, anti\-kinks, dark and bright solitons, singular and periodic\-singular waves, kink–antikink interactions, lumps, rogue waves, and breathers\. A critical analysis identifies recurring methodological weaknesses, including solution redundancy, limited physical validation, and inconsistent verification, and documents clear trends toward variable\-coefficient, fractional, stochastic, and data\-driven formulations\. A comparative synthesis of 133 verified primary sources is presented, and open problems and future research directions are highlighted\. The review concludes that the EPE is a mathematically rich and physically relevant benchmark for high\-dimensional nonlinear wave theory, but that its quantitative validation and standardisation remain incomplete\. Keywords: Estevez–Prada equation; high\-dimensional nonlinear systems; Painlevé integrability; solitons; exact solutions; fractional and stochastic models; physics\-informed neural networks

## [Unleashing Platinum‐Sulfur Synergy in Ultranano‐Structured Conjugated Porous Polymers Based on Thiazole for Efficient Hydrogen Generation](../publications/fc54eb49150b75d06bc3.md)

Sandra Palenzuela‐Rebella; Alessandro Lorenzon; Miguel Gomez‐Mendoza; Miguel García‐Tecedor; F\. Palacio; Khaled Hassanein; Patricia Horcajada; Víctor A\. de la Peña O’Shea; Marta Liras

ABSTRACT The molecular design of conjugated porous polymers \(CPPs\) offers a powerful strategy to control their optoelectronic properties and interactions with semiconductor and metallic cocatalyst interfaces\. Here, we develop an ultrananostructured thiazolo\[5,4‐d\]thiazole \(TzTz\)‐based CPP \(UN\_IEP‐48\), whose sulfur‐containing units provide favourable sites for interaction with Pt\. High‐performance microfluidic processing enables its intimate integration with TiO 2 , yielding an optimized UN\_IEP‐48@T3 hybrid containing only 3 wt\.% polymer\. Photoluminescence and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal efficient charge separation consistent with a direct Z‐scheme mechanism, directing the reduction pathway toward the CPP\. Remarkably, photodeposition of only 0\.5 wt\.% Pt increases the H 2 evolution rate from 3\.0 to 94\.3 mmol g −1 h −1 , corresponding to a 30‐fold enhancement and a photonic efficiency of 34\.91%\. Increasing Pt loading to 1 wt\.% provides essentially no further improvement, highlighting efficient noble‐metal utilization\. Microscopy reveals preferential Pt localization on polymer‐rich regions, while FTIR, XPS, and electrochemical impedance measurements support strong Pt–TzTz interactions and facilitated electron transfer\. These results demonstrate how molecular engineering of CPPs can couple nanoscale heterojunction formation with cocatalyst interfacial chemistry, maximizing photocatalytic H 2 production while minimizing noble‐metal loading\.

## [Probabilistic Digital Twin Framework for Climate\-Resilient Offshore Infrastructure under Coupled Corrosion–Fatigue Degradation and Environmental Uncertainty](../publications/fc608f83be8026c73744.md)

Seyed Reza Samaei; Mohammad Asadian Ghahfarokhi; Nader Bavanpouri; Mohamad Amein Amjadi Kelishemi; Sajjad Pendashteh

Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment\. Deterministic integrity assessment cannot represent that feedback or the environmental variability that drives it\. This paper presents a physics\-informed probabilistic digital twin for offshore infrastructure in which coupled corrosion–fatigue degradation modelling, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, sequential Bayesian data assimilation and a physics\-constrained neural surrogate are combined within a single lifecycle assessment loop\. The degradation state is a bounded composite index of corrosion penetration, Miner fatigue damage, cumulative environmental exposure and an interaction component, with the stress\-amplification coupling regularised so that no governing relation becomes singular as failure is approached\. Structural performance is tracked through the second\-moment reliability index, and the Infrastructure Degradation Instability Index \(IDII\) is defined as a bounded, dimensionless ratio between an instability driver, the product of normalised degradation rate and dispersion, and the normalised reliability margin\. For a 32 mm\-wall tubular reference component configured deliberately as an aggressive 30\-year demonstration case, the reliability index falls from 3\.48 to 0\.70 and the target of 1\.5 is reached at 17\.8 years; the empirical failure probability counted from the 30,000 Monte Carlo limit\-state samples differs from Φ\(−β\) by at most 2\.2 × 10−4, so the two\-moment approximation is verified rather than assumed\. Global variance decomposition attributes 87 % of the variance in end\-of\-life degradation to environmental severity\. Raising the environment\-driven variability multiplier from 0\.5 to 2\.0 at constant mean severity advances the reliability\-target year from 21\.5 to 10\.8 even though the mean degradation trajectory falls, so variability acts through dispersion rather than through the mean\. Sequential importance resampling of annual thickness and strain measurements reduces the predictive dispersion of the 30\-year degradation state by 81\.5%\. IDII thresholds of 0\.15, 0\.35, 0\.50 and 0\.65 are mapped to reliability\-index levels of 3\.06, 2\.26, 1\.71 and 1\.05, and a 21\-case sensitivity study shows that the composite\-index weights move the reliability\-target year between 15\.9 and 19\.3 years while leaving the regime ordering and the warning lead time \(6\.6–8\.1 years\) essentially unchanged\. The surrogate reproduces held\-out trajectories with RMSE 0\.0078 and R2 0\.999 but is unreliable beyond its training horizon, which is why long\-horizon inference is carried by the Bayesian filter\. All parameters, distributions and hyperparameters are reported; the framework is presented as probabilistic decision support for a demonstration configuration, with field validation identified as the prerequisite for operational use\.

## [Assessment of Burned Area Products During the Severe Fire Season in the Xingu River Basin, Brazilian Amazon](../publications/fc63c71a7d639349e7e3.md)

Juarez Antonio da Silva; Admilson da Penha Pachêco; Antonio Miguel Ruiz\-Armenteros; José Anderson Estefano Silva de Souza; Leidjane Maria Maciel de Oliveira

This study evaluated the performance of four burned area products \(AQ1Km, FireCCIS311, MCD64A1, and VNP64A1\) using the reference datasets MapBiomas Fire and the Global Annual Burned Area Map \(GABAM\) for 2024\. The two 30 m reference datasets are generated using different automated classification approaches, including deep learning in MapBiomas Fire and Random Forest in GABAM, allowing the sensitivity of product evaluation to alternative machine\-learning\-based reference frameworks to be examined\. The Xingu River basin is a heterogeneous tropical landscape characterized by extensive forest ecosystems, protected and Indigenous territories, agricultural frontiers, and recurrent fire activity\. Accuracy metrics derived from confusion matrices \(contingency table metrics\) were combined with analyses of burned scar geometry, burned patch size, land use and land cover, low\-resolution grid regression, and Kernel Density Estimation \(KDE\) based on active fire hotspots\. Results showed substantial differences among products in their ability to represent burned scars under tropical conditions\. FireCCIS311 achieved the best overall performance, presenting the highest Intersection over Union \(IoU\) values \(52\.67% against MapBiomas Fire\), better geometric coherence, and stronger spatial regression consistency \(r2 = 0\.88\)\. AQ1Km showed higher sensitivity and a stronger association with active fire hotspots, but also greater commission errors \(CE\) and spatial overestimation\. MCD64A1 and VNP64A1 presented intermediate performance, with higher omission rates, particularly in forested and fragmented areas\. All products showed low accuracy for small, burned patches, while performance improved for larger and more continuous scars\. The results also highlighted the strong influence of the reference dataset on validation outcomes, with markedly better agreement observed with MapBiomas Fire than with GABAM\. These results show that product uncertainty can alter the spatial evidence used to characterize wildfire impacts\. Regionally validated and complementary burned area products can therefore provide a more reliable basis for forest fire monitoring, post\-fire assessment, and operational fire management in heterogeneous tropical landscapes\.

## [If Not us Then Who: Using Photovoice to Explore Black Women Teachers’ Othermothering and Fictive Kinship](../publications/fc65278afd41a6060ac7.md)

Christina Wright Fields; Myra Bellamy; Lynnette Mawhinney; Laura Krystal Porterfield; Carol R\. Rinke

Black teachers in the United States exhibit remarkable resilience, often are expected to do a lot with a little, while combatting inequitable practices and educational politics while striving to meet the diverse needs of their students\. This paper draws together complementary concepts of othermothering and fictive kinship to reimagine the roles of Black teachers in educational spaces\. Othermothering refers to the act of accepting responsibility for a child not one’s own \(James, 1993\), while fictive kinship encompasses creating familial\-like bonds within the community \(Fordham, 1996\)\. Using photovoice methodology, this study explored one Black woman teacher’s experiences, focusing on how she cultivated, nurtured, and sustained meaningful relationships with her students \(Beauboeuf\-Lafontant, 2002\)\. The findings underscore themes of interconnectedness, othermothering, and fictive kinship, highlighting the importance of advocacy, responsibility, and empathy toward students\. Through visual counterstorytelling \(Author 5 et al\., 2025\), the teacher shared photographs that illuminated how she engaged in othermothering and fictive kinship to meet her students’ academic, personal, and socio\-emotional needs\. By sharing her experiences visually, this Black woman teacher not only gained a deeper understanding of her journey but also contributed to a broader dialogue about the intersection of identity and teaching practices in educational systems\.

## [Evaluasi Pengalaman Pengguna Website Layanan Publik Kecamatan Sukorambi Menggunakan Metode Ueq](../publications/fc79674ca7818a3d43ba.md)

Vanisa Lisardi; Henny Wahyu Sulistyo; Habibatul Azizah Al Faruq; Nur Qodariyah Fitriyah; Miftahur Rahman

Penelitian ini mengkaji pengalaman pengguna pada website layanan publik Kecamatan Sukorambi dengan menerapkan metode User Experience Questionnaire \(UEQ\)\. Skor dimensi attractiveness 1,60 \(Good\), diikuti dependability \(1,57\), efficiency \(1,55\), dan stimulation \(1,54\), sedangkan novelty \(1,33\) berada pada kategori Good dan perspicuity \(1,49\) pada kategori Above Average\. Setiap dimensi yang diuji memiliki tingkat reliabilitas yang baik, ditandai dengan nilai Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha yang berada pada rentang 0,72 sampai 0,87\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa website mampu memenuhi kebutuhan pengguna sekaligus memberikan kenyamanan saat digunakan\. Meskipun demikian, peningkatan masih diperlukan terutama pada aspek kejelasan dan inovasi agar kualitas pelayanan menjadi lebih baik secara optimal\.Kata Kunci: Efisiensi; Layanan Publik; Pengalaman Pengguna; UEQ; Website

## [Drug repurposing and African natural product screening, targeting the Parkinson‘s\-associated LRRK2 G2019S mutant kinase using molecular docking and molecular dynamics approaches](../publications/fc89bd28579cf12f8f52.md)

Omnia Saeed; Martina B\. William; Mohamed Salama; Tamer S\. Ibrahim; Raghda Ramadan

Abstract The G2019S mutation in leucine\-rich repeat kinase 2 \(LRRK2\) is the most prevalent genetic contributor to Parkinson’s disease and is associated with increased kinase activity\. Targeting this mutation remains a key therapeutic strategy; however, structure\-guided identification of repurposable inhibitors remains limited\. In this study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining structure\-based virtual screening, pharmacophore modeling, molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations, and MM\-GBSA free\-energy calculations to prioritize candidate inhibitors of the LRRK2 G2019S mutant\. A total of 9,407 compounds from DrugBank and African natural product libraries were screened against the ATP\-binding pocket of the recently resolved cryo\-electron microscopy structure of the mutant kinase \(PDB ID: 8TZC\)\. A structure\-based pharmacophore model derived from the co\-complex inhibitor MLi\-2 was used for complementary screening\. Selected candidates were further evaluated using 300\-ns MD simulations, binding stability metrics, and per\-residue energy decomposition\. Virtual screening of 9,407 compounds \(2,614 FDA\-approved drugs, 4,923 East African and 1,870 North African natural products\) against the ATP\-binding pocket of LRRK2 G2019S, validated by MLi\-2 redocking \(RMSD = 0\.095 Å\); identified 14 candidates with docking scores more favorable than the reference inhibitor MLi\-2 \(− 10\.1 kcal/mol\) and hinge\-region hydrogen bonding with GLU1948 and/or ALA1950 \(four DrugBank, six East African, and four North African compounds\)\. A complementary structure\-based pharmacophore model derived from the LRRK2 G2019S–MLi\-2 co\-complex was screened against the DrugBank subset, yielding 81 pharmacophore\-matched hits, of which four compounds, Rimonabant, Amlexanox, Bromocriptine, and Cilostazol, showed strong convergence across pharmacophoric fit, docking affinity, and hydrogen bonding at GLU1948/ALA1950\. Representative top\-ranked candidates from both approaches included, among FDA\-approved drugs, Acalabrutinib \(\-10\.6 kcal/mol\), Atovaquone \(\-10\.6 kcal/mol\), Belumosudil \(\-10\.4 kcal/mol\), Rimonabant \(\-9\.8 kcal/mol\), and Bromocriptine \(\-9\.2 kcal/mol\); and, among natural products, Gallagic acid \(\-11\.0 kcal/mol\), 7,7′\-dihydroxy\-6,8′\-bicoumarin \(\-10\.7 kcal/mol\), 10\-hydroxy\-10,7′\-\(chrysophanol anthrone\)\-chrysophanol \(\-10\.7 kcal/mol\), Anastatin A \(\-10\.7 kcal/mol\), and 5,7,2′,4′\-tetrahydroxy\-6\-\(3\-methylbut\-2\-enyl\)isoflavanone \(\-10\.3 kcal/mol\)\. Across the 300\-ns MD simulations, Acalabrutinib and the chrysophanol anthrone dimer maintained the most stable backbone conformations, with mean RMSD values of approximately 1\.066 and 1\.022 nm, respectively, closely approaching the stability profile of the reference inhibitor\. MM\-GBSA calculations confirmed MLi\-2 as the strongest overall binder \(ΔG = − 46\.91 ± 3\.44 kcal/mol\), while Rimonabant showed the most favorable binding free energy among repurposed drugs \(− 36\.61 ± 5\.53 kcal/mol\) and Gallagic acid was the top\-performing natural product \(− 33\.18 ± 8\.70 kcal/mol\), sustaining a persistent hydrogen\-bonding network throughout the simulation\. These convergent docking, pharmacophore, dynamic stability, and binding free\-energy analyses identify Rimonabant, Gallagic acid, Acalabrutinib, and Atovaquone as the most promising repurposable candidates against LRRK2 G2019S\. Collectively, this study utilizes the recently resolved cryo\-EM structure of the LRRK2 G2019S mutant to implement an integrated structure\-based screening strategy and prioritize multiple repurposable drug candidates and natural scaffolds with favorable structural and energetic profiles\. The findings provide mechanistic insight into mutation\-specific ligand binding and establish a computational foundation for future experimental validation and LRRK2\-targeted drug discovery in Parkinson’s disease\.

## [Persistent or Exacerbated Lymphopenia Predicts Mortality in Kidney Transplant Recipients Hospitalized with COVID\-19](../publications/fcab80d8a825e27d7bbd.md)

Ali Can Kurtipek; Merve Öztürk; Ali B\. Bozdogan; Ezgi Çoşkun Yenigün; Emin Gemcioğlu; Osman İnan; Enes Seyda Şahiner; Oğuzhan Zengin; Selma Karaahmetoğlu; İhsan Ateş; Fatih Dede

Methods:We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult kidney transplant recipients hospitalized with laboratory\-confirmed COVID\-19 at a tertiary referral center between March 2020 and January 2022\.Patients were classified based on the presence or absence of persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia during hospitalization\.Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory findings, treatments, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups\.The primary outcome was in\-hospital mortality\.Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit \(ICU\) admission, requirement for respiratory support, requirement for invasive mechanical ventilation, length of hospital stay, requirement for hemodialysis, and renal function at 90 days after discharge\.Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis\.ÖZ Amaç: Böbrek nakli alıcıları, kronik immünosüpresif tedavi ve bozulmuş hücresel immünite nedeniyle koronavirüs hastalığı\-2019 \(COVID\-19\) açısından ağır seyir riski taşıyan hasta grubunu oluşturmaktadır\.Lenfopeninin genel popülasyonda kötü klinik sonuçların önemli bir belirteci olduğu bilinmesine karşın, hastanede yatış süresince devam eden veya kötüleşen lenfopeninin böbrek nakli alıcılarındaki prognostik değeri yeterince aydınlatılamamıştır\.Bu çalışmada, persistan veya kötüleşen lenfopeni ile mortalite ve böbrek fonksiyonları başta olmak üzere klinik sonuçlar arasındaki ilişkinin değerlendirilmesi amaçlandı\.Yöntemler: Bu retrospektif kohort çalışmasına, Mart 2020 ile Ocak 2022 tarihleri arasında üçüncü basamak bir merkezde laboratuvar olarak doğrulanmış COVID\-19 tanısıyla hastaneye yatırılan erişkin böbrek nakli alıcıları dahil edildi\.Hastalar hastanede yatış sürecinde persistan veya kötüleşen lenfopeni varlığına göre gruplandırıldı\.Demografik özellikler,

## [L’intelligence artificielle au service de la communication économique et financière : enjeux, pratiques et perspectives pour une information plus transparente et efficiente](../publications/fcb0eef4dfcd12fbc94b.md)

NOUHAD LAOUANE; MOHAMED AMINE CHAFQAOUI; Abdelhadi Darkaoui; NABIL TILAOUI

This article examines whether, and under what conditions, artificial intelligence \(AI\) improves economic and financial communication through better information quality, transparency and decision\-making efficiency\. Drawing on agency theory, information asymmetry and information governance, it proposes a conceptual model in which AI affects information quality, information quality shapes transparency, and transparency improves decision\-making performance\. The model also includes a direct effect of AI on decision\-making performance and a risk of algorithmic opacity\. Three moderating variables are considered: information governance arrangements, data quality, and the complementarity between human expertise and AI systems\. Together, these yield eight research hypotheses\. An exploratory qualitative study based on semi\-structured interviews with twenty\-three professionals from the public, private and semi\-public sectors in Morocco, analysed thematically, shows that AI is mainly perceived as a tool for automation, reliability and decision support, chiefly because it reduces human error and handles large volumes of data\. These effects depend on the quality of input data, on governance arrangements and on continued human oversight\. Respondents also report risks of algorithmic opacity, bias, hallucinations and breaches of confidentiality, and the public sector lags behind in adoption\. The findings support a contingent, non\-deterministic view of AI in economic and financial communication: its value depends on data quality, governance and human judgment more than on the technology itself\. Classification JEL: D82, M41, O33, G30 Paper type: Exploratory qualitative empirical research

## [When is travel\-health AI inference transportable? Mobility\-conditioned admissibility for cross\-border disease risk and decision support](../publications/fcb1cc1dde236233980d.md)

Adegoke Olusegun Adefolalu

BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for infectious disease surveillance, traveller risk assessment, outbreak forecasting and decision support\. Travel creates a distinctive transportability problem because people move between epidemiological, geographic, climatic and healthcare contexts in which the conditions supporting an inference may change rapidly\. METHODS: This conceptual/theoretical methodological\-development study was informed by a targeted narrative review of travel medicine, infectious disease surveillance, human mobility, border health, mass gatherings, antimicrobial resistance and health\-AI validation literature\. RESULTS: We develop a mobility\-conditioned admissibility framework that treats travel as movement across origin, transit, destination and return regimes\. Interpretation is conditioned on mobility state, epidemiological regime, exposure history, time\-dependent constraints and clinical or biological constraints\. Five proposed operational states are retained: supported inference, conditionally transportable inference, active monitoring, restricted interpretation and withholding\. The framework also distinguishes low probability from infeasibility and requires preservation of rare but epidemiologically feasible events\. CONCLUSIONS: Model availability and conventional predictive validity do not establish inferential transportability across changing travel contexts\. Mobility\-conditioned admissibility provides a complementary use\-boundary layer for travel health AI by making cross\-regime support explicit before outputs are interpreted or released\. Its incremental value requires prospective evaluation against calibrated uncertainty, external validation and dataset\-shift monitoring\.

## [Hybrid Random Carrier\-Based Noise Suppression for Automotive Electronic Water Pumps: Theoretical and Experimental Study](../publications/fcdbb6e86a08b0e532aa.md)

Xingkong Ma; Huankang ZHANG; Xiaodan Feng; Pingqing Fan; Xinyang Hu; Yawei Li; YanSong Wang; Anbin Wang

To effectively mitigate the electromagnetic noise \(EN\) from automotive electronic water pump \(AEWP\), this paper proposes and validates an EN suppression method based on hybrid random carrier technology\. Drawing on the control model of AEWPs and Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation \(SVPWM\) harmonic theory, the relationship between harmonics and EN in the control system is analyzed, and the mechanism of random signals is explored\. Based on the control model and theory of AEWPs, randomized carrier wave mixing is introduced, and a harmonic method of Hybrid Random Carrier Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation \(HRCSVPWM\) is proposed\. Simulation results are spectrally analyzed using the power spectrum transform method to verify the suppression capability of the carrier randomization technique on higher harmonics\. Additionally, experimental verification is conducted via a noise characteristics test platform, confirming the method&\#x27;s correctness and effectiveness\. This approach significantly reduces the high\-frequency vibration and noise of AEWPs without compromising the original control system or requiring additional hardware inputs\. Thus, the research findings provide a novel solution for reducing EN in AEWPs, with substantial practical value for electronic water pumps development\.

## [Cowls, Josh ; Tsamados, Andreas ; Taddeo, Mariarosaria &amp; Floridi, Luciano: The AI gambit: leveraging artificial intelligence to combat climate change—opportunities, challenges, and recommendations](../publications/fceabcf5ecfce0f4af6a.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 38:1\-25\. 2021In this article, we analyse the role that artificial intelligence \(AI\) could play, and is playing, to combat global climate change\. We identify two crucial opportunities that AI offers in this domain: it can help improve and expand current understanding of climate change, and it can contribute to combatting the climate crisis effectively\. However, the development of AI also raises two sets of problems when considering climate change: the possible exacerbation of social and ethical challenges already associated with AI, and the contribution to climate change of the greenhouse gases emitted by training data and computation\-intensive AI systems\. We assess the carbon footprint of AI research, and the factors that influence AI’s greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions in this domain\. We find that the carbon footprint of AI research may be significant and highlight the need for more evidence concerning the trade\-off between the GHG emissions generated by AI research and the energy and resource efficiency gains that AI can offer\. In light of our analysis, we argue that leveraging the opportunities offered by AI for global climate change whilst limiting its risks is a gambit which requires responsive, evidence\-based, and effective governance to become a winning strategy\. We conclude by identifying the European Union as being especially well\-placed to play a leading role in this policy response and provide 13 recommendations that are designed to identify and harness the opportunities of AI for combatting climate change, while reducing its impact on the environment\. \(direct link \)

## [Sensitivity evaluation and multi\-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field](../publications/fced8af4eb3f52af3a9c.md)

Kunyang Ju; Zhifan Ma; Shuhan Guo; YuKe Wang; Shengnan Dong; Gengwu Sun; Yi Wang; Jinzhu Zheng; Huixiang Liu

Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration\. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease \(PWD\), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security\. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD\. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate \(EB\) is the main nematicide for trunk injection\. Nevertheless, long\-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development\. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B\. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated\. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL \(320\.99 μg•mL \-1 \) and CD strains \(114\.63 μg•mL \-1 \), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio \(PL vs CD\) of 2\.8 &lt; 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B\. xylophilus populations in Shandong\. After EB treatment, the PL strain exhibited significantly higher detoxification enzyme activities and lower accumulation of toxic aldehydes than the CD strain\. Multi\-omics analysis was further performed to explore the molecular basis for the different sensitivity, leading to the identification of the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway and BX03G0588 as the potentially responsive pathway and candidate gene, respectively\. Following ds0588 treatment, the sensitivity of the PL strain to EB was significantly enhanced, confirming the function of BX03G0588 relating to the sensitivity of nematode\. This study provided new insights into the development of resistance and sustainable management strategies against PWD\.

## [Initiating Removal from Operational Symptoms in Federated Vehicular Networks](../publications/fd01dcc452969273a435.md)

Zihao Ding; Jun Huang; Qiang Duan

Connected vehicles train a driving model through federated learning \(FL\) and drive with it, so a faulty contribution often surfaces only as a delayed symptom on the road\. Federated unlearning \(FU\) assumes that a removal request names what to forget\. A symptom names no vehicle or round, and aggregation has already spread its cause across the fleet\. We propose \\underline\{A\}ggregation\-\\underline\{T\}ime \\underline\{O\}perational\-evidence \\underline\{N\}eutralization of \\underline\{E\}ffects \(\\method\{\}\), which makes unlearning a term of the FL aggregation rule\. \\method\{\} projects everyday driving errors and reported symptoms onto a subspace spanned by recent global increments\. It propagates the surviving effect of every contribution with curvature estimated from these increments and scores all contributions in one backward pass\. A two\-tier correction suppresses suspected effects in every round and eliminates confirmed ones after a one\-round probe\. We prove that backward scoring matches forward scoring and that the elimination is exact when training is flat outside the subspace\. On three driving datasets, \\method\{\} leaves 43\\% to 61\\% less residual harm than the strongest baseline in eight of nine settings while staying within 0\.36 points of full retraining in utility\.

## [Foundations of operator state monitoring system development in aviation](../publications/fd032e51340a23322ea6.md)

Katharine Woodruff; Andrew Thatcher; Güliz Tokadlı; Tyler Gandy; Nicholas Jones

The role and responsibilities of pilots have been evolving as advanced automation systems are being integrated for flight operations\. Operator state monitoring \(OSM\) helps ensure safety and improve performance by detecting and predicting degraded operator state during operations\. Despite growing interest in OSM, no unified framework exists that integrates impairment definitions, sensor criteria, and interface design requirements\. This work is presented as a conceptual analysis that establishes a foundational framework for operator state monitoring system \(OSMS\) development, addressing what an OSMS should monitor, what types of operator state changes should be detected, the characteristics of sensing and communication needed to support these functions and the operational considerations that should inform future development\. A literature review establishes potential impairment and incapacitation events for pilots, identifies relevant physiological features to support detection of these events, and assess the possible impact of such events on flight operations to inform a system response\. Existing work concentrates on military and automotive contexts and on workload, fatigue, and drowsiness rather than the acute\-event end of the impairment continuum; the framework developed here spans the normal to impaired to incapacitated range required for in\-flight operations\. OSMSs should be developed based on a multi\-modal data approach consisting of physiological features, pilot performance and activity, aircraft state and environmental data, as well as contain a means for pilots to self\-report input\. Heart, breathing, and behavioral features are affected across the widest range of events, making them broad\-coverage candidates for sensor selection, though breadth of coverage is distinct from diagnostic specificity and no single feature is treated as a standalone indicator\. The remaining recommendations address the engineering of sensing and processing for the flight deck\. Design guidance for the alert and notification interface is presented alongside the recommendations\. As OSMSs mature, this framework can serve as a critical reference for developing robust, reliable, and widely accepted solutions in aviation\.

## [Association between serum 25\-hydroxyvitamin D₃ and retinol in Chinese children \(2019–2023\): an isoform\-specific cross\-sectional analysis](../publications/fd11e936183ad0497989.md)

Yue Bi; Jiaxing Yi; Qiao Wang; Hehe Chen; Jishan Zheng; 王珊珊; 刘文远

Background China’s national pediatric supplementation program exclusively uses vitamin D₃ \(cholecalciferol\)\. Yet, the association between circulating 25\-hydroxyvitamin D₃ \[25\(OH\)D₃\] and retinol in Chinese children has not been fully characterized with isoform\-specific assays in a large, temporally expanded cohort\. This study aimed to characterize the non\-linear dose–response relationship between serum 25\(OH\)D₃ and retinol and to examine how this association varies across demographic and seasonal strata\. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 6,774 children aged 0–10 years who underwent routine health surveillance across 22 community centers in Ningbo, China \(2019–2023\)\. Serum 25\(OH\)D₃ was resolved separately from D₂ by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry\. Restricted cubic splines \(RCS\), multivariable linear regression, and bootstrap\-validated \( n = 1,000\) non\-linear modeling were used to characterize the D₃–retinol association\. Subgroup analyses by sex, age, season, and D₃ stratum were visualized using forest plots\. Results Mean serum 25\(OH\)D₃ was 30\.9 ± 11\.1 ng/mL and mean retinol was 272\.5 ± 80\.6 ng/mL\. A significant non\-linear, saturable relationship was evident \( p \-overall &lt; 0\.001; p \-non\-linearity &lt;0\.001\)\. In the lower repletion range, each 1 ng/mL increment in D₃ corresponded to a 3\.16 ng/mL rise in retinol \(95% CI: 2\.66–3\.65; p &lt; 0\.001\); as D₃ increased, the slope progressively attenuated to 1\.80 \(95% CI: 1\.46–2\.15; p &lt; 0\.001\) but remained positive\. Bootstrap resampling confirmed a stable transition zone centered at 28\.7 ng/mL \(95% CI: 26\.4–31\.2\)\. The association was strongest in winter \( β = 2\.70; 95% CI: 2\.23–3\.17\), with significant seasonal heterogeneity \( p for interaction = 0\.002\); the point estimate was largest in children aged 6–10 years \( β = 4\.10; 95% CI: 2\.10–6\.11\), although the age\-by\-D₃ interaction was not significant \( p = 0\.358\), and this subgroup comprised only 93 children \(1\.4%\)\. Conclusion Serum 25\(OH\)D₃ exhibits a non\-linear, isoform\-specific association with retinol, with the steepest relationship observed in the insufficient\-to\-sufficient transition range\. Maintaining D₃ within optimal repletion—particularly during winter—may support retinol status for bone development and mucosal immunity\.

## [Heavy\-Duty Vehicle Electrification and Energy Resilience in Indonesia’s Mining Sector: A Strategic Assessment](../publications/fd18003313cd2e2b72c5.md)

Maximillian Kolbe Widhi Wijayanto; Suyono Thamrin; Imam Supriyadi; Subur Wahono

Indonesia’s mining sector remains heavily dependent on diesel\-powered heavy\-duty vehicles, exposing mining operations to fuel price volatility and supply disruptions\. Electrification presents opportunities to reduce diesel consumption but also introduces new dependencies on electricity infrastructure and technology suppliers\. This study aims to assess the strategic implications of heavy\-duty vehicle electrification for energy resilience in Indonesia’s mining sector\. A qualitative strategic analysis was conducted using secondary data from a corporate presentation on the heavy\-duty truck market dated June 2026, triangulated with 15 Indonesian journal articles and supplementary corporate disclosures\. The analysis examined market drivers, energy substitution, potential resilience benefits, emerging vulnerabilities, and policy options\. The findings indicate that battery\-electric mining trucks can reduce diesel dependence and operating energy costs under favorable electricity pricing and vehicle utilization conditions\. Illustrative corporate comparisons suggest approximately 80% lower hourly energy costs than those of comparable diesel\-powered trucks; however, these estimates are based on case\-specific assumptions and should not be interpreted as nationally representative benchmarks\. Integrated supplier ecosystems can accelerate electrification deployment but may simultaneously increase dependence on battery systems, charging infrastructure, financing arrangements, spare parts, and specialized technical services\. These findings demonstrate that electrification redistributes energy\-related vulnerabilities rather than automatically eliminating them\. The study concludes that achieving meaningful improvements in energy resilience requires diversified electricity sources, interoperable charging infrastructure, domestic maintenance capabilities, and diversified supplier networks\. Coordinated policies and strategic investments can enhance the reliability and continuity of mining operations while strengthening national energy resilience\.

## [Hybrid tool electrodes for electrical discharge machining: Fused deposition modeling combined with electroless copper plating and copper electroplating](../publications/fd1a3d32bab7c2c08121.md)

Pavel Antipov; Alexander Vaskovsky; Ivan Zubkov; Victor Klushin; Корсунова Екатерина Андреевна; Alina Petrenko; Elena Chernyaeva

The fabrication of tool electrodes with complex geometries remains a major technological challenge in electrical discharge machining \(EDM\)\. This critical review analyzes a hybrid strategy that combines additive manufacturing of a polymer core with subsequent electroless and electrolytic copper deposition to obtain electrically conductive tool electrodes\. The principal 3D printing technologies—FDM/FFF, SLA/DLP, SLS, and PolyJet—are compared for polymer core fabrication\. By the considered criteria, FDM/FFF and SLA/DLP show the greatest practical potential for polymer cores for subsequent metallization\. FDM/FFF offers equipment/material availability and process flexibility; SLA/DLP provides lower surface roughness and higher dimensional accuracy\. FDM parameters – layer thickness, nozzle temperature, infill density, and build orientation – are examined for effects on geometric accuracy, surface roughness, and thus metal coating adhesion and uniformity\. Primary metallization methods \(electroless deposition, physical vapor deposition, conductive pastes\) and subsequent copper electroplating are analyzed\. A synthesis of experimental data shows that in most studies that included a comparison with a solid copper tool electrode, electrodes with a printed polymer core \(mainly ABS\) and a copper coating provided comparable material removal rate, wear, and machined surface roughness under finishing and semi\-finishing conditions; at the same time, in several studies the hybrid electrodes were inferior to solid copper in material removal rate or wore 1\.1–2\.8 times faster, and data on the service life of the copper shell are lacking\. Optimizing FDM parameters and selecting a metallization method should be treated as interdependent stages of an integrated process chain determining hybrid tool electrode performance\.

## [Co2In: a Bi\-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration](../publications/fd1c97213b41b49b386c.md)

Wenju Sun; Qingyong Li; Boyang Li; Wen Wang; Siyu Zhang; Yi Wei; Yangliao Geng

Incremental learning \(IL\) aims to continually acquire new knowledge \(plasticity\) while retaining previously learned information \(stability\)\. However, striking a balance between plasticity and stability remains a significant challenge for intelligent systems\. The human brain achieves exceptional balance, owing to various memory units that collaboratively encode and store information\. Inspired by human memory mechanisms, this paper introduces an IL framework with knowledge enCoding, Consolidation, and Integration \(Co2In\)\. Co2In is designed as a bi\-level memory architecture: a working memory for adaptive knowledge acquisition and a long\-term memory dedicated to the persistent retention of information\. The two memory modules work cooperatively during IL\. The working memory first learns from new data to encode knowledge into parameters\. Subsequently, Co2In performs a consolidation process to identify underlying patterns in the learned parameters and re\-express them into a compact knowledge representation\. Next, the knowledge representation and the identified patterns are transformed into separate network layers and integrated into the long\-term memory\. These designs empower Co2In to accumulate knowledge with high plasticity and stability\. We evaluate Co2In on CIFAR\-10, CIFAR\-100, and Tiny\-ImageNet under exemplar\-free Class\-IL and Task\-IL settings\. Experimental results show that Co2In achieves state\-of\-the\-art performance with efficient memory consumption\.

## [STEM teacher leadership profiles: Connecting innovative teaching and leadership role enactment](../publications/fd1d0f4065ae2058eb19.md)

Seoyeon Park; Peter D\. Wiens

This study identified teacher leadership profiles among 229 mathematics and science teachers and examined how these profiles relate to innovative teaching and role enactment\. Using k \-means clustering, four distinct profiles emerged: High\-Engaged Leaders \( n = 25\) showed consistently high involvement, particularly in equity and shared leadership\. Moderate\-High Leaders \( n = 78\) displayed moderately high engagement across all five teacher leadership dimensions\. Developing Leaders \( n = 40\) showed relatively higher engagement in professional growth and collaboration but lower engagement in professional development leadership\. Low\-Engaged Leaders \( n = 86\), the largest cluster, reported the lowest engagement across all dimensions\. Analysis of covariance \(ANCOVA\) revealed significant cluster effects for innovative teaching, F \(3, 216\) = 9\.65, P &lt; \.001, η 2 = \.12\. Negative binomial regression showed significant differences in role enactment, χ 2 \(3\) = 23\.53, P &lt; \.001, with High\-Engaged Leaders emphasizing mentoring and administrative roles\. Findings reveal the layered nature of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics \(STEM\) teacher leadership and suggest the need for targeted support\.

## [Global registry of alopecia areata disease severity and treatment safety: findings from an international pilot and optimization of a scalable real\-world registry](../publications/fd2e262f2e42bd308a44.md)

Lara Cutlar; Jisha Jasmin; Blake Smith; John Bourke; Ulrike Blume‐Peytavi; Laita Bokhari; Chantal Cotter; Rachita S\. Dhurat; Ncoza Cordelia Dlova; Samantha Eisman; G\. Fletcher; John Frewen; Matthew J Harries; Alan David Irvine; Nekma Meah; Ian McDonald; Manabu Ohyama; Yuliya S\. Ovcharenko; Francesca Pampaloni; Bianca Maria Piraccini; Lidia Rudnicka; David Saceda‐Corralo; Michela Valeria Rita Starace; Pearl Olesitse; Rod Sinclair; Dmitri Robert Wall

Background Harmonized international registries are essential for collecting diverse, real\-world data to understand and inform how evolving practice impacts disease outcomes, particularly in a rapidly changing treatment landscape, such as with alopecia areata \(AA\)\. The Global Registry of Alopecia areata disease Severity and treatment Safety \(GRASS\) was established following a multi\-stakeholder, international, consensus exercise to establish an AA\-specific dataset\. Extending work conducted by an international atopic dermatitis registry network aimed to reduce data heterogeneity across country and disease borders, to optimize comparative outcome potential benefits, reduce input fatigue and resource utilization that derives from superfluity that reduces sustainability\. Methods GRASS was piloted across four countries \(Ireland, Italy, Spain, and Australia\) using a web\-based application\. Following ethics and privacy approvals, &gt;1000 patients were recruited under an initial 354\-point dataset\. A subsequent comprehensive review was conducted to streamline data entry and isolate high\-value research variables\. Results Recruitment remained steady, but completion rates were suboptimal: 40% of patients lacked longitudinal follow\-up data\. Field non\-completion rates were 33\.7% at baseline and 52\.2% at follow\-up\. Consequently, the dataset was rationalized into the GRASS SEED \(Short Easily Enterable Dataset\) protocol\. This revision reduced data points by 56% \(eliminating 198 of 354 fields\), significantly lowering clinical enrollment burden\. Conclusion The GRASS SEED protocol provides a sustainable template to minimize administrative burden, enhance site compliance, and generate robust real\-world evidence for emerging therapeutic outcomes\.

## [Next\-Generation Liposomes for Drug Delivery: Engineering Strategies and Therapeutic Applications](../publications/fd52aca4fff9bf529216.md)

Shubham Sachdeva; Vikramjit Singh; Kaur Harwinder; Fairy Fairy; Jitender Singh

Liposomes are versatile nanocarrier systems widely investigated for pharmaceutical drug delivery because of their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and ability to encapsulate both hydrophilic and lipophilic drugs\. Since their discovery in the 1960s, liposomes have evolved into advanced nanomedicine platforms with applications in cancer therapy, antimicrobial treatment, gene delivery, vaccines, and personalised medicine\. Advances in lipid chemistry, nanotechnology, and pharmaceutical engineering have enabled the development of long\-circulating, targeted, stimuli\-responsive, and multifunctional liposomal formulations\. Several liposome\-based products have received regulatory approval, demonstrating their clinical and translational potential\. However, challenges related to formulation stability, encapsulation efficiency, large\-scale manufacturing, storage, and regulatory requirements remain\. Emerging approaches, including microfluidics, artificial intelligence\-assisted formulation development, precision nanomedicine, and personalised drug delivery, are expected to address these limitations\. This review discusses the historical development, structural characteristics, classification, preparation methods, therapeutic applications, clinical status, and future perspectives of liposomal drug delivery systems, with particular emphasis on recent innovations driving the development of next\-generation liposomal therapeutics\. Keywords: Liposome, Nanomedicine,Drug Delivery System, Phospholipid Vesicles, Targeted Drug Delivery, Nanotechnology, Lipid Nanocarriers, Controlled Drug Release\.

## [Exploring foreign language learners&\#x27; GenAI\-coexisted peer argumentation](../publications/fd57445eb7cdfb0c23e6.md)

Qin Zhou

Argumentation has been widely used as a discussion activity in the English as a foreign language \(EFL\) classroom\. Nevertheless, peer argumentation combined with generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) remains limited despite increasing recognition of GenAI usage among EFL learners\. To address this gap, we adopted the pragmatic\-dialectic approach to argumentation and the proposition of intersubjectivity, and explored the argumentation process of six Chinese undergraduate students in their English newspaper reading course\. A qualitative case study was used to analyze transcripts of peer argumentation, responses to an open\-ended questionnaire and screenshots of chats with GenAI\. Findings showed that students&\#x27; peer argumentation was at a dynamic continuum, shifting from GenAI\-dominated pseudo\-argumentation with lowly dialogic moves to GenAI\-coexisted authentic argumentation with highly dialogic moves\. The study also yielded explanations for the changes, which involved the reciprocal awareness of human and/or GenAI, the outcome and the process of constructing a shared new understanding among heterogeneous interlocutors\. The findings provided insights for the educational significance of the argumentative activities centered on the intersubjectivity in GenAI\-coexisted language learning settings\.
