## [Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning](../publications/fd60ce4043f84a49b8d5.md)

Hannah Guan; Soukayna Mouatadid; Paulo Orenstein; Judah L\. Cohen; Haiyu Dong; Zekun Ni; Jeremy D\. Berman; Genevieve Flaspohler; Alex Lu; Jakob Schlör; Joshua Talib; Jonathan A\. Weyn; Lester Mackey

Decision\-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3\. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics\-based dynamical models and data\-driven artificial intelligence models4–10\. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales \(2–6 weeks ahead\) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15\. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts\. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium\-Range Weather Forecasts \(ECMWF\), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets\. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real\-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide\. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19\. The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme\-weather prediction\.

## [Fault Tolerance in IoT Networks for Industrial Automation Using Artificial Intelligence](../publications/fd61d64e50d4d7010b08.md)

Mubarak Jibril Yeldu

The Industrial Internet of Things \(IIoT\) has become a fundamental component of modern industrial automation by connecting sensors, actuators, programmable logic controllers, robotic systems, machines, edge devices, and cloud platforms for continuous monitoring and intelligent control\. However, the dependence of industrial operations on interconnected IoT networks introduces significant risks associated with communication failures, sensor faults, hardware degradation, software errors, cyber\-attacks, congestion, and edge computing failures\. A single failure can interrupt production, reduce product quality, increase maintenance costs, or create safety hazards\. This paper examines the application of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) to improve fault tolerance in IoT networks used for industrial automation\. The paper reviews recent developments in AI based fault detection, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, intelligent routing, and edge based recovery, and adaptive resource management\. Recent studies demonstrate that machine learning can identify abnormal device and sensor behavior before failures propagate, while Software Defined Networking can support rapid route restoration and network recovery\. AI enabled edge computing further reduces response latency by moving fault analysis closer to industrial devices\. The paper proposes a conceptual AI enabled fault tolerant architecture consisting of an IoT sensing layer, resilient communication layer, edge intelligence layer, AI fault analysis layer, decision and recovery layer, and industrial control layer\. The proposed approach combines real\-time monitoring, machine\-learning\-based prediction, redundant communication paths, automated recovery, and predictive maintenance\. The paper concludes that integrating AI with fault\-tolerance mechanisms can improve industrial network availability, reliability, resilience, and operational continuity\. Nevertheless, challenges involving data quality, explain ability, computational resources, cyber security, interoperability, and validation in real industrial environments require further investigation\.

## [The Impact of Home Supervisory Education on Mothers’ Knowledge and Practices in Prevention of Childhood Injuries in a Selected Community, Puducherry, India: Enhancing Safety](../publications/fd6255e0924b33c27049.md)

Sumathy Ponnambalam

Objectives Unintentional childhood injuries represent a significant global public health concern, particularly affecting children under five years old\. These injuries, often occurring at home or in community settings, are a leading cause of death and disability among young children\. Efforts to reduce unintentional childhood injuries align with global health initiatives, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3, which aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well\-being for all ages\. As there is a dearth of research conducted in the rural community of Puducherry, this study was undertaken with the aim of creating awareness among the mothers of children aged &lt;5 years to prevent unintentional childhood injuries\. Material and Methods The design for the study is a pre\-experimental research design\. The study was conducted in October 2024 at a selected community area in Puducherry\. A total of 280 mothers were selected\. Baseline data were collected to assess the level of knowledge and practice among mothers of children aged &lt;5 years\. The post\-test was done 45 days after the educational intervention using the same tool\. Results The calculated knowledge and practice paired “t” test values were 78\.408 and 26\.62, respectively, which showed a high level of significance at p &lt;0\.001, implying the effectiveness of the intervention\. Conclusion Statistical evidence proved that the Home Supervisory Educational Intervention was effective in enhancing under\-five mothers’ knowledge and practice regarding home injuries among children\.

## [Effects of postmortem interval on myelin integrity in rhesus macaque brain tissue](../publications/fd630b31a918d0190240.md)

Anna Novoseltseva; Rhiannon E\. Robinson; Peter Niziolek; Allen Jang; Ting Xie; Ankita Tiwari; Ayman A Abdelhakeem; Raymond Nicks; Yvonne Lucas; Qiong Yang; Farzad Mortazavi; David A\. Boas; Hui Wang; Tara L\. Moore; Douglas L\. Rosene; Irving J\. Bigio

Abstract When conducting microscopy of human brain sections, the postmortem interval \(PMI\) introduces myelin‐related artifacts that can confound neuropathological interpretation, yet the extent and detectability of these changes remain poorly characterized\. This study examined the impact of controlled PMI on myelin integrity in rhesus macaque brain tissue using advanced optical imaging approaches\. Brains from five aged rhesus macaques \(20\.5–28\.5 years\) were maintained at 4°C and analyzed at 0, 24, and 72 h postmortem\. Myelin integrity in white and gray matter was assessed using quantitative birefringence microscopy to measure relative retardance and polarization‐sensitive optical coherence tomography to quantify scattering coefficients, retardance, and volumetric features\. Increasing PMI was associated with progressive myelin degradation, reflected by significant reductions in relative optical retardance in white matter \( p &lt; 0\.01\) and gray matter \( p &lt; 0\.001\), alongside increased scattering coefficients in both regions \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Morphological analyses revealed a marked increase in myelin defects per mm 2 with longer PMI \( p &lt; 0\.001\), characterized by swellings, vesicles, and structural discontinuities\. These findings demonstrate that PMI causes significant detectable myelin changes, which can be quantified using optical imaging techniques, providing critical implications for interpreting postmortem neuropathological studies \(especially with human brain tissues\) and establishing a need for standardized PMI considerations in research protocols to ensure accurate pathological assessment in neurological disease investigations\.

## [Adaptive conformal prediction on the Grassmannian](../publications/fd637094f0c1b2bc2b12.md)

Dimitrios Loukrezis; Zachary J\. Grey; Dimitris G\. Giovanis

We introduce a conformal prediction framework for regression with Grassmann\-valued responses\. The proposed method constructs prediction regions in the form of metric balls directly on the Grassmann manifold, using basis\-invariant geometric distances as non\-conformity measures and scaling the corresponding non\-conformity scores through a learned prediction difficulty estimator\. This yields locally adaptive, input\-dependent prediction regions that respect the underlying manifold geometry, while retaining the finite\-sample marginal coverage guarantee of split conformal prediction under exchangeability\. We evaluate several Grassmannian distance metrics and compare their prediction\-region efficiency on synthetic benchmarks and an airfoil inverse shape\-design problem\. The results highlight the advantages of geometry\-aware non\-conformity scores, while local adaptation improves empirical coverage uniformity across prediction difficulty levels and, in strongly heteroscedastic settings, can substantially reduce prediction\-region size while maintaining the target coverage\.

## [Validation of the GreenX library time\-frequency component for efficient GW and RPA calculations](../publications/fd6a408a726aa6f03a0d.md)

Maryam Azizi; Jan Wilhelm; Dorothea Golze; Francisco A\. Delesma; Ramón L\. Panadés‐Barrueta; Patrick Rinke; Matteo Giantomassi; Xavier Gonze

Electronic structure calculations based on many\-body perturbation theory \[e\.g\., GW or the random\-phase approximation \(RPA\)\] require function evaluations in the complex time and frequency domain, for example, inhomogeneous Fourier transforms or analytic continuation from the imaginary axis to the real axis\.For inhomogeneous Fourier transforms, the time\-frequency component of the GreenX library provides time\-frequency grids that can be utilized in low\-scaling RPA and GW implementations\.In addition, the adoption of the compact frequency grids provided by our library also reduces the computational overhead in RPA implementations with conventional scaling\.In this paper, we present low\-scaling GW and conventional RPA benchmark calculations using the GreenX grids with different codes \(FHI\-aims, CP2K, and ABINIT\) for molecules, two\-dimensional materials and solids\.Very small integration errors are observed when using 30 time\-frequency points for our test cases, namely &lt;10 \-8 eV/electron for the RPA correlation energies, and 10 meV for the GW quasiparticle energies\.

## [Knowledge management practice conceptualisation and enactment in retail pharmacies in Namibia: Insights from a multiple case study](../publications/fd6b4c0ecacc15979b92.md)

Abraham Dongo; Eric E\. Mang’unyi

This paper assessed the Knowledge Management \(KM\) methods used in Namibian retail pharmacies\. Shortcomings in KM techniques breed inefficiencies, unsafe practices, poor standards, and high morbidity\. Namibian retail pharmacies significantly lack knowledge mobilisation, consequently leading to undesirable quality of practice standards\. The KM practices were qualitatively explored, with document scrutiny and semi\-structured interviews providing the research data\. The 10 retail pharmacies took part in the study, providing nine pharmacists and seven assistants as participants\. The recorded interviews were converted into transcripts, and together with the collected documents, thematically analysed\. The participants demonstrated little understanding of the KM phenomenon and participated passively\. Despite engaging in KM activities, the participants did not conceptualise this as KM but rather as routine work\. This study revealed the absence of KM systems in retail pharmacies to extract tacit knowledge and institutionalise it\. The findings demonstrate the need to introduce robust KM systems in retail pharmacies, which can externalise tacit knowledge into organisational intellectual material\. This research expands the current KM and pharmacy practice scholarship by focusing on the neglected retail pharmacy settings\. The outcomes refine the present KM models and provide context\-specific insights into KM practices in retail pharmacies\.

## [Context\-Aware Edge Computing for Service Response and Affective Interaction Design in Smart Home IoT Systems](../publications/fd6bb6369ad10e8563ed.md)

Xiang Li; Yue Wang; Yaxin Chen

Smart home Internet of Things \(IoT\) systems require service\-response decisions that account for uncertainty, device availability, service risk, and edge latency rather than relying solely on activity recognition\. To address this, we propose an edge\-constrained context\-aware service\-response framework\. It integrates activity prediction, recognition confidence, device state, service risk, and context into a service\-oriented context state\. An uncertainty\-aware policy then selects auto, ask, or none\. Experiments on Center for Advanced Studies in Adaptive Systems \(CASAS\)\-Aruba and Activity Recognition with Ambient Sensing \(ARAS\) compare the method with traditional Human Activity Recognition \(HAR\), deep HAR, lightweight edge HAR, rule\-based, context\-aware reasoning, and uncertainty\-removal baselines\. Macro\-F1, Service Response Accuracy \(SRA\), and Edge Response Latency \(ERL\) are primary metrics, with Ask\-F1 and Auto Error as supplementary indicators\. Results show improved response action consistency under rule\-mapped labels while maintaining context recognition and edge\-side decision\-making within latency constraints\. Response labels are rule\-constructed and do not reflect real user preferences\. Further validation with real service logs and long\-term user feedback is needed\.

## [Colorimetría y atmósfera como constructores de percepción emocional audiovisual: una revisión sistemática\.](../publications/fd6f37aa076a71e5f6dc.md)

Ian Abinadab Avila Ramos; Damian Uriel Rosado Castellanos; Mariana Ramirez Lopez

El cine y los contenidos audiovisuales están cambiando gracias a la evolución del color y las tecnologías visuales\. Actualmente, aspectos como la colorimetría, la gradación y la composición influyen de forma directa en las emociones del público\. A través de una revisión sistemática basada en el método PRISMA, esta investigación examina cómo los estudios recientes aprovechan la narrativa visual, la fotografía y la teoría del color para explicar estas reacciones\. Los resultados muestran que el análisis se enfoca cada vez más en el uso de herramientas digitales, y que la psicología del color junto a la narrativa visual son los ejes principales para entender lo que transmite la pantalla\. Aunque cada perspectiva tiene sus limitaciones, integrarlas mejora el análisis de la imagen\. Esto permite que el uso del color en la postproducción sea más comprensible y eficiente, beneficiando tanto a investigadores como a creadores del ámbito técnico y académico\.

## [qcGEM: A Graph‐Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness](../publications/fd7cacdf59a128f65c7c.md)

Haoyu Wang; Ziyan Zhang; Swee Hong Ng; Haipeng Gong

The advancement of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has reshaped drug discovery\. AI\-based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction\. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans\. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum\-chemistry\-aware graph\-based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning\. Through a specially designed model architecture to adequately process quantum chemistry information, qcGEM provides a compact, physics\-informed molecular representation that supports a diverse range of downstream applications\. Particularly, qcGEM demonstrates state\-of\-the\-art performance across a broad range of molecule\-related benchmarks, as evidenced by comprehensive evaluations on 83 tasks including molecular property prediction, activity cliff detection, protein\-ligand interaction modeling, and opioid drug regression, and simultaneously offers strong interpretability at multiple representation levels\. We additionally propose a simplified variant, qcGEM\-Hybrid, with substantially accelerated embedding generation and robust performance\. Overall, our method provides an advanced molecular representation that will benefit molecule\-related modeling and prediction, supporting further progress in AI\-aided drug discovery\.

## [LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero\-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs](../publications/fd99c6569b6b5ee5bb55.md)

Guy Bar\-Shalom; Mor Geva; Fabrizio Frasca; Haggai Maron

Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high\-stakes settings\. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive\. A well\-known and efficient class of monitors can detect such failures from internal representations \(such as activation probes\), but are tied to the model they were trained on, requiring costly re\-annotation as new LLMs appear\. A natural way to avoid this repeated annotation cost is to develop internal\-representation based monitors that transfer zero\-shot across LLMs\. However, such transfer is challenging because internal representations are not naturally aligned across models; in particular, attention maps, known to contain signals of misbehavior, may differ in head function, ordering, and model depth\. In this work, we characterize those cross\-model attention mismatches as algebraic symmetries and use geometric deep learning principles to build LEMON \(Language\-model Equivariant MOnitoring Network\) an online graph neural network\-based monitor, whose predictions are invariant under these symmetries\. LEMON processes attention maps token\-by\-token, as they are produced and outputs a score after every token \(or every window of $W$ tokens\) at negligible cost\. Across 16 LLMs and six datasets, in the zero\-shot cross\-model setting, LEMON outperforms all baselines on both hallucination and jailbreak monitoring tasks, improving over the strongest by up to 14 ROC\-AUC points\.

## [A Review of Fault\-Tolerant Reconfigurable Architectures for Autonomous Systems Based on Redundant Logic Mapping](../publications/fda59da9454fed973505.md)

B\.M\.Brinda; D Vaduganathan

Mission\-critical applications \(aerospace, automotive, and defense\) have autonomous systems that must have very high reliability to allow continued operation in varied environmental structures and fault conditions\. The medium of flexibility and adaptability of the computer hardware is represented by reconfigurable computing platforms and, especially, by Field\-Programmable Gate Arrays \(FPGAs\) and Coarse\-Grained Reconfigurable Architectures \(CGRAs\)\. The review will provide an orderly research into the fault\-tolerant reconfigurable architecture with an interest in redundant logic mapping which encompasses spatial, temporal, and hybrid redundancy model\. We study important analysis metrics including Mean Time to Failure \(MTTF\), fault coverage, resources overhead and reconfiguration latency\. Recent literature shows comparative results that hybrids are able to provide the MTTF with up to 3\.5x scaling without a drastically high resource overhead \(\~2\.1x LUTs, \+25% power\)\. The relevance also points to the real use in self\-governing frameworks e\.g\. UAV, self\-governing automobiles, and smart robotics, where fault cloaking, configuration abrasive, and flawless cycles are fundamental\. Lastly, it presents open research issues in scalable fault diagnosis, AI\-based reconfiguration as well as cross layer fault resilience, and states a guideline towards the design of next generation self\-sustainable systems comprising of both economic and fault tolerant systems\.

## [An Intelligent Tourism Recommender System Using Retrieval\-Guided Large Language Models](../publications/fdb8dc99da80ee3b28e9.md)

Ammar Alazab; Wei\-Jun Lim; N\. D\. Salih; Hairulnizam Mahdin

Travel planning has become more complex nowadays due to the information overload from numerous online platforms causing travelers to be overwhelmed when selecting destinations, accommodations, and activities that match their preferences and constraints\. Traditional tourism recommender systems usually provide static and generic suggestions that fail to match users’ needs and cannot understand natural user language\. This research develops and evaluates a Generative AI Chatbot for Tourism Recommendations that use Large Language Models \(LLMs\) to generate personalized travel itineraries through natural language interaction to solve these limitations\. The system can process user natural language inputs including travel origin and destination, trip duration and dates, and budget in a conversational way\. This project used the osunlp/TravelPlanner dataset which contains real\-world tourism information on attractions, restaurants, accommodations, and flights\. The chatbot uses carefully designed prompts with strict generation rules to produce day\-by\-day itineraries that match user constraints\. The preliminary results show the system’s capability to generate human–readable travel plans that include correct flight selections, accommodation recommendations, and structured daily activities\. The chatbot prototype also supports conversational refinement which allows users to modify their itineraries interactively\. The evaluation will be conducted using BLEU and NIST metrics to measure response quality while also using a user satisfaction survey to assess the usability and personalization of the itinerary in the next phase\. This research has contributed to AI\-driven tourism planning by showing how generative AI can be used to create interactive and context\-aware assistants in recommender systems\. Future work will focus on including external APIs and conducting a comprehensive user testing to measure the usability and satisfaction level in the real world\.

## [A Review of AI\-Based Women Safety and Emergency Response Systems](../publications/fdbf6c238fb167c860e8.md)

Achal M\.  Pande; Vaishnavi J\.  Katare; Ashutosh R\.  Parde; Gagan S\.  Dave; Om S\.  Wadurkar; Prof\.  S\.  S\.  Mamarde

Women&\#x27;s safety applications have increasingly adopted mobile sensing, Global Positioning System \(GPS\), cloud services, and artificial intelligence to support emergency communication and risk awareness\. However, existing systems differ considerably in their methods of detecting emergencies and responding to them\. Some applications primarily provide manual SOS functions and location sharing, while others introduce voice activation, contextual risk assessment, offline communication, predictive analysis, or evidence collection\. This paper reviews recent technology\-based women safety and emergency response systems, with particular attention to their emergency triggers, use of artificial intelligence, location services, evidence collection, communication mechanisms, and limitations\. The reviewed literature covers mobile applications, predictive safety systems, contextual monitoring, and cloud\-supported emergency platforms\. The analysis shows that current solutions have improved the speed and accessibility of emergency assistance, but several systems remain focused on individual functions rather than integrated risk detection and response\. Important gaps remain in continuous behaviour analysis, anomaly detection, automatic triggering, reliable operation under limited connectivity, evidence management, and reduction of false alarms\. Based on these observations, the paper discusses a proposed research direction for an integrated AI\-based women safety platform designed to combine predictive risk assessment, multiple emergency triggers, location tracking, evidence collection, and automated emergency response\.

## [STRUCTURING ORGANIZATIONAL COGNITIVE ADAPTATION PATHWAYS: AN ORDERED NETWORK ANALYSIS OF HOW FORMAL PLANNING INTEGRATES ENTREPRENEURIAL TRAINING INTO STRATEGIC ACTION](../publications/fdc21eeb40bb8b641fce.md)

Margaret Nganu

This study investigates how formal planning structures the cognitive integration between entrepreneurial training domains and strategic adaptation pathways\. Grounded in cognitive theory, we proposed that a proactive planning actively structures an entrepreneur’s knowledge network, establishing both direct and indirect conceptual pathways that link training domains to adaptive business actions\. Using Ordered Network Analysis \(ONA\), 198 coded dialog lines from nine aggregated units of micro, small, and medium\-sized enterprises \(MSMEs\) were analyzed, categorized by planning adoption \(planners vs\. non\-planners\), business maturity, and environmental pressure severity\. Results revealed a significant divergence in conceptual network structure along the primary dimension between planners \(Mdn = 0\.29\) and non\-planners \(Mdn = \-0\.39\), with a large effect size \(U = 0, p = \.02, r = 1\.00\)\. Planners exhibited a structured network where training domains connect to strategic adaptive actions through dual pathways\. Direct linkages \(e\.g\., business management → financial buffering\) and mediated sequences through intermediate adaptive strategies \(e\.g\., value addition → logistical innovation → financial buffering\)\. In contrast, non\-planners displayed fragmented, non\-integrated networks with weak or absent directional ties\. The findings demonstrate that formal planning acts as a cognitive disciplining mechanism that builds a layered, hierarchical architecture for strategic action\. This architecture enables entrepreneurs to operationalize training into resilience through intertwined direct and mediated routes, centering on key outcomes such as financial buffering\. This study advances organizational cognition theory by illustrating how planning facilitates non\-linear, configurational knowledge integration and validates ONA as a robust method for modeling ordered conceptual relationships in entrepreneurial decision\-making\. Keywords: Entrepreneurship, Cognitive integration, Ordered Network Analysis \(ONA\), strategic adaptation, resilience\.

## [Insights into the exciton\- tryptophan coupling and corona formation of the serum albumin with cerium oxide nanoparticle along with temperature dependent denaturation and unfolding of protein](../publications/fdd03010767784325bfc.md)

Amit Kumar Bhunia; Souradeep Roy; Satyajit Saha; Prasanta Kumar Guha

In this report, the coupling of the excitonic peak of the grown semiconducting cerium oxide \(CeO2\) NPs \( \~350 nm\) with tryptophan \(\~278 nm\) along with biophysical study of interaction have been studied through UV\-Vis, photoluminescence, and CD spectroscopy, TCSPC, DLS, and HRTEM, AFM imaging\. The interaction of small sizes CeO2 NPs with serum albumin protein \(SAP\) showed formation of ground state complex with association constant \(k\) varied from 8\.7x103 \(μM\)\-1 to 4\.8x103 \(μM\)\-1\. The kinetics of the interaction study showed that the initial corona formation binding time was \~9 min, and the binding induced albumin reorganization time was \~248\.5 min and unfolding was much prominent than binding\. Dynamic quenching was found to be the major mechanism for albumin, with an exothermic nature observed during the interaction study across the temperature range from room temperature to human body temperature \(298\-312 K\)\. The energy transfer efficiency varied from \~75\.9% to \~87\.4% with temperature\. The visualized images of HRTEM and AFM showed formation of albumin corona and protein fibrillation\. At body temperature the probability of soft corona formation was more prominent than room temperature\. The hydrodynamic sizes of the nano\-protein corona were changes from 33\.5 nm to 80\.5 nm and ultrafast life time of the corona changes from 6\.1 ns to 4\.05 ns with increment of temperature\. The change in the ratio of β strand to α\-helix of the SAP has been occurred from \~15% to \~26\.03% with change in the corona temperature from 298 K to 312 K\.

## [Digital Payment Adoption and Financial Vulnerability: Global Evidence From Multilevel Models](../publications/fdd1b4cabfabe5954cd0.md)

Zewei Liu; Jing Jian Xiao; Rui Yao

ABSTRACT Although digital financial services are emerging, whether adopting digital payment influences consumer vulnerability remains understudied and debated\. This study aims to examine mechanisms linking digital payment adoption, financial fragility, financial worry, and national socioeconomic development\. Guided by information and communication technology for development \(ICT4D\), financial capability, and consumer vulnerability theories, we utilized multilevel modeling on a unique multisource dataset including 122,717 adults across 139 economies\. Digital payment adoption was negatively associated with financial fragility across levels, while its associations with financial worry were positive at the individual level and negative at the country level on average\. Such associations were manifested through suppressive partial mediation pathways and exhibited heterogeneous strengths across regions worldwide\. The analysis revealed double‐edged effects of consumer digital payment adoption and uncovered cross‐level development paradoxes in digital financial vulnerability\. Specifically, although digital adoption reflects human adaptation to crisis‐driven transformation, it simultaneously exacerbates specific dimensions of consumer fragility\. The “macro–micro mismatch” identified a paradox capturing structural forces in shaping consumer welfare\. The cross‐level interactions identified another “enabling–amplifying context” functioning as diverse roles of socioeconomic development environments\. This study contributes a comprehensive and comparative framework to the multidisciplinary research on digital finance and well‐being\. It also informs policymakers about co‐creating inclusive financial ecosystems to address consumer vulnerability alongside the macro‐level development of digitalization, financialization, and globalization\.

## [Surgical Approaches for Complex Tibial Plateau Fractures Involving the Posterolateral Quadrant: A Comparative Analysis](../publications/fdd491f309aed0200682.md)

Boris A\. Maiorov; Igor G\. Belenkiy; Gennadii D\. Sergeev; Сергеева Мария Александровна

In complex tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral quadrants, the standard anterolateral approach has limited capabilities for visualization and stable fixation, which necessitates the search for alternative surgical approaches\. The aim of the study was to conduct a comparative analysis of outcomes following various surgical approaches in patients with tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral quadrant\. Materials and Methods\. This prospective multicenter cohort non\-randomized study included 100 patients with intra\-articular tibial plateau fractures extending to the posterolateral quadrant\. Based on the surgical approach used, patients were divided into four groups: direct posterolateral approach or the K\. Frosch approach \(n=25\); fibular head osteotomy approach \(n=22\); combined posteromedial and extended anterolateral approach \(n=26\); and standard anterolateral approach \(ALA\) \(n=27\)\. Reduction quality, complication rates, and functional outcomes \(assessed using the KSS and Lysholm scores\) were evaluated at 6, 12, and 24 months postoperatively\. Results\. The proportion of anatomical reduction was significantly higher in the groups with direct or extended approaches \(60\.0\-76\.9%\) compared to the ALA group \(25\.9%\)\. The rate of unsatisfactory reduction in the ALA group was 40\.7%, versus 3\.8\-9\.1% in the other groups \(p0\.05\)\. The complication rate in the ALA group was 55\.6%, significantly exceeding that of the other groups \(16\.0\-19\.2%; p0\.05\)\. Functional outcomes in the ALA group were inferior at all follow\-up time points: at 24 months, the median Lysholm score was 68\.0 versus 87\.0\-88\.0 in the alternative approach groups \(p=0\.015\), and the median KSS score was 66\.0 versus 86\.0\-87\.0, respectively \(p=0\.019\)\. Multivariate analysis confirmed that outcomes were dependent on the combination of fracture type and the chosen surgical approach\. Conclusion\. The use of extended surgical approaches provided superior reduction quality, lower complication rates, and better functional outcomes compared to the standard anterolateral approach in tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral fragment\. Keywords: tibial plateau, posterolateral fragment, surgical approach, fibular head osteotomy, Frosch approach, four\-column theory

## [Comparison of Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Among First\-Year MBBS and First\-Year BDS Students](../publications/fddf09f62381ba244283.md)

Humaira Fayyaz; Iram Hashmi; Wardah Anwar; Saba Khalid

Background: Medical as well as dental education is academically demanding and may contribute to psychological distress among students\. First year students, in particular, face significant academic and social adjustments that may affect their mental well\-being\. The research was conducted to compare the presence of symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress between first year MBBS and first year BDS undergraduates and to determine whether the two groups differ in their psychological well\-being\.Objective: The objective of the study is to compare presence of symptoms of depressive state, anxiety, and psychological stress within first\-year MBBS and first\-year BDS students using a validated psychological assessment tool\.Methods: A cross\-sectional, comparative research design was used involving 146 students \(73 MBBS and 73 BDS\) from a recognized medical college and dental college\. The Depression Anxiety Stress Scale\-21 \(DASS\-21\) along with GAD 7 were employed as the assessment tool\. Socio demographic information was obtained through a standardized questionnaire\. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 25\. Comparisons between groups were carried out using chi\-square tests and independent samples t\-tests\.Results: Among MBBS students, 74% reported depression, 78\.1% reported anxiety, and 52\.1% reported stress\. Among BDS students, 64\.4% reported depression, 79\.5% reported anxiety, and 54\.8% reported stress\. However no significant statistical differences were found among MBBS and BDS students for depression \(p = 0\.210\), anxiety \(p =0\.840\), stress = \(p=0\.740\)\. Conclusion: The findings of this study indicate that anxiety is the common psychological condition among first year MBBS and first year BDS students\. MBBS students demonstrated comparatively higher levels of depression, whereas BDS students showed higher anxiety levels\. However, the comparison between the two groups did not show statistical significance\. Early screening, institutional mental health support, and stress management workshops are strongly recommended\.

## [Dual\-Functional SiO x Cross\-Point Devices Enabled by Top Electrode Engineering for Ultralow\-Current Resistive Memory, Ultrasensitive Sarcosine Sensing, and Artificial Intelligence\-Assisted Biomarker Classification](../publications/fde9faf63bc4a991622e.md)

Sourav Roy; Long Nguyen Minh Le; Abhijit Aich; Punnatorn Boonyoung; Wachiraporn Poomeesap; Tingyang Shen; Yi\-Pin Chen; Shih\-Yin Huang; Siddheswar Maikap

Abstract In the pursuit of ultra\-low\-power neuromorphic and bioelectronic systems, this work investigates two complementary SiOx\-based resistive\-switching architectures with engineered top electrodes: a Cu/CuAl structure employing metallic\-filament CBRAM and an IrOx/SiOx/W cross\-point architecture employing vacancy\-mediated switching\. Introducing a Cu–Al alloy interfacial layer into a Cu/SiOx/W structure enables ultralow\-current operation with an energy consumption of ∼0\.03 fJ/bit, endurance exceeding 109 program/erase \(P/E\) cycles, and a memory window \(MW\) greater than 2500\. Further advancement to a three\-dimensional IrOx/SiOx/W cross\-point architecture significantly improves device reliability, achieving endurance beyond 1010 P/E cycles at operating currents of 10 and 50 μA while maintaining stable switching for more than 103 cycles at an ultralow current of 200 nA with an MW exceeding 3 × 104\. Beyond memory functionality, the porous IrOx top electrode enables label\-free biomarker sensing through its stable redox states and super\-Nernstian pH response\. TEM, HRTEM, and FESEM analyses reveal a porous nanostructured IrOx architecture that facilitates efficient oxygen exchange, proton transport, and redox activity\. The resulting platform achieves ultrasensitive sarcosine detection with a limit of detection as low as ∼10 fM\. To examine the feasibility of automated interpretation of sensing signals, current–time responses were analyzed using a Convolutional Spiking Neural Network \(CSNN\)\. The model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 95\.8%, together with a sensitivity of 96\.02% and specificity of 100%\. These results demonstrate that complementary top\-electrode\-engineered SiOx architectures can provide ultralow\-power memory operation, while the IrOx/SiOx/W cross\-point platform further enables ultrasensitive biomarker detection and AI\-assisted signal analysis, highlighting their potential for future bioelectronic and neuromorphic systems\.

## [EVIDÊNCIAS NEUROFARMACOLÓGICAS DOS BIOATIVOS DE ESPÉCIES NATIVAS DA CAATINGA NO CONTEXTO DA ANSIEDADE: UMA REVISÃO DE LITERATURA](../publications/fded0bab1082ef6cbd63.md)

Maria Clara Tomé Macedo; RENATO NOGUEIRA SOUSA NETO; Marlon Dayan Farias Menezes; Ítalo Silvestre Lima Coelho; Cirliane Nascimento do Vale; B\. R\. Oliveira; Marcus Vinícius Oliveira Barros de Alencar

A Caatinga apresenta expressiva diversidade vegetal e constitui uma fonte relevante de compostos bioativos com potencial farmacológico, incluindo substâncias capazes de atuar sobre alvos relacionados à neurobiologia da ansiedade\. O presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências neurofarmacológicas de bioativos provenientes de espécies nativas da Caatinga no contexto da ansiedade, considerando seus efeitos comportamentais e possíveis mecanismos de ação\. Realizou\-se uma revisão integrativa da literatura, de caráter sistemático e descritivo, mediante buscas nas bases PubMed, SciELO, Scopus, Web of Science e Portal de Periódicos CAPES, abrangendo publicações entre 2019 e 2026, conforme os princípios do PRISMA\. Foram incluídos estudos envolvendo espécies nativas da Caatinga e diferentes preparações vegetais, como extratos, frações, óleos essenciais, decoctos e compostos isolados, avaliados principalmente em modelos experimentais de ansiedade\. As evidências reunidas demonstraram atividade ansiolítico\-like para diferentes espécies, com achados envolvendo Annona vepretorum, Caryocar coriaceum, Croton blanchetianus, Lippia grata, Lippia sidoides, Mimosa tenuiflora, Morisonia flexuosa, Passiflora cincinnata e espécies do gênero Ziziphus\. A atividade observada esteve principalmente associada à modulação das neurotransmissões GABAérgica e serotoninérgica, com participação de receptores específicos e, em alguns estudos, de alterações relacionadas à resposta inflamatória\. Em conjunto, os achados indicam que a diversidade fitoquímica da Caatinga apresenta potencial para a prospecção de agentes com atividade neurofarmacológica relacionada à ansiedade, destacando a necessidade de aprofundamento quanto à caracterização dos bioativos, mecanismos de ação, segurança e padronização das preparações\.

## [A Framework for Pre\-Pages Generator and Visualiser for Journal Publishing Systems: A Case Study](../publications/fe30b8690b392c28ab39.md)

Jiaheng Lu; Karrthik Nadarajan

In the domain of academic publishing, publishers must establish an efficient editorial workflow for managing their publication schedule while producing quality content, as these two processes will ultimately provide a good experience to readers\. Many independent publishers utilizing Open Journal Systems \(OJS\) rely on a manual compilation of &quot;pre\-pages&quot; \(front matter\), including the Issue Cover, the Editorial Board List, and the Table of Contents, through a manual workflow that is labor\-intensive and highly prone to human error, resulting in a product that is inconsistently formatted\. Through this project, we have developed a web\-based Pre\-Pages Generator and Visualiser that automates the pre\-publishing process, developed using Python and the Streamlit framework\. The application utilizes a 5\-step Wizard workflow to accomplish the entire pre\-publishing process by integrating web scraping to extract existing editorial data from the target journal&\#x27;s website, cleansing the data, and leveraging template\-driven rendering to populate Word templates with the appropriate OJS submission data\. In addition, the Editorial Intelligence Dashboard provides an overview of issue composition and editorial insights into content trends across issues of the publication by transforming raw bibliometric data\. A prototype of this system was developed in Python and was evaluated using the metadata of the Journal of Informatics and Web Engineering \(JIWE\) as a validation case study\. Empirical output shows an estimated 80% time reduction in document preparation \(reducing hours of manual labor to minutes\) and a decrease in formatting inconsistencies\. The findings suggest that this prototype could help to increase operational efficiency, reduce metadata risk, and improve decision support for non\-technical editorial teams\.

## [Framing Spatial Hearing within the Free Energy Principle: A Hierarchical Model of Perceptual Learning](../publications/fe3a8603c9e6bf41cc42.md)

Roberto Barumerli; Nils Meyer\-Kahlen; Lorenzo Picinali

Spatial hearing relies on dynamic internal representations to decode spatial information from ever\-changing acoustic conditions\. A fundamental example is sound localisation, where listeners infer the direction of an invisible sound\. Bayesian inference provides a computational account of such a localisation process; however, modelling efforts are largely limited to static listening scenarios\. Instead, the free energy principle \(FEP\) describes perception, learning, and action as joint minimisation of variational free energy \(VFE\), providing a principled framework to account for dynamic conditions\. Here, we take a first step toward applying the FEP to spatial hearing\. We characterise how listeners&\#x27; beliefs evolve across trials, in which they estimated sound direction and received subsequent visual feedback on each trial\. Listeners are described by a hierarchical generative model where visual feedback drives gradient descent on VFE, updating beliefs over three independent quantities: lateral and polar localisation precisions and hemifield disambiguation\. The model captures individual learning trajectories and reveals components with different dynamics: lateral precision improves, as does hemifield disambiguation, consistent with increased sensitivity of the auditory pathway in decoding vertical direction\. Notably, polar precision also increases, most for listeners with the lowest initial precision, suggesting that the observed vertical improvement is driven by both hemifield disambiguation and polar precision\. This work establishes spatial hearing as a tractable domain for FEP and motivates future closed\-loop experiments with full action\-perception cycles\.

## [Pathologies and technologies for digital therapeutics: An analysis of global clinical trials](../publications/fe41e307bf187d93d7f6.md)

Paolo Rocco; Valentina Pagella; Umberto M\. Musazzi; Sara Manellari; Elena Paola Lanati; Paola Minghetti

CDigital therapeutics \(DTx\) are software\-based medical devices that deliver evidence\-based therapeutic interventions directly to patients\. While the clinical use of DTx is expanding rapidly, regulatory fragmentation and the absence of harmonized legal definitions hinder their assessment and reimbursement policies, as well as their integration into healthcare systems\. There is currently a lack of comprehensive overviews of DTx clinical development, which are essential for informing policy, research and regulatory priorities\. This paper provides an updated overview of randomised clinical trials involving DTx\. 254 eligible trials on DTx, \(defined according to ISO/TR 11147:2023\) registered through January 2025 were identified through a search on ClinicalTrials\.gov\. Mobile applications represent the most prevalent technology \(65%\), followed by web\-based tools and virtual reality \(20%\)\. Psychiatric disorders are the primary therapeutic target \(52% of the studies\) with insomnia, depression, and anxiety being the most addressed conditions\. Trials were primarily conducted in North America \(41%\) and Europe \(32%\), where Germany, Spain, and Italy represent the most active countries\. The analysis of clinical trials registrations on ClinicalTrials\.gov reveals a heterogenous geographical distribution of DTx development but also a clear direction in the type of conditions for which they are mostly indicated, namely psychiatric and nervous system disorders\. The fragmented policies on DTx reimbursement, even among EU countries, and the different capacity of governments to fund DTx research and development emerge as key factors, along with cultural and ethical issues, in determining the willingness of the industry to invest in these devices\.

## [Phenomenological Functionalism: Toward Resolving the Hard Problem Through Supersystemic Integration and Carrier\-Code Distinction](../publications/fe4639dd74e871d2edac.md)

Daria Fadaleva

This paper introduces Phenomenological Functionalism to address the Hard Problem of Consciousness by distinguishing between the physical medium and semantic configuration\. ## [HeRE: A Novel Benchmark for Hebrew Relation Extraction via LLM\-Guided Denoising of Knowledge Graph Alignments](../publications/fe594140cca25d306d00.md)

Ron Keinan; Amir David Nissan Cohen; Reut Tsarfaty

While LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in English Relation Extraction \(RE\) tasks, a significant gap remains in assessing their RE performance in low\-resource languages, due to a lack of standardized benchmarks\. Creating native, language\-specific annotated RE benchmarks is expensive and requires human expertise, while relying on translation yields suboptimal, inaccurate datasets that introduce English\-centric biases\. To tackle this, we propose a scalable, language\-agnostic methodology to create RE data by denoising naturally occurring yet noisy alignments of knowledge bases and corresponding texts\. We define a proper alignment via a Natural Language Inference \(NLI\) task, where a relation triplet is entailed by an input text\. We empirically assess five denoising strategies, and demonstrate that multilingual models outperform language\-specific models in the few\-shot LLM setting, while Hebrew\-specific encoders remain competitive under NLI fine\-tuning and are strongest in the label\-free cross\-training setting\. We further find that prompting in the native language achieves performance on par with or slightly exceeding English prompts, confirming that the pipeline operates naturally in the target language\. The best open\-weights model, Gemma\-4\-31B\-it \(F1\\,=\\,0\.915\), matches the best API model, GPT\-5\.4 \(0\.921\), and reaches F1\\,=\\,0\.844 on a fully held\-out, dual\-annotated test set\. Applying the optimized pipeline, we release HeRE: a novel, massive, 1\.5\-million\-instance silver dataset for Hebrew RE, designed to support data\-intensive experimentation and model fine\-tuning\. HeRE bridges a critical gap in standard Hebrew RE evaluation, while providing the NLP community with a reproducible, language\-agnostic pipeline for RE dataset construction in other low\-resource settings\.

## [Aquatic moss by\-products offer an alternative to algal biomasses for phytostimulant bioproduction](../publications/fe5bc4af9e0cba898fdf.md)

Chiara Anglana; Piergiorgio Capaci; Stigliano E\.; Lenka Plačková; Karel Doležal; Fabrizio Barozzi; Gian Pietro Di Sansebastiano

Introduction Aquatic mosses are recently gaining attention for commercial use, stimulating the development of new biomass cultivation approaches\. This study explores the potential of by\-products from aquatic moss propagation as natural plant biostimulants, addressing the need for low\-waste production and sustainable agricultural strategies\. Methods Using Temporary Immersion Bioreactors, Leptodictyum riparium and Taxiphyllum barbieri were cultivated, yielding solid non\-viable biomass and liquid spent culture medium capable of offering a convenient and eco\-sustainable alternative to similar products from algal and plant biomasses\. Chemical analyses were performed to identify key plant hormones, including cytokinins \(e\.g\., cis\-zeatin, N 6 \-isopentenyladenosine\), auxins \(indole\-3\-acetic acid, 2\-oxindole\-3\-acetic acid\), and abscisic acid \(ABA\)\. To evaluate efficacy, in vitro Nicotiana tabacum plants were grown under optimal, salt, and osmotic stress conditions and treated with various moss\-derived preparations\. Results Cytokinins dominated the extract fraction with higher concentrations than auxins in both moss species\. Cytokinin totals in the extracts were up to three orders of magnitude above the minimum threshold typically required for cytokinin\-responsive phenotypic changes\. In some cases, auxin concentrations approached, though remained below, the \~100 nM threshold commonly cited for bioactivity\. Under optimal conditions, T\. barbieri extract at 0\.1% was the most effective treatment, increasing root length by up to 49% and shoot fresh weight by 93%\. Under salt stress, L\. riparium culture water applied at 3% of medium induced the strongest response, enhancing root length and biomass by up to 260% and 301%, respectively\. Under osmotic stress, moderate biomass increases were observed, reaching 94% with L\. riparium by\-product and 48% with T\. barbieri extract\. Discussion Overall, biostimulant efficacy was species\- and matrix\-dependent, with extracts mainly promoting growth under optimal conditions and culture water mitigating salinity stress\. These findings indicate that moss\-derived by\-products are promising candidates for the development of innovative plant biostimulant formulations within a circular and low\-input production framework, offering an alternative to other phytohormone\-rich biomasses\.

## [Course\-embedded AI\-augmented teaching is associated with engagement and performance in software education](../publications/fe64f8d4af4db27eedac.md)

Zhe Gai; Junjun Wang; Jinyong Wu

AI\-augmented teaching may reduce feedback delays in software courses, but semester\-long classroom evidence remains limited\. This course\-level quasi\-experimental study evaluated a course\-embedded AI\-augmented teaching \(AIT\) model in an undergraduate Python course\. Two intact classes participated: 60 students in the AIT class used a large language model teaching assistant restricted to course\-specific materials and instructional rules for question answering, code diagnosis, personalized recommendations, and teacher monitoring, whereas 60 students in the conventional\-instruction class received the same course instruction without access to the AIT platform\. Student\-level analyses, interpreted cautiously because of the class\-level design, showed higher posttest, programming assignment and final composite scores in the AIT class after baseline adjustment\. Learning engagement also showed clearer gains, especially overall and behavioral engagement\. AI usage intensity was moderately associated with engagement but weakly associated with academic performance\. Mediation analysis provided clearer evidence for an indirect engagement pathway for project practice performance than for final composite performance\. Open\-ended feedback indicated that students valued immediate feedback and debugging support but remained concerned about accuracy, dependency and ethical boundaries\.

## [Hantaviral therapeutics: life cycle targets and chemotherapeutic interventions](../publications/fe79a5f8c8af8bf659f7.md)

Deren Zehra Kocabiyik; Jansen de Araújo; Edison Luíz Durigon; Carsten Wrenger

Orthohantaviruses represent a persistent global health threat, being responsible for life\-threatening diseases such as Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome \(HFRS\) and Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome \(HCPS\)\. Despite high case fatality rates and recent outbreaks, there are currently no universally licensed antivirals or vaccines\. Clinical management remains heavily reliant on supportive care and repurposed drugs, which often exhibit limited efficacy and dose\-limiting toxicities\. This review examines rational drug design strategies targeting critical steps in the viral life cycle, specifically Gn/Gc\-mediated cellular entry and RNA\-dependent RNA polymerase \(RdRp\)\-driven genome replication\. We evaluate the current landscape of viral inhibitors, including peptidomimetics, nucleoside analogues, and naturally derived compounds\. To accelerate the discovery of novel treatments, we advocate for the integration of modern in silico screening to evaluate extensive chemical and natural product libraries\. These broad compound collections offer a structurally diverse and largely untapped reservoir for antiviral development\. Ultimately, expanding preclinical testing to include globally neglected variants will be essential to develop broad\-spectrum hantaviral therapeutics capable of mitigating future epidemic threats\.

## [Academic stress and internet gaming addiction in college students: a moderated mediation model with anxiety as mediator and peer support as moderator](../publications/fe8567f692ea82818be9.md)

Jingjing Li; Liu Bao; Yu Wang

Background Academic stress is a known risk factor for internet gaming addiction among college students; however, the underlying mechanisms remain not fully elucidated\. The current study aimed to examine the mediating role of anxiety in the relationship between academic stress and internet gaming addiction, as well as the moderating role of peer support\. Methods A cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 636 Chinese college students in China\. Participants completed measures of academic stress, anxiety, peer support, and internet gaming addiction\. Analyses were performed using the PROCESS macro for SPSS\. Model 4 was used to test mediation, and Model 59 was used to test moderated mediation, with age and gender controlled for in all analyses\. Results Academic stress was positively associated with internet gaming addiction among college students \( r = 0\.28, p &lt; 0\.001\), and anxiety mediated this relationship \(indirect effect = 0\.22, 95% CI = \[0\.16, 0\.27\]\)\. Peer support significantly moderated this indirect effect by buffering the path from academic stress to anxiety \( b = \-0\.18, p &lt;\.01\)\. Specifically, for college students with lower peer support, the relationship between academic stress and anxiety was significant \( b = 0\.42, p &lt;\.001\); for those with higher peer support, the relationship remained significant but weaker \( b = 0\.24, p &lt;\.001\)\. Conclusion Academic stress was associated with internet gaming addiction among college students through increased anxiety, and peer support served as a protective buffer in this mechanism by weakening the association between academic stress and anxiety\. These findings highlight the importance of anxiety management and peer support interventions for preventing internet gaming addiction among college students facing academic stress\.

## [A Two\-Stage Unsupervised–Supervised Machine Learning Framework for Maximum Power Point Tracking of Photovoltaic Systems](../publications/fe900680a5ef0ac0fa37.md)

Maissa Farhat; Maen Takruri; Óscar Barambones; Mohammad Rabih; Aws Al\-Qaisi; Ghaya Alhebsi; Mariam Al Ali; Reem Al Nuaimi; Naema Alharmi; Muna Alshehhi

Maximum Power Point Tracking \(MPPT\) is essential for maximizing photovoltaic \(PV\) energy extraction under changing operating conditions\. This paper investigates a two\-stage machine\-learning framework combining K\-means or fuzzy C\-means \(FCM\) clustering of irradiance–temperature conditions with region\-specific support vector regression \(SVR\), Gaussian process regression \(GPR\), and bagged ensemble trees \(BET\) to estimate the maximum\-power\-point reference voltage\. The predicted voltage is supplied to a proportional–integral–derivative \(PID\)\-controlled boost converter, and closed\-loop performance is evaluated in MATLAB R2024/Simulink under changing irradiance, temperature, and load\. Under the original evaluation protocol, two\-cluster K\-means—BET achieved the lowest MAE among the K\-means prediction configurations, whereas integrated\-energy rankings did not consistently follow voltage\-prediction rankings\. An additional leakage\-controlled assessment used 70% of data for training and 30% for independent test observations, with clustering, standardization, and five\-fold cross\-validated Bayesian hyperparameter optimization performed using training observations only\. In this stricter comparison, unclustered SVR achieved the lowest overall MAE, while FCM with three clusters improved BET MAE by approximately 9\.7%\. These results show that clustering benefits depend on the regression model and evaluation protocol\. The closed\-loop energy findings apply to the original simulated configurations; the new strict hold\-out models were not separately tested in closed\-loop simulation\. Hardware implementation and broader\-dataset validation remain future work\.

## [Generative Artificial Intelligence, Pandemic Risk, and Biological Weapons: Implications for Clinical Immunology](../publications/fe9266e19292c886d97c.md)

Thauann Lima Silva Rufino

The convergence of generative artificial intelligence and the life sciences expands research opportunities, but also raises concerns about its misuse in biological threats\. This article critically reviews the evidence and uncertainties regarding pandemic risk associated with the possible use of AI in biological weapons, with particular attention to clinical immunology\. A narrative and critical review of peer\-reviewed studies, institutional documents, a corporate report, and selected journalistic coverage was conducted\. The reviewed evidence supports preventive concern and structured preparedness, but it does not establish that current AI systems can independently cause a pandemic, nor does it demonstrate generalized immune evasion attributable to AI\. Immunological evidence drawn from SARS\-CoV\-2 and COVID\-19 vaccination is used only as an illustrative framework for interpreting neutralization, cellular memory, mucosal immunity, and clinical protection; it is not treated as evidence that a hypothetical engineered agent would behave similarly\. The analysis emphasizes the distinction between computational capability and biological consequence, separates literature\-supported findings from the author&\#x27;s preparedness proposal, and identifies methodological and evidentiary gaps that require direct empirical study\.

## [Numerical Investigation of Flow Direction and Inlet–Outlet Configuration Effects on Thermo\-Hydraulic Performance in T\-Junction Tubes](../publications/fe9dbfee89c7f9efa5fe.md)

Ali Gürcan

Direct comparisons of diverging and converging T\-junction configurations under identical operating and boundary conditions remain limited, restricting the design\-oriented selection of suitable flow arrangements\. This study numerically investigates the effects of flow direction and inlet–outlet topology on the thermo\-hydraulic performance of a symmetric equal\-diameter T\-junction with water as the working fluid\. Four configurations were examined: axially fed and branch\-fed diverging flows \(K1 and K2\) and opposing\-stream and orthogonal\-stream merging flows \(K3 and K4\)\. Three\-dimensional steady Reynolds\-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations were performed in ANSYS Fluent using the standard k&quot;\-&quot; ε turbulence model with Enhanced Wall Treatment at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000, and 15000 and inlet temperatures of 313, 333, and 353 K\. The configurations were compared under identical geometry, total mass flow rate, and wall\-temperature conditions using the average Nusselt number, static pressure drop, and a common thermo\-hydraulic performance criterion \(PEC\)\. K1 consistently provided the highest average Nusselt number and the lowest pressure drop, while K2 was the closest alternative\. Relative to K1, the PEC values of K3 and K4 were lower by 43\.3–53\.4% and 45\.0–53\.5%, respectively\. The results show that stronger local flow interaction in converging configurations does not necessarily yield superior overall performance and provide a quantitative basis for selecting equal\-diameter T\-junction topologies in water\-based thermal and process\-piping applications\.

## [Hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling processes, and irrigation suitability assessment of groundwater in the Sanjiang Plain, China](../publications/fe9de42103000df18d21.md)

Lingbo Wang; Xin Liu; Panpan Xu; Xiangxu Guo; Hongyan Hu; Yanmin Su; Lu Wang; Weining Wang; Xu Derui

Abstract Groundwater is vital for global irrigation water supply, and its quality directly affects sustainable agricultural development\. However, studies on irrigation water quality and its dominant controlling factors in semi\-humid regions remain limited\. Therefore, taking the Sanjiang Plain as a case, hydrochemical analysis, irrigation water quality assessment, and multivariate statistical methods were employed to systematically reveal the hydrogeochemical characteristics, irrigation suitability, and their dominant controlling mechanisms\. The results indicate that the main hydrochemical type of groundwater is HCO 3 \-Ca, and most ions exhibit moderate to significant spatial variability\. Its hydrochemical composition is mainly controlled by rock weathering, dominated by the dissolution of carbonate minerals, silicate minerals, and evaporite rocks, with significant cation exchange and limited contribution from gypsum dissolution\. The groundwater in the study area is generally suitable for agricultural irrigation\. However, EC, Na%, RSC, and MH values are relatively high in the Jiansanjiang area in the northeast, while the EC and RSC values are high in the southeast, which poses a potential risk of soil salinization\. This spatial variation is mainly controlled by natural geological conditions\. Carbonate mineral weathering controls the spatial distribution of MH and RSC\. The dissolution of halite and silicate minerals affects variations in SAR and Na% and indirectly influences MH by inhibiting cation exchange processes\. RSC shows relatively low correlations with various hydrochemical parameters, indicating that its spatial distribution is regulated by multiple coupled factors\. These findings can provide a scientific basis for the rational utilization of groundwater resources, irrigation management, and salinity hazard prevention and control in similar regions\.

## [Camel milk concerning erythrocytic immune\-related gene expression in Escherichia coli\-challenged broilers](../publications/fe9e41854aae32c0b140.md)

Uroosa Arain; Nasir Ahmed Rajput; Mahum Arain; Ali Raza Jahejo; Yunkyoung Lee; Guiguo Zhang

Background Chicken erythrocytes play a role in immunity, yet the function of erythrocyte\-related immune genes during Escherichia coli \( E\. coli \) infection remains underexplored\. This study investigated the effects of camel milk powder supplementation on growth performance and erythrocyte\-specific immune gene expression in E\. coli \-challenged broiler chickens\. Methods A total of 240 one\-day\-old broiler chickens were randomly assigned to four groups with three replicates \(20 Chickens per replicate\): Control \(Basal diet \+ PBS\), Infected \( E\. coli challenged\), T1 \( E\. coli \+ 5 g/kg camel milk\), and T2 \( E\. coli \+ 10 g/kg camel milk\)\. Performance metrics, organ weights, intestinal and hepatic histomorphology, hematological parameters, and viable E\. coli counts in blood and cecum were assessed\. Bioinformatics analysis of microarray data \(GPL8764\) guided the selection of key immune genes\. Quantitative real\-time PCR was performed on purified erythrocytes to evaluate immune gene expression\. Results Feed intake, weight gain, and FCR were significantly \( p &lt; 0\.05\) improved in the T1 group compared to the Infected group\.While relative weights of the spleen and bursa did not differ significantly among groups, liver weight was influenced by supplementation, and histomorphological analysis revealed improved intestinal and hepatic architecture in camel milk\-supplemented chickens\. Hematological parameters \(RBC, WBC, PCV, Hb\) disrupted by infection were restored in treated groups\. Furthermore, viable E\. coli counts in the blood and cecum were significantly reduced in T1 and T2 groups on days 28 and 35\. Bioinformatics analysis of microarray data \(GPL8764\) guided the selection of key immune genes\. Quantitative real\-time PCR performed on purified erythrocytes demonstrated that camel milk supplementation modulated the expression of Interleukin genes \(IL\-2, IL\-6, IL\-10, and IL\-12\) in Infected chickens\. Conclusion The camel milk supplementation at 5 g/kg, effectively mitigated the negative impacts of E\. coli infection by enhancing growth performance, reducing bacterial load, and modulating immune responses\.
