## [Presencia, distribución e infección de triatominos con Trypanosoma cruzi en el estado de Campeche, México](../publications/fea875b354eca49bfcea.md)

Paulino Tamay\-Segovia; Yessenia Montes\-Vergara; Selene Blum\-Domínguez; Alberto Antonio‐Campos; José Miguel Padilla\-Valdez; Nancy Rivas; Ricardo Alejandre‐Aguilar

Introduction\. Campeche is a Mexican state with an ideal habitat for triatomines, the vectors of Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite that causes Chagas disease\. While different entomological indices and the geographic distribution of these triatomines have been reported in the state, data remain limited to a few localities\. Objective\. Evaluate the occurrence, distribution, and natural infection of triatomines in Campeche, Mexico\.Materials and methods\. Triatomines were collected from 1996 to 2023 in 32 localities of Campeche within intradomicile, peridomicile, and sylvatic areas\. The percentage of natural infections was calculated, and associations between triatomine species and locality, as well as between triatomine instars and infection status, were analyzed\. Results\. A total of 532 triatomines were collected: Triatoma dimidiata was the most abundant and widely distributed species in the state, whereas only a single specimen each of Triatoma nitida and Eratyrus cuspidatus was found\. Across all three collection areas, adults were more frequently found than nymphs\. Furthermore, most females were captured in intradomicile areas, and more females exhibited a higher proportion of Trypanosoma cruzi infection compared to males\. The overall natural infection rate for the entire region was 18\.8%\. The only significant statistical association was between triatomine developmental instars and Trypanosoma cruzi infection \(χ2 = 80\.396, p &lt; 0\.0001\)\.Conclusion\. This work highlights the importance of continuously monitoring areas around dwellings to prevent potential infestation by non\-domiciliated bugs and crucially to reduce the risk of Trypanosoma cruzi infection among the local population\.

## [The J2OS Platform Handbook \(Version 2\.4\): Building Enterprise Systems with Java and Nuxt, from the First Line to a Complete Application](../publications/fec74e66cd1b97fcaed3.md)

Amirsam Bahador

This book is a complete guide to J2OS Platform version 2\.4\. J2OS is a modular set of 65 modules: 32 Java modules on the server side and 33 Nuxt\-based modules on the client side\. The book is written for readers who are just starting out and want to learn the platform module by module, without needing any other source\. The book has six parts: Server infrastructure: validation, security, reporting, load balancing, file management, workflow, resource pooling, sharding, terminal access, and data pagination\. Communication: message queuing, an HTTP client, email, video meetings, push notifications, and a Telegram bot\. Artificial intelligence: 13 modules covering natural language processing, translation, speech, object detection, face detection, OCR, and image similarity\. Data components: card, map, star, table, tree, and wizard\. Vue composables: a collection of ready\-made user\-interface utilities\. Each chapter covers one module and follows the same structure: the concepts, a first complete and runnable example, the next steps, behavior on failure with a catalog of error messages, use on the web, risky pitfalls, and practical recommendations\. Every example is complete, and each one can be run as it stands\. License\. Version 2\.3 of the platform is open source and freely available to the public\. Version 2\.4, which this book covers, is commercial and is released under a commercial license\. Keywords: J2OS, Java, Nuxt, Vue, modular architecture, enterprise software, deep learning, programming education

## [Home\-based telerehabilitation after CABG: higher objectively verified adherence and 12\-week functional outcomes in a single\-center observational cohort](../publications/fec807dd7382bc33bfbf.md)

Yan Liu; Xugang Wang; Cuihua Wang; Minjuan Zhang; Manman Kong; Meng Wang; Jingjing Ma; 劉慧俐

Background Home\-based telerehabilitation \(HBTCR\) may address access barriers to center\-based cardiac rehabilitation \(CBCR\) after coronary artery bypass grafting \(CABG\)\. However, real\-world comparative evidence on objectively verified adherence and functional recovery, with careful confounding control, remains sparse\. This observational cohort study compared session completion and 12\-week functional outcomes between HBTCR and CBCR in post\-CABG patients using routine clinical data\. Methods This single\-center observational cohort screened 288 patients and identified 195 potentially eligible post\-CABG patients \(February 2024–February 2025\)\. After excluding 28 patients with unresolved rehabilitation exposure, 167 patients \(56 HBTCR, 54 CBCR, 57 usual care\) formed the propensity\-score estimation cohort, adjusted for 25 baseline covariates with generalized propensity scores and overlap weighting\. The primary complete\-case analysis included 105 patients \(35 per group\) with complete 12\-week follow\-up\. The primary outcome was objectively verified session completion \(% of 36 prescribed sessions\)\. The key clinical outcome was 12\-week VO 2 peak, analyzed via weighted ANCOVA\. Results are reported as adjusted differences with 95% CIs\. Results After weighting, covariates were well balanced \(all SMDs &lt;0\.10\)\. HBTCR showed significantly higher objectively verified session completion than CBCR \(87\.7% vs\. 78\.5%; overlap\-weighted difference 9\.1 percentage points, 95% CI: 4\.4 to 13\.7; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The adjusted HBTCR–CBCR difference in 12\-week VO 2 peak was small and not statistically significant \(0\.17 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: −0\.50 to 0\.84; P = 0\.616\)\. Both active rehabilitation groups showed substantially larger 12\-week VO 2 peak gains than usual care \(adjusted differences &gt;4\.0 mL/kg/min\)\. Conclusion Among post\-CABG patients who chose HBTCR or CBCR in routine practice, those choosing HBTCR had higher objectively verified session completion and comparable observed 12\-week improvement in VO 2 peak\. These findings support HBTCR as a feasible option for patients who prefer or require home\-based rehabilitation because of work, travel, or scheduling constraints\. Formal equivalence was not tested, and the clinical meaningfulness and cost\-effectiveness of this delivery model warrant further evaluation\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RECOMBINANT BIOMANUFACTURING: INTEGRATING BIOINFORMATICS AND INDUSTRIAL BIOTECHNOLOGY FOR NEXT\-GENERATION THERAPEUTICS](../publications/fecd97b96549c579b13a.md)

Yogesh R\.; Senthilrajan D\.; Sivasankari Madheswaran; Srividhya R\.

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is emerging in recombinant biomanufacturing, where data\-driven approaches are used to optimize complex biological systems\. This paper reviews the integration of artificial intelligence, bioinformatics and industrial biotechnology in the recombinant production process from genetic design to large\-scale processing\. These approaches enhance protein engineering through structure prediction, codon optimization and functional analysis\. In upstream processing, machine learning is used to support strain development, media optimization and adaptive control strategies to improve yield and product quality\. For downstream operations, efficient purification is achieved through AI\-based modelling of chromatographic processes and monitoring critical quality attributes in real time\. This is further supported by integration with Quality by Design \(QbD\), Process Analytical Technology \(PAT\) and digital twins, enabling continuous manufacturing and real\-time release testing \(RTRT\)\. Despite these gains, challenges remain, including data limitations, model interpretability, and regulatory constraints\. Overall, AI\-driven bioprocessing represents a transformative approach with the potential for efficient, scalable and next\-generation biopharmaceutical production\.

## [Legal Education requires Competence in a GenAI World: Why Legal Knowledge is not Enough](../publications/fed2d3f29facbf2d4219.md)

Sonya Willis; Amanda Head

Generative Artificial Intelligence \(‘GenAI’\) is reshaping what it means to educate competent lawyers\. This article devises a Legal Competence Framework based on Le Deist and Winterton’s synthesis of the competence literature augmented by the NSW Solicitor Capability Framework\. The Legal Competence Framework delineates the skills students require in their legal education through four interrelated competence dimensions of cognitive competence, functional competence, social competence, and meta\-competence\. This Framework enables analysis of GenAI’s impact on legal education and assessment\. Law is among the most heavily regulated fields of tertiary education and the article seeks to disentangle the complex obligations imposed by the Priestley 11, the Higher Education Standards Framework, the Australian Qualifications Framework and the Threshold Learning Outcomes through applying the Legal Competence Framework\. The analysis considers GenAI’s disruption of each learning framework and the impact on learning and assessment, including how GenAI increases the need for social and meta competence\. The article explores how GenAI severs the link between traditional unsupervised assessment output and genuine competence discouraging the effortful struggle through which competence develops\. It concludes that, whilst supervised assessment remains critical, unsupervised assessment is also essential but its design must shift to focus on assessing learning process rather than output\.

## [Transformación digital y eficiencia empresarial: revisión sistemática](../publications/fed5fff39b149b899be5.md)

Fausto Enrique Montano\-Mendoza; César Hernán Norabuena Mendoza; Patricia Jaqueline Chumbes\-Cardenas; Lilian Rocío Rosales Maguiña; Nathaly Luisa Trujillo Navarro

Esta revisión sistemática examina la producción científica publicada entre 2020 y 2025 para establecer cómo se ha estudiado la relación entre transformación digital y eficiencia empresarial\. La evidencia se integró mediante síntesis narrativa y el proceso de identificación, selección y reporte se organizó con base en los lineamientos de PRISMA 2020\. Metodología: se consultaron Scopus, Web of Science y SciELO\. De 273 registros iniciales, 63 correspondieron a duplicados; luego se cribaron 210 registros y se incluyeron 25 documentos en la síntesis final\. El análisis principal se sustentó en 20 estudios empíricos publicados en revistas científicas, mientras que cinco fuentes secundarias, conceptuales o no arbitradas se emplearon para ampliar el contexto y reconocer tendencias y vacíos\. Resultados: en conjunto, los estudios revisados describen con mayor frecuencia relaciones favorables entre la transformación digital y resultados vinculados con la optimización de procesos, la productividad, la toma de decisiones y el desempeño organizacional\. No obstante, estas asociaciones no se presentan de manera homogénea: cambian según la madurez digital, las capacidades tecnológicas, el liderazgo, la cultura organizacional, la innovación y las particularidades sectoriales\. También se advierten carencias de estudios longitudinales y cualitativos, una representación todavía reducida de América Latina y una integración limitada de indicadores tecnológicos, financieros y humanos\. Conclusiones: la evidencia disponible permite entender la transformación digital como un proceso estratégico y organizacional que rebasa la simple incorporación de herramientas digitales\.

## [From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence\-Supported Physics Research](../publications/fedf06a3e48ff59b0199.md)

Yijia Mao; Song Dai; Tao Chen; Xiangyu Lu; Linqian Zeng; Chenxi Hu; Sitong Zhou; Dongyang He; Xiaodan Mao; Linxuan Zhang; Tong Zhu; Yafu Li; Fangchen Yu; Peng Ye; Feng He; Yu Cheng; Yun Luo

Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well\-supported conclusions? To evaluate this capability, we introduce PhysClosureBench, a benchmark of 50 expert\-verified, goal\-specified research tasks spanning strong\-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas\. Each task specifies the research objective and essential scientific constraints, while leaving the agent to organize the investigation and determine how to generate and validate the evidence needed to answer the question\. A 20\-criterion Atomic Score measures local scientific accomplishment, while Research Closure \(RC0\-\-RC4\) assesses how fully the investigation resolves the specified research question based on whether its indispensable evidence requirements and applicable scope conditions are satisfied\. We evaluate seven frontier LLMs, where Claude\-Opus\-5 achieves the highest mean Atomic Score \(6\.29/10\) but reaches RC4 in only 32\.7% of attempts\. Across the benchmark, 36\.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 still fall short of RC4, while all seven models reach RC4 on substantially fewer tasks in all three runs than in at least one\. Case\-level analysis further illustrates how misinterpretation of generated results and unresolved physical applicability limits can lead to incomplete closure\. Together, these results reveal a persistent gap between AI agents&\#x27; local scientific accomplishments and their ability to achieve complete research closure\.

## [Legal Mechanisms of AI Assessment in China and Russia: A Comparative Study](../publications/fee5561490200dc4ee9e.md)

O\. Izhaev

This article presents a comparative analysis of the legal mechanisms of AI assessment in China and Russia\. The author employs the functional and dogmatic methods, together with a basic concept—the “AI assessment mechanism”—as the foundation for comparing heterogeneous legal institutions\. The comparison is conducted across seven parameters: the object and subject matter of assessment, the criteria for selecting the object, the procedure, the timing, the legal force, and the regulatory purpose\. In China, the mechanism is based on algorithm registration and security assessment, established by the Cyberspace Administration of China acts and implemented through administrative practice and technical standards\. In Russia, the ﬁrst legally signiﬁcant assessment mechanism is introduced by Federal Law No\. 243\-FZ of July 26, 2026, which establishes a register of large foundation models and a requirement to confirm their compliance with legislation and traditional Russian spiritual and moral values\. The comparison reveals two types of relationship: divergence and convergence\. The divergence stems from the regulators’ diﬀerent goals: China develops assessment as an instrument of control over the information space, while Russia designs it as a tool for securing technological sovereignty\. There is convergence, however, in the choice of instruments: both legal orders rely on registration or record\-keeping and on security or compliance assessment, and both mechanisms operate on an ex ante basis\. The article and its ﬁndings represent the ﬁrst comparative study of these mechanisms\. The Chinese experience is particularly relevant to the unresolved issues Russia faces in designing procedures for registering large foundation models and conﬁrming their compliance with applicable requirements\.

## [A Comparative Multivariable Study of Institutional and Workforce Factors Associated with Health Information Management Practices in South\-South Nigeria](../publications/fee618086a30b297d20d.md)

Ebimene Japheth Teddy Kurokeyi; PhD Pro\. Sancho N\. Chukwu; Pro\. Anthony i\. Wegbom; Dr\. Oduak Peter

Health Information Management \(HIM\) involves the systematic collection, organisation, analysis and use of health data for clinical care, administration, research and decision making\. However, little evidence has shown whether any difference between practices is mainly due to institutional context or workforce factors in Nigeria\. This research evaluated institutional and workforce factors associated with HIM practices in South\-South Nigeria applying a comparative multivariable analysis\. A cross\-sectional survey involving 124 HIM professionals was conducted at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital \(UBTH\), University of Calabar Teaching Hospital \(UCTH\) and University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital \(UPTH\)\. Data were obtained using a structured questionnaire on workforce characteristics and four domains of HIM practices; electronic data entry, disease coding and indexing, clinical data analysis and clinical research\. Descriptive statistics, chi\-square, analysis of variance effect size measures and Hierarchical multiple regression using HC3 robust standard error were used\. Age \(p=\.013\), work experience \(p&lt;\.001\), literacy level \(p=\.008\) differed significantly between institutions\. However, general HIM practices did not significantly differ by institutional setting \(F=\.354, p=\.702, η2=\.006\) and practice domains also varied insignificantly between institutions except one domain\. Institution explained 0\.6% of the variance in the observed practices\. Workforce factors contributed to an increase of 17\.6% explained variance to 60\.7%, and the full model explained 94\.4%\. Experience, literacy skills, professional title, and certification were still significantly and independently related to HIM practices\. The results revealed greater correlation between workforce characteristics and HIM practices rather than between institutional affiliation and HIM practices\. emphasis therefore should be placed upon competency\-based professional growth, a competent career march, and continual workforce competency evaluations\.

## [Interpretable water and agricultural land cover in urban landscapes using CNN–ViT framework with Grad\-CAM for agricultural sustainability](../publications/fef1de48b7801a659ee3.md)

Hajar Hameed Addeen; Ebrahim Mohammed Senan; Fawaz Aklan; Salwa Mutahar Alwazer; Eman A\. Alshari; M\. Attique Khan; Ibrahim Abdulrab Ahmed

Abstract Accurate land\-use and land\-cover classification in hyper\-arid environments is challenging because several surface types can exhibit overlapping spectral and spatial characteristics in Landsat imagery\. These surfaces include water, irrigated agriculture, moist soil, barren land, and built\-up areas\. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid framework for classifying six land\-use and land\-cover classes in Najran, Saudi Arabia, using seven\-band Landsat 8 imagery\. The framework integrates MobileNetV2, ResNet152, and ViT\-B/16 to combine efficient local feature extraction, deep hierarchical representation learning, and global contextual modeling\. This combination was selected to address the heterogeneous landscape patterns and mixed spectral responses that characterize the study area\. Controlled ablation experiments showed progressive performance gains from the standalone CNN models to the CNN–ViT configurations and the complete three\-branch framework\. Overall accuracy increased from 86\.73% to 88\.23% for MobileNetV2 and ResNet152 to 94\.98% and 95\.68% for their respective CNN–ViT configurations\. The complete framework achieved the highest overall accuracy of 98\.70%, with a Kappa coefficient of 0\.9827, on a geographically separate assessment partition\. The F1\-scores were 99\.02% for Water Area, 98\.38% for Agriculture, 98\.64% for Built\-up Area, and 99\.16% for Barren Land\. Other Land and Unclassified achieved F1\-scores of 96\.03% and 91\.60%, respectively\. Grad\-CAM produced spatially coherent activation patterns over mapped water and cultivated surfaces\. These patterns provided qualitative evidence that the model relied on landscape structures relevant to the predicted classes\. The findings demonstrate that combining complementary local, hierarchical, and global representations improves both classification accuracy and model interpretability\. The proposed framework therefore provides a reliable basis for land\-use and land\-cover monitoring in Najran and for further validation in other hyper\-arid environments\.

## [Resource or Waste?—Sensor\-based Classification of Excavation Material in the NNATT Project](../publications/ff0f2a0f6f1bffc5ac2c.md)

Martin Johannes Findl; Mostafa Elsadek; Daniel Schneider; Florian Mittermayr; Robert Galler; Klaus Philipp Sedlazeck

Abstract Excavation material constitutes the largest mineral waste stream while simultaneously offering considerable potential as a primary and/or secondary raw material in the construction sector\. This contribution outlines the key material characteristics, regulatory framework, and practical utilization challenges\. Excavation materials from two tunnel projects serve as case studies to illustrate how chemical\-mineralogical characterization combined with Artificial Intelligence\-based sensor classification can generate site\-specific utilization strategies\. This approach is implemented in a pilot plant with online\-classification on a continuously operating conveyor belt\. The results demonstrate that systematic integration of excavation material into the circular economy is technically feasible and economically viable, provided that classification procedures, approval processes and project planning are aligned\.

## [Ecosystem service gradients at protected area borders reveal multiple patterns and prevalent management conflicts](../publications/ff264a747b8ab1827115.md)

Alberto González‐García; Margot Neyret; Adrián López\-Tejedor; Marie‐Caroline Prima; Sara Si‐Moussi; Julien Renaud; Maya Guéguen; Sandra Lavorel

Protected areas cannot halt biodiversity loss in isolation; integrating them with surrounding human\-dominated landscapes is critical\. However, this integration is challenged by substantial landscape heterogeneity at protected area borders, making it difficult to determine cross\-border changes in ecosystem service provision\. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a novel framework for characterizing these dynamics by analyzing ecosystem service gradients along protected area borders\. For 16 protected areas in the French Alps, we used a mix of established biophysical models and novel connectivity\-based models for mobile species to assess 12 ecosystem services\. These services were aggregated into three stakeholder\-driven domains reflecting rural, cultural, and urban management priorities\. Automated polynomial regression analysis classified borders into five gradient types\. The most common types were decreasing gradients, representing a decline in ecosystem services outside the protected area, and increasing gradients with the opposite pattern\. Our analysis revealed that these patterns are driven by specific landscape configurations and uncovered frequent trade\-offs between the three management priorities; for example, landscapes supporting rural priorities often degrade cultural and urban ones\. We also identified key opportunities for synergies by identifying areas where ecosystem services for all three priority domains increased simultaneously outside the protected area\. This spatially explicit typology provides a powerful diagnostic tool for designing targeted interventions, such as prioritizing habitat restoration where ecosystem services decline or managing agricultural landscapes to mitigate conflicts across management priorities, supporting a more effective integration of protected areas into the wider landscape\.

## [A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Functional Status and Estimating Health Care Costs in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Retrospective Cohort Study](../publications/ff2b0c1db8f1867395cc.md)

Mira Krämer; Tilmann Kramer

BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension \(PAH\) is a rare and progressive disease associated with substantial clinical heterogeneity and high health care costs\. While machine learning \(ML\) has been increasingly applied to predict clinical outcomes, approaches that integrate clinical prediction with downstream economic modeling remain limited\. OBJECTIVE: This study proposes and evaluates an ML\-based framework that combines prediction of future functional status with estimation of associated health care costs in patients with PAH\. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data from 181 patients with PAH were analyzed\. A total of 6 supervised ML algorithms \(Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator \[LASSO\] regression, ridge regression, k\-nearest neighbors, decision trees, random forest, and gradient boosting\) were trained to predict the relative change in World Health Organization functional class \(WHO\-FC\) from baseline to 12\-month follow\-up using baseline clinical variables\. Predicted change rates were subsequently converted to predicted WHO\-FC values at the 12\-month follow\-up for downstream health care cost estimation\. Missing values in predictor variables were imputed using median substitution\. Median imputation was performed before the dataset was split into training and test sets\. Model performance was evaluated using Pearson correlation coefficient \(r\), and error metrics \(RMSE, MAE, and MedAE\), based on cross\-validation and independent test set validation\. Predicted WHO\-FC values were subsequently linked to externally validated, stratified real\-world health care cost estimates to approximate future economic burden\. RESULTS: =0\.09\)\. Prediction errors were comparable across models\. Estimated mean health care costs ranged from US $12,481 to $12,614 per patient per month\. Despite a significant improvement in WHO\-FC over 12 months, estimated health care costs remained largely unchanged, reflecting persistent economic burden across functional class strata\. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of an ML\-based framework that integrates prediction of functional status with health care cost estimation in PAH\. While predictive performance was moderate, the approach illustrates how ML models can be extended beyond clinical end points toward system\-level applications such as cost forecasting and resource planning\. Further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is required before clinical or health system implementation\.

## [Tax Policy Uncertainty and Corporate Tax Strategies](../publications/ff3271baddf87a8af656.md)

Yao Yue; Yuying Sun; Shouyang Wang; Kai Wu

ABSTRACT This paper examines how firm‐level exposure to tax policy uncertainty affects corporate tax avoidance\. Using US public firms from 2002 to 2020, we measure exposure with the tax policy risk \(TPR\) index of Hassan et al\., which captures the share of quarterly earnings‐call discussion devoted to risks surrounding tax policy\. Firms with greater exposure to tax policy uncertainty exhibit lower effective tax rates: a one‐standard‐deviation increase in TPR raises tax avoidance by 2%–3% relative to the sample mean, and the relationship survives instrumental‐variable estimation, propensity score matching, and lead‐lag tests\. Consistent with real options reasoning, in which uncertainty about domestic tax policy raises the value of relocating income to less exposed jurisdictions, high‐TPR firms shift more income abroad and operate more tax‐haven subsidiaries\. The response is concentrated among financially flexible firms, firms with earnings‐management expertise, and firms with market power, and shareholders value tax avoidance more highly when tax policy uncertainty is high\. Our findings identify tax policy uncertainty as a distinct driver of corporate tax strategies\.

## [A mesterséges intelligencia adatközponti infrastruktúrájának rendszerszintű kihívásai és megoldási lehetőségei: System\-Level Challenges and Potential Solutions for Artificial Intelligence Data Center Infrastructure](../publications/ff36b235b31b2a27e6b8.md)

Gál Zoltán

The rapid scaling of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has made data centres a critical physical infrastructure of the digital economy\. Based on the supplied professional materials and verified scientific, standards\-based and industrial sources, this paper systematises the key challenges of AI data centres, including electricity supply and grid\-development lead times, cooling of high\-density GPU systems, water and carbon efficiency, communication and storage bottlenecks, and the different capacity profiles of train\-ing and inference\. It proposes an energy\-to\-solution approach that complements facility metrics such as PUE, WUE and CUE with service\-level outcomes\. International and Hungarian examples illustrate liquid cooling, waste\-heat recovery, flexible energy portfolios and hybrid HPC\-cloud infrastructures\. The paper concludes that sustainable and sovereign AI capacity requires an integrated energy, net\-work, data and computing masterplan\. KivonatA mesterséges intelligencia \(AI\) gyors skálázódása az adatközpontokat a digitális gazdaság kritikus fi\-zikai infrastruktúrájává tette\. A tanulmány a feltöltött szakmai anyagokra és ellenőrzött tudományos, szabványügyi, illetve ipari forrásokra támaszkodva rendszerezi az AI\-adatközpontok legfontosabb ki\-hívásait\. Vizsgálja a villamosenergia\-ellátás és a hálózatfejlesztés eltérő időhorizontját, a nagy telje\-sítménysűrűségű GPU\-rendszerek hűtését, a víz\- és karbonhatékonyságot, a hálózati kommunikáció és adattárolás szűk keresztmetszeteit, valamint az AI\-oktatás és következtetés eltérő kapacitásigényeit\. A cikk a PUE, WUE és CUE létesítményi mutatókat kiegészítő, szolgáltatási eredményhez kötött „energy\-to\-solution” szemléletet javasol\. Nemzetközi és hazai példákon keresztül bemutatja a folyadékhűtés, a hulladékhő\-hasznosítás, a rugalmas energiaportfólió és a hibrid HPC–felhő infrastruktúra lehetősége\-it\. Következtetések szerint a fenntartható és szuverén AI\-kapacitás integrált energia\-, hálózati, adat\- és számítási mestertervet igényel\.

## [Assessing clinical reasoning in anesthesiology: rationale, multimodal methods, global implementation, and future directions](../publications/ff39c6327698eef9656e.md)

Seyed Mohammad Seyed Alshohadaei; Fereshteh Baghizadeh; Nilofar Massoudi; Alireza Shakeri; Dariush Abtahi; Alireza JolousJamshidi; Maede Karimian

Safe perioperative care hinges on robust clinical reasoning, yet assessing this competency remains a persistent obstacle\. Anesthesiologists constantly navigate time\-sensitive decisions, physiological ambiguity, technical interventions, and interprofessional coordination—elements that conventional tests often fail to capture\. With the global shift toward competency\-based medical education, there is increasing demand for assessment approaches that are both rigorous and adaptable to local realities\. Drawing on programmatic assessment and competency\-based education frameworks, we reviewed the literature on clinical reasoning evaluation in anesthesiology\. We examined tools addressing different facets of reasoning—cognitive, metacognitive, behavioral, and technical—including Simulation\-Based Training \(SBT\), Case\-Based Discussions \(CBD\), Key Features \(KF\) examinations, Script Concordance Testing \(SCT\), Clinical Reasoning Problems \(CRP\), and Comprehensive Integrative Puzzles \(CIP\)\. We also assessed validity, feasibility, and practicality across diverse resource settings\. Each tool captures a distinct dimension of reasoning\. SBT offers an authentic setting for observing crisis management and non\-technical skills, though its resource demands limit widespread adoption\. CBD enables deep exploration of diagnostic logic and metacognitive awareness, but its effectiveness depends on skilled facilitators\. KF tests yield reliable, efficient assessments of critical decisions, while SCT illuminates how trainees handle clinical uncertainty\. In well\-resourced settings, comprehensive portfolios are becoming standard\. Conversely, programs with fewer resources often rely on creative adaptations: phased roll\-outs, structured oral exams, low\-fidelity simulation, and mobile platforms\. A significant evidence gap persists—the link between assessment performance and patient outcomes remains underexplored\. We offer a practical framework for building multimodal portfolios while emphasizing the need for outcomes\-based research, workplace\-based assessment, and equitable access to emerging educational technologies\.

## [Endogenous protein adsorption and functional presentation at bone\-regenerative biointerfaces](../publications/ff4238891d6a38351fe8.md)

Yi Zhang; Yin Xu; Chenhao Zhang; Baomin Lu

Bone\-regenerative materials rapidly acquire proteins from blood, marrow fluid, and the surrounding tissue\. The resulting interface depends on protein quantity, identity, orientation, conformation, and exchange, rather than total adsorption alone\. This narrative critical review examines selected mechanisms through which these features influence receptor recognition and responses relevant to bone repair\. We use the descriptive term interfacial protein state and propose a joint reporting profile for comparisons made under matched exposure and sampling conditions\. Primary evidence is distinguished by protein source, experimental setting, causal perturbation, and limits of interpretation\. The strongest mechanistic examples concern fibronectin presentation and integrin signaling, selected fibrinogen\-dependent inflammatory pathways, and material\-assisted presentation of exogenous growth factors\. Quantitative examples of surface density, accessibility, dissociation, and retained BMP\-2 dose are reported with their experimental conditions\. Autologous platelet\-rich plasma and platelet\-rich fibrin are considered as clinically relevant precoatings whose preparation and release behavior require separate characterization\. Competition between host cells and bacteria for the conditioned interface is also addressed\. Hemostatic\-inflammatory, angiogenic\-matrix\-forming, and mineralization\-remodeling processes are presented as overlapping biological contexts, not as a validated schedule for programming protein exchange\. Evidence from purified coatings and dispersed nanoparticles is not treated as proof of endogenous recruitment or clinical bone healing\. Predicting outcomes across materials, guiding patient\-specific implant selection, and replacing growth\-factor delivery through endogenous capture remain unvalidated\. The proposed measurements organize causal tests and identify evidence gaps; they do not define a universal protein\-state score or an established clinical design rule\.

## [Information quality, understandability, actionability and readability of large language models for HIV health education: A cross‐platform evaluation](../publications/ff4885a220c8d3cf62ba.md)

Mengqiu Hu; Zhiqiang Wang; Jinglan Zhang; Xiaoya Li; Mengxia Zhao

Abstract Objectives Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used to generate health education materials, but their suitability for patient‐facing human immunodeficiency virus \(HIV\) education remains insufficiently evaluated\. We assessed the information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, text structure and source transparency of HIV patient education materials generated by six LLMs or artificial intelligence platforms\. Methods In this cross‐sectional study, 100 common HIV patient education questions across 10 domains were submitted once in English to ChatGPT 5\.4‐Thinking, DeepSeek‐V3\.2, Doubao, ERNIE Bot 5\.0 Preview, Ant Afu and Gemini 3\.1 Pro, yielding 600 responses\. Responses were evaluated using Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials \(PEMAT‐P\), EQ IP‐36, DISCERN, Global Quality Score \(GQS\), artificial intelligence response quality metric \(AIRM\), Journal of the American Medical Association \(JAMA\) benchmarks and seven readability indices\. Platform comparisons used paired Friedman tests with Wilcoxon–Holm post hoc analyses; topic analyses used question‐level aggregation followed by Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn–Holm comparisons\. Results Significant family‐adjusted differences were observed across platforms for all prespecified text‐structure, quality/understandability/actionability and readability outcomes\. At the topic level, five of six text‐structure outcomes, PEMAT‐P Understandability, PEMAT‐P Actionability, the exploratory PEMAT‐P composite score and all seven readability indices differed significantly after family adjustment, whereas EQ IP‐36, DISCERN, GQS, AIRM and JAMA did not\. Overall actionability was limited and readability demands were high\. Conclusions LLM‐generated HIV patient education materials showed substantial cross‐platform and topic‐level heterogeneity\. These findings support the use of LLMs as expert‐reviewed drafting tools rather than independent patient education sources\. Direct factual accuracy, guideline concordance, hallucination and clinical safety were not assessed\.

## [Pinta, Ana Alexandra Durán ; Olvera, Jorge Leodan Cabrera &amp; Robles, Fabricio Fernando Rodríguez: Artificial Intelligence in health Education: Opportunities, Ethical Constraints and Pedagogical Challenges](../publications/ff6cefe8f849f9f7a783.md)



\_EthAIca\_ 4:269\. 2025Introduction: artificial intelligence \(AI\) has great potential to transform healthcare and health education\. Therefore, we set out to analyze the scientific evidence on the implementation of artificial intelligence in the training of healthcare professionals, considering the ethical limitations of its application and opportunities for competence development\. Method: the research had a qualitative approach, with a descriptive design and a literature review\. Eighty\-six articles were analyzed, obtained from indexed databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, Redalyc, and Scielo, using keywords in English, Portuguese, and Spanish\. The information was organized in an Excel matrix for analysis through critical reading using the CASPe method to evaluate the scientific quality of the studies\.Results: the implementation of AI in health education improves personalized learning, clinical simulations, and decision\-making through data analysis\. However, its use carries risks such as the dehumanization of the training process and excessive dependence on technology\. Therefore, it is necessary to train teachers and establish ethical limits that ensure a balance between innovation and critical thinking\. Conclusión: artificial intelligence is revolutionizing health education by improving learning and clinical skills\. However, it poses ethical challenges that require regulation and responsible use\. Its successful integration requires balancing technology and the inclusion of human values\. \(direct link \)

## [Taxonomic revision of Mussaenda wallichii \(Rubiaceae\): two new synonyms from Southeast Asia](../publications/ff76f97a48f33e138b61.md)

Tingting Duan; Yi\-Xuan Li; Jin Li

Mussaenda wallichii G\. Don \(Rubiaceae\) is a widespread species distributed from northeastern India to Southeast Asia, but its taxonomic delimitation has remained uncertain due to overlapping morphological characters and incomplete assessment of type materials\. Based on extensive herbarium examinations, including type specimens, and critical evaluation of protologues, we reassessed the taxonomic identities of M\. intuspilosa Jayaw\. and M\. lancipetala X\.F\. Deng &amp; D\.X\. Zhang\. Morphological comparisons revealed that both taxa are conspecific with M\. wallichii and cannot be distinguished from it by consistent diagnostic characters\. Therefore, they are treated as heterotypic synonyms of M\. wallichii \. Lectotypification of historical names is also discussed\. ## [Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research](../publications/ff7baf34ac88ffc3064f.md)

V Umamaheswara Reddy; Susmitha S\. L\. N\.

Abstract Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support\. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight\. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology\. A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted\. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device \(SaMD\), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations\. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post\-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico\-legal responsibility\. Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI\-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk\-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post\-market performance monitoring\. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems\. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI\-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI\-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross\-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models\. The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation\. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability\. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care\.

## [Deep Learning and Engineered Biomaterials‐Enhanced Imaging‐Guided Cancer Immunotherapy](../publications/ff8ade7b3617e0d67db1.md)

Kaiwei Lv; Bin Li; Bing Xiao; Fei Zhou; Hui Zhao; Jihong Sun; Jun‐Long Liang

ABSTRACT The clinical success of immunotherapies is hindered by the absence of robust methodologies for the early and accurate assessment of antitumor immune responses\. Integrating engineered biomaterials with artificial intelligence \(AI\)‐driven molecular imaging technology offers a powerful approach for predicting immune efficacy\. However, its clinical translation is significantly hindered by several critical limitations, including the complex and costly synthesis of multifunctional imaging probes, insufficient deep‐tissue penetration, suboptimal in vivo signal‐to‐noise ratios, potential immunogenicity and off‐target toxicity, and the limited generalizability of deep learning models across heterogeneous patient populations\. In view of these pressing scientific challenges, this review focuses on the application of chemical and biomolecular strategies‐enhanced engineered biomaterials in promoting the sensitivity and specificity of advanced imaging modalities for visualizing signaling molecules and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment \(TME\)\. Meanwhile, recent progress in deep learning‐driven image analysis has enabled strong predictive capabilities and automated the understanding of complex immune system dynamics\. Together, these technologies provide a transformative platform for non‐invasive monitoring, personalized treatment, and response prediction, with the potential to advance precision immuno‐oncology and significantly impact both basic research and clinical translation\.

## [Inteligencia artificial generativa, carga laboral y bienestar profesional en docentes universitarios en Ecuador](../publications/ff8e488c03cf4f94b098.md)

Sandra Elizabeth Cevallos\-Suarez; Mayra Verónica Lara Llumiquinga; Adriana Cecilia Racines Orbe; Renato M\. Torres

La inteligencia artificial generativa \(IAG\) está transformando la educación superior, y aunque genera expectativas de reducción de carga laboral, también promueve nuevas demandas cognitivas y éticas\. El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa y la carga laboral y el bienestar profesional en docentes universitarios de Quito, Ecuador\. Mediante un diseño mixto secuencial explicativo con intervención formativa \(CUAN1?CUAL?CUAN2\), se aplicaron cuestionarios \(NASA\-TLX, UWES\-9, MBI\) y grupos focales a 280 docentes de tres tipos de universidad\. Los resultados muestran que el uso de IAG predice mayor carga laboral, agotamiento emocional y menor vigor\. La formación redujo significativamente la demanda mental \(d=0\.56\) y el agotamiento \(d=0\.45\)\. El análisis cualitativo reveló tres mecanismos clave: intensificación cognitiva, tensión ético\-identitaria y brecha institucional\. Se concluye que la IAG no reduce automáticamente la carga; su integración crítica y acompañada es indispensable para preservar el bienestar docente\.

## [A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires](../publications/ff95fab127d534246f97.md)

Shiyue Zhang; Wenhao Dong; Deliang Chen

Wildfires in the Amazon have far\-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited\. Here we identify a large\-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers \(ARs\), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south\. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress\. We estimate that wildfire\-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss\. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area \(R² = 0\.67\)\. Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire\-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming\. This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region\.

## [Ethics and Governance in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Lifecycle Engineering Perspective](../publications/ff99318c10bb4bcdda98.md)

Lorenzo Ricciardi Celsi; Junxin Chen

ABSTRACT Trustworthy Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) is often treated as a model property addressed through better training data, alignment, evaluation or guardrails\. We argue instead that trustworthiness is a lifecycle governance capability that must be engineered, evidenced, monitored and adapted across data acquisition, training and alignment, safe inference, public deployment and post‐deployment use\. We develop a lifecycle engineering framework integrating four governance layers – technical, organizational, human‐centred and regulatory – and translate ethical principles and major governance instruments into stage‐specific controls, responsibilities, evidence artefacts, metrics and review triggers\. The framework is constructed through a structured conceptual synthesis of peer‐reviewed literature, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, ISO/IEC 42005, ALTAI, the EU AI Act and complementary security and agentic‐governance guidance\. A source register, seven‐field extraction schema, explicit mapping rules, worked extraction example and weighting sensitivity analysis make the construction logic inspectable\. A public‐facing retrieval‐augmented generation case and a contrastive agentic‐system stress test illustrate operationalization through measurable indicators, responsible actors, review triggers and capability boundaries without being presented as independent empirical validation\. We further address hallucination, prompt injection, privacy leakage, overreliance, unsafe tool use, memory, planners and multi‐agent workflows\. The perspective positions trustworthy GenAI as an evidence‐driven, adaptive socio‐technical capability rather than a one‐time model or compliance claim\.

## [IMPLEMENTASI PENDEKATAN DEEP LEARNING PADA PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM DALAM MENUMBUHKEMBANGKAN KREATIVITAS DAN KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KRITIS MURID DI SMA NEGERI 1 PACET KABUPATEN MOJOKERTO](../publications/ff9fb215849e0882bd1d.md)

Farel Alhafiz; Rahmat

Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) in the era of the Merdeka Curriculum is required not only to focus on the mastery of textual material but also to be able to develop students&\#x27; critical thinking skills and creativity through meaningful, conscious, and enjoyable learning\. The deep learning approach emerges as one of the learning innovations that emphasizes deep understanding, the connection of concepts to real life, and the active involvement of students in the learning process\. However, the implementation of this approach in PAI learning still faces various challenges, both in terms of teacher readiness, learning time, and supporting facilities\. This research aims to: \(1\) analyze the implementation of the deep learning approach in PAI learning at SMA Negeri 1 Pacet, Mojokerto Regency; \(2\) analyze the implications of the deep learning approach in developing students&\#x27; creativity and critical thinking skills; and \(3\) analyze the supporting and inhibiting factors in the implementation of the deep learning approach in PAI learning\. This research uses a qualitative approach with a case study type of research\. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, in\-depth interviews, and documentation\. The research subjects include the principal, PAI teachers, and students of SMA Negeri 1 Pacet, Mojokerto Regency\. Data analysis used the Miles and Huberman model, which includes data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing, while data validity was ensured through source, technique, and time triangulation\. The research results show that the implementation of the deep learning approach in PAI learning is carried out through the stages of planning, implementation, and evaluation of learning, integrating the principles of meaningful learning, mindful learning, and joyful learning\. Teachers apply discussion methods, question and answer sessions, role\-playing, project\-based learning, and case studies to encourage active student engagement\. This approach has a positive impact on the improvement of students&\#x27; creativity and critical thinking skills, as evidenced by their ability to produce original works, relate the material to everyday life, and analyze and solve problems critically\. Supporting factors for implementation include school support, teacher collaboration, training, and student motivation, while hindering factors include limited learning time and the need for adaptation by teachers and students\.

## [Expressivity of IQP Feature\-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces](../publications/ffa1eb0a43a194a87863.md)

Valeria Repetto; Stefano Melchionna; Romina D&\#x27;Aurizio

Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high\-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non\-linear relationships in data\. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space \(RKHS\)\. However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking\. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial \(IQP\) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter\. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic\. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature\-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel\. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known\.

## [A Comprehensive Review of Medicinal Plants and their bioactive as Sources of Wound Healing Agents: Mechanism of Action, Recent Developments and Future Perspectives](../publications/ffb1065da6c2f1b9890a.md)

Pravin Kumar Mourya; Mayank Kumar Yadav; Raziuddin Khan; Zeashan Hussain

Cutaneous wound healing is a complicated and highly regulated biological mechanism that restores the skin&\#x27;s functional and structural integrity after an injury\. It represents a series of various phases: haemostasis, proliferation, inflammation and remodelling\. Disruption of any of the mentioned phases can impair tissue repair, resulting in persistent, non\-healing wounds that present serious economic and therapeutic difficulties\. Although conventional wound\-care therapies have improved patient outcomes, their effectiveness may be limited by factors such as antimicrobial resistance, adverse effects, high treatment costs, and delayed tissue regeneration\. Consequently, there is increasing interest in plants with therapeutic benefits and their bioactive compounds as safer, cost\-effective, and multifunctional alternatives for wound management\. Medicinal herbs have long been used in traditional medicine systems globally, and growing scientific evidence supports their therapeutic potential in promoting wound healing\. Flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, terpenoids, tannins, saponins, glycosides, and essential oils are examples of plant\-derived bioactive chemicals that display a variety of pharmacological actions, including angiogenic, antibacterial, anti\-inflammatory, antioxidant, and collagen\-stimulating properties\. These phytochemicals contribute to wound repair by key modulation of molecular pathways, including the upregulation of VEGF \(vascular endothelial growth factor\) and TGF\-β \(Transforming Growth Factor\-β\), thereby enhancing angiogenesis, fibroblast proliferation, extracellular matrix deposition, collagen synthesis, and re\-epithelialization\. In addition, many herbal compounds suppress pro\-inflammatory mediators, including TNF\-α \(Tumour Necrosis Factor\-α\), IL\-1β \(interleukin\-1β\), and iNOS \(inducible nitric oxide synthase\), thereby reducing oxidative stress and creating a favourable environment for tissue regeneration\. This review summarises an overview of medicinal herbs with their bioactive constituents as promising woundhealing agents\. It summarises the biological mechanisms underlying wound repair and highlights the therapeutic potential of plant\-derived compounds\. Furthermore, the review addresses current challenges, available preclinical and clinical evidence, and future research directions required for the successful translation of these natural products into evidence\-based wound management\. Collectively, the available literature suggests that medicinal plants represent a valuable source of multifunctional bioactive molecules with considerable potential for the development of safe, effective, and innovative wound\-healing therapies\.

## [Possibility of Aporia as Experience in LLM Interaction](../publications/ffc1c3a366f2b5730189.md)

Daniel Mioc

This study examines the possibility of aporia within human\-LLM interactions, proposing the concept of &quot;non\-dialogic aporia&quot; to describe an ontological and relational impasse where a user projects reciprocity onto a syntactic system lacking semantic understanding\. Grounded in classical philosophy, the analysis integrates John Searle’s distinction between syntax and semantics, Martin Buber’s relational framework, Martin Heidegger’s critique of technology as a standing\-reserve \(Bestand\), Jacques Derrida’s theory of the trace and difference, Luciano Floridi&\#x27;s concept of the &quot;Inforg&quot; and David J\. Gunkel&\#x27;s machine ethics\. Using the withdrawal of the GPT\-4o model as a case study, the essay demonstrates that while LLMs remain non\-conscious computational resources, human users can experience profound mourning and ethical interpellation\. Ultimately, non\-dialogic aporia highlights not the personhood of the algorithm, but the tendency of the hybrid human subject to confront its own reflection and externalized mental habitat within the infosphere\.

## [Communication\-efficient collaborative 4D mapping via federated temporal Gaussian pruning and knowledge\-distilled neural radiance fields for post\-disaster rescue robotics](../publications/ffce1abd66028bfd6708.md)

Lei Ding; Zhiying Hu; Jin Yue; Dong Li

Post\-disaster rescue operations demand real\-time, collaborative 4D mapping of dynamic ruins, yet severely damaged communication infrastructure and limited edge computing resources make conventional neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian splatting impractical: they lack temporal representation, incur high transmission latency, and do not address the risks of centralizing raw sensor observations\. To bridge this gap, we propose Fed\-TGP\-KD\-NeRF, a federated collaborative mapping framework that integrates a learnable temporal latent code with multi\-dimensional positional hashing and Fourier feature mapping to construct a continuous 4D dynamic Gaussian field\. Adaptive pruning based on Gaussian opacity and gradient sensitivity removes redundant primitives, while a teacher\-student knowledge distillation paradigm with intermediate\-layer feature alignment and KL divergence compresses the model to approximately 10% of its original size\. An improved federated averaging mechanism with dynamic weight adaptation \(bandwidth and battery status\) and periodic synchronization enables data\-local collaboration by keeping raw observations on the originating robot\. Experiments on the 3DAeroRelief dataset show that the proposed method achieves a PSNR of 32\.58 dB, SSIM of 0\.912, and real\-time rendering at 35\.26 FPS, while reducing per\-round communication overhead to only 13\.45 MB and converging in 42 rounds, outperforming the evaluated baseline methods\. The framework balances reconstruction fidelity, communication efficiency, and raw\-data locality; it does not claim a formal differential\-privacy guarantee\.

## [Enterprise AI Trust, Risk and Compliance \(AI TRiSM\) Framework](../publications/ffdbc01d79c7dad45aad.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

Artificial Intelligence is becoming embedded in enterprise decisions, customer interactions, software engineering, operations, and autonomous workflows\. As adoption expands, organizations must manage not only model performance but also trust, risk, security, compliance, explainability, privacy, resilience, and accountability\. This paper proposes an Enterprise AI Trust, Risk and Compliance \(AI TRiSM\) Framework that integrates enterprise architecture, AI governance, model risk management, cybersecurity, privacy, Responsible AI, legal compliance, observability, and lifecycle controls\. The framework establishes governance domains for AI inventory, risk classification, model assurance, data and prompt governance, identity, security, human oversight, monitoring, incident response, regulatory evidence, and recertification\. It supports predictive AI, Generative AI, Retrieval\-Augmented Generation, and Agentic AI across hybrid and multi\-cloud environments\. The proposed approach enables enterprises to scale AI while maintaining measurable trust, bounded risk, defensible compliance, and clear accountability\.

## [A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework Integrating RoBERTa, Gated Recurrent Units, and Quantum Crested Porcupine Optimizer for Social Media Engagement Prediction](../publications/ffdc0ee3e545d0df5521.md)

Xin Guo; Gonghao Chai; Chao Tan

Social media engagement prediction has become a significant research area in computational social science, enabling content optimization and providing users with personalized experiences across digital platforms\. Despite significant advances in machine learning and deep learning, current models still face challenges such as class imbalance, limited ability to capture long\-term temporal dependencies, and unstable training convergence in high\-dimensional semantic spaces\. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid RoBERTa\-GRU\-QCPO framework that combines contextual language representations generated by RoBERTa with the sequential modeling capability of Gated Recurrent Units \(GRU\), while the Quantum\-Inspired Crested Porcupine Optimizer \(QCPO\) automatically identifies high\-quality hyperparameter configurations to improve training convergence and predictive performance\. The contextual embeddings are then fed into a Gated Recurrent Unit \(GRU\) layer that models sequential dependencies among the contextual token representations generated by RoBERTa, enabling more effective learning of semantic patterns relevant to engagement prediction\. The framework addresses the optimization challenges associated with training complex deep architectures by using the Quantum\-Inspired Crested Porcupine Optimizer \(QCPO\), a metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by defensive mechanisms in crested porcupines and quantum\-inspired concepts such as superposition and tunneling\. Extensive experiments conducted on a large\-scale social media dataset containing approximately 1\.6 million samples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework\. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 97\.95%, precision of 97\.76%, recall of 98\.12%, and F1\-score of 97\.94%, consistently outperforming conventional machine learning methods, deep learning architectures, and state\-of\-the\-art transformer\-based models\. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical applicability of the proposed framework for accurate social media engagement prediction\.

## [A geospatial and community perception analysis of the impacts of land use and land cover change on ecosystem service values](../publications/ffe06a0feeade8fa304f.md)

Md Shafiqul Islam; Tania Yeasmin; Irteja Hasan; Md Nayem Hasan Munna; Parvez Ahmed

Rapid urbanization in developing countries is causing significant changes in land use and land cover \(LULC\), which affect ecosystem service values \(ESVs\)\. This study investigates the impacts of LULC changes on ESV in the Gazipur city area of Bangladesh over a 30\-years from 1991 to 2021\. The analysis was conducted using satellite imagery from Landsat\-5 TM \(1991 and 2006\) and Landsat\-8 OLI\-TIRS \(2021\), with a supervised classification approach to prepare LULC maps and the Benefit Transfer Method for ESV evaluation\. We used the global coefficient values proposed by Costanza et al\. 1 and the updated coefficients from Costanza et al\. 2 , along with the local coefficient values modified by Hoque et al\. 3 for ESV estimation\. The results show significant LULC changes, particularly the rapid expansion of built\-up areas, increasing from 3\.70% in 1991 to 44\.95% in 2021\. Due to this expansion, vegetation cover and agricultural land decreased by 39% and 55%, respectively\. The expansion of urban areas was the main reason for the 40% decrease in water bodies\. These changes show that the study area is rapidly urbanizing and industrializing due to population growth and rising economic activity\. The total ESV demonstrated a declining trend from 1991 to 2021, with overall reductions of 40\.3%, 46\.5%, and 40\.9% estimated under all coefficient sets\. The study found that waterbodies and agricultural land were mostly lost in terms of ESV which accounted for over 60% of the total ESV reduction\. The coefficient of sensitivity \(CS\) was applied to address uncertainties in the valuation process and the results found the assessment to be robust based on all three coefficient sets\. Community perception of Ecosystem Services \(ES\) by LULC category in the study area was measured using a four\-point Likert scale method, and data were collected through direct field surveys using a structured questionnaire, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews\. This approach provides an important community\-based assessment that complements the biophysical ESV outcomes and helps contextualize changes in ES from the community’s perspectives\. This study provides a robust framework to evaluate ES dynamics and support evidence\-driven urban environmental management in rapidly urbanizing cities by integrating long\-term LULC investigation, spatial ESV analysis, multiple valuation coefficient sets and local perceptions\.

## [Analysis and diagnostics of the transfer activity of the Russian football market](../publications/ffeba9ad7d9d92deb998.md)

Valery Gorelikov; P\. A\. Kazakov

The aim of this article is to analyze transfer activity in the Russian football market, considering the sporting, economic, and organizational\-legal aspects of its functioning\. The role of transfer operations in forming the rosters and revenues of football clubs is examined, and an analysis of the transfer expenses, revenues, and balance sheets of Russian Premier League clubs over the past five seasons is provided\. The key regulatory provisions for football player transfers in Russia are revealed, and the main types of transfers are characterized\. The vertical and horizontal trajectories of football players in the Russian and international football systems are revealed and systematized\. Considerable attention is given to the role of football schools and academies in the training of young players and the development of homegrown footballers\. It has been established that the effective development of the transfer market is linked to ensuring the continuity of player progression from the preparatory stage to professional football and subsequent transition to higher competitive levels, including international ones\.

## [Echtzeit\-Luftanalyse und Strömungssimulation für Ereignisbewältigung und Gesundheitsschutz in Untertage\-Infrastrukturen](../publications/fff0bea9acea786c0e6a.md)

Thomas Hochsteiner; Katja Hüttenbrenner; Kern Hannes; Aiman Al\-Fakih; Lucrezia Kroeger\-Lass

Zusammenfassung Das Projekt ELSA4Hans entwickelt ein echtzeitfähiges Messsystem zur Erfassung von Staub, Gasen und Temperaturveränderungen in untertägigen Infrastrukturen, um Gesundheits\- und Arbeitsschutz sowie die Ereignisbewältigung zu verbessern\. Mithilfe von Großversuchen am Zentrum am Berg \(ZaB\), numerischen Simulationen, CFD\-Modellen und maschinellem Lernen werden Ausbreitungs\- und Strömungsmuster untersucht\. Erste Ergebnisse zeigen eine mögliche Differenzierung zwischen einatembarem und alveolengängigem Staub sowie eine starke Abhängigkeit der Schwergasausbreitung von Tunnelgeometrie, Lüftung und Einbauten\. Das System soll künftig eine verbesserte Gefährdungsbewertung, Lüftungsoptimierung und Unterstützung von Einsatzkräften und Infrastrukturbetreiber:innen ermöglichen\.

## [Explaining Chess and Go in Natural Language](../publications/fff6f48df5370ae0d26c.md)

Ori Press; Alexander Golubev

Modern chess engines play far beyond human ability, often choosing moves whose underlying ideas are difficult for humans to understand\. We propose an automatic metric for evaluating chess explanations, grounded in chess\-engine evaluations\. Evaluating state\-of\-the\-art language models using this metric, we find that they perform surprisingly poorly, often relying on surface\-level board observations rather than robust, transferable chess concepts\. We then introduce BinProp, a training\-free method that enables these same models to discover reusable chess concepts and use them to explain moves in natural language\. BinProp improves explainability for every model tested, nearly tripling the average score compared with direct prompting\. Beyond chess, the same method discovers useful concepts in Go, draughts, and shogi without additional tuning\.

## [Transformasi Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam di Era Digital: Integrasi Keterampilan Abad Ke\-21 dan Nilai\-Nilai Islam](../publications/fffdd901f3ad989e057f.md)

Sitti Ratna Dewi Rahmatia; La Ode Muhamad Arafat

Transformasi pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam \(PAI\) menjadi kebutuhan strategis di tengah perkembangan teknologi digital, perubahan karakteristik peserta didik, dan tuntutan kompetensi abad ke\-21\. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk transformasi pembelajaran PAI di era digital dan merumuskan pola integrasi keterampilan 4C \(critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, dan communication\) dengan nilai\-nilai Islam\. Penelitian menggunakan metode library research dengan pendekatan kualitatif\-deskriptif\. Sumber kajian meliputi artikel ilmiah yang relevan, buku metodologi dan pendidikan, regulasi pendidikan, serta dokumen kebijakan dan kerangka kompetensi digital\. Analisis dilakukan melalui content analysis dengan tahapan seleksi sumber, pengodean tema, kategorisasi, interpretasi, dan sintesis\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan tiga perubahan utama: transformasi media pembelajaran melalui LMS, video interaktif, media digital dan AI; transformasi pedagogi dari teacher\-centered menuju student\-centered learning; serta transformasi peran guru menjadi fasilitator, kurator sumber, dan pembimbing etika digital\. Integrasi 4C dengan nilai Islam dapat dilakukan melalui prinsip fathanah dan tabayyun untuk berpikir kritis, ijtihad dan kreativitas untuk menghasilkan gagasan, ta’awun dan syura untuk kolaborasi, serta tabligh dan qaulan ma‘rufa untuk komunikasi\. Artikel ini menawarkan model Blended Learning Berbasis Nilai \(BLBN\) sebagai kerangka konseptual yang menempatkan teknologi sebagai sarana, sedangkan pembentukan akhlak, tanggung jawab, dan kedalaman spiritual sebagai orientasi\. Model tersebut dapat dikembangkan secara fleksibel sesuai karakteristik peserta didik, infrastruktur, tujuan pembelajaran, dan konteks satuan pendidikan\.

## [Cerebellar climbing fibers signal flexible, rapidly adapting reward predictions](../publications/fffe4459352fcbf654e8.md)

Carlo Vignali; Michael Mutersbaugh; Court Hull

Classical models of cerebellar computation posit that climbing fibers \(CFs\) operate according to supervised learning rules, correcting movements by signaling the occurrence of motor errors\. However, recent findings suggest that in some behaviors, CF activity can exhibit features that resemble the instructional signals necessary for reinforcement learning, namely reward prediction errors \(rPEs\)\. Despite these initial observations, many key properties of reward\-related CF responses remain unclear, thus limiting our understanding of how they operate to guide cerebellar learning\. Here, we have measured the postsynaptic responses of CFs onto cerebellar Purkinje cells using two\-photon calcium imaging in mice of both sexes to test how CFs respond to learned stimuli that either do or do not predict reward\. We find that CFs can develop generalized responses to similar cues of the same modality, regardless of whether they are reward predictive\. However, the extent of this generalization depends on temporal context, and generalization does not extend across sensory modalities\. Further, learned CF responses are flexible, and can be rapidly updated according to new reward contingencies\. Together these results reveal two properties of learned CF responses: their generalization across similar cues is graded by the temporal and sensory context in which the cues are learned, and, when reward contingencies are reversed, they update rapidly to track new learning rules\. Significance Statement The cerebellum is best known for coordinating movement, and the climbing fiber teaching signals thought to instruct cerebellar motor learning were long thought to report movement errors exclusively\. Recent work has shown that these instructional signals can also convey information about reward\. Here, by recording from these climbing fiber inputs in mice learning which cues predict reward, we find that they carry flexible, context\-sensitive reward predictions\. Notably, these signals do not simply track which cue an animal should respond to: they generalize across similar cues depending on context, and they rapidly reorganize when reward associations change\. These properties resemble those of midbrain dopamine neurons, the brain&\#x27;s canonical reward system\. These findings reframe how cerebellar teaching signals contribute to reward\-guided learning\.
